This checkpoint continues directly from C013-WIP14. It physically anchors the
stolen-visibility Permanent-Alliance lifecycle defect found during the final
espionage/persistent-field closure and preserves the current adversarial state
before the audit continues from F100.

F099 / provisional KI#421 -- Permanent Alliance leaves live teams' stolen-
visibility relation to the absorbed team active after that target dies, so the
old target's plot-level stolen visibility can become permanent
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
CvTeam::setStolenVisibilityTimer is not merely timer bookkeeping. Whenever a
team-target relation crosses zero, it adds or removes one
CvPlot::StolenVisibilityCount for the stealing team on every plot currently
visible to the target team:

    if (bOldStolenVisibility != isStolenVisibility(eIndex))
        for every plot visible to eIndex
            changeStolenVisibilityCount(getID(), active ? +1 : -1);

Permanent Alliance merging transfers the absorbed team's ordinary visibility
into the surviving team and merges stolen-visibility timers, but it never
performs the corresponding old-target -> 0 transition for live teams that had
stolen visibility against the absorbed team.

CONCRETE OUTSIDER REPRODUCTION
------------------------------
Let A absorb B while outsider C has an active stolen-visibility timer against B.
Before the alliance, C's C->B timer has already added +1 stolen-visibility count
to every plot B can currently see.

During CvTeam::addTeam:
1. B's ordinary visibility is copied into A.
2. The reverse outsider merge computes/sets a weighted C->A stolen-visibility
   timer from C->A and C->B.
3. C->B itself is never cleared through setStolenVisibilityTimer(B, 0).
4. B's players are now members of A and B is no longer an alive team.

CvTeam::doTurn decrements stolen-visibility timers only over
TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE,NOT_SAME_TEAM_AS>. C therefore never visits dead B again and
its old positive C->B timer freezes indefinitely.

When the new C->A timer later expires, setStolenVisibilityTimer(A,0) subtracts
only the plot-level +1 belonging to the new A relation. The old +1 originally
created by C->B remains on B's pre-alliance visible plots, leaving C with
permanent visibility there.

A weighted merged timer that rounds to zero makes the defect even simpler: no
new C->A relation need be created at all, yet the old C->B plot counts remain.

SURVIVOR-INTERNAL SIBLING
-------------------------
The cleanup also has to include survivor A's own A->B stolen-visibility
relation. After B's real sight has been copied into A, A no longer needs an
espionage relation against its new teammate. Leaving A->B active gives A an
extra plot-level stolen-visibility +1 tied to a dead target. As legitimate
merged sight later changes, that stale +1 can continue to reveal former-B plots.

WHY LATER RESET DOES NOT REPAIR IT
----------------------------------
CvTeam::reset does not call setStolenVisibilityTimer when clearing another
team's target slot. It directly executes:

    kLoopTeam.m_aiStolenVisibilityTimer.resetVal(getID());

Thus a later reset can erase the frozen timer value without invoking the
zero-transition that removes plot-level stolen-visibility counts. The leaked
plot state can therefore become permanently detached from its timer bookkeeping.

ANCESTRY / CONTROL
------------------
The underlying Permanent-Alliance stolen-timer merge exists in Civ4CE/BtS and
base AdvCiv as well. K-Mod/Kek-Mod later added a specifically documented fix for
"permanent espionage visibility" during Permanent Alliances, but that repair
only clears CvCity espionage visibility for the absorbed team through
CvCity::setEspionageVisibility. In the same merge machinery the stolen map-
visibility timers continue to be averaged/transferred without clearing the old
absorbed-target relation. No later current-source cleanup path was found.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The order matters because the old relation's plot counts must be removed without
throwing away legitimate merged sight:

1. Copy B's real visibility into survivor A as today.
2. Compute/set each live team's intended post-merge stolen-visibility timer
   against A, using the chosen PA merge policy while the old B timer is still
   available as input.
3. After that transfer, clear every live non-B team's stolen-visibility timer
   against B through setStolenVisibilityTimer(B, 0), not direct array reset.
   This includes survivor A itself and all outsiders such as C.

Calling the setter is essential: it subtracts the old B-derived plot-level
stolen counts. If the live team retains a merged A relation, A's legitimate
visibility/timer contribution remains independently represented.

Classification: inherited BtS/K-Mod Permanent-Alliance espionage-visibility
lifecycle bug.


POST-WIP14 CONTROLS / NORMALIZATION
-----------------------------------
- Repeat-tech Permanent-Alliance sharing was challenged because shareItems uses
  isHasTech while repeat technologies store counts separately and deliberately
  leave isHasTech false. Current SAS contains no bRepeat=1 technologies, so no
  live reproduction exists; retained as generic/modmod robustness only.
- The old Kek-Mod Permanent-Alliance "permanent espionage visibility" fix was
  traced and confirmed to address city espionage visibility only; it does not
  clear StolenVisibilityTimer relations or CvPlot stolen-visibility counts.
- CvPlayer::setTeam changes team aggregate membership/city/population/land state
  but performs no stolen-visibility cleanup.
- CvTeam::changeAliveCount(0) ends wars and related war-plan state but performs
  no stolen-visibility cleanup.
- CvTeam::doTurn's stolen-visibility decrement domain is explicitly alive target
  teams, proving that a surviving team's positive timer against absorbed/dead B
  does not naturally expire.

C013-WIP16 -- FILE 013 CvTeam.cpp -- F100 PROJECT-INHERITANCE ANNOUNCEMENT ROOT
===============================================================================

This checkpoint continues directly from C013-WIP15. It physically anchors the
false project-completion/replay event emitted when a Permanent Alliance inherits
projects from the absorbed team, and preserves the current closure state before
continuing from F101.

F100 / provisional KI#422 -- Permanent-Alliance project inheritance reuses the
ordinary positive project-completion path, generating false duplicate project
completion announcements and replay events
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
CvTeam::shareCounters merges completed Project counts by raising the survivor to
the maximum constituent count. When the absorbed team has more copies of a
project, it calls the survivor's ordinary positive transition:

    int iDelta = kShareTeam.getProjectCount(eProject) - getProjectCount(eProject);
    if (iDelta > 0)
    {
        changeProjectCount(eProject, iDelta);
        GC.getGame().incrementProjectCreatedCount(eProject, -iDelta);
    }

The later incrementProjectCreatedCount compensation repairs the global numerical
"projects created" count. It cannot undo the other positive-completion side
effects that changeProjectCount has already emitted.

FALSE EVENT PATH
----------------
CvTeam::changeProjectCount(...,+N) enters the normal "a project was just
completed by this team" branch whenever the game is final-initialized and not in
WorldBuilder. It builds TXT_KEY_MISC_COMPLETES_PROJECT[_THE], permanently adds a
REPLAY_MESSAGE_MAJOR_EVENT attributed to the survivor's leader/team name, and
sends every living major player the corresponding
TXT_KEY_MISC_SOMEONE_HAS_COMPLETED[_THE] notification with the project-completed
sound.

Permanent Alliances occur during an ordinary final-initialized game, so this
branch is live during shareCounters.

CONCRETE CURRENT-SAS REPRODUCTION
---------------------------------
Current SAS has ordinary pre-alliance projects such as PROJECT_APOLLO_PROGRAM,
PROJECT_SDI, PROJECT_THE_INTERNET, PROJECT_MANHATTAN_PROJECT and spaceship
components. There is no Permanent-Alliance rule requiring the two teams to own
identical project sets.

Let survivor A lack Apollo while absorbed team B already owns Apollo. During
A.addTeam(B):
1. shareCounters runs while B is still a separate team and its players have not
   yet been reassigned to A.
2. B.ProjectCount(Apollo)=1 and A.ProjectCount(Apollo)=0, so shareCounters calls
   A.changeProjectCount(Apollo,+1).
3. changeProjectCount emits a fresh replay event/message saying team A completes
   Apollo, even though B completed that Apollo earlier and no new project was
   built at the alliance turn.
4. shareCounters then decrements the global ProjectCreatedCount by one, restoring
   only that numerical counter.
5. B's players are reassigned to A later in addTeam. The already-created replay
   record and notifications remain permanently false/duplicated.

The same mechanism applies to any project where the absorbed team has a higher
count than the survivor. Multi-copy spaceship projects can emit the completion
message once per positive merge call as well, regardless of how many copies were
actually inherited in iDelta.

ORDERING CONTROL
----------------
CvTeam::addTeam calls shareCounters(eTeam) before looping through the absorbed
team's players and calling CvPlayer::setTeam(getID()). Therefore getReplayName,
getName and getLeaderID inside the survivor's changeProjectCount describe the
surviving team at the moment the false completion event is created; they do not
somehow report the absorbed team as the historical builder.

ANCESTRY / CONTROL
------------------
The same underlying pattern is present in Civ4CE/BtS: shareCounters calls
changeProjectCount for inherited positive project deltas and only afterward
compensates ProjectCreatedCount; BtS changeProjectCount also emits replay and
major-event project-completion notifications for every positive change. Base
AdvCiv retains the pattern. This is therefore an inherited BtS Permanent-
Alliance transition bug, not an SAS regression.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Project inheritance needs the state/effect processing of a positive project
count change but must not masquerade as a newly completed project. A conservative
repair is to give changeProjectCount (or a dedicated PA-transfer helper) an
explicit "announce completion" / transfer-mode control and suppress replay/UI
completion events during shareCounters inheritance while retaining legitimate
state updates such as project count, project effects, Tech Share count, victory
re-evaluation and AI production invalidation. The existing global-created-count
compensation can remain or be folded into the same transfer-aware path.

Classification: inherited BtS Permanent-Alliance project-transfer reporting bug.


POST-WIP15 CONTROLS / NORMALIZATION
-----------------------------------
- Current Project XML was checked for a concrete live reproduction: Apollo, SDI,
  The Internet, Manhattan and spaceship components provide ordinary projects
  whose counts can differ between two teams before a Permanent Alliance.
- addTeam ordering was rechecked: shareCounters runs before absorbed players are
  reassigned, so the completion event is deterministically attributed to the
  survivor rather than being neutralized by the later team merge.
- Civ4CE/BtS changeProjectCount contains the same positive-project replay/message
  branch, while its shareCounters likewise compensates only the numerical global
  project-created count after inheritance. F100 is therefore not caused by an
  SAS-only announcement customization.
- The earlier project-count-limit concern remains rejected: current PA project
  counts are max-merged, not summed; the old sum implementation is commented out.

--------------

C013-WIP17 -- FILE 013 CvTeam.cpp -- F101 AUTOLOG NO_PLAYER TECH-EVENT ROOT
===============================================================================

This checkpoint continues directly from C013-WIP16. It physically anchors the
optional BUG Autolog integration defect exposed by Permanent-Alliance technology
sharing and preserves the closure state before continuing from F102.

F101 / provisional KI#423 -- Permanent-Alliance technology sharing fires the
legitimate techAcquired player sentinel NO_PLAYER, but BUG Autolog dereferences
that sentinel as a real player and raises a Python handler exception
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
CvTeam::shareItems shares technologies between the two constituent teams before
players are reassigned. For a technology known by one constituent but not the
other, it deliberately calls setHasTech with no unique discovering player:

    setHasTech(eTech, true, NO_PLAYER, true, false, false,
               TECH_ACQUISITION_TEAM_MERGE);

CvTeam::setHasTech then sends the normal Python techAcquired event. SAS adds
TechAcquisitionCause only to its GameRecord logging; CvEventReporter explicitly
keeps the original Python signature and forwards ePlayer unchanged.

The base CvEventManager handler documents the contract directly:

    # Note that iPlayer may be NULL (-1) and not a refer to a player object

and guards player-only behavior with iPlayer > -1.

BUG Autolog's parallel handler does not preserve that contract. With technology
logging enabled it reaches, in its player-specific traded-tech branch:

    zsCiv = gc.getPlayer(iPlayer).getName() + ...

without first excluding iPlayer == -1.

SENTINEL FAILURE
----------------
CyGlobalContext::getCyPlayer explicitly returns NULL when idx == NO_PLAYER.
Therefore gc.getPlayer(-1) is exposed to Python as None. Calling getName or
getCivilizationShortDescription on it raises a Python exception.

BugEventManager catches exceptions from individual event handlers and traces the
failure, so this is not asserted to crash the DLL/game process. The Autolog
techAcquired handler nevertheless fails, the intended log entry is lost, and a
Python error/trace is produced.

NORMAL PERMANENT-ALLIANCE REPRODUCTION
--------------------------------------
1. Enable BUG Autolog and technology logging (LogTech defaults true once logging
   itself is active).
2. During the active human's normal input phase, accept/form a Permanent Alliance
   with another team that knows at least one technology the survivor does not.
3. CvDeal processes TRADE_PERMANENT_ALLIANCE immediately and calls CvTeam::addTeam.
4. addTeam -> shareItems transfers the differing tech with ePlayer=NO_PLAYER and
   fires techAcquired before the absorbed players are reassigned.
5. Autolog receives iPlayer=-1.
6. When its bHumanPlaying branch is active, it tries gc.getPlayer(-1).getName()
   and the handler raises.

The bHumanPlaying reachability is not guessed from its name. Autolog sets it true
on EndGameTurn and the sequential-turn player lifecycle does not enter
CvPlayer::doTurn / the handler's BeginPlayerTurn transition until the player ends
its active input turn. Human diplomacy and CvDeal acceptance occur during that
input window, so a human-formed PA can hit the branch normally.

ANCESTRY / CONTROL
------------------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains both sides of the mismatch: PA shareItems calls
setHasTech(...,NO_PLAYER,...) and autologEventManager.onTechAcquired performs the
unguarded gc.getPlayer(iPlayer) access. The ordinary CvEventManager in the same
base tree already guards the documented -1 contract, providing a direct correct
control. This is therefore an inherited BUG/AdvCiv optional-Autolog integration
bug, not an SAS regression.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Handle NO_PLAYER explicitly in autologEventManager.onTechAcquired before any
player lookup. The smallest safe repair is to skip the player-specific traded-
tech formatting when iPlayer < 0. A richer repair can log a team/alliance
acquisition using iTeam instead; it must not synthesize an arbitrary player
because team merges deliberately have no unique discovering/trading player.

Classification: inherited BUG/AdvCiv optional Autolog sentinel-contract bug,
exposed by CvTeam Permanent-Alliance tech sharing.


POST-WIP16 CONTROLS / NORMALIZATION
-----------------------------------
- CvDllPythonEvents was traced to confirm that the techAcquired Python signature
  remains (tech, team, player, announce); SAS's new acquisition-cause enum is
  intentionally GameRecord-only and does not sanitize the player sentinel.
- CyGlobalContext::getCyPlayer was traced rather than assumed: NO_PLAYER returns
  NULL, establishing the Python None dereference concretely.
- BugEventManager's event dispatch was traced: handler exceptions are caught and
  logged, so F101 is described as a Python handler failure/error, not a guaranteed
  whole-game crash.
- Autolog.xml was checked: Autolog itself is optional/disabled by default, while
  LogTech defaults true conditional on logging being active. F101 is therefore a
  live optional-feature defect, not a default-every-game failure.
- The earlier first-contact half-initialized state was checked against current
  Python firstContact handlers; no additional live handler failure beyond F092's
  Tech Share timing was established.

PURPOSE

Freeze the first correction produced by the final adversarial reread. WIP17
promoted an Autolog NO_PLAYER hypothesis as F101 / provisional KI#423. That
hypothesis is false because it stopped tracing the actor parameter one step too
early. The explicit NO_PLAYER supplied by Permanent-Alliance shareItems is
normalized inside CvTeam::setHasTech before the Python event is fired.

FORMER F101 / provisional KI#423 -- RETRACTED FALSE POSITIVE
------------------------------------------------------------
Incorrect WIP17 claim:
- Permanent-Alliance technology sharing calls setHasTech with ePlayer=NO_PLAYER.
- BUG Autolog's techAcquired handler does not guard iPlayer == -1.
- Therefore PA tech sharing was claimed to pass -1 to Autolog and trigger a
  Python None.getName()/None.getCivilizationShortDescription error.

Adversarial correction:
- CvTeam::shareItems really does call setHasTech(..., NO_PLAYER, ...).
- However CvTeam::setHasTech immediately performs:

      if (ePlayer == NO_PLAYER)
          ePlayer = getLeaderID();

  before either repeat-tech or ordinary-tech EventReporter calls.
- The later call is therefore:

      CvEventReporter::getInstance().techAcquired(
          eTech, getID(), ePlayer, ...);

  where ePlayer is already the valid team leader ID.
- CvEventReporter preserves that now-valid value when forwarding the ordinary
  Python techAcquired event.
- The unguarded BUG Autolog handler is thus not reached with -1 through this PA
  path. Its missing NO_PLAYER guard may still be weak defensive code, but this
  audit has no normal producer that sends NO_PLAYER through CvTeam::setHasTech.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 has the same early NO_PLAYER -> getLeaderID normalization, so
  this is not an SAS regression hidden by later changes.

Conclusion:
- RETRACT former F101 / provisional KI#423 completely.
- Do not implement/document KI#423 as a PA Autolog bug.
- Reopen F101 as the next unused root ID, matching the audit convention used
  after the earlier former F066/KI#387 false positive.

WHY THE FALSE POSITIVE WAS USEFUL TO RECORD
-------------------------------------------
The raw shareItems call and Python handler look convincing in isolation. The
mistake was failing to carry the argument through the first lines of
CvTeam::setHasTech. Recording this correction prevents the same cross-file
NO_PLAYER hypothesis from being rediscovered later and strengthens the closure
method: producer -> immediate normalizer -> reporter -> Python consumer must all
be traced before promoting an integration root.

------------------------

- Former F101 / provisional KI#423 is RETRACTED FALSE POSITIVE.
- NEXT ROOT ID: F101 UNUSED.
- CvTeam.cpp remains OPEN; C014 has not been earned yet.
- Continue final stateful-setter/persistent-field/source-order/caller closure
  plus adversarial reread of F078-F100 from F101 unused.

F098 / KI#420 STRENGTHENING -- EXACT HasMetCounter IS A SECOND MANIFESTATION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP14 proved that Permanent Alliance merges the deterministic CvTeam
m_aiTurnsAtPeace relation asymmetrically: survivor->outsider takes max while
outsider->survivor takes a team-size-weighted average.

The final counter audit shows that CvTeamAI::m_aiHasMetCounter belongs to the same
root.

CvTeamAI::AI_doCounter explicitly distinguishes exact from randomized counters:

    /* No randomization for atWar and hasMet. These are used by the AI in
       several places that more or less assume an exact count. */

Both directions of a normal first-contact relation therefore start together and
advance once per turn. Yet PA uses the same max-versus-weighted split:

    shareCounters: survivor->C = max(A->C, B->C)
    addTeam:        C->survivor = weighted(C->A, C->B)

For equal-size A/B with 100 and 5 contact turns, the merged relation becomes
100 in one direction and about 52 in the other. This breaks the exact bilateral
contact-history invariant just as the TurnsAtPeace split does.

Internal controls strengthen the classification:
- AI_getAtPeaceCounter is deliberately randomized and may legitimately diverge,
  so it does NOT join F098.
- OpenBordersCounter, DefensivePactCounter and ShareWarCounter are likewise
  randomized/decaying state in advc.130k and do not carry an exact bilateral
  invariant.
- AI_getAtWarCounter is exact, but PA explicitly reconciles the survivor's value
  to the already-computed reverse weighted result; that neighboring code is a
  direct control showing how exact bilateral state can be kept symmetric.

Normalize F098/KI#420 as: Permanent Alliance asymmetrically merges exact bilateral
peace/contact history. Proven manifestations are m_aiTurnsAtPeace and
AI_getHasMetCounter.

F099 / KI#421 PRECISION CONTROL -- ORDINARY ELIMINATION DOES NOT REPRODUCE PA LEAK
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The stolen-visibility lifecycle root remains PA-specific rather than a generic
"target becomes dead" defect.

During ordinary elimination, target-team units/cities lose legitimate sight and
CvPlot::changeVisibilityCount continues to visit alive observing teams. If an
observer still has isStolenVisibility(target), those sight-loss transitions
subtract the observer's plot-level stolen-visibility counts. Thus the secondary
plot state naturally drains as the defeated target loses visibility.

Permanent Alliance is different: addTeam copies absorbed B's legitimate sight to
survivor A and then kills team identity B by member reassignment, without driving
B through the ordinary sight-loss transition and without clearing observer->B
through setStolenVisibilityTimer(B,0). B's old plot-level stolen counts can
therefore remain after the new observer->A timer later expires.

This negative control narrows rather than weakens F099.

F100 / KI#422 RECHECK
---------------------
The project-inheritance replay/message root remains direct and current-source
provable. changeProjectCount(+delta) still runs its normal positive completion
side effects before addTeam compensates only ProjectCreatedCount. The project-art
vector is NOT a memory-safety sibling: changeProjectCount pushes one -1 art slot
per inherited project and asserts vector-size/project-count balance. Thus the
source-proven root remains false duplicate completion/message/replay state, not an
out-of-bounds art-vector defect.

RAW DIVISOR / INDEX / LIST / POINTER CLOSURE

Divisors:

root emerged.

Leader-capital helper:

PERSISTENT-FIELD / PA PROVENANCE CONTROLS
-----------------------------------------
The remaining serialized/transient fields were challenged for state that is
neither derived/recomputed nor explicitly migrated.

m_abJustDeclaredWar:
- PA does not explicitly inherit the absorbed team's flag.
- Its live consumers are AdvCiv's same-turn invasion move-spending option and the
  DoW-specific capturable-unit chance.
- Current SAS has SPEND_ALL_MOVES_ON_INVASION=0 and both
  BASE_UNIT_CAPTURE_CHANCE=50 and DOW_UNIT_CAPTURE_CHANCE=50.
- Therefore changing the flag has no current behavioral consequence. Keep this as
  config/modmod robustness only, not F101.

m_bMapCentering:
- The flag is one-way and PA does not explicitly max/copy it.
- In normal current SAS, Permanent Alliance trading is enabled by TECH_GAME_THEORY.
  Game Theory requires Corporation, whose current prerequisite chain runs through
  Paper; TECH_PAPER itself has bMapCentering=1.
- No current Python/gameplay path independently grants PA trading. Therefore every
  normally PA-eligible constituent already has the Paper map-centering state.
- A raw CyTeam API caller could manufacture a different state, but no normal
  current-SAS reproduction exists. Do not promote.

Repeat technologies / team-limited UnitClass/BuildingClass:
- Current SAS has no repeatable technologies, so generic repeat-count PA weakness
  remains dormant.
- Current SAS has no positive UnitClass/BuildingClass MaxTeamInstances; generic
  summed-count risk remains dormant. Projects are the live team-limited family
  and receive their dedicated max merge.

Vassal/master power and capitulation state:
- These values describe a vassal agreement at signing and PA trading excludes
  vassal teams. They therefore do not create a normal PA migration requirement.

Project default/art provenance:
- inherited counts create valid -1 project-art slots and -1 is a supported
  undefined/default art state. Loss of the absorbed team's cosmetic/default art
  choice remains a cosmetic/closed-EXE risk note only; no source-level gameplay
  failure has been established.

ADVERSARIAL F078-F100 RESULT
----------------------------
Every currently live root was re-challenged against the 2026-08-25 14:12 SAS
source, current XML/options where relevant, and the already-supplied AdvCiv 1.14
/ Civ4CE controls. No additional retraction survived.

F078 / KI#400 -- SURVIVES
Counterespionage turns+modifier remain keyed by TeamTypes and are not migrated in
either PA direction. Former-B players immediately use survivor A identity, so a
live B->C effect disappears; outsider C->B is likewise stranded. Current XML has
a live 10-turn/+100 Counterespionage mission, so this is not dormant capability.

F079 / KI#401 -- SURVIVES
m_aiHasMetTurn is genuine historical state consumed by the Info Screen graph /
partial-score-graph gates. The objection "A itself only met C at the alliance"
does not close the root: B's players become members of A, while the merged team
has only one team-level first-contact timestamp. Resetting that timestamp to the
alliance turn discards history possessed by members of the merged team. Both
A->C and C->A need the inherited earliest real date.

F080 / KI#402 -- SURVIVES
A live B<->C Disengage deal follows its players and therefore becomes A<->C after
B's player is reassigned, while the enforcement flag is TeamTypes-keyed and is
not migrated. The deal continuing while its team flag vanishes remains a direct
state/deal inconsistency.

F081 / KI#403 -- SURVIVES
Victory countdown/canLaunch is independent live team state. PA still has no
post-launch prohibition. Project transfer can both strand absorbed B's active
countdown and recompute survivor A's canLaunch from project counts even if A had
already launched. Ordinary construction's countdown guard is a useful control:
this is specifically a PA state-transfer path that bypasses it.

F082 / KI#404 -- SURVIVES
setResearchProgress still adds the overflow amount to an already-overflowed
stored progress value instead of reducing the completed-tech progress to that
overflow. The suspicious arithmetic is source-direct and independently
rediscovered by the final mechanical arithmetic pass; it remains normalized to
F082 rather than duplicated.

F083 / KI#405 -- SURVIVES
The non-repeat setHasTech transition still performs m_iTechCount++ for both
true->false and false->true. Advanced Start supplies a supported false transition,
and current gameplay consumers use the cached total. Save/load preserves the
bad cache rather than repairing it.

F084 / KI#406 -- SURVIVES
Current TECH_SATELLITES remains Advanced-Start refundable and bMapVisible. Full
plot revelation is irreversible, whereas the tech can be removed/refunded. The
repair remains refund-policy/validation rather than attempting to erase possibly
legitimate independent map knowledge.

F085 / KI#407 -- SURVIVES
Player currentEra remains monotonic in ordinary setHasTech acquisition and has
no inverse on Advanced Start tech removal. Current-era consumers are live
mechanics, not presentation only. Restricting any recomputation to the Advanced
Start removal transaction remains the least disruptive repair direction.

F086 / KI#408 -- SURVIVES
isInContactWithBarbarians still derives iUnitThresh directly from current era.
Era 0 therefore makes the own-unit filter `count < 0` impossible and the
barbarian-unit test `count > 0`, globalizing the intended local early contact
criterion as soon as any qualifying barbarian unit exists anywhere.

F087 / KI#409 -- SURVIVES
shareItems still processes the survivor team ID in the absorbed team's directed
EP array, converting ordinary B->A espionage into A->A self-target EP. K-Mod's
getTotalUnspentEspionage still includes self because it iterates CIV_ALIVE
without NOT_SAME_TEAM_AS, and live spy-transport AI uses that total as a target
share denominator. This is not harmless dead-slot residue.

F088 / KI#410 -- SURVIVES
Advanced Start removal validation is team-tech-wide at the mutation boundary but
still checks only the acting player's units/buildings and no already-purchased
map improvements/routes. Current Agriculture/The Wheel/etc. provide ordinary
buy-infrastructure-refund examples. The root remains incomplete dependency
validation, with teammate and infrastructure manifestations kept together.

F089 / KI#411 -- SURVIVES AND BROADENS BIDIRECTIONALLY
The historical K-Mod m_abHasSeen omission is real in BOTH observer directions.
The prior wording established that absorbed B's players can lose identity
knowledge of outsider C because A.hasSeen(C) is not unioned.

The reverse is equally direct: if outsider C historically saw B but never A,
then after B's player is reassigned to team A, identity-display checks for that
player consult C.hasSeen(A). addTeam never transfers C.hasSeen(B) into
C.hasSeen(A). Thus an outsider can also lose the identity of a civilization /
player it had already seen merely because that player joined the surviving team.
Current-map copying can reconstruct some cases but cannot reconstruct historical
residue after the revealing city/owner evidence has changed. Normalize F089 as
PA failure to union historical hasSeen identity knowledge in both directions.

F090 / KI#412 -- SURVIVES
TRADE_CITIES continues to carry a player-local city ID, while the reparations
announcement formatter resolves it through the giving team's leader after
player identity has been discarded. Multi-player teams created by PA make the
namespace collision reachable. Deal execution itself remains the clean control
because it uses the actual giving PlayerTypes.

F091 / KI#413 -- SURVIVES
turnsOfForcedPeaceRemaining still recognizes only a TRADE_PEACE_TREATY at the
head of the first list. AdvCiv deliberately keeps treaty items at the bottom of
ordinary offer lists, and valid reparations can precede them. The helper's live
AI callers therefore can see zero remaining forced-peace turns while the team
flag and deal still enforce peace.

F092 / KI#414 -- SURVIVES
meet still calls makeHasMet sequentially, and makeHasMet still triggers Tech
Share before reciprocal contact has been initialized. OTHER_KNOWN_TO examines
the reverse relation, preserving the initiator-dependent Internet grant. The
later firstContact callback reread found no second independent persistent root;
Tech Share remains the concrete gameplay manifestation.

F093 / KI#415 -- SURVIVES
The doWarWeariness loop remains CIV_ALIVE while retaining a branch explicitly
intended to apply accelerated decay to dead targets. The dead-target branch is
therefore unreachable after the AdvCiv iterator refactor, and old war-weariness
can remain frozen until revival. Neighboring dead-target timer pausing that was
already present in BtS is not folded into this regression.

F094 / KI#416 -- SURVIVES
Persistent tech effects and currentEra still use alive-only MemberIter even
though the pre-practical-1837 loops intentionally processed every player
assigned to the team. A dead member of a still-alive team can therefore miss
later team tech effects, and revival does not replay the team's known techs.

F095 / KI#417 -- SURVIVES
getDefensivePower(eExcludeTeam) still excludes only direct players of the
attacking team. A vassal whose master is eExcludeTeam can be counted through the
target master's Defensive Pact with that same master, putting the attacker's own
vassal power on the target side. Numerous UWAI/war-evaluation callers pass the
attacking team explicitly, so this is not a Python-only API corner.

F096 / KI#418 -- SURVIVES
Tech Share still counts getNumMembers() for each alive known team with the tech,
while getNumMembers includes dead assigned teammates. Current Internet threshold
is 2 players and the feature's AI valuation uses alive player iteration, leaving
a direct implementation/valuation semantic mismatch.

F097 / KI#419 -- SURVIVES
The Customizable Domestic Advisor X wrapper still returns city.getY() in its
map-centering-unlocked branch while Y also returns getY(). Current Paper /
Stonehenge map-centering sources make the branch reachable. This remains a
cross-file Python/UI root surfaced from the CvTeam map-centering audit.

F098 / KI#420 -- SURVIVES IN BROADENED FORM
Both deterministic m_aiTurnsAtPeace and exact AI_getHasMetCounter are merged
max-on-survivor versus weighted-on-outsider. AI_doCounter explicitly documents
HasMet and AtWar as exact; AtWar's explicit post-merge reconciliation is the
neighboring control. Randomized/decaying AtPeace/OpenBorders/DP/ShareWar counters
do not join this root.

F099 / KI#421 -- SURVIVES, PA-SPECIFIC
setStolenVisibilityTimer owns secondary per-plot visibility counts. PA transfers
B's real sight to A but never clears live observers' old ->B relation through the
setter before B dies by member reassignment. Normal civilization elimination is
a negative control because ordinary sight loss drains those plot counts. Direct
resetVal later can erase bookkeeping without removing leaked plot state.

F100 / KI#422 -- SURVIVES
PA project inheritance still calls ordinary positive changeProjectCount before
compensating only ProjectCreatedCount. The positive path can emit completion /
replay/message side effects for a project that B completed earlier. Project-art
vector sizing remains correct and is explicitly rejected as a memory-safety
sibling.

FINAL LIST-HEAD / SOURCE-ORDER CONTROL
--------------------------------------
The only other raw CvTeam.cpp `.head()` use is
allowDefensivePactsToBeCanceled(). Mixed dual deals are genuinely possible in
multiplayer (CvDeal::doTurn explicitly documents dual+GPT mixtures), so its
head-only DP recognition is generically fragile. However current SAS has
BBAI_DEFENSIVE_PACT_BEHAVIOR=0. In that mode triggerDefensivePacts first calls
kTarget.cancelDefensivePacts(), whose implementation scans the full first list
and kills every target DP deal before allowDefensivePactsToBeCanceled runs.
Therefore the head-only helper has no demonstrated current-SAS behavioral
consequence under the shipped configuration. Keep it as a configuration/modmod
robustness note, not F101. If BBAI behavior 1/2 is ever enabled, it deserves a
fresh focused audit.

The PA-Tech-Share intermediate-state candidate also remains rejected: Internet
thresholding counts players, so A and B as separate pre-merge teams contribute
exactly the same A-members+B-members total they contribute after merging. Any
dead-member inflation is already F096.

FINAL NORMALIZED ROOT LEDGER -- FILE 013 / CROSS-FILE ROOT REACHED FROM IT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

F078 / KI#400 -- RETAINED
Permanent Alliance fails to migrate active Counterespionage state in either
relevant direction. The turns/modifier arrays are TeamTypes-keyed live gameplay
state and current espionage missions still create nonzero 10-turn/+100 effects.
Player reassignment cannot reconstruct them.

F079 / KI#401 -- RETAINED
Permanent Alliance does not union inherited first-contact dates
`m_aiHasMetTurn`. The surviving team can replace an absorbed constituent's older
real contact date with the alliance-turn contact created during `meet`, changing
partial Info-Screen graph/history visibility for players who are now members of
the same merged team. The correct invariant is the earliest real inherited date
for the merged bilateral relationship, not merely the survivor's personal date.

F080 / KI#402 -- RETAINED
A live Disengage deal can follow reassigned players through a Permanent Alliance
while the TeamTypes-keyed `m_abDisengage` enforcement flag is not migrated. The
deal and the rule-enforcement state can therefore disagree after the merge.

F081 / KI#403 -- RETAINED
Permanent Alliance does not coherently merge spaceship/victory launch state.
An absorbed team's active victory countdown can be lost, while inherited project
counts can also make the survivor launch-capable again despite an earlier launch.
The PA trade gate has no post-launch exclusion. This is persistent team gameplay
state, not merely announcement/UI state.

F082 / KI#404 -- RETAINED
`setResearchProgress` mishandles completed-tech overflow by adding the computed
overflow to the already-overflowed stored progress value. The final mechanical
arithmetic pass independently rediscovered the same suspicious line and
normalized it back into F082 rather than creating a duplicate root.

F083 / KI#405 -- RETAINED
The non-repeat `setHasTech` branch increments `m_iTechCount` on both false->true
and true->false transitions. Advanced Start supplies a supported tech-removal
transition, so refunds can increase the cached total-tech count instead of
reducing it. Current gameplay consumers use that cache and save/load preserves
it.

F084 / KI#406 -- RETAINED
Current `TECH_SATELLITES` is Advanced-Start refundable and has `bMapVisible=1`.
Buying it reveals the full map irreversibly; refunding/removing the tech cannot
separate that knowledge from other legitimate revelation sources. The clean
repair direction is therefore to prevent/refine the refund rather than attempt a
blind map rollback.

F085 / KI#407 -- RETAINED
Advanced Start tech removal does not lower player `currentEra`, although tech
acquisition raises it. The era value has live gameplay consumers. Any repair
should remain narrowly transaction-aware rather than making ordinary era state
non-monotonic globally.

F086 / KI#408 -- RETAINED
`isInContactWithBarbarians` derives its own-unit threshold directly from current
era. In ERA_ANCIENT that threshold is 0, making the own-unit test `< 0`
impossible while the barbarian-unit side becomes `> 0`. The intended local
contact criterion can therefore globalize as soon as any qualifying barbarian
unit exists anywhere.

F087 / KI#409 -- RETAINED
Permanent-Alliance espionage summation includes the absorbed team's directed EP
against the survivor and stores it as survivor self-target EP. K-Mod's
`getTotalUnspentEspionage()` includes self because its alive-team iteration does
not exclude the same team, and live spy-transport AI consumes that total as a
share denominator. This is behaviorally observable state, not harmless dead-slot
residue.

F088 / KI#410 -- RETAINED
Advanced Start tech-refund validation is incomplete at the team mutation
boundary. It checks only the acting player's unit/building dependencies and does
not cover teammates or already-purchased tech-dependent map infrastructure such
as improvements/routes. Current Agriculture/The Wheel-style dependencies give
ordinary reproductions. These manifestations remain one dependency-validation
root.

F089 / KI#411 -- RETAINED, BIDIRECTIONAL NORMALIZATION
Permanent Alliance fails to union K-Mod historical `m_abHasSeen` identity
knowledge in both directions.

1. Absorbed B's players can lose historical identity knowledge of outsider C
   because, after reassignment, their team identity queries use A.hasSeen(C).
2. Outsider C can likewise lose historical identity knowledge of B's player/
   civilization because that player now belongs to A and C.hasSeen(A) was never
   inherited from C.hasSeen(B).

Current map/revealed-state copying can reconstruct some present evidence, but it
cannot reconstruct arbitrary historical residue once the original revealing
city/ownership evidence has changed.

F090 / KI#412 -- RETAINED
Reparations city announcement formatting receives only TeamTypes and resolves a
player-local city ID through the team's leader. Permanent Alliance makes
multi-player teams normal, so a city belonging to a nonleader member can be
misnamed or omitted. Deal execution is the control: it retains the actual giving
PlayerTypes and resolves the local city namespace correctly.

F091 / KI#413 -- RETAINED
`turnsOfForcedPeaceRemaining` recognizes a peace treaty only when
`TRADE_PEACE_TREATY` is the first item of the first deal list. Valid AdvCiv deal
construction can place reparations/other items before the treaty. AI callers can
therefore observe zero remaining forced-peace turns while `isForcePeace` and the
actual deal still enforce peace.

F092 / KI#414 -- RETAINED
`meet` initializes contact directionally through two sequential `makeHasMet`
calls, and `makeHasMet` triggers Tech Share before reciprocal contact is set.
`OTHER_KNOWN_TO` tests the reverse relationship, so an Internet/Tech-Share grant
can depend on which direction executes first. The final callback audit found no
second independent persistent first-contact root; Tech Share remains the proven
manifestation.

F093 / KI#415 -- RETAINED
`doWarWeariness` now iterates `TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE>` while retaining an inner
branch explicitly intended for `!target.isAlive()`. That dead-target branch is
unreachable after the iterator refactor, so war weariness against a dead team can
remain frozen and later matter again if the team revives.

F094 / KI#416 -- RETAINED
Persistent tech/player effects and era propagation use alive-only `MemberIter`.
A dead member of a still-alive team can miss tech-derived player state acquired
while dead, and revival does not replay the team's known technologies. The
pre-practical-1837 full-player loop provides the historical semantic control.

F095 / KI#417 -- RETAINED
`getDefensivePower(eExcludeTeam)` excludes only players whose direct team equals
the attacking team. An attacker's vassal can still be counted on the target side
through master/Defensive-Pact logic. Live UWAI/war-evaluation callers pass the
attacker explicitly, so this is a real combat-evaluation accounting problem.

F096 / KI#418 -- RETAINED
Tech Share counts `getNumMembers()` for each alive known team possessing the
technology. `getNumMembers()` includes dead assigned teammates, allowing dead
players to satisfy the current Internet player threshold. The project's own AI
valuation uses alive-player iteration, giving a strong internal semantic control.

F097 / KI#419 -- RETAINED CROSS-FILE ROOT
The Python Customizable Domestic Advisor X-coordinate wrapper returns
`city.getY()` in its map-centering-enabled branch, while Y also returns getY().
Current Paper/Stonehenge map-centering makes the branch reachable. This root was
found through CvTeam's map-centering audit but belongs to the Python/UI source;
do not rediscover or double-count it when that file is audited later.

F098 / KI#420 -- RETAINED, BROADENED EXACT-HISTORY ROOT
Permanent Alliance asymmetrically merges exact bilateral relationship history.
Two proven manifestations now belong to the same causal root:
- `m_aiTurnsAtPeace`
- `AI_getHasMetCounter`

The survivor direction takes the stronger/max constituent history while the
outsider reverse direction receives a team-size-weighted merge. `AI_doCounter`
explicitly documents HasMet and AtWar as exact counters. AtWar is the decisive
neighboring control because PA explicitly reconciles its two directions after
the weighted merge; HasMet and TurnsAtPeace are not reconciled. Randomized or
decaying AtPeace/OpenBorders/DefensivePact/ShareWar counters are deliberately
excluded from F098.

F099 / KI#421 -- RETAINED, PA-SPECIFIC
`setStolenVisibilityTimer` owns secondary per-plot stolen-visibility counts.
Permanent Alliance transfers absorbed B's legitimate visibility into A but does
not clear live observer->B timers through the stateful setter before B becomes a
dead team through member reassignment. Those old plot counts can therefore
survive after the intended observer->A timer expires. Direct resetVal can later
erase the bookkeeping timer without removing the leaked plot state.

Ordinary civilization elimination is an important negative control: normal
unit/city sight loss drives `changeVisibilityCount` and drains observers' stolen
plot counts even as the target dies. The leak is therefore specifically the PA
state-transfer lifecycle, not generic dead-team timer pausing.

F100 / KI#422 -- RETAINED
Permanent-Alliance project inheritance calls ordinary positive
`changeProjectCount` when the absorbed team owns more copies. That normal
completion path can emit a new project-completion message/replay event for an
already-completed inherited project. The later `ProjectCreatedCount`
compensation repairs only the numerical global count; it cannot retract emitted
side effects. Project-art vectors remain size-consistent and were explicitly
rejected as a memory-safety sibling.

FORMER F101 / provisional KI#423 -- RETRACTED FALSE POSITIVE
The WIP17 Autolog hypothesis is authoritatively rejected. `shareItems` does call
`setHasTech(..., NO_PLAYER, ...)`, but `setHasTech` immediately replaces
NO_PLAYER with `getLeaderID()` before `CvEventReporter::techAcquired`. Python and
BUG Autolog therefore receive a valid player ID. This historical false
hypothesis remains in the cumulative prefix so it will not be rediscovered.

F101 -- UNUSED
No new independent root survived file-013 closure.


FINAL WHOLE-FILE CLOSURE EVIDENCE
---------------------------------

1. Permanent-Alliance transition matrix exhausted

The audit mechanically classified and challenged serialized/team-owned state
against addTeam/shareItems/shareCounters and player reassignment. This produced
or strengthened F078-F081, F087, F089 and F098-F100. Late candidate fields were
not promoted without live consequences:
- `m_abJustDeclaredWar` is not explicitly inherited, but current SAS config has
  SPEND_ALL_MOVES_ON_INVASION=0 and identical base/DoW capture chances (50/50),
  making the flag behaviorally inert in the shipped configuration.
- `m_bMapCentering` is not explicitly merged, but normal current PA eligibility
  arrives through Game Theory; the current prerequisite chain has already passed
  Paper, which grants map centering. No normal current-SAS PA constituent lacks
  the state.
- repeat-tech count migration is generically weak, but current SAS has no
  repeatable technology.
- summed team-limited UnitClass/BuildingClass counts are a generic modmod risk,
  but current SAS has no positive UnitClass/BuildingClass MaxTeamInstances.
  Projects are the live team-limited family and have their own merge path.
- project default/art provenance can lose cosmetic/default choices, but inherited
  count slots are valid and no source-level gameplay/memory fault was proved.

2. Stateful-setter / secondary-state matrix exhausted

Stolen visibility remains exceptional because its timer setter owns secondary
per-plot state. Neighboring war/open-borders/Defensive-Pact/force-peace and
counter arrays either contain their gameplay state directly or are reset in
initialization/transition contexts where no analogous unreconciled secondary
state was established.

The old Kek-Mod PA espionage fix was also used as a control: it clears city-level
espionage visibility but never performs the stolen-map-visibility target cleanup,
which is why F099 is a neighboring lifecycle omission rather than a repaired
rediscovery.

3. Relationship-setter/source-order pass exhausted

Late candidates were explicitly challenged rather than inferred from “setter has
side effects” alone:
- Open Borders propagation can reset OpenBordersCounter, but ordinary
  `setOpenBorders(false)` already resets that relation's counter; there is no
  legitimate fading nonzero closed-treaty history to preserve.
- Defensive Pact propagation can emit a new A-C relation event, but A-C genuinely
  becomes a newly established relation through the merger, unlike F100's already
  completed project. No false-event sibling was established.
- `allowDefensivePactsToBeCanceled` inspects only the head trade item and is
  generically fragile for mixed multiplayer dual deals. However shipped
  `BBAI_DEFENSIVE_PACT_BEHAVIOR=0` first calls `cancelDefensivePacts`, whose full
  first-list scan kills target DP deals before that helper can matter. Keep this
  as configuration/modmod robustness debt; re-audit if behavior 1/2 is enabled.
- PA tech sharing before member reassignment does not transiently inflate current
  Internet thresholds: Tech Share counts players, and separate A-members +
  B-members equals the final merged member count. Dead-member inflation remains
  exactly F096.

4. Tech acquisition/removal and Advanced Start one-way effects exhausted

Every significant one-way `setHasTech/processTech` effect was challenged against
supported tech removal and current XML:
- cached total-tech count -> F083
- full-map reveal -> F084
- player currentEra -> F085
- teammate/map-infrastructure dependency validation -> F088
- map centering was normalized as an irreversible discovery-style state rather
  than a new root; its PA omission is unreachable under current PA tech gating.
- `makeSpecialBuildingValid` is another one-way acquisition side effect, but
  current SAS XML contains no SpecialBuildingInfo with a live TechPrereqAnyone,
  so there is no shipped Advanced-Start reproduction.
- first-discovery religion/free-tech/free-unit effects do not create an Advanced
  Start refund sibling because the Advanced Start acquisition path uses
  `bFirst=false`.

5. Exact-counter / iterator-predicate pass exhausted

The counter audit distinguished exact bilateral histories from intentionally
randomized directional AI counters. That distinction broadened F098 but rejected
AI AtPeace/OpenBorders/DP/ShareWar siblings. Exact AtWar remains the local
positive control because PA explicitly reconciles it.

The iterator-predicate audit found the F093 dead-target contradiction and F094
alive-only member regression, but no second impossible-branch analogue survived.
First-contact callback/event consumers were also traced after F092; no second
persistent callback-side half-contact bug was found.

6. Divisor / raw index / list-head / queue / pointer closure

A fresh mechanical pass covered the remaining arithmetic and container-risk
sites:
- current-era averaging checks the member divisor and returns NO_ERA for dead
  teams;
- culture/espionage denominators are guarded or clamped;
- Barbarian research reaches division only with structurally positive live-team
  domains;
- PA weighted merges divide by the merged live team's positive member count;
- addTeam/member vectors are size-bounded;
- reparations string indexing is size-bounded;
- F091's treaty-head bug is semantic ordering, not a null-head problem;
- the six multi-war queues are pushed and popped only in lockstep through
  queueWar/triggerWars;
- `getRandomMemberAlive` lacks a local zero guard, but every current C++ caller
  found operates through UWAI/live-team domains; no normal zero-domain call was
  established;
- `getLeaderCapital` has a strong live-team assumption, but every current caller
  found is a live trade/circumnavigation path. No dead-team dereference root was
  established.

7. Building/improvement/helper warning blocks exhausted

K-Mod's source-authored “heaps of bugs” comment around bonus connection describes
the rationale for `doesImprovementConnectBonus`; current callers use the
centralized helper and no new divergence was found.

`updateActivePaths` and `isCityDefense` warning comments likewise describe known
path/UI or assertion limitations, not a new reachable gameplay defect.

`shareItems` team-shared-building ordering was challenged specifically: both
teams' technology sets are synchronized before the building loops, so apparent
cross-team obsolescence disagreement collapses. Building map-centering remains a
one-way “ever discovered/obtained” state in inherited code and no independent
current regression was established.

8. Vassal / war-transition tail exhausted

The final pass re-read `setVassal`, `assignVassal`, `freeVassal`, queueWar and
triggerWars against the synchronized current source. Existing SAS repairs (for
example the KI#363 war-plan-count restoration ordering) are already present.
No new master/vassal transition ordering root survived.

The queue family is internally encapsulated: all six parallel queues receive one
entry per `queueWar` invocation and are consumed/popped together in
`triggerWars`. Checking only attacking_queue.empty() therefore does not create a
current desynchronization path.

9. Serialization / initialization / final helper closure

Current CvTeam read/write ordering is paired. Apparent scan mismatches reduce to
commented-out old vassal storage and the deliberately manual symmetric project-
art loop. `changeProjectCount` maintains project-art vector cardinality.

The advc.134a peace-offer fields are intentionally transient and excluded from
serialization; their source comment already acknowledges the networked-
multiplayer limitation. No stronger concrete reproduction was established in
this file audit, so it remains an acknowledged limitation rather than a newly
numbered root.

Old uiFlag migration branches have deliberately been removed under the current
SAS same-version-save policy (KI#46). Unsupported historical save compatibility
was not counted as a new defect.

The final spaceship helper tail (`getCompletedSpaceshipProjects`,
`getProjectPartNumber`, `hasLaunched`) is consistent with its current project
call domains and did not produce an additional count/art/index root beyond F081
and F100.

10. Adversarial F078-F100 reread completed

Every live root was actively challenged against current callers, current XML /
GlobalDefines where relevant, and later SAS fixes. None of F078-F100 required
retraction. Several were narrowed or strengthened instead:
- F089 is explicitly bidirectional historical identity loss.
- F098 contains only exact bilateral histories; randomized counters are excluded.
- F099 is explicitly PA-specific; ordinary elimination is the negative control.
- F100 is announcement/replay state, not project-art memory corruption.

The process also caught its own WIP17 F101/KI#423 mistake before closure, which is
why preserving adversarial retractions in the cumulative audit remains useful.
A high finding count was never used as a closure criterion.

STRUCTURAL MAP ESTABLISHED
--------------------------
WarEvaluator creates one instance of each WarUtilityAspect subclass, then loops
all alive members of the agent team:

    vector<WarUtilityAspect*> apAspects;
    fillWithAspects(apAspects);
    for (MemberIter itMember(m_kAgent.getID()); itMember.hasNext(); ++itMember)
        evaluate(itMember->getID(), apAspects);

The same aspect objects are deliberately retained across member evaluations;
WarUtilityAspect::m_iU is initialized to zero once and reset() does NOT clear it.
The final team utility then sums each aspect object's cumulative utility once.
This is consistent with AdvCiv's historical team-game design note that teammate
war utility is "already covered by adding up the war utility of all team members
in the end."

Current SAS differs semantically from AdvCiv 1.14 in this file mainly through
its faraway-target Risk::preEvaluate hard guard and its winning-war Distraction
cap. In addition, current SAS activates many non-100 UWAI aspect weights through
AI_Variables_GlobalDefines.xml; base AdvCiv 1.14 has all global aspect weights at
100 and therefore leaves F101 below numerically dormant.


F101 / provisional KI#424 -- CONFIRMED -- SAS-ACTIVATED INHERITED UWAI TEAM BUG
NON-100 WAR-UTILITY ASPECT WEIGHTS COMPOUND ACROSS TEAM MEMBERS INSTEAD OF
WEIGHTING EACH MEMBER ONCE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WarUtilityAspect::evaluate(MilitaryAnalyst const&) adds the current member's raw
contributions to the aspect object's persistent m_iU and then applies the XML
weight to the WHOLE accumulated m_iU:

    scaled rXMLAdjust = getUWAI().aspectWeight(xmlID());
    if (m_iU != 0 && rXMLAdjust != 1)
        m_iU = (m_iU * rXMLAdjust).round();

reset() clears only transient player/rival pointers and helper state; it does not
clear m_iU. WarEvaluator then calls this same method once for each alive team
member on the same aspect objects. Therefore member N reweights every earlier
member's already-weighted contribution again.

For two team members whose raw contribution to a 300% aspect is +10 each:
- intended additive team result: (10 + 10) * 3 = +60;
- current member 1: 10 * 3 = 30;
- current member 2: (30 + 10) * 3 = 120.

With three equal +10 contributors at 300%, current result becomes 390 instead of
90; with four it becomes 1200 instead of 120. Weights below 100 repeatedly
suppress earlier members instead: at 50%, two +10 members yield about 7.5 (then
integer/fixed-point rounding) instead of 10. The result is also member-iteration
order dependent whenever member raw utilities differ: earlier players are
reweighted once for every later teammate.

This is strongly live in current SAS. Of 27 global UWAI aspect weights, 17 are
currently non-100, including:
- Loathing 70%
- Military Victory 105%
- Preservation of Partners 80%
- Reconquista 130%
- Rebuke 200%
- Fidelity 110%
- Hired Hand 0%
- Border Disputes 90%
- Preemptive War 125%
- King Making 105%
- Risk 105%
- Distraction 300%
- Ulterior Motives 200%
- Fair Play 125%
- Tactical Situation 140%
- Third Party Intervention 200%
- Dramatic Arc 10%.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same cumulative weighting code but currently has
all these global aspect weights at 100%, so the arithmetic defect is dormant in
that baseline. Historical AdvCiv notes nevertheless explicitly support additive
member aggregation, and older/modmod non-100 weights can activate the same root.

No aspect implementation reads prior m_iU to make a cross-member decision; apart
from the wrapper, implementations only add/subtract their result. A conservative
repair can therefore preserve cumulative storage while weighting only the
current member's delta, e.g. snapshot m_iU before preEvaluate/rival evaluation,
compute the raw delta, apply rXMLAdjust to that delta once, then add the weighted
delta back to the prior cumulative value. Returning that weighted delta would
also repair the secondary diagnostic issue that WarEvaluator's current
"Total utility for <player>" log becomes cumulative for the second and later
team members even at 100% weights.

This root affects normal starting-team games and teams enlarged by Permanent
Alliances; its magnitude grows rapidly with member count for weights far from
100%. It is gameplay-significant because the final WarEvaluator result directly
feeds UWAI war/peace/war-trade decisions.


F102 / provisional KI#425 -- CONFIRMED -- ADVCIV-SAS REGRESSION / TEAM-GAME BUG
FARAWAY-WAR HARD REJECT USES ONE MEMBER'S PLAYER-LOCAL DISTANCE/LIFT CACHE AS A
PLAN-KILLING TEAM-WIDE VETO
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The SAS KI#61 guard lives in Risk::preEvaluate. WarEvaluator invokes that
preEvaluate once per alive member of the agent team, with m_pAgentCache pointing
to the current member's UWAICache. The guard scans:

    ourCache().cityAt(i)
    kCity.getDistance()
    kCity.canReachByLand()
    ourCache().canTrainAnyCargo()

and returns -100000 on unreachable / too-far / no-lift conditions, explicitly
commented as:

    return -100000; // kill this (agent,target) war plan

WarEvalParameters::agent and target are TeamTypes, and the final war decision is
team-level. But UWAICache::City::updateDistance(eCacheOwner) explicitly computes
paths "for each city of the cache owner" and iterates FOR_EACH_CITY over that
single player. Its getDistance/canReachByLand values are therefore player-local,
not a minimum across the team. canTrainAnyCargo is likewise stored on the
current player's cache.

A normal two-member team can consequently have:
- member A bordering target C, cached land contact 5 turns -> guard passes;
- member B isolated from C, unreachable or >15 turns -> guard returns -100000.

B's inability to personally reach C then overwhelms the aggregate team utility
and rejects a war for which A has a perfectly valid nearby front. The analogous
naval case lets one teammate with no transport capacity veto the team even when
another teammate can conduct the invasion.

This conflicts with the surrounding UWAI team design. WarEvaluator intentionally
sums all members' ordinary gains/costs, and other aspects contain explicit team-
size normalization/coordination logic. KI#61's own documentation describes an
outer sanity bound on a prospective war TARGET before ordinary UWAI evaluates
power, utility, diplomacy and context; it does not state that every teammate must
personally be within the contact limit. A remote teammate's lower expected gain
or higher risk can be represented by that member's normal utility; inability to
attack is not by itself a reason to make the target categorically illegal for
other members.

The safest policy-level repair is to make the hard eligibility test team-aware
and execute/derive it once per team: accept the contact sanity gate when at least
one alive team member has the required land/naval reach (and, for genuinely
naval contact, appropriate lift capability), while rejecting only when the team
collectively lacks a qualifying route/capability. Exact implementation should
preserve the existing KI#183 peace-scenario exclusion, ongoing-war exclusion,
existing-plan tolerance and victory-denial bypass.

This root is SAS-specific: base AdvCiv 1.14 has no KI#61 hard-reject block.


F103 / provisional KI#426 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV SEMANTIC BUG
PARTNER TECH-TRADE UTILITY TESTS THE RIVAL'S WILLINGNESS USING THE AGENT'S
TECH-REFUSAL PERSONALITY THRESHOLD
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
partnerUtilFromTech() intentionally tests both directions of potential future
tech trade:

    AttitudeTypes eOurAttitudeThresh = techRefuseThresh(eWe);
    AttitudeTypes eTheirAttitudeThresh = techRefuseThresh(eThey);

and rejects partner utility when either AI side's attitude is below its supposed
threshold. But the helper is:

    AttitudeTypes WarUtilityAspect::techRefuseThresh(PlayerTypes ePlayer) const
    {
        if (GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).isHuman())
            return ATTITUDE_FURIOUS;
        return (AttitudeTypes)(kOurPersonality.getTechRefuseAttitudeThreshold()+1);
    }

The ePlayer argument is honored for the human check but ignored for AI
personality lookup: kOurPersonality is always the current AGENT player's leader.
Thus the second call for eThey substitutes our leader's tech refusal threshold
for the rival's.

The live trade rule elsewhere in CvPlayerAI uses the prospective trading AI's
own personality:

    GC.getInfo(kPartner.getPersonalityType()).getTechRefuseAttitudeThreshold()

so this is not an intentional shared/team threshold policy.

Current SAS leader XML makes the difference very reachable: among parsed leader
entries, thresholds include NONE, ATTITUDE_FURIOUS, ATTITUDE_ANNOYED and
ATTITUDE_CAUTIOUS. For example, a permissive rival can be incorrectly treated as
requiring the agent's stricter attitude, or a strict rival can be treated as
more willing than it really is.

partnerUtilFromTech feeds multiple gameplay utility families, including
Assistance (value of preserving a partner), IllWill/lost-partner costs and the
cost assigned to diplomatic penalties. It can therefore over- or understate war
utility depending on the leader pairing.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 has the same helper and call pattern; this is inherited rather
than introduced by SAS. The direct repair is to read the personality of ePlayer
for the AI case, e.g. GC.getInfo(GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).getPersonalityType()), while
retaining the human special case.

ALIVE members and GreedForAssets::teamSizeMultiplier explicitly uses

F096 / KI#418 -- BROADENED MANIFESTATION -- DEAD ASSIGNED TEAM MEMBERS ARE USED
WHERE WARUTILITYASPECT SEMANTICS REQUIRE LIVING PARTICIPANTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The CvTeam.cpp audit had already established the root fact behind F096:
CvTeam::getNumMembers() counts assigned team slots including eliminated players,
whereas getAliveCount() counts living members. That finding was originally
promoted through Tech Share, whose threshold explicitly intends players that can
actually know/share the technology. At that time the audit deliberately refused
to generalize every getNumMembers call without a consumer-specific invariant.

WarUtilityAspect.cpp now supplies that invariant for several additional sites.
WarEvaluator evaluates an AI team by iterating its living MemberIter players and
adding those living members' aspect contributions. Nevertheless the common
normalizer divides the resulting team-on-team utility by:

    GET_TEAM(eOther).getNumMembers() * kOurTeam.getNumMembers()

An eliminated-but-still-assigned teammate therefore contributes no numerator
utility, because it is not evaluated, but continues inflating the denominator.
The team utility can remain permanently diluted simply because a dead historical
member slot still belongs to the team.

lossesFromFlippedTiles is an even more explicit local proof. Its comment says:

    Tiles are counted per team, but this function gets called once per rival player.

It consequently divides the team-level tile count by iRivalMembers, but defines
that as kTheirTeam.getNumMembers(). The actual aspect evaluation only visits
living rival players. A dead assigned rival therefore makes the per-live-player
share too small and also raises the early 4*iRivalMembers significance threshold.

The file contains a strong internal control: GreedForAssets::teamSizeMultiplier
explicitly uses:

    min(kOurTeam.getAliveCount(), kTheirTeam.getAliveCount())

when it means active participants in team-on-team warfare. GreedForVassals also
starts its current-vassal count with PlayerIter<ALIVE,VASSAL_OF>::count and then
adds getNumMembers for predicted new vassal teams, another mixed live/assigned
semantic seam worth repairing consistently.

This does NOT mean every getNumMembers in the file is automatically wrong. The
root is broadened only where surrounding iteration/comment semantics establish
that the quantity represents living participants. The direct repair is to use
getAliveCount (or the corresponding alive-player iterator count) at those sites,
with each remaining team-size use reviewed individually rather than globally
replaced.


F104 / provisional KI#427 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV OFF-BY-ONE
PARTNER TRADE UTILITY'S DECLARED FOUR-RESOURCE CAP ACTUALLY COUNTS ONLY THREE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WarUtilityAspect::partnerUtilFromTrade() explicitly says:

    // Count only the first four resource trades

and sets:

    int const iMaxResourceTrades = 4;

However, for each qualifying resource deal it first increments iResourceTrades
and then skips when:

    if (iResourceTrades >= iMaxResourceTrades)
        continue;

Thus resource deals 1, 2 and 3 are valued, while deal 4 is already skipped. The
log message compounds the contradiction by saying that trades "in excess of 4"
are skipped even though the fourth itself is discarded.

This is a live utility input: partnerUtilFromTrade contributes to the value of
preserving a diplomatic/trading partner, including Assistance and IllWill costs.
A relationship with four ongoing qualifying resource deals is therefore valued
as though only three existed.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same code and comment, so this is inherited. The
minimal repair is to skip only when iResourceTrades > iMaxResourceTrades (or test
before increment with an equivalent >= condition), preserving exactly the first
four as documented.


F105 / provisional KI#428 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV BOUNDARY / DIVISOR BUG
DOMINATION WAR-UTILITY PROGRESS MISHANDLES EXACT POPULATION-THRESHOLD EQUALITY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
MilitaryVictory::progressRatingDomination computes:

    iPopToGo = iPopTarget - kOurTeam.getTotalPopulation();

and later treats population as already satisfied only when:

    if (iPopToGo < 0)

The real CvGame Domination victory check, however, rejects population only when:

    100 * teamPopulation < totalPopulation * adjustedPopulationPercent

so exact equality already satisfies the population requirement. Therefore
`iPopToGo == 0` is a normal boundary state in which the population half of the
victory condition is complete.

The utility code does not recognize that state. It first executes:

    rPopGained.decreaseTo(iPopToGo);

which clamps projected population gain to zero, then enters the non-negative
branch and can evaluate either:

    rPopGained / iPopToGo

or the two-component expression containing the same division. That is division
by zero in ScaledNum's MulDiv-backed arithmetic, and independently of the exact
platform error/sentinel behavior it is semantically wrong: a fully satisfied
population component is being represented as zero/error progress.

Current SAS has a live Domination victory, so this is reachable whenever a team
lands exactly on the population threshold while still needing land/cities and
WarUtility evaluates projected conquests. Base AdvCiv 1.14 has the same `< 0`
boundary and division structure, making the bug inherited.

The direct boundary repair is to treat `iPopToGo <= 0` as population already
satisfied and route equality through the existing completed-population logic,
thereby both preserving victory semantics and eliminating the zero divisor.


F106 / provisional KI#429 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV SCORE-COMPARISON BUG
KINGMAKING COMPUTES AN ADJUSTED BEST SCORE BUT COMPARES CANDIDATES USING RAW SCORE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
KingMaking::addLeadingPlayers first computes rBestScore from an adjusted score for
each free major player. In the midgame it deliberately adds half of estimated
commerce:

    // Count extra score for commerce so that players that are getting far
    // ahead in tech are identified as a threat

and can further multiply a peaceful overseas culture/space contender's score by
4/3. rBestScore therefore represents the maximum ADJUSTED contender score.

The second pass does not apply those adjustments to candidates. It compares:

    raw predicted/current game score / rBestScore

against 70% for humans or 75% for AI.

This defeats the stated purpose of the adjustments. A tech leader's commerce
bonus raises the denominator used against everybody but never raises that same
leader's numerator. In a sufficiently strong case, the player that established
rBestScore can fail its own 75% cutoff; the adjusted leader can therefore be
omitted from kLeading, and in the extreme the set can be empty despite the
nearby invariant comment that someone is normally always ahead.

The 4/3 overseas-victory adjustment has the same mismatch. Base AdvCiv 1.14
contains the same two-pass implementation, so the root is inherited.

The robust repair is to centralize the adjusted contender-score calculation and
use that same quantity both when deriving rBestScore and when testing each
candidate against the margin. This also prevents future changes to the first-pass
threat adjustment from silently diverging from the second pass again.
