F158 / provisional KI#481 -- inherited AdvCiv isRemovableFeature current-research regression
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
AIFoundValue::isRemovableFeature incorrectly handles a feature-removing Build whose
normal build prerequisite and feature-removal prerequisite are different technologies.
After first testing whether the team already has both technologies, its fallback for
"CurrentResearch should be good enough" requires one player's single current research
to equal BOTH eTech1 and eTech2 simultaneously:

    if (kMember.getCurrentResearch() == eTech1 &&
        kMember.getCurrentResearch() == eTech2)
        return true;

For distinct prerequisites this can never succeed. The intended state -- one
prerequisite already known and the other being researched -- is therefore classified
as not removable even though the feature is about to become removable.

SHIPPED REPRODUCTION
Current BuildInfos supplies ordinary distinct-tech cases. For example, BUILD_FARM has
TECH_AGRICULTURE as its normal build prerequisite while Forest removal requires
TECH_MASONRY and Jungle removal requires TECH_METAL_CASTING. A team that already knows
Agriculture and is currently researching Masonry therefore fails the fallback for a
Forest Farm: currentResearch cannot simultaneously be Agriculture and Masonry.
Mine and other feature-removing build paths provide the same shape.

CONSEQUENCE
isRemovableFeature feeds the central city-site plot evaluation and the longer-horizon
evaluateWorkablePlot path. During the affected research turn(s), removable Forest /
Jungle can be treated as persistent or unavailable for improvement, changing feature
yield/health handling, improvement potential and found-value comparisons. This is a
scoring correctness regression, not merely a diagnostic mismatch.

ANCESTRY
The pre-refactor AdvCiv AI_foundValue logic used the correct independent condition for
each prerequisite: each tech could be either already known OR the player's current
research. AdvCiv commit

    078fc9bd7c7962bdd944073c372ffd2e5853b16e
    2019-12-15 -- "Move AI_foundValue computation into a new class"

split the logic into AIFoundValue::isRemovableFeature and introduced the impossible
same-current-research conjunction. Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains it and current SAS inherits
it unchanged.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Test the two prerequisites independently. Conceptually, each prerequisite should pass
when NO_TECH, already held by the team, or currently researched by the relevant team
member. Do not require one current-research slot to equal two distinct technologies.
Keep team/member semantics consistent with the old known-good implementation.


F159 / provisional KI#482 -- inherited AdvCiv regression makes K-Mod other-island starting badness branch unreachable
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
AIFoundValue::adjustToStartingSurroundings currently wraps the nearby-plot evaluation
in:

    if ((p.isWater() || p.isArea(kArea)) && it.currPlotDist() <= iRange)

but later, inside that already-filtered block, retains K-Mod's intended distinction:

    if (p.isWater() || p.isArea(kArea))
        iR += iTempValue;
    else if (iTempValue >= 13)
        iGreaterBadTile++; // add at least 1 badness point for other islands.

For a land plot on another area, the outer condition has already rejected the plot.
The inner "other islands" else branch can therefore never execute.

INTENDED K-MOD CONTRACT
K-Mod commit

    51e5ee601626cd188f6beb21a0c0ea65de0bd471
    2015-01-24 -- "Land on other islands is now counted as \"bad\" for starting locations."

explicitly commented out the old outer same-area gate. Its diff also moved the yield
addition behind an inner area test: nearby other-island land should NOT contribute its
yields to the capital, because the capital cannot work it, but sufficiently good land
on that inaccessible island SHOULD increase the bad-tile count because it consumes
nearby geographic space without helping the starting city.

REGRESSION ANCESTRY
AdvCiv's 2017 initial import continuation

    f6ff6a182f5187541fff6e5bbbe12f9573b3778c
    2017-04-16 -- "Initial commit (cont.)"

restored the old outer same-area condition while retaining K-Mod's inner other-island
branch and comment. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS still have this contradictory
combination.

CONSEQUENCE
Starting-location surroundings can undercount inaccessible nearby land on a different
island/area. Such plots neither add usable yields nor the K-Mod badness point they were
specifically meant to add, so starts near tight coast/island boundaries can be rated
better than the intended K-Mod heuristic.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Restore K-Mod's structure: let the distance-qualified nearby plot reach the scoring
body regardless of land area, add iTempValue only for water or same-area land, and use
the existing other-island branch to add badness for sufficiently valuable but
unworkable land.


F160 / provisional KI#483 -- inherited Warlords/BtS bonus-improvement scan ignores actual plot domain; water Oil can use land Well timing/yields
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
AIFoundValue::getBonusImprovement receives the actual CvPlot& p, but its Build /
Improvement scan never verifies that a candidate improvement can exist on that plot.
It checks bonus validity/trade, technology nearness, feature-removal technology and
Fort exclusion, but not water/land domain (nor a stronger plot-validity predicate).

CURRENT SAS DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION
Oil has two connecting improvements in current XML:

* IMPROVEMENT_WELL: bWater=0; Oil trade improvement; +2 production, +3 commerce;
  BUILD_WELL requires TECH_COMBUSTION.
* IMPROVEMENT_OFFSHORE_PLATFORM: bWater=1; Oil trade improvement; matching current
  Oil improvement yield; its build requires the later TECH_MARINE_TECHNOLOGY.

Well appears before Offshore Platform in the Build/Improvement iteration. Oil itself is
revealed and city-trade enabled at Combustion. Therefore, for a WATER Oil plot after
Combustion but before Marine Technology, getBonusImprovement can select the land-only
Well, set bCanImprove/bCanImproveSoon from Well's tech path, and calculate Well as the
chosen bonus improvement even though a Well cannot be built on that water tile.

This is not caused by SAS's recent decision to continue scanning after an available
improvement. In current data Well and Offshore Platform have tied Oil improvement
yields, and Well is encountered first, so Base AdvCiv's old early-available shortcut
also lands on Well. The deeper defect is the missing plot/domain validity check.

CONSEQUENCE
The timing flags are materially wrong even though current Well and Offshore Oil yield
bonuses happen to tie. calculateSpecialYieldModifier sees the water Oil as currently
or soon improvable and avoids the intended delayed-improvement discount. The
longer-horizon evaluateWorkablePlot path likewise can skip its later-era devaluation
because bCanSoonImproveBonus was derived from the illegal Well path. This can overrate
water Oil before Offshore Platforms are technologically available.

The file itself contains a useful negative control: evaluateWorkablePlot later asks

    GC.getInfo(eBonus).getTechImprove(p.isWater())

when it needs eventual bonus-improvement timing. CvBonusInfo::getTechImprove(bool
bWater) is explicitly domain-aware, demonstrating that land and water Oil technology
paths are expected to differ.

ANCESTRY
The same shape is present in supplied Firaxis Warlords CvPlayerAI::AI_foundValue:
it loops all improvements and picks the first isImprovementBonusMakesValid(eBonus)
without checking the resource plot's domain. BtS retains it. Supplied Vanilla Civ4
does not contain this same eBonusImprovement found-value path, so the root is best
classified as inherited Warlords/BtS rather than Vanilla.

K-Mod strengthened the resource check (notably BonusTrade), and AdvCiv later refactored
it. AdvCiv commit

    891273d300ade2b2adc69bb9cc0a907c74e59267
    2019-12-21 -- "AI city placement tweaks"

added/used the actual plot parameter while fixing resource tech/yield details, but the
scan still did not acquire a domain/plot-legality test. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS
therefore retain the Firaxis root.

REPAIR DIRECTION
At minimum reject improvement candidates whose water/land domain disagrees with p.
A stronger solution can use the existing SAS bonus-specific plot/domain helper or an
appropriate plot-validity predicate, provided it does not accidentally require current
technology when this routine intentionally predicts near-future improvements.

RELATED NON-FINDING / LATENT SIBLING
Current SAS calculateBonusConnectionEra performs a similar all-Build scan without plot
domain filtering, so water Oil can nominally inherit Well's earlier Industrial-era
connection path there too. However, the current connection-era adjustment only acts on
positive explicit health/happiness/building-effect non-yield value. Current Oil has
zero health and happiness and no positive counted building health/happiness effect, so
this sibling has no demonstrated shipped scoring consequence at present. It is kept as
a latent robustness concern rather than a separate root.


F161 / provisional KI#484 -- current SAS contested-future-BFC helper filters rival cities by the candidate site's unrelated area
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
SAS's isPlotInKnownRivalFutureBFC(CvPlot const& p) is asked whether the SPECIFIC bonus
plot p is threatened by a known rival future BFC. Its rival-city loop nevertheless
contains:

    if (!pCity->isArea(kArea))
        continue;

AIFoundValue::kArea is not p's area. It is permanently bound in the constructor to the
land area of the NEW candidate city site kPlot currently being evaluated. The helper is
called while scanning bonus plots around all EXISTING own cities. Candidate site and
existing bonus can therefore be on entirely different continents.

DETERMINISTIC CROSS-AREA REPRODUCTION
1. Existing own city A is on land area A. An unowned Maize lies in A's future BFC.
2. Known rival city R, also on area A, has that same Maize within CITY_PLOTS_RADIUS;
   the Maize is genuinely contested and ownership is not reliable.
3. Evaluate a new city candidate B on a different land area B containing another
   Maize (or otherwise causing the same bonus type to be scored).
4. isBonusOwnedOrClaimedByFutureBFC(Maize) finds A's Maize and calls
   isPlotInKnownRivalFutureBFC on that plot.
5. Rival R is skipped solely because R is not on candidate B's kArea.
6. The helper falsely reports the A-area Maize unopposed; the caller then treats Maize
   as already reliably covered.

CONSEQUENCE
This is more than the flat diversity nudge. In current evaluate(), a falsely
"already covered" bonus loses the configured
SAS_EVALUATE_UNOWNED_BONUS_EXTRA_VALUE (currently 250). The same helper is also used by
nonYieldBonusValue to initialize bSurplus; false surplus status zeroes the candidate
copy's explicit health/happiness and counted building-effect value. Overseas/colony
site comparisons can therefore be distorted based on a rival-city filter tied to an
unrelated candidate continent.

INTRODUCTION / INTENT
The helper was introduced in SAS commit

    6341d3d556a7f580e3664b8631d52446c2c7c4da
    2026-07-11 -- "(Fixed/Improved) City-site bonus valuation used broad trade-style
    AI_bonusVal instead of settlement-specific long-term value and other related AI
    bonus settler valuation issues (KI#178)"

whose commit message explicitly says to avoid over-counting reliable future-BFC
coverage WHILE PRESERVING value for contested bonuses. The current area filter violates
that exact contract.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Do not filter rival cities by AIFoundValue::kArea here. The radius-2 test already
localizes the scan to cities that can actually threaten p. Replacing kArea with
p.getArea() is also unsafe for coastal resources: a water bonus' area differs from the
land area containing the coastal rival city that can claim it. Removing the unrelated
area filter is the straightforward correctness-first repair.


F162 / provisional KI#485 -- current SAS future-BFC coverage result is order-dependent because the first matching bonus returns immediately
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
isBonusOwnedOrClaimedByFutureBFC asks an empire-wide existential question: is this
bonus type already owned or reliably covered by ANY existing city's future BFC?
However, once it encounters the first matching unowned/self-owned bonus plot, it does:

    return !isPlotInKnownRivalFutureBFC(*pLoopPlot);

A contested first copy therefore returns false immediately and prevents the search
from discovering a later safely claimable copy of the same bonus type.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION
1. The player does not yet have an actually available Maize.
2. Existing city A has an unowned Maize in its future BFC, but that plot is also inside
   a known rival city's future BFC and is therefore contested.
3. Existing city B has another unowned Maize in its future BFC with no known rival
   future-BFC contest; this second copy is reliable long-term coverage.
4. If the A/contested occurrence is encountered first in city/BFC iteration,
   isBonusOwnedOrClaimedByFutureBFC returns false immediately and never examines B.
5. If the safe occurrence is encountered first, the same empire state returns true.

CONSEQUENCE
Found value depends on city/BFC iteration order rather than resource-coverage state.
The false result can add the +250 unowned-resource diversity value to another Maize and
can preserve long-term non-yield Maize value even though a separate safe existing-city
copy already satisfies the helper's intended definition of reliable coverage.

INTRODUCTION / INTENT
This is independent of F161 but originates in the same KI#178 helper introduced by
SAS commit 6341d3d556a7f580e3664b8631d52446c2c7c4da. F161 asks the wrong rivals because
of unrelated area state; F162 stops searching after one contested occurrence even when
that individual contest test itself is correct.

REPAIR DIRECTION
A contested matching plot should mean "this occurrence does not establish reliable
coverage; keep searching", not "the whole empire has no reliable copy". Return true
when any safe qualifying copy is found; after exhausting all copies, return false.


F163 / provisional KI#486 -- current SAS future-BFC helper counts temporary trade imports as owned despite explicit opposite contract
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
The first line of isBonusOwnedOrClaimedByFutureBFC is:

    if (kPlayer.getNumAvailableBonuses(eBonus) > 0)
        return true;

But CvPlayer::getNumAvailableBonuses reads the capital plot group's bonus count, and
CvPlot::updatePlotGroupBonus explicitly ADDS getBonusImport at the capital. The DLL
also defines:

    getNumTradeableBonuses(eBonus) =
        getNumAvailableBonuses(eBonus) - getBonusImport(eBonus)

so imported bonuses are demonstrably included in getNumAvailableBonuses.

This directly contradicts the active CitySiteEvaluator comment, XML define comment,
Main Changes Guide and KI#147/KI#178 documentation, all of which say that trade imports
DO NOT count as owned here because they are temporary/non-permanent.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION
1. The player owns no Wheat and has no existing-city future-BFC Wheat that would count
   as reliable coverage.
2. The player temporarily imports Wheat in a resource trade deal connected to its
   capital network.
3. getNumAvailableBonuses(Wheat) becomes positive because imports are included in the
   capital plot-group bonus count.
4. Evaluate a post-capital candidate containing Wheat.
5. isBonusOwnedOrClaimedByFutureBFC returns true immediately because of the import.

CONSEQUENCE
The candidate Wheat can lose the configured +250 unowned-bonus diversity value, and
nonYieldBonusValue can set bSurplus and suppress the new permanent copy's explicit
health/happiness/building-effect settlement value. A cancellable trade deal is thus
allowed to erase precisely the permanent-resource value the SAS feature was designed
to preserve.

INTRODUCTION / REGRESSION ANCESTRY
KI#147's original SAS implementation (commit 24cf2b8853..., practical 5929) did NOT use
getNumAvailableBonuses. It scanned the player's cities with AI_countNumBonuses, which
did not convert temporary imports into owned map copies.

KI#178 commit

    6341d3d556a7f580e3664b8631d52446c2c7c4da

replaced that local scan with isBonusOwnedOrClaimedByFutureBFC and introduced the
getNumAvailableBonuses early return while retaining the explicit "Trade imports do not
count" contract. F163 is therefore a current SAS regression introduced by KI#178, not
an inherited AdvCiv defect.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Use an owned/permanent resource test that excludes getBonusImport. At minimum, do not
use raw getNumAvailableBonuses as the ownership predicate when its imported component
is explicitly outside this feature's semantics. Preserve the helper's later
existing-city/future-BFC coverage logic for not-yet-connected owned/claimable copies.

F164 / provisional KI#487 -- rival culture-pressure gate ignores real cross-area culture solely because the rival city tile is on another land area
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
The current SAS replacement for AdvCiv's adjustToCivSurroundings culture-pressure
logic scans known foreign cities, but begins each city with:

    if (!pCity->isArea(kArea)) continue;

kArea is the land area of the candidate settlement tile. This assumes a foreign city
on another land area cannot exert relevant culture pressure on the candidate.

That assumption is false in the actual culture engine. CvCity::doPlotCultureTimes100
explicitly permits culture to spread onto a plot in another area when the culture
distance is at most:

    eCultureLevel + 1

(the broader same-area range is larger). Thus a coastal city on one island can exert
real plot culture across a narrow channel onto another island.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION
1. Put a candidate land city site on island A.
2. Put a revealed/known rival city on nearby island B, so the city tiles have different
   CvArea IDs but are only two culture-distance steps apart.
3. Give the rival city culture level 2 or greater.
4. CvCity::doPlotCultureTimes100 can legally spread that city's culture onto the
   candidate-side plots because the cross-area distance is <= cultureLevel + 1.
5. CitySiteEvaluator nevertheless skips the rival city before even calculating its
   pressure because !pCity->isArea(kArea).

For the current simple pressure formula, a level-2 city at distance 2 has r=5 and would
produce pressure 10 + 90*(5-2)/5 = 64. With ordinary SOFT/HARD settings this is enough
to cause a substantial down-weight. The area filter instead forces its contribution to
zero.

CONSEQUENCE
Narrow-channel / island-chain sites can be rated as culturally safe even while an
existing known rival city can already project culture across the water toward them.
Depending on distance and XML thresholds, a site that should receive a medium penalty
or even rejection can receive none from this gate.

ANCESTRY / INTENT
The area restriction is inherited conceptually from K-Mod's 2012 foreign-proximity
found-value work and Base AdvCiv's adjustToCivSurroundings, which likewise considered
only same-area cities. SAS later disabled that complex routine and migrated a simpler
culture-pressure subset inline, carrying the same-area restriction with it.

The culture engine itself is the stronger authority for reachability and explicitly
contains special cross-area handling. This is therefore a long-standing geographic
assumption exposed by the simplified SAS gate, not merely a tuning disagreement.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Do not equate different land-area IDs with zero possible culture pressure. Preserve a
cheap same-area fast path if desired, but for a different-area rival city allow the
narrower range actually supported by CvCity::doPlotCultureTimes100 (culture level + 1)
rather than applying the full same-area range blindly. The no-cheat
AI_deduceCitySite/KNOWN_TO checks should remain intact.


F165 / provisional KI#488 -- SAS cautious-health score drops all Forest/Jungle health whenever the plot contains a visible bonus
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
The current cautious-health accumulator is located in the `else` of:

    if (eBonus != NO_BONUS)
        ... resource valuation ...
    else
        if (eFeature == Jungle/Forest)
            iCautiousHealthPercent += feature health percent;

So a Forest or Jungle contributes to the first/later-city bad-health dampener only when
that plot has NO visible bonus. A bonus does not itself remove the feature and does not
make its health effect disappear.

CURRENT SHIPPED DATA
SAS XML permits many bonuses on Forest and/or Jungle plots. Examples include current
food, luxury and strategic resources such as Pig/Deer on Forest and Rice/Banana,
Dye/Gems/Elephants/Spices on Jungle-related placements (exact map generation also
depends on terrain/feature rules). The important property is shipped, ordinary
feature+bonus coexistence: the feature health modifier remains real while the
CitySiteEvaluator accumulator ignores it.

DETERMINISTIC EFFECT
With the current comments' own scale, Jungle contributes -50 and Forest +50 to the
quick health estimate. Seven ordinary Jungle plots produce -350 and can cross a -300
start threshold. If one of those Jungle plots contains a bonus, the current accumulator
sees only -300. Conversely, a resource on Forest can erase +50 of mitigating health.
The site can therefore cross a configured penalty threshold in either direction merely
because a resource marker shares the feature.

CONSEQUENCE
The start/later bad-health dampener is not estimating BFC feature health as documented.
Resource-rich jungle starts can be treated as healthier than the same actual feature
layout without the resource, while resource-bearing Forest can fail to offset Jungle.
Because the dampener is thresholded and multiplicative, the discrepancy can be much
larger than 50 raw health-percent points once it changes whether the penalty runs.

INTRODUCTION / INTENT
This is SAS-specific custom logic. The active comments describe the accumulator simply
in terms of Jungle and Forest health (e.g. 7 Jungle = -350; 8 Jungle + 2 Forest = -300)
and do not document bonus plots as exempt. The exclusion comes from control-flow
placement rather than from bRemovableFeature, improvement legality, or a rule that the
feature will actually be removed.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Accumulate the relevant Forest/Jungle feature health independently of whether eBonus is
NO_BONUS. If the intended model is instead "health after likely improvements," that
needs an explicit feature-removal/improvement test; bonus presence alone is not such a
test.


F166 / provisional KI#489 -- SAS raw zero-city start-phase gates accidentally reintroduce a first-Barbarian-city distinction AdvCiv explicitly suppresses
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
AIFoundValue construction deliberately normalizes Barbarian city count:

    // Barbarians shouldn't distinguish between earlier and later cities
    iCities = (bBarbarian ? 5 : kPlayer.getNumCities());

Current SAS evaluate() later introduces a separate raw state:

    int const iNumCities = kPlayer.getNumCities();
    bool const bStartPhase = (iNumCities == 0);

and uses bStartPhase for custom capital/first-city rules, including the hard minimum
`iGoodEnoughFirstCityBFCTiles` gate, the stricter starting very-bad-tile allowance and
the harsher starting health dampener.

REACHABILITY
The Barbarian player can genuinely pass through this evaluator with zero cities.
CvGame's Barbarian-city creation/site-selection path constructs/evaluates city sites for
BARBARIAN_PLAYER before its first city exists. Thus this is not merely a theoretical
state reachable only through WorldBuilder or API misuse.

DETERMINISTIC BEHAVIOR DIFFERENCE
Evaluate the same ordinary Barbarian candidate once when the Barbarian player has zero
cities and again after it has one unrelated city, with the local map state otherwise
unchanged. On the first call bStartPhase is true and the candidate can be hard-rejected
for failing the capital-only good-enough BFC count or can receive the stricter start
health/very-bad penalties. Once any Barbarian city exists, those exact SAS gates switch
to the later-city settings.

CONSEQUENCE
The first Barbarian city is subject to a unique capital-like quality policy despite the
inherited AdvCiv design explicitly preventing Barbarians from distinguishing early vs
later cities. This can suppress or reshape initial Barbarian settlement in ways that
disappear immediately after city #1 and can interact strongly with the hard first-city
BFC return-0 gate.

ANCESTRY / REGRESSION CLASS
The `iCities = 5` Barbarian normalization is inherited AdvCiv behavior (advc.108).
The conflicting bStartPhase gates are later SAS custom additions. This is therefore a
SAS regression against an explicit inherited contract rather than a Base AdvCiv bug.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Derive these first-city-only SAS gates from the evaluator's already-normalized notion of
early/late city state, or explicitly exclude bBarbarian from bStartPhase. Do not change
ordinary player first-city behavior while fixing the Barbarian special case.


F167 / provisional KI#490 -- first-city preliminary BFC hard gates count plots before the established usability/ownership filter rejects them
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
SAS practical/commit 7a6be1b482c631ab46fe891e44fdedacd5e3871b
(2026-06-28, "Replace Settler/Found AI hardcoded enough good enough first-city plots
with a dynamic one") added XML-aware preliminary BFC counters. During the CityPlot
loop it now evaluates revealed non-home plots and increments, among other state:

    iGoodEnoughFirstCityBFCTiles
    iVeryBadBFCTiles
    iLowFoodLocationScore

BEFORE calling:

    isUsablePlot(...)

The latter is the established filter that decides whether the candidate may actually
count on the plot after existing-city radius ownership/sharing/steal/reservation rules.
If isUsablePlot returns false, normal found-value processing immediately `continue`s --
but the preliminary first-city counters have already been changed.

WHY EXISTING CITY RADIUS STATE IS PRESENT
When a city is founded, CvPlot::setPlotCity iterates its entire CityPlot radius and
increments each plot's `cityRadiusCount` / player city-radius count immediately. This is
not limited to plots already culturally owned or currently workable. Therefore a plot
inside a revealed rival city's BFC can participate in the preliminary SAS classification
while the later usability filter knows it belongs to an existing competing radius.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION
1. Evaluate a first-city candidate whose BFC overlaps the inner/radius claims of a
   revealed rival city.
2. Put a strong revealed Grass/resource or otherwise "good enough" tile in that rival
   claimed portion at a CityPlot index reached during the preliminary pass.
3. SAS_isGoodEnoughFirstCityBFCPlot counts it toward the configured hard minimum.
4. isUsablePlot then rejects that same plot because the candidate must not count on
   working/stealing it under the established overlap rules.
5. The unusable plot can nevertheless be the tile that raises
   `iGoodEnoughFirstCityBFCTiles + iUnrevealedTiles` to the minimum and prevents a hard
   return 0.

The reverse direction also exists: unusable rival/overlap plots can feed preliminary
very-bad or low-food counters and penalize/reject a candidate even though the main plot
evaluator intentionally discards those tiles.

CONSEQUENCE
The new gate is documented and named in terms of "usable" / "good enough" BFC slots,
but its hard acceptance decision can depend on plots the evaluator itself later says
are unusable. First-city acceptance can therefore depend on rival-overlap geometry in
the wrong direction and disagree internally within one loop iteration.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Run the ownership/sharing/reservation usability decision before mutating the preliminary
first-city counters, or factor the relevant non-yield usability predicate into the
preliminary classification. Take care not to lose intentional accounting for fogged
plots (`iUnrevealedTiles`) or the home plot.


F168 / provisional KI#491 -- same-type resource empire value is assigned to the first CityPlot copy, making found value depend on arbitrary BFC enumeration order
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
nonYieldBonusValue receives the BFC's partial `aiBonusCount`. Current SAS does:

    bool bSurplus = isBonusOwnedOrClaimedByFutureBFC(eBonus);
    if (paiBonusCount != NULL)
    {
        if ((*paiBonusCount)[eBonus] > 0)
            bSurplus = true;
        (*paiBonusCount)[eBonus]++;
    }
    int const iEffectiveHappyHealthValue = (bSurplus ? 0 : iHappyHealthValue);

Thus, when the empire does not already have reliable coverage, the FIRST BFC copy of a
bonus type receives the once-per-type empire health/happiness/building value; every
later copy receives zero for that component.

But each copy's non-yield result is also adjusted by that individual plot's culture
modifier. The first copy need not be the safest, most culturally reliable or otherwise
best representative of the resource type. CityPlot iteration order, not resource-state
semantics, chooses the representative.

DETERMINISTIC ROTATION REPRODUCTION
Take a candidate BFC with two otherwise ordinary Rice plots. Let one be a reliably
claimable 100%-culture-modifier copy and the other a contested/less reliable 50% copy.
Assume the empire has no existing reliable Rice. Under the current Granary-style
health/building setup, Rice's explicit once-per-type value can be about 300 before
culture adjustment.

Layout A: the 50% copy occupies the earlier CityPlot index. It receives the once-per-type
value and contributes about 150; the later 100% copy is surplus and contributes 0.

Layout B: rotate/rearrange the equivalent BFC so the 100% copy occupies the earlier
CityPlot index. It receives about 300; the later 50% copy gets 0.

The two local resource tile yields are still evaluated independently. The difference in
empire-wide resource value is created solely by enumeration order.

ANCESTRY
This is older than KI#178. Base AdvCiv's nonYieldBonusValue already documents
`aiBonusCount` as "only a partial count" and gives the first duplicate more value while
dividing later copies. The shape is present in the BBAI-derived/K-Mod found-value line
rather than in the supplied Civ4CE/BtS reference implementation's simpler bonus value.

SAS KI#178 (commit 6341d3d556a7f580e3664b8631d52446c2c7c4da) did not invent the
ordering dependency, but amplified it: later duplicates' explicit health/happiness
settlement value is now exactly zero rather than merely diminished.

CONSEQUENCE
Geometrically/resource-equivalent candidate sites can receive materially different
found values depending on which same-type copy happens to occupy the earlier CityPlot
index. The error is strongest when duplicate copies differ in culture reliability.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Compute the once-per-bonus-type empire value outside arbitrary per-plot first-hit
assignment, or accumulate/select the best eligible representative (e.g. highest
reliability) before applying the marginal value. Keep local tile yield values per plot.

F169 / provisional KI#492 -- StartingPositionIteration workable-plot precompute runs a discarded full city-site evaluation for every candidate plot
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
StartingPositionIteration precomputes a map-wide workable-plot value table through:

    CitySiteEvaluator yieldEval(..., bNormalize=true);
    ...
    rYieldVal = yieldEval.evaluateWorkablePlot(kPlot);

CitySiteEvaluator::evaluateWorkablePlot first chooses a hypothetical city center and
then constructs:

    AIFoundValue foundVal(*pBestCityPlot, *this);

AIFoundValue's constructor unconditionally finishes with:

    m_iResult = evaluate();

Only after that complete city-site evaluation has run does the wrapper call the
separate:

    foundVal.evaluateWorkablePlot(kPlot)

and return that result. The constructor's m_iResult is never read in this path.

WHY THE FULL EVALUATION IS NOT INITIALIZATION FOR THE WORKABLE PATH
The mutable intermediate state produced by evaluate() -- aiCitySiteRadius,
abOwnCityRadius, abFlip, bFirstColony and iUnrevealedTiles -- is not consumed by
AIFoundValue::evaluateWorkablePlot or the helpers it calls. The fields that path does
need (player/team/era/candidate-area/coastal context, city count, etc.) are initialized
before the constructor invokes evaluate(). Thus the expensive full evaluation is pure
discarded work here rather than a hidden prerequisite.

REACHABILITY / SCALE
This is the normal StartingPositionIteration constructor path. SPI loops over essentially
the whole map, skipping only plots that are not potential city work, and performs this
wrapper call once per remaining plot to build yieldValues/yieldsPerArea. Each successful
hypothetical city center therefore triggers a full found-value pass over a BFC and its
associated overlap/resource/culture/health/modifier logic merely so that the object can
then run the independent workable-plot calculation.

ANCESTRY
The redundant shape was introduced with AdvCiv's StartingPositionIteration work in
practical 2280 / commit a70e4ce3a1 (2020-05-28). The initial implementation already
constructed AIFoundValue in CitySiteEvaluator::evaluateWorkablePlot and then ignored
get()/m_iResult. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain that contract.

CONSEQUENCE
Starting-position iteration pays thousands of avoidable full city-site evaluations on
ordinary maps. This is a pure performance defect: removing the discarded evaluation
should not change the returned workable-plot value.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Allow AIFoundValue construction without immediately running evaluate(), or factor the
immutable helper context used by evaluateWorkablePlot into a lightweight path. Preserve
normal CitySiteEvaluator::evaluate behavior while ensuring the SPI wrapper initializes
only the state its workable-plot calculation actually consumes.


F170 / provisional KI#493 -- first-colony landmass bonus reads unrevealed foreign city count despite AdvCiv's explicit no-cheat area-size adjustment
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
adjustToCitiesPerArea applies up to a x2 value modifier when:

    if (kArea.getNumCivCities() <= 0)

and describes this as the bonus for being the first civilization to colonize the
landmass. CvArea::getNumCivCities() is simply total cities minus Barbarian cities; it has
no team-visibility or city-deduction filter.

The same block then sizes that bonus from:

    kArea.getNumRevealedTiles(eTeam) // advc.031: Don't cheat

So the amount of land considered is deliberately knowledge-limited, while the preceding
question "does another civilization already have a city here?" still uses omniscient
map state.

REACHABILITY
adjustToCitiesPerArea is called unconditionally near the end of ordinary AIFoundValue::
evaluate. It is not restricted to all-seeing map generation. For a player with existing
cities evaluating its first colony on another sufficiently revealed continent, a rival
city can exist elsewhere in that same CvArea while remaining entirely unknown to the
player/team.

DETERMINISTIC INFORMATION-LEAK REPRODUCTION
Take two game states with identical evaluated site, revealed tiles, known cities and all
other information available to the evaluating team. In state A, no other civilization
has a city anywhere on that landmass. In state B, an unknown rival city exists beyond
fog on the same landmass.

State A enters the first-colony modifier and can receive as much as x2 on a large,
sufficiently revealed area. State B receives no such modifier solely because
getNumCivCities sees the hidden city. The AI's found value therefore changes based on
information it cannot know.

ANCESTRY
K-Mod practical/history commit 7cfc27cd59 changed the BtS pArea->getNumCities()==0
bonus into a size-scaled "first on a new continent" bonus, still using omniscient city
count. AdvCiv later changed the city test to civilian-only and, importantly, changed the
area-size input to getNumRevealedTiles(eTeam) with the explicit "Don't cheat" comment,
but did not knowledge-limit the city-existence half. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS retain
the mixed contract.

CONSEQUENCE
A hidden rival colony can remove a very large expansion bonus and alter site ranking.
This is not merely imperfect forecasting; two states identical from the AI's point of
view can produce different found values.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Determine whether the area contains a known/deducible non-Barbarian rival city (plus
our/team cities as appropriate) using the same knowledge policy as the rest of
CitySiteEvaluator, rather than raw CvArea city totals. Keep the revealed-area sizing and
do not reveal a hidden city merely to decide whether the player is "first."


F171 / provisional KI#494 -- advc.181 visibility-hardening defeats isDeadlockedBonus's explicit adjacent-revealed fog allowance, causing false deadlock penalties
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
isDeadlockedBonus deliberately allows a potential future city center around a visible
resource to proceed when either the center itself is revealed OR it is merely adjacent
to revealed terrain:

    if (!isRevealed(kOtherSite) &&
        !kOtherSite.isAdjacentRevealed(eTeam))
        continue;

The comment says this is because the evaluator needs enough information to know there is
land. But the very next test is now:

    kPlayer.canFound(kOtherSite, false, kSet.isAllSeeing())

For an ordinary non-all-seeing evaluation, bIgnoreFoW is false. Since advc.181,
CvPlot::canFound immediately returns false whenever the candidate center itself is not
revealed to eTeam. Consequently the `isAdjacentRevealed` alternative above can never
make an unrevealed center count as a viable site.

DETERMINISTIC FALSE-DEADLOCK REPRODUCTION
Let a visible bonus just outside the candidate city's BFC have two otherwise valid
future city centers within its radius:

1. one revealed center lies within MIN_CITY_RANGE of the candidate. canFound succeeds,
   so bNeverFound becomes false, but this site would be blocked by founding the current
   city;
2. a second same-area center lies farther than MIN_CITY_RANGE and is actual valid land,
   but its center tile is still fogged while adjacent terrain is revealed.

The explicit precheck admits center #2, but advc.181 canFound rejects it solely because
that center is unrevealed. The loop therefore ends with !bNeverFound && !bCanFound and
classifies the resource as deadlocked. Revealing only center #2, with no geography or
ownership change, makes canFound succeed and the deadlock disappear.

CONSEQUENCE
adjustToBonusCount applies:

    iValue = (2 * iValue) / (2 + iDeadLockCount);

so one false deadlock cuts the site to 2/3 value; multiple ones are even harsher. The
result depends on a visibility detail the helper's own adjacent-revealed policy was
written to tolerate.

ANCESTRY / REGRESSION
The adjacent-revealed allowance predates advc.181. AdvCiv practical 3597 / commit
c12bd6b877 ("Fix map knowledge leaked by unit action recommendations") changed this
call to the new fog-aware CvPlayer::canFound overload. The same commit added
CvPlot::canFound's explicit `!isRevealed(eTeam) -> false` guard. It fixed information
leaks elsewhere but unintentionally made the older adjacent-revealed branch in
isDeadlockedBonus ineffective. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS inherit the mismatch.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Give isDeadlockedBonus a no-cheat prospective-site predicate that preserves its intended
adjacent-revealed terrain allowance without consulting hidden ownership/cities. Simply
switching back to omniscient canFound would reintroduce the information leak advc.181
was designed to remove; the fix should explicitly separate known terrain/founding
legality from hidden-state restrictions.

F172 / provisional KI#495 -- calculateCultureModifier leaks a completely unrevealed second rival city through area city totals
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
calculateCultureModifier starts from a revealed foreign-owned plot, but one of its
opposing-culture multipliers asks:

    p.getArea().getCitiesPerPlayer(getRevealedOwner(p)) > 1

when we have no cities in that area. CvArea::getCitiesPerPlayer is an omniscient total;
it does not filter the rival's cities by reveal state or AI_deduceCitySite.

DETERMINISTIC INFORMATION-LEAK REPRODUCTION
Hold the evaluated plot, its revealed owner, all visible culture clues and the entire
player-visible map state fixed. In state A the rival has exactly one city in that land
area. In state B it has a second city elsewhere in the same area, completely unknown to
the evaluating team. State B alone multiplies the foreign culture-rate estimate by 1.5.
The same contested tile therefore receives a different culture modifier solely from a
hidden city.

ANCESTRY
This particular `citiesPerPlayer > 1` clause was added during AdvCiv's 2019
AIFoundValue/CitySiteEvaluator refactor. The older inline culture block had the rival
capital special case but not this hidden second-city multiplier. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
current SAS retain it.

CONSEQUENCE
Culture reliability is applied to plot yield and bonus valuation. A hidden remote city
can therefore alter settlement ranking for a known contested tile without providing any
new information to the AI.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Base this multiplier on known/deducible rival cities in the relevant area, or remove the
city-count proxy. Do not use raw CvArea city totals in a knowledge-limited evaluation.


F173 / provisional KI#496 -- KI#178 future-BFC bonus ownership check reads live actual plot owner after requiring only team-revealed resource knowledge
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
SAS KI#178's isBonusOwnedOrClaimedByFutureBFC deliberately reasons about resources that
are known to the player's team. It starts by requiring a team-revealed bonus, but then
uses:

    pLoopPlot->getOwner()

rather than the team-visible/revealed owner. Plot ownership can change while a plot is
fogged, whereas CvPlot maintains a separate revealed-owner value specifically for
knowledge-limited consumers.

DETERMINISTIC INFORMATION-LEAK REPRODUCTION
Take a known resource in the future BFC of one of our existing cities, leave the plot
under fog, and let rival culture gain or lose current ownership without the evaluating
team seeing the plot again. The actual-owner branch inside the helper changes even
though the team's remembered owner and resource knowledge do not.

CONSEQUENCE
The same hidden ownership transition can alter both the +250 unowned-resource diversity
nudge and the long-term health/happiness/building value path that asks whether the
empire already safely owns or claims that bonus.

ANCESTRY
This is SAS-specific to the KI#178 helper introduced in practical 6025 / commit
6341d3d556. The helper's comments frame the test in terms of known/claimed resources,
so omniscient ownership is not an intentional all-seeing contract.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Use the same revealed-owner helper/policy as the surrounding CitySiteEvaluator code.
Current ownership may be used only when all-seeing or currently visible under an
explicit knowledge rule.


F174 / provisional KI#497 -- raw city-radius counters leak undeduced hidden city existence throughout ordinary site evaluation
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
CvPlot::isCityRadius() and getCityRadiusCount() are global map-state counters. When a
city is founded, setPlotCity updates the radius count for the full BFC immediately;
there is no per-team visibility component. CitySiteEvaluator nevertheless reads those
raw counters in several ordinary non-all-seeing paths, including overlap/flip setup,
bad-tile rescue, isTooManyBadTiles, isUsablePlot and isDeadlockedBonus.

This is independent of revealed plot ownership. A city can remain entirely undeduced
while its BFC has already changed the raw city-radius counters consumed here.

DETERMINISTIC INFORMATION-LEAK REPRODUCTION
Hold all terrain, revealed ownership/culture and known city sites fixed. Add an enemy
city wholly under fog such that one or more already-revealed candidate-BFC plots fall in
its radius, but leave too few ownership clues for AI_deduceCitySite. The corresponding
isCityRadius/getCityRadiusCount reads change immediately. Depending on the path, the
plot can become taken/shared, stop rescuing a bad-site test, alter flip assumptions, or
make a nearby resource cease to count as deadlockable. None of those changes require
the AI to have learned that the city exists.

ANCESTRY / WHY THIS LOOKS LIKE AN OMISSION
AdvCiv practical/commit ca3e110fd5 is explicitly titled "AI city site eval respects fog
of war wrt. tile ownership." It systematically replaced raw owner/team reads with
revealed-state helpers and added/used AI_deduceCitySite, but raw city-radius counters in
the same evaluator survived that cleanup. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS therefore retain a
second channel through which hidden city existence leaks back in.

CONSEQUENCE
Two states that are identical under the evaluator's intended map-knowledge contract can
produce different found values, including hard site rejection, solely because an
undeduced city exists in fog.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Introduce a knowledge-limited "known/deducible city radius" predicate for this evaluator
(or derive radius membership only from own/team cities plus known/deducible foreign
cities). Do not simply remove the radius checks; they serve valid overlap/sharing and
deadlock purposes once the city that creates the radius is knowable.


F175 / provisional KI#498 -- calculateCultureModifier reads exact hidden working-city identity, geometry and capital status even when that city is not deducible
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
Even if the raw city-radius leak in F174 is repaired, calculateCultureModifier has an
independent hidden-city channel:

    CvCity* pForeignCity = p.getWorkingCity();

It then uses that actual city's exact area relationship / position and capital status to
modify the assumed foreign culture pressure. The preceding site-usability logic can
explicitly decline to deduce a foreign city, but this routine receives the hidden
working-city pointer anyway.

ISOLATED REPRODUCTION
Use a revealed foreign-owned plot with too little surrounding ownership information for
AI_deduceCitySite to identify the underlying rival city. Keep the player's revealed map
state identical, but place the actual hidden working city adjacent to the plot in one
state and two plots away in another. The geometry-dependent culture-rate multiplier can
differ (including the x1.8 branch) despite the city location remaining unknowable.
Changing whether that hidden city is the capital provides another independent hidden
input.

ANCESTRY
AdvCiv's older culture-value work introduced a raw getWorkingCity()->isCapital() special
case, and later geometry refinements made the hidden pointer matter still more. The
subsequent fog-of-war cleanup that added revealed-owner and city-deduction safeguards
did not knowledge-limit this working-city access. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS retain it.

CONSEQUENCE
Known rival ownership on a tile can reveal information about the exact hidden city that
works/claims it through settlement scoring, and can change plot/bonus value without a
corresponding observation.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Only use a foreign-city pointer when that city is revealed/deducible to the evaluating
team; otherwise use a conservative owner-only culture estimate that does not depend on
hidden city coordinates or capital status.


F176 / provisional KI#499 -- live plot-culture amounts and culture ranking are read through fog after ownership was made knowledge-limited
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
calculateCultureModifier correctly obtains the foreign player from getRevealedOwner,
but then reads current map state directly:

    p.getCulture(ePlayer)
    p.getCulture(getRevealedOwner(p))

and related overlap logic uses culture-derived getSecondOwner / findHighestCulturePlayer
on the live plot. isUsablePlot requires only that the plot has ever been revealed; it
does not require active visibility.

CvPlot stores remembered owner/improvement/route information per team, but not a
per-team snapshot of exact plot culture. The UI likewise only exposes exact plot culture
percentages while the plot is actively visible. Plot culture can continue changing
while the tile is fogged.

DETERMINISTIC INFORMATION-LEAK REPRODUCTION
Reveal a contested rival-owned tile, move vision away, then let either side's culture
accumulate while the plot remains fogged. The team's remembered ownership/map state can
remain unchanged while the live getCulture values and possibly second/highest culture
player change. Re-evaluating a settlement site therefore changes its culture modifier
or flip inference solely from hidden culture growth.

ANCESTRY
The 2021 AdvCiv fog-of-war cleanup ca3e110fd5 explicitly replaced raw owner/team reads
inside calculateCultureModifier with revealed-owner helpers, but left the raw culture
amounts and culture-ranking queries untouched. This is therefore a close sibling of
F174/F175 in the same incomplete knowledge-boundary cleanup, not a SAS invention.

CONSEQUENCE
Yield and resource reliability on already-seen but currently fogged plots can track
exact hidden culture progress. Two player-indistinguishable states can receive different
found values.

REPAIR DIRECTION
For non-visible plots, avoid exact live culture ratios/rankings unless a deliberate
knowledge snapshot exists. Use revealed ownership plus a conservative/stale proxy; keep
raw culture for all-seeing or actively visible evaluation.


F177 / provisional KI#500 -- SAS runtime first-settler wrapper disables allSeeing but leaves starting-location-only omniscient helpers active
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
SAS practical 6008 introduced SAS_evaluateFirstCityFoundValue specifically to retain
starting-capital weights while removing map-generation omniscience during live first
settler movement:

    CitySiteEvaluator kEvaluator(kOwner, -1, true);
    kEvaluator.setAllSeeing(false);

The commit message explicitly says runtime first-city evaluation should use only
revealed BFC terrain, bonuses and improvement potential, with all-seeing evaluation kept
for map generation. But `bStartingLoc=true` still activates older code that treats
"starting location" itself as an omniscient map-generation mode rather than consulting
isAllSeeing.

LIVE MANIFESTATION 1 -- hidden land-area boundary/topology (default configuration)
evaluate() unconditionally calls adjustToLandAreaBoundary whenever isStartingLoc().
With the recommended/default PASSABLE_AREAS=1, that routine scans raw plots out to range
4, tests hidden impassable peak chains / representative areas, and sums complete
CvArea::getNumTiles sizes. No reveal or allSeeing guard exists. Two first-settler
positions with identical revealed BFC information can therefore receive different
scores because of unrevealed mountain/land-area topology outside what the settler knows.

LIVE MANIFESTATION 2 -- hidden resources on Balanced/HIGH normalization games
AIFoundValue::getBonus contains an older normalization rule:

    if (kSet.isStartingLoc() || kSet.isNormalizing())
        if (getStartingPlotNormalizationLevel() > NORMALIZE_LOW)
            return p.getBonusType();

Balanced maps explicitly set the game's normalization level to HIGH during map
generation, and CvGame::initDiplomacy deliberately preserves HIGH rather than resetting
it. Thus the new runtime wrapper's setAllSeeing(false) still returns raw hidden bonuses
on Balanced games simply because isStartingLoc remains true.

ADDITIONAL START-MODE OMNISCIENCE
The first-city evaluateSeaAccess path also consults full-map starting-plot counts and
findBiggestArea(true)/complete water-area topology. This is the same mode-boundary root:
starting-capital weighting and map-generation knowledge are still coupled in inherited
helpers.

ANCESTRY / REGRESSION
The omniscient helpers predate SAS and were valid when starting-location evaluation was
an all-seeing map-generation operation. SAS practical 6008 / commit a5f183a489
introduced a new runtime use and assumed setAllSeeing(false) was sufficient to make that
mode knowledge-limited. It fixed the range-6 starting-surroundings adjustment explicitly,
but did not audit every other `isStartingLoc()` path.

CONSEQUENCE
The first Settler's new supposedly no-cheat roaming/site ranking can still react to
hidden map geometry in ordinary default games and hidden bonuses in HIGH/Balanced games.
That can directly alter which capital site it walks toward or founds.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Separate "use starting-capital weights" from "map-generation/normalization omniscience."
Gate genuinely omniscient start-only helpers on isAllSeeing (or an explicit map-generation
mode), not merely isStartingLoc. Audit every isStartingLoc branch reached by the runtime
wrapper rather than patching only the already-disabled starting-surroundings modifier.


F178 / provisional KI#501 -- foreign-city culture pressure uses the live hidden culture level after a city is merely known/deduced
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
The current SAS culture-pressure gate says "No-cheat preserved" and skips cities that
cannot be known/deduced, but for every admitted city it computes:

    int const r = pCity->getCultureLevel() + 3;

A CvCity stores only per-team revealed and espionage-visibility booleans; there is no
per-team remembered CultureLevel value. A city that was seen earlier can remain revealed
while currently fogged, and its actual culture level can rise in the meantime.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION
Take a known/deduced rival city under fog and a candidate at distance 3. With culture
level 1, r=4 and the current linear pressure is 32, below the configured SOFT=35 and thus
ignored. If the hidden city grows to culture level 2, r=5 and pressure becomes 46,
triggering a substantial soft multiplier (78% with current tuning). No new observation
of the city is required for that ranking change.

ANCESTRY
This exact knowledge blind spot is inherited rather than created by the SAS replacement:
Base AdvCiv's preceding foreign-proximity code also used
`pLoopCity->getCultureLevel()+3` during ordinary runtime evaluation, and K-Mod's
AI_deduceCitySite itself uses the city's current culture level while deciding whether
its site can be inferred. SAS practical 4962 replaced the old proximity formula with the
simpler pressure gate but retained the live exact level while explicitly describing the
new gate as no-cheat.

CONSEQUENCE
A known but fogged rival city can silently expand the range/strength of settlement
pressure and flip a candidate from unpenalized to strongly down-weighted (or eventually
hard rejected) based on hidden current culture progress.

REPAIR DIRECTION
For a city that is not currently visible, use only a knowledge-limited/stale culture
range estimate rather than live getCultureLevel. The same principle should be reviewed
inside AI_deduceCitySite, but that cross-file helper issue should not be multiplied into
another CitySiteEvaluator finding unless independently audited.

F179 / provisional KI#502 -- ordinary runtime site evaluation reads complete hidden CvArea topology and size
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
Several ordinary non-all-seeing found-value paths use the complete CvArea graph or
getNumTiles rather than team-revealed geography. Unlike the map-generation-only
starting-location omniscience grouped under F177, these branches also run while AI
players evaluate later city sites with fog of war still active.

The codebase itself establishes a contrary knowledge contract nearby: settlement-area
logic sometimes substitutes getNumRevealedTiles(eTeam), explicitly with comments such
as "Don't cheat." CvArea::getNumTiles and area connectivity have no per-team remembered
or revealed-state equivalent behind them.

CLEAN DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION -- CANAL VALUE
Use an ordinary later-city candidate touching two revealed water tiles / water areas.
Keep every plot currently revealed to the evaluating team unchanged, but extend one or
both water bodies only through unrevealed terrain. evaluateSeaAccess tests the complete
sizes of those CvArea objects against MIN_WATER_SIZE_FOR_OCEAN. Merely making the hidden
continuations large enough can turn the canal branch on and add substantial found value
(up to 270 with the current formula), although the player has learned nothing new.

OTHER LIVE MANIFESTATIONS OF THE SAME ROOT
* An inaccessible resource's long-term non-yield value uses the complete size of its
  other land area and changes between the 45% and 60% cases around the <=2-tile test.
* Water-resource bEasyAccess can become true because the globally connected water area
  contains one of our cities, even if the channel establishing that connection is still
  wholly under fog.
* The inherited bad-tile rescue / small-area logic also branches on full candidate-area
  size rather than known area extent.

ANCESTRY
An area-size dependency is already present in Firaxis BtS found-value logic; K-Mod and
AdvCiv add further full-area / water-connectivity heuristics. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS
therefore inherit a family of ordinary-runtime hidden-topology inputs rather than one
single recent SAS regression.

CONSEQUENCE
Two maps that are identical under the evaluating team's map knowledge can rank the same
city site differently solely because unrevealed terrain completes, enlarges or connects
an area behind fog.

REPAIR DIRECTION
For ordinary non-all-seeing evaluation, derive area-size / connectivity proxies from
team-revealed plots where the heuristic is intended to model player knowledge. Preserve
raw CvArea topology for map-generation/all-seeing evaluation. Treat the repeated size
and connectivity symptoms as one knowledge-boundary root rather than patching only the
canal formula.


F180 / provisional KI#503 -- practical 5976 low-food bonus-improvement helper omits already-available irrigated Farm food
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
Practical 5976 introduced CvPlot::SAS_getBonusImprovementFoodChange so the new dynamic
low-food-BFC score could include food from the resource's bonus-specific improvement.
The helper manually sums:

    base improvement food
    + bonus-specific improvement food
    + river-side improvement food
    + hill improvement food
    + feature-removal terrain/feature adjustments

but it never adds CvImprovementInfo::getIrrigatedYieldChange.

That differs from Civ4's normal CvPlot::calculateImprovementYieldChange, which adds the
improvement's irrigated yield whenever isIrrigationAvailable() is true.

CURRENT SHIPPED DATA / DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION
IMPROVEMENT_FARM currently has:

    IrrigatedYieldChange: +1 food
    bRequiresIrrigation: 1

and is the bonus-trade improvement for Maize (+2 improvement food), Rice (+1 food,
+1 production) and Wheat (+2 food). Put any of those visible resources on an already
irrigable flat plot -- most simply a riverside / otherwise fresh-water plot. Civ4's
actual Farm yield receives the +1 irrigated food immediately, but
SAS_getBonusImprovementFoodChange omits it.

For example, a fresh-water Maize Farm contributes one less potential food to
SAS_getLowFoodEnvironmentScore than the same improvement contributes through
calculateImprovementYieldChange. This does not depend on assuming a future irrigation
chain or future Civil Service; irrigation is already available in the reproduction.

INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY
SAS_isVeryBadBFCPlot evaluates improvement potential through
calculateImprovementYieldChange and therefore can count this same already-available +1
irrigated Farm food. The newer low-food scorer evaluates the same plot through the
manual helper and misses it. A single plot can therefore have two different notions of
its current improvement food inside the same first-city preliminary pass.

ANCESTRY / INTENT
This begins in SAS practical 5976 / commit f3137a536b (2026-06-28), whose commit message
says the hardcoded low-food heuristic is being replaced by a dynamic one based on actual
yields so that XML changes and food bonuses are reflected automatically. The helper was
introduced in that commit with the irrigated-yield omission already present.

The maintained GlobalDefines comment likewise defines the low-food score in terms of
natural food, visible bonus food and "food from its bonus-specific improvement." Farm's
current +1 irrigated food is part of that improvement's actual yield when irrigation is
available.

CONSEQUENCE
Already-irrigable Maize/Rice/Wheat plots are understated by exactly 1 potential food.
Because each missing food increases iLowFoodLocationScore by 1 and the non-coastal gate
penalizes totals above the configured threshold (currently 5, with -75 base value), the
omission can move an otherwise equivalent candidate across the low-food penalty boundary
or make that penalty stronger.

REPAIR DIRECTION
At minimum, include kImprovement.getIrrigatedYieldChange(YIELD_FOOD) when
isIrrigationAvailable() is true. If the intended contract is later broadened from
currently available yield to fully long-term potential, decide separately whether
canHavePotentialIrrigation should also be credited; that broader design choice is not
needed to fix the deterministic current-irrigation mismatch.

F181 / provisional KI#504 -- inherited AdvCiv medium-term production estimate mistakes "already owns one" for "can build it"
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
AIFoundValue::estimateImprovementProduction is documented as estimating how much
production an unimproved non-resource plot might gain in the medium term. Once the
player has more than two cities, however, its first filter for every improvement is:

    if (kPlayer.getImprovementCount(eLoopImprovement) <= 0)
        continue;

The introducing AdvCiv comment explicitly calls this a fast way to check whether the
player can build the improvement. Existing empire improvement count is not a capability
test: an improvement may be newly buildable before the first copy exists, and a retained
or captured copy may exist when its build prerequisite is not currently available.

CURRENT SHIPPED DATA / DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION
Use an empire with at least three cities that has just acquired TECH_MINING and has not
yet completed its first Mine. IMPROVEMENT_MINE has +2 production and ordinary valid
hill plots can now legally receive it, but getImprovementCount(IMPROVEMENT_MINE) is 0,
so estimateImprovementProduction skips Mine entirely. Completing the first unrelated
Mine anywhere in the empire makes the same candidate plots suddenly gain the medium-term
Mine production estimate despite no change to the candidate terrain or the player's
technology.

The opposite error is possible in scenarios/captured territory: possessing a retained
improvement can make this first proxy pass even though ownership of that improvement does
not establish that the player currently has its matching Build/tech capability. The later
p.canHaveImprovement check tests plot legality, not build-tech availability, so it does
not repair the capability mismatch.

ANCESTRY
This proxy was introduced by AdvCiv practical 1275 / commit 71fa4eef1a (v0.90rc found-
value retuning). Its introducing comment already acknowledges that the check is "not a
perfectly safe way" to determine buildability. The 2019 AIFoundValue extraction moved it
into estimateImprovementProduction unchanged. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain it.

CONSEQUENCE
Future-site production value can depend on whether the empire happens already to own one
copy of an improvement rather than on whether that improvement can actually be built.
The first copy of a newly unlocked improvement can therefore produce a discontinuous,
unrelated jump in settlement ranking; retained/captured improvements can cause the
opposite false-positive capability assumption.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Replace the getImprovementCount capability proxy with a cheap test for at least one
matching currently available Build/tech, then retain p.canHaveImprovement for the
candidate plot's terrain/feature legality. Cache/build a per-player set of currently
buildable improvement types if the old loop-cost concern still matters.


F182 / provisional KI#505 -- inherited AdvCiv AIFoundValue refactor logs zero unrevealed tiles from countBadTiles
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
countBadTiles receives the current unrevealed count through its local reference parameter
`iUnrevealed`, increments that value during the BFC scan, and then logs:

    logBBAI("Bad tiles: %d known bad, %d unrevealed",
            iBadTiles, iUnrevealedTiles)

The second argument is the AIFoundValue member, not the freshly computed local/reference
value. The member is initialized to 0 in the constructor. In evaluate(), the caller only
copies the returned local value into the member after countBadTiles has already finished
and emitted its log:

    int iUnrevealed = 0;
    iBadTiles = countBadTiles(..., iUnrevealed, ...);
    iUnrevealedTiles = iUnrevealed;

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION
Enable found-value logging and evaluate any candidate whose BFC contains at least one
unrevealed plot. Inside countBadTiles, the `iUnrevealed > 0` condition correctly selects
the two-number logging branch, but the printed unrevealed value is still the pre-call
member value 0. Thus e.g. three truly unrevealed BFC tiles are logged as:

    Bad tiles: <known> known bad, 0 unrevealed

The gameplay count returned through the reference and later stored in iUnrevealedTiles is
correct; this finding is diagnostic-only.

ANCESTRY
The bad argument is present in the extracted countBadTiles added by AdvCiv commit
078fc9bd7c (2019-12-15, "Move AI_foundValue computation into a new class"). Base AdvCiv
1.14 and current SAS retain the same line.

CONSEQUENCE
Found-value diagnostics systematically lie about unrevealed BFC count exactly in the
cases where the special fog/first-colony logic is most important. This can mislead manual
AI-site debugging even though settlement scoring itself receives the correct count.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Log the local/reference `iUnrevealed` value inside countBadTiles. The member should remain
the post-call stored value used by later evaluation stages.

WHY FILE 016 IS CLOSED
----------------------
The closure pass covered the complete active CitySiteEvaluator/AIFoundValue surface,
including the current SAS additions in CvPlot that directly feed the new first-city
plot-quality helpers. The audit specifically challenged:

* constructor/settings modes and normalizing/starting/runtime-first-settler boundaries;
* site validity, overlap, city-radius ownership/sharing/stealing and planned-site state;
* bad/unrevealed/inner-ring tile accounting and first-colony selection;
* feature removal, chop production and current/future tech eligibility;
* bonus discovery, improvement selection, connection timing and improvement yields;
* nature/special/building/resource health/happiness valuation;
* KI#178 future-BFC ownership, duplicate handling and civilization building effects;
* culture claim/flip/foreign-city geometry and fog-of-war knowledge boundaries;
* first-city low-food, very-bad, minimum-good-slot and cautious-health gates;
* home-resource settlement penalties and current shipped bonus/improvement XML;
* production potential, fresh water, sea access, canals and complete-area heuristics;
* normalization workable-plot precomputation and StartingPositionIteration contract;
* starting surroundings/choices/land-boundary normalization helpers;
* city-per-area, resource-count and deadlocked-resource adjustments;
* logging, assertions, TODO/warning comments and diagnostic-only code paths;
* Base AdvCiv/K-Mod/Firaxis ancestry and current SAS commit-diff history where needed;
* current shipped XML legality and negative controls for every promoted data-contract
  claim rather than relying only on generic mod-mod possibilities.

The final adversarial reread rejected or bounded several plausible but unsupported
follow-ups:

* the shared SPI representative-player table was already player-sensitive in Base
  AdvCiv and does not promise exact per-civilization valuation;
* the apparent tiny-lake Lighthouse/Harbor mismatch was false because AdvCiv's
  isCoastalLand(-1) resolves to MIN_WATER_SIZE_FOR_OCEAN;
* the historical double special-food culture modifier remains mostly dormant after SAS
  disabled its meaningful consumers and therefore was not assigned an ID;
* calculateBonusConnectionEra has no single universally required route-tech input because
  city/river/coast/route connectivity are alternative mechanisms;
* current water-improvement data does not make estimateImprovementProduction's water TODO
  a live non-resource production omission;
* the home-resource penalty's negative coefficients make its `iValue += r` sign correct,
  while bonus-specific-only lost-yield weighting is an explicit tuning choice rather than
  an accidental omission;
* the remaining logPlot "soon" wording/assertion oddity under hidden starting bonuses is
  downstream of F177's runtime-starting-mode leak rather than an independent gameplay
  root;
* no additional independent active assert/TODO/data-contract defect survived current XML
  and helper-semantics checking.

With those negative controls recorded, continuing to mine CitySiteEvaluator.cpp would now
be more likely to split existing roots or elevate tuning disagreements than to discover a
new independent correctness issue. F183 is therefore deliberately left unused.

F183 / provisional KI#506
-------------------------
TITLE
    reviewWarPlans retains superseded cross-pass state when a plan change forces
    the deliberate retry loop.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED. Inherited UWAI/AdvCiv defect; present before the 2021 UWAI style
    rewrite and retained by Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS.

ROOT
    reviewWarPlans intentionally repeats its complete review whenever reviewPlan
    changes a target plan, because that change can alter evaluation of the other
    plans. However, state intended to describe the final reviewed plan set is
    initialized before the do/while retry loop and then only accumulated:

        bool bScheme = true;
        bool bAllNaval = true, bAnyNaval = false;
        bool bAllLand = true, bAnyLand = false;
        do
        {
            ...
            if (iU < -100 && kAgent.isAtWar(eTarget))
                bScheme = false;
            ...
            if (aPlans[i].bNaval)
            {
                bAnyNaval = true;
                bAllLand = false;
            }
            else
            {
                bAnyLand = true;
                bAllNaval = false;
            }
        } while (bPlanChanged);

    abTargetDone deliberately removes a target after that target changes, but the
    classifications and bad-war state learned from earlier, superseded passes are
    never removed.

REACHABLE MULTI-PASS SHAPE
    Pass 1 can review target A successfully and classify it as land, then target B
    changes and triggers a retry. The retry exists precisely because B's change can
    alter the simulated context and therefore A's utility/plan character. On pass 2,
    A can then itself be canceled/switched and become done. A is omitted thereafter,
    but its pass-1 land bit remains latched. If the final surviving positive plans are
    all naval, bAllNaval is still false and the final alignAreaAI(true) call is lost.

    The same root is even more direct for bScheme: pass 1 can observe a current war
    below -100 utility and set bScheme=false. If reviewPlan then succeeds in ending
    that war and the review repeats, the final plan set can contain no disastrous
    current war at all, yet bScheme remains false and doWar skips scheme() for the
    whole turn.

CONSEQUENCE
    * AreaAI alignment can describe a superseded intermediate review pass rather
      than the final surviving plan set, despite the trailing source comment saying
      this review is the "last word on AreaAI".
    * A war that is ended during review can leave stale bScheme=false behind and
      suppress all new-war scheming until the next team turn.

ANCESTRY
    The pre-2021 UWAI implementation already initializes allNaval/anyNaval and
    allLand/anyLand outside the retry loop. AdvCiv's 2021 commit 4ae382e5db
    ("Revised all code in the UWAI component") mechanically retained that placement;
    current Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS still do so. Current SAS also retains bScheme
    outside the loop, exposing the same stale-pass contract on whether scheming is
    allowed.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Recompute all state that is meant to describe the current/final pass at the start
    of each do/while iteration. The simplest correctness-first repair is to use
    per-pass bScheme/bAllNaval/bAnyNaval/bAllLand/bAnyLand values and preserve only
    the values from the final no-change pass. Do not merely clear the four AreaAI
    flags while leaving bScheme monotonic across superseded passes.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS
    This is not based on a hypothetical retry: reviewWarPlans explicitly changes a
    plan, marks that target done, logs "repeating review", and re-runs WarEvaluator
    for the remaining plans. Nor does the bug require the changed target itself to be
    classified; a plan classified before the changed target can become invalid on a
    later pass, which is exactly the dependency the retry is meant to handle.


F184 / provisional KI#507
-------------------------
TITLE
    Brokered-peace low-score relaxation is dead because makePeaceTrade immediately
    returns DENIAL_VICTORY after setting bNoDenial=true.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED. AdvCiv regression introduced by ca3cdbcdce (2020-05-17), retained by
    Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS.

ROOT
    makePeaceTrade contains an explicit low-score exception when the enemy already
    wants peace but our own reluctance is moderately high:

        if (iEnemyReluct <= 0)
        {
            if (iAgentReluct < 55)
                bNoDenial = true;
            else
            {
                ...
                if (rGameEra > 0 && rScoreRatio < ...)
                {
                    // We're not doing well in score; the broker might be doing much better.
                    if (iAgentReluct < 70)
                        bNoDenial = true;
                    else return DENIAL_TOO_MUCH;
                }
                return DENIAL_VICTORY;
            }
        }
        ...
        if (bNoDenial)
            return NO_DENIAL;

    For the intended low-score case with iAgentReluct in [55,69], the function sets
    bNoDenial=true and then unconditionally returns DENIAL_VICTORY before the later
    NO_DENIAL branch can run.

INTRODUCING-COMMIT PROOF
    AdvCiv commit ca3cdbcdce, dated 2020-05-17 and titled
    "UWAI: Tweak brokered-peace denial reason", introduced this exact branch. Its
    commit message says:

        Civs that are clearly not winning the game shouldn't respond
        "we'd rather win this game".

    The diff added bNoDenial plus the low-score test, including the assignment
    bNoDenial=true for reluctance below 70, but also added the unconditional
    DENIAL_VICTORY return immediately after the test. The resulting control flow
    therefore contradicts the stated purpose of the introducing commit.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION STATE
    During brokered peace:
    * enemy reluctance <= 0;
    * agent reluctance is 55 through 69;
    * game era factor > 0;
    * the agent's score ratio passes the explicit "not doing well" threshold;
    * enemy willingness-to-talk and ordinary trade legality otherwise permit the
      later NO_DENIAL path.

    The low-score branch sets bNoDenial but returns DENIAL_VICTORY anyway. The broker
    is refused specifically with the victory-denial reason that this commit intended
    to suppress for a clearly trailing civ.

CONSEQUENCE
    Brokered peace is refused when the function's own score policy says it should be
    allowed. At minimum, the denial reason is wrong; because bNoDenial is the actual
    gate for NO_DENIAL, the misplaced return also blocks the peace trade itself in
    the moderate-reluctance low-score window.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    After the low-score branch succeeds with iAgentReluct < 70, fall through to the
    later bNoDenial handling. Preserve DENIAL_TOO_MUCH for the >=70 low-score case and
    DENIAL_VICTORY for the cases that fail the low-score exception.

NEGATIVE CONTROL
    This is not inferred merely from indentation or naming: the tracked introducing
    diff and its commit message establish that the low-score exception was intended
    to change behavior, and the current unconditional return makes the successful
    half of that new branch dead.
