F214 / provisional KI#537
-------------------------
TITLE
    MilitaryBranch typical-unit refresh is sticky: when a branch loses every currently
    trainable candidate, the cache keeps its old unit and can forecast military capacity
    that no longer exists (current concrete case: losing Uranium retains nuclear buildup).

STATUS
    CONFIRMED CURRENT CROSS-FILE CACHE-REFRESH DEFECT. Root is inherited from the initial
    2017 UWAI/MilitaryBranch integration and is unchanged in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current
    AdvCiv-SAS. Reached from queue 031 through UWAICache::updateTypicalUnits; the local
    implementation lives in queue 064 MilitaryBranch.cpp and must be treated as an
    already-owned root when that file is audited later.

ROOT
    UWAICache::update() calls updateTypicalUnits() every ordinary cache refresh:

        updateTypicalUnits();

    and UWAICache::updateTypicalUnits() asks every persistent MilitaryBranch object to
    refresh itself:

        for (size_t i = 0; i < m_militaryPower.size(); i++)
            m_militaryPower[i]->updateTypicalUnit();

    However, MilitaryBranch::updateTypicalUnit() does not invalidate m_eTypicalUnit or
    m_rTypicalPower before looking for the best CURRENTLY trainable candidate. It merely
    overwrites them when a candidate beats the default-zero rBestValue. If no candidate
    survives the trainability/domain/utility checks, the previous turn's unit and power
    remain cached.

    NuclearArsenal::updateTypicalUnit() independently repeats the same pattern rather
    than calling the base implementation. It even returns immediately when the owner has
    no capital without clearing the old nuke first.

    Therefore these functions implement "replace if a new candidate exists" rather than
    the required refresh/replacement semantics "compute the best current candidate, or
    NO_UNIT if there is none."

CURRENT-SAS NUCLEAR REPRODUCTION
    This is live under the supplied current XML, not merely a future-mod robustness case.
    Both current nuclear units require Uranium:

        UNIT_TACTICAL_NUKE  -> BonusType BONUS_URANIUM
        UNIT_ICBM           -> BonusType BONUS_URANIUM

    and both require Fission + Rocketry. CvCity::canTrain delegates to CvPlot::canTrain;
    with bTestVisible=false, CvPlot::canTrain explicitly rejects a unit whose required
    BonusType is not connected/available in that city.

    Supported sequence:

    1. Player P has Fission/Rocketry and Uranium. Its capital can train an ICBM or
       Tactical Nuke. UWAICache::update -> NuclearArsenal::updateTypicalUnit stores a
       nuclear m_eTypicalUnit and matching m_rTypicalPower.
    2. P then loses its last connected Uranium (e.g. improvement/resource connection is
       lost or the supplying trade ends) while remaining otherwise alive and developed.
    3. On the next cache update, the Nuclear branch scans the same civ units. The capital
       canTrain checks now reject both nukes.
    4. No candidate enters the rLoopValue > rBestValue assignment, but the routine never
       first sets m_eTypicalUnit=NO_UNIT. The old nuke therefore survives indefinitely
       while Uranium remains unavailable.

    This is a post-refresh stale value, not merely the expected one-turn interval between
    an asynchronous resource change and the next UWAICache update.

DIRECT WAR-EVALUATION CONSEQUENCE
    InvasionGraph::Node::initMilitary() copies the current cached MilitaryBranch objects,
    including the stale NuclearArsenal, into the simulation.

    ArmamentForecast then deliberately reserves an offensive nuclear buildup share
    (20 percent in current AdvCiv/SAS) and documents the intended safeguard:

        // Undone below if unable to build nukes

    The safeguard is exactly the typical-unit test shared by all branches:

        if (m_kMilitary[i]->getTypicalUnit() == NO_UNIT)
        {
            rSurplus += rBranchPortions[i];
            rBranchPortions[i] = 0;
        }

    Because the stale Nuclear branch still reports the old nuke, the safeguard does not
    fire. The forecast later calls getTypicalCost/getTypicalPower and converts the
    nuclear branch's production share into predicted extra nuclear military power even
    though no city can currently train a nuke.

    This can feed InvasionGraph/MilitaryAnalyst/WarEvaluator with an overstated armament
    trajectory and therefore alter war/peace utility decisions. It does not require the
    player to have zero existing nukes; the defect is specifically that FUTURE production
    is forecast from a unit that is no longer trainable.

BROADER SAME-ROOT MANIFESTATIONS
    The stale-refresh contract is not nuclear-specific.

    * For sea branches the base update uses CvTeamAI::AI_isExpectingToTrain, which scans
      actual cities and requires a qualifying coastal city that can train the unit. A civ
      that loses its last useful coastal city can therefore have no current Fleet or
      Logistics candidate while retaining the old cached ship/transport. ArmamentForecast
      can then continue assigning naval production to capacity the civ can no longer
      build, and UWAICache::shipSpeed can continue using a stale Logistics transport.

    * Any branch whose last trainable candidate disappears through a resource/prerequisite
      change has the same sticky-unit behavior. Nuclear is the clearest current-data case
      because both current nuke types share the same removable Uranium requirement.

    These are manifestations of one refresh-invalidation root, not additional finding IDs.

ANCESTRY / INTENT PROOF
    Practical AdvCiv commit 1253 (f6ff6a182f, 2017-04-16), the initial WarAndPeace/UWAI
    cache integration, already contains both sides of the contradiction:

    * MilitaryBranch::updateTypicalUnit and NuclearArsenal::updateTypicalUnit assign the
      stored typical unit only after finding a better candidate and never clear it at
      refresh start.
    * The initial ArmamentForecast comments that its 25-percent nuclear share is
      "Undone below if unable to build nukes" and implements that by testing whether the
      branch's typical unit is NULL.

    Thus the cache value was intended from its introduction to represent CURRENT
    buildability, but the invalidation case was omitted. Later refactors changed names,
    containers and numeric types but preserve the sticky refresh. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
    current SAS remain behaviorally the same here.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
    At minimum, each typical-unit refresh must begin from an invalid/no-candidate state:

        m_eTypicalUnit = NO_UNIT;
        m_rTypicalPower = 0;

    before scanning candidates. This must also be done in NuclearArsenal's independent
    override (or centralized in a helper that every override invokes), and before its
    early no-capital return.

    Do not reset m_rTotalPower or m_iUnits: those are separately maintained counts of the
    military actually possessed, not trainability estimates.

    Fleet has one related derived-cache detail that must not be missed when implementing
    the general repair. Fleet::updateTypicalUnit currently updates m_bCanBombard only if
    getTypicalUnit()!=NO_UNIT. Once the typical unit is correctly invalidated, a no-candidate
    Fleet must also leave m_bCanBombard false rather than retaining the old ship's flag.
    Army::updateCanBombard/updateCanSoften already recompute their booleans to a false
    fallback on every refresh.

    Queue 064 MilitaryBranch.cpp should revisit implementation mechanics and any additional
    derived-field siblings, but must not allocate a new root for this already-proven
    typical-unit invalidation defect.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS
    * This is not a serialization-only issue. A correctly serialized old typical unit
      should be refreshed on the next UWAICache update; the bug is that refresh itself
      cannot express "no candidate now."
    * Existing nuclear power is tracked separately by m_rTotalPower and unit reports.
      Clearing the typical unit does not erase or undercount already-built nukes.
    * The issue does not depend on tech loss, which ordinary Civ4 rarely permits. Current
      SAS Uranium availability can change during normal play while the nuclear techs and
      player remain valid.
    * A branch changing from one trainable unit to another is normally safe because a new
      candidate overwrites the old value. The failing transition is specifically
      SOME_CANDIDATE -> NO_CURRENT_CANDIDATE.


PRESERVED-FIELD MATRIX -- INTERIM NOTES
---------------------------------------
* The earlier onTeamLeaderChanged / m_abCanBeHiredAgainst seam remains under review and is
  NOT F215 at this checkpoint. A newly selected AI team leader can carry its old team's
  hireability bits through a Permanent Alliance because onTeamLeaderChanged does not reset
  that map despite its comment saying CanBeHired should start false. However, the actual
  declareWarTrade path still performs legality/attitude checks and a fresh WarEvaluator
  before accepting a sponsored war. The stale true bit may therefore be chiefly an
  alert/evaluation-suppression timing discrepancy rather than a demonstrated incorrect
  war authorization. Do not promote without a stronger consequence proof.

* F214 is distinct from F213. F213 is a full-reset/read replacement failure in a serialized
  capitulation-authorization set. F214 is an ordinary per-turn refresh failure in a
  trainability-derived military estimate.

F215 / provisional KI#538
-------------------------
TITLE
    Team-leader migration leaves CanBeHired state in the promoted player's private cache;
    a new leader can inherit default/stale TRUE hireability and immediately allow a
    sponsored war that the migration contract says must start disabled.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED INHERITED UWAI TEAM-STATE MIGRATION DEFECT. Current in Base AdvCiv 1.14
    and AdvCiv-SAS. Especially clear when an AI team leader dies and an existing AI
    teammate becomes leader; Permanent Alliance leader replacement is another supported
    path. The defect predates SAS and is rooted in the interaction between advc.104t
    leader-cache migration and the later war-trade-alert/hireability cache.

ROOT
    UWAICache stores some team-level UWAI state in only the current team leader's player
    cache. UWAICache::leaderCache() redirects accesses to that current leader. The header
    explicitly documents that this team data has to be moved whenever the team's leader
    changes.

    CvTeam::updateLeaderID() detects a leader change and calls onTeamLeaderChanged on the
    NEW leader's UWAICache:

        if (m_eLeader != eFormerLeader && getUWAI().isEnabled() &&
            GET_PLAYER(m_eLeader).isAlive())
        {
            GET_PLAYER(m_eLeader).uwai().getCache().onTeamLeaderChanged(eFormerLeader);
        }

    UWAICache::onTeamLeaderChanged copies selected team-level state from the former
    leader, including m_aiWarUtilityIgnoringDistraction and human-target capitulation
    readiness, then ends with the explicit contract comment:

        /*  (CanBeHired and ReadyToCapitulate will get updated soon enough.
            Start out as false for the new leader.) */

    However it never modifies m_abCanBeHiredAgainst.

    That omission is not neutral. m_abCanBeHiredAgainst is declared as

        CivTeamMap<bool,void*,true> m_abCanBeHiredAgainst;

    so its enum-map default is TRUE. A normal reset() also restores TRUE, not false.
    Moreover, while a player is a non-leader, the live team hireability state is updated
    in the current leader's cache; the subordinate player's own map can therefore remain
    at its old/default contents. Promoting that player makes this previously private map
    the new live leader cache without the intended false initialization.

CONCRETE CURRENT RUNTIME PATH -- LEADER DEATH
    This does not require the more complicated Permanent Alliance case.

    1. Two AI players share a team. Player A is the current team leader; player B is a
       surviving teammate.
    2. UWAI war planning updates hireability through the team leader cache. Player B's
       private m_abCanBeHiredAgainst does not represent the team's current values. In a
       clean/default cache its entries are TRUE.
    3. Player A is eliminated while B remains alive. Normal player/team lifecycle calls
       CvTeam::updateLeaderID(), which promotes B and invokes B's
       UWAICache::onTeamLeaderChanged(A).
    4. onTeamLeaderChanged copies some team data but never clears B's CanBeHired map.
       Consequently B becomes the authoritative leader with default/stale TRUE entries
       even where the former team state was false and despite the function's own
       "Start out as false" contract.

    Permanent Alliance formation supplies another supported path: CvTeam::addTeam saves
    the absorbed team's old leader, moves its players to the surviving team, and the
    repeated setTeam/updateLeaderID sequence can select an absorbed AI player as the new
    surviving-team leader (e.g. the lower player id when both candidates are otherwise
    equal). That player's old-team hireability bits then become the merged team's live
    bits unless explicitly reset.

GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCE -- NOT ONLY AN ALERT/CPU THROTTLE
    canBeHiredAgainst is documented as only a necessary condition, but it is a real
    branch controlling whether sponsored-war evaluation is allowed.

    UWAI::Team::declareWarTrade uses the bit for a human sponsor in a large game:

        if (!kSponsor.isHuman() || kSponsor.getHasMetCivCount() < 8 ||
            leaderCache().canBeHiredAgainst(eTarget))
        {
            ... WarEvaluator ...
            if (iU > iUtilityThresh)
                return NO_DENIAL;
        }

    Therefore FALSE does not merely suppress an alert message: for the gated large-game
    human-sponsor case it prevents this path from returning NO_DENIAL at all. A stale
    TRUE left in the promoted leader's private cache permits a fresh WarEvaluator and can
    immediately make the sponsored declaration tradeable. Had onTeamLeaderChanged
    obeyed its stated false-initialization contract, that same request would remain
    denied until normal UWAI war planning recomputed hireability for the new leader.

    The later legality/attitude/power checks in CvTeamAI::AI_declareWarTrade still run,
    so this does not bypass core war legality. The bug is narrower and deterministic:
    the leader transition can incorrectly bypass UWAI's deliberate large-game
    hireability gate and change diplomatic deal availability/timing.

ANCESTRY / INTENT PROOF
    The history separates the pieces unusually well.

    * Practical AdvCiv 1268 (e11525d303) introduced onTeamLeaderChanged for team-level
      WarAndPeace/UWAI state before the hireability cache existed.
    * Practical AdvCiv 1343 (f79b7f7d5f), titled
      "Tried to reduce the flickering of the war trades alert", introduced hireAgainst,
      serialized it, initialized/reset it TRUE in that version, and made
      declareWarTrade condition its large-game human evaluation on canBeHiredAgainst.
      That commit did not extend the already-existing leader-migration routine.
    * Practical AdvCiv 2920 (4ae382e5db), "Revised all code in the UWAI component",
      contains the modern onTeamLeaderChanged form and added the explicit comment that
      CanBeHired should start FALSE for the new leader, but still added no assignment.
    * The current CivTeamMap conversion preserves TRUE as the map's default and the
      omission survives unchanged in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS.

    Thus both historical behavior and a later explicit maintenance comment support the
    same contract: the newly authoritative leader must not inherit arbitrary private
    hireability state.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
    In UWAICache::onTeamLeaderChanged, explicitly initialize the NEW leader's
    m_abCanBeHiredAgainst entries to false as part of the leader migration, before they
    can be queried as authoritative team data.

    A plain

        m_abCanBeHiredAgainst.reset();

    is NOT sufficient because this map's declared default is true. Use an explicit false
    fill or set the relevant major-civ team entries false in the migration loop.

    Do not copy the former leader's CanBeHired bits blindly. The source comment's design
    is specifically to start false and allow normal UWAI war planning to recompute the
    new leader's willingness soon afterward; this also avoids carrying old personality/
    planning-derived suppression state through the leadership transition.

    This repair is independent of F213/KI#536. F213 concerns full reset/read replacement
    of m_readyToCapitulateTo across games/loads. F215 concerns transfer of a team-level
    runtime cache when the authoritative PLAYER cache changes within a live game.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SCOPE
    * CvTeamAI::AI_declareWarTrade still performs canDeclareWar, attitude, nukes and
      other checks before UWAI::Team::declareWarTrade. F215 does not permit an illegal
      declaration; it can change a normally legal sponsored war from gated/denied to
      evaluable/acceptable too early.
    * In small games or for AI sponsors, declareWarTrade deliberately does not consult
      CanBeHired. The concrete effect is the large-game human-sponsor branch for which
      the cache was introduced.
    * If the promoted player's private bit happens already to be false, that target is
      unaffected. The defect is that private/default history is allowed to determine
      new team state at all.
    * The explicit true default is not itself a defect during ordinary cache init; that
      behavior came from the alert-throttling design. The defect is failing to perform
      the special FALSE initialization required by leader migration.


CITY / POINTER LIFECYCLE PASS -- INTERIM NEGATIVE CONTROLS
-----------------------------------------------------------
* cacheCitiesAfterRead is called only after all CvPlayer/CvCity objects have been read,
  and each serialized UWAICache::City then resolves its plot index back to the plot's
  current CvCity. No ordinary pre-city-load dereference was found.
* City destruction removes the UWAICache entry after CvPlot::setPlotCity(NULL), but the
  CvCity object itself is still alive at that point. remove() dereferences its cached
  CvCity pointer only for owner metadata, then erases/deletes the cache object before
  the CvCity is destroyed; no dangling-pointer use was established there.
* Acquisition creates a new city object after the old city has gone through the kill /
  reportCityDestroyed path, and then notifies all major AI caches through
  reportCityCreated. This is consistent with the source comment that ownership changes
  are represented as destruction + creation and avoids an in-place owner mutation in
  the cached City object.
* m_aiReachableCities intentionally does not increment same-team member cities in add();
  current numReachableCities consumers are target/enemy reachability logic, so no
  teammate-count consumer has yet been established. Keep this as a negative control
  unless a same-team caller appears later.

F216 / provisional KI#539
-------------------------
TITLE
    Permanent Alliance cache merge iterates the already-merged live team and applies
    the absorbed leader's history back onto absorbed members; the absorbed leader
    self-adds and doubles its own past-war score.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED INHERITED ADVCIV/UWAI REGRESSION. Current in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
    AdvCiv-SAS. Introduced by the AgentIterator conversion in practical AdvCiv commit
    1818 (854cb8058c, "Use AgentIterators in all UWAI classes"), which changed the
    membership source at exactly the point where CvTeam::addTeam has already reassigned
    the absorbed players to the surviving team.

ROOT
    CvTeam::addTeam saves the absorbed team's old leader id, then reassigns every player
    on the absorbed team to the surviving team:

        PlayerTypes eTeamLeader = GET_TEAM(eTeam).getLeaderID();
        for (int i = 0; i < MAX_PLAYERS; i++)
        {
            if (GET_PLAYER((PlayerTypes)i).getTeam() == eTeam)
                GET_PLAYER((PlayerTypes)i).setTeam(getID());
        }
        updateLeaderID();

    Only much later, after those player-team identities have changed, the UWAI merge is
    invoked:

        if (getUWAI().isEnabled())
            AI().uwai().addTeam(eTeamLeader);

    UWAI::Team::addTeam then uses the CURRENT team membership:

        for (MemberAIIter it(m_eAgent); it.hasNext(); ++it)
            it->uwai().getCache().addTeam(eOtherLeader);

    and UWAICache::addTeam obtains the absorbed leader's cache and adds its stored
    history into the recipient cache:

        UWAICache& kOther = GET_PLAYER(eOtherLeader).uwai().getCache();
        ...
        m_aiPastWarScore.add(eTeam, kOther.m_aiPastWarScore.get(eTeam));

    Because the former absorbed leader is now itself a MemberAIIter member of m_eAgent,
    one loop iteration has

        &it->uwai().getCache() == &kOther

    and consequently performs, for every iterated target team,

        ownPastWarScore += ownPastWarScore;

    All other absorbed-team members are likewise treated as if they had belonged to the
    original surviving team and receive the absorbed leader's history, even though that
    was not the pre-regression membership boundary.

CONCRETE GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCE
    m_aiPastWarScore is live decision state, not archival statistics. It feeds:

        UWAICache::pastWarScore
          -> UWAI::Player::confidenceFromPastWars
          -> UWAI::Player::warConfidenceLearned
          -> InvasionGraph attack/defense confidence

    confidenceFromPastWars converts the score through a square-root confidence term.
    For example, an absorbed leader with pastWarScore -100 against a rival has roughly
    85% past-war confidence from this component. The self-add changes the stored score
    to -200 and lowers that component to about 79%. Positive history is amplified in the
    same way. Larger accumulated scores can create still larger changes until the
    function's final confidence clamp applies.

    Therefore a Permanent Alliance can instantaneously rewrite the absorbed leader's
    learned military confidence merely because its player object changed teams. The
    same cache also merges sponsored-war bounty/sponsor state; the post-1818 live-team
    loop can apply absorbed-leader data to absorbed teammates that the original merge
    loop did not visit. The past-war self-double is the simplest deterministic proof and
    is sufficient for the root.

ANCESTRY / REGRESSION PROOF
    The old and new implementations make the accidental membership expansion unusually
    clear.

    * The initial WarAndPeace/UWAI implementation used a Team::members vector. Its
      Team::addTeam loop was:

          for (size_t i = 0; i < members.size(); i++)
              GET_PLAYER(members[i]).warAndPeaceAI().getCache().addTeam(otherLeaderId);

      CvTeam::addTeam invoked this merge and only AFTERWARD called the global UWAI
      update. Thus, at the merge call, Team::members still described the surviving
      team's PRE-MERGE members. The absorbed leader was not visited and could not
      self-add.

    * Practical AdvCiv commit 1818 (854cb8058c), titled
      "Use AgentIterators in all UWAI classes", replaced that cached-vector loop with:

          for (MemberIter it(agentId); it.hasNext(); ++it)
              it->warAndPeaceAI().getCache().addTeam(otherLeaderId);

      In the same conversion series, the old post-addTeam global UWAI refresh was
      removed because AgentIterators made cached membership unnecessary.

    * But CvTeam::addTeam already changes each absorbed player's CvPlayer::team before
      calling UWAI::Team::addTeam. The new live iterator therefore sees the merged
      membership, not the old surviving-team membership that the replaced vector had
      represented at this call site.

    * Later UWAI renames/revisions retain the dynamic MemberIter/MemberAIIter loop and
      the current bug survives unchanged in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS.

    This is therefore not an ambiguous choice about how alliance history ought to be
    blended. The AgentIterator refactor changed the actual recipient set and introduced
    a self-add that the immediately preceding implementation could not perform.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
    Restore the original PRE-MERGE recipient boundary. Do not merely special-case
    eOtherLeader: a multi-member absorbed team would still have its other absorbed
    members incorrectly visited by the live post-merge iterator.

    The cleanest structural repair is to perform the UWAI cache merge while the
    surviving team's membership still has its pre-merge identity (before the absorbed
    players' setTeam loop), or otherwise explicitly preserve/pass the original survivor
    member set to UWAI::Team::addTeam. UWAICache::addTeam itself can then retain its
    existing per-recipient merge logic.

    If moving the call earlier, re-check the now-soon-to-disappear absorbed-team key in
    the TeamIter<MAJOR_CIV> loop; the essential invariant is that only ORIGINAL survivor
    members receive eOtherLeader's cache contribution. Avoid a repair based solely on
    current MemberAIIter membership after setTeam, because the information about which
    players belonged to which side has already been erased.

    Do not 'fix' this by clearing or averaging all past-war scores on a Permanent
    Alliance. reportWarEnding explicitly treats past-war interpretation as player-level
    state; F216 is about applying the other leader's contribution to the wrong recipient
    set, not about redesigning that heuristic.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SCOPE
    * Original surviving-team members are legitimate recipients of the absorbed
      leader's cache contribution; their addTeam call is not the defect.
    * The absorbed leader's self-add is deterministic whenever a relevant nonzero
      m_aiPastWarScore exists. No save/load timing, RNG or UI action is required.
    * F215/KI#538 is a distinct Permanent-Alliance/leader-change root: F215 concerns
      failure to false-initialize team-level CanBeHired when the authoritative leader
      cache changes. F216 concerns the recipient set used when merging per-player
      history/sponsorship caches.


UNIT REPORTING / CONVERSION TIMING -- REJECTED F216 CANDIDATE
--------------------------------------------------------------
The earlier apparent temporary double count during CvUnit::convert does not justify a
separate root:

* initUnit reports the replacement unit immediately and convert ends by kill(true) on
  the source, so there is indeed a short staging interval before the old unit's
  reportUnitDestroyed callback.
* Human COMMAND_UPGRADE and COMMAND_GIFT both return through CvUnit::doCommand, which
  immediately calls getGroup()->doDelayedDeath().
* The normal AI upgrade path explicitly calls doDelayedDeath immediately after upgrade.
* AI_doSplit can call gift() directly, but this occurs inside AI_doTurnUnitsPre; after it
  returns, CvPlayer::doTurnUnits immediately performs doDelayedDeath on every group
  before normal group turns. No intervening UWAI cache consumer was found in that path.
* CyUnit::convert exposes raw conversion to Python, but current SAS source contains no
  Python caller of that wrapper. Do not promote a hypothetical external-mod misuse as a
  current SAS/AdvCiv cache bug.

Thus the +1-before--1 interval is supported delayed-death staging on live current paths,
not F216. F216 is the independent Permanent Alliance history merge regression above.

F217 / provisional KI#540
-------------------------
TITLE
    UWAICache identifies Fallout as the first feature with <= -50 health; SAS Jungle is
    now first and also -50, so UWAI believes Fallout can be scrubbed at Metal Casting
    instead of Environmentalism and understates nuclear-war damage.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED SAS CROSS-LAYER REGRESSION exposing a brittle inherited AdvCiv/UWAI data
    assumption. Base BtS/AdvCiv 1.14 data satisfy the old uniqueness assumption because
    FEATURE_FALLOUT is the only feature at <= -50 health. Current SAS no longer does.

ROOT
    UWAICache::updateCanScrub does not identify Fallout by type. It searches FeatureTypes
    in enum/XML order and caches the first sufficiently unhealthy feature:

        static FeatureTypes eFallout = NO_FEATURE;
        if (eFallout == NO_FEATURE)
        {
            FOR_EACH_ENUM(Feature)
            {
                if (GC.getInfo(eLoopFeature).getHealthPercent() <= -50)
                {
                    eFallout = eLoopFeature;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }

    It then asks whether the owner knows any BuildInfo feature-removal tech for that
    selected feature:

        TechTypes eFeatureTech = GC.getInfo(eLoopBuild).getFeatureTech(eFallout);
        if (eFeatureTech != NO_TECH && GET_TEAM(m_eOwner).isHasTech(eFeatureTech))
            m_bCanScrub = true;

    In current SAS CIV4FeatureInfos.xml the relevant order/health values are:

        0 FEATURE_ICE           0
        1 FEATURE_JUNGLE      -50
        2 FEATURE_OASIS         0
        3 FEATURE_FLOOD_PLAINS -50
        4 FEATURE_FOREST       +50
        5 FEATURE_FALLOUT      -75

    Thus the static variable named eFallout is actually initialized to FEATURE_JUNGLE
    on its first call and remains that value for the process lifetime.

CURRENT SAS DATA PROOF
    CIV4BuildInfos.xml gives Jungle-removal FeatureTech TECH_METAL_CASTING on the normal
    improvement builds and BUILD_REMOVE_JUNGLE. Real FEATURE_FALLOUT removal uses
    TECH_ENVIRONMENTALISM, including BUILD_SCRUB_FALLOUT and the improvement builds.

    Therefore once the player knows Metal Casting, updateCanScrub sets:

        m_bCanScrub = true

    despite the player still lacking Environmentalism and being mechanically unable to
    scrub Fallout. The cache is cleared/recomputed each update, but the same wrong
    FeatureTypes singleton is selected each time, so the error persists from Metal
    Casting until real Fallout cleanup finally becomes available.

GAMEPLAY / UWAI CONSEQUENCE
    canScrubFallout is consumed by nuclear-war utility code, not just UI.

    WarUtilityAspect::lossesFromNukes adjusts the expected asset loss per nuclear hit:

        rHits * (kVictimCache.canScrubFallout() ?
                 rLossRate - 0.05 : rLossRate + 0.05) * rScorePerCity

    With the false TRUE state, a non-agent victim uses roughly 0.30 instead of 0.40 from
    the normal 0.35 baseline (25% lower damage estimate), while the agent/victim case
    uses roughly 0.40 instead of 0.50 from the 0.45 baseline (20% lower).

    The peaceful-victory nuclear penalty similarly uses 0.35 population-loss weighting
    when canScrubFallout is true versus 0.45 when false. Thus Metal Casting can make
    UWAI materially less pessimistic about nuclear damage many eras before the actual
    Fallout-removal tech.

ANCESTRY / DATA-CONTRACT PROOF
    The helper dates to the initial 2017 WarAndPeace/UWAI integration, practical AdvCiv
    1253 (f6ff6a182f). Its original code used the same <= -50 search and even documented
    the assumption through the assertion message:

        "Fallout feature not found; should have -50 health"

    Under Base BtS and Base AdvCiv 1.14 XML this happened to be unambiguous:

        FEATURE_FALLOUT  -50

    is the only feature at or below -50. Jungle is -25 and Flood Plains is above the
    threshold. So this is not presented as a live Base AdvCiv defect under its own data.

    SAS practical commit 4876 (4622d268ac) changed FEATURE_JUNGLE health from -25 to
    -50 as part of the Jungle rebalance. Since Jungle precedes Fallout in FeatureTypes,
    that change immediately invalidated the inherited sentinel heuristic. SAS practical
    commit 4905 (6c08e62699) later also changed Flood Plains from -40 to -50 and Fallout
    from -50 to -75, further demonstrating that health magnitude is no longer a unique
    identifier. The bug is therefore a cross-layer integration failure between an
    inherited code assumption and legitimate SAS balance-data changes.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
    Identify the exact Fallout feature rather than inferring identity from health.
    Current SAS already uses the appropriate pattern elsewhere, e.g. CvUnitAI caches:

        static const FeatureTypes eFeatureFallout =
            (FeatureTypes)GC.getInfoTypeForString("FEATURE_FALLOUT");

    UWAICache::updateCanScrub should use the same exact FeatureTypes lookup (cached once)
    and then retain its existing scan for a known FeatureTech that removes that feature.
    An exact BUILD_SCRUB_FALLOUT lookup would also be possible, but the existing helper
    is intentionally asking whether ANY available build can remove Fallout, so exact
    feature identity preserves that broader contract better.

    Do not repair this by changing Jungle/Flood-Plains health back solely to protect the
    heuristic; those are independent SAS balance choices. Do not change the comparison
    from <= -50 to a different magic threshold either: Fallout identity should not depend
    on unrelated feature balance values.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SCOPE
    * Base AdvCiv 1.14 and the supplied Civ4CE/BtS data have only FEATURE_FALLOUT at
      <= -50, so their current data do not trigger F217 even though they carry the brittle
      helper.
    * The error does not grant Workers a mechanically legal Fallout-removal action.
      Worker/build legality still uses actual BuildInfo prerequisites. F217 changes UWAI
      strategic valuation because the cache reports a false capability.
    * F214/KI#537 is unrelated despite also involving capability caching: F214 is stale
      MilitaryBranch typical-unit state after capability is LOST; F217 freshly
      recomputes the wrong capability from a misidentified feature each turn.

CHECKPOINT C019-WIP06 -- FILE 019 OPEN / QUEUE 031 UWAICache.cpp
===============================================================================
Date: 2026-08-27
Model: GPT-5.6-Sol
Authoritative source snapshot:
    AdvCiv-SAS_light_source_20260827T134157.zip

F218 / provisional KI#541
-------------------------
TITLE
    UWAICache::updateTransports uses player-level canTrain, which ignores city/resource
    prerequisites; SAS obsoletes every resource-free assault transport by Combustion, so
    an Oil-less civ is cached as able to train ocean transports although no city can,
    producing false overseas reachability and defeating the SAS no-lift war-target gate.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED SAS CROSS-LAYER REGRESSION exposing an inherited UWAI cache assumption.
    The player-level capability test dates to the initial 2017 WarAndPeace/UWAI cache.
    Base AdvCiv's standard unit progression masks the clean resource-loss reproduction
    because its resource-free Galleon never becomes mechanically obsolete; current SAS's
    explicit ObsoleteTech chain removes that fallback.

ROOT
    UWAICache::updateTransports runs before city-distance caching and currently does:

        CvPlayerAI const& kOwner = GET_PLAYER(m_eOwner);
        CvCivilization const& kOwnerCiv = kOwner.getCivilization();
        for (int i = 0; i < kOwnerCiv.getNumUnits(); i++)
        {
            UnitTypes const eUnit = kOwnerCiv.unitAt(i);
            CvUnitInfo const& kUnit = GC.getInfo(eUnit);
            if (kUnit.getUnitAIType(UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA) && kOwner.canTrain(eUnit))
            {
                m_bHaveAnyTransports = true;
                if (!kOwner.AI_isAnyImpassable(eUnit))
                    m_bHaveDeepSeaTransports = true;
            }
        }

    The public accessors are explicitly named canTrainAnyCargo and
    canTrainDeepSeaCargo. However CvPlayer::canTrain is only the player/global layer. It
    checks the civilization's unit mapping, technology requirements (including SAS
    ObsoleteTech), state religion, and global/team/player class limits. It does NOT
    inspect a city's plot-group resources or whether any city is geographically able to
    train a sea unit.

    Actual city trainability is stricter:

        CvCity::canTrain(...)
            -> GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).canTrain(...)
            -> getPlot().canTrain(...)

    and CvPlot::canTrain explicitly checks both the AND resource and every
    PrereqOrBonus against pCity->hasBonus(...), rejecting the unit if its required bonus
    is unavailable. It also enforces city/sea placement constraints. Thus
    CvPlayer::canTrain(eUnit) == true is not evidence that ANY owned city can actually
    train eUnit.

CURRENT SAS DATA PROOF
    Current SAS has exactly three UnitInfo entries carrying UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA:

        UNIT_GALLEY
            PrereqTech   TECH_SAILING
            ObsoleteTech TECH_ASTRONOMY
            bonuses      none

        UNIT_GALLEON
            PrereqTech   TECH_ASTRONOMY
            ObsoleteTech TECH_COMBUSTION
            bonuses      none

        UNIT_TRANSPORT
            PrereqTech   TECH_COMBUSTION
            ObsoleteTech NONE
            PrereqOrBonus BONUS_OIL (the only non-NONE entry)
            impassable terrain/features: none

    Therefore take an ordinary coastal civilization that has learned Combustion, owns
    no Oil, and has no already-built lift that should be considered under a separate
    operational-capacity policy:

        * UNIT_GALLEY fails CvPlayer::canTrain because Astronomy is already known and
          SAS marks it obsolete there.
        * UNIT_GALLEON fails CvPlayer::canTrain because Combustion is known and SAS
          marks it obsolete there.
        * UNIT_TRANSPORT PASSES CvPlayer::canTrain because the player-level function
          sees Combustion and no obsolete-tech/global-limit failure.
        * UNIT_TRANSPORT FAILS every CvCity::canTrain in an Oil-less empire because
          CvPlot::canTrain sees its sole PrereqOrBonus BONUS_OIL and requires a city
          with that connected bonus.

    updateTransports nevertheless sets both:

        m_bHaveAnyTransports = true;
        m_bHaveDeepSeaTransports = true;

    because Transport has no impassable terrain. The cache has therefore asserted an
    immediate training capability that no city possesses.

GAMEPLAY / UWAI CONSEQUENCE
    This state is consumed before and during war evaluation, not only exposed through a
    diagnostic getter.

    1. UWAICache::City::updateDistance reads both cargo booleans. When
       bAnyTransports is true and one of the cache owner's cities is coastal, it is
       allowed to search a naval route to a target. Because the false Transport state
       also sets bDeepSeaTransports, it uses the ANY_WATER pathfinder rather than the
       shallow-water finder. A successful route can set bReachBySea and contribute a
       finite m_iDistance. Thus a target that would otherwise have no supported sea
       route can be cached as reachable solely because the Oil requirement was skipped.

    2. UWAI::Team::isLandTarget and InvasionGraph::Node::canReachByLand consume
       canTrainDeepSeaCargo when deciding whether long land routes may instead be
       treated as naval/overseas problems. The false flag can therefore alter scenario
       classification and invasion reachability assumptions.

    3. Current SAS WarUtilityAspect::Risk::preEvaluate uses
       canTrainAnyCargo explicitly as its pre-war naval lift gate. For each team member
       it records a cargo-qualified contact distance only when:

           bool const bMemberCanTrainCargo = kMemberCache.canTrainAnyCargo();

       and later defines bNoLift from whether any such route exists. Because the same
       false transport flag can already have made an overseas city reachable in the
       cache, an Oil-less post-Combustion coastal civ can satisfy both the route and
       cargo-building parts of this test. The hard reject intended for a naval target
       with no trainable lift can therefore be bypassed.

    A concrete reproduction does not require loss of an existing transport: a civ can
    simply research/acquire Combustion while lacking Oil and have no pre-built
    Galleons. At that instant the SAS ObsoleteTech transition removes its last
    resource-free trainable assault transport, while updateTransports still reports the
    Oil-gated Transport as trainable.

ANCESTRY / ACTIVATION BOUNDARY
    The underlying player-level assumption is old. Initial practical AdvCiv commit 1253
    (f6ff6a182f, "Initial commit (cont.)") introduced WarAndPeaceCache::updateTrainCargo
    with the same essential test:

        if(info.getUnitAIType(UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA) && owner.canTrain(ut))
            trainAnyCargo = true;

    Later UWAI revisions renamed/restructured this as updateTransports but retained
    CvPlayer::canTrain. Practical AdvCiv 2920 (4ae382e5db, "Revised all code in the
    UWAI component") shows that direct continuity.

    Base AdvCiv 1.14 also gives UNIT_TRANSPORT an Oil PrereqOrBonus, but its Galley and
    Galleon have no ObsoleteTech mechanism/tag and remain player/city-trainable once
    unlocked. Hence an Oil-less post-Combustion standard Base-AdvCiv civ can still
    genuinely train the resource-free Galleon, so this exact all-transports-untrainable
    resource reproduction is masked under base data.

    SAS practical commit 5321 (6bd3873c83) changed the naval progression so Galley
    obsoletes at Astronomy and Galleon (including the then-current Carrack replacement)
    obsoletes at Combustion. Current SAS later removed that Carrack replacement, leaving
    exactly the three assault-sea UnitInfos listed above. This makes the inherited
    distinction between player-level and city-level trainability gameplay-live for an
    ordinary civ as soon as Combustion is known without Oil.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
    If the cached contract remains "can train cargo," require at least one actual owned
    city for which CvCity::canTrain(eUnit) succeeds before setting either transport
    capability bit. updateTransports already runs before cached-city reconstruction, so
    it can iterate the owner's real CvCity list directly; it does not need a UWAICache
    City object. There are only a few assault-sea candidates and the scan can stop on the
    first qualifying city/unit, so the extra legality checks are bounded.

    This is preferable to hand-checking only Oil or player-global bonus counts: city
    trainability also captures disconnected plot-group resources, coast/sea placement,
    civilization-specific replacements and other local prerequisites. It restores the
    meaning promised by canTrainAnyCargo/canTrainDeepSeaCargo instead of adding another
    partial approximation.

    Do NOT automatically fold already-owned obsolete transports into this narrow repair.
    Existing operational lift is a legitimate separate design question because some
    callers may care about what the player can use now rather than what it can produce.
    The inherited cache and SAS contact-gate variable are explicitly framed as TRAINING
    capability, and broadening them to "can train or already owns" would change that
    contract. Review that policy independently if desired rather than using it to leave
    the proven false canTrain result in place.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SCOPE
    * The fault is not CvCity/CvPlot resource legality; those functions correctly reject
      an Oil-less Transport. The incorrect abstraction boundary is UWAICache using only
      CvPlayer::canTrain to answer an any-city training question.
    * Existing Base AdvCiv still has a coarse player-level transport capability helper,
      including questions such as landlocked empires. F218 does not claim every such
      approximation is newly caused by SAS. Its concrete current-SAS root is the
      resource-gated-only post-Combustion transport chain and the resulting false
      training/reachability state.
    * A civ that currently has a city with Oil and can actually train Transport is not a
      reproduction; city-level and player-level capability agree there.
    * A pre-Combustion civ that can still train the resource-free Galleon is likewise
      not the clean F218 reproduction even without Oil.
    * F214/KI#537 is distinct: F214 preserves a stale MilitaryBranch unit after a valid
      capability is lost. F218 freshly recomputes TRUE every turn from an insufficient
      player-level legality test.
    * F217/KI#540 is also distinct: F217 misidentifies an XML feature by health/order;
      F218 identifies the right unit but asks the wrong layer of the training API.

F219 / provisional KI#542
-------------------------
TITLE
    UWAICache::goldPerProdVictory checks peaceful-victory stage 3 before stage 4
    even though the victory-stage hash is cumulative, making both stage-4 branches
    unreachable and feeding systematically wrong production opportunity costs into
    UWAI war evaluation.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv/UWAI logic bug. The reversed stage test is present in
    the initial 2017 WarAndPeace cache implementation and survives current SAS.

ROOT
    Current UWAICache::goldPerProdVictory determines the cache owner's peaceful-victory
    stage as follows:

        int iOwnerVictoryStage = 0;
        if (kOwnerTeam.AI_anyMemberAtVictoryStage(
                AI_VICTORY_CULTURE3 | AI_VICTORY_SPACE3))
            iOwnerVictoryStage = 3;
        else if (kOwnerTeam.AI_anyMemberAtVictoryStage(
                AI_VICTORY_CULTURE4 | AI_VICTORY_SPACE4))
            iOwnerVictoryStage = 4;

    The rival loop repeats the same ordering:

        int iRivalVictoryStage = 0;
        if (itRival->AI_anyMemberAtVictoryStage3())
            iRivalVictoryStage = 3;
        else if (itRival->AI_anyMemberAtVictoryStage4())
            iRivalVictoryStage = 4;

    However CvPlayerAI::AI_updateVictoryStageHash constructs each victory strategy
    cumulatively. For Space, for example, a stage-4 result first executes:

        m_eVictoryStageHash |= AI_VICTORY_SPACE3;

    and only inside that stage-3 block then executes:

        m_eVictoryStageHash |= AI_VICTORY_SPACE4;

    Culture is constructed the same way. CvPlayerAI::AI_atVictoryStage simply tests
    whether any requested bit is present, and CvTeamAI::AI_anyMemberAtVictoryStage3/4
    delegate to those player tests. Therefore a Space4/Culture4 player or team is also
    necessarily Space3/Culture3 for these predicates.

    The first branch is thus TRUE whenever the second branch could be TRUE. Both
    `else if (...stage4...)` branches in goldPerProdVictory are unreachable for valid
    current stage-4 states.

GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCE
    goldPerProdVictory is one lower-level component of m_rGoldPerProduction, exposed as
    goldValueOfProduction(). WarUtilityAspect::Effort reads that value directly when
    converting projected production/unit losses and wartime opportunity cost into UWAI
    utility. The function intentionally raises the value of production for peaceful
    victory pursuit and lowers it when rivals are as close or closer to victory:

        scaled r = iOwnerVictoryStage + 1;
        ...
        if (iRivalVictoryStage >= iOwnerVictoryStage)
            r--;
        if (iRivalVictoryStage > iOwnerVictoryStage)
            r--;

    Misclassifying stage 4 as stage 3 therefore changes real war evaluation.

    Clean examples:

    * Owner at peaceful stage 4, no stage-3/4 rival:
          intended base = 5
          current base  = 4
      Production is undervalued despite the owner being at the most urgent peaceful
      victory stage, making diversion into war cheaper than intended.

    * Owner at peaceful stage 4, rival at stage 3:
          intended: owner 4 vs rival 3 => 5 (rival is behind; no deduction)
          current:  owner 3 vs rival 3 => 4 - 1 = 3
      The combination of demoting the owner and falsely treating the rival as tied can
      lower the victory-production valuation by two full points.

    * Owner at peaceful stage 3, rival at stage 4:
          intended: 4 - 1 (rival >= owner) - 1 (rival > owner) = 2
          current:  rival stage 4 is seen as stage 3, so result = 3
      The extra urgency adjustment for a rival who is strictly closer to victory is
      never applied.

    updateGoldPerProduction takes the maximum of this term and its other production-
    valuation terms, so another term can mask F219 in a particular position; the bug
    does not guarantee a changed final ratio every turn. But whenever the victory term
    is controlling or near-controlling, the erroneous stage classification feeds
    WarUtilityAspect::Effort and can alter war-plan utility.

ANCESTRY
    Initial practical AdvCiv/WarAndPeace commit 1253 (f6ff6a182f, "Initial commit
    (cont.)") introduced WarAndPeaceCache::goldPerProdVictory with the same ordering:

        if (... AI_VICTORY_CULTURE3 ... || ... AI_VICTORY_SPACE3 ...)
            ourVictLevel = 3;
        else if (... AI_VICTORY_CULTURE4 ... || ... AI_VICTORY_SPACE4 ...)
            ourVictLevel = 4;

    and likewise checked the rival's level-3 helper before its level-4 helper. Later
    WarAndPeace/UWAI refactors preserved that logic essentially verbatim. F219 is
    therefore inherited from the original UWAI cache design rather than introduced by
    SAS.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
    Test stage 4 before stage 3 in both places:

        if (... CULTURE4 | SPACE4 ...)
            iOwnerVictoryStage = 4;
        else if (... CULTURE3 | SPACE3 ...)
            iOwnerVictoryStage = 3;

    and:

        if (itRival->AI_anyMemberAtVictoryStage4())
            iRivalVictoryStage = 4;
        else if (itRival->AI_anyMemberAtVictoryStage3())
            iRivalVictoryStage = 3;

    No change to victory-stage construction is needed; cumulative lower-stage bits are
    widely intentional. The local consumer simply has to query from highest stage to
    lowest.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SCOPE
    * This is not the retracted F113/KI#436 PlayerTypes/GET_TEAM false positive;
      overloaded GET_TEAM(PlayerTypes) resolves through TEAMID correctly. F219 depends
      only on the order of cumulative stage predicates.
    * Military and Diplomacy victory stages are intentionally not used for the owner's
      peaceful-production premium. The bug is specifically the unreachable stage-4
      classification within the peaceful Space/Culture logic and the generic rival
      stage comparison used by that same helper.
    * Another gold/production heuristic may dominate the final max in
      updateGoldPerProduction, so F219 is an input correctness defect rather than a
      claim that every stage-4 turn necessarily changes the final war utility.

C019-WIP08 CONTINUATION -- THREAT CACHE FRESHNESS REJECTION + TEAM NUKE SCOPE
===============================================================================
STATUS: WIP / append-only continuation of authoritative C019-WIP07.
COMPLETED FIRST-PASS FILES: 18 / 169.
CURRENT FILE: queue 031 CvGameCoreDLL/UWAICache.cpp OPEN.
NO REPOSITORY SOURCE FILES MODIFIED.

CROSS-PLAYER THREAT-REACHABILITY FRESHNESS -- NOT PROMOTED
----------------------------------------------------------
The unfinished WIP07 question about calculateThreatRating reading the rival player's
cached City::canReach state does not presently cross the finding bar.

Current turn orchestration intentionally refreshes each team's UWAI member caches at
that team's turn start:

    CvTeamAI::AI_doTurnPre()
      -> UWAI::Team::turnPre()
      -> each UWAI::Player::turnPre()
      -> UWAICache::update()

and CvPlayer city creation/acquisition/destruction additionally broadcasts incremental
city-cache maintenance to all major players. In a sequential-turn game, a rival cache
can therefore be one refresh behind changes made after that rival's own turn-start
cache build (for example, end-of-turn research that changes naval reachability), but
that is part of the broader per-turn cache staging model rather than a unique broken
invariant in calculateThreatRating.

There is historical evidence that the authors were conscious of genuinely unsafe
cross-cache startup state: practical commit 2751 added bPlayerHistAvailable specifically
because other civs' caches can be unready at scenario/turn-0 startup. Separate special
paths also force cache updates when a new player's first city appears so higher-ID
rivals can evaluate it immediately. Those safeguards do not establish a requirement
that all foreign derived fields be transactionally recomputed after every mid-turn
tech/resource mutation.

A stale reachability bit could certainly make long-term threat react one opposing turn
later in some player-order situations, but I have not proved a stronger contract or a
persistent/order-dependent state corruption analogous to F213-F219. Treat this as an
accepted cache-latency limitation unless a concrete gameplay trace later proves that a
consumer requires same-slice foreign reachability freshness.

F220 / provisional KI#543 -- CONFIRMED
UWAI LONG-TERM NUCLEAR DETERRENCE CHECKS ONLY THE CURRENT PLAYER EVEN THOUGH THE
THREAT AND ANY RESULTING WAR ARE TEAM/MASTER-SIDE OBJECTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TITLE
    UWAICache::teamThreat applies its nuclear deterrent only when m_eOwner personally
    owns a nuke. A teammate (or master-side partner) can possess the retaliation
    capability that necessarily participates in any team war, yet the owner's threat
    cache ignores it and overstates the rival's long-term threat.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv/UWAI team-scope defect. The per-player nuke test is
    present from the initial 2017 WarAndPeace cache implementation and survives Base
    AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS.

ROOT CONTRACT
    calculateThreatRating(PlayerTypes eRival) is player-indexed only for the rival
    reachability gate. Its substantive threat value is then:

        return teamThreat(TEAMID(eRival));

    teamThreat itself is overwhelmingly team/master-side:

    * rival attitude is AI_getAttitude(eOwnerTeam);
    * rival victory pressure is queried through team-wide any-member stages;
    * rival long-term power is computed for the rival team/master side;
    * owner long-term power is computed from the OWNER TEAM'S MASTER TEAM, including
      allied/vassal-side military branches and defensive-pact support as applicable;
    * alternative targets are counted as teams;
    * the modeled future conflict can only be declared against the owner team, not an
      isolated member player.

    Yet the nuclear term alone switches ownership domain:

        // Nuclear deterrent
        if (GET_PLAYER(m_eOwner).getNumNukeUnits() > 0)
            rDiploFactor -= fixp(0.2);

    Thus the model asks whether the one cache-owning PLAYER has a nuke instead of
    whether the owner war side has nuclear retaliation capability.

DETERMINISTIC TEAM REPRODUCTION
    Consider a normal two-member team A+B and rival team R:

    * A owns zero nuclear units;
    * B owns at least one nuclear unit;
    * R otherwise has a positive teamThreat against TeamAB;
    * both A and B are alive normal teammates.

    Any war R declares on A is a war against TeamAB. B joins automatically and B's
    nukes are available against the common enemy. The deterrent therefore exists for
    the whole target team.

    Nevertheless:

        A.uwai().cache.teamThreat(R)

    receives NO -0.2 nuclear deterrent because A personally has zero nukes, while:

        B.uwai().cache.teamThreat(R)

    receives the deterrent solely because B happens to own the units.

    The probability proxy for one indivisible team war therefore changes according to
    which teammate's cache happens to represent the same team-side future conflict.

LIVE CONSUMER / WHY LATER AGGREGATION DOES NOT REPAIR IT
    threatRating feeds WarUtilityAspect::PreEmptiveWar. WarEvaluator explicitly
    evaluates the aspect once for every alive member of the agent team, binding
    ourCache() to that member's UWAICache each time.

    The recent F137/KI#460 repair correctly consumes each RIVAL TEAM'S common threat
    forecast only once per agent member, taking the maximum threatRating over that
    rival team's members. It does not and cannot repair F220's OWNER-SIDE mismatch:
    the A pass and B pass still begin from different teamThreat values solely because
    one teammate owns the team's nukes.

    PreEmptiveWar then compares team-wide current/predicted city sides and converts the
    threat into actual war utility. The per-player nuke omission can therefore raise
    the pre-emptive-war pressure contributed by a teammate whose partner supplies the
    real retaliation capability.

ENGINE NEGATIVE CONTROL / INTENDED DOMAIN EVIDENCE
    Civ4/AdvCiv already exposes exactly the team-level nuclear capability primitive:

        int CvTeam::getNumNukeUnits() const

    which sums nuclear units across the team's members and its vassals. Other
    team-war/diplomacy code uses that team-level API for nuclear deterrence; e.g.
    CvTeamAI::AI_declareWarTrade checks:

        if (GET_TEAM(eTarget).getNumNukeUnits() > 0)
            return DENIAL_POWER_THEM;

    i.e. "don't want to get nuked" is correctly a property of the target team, not of
    a singled-out target player. This is a strong negative control for teamThreat's
    otherwise isolated player-level check.

ANCESTRY
    Initial practical AdvCiv/WarAndPeace commit 1253 (f6ff6a182f, "Initial commit
    (cont.)") introduced the long-term threat calculation with the same structure and
    the same line:

        // Nuclear deterrent
        if(GET_PLAYER(ownerId).getNumNukeUnits() > 0)
            diploFactor -= 0.2;

    Later UWAI refactors renamed the owner field and converted doubles to scaled, but
    retained the player-owned nuclear test verbatim in substance. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
    current SAS remain the same here. F220 is therefore inherited from the feature's
    original ownership model rather than introduced by SAS.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
    The deterrent should use the same owner-side scope as the future war/power model.
    At minimum, ordinary teammate nuclear capability must count. Because teamThreat's
    owner power is based on the owner's master side, the most internally consistent
    repair should deliberately decide whether master/vassal nuclear capability belongs
    in the deterrent as well, rather than merely replacing GET_PLAYER(m_eOwner) with an
    arbitrary teammate.

    CvTeam::getNumNukeUnits() already aggregates team members and vassals. If the
    intended scope is the full master side used by longTermPower, prefer querying the
    owner's master team through that API. If design intent is deliberately narrower,
    at least query the owner team so normal teammate nukes cannot disappear.

    Do NOT alter the rival-player reachability gate as part of F220; that is the
    separate cache-staging/modeling question rejected above.

RELATION TO EXISTING ROOTS
    * F137/KI#460 was a rival-side multiplicity defect: the same rival-team threat was
      exposed through several rival PlayerTypes and consumed repeatedly. Its repair
      deduplicates the rival team per agent member. F220 instead says the supposedly
      team-owned threat value itself changes with WHICH OWNER MEMBER'S cache computes
      it. The fixes are independent.
    * F134/KI#457 found another team-war capability modeled with current-player army
      power inside IllWill. That supports the ownership principle but is a different
      consumer and quantity; fixing revenge capability there does not change
      UWAICache::teamThreat's nuclear deterrent.
    * The cross-player reachability freshness question above remains unpromoted; F220
      does not depend on cache age. A fully current cache still produces the wrong
      deterrent for teammate-owned nukes.

C019-WIP09 CONTINUATION -- TARGET-MISSION CARGO MULTIPLICITY + SIBLING CENSUS
===============================================================================
STATUS: WIP / append-only continuation of authoritative C019-WIP08.
COMPLETED FIRST-PASS FILES: 18 / 169.
CURRENT FILE: queue 031 CvGameCoreDLL/UWAICache.cpp OPEN.
NO REPOSITORY SOURCE FILES MODIFIED.

F221 / provisional KI#544 -- CONFIRMED
TARGET-MISSION CENSUSES COUNT BOARDED LAND CARGO TWICE BECAUSE TRANSPORT CARGO
AND THE PERSISTENT BOARDED CARGO SELECTION GROUPS ARE BOTH ENUMERATED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TITLE
    UWAICache::updateTargetMissionCount adds both a group's own units and its cargo,
    but K-Mod deliberately keeps loaded land units in their own selection groups.
    Those boarded groups remain enumerable and follow the transport plot. In enemy
    territory the same physical cargo can therefore contribute once through the
    transport's getCargo() count and again through its own boarded group.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited BBAI/K-Mod representation mismatch, copied into AdvCiv UWAI.
    The current SAS cache reproduces the same multiplicity. The ancestral
    CvPlayerAI::AI_enemyTargetMissions census has the same root and must be reviewed
    together with the cache repair.

CURRENT CACHE CENSUS
    UWAICache::updateTargetMissionCount(PlayerTypes ePlayer) iterates every owner
    selection group and, when the group's MissionAI plot or fallback current plot is
    owned by ePlayer, counts:

        iMissions += pGroup->getNumUnits();
        iMissions += pGroup->getCargo();

    The helper explicitly says it is based on CvPlayerAI::AI_enemyTargetMissions.

BOARDED CARGO REMAINS A SEPARATE ENUMERATED GROUP
    FOR_EACH_GROUPAI is a raw traversal of CvPlayerAI::AI_firstSelectionGroup /
    AI_nextSelectionGroup. It has no activity-type filter. ACTIVITY_BOARDED groups
    therefore remain in this census.

    K-Mod loading clears the cargo group's executable mission queue but deliberately
    leaves the unit/group object alive and sets:

        getGroup()->setActivityType(ACTIVITY_BOARDED);

    The cargo is not merged into the transport selection group.

BOARDED GROUP FOLLOWS THE TRANSPORT PLOT
    CvUnit::setXY contains K-Mod cargo-preservation logic. When a transport moves, it
    finds units whose getTransportUnit() is that transport and recursively calls:

        pLoopUnit->setXY(iX, iY, bGroup, false);

    while retaining their cargo group IDs. Thus a boarded land group's plot() really
    follows the transport's current tile.

MISSIONAI IS NOT REQUIRED FOR THE DUPLICATE
    updateTargetMissionCount deliberately falls back to the group's current plot:

        pMissionPlot = pGroup->AI_getMissionAIPlot();
        if (pMissionPlot == NULL)
            pMissionPlot = pGroup->plot();

    Consequently the duplicate does not depend on stale MissionAI state surviving
    loading. If an invasion fleet ends its turn loaded on an enemy-owned coastal tile,
    both the transport group and the boarded cargo groups can satisfy the same owner
    test through their current plot alone.

CACHE-UPDATE TIMING MAKES THE STATE OBSERVABLE
    UWAI refresh runs from CvTeamAI::AI_doTurnPre -> UWAI::Team::turnPre ->
    UWAI::Player::turnPre -> UWAICache::update, before that turn's unit movement.
    Therefore a fleet that ended the preceding turn loaded in enemy coastal water is
    sampled exactly while:

      * the transport group still reports its loaded units through getCargo();
      * each boarded land unit still belongs to its own enumerable selection group;
      * those boarded groups are at the transport's enemy-owned plot.

DETERMINISTIC MINIMAL REPRODUCTION
    Consider one assault transport carrying two land units, all ending the previous
    turn on a tile owned by enemy player E.

    The transport selection group contributes:

        getNumUnits() = 1
        getCargo()    = 2
        ----------------
                        3

    The two physical land units still exist in boarded cargo group(s). Through the
    current-plot fallback those group(s) contribute the same two land units again.

        nonduplicated physical census = 3
        current cached census         = 5

    The exact group partition of the two cargo units does not matter: whether they are
    together or in separate boarded groups, their aggregate second contribution is 2.

LIVE BEHAVIORAL THRESHOLD
    InvasionGraph::Node::findTarget consumes UWAICache::targetMissionCount and begins
    with:

        int iMaxMissions = 3;

    A mission-derived target is considered only when:

        iMissions > iMaxMissions

    Therefore the ordinary one-transport/two-cargo example crosses a real branch:

        intended/nonduplicated 3 -> no mission-determined target
        current duplicated      5 -> target may be determined from unit missions

    This can change which current war opponent UWAI assumes the army is committed to,
    and therefore changes the invasion simulation rather than merely a displayed or
    unused statistic.

ANCESTRAL SIBLING -- CvPlayerAI::AI_enemyTargetMissions
    The BBAI/K-Mod function that inspired the cache contains the same accounting:

        iCount += pLoopSelectionGroup->getNumUnits();
        iCount += pLoopSelectionGroup->getCargo();

    and traverses the same persistent selection groups with the same MissionAI/current
    plot fallback. K-Mod 1.46 retains this BBAI-era census while also retaining the
    later K-Mod cargo-group representation in which loaded units remain in their own
    groups. AdvCiv/SAS inherit both sides.

    Current AdvCiv/SAS live callers use AI_enemyTargetMissions for team-level war
    reasoning, including estimates of attackers/missions in enemy territory and the
    related peace/capitulation logic. Therefore repairing only UWAICache would leave
    the ancestral live census with the same multiplicity defect.

ROOT CONTRACT
    A target-mission census is an estimate of committed physical units. One physical
    unit must contribute at most once to a given target census. Current code violates
    that invariant specifically for transported land cargo by exposing one physical
    unit through two simultaneous representations:

      1. transport-side cargo count;
      2. boarded cargo selection-group unit count.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
    Do NOT simply delete getCargo() from the transport count. Cargo-side counting is
    useful when boarded land groups have no meaningful MissionAI target; the transport
    is often the only object carrying the invasion destination context.

    Instead choose exactly one representation for loaded units. A conservative family
    of repairs is:

      * count transport cargo through the transport group;
      * skip units/groups whose members are currently cargo when evaluating their own
        boarded group contribution, or otherwise subtract cargo already represented by
        its transport;
      * preserve ordinary non-cargo group counting and the MissionAI/current-plot
        fallback for untransported units.

    Apply the same physical-unit uniqueness rule to both
    UWAICache::updateTargetMissionCount and CvPlayerAI::AI_enemyTargetMissions so their
    intentionally overlapping semantics do not diverge.

    Be careful with mixed cargo groups: K-Mod's movement code can separate groups whose
    members are not all transported by the same transport. Prefer counting at a level
    that can distinguish actually loaded units rather than blindly dropping an entire
    group solely because its activity is ACTIVITY_BOARDED.

RELATION TO OTHER ROOTS
    * F211/KI#534 concerned empty transient groups reaching AI_isDeclareWar's debug
      precondition. updateTargetMissionCount explicitly skips zero-unit groups, so F221
      is independent and occurs with perfectly valid non-empty boarded groups.
    * The ordinary foreign-cache freshness question rejected before F220 is unrelated;
      F221 is reproducible even with a perfectly current cache.
    * This finding does not require stale MissionAI state. The current-plot fallback is
      sufficient, although retained MissionAI state can provide an additional route.

FOLLOW-UP REJECTION -- reportWarEnding POINTER EXCLUSIVITY
----------------------------------------------------------
The apparent if (pWeReceive) / else if (pWeGive) asymmetry in
UWAICache::reportWarEnding is not a defect. CvTeamAI::AI_preMakePeace deliberately
calls one side as (pReparations, NULL) and the opposing side as (NULL, pReparations).
The two lists are an intentionally mutually exclusive API representation of which side
received the peace concessions. Do not spend F222 on this local shape.

HISTORICAL CLOSURE PROGRESS
---------------------------
A mechanical history pass found 142 tracked AdvCiv/SAS commits whose diff actually
contains UWAICache.cpp or its former WarAndPeaceCache.cpp name. Reopened bugfix-shaped
hunks checked so far remain present in current code rather than exposing another root:

    1909  old UWAI city-cache out-of-bounds/hole handling
    2644  teammate-owned cities valid in the cache
    2706  human-player vs human-team update distinction
    2921  revised-UWAI mix-up corrections
    2929/2931 deployment-distance / transport-destination corrections
    3044  new-player history and vassal-score consistency fixes

The older city-sorting, cache-initialization and distance-0 team-city repairs checked
in the same pass likewise survive in current source. Continue the finite historical
matrix rather than assuming every old repair is clean, but do not reopen these without
new contradictory evidence.

C019-WIP10 CONTINUATION -- GOLD-PER-PRODUCTION SITE-WEIGHT CONVERSION REGRESSION
===============================================================================
STATUS: WIP / append-only continuation of authoritative C019-WIP09.
COMPLETED FIRST-PASS FILES: 18 / 169.
CURRENT FILE: queue 031 CvGameCoreDLL/UWAICache.cpp OPEN.
NO REPOSITORY SOURCE FILES MODIFIED.

SPONSORED-WAR MULTI-TARGET SEAM -- NOT PROMOTED
-----------------------------------------------
The WIP09 cursor asked whether one compensation list could be copied into several
sponsored-war targets when a single deal contains multiple TRADE_WAR items.

The generic deal representation can contain multiple trade items and CvDeal would call
reportSponsoredWar once per TRADE_WAR item. However, UWAI's own deal valuation has an
explicit supported-policy guard:

    // advc.104o: Can't be hired for more than one war at a time
    int iWars = 0;
    ...
    case TRADE_WAR:
        if (getUWAI().isEnabled())
        {
            iWars++;
            if (iWars > 1)
                iValue += 1000000; // More than they can pay
        }

Thus the ordinary UWAI trade-acceptance layer intentionally makes the exact multi-war
sponsorship deal effectively unaffordable. Do not spend F222 merely because CvDeal's
reporting loop is structurally capable of receiving such a list through forced or
external deal construction.

A separate possible approximation remains: a single sponsored-war deal can in
principle bundle unrelated reciprocal trade items, while reportSponsoredWar values the
entire received list rather than computing the war item's marginal payment. HiredHand
would then remember some value that economically belongs to other items. The original
implementation already described the whole received list as the sponsorship and even
accepted overpayment as increasing later obligation. Without a sharper supported
reproduction/contract showing that bundled-item marginal attribution is required, keep
this as a modeling limitation rather than F222.

F222 / provisional KI#545 -- CONFIRMED
UWAI REVISION MIS-PARENTHESIZED THE SETTLER ADJUSTMENT IN goldPerProdSites,
DIVIDING THE FIXED SITE WEIGHT BY 10 AND SYSTEMATICALLY UNDERVALUING EXPANSION
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TITLE
    AdvCiv practical commit 2920's scaled-number rewrite changed the algebra of
    UWAICache::goldPerProdSites. The old expression divided only the settler count by
    10; the rewritten expression divides the entire site-weight-plus-settler term by
    10. Good expansion sites are therefore valued far below the pre-rewrite model.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv regression introduced by practical commit 2920 /
    4ae382e5db ("Revised all code in the UWAI component"). Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
    current SAS retain the changed expression.

PRE-2920 CONTRACT / INTENT CONTROL
    Immediately before the large UWAI rewrite, goldPerProdSites used ordinary double
    arithmetic:

        double weights[sitesMax] = { 1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2 };
        ...
        sites += foundVals[i] * (weights[i] + settlers / 10.0) / 2500;

    The comment explains the small settler-dependent addition:

        Once the settlers have been used, the found value of more remote sites
        may increase a bit

    Algebraically the intended weight is therefore:

        siteWeight + settlers / 10

    The 1.0/0.8/... fixed site ranking is not itself supposed to be divided by 10.

2920 REGRESSION
    The scaled rewrite converted the same block to:

        scaled arSiteWeights[] = { 1, fixp(0.8), fixp(0.6), fixp(0.4), fixp(0.2) };
        ...
        rSiteScore +=
            (aiFoundVals[i] * (arSiteWeights[i] + iSettlers) / 10) / 2500;

    ScaledNum's integer overloads have normal numeric semantics:

        r + int  -> add ScaledNum(int)
        r / int  -> divide the whole scaled value by int

    so the rewritten coefficient is:

        (siteWeight + settlers) / 10

    rather than:

        siteWeight + settlers / 10

    This is not a representation trick; the formulas are mathematically different.

DETERMINISTIC NUMERIC PROOF
    With zero settlers, the best site's fixed weight is 1.0.

    Old coefficient:

        1.0 + 0 / 10 = 1.0

    Current coefficient:

        (1.0 + 0) / 10 = 0.1

    For a reference found value of 2500 (the function's own normalizing divisor):

        old site-score contribution     = 2500 * 1.0 / 2500 = 1.0
        current site-score contribution = 2500 * 0.1 / 2500 = 0.1

    The simplest expansion site is therefore undervalued by exactly a factor of 10.

    The error remains for nonzero settlers. Because the loop starts at iSettlers, the
    corresponding coefficients are for example:

        settlers 1, weight 0.8:
            old     = 0.8 + 0.1 = 0.9
            current = (0.8 + 1) / 10 = 0.18

        settlers 2, weight 0.6:
            old     = 0.6 + 0.2 = 0.8
            current = (0.6 + 2) / 10 = 0.26

    Thus the conversion does not merely shift a corner case; it systematically shrinks
    the city-site opportunity term throughout the normal settler range.

DOWNSTREAM EFFECT
    goldPerProdSites returns:

        min(4.5, 4.5 * rSiteScore / iCities)

    and updateGoldPerProduction begins with:

        m_rGoldPerProduction = max(goldPerProdBuildings(), goldPerProdSites());

    before applying amortization and the process/floor/victory lower bounds.

    For one city, one 2500-value unclaimed site and zero settlers, the site component
    was designed to reach the 4.5 cap:

        old:     rSiteScore = 1.0 -> 4.5 gold per production
        current: rSiteScore = 0.1 -> 0.45 gold per production

    The later global floor of 1 can mask part of the numerical collapse when no other
    peaceful use dominates, but it cannot restore the intended expansion opportunity
    signal. In ordinary early states where building demand is between those values,
    current code chooses the building term whereas the original model would choose the
    stronger expansion-site term.

LIVE WAR-UTILITY CONSUMER
    WarUtilityAspect::Effort reads:

        scaled rGoldPerProduction = ourCache().goldValueOfProduction();

    and multiplies wartime build-up/lost production by that value before converting it
    to utility. Therefore F222 systematically makes war production look cheaper in
    game states where good expansion sites should be the dominant peaceful alternative.
    It is not dead cache arithmetic or a display-only discrepancy.

ANCESTRY
    Practical commit 1253 introduced the original site-opportunity model. Practical
    commit 1358 refined it to weighted found values and introduced the exact expression:

        foundVals[i] * (weights[i] + settlers / 10.0) / 2500

    That double-arithmetic form survives later pre-revision commits.

    Practical commit 2920 / 4ae382e5db ("Revised all code in the UWAI component")
    changes the old line directly to:

        (aiFoundVals[i] * (arSiteWeights[i] + iSettlers) / 10) / 2500

    The same rewritten expression is reproduced in later history snapshots and remains
    in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS. No subsequent fix restores the original
    parentheses/algebra.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
    Preserve the pre-2920 numeric formula while using scaled arithmetic. For example:

        rSiteScore += aiFoundVals[i] *
                (arSiteWeights[i] + scaled(iSettlers, 10)) / 2500;

    or an exactly equivalent scaled expression such as:

        rSiteScore += aiFoundVals[i] *
                (10 * arSiteWeights[i] + iSettlers) / 10 / 2500;

    Prefer the first form because it mirrors the documented original intent and makes
    the "settlers / 10" adjustment visually explicit.

    Do not change the five fixed site weights, the settler-based starting index, the
    Barbarian-city contribution, city-count cap or rGoldPerProductionCap as part of
    F222; none of those is needed to repair the proven conversion regression.

RELATION TO F219
    F219/KI#542 found a separate ordering bug in goldPerProdVictory where cumulative
    stage-3 bits shadow stage 4. F222 is another updateGoldPerProduction input but is
    algebraically independent: fixing victory-stage detection does not alter site
    opportunity valuation, and restoring the site formula does not alter victory-stage
    logic.
