F230 / provisional KI#553
-------------------------
TITLE
    Pre-v4 past-war save conversion scales only teams alive at load; legacy history
    against a dead rival remains at the old granularity and becomes mis-scaled if that
    rival is later revived.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv backward-save / revival compatibility regression.
    Present in current base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

CURRENT CODE
    UWAICache::read restores the legacy pre-v9 past-war array first:

        if (iSaveVersion >= 9)
            m_aiPastWarScore.read(pStream);
        else m_aiPastWarScore.readArray<int>(pStream);

    It then performs the pre-v4 granularity migration only for teams that are alive at
    load time:

        if (iSaveVersion < 4)
        {
            for (TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE> it; it.hasNext(); ++it)
                m_aiPastWarScore.multiply(it->getID(), 100);
        }

    The two operations have different domains. readArray<int> restores the serialized
    CivTeamMap slots; the migration subsequently touches only the currently living
    subset.

ORIGINAL COMPATIBILITY CONTRACT
    AdvCivPreSAS commit 1378, 2348464189, introduced save version 4 specifically for
    the increased granularity of pastWarScore.

    Its migration was deliberately slot-complete:

        if(savegameVersion < 4)
            for(int i = 0; i < MAX_CIV_TEAMS; i++)
                pastWarScores[i] *= 100;

    The same change made the live consumer interpret the stored value in hundredths
    and changed new reportWarEnding contributions to roughly +/-100 instead of +/-1.

    Therefore the migration contract was not "convert currently relevant teams."
    It was "convert every serialized legacy team slot."

REGRESSION POINT
    AdvCivPreSAS commit 1818, 854cb8058c,
        "Use AgentIterators in all UWAI classes"
    replaced the all-slot loop with:

        for (TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE> it; it.hasNext(); ++it)
            pastWarScores.multiply(it->getID(), 100);

    That iterator substitution is harmless for many live-game loops, but not for a
    save-format migration whose input contains values for identities that can be dead
    at load time.

WHY THE SKIPPED VALUE IS REALLY STILL DESERIALIZED
    Current EnumMap::readArray reads the full stored key range one value at a time and
    calls setUnsafe for each key. It does not filter the data according to current
    alive status.

    Therefore a dead team's pre-v4 pastWarScore can be present in m_aiPastWarScore
    immediately after deserialization and still escape the required x100 conversion.

SUPPORTED OBSERVABLE STATE
    1. Team A and team B fight and finish a war in a save-format version older than 4.
       A therefore has a nonzero legacy pastWarScore entry for B.
    2. B is later eliminated before that game is saved.
    3. The old save is loaded by current AdvCiv / AdvCiv-SAS.
    4. readArray restores B's serialized legacy score, but TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE> skips B,
       so B's entry remains in old +/-1-scale granularity rather than the new
       +/-100-scale granularity.
    5. B is later revived. AdvCiv explicitly supports player revival; current
       CvPlayer::setAlive(true) reports playerRevived and refreshes UWAI state.
    6. Other players can again evaluate B, and confidenceFromPastWars(B) consumes A's
       still-mis-scaled history.

    Revival is not merely hypothetical dead data. AdvCivPreSAS commit 2010,
    56af3a8dfa, "Fix issues with AI Auto Play ending upon player defeat", added the
    explicit playerRevived lifecycle, and current SAS retains and extends that path.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE
    UWAI::Player::confidenceFromPastWars currently does:

        scaled rPastWarScore = per100(m_cache.pastWarScore(eTarget));
        int iSign = (rPastWarScore < 0 ? -1 : 1);
        scaled r = 1 + iSign * rPastWarScore.abs().sqrt() * fixp(0.15);
        r.clamp(fixp(0.5), fixp(1.5));

    For the simplest old score of +1:
        correct migration: +1 -> +100 -> per100 = 1
        confidence term:   1 + sqrt(1) * 0.15 = 1.15

        skipped migration: +1 remains +1 -> per100 = 0.01
        confidence term:   1 + sqrt(0.01) * 0.15 = 1.015

    Likewise for -1:
        correct: 0.85
        skipped: 0.985

    The stored score is therefore 100x too small. Because confidence uses sqrt, the
    displacement from neutral is 10x too small for the same legacy score before clamp.

WHY THIS IS NOT JUST A DEAD-SLOT CLEANLINESS ISSUE
    If the skipped team remained permanently dead, the stale scale would normally be
    behaviorally irrelevant. The explicit revival lifecycle makes the old key live
    again without rerunning the save-version migration. The defect therefore becomes
    observable precisely in the compatibility state that the current reader claims to
    support.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    For iSaveVersion < 4, multiply every valid CivTeam key represented by the legacy
    serialized map, not TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE>.

    Conceptually:

        if (iSaveVersion < 4)
        {
            FOR_EACH_ENUM(CivTeam)
                m_aiPastWarScore.multiply(eLoopCivTeam, 100);
        }

    Use the project's exact all-CivTeam enum iteration spelling after compile review.
    An explicit 0 .. MAX_CIV_TEAMS-1 loop is also semantically faithful to the original
    migration if that is safer for this old-format branch.

    No save-version bump should be needed: this repairs the read conversion of an
    already-supported old format.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SCOPE
    * Current-format saves are unaffected.
    * Pre-v4 entries for teams alive at load are converted correctly.
    * A skipped dead entry matters only if it contains legacy history and later becomes
      behaviorally reachable again, e.g. through revival.
    * This is separate from F228. F228 concerns one-way migration of persistent
      team-keyed history during a Permanent Alliance team absorption. F230 concerns a
      backward-save conversion whose domain was accidentally narrowed.
    * This is also separate from F225 / KI#548, which concerns reconstruction of the
      revived player's own military cache from already-existing units.


REMAINING C019-WIP17 CURSOR -- RESULTS SO FAR
---------------------------------------------

1. totalAssetScore positivity / denominator seam -- NOT PROMOTED
    updateTotalAssetScore starts from a +5 Palace baseline and then adds own-city asset
    scores plus national-wonder contributions.

    Individual per-city AI_assetVal(..., true) scores can indeed be negative because
    maintenance is subtracted. Historical commit 3038, 23545fcd6e,
        "Fix two minor issues with UWAI asset score values"
    explicitly notes that a per-city score can be negative and defensively clamps a
    vassal-loss calculation.

    However, the historical totalAssetScore == 0 observation was subsequently traced
    to an incomplete new-player refresh. Commit 3044, 8a2a75e1e0,
        "Fix two minor inconsistencies in the UWAI cache"
    changed UWAI::processNewPlayerInGame from a partial typical-unit refresh to a full
    cache.update(true), and its comment says the bad total "Had not worked correctly
    when called from UWAI::processNewPlayerInGame. Should be fixed now".

    Risk::evaluate still divides by totalAssetScore + epsilon rather than max(1,...),
    so a genuinely nonpositive aggregate would be dangerous. But this audit has not
    established a supported normal full-refresh state that makes the aggregate
    nonpositive. Mathematical possibility from a negative constituent is not enough.

    RESULT:
        Keep as a robustness seam / historical check, not a new root.

2. remaining compact EnumMap producer bounds -- NO NEW ROOT AFTER F229
    F229 remains the concrete compact-type defect because a legal full-width human
    sponsored-war payment can cross signed-short range before assignment to m_aiBounty.

    The other reviewed compact fields have substantially tighter domains in the
    supported default geometry, or require only an extreme theoretical count with no
    supported reproduction established here.

    In particular, the prior WIP17 bound for the default SAS48 standard map remains
    useful: 198 * 140 = 27,720 plots, below signed-short max 32,767. That gives a real
    default-world upper bound for plot-loss counts and an even tighter practical bound
    for reachable-city counts.

    targetMissions could only overflow a signed short through an extreme number of
    simultaneously counted units / missions; no supported practical state was proved.

    RESULT:
        No F230-style "short is suspicious, therefore bug" finding is manufactured.

3. remaining old-version read defaults -- CLEAN EXCEPT F230
    * pre-v3 m_abCanBeHiredAgainst omission inherits the map's intended true reset from
      clear(), so old saves receive the correct default.
    * pre-v5 m_bFocusOnPeacefulVictory omission inherits false from clear(), matching
      the feature's introduction semantics.
    * pre-v1 relative-navy reconstruction calls updateRelativeNavyPower(), but the
      feature remains explicitly "Not implemented; work in progress" and has no live
      consumer found in the current source.
    * City pre-v4 capital-area fallback from reach-by-land is deliberate compatibility
      behavior; no defect established.
    * pre-v3 / pre-v1 discarded City fields are consumed only to preserve stream
      alignment; no live state was found to depend on them.

4. City construction / target-value initialization -- CLEAN
    City construction computes distance/reachability and asset score before passing
    the cache-city pointer into AI_targetCityValue. The fields needed by the current
    target-value path are therefore initialized first.

    No use-before-initialization root was found in this pass.

5. reportCityCreated human-cache asymmetry -- OBSERVED, NOT PROMOTED YET
    Full updateCities includes a foreign city for a human cache without requiring
    AI_deduceCitySite, while reportCityCreated requires same-team or deducible city and
    has no corresponding human override.

    City transfer also reports destruction of the old city before creation of the
    replacement, so a human cache can transiently lose a newly transferred foreign
    city until a full refresh when it is not deducible.

    However, the report callbacks are explicitly motivated by keeping AI caches aware
    of changes during a human turn, and this pass has not yet proved a live
    post-transfer-before-refresh consumer for the human cache whose behavior is wrong.

    RESULT:
        Preserve as an open cadence/contracts question for F231+, not a finding.

6. F224 refinement -- NO NEW ROOT
    Normal city founding also calls AI_cityCreated for major caches, so the same
    reportCityCreated path that does not recompute m_rTotalAssets is reached outside
    conquest as well.

    This broadens the producer side of F224's stale-total-assets mechanism, but the
    strongest already-proved behavioral reproduction remains the mid-turn
    conquest/diplomacy path recorded under F224. Do not duplicate it as a new root.

PURPOSE OF THIS WIP
-------------------
Continue the queue-031 UWAICache.cpp audit from F231 unused, with emphasis on the
remaining City/report-state lifecycle, incremental versus full-cache invariants,
backward-save decoding, and low-mention persistent-state producer/consumer paths.

This pass promotes two distinct roots:
    * F231: incremental city callbacks leave deployment geometry and reachable-city
      counts stale for surviving cached foreign cities after the cache owner's own
      city set changes;
    * F232: the first City-subrecord versioning retrofit decodes version-0 raw
      distances with the versioned "-1" transform, shifting every legacy distance.

It also strengthens two existing roots without consuming new root numbers:
    * F216's Permanent Alliance migration needs a full persistent target-team domain,
      not TeamIter<MAJOR_CIV>;

      into the new short-backed map during deserialization.

F231 / provisional KI#554
-------------------------
TITLE
    Incremental city create/destroy callbacks update only the changed cache entry;
    deployment geometry and reachable-city counts for surviving foreign cached cities
    remain stale when the cache owner's own city set changes.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv UWAI incremental-cache consistency defect.
    Present in current base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

CORE FULL-REFRESH CONTRACT
    A cached foreign City's deployment geometry is not a property of the target city
    alone. City::updateDistance computes it from the CACHE OWNER'S current city set.

    For every relevant owner city it can use:
        * land reachability to the target;
        * coastal access and naval paths;
        * source-city population / production filters;
        * primary-area status;
        * the current capital, which receives extra weight;
        * whether the current capital has a land route to the target.

    It derives and stores:
        m_iDistance
        m_bReachByLand
        m_bCapitalArea

    A full updateCities pass constructs every foreign City from this current geometry.
    add(City&) also increments m_aiReachableCities for every foreign cached City whose
    canReach() is true.

INCREMENTAL CONTRACT IS NARROWER
    Current reportCityCreated:

        if (kCity.getTeam() == TEAMID(m_eOwner) ||
            GET_TEAM(m_eOwner).AI_deduceCitySite(kCity))
        {
            add(kCity);
            sortCitiesByAttackPriority();
        }

    add(CvCity&) creates pathfinders and constructs ONLY kCity.

    Current remove(CvCity const&) removes ONLY the matching cached City. It decrements
    m_aiReachableCities only when the removed city itself is a reachable FOREIGN city.

    Neither callback recomputes m_iDistance / m_bReachByLand / m_bCapitalArea for
    surviving foreign cached cities. Nor does it reconstruct m_aiReachableCities from
    those surviving entries.

WHY THE CACHE OWNER'S OWN CITY CHANGES INVALIDATE SURVIVING TARGETS
    Any own city-set change can change foreign-target deployment geometry.

    Examples:
        * Founding or conquering a coastal city can make previously unreachable
          overseas targets reachable by sea.
        * Losing or razing the only useful coastal launch city can make previously
          reachable overseas targets unreachable.
        * Adding/removing a large productive source city changes the weighted
          deployment-distance average.
        * Losing the capital and selecting a new capital can change
          m_bCapitalArea / canReachByLandFromCapital for many existing targets.
        * The capital itself receives duplicate weight in the distance sample, so a
          capital move can change m_iDistance even when broad reachability remains.

    Thus this is not merely "the new/removed city entry is stale." Existing target
    entries are derived from a source set that has changed underneath them.

CAPITAL-LOSS CALLBACK ORDERING GIVES A CLEAN REPRODUCTION
    CvCity::kill currently notifies every major AI cache first:

        for (PlayerAIIter<MAJOR_CIV> it; it.hasNext(); ++it)
            it->AI_cityKilled(*this);

    The owner's city object is deleted later:

        kOwner.deleteCity(getID());

    Only after that deletion does the old-capital branch call:

        kOwner.findNewCapital();

    Therefore reportCityDestroyed is too early even if it wanted to recompute the
    owner's deployment geometry: at callback time the old city still exists and an old
    capital is still the capital. No second UWAI geometry refresh follows
    findNewCapital.

    City acquisition later reports the newly created replacement through
    AI_cityCreated, but reportCityCreated again constructs only that one city and sorts.
    It does not rebuild the surviving foreign targets from the new owner-city set.

NORMAL FOUNDING HAS THE SAME STRUCTURAL ISSUE
    CvPlayer::found also notifies major AI caches through AI_cityCreated after creating
    the new city.

    For the founding player's own cache, that newly existing source city can alter
    deployment distance/reachability to all previously cached foreign cities, yet only
    the founded city's own cache record is constructed.

    So the root is broader than conquest/capital loss. Capital capture is simply the
    clearest high-impact demonstration.

STALE m_aiReachableCities IS LIVE STATE, NOT DISPLAY-ONLY METADATA
    m_aiReachableCities is reconstructed by full update logic from each cached foreign
    city's canReach state, but incremental own-city changes do not rebuild it.

    Multiple live consumers use it as a hard gate, including:
        * UWAI::Team::canReach;
        * UWAI::Player::canReach;
        * WarUtilityAspect::GreedForCash;
        * WarUtilityAspect::TacticalSituation::evalOperational;
        * WarUtilityAspect::LoveOfPeace;
        * loss / elimination war-utility logic;
        * CvPlayerAI diplomacy demand/tribute reachability checks when UWAI is active.

    Therefore, for example, loss of the only practical coastal launch city can leave
    the AI behaving as though an overseas rival still has reachable cities until the
    next full owner-cache update. The inverse can happen after gaining a launch city.

STALE PER-CITY GEOMETRY ALSO HAS DIRECT WAR-MODELING CONSUMERS
    InvasionGraph deliberately works with the analyzed player's own cache:

        m_kCache(GET_PLAYER(m_ePlayer).uwai().getCache())

    Its target selection stops when cached cities are unreachable or classified as
    own-team:

        if (!kCacheCity.canReach() || kCacheCity.isOwnTeamCity())
            break;

    Its land-reach calculations directly consult:
        canReachByLandFromCapital()
        canReachByLand()
        getDistance()

    ArmamentForecast likewise consults canReachByLandFromCapital() and getDistance()
    when deciding naval versus land armament.

    Thus stale fields influence invasion topology, deployment timing and armament
    forecasts independently of the aggregate reachable-city count.

SUPPORTED SAME-TURN BEHAVIORAL REPRODUCTION
    A strong ordering is:

        1. During the human player's turn, a human captures/razes a victim AI's sole
           useful coastal source city or its capital.
        2. AI_cityKilled causes the victim cache to remove the changed city, but all
           surviving foreign cached targets retain pre-loss geometry.
        3. For a capital, findNewCapital runs only after that callback.
        4. The human then negotiates peace during the same turn, before the victim's
           next turnPre/full cache update.
        5. CvPlayerAI::AI_dealVal for an at-war human deal reaches
           UWAI::Team::endWarVal / reluctanceToPeace.
        6. WarEvaluator -> MilitaryAnalyst -> InvasionGraph consumes the victim's
           stale deployment geometry and/or reachable-city state.

    This establishes a live consumer between mutation and the next full refresh.

HISTORICAL ANCESTRY
    AdvCivPreSAS commit 2605, f788c46a21,
        "Various optimizations for UWAICache"
    introduced the split city-killed / city-created callback architecture.

    Its own comment states:

        "City ownership changes result in the creation of a new city.
         It's important that the cache keep up with ownership changes
         so that the AI is aware of conquests made throughout a human turn."

    That goal explains the incremental updates, but the implementation updates the
    changed target entry rather than all cache entries whose deployment geometry is
    derived from the cache owner's mutable city set.

    AdvCivPreSAS commit 2606, 1fdeb92b6f,
        "Minor tweaks to UWAI distance computation"
    added the human full-refresh city-location override discussed separately below;
    it did not add geometry reconstruction to incremental city callbacks.

BASELINE COMPARISON
    Current base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same incremental add/remove behavior.
    K-Mod and Civ4CE do not carry this UWAI cache layer, so they do not provide a
    direct equivalent implementation to compare.

DISTINCTION FROM EXISTING ROOTS
    F224:
        stale total-asset denominator after create/destroy.
        F231 concerns per-target path/deployment geometry and aggregate reachability.

    F227:
        stale stateful attack ordering / area-clustering after remove-only destruction.
        F231 persists even if the vector is perfectly resorted because the underlying
        surviving target geometry itself is outdated.

    F226:
        path-choice logic inside one City::updateDistance calculation.
        F231 concerns failing to rerun that calculation after its source-city inputs
        change.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    The important ordering requirement is that surviving target geometry must be
    recomputed AFTER the owner-city mutation is stable.

    In particular, recomputing inside the existing AI_cityKilled callback is
    insufficient because CvCity::kill invokes it before deleteCity and, for a capital,
    before findNewCapital.

    A robust design could introduce a post-city-set-change cache refresh/helper that:
        * rebuilds or updates pathfinders for foreign target teams;
        * reruns City::updateDistance for surviving foreign cached Cities belonging to
          the player whose own source-city set changed;
        * reconstructs m_aiReachableCities from the resulting canReach values;
        * refreshes any derivative target ordering/value state whose inputs changed;
        * resorts after those values are stable.

    A whole cache.update() would be simple but may be unnecessarily expensive and may
    touch unrelated cadence/persistent state. A targeted geometry/reachability helper
    looks preferable if it can be kept lifecycle-safe.

    The destruction path needs a post-delete/post-findNewCapital hook or equivalent.
    The creation path already fires after the new city exists, so it can invoke the
    targeted owner-geometry refresh from there.

    Compile/runtime review is needed before choosing exact hook placement.


F232 / provisional KI#555
-------------------------
TITLE
    Version-0 UWAICache::City save records wrote raw distance, but the versioned reader
    unconditionally subtracts 1; every legacy distance is shifted and distance 1 is
    misclassified as an own-team city.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv backward-save decoder defect.
    Present in current base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

CURRENT FORMAT
    Current City::write folds the City-subrecord version into distance:

        int iDistance = ::range(m_iDistance, -1, 9999);
        pStream->Write(iDistance + 1 + 10000 * iSaveVersion);

    Current iSaveVersion is 4.

    Current City::read always decodes:

        pStream->Read(&iTmp);
        iSaveVersion = iTmp / 10000;
        m_iDistance = (iTmp % 10000) - 1;

ORIGINAL VERSION-0 FORMAT
    The history is explicit.

    Before City subrecord versioning, the writer and reader simply did:

        stream->Write(distance);
        ...
        stream->Read(&distance);

    AdvCivPreSAS commit 1287, ad5faf8aa2,
        "Test version incl. DLL and manual; needs some more work."
    introduced version 1 and changed writing to:

        stream->Write(distance + 1 + 10000 * savegameVersion);

    But its new reader immediately changed to:

        savegameVersion = tmp / 10000;
        distance = (tmp % 10000) - 1;

    with no version-0 branch.

    Therefore the new encoding transform was retroactively applied to values that had
    been stored in the old raw encoding.

EXACT LEGACY SHIFT
    For a version-0 record, abs(distance) values are below 10000, so:

        iSaveVersion = rawDistance / 10000 = 0
        decodedDistance = rawDistance - 1

    Therefore:
        old -1 -> -2
        old  0 -> -1
        old  1 ->  0
        old  N -> N - 1

    The current writer's assertion message even acknowledges one symptom:

        "-2 is OK if loaded from an old savegame version"

    but the compatibility shift is not confined to the -1 sentinel. Every legacy
    distance is displaced.

BEHAVIORAL CONSEQUENCE: FOREIGN DISTANCE 1 BECOMES "OWN TEAM"
    Current:

        bool isOwnTeamCity() const { return (m_iDistance == 0); }

    A perfectly ordinary legacy foreign target with deployment distance 1 therefore
    loads as distance 0 and is falsely classified as an own-team city.

    attackPriority returns the special own-team priority:

        if (m_iDistance < 0)
            return -1;
        else if (isOwnTeamCity())
            return -2;

    Current InvasionGraph target iteration checks the same classification and can break
    upon encountering an own-team/unreachable cached city.

    Thus this is not merely a one-turn numeric underestimate: a foreign target can
    cross a semantic sentinel boundary and disrupt target enumeration/modeling.

OTHER POSITIVE DISTANCES ARE ALSO TOO SMALL
    Legacy distance N > 1 becomes N-1. Consumers that directly use getDistance for
    deployment timing, land-reach thresholds, invasion modeling and armament
    forecasting therefore receive systematically understated values until refresh.

LOAD-TIME CACHE RELINK DOES NOT RECOMPUTE DISTANCE
    After UWAICache has been deserialized, CvPlayerAI::read eventually calls:

        kPlayer.uwai().getCache().cacheCitiesAfterRead();

    cacheCitiesAfterRead only relinks each cached City to its CvCity:

        for (...)
            cityAt(i).cacheCvCity();

    It does not rerun updateDistance, rebuild reachable-city counts or resort by newly
    recomputed geometry.

    CvGameAI::read likewise does not perform an immediate full UWAI cache update.

    The normal complete recomputation occurs at a later UWAI player turnPre/cache
    update. Therefore the bad decoded distance is genuinely live between load and that
    refresh.

SUPPORTED OBSERVABILITY
    A manual save can be loaded into an active turn. Diplomacy and UWAI war-evaluation
    entry points can be invoked before the affected cache owner's next turnPre.

    In particular, the distance-1 -> 0 semantic collision can be consumed by
    InvasionGraph / war-evaluation machinery in that interval.

HISTORICAL / BASELINE COMPARISON
    The defect originates in the very first City-subrecord versioning retrofit and is
    retained in current base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS.

    This is an AdvCiv backward-save issue; K-Mod/Civ4CE do not provide the same UWAI
    City-subrecord format.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Decode the raw version-0 representation separately:

        pStream->Read(&iTmp);
        iSaveVersion = iTmp / 10000;
        if (iSaveVersion <= 0)
            m_iDistance = iTmp; // legacy record stored raw distance
        else
            m_iDistance = (iTmp % 10000) - 1;

    Keep the existing version-gated field consumption after distance:
        * capitalArea for v4+;
        * discarded reachBySea for versions <3;
        * discarded canDeduce for version 1.

    Verify signed integer division/modulo behavior for the legacy -1 sentinel under the
    VC2003 compiler/runtime during implementation review. The intended semantic rule is
    still simple: version-0 is raw; versioned records use the +1/+10000 packing.

    No new save-version bump should be required because this is a read-side correction
    for an already-supported historical format.

DISTINCTION FROM F230
    F230 concerns a top-level pre-v4 pastWarScore scale migration whose iteration
    domain was narrowed to alive teams.

    F232 concerns the nested City record's original encoding transition and an
    unconditional arithmetic transform. They are independent backward-save bugs.


F216 / provisional KI#539 -- SAME-ROOT REFINEMENT
--------------------------------------------------
Permanent Alliance cache merge also narrows the persistent TARGET-team domain to
currently alive major teams.

Current UWAICache::addTeam(PlayerTypes eOtherLeader) merges persistent values with:

    for (TeamIter<MAJOR_CIV> itTeam; itTeam.hasNext(); ++itTeam)
    {
        TeamTypes eTeam = itTeam->getID();
        m_aiPastWarScore.add(eTeam, kOther.m_aiPastWarScore.get(eTeam));
        ...
    }

Agent predicate/iterator definitions confirm that MAJOR_CIV implies ALIVE and maps to
the major-alive collection.

Persistent war history and related team-keyed state can nevertheless exist for an
eliminated major rival, and AdvCiv supports revival. If such a rival is dead when the
Permanent Alliance is formed, the absorbed member's persistent history versus that
rival is not merged into the surviving cache. A later revival makes the omitted key
behaviorally relevant again.

This belongs under F216 rather than a new root because F216 already establishes that
addTeam's Permanent Alliance migration is structurally using the wrong iteration
contract.

A correct migration needs BOTH:
    1. the pre-merge recipient membership boundary, so the absorbed leader does not
       merge itself into itself and double its score (original F216);
    2. a full persistent CivTeam target-key domain, not an alive-only iterator, so
       historical state against dead/revivable rivals is not discarded.

F228 remains distinct: it concerns outsider caches whose stored references point to
the absorbed team. This F216 refinement concerns state copied FROM the absorbed
member into the surviving alliance cache.


F229 / provisional KI#552 -- BACKWARD-SAVE REFINEMENT
------------------------------------------------------
The bounty int-to-short regression also affects pre-v9 save migration.

AdvCivPreSAS commit 3183, 59a3e31900,
    "Rewrite of enum map classes"
did two relevant things together:
    * changed m_aiBounty from a full int map to CivTeamMap<int,short>;
    * bumped the UWAICache save version to 9 for the new enum-map save behavior.

Current backward reader for old saves uses:

    if (iSaveVersion >= 9)
        m_aiBounty.read(pStream);
    else m_aiBounty.readArray<int>(pStream);

The old serialized value is therefore read as full-width int, but assignment into the
current map ultimately compacts it into the short backing type.

With the normal non-extra-assert compact path, a legal old bounty above signed-short
range can wrap rather than being range-preserved.

This is especially damaging because the sponsor is deserialized separately from the
old full-width sponsor map. A loaded cache can therefore contain:

    sponsorAgainst(target) != NO_PLAYER
    bountyAgainst(target) <= 0

Current HiredHand logic asserts the inverse relationship:

    FAssert((eSponsor == NO_PLAYER) == (iOriginalUtility <= 0));

and in release behavior only honors the sponsored-war obligation when the bounty is
positive.

So the backward-save manifestation can:
    * trip the sponsor/bounty invariant in debug;
    * silently erase the practical paid-war obligation in release.

Do not allocate a new root. This is the same representability defect as F229, reached
through the old-save reader rather than reportSponsoredWar's live assignment.

Repair choices remain:
    * restore a full-width bounty representation; or
    * for old-save migration, read to temporary full-width storage and explicitly
      saturate/range-check before assigning compact storage, while keeping the sponsor
      invariant consistent.


OPEN QUESTION -- HUMAN FULL-REFRESH / INCREMENTAL-CREATE ASYMMETRY
------------------------------------------------------------------
NOT PROMOTED AS F233 IN THIS WIP.

Full updateCities deliberately gives a human cache omniscient city-location treatment:

    if (same team ||
        bHuman ||
        kCacheTeam.AI_deduceCitySite(*pCity))
    {
        add(...);
    }

Historical commit 2606 explains the intent:
    "Assume that human can locate all cities of known civs"

Incremental reportCityCreated does NOT carry the bHuman override. It adds a foreign
new city only if the cache owner's team can deduce the site.

Therefore a newly founded unseen foreign city can be absent from the human player's
cache until the next human full refresh even though the full-refresh contract says it
belongs there.

There is a plausible cross-cache consequence because InvasionGraph deliberately uses
the analyzed player's own cache. An AI evaluating a human's possible operations can
therefore model the human from a cache that temporarily omits a city the full-refresh
policy would include.

However:
    * this is a narrow cadence/fairness asymmetry;
    * the callback comment is primarily concerned with keeping AI aware of HUMAN
      conquests during a human turn;
    * no sufficiently strong direct behavioral reproduction distinct from F231 has yet
      been established.

Keep this as the leading F233 candidate, but do not promote it merely from mismatch.


OTHER CHECKS / NEGATIVE CONTROLS THIS PASS
------------------------------------------

1. updateTraits offensive/defensive else-if -- CURRENT DATA DOES NOT TRIGGER IT
    The code marks a trait as offensive when a trait-granted free promotion has
    positive generic combat, otherwise checks city defense through else-if.

    A promotion with both positive combat and city defense would therefore set the
    offensive flag but miss the defensive flag.

    Current SAS trait/free-promotion XML was checked. No currently trait-granted free
    promotion has both positive generic combat and positive city defense.

    RESULT:
        Generic mod-robustness smell only. No current-data root.

2. m_abPlayerLocated -- DEAD MEMBER / CLEANUP ONLY
    No live uses were found.

3. updateRelativeNavyPower -- EXPLICITLY UNIMPLEMENTED / NO LIVE CONSUMER
    It remains a work-in-progress field and does not support a current root.

4. updateAdjacentLand / updateLostTilesAtWar / longTermPower / updateVassalScore
    Reviewed in the remaining low-mention sweep. No supported new defect established.

5. reportWarEnding reparations direction
    Caller supplies received/given reparations to the two team caches in the intended
    direction. The function's if/else-if is not a lost-state bug.

6. City::updateDistance capital pointer
    Normal cache lifecycle structurally gives an owner with cities a capital. The
    destruction callback occurs before old-capital deletion, while creation occurs
    after city creation. No supported null-capital crash state was established here.

7. updateCanBeHiredAgainst
    Reviewed caller/leader-cache usage; no new root established.

8. reportWarEnding score accumulation
    Persistent score is full-width integer. No realistic supported overflow root was
    established.

9. cvCityById
    Used for simulated city-loss IDs while underlying actual cities remain present.
    No null/stale identity root established in the inspected consumers.


HISTORICAL "KNOWN WEAK SPOTS" SWEEP
-----------------------------------
The audit also checked older commits whose titles explicitly mention UWAI crashes,
distance corrections or cache inconsistencies. These are valuable negative controls
because several queue-031 findings arose when later refactors narrowed an older
compatibility contract.

Reviewed examples:

    AdvCivPreSAS 1909, 8095a0a0a3
        "Fix array index out of bounds in UWAI code"

PURPOSE OF THIS WIP

Continue the queue-031 UWAICache.cpp audit from F233 unused.

This pass first resolved the full-refresh / incremental human-city membership mismatch,

F233 / provisional KI#556
-------------------------
TITLE
    Incremental reportCityCreated omits the full-refresh human known-city rule; later
    AI military analysis can model a human from a stale human cache that is missing a
    newly founded foreign city.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv UWAI incremental-cache policy mismatch.
    Present in current base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

FULL-REFRESH POLICY
    UWAICache::update first iterates only major teams KNOWN_TO the cache owner's team.
    For each such team, updateCities applies:

        if (eTeam == kCacheTeam.getID() ||
            // Assume that human can locate all cities of known civs
            bHuman || kCacheTeam.AI_deduceCitySite(*pCity))
        {
            add(...);
        }

    Therefore the intended human policy is:
        * same-team cities are included;
        * for a FOREIGN TEAM ALREADY KNOWN to the human, every city is included even
          when AI_deduceCitySite would currently fail.

    The "known civ" scope is important: bHuman is not global omniscience over unmet
    teams. update() reaches updateCities only through TeamIter<MAJOR_CIV,KNOWN_TO>.

INCREMENTAL POLICY
    reportCityCreated instead uses:

        if (kCity.getTeam() == TEAMID(m_eOwner) ||
            GET_TEAM(m_eOwner).AI_deduceCitySite(kCity))
        {
            add(kCity);
            sortCitiesByAttackPriority();
        }

    There is no human override corresponding to updateCities.

    Thus a newly founded city of an already-known foreign civ can belong in the human
    cache under the full-refresh contract but be skipped by the incremental callback.

HISTORICAL ORIGIN IS A TWO-COMMIT CONTRACT SPLIT
    AdvCivPreSAS commit 2605, f788c46a21,
        "Various optimizations for UWAICache"
    introduced the current reportCityCreated-style callback with:
        same team OR AI_deduceCitySite
    and no human override.

    The very next commit, AdvCivPreSAS 2606, 1fdeb92b6f,
        "Minor tweaks to UWAI distance computation"
    changed full updateCities from:
        same team OR AI_deduceCitySite
    to:
        same team OR human OR AI_deduceCitySite
    with the explicit comment:
        "Assume that human can locate all cities of known civs"

    It also removed the older human-location check from City::updateDistance.

    reportCityCreated was not updated to match the new membership policy.

WHY A STALE HUMAN CACHE IS USED BY AI CODE
    InvasionGraph::Node deliberately models each player from THAT PLAYER'S cache:

        m_kCache(GET_PLAYER(m_ePlayer).uwai().getCache())

    while retaining the evaluating agent's own cache separately:

        m_kAgentCache(GET_PLAYER(m_eAgent).uwai().getCache())

    The source comment explicitly says:
        "agent cheats by using info from other players' caches"

    and the agent cache is then used to sanitize target cities that the evaluating AI
    itself should not know about.

    findBestTarget iterates m_kCache.cityAt(i). Therefore a city absent from the
    modeled player's cache cannot be selected/modelled at all, even if the evaluating
    agent's own fresh cache knows that city.

SUPPORTED TURN-ORDER REPRODUCTION
    Choose three major players:
        H = human being modeled
        A = known foreign rival of H
        B = later-turn AI doing military analysis

    1. H's turn begins. H's UWAICache receives its normal full update. At this time
       the cache obeys the intended human policy: all cities of known civs are eligible
       independent of AI_deduceCitySite.

    2. Later in the same round, A founds a new city C.

    3. CvPlayer::found broadcasts AI_cityCreated(C) to the major AI-player objects.

    4. H knows A, but choose C so that H's team cannot currently deduce the exact site.
       H's reportCityCreated therefore skips C even though the next full updateCities
       would include it solely because H is human.

    5. Still later in the round, B's turn starts. B gets its own normal full cache
       refresh. Choose an ordinary state where B can see/deduce C, so B's own cache
       correctly contains C.

    6. B performs a military analysis that includes H as a modeled belligerent
       (for example H and A are at war).

    7. The InvasionGraph node for H binds m_kCache to H's stale cache and
       m_kAgentCache to B's fresh cache.

    8. C is absent from H's target list before the agent-cache visibility sanitizer
       even gets a chance to approve it.

    The mismatch can therefore change B's model of which city H would target, the
    invasion topology and downstream war-utility estimates.

    A clean illustrative state is for C to be H's only / clearly best newly reachable
    city of A. The omission then changes modeled target selection directly.

WHY THIS IS DISTINCT FROM F231
    F231:
        entries for surviving foreign cities exist but their distance/reachability
        geometry is stale after the cache owner's own city set changes.

    F233:
        the newly created foreign city entry is entirely ABSENT from the human cache
        because full refresh and incremental creation disagree about membership.

    Correcting F231's geometry recomputation does not create the missing F233 entry.

BASELINE
    Current base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same updateCities/reportCityCreated mismatch.
    K-Mod and Civ4CE do not carry this UWAI cache architecture.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    reportCityCreated should mirror the membership contract of full updateCities, not
    merely append `|| isHuman()` to the current condition without regard to contact.

    Conceptually:
        * same-team city: eligible;
        * foreign city:
            - foreign team must be known/met by the cache owner's team, matching the
              TeamIter<...,KNOWN_TO> outer scope of full update;
            - then human OR AI_deduceCitySite decides location eligibility.

    In other words, preserve BOTH parts of the full-refresh policy:
        KNOWN foreign team
        AND (human OR deducible city site).

    Use TEAMID(m_eOwner) / the project's type-safe owner-team form in the repair.
    Do not copy the current `GET_TEAM(m_eOwner)` PlayerTypes-vs-TeamTypes misuse;
    that broad type-domain family is already tracked separately under F113 / KI#436.

    The eventual city-callback repair should also be reconciled with F224, F231,
    F227 and F234 so that one lifecycle helper does not fix membership while leaving
    total assets, surviving-target geometry, ordering or uniqueness stale.


F234 / provisional KI#557
-------------------------
TITLE
    First-city full refresh plus reportCityCreated inserts the same city twice; the
    city vector and plot-ID map diverge, and a same-round later capture can leave a
    dangling cached City that sortCitiesByAttackPriority dereferences.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv cache-uniqueness / memory-safety regression.
    Present in current base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

THE TWO INDEPENDENT INSERTION PATHS
    CvPlayer::initCity finishes CvCity::init and then calls:

        setFoundedFirstCity(true);

    The advc.104 comment says this was deliberately moved out of CvCity::init so that
    the new city is already fully initialized.

    On the false -> true transition, setFoundedFirstCity performs:

        if (!isBarbarian() && getParent() == NO_PLAYER &&
            getUWAI().isEnabled() && GC.getGame().isFinalInitialized())
        {
            AI().uwai().getCache().update();
        }

    The comment explains why:
        "So that rivals (with higher ids) can immediately evaluate war plans
         against this player"

    A full update clears the city cache and updateCities inserts the owner's newly
    created city.

    CvPlayer::found then continues its post-init founding work. For an ordinary
    non-Advanced-Start founding it later broadcasts:

        for (PlayerAIIter<MAJOR_CIV> it; it.hasNext(); ++it)
            it->AI_cityCreated(*pCity);

    This includes the founding player's own AI object/cache.

    reportCityCreated sees a same-team city and calls add(kCity) again.

WHY NORMAL FIRST-TURN FOUNDING IS INSIDE THE CONDITION
    CvGame setup calls setInitialItems and only afterward calls:

        setFinalInitialized(true);

    Standard start settlers therefore found their first playable city after final
    initialization is true. This is not limited to a WorldBuilder or load-only path.

    The same structural duplication can also occur whenever an alive cityless player
    acquires its first city during a finalized game: acquireCity calls initCity
    (triggering the first-city full update) and later broadcasts AI_cityCreated for the
    replacement city.

ADVANCED START IS AN EXCEPTION, NOT A DEFENSE
    CvPlayer::found intentionally skips the AI_cityCreated broadcast while
    getAdvancedStartPoints() >= 0. Therefore this exact duplicate insertion is avoided
    for Advanced Start placement. That does not protect ordinary first-city founding.

ADD DOES NOT ENFORCE UNIQUE PLOT IDS
    UWAICache::add(City&) does:

        m_cityList.push_back(&kCacheCity);
        m_cityMap.insert(std::make_pair(kCacheCity.getID(), &kCacheCity));

    std::map::insert does not replace an existing key.

    Its return value is ignored and there is no assertion that insertion succeeded.

    After the second insertion:
        m_cityList contains TWO separately allocated UWAICache::City objects for the
        same plot;
        m_cityMap still points to the FIRST object only.

    numCities() therefore sees a duplicate that lookupCity(plot) cannot expose.

THE TWO CACHED COPIES CAN ALSO REPRESENT DIFFERENT SNAPSHOTS
    setFoundedFirstCity's full update occurs inside initCity.

    CvPlayer::found continues afterward, including such work as adding free
    start-era buildings before the AI_cityCreated broadcast.

    Therefore the first map-owned cache record can be an earlier snapshot while the
    later vector-only duplicate is constructed from the more-final city state.

    This further violates the intended "one cache City per plot" identity invariant.
    F224 already covers stale total-asset accounting from incremental city lifecycle;
    F234 is not allocated merely for that stale-value consequence.

REMOVE DELETES ONLY THE MAP-OWNED COPY
    UWAICache::remove finds a cached City exclusively through m_cityMap:

        posMap = m_cityMap.find(kCity.plotNum());
        pCacheCity = posMap->second;

    It erases that map entry, finds exactly that pointer in m_cityList, deletes it and
    erases that one vector element.

    If F234's duplicate exists, the second vector-only City survives.

    UWAICache.h states the intended destruction contract directly:

        // No checks upfront; make sure we're not keeping any dangling pointer.
        void reportCityDestroyed(...) { remove(kCity); }

    F234 violates that contract.

CONCRETE DANGLING-POINTER / USE-AFTER-FREE REPRODUCTION
    A supported sequential state can be constructed without corrupt data:

    1. Player P begins a finalized normal game/turn with no city and at least two ways
       to obtain cities in the same turn (e.g. two settlers, or founding plus another
       ordinary acquisition).

    2. P founds first city C1.
       setFoundedFirstCity(true) full-refreshes P's cache and inserts C1 once.
       found -> AI_cityCreated(C1) inserts C1 a second time.
       The vector now contains duplicate wrappers for C1; the map owns only the first.

    3. P founds/acquires another city C2 before P's next turnPre/full cache refresh.
       P can therefore survive the later loss of C1.

    4. A later-turn rival Q captures C1 during the same round.

    5. The old CvCity::kill broadcasts AI_cityKilled before deleting the old CvCity.
       P's reportCityDestroyed/remove removes ONLY the map-owned first C1 wrapper.
       The vector-only duplicate remains.

    6. CvCity::kill later executes kOwner.deleteCity(getID()), destroying the old
       CvCity object. The surviving duplicate UWAICache::City now holds m_pCity
       pointing at freed city storage.

    7. acquireCity creates Q's replacement city on the same plot and eventually
       broadcasts AI_cityCreated(kNewCity) to all major caches.

    8. P still owns C2, so reportCityCreated does not take the zero-city early return.
       The captured plot was revealed to P as its own former city, so
       AI_deduceCitySite succeeds for the replacement city. P adds the new foreign
       cache record and immediately calls sortCitiesByAttackPriority().

    9. sortCitiesByAttackPriority iterates every vector entry. Its area-clustering
       expression calls:

           m_cityList[j]->city().isArea(*pPrevArea)

       before checking whether the priority is positive.

       The surviving duplicate's city() dereferences the freed m_pCity.

    Result:
        a direct use-after-free / possible crash during the capture callback.

    Even when freed storage happens still to look readable in release, behavior is
    undefined and the vector/map invariants remain corrupted until a full cache clear.

WHY A SECOND CITY MATTERS IN THE CLEAN CRASH REPRO
    If C1 is P's only city, reportCityCreated for P returns when getNumCities() <= 0,
    and acquireCity later eliminates/uninitializes P. That can remove the stale wrapper
    before this particular sort path dereferences it.

    Keeping C2 makes P remain a live cache owner, so the replacement-city callback
    proceeds and provides the immediate dereference.

    The requirement is narrow but fully supported. Nothing in ordinary game rules or
    cache code forbids obtaining two cities in one turn before the next UWAI refresh.

HISTORICAL REGRESSION CHAIN
    AdvCivPreSAS commit 1494, 59ebdf364a, moved setFoundedFirstCity to
    CvPlayer::initCity and added the full UWAI cache update specifically so later-ID
    rivals could immediately evaluate the newly established player.

    AdvCivPreSAS commit 2605, f788c46a21,
        "Various optimizations for UWAICache"
    later introduced the generalized AI_cityCreated/reportCityCreated callback and
    added the ordinary-founding broadcast in CvPlayer::found.

    The older first-city full refresh remained in place.

    Thus each mechanism is locally understandable, but their composition inserts the
    first city twice into the owner's cache.

BASELINE
    Current base AdvCiv 1.14 retains:
        * setFoundedFirstCity -> cache.update();
        * ordinary found/acquire -> AI_cityCreated broadcast;
        * reportCityCreated -> unconditional add for eligible city;
        * add -> vector push plus unchecked std::map::insert;
        * remove -> delete only the one pointer reached through the map.

    This is therefore inherited rather than SAS-created.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Enforce the one-plot/one-cache-City invariant centrally.

    Do not merely hide this case by skipping the cache owner in the founding broadcast:
    the later callback can contain a more-final city snapshot than the early
    setFoundedFirstCity refresh, and incremental creation is needed for other caches.

    Safer architecture:
        * before incrementally inserting a city, detect an existing entry for the same
          plot;
        * explicitly replace/refresh the existing cache record exactly once, keeping
          vector and map ownership synchronized;
        * correctly undo/reapply reachable-city accounting when replacing a foreign
          entry;
        * assert successful unique insertion in debug builds so future duplicate paths
          cannot silently split vector/map ownership;
        * then perform the broader F224/F231/F227 refresh work in a lifecycle-safe
          order.

    A central helper that owns add/replace/remove invariants is preferable to fixing
    only the current first-city caller.

    Because F231 requires post-owner-city-set geometry rebuilding and F224 requires
    aggregate asset refresh, implementation review should solve these city lifecycle
    roots together rather than stacking independent partial callback patches.

DISTINCTION FROM F227
    F227 is stale ordering after a legitimate cached city is removed.

    F234 corrupts cache identity ownership itself: two wrappers exist for one plot,
    only one is represented by the map, and removal can leave a dangling wrapper.
    Resorting after remove cannot safely fix F234 because sorting may be the operation
    that dereferences the dangling copy.


ADVANCED START MULTI-CITY CALLBACK GAP -- NOT PROMOTED AS F235
--------------------------------------------------------------
CvPlayer::found skips AI_cityCreated while Advanced Start points are active.

At first glance this means every Advanced Start city can be absent from incremental
UWAI caches.

The first Advanced Start city, however, flips setFoundedFirstCity and therefore
triggers the older full cache.update() path once final initialization is active.
Historical commit 1494 added that refresh intentionally.

Only additional Advanced Start cities placed after foundedFirstCity is already true
lack both:
    * the first-city full refresh;
    * the normal AI_cityCreated broadcast.

CvPlayerAI::AI_doAdvancedStart can indeed place multiple cities in a loop, so a
partial own cache is structurally possible during setup.

Why this WIP does NOT promote it:
    * first-round/team startup ordering limits normal UWAI war-evaluation consumers;
    * setTurnActive does not run the usual team doTurn path while elapsed game turns
      are zero;
    * UWAI scenario readiness and later per-turn refreshes repair the cache before many
      relevant consumers;
    * a behavioral reproduction that requires a particular first-contact / player-ID
      ordering is possible-looking but not yet established strongly enough to call a
      defect.

Keep as a setup robustness/cadence seam for F235+ if later evidence supplies a clean
consumer before refresh.


MILITARY-BRANCH SAVE-LAYOUT CONCERN -- REJECTED
------------------------------------------------
UWAICache serializes the m_militaryPower vector by current branch count without writing
an outer branch count/version. That would be fragile if the branch roster had ever
changed after UWAI saves existed.

Historical review found the six-branch roster stable since initial UWAI integration:
    HOME_GUARD
    ARMY
    FLEET
    LOGISTICS
    CAVALRY
    NUCLEAR

No add/remove/reorder transition requiring an outer migration was found.

MilitaryBranch later versioned its own record and, importantly, its reader DOES
explicitly distinguish raw version-0 data before applying the newer packed encoding.

That is a useful negative control for F232: MilitaryBranch contains the v0 guard that
the older UWAICache::City distance retrofit omitted.

RESULT:
    No F235.


PACKED VERSION-SENTINEL RANGE CHECK -- CLEAN
--------------------------------------------
The principal folded version encodings were checked against current SAS data/domain
sizes:

    UWAICache owner:
        base 100
        SAS current maximum civ-player domain is 48
        => no owner/version collision.

    MilitaryBranch typical unit:
        base 1000
        current SAS unit-info count is far below 1000
        => no unit/version collision.

    UWAICache::City distance:
        base 10000
        current writer explicitly clamps the current encoded distance to [-1,9999]
        and normal UWAI deployment-distance limits are far below the boundary
        => no modern current-format collision.

This does not alter F232: F232 is the missing raw-v0 decoding branch, not a current
sentinel-capacity problem.


ADDITIONAL LOW-MENTION / CALLBACK SWEEP
---------------------------------------

1. Unit create/destroy military cache callbacks -- NO NEW ROOT
    CvUnit creation updates owner power/assets and then calls reportUnitCreated.
    CvUnit kill reverses the owner power/assets and calls reportUnitDestroyed before
    the unit object is deleted.

    The inspected ownership/capture lifecycle did not expose a queue-031 cache-count
    imbalance independent of already-tracked initialization/revival issues.

2. clear/read/createMilitaryBranches lifecycle -- CLEAN IN THIS PASS
    read sets the owner before clear, clear(false) deletes any prior branch state, and
    read later reconstructs the fixed branch roster before consuming branch records.
    No duplicate branch allocation path was established.

3. updateLostTilesAtWar early return -- CLEAN
    clear(true) resets the map before the update. If OWN_EXCLUSIVE_RADIUS is disabled,
    returning early therefore leaves the intended zero state rather than stale values.

4. updateWarAnger anarchy early return -- CLEAN
    m_arWarAnger is reset by the enclosing full cache update before this function.
    Returning during anarchy does not preserve old anger values.

5. City::updateAssetScore -- NO NEW LOCAL ROOT
    The negative per-city score possibility and aggregate denominator implications were
    already examined in WIP18. No additional independent asset-score calculation defect
    was established here.

6. City::updateDistance -- NO NEW ROOT BEYOND F226/F231/F232
    The detailed path body was reread after those findings. Remaining concerns map to:
        F226 -- which sea/land route is chosen;
        F231 -- failing to rerun geometry after source-city-set mutation;
        F232 -- legacy distance decoding.
    No additional independent path arithmetic defect was promoted.

7. zero-city cache-owner guard in reportCityCreated -- PURPOSEFUL ENOUGH TO KEEP
    The foreign-target distance calculation is fundamentally based on the cache
    owner's source cities. A zero-city player's cache has special lifecycle constraints.
    No independent team-game defect was proved from this early return in this WIP.
