    * F235: cached trait personality flags are not invalidated when True Starts changes
      the leader after UWAI initialization;
    * F236: contact / revelation of pre-existing foreign cities does not incrementally
      refresh the city cache, so reachability can remain zero and immediate sponsored
      war offers can be falsely denied.

F234 is also strengthened: its duplicate vector/map identity divergence is serialized,
so save/load does not heal the cache and can preserve the later dangling-entry hazard.

The remaining leader/team-transition anomalies inspected in this pass predominantly map
onto existing F213/F215/F216/F228/F230 contracts. No F237 is manufactured.


F235 / provisional KI#558
-------------------------
TITLE
    UWAICache trait flags are initialized and serialized but never refreshed; True
    Starts can change the player's leader after UWAI initialization and leave the
    previous leader's offensive/defensive military personality cached indefinitely.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv integration/lifecycle defect.
    Present in current base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

CACHED DERIVED STATE
    UWAICache::init does:

        m_eOwner = eOwner;
        clear();
        updateTraits();
        createMilitaryBranches();

    updateTraits derives two booleans from the cache owner's CURRENT traits and their
    free promotions:

        m_bOffensiveTrait = false;
        m_bDefensiveTrait = false;

        ...
        if (promotion.getCombatPercent() > 0)
            m_bOffensiveTrait = true;
        else if (promotion.getCityDefensePercent() > 0)
            m_bDefensiveTrait = true;

    The header describes the intended meanings as:
        offensive:
            any trait granting an unconditional combat bonus through a free promotion;
        defensive:
            any trait boosting city defense through a free promotion.

REGULAR CACHE REFRESH DOES NOT RECOMPUTE THEM
    UWAICache::update(bool) calls clear(true) and refreshes cities, transports,
    missions, typical units, threat, vassal scores, geometry, economy, war anger,
    fallout capability and war utility.

    It never calls updateTraits().

    clear(true) deliberately does not reset the two trait flags either.

    Therefore these booleans behave as immutable identity-derived cache state after
    init.

SAVE/LOAD ALSO TRUSTS THE CACHED DERIVATION
    UWAICache::write serializes:

        m_bOffensiveTrait
        m_bDefensiveTrait

    UWAICache::read reads the serialized booleans directly.

    It does not recompute them from the player's current leader/traits after load.

    This makes the cache vulnerable both to runtime leader replacement and to future
    XML reinterpretation of traits/promotions across compatible save versions.

SUPPORTED NORMAL-GAME INVALIDATION: TRUE STARTS
    The important point is that AdvCiv itself has a normal game feature that changes
    leaders AFTER player AI/UWAI initialization.

    CvPlayerAI::AI_init initializes UWAI:

        if (isEverAlive() && !isBarbarian() && !isMinorCiv())
            m_pUWAI->init(getID());

    At this point updateTraits has cached the leader/trait assignment that existed
    during player initialization.

    Later, CvGame::setInitialItems performs starting-plot assignment and then:

        if (isOption(GAMEOPTION_TRUE_STARTS))
        {
            TrueStarts ts;
            ts.changeCivs();
            ...
        }

    TrueStarts::changeCivs chooses the selected leader and calls:

        itPlayer->changeCiv(...);
        itPlayer->changeLeader(eLeader, ...);

    Thus the supported startup sequence can replace the leader after UWAICache::init.

CHANGELEADER CORRECTLY UPDATES REAL PLAYER TRAITS, BUT NOT UWAI DERIVED FLAGS
    CvPlayer::changeLeader:

        processTraits(-1);
        set new leader;
        processTraits(1);
        changePersonalityType();

    so the player's actual game traits and ordinary AI personality become correct.

    The old blanket AI reinitialization is intentionally disabled:

        /* Re-initializing the AI here was probably always a bad idea,
           but definitely mustn't re-initialize UWAI. Instead call
           AI_updatePersonality from setPersonalityType. */
        // AI().AI_init();

    That is sensible: reinitializing UWAI wholesale would destroy persistent state.

    But no targeted UWAICache::updateTraits call replaces the stale derived booleans.

    Subsequent normal UWAICache::update calls still do not recompute them, so the
    mismatch is not a one-turn transient. It can persist for the entire game.

HISTORICAL INTEGRATION CHAIN
    AdvCivPreSAS commit 1766, a26d4f8362,
        "Repair the ChangePlayer component"
    deliberately removed/rejected full AI reinitialization from changeLeader and
    moved the ordinary personality refresh into AI_updatePersonality.

    At that point avoiding UWAI reinitialization was correct and necessary.

    Later AdvCivPreSAS commit 3579, 4977b513da,
        "Merge true_starts into 1.05"
    added the ordinary startup True Starts path that can call changeLeader after the
    earlier UWAI initialization.

    The later integration therefore invalidated the implicit assumption behind the
    separately cached trait flags without adding a targeted invalidation/refresh.

LIVE CONSUMERS
    The flags are not decorative.

    UWAI::Player::distrustRating:
        if (m_cache.hasDefensiveTrait())
            iR += 30;

    InvasionGraph:
        * attacker hasOffensiveTrait -> roughly +0.1 army modifier;
        * defender hasOffensiveTrait -> roughly +0.1 army modifier;
        * defender hasDefensiveTrait -> +0.3 city-defender modifier.

    CvCityAI::AI_calculateSettlerPriority:
        the defensive UWAI trait branch adds a settler-priority adjustment.

    Therefore stale flags can change diplomacy/war confidence, invasion force
    estimates and expansion prioritization.

CURRENT SAS DATA GIVES A CLEAN DEFENSIVE REPRODUCTION
    Current SAS TRAIT_PROTECTIVE grants CITY_GARRISON1.
    That promotion has positive city-defense percentage and no generic combat
    percentage, so updateTraits sets m_bDefensiveTrait = true.

    Current SAS TRAIT_AGGRESSIVE has been reworked to grant LEADERSHIP rather than
    COMBAT1. Leadership has neither generic combat nor city-defense percentage, so
    current SAS does not classify Aggressive as offensive through this cache.

    Hence a simple current-SAS True Starts reproduction is:

        initial temporary leader: Protective
        True Starts selected leader: non-Protective

        actual player traits after changeLeader:
            non-Protective

        cached UWAICache flag:
            m_bDefensiveTrait remains true

    Result:
        phantom Protective-style UWAI modeling can persist indefinitely.

    Reverse ordering gives a missing defensive-trait model.

BASE ADVCIV EFFECT IS BROADER
    Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same lifecycle.

    Its ordinary Aggressive trait uses COMBAT1, whose generic combat modifier makes
    updateTraits classify it as offensive. Thus base AdvCiv can stale BOTH the
    offensive and defensive cached models after a True Starts leader reassignment.

SECONDARY SAVE/XML MANIFESTATION
    Because the booleans are serialized as derived data and trusted on load, an
    otherwise compatible save can also retain a flag computed under an older XML
    interpretation.

    For example, a save written when a trait granted a generic-combat promotion can
    retain offensive=true even if the current compatible data no longer give that
    trait such a promotion.

    This is secondary to the fully supported True Starts reproduction, but reinforces
    that these fields should be treated as derivable state rather than immutable
    serialized truth.

NOT THE ELSE-IF DATA SMELL
    updateTraits contains:

        if (combat > 0)
            offensive = true;
        else if (cityDefense > 0)
            defensive = true;

    A single trait-granted promotion with BOTH bonuses would therefore fail to set the
    defensive flag.

    Current SAS trait/free-promotion XML was checked and does not presently contain
    such a triggering promotion. That generic robustness concern is NOT promoted as a
    separate finding.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Do not restore whole AI/UWAI reinitialization in changeLeader.

    Prefer targeted invalidation/recomputation:
        * expose a UWAICache helper for leader/trait identity change; and
        * call updateTraits after processTraits(1) / leader replacement is complete.

    As a defensive backstop, updateTraits is cheap enough to consider during every
    ordinary UWAICache::update as well.

    Save reading should also consider consuming the serialized legacy booleans for
    stream compatibility, then recomputing the current derived values from actual
    traits after the player/leader state is available.

    Exact load ordering should be checked before implementing that read-side hardening.


F236 / provisional KI#559
-------------------------
TITLE
    Contact and map-revelation transitions do not refresh UWAICache city knowledge;
    newly known/deducible pre-existing cities can remain absent with zero cached
    reachability, causing false immediate DENIAL_NO_GAIN for sponsored-war trades.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv incremental-cache coverage defect.
    Present in current base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

FULL-REFRESH KNOWLEDGE CONTRACT
    UWAICache::update rebuilds cached cities only for currently known major teams:

        for (TeamIter<MAJOR_CIV,KNOWN_TO> it(...))
            updateCities(it->getID(), ...);

    For an AI owner, updateCities includes an existing foreign city only when:

        kCacheTeam.AI_deduceCitySite(*pCity)

    AI_deduceCitySite immediately returns true for a city whose site is revealed:

        if (kCity.isRevealed(getID()))
            return true;

    Thus, after contact/revelation, a fresh cache can legitimately contain pre-existing
    cities that were absent at the preceding refresh.

WHAT THE INCREMENTAL LAYER COVERS
    UWAICache has an add(CvCity&) helper capable of constructing one cache City with
    fresh pathfinders and reachability.

    Historical/current comment:

        "Only for updates triggered by unit movement of other players.
         Caller is assumed to check visibility and civ status"

    In current source, however, the live route to this helper is reportCityCreated.

    reportCityCreated handles a city OBJECT being created / ownership-recreated. It
    does not handle an already-existing city becoming known, revealed or deducible.

FIRST CONTACT HAS NO UWAI INVALIDATION
    CvTeam::meet / makeHasMet establishes reciprocal contact, Tech Share, attitudes,
    vassal/master propagation and related diplomacy state.

    No UWAICache city refresh/invalidation is performed.

    Therefore a team that was not KNOWN_TO the cache owner at the previous full update
    remains completely absent from the cached city list after first contact, even when
    the contact movement also reveals one of its cities.

MAP REVELATION HAS THE SAME ROOT
    TRADE_MAPS loops the map and calls:

        kPlot.setRevealed(kToPlayer.getTeam(), true, false,
                kFromPlayer.getTeam(), false);

    CvPlot::setRevealed propagates city revelation through:

        pCity->setRevealed(eTeam, true);

    CvCity::setRevealed updates seen/attitude/visibility state but does not notify UWAI.

    Therefore an AI can ALREADY know rival team T at its last cache refresh, omit T's
    hidden/non-deducible city C, then receive a map that makes C revealed/deducible.
    C remains missing until a later full cache rebuild.

    This is the same invariant failure as first contact:
        world/knowledge state changed such that a pre-existing city now satisfies the
        full-refresh inclusion rule, but no incremental cache transition mirrors it.

REACHABILITY CONSEQUENCE
    m_aiReachableCities is populated only from cached City entries.

    UWAICache::add(City&) increments the foreign owner's count when the added City is
    reachable.

    If a newly known/revealed city is never added, the foreign player's count can
    remain zero even though a fresh cache would add a reachable target.

    UWAI::Team::canReach uses that count directly:

        if (itAgent->uwai().getCache().
                numReachableCities(itTarget->getID()) > 0)
            return true;

    There is no fresh path or visibility calculation in this gate.

HIGH-CONFIDENCE NORMAL TURN REPRODUCTION
    Use three teams:
        A = AI that may be hired for war
        T = target
        H = human sponsor

    H already knows both A and T.

    1. At the start of A's sequential turn, A's team turnPre performs the normal UWAI
       cache refresh.
       A has not yet met T, so T is outside the KNOWN_TO updateCities domain and A has
       no cached T cities / zero reachable-city count for T.

    2. Later in A's same active turn, one of A's units moves adjacent to a T city.
       Normal visibility/contact processing makes A meet T and reveals/deduces that
       same-land reachable city.

    3. CvTeam::meet performs no UWAI cache refresh. The existing T city was not
       created, so reportCityCreated is not called either.

    4. A's turn ends. Before A's NEXT turnPre, H's sequential turn begins.

    5. H asks A to declare war on T.
       CvPlayer::canTradeItem accepts the TRADE_WAR item when both A and H have met T
       and A can legally declare war.

    6. CvPlayer::getTradeDenial reaches:
           CvTeamAI::AI_declareWarTrade
           -> UWAI::Team::declareWarTrade

       Choose ordinary attitude/war-state conditions that pass the preceding refusal
       gates.

    7. UWAI::Team::declareWarTrade begins with:

           if (!canReach(eTarget))
               return DENIAL_NO_GAIN;

       A's stale cache still reports zero reachable T cities.

       The function returns DENIAL_NO_GAIN BEFORE constructing/evaluating the
       WarEvaluator for the sponsored war.

    8. A fresh UWAICache at this moment would iterate newly known T, include the
       revealed same-land city and give a positive reachable-city count.

    Therefore the denial is caused specifically by stale cache knowledge, not by an
    actually unreachable target or ordinary attitude/power refusal.

TURN ORDER SUPPORT
    CvPlayer::setTurnActive(true) performs:
        AI_updateCacheData;
        for elapsed turns > 0 and the team leader:
            GET_TEAM(getTeam()).doTurn();
        then:
            doTurnUnits();

    CvTeam::doTurn reaches the UWAI team/player turn-pre refresh before the subsequent
    unit movement that can establish new contact.

    Hence the required "refresh first, contact later in same AI turn" ordering is
    normal sequential-turn behavior.

MAP-TRADE VARIANT
    A second ordinary reproduction does not require a new team:

        * A already knows T at A's last full update.
        * T's relevant city was still hidden/non-deducible, so it was omitted.
        * A receives a map later in the round that reveals that existing city.
        * no UWAICache callback adds it;
        * immediate diplomacy/war evaluation before A's next refresh still sees the old
          reachability set.

    This broadens the repair contract beyond merely hooking CvTeam::meet.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT
    AdvCivPreSAS commit 2605, f788c46a21,
        "Various optimizations for UWAICache"
    introduced the incremental add/remove City layer and changed city ownership updates
    to reportCityCreated/reportCityDestroyed so AI caches could follow conquests during
    a human turn.

    That optimization solves world-object mutation, but the cached city's inclusion
    condition also depends on mutable KNOWLEDGE state. No corresponding transition was
    added for already-existing cities becoming known/deducible.

    Commit 2606, 1fdeb92b6f,
        "Minor tweaks to UWAI distance computation"
    later strengthened the full-refresh human-known-city policy but likewise did not
    add a revelation/contact invalidation path.

DISTINCTION FROM F233
    F233:
        a NEW foreign city of an ALREADY KNOWN civ is omitted from a HUMAN cache
        because reportCityCreated lacks the full-refresh human override.

    F236:
        a PRE-EXISTING city becomes newly eligible for an AI cache because contact or
        revelation/knowledge changed, but no city-creation callback occurs at all.

    Their producers and repair hooks are different, so keep separate roots.

DISTINCTION FROM F231
    F231 concerns cached cities that ARE PRESENT but whose deployment geometry and
    aggregate reachability become stale when the cache owner's source-city set changes.

    F236 concerns cities that SHOULD NOW EXIST in the cache but are still entirely
    ABSENT because knowledge changed.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    A robust fix needs a knowledge-change invalidation policy, not only a first-contact
    special case.

    Candidate architecture:
        * provide a targeted "refresh known cities for team" / city-knowledge-dirty
          helper;
        * after reciprocal CvTeam::meet is stable, refresh newly eligible cities for
          affected major-player caches;
        * for bulk map revelation, avoid an expensive UWAI rebuild per plot. Mark the
          recipient team/player caches dirty while plots are revealed and flush once
          after TRADE_MAPS finishes;
        * rebuild/recompute m_aiReachableCities and attack ordering consistently with
          any newly inserted cities;
        * ensure required pathfinders use the now-current contact/revelation state.

    Alternatively, force an appropriate full cache update before diplomacy consumers
    use reachability, but broad full updates during map trades/contact may be more
    expensive and may disturb unrelated cadence/persistent state.

    Exact hook/batching design should be reviewed before implementation.


F234 / provisional KI#557 -- SAME-ROOT SAVE/LOAD REFINEMENT
------------------------------------------------------------
The duplicate first-city vector/map divergence is SAVE-PERSISTENT.

F234 already established the runtime sequence:
    * first-city setFoundedFirstCity(true) performs a full owner-cache update;
    * CvPlayer::found later broadcasts AI_cityCreated for the same city;
    * reportCityCreated -> add(CvCity&) appends a second City wrapper;
    * m_cityMap::insert for the duplicate plot key fails silently;
    * m_cityList contains two allocated wrappers while m_cityMap owns/addresses only
      the first.

This pass checked serialization.

UWAICache::write serializes:
    pStream->Write(numCities());
    for (int i = 0; i < numCities(); i++)
        m_cityList[i]->write(pStream);

numCities() is the VECTOR size.

Therefore both duplicate wrappers are written to a manual save.

UWAICache::read then reconstructs all serialized vector entries:

    for (...)
    {
        m_cityList.push_back(new City);
        m_cityList[i]->read(pStream);
        m_cityMap.insert(std::make_pair(m_cityList[i]->getID(), m_cityList[i]));
    }

Again, duplicate map insertion is not checked. The vector is rebuilt with both
wrappers while only the first duplicate key wins the map entry.

cacheCitiesAfterRead subsequently does:

    for (...)
        cityAt(i).cacheCvCity();

Both wrappers relink to the SAME surviving real CvCity. It does not deduplicate or
rebuild the map/vector uniqueness invariant.

Consequences:
    * save/load does not heal F234;
    * the divergent vector/map representation can survive arbitrarily long through a
      manual save;
    * later removal still deletes only the map-owned first wrapper, leaving the
      duplicate vector wrapper able to become stale/dangling after the real city dies;
    * the crash/UAF window is therefore not restricted to the original founding round.

Keep this under F234. No new root number is needed.


ADVANCED START FOLLOW-UP -- REJECTED
-------------------------------------
A suspicious callback asymmetry was checked more fully:

    CvPlayer::found does not broadcast AI_cityCreated while Advanced Start points are
    active.

The first Advanced Start city can still trigger the first-city full refresh through
setFoundedFirstCity. Later Advanced Start cities can therefore be temporarily absent.

However, for a normal AI activation:
    * AI_doAdvancedStart executes before the normal elapsed-turn team doTurn;
    * team doTurn performs UWAI turnPre/full cache refresh before ordinary unit/war
      planning.

No concrete normal supported consumer was established between the later Advanced Start
city creation and that corrective refresh. Initial elapsed-turn-zero ordering likewise
did not establish a meaningful pre-refresh war consumer.

RESULT:
    Keep as a lifecycle oddity / negative control.
    Do not promote a root without a behaviorally live window.


RESIDUAL LEADER/TEAM-TRANSITION MATRIX
---------------------------------------

1. onTeamLeaderChanged and canBeHired -- ALREADY F215
    The function comments that CanBeHired / ReadyToCapitulate will be updated and
    should start false for the new leader.

    But m_abCanBeHiredAgainst is a default-true CivTeamMap, and the new leader's
    existing cache can contain its own prior state.

    This is precisely the already-recorded team-leader migration defect F215.
    Do not duplicate it as F237.

2. onTeamLeaderChanged persistent target-domain narrowing -- NO NEW ROOT
    The function copies selected leader-level state over TeamIter<MAJOR_CIV>, i.e.
    living major teams.

    Dead/revivable target-domain concerns are structurally similar to the already
    recorded migration/history roots F216/F228/F230.

    For warUtilityIgnoringDistraction specifically, ordinary cache refresh recomputes
    needed free-major targets; no independent durable behavioral reproduction was
    established here.

3. addTeam persistent target domain -- remains F216 refinement
    The absorbed leader's persistent team-keyed history needs a full persistent
    CivTeam target domain, as recorded in WIP19.

4. outsider references after Permanent Alliance -- remains F228
    No second independent migration mechanism was found in this pass.

5. ready-to-capitulate reset/reuse -- remains F213
    Current SAS source contains the custom full-clear fix recorded under F213.


OTHER NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SATURATION NOTES
-------------------------------------------

1. Trait free-promotion double-property else-if
    As noted above, current SAS data do not trigger the "combat AND city-defense on the

    MilitaryBranch objects are owner-bound rather than permanently leader/civ-bound,

    No additional independent old-format transition survived beyond:
        F229 -- compact bounty + pre-v9 narrowing;

    Current range checks from WIP20 remain clean.

7. City callback identity
    F234 now covers duplicate first-city identity and its save persistence.
    Remaining ordinary found/acquire/kill paths inspected in this pass did not establish
    a different vector/map identity failure.

SATURATION ASSESSMENT
    UWAICache.cpp is now substantially closer to first-pass closure:
        * ordinary refresh fields have been swept;
        * compact representations have been bounded;
        * save-version transitions have been inspected historically;
        * city create/destroy and knowledge/revelation lifecycles have been traced;
        * player revival, team merging, team-leader migration and True Starts identity
          transitions have been checked;
        * many apparent anomalies now resolve to existing roots rather than new ones.

    Because F235 and F236 are both substantial new lifecycle roots found in this pass,
    keep the file OPEN for one more residual pass instead of declaring closure in the

F237 / provisional KI#560
-------------------------
TITLE
    MilitaryBranch::Army is documented to include air units, but the incremental
    actual-unit census rejects ordinary aircraft because it tests ground getCombat();
    fighters, bombers and guided missiles therefore contribute zero cached Army power.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv/UWAI military-cache accounting defect.
    Present in current Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.
    The mismatch is already present in the original UWAI MilitaryBranch design.

DECLARED BRANCH CONTRACT
    MilitaryBranch.h describes Army explicitly:

        "Includes air and siege units."

    It also explains that Army tracks the full trained force before HomeGuard is split
    out.

    MilitaryBranch::updateTypicalUnit makes the intended distinction especially clear:

        // Siege and air units count for power but aren't typical
        if (kUnit.getCombat() <= 0 || ... ||
            kUnit.getDomainType() == DOMAIN_AIR ||
            kUnit.getDomainType() == DOMAIN_IMMOBILE)
        {
            continue;
        }

    In other words:
        * air units are deliberately excluded from selecting the representative
          "typical" Army unit;
        * they are nevertheless supposed to count in ACTUAL Army power.

ACTUAL REPORTING CONTRACT
    UWAICache::reportUnit forwards each unit creation/destruction to every military
    branch except HomeGuard.

    MilitaryBranch::reportUnit then admits a unit only when:

        if ((GC.getInfo(eUnit).getCombat() > 0 ||
             GC.getInfo(eUnit).isNuke()) &&
            isValidDomain(eUnit))
        {
            ...
            m_rTotalPower += rPowChange;
            m_iUnits += iChange;
        }

    Army::isValidDomain correctly allows:

        DOMAIN_LAND
        DOMAIN_AIR
        DOMAIN_IMMOBILE

    but the preceding getCombat() gate is ground-combat strength. Civ4 aircraft use
    iAirCombat/getAirCombat instead; ordinary aircraft normally have iCombat == 0.

CURRENT SAS DATA PROOF
    Current CIV4UnitInfos.xml contains these non-nuclear air combatants:

        UNIT_FIGHTER
            DOMAIN_AIR
            iCombat       0
            iAirCombat   12
            iPower       12
            bMilitaryProduction 1

        UNIT_JET_FIGHTER
            iCombat       0
            iAirCombat   24
            iPower       24

        UNIT_BOMBER
            iCombat       0
            iAirCombat   16
            iPower       16

        UNIT_STEALTH_BOMBER
            iCombat       0
            iAirCombat   20
            iPower       20

        UNIT_GUIDED_MISSILE
            iCombat       0
            iAirCombat   40
            iPower        6

    All pass Army's domain test and have positive XML power, but all fail the
    getCombat() > 0 / isNuke() admission gate.

    Tactical Nukes and ICBMs are admitted only through the explicit isNuke exception;
    that exception does not help ordinary air combatants.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE
    The Army branch is not a display statistic. Many WarUtilityAspect calculations use
    the present cached:

        getPowerValues()[ARMY]->power()

    directly for relative military strength, risk, tactical situation, intervention,
    vassal and other war-utility calculations.

    InvasionGraph::Node::initMilitary likewise copies the actual cached Army branch as
    the starting present force for its war simulation.

    Consequently a late-game empire can own a substantial Fighter/Bomber/Guided
    Missile force whose positive military power is completely absent from these cached
    Army totals.

HOME-GUARD SIDE EFFECT
    UWAICache::m_iNonNavalUnits DOES count those aircraft because its predicate is based
    on non-sea + bMilitaryProduction (excluding Recon), not getCombat().

    HomeGuard::initTotals also counts UNITAI_DEFENSE_AIR in its guard numerator.

    The current system can therefore have:
        denominator/headcount: includes aircraft
        Army power pool:       excludes ordinary aircraft

    For defensive Fighters this can additionally cause their headcount to raise the
    HomeGuard ratio while their own power is missing, shifting unrelated ground Army
    power into HomeGuard. Offensive aircraft can move the ratio in the other direction.
    This is a consequence of the same missing-air Army census, not a separate root.

ANCESTRY
    The historical MilitaryBranch implementation already used:

        (u.getCombat() > 0 || u.getNukeRange() >= 0)

    for actual unit-power updates while the contemporaneous Army class comment said:

        "Includes air force."

    The later scaled/UWAI rewrite changed names/types but preserved that predicate.
    Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains it.

    Thus this is not a SAS unit-data regression; current SAS aircraft merely make the
    inherited contract failure concrete.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Separate "is a military unit with branch power" from "has ground iCombat".

    For the generic actual-unit census, an admission check needs to include valid air
    combatants as well as ground combatants and nukes, while still letting each
    branch's unitPower/isValidDomain reject units that do not belong.

    Conceptually an admission predicate could include:
        getCombat() > 0
        OR getAirCombat() > 0
        OR isNuke()

    but implementation review should check unusual domains/special units rather than
    mechanically adopting that exact expression.

SAVE / MIGRATION WARNING
    MilitaryBranch actual unit count and total power are serialized.

    Existing saves produced by old code contain Army totals that OMIT existing ordinary
    aircraft. If patched code merely starts applying +1/-1 callbacks to aircraft after
    loading such a save, destroying or upgrading an aircraft that existed at save time
    will subtract power/count that was never present in the serialized Army total.

    Therefore the safe repair should also rebuild present MilitaryBranch inventories
    from the owner's actually existing units after loading/migration, or otherwise
    explicitly invalidate/reconstruct those totals.

    This overlaps naturally with F225's already-needed "rebuild unit-derived military
    cache" helper for revived players. A common reconstruction helper may repair both
    lifecycle problems cleanly without turning ordinary per-turn update into an
    expensive full unit scan.

DISTINCTION FROM F225
    F225:
        revival creates a fresh zero inventory and fails to replay units that already
        physically exist.

    F237:
        even during normal continuous play, ordinary aircraft are never admitted into
        Army actual-unit power in the first place.

    A shared reconstruction helper can be part of both repairs, but the admission
    predicate still has to be corrected or future aircraft creations remain missing.


F238 / provisional KI#561
-------------------------
TITLE
    HomeGuard computes one guard ratio from a unit-count population that includes
    nuclear weapons, then uses that same ratio to partition Army POWER after nuclear
    power has been removed; adding nukes can manufacture deployable conventional Army
    power without changing the conventional force.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited UWAI military-population mismatch.
    Present in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.
    The same structure is present in the original UWAI implementation.

CURRENT FLOW
    UWAICache::reportUnit increments m_iNonNavalUnits for a unit when:

        domain != DOMAIN_SEA
        bMilitaryProduction
        default UnitAI != UNITAI_EXPLORE

    No conventional-combat or non-nuclear check is applied.

    Current SAS ICBMs and Tactical Nukes satisfy the count predicate:
        ICBM          DOMAIN_IMMOBILE, bMilitaryProduction=1
        Tactical Nuke DOMAIN_AIR,      bMilitaryProduction=1

    Nukes are also intentionally counted in Army:
        Army::unitPower comment: "(Do include nukes in army)"
        MilitaryBranch::reportUnit admits nukes explicitly.

    They additionally have a separate NUCLEAR branch.

INCONSISTENT HOME-GUARD SPLIT
    InvasionGraph::Node::initMilitary calls:

        rGuardRatio = pHomeGuard->initTotals(
            m_kCache.numNonNavalUnits(),
            kCacheMilitary[ARMY]->power() -
            kCacheMilitary[NUCLEAR]->power());

    Thus the ratio denominator is a headcount that includes nukes, while the power pool
    being apportioned explicitly excludes all Nuclear-branch power.

    That one rGuardRatio is then reused to split both Army unit count and conventional
    Army power.

DETERMINISTIC EXAMPLE
    Suppose an empire has:
        5 conventional guard units
        5 conventional offensive units
        total conventional Army power P
        no nukes

    Then:
        non-naval headcount = 10
        guard count          = 5
        guard ratio          = 0.50
        HomeGuard power      = 0.50 P
        deployable conventional power ~= 0.50 P

    Now add 10 ICBMs, while leaving every conventional unit unchanged.

    Nuclear power is explicitly subtracted before the HomeGuard power split, so the
    conventional power pool remains P.

    But:
        non-naval headcount = 20
        guard count          = 5
        guard ratio          = 0.25

    The simulation now assigns:
        HomeGuard power      = 0.25 P
        conventional deployable share ~= 0.75 P

    Merely stockpiling immobile strategic missiles has made another quarter of the
    unchanged conventional military appear available for invasion.

WHY THIS IS DISTINCT FROM F237
    Fixing F237 so Fighters/Bombers enter Army power does not remove nuclear weapons
    from the headcount population while Nuclear power is excluded from the HomeGuard
    power pool.

    F238 therefore survives an F237 repair.

WHY A ONE-LINE "DON'T COUNT NUKES" FIX IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY SAFE
    The same rGuardRatio is also applied to:

        kCacheMilitary[ARMY]->numUnits()

    and Army's unit count currently includes nuclear units.

    Removing nukes only from m_iNonNavalUnits without changing the Army-headcount split
    can therefore create a different mismatch.

    The robust design likely needs explicit conventional non-naval headcount for the
    HomeGuard POWER split, and possibly separate handling for the simulated Army unit
    count instead of forcing one ratio to represent both populations.

ANCESTRY / DESIGN CONTEXT
    The original UWAI InvasionGraph already:
        * counted non-naval units;
        * subtracted Nuclear power;
        * applied one guard ratio to Army count and conventional Army power.

    Later rewrites preserve this arithmetic.

    The HomeGuard comment acknowledges that unit-count allocation is approximate, but
    F238 is stronger than "garrisons may be cheaper": the count and power populations
    are structurally different, and adding a unit whose entire power is deliberately
    excluded changes the partition of unchanged conventional power.


F239 / provisional KI#562
-------------------------
TITLE
    Team elimination ends wars through raw setAtWar(false) rather than makePeace;
    UWAICache::reportWarEnding is bypassed, so sponsored-war bounty/sponsor state can
    survive target death and later revival into an unrelated new war.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv/UWAI war-lifecycle cleanup defect.
    Present in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

NORMAL WAR-END CONTRACT
    CvTeam::makePeace invokes:

        AI().AI_preMakePeace(eTarget, pReparations);

    When UWAI is enabled/ready, CvTeamAI::AI_preMakePeace forwards both sides to:

        UWAI::Team::reportWarEnding

    which forwards to every living team member's UWAICache::reportWarEnding.

    That cache function unconditionally begins:

        // Forget sponsorship once a war ends
        m_aiBounty.set(eEnemy, 0);
        m_aeSponsorPerTarget.set(eEnemy, NO_PLAYER);

    These clears occur BEFORE any significance/duration test for past-war learning.
    Therefore the intended sponsorship lifetime is explicitly "until this war ends",
    including an otherwise insignificant/short peace.

ELIMINATION BYPASSES THAT CONTRACT
    When a team's alive count reaches zero, CvTeam::changeAliveCount ends its wars
    directly:

        kLoopTeam.setAtWar(getID(), false);
        setAtWar(kLoopTeam.getID(), false);
        ... clear war plans ...

    It does not call makePeace, AI_preMakePeace or UWAI::Team::reportWarEnding.

    The eliminated player's own UWAI cache is later uninitialized, but the SURVIVING
    enemy/hireling caches are not. Their bounty/sponsor entries keyed by the now-dead
    target remain.

REVIVAL MAKES THE STALE KEY LIVE AGAIN
    AdvCiv supports dead-player/team revival.

    Current SAS revival correctly initializes and refreshes UWAI caches (including the
    KI#475.3/F225 work), but ordinary cache.update/clear(true) deliberately preserves
    asynchronously maintained:

        m_aiBounty
        m_aeSponsorPerTarget

    A later declaration of war against the revived target does not clear those fields
    either.

    Therefore the old sponsorship can survive:
        paid war A
        -> target elimination
        -> target revival
        -> unrelated war B

LIVE CONSUMER
    WarUtilityAspect::HiredHand, when considering peace in war B, reads:

        ourCache().sponsorAgainst(eTheirTeam)
        ourCache().bountyAgainst(eTheirTeam)

    If the stored sponsor is still alive and sufficiently liked, HiredHand treats the
    old payment as an obligation to continue fighting.

    Its duration calculation uses the CURRENT war's at-war counters, so revival/new-war
    state does not naturally age out the old obligation. The old bounty can become
    behaviorally strong again as if sponsor S had paid for war B.

SUPPORTED SEQUENCE
    1. Sponsor S pays AI/team H to declare war on target team T.
    2. H fights T.
    3. T's final living member is eliminated.
    4. changeAliveCount removes H-T war with raw setAtWar(false); H's cache never
       receives reportWarEnding(T).
    5. H retains sponsor S and bounty against dead team T.
    6. T is later revived.
    7. H and T enter a later unrelated war.
    8. H considers peace. HiredHand sees S's ancient sponsorship and adds utility to
       continue the new war.

    Ordinary HiredHand conditions still apply; this finding does not claim every such
    revived war is forcibly prolonged. The defect is reuse of a paid-war contract whose
    documented cleanup boundary -- the end of the sponsored war -- was skipped.

PAST-WAR HISTORY REFINEMENT
    The same elimination path also bypasses the normal reportWarEnding computation of
    m_aiPastWarScore.

    If T never returns, history keyed to T is behaviorally irrelevant. Upon revival,
    however, confidenceFromPastWars(T) can again be consulted, and the decisive prior
    war ending may be absent from learned confidence.

    Keep this under F239 as an additional consequence of bypassing the normal UWAI
    war-end event; the sponsored-war stale contract is already the strongest
    deterministic proof.

SCENARIO-START SIBLING PATH
    There is a second, narrower cleanup asymmetry.

    CvDeal records TRADE_WAR sponsorship whenever UWAI is ENABLED:

        bool const bReportUWAI = getUWAI().isEnabled();
        ...
        reportSponsoredWar(...);

    This does not require UWAI::isReady().

    CvTeamAI::AI_declareWarTrade likewise routes to UWAI declareWarTrade when enabled;
    it has no top-level isReady guard.

    But AI_preMakePeace reports the war ending only when:

        getUWAI().isEnabled() && getUWAI().isReady()

    UWAI::isReady deliberately returns false during the first two elapsed turns of a
    scenario.

    Therefore an otherwise valid sponsored war recorded during that startup window can
    end by ordinary makePeace while its bounty/sponsor cleanup is skipped.

    This is the same lifetime contract violation as F239, reached through a different
    bypass, so do NOT allocate a new root. A robust repair should distinguish
    "war-evaluation history needs ready caches" from "transient paid-war obligation must
    be cleared whenever the war ends."

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Ensure every semantically real war termination clears transient UWAI war-contract
    state for surviving caches, including elimination.

    Do not simply call the current full reportWarEnding blindly from a state where its
    war-success/reparation assumptions are invalid; an explicit lifecycle helper may be
    cleaner:
        * always clear bounty/sponsor at war termination;
        * separately record past-war success only when the required history/context is
          valid.

    For elimination, if pastWarScore learning should be preserved, invoke that part
    while the old war-success/context still exists and before low-level state is erased.

    For scenario startup, do not gate sponsorship cleanup itself on isReady merely
    because the war-evaluation/history component is not ready.


F196 / KI#519 -- CROSS-FILE REVALIDATION, NOT F240
---------------------------------------------------
While auditing m_readyToCapitulateTo from UWAICache.cpp, a seemingly strong new root was
reconstructed:

    * considerCapitulation sets ReadyToCapitulate(H)=true for a human master and leaves
      it true after a successful AI-turn decision;
    * ordinary peace does not clear it;
    * reviewWarPlans clears it only after an early "no war plans" return;
    * a later unrelated war can therefore reuse the old authorization and bypass
      AI_surrenderTrade's "considerPeace must have run this AI turn" gate.

Before assigning F240, the earlier audit album was searched.

This exact lifecycle is already:
    F196 / provisional KI#519
    "Human-capitulation readiness persists across peace, so a later war can inherit an
     obsolete considerPeace authorization and bypass UWAI's AI-turn surrender gate."

The earlier entry contains the same war-A -> peace -> war-B reproduction, the same
willTalk ordering consequence and the same recommended reportWarEnding clear.

RESULT
    Independently revalidated from the cache side.
    No duplicate root.
    F240 remains UNUSED.

This also reinforces why F213 is distinct:
    F196 = ordinary live-game war lifetime;
    F213 = full cache reset / save-load object reuse.
Current SAS already carries the F213 full-reset fix; F196 remains the separate lifecycle
finding in the album.


F231 / KI#554 -- TARGET-VALUE SAME-ROOT REFINEMENT
---------------------------------------------------
F231 already proves that incremental city create/destroy callbacks fail to recompute
surviving cached foreign-city deployment geometry when the cache owner's city set
changes.

The residual pass found another derived field at the same invalidation boundary:
    City::m_iTargetValue

City construction computes m_iTargetValue once via:

    GET_PLAYER(eCacheOwner).AI_targetCityValue(kCity, false, true, this);

AI_targetCityValue depends on dynamic city/strategic properties including:
    * whether kCity is the capital;
    * war-plan type;
    * national wonders;
    * ownership/cultural adjacency;
    * owner victory stages;
    * Space-victory capital status;
    * city defensive strength;
    * cached distance/reachability.

When an enemy capital is destroyed/captured, the existing cache callbacks remove the old
capital BEFORE CvCity::kill later calls the victim's findNewCapital().

The surviving cached wrapper for the newly selected capital is not reconstructed.
It therefore retains the target value computed when that city was NOT the capital,
despite AI_targetCityValue having several explicit capital-specific branches.

No new root:
    This is another surviving-City derived value invalidated by the same incomplete
    incremental city lifecycle as F231.

Repair implication:
    F231's targeted post-city-set-change reconstruction should reconsider target value
    as well as distance/reachability/reachable-city totals before final resorting.


F236 / KI#559 -- PROPAGATED-CONTACT REPAIR-DOMAIN REFINEMENT
-------------------------------------------------------------
F236 establishes that newly knowable existing foreign cities are not inserted into
UWAICache when contact/map knowledge changes.

The final contact sweep confirms that a repair cannot assume only the directly meeting
two teams are affected.

CvTeam::meet can propagate knowledge through master/vassal relationships, and vassal
setup synchronizes third-party contacts through additional meet calls.

Thus one diplomacy/contact event can make cities newly eligible for caches belonging to
multiple related teams/members.

No new root:
    This broadens F236's invalidation set. A repair should dirty/rebuild every cache
    whose effective known-team/city-deduction set changes after propagation, rather
    than updating only the initiating pair.


OTHER RESIDUAL CHECKS / NEGATIVE CONTROLS
------------------------------------------

1. Human-capitulation lifetime candidate
    Deduplicated to F196 as described above.

2. Sponsorship in multi-member teams
    CvDeal records the payment in the specific signing player's cache, and
    WarEvaluator evaluates HiredHand once per agent-team member, summing those member
    contributions. This produces one paid obligation for the player who actually
    received the deal rather than automatically multiplying it by team size.

    A signing player's later elimination while teammates survive raises a policy
    question about whether the team's moral/strategic obligation should transfer, but
    no clear original contract proving such transfer was found. Do not promote.

3. MilitaryBranch::canEmploy
    canEmploy still uses getCombat()>0, but the only current live caller found is
    ArmamentForecast's Cavalry check against Army's typical unit. Army typical units
    intentionally exclude air/immobile units, so this does not create a second F237
    path with current callers.

4. Recon mismatch in m_iNonNavalUnits
    The earlier C019 note remains: combat Recon is excluded from the non-naval
    denominator while Army can include it. This is an explicit original "exclude Recon"
    approximation. No stronger deterministic decision error was established here.
    F237/F238 are structurally sharper and do not convert this old note into a root.

5. Packed MilitaryBranch save version
    Current typical-unit packing uses a 1000 enum stride. Current SAS has far fewer
    than 1000 UnitTypes. The version-0 reader also has an explicit raw-value branch,
    unlike F232's City decoder. No current compatibility root.

6. Apparent duplicate legacy m_aiAdjLandPlots read
    Reopened against authoritative source and original enum-map history.
    The source contains one legacy read, not two; the earlier visual duplication came
    from overlapping/combined output. Rejected.

7. Ordinary unit conversion staging
    Remains the prior F216 negative control. No live consumer was found between the
    balanced +1/-1 conversion callbacks on supported normal upgrade/gift paths.

8. Full old-save top-level field matrix
    No new independent transition survived beyond F229/F230/F232 and F229's pre-v9
    narrowing refinement.

PURPOSE
-------
Preserve the resolved TeamPathFinder/maxLandDist investigation before continuing the
remaining queue-031 closure pass.

The finding below is unusually well supported by the historical transition:
the pre-refactor code explicitly treated maxLandDist as a travel-duration horizon and
expanded the pathfinder's tile-count upper bound by estimated movement speed; the

F240 / provisional KI#563
-------------------------
TITLE
    The 2020 TeamPathFinder refactor lost the movement-speed expansion of UWAI's LAND
    search horizon: maxLandDist is a travel-duration threshold, but it is now also used
    as a raw tile-count cap, so road/rail land targets beyond that many plots can be
    classified as naval or unreachable even when deployment takes far fewer turns.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv/UWAI refactor regression.
    Present in current Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.
    Introduced by AdvCivPreSAS commit 2604, 0866f78275,
        "Use TeamPathFinder for UWAI distance computations".

CURRENT CODE
    UWAICache::resetTeamPathFinders currently sets:

        int const iSeaLimit = getUWAI().maxSeaDist() * shipSpeed();
        int const iLandLimit = getUWAI().maxLandDist();

        landFinder.reset(..., iLandLimit);
        anyWaterFinder.reset(..., iSeaLimit);
        shallowWaterFinder.reset(..., iSeaLimit);

    TeamPathFinder's class contract explicitly says:

        "The length of a path is the number of plots entered (not counting the start),
         i.e. the speed (base moves) of the units doesn't matter and no travel time
         (number of turns) is computed."

    StepMetricBase/KmodPathFinder enforce that limit on PathNode::getPathLength().
    TeamStepMetric initializes path length to 0 and increments it uniformly by one per
    entered plot.

    Therefore a LAND finder reset with maxLandDist=N cannot return any route entering
    more than N plots, regardless of the route movement cost.

BUT LAND PATH COST IS EXPLICITLY ROUTE-AWARE
    TeamStepMetric<LAND>::cost starts at MOVE_DENOMINATOR, but when both plots have
    usable non-enemy routes it substitutes the route movement cost plus the team's
    route movement modifier.

    Current SAS route data, for example:
        Road:
            iMovement = 30
            Engineering change = -10
        Railroad:
            iMovement = 20

    Thus a long route can have travel cost far below one turn per entered plot.

    City::updateDistance consumes precisely that route-aware path cost as estimated
    deployment duration:

        iPairwDuration =
            landFinder.getPathCost() / MOVE_DENOMINATOR

    and later stores a weighted travel-duration estimate in m_iDistance.

    So two different metrics are currently being mixed:
        search admissibility: raw number of entered plots <= maxLandDist
        resulting distance: route-aware movement duration in turns

HISTORICAL CONTRACT BEFORE THE REFACTOR
    Immediately before commit 2604, City::measureDistance explicitly distinguished the
    travel horizon from the pathfinder's step-count horizon.

    It first chose:
        maxDist = maxLandDist or maxSeaDist

    and, in later eras, deliberately increased maxDist by 4/3 so remote targets
    remained targetable.

    It then computed:
        stepDist = geometric step distance
        speedEstimate = estimateMovementSpeed(...)

    and rejected only when:

        stepDist / speedEstimate > maxDist

    Most importantly, its call into the old FAStar-based team pathfinder said:

        /* Path distance counts each step as 1 move; upper bound needs to
           account for faster movement. */
        ceil(maxDist * speedEstimate)

    That comment is the exact old invariant that commit 2604 lost.

OLD LAND SPEED MODEL
    The deleted estimateMovementSpeed function returned 1 for primitive unroaded land,
    but deliberately increased land speed as infrastructure improved:

        Classical+:
            up to roughly 2x from roads;
            Fast Roads multiplied that further.

        Industrial / railroad age:
            roughly 4.5x expected land speed.

        Future:
            another factor of two before the railroad multiplier.

    Therefore the old LAND pathfinder could search many more than maxLandDist tiles
    when the estimated travel time was still within maxLandDist turns.

    For Industrial-era land, the old path-length upper bound could be on the order of:
        maxDist * 4.5
    and maxDist itself was raised by 4/3 from era 4 onward.

THE REFACTOR CHANGE
    Commit 2604 replaced that code with TeamPathFinder.

    SEA received:

        seaLimit = maxSeaDist * shipSpeed

    LAND received:

        landLimit = maxLandDist

    The new TeamPathFinder had already documented that max path length is plot count,
    not movement duration. Its LAND cost function also already modeled routes.

    This is exactly the situation in which the old comment said the upper bound must
    be expanded for faster movement.

    Commit 2605 then deleted estimateMovementSpeed/measureDistance as obsolete.

    Commit 2606 made "Minor tweaks to UWAI distance computation", changing
    maxLandDist to maxSeaDist - 1 and adjusting the final cached-distance clamp, but it
    left the raw LAND path-length cap unchanged. No later historical change found in
    the reachable history redefined maxLandDist as a geometric tile radius.

CURRENT SEMANTIC EVIDENCE THAT maxLandDist IS STILL A TURN/DURATION THRESHOLD
    Current consumers compare m_iDistance -- which City::updateDistance derives from
    path COST / MOVE_DENOMINATOR -- against maxLandDist.

    Examples:
        ArmamentForecast:
            if target distance > maxLandDist -> naval armament

        UWAI::Team::isLandTarget:
            cached travel distance <= maxLandDist

        InvasionGraph::Node::canReachByLand:
            cached distance <= maxLandDist unless no deep-sea cargo

    Therefore maxLandDist still acts as a strategic deployment-duration threshold in
    current code. It has not become a pure geometric path-length constant.

SUPPORTED REPRODUCTION SHAPE
    On a common wrapped map with dimensions <=100, current:
        maxSeaDist = 15
        maxLandDist = 14

    Consider a same-area enemy city whose shortest land route from every significant
    source city enters 16 plots.

    Suppose roughly four of those steps are in enemy territory, where routes are
    intentionally ignored, and twelve are on usable Road/Railroad infrastructure.

    With MOVE_DENOMINATOR-scale full-cost enemy steps and route cost around one third of
    a full move, the route-aware deployment cost is roughly:

        4 full-cost steps + 12 * (1/3) move
        ~= 8 turns

    That is comfortably below the 14-turn strategic horizon.

    Current behavior:
        landFinder max path length = 14 plots
        16-plot path is not returned at all
        -> m_bReachByLand remains false for that source.

    Pre-2604 behavior:
        the step-count upper bound was multiplied by estimated land movement speed;
        such a route was within the search horizon and its duration was then reduced
        according to infrastructure-era movement speed.

    No exotic map size or overflow is required; distances moderately above 14 plots
    are ordinary on Standard-and-larger maps.

BEHAVIORAL CONSEQUENCES
    If every significant owner city is beyond the raw tile cap:

    * A same-continent coastal target can be treated as naval because the valid fast
      land path is never found; ArmamentForecast can consequently prepare naval rather
      than land armament.

    * A landlocked target can be left with m_iDistance == -1 if no sea/mixed path
      supplies an alternative, causing the cache and UWAI reachability logic to treat
      a strategically nearby-by-rail rival as unreachable.

    * m_aiReachableCities can consequently undercount reachable foreign cities.

    * InvasionGraph land topology and deployment modeling use
      canReachByLand/canReachByLandFromCapital/getDistance and inherit the false
      negative.

    * UWAI::Team::isLandTarget can fail to recognize a long-but-fast same-continent
      target as a land target.

    This can be especially visible in the industrial/modern game, exactly when roads
    and railroads make tile count diverge most from travel duration.

CROSS-FILE SAME-ROOT SIBLING: UWAIAgent::alignAreaAI
    The same commit 2604 changed an "easily reachable target" check from:

        measureDistance(..., DOMAIN_LAND, ..., &d);
        round(d / estimateMovementSpeed(...)) <= 8

    to:

        TeamPathFinder<LAND> pf(..., 8);
        if (pf.generatePath(...))
            ...

    The old test was explicitly <=8 estimated travel turns.
    The new test is <=8 entered plots.

    Therefore a 9+ tile capital-to-target route that takes <=8 turns because of roads
    is no longer considered "easily reachable" in this alignment decision.

    This is the same refactor invariant loss, not a second root number. It lives in
    UWAIAgent.cpp, whose first-pass audit is already closed, so preserve it here as a
    cross-file F240 scope refinement rather than inventing a duplicate finding.

BASELINE COMPARISON
    Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains:
        iSeaLimit = maxSeaDist * shipSpeed
        iLandLimit = maxLandDist

    and the same TeamPathFinder length contract.

    SAS inherited the behavior. K-Mod/Civ4CE do not carry the same UWAI deployment
    cache/refactor and therefore do not provide a direct equivalent.

WHY THIS IS NOT MERELY "PATHFINDING IS APPROXIMATE"
    UWAI deliberately approximates terrain and route movement, but the specific
    invariant here was explicit before the refactor:

        the geometric path upper bound must account for movement speed.

    The replacement pathfinder actually improves route-cost modeling, yet the raw
    tile-count cap prevents that better model from ever evaluating long fast routes.

    The asymmetric SEA treatment strengthens the proof: sea path length is still
    multiplied by ship speed precisely because TeamPathFinder max length counts plots.
    LAND lacks the corresponding expansion despite route-aware movement.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Do not simply remove all path limits; deployment pathfinding is a documented
    performance hotspot, especially in very large/high-player-count games.

    Preserve a computational tile-count horizon that is large enough to admit paths
    whose route-aware travel COST can still fall within the intended strategic
    duration.

    Possible implementation directions:
        * derive a conservative LAND step cap from maxLandDist and plausible current
          land route speed, analogous to the old maxDist * speedEstimate;
        * or extend the pathfinder so this use can impose a cost/duration ceiling
          rather than a raw step ceiling, while retaining a separate generous
          geometric safety cap.

    City::updateDistance already uses path cost to compute deployment duration, so once
    the path is admitted it has the correct metric available.

    For alignAreaAI, merely enlarging the path-length cap is not sufficient: the old
    semantic test was <=8 travel turns. After finding a sufficiently generous land
    route, compare route-aware path cost against an 8-turn threshold.

    Any repair should be benchmarked on 36/48-civ large maps because commit 2604's main
    purpose was a major UWAI pathfinding performance improvement.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SCOPE
    * Primitive unroaded paths, where cost is about one move per entered plot, are
      largely unaffected; the metrics coincide there.
    * Paths already <=maxLandDist tiles are not rejected by this specific defect.
    * Enemy-owned route segments intentionally receive full movement cost in
      TeamStepMetric and are not evidence for F240.
    * F226 is different: it concerns which available path is selected / how path
      direction and route ownership affect one City::updateDistance computation.
      F240 concerns a valid fast path being excluded before its cost can be evaluated.
    * F231 is different: it concerns failure to recompute cached geometry after the
      cache owner's city set changes.
    * F190 is different: it concerns a team-member loop leaking the no-ocean-cargo
      max-distance exemption into later members.
    * This does not claim that every route beyond maxLandDist plots should be used;
      only that raw tile count cannot stand in for the documented movement-duration
      horizon when route-aware cost says the path is strategically short.


OTHER CLOSURE CHECKS COMPLETED BEFORE F240
------------------------------------------
The pass leading into F240 also revalidated several apparent seams as clean:

* Advanced Start city founding:
    CvPlayer::found suppresses incremental AI_cityCreated while Advanced Start points
    remain active, but ordinary UWAI war-planning turnPre is itself unavailable during
    setup/turn-zero initialization. The first real cache.update reconstructs setup
    cities before normal UWAI planning consumes the cache. Not a root.

* GET_TEAM(m_eOwner) / leaderCache:
    An intermediate suspicion that PlayerTypes was being used as a raw TeamTypes index
    was rejected. The project intentionally provides GET_TEAM(PlayerTypes) semantics
    through TEAMID. The earlier album had already retracted old F113/KI#436; that
    retraction remains correct.

* reportWarEnding reparations if/else-if:
    AI_preMakePeace intentionally calls one side with (received,NULL) and the other
    with (NULL,given). The mutually exclusive branches encode direction and do not
    discard a simultaneous second list.

* updateCanBeHiredAgainst:
    Although setter routing and updater storage look asymmetric, normal UWAI::Team
    scheduling updates this leader-only state on the team leader's cache. No new root.

* m_iNonNavalUnits zero-power junk:
    Current SAS unit XML was checked after F237/F238. No additional ordinary
    zero-ground/zero-air/non-nuclear bMilitaryProduction units were found slipping into
    the denominator beyond the already documented air/nuclear accounting roots.

* m_aiWarUtilityIgnoringDistraction MIN_INT sentinel:
    Current consumers either query targets expected to have been evaluated, normalize
    vassal/master/current-war targeting appropriately, or clamp the sentinel
    conservatively. No favorable-war decision from an uncomputed sentinel was proved.

* ScaledNum rewrite archaeology:
    The old updateWarAnger wrong-team-size divisor was independently rediscovered in
    the historical 2920 rewrite but is already F112/KI#435 and is fixed in current
    SAS. Other suspicious algebra changes mapped onto existing F219/F222/F223 or
    historically corrected follow-up commits. No duplicate root was allocated.

QUEUE-031 FINDING INDEX
-----------------------

F213 / provisional KI#536
    Full UWAICache reset did not clear m_readyToCapitulateTo, allowing a new game or
    loaded save in the same process to inherit human-capitulation authorization.
    Current staged SAS source contains the reviewed full-reset repair.

F214 / provisional KI#537
    MilitaryBranch typical-unit refresh is sticky when no currently trainable
    replacement exists; stale capability can survive loss of prerequisites.

F215 / provisional KI#538
    Team-leader migration fails to initialize/migrate CanBeHired according to its
    explicit "new leader starts disabled" contract.

F216 / provisional KI#539
    Permanent Alliance addTeam migration iterates an already-merged membership state
    and can self-add/double absorbed-leader history.
    Later refinement: the persistent TARGET-team domain also needs dead/revivable team
    keys rather than only currently alive major teams.

F217 / provisional KI#540
    Fallout discovery by "first feature with <= -50 health" aliases SAS Jungle after
    Jungle became -50 health, causing wrong scrub-tech/nuclear-damage reasoning.

F218 / provisional KI#541
    Transport capability can be cached from player-level trainability despite actual
    city/resource prerequisites, producing false ocean-lift reachability in SAS.

F219 / provisional KI#542
    goldPerProdVictory checks peaceful-victory stage 3 before cumulative stage 4,
    making stage-4 valuation branches unreachable.

F220 / provisional KI#543
    Nuclear deterrence in teamThreat checks only the cache owner's personal nukes,
    ignoring retaliation capability supplied by a teammate/master-side partner.

F221 / provisional KI#544
    Target-mission counting can count loaded cargo both through the transport and
    through the cargo unit's own still-enumerable selection group.

F222 / provisional KI#545
    ScaledNum rewrite changed goldPerProdSites parentheses, dividing the whole
    site-weight-plus-settler expression by 10 instead of only the settler term.

F223 / provisional KI#546
    ScaledNum rewrite changed CanBeHired hysteresis probability from
        1 - delta / 100
    to
        (1 - delta) / 100,
    collapsing the intended persistence anti-flicker behavior.

F224 / provisional KI#547
    Incremental city conquest/destruction keeps the detailed city set current but
    leaves m_rTotalAssets stale until the next full refresh.

F225 / provisional KI#548
    Revived players receive a fresh empty UWAI military inventory but existing
    physical units are not replayed into it; later destruction can even drive counts
    and power negative.

F226 / provisional KI#549
    City::updateDistance can treat the existence of a shorter locally valid land path
    as reason not to retain a valid sea path even when that land path is forbidden from
    establishing strategic reachability.

F227 / provisional KI#550
    Incremental city destruction erases an entry from the stateful attack-priority
    ordering without re-sorting surviving cities.

F228 / provisional KI#551
    Permanent Alliance migration is one-way for persistent team-keyed history:
    outsider caches that reference the absorbed team are not remapped to the survivor.

F229 / provisional KI#552
    Sponsored-war bounty is narrowed from full int utility to signed short without
    representability checking; large legal payments can wrap and erase sponsorship.
    Later refinement: pre-v9 old-save full-int bounty values can narrow during read.

F230 / provisional KI#553
    Pre-v4 pastWarScore migration multiplies only teams alive at load, although the
    original migration converted every serialized team slot; dead/revivable rival
    history can remain at 1/100 scale.

F231 / provisional KI#554
    Incremental own-city-set changes update only the changed cache entry and leave
    surviving foreign targets' deployment geometry and reachable-city aggregate stale.
    Later refinement: target value can also go stale, especially when a new capital is
    selected after the old capital is lost.

F232 / provisional KI#555
    Version-0 City records stored raw distance, but the versioned reader always applies
    the new "-1" unpacking transform; legacy distance 1 becomes the own-team sentinel 0.

F233 / provisional KI#556
    Incremental reportCityCreated omits the full-refresh human known-city rule; an AI
    can temporarily model a human through a human cache missing a newly founded city.

F234 / provisional KI#557
    First-city full refresh followed by the ordinary city-created callback can insert
    the same city twice, diverging vector and ID-map ownership and enabling a dangling
    cached City after same-round destruction.

F235 / provisional KI#558
    Cached offensive/defensive trait flags are not refreshed when True Starts changes
    the player's leader after UWAI initialization.

F236 / provisional KI#559
    Contact/map-revelation transitions can make pre-existing cities newly knowable
    without adding them to the cache, producing false zero reachability.
    Later refinement: master/vassal contact propagation broadens the invalidation set.

F237 / provisional KI#560
    Army is explicitly documented to include air units, but actual-unit accounting
    admits ground getCombat()>0 or nukes only; ordinary Fighters/Bombers/Guided
    Missiles contribute zero cached Army power.

F238 / provisional KI#561
    HomeGuard uses a headcount denominator that includes nuclear weapons to partition
    Army power after nuclear power has been removed; adding nukes can manufacture
    deployable conventional power.

F239 / provisional KI#562
    Team elimination ends war through raw setAtWar(false), bypassing the normal
    reportWarEnding sponsorship cleanup; stale paid-war state can survive target death,
    revival and a later unrelated war.
    A scenario-start isReady gate supplies a narrower sibling cleanup bypass.

F240 / provisional KI#563
    TeamPathFinder refactor changed LAND's search horizon from a movement-speed-expanded
    travel-duration search into raw maxLandDist plot count, while route-aware path cost
    is still interpreted as deployment turns. Long fast road/rail targets can therefore
    be excluded before their low travel cost is evaluated.
    Same-root UWAIAgent::alignAreaAI sibling: old <=8 estimated-turn test became <=8
    entered plots.
