FINAL ROOT-OVERLAP / INDEPENDENCE REVIEW
----------------------------------------
The final convergence pass challenged the live findings against one another by asking
whether each root can reproduce while the nearest-looking sibling is neutralized. No
root needed to be merged or retracted beyond the already-retired F263.

Naval accounting cluster:

    F261 versus F262:
        DISTINCT.
        F261 is produced by asymmetric confidence conversion of attacker LOGISTICS
        casualties. It reproduces with repeat-trip amplification neutralized.

        F262 is produced by operation ordering: pre-battle cargo capacity is multiplied
        for repeat trips before destroyed transport capacity is subtracted. It reproduces
        at confidence 1, where F261 disappears.

    F264 versus F261/F262:
        DISTINCT.
        F264 lives on the coastal-bombardment / no-landing defender path. Transport hulls
        may contribute to and be removed from FLEET while LOGISTICS is left unchanged,
        allowing stale cargo capacity to survive into a later outgoing invasion.
        It does not require the attacker LOGISTICS confidence conversion of F261 or the
        repeat-trip ordering of F262.

Overlapping-branch cluster:

    F260 versus F265:
        DISTINCT.
        F260 is the later battle-area projection: attacker ARMY is area-weighted while
        overlapping CAVALRY is not. It reproduces with deployment attenuation neutral.

        F265 is the earlier deployment-distance attenuation: attacker ARMY is reduced
        while overlapping CAVALRY is not. It reproduces with battle-area weight 1.
        Its repair scope remains deliberately attacker-focused; changing defender
        CAVALRY requires mirroring the later defender-ARMY retreat-to-city undo.

    F266 versus F260/F265:
        DISTINCT.
        F266 concerns HOME_GUARD plus the separate virtual emergency-defense pool and
        the cumulative base-branch loss cap. It needs neither CAVALRY nor the Army
        availability transforms of F260/F265.

Cycle / confidence cluster:

    F255 versus F256:
        DISTINCT.
        F255 swaps ownership of already-computed `this`/target Army portions when writing
        cycle distraction state. It reproduces even if those portions were calculated
        correctly.

        F256 changes the portion values themselves through the practical-2923 `*=`
        regression. It reproduces before any F255 distraction assignment is consumed.

    F257 versus F261:
        DISTINCT.
        Both expose confidence-space conversion errors, but in separate branch/state
        systems: F257 converts open-field/cycle ARMY clash losses back to persistent
        physical Army power without undoing confidence, whereas F261 converts attacker
        transport/LOGISTICS casualties. Either can reproduce with the other branch absent.

Deployment / route / horizon cluster:

    F254 versus F268:
        DISTINCT.
        F254 is a resolveLosses time-horizon error after a genuinely naval step exists:
        the defender-zero preliminary probe is not guaranteed to be a lower-duration
        bound and `break` can erase an in-horizon real combat.

        F268 occurs earlier, while classifying the route: a land-existence boolean is
        combined with a best-route distance that may belong to sea travel, turning sea
        duration into a nominal land invasion and bypassing naval modeling entirely.
        F254 reproduces with route classification already correct; F268 reproduces before
        the F254 probe/horizon logic matters.

    F259 versus F265:
        DISTINCT.
        F259 is the clash-distance split itself going negative on the defender side when
        attacker personality weighting expands one half beyond the fixed total; this can
        violate `uround` assumptions and boost defender power above 100%.
        F265 needs only an ordinary positive attacker deployment attenuation and the
        missing CAVALRY sibling transform.

Graph lifecycle / target cluster:

    F251 versus F267:
        DISTINCT.
        F251 requires a terminal/eliminated/capitulated node that retains an outgoing
        edge and can act as a zombie attacker.

        F267 requires a still-surviving node after a partial third-party conquest. The
        source says its offensive stops and its Army returns to defense, but its outgoing
        edge remains live and can later receive a fresh local horizon. No terminal-node
        condition is needed.

Ownership / observer cluster:

    F252 versus F258:
        DISTINCT.
        F252 calculates attacker's post-conquest occupation power from defender-owned
        representative Army power / adjacent defender-era quantity.
        F258 reads the evaluating graph agent's Defensive trait when modifying a different
        defender's city defense. Separate producer sites, state and consumers.

Spatial-state cluster:

    F268 versus F269:
        DISTINCT.
        F268 is missing route-type-specific distance state (`distByLand`) and contaminates
        route classification / clash distance / ArmamentForecast.
        F269 is missing simulated per-area city inventory after hypothetical conquests and
        contaminates area availability, rally caps and clash-area selection.

Speculative-state / emergency cluster:

    F253 versus F266:
        DISTINCT.
        F253 is a query-side mutation: speculative `step()` halves another node's
        emergency-defense power even when the step is discarded.
        F266 reproduces using actually-applied sequential assaults: casualties inflicted
        on emergency defenders can be clipped away by the HOME_GUARD base-power cap.

No additional independent producer -> state -> consumer contradiction survived the final
pass. In particular, the following late candidates remained controls rather than roots:
    * omitted `scaled` initializers are zero-safe by type construction;
    * player-typed GET_TEAM calls are safe through the overload / TEAMID conversion;
    * phase-boundary emergency-defense reset is consistent with ArmamentForecast timing;
    * LOGISTICS need not mechanically receive the same front portion as ARMY/FLEET;
    * conquest occupation shifts do not create a separate persistent CAVALRY consumer
      because each later step reconstructs availability and clamps CAVALRY <= ARMY;
    * defender CAVALRY deployment asymmetry is already a repair-boundary concern of F265,
      not a second independent current root;
    * stable real-map population average is historically intentional city-importance
      modeling, unlike F269's concrete stale per-area inventory contradiction;
    * the inverted teammate recursion in setCapitulated remains dormant under the live
      `getAliveCount() <= 1` capitulation caller contract;
    * post-2920 operator/condition archaeology found the known F256 regression and known
      later upstream repairs, but no further live semantic migration bug.

         getSASVictoryStageLevel and per-victory wrappers
         getSASTeamMaxVictoryStage
         getSASTeamSpaceVictoryStage
         getSASTeamSpaceshipPartsBuilt / Required / Percent
         getSASVictoryDelayTurnsFromNormalGameSpeed
         getSASLeadingSpaceshipPartsBuilt
         isSASTeamStage3SpaceVictoryThreat
         isSASUWAIVictoryDenialPeaceThreat
         getSASTeamStage3SpaceLeaderPartGap

    3. Minor formatting-only signature collapses.

    4. `baseYieldToSymbol` caches MAX_YIELD_STACK in a local static const.
       The function is documented unused in current BtS/AdvCiv; no live issue inferred.

    5. `getTurnMonthForGame` hoists the current CvGameSpeedInfo and increment count;
       behavior is equivalent for valid game-speed XML. CALENDAR_WEEKS caches the
       WEEKS_PER_MONTHS define in a local static const.

    6. SAS UnitAI enum renames in getUnitAIString.

Everything else in the old high-fanout utility/PUF region is essentially Base AdvCiv
rather than a broad SAS rewrite. Therefore the audit should treat the file as two layers:

    A. SAS-added helper contracts and their cross-file consumers;
    B. inherited AdvCiv/K-Mod/vanilla utility and PUF contracts, compared against K-Mod
       and Civ4CE for missed fixes.

CROSS-FILE DEDUP CONTROL -- F250 ALREADY OWNS THE BROKEN LOCAL INVASIONGRAPH EXTRACTOR
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The current shared helper in this file:

    getSASVictoryStageLevel(...)

correctly checks cumulative victory-stage bits highest-to-lowest (stage4 -> stage1).

Queue 023's F250 is NOT a defect in this shared helper. F250 owns a separate old local
InvasionGraph macro that checks `AI_atVictoryStage(stage1)` first and therefore collapses
all cumulative stages 1..4 to numeric 1.

This file is useful internal control evidence for F250, but the helper itself must not be
rediscovered/re-numbered as F270.

SAS-ADDED HELPER FIRST CONTROLS
-------------------------------
`handicapFromDifficulty`:
    * introduced because SAS handicap `iDifficulty` values are scores, no longer safely
      reconstructible as enum-index * 10 after adding Rookie / Deity+ levels;
    * current callers pass averaged/rounded difficulty scores from CvGame/CvTeam;
    * nearest-score lookup is coherent for current ordered XML;
    * exact midpoint ties choose the earlier XML enum because comparison uses `<`, but no
      caller-visible contract requiring upward tie-breaking has been established.
      CONTROL for now; do not promote.

Spaceship helpers:
    * current SAS XML has each spaceship project's `iMaxTeamInstances` equal to its Space
      `VictoryThreshold`, so summing max-team instances currently matches full ship parts;
    * a hypothetical mod where these diverge would make `getSASSpaceshipPartsRequired`
      less generic, but current SAS does not reproduce such a mismatch;
    * therefore no live F270 on this basis.

`getSASVictoryDelayTurnsFromNormalGameSpeed`:
    * deliberately does NOT static-cache game-speed output, avoiding stale speed if a new
      game is started in the same Civ4 process;
    * current victory-denial defines are 20 Normal-speed turns, and all shipped
      VictoryDelayPercent values produce exact integer scaled windows for 20;
    * helper rounds to nearest whereas CvGame::victoryDelay uses integer truncation, but
      no current shipped threshold divergence results from the configured value.
      Keep as a precision/design control unless a live boundary consumer is found.

`getSASUWAIVictoryDenialPeaceThreat`:
    * parameter is TeamTypes and current UWAIAgent calls pass `kAgent.getID()` where
      kAgent is CvTeamAI; no player/team type confusion there;
    * CvDeal/CvTeamAI callers likewise supply TeamTypes;
    * no ownership mismatch found in opening pass.

which matches that contract.

C022-WIP02 — QUEUE 039 CvGameCoreUtils.cpp / HIGH-FANOUT HELPER PASS
===============================================================================
Date: 2026-08-28
Model: GPT-5.6-Sol
Status: UNFINISHED WIP; queue 039 remains OPEN.
Repository source files modified: NONE.

This checkpoint preserves the first confirmed queue-039 root plus controls from the
contested-plot, direction, hash and calendar opening pass. It appends to C022-WIP01;
all earlier findings remain unchanged.

F270 / provisional KI#593
K-MOD-INHERITED CROSS-FILE BUG — CvPlayerAI::AI_localAttackStrength passes the
EVALUATING/DEFENDING team as estimateCollateralWeight's ATTACK team
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: CONFIRMED.
OWNING FILE FOR SHARED HELPER: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameCoreUtils.cpp.
FAULTY LIVE CALLER: CvGameCoreDLL/CvPlayerAI.cpp::AI_localAttackStrength.
LINEAGE: K-Mod inherited; wrong caller semantics originate when collateral weighting
was introduced into AI_localAttackStrength (K-Mod practical 448) and become explicit
under the current helper contract at K-Mod practical 1200.

CURRENT PRODUCER CONTRACT
-------------------------
Current CvGameCoreUtils.cpp declares:

    int estimateCollateralWeight(CvPlot const* pPlot,
            TeamTypes eAttackTeam, TeamTypes eDefenseTeam)

`eAttackTeam` is not merely a label. The helper uses it to:

    * decide which plot team should receive defensive bonuses when eDefenseTeam is not
      supplied;
    * pass the attacking team into CvPlot::defenseModifier;
    * exclude the attacking team's own units from the population sampled for collateral
      immunity / Collateral Damage Protection.

This is the same semantic contract introduced by K-Mod practical 1200 when the helper
changed from a one-team `eDefenceTeam` API to explicit attacker + optional defender.

FAULTY CALLER
-------------
Current CvPlayerAI::AI_localAttackStrength is documented as:

    "Total attack strength of units (potentially) hostile to us ..."

and accepts `eAttackTeam`, defaulting to NO_TEAM. Its unit loop then counts either:

    kUnit.getTeam() == eAttackTeam

or, for NO_TEAM, teams currently at war with `getTeam()`.

Despite this, the collateral scale is initialized as:

    estimateCollateralWeight(pTargetPlot, getTeam())

(or the NULL-plot equivalent).

Here `getTeam()` is the CvPlayerAI object whose local danger/offense is being queried.
For the very common hostile/default mode it is therefore the DEFENDING/evaluating team,
not the team(s) whose attacking units are being valued.

END-TO-END WRONG-STATE PATH
---------------------------
A common concrete case is our city/stack being evaluated against hostile siege units:

    pTargetPlot->getTeam() == getTeam()
    eAttackTeam == NO_TEAM (or a known enemy team)
    actual collateral dealers == hostile team(s)

The helper receives our team as `eAttackTeam` and therefore:

1. Plot defensive bonus is evaluated for the wrong sides.

   With no explicit eDefenseTeam, current helper computes:

       ePlotBonusTeam =
           (pPlot->getTeam() == eAttackTeam ? NO_TEAM : pPlot->getTeam());

   On our own plot, the wrong `eAttackTeam == getTeam()` makes ePlotBonusTeam NO_TEAM.
   Current CvPlot::defenseModifier immediately returns after terrain/feature/hills when
   eDefender == NO_TEAM, before improvement/city defense. Thus the collateral scale for
   enemy attackers can omit the target city's defensive bonus entirely.

2. Resistance is sampled from the wrong unit population.

   The helper excludes:

       if (eAttackTeam != NO_TEAM && pUnit->getTeam() == eAttackTeam)
           continue;

   With the erroneous `eAttackTeam == getTeam()`, that skips our own defenders — exactly
   the units whose collateral immunity/protection should reduce the expected collateral
   inflicted by the hostile siege force. Other co-located units can instead influence
   the sample when eDefenseTeam is unspecified.

3. The bad scale is consumed for every hostile collateral attacker.

   AI_localAttackStrength passes `iBaseCollateral` into:

       kUnit.AI_currEffectiveStr(..., true, iBaseCollateral, ...)

   AI_currEffectiveStr adds an explicit collateral-strength term proportional to
   `iBaseCollateral`, number of possible collateral targets and the attacker's
   collateral factor. The wrong side assignment therefore changes the returned enemy
   local-attack estimate rather than merely affecting a debug/display value.

CALLER IMPACT
-------------
AI_localAttackStrength is high fanout. Current callers use it for, among other things:

    * city safety / danger and evacuation-strength comparisons;
    * unit/group danger and attack/retreat decisions;
    * team surrender / power comparisons;
    * local enemy-offense estimates;
    * UI/debug strength displays.

Many calls use the default `eAttackTeam = NO_TEAM`, i.e. specifically "hostile to us"
mode. Other calls pass a known enemy team. Calls that explicitly ask a player object to
estimate its own team's attack can happen to make `getTeam()` equal the actual attacker,
but that does not rescue the general helper contract.

The error is not monotonic. For example:

    * omitting real city defense can undervalue the relative benefit of enemy collateral;
    * excluding defenders with high collateral protection/immunity can overvalue it.

So this can move tactical strength estimates in either direction depending on the plot
and defending stack.

HISTORY / REGRESSION BOUNDARY
-----------------------------
K-Mod practical 448 (`3db35153a5...`, "Increased the AI's estimate of collateral damage
when calculating attack strength") first introduced estimateCollateralWeight and wired
it into AI_localAttackStrength. At that point the helper took only an eDefenceTeam, but
AI_localAttackStrength chose that team from the plot's relation to `getTeam()` rather
than from the method's `eAttackTeam` mode. Thus the caller was already incapable of
representing both hostile-vs-us and own-vs-target modes correctly.

K-Mod practical 1200 (`8b46440a9c...`, "estimateCollateralWeight now takes collateral
resistance into account") changed the helper to the current explicit contract:

    estimateCollateralWeight(pPlot, eAttackTeam, eDefenceTeam = NO_TEAM)

and changed AI_localAttackStrength to:

    estimateCollateralWeight(pTargetPlot, getTeam())

This makes the ownership mismatch unambiguous: the new first argument is explicitly the
collateral DEALER, while the caller supplies the CvPlayerAI evaluator.

K-Mod 1.46 still contains the same call. Base AdvCiv 1.14 still contains it. Current SAS
still contains it. This is inherited K-Mod behavior, not a SAS regression.

CROSS-FILE / DUPLICATE CHECK
----------------------------
The current CvSelectionGroupAI callers also pass `getTeam()`, but there `getTeam()` is
the team of the group whose ATTACK strength is being evaluated, so those callers match
the helper's K-Mod-1200 contract. CvUnitAI's NULL-plot caller likewise uses its actual
team as attacker.

This explains why the earlier queue-041 history note saying the current helper/caller
lineage was coherent was valid for that file's attacking-group call sites yet did not
close this CvPlayerAI cross-file mode. No prior album root owns the AI_localAttackStrength
argument-role mismatch. F270 is therefore independent rather than a rediscovery.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Do not blindly replace the second helper argument with a single hard-coded team. This
method supports two materially different modes:

    * default/hostile mode: attackers are enemy team(s), evaluator's team is defender;
    * explicit own-offense mode: eAttackTeam can equal getTeam(), while the target plot's
      opposing team is the defender.

The repair should derive the helper's attacking and defending roles from `eAttackTeam`
and the target context, e.g. conceptually:

    attacker = eAttackTeam (NO_TEAM is acceptable for generic multiple-hostile mode)
    defender = known target/evaluator defender when one can be identified

and pass both explicitly. In the common NO_TEAM hostile-to-us mode, supplying
`eDefenseTeam = getTeam()` is important so the resistance sample is restricted to the
actual defending side even though no single enemy attack team is known. In a known
attacker-vs-owned-target case, the plot/evaluator team is defender; in an own-attack
against an enemy-owned target, the target plot team is defender.

Any patch should re-test both categories rather than merely changing `getTeam()` to
`eAttackTeam`, because the helper's optional defender parameter also controls city
bonus and collateral-resistance sampling.

SEVERITY / CONFIDENCE
---------------------
Confidence: HIGH.
Severity: gameplay-relevant AI valuation bug; magnitude situational but high-fanout.
The helper itself is approximately modeling collateral, but the attacker/defender role
mismatch is an argument-contract error independent of approximation quality.


OPENING CONTROLS / NON-FINDINGS SINCE WIP01
===========================================

A. contestedPlots coordinate dedup key — CONTROL
------------------------------------------------
`contestedPlots` uses `x * 1000 + y` as a local dedup key. This would collide if the
supported Y dimension reached 1000, but current shipped/custom SAS map dimensions are
far below that regime (current XML maxima inspected are ~99x70 before any normal map
script scaling). No supported-map collision was established. Keep as a theoretical
future-proofing concern, not F271.

B. estimateDirection zero displacement — CONTROL
-------------------------------------------------
The helper returns NO_DIRECTION/-1 for zero displacement. For every nonzero displacement
one of the eight direction dot products is positive, so no invalid "best direction"
state was found. No root.

C. intHash signed-overflow / capital salt — CONTROL FOR NOW
-----------------------------------------------------------
`intHash` intentionally folds inputs with multiplier 31 and optionally salts by the
player capital plot. The capital term is documented as range diversification and its
callers use the result as deterministic pseudo-random material. Although signed-overflow
portability is theoretically undesirable under modern C++ rules, the target Civ4 MSVC
runtime has stable wrap-style behavior and no supported current cross-build/OOS failure
was proved. Do not promote merely on language-lawyer UB.

D. BC fractional-year conversion — STRONG LOW-SEVERITY CANDIDATE, NOT YET NUMBERED
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`getTurnYearForGame` currently returns:

    getTurnMonthForGame(...) / max(1, GC.getNumMonthInfos())

For negative month counts not divisible by 12, C++ integer division truncates toward
zero instead of flooring. Example with 12 months:

    -48000 months -> -4000
    -47999 months -> -3999   // C++ truncation, but still February 4000 BC

AdvCiv practical 4317 explicitly fixed the sibling negative-modulo problem in
CvGameTextMgr::setDateStr using `intdiv::umodulo`, noting ordinary `%` fails for BC
calendar dates; the year division was left unchanged. K-Mod and Civ4CE also retain
ordinary division.

Current shipped CALENDAR_DEFAULT game-speed BC increments were checked and are divisible
by 12 up to AD, so normal default games do not reproduce this. However Civ4 supports
CALENDAR_MONTHS/SEASONS/WEEKS, WorldBuilder Calendar/StartYear scenarios and custom
increment XML, where fractional-year BC dates are supported. Preserve this for final
queue-039 disposition; it may warrant a low-severity F271 if the supported scenario API
is judged sufficient, but do not promote merely because the arithmetic is theoretically
wrong outside current default speed data.

C022-WIP03 — QUEUE 039 CvGameCoreUtils.cpp / CALENDAR + PUF PASS
===============================================================================
Date: 2026-08-28
Model: GPT-5.6-Sol
Status: UNFINISHED WIP; queue 039 remains OPEN.
Repository source files modified: NONE.

F271 / provisional KI#594
CIV4/K-MOD/ADVCIV-INHERITED BUG — getTurnYearForGame truncates negative fractional
BC years toward zero instead of flooring them
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: CONFIRMED (LOW SEVERITY, SUPPORTED NONDEFAULT CALENDARS / SCENARIOS).
OWNING FILE: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameCoreUtils.cpp.

CURRENT CODE
------------
Current SAS returns:

    getTurnMonthForGame(iGameTurn, iStartYear, eCalendar, eSpeed) /
        max(1, GC.getNumMonthInfos())

from getTurnYearForGame.

For positive dates ordinary integer division gives the desired containing year. For a
negative month count that is not exactly divisible by the number of months in a year,
C++ integer division truncates toward zero rather than toward negative infinity.

With 12 months, for example:

    -48000 / 12 = -4000                     // January 4000 BC, fine
    -47999 / 12 = -3999 in C++             // February is still in 4000 BC

The most obvious era-boundary example is:

    turn-month -1  -> C++ year 0

CvGameTextMgr::setYearStr deliberately represents year 0 as 1 AD (there is no displayed
year zero). Under CALENDAR_MONTHS this can therefore label the month immediately before
the era boundary as "December, 1 AD", followed by "January, 1 AD" one turn later,
instead of December 1 BC followed by January 1 AD.

SUPPORTED INPUT / NOT MERELY HYPOTHETICAL XML
----------------------------------------------
This reproducer does not require an invented calendar enum:

    CALENDAR_DEFAULT
    CALENDAR_BI_YEARLY
    CALENDAR_YEARS
    CALENDAR_TURNS
    CALENDAR_SEASONS
    CALENDAR_MONTHS
    CALENDAR_WEEKS

are first-class CalendarTypes in CvEnums and exposed through CyEnumsInterface/Python.
WorldBuilder scenario serialization explicitly writes and reads both:

    Calendar=<calendar type>
    StartYear=<integer>

and CvGame/CvInitCore expose the selected calendar/start year. Thus a BC scenario using
CALENDAR_MONTHS, CALENDAR_SEASONS or CALENDAR_WEEKS is a supported Civ4 configuration,
not just malformed mod data.

Current shipped SAS CALENDAR_DEFAULT game-speed increments were separately checked:
the BC increments currently in the normal game-speed XML are multiples of 12 until AD,
so ordinary default games avoid fractional BC years and do not normally display the bug.
That bounds severity but does not invalidate the supported scenario/nondefault-calendar
path.

DOWNSTREAM EFFECTS
------------------
1. Date/year display and save-format text
   CvGameTextMgr::setYearStr calls getTurnYearForGame. CALENDAR_MONTHS, SEASONS and
   WEEKS then combine that wrong year with their month/season/week label.

2. Public game/Python API
   CvGame::getGameTurnYear -> getTurnYearForGame, and CyGame exposes getGameTurnYear.
   Scenario scripts therefore receive the same off-by-one BC year for fractional years.

3. Logs / diagnostics
   SASGameRecordLog, BBAILog, CitySiteEvaluator and other reporting paths record
   getGameTurnYear and therefore inherit the wrong BC year.

4. Small real gameplay timing effect
   CvCity::setNumRealBuilding stores GC.getGame().getGameTurnYear as the building's
   original time. CvCity::getBuildingCommerceByBuilding later compares the current
   getGameTurnYear against that stored year for CommerceChangeDoubleTime (1000 years in
   current building XML for applicable culture commerce). A building constructed during
   a fractional BC year can therefore have the year-based doubling threshold shifted by
   one calendar year in such a scenario. This is small compared with the display/API
   defect but proves that the helper is not presentation-only.

HISTORY / CONTROL
-----------------
Civ4CE's BtS source and K-Mod 1.46 both retain the same ordinary `/ numMonths` year
conversion. Base AdvCiv 1.14 likewise retains it (with only a divisor max guard).
Current SAS inherits the same behavior.

The diagnosis is strengthened by AdvCiv practical 4317, "Fix month display for BC game
dates." That fix explicitly notes that ordinary C++ `%` "doesn't work for negative
dates, i.e. BC" and replaces the month-index modulo in CvGameTextMgr with
`intdiv::umodulo`. The mathematically paired year quotient was not changed, leaving the
same negative-number issue in division form.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Use floor division by the positive number of months rather than C++ truncation. The
existing positive-remainder helper makes the relation explicit:

    n = max(1, GC.getNumMonthInfos())
    m = getTurnMonthForGame(...)
    year = (m - intdiv::umodulo(m, n)) / n

For nonnegative m this is equivalent to current division. For negative fractional years
it returns the containing BC year. A dedicated signed floor-div helper would also be
reasonable if useful elsewhere.

Regression tests should include at least:

    * CALENDAR_MONTHS, StartYear=-1: Jan through Dec 1 BC, then Jan 1 AD;
    * a much earlier negative year such as -4000 with turn-month +1;
    * positive/AD dates unchanged;
    * CALENDAR_DEFAULT current shipped speeds unchanged.

SEVERITY / CONFIDENCE
---------------------
Confidence: HIGH.
Severity: LOW overall because shipped default game speeds avoid fractional BC years;
real correctness bug for supported nondefault calendars/scenarios, public year API and
small year-based building-commerce timing.


POST-F270 COLLATERAL POPULATION CONTROL
=======================================
After separating F270's definite caller role mismatch, the helper's broader
`eDefenseTeam = NO_TEAM` population behavior was challenged independently.

When no defender team is supplied, estimateCollateralWeight counts canDefend units that
are not on the supplied attack team. In a plot shared with a neutral third party this
can sample a unit that actual CvUnit::collateralCombat would not necessarily hit, since
actual victim selection uses unit-level isEnemy. However:

    * the helper explicitly documents itself as a rough estimate;
    * multiple allied enemy teams can legitimately contribute collateral victims;
    * hidden-nationality / always-hostile combat can make simple diplomatic team filters
      misleading;
    * callers lacking an explicit eDefenseTeam intentionally use the generic mode.

No independent hard contract comparable to F270's wrong attacker argument was proved.
Do not split this into F272 merely because a neutral-coexistence edge can make the rough
sample imperfect. A future improvement could pass explicit defender information where
known and/or use attacker-relative combat-enemy semantics, but that is tuning unless a
specific caller invariant is established.


PUF REFACTOR PASS — CURRENT CONTROL STATE
=========================================
The high-fanout PUF enemy/combat-owner helpers were compared against K-Mod and the
AdvCiv practical-2731 refactor. So far the apparently unusual cases are deliberate:

    * PUF_isPotentialEnemy / PUF_isEnemy use the querying player's team as `eOurTeam`
      and pUnit->getCombatOwner(eOurTeam), matching hidden-nationality/always-hostile
      perspective semantics;
    * PUF_canDeclareWar asks whether the querying player can declare on the unit's
      combat owner; AdvCiv's swapped variable names corrected the readability of the
      inherited K-Mod orientation rather than reversing behavior;
    * canCoexistWithEnemyUnit exclusions are intentional for spies/coexisting units;
    * PUF_isPlayer's viewer-aware hidden-nationality/invisibility branch is part of
      advc.061 and has no current NO_PLAYER caller that violates its refactored enum
      assertion contract.

No PUF root has crossed F272 yet. Continue caller-specific checks rather than treating
hidden-nationality complexity itself as a defect.

C022-WIP04 CONTINUATION — QUEUE 039 CONTROL FREEZE
====================================================
Status: queue 039 CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameCoreUtils.cpp remains OPEN.

PUF / TRANSPORT / STRING-HELPER CONTROLS FROZEN
-----------------------------------------------
1. PUF callback argument-type audit:
   Despite generic int callback slots and some legacy/misleading names, traced live callers
   supply the semantic type expected by each predicate. In particular,
   PUF_isOtherTeam expects a PlayerTypes value and callers pass players; PUF_isCombatTeam
   expects TeamTypes and callers pass teams. No live player/team reinterpretation root was
   established.

2. PUF_isEnemyCityAttacker transport proxy:
   Its treatment of generic cargo transports as potential city threats is longstanding and
   intentional-looking, not a hard defect. The helper was introduced to classify units that
   can endanger a city, and cargo vessels can carry city attackers even when the hull itself
   cannot attack cities. Current consumers are conservative city-safety/trade gates. Do not
   make F272 merely from empty transports satisfying this proxy without an independent
   contract contradiction.

3. eAssumePeaceTeam hidden-nationality edge:
   The hypothetical-peace parameter could deserve care with always-hostile/hidden-nationality
   combat ownership, but every live isVisibleEnemyCityAttacker caller currently passes
   NO_TEAM. This is dormant in current SAS and is not F272.

4. setListHelp(NULL, ...) concern:
   The live NULL-start calls resolve to the CvWStringBuffer overload. CvWStringBuffer::append
   explicitly ignores a NULL wchar pointer. No current NULL-start call into the less-tolerant
   CvWString overload was found. This is safe by current caller/overload contract.

5. Debug enum/string helpers:
   Preliminary automated enum-vs-switch comparison suggests some MissionTypes/MissionAITypes
   lack dedicated symbolic names, but these diagnostic helpers have numeric UNKNOWN fallbacks.
   This remains under challenge; omission alone is not a gameplay/root finding.

No repository source files modified. Audit album only.

C022-WIP05 — QUEUE 039 CvGameCoreUtils.cpp / SATURATION CONTROLS
===============================================================================
Date: 2026-08-28
Model: GPT-5.6-Sol

STATUS:

CONTROLS / NON-FINDINGS ADDED SINCE WIP04
=========================================

A. `handicapFromDifficulty` exact-midpoint tie -- CONTROL
---------------------------------------------------------
The SAS helper scans handicap XML in enum order and updates only on strictly smaller
absolute distance. Therefore an exact midpoint between two current scores chooses the
earlier/lower entry; e.g. Noble 50 + Prince 58 average to 54 and map to Noble.

This differs from some pre-SAS averaging callers, but there is no single inherited tie
contract to preserve:

  * AdvCiv `CvGame::initGameHandicap` averaged enum-derived difficulty and used
    `intdiv::round`, so an exact adjacent .5 generally rounded upward;
  * AdvCiv `CvGame::updateAIHandicap` averaged enum IDs with `intdiv::uround`, likewise
    generally choosing the upper adjacent enum on a .5;
  * AdvCiv `CvTeam::getHandicapType`, however, deliberately used integer division and
    therefore chose the lower entry for the comparable midpoint.

SAS commit 5970 replaced these assumptions because Rookie/Deity+ and XML `iDifficulty`
scores make enum-index arithmetic invalid. "Nearest XML score, earlier/lower on an exact
tie" is internally coherent, and the old callers themselves disagreed about tie direction.
Do not promote F272 merely from the changed tie-break outcome.

B. live-unit selection-group assumptions in PUF helpers -- CONTROL
-------------------------------------------------------------------
`PUF_isAirIntercept`, `PUF_isMissionAIType`, `PUF_isGroupHead` and the group-head helper
family dereference a unit selection group without local NULL guards. This initially looks
fragile because `CvUnit::getGroup()` can technically return NULL for an invalid group ID.

Lifecycle tracing does not establish a live bug:

  * normal live units are attached/re-attached to selection groups;
  * `CvUnit::isGroupHead()` itself unconditionally dereferences `getGroup()`, making group
    existence a broad core live-unit invariant rather than a special PUF assumption;
  * the deliberate `joinGroup(NULL, false, false)` no-rejoin path occurs during
    `CvUnit::kill`, after the unit is removed from the map and immediately before
    `unitLost`/deletion, so normal plot-count PUF callers cannot encounter that detached
    dying unit as a live plot unit.

No transient live caller violating the invariant was proved. Keep as contract control.

C. `PUF_isFiniteRangeAndNotJustProduced` uses `> 1` -- CONTROL
-------------------------------------------------------------
Despite the helper name, it excludes units whose creation turn is either the current turn
or the immediately preceding game turn. The sole current gameplay use is the inherited
BBAI/K-Mod transport-pickup valuation, whose own comment says it wants units that "have
had a chance to move since being built." The condition is inherited together with that
caller. Without proving the intended turn-order window is only one global turn, the name
alone is insufficient evidence of an off-by-one defect. Do not allocate F272 on this basis.

D. `setListHelp` integer-list-ID sentinel -- CONTROL
---------------------------------------------------
The int-reference overload treats `iLastListID == iListID` as a continuation and otherwise
emits `szStart`. Many callers initialize `iLast = 0`, which would be wrong if the first
actual list ID could also be zero.

All current caller families inspected either explicitly skip zero-valued modifiers before
calling the helper or sit inside an outer nonzero-value condition. Negative nonzero values
also correctly differ from the zero sentinel. Thus current first-item formatting is safe;
no uninitialized/zero-key caller was found.

E. hotkey description mapping -- CONTROL
----------------------------------------
The legacy mapping declares `iNumKeyBoardMappings = 108` and contains exactly 108 mapping
initializers. The longest `KB_*` token is well below the fixed 25-TCHAR storage capacity.
A scan of all current SAS XML found 49 distinct nonempty `<HotKey>` codes, and every one is
present in the mapping. No current hotkey-description omission or array-count mismatch.

F. `applyColorToString` self-format alias -- CONTROL
----------------------------------------------------
The helper calls `s.Format(..., s.GetCString())`. `CvWString::Format` first formats into a
separate local `std::wstring result` and only assigns `*this = result` afterward, so the
source pointer is not invalidated before formatting consumes it. No self-alias corruption.

G. debug Mission string omission -- DIAGNOSTIC CLEANUP, NOT F272
----------------------------------------------------------------
Current `getMissionTypeString` lacks an explicit `MISSION_RANGE_ATTACK` case while that
mission is live (`CvUnitAI::AI_rangeAttack` queues it). Debug plot help therefore falls
back to `UNKOWN_MISSION(<numeric id>)` rather than the symbolic mission name. The numeric
fallback remains unique and no gameplay state depends on the string. K-Mod, AdvCiv and
Civ4CE carry the same omission. Useful cleanup for diagnostics, but below the current root
bar unless an independent diagnostic failure is demonstrated.

H. `intHash` / coordinate-key controls remain unchanged
-------------------------------------------------------
No supported deterministic OOS failure was established from signed 32-bit polynomial
wrap on the fixed legacy MSVC/Win32 target, and `contestedPlots`' x*1000+y key remains far
outside the collision regime for all shipped SAS world sizes. Both remain future-proofing
notes rather than live roots.

CURRENT ASSESSMENT
==================
The inherited utility/PUF body has now had argument types, hidden-nationality ownership,
group lifecycle, list formatting, hotkey data, direction helpers, hash callers, calendar
boundaries, and K-Mod/Civ4CE cognates challenged. The late pass is increasingly yielding
controls rather than uncovered state/consumer contradictions.

F272 remains deliberately UNUSED.

FINAL ROOT INDEPENDENCE / REPAIR-BOUNDARY REVIEW
=================================================

F270 / KI#593 -- collateral attacker-team role in AI_localAttackStrength
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Root:
    `estimateCollateralWeight` defines its first team argument as the team dealing
    collateral damage. `CvPlayerAI::AI_localAttackStrength`, however, hardwires the
    evaluating player's `getTeam()` into that role while the actual candidate attackers
    are selected by `eAttackTeam` (or by all teams currently at war when eAttackTeam is
    NO_TEAM).

Why this is independently live:
    * the helper uses the supplied attack team in defender-bonus context and when
      excluding the attacking side from the resistance sample;
    * explicit enemy-team calls therefore evaluate hostile collateral using the defender's
      team identity;
    * explicit own-team offense calls and default all-hostiles calls demonstrate that this
      cannot be repaired safely by blindly swapping one hardcoded team for another.

History:
    K-Mod 448 introduced collateral weighting into local attack-strength valuation.
    K-Mod 1200 made the helper contract explicit as attacking team first, defender team
    optional, while the local-attack-strength caller retained the evaluator-team argument.
    The mismatch survives K-Mod -> AdvCiv -> SAS. Selection-group callers are not affected
    by the same root because there `getTeam()` genuinely is the attacking group team.

Repair boundary:
    * when `eAttackTeam` is explicit, collateral attacker semantics must use that team;
    * when AI_localAttackStrength is aggregating all hostile teams (`NO_TEAM`), there is no
      single truthful attack-team identity, so use an explicitly generic/per-team policy
      rather than silently treating the evaluator as the attacker;
    * defender-team sampling must likewise follow whether the evaluator is defending the
      target, attacking it, or merely estimating nearby hostile strength.
Do not mechanically replace `getTeam()` with `eAttackTeam` in every mode without preserving
these caller semantics.

F271 / KI#594 -- negative fractional BC year division
-----------------------------------------------------
Root:
    `getTurnMonthForGame` can produce negative month counts not divisible by the number of
    months per year for supported fractional-year calendars. `getTurnYearForGame` converts
    months to years with ordinary signed C++ integer division, which truncates toward zero
    rather than flooring the calendar year.

Concrete supported example:
    With a monthly calendar around the BC/AD boundary, turn-month -1 represents the final
    month of 1 BC. `-1 / 12` becomes 0 in C++, and the year formatter intentionally renders
    year 0 as 1 AD. The chronology can therefore display a month of 1 AD before January
    1 AD. CALENDAR_MONTHS, CALENDAR_SEASONS and CALENDAR_WEEKS are first-class Civ4
    calendar modes and WorldBuilder scenarios serialize Calendar/StartYear, so this is not
    merely an impossible custom-mod input.

Non-display consumer:
    `CvGame::getGameTurnYear()` feeds the building-age comparison used for the 1000-year
    building commerce/culture doubling mechanic, so a fractional BC scenario can also shift
    that threshold by a calendar year.

History:
    Civ4/K-Mod/AdvCiv and Civ4CE retain the truncating quotient. AdvCiv separately repaired
    the sibling negative `%` problem in `CvGameTextMgr::setDateStr` by introducing
    `intdiv::umodulo`, but the quotient half remained unchanged.

Repair boundary:
    Let `m = getTurnMonthForGame(...)` and `n = max(1, GC.getNumMonthInfos())`.
    A clean integer floor quotient is:

        (m - intdiv::umodulo(m, n)) / n

    For nonnegative and exact-year dates this is identical to existing behavior. For a
    negative fractional year it subtracts the positive calendar remainder before exact
    division, giving the mathematically correct floor year.

F270 vs F271:
    DISTINCT / INDEPENDENT.
    F270 is a combat-AI caller-role bug in collateral valuation. F271 is calendar arithmetic
    used by date/API/gameplay year consumers. Either reproduces with the other subsystem
    absent; their repairs share no state or contract.

I. SAS-vs-Base AdvCiv semantic delta — BOUNDED / CONTROL
--------------------------------------------------------
Normalized current SAS vs Base AdvCiv 1.14 comparison is very small. Current SAS mainly:
    * reformats several signatures/comments;
    * replaces terse missing-GlobalDefine assertions with richer diagnostics;
    * retains the Base AdvCiv global/cache/info-array implementation otherwise.

This makes inherited CvGlobals lifetime, cache and XML registration contracts the primary
queue-040 target rather than a broad SAS rewrite.

II. SetGlobalDefines -> cacheGlobals -> m_pPythonCaller — OPEN LIFECYCLE CANDIDATE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CvXMLLoadUtility::SetGlobalDefines() finishes with:

    GC.cacheGlobals();

CvGlobals::cacheGlobals() performs full integer/float cache initialization and then:

    m_pPythonCaller = new CvPythonCaller();
    CvEventReporter::getInstance().initPythonCallbackGuards();

m_pPythonCaller is deleted in CvGlobals::uninit(), but cacheGlobals() itself does not first
free an existing object.

Important narrowing:
    * K-Mod/Civ4CE also called cacheGlobals() from runtime define setters;
    * AdvCiv intentionally replaced those full recaches with targeted cacheGlobalInts /
      cacheGlobalFloats updates before introducing/retaining the Python-caller allocation;
    * therefore current runtime setDefineINT/FLOAT does NOT itself repeat the allocation.

The remaining question is whether the EXE can invoke SetGlobalDefines() multiple times in a
single CvGlobals lifetime (e.g. supported XML reload). That call is external to the DLL-side
source available here. Without proving repeat execution, this is not F272.

III. info/type-map reset orchestration — CONTROL / EXTERNAL CONTRACT
-------------------------------------------------------------------
CleanUpGlobalVariables() calls deleteInfoArrays(), which deletes info objects/string arrays
and clears m_typesMap through clearTypesMap(). m_infosMap is instead cleared by the separately
exported CvGlobals::infoTypeFromStringReset().

The latter contains the inherited diagnostic:

    FErrorMsg("Just to see if and when CvGlobals::infoTypeFromStringReset is ever called");

This looks awkward, but the function is DllExport and therefore can be part of the EXE's XML
reload orchestration. A stale removed-info mapping would be real if arrays were reloaded
without this callback, but the available DLL source cannot establish that omission. Keep as
an external-lifecycle control; do not infer F272 from absence of an in-DLL caller.

IV. CvAgents ownership — REAL CLEANUP OMISSION, CURRENT IMPACT NOT YET PROVED
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CvGlobals::init() allocates:

    m_agents = new CvAgents(MAX_PLAYERS, MAX_TEAMS);

CvGlobals::uninit() frees CvPlayer/CvTeam statics but never deletes m_agents. The CvAgents
object therefore remains allocated and retains vectors of pointers to player/team instances
that have just been freed.

This is a genuine ownership asymmetry, but no supported same-DLL init->uninit->init cycle has
yet been established. If uninit occurs only at process/DLL shutdown, the OS reclaims the
allocation and no later consumer dereferences the stale cache. Keep below gameplay-root bar
unless a re-init path is proved.

V. getDirectionTypes indexed overload — INHERITED TYPE-SIGNATURE MISMATCH / LATENT CONTROL
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Neighboring accessors are:

    getAutomateTypes(AutomateTypes e)
    getDirectionTypes(AutomateTypes e)

The second clearly ought, by semantic type, to take DirectionTypes. This exact copy/paste
signature exists in Civ4CE and K-Mod and survives Base AdvCiv/SAS.

However:
    * current DLL source uses only the pointer-returning getDirectionTypes() overload when
      loading/deleting the array;
    * no indexed current DLL caller was found;
    * K-Mod/Civ4CE exported the indexed overload, whereas current AdvCiv/SAS no longer marks
      it DllExport.

So the signature is incorrect as an API contract but no current caller-visible failure has
been proved. Keep as latent cleanup/control, not F272.

VI. define-cache update preliminaries — CONTROL
-----------------------------------------------
ReadGlobalDefines writes directly into FVariableSystem during startup, then cacheGlobals()
initializes the cached arrays. Runtime setDefineINT/FLOAT uses targeted update helpers in
current AdvCiv/SAS, so the old K-Mod/CE full-cache recache behavior no longer causes repeated
m_pPythonCaller allocation.

cacheGlobalFloats' startup recursion through updateCityCamDist is bounded: the outer call
stores the new FIELD_OF_VIEW before updateCityCamDist -> setDefineFLOAT triggers the inner
cacheGlobalFloats call, so the inner pass observes unchanged FoV and does not recurse again.

VII. FootstepAudio "ByTag" lookup — REJECTED / NAMING CONTROL
-------------------------------------------------------------
CvGlobals::getFootstepAudioTypeByTag(strTag) searches m_paszFootstepAudioTypes rather than
m_paszFootstepAudioTags. The name initially suggests an array mix-up, but shipped XML proves
the current semantics are correct:
    * unit-art AudioRunTypeLoop / AudioRunTypeEnd fields contain tokens such as
      LOOPSTEP_TANK / ENDSTEP_TANK;
    * those tokens are entries in FootstepAudioTypes;
    * the parallel FootstepAudioTags array maps the resulting index to the actual AS3D sound
      script identifier.
So this function is really "type-index from XML type token" despite its confusing name.
No F272.

VIII. AnimationOperator indexed accessor — LATENT TYPE/API MISMATCH, NO LIVE FAILURE PROVED
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
AnimationOperatorTypes enum constants start at ANIMOP_FIRST = 1001, while
m_paszAnimationOperatorTypes is a normal 0..count-1 array. Yet
CvGlobals::getAnimationOperatorTypes(AnimationOperatorTypes e) directly indexes that array.
Passing a real ANIMOP_* enum constant would therefore assert/go out of bounds.

However, the live CyGlobalContext wrapper accepts a plain Python integer index and casts that
0..count-1 value to AnimationOperatorTypes before calling the accessor. No current C++/Python
caller was found passing an actual 1001+ ANIMOP_* constant. This is an inherited/domain-type
API defect, but presently latent; do not allocate F272 without a live caller-visible failure.

IX. lazy plot-group FAStar geometry — DORMANT CONTROL
-----------------------------------------------------
CvGlobals::getPlotGroupFinder() lazily initializes an FAStar instance with current map width,
height and wrap flags and does not locally reinitialize it for a later map geometry change.
That would be dangerous if used across regenerated maps.

Current AdvCiv/SAS CvPlotGroup::recalculatePlots, however, has the old plot-group-finder calls
commented out and uses the replacement DFS implementation. No other live DLL caller was found;
the getter itself carries an old diagnostic wondering whether it is called. Therefore the
stale-geometry concern is dormant in current code, not F272.

X. CvXMLLoadUtility raw global pointer — EXTERNAL LIFETIME CONTROL
-----------------------------------------------------------------
AdvCiv stores the current CvXMLLoadUtility* in CvGlobals so optional XML and throne-room XML
can be loaded lazily. CvXMLLoadUtility's destructor contains an explicit comment about the
EXE's unusual ownership/lifetime and warns against deleting the global pointer from the popup
path because that could double-delete.

Normal lazy consumers (CvGame reset optional load; throne-room late load) necessarily rely on
this utility surviving the initial XML phase. Available DLL source does not prove an interval
where the EXE deletes the utility while later retaining/using GC.m_pXMLLoadUtility. Treat this
as an externally-owned raw-pointer seam, not a use-after-free finding without lifecycle proof.

XI. playable-civilization counters and reload — SAME EXTERNAL-RELOAD FAMILY
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
LoadPreMenuGlobals increments m_iNumPlayableCivilizationInfos and
m_iNumAIPlayableCivilizationInfos; constructor initializes them to zero and cleanup does not
locally reset them before a hypothetical second full pre-menu load. That would double counts
on an in-process XML reload. But, like repeated cacheGlobals/PythonCaller allocation, the
available DLL source does not establish a supported second LoadPreMenuGlobals invocation in
one CvGlobals lifetime. Keep under the same external-reload candidate family, not F272.

XII. info-vector/string-array ownership inventory — CLEAN SO FAR
----------------------------------------------------------------
The advc.enum DO_FOR_EACH_INFO_TYPE list drives the ordinary info-vector deletion/reset paths.
CvWorldInfo is intentionally handled separately and is not also present in the macro, so there
is no double deletion there. Manual global string arrays (entity event, animation operator,
function, flavor, art style, city size, contact, diplomacy power, automate, direction,
FootstepAudio types/tags) are separately deleted by deleteInfoArrays(). No current loaded info
family has yet been found omitted from the corresponding cleanup family; Quest remains an
unused/commented legacy case rather than a live missing vector.

XIII. NUM_* macro apparent self-recursion — REJECTED / BUILD-MODE CONTROL
------------------------------------------------------------------------
CvGlobals.h defines, under `#ifndef _USRDLL`, macros such as:

    #define NUM_DIRECTION_TYPES (GC.getNumDirections())

while CvGlobals.cpp defines:

    int CvGlobals::getNumDirections() const { return NUM_DIRECTION_TYPES; }

This looks recursively self-referential in a textual read. It is not recursive in the DLL
build: `_USRDLL` is defined while compiling CvGameCoreDLL, so the compatibility macros are not
defined there and the getter returns the underlying enum constant. The macros exist for the
non-DLL/EXE side of the shared header. No F272.

F272 / provisional KI#595 — FOREIGN-REPLAY COLOR REMAP WRAPS BACK INTO THE
"SKIPPED" SYSTEM-COLOR PREFIX
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED; inherited AdvCiv feature bug (advc.106i), optional/config-gated.
Primary file: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGlobals.cpp
Same-root consumer/input contract: CvGameCoreDLL/CvReplayInfo.cpp

Current CvGlobals::getColorInfo(ColorTypes eColor) contains an out-of-range replay fallback:

    if (eColor >= getNumColorInfos())
    {
        FAssert(m_bHoFScreenUp || eColor < getNumColorInfos());
        // +7: Skip colors from COLOR_CLEAR to COLOR_LIGHT_GREY
        eColor = (ColorTypes)((eColor + 7) % getNumColorInfos());
    }

The stated invariant is explicit: remapped foreign colors should skip indices 0..6
(COLOR_CLEAR through COLOR_LIGHT_GREY). The arithmetic does not preserve that invariant after
one wrap of the normal color table.

CURRENT SAS COUNTEREXAMPLE
--------------------------
Current CIV4ColorVals.xml contains 128 ColorVal entries:
    0 COLOR_CLEAR
    1 COLOR_ALPHA_GREY
    2 COLOR_WHITE
    3 COLOR_BLACK
    4 COLOR_DARK_GREY
    5 COLOR_GREY
    6 COLOR_LIGHT_GREY
    7 COLOR_RED
    ...

CvReplayInfo::read accepts a foreign-mod player color through:

    checkBounds(info.m_eColor, 0, GC.getNumColorInfos() - 1)

and checkBounds deliberately doubles its upper bound when HOF_DISPLAY_OTHER_MOD_REPLAYS is
enabled. With 128 local colors, foreign replay IDs 0..254 are therefore accepted.

For the accepted high foreign IDs:
    249 -> (249 + 7) % 128 = 0  -> COLOR_CLEAR
    250 -> 1                    -> COLOR_ALPHA_GREY
    251 -> 2                    -> COLOR_WHITE
    252 -> 3                    -> COLOR_BLACK
    253 -> 4                    -> COLOR_DARK_GREY
    254 -> 5                    -> COLOR_GREY

Thus six IDs that the parser intentionally accepts as valid foreign extra colors are mapped
straight into the very prefix that getColorInfo says it is skipping. COLOR_CLEAR is especially
bad for replay/Hall-of-Fame display because the mapped marker/color can become transparent.

PRODUCER -> STATE -> CONSUMER
-----------------------------
1. HOF_DISPLAY_OTHER_MOD_REPLAYS enables permissive loading of replay data produced by another
   mod.
2. CvReplayInfo::checkBounds allows foreign player-color IDs up to twice the local normal upper
   bound.
3. CvReplayInfo stores the accepted foreign m_eColor unchanged.
4. Hall-of-Fame/replay UI consumes those stored ColorTypes (e.g. color markers, graph/minimap
   layers); m_bHoFScreenUp deliberately permits CvGlobals::getColorInfo to receive an ID beyond
   the local array.
5. getColorInfo remaps it with `(eColor + 7) % N`.
6. For the final accepted IDs of the doubled range, the result is 0..5, violating the explicit
   skip-system-colors contract.

This is config-gated in current SAS because HOF_DISPLAY_OTHER_MOD_REPLAYS defaults to 0, but it
is a real defect in the supported/configurable compatibility feature, not merely hypothetical
bad input.

ANCESTRY / BOUNDARY
-------------------
K-Mod does not contain this remapping feature; it simply asserts a normal in-range ColorTypes.
AdvCiv practical 1430 (8377887745-family history around advc.106i introduction; exact tracked
file AdvCivPreSAS_1430_efd11afbeb.diff) introduced the foreign-replay fallback already as:

    // +7: Skip COLOR_CLEAR to COLOR_LIGHT_GREY
    e = (ColorTypes)((e + 7) % getNumColorInfos());

Later AdvCiv changes only refactored/renamed the accessor and comment. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
current SAS retain the same arithmetic, while CvReplayInfo retains the generous doubled bound.
Therefore this is inherited from AdvCiv's advc.106i replay-compatibility feature, not SAS.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Map out-of-range IDs into the intended usable suffix [7, N) rather than shifting then taking
modulo N. For N > 7 and eColor >= N, a direct form is conceptually:

    7 + ((eColor - 7) % (N - 7))

(or equivalently offset relative to N). This guarantees every fallback result is >= 7 and < N.
Keep a defensive fallback/assert for pathological N <= 7 even though current assets have 128.

Do not merely lower CvReplayInfo's generous upper bound enough to hide the arithmetic problem;
that would unnecessarily reject foreign colors that can safely be represented through a
correct suffix remap.

SEVERITY / SCOPE
----------------
Low-to-moderate UI/compatibility severity; optional because display of other mods' replays is
disabled by default. No normal current-game ColorTypes are affected because the remap branch
runs only for eColor >= local color count.

DUPLICATE CHECK
---------------
No earlier album root was found for replay extra-color remapping/getColorInfo. This is separate
from replay-format/range changes such as SAS KI#166 and from queue-039 calendar/HOF-adjacent
utilities.

QUEUE STATUS AFTER F272
-----------------------

F273 / provisional KI#596 — SAS RICH GLOBALDEFINE DIAGNOSTICS ACCIDENTALLY
DISABLE THE INHERITED ASSERTION IN THE OPTIMIZED ASSERT BUILD
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED; SAS-specific diagnostic/build-configuration regression.
Primary file: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGlobals.cpp
Same-root sibling: CvGameCoreDLL/CvSelectionGroupAI.cpp
Build contract: CvGameCoreDLL/Project/Makefile + CvGameCoreDLL/FAssert.h

ROOT CONTRACT
-------------
AdvCiv's build system intentionally supports two assertion-capable configurations:

    Debug  = _DEBUG (which in FAssert.h also defines FASSERT_ENABLE)
    Assert = Release flags + /DFASSERT_ENABLE, without _DEBUG

The Makefile is explicit:

    Debug_DEFINES=/DWIN32 /D_WINDOWS /D_USRDLL /D_DEBUG
    Release_DEFINES=/DWIN32 /D_WINDOWS /D_USRDLL /DNDEBUG
    ...
    !IF "$(TARGET)" == "Assert"
    CFLAGS  = $(Release_CFLAGS) /DFASSERT_ENABLE

and FAssert.h independently gates the assertion macros on FASSERT_ENABLE:

    #ifdef _DEBUG
        #define FASSERT_ENABLE
    #endif
    ...
    #ifdef FASSERT_ENABLE
        #define FAssert(...)
        #define FAssertMsg(...)
    #else
        #define FAssert(...) (void)0
        #define FAssertMsg(...) (void)0
    #endif

Therefore `_DEBUG` is a sufficient condition for assertions, but it is NOT the assertion
feature flag. `FASSERT_ENABLE` is the actual contract and can intentionally be enabled in an
optimized/non-debug DLL.

PRIMARY FAILURE: CvGlobals GlobalDefine accessors
-------------------------------------------------
Base AdvCiv retains a cheap FAssert/FAssertMsg after the GlobalDefine lookup. Current SAS
replaced those plain assertions with richer lazy diagnostics in all three accessors:

    CvGlobals::getDefineINT
    CvGlobals::getDefineFLOAT
    CvGlobals::getDefineSTRING

The lookup status itself is correctly compiled whenever FASSERT_ENABLE is active, e.g.:

    #ifdef FASSERT_ENABLE
    bool bSuccess =
    #endif
    getDefinesVarSystem()->GetValue(...);

but the new diagnostic/assert block is guarded by `_DEBUG` instead:

    #ifdef _DEBUG
        if (!bSuccess) { ... FAssertMsg(...); }
    #endif

(or the FLOAT equivalent with CAMERA_MIN_DISTANCE exempted).

That changes the inherited build behavior:

    Build      Base AdvCiv                 current SAS
    -----      -----------                 -----------
    Debug      assertion active            richer assertion active
    Assert     assertion active            assertion SILENTLY REMOVED
    Release    assertion compiled out      assertion compiled out

The Assert target exists specifically to preserve assertions while running release-like code.
Missing/mistyped GlobalDefines therefore lose the inherited detection exactly in that useful
configuration. The lookup still falls back to the normal default, so this is a diagnostic
regression rather than a gameplay-state defect by itself; however it can materially hide XML
or refactor mistakes from the Assert DLL (the richer INT diagnostic was added precisely after
such a define typo was caught during SAS development).

REPAIR DIRECTION — CvGlobals
----------------------------
Gate the rich failure-only diagnostic on `FASSERT_ENABLE`, not `_DEBUG`:

    #ifdef FASSERT_ENABLE
        if (!bSuccess) { ... FAssertMsg(...); }
    #endif

and analogously for FLOAT/STRING. This keeps:

    * Debug: rich assertion, unchanged;
    * Assert: rich assertion restored;
    * Release: no assertion/formatting machinery;
    * normal successful lookups: no expensive message formatting, because the existing
      failure condition remains outside/around the formatting work.

No need to revert to the old uninformative Base assertion merely to fix the build guard.

SAME-ROOT SIBLING: CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_update
-------------------------------------------------
The same SAS optimization pattern was applied to AdvCiv's inherited stuck-loop assertion.
Base AdvCiv executes:

    FAssertMsg(iAttempts != iMaxAttempts, "Unit stuck in a loop");

outside `_DEBUG`, so it remains active in the Assert target. SAS moved the richer version
inside:

    #ifdef _DEBUG
        const bool bAssertCondition = (iAttempts != iMaxAttempts);
        if (!bAssertCondition) { ... FAssertMsg(...rich state...); }
        iMaxAttempts += 4; // restore Debug-only early-trigger adjustment
    #endif

The result is the same root: the Assert DLL no longer has the inherited stuck-loop assertion.

IMPORTANT REPAIR BOUNDARY FOR THE SIBLING
-----------------------------------------
Do NOT blindly replace that entire `_DEBUG` block with `FASSERT_ENABLE`: the
`iMaxAttempts += 4` line repairs an earlier `_DEBUG`-only `iMaxAttempts -= 4` adjustment and
must remain Debug-only. A safe conceptual split is:

    #ifdef FASSERT_ENABLE
        // lazy rich assertion block
    #endif
    #ifdef _DEBUG
        iMaxAttempts += 4; // restore only the Debug-only subtraction
    #endif

This restores Assert-build detection without changing its normal iteration limit.

CORRECTION TO THE ALREADY-CLOSED QUEUE 041 AUDIT
-------------------------------------------------
The queue-041 closure currently contains this rejected-control statement:

    "This does not disable an assert-enabled non-debug configuration: FAssert.h defines
     FASSERT_ENABLE only when _DEBUG itself is defined. Outside _DEBUG the old assert was
     already a no-op."

That statement is WRONG because it considered only FAssert.h's automatic `_DEBUG` enablement
and missed the Makefile's separate Assert target (`Release_CFLAGS /DFASSERT_ENABLE`).

Amend that old control as follows:

    * the expensive-formatting concern was valid;
    * moving message construction behind the failure condition was good;
    * moving the assertion itself behind `_DEBUG` was not equivalent to the inherited
      behavior and disabled it in the optimized Assert build;
    * reopen that rejected diagnostic candidate only as SAME-ROOT evidence for F273, not as
      a new independent numbered root and not as a retraction of queue-041's established
      gameplay findings.

ANCESTRY / INDEPENDENCE
-----------------------
Base AdvCiv has the plain assertions and the two-build assertion contract. The loss occurs in
SAS's richer diagnostic replacements, so F273 is SAS-specific. It is independent of F272:
F272 is an inherited Hall-of-Fame/replay color-remapping arithmetic bug; F273 is a build-guard
diagnostic regression affecting assertion coverage.

QUEUE STATUS AFTER F273
-----------------------

F273 / provisional KI#596 confirmed here.

II. WAR_SUCCESS_CITY_CAPTURING LOWER-BOUND ASYMMETRY — LATENT ROBUSTNESS CONTROL

source explicitly says 0 can crash AI code. A later runtime setDefineINT of that same name would
use cacheGlobalInts(szChangedDefine, iNewValue), which stores iNewValue directly and therefore
does not reapply the >=1 normalization.

This is a real API robustness asymmetry, but current SAS contains no runtime setter for this
define. XML startup goes through the normalized full-cache path. Do not allocate F274 without
a supported/live mutation path; record the invariant for any future generic define editor.

III. CvGlobals init/uninit / CvAgents — OWNERSHIP OMISSION STILL BELOW ROOT BAR

Rechecked the whole init/uninit pair and CvAgents implementation.

CvGlobals::init allocates m_agents after CvPlayer/CvTeam statics and CvAgents stores vectors of
raw player/team pointers plus installs itself into AgentIteratorBase's global cache pointer.
CvGlobals::uninit frees CvPlayer/CvTeam statics but does not delete m_agents.

So the ownership omission is genuine, and the leaked object contains stale pointers during
teardown. init/uninit are DllExport, but the current DLL source contains no second local init
call, no post-uninit AgentIterator consumer, and no proof that the Civ4 EXE performs a supported
same-loaded-DLL reinit cycle rather than unloading the DLL/process. Keep as cleanup/lifecycle
debt rather than inventing a live F274.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CvGlobals retains m_pXMLLoadUtility for lazy optional/throne-room XML. CvXMLLoadUtility's own
destructor explicitly comments that the EXE appears to destroy it only when exiting from the
opening menu and that deleting it from another path risks double deletion. Current source does
not clear GC.m_pXMLLoadUtility in that destructor.

The pointer can therefore look dangling in isolation, but its only lazy consumers are meaningful
before that menu-exit teardown. No local post-destruction consumer is proved. Preserve as an
external-lifetime seam, not F274.

VI. CAMERA_START_DISTANCE STATIC BASELINE — INTENTIONAL, NOT A CACHE BUG
------------------------------------------------------------------------
The current source comment questions the function-local static
m_fCAMERA_START_DISTANCE_Override. History resolves the intent: the automatic/default-camera
feature deliberately captures the original XML CAMERA_START_DISTANCE before the function starts
overwriting that same GlobalDefine. BUG's "Custom (XML)" option calls updateCameraStartDistance
with bReset=true specifically to restore this captured XML baseline. Re-reading the already
mutated define instead would lose the original custom XML value.

The static is therefore the persistence mechanism for the baseline, not accidental stale caching.
No F274.

CONTROL / CORRECTION — FunctionTypes does NOT numerically match GlobalTypes.xml, but this is a stock dormant asymmetry rather than a current SAS defect

The earlier broad fixed-string-array control was too strong when it said that every inherited fixed GlobalTypes count matched its C++ enum. Rechecking the current enum against an independent Civ4CE BtS GlobalTypes.xml exposed one exception:

Current SAS CvEnums.h contains six FunctionTypes:

    FUNC_NOINTERP,
    FUNC_LINKEY,
    FUNC_BEZKEY,
    FUNC_TCBKEY,
    FUNC_EULERKEY,
    FUNC_STEPKEY,

so NUM_FUNC_TYPES is 6 in the DLL build.

CvXMLLoadUtility::SetGlobalTypes() deliberately calls:

    int iEnumVal = NUM_FUNC_TYPES;
    SetGlobalStringArray(&GC.getFunctionTypes(),
            "Civ4Types/FunctionTypes/FunctionType",
            &iEnumVal, true);

With bUseEnum == true, SetGlobalStringArray does not replace iEnumVal with the number of XML nodes. It allocates exactly *iNumVals CvString objects, reads siblings until there are no more, and breaks. Therefore a five-entry FunctionTypes XML section leaves the sixth allocated CvString default/empty rather than overflowing memory.

Independent Civ4CE comparison proves this is not a SAS or AdvCiv regression:
- Civ4CE's stock/BtS CvEnums.h also has the same six FunctionTypes including FUNC_STEPKEY.
- Civ4CE's loader uses the same NUM_FUNC_TYPES + bUseEnum=true loading pattern.
- Civ4CE's BtS GlobalTypes.xml contains only five FunctionType entries: NOINTERP, LINKEY, BEZKEY, TCBKEY and EULERKEY.
- A scan of Civ4CE BtS assets found no STEPKEY / FUNC_STEPKEY reference.

Current SAS evidence is equally non-live:
- The current light-source XML snapshot contains no STEPKEY / FUNC_STEPKEY reference.
- Current C++ references to FUNC_STEPKEY are only the enum declaration itself.
- getFunctionTypes is present in CvGlobals and the CyGlobalContext wrapper, but no current SAS Python caller of getFunctionTypes was found.
- Thus the empty sixth string is not consumed by current repository code/assets, and no current type lookup requires a FUNC_STEPKEY string mapping.
- Commit history shows FUNC_STEPKEY predates SAS and AdvCiv; it is already present in the imported K-Mod/BtS enum lineage.

Disposition:
- Correct the earlier blanket "all fixed counts match" wording: all checked fixed arrays match except this longstanding FunctionTypes 6-enum/5-XML asymmetry.
- Do NOT allocate F274. The actual load is memory-safe, the asymmetry is inherited from stock BtS/Civ4CE, and no current consumer reaches the empty FUNC_STEPKEY slot.
- Keep as latent API/data-contract debt only: a future Python/C++ caller asking GC.getFunctionTypes(FUNC_STEPKEY), or future XML relying on that token through this mapping, would get an empty/unregistered sixth string unless GlobalTypes.xml were extended.

RELATED ASSERT-BUILD CONTROL — duplicate-info-type detection is deliberately/inheritedly _DEBUG-only, but current XML has no trigger

CvGlobals::setInfoTypeFromString contains an additional duplicate-type assertion under #ifdef _DEBUG rather than FASSERT_ENABLE. This superficially resembles F273, but it is not the same SAS regression:
- commit history shows the _DEBUG guard already existed in pre-SAS AdvCiv;
- SAS did not replace an inherited FAssert-visible-in-Assert-build check here;
- the current non-text XML Type scan found 3,869 Type tokens and zero duplicate tokens across files and zero duplicates within a file.
Therefore there is no current duplicate-map overwrite trigger and no independent F274. It remains inherited diagnostic coverage debt if the project ever wants all assertion diagnostics available in the optimized Assert target.
