F272 FINAL REPAIR-BOUNDARY CHECK
--------------------------------
Current SAS has N = 128 ColorInfos and the foreign-replay compatibility path accepts foreign
player-color IDs through 254 when HOF_DISPLAY_OTHER_MOD_REPLAYS is enabled. The current remap:

    (eColor + 7) % N

was intended to skip reserved/system colors 0..6 but maps foreign IDs 249..254 to 0..5.

The narrow suffix-domain repair:

    7 + ((eColor - 7) % (N - 7))

for N > 7 was exhaustively compared across the current accepted foreign range 128..254:

    * 121 already-good mappings, IDs 128..248, remain EXACTLY unchanged;
    * only the six bad mappings change:
          249: 0 -> 7
          250: 1 -> 8
          251: 2 -> 9
          252: 3 -> 10
          253: 4 -> 11
          254: 5 -> 12
    * the repaired result range is 7..127, so the promised reserved prefix is actually skipped.

Thus the repair can preserve every current mapping that already satisfied the contract while
correcting only the proven wrap-back cases. Keep a defensive N <= 7 fallback/assert so the
modulo denominator can never become zero or negative in malformed/future data.

F273 FINAL REPAIR-BOUNDARY / SIBLING CHECK
------------------------------------------
Re-proved the project build contract rather than relying on the prior album statement:

    Debug  -> _DEBUG, which causes FAssert.h to enable FASSERT_ENABLE
    Assert -> release-like flags + /DFASSERT_ENABLE, WITHOUT _DEBUG
    Release-> neither assertion mode

Therefore SAS's richer getDefineINT/FLOAT/STRING diagnostics must be guarded by
FASSERT_ENABLE, not _DEBUG, if they are to preserve Base AdvCiv's optimized Assert-build
coverage.

The already-closed queue-041 CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_update has the same SAS regression root.
Its rich stuck-loop diagnostic can also be guarded by FASSERT_ENABLE, but its
`iMaxAttempts += 4` must remain under _DEBUG because it compensates an earlier _DEBUG-only
`iMaxAttempts -= 4`.

A useful independent in-tree model is CvGame::updateMoves:

    int iMaxUnitUpdateAttempts = 18;
    FAssertMsg(...);              // assertion remains available in Assert
    #ifdef _DEBUG
        iMaxUnitUpdateAttempts += 4; // Debug-only behavioral adjustment
    #endif

This is exactly the separation the CvSelectionGroupAI sibling needs.

A targeted repository-wide scan of assertions near _DEBUG/custom SAS diagnostic blocks found
no second SAS replacement of an inherited always-assert-capable check beyond the already-known
CvGlobals and CvSelectionGroupAI cases. Other hits were inherited Debug-only invariant sweeps
or deliberately SAS-added diagnostic probes that have no Base assertion contract to preserve.
The inherited CvGlobals::setInfoTypeFromString duplicate-type assertion is also _DEBUG-only,
but it predates SAS and current XML contains no duplicate Type trigger; it remains diagnostic
coverage debt, not F273 ancestry and not F274.

FINAL HIGH-FANOUT CONTROLS / REJECTIONS
---------------------------------------
1. GlobalDefine mutation and caches
   Every current literal setDefineINT/FLOAT/STRING path was matched against CvGlobals caching.
   MINIMAP_RENDER_SIZE receives the intended targeted integer-cache update; river generation
   controls are uncached and read directly; current camera/FoV float mutations refresh the
   float cache or deliberately defer and then refresh it. No current stale-cache path survived.

   WAR_SUCCESS_CITY_CAPTURING is clamped to >=1 during full caching because 0 can crash AI,
   while a hypothetical targeted runtime setter would bypass that clamp. Current repository
   code has no such setter, so this is latent API robustness debt, not F274.

2. Type/info maps and current XML
   A current non-text XML scan found 3,869 <Type> tokens and zero duplicate tokens, both within
   individual files and across files. The fixed GlobalTypes string categories likewise contain
   no current cross-category duplicate token that would silently overwrite m_typesMap.

3. FunctionTypes count correction
   The earlier blanket statement that every fixed GlobalTypes count matches its C++ enum was
   corrected. FunctionTypes has six C++ values including FUNC_STEPKEY but stock/current XML has
   five strings. Civ4CE independently reproduces the same six-enum/five-XML contract and the
   same NUM_FUNC_TYPES loader behavior. The sixth CvString remains default-empty safely, and
   neither current SAS nor CE assets/code use FUNC_STEPKEY. Longstanding dormant stock contract
   debt; no F274.

4. Direction / animation string accessor shapes
   getDirectionTypes takes AutomateTypes instead of DirectionTypes, a genuine copy/paste API
   mismatch, but there is no current indexed DLL/Python caller exposing it. AnimationOperator
   constants start at 1001 while the string accessor operationally expects a 0-based array index;
   current CyGlobalContext passes ordinary indices and no C++ caller passes real 1001+ constants.
   Both remain latent API defects rather than current roots.

5. Footstep audio
   getFootstepAudioTypeByTag is badly named but correct. Unit-art RunLoopSoundTag/RunEndSoundTag
   values such as LOOPSTEP_TANK are FootstepAudioTypes tokens; the resulting index is then used
   to fetch the parallel actual sound-script tag such as AS3D_LOOPSTEP_TANK.

6. CvAgents ownership
   CvGlobals::init allocates m_agents and uninit does not delete it. CvAgents retains player/team
   pointers, so this is a real shutdown ownership leak/stale-pointer object. However, no local
   same-loaded-DLL second init or post-uninit consumer could be established. Without the EXE
   lifecycle proof needed to turn it into a live re-entry failure, it stays cleanup debt.

7. cacheGlobals / CvPythonCaller / XML-loader lifetime
   cacheGlobals allocates m_pPythonCaller without first deleting an existing one, and CvGlobals
   retains a raw CvXMLLoadUtility pointer for lazy loading. Both are potentially dangerous under
   an undocumented repeated EXE bootstrap/reload cycle, but current DLL source does not prove
   that cycle. CvXMLLoadUtility's own destructor history explicitly discusses EXE ownership and
   double-deletion risk. Do not infer a root from external lifecycle speculation.

8. Lazy throne-room sequencing
   AdvCiv advc.003v deliberately introduced the lazy-load call specifically in exported
   getNumThroneRoomInfos(), with the comment "Load it as late as possible." LoadThroneRoomInfo
   atomically loads camera, room and style arrays and guards repeat loading with bThroneRoomLoaded.
   Other exported room/style accessors do not independently force the load, so this relies on the
   known EXE enumeration order. No current DLL-side caller violates that order and this exact
   sequencing is the original AdvCiv design; keep as an external-engine contract, not F274.

9. Main-menu / landscape exported bounds
   getMainMenus repairs a saved index >= current menu count because switching to a mod with fewer
   menu backgrounds is the known producer. It does not repair a negative index, but current UI
   producers emit valid nonnegative indices and the Python wrapper checks both bounds. Negative
   handling would harden corrupted/external profile input; no current producer was found.

   setActiveLandscapeID has no local bounds check and the derived plot-cell getters index by the
   active ID. It is EXE-owned state with no DLL setter caller; no invalid current producer was
   proved. Add an assertion if desired for robustness, but not as F274.

10. Plot-group FAStar
    getPlotGroupFinder contains an advc.test FError and lazily initializes geometry once, which
    initially raised stale-map-size concerns. AdvCiv explicitly marks it unused inside the DLL
    after CvPlotGroup::recalculatePlots stopped using it. No current internal consumer exists;
    exported legacy contract only, so no live stale-geometry root.

11. XML binary cache
    The binary info-cache read/write machinery is behind ENABLE_XML_FILE_CACHE == 0 in current
    SAS. Historical compile fixes for the branch do not make it a current runtime issue.

12. Camera baseline
    The function-static CAMERA_START_DISTANCE override is intentional: it preserves the original
    XML baseline while runtime camera logic overwrites the GlobalDefine, enabling the BUG
    "Custom (XML)" reset. Treating the static as stale and replacing it with repeated define reads
    would destroy the very baseline it is meant to preserve.

13. History / independent implementation scan
    AdvCiv repair streams touching CvGlobals were challenged for adjacent misses: async-random
    memory corruption/type ownership, startup audio EVENT_MESSAGE_TIME caching, optional/throne
    assertion-variable compile fixes, XML-info refactors/cache compilation, invalid menu-profile
    guard, camera evolution and replay compatibility. K-Mod/Civ4CE comparisons did not expose an
    additional surviving current root. The normalized SAS-vs-Base semantic delta in CvGlobals is
    tiny; beyond F273 it is predominantly comments/formatting rather than a broad SAS rewrite.

FUNCTION-FAMILY SATURATION
--------------------------
The final inventory covered constructor/init/uninit ownership; external engine pointers;
pathfinder globals; replay color access; lazy optional/throne loading; active landscape and
playable-civ state; fixed global string arrays; footstep mappings; GlobalDefine integer/float
caches and runtime setters; camera updates; hardcoded EXE define-pointer fallback; type/info
maps and reset seams; XML binary cache helpers; enum/count adapters; profiler/graphics globals;
and the remaining exported integer-index accessors.

No unexamined CvGlobals.cpp function family remains that plausibly hides an independent current
root under the audit standard. F272 and F273 are independent: replay-color arithmetic versus
SAS assertion-build gating. Queue 040 therefore closes with those two roots and F274 unused.

F274 / provisional KI#597
-------------------------
TITLE: USE_DO_GOODY_CALLBACK can null-dereference when a goody hut is removed by plot ownership

CURRENT CODE ROOT
-----------------
CvPythonCaller::doGoody accepts a nullable unit pointer:

    bool CvPythonCaller::doGoody(CvPlot const& kPlot, CvUnit const* pUnit,
        PlayerTypes ePlayer) const

and its own adjacent comment explicitly preserves the old contract:

    // Note: pUnit can be NULL, but pyUnit can still be initialized (and is expected by Python).

but current AdvCiv/SAS then does:

    CyUnit* pyUnit = new CyUnit(*pUnit);

Dereferencing pUnit is undefined/crashing when pUnit == NULL.

LIVE NULL CALLER
----------------
This is not merely a misleading nullable signature. CvPlot::setOwner still contains a live call:

    if (isOwned())
    {
        if (isGoody())
            GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).doGoody(this, NULL);
        ...
    }

CvPlayer::doGoody immediately calls the wrapper before ordinary hut handling:

    if (GC.getPythonCaller()->doGoody(*pPlot, pUnit, getID()))
        return;

Therefore, when USE_DO_GOODY_CALLBACK is enabled, an owned goody plot that reaches this
ownership path invokes CvPythonCaller::doGoody with NULL and crashes while constructing the
CyUnit Python wrapper. Typical exposure is a goody hut being absorbed/removed through plot
ownership or culture rather than being entered by a unit.

CONFIGURATION / SEVERITY BOUNDARY
---------------------------------
Current Assets/XML/PythonCallbackDefines.xml sets:

    USE_DO_GOODY_CALLBACK = 0

so stock SAS defaults do not execute the bad dereference. This remains a real supported callback
configuration defect rather than a default-game crash: the define exists specifically to enable
this Python override, and enabling it exposes the live NULL caller immediately when the
ownership-hut path occurs.

ANCESTRY / INDEPENDENT CONTROL
------------------------------
K-Mod 1.46 uses the safe nullable-pointer form directly in CvPlayer::doGoody:

    CyUnit kGoodyUnit(pUnit);

CyUnit has a pointer constructor:

    CyUnit::CyUnit(CvUnit* pUnit) : m_pUnit(pUnit) {}

so NULL is a deliberate representable Python-wrapper state.

AdvCiv practical 2066, commit ffe04c3efd, is titled "Avoid some const_casts". Its CvPythonCaller
change is exactly:

    - CyUnit* pyUnit = new CyUnit(const_cast<CvUnit*>(pUnit));
    + CyUnit* pyUnit = new CyUnit(*pUnit);

The surrounding comment saying pUnit can be NULL was left unchanged. Thus the root is narrowly
identified: a const-cast cleanup replaced the nullable pointer constructor with the reference
constructor and broke the preserved NULL contract. Current Base AdvCiv 1.14 still contains the
same regression; SAS inherits it unchanged.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The repair must preserve both existing modes:

1. non-NULL unit: Python receives a CyUnit wrapper for that unit;
2. NULL unit: Python still receives a CyUnit Python object whose internal unit pointer is NULL,
   matching BtS/K-Mod and the explicit comment/contract.

The smallest historical repair is to restore the pointer constructor (requiring the old
const_cast because the wrapper stores CvUnit*), e.g. the exact pre-2066 form. An alternative
without dereferencing NULL is to explicitly choose default/null CyUnit construction for the NULL
case and the reference constructor for non-NULL. Do not "fix" this by refusing the callback when
pUnit is NULL; that would change the inherited Python callback contract on the ownership path.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F274 is independent of queue-040 F272/F273. It is a nullable Python-wrapper construction
regression in AdvCiv's callback refactor/const cleanup, not replay-color arithmetic or assertion
build gating.

EARLY QUEUE-037 CONTROLS / COVERAGE
-----------------------------------
- Normalized SAS-vs-Base AdvCiv semantic delta in CvPythonCaller.cpp is very small. The current
  substantive SAS changes are already-reviewed repairs such as the int AI_foundValue contract,
  riverValue hybrid/default handling and minStartingDistanceMod lower-bound restoration.
- The four central call(...) overloads initialize m_bLastCallSuccessful on both the module-missing
  and actual-call paths; no stale-success carryover was found in those wrappers in this opening
  pass.
- The F274 trigger is not inferred from the signature alone: the live CvPlot::setOwner NULL caller,
  current callback define, CyUnit constructors, K-Mod predecessor and precise AdvCiv regression
  commit were all checked locally before promotion.

NEXT CURSOR
-----------

constructions for nullable/lifetime mismatches; then callback result/default semantics,
isOverride/pythonUsingDefaultImpl state, exceptional or missing-function paths, random-event
object mutation, map-script vector/enum bounds, and practical-history sibling regressions.

F275 / provisional KI#598
-------------------------
TITLE: CvPythonCaller::canBuild rejects positive Python override values above 1 despite the
       inherited callback contract

CURRENT CODE
------------
CvPythonCaller::canBuild contains the preserved contract comment:

    "Returning -1 means ignore; 0 means Build cannot be performed; 1 or greater means it can"

but after handling -1 it does:

    bOverride = true;
    FAssertBounds(-1, 2, lResult);
    return toBool(lResult);

CvPythonCaller::toBool is:

    static bool toBool(long l) { FAssert(l >= 0); return (l == TRUE); }

Therefore a valid positive callback result such as 2 has two wrong consequences:

- Assert DLL: FAssertBounds(-1, 2, 2) fires because the upper bound is exclusive;
- Release DLL: the assertion disappears, but toBool(2) returns false because 2 != TRUE (1).

The wrapper thus interprets 2+ as "cannot build" even though its own inherited contract says
1 or greater means the build can be performed.

PRE-REFACTOR / K-MOD CONTROL
----------------------------
The practical-1648 source immediately before extraction into CvPythonCaller used:

    long lResult = 0;
    callFunction(..., "canBuild", ..., &lResult);
    if (lResult >= 1)
        return true;
    else if (lResult == 0)
        return false;

Current K-Mod 1.46 retains the same >= 1 interpretation. Civ4CE's stock BtS CvGameUtils.py also
documents the same callback contract: -1 ignore, 0 deny, 1 or greater allow.

ANCESTRY
--------
The mismatch was introduced directly by AdvCiv practical 1648 (commit 553b1a0f8d, "Moved
DLL-to-Python calls and logging into separate classes"). The new wrapper copied the correct
contract into a comment but immediately narrowed it to {-1,0,1} through FASSERT_BOUNDS and then
used the exact-one helper. Base AdvCiv 1.14 still contains the regression; SAS inherits it.

CONFIGURATION BOUNDARY
----------------------
USE_CAN_BUILD_CALLBACK is 0 in current SAS defaults, as are all 54 callback defines cached by
CvPythonCaller. The defect becomes live when the supported canBuild callback is enabled and the
Python override returns a positive value greater than 1. This is therefore configuration-gated,
not a default-gameplay regression.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Preserve all three documented states:

    -1      -> no Python override; continue C++ canBuild logic
     0      -> Python override denies build
    >= 1    -> Python override allows build

A narrow repair should therefore return lResult >= 1 once lResult != -1 and remove/relax the
incorrect exclusive upper-bound assertion. Do not change CvPythonCaller::toBool globally on the
strength of this finding: several other inherited callbacks historically used exact == 1, and
queue 037 is auditing those contracts individually rather than assuming one universal Python
truthiness convention.

ADDITIONAL CONTROLS
-------------------
- The callback-define table itself is internally complete: all 54 DO_FOR_EACH_CALLBACK_DEFINE
  entries have exactly one matching USE_*_CALLBACK integer define in current
  PythonCallbackDefines.xml. Eight additional USE_* event callbacks belong to the separate
  CvDllPythonEvents path, so they are not omissions from this table. All 62 current callback
  defines are 0 by default.
- K-Mod controls show that many UI callbacks really did use exact == 1, so the existence of
  CvPythonCaller::toBool is not itself enough to report a broad defect. F275 is promoted because
  canBuild has a specific explicit >= 1 contract and direct pre-refactor comparison.
- `updateColoredPlots` is the only wrapper-local `long lResult;` without initialization. Its
  Python function is expected to exist and the pre-refactor K-Mod code also depended on a
  successful call after setting the local result to 0. Current uninitialized-on-Python-error
  behavior is being retained as an error-path robustness lead, not yet F276.

NEXT CURSOR
-----------
Continue from F276 unused. Highest-value active checks:
- doPillageGold's negative/error sentinel versus K-Mod's old `lPillageGold < 0` fallback;
- callback call-failure defaults and uninitialized return storage;
- random-event mutable EventTriggeredData and pointer-output refresh consistency;
- map-script `isOverride()`/usingDefaultImpl and result validation;
- history commits that fixed post-1648 callback regressions, looking for unfixed siblings.

F275 SAME-ROOT SIBLING EVIDENCE
-------------------------------
The exact-one narrowing introduced by practical 1648 is not limited to canBuild. The two map
placement callbacks were also moved behind CvPythonCaller::toBool by the same refactor:

    CvPythonCaller::canPlaceBonusAt -> canPlaceItemAt
    CvPythonCaller::canPlaceGoodyAt -> canPlaceItemAt

Current canPlaceItemAt validates only negativity and then does:

    if (lResult < 0)
    {
        ...
        bOverride = false;
        return false;
    }
    return toBool(lResult);

Before practical 1648, both CvMapGenerator callbacks did this directly:

    if (result >= 0)
        return result;

where the function return type is bool. C++ therefore treated every nonzero positive long as
true. Practical 1648 replaced that implicit nonzero truth conversion with toBool(result), which
returns true only for exactly 1. Hence a custom map callback that historically returned 2 (or
another positive integer) changes from true to false after the refactor.

This is recorded as SAME-ROOT SUPPORT for F275 rather than a new finding. The canBuild case is the
strongest proof because its Python documentation explicitly says "1 or greater"; the canPlace*
case has direct predecessor behavior but no equally explicit current Python contract. Current SAS
ships only one script defining those hooks, Planet_Generator_0_68.py, and it delegates to the
default implementation rather than returning a custom positive integer, so no shipped default
trigger was found. The evidence nevertheless confirms that toBool cannot safely be assumed to
preserve every pre-refactor callback contract.

F276 / provisional KI#599
-------------------------
TITLE: Enabled doPillageGold callback suppresses the inherited C++ gold fallback on negative or
       failed Python results

CURRENT CODE ROOT
-----------------
CvPythonCaller::doPillageGold initializes a distinct error sentinel but returns true whenever the
callback define is enabled:

    int const iError = MIN_INT;
    ARGSLIST(iError);
    ...
    call("doPillageGold", argsList, lResult);
    ...
    if (lResult != iError)
        iPillageGold = toInt(lResult);
    else FAssert(lResult != iError);
    return true;

Its caller in CvUnit treats the wrapper's bool as "Python supplied the pillage result":

    int iPillageGold = 0;
    if (!GC.getPythonCaller()->doPillageGold(*this, kPlot, iPillageGold))
    {
        // K-Mod C++ fallback calculation
        ...
    }

Consequences when USE_DO_PILLAGE_GOLD_CALLBACK is enabled:

1. Python returns -1 (or any other negative value except MIN_INT): the wrapper copies the negative
   value to iPillageGold and returns true. The C++ fallback is skipped; the later `> 0` test then
   awards no pillage gold.
2. The Python call fails and leaves the MIN_INT initializer unchanged: the wrapper asserts in an
   assertion build but still returns true. In Release, iPillageGold remains the caller's 0 and the
   C++ fallback is again skipped, yielding no pillage gold.

PRE-REFACTOR / K-MOD CONTRACT
------------------------------
The practical-1648 diff shows the exact displaced K-Mod logic:

    long lPillageGold = -1;
    int iPillageGold = -1;
    if (GC.getUSE_DO_PILLAGE_GOLD_CALLBACK())
    {
        ... callFunction(..., &lPillageGold);
        iPillageGold = (int)lPillageGold;
    }
    if (lPillageGold < 0)
    {
        // K-Mod. C version of the original python code
        ... calculate pillage gold in C++ ...
    }

Thus negative values were explicitly the fallback state, not merely an accidental result of a
particular Python implementation. Initialization to -1 also meant a failed/no-result Python call
fell through to the C++ calculation.

The stock BtS/Civ4CE CvGameUtils.doPillageGold implementation returns an ordinary nonnegative gold
amount, so default Python does not intentionally exercise the negative sentinel. The regression is
therefore a callback/error-path compatibility defect, not a default-config gameplay problem.
Current SAS sets USE_DO_PILLAGE_GOLD_CALLBACK = 0 by default.

SIBLING CONTROL: captureGold PRESERVES ITS ERROR FALLBACK
---------------------------------------------------------
The same practical-1648 refactor created CvPythonCaller::captureGold with an almost identical
MIN_INT sentinel, but that wrapper correctly distinguishes failure:

    if (lResult != iError)
    {
        iCaptureGold = toInt(lResult);
        return true;
    }
    else FAssert(lResult != iError);
    return false;

Its caller performs the C++ capture-gold calculation when false is returned. This sibling design
supports the interpretation that doPillageGold's unconditional `return true` is an accidental
loss of fallback semantics rather than an intentional policy that callback enablement must suppress
C++ fallback after Python failure.

ANCESTRY
--------
The root is introduced directly by AdvCiv practical 1648 (commit 553b1a0f8d), which extracted the
old CvUnit Python call into CvPythonCaller. Later AdvCiv history moves/reformats the pillage caller
but does not repair CvPythonCaller::doPillageGold's result contract. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current
SAS retain it.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Preserve the inherited and current successful modes:

- callback disabled -> return false so C++ computes pillage gold;
- callback enabled and Python returns a valid nonnegative amount -> write it, return true;
- callback enabled but Python returns a negative sentinel or the call fails -> return false and
  leave iPillageGold untouched so the existing C++ fallback runs.

A narrow repair can therefore treat `lResult < 0` as "no valid Python amount" and return false.
That naturally includes the MIN_INT call-failure initializer and restores K-Mod's old any-negative
fallback. Do not blindly clamp negative Python results to zero; zero is a valid explicit override
meaning no pillage gold, while a negative result historically requested/defaulted to C++ logic.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F276 is independent of F274's nullable CyUnit construction and F275's positive-boolean narrowing.
It is a lost fallback/sentinel contract in the output-valued pillage callback, though all three
were exposed by auditing the practical-1648 extraction boundary.

ADDITIONAL CONTROLS / COVERAGE
-------------------------------
- History grep found no later CvPythonCaller doPillageGold repair after practical 1648; later
  commits touching the call site reorganize CvUnit pillaging but retain the wrapper contract.
- `captureGold` provides an internal same-refactor control showing that an output callback can and
  should return false when its Python result remains at an error sentinel.
- `updateColoredPlots` still has an uninitialized `long lResult` unlike the pre-refactor `= 0`;
  this remains a separate failure-path robustness lead, not folded into F276 without further
  sibling/error-contract review.

NEXT CURSOR
-----------
Continue from F277 unused / provisional KI#600 next. Highest-value active checks:
- determine whether updateColoredPlots's uninitialized result is an isolated failure-path defect
  or part of a wider practical-1648 default-initialization regression;
- systematically compare all map-script callback result/default/override semantics against the
  pre-1648/Civ4CE implementations, especially enum and pointer-return outputs;
- audit random-event mutable EventTriggeredData copy-back and output-pointer refresh contracts;
- inspect central call(...) exception/missing-module behavior and callback recursion guards;
- use later AdvCiv callback-fix commits (1662, 1677, 1850, 1917, 1966, 2460, 2531, 2571) as
  repair-boundary probes for unfixed siblings.

F277 / provisional KI#600
-------------------------
TITLE: CvPythonCaller::addFeatures falsely asserts when a valid map script omits the optional
       Python hook and falls back to C++ feature generation

CURRENT CODE ROOT
-----------------
Most optional map-generation phase wrappers explicitly suppress call-success assertions because
absence of the Python override is a normal signal to run the inherited C++ implementation:

    bool CvPythonCaller::addBonuses() const
    {
        call("addBonuses", m_python.getMapScriptModule(), false);
        return isOverride();
    }

    bool CvPythonCaller::addGoodies() const
    {
        call("addGoodies", m_python.getMapScriptModule(), false);
        return isOverride();
    }

    bool CvPythonCaller::addLakes() const
    {
        call("addLakes", m_python.getMapScriptModule(), false);
        return isOverride();
    }

    bool CvPythonCaller::addRivers() const
    {
        call("addRivers", m_python.getMapScriptModule(), false);
        return isOverride();
    }

But addFeatures uniquely leaves the default bAssertSuccess=true:

    bool CvPythonCaller::addFeatures() const
    {
        call("addFeatures", m_python.getMapScriptModule());
        return isOverride();
    }

The central no-result call wrapper does:

    m_bLastCallSuccessful = m_python.callFunction(...);
    FAssert(!bAssertSuccess || m_bLastCallSuccessful);

Thus a selected map module that simply omits addFeatures produces an assertion in an
assertion-enabled DLL even though `isOverride()` then correctly returns false and
CvMapGenerator::addFeatures continues with the normal C++ fallback.

LIVE CURRENT SAS TRIGGER
------------------------
Current SAS ships 50 PrivateMaps scripts. A direct current-data scan finds exactly one without a
`def addFeatures(` callback:

    PrivateMaps/SAS_Simple_Flat_Grass.py

This is not an accidental empty/broken script. It is a deliberately minimal playable SAS map
wrapper. Its only wildcard import is SAS_WorldSizeUtils, whose exported functions are world-size
helpers and do not define addFeatures. Therefore selecting this current map script reaches the
missing-hook path.

The practical consequence is build-dependent:

- Debug / Assert DLL: the missing optional hook makes m_bLastCallSuccessful false and triggers the
  FAssert in CvPythonCaller::call;
- Release DLL: the assertion is absent; isOverride() is safely false and CvMapGenerator performs
  its inherited C++ feature placement as intended.

This is therefore a false-positive diagnostic/assertion regression on a supported current SAS map,
not a Release-gameplay failure.

PRE-REFACTOR CONTRACT
---------------------
Immediately before practical 1648, CvMapGenerator::addFeatures used:

    if (gDLL->getPythonIFace()->callFunction(mapModule, "addFeatures", NULL))
    {
        if (!gDLL->getPythonIFace()->pythonUsingDefaultImpl())
            return;
    }
    // C++ feature generation follows

A missing/failed Python function therefore did not assert; it simply left the function in the C++
fallback path. Practical 1648 replaced that block with:

    if (GC.getPythonCaller()->addFeatures())
        return;

and the newly extracted wrapper accidentally retained call()'s assertion-on-success default.

INTERNAL / HISTORY CONTROL
--------------------------
The neighboring addBonuses/addGoodies/addLakes/addRivers wrappers created in the same extraction
all pass `false`, matching their optional/fallback nature. This makes addFeatures the local outlier.

AdvCiv practical 1662 provides an independent meaning-of-the-flag control: it explicitly changed
applyEvent to pass `false` because “Many of the apply functions named in XML don't exist.” That
history confirms callFunction failure for a missing Python function is exactly the condition the
bAssertSuccess parameter is meant to tolerate when absence is valid.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 currently bundles eight PrivateMaps scripts and all eight define addFeatures, so
the inherited wrapper bug is latent under Base's shipped map set. SAS's new minimal map script
makes the defect live without changing CvPythonCaller itself.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Make addFeatures consistent with the other optional map phase hooks:

    call("addFeatures", m_python.getMapScriptModule(), false);

Do not force SAS_Simple_Flat_Grass.py to define a dummy function merely to satisfy the wrapper;
omitting the hook is an inherited valid way to request/default to C++ generation. Preserve
isOverride()/pythonUsingDefaultImpl behavior for scripts that do implement addFeatures.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F277 is separate from F273. F273 accidentally removes legitimate assertions from the optimized
Assert build by gating richer diagnostics with `_DEBUG`; F277 is the opposite kind of diagnostic
contract error: it emits an assertion on a valid optional-callback fallback. The repairs and code
roots are independent.

F278 / provisional KI#601
-------------------------
TITLE: CvPythonCaller::updateColoredPlots consumes an uninitialized Python result when the
       callback call fails, losing the inherited deterministic C++ fallback

CURRENT CODE ROOT
-----------------
CvPythonCaller::updateColoredPlots is the only function in the current file that declares a bare
uninitialized result variable:

    bool CvPythonCaller::updateColoredPlots() const
    {
        long lResult;
        call("updateColoredPlots", lResult);
        return toBool(lResult);
    }

The central call wrapper records Python call success separately:

    m_bLastCallSuccessful = m_python.callFunction(..., &lResult);
    FAssert(!bAssertSuccess || m_bLastCallSuccessful);

and CvDLLPythonIFaceBase exposes callFunction as a bool-returning interface with an output pointer;
there is no DLL-side contract that the output is written when the call returns false. Therefore,
if Python fails before producing a long result, updateColoredPlots still evaluates the untouched
stack value through toBool().

The behavior depends on build/error handling:

- Debug / Assert: the central FAssert reports the failed call, but if execution continues/Ignore is
  chosen then the indeterminate result is still consumed;
- Release: the assertion vanishes and the uninitialized value is consumed immediately. It can
  spuriously return true and skip all inherited C++ colored-plot generation, or false by accident.

This is undefined behavior in C++, not merely an arbitrary fallback choice.

PRE-REFACTOR / K-MOD CONTROL
----------------------------
Immediately before AdvCiv practical 1648 extracted this callback, CvGame::updateColoredPlots used:

    long lResult = 0;
    gDLL->getPythonIFace()->callFunction(PYGameModule,
            "updateColoredPlots", NULL, &lResult);
    if (lResult == 1)
        return;

Thus a failed/no-result Python call deterministically left zero in place and continued into the
normal C++ colored-plot implementation. Current K-Mod 1.46 retains that same `lResult = 0`
initialization, and BUG's current default for updateColoredPlots is false, matching the fallback.

ANCESTRY
--------
The bug is introduced directly by AdvCiv practical 1648 (553b1a0f8d, "Moved DLL-to-Python calls
and logging into separate classes"). The same commit removes `long lResult = 0` from
CvGameInterface.cpp and creates CvPythonCaller::updateColoredPlots with `long lResult;`.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the regression; SAS inherits it unchanged.

TRIGGER / SEVERITY BOUNDARY
---------------------------
The normal SAS PYGameModule and CvGameInterface.updateColoredPlots function exist, and BUG supplies
an ordinary false default, so normal successful calls do not exercise the bad value. The live
trigger is a Python call failure/exception/no-result path (for example while developing/reloading
Python or after a script error). updateColoredPlots is invoked repeatedly by ordinary UI/game
state changes, so once the Python side is broken the path is reachable without special XML callback
enablement.

This is therefore best classified as an error-path robustness/undefined-behavior regression rather
than a default healthy-script gameplay defect. It is still stronger than a mere assertion issue:
Release builds can make a control-flow decision from indeterminate storage.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Restore the inherited false/default state locally:

    long lResult = false; // or = 0

before the call. Do not attempt to solve this by globally changing call() to overwrite all output
arguments on failure; other wrappers intentionally use distinct sentinels such as MIN_INT, -1,
NO_TECH and caller-provided defaults. updateColoredPlots simply needs its own historical default
restored.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F278 is independent of F274-F277. It is an uninitialized-output regression on Python call failure,
not nullable wrapper construction (F274), numeric boolean-contract narrowing (F275), lost negative
fallback sentinel (F276), or optional map-hook assertion policy (F277).

ADDITIONAL CONTROL
------------------
A file-wide declaration scan found no second bare `long lResult;` in current CvPythonCaller.cpp.
All other ordinary long-result wrappers initialize through ARGSLIST(default) or explicit sentinel/
default variables. Therefore F278 is a localized extraction omission, not evidence that every
callback return is uninitialized on failure.

NEXT CURSOR
-----------
Continue from F279 unused / provisional KI#602. Audit map-script enum/index/vector return bounds and
hybrid/default semantics; then random-event mutable output refresh, ordinary callback sentinel/
truthiness contracts, and later practical-history fixes. Keep malformed-script-only bounds issues
as controls unless current SAS assets or a supported fallback path make them live.

F279 / provisional KI#602
-------------------------
TITLE
Active EVENT_FARM_BANDITS_2 names a nonexistent PythonHelp function, while
CvPythonCaller::eventHelp treats Python-help dispatch as mandatory and asserts on failure.

CURRENT DATA / CODE
-------------------
Current SAS CIV4EventInfos.xml contains this active (not commented-out) field:

    <Type>EVENT_FARM_BANDITS_2</Type>
    ...
    <PythonHelp>getHelpFarmBandit2</PythonHelp>

A comment-aware scan of the complete current random-event Python namespace finds no definition of
`getHelpFarmBandit2` in Assets/Python/EntryPoints/CvRandomEventInterface.py.

The wrapper is strict:

    CvWString CvPythonCaller::eventHelp(EventTypes eEvent,
            EventTriggeredData const* pTriggered) const
    {
        char const* szHelp = GC.getInfo(eEvent).getPythonHelp();
        if (std::strlen(szHelp) <= 0)
            return L"";
        CvWString szResult;
        CyArgsList argsList;
        argsList.add(eEvent);
        argsList.add(m_python.makePythonObject(pTriggered));
        m_bLastCallSuccessful = m_python.callFunction(PYRandomEventModule, szHelp,
                argsList.makeFunctionArgs(), &szResult);
        FAssert(m_bLastCallSuccessful);
        if (std::wcslen(szResult) == 0)
            return L"";
        szResult.insert(0, NEWLINE);
        return szResult;
    }

CvGameTextMgr::setEventHelp unconditionally appends eventHelp(...) while constructing an event
choice's displayed help, so this is a display-time callback contract rather than an apply-event-only
path.

REACHABILITY
------------
EVENT_FARM_BANDITS_2 is one of the three choices of the active
EVENTTRIGGER_FARM_BANDITS trigger. Current XML gives that trigger:

    <iPercentGamesActive>85</iPercentGamesActive>
    <iWeight>200</iWeight>
    ...
    <Events>
        <Event>EVENT_FARM_BANDITS_1</Event>
        <Event>EVENT_FARM_BANDITS_2</Event>
        <Event>EVENT_FARM_BANDITS_3</Event>
    </Events>

and the recurring EVENTTRIGGER_FARM_BANDITS_AGAIN also includes the same event choices. Thus the
missing callback is not dead/commented XML.

The choice's actual effects are already represented in ordinary EventInfo fields (not Python):
among them iUnitImmobileTurns=2 and iFood=-5. There is no PythonCallback or PythonCanDo attached to
the event. That makes the dangling PythonHelp look like stale data rather than evidence that a
missing custom behavior needs to be reconstructed.

OBSERVED CONTRACT CONSEQUENCE
-----------------------------
When help for EVENT_FARM_BANDITS_2 is built:

- Assert/Debug builds: the failed call reaches `FAssert(m_bLastCallSuccessful)`, producing a false
  assertion on a valid shipped random event.
- Release builds: the failed call yields no custom Python help; eventHelp returns an empty string
  after the failed dispatch. The generic C++ help for the XML-defined effects is still constructed.

This is therefore primarily a shipped-data/diagnostic defect rather than a gameplay-state defect,
but it is live under ordinary random-event play and stronger than a malformed-mod-only input.

ANCESTRY
--------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same active XML PythonHelp token and likewise has no corresponding
Python definition. K-Mod also contains the same XML token and no definition. The mismatch is
therefore inherited rather than SAS-created.

A first raw-text namespace scan appeared to find additional missing hooks such as
canTriggerIndependentFilms/getHelpIndependentFilms. That was a false positive because SAS preserves
their removed values inside XML comments. Re-running the scan after stripping XML comments proves
that all active trigger eligibility hooks resolve:

- EventTrigger PythonCanDo: 72 unique, 0 missing.
- EventTrigger PythonCanDoCity: 9 unique, 0 missing.
- EventTrigger PythonCanDoUnit: 1 unique, 0 missing.
- EventInfo PythonCanDo: 31 unique, 0 missing.
- EventInfo PythonExpireCheck: 6 unique, 0 missing.

The only active EventInfo PythonHelp name missing from current random-event Python is
`getHelpFarmBandit2`.

The EventInfo PythonCallback namespace has 11 missing apply* names. Those are a separate, known
contract: AdvCiv practical 1662 explicitly changed applyEvent dispatch to `bAssertSuccess=false`
because many XML-named apply functions legitimately do not exist. They do not strengthen F279.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The narrowest evidence-supported repair is data-side:

    <PythonHelp/>

for EVENT_FARM_BANDITS_2.

Do not invent a new Python function merely to satisfy the stale name unless historical upstream
material establishes an intended extra help string. All currently visible gameplay effects of the
choice are already encoded in XML and therefore described through the ordinary event-help path.

A broader wrapper change that suppresses all eventHelp failures would hide genuinely misspelled
PythonHelp names elsewhere and is not justified by this single bad shipped entry.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F279 is independent of F274-F278. Its root is an active shipped XML -> Python symbol mismatch. It
does not depend on nullable CyUnit construction, truth-value narrowing, sentinel fallback,
optional-map-hook assertion policy, or uninitialized result storage.

F279 ANCESTRY REFINEMENT
------------------------
The WIP06 wording needs one important distinction.

The dangling shipped XML token

    <PythonHelp>getHelpFarmBandit2</PythonHelp>

is inherited: Base AdvCiv and K-Mod contain the same active token and no matching random-event
Python definition.

However, K-Mod's pre-extraction event-help path did NOT assert that the Python dispatch succeeded.
It simply called:

    gDLL->getPythonIFace()->callFunction(
        PYRandomEventModule, kEvent.getPythonHelp(), ..., &szHelp);

and then appended the resulting help string.

AdvCiv practical 1648 moved this into CvPythonCaller::eventHelp and added:

    m_bLastCallSuccessful = m_python.callFunction(...);
    FAssert(m_bLastCallSuccessful);

Therefore F279 has two layers:

1. inherited BtS/K-Mod shipped-data defect: one active PythonHelp symbol has no implementation;
2. AdvCiv practical-1648 policy regression: the old silent missing-help mismatch becomes a repeatable
   Assert/Debug failure when that shipped event choice's help is built.

The repair recommendation remains data-side `<PythonHelp/>`, because the event's actual effects are
already encoded generically in XML and suppressing all eventHelp dispatch failures would hide real
future misspellings.


F280 / provisional KI#603
-------------------------
TITLE
Practical 1648 changed the getUnitCostMod application threshold from `> 1` to `> 0`, so callback
result 1 now reduces unit production cost to 1% instead of preserving the inherited no-override
behavior.

CURRENT CODE
------------
CvPythonCaller::unitCostMod returns the callback integer:

    int CvPythonCaller::unitCostMod(PlayerTypes ePlayer, UnitTypes eUnit) const
    {
        if (!isUse(GET_UNIT_COST_MOD))
            return 0;
        ARGSLIST(0);
        argsList.add(ePlayer);
        argsList.add(eUnit);
        call("getUnitCostMod", argsList, lResult);
        return toInt(lResult);
    }

CvPlayer::getProductionNeeded(UnitTypes) then does:

    int iPyMod = GC.getPythonCaller()->unitCostMod(getID(), eUnit);
    if (iPyMod > 0)
    {
        iProductionNeeded *= iPyMod;
        iProductionNeeded /= 100;
    }
    return std::max(1, iProductionNeeded);

So a result of exactly 1 applies a 1% multiplier. Integer division plus the final clamp means many
ordinary units collapse to 1 hammer.

INHERITED CONTRACT / REGRESSION PROOF
-------------------------------------
Immediately before practical 1648, the same CvPlayer code was:

    long lResult = 0;
    gDLL->getPythonIFace()->callFunction(
        PYGameModule, "getUnitCostMod", ..., &lResult);

    if (lResult > 1)
    {
        iProductionNeeded *= lResult;
        iProductionNeeded /= 100;
    }

K-Mod 1.46 independently retains the same `if (lResult > 1)` contract.

The building-cost sibling also used `> 1` before extraction and CURRENT SAS still preserves it:

    int iPythonModifier = GC.getPythonCaller()->buildingCostMod(*this, eBuilding);
    if (iPythonModifier > 1)
    {
        iProductionNeeded *= iPythonModifier;
        iProductionNeeded /= 100;
    }

Thus the unit-side `> 0` is not a general redesign of the cost callbacks. It is an isolated
extraction-time threshold drift.

BUG/PYTHON DEFAULT CROSS-CHECK
------------------------------
BUG/BugGameUtils.py declares:

    self._setDefault("getUnitCostMod", -1)
    self._setDefault("getBuildingCostMod", -1)

The C++ wrapper's local failure/disabled default of 0 is behaviorally harmless under the inherited
`> 1` consumer contract: -1, 0 and 1 are all non-overrides. The strong bug is therefore not the
wrapper's 0 versus BUG's -1 in isolation; it is that the CURRENT unit consumer accidentally made
1 active.

TRIGGER / SEVERITY
------------------
Current SAS ships:

    USE_GET_UNIT_COST_MOD_CALLBACK = 0

so ordinary default SAS gameplay does not trigger F280. This is a callback/modding-configuration
compatibility regression.

When the callback is enabled, however, result 1 is not malformed according to the inherited C++
interface in the sense relevant here: old K-Mod/AdvCiv explicitly accepted it as a non-applying
result. Any existing callback/mod that returns 1 therefore experiences a drastic behavior change
after the extraction.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Restore the inherited consumer threshold only:

    if (iPyMod > 1)

This exactly matches:
- pre-practical-1648 AdvCiv,
- K-Mod 1.46,
- the current building-cost sibling.

Do not change the meaning of values >=2, and do not globally reinterpret all Python integer
callbacks.

Optionally, the wrapper's local default could later be documented against BUG's -1 default, but
changing it is unnecessary for F280 because both values remain inert once the proper `> 1` guard is
restored.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F280 is independent of F274-F279. It is a percentage-application threshold regression at the
CvPythonCaller consumer boundary. It is not the canBuild truthiness narrowing of F275: here the
callback's numeric value is itself a percentage modifier, and the regression is specifically the
consumer changing an inherited threshold.

ADDITIONAL CONTROLS FROM THIS PASS
----------------------------------
1. BUG game-callback default audit:
   The canonical BUG defaults and CvPythonCaller local defaults line up semantically across the
   ordinary boolean/sentinel callbacks inspected. `getUnitCostMod` / `getBuildingCostMod` are the
   only conspicuous textual -1-vs-0 pair; under the proper >1 consumer contract that textual
   difference does not itself change behavior.

2. Ordinary fallback sentinels:
   `upgradePrice` and `experienceNeeded` return -1 when disabled/failed, and both CvUnit consumers
   explicitly treat `<0` as "use native C++ computation". No lost fallback there.

3. Recommended UI enums:
   recommended tech/unit/building wrappers initialize to NO_TECH/NO_UNIT/NO_BUILDING and the popup
   consumers fall back to native AI recommendations. Out-of-range non-sentinel values remain a
   malformed-Python robustness issue only; no current shipped callback produces them.

4. PrivateMaps custom-option namespace:
   46 shipped scripts define getNumCustomMapOptions; every one of those 46 also defines both
   getCustomMapOptionDefault and getCustomMapOptionDescAt. The four scripts without the count
   function are no-option/special cases handled by the tolerant count wrapper. No second F277-style
   optional-hook assertion was found there.

5. PYGameModule entry-point namespace:
   All 67 literal current game-module callback names used by CvPythonCaller resolve in the current
   CvGameInterface entry-point module. There is no second current shipped missing-symbol analogue
   to the random-event PythonHelp mismatch.

C024-WIP08 — F277 map-default siblings + F281 remains unused

F277 SAME-ROOT EXPANSION — SAS_Simple_Flat_Grass intentionally relies on native/default plot and terrain generation too
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The WIP04 F277 root originally covered the uniquely strict `addFeatures()` wrapper:

    call("addFeatures", m_python.getMapScriptModule());

which falsely asserts when the supported current SAS map `SAS_Simple_Flat_Grass.py` omits that
optional hook and correctly falls back to the native C++ feature generator.

A deeper current-map audit shows that the same supported map intentionally omits two earlier map
generation callbacks as well:

    generatePlotTypes
    generateTerrainTypes

The map file contains only:
- a description callback;
- compact almost-all-land `getGridSize`;
- an import from callback-free `SAS_WorldSizeUtils`.

This is deliberate architecture, not an accidentally truncated script. Current project comments
and history describe it as a playable "simple flat-grass sandbox map" / "almost all land" wrapper.
Before the helper split, the predecessor playable `SAS_WorldSizes.py` likewise exposed only the
description/grid-size callbacks.

WHY THE MINIMAL MAP STILL WORKS
-------------------------------
CvMapGenerator has a native fallback when Python does not provide an overriding plot list:

    if (!GC.getPythonCaller()->generatePlotTypes(paiPlotTypes, iNumPlots))
    {
        for (...)
            paiPlotTypes[i] = PLOT_LAND;
    }

`CvPlot::setPlotType(PLOT_LAND, ...)` then assigns the configured LAND_TERRAIN whenever the plot's
terrain is still NO_TERRAIN:

    if (getTerrainType() == NO_TERRAIN ||
        GC.getInfo(getTerrainType()).isWater() != isWater())
    {
        setTerrainType(isWater() ? ... : eLAND_TERRAIN, ...);
    }

Thus the native plot fallback itself supplies the intended all-land/default-land-terrain baseline.
The later no-override `generateTerrainTypes` path can legitimately leave that terrain in place.
This locally explains the documented flat-grass sandbox behavior without inventing a missing
Python generator.

ADVCIV DIAGNOSTIC REGRESSION
----------------------------
Despite those inherited fallback semantics, practical 1648 introduced hard diagnostic assertions
inside the extracted wrappers:

    if (!isOverride())
    {
        FErrorMsg("Map script has to override generatePlotTypes and mustn't call usingDefaultImpl");
        return false;
    }

and:

    if (!isOverride())
    {
        FErrorMsg("Map script has to override generateTerrainTypes and mustn't call usingDefaultImpl");
        return false;
    }

`FErrorMsg` is simply `FAssertMsg(false, msg)`, so an assertion-enabled build flags the map even
though the C++ fallback path is coherent and, for this current supported SAS script, intentional.

Pre-practical-1648 K-Mod/AdvCiv did not assert either condition. It simply tested:

    callFunction(...) && !pythonUsingDefaultImpl()

and otherwise:
- generated all PLOT_LAND for plot types;
- left terrain unchanged for terrain generation.

Therefore practical 1648 converted normal inherited default-implementation/fallback states into
false diagnostics, just as the strict `addFeatures` extraction did for a missing optional hook.

ROOT CLASSIFICATION
-------------------
Do NOT allocate F281 for these two additional assertions.

They are best recorded as same-root expansion of F277:
"map-script fallback/default implementation is valid, but extracted CvPythonCaller diagnostics
treat fallback as an error."

The concrete code sites differ:
- generatePlotTypes hard FError on !isOverride;
- generateTerrainTypes hard FError on !isOverride;
- addFeatures uses call()'s default bAssertSuccess=true;

but all three are exercised by the same supported deliberately-minimal current SAS map and all
three were non-asserting fallback paths before the extraction.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
F277's original narrow repair remains valid for addFeatures:

    call("addFeatures", mapModule, false);

For generatePlotTypes / generateTerrainTypes, the evidence says that !isOverride itself cannot
universally be diagnosed as an error, because current SAS intentionally supports a map relying on
those fallbacks. Remove/downgrade those FErrorMsg calls (or otherwise exclude the legitimate
default/fallback state) while retaining:
- the result-size diagnostics when an actual overriding Python result has the wrong size;
- the native all-land plot fallback;
- the current terrain already established through setPlotType.

Do not add dummy Python generators merely to silence the wrapper. That would duplicate native
behavior and obscure the intended minimal-script contract.

ADDITIONAL TRUTHINESS CONTROL
-----------------------------
A current shipped-Python scan was performed for literal integer returns from game callbacks whose
practical-1648 extraction moved them through CvPythonCaller::toBool (exactly TRUE == 1).

No current shipped callback implementation was found returning a literal positive integer >1 in
those boolean roles. Therefore the historical nonzero/positive -> exact-one narrowing remains:
- a confirmed F275 root where canBuild's own interface explicitly documents >=1 as yes;
- same-root compatibility evidence for canPlaceBonusAt/canPlaceGoodyAt, whose old C++ bool return
  accepted any nonzero positive result;
- a control for generic boolean callbacks without a current differing-value trigger or explicit
  broader contract.

Do not create F281 merely from theoretical `return 2` behavior in ordinary boolean callbacks.

C024-WIP09 — central-state / mutability / fallback-policy controls
===============================================================================

F281 remains UNUSED / provisional KI#604 next.

RANDOM-EVENT MUTABILITY — CONTROL, NOT A NEW ROOT
-------------------------------------------------
`CvPythonCaller::doEventTrigger` takes:

    EventTriggeredData const& kTriggered

yet passes `&kTriggered` to Python and then deliberately rereads fields with the comment:

    // Python may have changed kTriggered

At first glance this looks like mutation through a const C++ view. The live caller establishes the
important ownership fact, however:

    EventTriggeredData* pTriggerData = addEventTriggered();
    ...
    GC.getPythonCaller()->doEventTrigger(getID(), *pTriggerData, ...)

The underlying object is genuinely mutable and owned by CvPlayer's event-trigger store. The const
reference is merely the wrapper function's local C++ view; it is not an object originally declared
const. Current random-event Python demonstrably uses this historical mutation channel, and the C++
caller explicitly rereads the resulting IDs/types afterward.

`CvDLLPythonIFaceBase::makePythonObject` is a templated non-owning Boost.Python wrapper creator.
Passing `&kTriggered` deduces a const-qualified pointer at that call site, but this interface has
longstanding binding machinery for EventTriggeredData and current shipped hooks successfully mutate
fields exposed through the Python class. No locally demonstrated corruption or mutation of a truly
const object was found.

Classification:
- const-correctness / API-shape debt;
- historical mutable Python data contract;
- not F281 absent a concrete call path with genuinely const storage.

CENTRAL `m_bLastCallSuccessful` / `isOverride` REENTRANCY — CONTROL
-------------------------------------------------------------------
All current uses of `isOverride()` consume the state immediately after the specific wrapper call
whose override status they query. There is no intervening CvPythonCaller invocation on the C++ path.

A nested Python -> DLL -> Python call can temporarily modify the shared member while the outer
`m_python.callFunction(...)` is executing, but the outer statement is:

    m_bLastCallSuccessful = m_python.callFunction(...);

so the outer call's success value is assigned only after the RHS returns, overwriting any temporary
nested value before the outer caller reaches `isOverride()`.

`pythonUsingDefaultImpl()` remains EXE-owned/opaque state, but K-Mod and pre-extraction code used
the same immediate "callFunction, then pythonUsingDefaultImpl" protocol. No current local
counterexample was found.

No F281.

NULLABLE CY-WRAPPER FAMILY — F274 IS LOCALIZED
-----------------------------------------------
A constructor/use scan found no second live F274-style dereference of a nullable raw gameplay
pointer.

Notably:
- `doGoody` remains the exceptional bad case: it dereferences nullable `CvUnit const* pUnit` into a
  reference-taking CyUnit constructor.
- `cannotHandleActionOverride(CvPlot* pPlot, ...)` passes `pPlot` to the pointer-taking `CyPlot`
  constructor and therefore preserves nullability rather than dereferencing it.
- Other reference-taking Cy wrappers are reached through caller contracts that supply live objects.

This strengthens F274's precision rather than broadening it.

ENABLED-CALL FAILURE DEFAULTS FOR POSITIVE PERMISSION CALLBACKS — CONTROL
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Practical 1648 changed several wrappers from old direct-call local result `0` to an initialized
`true` result before dispatch, including:
- `canPickPlot`
- `citiesDestroyFeatures`
- `canRazeCity`
- `canDeclareWar`

Therefore an enabled callback that *fails to execute* can now fall back permissively where the old
direct code failed closed.

However, BUG/BugGameUtils.py independently declares the canonical callback defaults as True for
all four:
- canPickPlot -> True
- citiesDestroyFeatures -> True
- canRazeCity -> True
- canDeclareWar -> True

The refactor therefore appears to align call-failure/default initialization with each callback's
normal Python/native default, rather than accidentally choosing arbitrary true values. Healthy
callback behavior is unchanged.

This is materially different from:
- F276, where a failed/negative pillage callback suppresses an explicit C++ native calculation;
- F278, where a failed callback leaves an indeterminate stack value;
- F280, where a valid inherited numeric return changes meaning.

Without a healthy shipped trigger or explicit inherited requirement that exceptions must deny the
action, this fail-open-on-error policy change is ambiguous/arguably deliberate graceful
degradation. Keep it as a compatibility/error-policy control, not F281.

GETGRIDSIZE / WORLD-SIZE SENTINEL — CONTROL
-------------------------------------------
Every current shipped PrivateMaps `getGridSize` implementation was enumerated. The common
NO_WORLDSIZE convention is `return []`; `Planet_Generator_0_68.py` is the conspicuous exception:

    if (argsList[0] == -1): # (-1,) is passed to function on loads
        return (-1,-1)

At first glance this looks dangerous because CvPythonCaller::mapGridDimensions accepts any result
with size >=2 and only *asserts* positivity before assigning the dimensions.

The live DLL caller bounds the issue:

    if (pInitInfo != NULL)
        use pInitInfo dimensions;
    else
    {
        WorldSizeTypes eWorldSize = GC.getInitCore().getWorldSize();
        if (eWorldSize != NO_WORLDSIZE)
            ... mapGridDimensions(eWorldSize, ...);
    }

Thus the local DLL path never calls `mapGridDimensions` with NO_WORLDSIZE/-1. Saved-map reset uses
pInitInfo dimensions instead. Planet Generator's comment evidently describes an external
EXE/Python callback circumstance, not this C++ wrapper call.

Current shipped normal-world-size returns are positive tuples or helpers that resolve to positive
dimensions. No live F281.

The wrapper still has malformed-script robustness debt:
- it accepts vectors with >2 values whereas the old/stock code required exactly 2;
- positivity is Assert-only, so a malformed override can install <=0 dimensions in Release.
Both are inherited/third-party malformed-input concerns with no shipped trigger found.

FINDSTARTINGAREA -1 COLLAPSE — CONTROL
--------------------------------------
Pre-practical-1648 code explicitly accepted a Python override result of -1:

    if (result == -1 || m.getArea(result) != NULL)
    {
        areas_by_value.push_back(std::make_pair(result,1));
        return areas_by_value;
    }

Current CvPythonCaller maps -1 to GC.getMap().getArea(-1) == NULL, and the caller interprets NULL as
"no Python area override", proceeding into native area selection.

This is a semantic drift, but downstream inspection weakens rather than strengthens it as a live
bug. Current AdvCiv's `findStartingAreas`/`findStartingPlot` multi-area algorithm filters plots by
exact area id from `areasByValue`. An overriding singleton `(-1,1)` would match no real plot and can
drive starting-plot search to "Could not find starting plot." It is therefore not credible evidence
that current AdvCiv intentionally uses overriding -1 to mean "all areas."

Current shipped scripts support that interpretation:
- scripts that return -1 do so together with `CyPythonMgr().allowDefaultImpl()`;
- ordinary overriding scripts return a real area id;
- no shipped script was found intentionally overriding with -1.

Keep the old explicit allowance as historical API oddity / third-party compatibility seam. Do not
allocate F281 without evidence of a real map that depended on overriding -1.

RUNTIME USE_*_CALLBACK FLAG REFRESH — CONTROL
----------------------------------------------
K-Mod's older generic `CvGlobals::setDefineINT` called full `cacheGlobals()`. This incidentally
meant a runtime:

    gc.setDefineINT("USE_..._CALLBACK", ...)

would refresh the corresponding cached callback guard.

However the loss of that dynamic behavior is NOT a practical-1648 CvPythonCaller regression.
AdvCiv practical 1631 ("Performance optimizations for access to XML data") had already changed
setDefineINT to pinpoint `cacheGlobalInts(szChangedDefine, iNewValue)`. Its changed-define branch
explicitly returned before the callback-flag reload block, with the source comment:

    return; // Don't bother checking the Python callback flags

Practical 1648 later removed those old CvGlobals callback fields and had CvPythonCaller /
CvDllPythonEvents snapshot the flags in arrays. That preserves practical 1631's already-static
assumption rather than newly changing a supported runtime contract.

Current repository scan finds no `setDefineINT`/Python write to any `USE_*_CALLBACK` define.
Current live setDefine uses concern camera/minimap/river-generation values, not callback guards.

Classification:
- K-Mod-to-AdvCiv modding compatibility change;
- explicitly assumed static by pre-CvPythonCaller AdvCiv;
- no current SAS trigger;
- not F281.

MODULE EXISTENCE / SAVED-GAME PATH — CLEAN CONTROL
---------------------------------------------------
The four private `call` overloads all use the same bCheckExists protocol. When requested they call:

    m_python.moduleExists(szModuleName, true)

and set m_bLastCallSuccessful=false without dispatch if the module cannot be loaded.

History establishes why this exists:
- practical 2460 added module-existence checks to prevent a Python error when the Settings tab
  examines a save whose original map script is no longer installed;
- practical 2531 changed bLoadIfNecessary from false to true to recover cleanly after Python reload
  errors when possible.

Current consumers line up with that policy:
- numCustomMapOptions tolerates absence and returns initialized 0;
- customMapOptionDefault asserts success only for a non-saved game; saved games may return
  NO_CUSTOM_MAPOPTION, and CvMap::getNonDefaultCustomMapOptionDesc explicitly treats negative
  default as "couldn't be loaded (script may have been removed)";
- customMapOptionDescription independently tolerates failure for saved games and returns an empty
  string;
- CvInitCore::refreshCustomMapOptions checks `gDLL->pythonMapExists` before querying a script.

No stale `m_bLastCallSuccessful` use was found after the module-missing branch.

MAP LATITUDE / WRAP PAIRING — CONTROL
--------------------------------------
Practical 1648 changed latitude handling from an inherited all-or-nothing pair to independent
top/bottom application. That is a semantic difference if a third-party map overrides only one
latitude function. Current shipped map scan finds:
- 16 maps defining getTopLatitude;
- exactly the same 16 defining getBottomLatitude;
- no one-sided latitude implementation.

Wrap behavior deliberately remains all-or-nothing. Current shipped scan likewise finds the same
41 scripts on both getWrapX and getWrapY.

No current trigger and no stronger inherited contract evidence: no F281.

MAP PLOT-PERCENT / DEFAULT-OPTION OUTPUTS — CONTROL
----------------------------------------------------
All current getNumPlotsPercent implementations were inspected. Their normal world-size paths return
positive percentage values; none returns zero/negative for a supported world size. The wrapper
initializes to 100 and its caller consumes iModifier only when isOverride() is true.

Current `isClimateMap` / `isSeaLevelMap` implementations return ordinary 0/1 / False/True values.
The wrapper's default `1` corresponds to "option flexible" and is a safe permissive fallback if a
hook is absent/fails.

No F281.

VECTOR OUTPUT OWNERSHIP — CURRENT CALLERS CLEAN
-----------------------------------------------
`generateTerrainTypes` receives a fresh empty local vector from CvMapGenerator::generateTerrain on
every call. Its `reserve` therefore cannot preserve stale elements from an earlier generation.
Wrong output size is diagnosed and rejected before the caller indexes the vector.

`generatePlotTypes` similarly checks exact output size before copying into the caller-owned array.
On failure the caller overwrites every plot entry with PLOT_LAND.

Neither wrapper individually validates each returned enum value. A malformed third-party map could
therefore supply an invalid PlotTypes/TerrainTypes integer. No current shipped trigger has been
identified; this remains robustness debt, not F281.

CALLBACK-GUARD STORAGE LIFETIME — CLEAN LOCALLY
-----------------------------------------------
CvPythonCaller owns exactly one `bool[NUM_CALLBACK_DEFINES]` allocation and deletes it in its
destructor. Macro-generated string and enum counts are asserted equal. Current callback guard
values are read after GlobalDefines have loaded, when CvGlobals::cacheGlobals constructs the
CvPythonCaller.

The broader question of whether CvGlobals::cacheGlobals can repeat in one global lifetime was
already audited under queue 040 and not locally proven; do not duplicate that speculative lifecycle
seam as a queue-037 root.

F275 SAME-ROOT EXPANSION — practical 1648 narrowed several inherited Python truth contracts to exact 1
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F275 was promoted from the strongest explicit contract:

    canBuild:
        -1 = ignore / no Python override
         0 = cannot build
         1 or greater = can build

Current CvPythonCaller::toBool instead returns true only for exactly TRUE/1:

    static bool toBool(long l)
    {
        FAssert(l >= 0);
        return (l == TRUE);
    }

A complete practical-1648 old-condition audit now proves that canBuild was not the only callback
whose inherited consumer accepted a broader Python truth value.

Pre-extraction callbacks whose healthy-result semantics were broader than exact 1 include:

1. canBuild
   old:
       if (lResult >= 1)
           return true;
   current:
       return toBool(lResult);
   This remains F275's strongest contract because the accompanying Python interface comment
   explicitly documents "1 or greater" as the affirmative result.

2. isPlayerResearch
   old:
       if (lResult == 0)
           return false;
       // any nonzero result allowed research
   current:
       return toBool(lResult);

3. canDeclareWar
   old:
       if (lResult == 0)
           return false;
       // any nonzero result allowed declaration
   current:
       return toBool(lResult);

4. unitCannotMoveInto
   old:
       if (lResult != 0)
           return true;
   current:
       return toBool(lResult);

5. cannotSpreadReligion
   old:
       if (lResult > 0)
           return true;
   current:
       return toBool(lResult);

6. CvGame::isVictory
   old:
       if (lResult == 0)
           return false;
       // any nonzero result was true
   current:
       return toBool(lResult);

7. CvGame::isVictoryTest
   old:
       if (lResult == 0)
           return false;
       // any nonzero result was true
   current:
       return toBool(lResult);

8. canPickPlot / canPickRevealedPlot
   old:
       if (lResult == 0)
           ...
       // any nonzero result was affirmative
   current:
       return toBool(lResult);

9. map canPlaceBonusAt / canPlaceGoodyAt
   old:
       if (result >= 0)
           return result;
   The C++ return type was bool, so every positive integer converted to true.
   current:
       validates the nonnegative override, then returns toBool(lResult);
   Thus positive values >1 changed from true to false.

10. canRazeCity has a particularly instructive split inherited contract.
    The old acquireCity call site used:
        if (lResult == 1)
    whereas CvPlayer::canRaze used:
        if (lResult == 0)
            return false;
    so positive values >1 were accepted by the ordinary canRaze query but not by the acquisition
    branch. Practical 1648 unified both callers through one exact-1 CvPythonCaller::canRaze wrapper.
    This preserves acquireCity's old condition but narrows CvPlayer::canRaze.

These are best treated as SAME-ROOT F275 evidence rather than independent findings. The common
refactor mechanism is that practical 1648 imposed one exact-1 boolean conversion onto callbacks
whose inherited call sites did not all share exact-1 semantics.

WHY THIS IS NOT A CLAIM THAT ALL PYTHON BOOLS MUST ACCEPT ANY NONZERO VALUE
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
The same practical-1648 audit also finds many inherited callbacks that already used `== 1`.
Those are semantically preserved by toBool and should not be swept into F275 merely because Python
itself normally treats nonzero integers as truthy.

Examples whose old condition was already exact 1 include:
- citiesDestroyFeatures;
- canTrain / cannotTrain;
- canConstruct / cannotConstruct;
- canCreate / cannotCreate;
- canMaintain / cannotMaintain;
- doGrowth / doCulture / doPlotCulture / doProduction / doReligion / doGreatPeople / doMeltdown;
- AI_chooseProduction;
- skipProductionPopup / showExamineCityButton / skipResearchPopup / showTechChooserButton;
- doReviveActivePlayer / doHolyCity;
- createBarbarianCities / createBarbarianUnits;
- cannotSelectionListMove / cannotSelectionListGameNetMessage;
- cannotHandleAction;
- cannotDoControl;
- cannotFoundCity;
- canFoundCitiesOnWater;
- canResearch;
- canDoCivic / cannotDoCivic;
- doGold / doResearch;
- AI_doDiplo / AI_doWar;
- doCombat;
- isActionRecommended;
- AI_unitUpdate.

This distinction matters: F275 is an inherited-contract-preservation issue, not a proposal to make
every numeric Python callback use generic Python truthiness.

RANDOM-EVENT WRAPPERS CONFIRM THAT EXACT 1 IS NOT A UNIVERSAL BRIDGE CONTRACT
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current CvPythonCaller itself deliberately preserves nonzero truth semantics for several
random-event callbacks, e.g. by returning:

    (lResult != 0)

rather than toBool(lResult). Existing source comments even question whether the usual `== 1`
conversion would be suitable there.

This is useful internal evidence that the bridge does not have one universal "only integer 1 is
true" convention. Each callback's inherited/native contract matters.

CURRENT-DATA / SEVERITY BOUNDARY
--------------------------------
All 54 CvPythonCaller USE_*_CALLBACK GlobalDefines were checked against current SAS XML:
- 54 expected;
- all 54 exist exactly once;
- all are integer 0/1 values;
- all 54 are currently 0.

Therefore F275 and several neighboring guarded-callback regressions are not active under SAS's
default configuration. They remain real compatibility/configuration bugs because the callback API
is intentionally retained and old K-Mod/AdvCiv semantics are externally observable once a flag is
enabled.

No current shipped healthy callback was found returning literal positive integer >1 in one of the
broader-boolean roles. Do not exaggerate default-gameplay severity.

REPAIR BOUNDARY FOR F275
------------------------
A global change to toBool is unsafe because numerous callbacks intentionally inherited exact-1
semantics.

Repair must therefore preserve the affected callback's own old contract, for example:
- canBuild: explicit >=1 handling while keeping -1 as no override;
- inherited nonzero callbacks: `lResult != 0` where compatibility is desired;
- inherited positive callbacks: `lResult > 0`;
- canPlaceBonusAt / canPlaceGoodyAt: nonnegative validation plus normal C++ bool conversion
  semantics (or explicit `lResult != 0`);
- canRaze needs deliberate consideration because its two old call sites were not themselves
  semantically identical.

The minimum F275 repair can target canBuild alone if scope is deliberately limited to the explicit
documented regression, while the sibling list above should be reviewed as compatibility follow-up.
Do not blindly broaden toBool globally.
