F274 ANCESTRY CORRECTION — practical 2066, not practical 1648, introduced the NULL dereference
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Earlier queue-037 notes correctly identified the live defect but were too broad about its origin.

Practical 1648's initial CvPythonCaller extraction preserved the nullable-pointer construction:

    // Note: pUnit can be NULL, but pyUnit can still be initialized (and is expected by Python).
    CyUnit* pyUnit = new CyUnit(const_cast<CvUnit*>(pUnit));

That is behaviorally consistent with the older K-Mod/CvPlot path, which constructed a CyUnit from
the nullable CvUnit pointer. The CyUnit pointer-taking constructor is capable of representing NULL.

The actual regression was introduced later by AdvCiv practical 2066, commit ffe04c3efd,
whose title is:

    Avoid some const_casts

Its diff is unusually self-documenting:

    // Note: pUnit can be NULL, but pyUnit can still be initialized (and is expected by Python).
-   CyUnit* pyUnit = new CyUnit(const_cast<CvUnit*>(pUnit));
+   CyUnit* pyUnit = new CyUnit(*pUnit);

The comment explicitly preserves the nullable contract while the new reference-taking expression
dereferences that nullable pointer before the CyUnit constructor is entered.

Therefore F274's precise ancestry is:
- K-Mod / pre-2066 AdvCiv: nullable pointer preserved;
- practical 1648: extraction still preserved it;
- practical 2066: const-correctness cleanup changed pointer construction to reference construction
  and created the NULL dereference;
- current SAS inherits the practical-2066 regression.

This strengthens confidence in the root and narrows review of the repair. Restoring the
pointer-taking construction (or adding an equivalent const-pointer CyUnit overload) preserves the
old nullable Python-object contract without redesigning doGoody.

A later AdvCiv fix is a useful sibling control: practical 2571 changed
cannotHandleActionOverride's plot plumbing to a pointer precisely where a plot can be NULL and uses
the pointer-taking CyPlot constructor. That neighboring repair reinforces that optional gameplay
objects should stay pointer-shaped across the Python wrapper boundary.

F275 EXTRA CONTRACT DETAIL — documented result 2 also trips FAssertBounds
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current canBuild contains:

    FAssertBounds(-1, 2, lResult);
    if (lResult == -1)
        return false;
    bOverride = true;
    return toBool(lResult);

`FAssertBounds(lower, upper, value)` uses a half-open upper bound. Thus this check accepts:
    -1, 0, 1

but rejects:
    2

That matters because the inherited/Python-facing canBuild contract explicitly says:
    -1 = ignore/no override
     0 = cannot build
     1 or greater = can build

So a perfectly valid affirmative callback result of 2 has two regressions:
1. Assert/Debug: it trips the bounds assertion;
2. all builds: exact-1 toBool converts it to false.

This is still the same F275 root, not a separate diagnostic finding. A repair that restores >=1
truth semantics must also widen/remove the incompatible half-open bounds assertion.

INDEPENDENT K-MOD / CIV4CE CONFIRMATION OF THE SEVEN ROOTS
-----------------------------------------------------------
An independent pass through K-Mod 1.46 and current Civ4CE was used to challenge the proposed
ancestry/semantics rather than relying only on AdvCiv history.

F274:
- K-Mod doGoody passes the nullable CvUnit pointer into CyUnit instead of dereferencing it.
- practical-1648 AdvCiv initially did the same after extraction.
- practical 2066 is therefore the pinpoint introduction.

F275:
- K-Mod and Civ4CE CvPlot::canBuild both retain:
      if (lResult >= 1) return true;
      else if (lResult == 0) return false;
  independently confirming the broader documented affirmative range.

F276:
- K-Mod initializes pillage Python result to -1 and executes the native C++ calculation whenever
  the callback remains negative.
- Current extracted wrapper's "enabled means handled" behavior therefore loses a concrete inherited
  fallback contract.

F277:
- K-Mod and Civ4CE CvMapGenerator test whether generatePlotTypes / generateTerrainTypes /
  addFeatures are actually supplied/overridden and otherwise continue through native generation.
- They do not treat ordinary native/default fallback itself as an assertion failure.
- This independently supports the current minimal SAS map's use of fallback.

F278:
- K-Mod and Civ4CE initialize the updateColoredPlots Python result to 0 before dispatch.
- Current CvPythonCaller is the divergent uninitialized form.

F279:
- K-Mod carries the same active EVENT_FARM_BANDITS_2 XML PythonHelp token with no matching Python
  implementation, confirming the stale data is inherited.
- K-Mod's old event-help call path did not assert dispatch success; the repeatable assertion layer
  is therefore an AdvCiv extraction-policy change.

F280:
- K-Mod and Civ4CE both retain:
      if (lResult > 1)
  for getUnitCostMod.
- Current SAS's building-cost sibling also retains >1.
- The unit-side >0 condition is consequently isolated threshold drift, not a broad callback-policy
  redesign.

POST-1648 HISTORY ORACLE — LATER FIXES MOSTLY EXPLAIN EXISTING ROOTS / CONTROLS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Every later AdvCiv commit materially touching CvPythonCaller found in the local commit-diff mirror
was used as a "what did the author later discover?" oracle.

Relevant repairs / changes include:
- practical 1662: tolerate missing random-event apply functions instead of asserting them;
- practical 1677: saved-game custom-map-option / wrap handling becomes tolerant where scripts may
  be unavailable;
- practical 1850: no-assert numCustomMapOptions because a legitimate map lacks the hook;
- practical 1917: repair the human-explorer-placement truth inversion;
- practical 1966: reject/handle invalid random-event object IDs and sentinels;

doPlayerScore OUTPUT SENTINEL — CURRENT FAILURE BEHAVIOR IS A FALLBACK IMPROVEMENT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current wrapper:

    int const iError = MIN_INT;
    ARGSLIST(iError);
    ...
    call("calculateScore", argsList, lResult);
    if (lResult != iError)
        iScore = toInt(lResult);
    else FAssert(...);

At first glance this differs substantially from the pre-practical-1648 path, where the score result
was initialized to 0 and the Python result was returned directly.

The surrounding practical-1648 change is decisive: the same refactor moved the normal CvGameUtils
score calculation into C++. CvPlayer::calculateScore now computes a complete native score first and
passes it by reference to doPlayerScore only as an optional callback override.

Therefore:
- callback disabled -> preserve native C++ score;
- callback succeeds -> replace it with Python result;
- callback fails / does not write the MIN_INT sentinel -> assert diagnostically and preserve the
  already-computed native score.

This is coherent graceful fallback, not an output-sentinel regression. It differs from F276 because
pillage's caller explicitly expects "not handled" to trigger a native calculation that current
doPillageGold wrongly suppresses.

F281 / provisional KI#604
-------------------------
TITLE
CvDeal::isPeaceDeal scans only the first saved trade list, so an ordinary one-sided AI reparations
peace treaty saved only in the second list is never recognized as a peace deal and can remain
force-peace indefinitely.

CURRENT CODE
------------
Current CvDeal::isPeaceDeal is:

    bool CvDeal::isPeaceDeal() const
    {
        FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(getFirstList())
        {
            if (pItem->m_eItemType == getPeaceItem())
                return true;
        }
        return false;
    }

It never examines getSecondList().

This matters because current AdvCiv/SAS does NOT require the peace treaty item to be stored on both
sides. CvPlayerAI::AI_negotiatePeace explicitly says:

    AI_counterPropose (and the EXE) don't like peace treaties on both sides

and deliberately inserts the treaty on only one side.

The relevant branch is:

    if (weGive.getLength() <= 0 &&
        (theyGive.getLength() > 0 || iTheirBenefit > iOurBenefit))
    {
        theyGive.insertAtEnd(peaceTreaty);
    }
    else
        weGive.insertAtEnd(peaceTreaty);

For AI-AI peace it then calls:

    GC.getGame().implementDeal(getID(), eOther, weGive, theyGive);

`CvGame::implementAndReturnDeal` preserves this orientation:

    pDeal->init(..., eWho, eOtherWho);
    pDeal->addTradeItems(kOurList, kTheirList, ...);

and CvDeal processes/saves kFirstList as the first player's gives list and kSecondList as the second
player's gives list.

LIVE SECOND-LIST-ONLY CONSTRUCTION
----------------------------------
The normal branch:

    if (iTheirBenefit > iOurBenefit)
        // "They need to give us sth."

can add reparations to `theyGive`, leaving `weGive` empty. The treaty-placement rule then inserts
TRADE_PEACE_TREATY into `theyGive`, not `weGive`.

During CvDeal::addTradeItems:
- one-shot reparations such as gold/tech/city are applied but not saved;
- TRADE_PEACE_TREATY returns bSave=true.

A perfectly ordinary resulting persistent deal can therefore be:

    firstList  = empty
    secondList = [TRADE_PEACE_TREATY]

with team-level setForcePeace already enabled.

FAILURE CHAIN
-------------
1. The treaty begins normally and setForcePeace is true.
2. CvGame::verifyDeals calls CvDeal::verify at game/deal turn boundaries.
3. CvDeal::verify is supposed to expire peace deals once their minimum duration becomes cancelable:

       if (... || (isCancelable(NO_PLAYER) && isPeaceDeal()))
           kill();

4. After PEACE_TREATY_LENGTH turns:
       isCancelable(NO_PLAYER) == true
   but:
       isPeaceDeal() == false
   because the treaty is only in secondList.

5. The deal is therefore not killed.
6. CvDeal::endTrade(TRADE_PEACE_TREATY), the normal teardown that executes:

       GET_TEAM(eFromPlayer).setForcePeace(TEAMID(eToPlayer), false);

   never runs for this expiry.
7. No general time-based auto-clear exists in CvTeam::setForcePeace; the flag is persistent state.
   Thus the two teams can remain unable to declare war indefinitely unless some unrelated later
   path destroys/changes the relationship.

SECONDARY CONSEQUENCES
----------------------
Because the same deal is misclassified:
- CvDeal::doTurn treats it as a non-peace annual-ish deal after it becomes cancelable and can feed
  its list through peacetime trade/grant accounting.
- CvPlayer::isTradingWithTeam / stopTradingWithTeam / isAnyDealTooRecentToCancel and AI trade-value
  consumers also use isPeaceDeal as an exclusion. The permanent-force-peace lifetime error is the
  strongest concrete consequence; these are same-root downstream misclassifications.

ANCESTRY / REGRESSION
---------------------
K-Mod 1.46 scans BOTH lists in CvDeal::isPeaceDeal.

Earlier AdvCiv used a combined `headTradesNode()/nextTradesNode()` traversal, likewise scanning both
lists.

During the later list-interface refactor visible in practical-count 2998 / commit
8c36049d431fd085eac8269bef81722061b53a11, this changed from:

    for (... = headTradesNode(); ... = nextTradesNode(...))

to:

    FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(getFirstList())

while preserving the "simplified" label. The second-list half of the logical combined traversal was
lost.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 still has the same first-list-only implementation, so SAS inherits this regression.

INDEPENDENT EXISTING-ALBUM EVIDENCE
-----------------------------------
Earlier F091 / KI#413 in CvTeam.cpp independently established that live forced-peace treaty
representation cannot assume first-list/head placement. That helper originally recognized only a
first-list/head treaty and was repaired in current SAS to:
- filter relevant master teams;
- scan the entire first list;
- if not found, scan the entire second list.

Current CvTeam::turnsOfForcedPeaceRemaining therefore already encodes the correct representation
invariant that CvDeal::isPeaceDeal still violates.

F091 is NOT the same root:
- F091 caused the *reported remaining duration* to be wrong while the live deal still existed;
- F281 prevents the actual deal from being recognized for expiry/peace exclusions and can leave
  force-peace state persistent indefinitely.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Restore logical both-list scanning, e.g.:

    FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(getFirstList())
        if (pItem->m_eItemType == getPeaceItem())
            return true;
    FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(getSecondList())
        if (pItem->m_eItemType == getPeaceItem())
            return true;
    return false;

or introduce a shared both-list helper if desired.

Do not restrict the repair to head items or reparations ordering. The representation contract is
simply "the peace item may live in either list."

This restores K-Mod / older AdvCiv behavior and matches the already-repaired KI#413 helper.

F282 / provisional KI#605
-------------------------
TITLE
Vassal-break memory duration logic became non-additive when addEndTradeMemory changed from
AI_changeMemoryCount to AI_setMemoryCount, so "2x10" / "3x10" intended memories collapse to a
single fixed count.

CURRENT CODE
------------
The vassal/surrender endTrade branch contains:

    addEndTradeMemory(eFromPlayer, eToPlayer, TRADE_VASSAL);
    if(!bDeniedHelp) // Master remembers for 2x10 turns
        addEndTradeMemory(eFromPlayer, eToPlayer, TRADE_VASSAL);
    else /* Vassal remembers for 3x10 turns (and master for 1x10 turns, ...) */
    {
        for(int i = 0; i < 3; i++)
            addEndTradeMemory(eToPlayer, eFromPlayer, TRADE_VASSAL);
    }

But addEndTradeMemory currently does:

    itRememberingMember->AI_setMemoryCount(
        itEndingMember->getID(),
        eMemory,
        bHalve ? 1 : 2);

So repeated calls are idempotent:
- two calls set 2, then set 2 again -> final count 2;
- three calls set 2 three times -> final count 2.

The comments and historical behavior require those repetitions to represent different durations.

HISTORY / REGRESSION PROOF
--------------------------
The original advc.143 implementation introduced the same repeated-call structure while
addEndTradeMemory used additive memory semantics:

    AI_rememberEvent(...)

Later, before practical-count 1497, the helper had been converted to:

    AI_changeMemoryCount(..., 2)

to match the faster memory-decay scale. Thus:
- one remembered event added 2;
- "2x10" used two calls -> +4;
- "3x10" used three calls -> +6.

Practical-count 1497 / commit 20e0f168829b6befe2de4dc2f77f123c877c1bc0
("Many style changes; header inclusions; embargo bugfix") changed:

    AI_changeMemoryCount(..., 2)

to:

    AI_setMemoryCount(..., 2)

without changing the repeated-call logic.

That turns the intended additive repetitions into repeated assignment of the same value.

Later practical-count 3118 added the `bHalve` parameter and retained the setter:

    eMemory, bHalve ? 1 : 2

with the comment that memories are "Twice remembered ... b/c now twice as fast forgotten."
That confirms count 2 represents one ordinary remembered event on the new decay scale, not the
whole intended 2x/3x duration.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE
----------------
When a vassal relationship ends:
- normal/non-denied-help case intends the master to remember the former vassal for 2x10 turns,
  but the repeated setter leaves only one-event count 2;
- denied-help case intends the former vassal to remember the master for 3x10 turns,
  but three setter calls still leave only count 2.

This shortens the intended diplomatic memory and can affect future vassal/capitulation willingness.
Current CvTeamAI explicitly consults MEMORY_CANCELLED_VASSAL_AGREEMENT in surrender/vassal trade
logic, so the memory has live strategic consumers despite its XML attitude weight being 0.

TEAM-PROXY INTERACTION / REPAIR BOUNDARY
----------------------------------------
Vassal/open-border/team trades are expanded into per-member proxy CvDeal objects through
startTeamTrade. When a top-level team trade ends, endTeamTrade kills sibling proxies with
`kill(false)`.

For OB/DP, cancellation memory is already gated by `if (bTeam)`. The vassal branch is not similarly
gated, so every proxy currently also executes the setter. Because it is a setter, these repetitions
do not multiply the value; they merely rewrite the same count.

This matters for the repair:
- blindly reverting `AI_setMemoryCount` to `AI_changeMemoryCount` would make every proxy additive
  and could grossly overcount memory on multi-member teams;
- the safe repair should preserve "exactly once per logical team-trade teardown."

Evidence-supported repair shapes include:
1. gate vassal cancellation-memory assignment behind `bTeam`, matching OB/DP's logical-team-trade
   treatment, then set the intended final count directly (2x or 3x on the current doubled-decay
   scale);
2. or refactor addEndTradeMemory to accept an explicit desired count and ensure proxy `bTeam=false`
   teardown does not add another logical memory event.

The exact numeric final counts should follow the current decay convention:
- one ordinary event = 2;
- intended 2x duration = 4;
- intended 3x duration = 6;
unless review of current decay code establishes a later scale change.

Do NOT simply replace setMemoryCount with changeMemoryCount without addressing proxy deals.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F282 is independent of F281.
- F281 is a both-list peace-deal classification/lifetime bug.
- F282 is an additive-to-assignment regression in diplomatic memory duration during vassal teardown.

CONTROLS FROM THIS BRANCH
-------------------------
- The initial suspicion that team-expanded vassal proxy deals directly multiply current memory was
  false under current code because the helper uses a setter.
- The deletion-while-iterating pattern in endTeamTrade remains consistent with the free-list iterator
  contract: iteration position is advanced before each returned object; same architecture exists in
  K-Mod.
- `kill(false)` for deal objects is used here to suppress recursive team-wide teardown; the only
  unrelated current deal `kill(false)` found is disengagement cancellation, which has no vassal
  memory path.

F283 / provisional KI#606
-------------------------
TITLE
CvPlayer::resetDualDeal scans only a deal's first trade list, so a valid second-list-only peace
treaty cannot be prolonged; a new overlapping treaty is created and the older treaty can later
clear force-peace while the newer treaty is still supposed to be active.

CURRENT CALL PATH
-----------------
CvDeal::startTrade handles TRADE_PEACE_TREATY as follows:

    if (GET_TEAM(eFromPlayer).isForcePeace(kToPlayer.getTeam()))
    {
        if (kFromPlayer.resetDualDeal(eToPlayer, TRADE_PEACE_TREATY))
        {
            ...
            break;
        }
    }
    GET_TEAM(eFromPlayer).setForcePeace(kToPlayer.getTeam(), true);
    bSave = true;

The purpose is explicit: if the same dual agreement already exists, reset its initial turn instead
of creating a second overlapping persistent agreement.

Current CvPlayer::resetDualDeal:

    bool CvPlayer::resetDualDeal(PlayerTypes ePlayer, TradeableItems eDealType)
    {
        int iGameTurn = GC.getGame().getGameTurn();
        FOR_EACH_DEAL_VAR(d)
        {
            if (d->isBetween(getID(), ePlayer))
            {
                FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(d->getFirstList())
                {
                    if (pItem->m_eItemType == eDealType)
                    {
                        d->setInitialGameTurn(iGameTurn);
                        return true;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return false;
    }

It never scans getSecondList().

LIVE REPRESENTATION
-------------------
F281 independently proves a normal live path where AI peace negotiation stores
TRADE_PEACE_TREATY only in the SECOND list:
- AI_negotiatePeace deliberately places the treaty on only one side because the EXE/counterproposal
  path dislikes treaties on both sides;
- reparations orientation can leave firstList empty and secondList containing the only saved treaty.

This is not malformed deal data.

FAILURE CHAIN
-------------
Assume an existing still-active treaty:

    deal A:
        firstList  = empty
        secondList = [TRADE_PEACE_TREATY]
        initialTurn = T0

At T1 < T0 + PEACE_TREATY_LENGTH, another trade legitimately includes/prolongs a peace treaty.

1. Team state already has isForcePeace == true.
2. startTrade calls resetDualDeal.
3. resetDualDeal scans only deal A.firstList, misses the treaty and returns false.
4. startTrade falls through:
       setForcePeace(..., true); // already true
       bSave = true;
5. A second persistent treaty, deal B, is saved with initialTurn = T1.

Now assume F281 itself has been repaired so both deals are recognized correctly.

At T0 + PEACE_TREATY_LENGTH:
6. deal A becomes cancelable and verify kills it.
7. endTrade(TRADE_PEACE_TREATY) executes:
       setForcePeace(..., false);
8. deal B is still younger and should keep peace forced until:
       T1 + PEACE_TREATY_LENGTH
   but forcePeace has already been cleared.

Thus F283 can cause the opposite lifetime failure from F281:
- F281 can make peace last indefinitely;
- F283 can make a renewed peace treaty end too early.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE FROM F281
---------------------------
This is a distinct root, not merely a second symptom of isPeaceDeal.

If F281 is fixed and F283 is not:
- second-list treaties expire normally;
- resetDualDeal still fails to find them;
- overlapping deals are still created;
- expiration of the older deal still clears the shared team flag prematurely.

If F283 is fixed but F281 is not:
- renewal finds and resets a second-list treaty correctly;
- but isPeaceDeal still fails to expire it later.

Both repairs are therefore required.

WHY OPEN BORDERS / DEFENSIVE PACT USUALLY MASK THE HELPER BUG
--------------------------------------------------------------
resetDualDeal is also used for TRADE_OPEN_BORDERS and TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT.

Those team agreements are materialized by startTeamTrade(..., bDual=true), which creates proxy
deals with the item in BOTH lists. Therefore the first-list-only search happens to find them.

Peace treaties are the live exceptional "dual state, one-sided saved representation" case.

ANCESTRY
--------
The first-list assumption predates the later list-interface refactor.

Practical count 1270 / commit beb230a3ba introduced advc.032 `resetPeaceTreaty`.
Its original implementation already:
- iterated deals between the two players;
- scanned only `d->getFirstTrades()`;
- reset the deal turn when it found TRADE_PEACE_TREATY.

Practical count 2998 / commit 8c36049d431fd085eac8269bef81722061b53a11 generalized:

    resetPeaceTreaty -> resetDualDeal(ePlayer, eDealType)

and reused it for OB/DP, but preserved the first-list-only loop.

So unlike F281, whose both-list combined traversal was specifically lost in a later refactor,
F283 is a longstanding advc.032 representation assumption from the helper's introduction.

K-Mod does not provide this AdvCiv-specific renewal helper; its both-list deal representation still
serves as a useful baseline, but the bug is specifically in AdvCiv's prolong-existing-dual logic.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
For a deal between the requested players, reset the initial turn if eDealType occurs in EITHER
trade list.

For example:
    scan d->getFirstList();
    scan d->getSecondList();
    if found:
        d->setInitialGameTurn(iGameTurn);
        return true;

Do not require the item to be on the side corresponding to the caller. The agreements using this
helper are team-level/dual state; the stored list side is representational.

This repair:
- preserves existing OB/DP behavior;
- handles one-sided peace treaties;
- prevents overlapping peace deals caused solely by list orientation.

RELATED BUT NOT PROMOTED YET
----------------------------
CvTeam::addTeam's permanent-alliance cleanup also scans only each internal deal's first list when
looking for OB/DP/peace/vassal/surrender/disengagement items.

A second-list-only peace treaty can therefore be missed when two teams merge. PA trade legality
does not explicitly prohibit force-peace, so the state is plausible, including human-driven trade.
However the strongest currently proven consequence is a stale internal deal/state-accounting seam,
not yet a comparably crisp independent gameplay failure. Keep this candidate open; do not allocate
F284 from it without a stronger downstream consequence.

HISTORY-GUIDED CONTROLS
-----------------------
- practical counts 1577/1578 repaired AI cancellation/renegotiation and trade-table handling but do
  not repair the first-list peace representation assumptions.
- practical 2485 fixes repeated loud cancellation sounds when war kills multiple deals; current
  bNoSound handling remains coherent.
- practical 2765 force-cancels GPT deals under a specific broke-player condition; this is policy
  logic, not yet evidence of a general GPT balance invariant.
- startTeamTrade persistent representation clarified: the initiating item with m_iData<=0 creates
  per-member m_iData=1 proxy deals; the original initiating deal item itself is not saved. Exactly
  one proxy cancellation normally enters endTrade with bTeam=true; nested sibling kills use
  bTeam=false. This supports F282's proposed "once per logical team teardown" repair boundary.

F282 SAME-ROOT EXPANSION — setter conversion broke all cancellation-memory accumulation
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The WIP02 proof used the strongest self-documenting symptom:
- vassal teardown comments say "2x10 turns" and "3x10 turns";
- repeated calls became repeated `AI_setMemoryCount(..., 2)` assignments;
- therefore 2x/3x collapsed to a single event.

The practical-1497 diff establishes a broader same-root semantic regression.

Before practical count 1497, shared addEndTradeMemory ended with:

    AI_changeMemoryCount(..., eMemory, 2);

Practical 1497 changed ONLY that update primitive to:

    AI_setMemoryCount(..., eMemory, 2);

The helper is shared by:
- cancelled Open Borders;
- cancelled Defensive Pacts;
- cancelled vassal agreements.

Therefore the regression is not limited to the explicit repeated vassal calls.

Under the old additive contract:
- a new cancellation while an older same-type memory remains ADDS the new event;
- two remembered cancellations can produce e.g. 4;
- a later cancellation never shortens the memory already accumulated.

Under the current setter:
- every ordinary cancellation overwrites the entire count with 2;
- if the old count is 1, it becomes 2;
- if the old count is 4 or 6, a fresh cancellation REDUCES it to 2.

Practical 3118 later added per-event halving:

    AI_setMemoryCount(..., bHalve ? 1 : 2);

This can be even more counterintuitive when an AI ends the agreement:
an already-large memory can be overwritten downward to 1 merely because the latest cancellation is
supposed to count half as much.

The practical-3118 intent is "halve the cancellation memory [for this cancellation]," not
"replace all accumulated past cancellation memory with a one-unit total." The old additive helper
and the unchanged repeated-event structure make that distinction especially clear.

Thus F282's root should be stated broadly as:

    practical 1497 accidentally changed addEndTradeMemory from an additive event operation into
    absolute assignment, breaking both repeated-event accumulation and the explicitly coded
    2x/3x vassal-duration multipliers.

REPAIR REFINEMENT
-----------------
The repair still must account for team-proxy deals.

Important representation clarification:
- startTeamTrade called from an initiating m_iData<=0 team agreement creates per-member m_iData=1
  proxy CvDeals;
- the initiating item itself is NOT saved in the original deal;
- the persistent agreement is represented by the proxy deals;
- when one proxy is logically canceled, its endTrade runs with bTeam=true and endTeamTrade kills
  the remaining proxies with kill(false);
- those nested proxy endTrade calls therefore have bTeam=false.

A safe additive repair can consequently use bTeam as the logical-event gate:
- perform cancellation-memory event accounting only on the one bTeam=true teardown;
- suppress memory additions for proxy bTeam=false teardown;
- add the intended event amount rather than assigning the total.

On the current doubled-decay scale:
- ordinary event: +2;
- halved event: +1;
- intended 2x vassal memory: +4 total for that logical event;
- intended 3x vassal memory: +6 total.

This preserves historical accumulation across independent cancellations while avoiding MxN proxy
multiplication.

Do NOT simply replace setMemoryCount with changeMemoryCount inside the current helper while leaving
proxy bTeam=false calls active.


F283 REPAIR-BOUNDARY EXPANSION — team scope, not merely both-list scope
------------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP03 proved that resetDualDeal's first-list-only scan misses a second-list-only peace treaty and
can create overlapping treaties whose expiries fight over one shared forcePeace flag.

A deeper representation audit shows that "scan both lists" is necessary but NOT sufficient.

The agreements using resetDualDeal are team-level state:
- Open Borders;
- Defensive Pact;
- Peace Treaty / forcePeace.

Yet resetDualDeal searches only:

    d->isBetween(getID(), ePlayer)

i.e. one specific PLAYER pair.

MULTI-MEMBER PEACE FAILURE
--------------------------
Suppose teams A and B each have multiple members.

At T0:
- A1 and B1 create the live peace treaty;
- team-level forcePeace(A,B) becomes true;
- persistent treaty may be stored in a deal A1<->B1.

At T1:
- A2 and B2 legitimately include/prolong TRADE_PEACE_TREATY.

This is reachable because:
    canPossiblyTradeItem(TRADE_PEACE_TREATY)
        -> canChangeWarPeace(otherTeam)

and canChangeWarPeace deliberately does NOT reject temporary forcePeace. The startTrade renewal
branch exists specifically to handle an already-force-peace state.

A2.resetDualDeal(B2, PEACE_TREATY):
- searches only deals between A2 and B2;
- cannot see A1<->B1 even if that older treaty is in its first list;
- returns false;
- creates another team-level treaty.

The shared boolean forcePeace then has multiple player-level lifetime owners. When the older deal
expires first it clears the shared flag while the newer deal is still in duration.

This failure is independent of the first-vs-second-list bug.

OPEN BORDERS / DEFENSIVE PACT REPRESENTATION
----------------------------------------------
OB/DP are expanded by startTeamTrade into all member-pair proxy deals, so resetDualDeal usually does
find a proxy for the invoking pair. However it resets only THAT proxy's initial turn, not the
parallel proxy deals for the same team-level agreement.

Under ordinary legality:
- canPossiblyTradeItem currently rejects a new OB/DP item while the state is already active;
- therefore the renewal branches are less routinely reachable than peace renewal.

Still, if a forced/nonstandard path reaches those explicit prolong branches, resetting one proxy
does not coherently prolong the entire team agreement. The other proxies retain their older
cancelability age and any one proxy cancellation tears down the whole team trade.

This is same-root representation evidence, not a new finding.

CORRECT F283 REPAIR CONTRACT
----------------------------
For a TEAM-LEVEL dual agreement, renewal must operate on the logical team agreement, not one
player/list location.

At minimum for TRADE_PEACE_TREATY:
- search deals between the two teams, not merely the two players;
- search both saved lists;
- locate the already-live logical treaty and reset its initial turn instead of creating another.

For OB/DP if the generic helper remains shared:
- either reset every proxy deal belonging to that logical team agreement to the same current turn;
- or refactor renewal around a single logical team-trade helper rather than pretending one
  player-pair proxy owns the agreement.

A patch that only adds a second-list loop fixes the WIP03 example but leaves the multi-member
peace-overlap bug intact.


FIRST-LIST PEACE SIBLINGS — CONTROLS, NOT F284
-----------------------------------------------
A repository-wide scan found two further first-list-only cleanup sites:

1. CvTeam::addTeam permanent-alliance internal-deal cleanup.
2. CvTeam::setVassal cleanup of defensive-pact / peace-treaty deals involving the new vassal.

Both can miss a second-list-only peace treaty.

They should be reviewed when F281/F283 are implemented because they violate the same representation
fact. However current downstream consequences are weaker:
- after a permanent alliance the two players become same-team and the old inter-team forcePeace
  relation is no longer strategically meaningful;
- vassalization separately clears forcePeace with the master and aligns third-party wars/peace;
- DP is dual and therefore present in firstList.

The missed treaty can become stale bookkeeping and can later execute same-team/no-op teardown, but
no independent default-gameplay state corruption stronger than F281/F283 has yet been established.
Do not allocate F284 merely for code-pattern symmetry.


OTHER HISTORY-GUIDED CONTROLS
-----------------------------
- practical 1519 corrected city transfer semantics in peace deals (cede vs gift); current code
  preserves that.
- practical 2691 made implied peace treaties visible/explicit in trade-table handling; current
  sequencing is coherent.
- practical 3275 deferred implied treaty signing until the complete bundle has been applied, avoiding
  unilateral/double-treaty sequencing; current code preserves that.

C025-WIP05 — F284 / provisional KI#607 confirmed

F284 / provisional KI#607
-------------------------
TITLE
Eliminating one player from a still-alive multi-member team tears down the entire surviving teams'
Open Borders / Defensive Pact / Disengagement agreement because a player-pair proxy deal owns
team-level state and killAllDeals cancels it with team-wide teardown.

LIVE REPRESENTATION
-------------------
AdvCiv represents several team-level agreements through player-pair proxy CvDeals.

CvDeal::startTeamTrade:

    for (MemberIter itFromMember(eFromTeam); ...)
    {
        for (MemberIter itToMember(eToTeam); ...)
        {
            TradeData item(eItem, 1);
            ...
            GC.getGame().implementDeal(itFromMember->getID(), itToMember->getID(),
                    ourList, theirList);
        }
    }

`MemberIter` is explicitly the ALIVE/MEMBER_OF iterator:
    PlayerIter<ALIVE, MEMBER_OF>.

For a dual Open Borders / Defensive Pact / Disengagement agreement between:
    Team A = {A1, A2}
    Team B = {B1}
the persistent representation therefore includes live proxies:
    A1 <-> B1
    A2 <-> B1

while the actual diplomatic state is stored on CvTeam:
    CvTeam::setOpenBorders
    CvTeam::setDefensivePact
    CvTeam::setDisengage

PLAYER-DEATH PATH
-----------------
CvPlayer::setAlive(false) does NOT require the whole team to die.

It:
1. sets m_bAlive = false;
2. decrements CvTeam::m_iAliveCount;
3. only CvTeam::changeAliveCount reaching 0 marks the team as having no living members / performs
   whole-team death cleanup;
4. then, for every individual defeated player, calls:

       killAllDeals();

CvPlayer::killAllDeals:

    FOR_EACH_DEAL_VAR(pLoopDeal)
    {
        if (pLoopDeal->involves(getID()))
            pLoopDeal->kill();
    }

Thus A1 can die while A2 remains alive and Team A remains alive, and A1's proxy deal is still
destroyed through ordinary `kill()` with bKillTeam=true.

CURRENT endTrade CONSEQUENCE
----------------------------
CvDeal::endTrade computes:

    bool const bAlive = (GET_PLAYER(eFromPlayer).isAlive() &&
                         GET_PLAYER(eToPlayer).isAlive());

and disables attitude updates if either player is dead.

But for these team-level items it still changes the team state:

TRADE_OPEN_BORDERS:
    GET_TEAM(eFromPlayer).setOpenBorders(TEAMID(eToPlayer), false);
    if (bTeam)
        endTeamTrade(TRADE_OPEN_BORDERS, ...);

TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT:
    GET_TEAM(eFromPlayer).setDefensivePact(TEAMID(eToPlayer), false);
    if (bTeam)
        endTeamTrade(TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT, ...);

TRADE_DISENGAGE:
    GET_TEAM(eFromPlayer).setDisengage(TEAMID(eToPlayer), false);
    if (bTeam)
        endTeamTrade(TRADE_DISENGAGE, ...);

So when A1 dies:
1. A1<->B1 proxy is killed.
2. endTrade sees A1 dead but still clears Team A/Team B's team-level agreement.
3. because bKillTeam/bTeam is true, endTeamTrade locates the remaining A2<->B1 proxy and kills it
   too.
4. A2 and B1 are both alive and their teams remain alive, but their agreement has been destroyed
   solely because teammate A1 was eliminated.

This is a direct live state consequence, not merely stale bookkeeping.

INTERNAL PRECEDENT — VASSAL TEARDOWN ALREADY RECOGNIZES THE DISTINCTION
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
The neighboring vassal/surrender branch begins:

    if (!bAlive)
        break;

before:
    setVassal(..., false, ...)
    endTeamTrade(...)

Thus when an individual member dies, deleting that member's vassal proxy does NOT itself dissolve
the team-level vassal relation. Surviving proxies and team state remain; whole-team death has its
own CvTeam::changeAliveCount cleanup.

That is exactly the ownership distinction missing from OB/DP/disengagement.

ANCESTRY
--------
The broad proxy-teardown behavior is inherited from BtS/K-Mod/Civ4CE:
- K-Mod and Civ4CE also clear Open Borders, Defensive Pact and Peace Treaty team state when a deal
  involving a dead player is ended.

AdvCiv practical count 1885 / commit 3c99f281643deb793534c983d463d7c009aae181
("Fix some assertions on player death") introduced the current `bAlive` handling.

The source comment says:

    Skip some steps when a trade ends through the defeat of one party -
    to avoid failed assertions

That commit:
- disables attitude updates on death;
- suppresses OB/DP cancellation memories on death;
- and, importantly, adds `if (!bAlive) break;` to VASSAL/SURRENDER.

It does NOT suppress team-state teardown for OB/DP.

So AdvCiv partially recognized that defeat-driven proxy deletion is not an ordinary diplomatic
cancellation, but the team-state lifetime distinction was applied only to vassalage.

A later player-death fix (practical 2437) deliberately moves `killAllDeals()` until after
`m_bAlive=false`, with the explicit comment:

    killAllDeals relies on bAlive=false.

That confirms death is intentionally observable inside endTrade; the current omission is not caused
by accidental call ordering.

SEVERITY / REACHABILITY
-----------------------
This requires a team with multiple living players:
- preconfigured multiplayer/team game;
- a larger team created through game mechanics such as Permanent Alliance can also create
  multi-member teams.

Individual player elimination while teammates survive is supported directly by CvTeam's
AliveCount; only count 0 triggers whole-team death handling.

Open Borders and Defensive Pact are ordinary persistent team agreements. Therefore this is a live
gameplay bug in supported team configurations, though less common than standard one-player teams.

Disengagement is AdvCiv-specific but uses the same proxy/team-state pattern and same failure.

PEACE TREATY — RELATED BUT REPAIR-DIFFERENT
-------------------------------------------
TRADE_PEACE_TREATY is also team-level forcePeace state, and player death currently clears it
unconditionally.

However peace treaties are NOT represented as the same all-member MxN proxy set. If the signing
player dies while the team survives:
- simply skipping setForcePeace(false) would delete the only timer-bearing CvDeal;
- forcePeace could then have no deal left to expire it later.

Therefore peace has the same ownership mismatch in spirit but requires migration/re-homing or a
team-level timer solution, not the simple surviving-proxy repair below.

Do not fold peace into the minimal F284 patch unless its lifetime is explicitly preserved.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
For proxy-backed team agreements (at minimum OB / DP / DISENGAGE), distinguish:

    a participant player died
from:
    one of the participant teams is now dead.

If one player is dead but BOTH teams remain alive:
- remove only deal/proxy state involving the dead player;
- do NOT clear the CvTeam-level agreement;
- do NOT call endTeamTrade to kill the surviving player-pair proxies;
- do NOT add cancellation memory (already suppressed today).

If an entire team is dead:
- normal whole-team cleanup may clear the team-state relation as appropriate.

The existing VASSAL/SURRENDER death branch is the strongest local model, but the condition should
be team-aware if generalized.

Do NOT merely call kill(false) from killAllDeals:
`bTeam=false` suppresses endTeamTrade, but OB/DP/disengage endTrade still unconditionally clears the
team-level flag before the bTeam check. The state teardown itself must be skipped for a dead
player whose team still survives.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F284 is independent of:
- F281 (peace-deal list classification/expiry);
- F282 (diplomatic-memory accumulation);
- F283 (renewal/reset scope and overlapping agreements).

F284 is an ownership/lifetime mismatch between individual-player deal cleanup and team-level
agreement state.

RELATED CONTROL
---------------
The earlier concern about CvTeam::addTeam / CvTeam::setVassal first-list-only cleanup remains below
the independent finding bar. F284 instead has a direct default code path where surviving proxy
owners are actually destroyed.

NEXT CURSOR
-----------
Continue from F285 unused:
1. challenge the PEACE_TREATY-on-player-death subcase separately; determine whether existing code

   may need proxy materialization when that player revives;

C025-WIP06 — F285 / provisional KI#608 confirmed + saturation controls

F285 / provisional KI#608
-------------------------
TITLE
AI_stopTradingTrade checks only the AI team's own gives-list for BOTH the peace treaty and annual
reparations, so a normal one-sided saved treaty on the opposite list can make the AI accept an
embargo it cannot actually fulfill.

CURRENT DENIAL CODE
-------------------
CvPlayerAI::AI_stopTradingTrade contains the AdvCiv reparations safeguard:

    // Avoid canceling reparations
    if (GET_TEAM(getTeam()).isForcePeace(eTradeTeam))
    {
        FOR_EACH_DEAL(d)
        {
            if (!d->isBetween(getTeam(), eTradeTeam))
                continue;
            bool bPeaceTreaty = false;
            bool bAnnualPayment = false;
            FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(d->getGivesList(getTeam()))
            {
                TradeableItems eType = pItem->m_eItemType;
                if (eType == TRADE_PEACE_TREATY)
                    bPeaceTreaty = true;
                if (eType == TRADE_RESOURCES ||
                    eType == TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN)
                {
                    bAnnualPayment = true;
                }
            }
            if (bPeaceTreaty && bAnnualPayment)
                return DENIAL_RECENT_CANCEL;
        }
    }

`CvPlayer::getTradeDenial` really uses this for TRADE_EMBARGO:

    case TRADE_EMBARGO:
        return AI().AI_stopTradingTrade((TeamTypes)kTrade.m_iData);

So failure of this check changes whether the AI can agree to a stop-trading request.

LIVE SAVED DEAL ORIENTATION
---------------------------
A normal bilateral peace bundle can contain:
- peace-treaty entries on both incoming offer lists;
- GPT/resources as reparations from one side.

CvDeal processes the first side first. The first TRADE_PEACE_TREATY:
- enables team forcePeace;
- is saved.

When the second peace-treaty item is later processed:
- forcePeace is already active;
- startTrade calls resetDualDeal;
- if that finds the first saved treaty, the duplicate treaty item is not saved.

Thus an ordinary persisted deal can naturally have:
    firstList  = [TRADE_PEACE_TREATY, ...]
    secondList = [TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN, ...]

or the mirror orientation.

No malformed deal construction is required.

CONCRETE FAILURE
----------------
Choose the orientation where:
- the AI is the SECOND player/team;
- the saved peace treaty is in the FIRST list;
- the AI pays GPT reparations in the SECOND list.

Then:
- `d->isPeaceDeal()` is already true even under current unfixed F281, because the treaty happens to
  be in firstList;
- `d->getGivesList(getTeam())` for the AI sees the GPT reparations but NOT the treaty;
- AI_stopTradingTrade therefore fails to set bPeaceTreaty and does NOT return DENIAL_RECENT_CANCEL.

Now suppose the AI also has any other ordinary cancellable trade with the embargo target
(e.g. a resource trade established separately). That makes:
    canStopTradingWithTeam(target) == true
and TRADE_EMBARGO can be offered.

If the AI accepts:
- the broker/requester gets the accepted-stop-trading diplomatic outcome;
- the target receives the corresponding hired-embargo memory;
- CvPlayer::stopTradingWithTeam executes.

But stopTradingWithTeam deliberately preserves peace deals:

    if (... && !pLoopDeal->isPeaceDeal() && !pLoopDeal->isDisengage())
        pLoopDeal->kill();

Therefore:
- the unrelated resource deal is canceled;
- the peace+GPT reparations deal is deliberately NOT canceled;
- the AI keeps paying the target despite having agreed/rewarded the request to stop trading.

This is the exact inconsistency the reparations safeguard exists to prevent.

HISTORY / REGRESSION PROOF
--------------------------
The safeguard was introduced by advc.130f, practical count 1383 / commit d4fd8b6277.
The original code explicitly examined both trade lists while determining whether a peace deal
contained annual reparations.

A later traversal refactor (practical count 1626) converted that to the old combined
headTradesNode()/nextTradesNode() traversal, still covering BOTH lists and allowing the
peace-treaty item and annual item to reside on opposite sides of the same deal.

During practical-count 2998's list-interface refactor, the combined traversal was replaced with:

    FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(d->getGivesList(getTeam()))

This changed the semantic domain from "all items in this deal" to "only items given by the AI team."
The peace marker can live on the opposite side, so the representation invariant was lost.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 inherits this regression.

RELATION TO F281
----------------
F285 is independent of F281.

The concrete orientation above deliberately puts the treaty in FIRST list, so current
CvDeal::isPeaceDeal() already returns true:
- stopTradingWithTeam correctly preserves the reparations deal;
- only the AI denial precheck is wrong.

Fixing F281 does not fix F285 because AI_stopTradingTrade still scans only the AI gives-list for
the treaty marker.

Conversely, fixing F285 does not repair F281's second-list treaty expiry bug.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The intended modern condition is more precise than simply restoring the old combined "any annual
item anywhere" scan.

The reason for denial is:
    "I am currently obliged to GIVE annual reparations under a peace treaty to the embargo target."

Therefore for each deal between the teams:
1. detect the peace treaty anywhere in the deal (both saved lists, or `d->isPeaceDeal()` after F281
   is fixed);
2. inspect the AI team's own gives-list for:
       TRADE_RESOURCES
       TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN
3. if both conditions hold, return DENIAL_RECENT_CANCEL.

Conceptually:

    bool bPeaceTreaty = scanBothListsForPeace(*d); // or fixed d->isPeaceDeal()
    if (!bPeaceTreaty)
        continue;

    FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(d->getGivesList(getTeam()))
    {
        if (pItem->m_eItemType == TRADE_RESOURCES ||
            pItem->m_eItemType == TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN)
        {
            return DENIAL_RECENT_CANCEL;
        }
    }

This:
- handles treaty marker on either side;
- refuses only when the AI itself owes annual reparations;
- does not unnecessarily refuse because the OTHER side pays GPT/resources.

If implementation is deliberately independent of F281, scan both lists locally for the peace item.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F285 root:
    reparations embargo-denial lost whole-deal treaty visibility during list-interface refactor.

Independent of:
- F281 deal classification/expiry;
- F282 memory accumulation;
- F283 renewal ownership;
- F284 player-death/team-proxy ownership.

ADDITIONAL CONTROLS FROM THIS SLICE
-----------------------------------
1. Empty persistent deal / CvDeal::doTurn head dereference:
   REJECTED. CvGame::implementAndReturnDeal checks both saved list lengths after addTradeItems.
   If both are empty it immediately kills the deal and returns NULL. Ordinary one-shot/rejected
   bundles do not survive as empty CvDeals.

2. Team-proxy implementation-time attitude/value multiplication:
   REJECTED. AI_processTradeValue calls AI_dealVal(..., bIgnoreAnnual=true), and OB/DP/disengage/
   vassal proxy items are annual for that calculation. Pure dual deals are also suppressed in
   CvDeal::doTurn. MxN proxy count does not multiply ordinary trade-history value.

3. Resource verify `< 0`:
   CLEAN. After one exported copy is consumed, zero can be a valid "last copy is being exported"
   state. Negative indicates oversubscription/lost source and is the proper cancellation threshold.

4. Permanent Alliance mixed-bundle reentrancy:
   BELOW BUG BAR. AI-generated PA offers are PA-only and current PA legality requires one-member
   teams. Human/EXE mixed-bundle behavior is not locally established strongly enough for F286.

5. First-list cleanup siblings in CvTeam::addTeam / CvTeam::setVassal:
   remain representation debt/control. No independent state consequence stronger than F281/F283
   established.

F283 SAME-ROOT EXPANSION — practical 2658 vote-prolongation proves all team proxies must share age
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Practical count 2658 explicitly added the `bProlong` paths to Open Borders and Defensive Pact so
diplomatic votes can reset the turns before those agreements become cancelable.

Current CvGame::processVote:

    if (kVote.isOpenBorders())
        itFirst->signOpenBorders(itSecond->getID(), true);
    if (kVote.isDefensivePact())
        itFirst->signDefensivePact(itSecond->getID(), true);

CvTeam::signOpenBorders / signDefensivePact call implementDeal using the two TEAM LEADERS. Their
startTrade paths contain:

    if (isOpenBorders(...))
    {
        if (kFromPlayer.resetDualDeal(eToPlayer, TRADE_OPEN_BORDERS))
            break;
    }

and the analogous DP path.

But the persistent OB/DP representation is an MxN set of player-pair proxy deals created by
startTeamTrade for every living member pair. resetDualDeal:
- searches only deals between the two leader players;
- scans only the first list;
- resets only the first matching proxy;
- then returns under the source assumption "at most one deal of eDealType."

For a multi-member team agreement, that assumption is false by construction.

Consequently a vote intended to "prolong the Open Borders / Defensive Pact agreement" resets only
the leader-leader proxy. Other proxies retain their older initial turns. Once one older proxy is
cancelable, canceling it can endTeamTrade the entire logical agreement even though the diplomatic
vote intended to refresh its minimum duration.

This is especially strong F283 evidence because practical 2658 is the feature that introduced the
renewal helper for OB/DP. The current player-pair implementation cannot fulfill that feature's
team-level intent on multi-member teams.

F283 repair contract therefore remains:
- locate the logical TEAM agreement;
- inspect both saved lists;
- update every proxy deal that owns the same team-level OB/DP lifetime, or replace proxy-local ages
  with one logical agreement age;
- for peace, locate the treaty across the two teams rather than one particular player pair.

A both-list-only patch remains incomplete.


F284 SAME-ROOT EXPANSION — PEACE_TREATY has the same player-owner/team-state mismatch, but no proxy fallback
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP05 proved the clean proxy-backed failure for OB/DP/DISENGAGE:
individual player death calls killAllDeals even while teammates survive, and deleting one proxy
clears team-level state plus kills surviving proxies.

TRADE_PEACE_TREATY has the same ownership mismatch:
- forcePeace is stored on CvTeam;
- the treaty timer/lifetime is stored in a CvDeal owned by two Players;
- unlike OB/DP, peace is normally represented by ONE saved treaty item rather than an MxN proxy set.

If the player owning that treaty dies while his team still has living members:
- setAlive(false) calls killAllDeals;
- endTrade(TRADE_PEACE_TREATY) unconditionally calls setForcePeace(..., false);
- the surviving teammate's team therefore loses the rest of the temporary peace period early.

This is the same conceptual F284 root:
    an individual-player deal lifetime is allowed to destroy team-level diplomatic state even
    though the participant team itself survives.

However its minimal repair differs from proxy-backed agreements.

For OB/DP/DISENGAGE:
- surviving member-pair proxy deals remain, so defeat cleanup can simply avoid team-wide teardown
  and let the surviving proxies continue owning the state.

For PEACE_TREATY:
- the dying player's deal may be the ONLY timer-bearing owner.
- merely skipping setForcePeace(false) and deleting the deal would leave forcePeace with no treaty
  left to expire it later.

Therefore a complete F284 repair should either:
1. re-home/migrate the surviving treaty duration to a deal between living members of the same two
   teams before deleting the dead player's deal; or
2. move temporary-peace lifetime ownership to team-level state independent of a particular
   player's CvDeal.

Do not patch peace by merely adding the OB/DP death guard.

The live consequence strengthens F284 but does not justify a separate F286: both cases arise from
the same player-object ownership being used to control team-object state during individual defeat.


REVIVAL / NEWLY ALIVE MEMBER — CONTROL
--------------------------------------
A revived player on an already-living team does not need a new proxy merely to USE existing
team-level Open Borders / Defensive Pact / Disengagement:
- the actual permission/state flags live on CvTeam;
- revived player units inherit those team relations immediately.

The absence of a newly materialized player-pair proxy can affect who carries cancellation age and
how later renewal/cancellation is represented. That is already F283's logical-team-agreement versus
player-proxy lifetime problem, not an independent root.

No separate F286 from revival.


EMPTY DEAL / TURN PROCESSING — CONTROL
--------------------------------------
CvDeal::doTurn dereferences firstList.head() in its pure-dual fast-path condition, which initially
looked unsafe for an empty persistent CvDeal.

The allocation wrapper closes that path:
CvGame::implementAndReturnDeal calls addTradeItems, then if BOTH saved lists are empty it
immediately kills the deal and returns NULL.

One-shot-only bundles and rejected/blocked bundles therefore do not survive as empty CvDeals into
the turn loop. No F286.


PROXY TRADE-VALUE MULTIPLICATION — CONTROL
-------------------------------------------
startTeamTrade creates MxN proxy CvDeals, but implementation-time AI trade-value accounting does
not multiply the ordinary attitude value per proxy:
- AI_processTradeValue uses AI_dealVal(..., bIgnoreAnnual=true);
- OB / DP / disengagement / vassal items are treated as annual for this purpose and skipped;
- CvDeal::doTurn separately skips pure one-item dual deals.

No F286.

F286 / provisional KI#609
-------------------------
TITLE
A human mixed Permanent Alliance + city/implied-peace bundle can delete the CvDeal from inside
CvDeal::addTradeItems and then CvGame::implementAndReturnDeal immediately dereferences the freed
pointer.

SUPPORTED TRIGGER
-----------------
Current CvPlayer::updateTradeList explicitly says:

    if (!isHuman() || !GET_PLAYER(eOtherPlayer).isHuman())
        ...
        // mixed annual/nonannual items restricted
    // everything allowed in human-human trades

Permanent Alliance is a normal inventory item when:
- GAMEOPTION_PERMANENT_ALLIANCES / PA trading is available;
- both teams are non-vassals, at peace, distinct;
- both teams currently have exactly one member.

A non-liberation city offer at peacetime is one of the current items that implies temporary peace.
Current updateTradeList therefore appends explicit TRADE_PEACE_TREATY entries to BOTH human offer
lists for display/implementation:

    TradeData item(TRADE_PEACE_TREATY);
    ...
    item.m_iData = eForcePeaceItemType;
    apOffersVar[i]->insertAtEnd(item);

Thus a supported human-human bundle can contain, for example:
- first side: city + permanent alliance + appended peace treaty;
- second side: appended peace treaty
(or equivalent orientation/order supplied by the trade screen).

No malformed direct-DLL call is needed.

EXECUTION CHAIN
---------------
CvGame::implementAndReturnDeal:

    CvDeal* pDeal = addDeal();
    pDeal->init(...);
    pDeal->addTradeItems(kOurList, kTheirList, !bForce);
    if (pDeal->getLengthFirst() <= 0 && pDeal->getLengthSecond() <= 0)
    {
        pDeal->kill();
        return NULL;
    }
    return pDeal;

Inside addTradeItems:

1. Trade items are processed before the Permanent Alliance merge.

2. The first explicit TRADE_PEACE_TREATY encountered:
       setForcePeace(..., true);
       bSave = true;
   and is inserted into the current CvDeal's saved list.

3. When the opposite-side peace-treaty item is later processed, forcePeace is already true.
   resetDualDeal can find the just-created current deal and the already-saved treaty, so the
   duplicate treaty normally is not saved. The current deal nevertheless contains at least one
   saved TRADE_PEACE_TREATY.

4. TRADE_PERMANENT_ALLIANCE itself sets:
       bAlliance = true
   and is not saved.

5. After both item loops:
       if (bAlliance)
           GET_TEAM(...).addTeam(...);

CvTeam::addTeam reassigns the absorbed team's players into the surviving team and then iterates
deals that are now internal to the merged team:

    if (!pLoopDeal->isBetween(getID(), getID()))
        continue;

    FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(pLoopDeal->getFirstList())
    {
        if (eType == TRADE_OPEN_BORDERS ||
            eType == TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT ||
            eType == TRADE_PEACE_TREATY ||
            ...)
        {
            pLoopDeal->kill();
            break;
        }
    }

The currently executing CvDeal now has:
- both players on the same merged team;
- a saved first-list peace treaty.

Therefore addTeam can call `kill()` on the very `this` whose addTradeItems stack frame is active.

IMMEDIATE DELETION / UAF PROOF
------------------------------
CvDeal::kill -> killSilent -> GC.getGame().deleteDeal(getID()).

CvGame::deleteDeal:
    m_deals.removeAt(iID);

FFreeListTrashArray::removeAt:
    SAFE_DELETE(m_pArray[iIndex].pData);

So the CvDeal object is actually destroyed before CvTeam::addTeam returns.

CvDeal::addTradeItems then returns through a member function whose `this` is already freed.
Even if its final bBumpUnits block happens not to dereference members in the concrete path, the
caller unconditionally does:

    pDeal->getLengthFirst()
    pDeal->getLengthSecond()

immediately after addTradeItems returns.

That is an unambiguous use-after-free.

ANCESTRY
--------
The dangerous interaction is AdvCiv-specific.

Practical count 2691 / commit 195785f015f5e71cffa4b6c52e2307ad8cc08a94:
    "Show implied peace treaties on the trade table"

added explicit PEACE_TREATY entries to human-visible offers for city/war items that imply temporary
peace. Its own comment says that, for deals involving humans, the game will attempt to implement
the treaty twice and considers that harmless.

Before that display change, the underlying city trade could merely set an internal
`bPeaceTreatyImplied`/sign-treaty path; a PA bundle takes the `bAlliance` branch and does not
materialize an explicit saved treaty that addTeam's internal-deal cleanup can recognize.

Practical 3275 later deferred implied-treaty signing until all bundle items had been applied to
avoid two unilateral treaties, but explicit treaty items added by the human trade table remain
processed/saved before the PA merge. It does not close this self-deletion path.

K-Mod/Civ4CE do not contain AdvCiv's same implied-peace-display mechanism in this form, so they do
not independently reproduce this exact trigger.

WHY CURRENT PREVALIDATION DOES NOT SAVE IT
------------------------------------------
addTradeItems validates each individual item through canTradeItem before applying the bundle.
There is no bundle-level rule forbidding Permanent Alliance + city/explicit implied peace for
human-human trades.

updateTradeList deliberately skips the annual/nonannual combination restriction when both players
are human ("everything allowed in human-human trades").

TRADE_PERMANENT_ALLIANCE canPossiblyTradeItem checks the two teams are single-member BEFORE the
merge; that condition is satisfied at validation time.

So all items can pass individually while their combined execution causes reentrant deletion.

SEVERITY
--------
High when triggered:
- heap object is freed while its method remains active;
- caller immediately dereferences the dangling CvDeal*;
- outcome can be crash, assertion, allocator-dependent corruption or apparently surviving stale
  memory depending on build/runtime.

The trigger is specialized (human-human PA enabled + mixed implied-peace bundle) but uses supported
trade-screen mechanics.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The core invariant should be:

    CvTeam::addTeam must not delete the CvDeal that is currently implementing the Permanent Alliance
    until addTradeItems / implementAndReturnDeal have completed using that object.

Evidence-supported repair shapes include:

1. Preferred transaction/order repair:
   - do not persist an explicit implied peacetime PEACE_TREATY inside a deal that also executes a
     Permanent Alliance, because after the teams merge the treaty is meaningless anyway;
   - still display it to humans if needed, but suppress its saved lifetime when PA is in the same
     bundle.

2. Deferred cleanup:
   - let addTeam identify internal deals for cleanup but defer deletion of the currently executing
     deal until implementAndReturnDeal is done with it.

3. Bundle pre-normalization:
   - strip/ignore redundant PEACE_TREATY items from PA bundles before startTrade saves them.

A weak patch such as "don't dereference pDeal after addTradeItems" is insufficient unless ownership
and return semantics are redesigned, because `addTradeItems` itself may continue after deletion and
the function still conceptually returns through a dead `this`.

Do NOT remove all addTeam internal-deal cleanup: stale OB/DP/vassal/etc. agreements between newly
same-team players still need normalization.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F286 is independent of F281-F285.

It is a reentrant object-lifetime/use-after-free bug caused by:
- explicit implied treaty materialization in a PA bundle;
- addTeam's internal-deal cleanup;
- immediate free-list deletion;
- post-call use of the CvDeal pointer.

It reproduces even if:
- F281 both-list peace classification is fixed;
- F282 memory accumulation is fixed;
- F283 team-level renewal is fixed;
- F284 player-death ownership is fixed;
- F285 embargo reparations detection is fixed.

CONTROLS / CAVEATS
------------------
- A pure PA offer does not save any item in the implementing CvDeal and is safely discarded as an
  empty deal after the merge.
- PA + ordinary one-shot items without an explicit saved internal team-state item do not
  automatically trigger this exact self-delete path.
- The strongest current trigger is PA + non-liberation city, because updateTradeList itself inserts
  explicit peace treaty items for human-visible implied peace.

F287 / provisional KI#610
-------------------------
TITLE
Automatic invalidation of one annual item kills the entire mixed peace deal, so a broke GPT payer
can terminate the mandatory peace treaty before PEACE_TREATY_LENGTH expires.

CURRENT CODE
------------
CvDeal::verify:

    if (!verify(getFirstPlayer(), getSecondPlayer()) ||
        !verify(getSecondPlayer(), getFirstPlayer()) ||
        (isCancelable(NO_PLAYER) && isPeaceDeal()))
    {
        kill();
    }

The directional helper checks persistent annual items regardless of deal age.

For GPT:

    if (pItem->m_eItemType == TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN)
    {
        if (kGiver.getCommercePercent(COMMERCE_GOLD) >= 100 &&
            kGiver.getGold() < pItem->m_iData && !kGiver.isAnarchy() &&
            kGiver.calculateGoldRate() < 0)
        {
            return false;
        }
    }

A false result kills the entire CvDeal immediately.

If that same persistent deal also contains TRADE_PEACE_TREATY, kill -> endTrade processes the
treaty and executes:

    GET_TEAM(eFromPlayer).setForcePeace(TEAMID(eToPlayer), false);

There is no independent remaining-turn field inside CvTeam::forcePeace; `isForcePeace` is simply
the stored team boolean. The CvDeal is the timer/lifetime owner.

SUPPORTED MIXED DEAL
--------------------
GPT is explicitly tradeable during war/peace negotiation:
- TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN canPossiblyTradeItem only requires gold trading;
- canTradeItem itself accepts any nonnegative GPT amount;
- it does not require an existing peacetime trade network.

Human peace settlements can therefore legitimately contain:
    TRADE_PEACE_TREATY + TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN reparations

in one persistent CvDeal.

The first PEACE_TREATY entry is saved as the temporary-peace lifetime item. GPT is also persistent
and saved in the same deal.

FAILURE CHAIN
-------------
Example:
- turn T0: peace signed with 10-turn treaty and 8 GPT reparations;
- T1/T2/... before T0+PEACE_TREATY_LENGTH: payer reaches 100% gold slider, cannot cover the GPT
  payment, is not in anarchy and still has a negative gold rate;
- CvGame::verifyDeals -> CvDeal::verify;
- GPT condition returns false;
- CvDeal::kill executes immediately despite `turnsToCancel() > 0`;
- GPT payment ends;
- TRADE_PEACE_TREATY teardown clears team forcePeace;
- the teams can resume war before the mandatory treaty duration has elapsed.

The normal treaty age protection:

    (isCancelable(NO_PLAYER) && isPeaceDeal())

only governs scheduled treaty expiry. It does NOT protect a peace deal from the earlier
resource/GPT invalidation branches.

ANCESTRY
--------
The general "invalid resource item kills whole deal" architecture is inherited from BtS/K-Mod/
Civ4CE.

The particularly common GPT trigger is AdvCiv-specific.

Practical count 2765 / commit c66c29025a3be4912b019a7b6128889ae07aacac:
    "Force-cancel gold-per-turn deals when broke"

added exactly the GPT false-return block to CvDeal::verify.

The patch did not special-case mixed peace deals or preserve the remaining treaty duration.
Therefore practical 2765 made ordinary GPT peace reparations capable of terminating temporary
peace early.

K-Mod/Civ4CE do not contain this GPT insolvency branch, though their inherited resource-invalid
whole-deal behavior shows the broader structural hazard.

RESOURCE SIBLING
----------------
Resource invalidation has the same whole-deal teardown behavior:
- lost trade network;
- oversubscribed resource;
- obsolete resource.

A resource + peacetime temporary treaty bundle could therefore exhibit the same lifetime problem.
For wartime peace negotiations, resource trading is often unavailable because canTradeNetworkWith
fails while enemies are at war, so GPT is the cleaner supported/default reproduction.

Treat resource invalidation as same-root structural evidence; F287 does not depend on proving a
wartime resource reparations case.

WHY THIS IS NOT NORMAL CANCELLATION
-----------------------------------
Manual cancellation is intentionally blocked while:
    turnsToCancel() > 0.

The GPT verify branch bypasses isCancelable entirely. So this is not simply "the payer is allowed
to cancel because insolvent." The engine itself tears down an uncancelable treaty as a side effect
of an annual payment failure.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
When an individual annual component of a deal becomes impossible during an uncancelable peace
period, the temporary peace lifetime must survive.

Possible evidence-supported designs:

1. Remove/end only the invalid annual item from the deal while retaining TRADE_PEACE_TREATY and its
   original initial turn.

2. If deal-level killing is retained, immediately re-home/recreate the treaty with the exact
   remaining duration before clearing forcePeace.

3. Split peace treaty lifetime from annual-payment deal lifetime when the bundle is implemented.

For the narrow GPT repair:
- cancel the impossible GPT obligation;
- do not clear temporary peace before its existing expiry.

Do NOT merely skip GPT verification while peace is active if that would leave an impossible payment
continuing indefinitely. The payment and the treaty have different failure/lifetime semantics.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F287 is independent of F281-F286.

Even with:
- correct both-list isPeaceDeal;
- correct renewal;
- correct team-member death ownership;
- correct reparations embargo denial;
- no PA self-deletion;

an insolvent GPT component can still make `verify()` kill the whole still-young peace deal.

F286 SAME-ROOT EXPANSION — vassalization can self-delete the active transaction too
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP08 proved a high-confidence self-deletion path through Permanent Alliance.

The same transaction-lifetime invariant is violated by `CvTeam::setVassal(true)` under a supported
human peacetime mixed bundle.

SUPPORTED BUNDLE
----------------
At peacetime:
- human-human diplomacy permits mixed trade classes;
- a non-liberation city offer causes updateTradeList to append explicit PEACE_TREATY entries to
  both offer lists;
- voluntary TRADE_VASSAL is tradeable when neither team is already a vassal and the two sides are
  not at war.

Thus a supported bundle can contain:
    non-liberation city + voluntary vassal + displayed implied peace treaty.

EXECUTION
---------
addTradeItems deliberately processes non-vassal items in pass 0 and vassal items in pass 1.

Therefore before TRADE_VASSAL is executed:
- city transfer has occurred;
- the first explicit PEACE_TREATY has been saved in the current CvDeal.

TRADE_VASSAL then calls:

    startTeamTrade(...);
    GET_TEAM(eFromPlayer).setVassal(eToTeam, true, false);

Inside setVassal(true), current code iterates global deals involving the new vassal and kills
Defensive Pact / Peace Treaty deals whose FIRST list contains such an item:

    FOR_EACH_DEAL_VAR(pLoopDeal)
    {
        ...
        FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(pLoopDeal->getFirstList())
        {
            if (pItem->m_eItemType == TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT ||
                pItem->m_eItemType == TRADE_PEACE_TREATY)
            {
                pLoopDeal->kill();
                break;
            }
        }
    }

The currently executing deal is already in the global free-list container and can satisfy this
test. Its first-list displayed implied treaty was saved before the vassal pass.

`kill()` therefore immediately SAFE_DELETEs the active CvDeal through `deleteDeal/removeAt`, exactly
as in the PA path.

Control then returns to the active `startTrade` / `addTradeItems` stack and ultimately to
implementAndReturnDeal, which dereferences the dangling pDeal pointer.

ROOT CLASSIFICATION
-------------------
Do not allocate F288.

The PA and vassal paths are the same root:
    a state transition invoked while applying a bundle is allowed to synchronously delete the
    CvDeal transaction object that is still executing that bundle.

The exact cleanup walker differs (`CvTeam::addTeam` vs `CvTeam::setVassal`), but the object-lifetime
contract and use-after-free consequence are identical.

This broadens the F286 repair requirement:
- transaction execution must survive all state-transition cleanup it invokes;
- implied/internal treaty normalization cannot synchronously destroy the active transaction.

WAR-BRIBE REENTRANCY CHALLENGE — CLEAN UNDER NORMAL DENIAL
-----------------------------------------------------------
TRADE_WAR calls `CvTeam::declareWar` synchronously, and defensive-pact cascades can themselves
declare additional wars and kill deals. This initially suggested another possible active-transaction
deletion.

A concrete dangerous shape would be:
- B brokers A into declaring war on C;
- B has a Defensive Pact with C;
- C's pact then causes B to declare war on A;
- B-vs-A war cleanup could kill the active A<->B bribe deal.

The trade denial closes the normal path.

`CvTeamAI::AI_declareWarTrade(eTarget=C, eSponsor=B)` begins with:

    if (GET_TEAM(eTarget).isVassal(eSponsor) ||
        GET_TEAM(eTarget).isDefensivePact(eSponsor))
        return DENIAL_JOKING;

TRADE_WAR can only be given by a non-human team through normal trade legality, and addTradeItems
prevalidates with denial checks unless the caller explicitly forces the deal.

Therefore the DP-with-sponsor cascade cannot occur through an ordinary accepted war-bribe deal.
A forced/malformed direct implementation could bypass this, but that is below the finding bar.

No F288.


`doTurn` ONE-ITEM DUAL FAST PATH — CLEAN
----------------------------------------
The condition:

    getLengthSecond() == getLengthFirst() &&
    getLengthSecond() <= 1 &&
    isDual(getFirstList().head()->m_data.m_eItemType)

looks as though it could skip peacetime-value processing based only on the first-side item even if
the second-side item were non-dual.

Current persistence semantics prevent the concerning normal shape:
- initial OPEN_BORDERS / DEFENSIVE_PACT / DISENGAGE items with m_iData<=0 are not saved in the
  initiating mixed deal; they create separate generated team-proxy deals;
- those generated dual proxies contain the same dual item on both sides;
- PEACE_TREATY is saved but `isPeaceDeal()` excludes the whole deal before this shortcut;
- PERMANENT_ALLIANCE is not saved;
- vassal items are not `isDual`.

So the live one-item-each dual case is the intended pure proxy agreement. No hidden GPT/resource
mixed deal is skipped by this shortcut.

No F288.


SMALL METHOD / ACCESSOR FAMILY — CONTROLS
-----------------------------------------
`isVassalTrade`
    whole-list scan; orientation-independent.

`isUncancelableVassalDeal`
    current generated vassal proxy representation gives exactly one vassal/master team side;
    getGivesList(team) contract is satisfied.

`isVassalTributeDeal`
    the static all-resources predicate is vacuously true for an empty list, but the persistent
    instance form cannot become a meaningful empty deal because empty CvDeals are deleted by
    implementAndReturnDeal. No live queue-042 root established.

`isDisengage`
    requires exactly one item on each side and generated disengagement proxies are dual, so the
    first-list head is guaranteed.

`getGivesList/getReceivesList(TeamTypes)`
    assert that exactly one participant belongs to the queried team. Same-team ordinary deals can
    exist after Permanent Alliance, but current team-overload callers first scope deals to two
    distinct relevant teams; no live assertion trigger found.

`isAllDual`
    empty-list true is mathematically vacuous but persistent empty deals are removed immediately;
    display/filter callers therefore see nonempty deals.

`isAnnual/isDual/hasData/isEndWar`
    current callers and trade categories line up with the persistence/valuation semantics examined;
    no omitted current trade enum found.
