C025-WIP19 ADDENDUM — queue 042 CvDeal.cpp / cross-file accessor consumer
F294 / provisional KI#617 confirmed; F295 unused
================================================================================

F294 / provisional KI#617
Title:
  Embargo valuation scans the hired player's whole team instead of the hired
  player's own deals, overpricing teammate trade that will survive the embargo
  and violating CvDeal's player-accessor contract on multi-member teams.

Root:
  CvPlayerAI::AI_stopTradingTradeVal describes its contract directly:

      "This player pays for the embargo and ePlayer stops trading
       with eTradeTeam."

  The actual embargo machinery has the same player-specific contract.

  CvPlayer::isTradingWithTeam documents:
      "- It checks if this player is trading with any member of eToTeam.
         Likewise, an embargo will affect only the enacting player - but the
         entire target team."

  CvPlayer::stopTradingWithTeam therefore filters:
      if (!pLoopDeal->isBetween(getID(), eTeam))
          continue;

  i.e. only deals involving the specific enacting player are candidates for
  cancellation.

  AI_stopTradingTradeVal instead scans:
      if (!pLoopDeal->isBetween(TEAMID(ePlayer), eTradeTeam))
          continue;

  That is a team-vs-team filter. On a team with more than one player it admits
  persistent deals owned by ePlayer's teammates even though those deals will not
  be canceled when ePlayer executes the embargo.

Concrete live topology:
  Let A1 and A2 be two living players on Team A (e.g. after a Permanent Alliance
  or in a preconfigured multi-player team), and let T be the embargo target team.

  A1 is the player being asked to stop trading with T. A1 has some valid
  outgoing trade to T, so:
      A1.canStopTradingWithTeam(T) == true.

  A2 independently has a valuable persistent resource/GPT deal with a member of
  T. Such player-level deals remain normal after the players share Team A.

  AI_stopTradingTradeVal(T, A1):
    * pLoopDeal(A2,T) passes isBetween(Team A, T);
    * its incoming consideration can therefore be added to A1's embargo price.

  Actual execution:
      A1.stopTradingWithTeam(T)

  only visits deals satisfying isBetween(A1,T), so A2's deal survives.

  Result: the sponsor can be charged for trade value that the hired player does
  not give up and that the embargo does not cancel.

CvDeal accessor-contract failure introduced on top of the semantic root:
  Current AdvCiv/SAS refactored the duplicated orientation branches into:

      pLoopDeal->getReceivesList(TEAMID(ePlayer))
      pLoopDeal->getOtherPlayer(ePlayer)
      pLoopDeal->getGivesList(ePlayer)

  The first call is deliberately team-scoped, but the latter two require the
  exact player to participate:

      CvDeal::getOtherPlayer(PlayerTypes ePlayer):
          FAssert(ePlayer == getFirstPlayer() ||
                  ePlayer == getSecondPlayer());

      CvDeal::getGivesList(PlayerTypes eGivingPlayer):
          same exact-participant assertion.

  Therefore, for an admitted A2<->T deal while ePlayer=A1:
    * Debug/Assert DLLs trip getOtherPlayer(A1);
    * if execution continues, getGivesList(A1) trips too.

Release behavior is not merely "assert removed":
  getOtherPlayer uses:
      return (ePlayer == getFirstPlayer() ?
              getSecondPlayer() : getFirstPlayer());

  When A1 is absent, it always falls through to getFirstPlayer.

  Thus result quality becomes deal-orientation dependent:
    * if A2 is first, getOtherPlayer(A1) returns A2 itself and A1.AI_dealVal is
      asked to value target-supplied items as though teammate A2 supplied them;
    * if T's player is first, the returned "other" happens to be the target
      participant by accident.

  getGivesList(A1) has the analogous absent-player fall-through to the second
  list, so the 5-vs-3 gift/trade multiplier can likewise inspect the wrong side
  depending on orientation.

  The underlying overcount exists even if those fall-through results happened
  to be benign: the teammate deal should not have entered this loop at all.

Direct normal embargo consequence:
  CvPlayerAI::AI_dealVal prices each TRADE_EMBARGO by:
      AI_stopTradingTradeVal(targetTeam, eFromPlayer)

  so this inflated/misoriented result feeds ordinary trade valuation and can
  alter whether/how much an AI sponsor is willing to pay for the embargo.

War-bribe lower-bound sibling:
  CvTeamAI::AI_declareWarTradeVal deliberately computes an embargo lower bound:

      "an embargo ... would only compel one player to stop trading with the
       (whole) target team, so we need to sum up the embargo trade values of
       the members of this team."

  It loops each hireling-team member that canStopTradingWithTeam(eTarget) and
  calls:
      sponsorLeader.AI_stopTradingTradeVal(eTarget, member, true);

  That design confirms the unit of cancellation/value is one player at a time.

  With a multi-member team, however, every one of those per-player calls scans
  the whole team's T-deals. If A1 and A2 each have cancelable player-level trade
  with T, A1's call can count A2's deal and A2's call can count A1's deal; the
  sum can therefore count the same trade losses repeatedly. This can inflate
  the lower bound used for a declaration-of-war bribe in addition to the direct
  embargo-price error.

Ancestry:
  The semantic player-vs-team mismatch is inherited from BtS/K-Mod/Civ4CE.

  Their AI_stopTradingTradeVal loops classify a deal as relevant whenever a
  participant's TEAM equals ePlayer's team. That already counts teammate-owned
  deals on multi-member teams, despite stopTradingWithTeam being player-scoped.

  AdvCiv practical 1352
  "Bugs fixed in AI war trade behavior; tech cost adjustments"
  (advc.130f/advc.001q) improved the inherited scan by adding the missing
  opposite-side target-team condition. Before that, BtS effectively checked only
  whether one participant belonged to ePlayer's team; the AdvCiv source comment
  records this explicitly:
      "BtS had only checked for ePlayer's team"

  That repair correctly stopped unrelated third-team deals from entering the
  price, but retained TEAMID(ePlayer) rather than the exact ePlayer identity.

  AdvCiv practical 1618
  "FOR_EACH macros everywhere; changes to AI class design."
  later rewrote the two orientation branches with the new CvDeal accessors.
  The refactor preserved the team-level filter but then called exact-player
  getOtherPlayer/getGivesList, turning the older semantic mismatch into a
  deterministic assertion-contract violation as well.

  Current Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains this shape. SAS inherits it; SAS's nearby
  local change merely caches GET_PLAYER(ePlayer) as kPlayer.

Why multi-member teams are not exotic malformed state:
  Permanent Alliance is a shipped trade item and deliberately combines players
  onto one team; scenario/team-game setups can also begin with multiple players
  sharing a team. Player-level resource/GPT deals remain represented by their
  individual player IDs. The embargo APIs themselves are explicitly documented
  around this distinction, so the code cannot assume one player per team here.

Independence from earlier findings:
  * F285 is an embargo-DENIAL/list-orientation bug involving peace reparations.
    F294 can reproduce with ordinary resource/GPT deals and no peace treaty.
  * F290 concerns old team identities while tearing down agreements during a
    Permanent Alliance merge. F294 applies after a multi-member team already
    exists and concerns current player-owned trade valuation.
  * F284 concerns a player death tearing down team-owned agreements. F294 is the
    inverse scope error: team-wide scanning of player-owned persistent deals.
  * F293 concerns lossy multi-target political attitude context, not deal owner
    identity.

Repair boundary:
  For the persistent ordinary-deal loop in AI_stopTradingTradeVal, use the same
  player scope as the operation being valued:

      if (!pLoopDeal->isBetween(ePlayer, eTradeTeam))
          continue;

  Once that invariant is established, use player-scoped list accessors
  consistently:
      getReceivesList(ePlayer)
      getOtherPlayer(ePlayer)
      getGivesList(ePlayer)

  This simultaneously:
    * excludes teammate deals that survive ePlayer's embargo;
    * satisfies getOtherPlayer/getGivesList's exact-participant contracts;
    * removes orientation-dependent Release fall-through.

  Important boundary:
  Keep the separate Open Borders / Defensive Pact terms under review as
  team-level relationship costs. Those relationships are genuinely stored and
  torn down at team scope through their proxy/agreement machinery. Do not
  mechanically convert every TEAMID(ePlayer) use in the function to player
  scope; F294 is specifically the ordinary persistent-deal inventory whose
  actual cancellation path is player-specific.

  The war-bribe member-sum should then naturally aggregate disjoint per-player
  trade losses instead of recounting the full team inventory for every member.
  Its team-level OB/DP contribution may still deserve independent heuristic
  review, but that is not required to repair the proven F294 root.

Queue state after this checkpoint:
  queue 042 CvGameCoreDLL/CvDeal.cpp — still OPEN
  F281-F294 / provisional KI#604-KI#617 — confirmed
  F295 / provisional KI#618 — UNUSED / next

Remaining saturation cursor:
  * challenge the team-level OB/DP contribution in the multi-member war-bribe
    member sum without assuming it is a bug merely because it is repeated;
  * finish the historical repair-stream ledger and remaining classification /
    serialization / cancellation controls;
  * if no independent F295 survives, close queue 042 cleanly rather than
    manufacturing another root.

C025-WIP20 ADDENDUM — queue 042 CvDeal.cpp / war-trade embargo lower bound
F295 / provisional KI#618 confirmed; F296 unused
================================================================================

F295 / provisional KI#618
Title:
  Multi-member war-bribe embargo lower bound counts shared team-level
  Open-Borders / Defensive-Pact loss once per player even though the first
  embargo tears the shared agreement down for the whole team.

Root:
  CvTeamAI::AI_declareWarTradeVal deliberately constructs an embargo-equivalent
  lower bound by summing AI_stopTradingTradeVal for every member of the hireling
  team that can stop trading with the target:

      int iEmbargoTradeVal = 0;
      for (MemberIter itMember(getID()); itMember.hasNext(); ++itMember)
      {
          if (itMember->canStopTradingWithTeam(eTarget))
          {
              iEmbargoTradeVal += sponsorLeader.AI_stopTradingTradeVal(
                      eTarget, itMember->getID(), true);
          }
      }
      iTradeVal = max(iTradeVal, 0.83 * iEmbargoTradeVal);

  This decomposition is valid for independent player-owned resource/GPT deals:
  an embargo by A1 cancels A1's deals, and a separate embargo by A2 cancels A2's
  deals.

  It is not additive for Open Borders or Defensive Pact. Those are team-level
  relationships represented by replicated player-pair proxy deals. Killing one
  qualifying proxy with normal bKillTeam=true tears down the relationship for
  the entire pair of teams and deletes all sibling proxies.

Source-proven shared state:
  CvDeal::startTeamTrade(TRADE_OPEN_BORDERS / TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT, ...)
  creates a proxy deal for every member-pair.

  CvDeal::endTrade for either item:
      GET_TEAM(eFromPlayer).setOpenBorders/DefensivePact(..., false);
      if (bTeam)
          endTeamTrade(...);

  CvDeal::endTeamTrade then finds all sibling proxies between those teams and
  kills them with kill(false).

  CvPlayer::stopTradingWithTeam kills a qualifying player deal with ordinary:
      pLoopDeal->kill();
  i.e. bKillTeam defaults true.

  Therefore the first member embargo that kills an OB/DP proxy removes the
  shared team relation and every other member's corresponding proxy. A second
  member does not independently lose another copy of that relationship.

How AI_stopTradingTradeVal nevertheless prices it on every member call:
  For each ePlayer member it derives:
      CvTeam const& kTeam = GET_TEAM(ePlayer);

  and applies the same team-level Open-Borders state:
      if (kTeam.isOpenBorders(eTradeTeam))
      {
          iModifier += 50;
          ...
      }

  followed by the same team-level Defensive-Pact state:
      if (GET_TEAM(ePlayer).isDefensivePact(eTradeTeam))
          iValue *= 3;

  All players on the same team therefore carry identical OB/DP relationship
  state into every pre-cancellation member valuation.

Concrete two-member Open-Borders case:
  Let A1 and A2 share Team A, and T be the proposed war target.

  Team A has Open Borders with T and no other ordinary trade is required.

  startTeamTrade has created OB proxies involving both A1 and A2, so both can
  satisfy canStopTradingWithTeam(T).

  AI_declareWarTradeVal computes:
      stopTradeVal(T, A1, true)
    + stopTradeVal(T, A2, true)

  Both calls independently include the Open-Borders modifier.

  But actual embargo execution is sequential state mutation:
      A1.stopTradingWithTeam(T)
        -> kills A1's OB proxy with bKillTeam=true
        -> setOpenBorders(T,false)
        -> endTeamTrade removes all remaining A<->T OB proxies.

  At that point A2 has no second Open-Borders relation left to sacrifice.
  The lower-bound sum has counted one shared loss twice.

  With N hireling-team members the same shared relationship contribution can be
  repeated N times.

Defensive-Pact magnification:
  Defensive Pact is also one team-level relation with replicated proxies, but
  AI_stopTradingTradeVal applies:
      iValue *= 3
  for every member call while the pact is present.

  Thus the same shared DP loss can magnify every component of the N-member sum,
  even though the first actual cancellation removes the pact for the whole team.
  This makes the non-additivity substantially larger than the OB-only case.

Why this is independent of F294:
  F294 is the ordinary persistent-deal inventory scope error inside
  AI_stopTradingTradeVal:
      isBetween(TEAMID(ePlayer), eTradeTeam)
  admits teammate-owned resource/GPT deals and can violate exact-player
  CvDeal accessor contracts.

  Repairing F294 to:
      isBetween(ePlayer, eTradeTeam)
  correctly makes player-owned annual losses disjoint across member calls.

  F295 survives unchanged after that repair because the Open-Borders modifier
  and Defensive-Pact multiplier are explicit team-state terms outside the
  ordinary-deal loop. Every member call still sees the same shared team
  relationship before any hypothetical cancellation has been applied.

History / introduced intent:
  AdvCiv practical 2930, commit
      a16555656d83d7bc92067d6c1156ce0303d1f69d
  "Fix minor issue with war trade val computation"
  changed the prior leader-only embargo lower bound into the current
  member-summed form.

  Commit message:
      "The lower bound based on the embargo trade value hadn't been calculated
       correctly at all. [advc.104o]"

  The introduced source comment is explicit about the model:
      "Don't charge much less than for an embargo. An embargo (weirdly)
       would only compel one player to stop trading with the (whole) target team,
       so we need to sum up the embargo trade values of the members of this team."

  That rationale correctly identifies the player scope of ordinary embargo
  cancellation. It does not account for the fact that OB/DP are team-level
  exceptions whose first member cancellation removes the relationship globally.

  No later substantive repair to that member-sum pattern was found in current
  Base AdvCiv 1.14; SAS inherits it. K-Mod/Civ4CE do not contain this later
  AdvCiv member-summed lower-bound design in the same form.

Cross-check against normal relationship valuation:
  CvTeamAI::AI_openBordersTradeVal(eTeam) returns:
      getNumCities() + target.getNumCities()

  CvTeamAI::AI_defensivePactTradeVal(eTeam) returns the same team quantity * 3.

  Both are naturally team-scoped and priced once for the relationship, which is
  consistent with the actual state lifetime and inconsistent with treating OB/DP
  as N independently cancelable player assets.

Why this is not merely a heuristic disagreement:
  AI_stopTradingTradeVal is heuristic, but F295 does not assert that its absolute
  OB/DP price is objectively correct or incorrect. The provable defect is the
  decomposition boundary used by AI_declareWarTradeVal:
    * the comment says member values are summed to model the losses of multiple
      player-scoped embargoes;
    * ordinary player deals are disjoint under that decomposition;
    * shared team agreements are not disjoint;
    * the code nevertheless evaluates their same pre-state contribution once in
      every member summand.

  Therefore the result changes with the number of players sharing the same team
  even when the team-level relationship being sacrificed is unchanged.

Gameplay consequence:
  The inflated sum is multiplied by 0.83 and used as a lower bound for
  AI_declareWarTradeVal. On multi-member hireling teams, especially with a
  Defensive Pact to the target, this can make a war bribe more expensive or
  unattainable because a shared relationship cost is counted repeatedly.

Repair boundary:
  Do not divide the whole embargo sum by team size. Player-owned resource/GPT
  losses really are additive and should still be summed per member.

  The robust decomposition is:
    1. Sum each member's player-owned cancelable ordinary-deal loss, using the
       exact-player scope required by F294.
    2. Evaluate shared team-level relationship loss (Open Borders / Defensive
       Pact and any analogous team agreement) once for the hireling team.
    3. Combine those once before applying the 0.83 embargo lower bound.

  Implementation could expose a flag/helper that suppresses shared OB/DP terms
  in per-player AI_stopTradingTradeVal calls, then add one team-level component;
  or separate AI_stopTradingTradeVal into player-deal and team-relationship
  components explicitly.

  Preserve:
    * normal one-player-team behavior;
    * ordinary direct TRADE_EMBARGO valuation, where one player's embargo really
      can terminate the shared relation and should still charge for doing so;
    * the member sum for genuinely separate player-owned trades;
    * UWAI/legacy base war valuation before the embargo lower bound.

Queue state after this checkpoint:
  queue 042 CvGameCoreDLL/CvDeal.cpp — still OPEN
  F281-F295 / provisional KI#604-KI#618 — confirmed
  F296 / provisional KI#619 — UNUSED / next

Remaining saturation cursor:
  * finish the old-CvDeal repair-stream ledger and verify that each substantive
    historical fix is either preserved, absorbed by F281-F295, or explicitly
    rejected as a control;
  * rerun the complete method/classification/accessor/serialization inventory
    against the final finding set so no family was skipped;
  * re-challenge the last cross-item state transitions only where one item can
    invalidate a sibling after whole-bundle prevalidation;
  * if no independent F296 survives, close queue 042 rather than inventing one.

No repository source files modified.

C025-WIP21 ADDENDUM — queue 042 CvDeal.cpp / annual-deal attitude-cache timing
F296 / provisional KI#619 confirmed; F297 unused
================================================================================

F296 / provisional KI#619
Title:
  Annual-deal rival-trade attitude refresh is deferred for only one deal
  direction; the other direction updates third-party attitude caches mid-loop,
  making later resentment depend on CvDeal orientation / deal iteration order.

Root:
  AdvCiv practical 3309 added a bUpdateAttitude switch specifically to defer
  annual-deal attitude-cache refreshes until CvGame::doDeals has processed all
  deals. The current CvDeal::doTurn applies that switch only to the SECOND trade
  direction:

      if (getLengthSecond() > 0)
      {
          ...
          GET_PLAYER(getFirstPlayer()).AI_processPeacetimeTradeValue(
                  getSecondPlayer(), iValue);
          // or AI_processPeacetimeGrantValue(..., iValue)
          // ^ default bUpdateAttitude == true
      }

      if (getLengthFirst() > 0)
      {
          ...
          GET_PLAYER(getSecondPlayer()).AI_processPeacetimeTradeValue(
                  getFirstPlayer(), iValue, false);
          // grant path also passes false explicitly
      }

  The comment immediately below says the intended opposite:
      "we do not update attitudes of particular players here,
       but instead update all of them at the game turn boundary
       [advc: i.e. in CvGame::doDeals]."

  CvGame::doDeals indeed does:
      verifyDeals();
      FOR_EACH_DEAL_VAR(pLoopDeal)
          pLoopDeal->doTurn();
      CvPlayerAI::AI_updateAttitudes();

  Therefore first-direction annual value processing is the lone premature cache
  refresh inside the deal loop.

Why default true actually updates third-party caches:
  AI_processPeacetimeTradeValue / GrantValue forwards bUpdateAttitude into
  AI_processPeacetimeValue.

  For each third-party team that resents the trade:
      kThirdParty.AI_changeEnemyPeacetimeTradeValue(
          TEAMID(eFromPlayer), ..., bUpdateAttitude);

  CvTeamAI::AI_setEnemyPeacetimeTradeValue then does:
      if (bUpdateAttitude)
          AI_updateAttitude(eIndex, false);

  CvTeamAI::AI_updateAttitude iterates the member players and recomputes their
  cached m_aiAttitude toward the affected team.

  The false parameter there suppresses worst-enemy recomputation only; it does
  NOT suppress the attitude-cache refresh itself.

Why a later annual deal can observe that premature refresh:
  CvPlayerAI::AI_processPeacetimeValue calculates each new rival-trade increment
  through:
      kThirdParty.AI_enemyTradeResentmentFactor(
          eTo, eFrom, ...);

  AI_enemyTradeResentmentFactor reads cached attitude values:
      AI_getAttitude(...)
      AI_getAttitudeVal(eFrom)
      AI_getAttitudeVal(AI_getWorstEnemy())

  and builds:
      iAttitudeDiff =
          AI_getAttitudeVal(eFrom)
        - ...
        - AI_getAttitudeVal(AI_getWorstEnemy())
        + ...
      r = iAttitudeDiff / 5
  (clamped to the documented bounds).

  Meanwhile AI_updateAttitude includes AI_getRivalTradeAttitude, and
  AI_getRivalTradeAttitude is directly derived from the just-changed
  EnemyPeacetimeTrade/Grant values. A sufficiently large increment, or any
  increment crossing an existing rounding threshold, can therefore change the
  cached integer attitude that the next resentment-factor calculation reads.

Clean supported two-deal reproducer:
  Let:
    E = an AI third party
    W = E's current worst-enemy team
    X = another civ/team

  Suppose there are two mature cancelable annual deals whose recurring value
  includes X giving something valuable to W. Multiple persistent deals between
  the same player pair are supported by CvGame's deal container; AdvCiv's
  AI_foldDeals only folds the narrow AI-AI opposite GPT-for-single-resource case,
  and human-involved/resource arrangements remain ordinary separate deals.

  Deal D1 is stored:
      firstPlayer  = W
      secondPlayer = X
  with X's annual item in secondList.

  D1::doTurn therefore executes the FIRST processing branch:
      W.AI_processPeacetime*(X, value)
  with default bUpdateAttitude=true.

  Because W is E's worst enemy, E can record RivalTrade resentment against X for
  trading with W. That increment immediately recomputes E's cached attitude
  toward X.

  Deal D2, processed later in FOR_EACH_DEAL order, again evaluates X trading
  with W. Its call to:
      E.AI_enemyTradeResentmentFactor(W, X, ...)
  now sees the post-D1 cached E->X attitude rather than the turn-boundary cache.
  Since the factor explicitly uses attitude(X) relative to attitude(worstEnemy),
  D1 can alter D2's resentment multiplier.

Orientation proof:
  Store the economically same X->W annual item with participants reversed:
      firstPlayer  = X
      secondPlayer = W
  and X's item in firstList.

  W receives exactly the same recurring value, but it is now processed by the
  SECOND CvDeal::doTurn branch:
      W.AI_processPeacetime*(X, value, false)

  No E->X cache refresh occurs until the global CvGame::doDeals update.
  Therefore a subsequent deal in the same deal loop can receive a different
  rival-trade multiplier solely from which endpoint happened to occupy
  CvDeal::firstPlayer.

  This is not theoretical undefined list ordering: CvGame::implementAndReturnDeal
  preserves the caller's eWho/eOtherWho identities directly as first/second
  players, so storage orientation is part of deal construction rather than a
  canonical ordering by player/team ID.

Magnitude / threshold note:
  AI attitude is integer-cached, while rival-trade value uses a nonlinear
  diminishing-return calculation and rounding. Not every small annual increment
  changes the cached integer attitude. F296 does not require every deal to show
  the effect; an existing RivalTrade value near an attitude rounding boundary,
  or a sufficiently valuable recurring increment, makes the feedback live.
  Once the cached value changes, AI_enemyTradeResentmentFactor uses it
  immediately before the intended global refresh point.

History:
  This is an AdvCiv practical-3309 regression/partial fix, commit:
      a8192ca7faab182fa7dfa589c097c83a23f07509
      "Fix timing of attitude cache update during turn sequence"

  Commit message:
      "Needs to happen after each player turn; after the team turn isn't enough.
       [advc.001]

       There were also some unnecessary updates, in part due to change
       [advc.130p] (I think)."

  The commit:
    * added bUpdateAttitude to AI_processPeacetimeTradeValue,
      AI_processPeacetimeGrantValue and downstream enemy-value setters;
    * changed CvGame::doDeals from updating only direct trade participants to a
      global all-major-civ attitude refresh after all CvDeal::doTurn calls;
    * explicitly passed false in CvDeal::doTurn's SECOND-direction trade/grant
      calls;
    * did NOT change the symmetric FIRST-direction calls, which therefore kept
      the new default=true;
    * updated the local comment to explicitly identify CvGame::doDeals as the
      deferred refresh point.

  Base AdvCiv 1.14 still has this exact one-sided false/default-true shape.
  SAS inherits it unchanged.
  K-Mod predates the bUpdateAttitude mechanism; its doTurn comment already said
  attitudes should be updated at the game-turn boundary, but its enemy-value
  setters updated caches immediately. Practical 3309 was AdvCiv's attempt to
  repair/refine that timing and left one half behind.
  Civ4CE follows the older BtS/K-Mod-style path and does not contain this
  partial AdvCiv switch in the same form.

Why this is independent of F293:
  F293 is lossy scalar representation of multiple brokered political targets
  during initial trade-value processing.
  F296 concerns recurring annual CvDeal::doTurn processing with no brokered
  peace/war target at all; its defect is one-sided cache-update timing.

Why this is independent of F282:
  F282 is cancellation-memory accumulation (setter vs additive changer).
  F296 modifies neither cancellation nor memory. It changes third-party cached
  attitude timing while annual trade/grant values continue to accumulate.

Repair boundary:
  Make the two annual directions symmetric and honor practical 3309's own stated
  game-turn-boundary contract:

      GET_PLAYER(getFirstPlayer()).AI_processPeacetimeTradeValue(
          getSecondPlayer(), iValue, false);

      GET_PLAYER(getFirstPlayer()).AI_processPeacetimeGrantValue(
          getSecondPlayer(), iValue, false);

  The already-correct second-direction calls remain false.

  Do NOT globally change the default bUpdateAttitude to false. Other callers
  intentionally process immediate events outside the CvGame::doDeals batch,
  including unit gifts and newly implemented diplomacy, and rely on the normal
  default update semantics.

  Keep CvGame::doDeals' final CvPlayerAI::AI_updateAttitudes() call; it is the
  synchronization point practical 3309 established precisely so all recurring
  deal-value changes are visible together after the batch.

F294 same-root extension — embargo denial also uses the wrong team scope
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

The final accessor-consumer sweep found a second live consumer of the same
player-vs-team embargo-scope invariant already established by F294.

CvPlayer::stopTradingWithTeam is explicitly player-scoped:
    if (!pLoopDeal->isBetween(getID(), eTeam))
        continue;

Only deals belonging to the particular player who enacts the embargo are
cancelled. This is also stated by the isTradingWithTeam source comment:
    "an embargo will affect only the enacting player - but the entire target
     team."

F294 already established that CvPlayerAI::AI_stopTradingTradeVal violates this
contract by selecting ordinary deals with:
    pLoopDeal->isBetween(TEAMID(ePlayer), eTradeTeam)

The denial path CvPlayerAI::AI_stopTradingTrade contains the same scope error
when trying to protect peace reparations:

    if (GET_TEAM(getTeam()).isForcePeace(eTradeTeam))
    {
        FOR_EACH_DEAL(d)
        {
            if (!d->isBetween(getTeam(), eTradeTeam))
                continue;
            ...
            FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(d->getGivesList(getTeam()))
            {
                if (type == TRADE_PEACE_TREATY)
                    bPeaceTreaty = true;
                if (type == TRADE_RESOURCES || type == TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN)
                    bAnnualPayment = true;
            }
            if (bPeaceTreaty && bAnnualPayment)
                return DENIAL_RECENT_CANCEL;
        }
    }

On a multi-member Team A, player A1 can therefore refuse an embargo against T
because teammate A2 has a reparations deal with T, even though
A1.stopTradingWithTeam(T) would not cancel A2's player-owned annual payment.

This does not warrant a new finding number:
  * the underlying invariant is identical to F294 — valuation/denial asks what
    one player loses by stopping trade, but searches the whole team;
  * exact-player scoping is the same repair boundary;
  * the previously established F285 list-orientation problem in reparations
    recognition is separate and still needs its own treaty-anywhere correction.

F294 repair review should therefore cover BOTH:
  1. AI_stopTradingTradeVal ordinary-deal inventory:
         isBetween(ePlayer, eTradeTeam)
     plus player-scoped getGivesList/getReceivesList/getOtherPlayer;
  2. AI_stopTradingTrade reparations-preservation scan:
         isBetween(getID(), eTradeTeam)
     and then recognize the peace marker anywhere in that exact player's deal
     while checking annual reparations actually given by getID() (F285 boundary).

Do not replace these with TEAMID/getTeam merely because the embargo target is a
team. Target scope is team-wide; enacting-owner scope is player-specific.

Final accessor / serialization / lifecycle controls
----------------------------------------------------

The small-method surface has now been rerun against the full queue-042 finding
map rather than merely assumed safe.

* CvDeal::write / read:
  ID, initial turn, first player, second player, first list and second list are
  serialized/deserialized in matching order. No missing current member.

* reset / uninit:
  both trade lists are cleared and all serialized scalar members reset. There is
  no extra owned heap state in CvDeal.

* getOtherPlayer(PlayerTypes), getGivesList(PlayerTypes),
  getReceivesList(PlayerTypes):
  exact-player assertions are intentional and useful. The F294 violation is in
  a caller that admits teammate deals before invoking these accessors.

* getGivesList(TeamTypes), getReceivesList(TeamTypes):
  deliberately require exactly one endpoint to belong to the queried team.
  Current live team-typed consumers were enumerated:
    - CvPlayerAI embargo valuation / denial: F294 family;
    - CvTeam::freeVassal: team distinction is valid before the vassal proxy is
      killed;
    - CvDeal::isUncancelableVassalDeal: explicitly returns before the accessor
      when both endpoints have become the same team.
  No additional independent same-team consumer survived beyond F290/F294.

* isDisengage:
  its first-list-only item check is safe for the real representation.
  Disengagement is created through startTeamTrade(..., bDual=true), so each
  proxy contains one TRADE_DISENGAGE item in both lists. The item also lies
  beyond NUM_TRADEABLE_ITEMS and is not an ordinary voluntary trade-table
  choice.

* isVassalTributeDeal(CLinkList*):
  returns true for an empty list vacuously, but meaningful callers additionally
  require the opposite/value conditions that make an empty persistent deal
  irrelevant. CvGame::implementAndReturnDeal immediately kills a newly-created
  CvDeal whose two saved lists are both empty.

* CvDeal::doTurn empty-list head access:
  for a persistent deal both lists cannot be empty under the normal creation /
  deletion lifecycle. The apparently unsafe getFirstList().head() expression is
  therefore protected by representation plus short-circuiting for one-sided
  deals. No live null-head root established.

* isAllDual / isAnnual / isDual / hasData / isEndWar:
  every current TradeableItems family has been reconciled. PA's "annual"
  classification does not create a recurring PA deal because the PA item itself
  is not saved; the classification is used by generic trade/UI/value machinery.
  No independent state-lifetime defect established there.

Representation-debt siblings absorbed by existing findings
-----------------------------------------------------------

Several final first-list-only observations are real asymmetries but not new
roots:

1. CvDeal::kill determines "forced" cancellation sound/visibility by looking for
   dual items only in getFirstList(). Normally this is sufficient because OB,
   DP and disengagement proxies are dual. A legitimate one-sided
   TRADE_PEACE_TREATY in the second list is the exception and can therefore miss
   the dual-item bForce path. This is a diagnostic/UI sibling of F281's
   one-sided peace-treaty representation, not a new gameplay root.

2. CvTeam::setVassal still contains first-list peace-treaty cleanup inherited
   from the same representation assumption. This belongs in the F281/F283
   repair review; fixing only CvDeal::isPeaceDeal or resetDualDeal would leave
   another consumer of the outdated "peace marker lives in first list" model.

3. Other first-list-only checks for OB/DP/disengagement remain safe because
   startTeamTrade creates those proxy items symmetrically or in a fixed
   orientation known to the consumer.

Rejected transaction candidate — Open Borders + Disengagement
--------------------------------------------------------------

A synthetic bundle containing TRADE_OPEN_BORDERS and TRADE_DISENGAGE would be
order-sensitive: setOpenBorders(true) cancels disengagement, then a later
TRADE_DISENGAGE start could restore the disengage flag without rechecking OB.

This is not a normal accepted trade state:
  * TRADE_DISENGAGE is declared after NUM_TRADEABLE_ITEMS;
  * ordinary trade-table iteration does not offer it;
  * its live producer is CvTeam::makePeace -> signDisengage ->
    startTeamTrade(TRADE_DISENGAGE, ..., true);
  * capitulation suppresses the disengagement producer;
  * while the negotiating teams are still at war, OB/DP cannot independently
    prevalidate.

No F297.

Rejected transaction candidate — brokered peace with master + vassal
--------------------------------------------------------------------

Raw TRADE_PEACE inventory construction iterates third teams and can enumerate a
vassal at the game-rule level, so a master+vassal pair initially looked capable
of being redundantly priced: CvTeam::makePeace(master) cascades peace to the
master's vassals.

The AI denial contract closes the producer:
    CvTeamAI::AI_makePeaceTrade:
        if (GET_TEAM(ePeaceTeam).isAVassal())
            return DENIAL_VASSAL;

TRADE_PEACE itself is only offered by nonhuman givers
(CvPlayer::canPossiblyTradeItem returns false when the giving team is human).
AI_considerOffer applies getTradeDenial to every item the AI gives.

Therefore an accepted ordinary deal cannot contain the redundant
TRADE_PEACE(master) + TRADE_PEACE(vassal) pair. No F297.

Tech / resource / civic / religion transaction controls retained
-----------------------------------------------------------------

* Tech + resource self-obsolescence:
  resource prevalidation checks bonus obsolescence for BOTH giver and recipient;
  if one side already owns the obsoleting tech needed for the cross-item
  scenario, the resource item is rejected before implementation.

* Tech that newly enables another item:
  whole-bundle prevalidation occurs before the tech is transferred, so the
  newly-enabled civic/tech/etc. item fails conservatively rather than being
  accepted and then invalidated.

* Same-column multiple civics and duplicate religions:
  AI_checkCivicReligionConsistency explicitly rejects these accepted-offer
  states.

* Different civic columns:
  deliberately supported and therefore remain the exact F291 case.

* Multiple GOLD / GPT instances:
  normal trade-table representation exposes one editable item of each kind
  rather than an arbitrary duplicated-item producer. No independent normal
  duplicate-obligation root established.

Remaining single candidate before closure
-----------------------------------------

The only transaction candidate still under active challenge is multiple
TRADE_WAR items under the supported legacy/K-Mod-war-AI configuration where
UWAI is disabled.

Full UWAI explicitly makes a second hired war unaffordable:
    "Can't be hired for more than one war at a time"
    iWars > 1 -> +1,000,000 value.

When UWAI is disabled, legacy valuation can accept multiple war items. If two
targets have a Defensive Pact, the first primary hired declaration can cause the
second target to enter the war through the DP cascade before its own prevalidated
TRADE_WAR executes. The second CvTeam::declareWar then returns because the teams
are already at war, while surrounding sponsorship-memory code still runs.

This is suspicious but not yet promoted:
  * the sponsor explicitly requested both war states;
  * both requested final war relationships do exist;
  * it remains to prove that the second item is semantically supposed to buy a
    distinct primary declaration rather than merely guarantee the war state;
  * full UWAI intentionally prohibits the multi-war bundle, narrowing exposure
    to the supported legacy/K-Mod-war-AI mode.

F297 remains UNUSED pending that last contract check.

C025-WIP23 ADDENDUM — queue 042 CvDeal.cpp / legacy multi-war bundle

F297 / provisional KI#620
Title:
  With UWAI disabled, a multi-TRADE_WAR bundle can charge separately for a
  Defensive-Pact ally whose entry into the war is already priced and triggered
  by the first hired declaration.

Supported configuration / producer:
  AdvCiv deliberately supports two war/peace AI modes.

  Current XML documents:
    * normal/default UWAI;
    * K-Mod war/peace AI when "Aggressive AI (K-Mod)" is selected;
    * USE_KMOD_AI_NONAGGRESSIVE / DISABLE_UWAI as additional supported switches.

  TRADE_WAR inventory construction creates one item for each eligible third
  team when the giver is AI. A human sponsor can therefore place more than one
  war item from the same AI hireling onto the diplomacy table.

  AI_considerOffer checks getTradeDenial independently for every item against
  the unchanged pre-deal world state.

  In the legacy/K-Mod branch, AI_declareWarTrade refuses a hired war when:
      getNumWars() > 0
  but if the hireling is initially at peace, two different TRADE_WAR items in
  the same proposed list each see getNumWars()==0 and can each pass.

  Full UWAI has an additional bundle-level policy in AI_dealVal:
      // "Can't be hired for more than one war at a time"
      iWars++;
      if (iWars > 1)
          iValue += 1000000;
  Crucially, that guard is inside:
      if (getUWAI().isEnabled())
  so the supported legacy/K-Mod-war-AI mode has no equivalent multi-item guard.

Concrete Defensive-Pact trigger:
  Let:
    H = human sponsor;
    B = AI hireling, currently at peace with everyone relevant and using the
        legacy/K-Mod war AI (UWAI disabled);
    A and D = two independent teams with an active Defensive Pact.

  Assume B is individually willing and able to declare war on both A and D and
  H can afford the quoted bundle.

  H asks B for:
      TRADE_WAR(A)
      TRADE_WAR(D)

  Both items can pass getTradeDenial before the deal because B still has zero
  current wars and canDeclareWar each target.

Why the price is provably overlapping rather than merely "two requested wars":
  CvTeamAI::AI_declareWarTradeValLegacy(A,H) explicitly prices the consequences
  of A's Defensive Pacts.

  When A currently has no wars, the function:
      iValue *= 2;
      for each eligible kDPTeam:
          if master(DPTeam).isDefensivePact(master(A)):
              iValue += DPTeam.numCities * 30;
              iValue += DPTeam.totalPopulation * 20;

  Thus the price of the FIRST item, TRADE_WAR(A), already charges B for D being
  pulled into the conflict through A's Defensive Pact.

  AI_dealVal then encounters TRADE_WAR(D) and adds a second full:
      AI_declareWarTradeValLegacy(D,H)

  D's own valuation can analogously include A as its Defensive-Pact ally.
  The same coalition-war consequence is therefore priced again.

Execution confirms that the second primary declaration is redundant:
  CvDeal::startTrade(TRADE_WAR(A)):
      B.declareWar(A, ..., sponsor=H)

  CvTeam::declareWar(A) triggers A's Defensive Pacts. D queues and executes a
  declaration of war against B through WAR_DECLARATION_DEFENSIVE_PACT.

  By the time CvDeal reaches TRADE_WAR(D), B and D are already at war.

  CvDeal still calls:
      B.declareWar(D, ..., sponsor=H)

  but CvTeam::declareWar begins with:
      if (isAtWar(eTarget))
          return;

  Hence the second purchased "declare war on D" does not perform a second
  primary sponsored declaration at all. Its war state already exists because
  the first purchased declaration caused the DP cascade.

Surrounding bookkeeping makes the mismatch visible:
  Although CvTeam::declareWar(D) returns immediately, CvDeal::startTrade
  continues after that call:
    * bPeaceTreatyImplied is set;
    * every member of D receives MEMORY_HIRED_WAR_ALLY against H;
    * DECLARED_WAR_RECENT helper memories may also be updated.

  The actual B<->D war, however, was created by D's Defensive-Pact declaration,
  with the DP cascade's war cause and no primary sponsored B->D declaration.
  Thus transaction bookkeeping can describe H as having hired a declaration
  that the declaration function itself never executed.

Why the final symmetric "at war" relation does not make the price correct:
  If one TRADE_WAR(A) already:
    1. creates B<->A war,
    2. causes the A-D Defensive Pact to create B<->D war, and
    3. explicitly charges extra in AI_declareWarTradeValLegacy(A,H) for D's
       expected DP participation,

  then adding TRADE_WAR(D) cannot legitimately charge the same DP consequence a
  second time merely because the final relation is symmetric.

  The legacy price function itself is the source contract that resolves the
  ambiguity: DP allies are included in the price of the primary target.

Ancestry:
  This is inherited from BtS/K-Mod legacy diplomacy and exposed by AdvCiv's
  dual-AI-mode architecture.

  Civ4CE/BtS:
    * AI_dealVal sums every TRADE_WAR separately;
    * AI_declareWarTradeVal adds cities/population of Defensive-Pact allies;
    * AI_declareWarTrade tests current/predeal war-plan state item-by-item.
    No bundle-level multi-war normalization.

  K-Mod:
    * retains per-item TRADE_WAR valuation;
    * its legacy war-trade value explicitly includes Defensive-Pact allies;
    * its denial refuses when already at war, but independent predeal item
      checks do not mutate state.

  AdvCiv practical/WPAI/UWAI work added the explicit policy:
      "Can't be hired for more than one war at a time"
  as early as the initial AdvCiv/UWAI integration (advc.104o), but deliberately
  gates the million-point second-war rejection on UWAI being enabled.

  Current Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS retain that conditional guard unchanged.
  Thus default UWAI avoids the accepted bundle, while the supported legacy mode
  still exposes the inherited transaction/valuation mismatch.

Relationship to F293:
  F293 concerns multiple brokered political targets losing all but the last
  target in rival-trade ATTITUDE metadata.

  F297 does not depend on that metadata. Even if F293 is repaired with a full
  target set, legacy AI_dealVal still charges overlapping war consequences and
  execution still finds the second target already at war.

Relationship to F289:
  F289 is a game-rule/relationship validation hole for a single brokered war
  involving the sponsor's master locus.

  F297 uses two individually valid independent targets and a Defensive Pact.
  The defect is cross-item consequence overlap after whole-bundle prevalidation.

Relationship to F292:
  Both are transaction-level "individually valid before implementation" bugs,
  but the invalidated invariant differs:
    * F292: a city transfer removes physical resource supply required by a
      persistent sibling resource item;
    * F297: the first hired war creates the second requested war as a DP cascade
      while its valuation already includes that cascade, making the second
      priced primary declaration redundant.

Repair boundary:
  The narrowest repair is to apply AdvCiv's already-stated policy
      "Can't be hired for more than one war at a time"
  regardless of whether UWAI is enabled.

  Concretely, the AI_dealVal iWars guard can be made unconditional (or an
  equivalent bundle-consistency denial can reject the second TRADE_WAR) while
  leaving the choice of legacy vs UWAI single-war pricing intact.

  This preserves:
    * all current one-war legacy/K-Mod trade valuation;
    * all current full-UWAI behavior;
    * the existing explicit design policy rather than inventing a new rule.

  If multiple hired wars are intentionally desired in the future, a larger
  repair is required:
    * compute the closure/union of vassal and Defensive-Pact war consequences
      for the whole bundle;
    * price each resulting war consequence once;
    * distinguish primary sponsored declarations from alliance/cascade wars;
    * execute/report sponsorship consistently with that staged result.

  Merely revalidating the second item after executing the first is insufficient
  for AI fairness because the sponsor has already been accepted at a price that
  included both independently computed items.

Severity:
  Moderate, configuration-gated.
  Default UWAI avoids accepted multi-war bundles through the million-point
  guard. The bug remains live in the explicitly supported legacy/K-Mod war AI
  configuration and can overprice a human war bribe while recording sponsorship
  semantics inconsistent with the declaration path.

C025-WIP24 ADDENDUM — queue 042 CvDeal.cpp / incompatible team-status bundle
F298 / provisional KI#621 confirmed; F299 unused
================================================================================

F298 / provisional KI#621
Title:
  A voluntary-vassal + Defensive-Pact bundle can be accepted and valued while
  both teams are free, but the mandatory vassal-last execution immediately
  destroys the just-signed Defensive Pact and records cancellation effects.

Root:
  Bundle legality is checked item-by-item against the unchanged pre-deal state.
  TRADE_VASSAL and TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT are individually legal between two free,
  peaceful teams, but they are mutually incompatible final states.

  CvDeal then deliberately executes vassal/surrender items in a second pass.
  Therefore a bundled Defensive Pact is signed first and the voluntary-vassal
  transition is applied afterward. CvTeam::setVassal explicitly cancels every
  Defensive-Pact deal involving the new vassal.

  The accepted transaction thus contains an item whose own later sibling is
  guaranteed to undo it before addTradeItems finishes.

Reachable trade-table state:
  CvPlayer::buildTradeTable exposes TRADE_VASSAL and TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT as
  ordinary basic trade items when their individual canTradeItem checks pass.

  Pre-deal:
    * TRADE_VASSAL is possible at peace when neither side is already a vassal
      and the prospective master has vassal-state trading.
    * TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT is possible when both teams are free (not vassals),
      at peace, satisfy the DP trading/war-state rules and can sign a pact.

  CvPlayer::updateTradeList contains no vassal-vs-DP incompatibility rule.

  Its vassal special cases hide:
    * another vassal/surrender item from the opposite side; and
    * an end-war item while the negotiating teams are at war.

  They do not hide TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT.

  The generic peacetime mixing filter also does not help:
    CvDeal::isAnnual(TRADE_VASSAL)          == true
    CvDeal::isAnnual(TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT) == true

  so both remain in the same annual class.

  Human-human diplomacy is the strongest unconditional producer because
  updateTradeList explicitly says:
      "everything allowed in human-human trades"

  The state is not limited to human-human games. An AI can also individually
  return NO_DENIAL for a voluntary-vassal relation and for a Defensive Pact
  (e.g. sufficiently favorable relationship with Open Borders and compatible
  war state), so human-AI negotiation has no backend bundle-consistency rule
  that would make the pair intrinsically impossible.

Whole-bundle prevalidation:
  CvDeal::addTradeItems first checks every item with canTradeItem before mutating
  anything.

  At that moment both teams are still free, so:
    canTradeItem(TRADE_VASSAL)          can pass;
    canTradeItem(TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT) can pass.

  No second validation is performed after another item changes team status.

Deterministic current execution:
  AdvCiv replaced K-Mod's list-reordering approach with explicit two-pass
  execution:

      for (int iPass = 0; iPass < 2; iPass++)
      {
          ...
          if (isVassal(pItem->m_eItemType) == (iPass == 0))
              continue;
          startTrade(...);
      }

  Consequently all non-vassal items run in pass 0 and vassal/surrender items in
  pass 1 regardless of list insertion order.

  For a same-direction bundle:
      TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT
      TRADE_VASSAL

  pass 0:
    CvDeal::startTrade(TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT)
      -> startTeamTrade(..., bDual=true)
      -> creates persistent DP proxy deal(s)
      -> setDefensivePact(otherTeam, true)

  pass 1:
    CvDeal::startTrade(TRADE_VASSAL)
      -> startTeamTrade(TRADE_VASSAL,...)
      -> setVassal(master, true, false)

  CvTeam::setVassal, once the new vassal state is current, iterates live deals
  involving the vassal and explicitly kills any first-list item equal to:
      TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT
      TRADE_PEACE_TREATY

  DP proxies are dual, so the first-list test finds the just-created pact.

  kill -> CvDeal::endTrade(TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT):
      setDefensivePact(master,false);
      endTeamTrade(...) removes sibling proxies.

  Final state of the accepted bundle:
      vassal relation = present
      Defensive Pact  = absent

  The pact that was just agreed to does not survive the implementation of the
  very deal that contained it.

Immediate cancellation side effects:
  This is not merely a display inconsistency.

  DP teardown occurs while both players remain alive. endTrade therefore calls
  addEndTradeMemory for the Defensive Pact. With no explicit canceling player,
  the cancellation-memory path can record
      MEMORY_CANCELLED_DEFENSIVE_PACT
  between the newly-created master/vassal participants.

  Thus a single accepted transaction can:
    1. sign a Defensive Pact;
    2. immediately cancel it because vassalage was also accepted; and
    3. leave diplomatic cancellation memory for that synthetic cancellation.

  Depending on UI/notification circumstances, the separate DP proxy teardown can
  also produce normal cancellation handling even though no player subsequently
  chose to break the pact.

AI valuation consequence:
  AI_considerOffer / AI_dealVal prices the proposed item list before execution
  with bIgnoreAnnual=false.

  AI_dealVal has independent cases:
      TRADE_VASSAL:
          iValue += AI_vassalTradeVal(...)
      TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT:
          iValue += AI_defensivePactTradeVal(...)

  There is no bundle-level "DP will disappear after vassalization" adjustment.

  Therefore, in an AI-involved proposal that otherwise clears the individual
  denials, the Defensive Pact can affect whether the bundle is considered fair
  even though implementation guarantees that it will not exist afterward.
  A human can be asked to compensate for a benefit the accepted transaction
  immediately removes, or the AI can count a DP benefit on the receiving side
  that likewise never survives.

  F298 does not rely on finding one exact leader/power configuration where both
  AI denials happen to clear; the human-human producer alone establishes the
  accepted-invalid transaction. The AI valuation path establishes the additional
  consequence when such an AI combination is individually acceptable.

Ancestry:
  The underlying incompatibility is inherited from BtS/K-Mod diplomacy:
    * the trade table permits vassal and DP items independently;
    * vassal establishment cancels Defensive Pacts;
    * there is no whole-bundle vassal-vs-DP exclusion.

  BtS/Civ4CE executes ordinary items in list order, so the final malformed result
  can depend on whether vassal or DP happens to execute first:
    * DP then vassal -> pact is canceled;
    * vassal then DP -> startTrade can sign a pact after the vassal transition
      because the item is not revalidated.

  K-Mod deliberately changed deal implementation so vassal items are moved to
  the end ("Vassal deals need to be implemented last, so that master/vassal
  power is set correctly"). Its second-list movement code had a copy/paste
  issue; AdvCiv replaced the approach with the current two-pass execution.

  In current Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS the result is therefore deterministic:
  non-vassal DP first, vassal last, immediate DP cancellation.

Why this is independent of F288:
  F288 is the distinct Permanent-Alliance + vassal combination:
    * PA execution is deferred until after the vassal pass;
    * merging the teams can turn the surviving team into its own vassal;
    * final persistent team state is corrupted (`m_eMaster == getID()`).

  F298 requires no Permanent Alliance and creates no self-vassal.
  It instead accepts a DP whose final state is guaranteed to be absent and
  triggers cancellation side effects.

  Rejecting only PA+vassal (the narrow F288 repair) leaves F298 untouched.
  Rejecting only vassal+DP leaves F288 untouched.

Why this is independent of F282:
  F282 concerns whether cancellation-memory changes are additive vs absolute.
  Even if F282 is repaired perfectly, F298 still performs an artificial DP
  cancellation and writes whatever correctly-implemented cancellation memory
  policy endTrade specifies.

Why this is independent of F292:
  Both involve whole-bundle prevalidation followed by cross-item mutation, but
  the violated contracts are different:
    * F292: city ownership removes physical resource supply required by an
      annual resource obligation;
    * F298: vassal team status is structurally incompatible with a DP that the
      same bundle has just established.

Repair boundary:
  The safest narrow rule is to reject mutually incompatible team-status items in
  the same negotiated bundle before any item is committed.

  For current F298:
    * TRADE_VASSAL (peacetime voluntary vassal) and
      TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT between the negotiating teams must not coexist in one
      accepted bundle.

  Apply the rule in backend bundle validation, not only in updateTradeList, so
  script/EXE/direct callers cannot bypass it.

  The UI should also hide the counterpart for clarity:
    * once a vassal item is offered, hide DP;
    * once DP is offered, hide vassal.

  Preserve:
    * ordinary single voluntary-vassal deals;
    * ordinary single Defensive Pacts;
    * the deliberate vassal-last execution required for power/war alignment;
    * capitulation handling (TRADE_SURRENDER occurs during war, where DP cannot
      independently prevalidate anyway).

  Do not merely suppress DP cancellation inside CvTeam::setVassal. A master and
  its vassal are not supposed to retain an ordinary Defensive Pact; the error is
  accepting the incompatible bundle, not the cleanup that enforces the final
  vassal invariant.

Queue state after this checkpoint:
  queue 042 CvGameCoreDLL/CvDeal.cpp — still OPEN
  F281-F298 / provisional KI#604-KI#621 — confirmed
  F299 / provisional KI#622 — UNUSED / next

Final saturation cursor:
  * rerun the remaining vassal-status pairings (OB, treaty, disengage, PA) only
    for independent final-state contradictions:
      - PA already F288;
      - peace/list lifetime already F281/F283/F287 family;
      - disengage is not voluntarily tradeable;
      - OB is not canceled by setVassal and needs separate proof before any
        claim;
  * finish F281-F298 root-independence / repair-boundary review;
  * complete the remaining historical/refactor entries that changed CvDeal only
    mechanically or diagnostically;
  * if no independent F299 survives, close queue 042 and advance to queue 047
    rather than continuing to mine a saturated file.

C025-WIP25 ADDENDUM — queue 042 CvDeal.cpp
F298 strengthened: dual-DP orientation can leave a one-way pact bit with no backing deal
F299 remains unused
================================================================================

F298 SAME-ROOT REFINEMENT
-------------------------
WIP24 proved the basic accepted-invalid transaction:

    voluntary vassal + Defensive Pact

Both items can pass whole-bundle prevalidation while the teams are still free.
The DP is incompatible with the final vassal state, and CvTeam::setVassal removes
Defensive Pact deals when the vassal relation is established.

The final sequencing is more dangerous than WIP24's simplified "all non-vassal
items, then all vassal items" summary, because current AdvCiv/SAS does NOT stage
the two outer offer lists globally.

Actual CvDeal::addTradeItems order:
    firstList pass 0  — all non-vassal items
    firstList pass 1  — all vassal/surrender items
    secondList pass 0 — all non-vassal items
    secondList pass 1 — all vassal/surrender items

This matters for dual team agreements.

NORMAL DEFENSIVE-PACT REPRESENTATION REALLY IS DUAL
----------------------------------------------------
TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT is classified by CvDeal::isDual.

More importantly, DLL-owned normal producers physically put the item into BOTH
outer offer lists.

CvTeam::signDefensivePact:

    TradeData item(TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT);
    ...
    ourList.insertAtEnd(item);
    theirList.insertAtEnd(item);
    GC.getGame().implementDeal(..., ourList, theirList, ...);

CvPlayerAI::AI_doDiplo does the same for an AI Defensive-Pact proposal:

    TradeData item(TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT);
    ...
    weGive.insertAtEnd(item);
    theyGive.insertAtEnd(item);

and then either opens the diplomacy screen with those two lists or directly
implements them.

CvDeal::doTurn also explicitly documents that in multiplayer, "dual deals can be
mixed with e.g. gold per turn"; current trade-table filtering says
"everything allowed in human-human trades."

Thus two-sided outer-list representation is not merely a theoretical meaning of
the enum flag. It is the normal contract used by the DLL's own DP constructors.
The exact EXE mechanics for every human-edited mixed proposal remain opaque, so
the stronger branch below is not needed to establish F298; it is an additional
normal-representation consequence when the accepted bundle contains the usual
dual DP pair.

DANGEROUS ORIENTATION
---------------------
Let:
    A = first player/team, offering voluntary vassalage to B
    B = second player/team

Accepted outer bundle:
    firstList:
        TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT
        TRADE_VASSAL
    secondList:
        TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT

All three items pass the initial canTradeItem checks while A and B are still
separate free teams.

Current execution:

1. firstList pass 0 — first TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT
   startTrade calls:
       startTeamTrade(DP, A, B, true);
       A.setDefensivePact(B, true);

   startTeamTrade creates the ordinary persistent dual DP proxy CvDeal(s) with
   m_iData=1 saved on both sides.

2. firstList pass 1 — TRADE_VASSAL
   A.setVassal(B, true, false).

   CvTeam::setVassal scans live deals involving the new vassal and kills
   TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT proxies.

   CvDeal::killSilent processes BOTH saved proxy lists:
       A.setDefensivePact(B, false);
       B.setDefensivePact(A, false);

   So the pact is fully cleared at this point.

3. secondList pass 0 — second TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT
   This outer item was prevalidated BEFORE vassalization and is not revalidated
   here.

   startTrade sees no current DP flag, so it attempts:
       startTeamTrade(DP, B, A, true);

NESTED PROXY CREATION IS CORRECTLY REJECTED — BUT THE FLAG SET IS NOT
----------------------------------------------------------------------
startTeamTrade creates its proxy through a fresh:

    CvGame::implementDeal(...)

with bForce=false.

That nested CvDeal::addTradeItems therefore re-runs canTradeItem NOW, after A has
become B's vassal.

CvPlayer::canPossiblyTradeItem(TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT) requires:
    !ourTeam.isAVassal()
    !toTeam.isAVassal()

so the nested persistent DP proxy is rejected. implementAndReturnDeal sees both
saved lists empty, kills the empty deal and returns NULL.

However CvDeal::startTrade ignores whether startTeamTrade actually succeeded and
immediately executes:

    GET_TEAM(eFromPlayer).setDefensivePact(kToPlayer.getTeam(), true);

There is no return status from startTeamTrade and no post-state legality check.

CvTeam::setDefensivePact itself only asserts that the two team IDs differ; it
does NOT prohibit master/vassal status.

Therefore the final state can be:

    A.isVassal(B)             == true
    A.isDefensivePact(B)      == false
    B.isDefensivePact(A)      == true
    backing DP CvDeal/proxy   == NONE

This is stronger than "the pact is immediately canceled":
- the symmetric team relation becomes one-way;
- the surviving true bit has no CvDeal lifetime owner;
- normal deal cancellation / turnsToCancel / scoreboard-deal lookup cannot own
  or expire it;
- it exists despite the exact post-vassal canTradeItem check having rejected the
  corresponding persistent agreement.

The mirror orientation can instead end with the DP removed. Thus one logical
mixed vassal+dual-DP transaction can have orientation-sensitive final state.

WHY THIS REMAINS F298, NOT F299
-------------------------------
The root is unchanged:
    the bundle accepts a DP and a vassal transition whose final states are
    incompatible, then mutates them sequentially without a bundle-level
    consistency contract.

The one-way no-proxy DP is a stronger consequence of that same incompatibility
plus current per-list vassal-last sequencing. A backend rule that forbids
TRADE_VASSAL + TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT in one accepted bundle prevents BOTH the
WIP24 immediate-cancel branch and this WIP25 asymmetric-bit branch.

Do not allocate a separate finding merely because the same invalid bundle has a
second execution orientation.

REPAIR-BOUNDARY REFINEMENT
--------------------------
F298 should be repaired before startTrade mutates either relation.

Required backend invariant:
    an accepted transaction between two teams must not contain voluntary
    TRADE_VASSAL and TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT as coexisting requested final states.

UI hiding is useful but not sufficient.

Do NOT repair only by:
- changing the list pass order;
- making vassal items globally last;
- suppressing CvTeam::setVassal's DP cancellation;
- making startTeamTrade forced;
- or teaching setDefensivePact to silently accept the incompatible relation.

A defensive secondary improvement would also be reasonable:
    startTeamTrade could return success/failure and startTrade should not mutate
    the team-level flag when proxy creation was rejected.

That would prevent this particular orphan one-way bit under other future
mid-transaction invalidations, but it would NOT make vassal+DP a coherent
bundle. The primary repair remains bundle incompatibility rejection.

ANCESTRY
--------
Current Base AdvCiv 1.14 has the same:
- first-list two-pass loop followed by second-list two-pass loop;
- DP startTeamTrade followed by unconditional setDefensivePact(true);
- vassal cleanup of DP proxy deals.

So this stronger F298 consequence is inherited by SAS from current AdvCiv.

K-Mod's older "move vassal to end" implementation is different and even contains
the second-list copy/paste defect that AdvCiv comments on; Civ4CE/BtS use older
item-order behavior. The exact one-way/no-proxy sequence above is therefore most
directly a current AdvCiv/SAS execution-shape consequence, while the underlying
vassal+DP incompatibility is older.

OTHER VASSAL-STATUS PAIRING CONTROL — OPEN BORDERS
---------------------------------------------------
Vassal + Open Borders initially looks analogous but is NOT interchangeable with
F298.

CvTeam::setVassal does not cancel Open Borders, and Open Borders can still have
a distinct economic role after vassalization:
    CvTeam::isFreeTrade = isOpenBorders || global free-trade option.

AdvCiv explicitly removed/commented older unconditional vassal shortcuts from
trade-route eligibility; peaceful territorial entry and international trade
routes are not the same contract.

Therefore a master/vassal Open-Borders agreement is not proven to be an
impossible final state merely because movement access is partly implied by
vassalage. No F299 from the OB pairing.

Queue state:
  queue 042 CvGameCoreDLL/CvDeal.cpp — OPEN
  F281-F298 / provisional KI#604-KI#621 — confirmed
  F299 / provisional KI#622 — UNUSED / next

  * complete F281-F298 independence/root-merging and repair-interaction review;
  * finish the remaining no-finding vassal/treaty/disengage and team-proxy
    controls;
  * inspect remaining current CvDeal assertions/TODOs/history entries one final
    time against the completed map;
  * if no independent F299 survives, close queue 042 at 25/169 and move to the
    next reconciled priority queue.

QUEUE 042 — CvGameCoreDLL/CvDeal.cpp
STATUS: FIRST-PASS COMPLETE

CONFIRMED ROOTS
---------------
F281 / provisional KI#604
  isPeaceDeal scans only the first saved list. A legitimate one-sided peace
  treaty in the second list is not recognized as a peace deal, breaking expiry
  and related logical-treaty behavior.

F282 / provisional KI#605
  addEndTradeMemory uses absolute AI_setMemoryCount where the surrounding
  cancellation design requires additive accumulation; repeated/weighted
  cancellation memory is collapsed or overwritten.

F283 / provisional KI#606
  resetDualDeal renewal is player-pair / first-list scoped instead of logical
  team-agreement scoped, so one proxy can be prolonged while sibling proxies
  retain different ages; one-sided peace representation is also missed.

F284 / provisional KI#607
  death of one player on a still-alive multi-member team can destroy a
  player-pair proxy and thereby tear down the whole surviving team's OB/DP/
  disengagement agreement.

F285 / provisional KI#608
  reparations-aware embargo denial checks the wrong list/orientation for the
  peace marker and can approve an embargo that would cancel protected
  reparations.

F286 / provisional KI#609
  addTradeItems can be synchronously re-entered through team/state transitions
  that delete the currently executing CvDeal, after which the caller continues
  through a freed object. Confirmed trigger families include mixed PA/state
  mutations; relation bugs such as F289 can expand the trigger surface.

F287 / provisional KI#610
  failure of one annual component in verify kills the entire mixed persistent
  deal, including a still-mandatory peace treaty. Resource/GPT failure can
  therefore terminate protected peace early.

F288 / provisional KI#611
  a supported Permanent-Alliance + voluntary-vassal bundle can merge team
  identity after vassal establishment and leave the surviving team as its own
  vassal.

F289 / provisional KI#612
  brokered-war validity is not checked against the sponsor's canonical master
  coalition. A voluntary vassal can hire war against its own master, or against
  a coalition whose Defensive Pact necessarily pulls its master/sponsor into
  war with the hireling.

F290 / provisional KI#613
  Permanent-Alliance cleanup cancels old team-proxy agreements only after
  participant team reassignment; generic endTrade therefore reconstructs the
  wrong old team identity. A valid pre-PA Defensive Pact reaches
  setDefensivePact(self,false), tripping the AdvCiv/SAS self-team assertion and
  polluting same-team teardown state.

F291 / provisional KI#614
  multiple TRADE_CIVIC items from different civic columns are executed as
  separate forced revolutions instead of one CivicMap revolution. Fixed/city
  anarchy overhead is charged repeatedly and the revolution timer is overwritten
  per item.

F292 / provisional KI#615
  a city + resource bundle can pass whole-bundle prevalidation while the city
  still supplies the giver's last copy, then the city transfer removes that
  supply before/under the resource obligation. The annual promise becomes
  invalid while the one-shot city transfer cannot be rolled back.

F293 / provisional KI#616
  brokered peace/war rival-trade bookkeeping stores only one scalar
  ePeaceTradeTarget/eWarTradeTarget. Multi-target political bundles therefore
  discard all but the last target and make third-party resentment depend on
  item order.

F294 / provisional KI#617
  embargo valuation and reparations-preservation denial use team-wide ordinary
  deal scans even though an embargo cancels only the enacting player's deals.
  Multi-member teams can therefore price/refuse based on teammate-owned trades;
  the valuation path also violates exact-player CvDeal accessor contracts.

F295 / provisional KI#618
  the war-bribe embargo lower bound sums one embargo value per team member, but
  every member summand also contains the same shared team-level Open Borders /
  Defensive Pact loss. The first real embargo tears that shared relation down,
  so the relationship cost is counted repeatedly.

F296 / provisional KI#619
  practical 3309's deferred annual-deal attitude refresh is applied only to one
  CvDeal direction. The opposite direction keeps default
  bUpdateAttitude=true, letting later deals in the same doDeals batch observe
  prematurely refreshed third-party attitude caches.

F297 / provisional KI#620
  with UWAI disabled (supported legacy/K-Mod war AI), several TRADE_WAR items
  can be accepted together. A Defensive-Pact ally is already priced and pulled
  into war by the first purchased declaration, yet a second TRADE_WAR on that
  ally is independently priced and sponsorship-bookkept even though the actual
  declaration returns immediately because the war already exists.

F298 / provisional KI#621
  voluntary vassalage and Defensive Pact are individually valid predeal but
  mutually incompatible final team states. Current per-list vassal-last
  execution can first create a DP, vassalize and remove it, then process the
  opposite dual DP item after vassalization. Nested proxy creation correctly
  fails the new vassal legality check, but outer startTrade unconditionally sets
  the team DP bit anyway, allowing a one-way master/vassal DP flag with no
  backing CvDeal.

F299 / provisional KI#622 remains UNUSED.

ROOT-INDEPENDENCE / REPAIR-BOUNDARY REVIEW
------------------------------------------

The final review intentionally grouped findings by architecture and then applied
a stricter test: two findings merge only when the narrow repair for one
necessarily removes the other's proven trigger/consequence. A broad redesign
that happens to fix several roots is not enough to collapse them.

Peace/list representation:
  F281 vs F283:
    scanning both lists in isPeaceDeal fixes F281 but does not make renewal
    team-scope or reset all proxies; F283 survives.

  F281 vs F285:
    fixing generic peace recognition does not repair AI_stopTradingTrade's
    exact-owner/list interpretation of reparations; F285 survives.

  F283 vs F285:
    team-wide renewal age repair does not change embargo denial orientation;
    neither narrow repair subsumes the other.

Team-proxy / lifetime:
  F283 vs F284:
    renewal-age synchronization does not stop player death from destroying a
    surviving team's agreement. A death-lifetime repair does not fix renewal.

  F284 vs F290:
    preventing one dead player's proxy from tearing down a living team relation
    does not preserve old team identities during PA merge teardown. Conversely,
    a PA-specific old-ID teardown does not fix player-death ownership.

Permanent Alliance:
  F286 vs F288:
    reentrancy/self-deletion hardening leaves the PA+vassal self-vassal final
    state live; rejecting PA+vassal does not cure other synchronous self-delete
    paths.

  F288 vs F290:
    PA+vassal incompatibility is unrelated to old team-proxy identity when an
    ordinary pre-existing DP is cleaned during a normal PA.

  F288 vs F298:
    both are bundle-state incompatibilities, but one is PA+vassal/self-master
    and one is vassal+DP/orphan DP state. Rejecting either pair leaves the other.

Transaction consistency:
  F291:
    needs aggregation of several civic columns into one revolution; unrelated to
    city supply, coalition-war closure or team-status compatibility.

  F292:
    needs post-city resource consistency/staging. Ordinary later resource
    failure still exercises F287 even after F292 is rejected.

  F297:
    needs one-hired-war policy or union/closure pricing for a multi-war bundle;
    resource/civic/team-status fixes do not touch it.

  F298:
    needs explicit vassal+DP incompatibility plus optional defensive handling of
    failed nested proxy creation. Merely reordering items is insufficient.

Embargo:

FINAL SATURATION CONTROLS
-------------------------

1. Permanent Alliance + Open Borders / Defensive Pact
   PA can legitimately supersede these weaker bilateral relationships. OB/DP
   are dual and their immediate reciprocal value is not a one-sided extra
   promise. The problematic part of post-merge proxy cleanup is already F290.
   No independent F299.

2. Generic startTeamTrade failure followed by unconditional team-state setter
   This is a real robustness shape for OB/DP/disengage, but a separate normal
   trigger was not established beyond F298:
     * vassal+DP is F298;
     * vassal+OB remains a coherent potentially economically meaningful state;
     * disengagement is not an ordinary voluntary trade-table item;
     * surrender+DP cannot prevalidate between the warring negotiating teams.
   No F299 from the helper pattern alone.

3. Vassal + Open Borders
   Not proven incompatible. Current free-trade/trade-route semantics retain a
   role for Open Borders after vassalization. No F299.

4. Master + vassal as two brokered-peace targets
   Raw inventory can suggest the shape, but AI_makePeaceTrade returns
   DENIAL_VASSAL for the vassal target; a human cannot be the TRADE_PEACE giver.
   No accepted normal bundle established.

5. Open Borders + Disengagement
   Synthetic ordering is contradictory, but TRADE_DISENGAGE lies beyond
   NUM_TRADEABLE_ITEMS and is produced through the makePeace/signDisengage
   machinery rather than ordinary voluntary negotiation. No normal mixed
   producer.

6. Tech + resource self-obsolescence
   Resource legality checks obsolescence for both sides before implementation,
   so the candidate is preblocked.

7. Tech enabling a later sibling item
   Whole-bundle prevalidation fails conservatively before the tech transfer
   rather than accepting a newly legal sibling.

8. Duplicate civic/religion items
   same-column civic duplicates and multiple religions are rejected by
   AI_checkCivicReligionConsistency. Different civic columns are deliberately
   allowed and are exactly F291.

9. Multiple GOLD/GPT items
   normal trade-table representation exposes one editable entry rather than an
   arbitrary duplicate-obligation producer. No supported duplicate root found.

10. PA + OB/DP teardown after team reassignment
    old agreement cancellation assertions/state pollution remain F290; no
    separate final-state root emerged.

11. Vassal/surrender + remaining team-status pairings
    PA is F288; DP is F298; disengage lacks a voluntary producer; surrender+DP
    fails prevalidation at war; treaty/list issues are already F281/F283/F287.

12. Serialization / reset / ownership
    CvDeal writes and reads ID, initial turn, both players and both lists
    symmetrically. reset/uninit clear both lists and serialized scalars. No
    missing owned member or independent persistence bug.

13. Accessors
    exact-player and exact-one-team assertions are valid contracts. Confirmed
    violations are caller-scope/identity defects already represented by
    F290/F294.

14. Small classifiers
    isVassalTrade, isVassalTributeDeal, isDisengage, isAllDual, isAnnual,
    isDual, hasData and isEndWar were reconciled against current item
    representation. The empty-list vacuous tribute helper has no live persistent
    empty-deal consequence.

15. kill / endTeamTrade list orientation
    normal OB/DP/disengagement team proxies are dual and satisfy the current
    orientation assumptions. The one-sided exception is peace-treaty
    representation and remains under F281/F283 sibling evidence rather than a
    new root.
