QUEUE 047 — CvGameCoreDLL/CvDllPythonEvents.cpp
STATUS: OPEN
F299 / provisional KI#622 — CONFIRMED
F300 / provisional KI#623 — UNUSED / next
Progress remains 25 / 169 until queue 047 closes.

F299 / provisional KI#622
Title:
  BUG's live event-manager override discards the consumable-event return value,
  so the DLL never learns that Python consumed a keyboard or mouse event.

Why this belongs in the queue-047 integration audit:
  CvDllPythonEvents.cpp is the native half of the event ABI. For keyboard and
  mouse input it is not a fire-and-forget notification: postEvent deliberately
  retrieves the Python return value and reportKbdEvent/reportMouseEvent return
  it to the exported CvEventReporter input hooks.

  The C++ side is internally coherent. The live Python event manager breaks the
  other half of that contract.

Native contract:
  CvDllPythonEvents::postEvent:

      long lResult = -1;
      bool bOK = gDLL->getPythonIFace()->callFunction(
          PYEventModule, "onEvent",
          eventData.makeFunctionArgs(), &lResult);

      return (bOK && lResult == 1);

  reportKbdEvent(...) and reportMouseEvent(...) directly return postEvent(...).

  CvEventReporter exposes both as DllExport bool methods and documents:

      // Returns true if the event is consumed by Python
      bool CvEventReporter::mouseEvent(...)
      bool CvEventReporter::kbdEvent(...)

  Thus the engine-facing interface explicitly expects Python's consumed/not-
  consumed result to propagate through this chain.

Stock Python contract:
  Assets/Python/EntryPoints/CvEventInterface.py:

      def onEvent(argsList):
          ...
          return getEventManager().handleEvent(argsList)

  Stock CvEventManager.handleEvent correctly preserves the handler result:

      ret = 0
      if self.EventHandlerMap.has_key(tag):
          fxn = self.EventHandlerMap[tag]
          ret = fxn(argsList[1:idx])
      return ret

BUG override:
  The live manager is BugEventManager.BugEventManager:

      eventManager = BugEventManager.BugEventManager()

  Its handleEvent override currently does:

      def handleEvent(self, argsList):
          self.bDbg, self.bMultiPlayer, self.bAlt, self.bCtrl, \
              self.bShift, self.bAllowCheats = argsList[-6:]
          self._dispatchEvent(argsList[0], argsList[1:-6])

  The return value of _dispatchEvent is discarded.

  Yet _dispatchEvent itself explicitly returns the selected dispatcher:

      return EVENT_FUNCTION_MAP.get(
          eventType,
          BugEventManager._handleDefaultEvent)(
              self, eventType, argsList)

  and both consumable native input events are intentionally mapped to:

      "kbdEvent":   BugEventManager._handleConsumableEvent
      "mouseEvent": BugEventManager._handleConsumableEvent

  _handleConsumableEvent has the intended semantics:

      result = eventHandler(argsList)
      if result > 0:
          return result
      ...
      return 0

  So the framework computes the consumed result correctly and then drops it one
  call frame before CvEventInterface.onEvent returns to C++.

Live current triggers:
  This is not a dead API path.

  BugEventManager.onKbdEvent returns 1 for a registered BUG shortcut. Current
  SAS assets ship multiple shortcut registrations, including:
      Alt M               — Reminder
      Ctrl X / Ctrl F10   — Strategy Overlay visibility
      Alt X / Alt F10     — Strategy Overlay edit mode
      Alt Ctrl O / Alt J  — BUG Options
      Alt Ctrl F1         — BUG Help
      Shift M             — friendly-move display toggle
      Ctrl Z              — debug mode toggle
      Alt Shift M         — save-map shortcut
      Ctrl Shift E        — trigger-event popup

  The handler also returns 1 for several built-in debug/utility key
  combinations.

  CvEventManager.onMouseEvent, which remains registered through BUG's handler
  map, likewise returns 1 for:
      * handled Ctrl+Alt / Ctrl+Shift debug clicks; and
      * screen Back / Forward events when CvScreensInterface consumes them.

Observable contract consequence:
  Inside Python, _handleConsumableEvent still stops later Python handlers after
  the first positive result, so the shortcut itself can appear to work.

  Across the DLL boundary, however, BugEventManager.handleEvent implicitly
  returns None. CvEventInterface.onEvent therefore returns None rather than the
  integer 1 that postEvent is waiting for.

  Consequently postEvent cannot satisfy:
      bOK && lResult == 1

  and CvEventReporter::kbdEvent/mouseEvent cannot report the consumed state back
  through their exported bool contract.

  The engine can therefore continue native/interface processing for an input
  that Python has already treated as consumed. The exact visible follow-on
  depends on the key/button and current screen, but the contract violation is
  deterministic and current shortcuts produce the positive result needed to
  exercise it.

Why this is not merely "BUG handles consumption internally":
  BUG's internal early-return solves only multiple Python handlers reacting to
  the same input.

  The exported C++ comment and postEvent implementation define a second,
  engine-facing purpose for the return value. If the intended contract ended
  inside Python, reportKbdEvent/reportMouseEvent would not need to return
  postEvent, and CvEventReporter would not expose/document the bool as consumed
  by Python.

Ancestry:
  The same missing return is present in:
      * Base AdvCiv 1.14 BugEventManager.py;
      * the supplied K-Mod BugEventManager.py.

  Their CvDllPythonEvents::postEvent implementations also retrieve lResult and
  require lResult == 1 in exactly the same way.

  Stock CvEventManager (including current SAS/Base) still returns ret correctly.
  The loss occurs specifically in the BUG/K-Mod event-manager override.

  Civ4CE/BtS does not contain this bundled BUG manager in the supplied tree, so
  the cross-layer regression is from the BUG/K-Mod integration lineage rather
  than the original stock CvEventManager contract.

Repair:
  Minimal and local:

      def handleEvent(self, argsList):
          self.bDbg, self.bMultiPlayer, self.bAlt, self.bCtrl, \
              self.bShift, self.bAllowCheats = argsList[-6:]
          return self._dispatchEvent(argsList[0], argsList[1:-6])

  This restores the return value that _dispatchEvent and
  _handleConsumableEvent already compute.

Repair boundary / compatibility:
  * Do not change CvDllPythonEvents::postEvent; its exactly-1 contract matches
    stock Civ4 and the existing input handler convention.
  * Do not make all default event handlers return 1. Ordinary notifications
    should remain unconsumed.
  * Existing default dispatchers commonly return None; returning that through
    handleEvent is harmless for fire-and-forget events and preserves current
    behavior there.
  * OnSave has its own special dispatcher returning a string, which is another
    reason the generic wrapper should preserve rather than discard dispatcher
    return values. Queue 047 does not rely on OnSave for F299's proof.
  * Current consumable handlers return 1, so no broader "any positive integer"
    policy change is needed on the C++ side.

Severity:
  Low-to-moderate UI/input integration defect. Python shortcuts still execute,
  which can hide the problem, but the native engine is never told they consumed
  the input. Depending on overlap with native screen/key handling this can
  permit duplicate/fall-through actions.

CYARGSLIST CAPACITY / TEMP ARRAY OWNERSHIP
-----------------------------------------
CyArgsList::MAX_CY_ARGS == 20.

A direct count of every native packet shows the maximum current packet is
reportMouseEvent:
    8 entries before postEvent
  + 6 context flags
  = 14 total tuple arguments.

reportKbdEvent is 13 total; all others are <= 12.
No current overflow of CyArgsList's fixed argument array.

reportSelectionGroupPushMission:
    iNumUnits = pSelectionGroup->getNumUnits()
    aiUnitIds = new int[iNumUnits]
    traverse same selection-group unit list
    eventData.add(aiUnitIds, iNumUnits)
    delete[] aiUnitIds

CyArgsList::add(const int*, length) constructs a fresh Python list and converts
each integer before postEvent. The Python packet therefore does not retain the
temporary C++ array.

Current AdvCiv/SAS uses delete[] correctly. K-Mod fixed the older scalar-delete
bug ("Memory leak"); Civ4CE/BtS retains the older delete form. No current SAS
root.

The count and traversal occur synchronously with no Python callback between
them, so no supported mutation window was found that would make getNumUnits and
the node traversal diverge.

COMBATDETAILS TEMPORARY-LIFETIME CANDIDATE — REJECTED
------------------------------------------------------
This was the strongest lifetime concern after WIP01.

Native generic combat events pass pointers to CombatDetails values that can be
stack locals in CvUnit::resolveCombat. Current autolog deliberately stores the
received Python CombatDetails objects in self.WdlAttacker/self.WdlDefender and
can read them later from selectionGroupPushMission, after resolveCombat has
returned.

That looks like a dangling-reference bug if makePythonObject exposes a borrowed
reference to the native CombatDetails.

The Boost.Python conversion contract shows that it does not.

CvDLLPythonIFaceBase::makePythonObject<T>(T* pObj) constructs a
boost::python::object from the raw pointer.

Boost.Python arg_to_python selects:
    pointer_deep_arg_to_python<T*>
for raw pointers.

The distinct shallow/reference path is:
    pointer_shallow_arg_to_python
which uses make_reference_holder and is selected for pointer/reference wrapper
types, not an ordinary raw T*.

pointer_deep_arg_to_python passes the pointee through the registered pointee
converter. CombatDetails is registered as a normal:
    python::class_<CombatDetails>("CombatDetails")
with no noncopyable/reference-holder restriction.

The corresponding class converter is the copy-constructor/value-holder path
(class_cref_wrapper -> make_instance). Thus the Python CombatDetails object owns
a copied CombatDetails value rather than borrowing the stack address.

This is consistent with the pervasive Civ4 pattern:
    CyUnit* wrapper = new CyUnit(pUnit);
    makePythonObject(wrapper);
    postEvent(...);
    delete wrapper;
The Python object survives deletion of the temporary wrapper because the wrapper
value was converted/captured independently; a CyUnit copy itself contains the
underlying CvUnit pointer, whereas CombatDetails is a self-contained value
record.

Therefore autolog retaining the CombatDetails Python objects across the later
mission event is safe with respect to the C++ CombatDetails stack lifetime.
No F300.

SAS battle-history handlers are even more conservative: they immediately copy
the relevant CombatDetails fields into plain integer tuples rather than retaining
the wrapper.

NULLABLE WRAPPER / CALL-SITE CONTROLS
-------------------------------------
Additional current handler checks:

* greatPersonBorn:
  current stock handler explicitly checks pUnit.isNone() and pCity.isNone()
  before dereferencing.

* nukeExplosion:
  CyUnit can wrap a null pNukeUnit, but the current stock handler logs only the
  plot and does not dereference the optional unit.

* goodyReceived:
  stock/autolog listeners do not dereference a possibly-null pUnit. The unit
  naming extension only performs unit naming when the goody type itself grants
  a unit and searches the player's resulting units rather than relying on a null
  wrapper.

* plotFeatureRemoved:
  pCity is documented as nullable in Python. The only current handler does no
  work; argument ordering remains the already-recorded latent ABI control.

* cityAcquired:
  CvPlayer::acquireCity creates/initializes kNewCity, updates visibility and plot
  groups, then emits cityAcquired(&kNewCity) before the subsequent raze/disband/
  keep decision. The Python CyCity therefore references a live city throughout
  the synchronous callback.

* combatResult:
  both winner and loser still exist when CvEventReporter::combatResult is fired;
  lethal kill/removal occurs afterward. Current Python reads/copies the required
  data synchronously.

The earlier WIP01 timing controls for unitKilled, unitLost, unitCaptured,
cityLost, cityRazed, cityAcquiredAndKept and unit gifts remain intact.

GENERIC-EVENT SHAPE CONTROLS
----------------------------
Native reportGenericEvent nests the caller-created Python tuple as one event
argument. Stock generic-event consumers intentionally unpack through:
    genericArgs = argsList[0][0]

Current native generic callers:
    gameUpdate
    AutoPlayComplete
    SwitchHotSeatPlayer
    combatLogHit
    combatLogCalc
    sasBattleHistoryCombatDetails
    sasBattleHistoryCombatRetreat

The combat/gameUpdate consumers are written for this nesting.

SwitchHotSeatPlayer has an old cross-source shape inconsistency:
  native genericEvent -> nested ePlayer tuple;
  BUG's own fireEvent path -> flat ePlayer argument.

Current listeners do not interpret the native nested value in a way that
produces a shipped failure:
  Civ4lerts resets state and ignores it;
  Reminder clears reminder text;
  BUG screen reset listeners ignore it;
  StrategyOverlay forwards the value, but the live DotMap switch handler simply
  hides the layer and does not inspect the player ID.

Keep as an integration/API control, not F300.

GENERIC-EVENT OWNERSHIP — CURRENT BOUND
---------------------------------------
reportGenericEvent receives a tuple returned by an inner CyArgsList::
makeFunctionArgs() and inserts that PyObject pointer as one element of the outer
event packet. CyArgsList::add(void*) deliberately stores a PyObject pointer
without creating a second wrapper, matching the same ownership convention used
throughout the DLL for makePythonObject results and nested argument packets.

The concrete MakeFunctionArgs implementation is engine-side through the pure
virtual Python interface and is not present in the supplied SDK source. Local
source therefore cannot prove its exact steal/incref sequence line-by-line.
However, the generic-event nesting idiom is inherited from BtS/K-Mod and is used
repeatedly by current native callers; no current double-free, dangling tuple or
retained nested-tuple consequence has been established.

Keep this as a bounded ownership control unless a concrete current failure can
be tied to the opaque engine-side MakeFunctionArgs implementation; do not invent
one from missing implementation detail.

QUEUE 047 — CvGameCoreDLL/CvDllPythonEvents.cpp
STATUS: FIRST-PASS COMPLETE

CONFIRMED ROOT
--------------
F299 / provisional KI#622
  BUG's live event-manager override drops the return value from
  `_dispatchEvent`. Native CvDllPythonEvents::postEvent deliberately retrieves
  CvEventInterface.onEvent's Python return and recognizes integer 1 as
  "consumed"; CvEventReporter::kbdEvent/mouseEvent export that bool with the
  explicit contract "Returns true if the event is consumed by Python."

  CvEventInterface.onEvent correctly returns `getEventManager().handleEvent`,
  and BUG's `_handleConsumableEvent` correctly stops at and returns the first
  positive keyboard/mouse-handler result. But BugEventManager.handleEvent calls
  `_dispatchEvent(...)` without returning it. A live Python handler can
  therefore consume the event internally while the event-interface boundary
  returns None instead of 1, making the native consumed predicate false.

  Current SAS has multiple live consumers that really return 1, including BUG
  keyboard shortcuts and debug mouse/keyboard paths. The minimal repair is:

      def handleEvent(self, argsList):
          self.bDbg, self.bMultiPlayer, self.bAlt, self.bCtrl, self.bShift, self.bAllowCheats = argsList[-6:]
          return self._dispatchEvent(argsList[0], argsList[1:-6])

  Do not change CvDllPythonEvents::postEvent. Its exactly-1 test is consistent
  with the stock event-interface contract and current positive consumers.

  Ancestry: the missing BUG wrapper return is inherited by Base AdvCiv and the
  K-Mod BUG integration. Civ4CE/BtS stock CvEventManager itself preserves its
  computed return. This is not a SAS-only regression.

ENGINE-FACING CONSEQUENCE BOUND
-------------------------------
The audit deliberately stops at the strongest locally provable boundary:

  * Python's documented entry point says to return 1 when an event is consumed.
  * BugEventManager's consumable dispatcher can and currently does compute 1.
  * the wrapper drops that value and returns None;
  * CvDllPythonEvents::postEvent asks the Python interface for a long result and
    returns true only when that result equals 1;
  * CvEventReporter::kbdEvent/mouseEvent directly return this bool and document
    it as the Python-consumed state.

The proprietary EXE-side caller is not present in the supplied SDK material, so
this checkpoint does NOT invent a more specific engine fall-through behavior
(e.g. a particular second action or UI side effect). The proven defect is the
broken exported consumed/not-consumed contract itself.

GENERIC-EVENT PRODUCER / RETENTION CLOSURE
------------------------------------------
All seven current native generic-event names were rechecked from producer to
listener:

  gameUpdate
    Payload: one turn-slice integer. It is emitted from CvGame::updateUnprofiled
    when not between turns and from the active-player message-processing bridge

  AutoPlayComplete
    Payload: one turn-slice integer. AIAutoPlay's current completion handler does

    Payload: eight integers (owners, unit types, plot coordinates, ending

Thus the only uninspectable ownership detail is the proprietary engine-side

SAS-vs-BASE NORMALIZED DELTA
----------------------------
Whitespace/signature-normalized comparison against Base AdvCiv 1.14 found only
one functional current-SAS delta inside GroupPathFinder.cpp itself:

  GroupPathFinder::generatePath(CvPlot const& kTo)

SAS keeps the inherited assertion that setGroup must first establish a group,
but additionally checks pGroup == NULL and returns false in release builds
instead of dereferencing pGroup through getPlot. This is an already-applied SAS
hardening fix, not a new queue-054 finding.

The remaining apparent source differences are formatting / collapsed signatures.
Thus a new root in this queue is expected to be inherited unless archaeology
proves otherwise.

CACHE / GROUP-IDENTITY BOUNDARY
-------------------------------
GroupPathFinder is a process-global reusable finder shared by selection groups.
setGroup performs a full reset when the group pointer changes, and conditionally
when path-relevant MovementFlags change. The start-plot change inside the generic
KmodPathFinder also resets cached nodes.

The current SAS membership invalidations from earlier F152 / KI#475 are present:
  * addUnit invalidates the reusable main finder when this group is cached;
  * deleteUnitNode does the same;
  * full-list teardown invalidates while m_pPathFinder exists, with the later
    KI#475.2 map-teardown null guard;
  * group kill invalidates both main and alternate finder pointers.

Do NOT duplicate that already-fixed root in queue 054.

Normal promotion is also not a surviving stale-cache path. CvUnit::promote calls
CvSelectionGroup::resetPath immediately after setHasPromotion, preserving the
K-Mod safeguard. A direct external setHasPromotion mutation could bypass this,
but no shipped producer/consequence sufficient for F300 has been established.

MOVE_DECLARE_WAR REUSE OPTIMIZATION
-----------------------------------
setGroup intentionally avoids resetting when MOVE_DECLARE_WAR is the only flag
change and the group team is not sneak-attack ready. This initially looked risky
because the flag participates in both movement legality and path cost.

Current controls:
  * for human groups, MOVE_DECLARE_WAR is deliberately not used for intermediate
    canStepThrough legality; destination legality may still use it;
  * AI war-route cost / bIgnoreRoutes differences are tied to
    AI_isSneakAttackReady(target); the no-argument AI_isSneakAttackReady check in
    setGroup forces a reset if any such target state is live;
  * the remaining human-only cost difference is the advc.035 exclusive-radius
    flip bias, but current GlobalDefines_advc.xml has OWN_EXCLUSIVE_RADIUS = 0.

Decision so far: no current F300. If OWN_EXCLUSIVE_RADIUS were enabled, this
optimization would need re-review because toggling MOVE_DECLARE_WAR can then
change human path costs without triggering the sneak-attack reset. That is a
disabled-configuration caveat, not a shipped defect.

HEURISTIC ADMISSIBILITY — CURRENT SAS MOVEMENT DATA
----------------------------------------------------
Sea default heuristic weight is one MOVE_DENOMINATOR, under the source comment
that water has no routes and no promotions that reduce water movement cost.
The current SAS XML preserves that assumption:
  * PROMOTION_NAVIGATOR / naval movement promotions add movement points rather
    than reducing per-tile water movement cost;
  * the only current iMoveDiscountChange=1 promotion is
    PROMOTION_MOBILITY_COST, restricted to armor / mounted land combat classes;
  * current naval combat classes do not receive raw movement-cost discounts or
    water double-move promotions that undercut the denominator lower bound.

Land heuristic weight uses KmodPathFinder::minimumStepCost(baseMoves), whose
initialization caps both route minima at MOVE_DENOMINATOR/2 and then takes the
minimum of base and scaled route costs. Current terrain/double-move discounts do
not undercut this intentionally conservative lower bound.

World-wrap handling is also correct at this layer: heuristic stepDistance uses
CvMap::xDistance/yDistance, which apply map wrapping before taking the Chebyshev
step distance.

Decision: no heuristic-admissibility root established.

2024 DANGER-AVOIDANCE REPAIR — VERIFIED BOUNDARY
------------------------------------------------
AdvCiv practical 4196 / b3de867844 (“Fix danger avoidance checks in pathfinder”)
is present in current SAS. It split canStepThrough into:
  1. a path-independent predicate that may permanently close a node; and
  2. a path-data predicate for the AI danger check, which may reject only the
     particular partial path while leaving the node UNINITIALIZED so another
     parent can try it.

This directly repairs the older K-Mod/AdvCiv failure where first reaching a
dangerous tile from a slow direction could permanently rule out a later roaded
route that crosses the dangerous tile without ending the turn there. The legacy
verification finder was updated in parallel.

The current path-data predicate rejects a dangerous plot when:
  (pathTurns > 1 || moves == 0)
  && AI-controlled
  && !MOVE_IGNORE_DANGER
  && (!canFight || MOVE_AVOID_DANGER)
  && !alwaysInvisible.

The Base AdvCiv manual explicitly records that the 2024 repair removed the known
failure-to-find mode while retaining a Tbd caveat: GroupStepMetric::cost still
uses path history and can generate occasional suboptimal danger-averse paths.
That documented limitation by itself is not a new F300.

REMAINING DANGER REPARENTING QUESTION — OPEN, NOT A FINDING
------------------------------------------------------------
A narrower algorithmic boundary remains under challenge.

KmodPathFinder::processChild applies the path-data canStepThrough predicate only
when a node is first initialized. If that opened node later receives a cheaper
parent, processChild calls updatePathData again but does NOT re-run the
path-dependent danger predicate. forwardPropagate likewise recalculates
moves/path turns and descendant costs without revalidating path-dependent
canStepThrough.

Therefore the code shape permits this state transition in principle:
  safe/opened node (first path: first turn with moves remaining)
    -> cheaper reparent
    -> updated node state has moves == 0 or later path turn
    -> the same dangerous plot would now fail canStepThrough(path data)
    -> node/descendant tree is nevertheless retained and propagated.

This is stronger than the already-documented “cost may be suboptimal” caveat if
it can lead to an actually returned unsafe MOVE_AVOID_DANGER path. It is NOT yet
F300 because a reachable game-state/cost ordering and returned-path consequence
still need proof. If those cannot be established, record it as a theoretical
algorithmic boundary/control only.

OPEN-BORDERS / WORLD-STATE CACHE CHALLENGE — OPEN, NOT A FINDING
----------------------------------------------------------------
A second cache boundary is being tested adversarially.

CvTeam::declareWar explicitly calls CvSelectionGroup::resetPath after movement
permissions/costs change. CvTeam::setOpenBorders does not reset the reusable
K-Mod GroupPathFinder. AdvCiv practical 4324 / 751d73e5f7 (“Update pathfinder
waypoints after signing OB”) adds updateActivePaths for the active-player UI,
but its own comment states that resetting the K-Mod/original finder did not fix
the waypoint problem. That commit is about UI waypoint refresh, not proof that
gameplay cache reuse is semantically valid across Open Borders changes.

At the generic A* level, a foreign-border tile previously rejected by the
path-independent canStepThrough predicate is cached CLOSED. After Open Borders
makes the tile traversable, a same-group/same-start/same-flags call does not
have an intrinsic world-state generation check. A previously CLOSED intermediate
node is not reopened, so stale cache state could in principle block a newly
legal path until some other reset occurs.

However, the normal shipped reachability is not yet proven:
  * the finder is global across all groups, so a different group path call resets
    it before reuse;
  * AI diplomacy happens at the end of CvPlayer::doTurn, before doTurnUnits, and
    the cached group immediately before diplomacy is often from another context;
  * human direct movement uses interface/final-path machinery rather than this
    AI-only reusable generatePath path in the ordinary case;
  * no shipped Python CySelectionGroup.generatePath consumer was found.

Thus the stale-OB cache shape is real, but F300 remains unused unless a normal
same-group producer sequence and current consequence can be proved.

NULL / GETTER PRECONDITION CONTROL
----------------------------------
The SAS release guard in generatePath(kTo) prevents its former null-group crash.
Other path getters such as getPathFirstPlot/getPathEndTurnPlot assume successful
path generation. Current C++ call sites are generally success-guarded, and no
shipped Python consumer was found that makes the getter precondition a current
reachable crash. Keep as API contract/control unless a concrete caller disproves
that later in the queue.

QUEUE 054 — CvGameCoreDLL/GroupPathFinder.cpp
STATUS: OPEN
F300 / provisional KI#623 — STILL UNALLOCATED pending final consequence/repair-boundary review
Progress remains 26 / 169.

CORRECTION TO THE EARLY DANGER-PRODUCER NARROWING
-------------------------------------------------
The path-dependent danger predicate is not limited to callers that explicitly
set MOVE_AVOID_DANGER. It applies whenever:

  (pathTurns > 1 || moves == 0)
  && AI-controlled
  && !MOVE_IGNORE_DANGER
  && (!group.canFight() || MOVE_AVOID_DANGER)
  && !alwaysInvisible
  && AI_isAnyPlotDanger(plot).

Therefore every ordinary AI-controlled non-fighting group (Workers, Settlers,
missionaries, executives, many Great People, etc.) is danger-sensitive even
under NO_MOVEMENT_FLAGS. The earlier grep showing only a few explicit
MOVE_AVOID_DANGER producers is useful for fighting groups but does not bound the
noncombat surface.

The explicit MOVE_AVOID_DANGER producers themselves are narrow. Current direct
producers are first-city settler scouting and explore routines. Explore groups
also receive the 2/3 unexplored-tile cost modifier, which removes the particular
4/3 deep-fog asymmetry discussed below. The important current surface is instead
ordinary noncombat AI pathing.

CONCRETE REPARENT STATE — CURRENT SAS CAN INVERT SAFE VS UNSAFE PATH DATA
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
The theoretical WIP01 state can be instantiated with current SAS movement data.
No invented unit or hypothetical XML value is needed.

Current XML contains the live Dutch Worker replacement:

  UNIT_NETHERLANDS_SWIFT_WORKER
    class       UNITCLASS_WORKER
    combat      NONE / iCombat 0
    domain      DOMAIN_LAND
    default AI  UNITAI_WORKER
    iMoves      3

CIV4CivilizationInfos maps the Dutch UNITCLASS_WORKER replacement to this unit.
It has no flat/ignore-terrain movement flag. A singleton full-move group
therefore begins with 3 * MOVE_DENOMINATOR = 180 movement points.

Current routes:

  ROUTE_ROAD      iMovement 30, iFlatMovement 30
  ROUTE_RAILROAD  iMovement 20, iFlatMovement 6

For a 3-move unit, a revealed railroad step costs
min(20, 6 * 3) = 18; a revealed road step costs 30.

CvPlot::movementCost deliberately returns exactly MOVE_DENOMINATOR = 60 when
the destination plot has never been revealed and bAssumeRevealed is false,
which is how GroupStepMetric calls it.

GroupStepMetric::cost then applies:
  * unexplored destination from a revealed predecessor: modifier 3/3;
  * unexplored destination from an also-unrevealed predecessor, for a normal
    non-explorer: modifier 4/3.

Thus an unrevealed -> unrevealed step has the same movement-point effect on the
unit (60) but carries 80 units of movement weight in A* cost.

A fully constructible two-corridor local state can therefore have, from the
same full-move start S to the same unrevealed intermediate D:

  first/safe corridor:
    3 revealed railroad steps + first fog step + deep-fog step
    actual movement spent = 18 + 18 + 18 + 60 + 60 = 174
    final moves at D = 6
    weighted movement component = 18 + 18 + 18 + 60 + 80 = 194

  later/unsafe corridor:
    4 revealed road steps + first fog step
    actual movement spent = 30 + 30 + 30 + 30 + 60 = 180
    final moves at D = 0
    weighted movement component = 180

The small PATH_STEP/symmetry/no-route weights cannot erase a 14*1024 movement-
weight gap.

EXACT A* ORDERING CONSTRUCTION
------------------------------
The ordering can be made explicit rather than assumed. One non-wrapped local
coordinate arrangement is:

  S = (10,5)

  safe corridor:
    (10,5) -> (9,6) -> (8,7) -> (8,8) -> U=(9,9) -> D=(10,10)

  cheaper-later corridor:
    (10,5) -> (11,6) -> (12,7) -> (12,8) -> R=(11,9) -> D=(10,10)

  choose a safe final destination beyond D, e.g. toward (10,12), and make
  irrelevant cross-links impassable. U and R have equal Chebyshev heuristic
  distance to that destination.

With current PATH_* weights and current land heuristic weight 18, the exact
known/heuristic/total costs along the two designated corridors are:

  SAFE
    (9,6):  known  18445, h 110592, total 129037, moves 162
    (8,7):  known  36890, h  92160, total 129050, moves 144
    (8,8):  known  55332, h  73728, total 129060, moves 126
    U(9,9): known 116785, h  55296, total 172081, moves  66
    D:      known 198717, h  36864, total 235581, moves   6

  LATER CHEAPER ROUTE
    (11,6): known  30732, h 110592, total 141324, moves 150
    (12,7): known  61466, h  92160, total 153626, moves 120
    (12,8): known  92194, h  73728, total 165922, moves  90
    R(11,9):known 122924, h  55296, total 178220, moves  60
    D:      known 184376, h  36864, total 221240, moves   0

Therefore the generic A* processing order can be:
  * process the safe-prefix parents;
  * process U before R and initialize/open D with moves=6;
  * D is expensive enough to remain OPEN;
  * process R before D;
  * R offers a strictly cheaper path to D;
  * processChild reparents D and updatePathData changes D from moves=6 to
    moves=0;
  * the path-dependent canStepThrough predicate is NOT called after this
    reparent;
  * D therefore remains an OPEN node even though, if tested now, the same
    predicate would reject it whenever AI_isAnyPlotDanger(D) is true.

The 2024 repair's intended invariant is therefore still violated after a
cheaper-parent transition. This is no longer merely a theoretical possibility
from source shape; current SAS movement/XML values admit a concrete cost and
processing order.

DANGER ON AN UNREVEALED D IS REACHABLE FOR AI
----------------------------------------------
The fog-cost construction does not imply that AI_isAnyPlotDanger(D) must be
false. CvPlayerAI::AI_countDangerousUnits deliberately allows AI danger checks
against non-visible attacker plots through AI_cheatDangerVisibility, and that
helper deterministically returns a 50% hash result based on plot coordinates,
game turn and player ID. A hidden hostile unit adjacent to D can therefore make
AI_isAnyPlotDanger(D) true while D itself remains unrevealed and path-independent
canMoveThrough(D) remains legal.

This is an intentional AdvCiv AI information rule; the reparent defect does not
require inventing visibility semantics outside current code.

CURRENT CALLER CONSEQUENCE — IMPORTANTLY MORE CONSERVATIVE THAN "WORKER DIES"
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Do NOT overstate the consequence as "the Worker necessarily ends its turn on
D." MISSION_MOVE_TO execution uses CvSelectionGroup::getClearPathFinder and
recomputes a final path for each physical step. A later per-step recomputation
can reject the danger and prevent an actual unsafe landing.

There is nevertheless a current shipped consequence before physical movement.
SAS AI_nextCityToImprove does:

  GroupPathFinder& pf = CvSelectionGroup::pathFinder();
  pf.setGroup(*getGroup(), NO_MOVEMENT_FLAGS);

then, for every same-land-area city, asks AI_bestCityBuild for its best job and
uses:

  if (!pf.generatePath(*pPlot)) continue;
  int const pathTurns = pf.getPathTurns();
  score -= pathTurnPenalty * pathTurns;

There is no requirement that every intermediate plot be revealed. Thus a normal
AI Worker path evaluation can receive TRUE plus path-turn data from the
reparented tree even though the returned partial path contains a dangerous D
at which the path data says the group ends its turn and the path-dependent
validity predicate would now return false.

That can make a job count as pathable and affect cross-city target ranking. The
subsequent movement mission may then replan, change route or fail after movement
has begun. This is precisely a CvUnitAI-versus-CvSelectionGroup consistency
boundary; practical 4196's own commit message says the repair was intended to
avoid rare worker path failures/suboptimal paths and possible loop-like
inconsistencies.

So the strongest proven current consequence at this checkpoint is:
  * generatePath can return success / pathTurns for a partial-path tree that no
    longer satisfies GroupStepMetric's own path-dependent danger contract;
  * current worker AI consumes exactly that success/pathTurns for decisions;
  * final movement has a later revalidation layer, so actual unsafe end-turn is
    not yet claimed.

This is likely sufficient for a correctness finding, but F300 is deliberately
left unallocated until the remaining ancestry/repair-boundary and final-movement
review is complete.

ANCESTRY — STRONG SO FAR
------------------------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 has the same GroupStepMetric split and the same generic
processChild/forwardPropagate behavior. SAS's functional delta in
GroupPathFinder.cpp remains only its already-known null-group release guard, so
this reparent issue is not introduced by that SAS C++ file.

K-Mod's original custom pathfinder has the same generic shape:
  * pathValid_source is checked only when a child node is first put on the
    stack/opened;
  * pathValid_source contains the noncombat path-data danger check;
  * later cheaper-parent replacement calls pathAdd(... ASNC_PARENTADD_UP ...)
    and ForwardPropagate but does not call pathValid_source again.

Thus the reparent-invalidates-danger-state pattern is inherited from K-Mod.
AdvCiv practical 4196 substantially improved it by preventing a first
path-dependent rejection from permanently closing the plot, but did not add
revalidation on later reparent/propagation.

The practical-4196 source comment itself contains a remarkably relevant caveat
at the split point:

  the second predicate "merely invalidates the path we've taken so far" and
  "it's possible we might have to(?)" check further paths reaching the child.

Its commit message says the author had convinced himself the change was
"strictly more correct than before," while explicitly retaining concern about
path-data-dependent cost and CvUnitAI/CvSelectionGroup inconsistencies. The
current reparent construction lives exactly on that remaining boundary.

Civ4CE/BtS exposes the same path-data danger condition in its pathValid callback,
but the supplied CE source does not expose the EXE's internal FAStar reparent
algorithm. Do not claim the exact reparent defect for stock BtS solely from that
callback.

OPEN-BORDERS CACHE SEQUENCING — LEANING REJECTED
-------------------------------------------------
The WIP01 stale-CLOSED-node shape remains true in abstract, but normal producer
sequencing now strongly argues against a current finding.

Sequential turns:
  * AI unit movement occurs before that AI's end-of-turn diplomacy.
  * signing/canceling OB through AI diplomacy therefore occurs after the team's
    units have used their movement AI;
  * before the same group normally paths again, another group/player or the next
    game-turn cache reset replaces/resets the global finder state.

Simultaneous turns:
  * CvGame::doUpdateCacheOnTurn resets the global selection-group pathfinder at
    the game-turn boundary;
  * CvPlayer::doTurn (including AI diplomacy) happens before doTurnUnits;
  * traced AI_doTurnPre/AI_doDiplo paths do not populate the main reusable
    selection-group finder for that player's later unit group; where player-AI
    code needs temporary group paths, it uses a separate/clear finder.
  * the first actual unit-group caller therefore starts from a fresh or
    different-group cache and setGroup resets as needed.

Automatic deal processing also occurs after the game-turn cache reset. War
transitions have their own explicit reset. Human direct movement uses the
interface/final path layer in the ordinary case; automated human groups act in
their normal unit phase rather than repeatedly around a manual diplomacy change.

Manual automation-toggle / scripting sequences could manufacture same-group
reuse across an OB transition, but no ordinary shipped producer sequence has
survived. Unless a remaining edge disproves this, close it as a cache-theory
control rather than F300.

F300 / KI#623 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------
Title:
Reparented GroupPathFinder nodes are not revalidated after path-dependent
movement state changes, allowing danger-invalid AI noncombat paths to remain
accepted and scored.

Status after the WIP02 adversarial review: CONFIRMED.

WHY THIS NOW CROSSES THE FINDING THRESHOLD
------------------------------------------
All four required links are now proven in current shipped source rather than
inferred from a suspicious code shape:

1. Contract violation.
   StepMetricBase documents that the path-dependent canStepThrough(p,w) part
   must describe whether a step can be added to the current partial path w.
   GroupStepMetric's danger rule depends exactly on path state: path turns and
   remaining moves.

   KmodPathFinder::processChild checks that path-dependent predicate when a node
   is first initialized, but when an already-known node receives a cheaper
   parent it calls updatePathData after removing the old parent and DOES NOT
   call canStepThrough(plot,node) again. forwardPropagate can then change the
   same moves/path-turn data in descendants without revalidating them either.

2. Concrete current-SAS state.
   WIP02 gives an exact current-data counterexample using the live
   UNIT_NETHERLANDS_SWIFT_WORKER (3 moves), current road/railroad movement
   values, current fog movement cost and current unexplored-tile cost modifier.
   A node D can be opened through a path with 6 moves left (danger predicate
   accepts it), then reparented to a strictly cheaper path with 0 moves left
   (danger predicate would reject it) while remaining open. The A* ordering and
   costs were enumerated numerically rather than hand-waved.

3. Reachable danger and shipped consumer.
   AI danger can be true on the unrevealed construction through AdvCiv's
   deterministic cheat-danger visibility for hidden nearby hostile units.
   Current SAS AI_nextCityToImprove uses the reusable GroupPathFinder under
   NO_MOVEMENT_FLAGS for ordinary noncombat Workers, treats generatePath==true
   as pathable, consumes getPathTurns in cross-city job scoring, and does not
   require intermediate plots to be revealed. Thus the invalid tree changes a
   real shipped AI decision interface.

4. Ancestry/history corroboration.
   The generic cheaper-parent/ForwardPropagate shape is inherited from K-Mod.
   Base AdvCiv 1.14 still has it. AdvCiv practical 4181 added an explicit
   "Danger-averse unit failed to move?" diagnostic/skip workaround for fresh
   mission failures involving path-data danger, and practical 4196 then split
   path-independent from path-dependent danger so first-arrival rejection would
   no longer permanently close a node. Practical 4196's own source comment
   explicitly wondered whether further paths reaching the child might also need
   checking. Its commit message retained concern about path-data-dependent cost
   and CvUnitAI/CvSelectionGroup inconsistencies. The cheaper-reparent path is
   the remaining mutation boundary that 4196 did not cover.

PROVEN CONSEQUENCE / NON-CLAIMS
-------------------------------
Proven current consequence:
  * generatePath can report success and path-turn data for a parent tree whose
    current path-dependent GroupStepMetric danger predicate is false;
  * current Worker target evaluation consumes that result for pathability and
    scoring, so an actually danger-invalid route can affect selected work;
  * later mission execution can therefore have to choose a different route,
    fail/replan, or skip after the evaluator had treated the target as pathable.

Do NOT claim from this source proof alone:
  * that a Worker must actually end its turn on the dangerous plot;
  * that the Worker must die;
  * that every such evaluation visibly fails a mission.

CvSelectionGroup::groupPathTo uses the clear/final finder and movement missions
recalculate as physical steps execute. That later layer can catch the danger.
The defect is therefore a pathfinder/evaluator consistency and AI-targeting
correctness defect, with mission churn/wasted movement as a plausible downstream
manifestation, not a proven guaranteed death path.

SEVERITY / SCOPE
----------------
Recommended severity: low-to-moderate AI pathfinding correctness, rare-state
but deterministic once the required map/path/danger configuration occurs.

Exposure is not limited to explicit MOVE_AVOID_DANGER users: the path-dependent
danger rule applies to ordinary AI-controlled groups that cannot fight, so
Workers, Settlers, missionaries, executives and many Great People are in the
logical surface. The exact WIP02 reproducible cost inversion uses the current
Dutch 3-move Worker. SAS's movement additions can broaden the set of reachable
movement states, but the algorithmic root is inherited rather than introduced
by SAS GroupPathFinder.cpp.

REPAIR BOUNDARY — DO NOT APPLY A NAIVE ONE-LINE RECHECK
-------------------------------------------------------
A correct repair has to preserve the A* tree invariant, not merely add

    if (!canStepThrough(kChildPlot, kChild)) return;

AFTER mutating kChild.

Why that naive repair is unsafe/incomplete:
  * the old parent/path may remain valid. A proposed cheaper parent that produces
    danger-invalid path data should not destroy the old valid route;
  * processChild currently changes cost and removes the old-parent relationship
    before updatePathData, so post-mutation rejection would require rollback;
  * forwardPropagate can change moves/pathTurns for every descendant and can
    therefore invalidate their path-dependent predicates too. Checking only the
    direct child leaves the same invariant violation in grandchildren.

Robust repair families to evaluate during implementation review:
  A. Compute prospective child path data before committing the reparent, reject
     a path-dependent-invalid proposed parent while preserving the old tree,
     then recursively revalidate any descendant whose propagated path data
     changes; invalid descendants must be safely detached/reopened/re-discovered.
  B. Conservatively invalidate/re-discover the affected subtree whenever a
     reparent changes path-dependent data in a danger-sensitive metric.
  C. More fundamentally, make the path state that affects legality part of node
     identity (multiple states per plot). This is algorithmically cleanest but
     is a much larger change.

The current OpenList/NodeMap design does not provide a trivial generic subtree
rollback primitive, so implementation should be reviewed as an algorithmic
change. Prefer a correctness-first localized solution plus reproducible test
scenario over a superficially tiny patch.

ANCESTRY CLASSIFICATION
-----------------------
  K-Mod: root shape inherited. Original pathValid_source contains the path-data
         danger rule; cheaper-parent replacement uses pathAdd(PARENTADD_UP) and
         ForwardPropagate without rerunning pathValid_source.
  AdvCiv: practical 4196 repairs first-arrival closure by splitting the predicate
          but leaves reparent/propagation without path-dependent revalidation.
  SAS:    current GroupPathFinder.cpp functional delta from Base 1.14 is not the
          cause. Current SAS content provides a concrete 3-move-worker state and
          a current Worker evaluator consumer.
  BtS/CE: callback exposes a similar path-data danger rule, but supplied source
          does not expose the EXE FAStar reparent internals. Do not attribute the
          exact reparent defect to stock BtS without engine evidence.

NUMBERING AFTER PROMOTION
-------------------------
F300 / KI#623 CONFIRMED.
F301 / provisional KI#624 remains UNUSED.
Queue 054 remains OPEN pending saturation.

OPEN-BORDERS CONTROL
--------------------
No ordinary shipped same-group reuse sequence has emerged across an Open Borders
state change. Sequential/simultaneous turn ordering, game-turn pathfinder reset,
group switching and final-path separation all make the abstract stale-cache
shape hard to reach normally. Keep this as a documented control unless a new
producer sequence is proven; do not allocate F301 merely because setOpenBorders
lacks an explicit pathfinder reset.

NEXT SATURATION WORK

  * inspect max-path and OPEN/CLOSED/reparent state invariants, folding any

  * close Open Borders as a control if no current same-group producer appears;
  * only then decide whether queue 054 closes with F300 as its sole finding or
    whether a genuinely independent F301 survives.

C027-WIP04 CONTINUATION — QUEUE 054 / GROUPPATHFINDER.CPP

CORRECTION TO THE EARLY MAX-PATH PRODUCER HYPOTHESIS
----------------------------------------------------
The initially suspected CvGameInterface sitePath sequence (broad city-site
search followed by a smaller goody-hut range using the same local finder) is
NOT a valid current producer and must not be used as evidence.

The first path-generation phase requires pHeadSelectedUnit->isFound(), whereas
the later goody phase requires the same head unit to canFight(). Current Settler
content is noncombat, so the two phases cannot populate/reuse the same finder in
that way. This is a rejected candidate/control.

A stronger defect was found that needs no prior cache reuse at all.

F301 / KI#624 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------
Title:
A cheaper over-limit route can overwrite a valid bounded route in
KmodPathFinder, causing generatePath to return false even though a path within
its requested max-turn limit exists.

ROOT / CONTRACT FAILURE
-----------------------
StepMetricBase documents m_iMaxPath as a hard search bound:

    KmodPathFinder will only consider paths of this length or shorter.

and explicitly says that KmodPathFinder, not the path-dependent step checker,
handles that length limit.

The implementation enforces the bound only incompletely:

  * processNode filters OPEN *parents* by
        node.getPathLength() <= m_stepMetric.getMaxPath();
  * processChild may expand a parent whose path length is exactly maxPath;
  * GroupStepMetric::updatePathData increments the child's path turns when that
    parent has zero moves, so the child can become maxPath+1;
  * processChild has no max-path check on that newly-computed child state;
  * if the child is the destination, m_pEndNode is set regardless of its new
    path length;
  * an existing destination/node can then be reparented to a cheaper route that
    has MORE path turns, again without checking the bound;
  * only after the search terminates does generatePath test
        m_pEndNode->getPathLength() <= maxPath.

The one-node-per-plot representation therefore optimizes cost across both
in-bound and out-of-bound routes, even though an out-of-bound route is not a
legal candidate for a bounded search. A cheaper illegal state can replace and
destroy the only stored legal state for the same plot.

CONCRETE CURRENT-SAS REPRODUCTION CLASS
---------------------------------------
Current shipped data contains a direct normal caller/unit combination:

  * UNIT_SELF_PROPELLED_ARTILLERY has iMoves=2, bPillage=1 and
    DefaultUnitAI=UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY.
  * AI_attackCityMove always includes MOVE_AVOID_ENEMY_WEIGHT_2 in eMoveFlags.
  * when a nearby target city is too strong and at step distance <=2, it calls
        AI_choke(1, false, eMoveFlags)
  * AI_choke scans enemy worked plots and calls
        generatePath(plot, eFlags, true, &iPathTurns, iRange)
    with iRange=1.

A minimal ordinary local state can therefore use one 2-move self-propelled
artillery (120 movement points), all relevant plots revealed, no defenders on
the candidate worked tile, and an established war/war plan.

Use these local coordinates solely to make the cost accounting deterministic:

    S = (10,10)  start, own plot, no route
    A = (11,10)  own plot, no route
    B = (12,11)  own plot, railroad
    D = (12,10)  enemy worked plot, railroad

D may be worked by the nearby too-strong target city at e.g. (11,8), which is
within two steps of S and can work D, while B remains a normal contested-border
own plot. Configure no other enemy-owned tile adjacent to B; other alternate
corridors can simply be impassable/blocked. D itself has no visible defender,
which is exactly the kind of plot AI_choke evaluates.

Current route data:
  * ordinary flat movement step = 60 points;
  * railroad iMovement=20, iFlatMovement=6;
  * for a baseMoves=2 unit, railroad-to-railroad movement therefore costs
        min(20, 6*2) = 12 points.

Current land heuristic weight for baseMoves=2 is 12:
  * minimum route movement cost after tech modifiers = 20;
  * minimum flat route value = 6;
  * minimumStepCost(2) = min(20, 2*6) = 12.

With current GroupPathFinder weights, no combat defenders, no defensive bonus
on Self-Propelled Artillery, and MOVE_AVOID_ENEMY_WEIGHT_2, the two routes are:

VALID <=1-turn route S -> A -> D
  S -> A:
    60*1024 movement + step/symmetry/no-route terms = 61,451.
  A -> D:
    consumes the remaining 60 movement points;
    base/symmetry = 61,450;
    +9 territory;
    +1,400 no-defensive-bonus end-turn defence preference;
    +280 enemy-territory aggregate defence preference;
    subtotal 63,139;
    ending the turn on an owned war-plan target applies WEIGHT_2 => 126,278.
  Total valid known cost = 187,729.
  D has pathTurns=1 and is a valid result for iMaxPath=1.

CHEAPER >1-turn route S -> A -> B -> D
  S -> A = 61,451.
  A -> B:
    consumes the remaining 60 movement points and ends turn on B;
    before enemy-adjacency weighting = 62,852;
    B is own territory but adjacent to D, an enemy wartime plot, so
    WEIGHT_2 adjacency applies *4/3 => 83,802 (integer arithmetic).
  B known cost = 145,253.
  B is adjacent to D and its A* total is 145,253 + 12,288 heuristic
    = 157,541, still well below the already-found valid D cost 187,729.
  B is therefore processed.
  B -> D:
    B has zero moves, so updatePathData begins turn 2;
    railroad movement costs only 12 points, leaving 108;
    because moves remain, none of the end-turn defence/enemy-avoid weighting is
    applied;
    exact step cost = 12,298.
  New D known cost = 157,551, strictly cheaper than 187,729.
  processChild therefore reparents D from the valid S-A-D route to S-A-B-D and
  updatePathData changes D from pathTurns=1 to pathTurns=2.

At that point the sole stored D node is cheaper but illegal for maxPath=1.
processNode excludes it because pathTurns=2; no alternative valid D state was
preserved. The final generatePath check sees 2>1 and returns FALSE.

Therefore the bounded caller can receive "no path within one turn" even though
the pathfinder itself had already found S-A-D within one turn.

CURRENT SHIPPED CONSEQUENCE
---------------------------
AI_choke is a live current bounded evaluator. In the configuration above the
candidate enemy worked plot is skipped at the generatePath test even though it
is genuinely reachable within the requested turn. This can change attack-city
stack choking/positioning decisions.

The root is broader than AI_choke: many current AI routines pass finite
max-turn limits to the same pathfinder. The exact reproduction above is enough
to establish shipped consequence; do not claim every bounded caller is affected
without its own state proof.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod:
  * practical 354 ("Wrote the K-Mod pathfinder, and enabled it") introduced the
    custom pathfinder/max-path design;
  * practical 355 enabled iMaxPath for the custom finder;
  * the original ProcessNode filters parents by m_iData2 <= iMaxPath but its
    child/reparent code never rejects a cheaper child state for exceeding the
    bound. It can therefore overwrite the destination exactly as above.
  * K-Mod also ships UNIT_MOBILE_ARTILLERY with 2 moves, UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY,
    pillaging enabled, MOVE_AVOID_ENEMY_WEIGHT_2 in attack-city movement, and
    the same AI_choke(1,false,...) call class.

Base AdvCiv 1.14:
  * retains the same generic max-path structure and the same 2-move Mobile
    Artillery / bounded attack-city caller class.
  * the later template/refactor work (including practical 2588) preserved this
    behavior rather than introducing the defect.

SAS:
  * inherits the algorithm. Self-Propelled Artillery is the current SAS
    counterpart with the same relevant 2-move attack-city/pillage role.
  * the only functional SAS-vs-Base edit in GroupPathFinder.cpp remains the
    already-present null-group guard; it is not causal.

BtS/Civ4CE:
  * supplied stock-style source uses the EXE FAStar pathfinder rather than this
    K-Mod custom implementation. Do not attribute the exact custom reparent bug
    to stock BtS/CE without engine evidence.

WHY THIS IS INDEPENDENT OF F300
-------------------------------
Both defects are exposed by cheaper-parent replacement, but they violate
separate contracts:

  F300: path-dependent legality (danger) can become false after path-state
        mutation and is not revalidated.
  F301: the generic hard path-length limit is not enforced when child/reparent
        state is committed, so an illegal >max state can replace a legal <=max
        state even when every step is otherwise valid.

F301 exists with no danger predicate at all. Keep separate numbering.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
A final `if (endNode.pathLength <= max)` cannot repair the root; that check is
already present and merely detects the corruption after the valid state has
been discarded.

At minimum, bounded legality must be checked prospectively BEFORE committing a
new/cheaper parent:
  * a new child whose candidate path length exceeds max must not become the
    stored goal/path state for this bounded search;
  * an existing valid node must not be reparented onto an over-limit cheaper
    path while destroying its old legal parent.

The generic design makes a robust patch subtler than a direct child guard:
forwardPropagate can change descendants' path lengths after an ancestor is
reparented. A descendant that was <=max can therefore become >max too. A safe
implementation needs either prospective subtree handling/rollback, conservative
subtree invalidation and rediscovery, or path state rich enough to retain
multiple cost/turn states for one plot. This overlaps the architectural pressure
seen in F300 but is a distinct max-bound invariant.

Do not prescribe a tiny patch until implementation review proves that it also
handles descendant propagation and preserves old still-valid bounded states.

POST-WIP04 SATURATION / CONTROLS
--------------------------------
1. Signed-int arithmetic has still not earned a finding. Ordinary movement is
   comfortably bounded by current XML. MOVE_ATTACK_STACK is the dominant large
   per-step term, but current reachable overflow still lacks a realistic producer
   and consequence. Keep "no saturation arithmetic" as technical debt unless a
   concrete shipped state proves otherwise.

2. The OPEN/CLOSED history pass strengthens F300 rather than creating a new root.
   If a previously processed/CLOSED node is reparented with changed moves/path
   data, forward propagation updates existing descendants but the parent is not
   reopened to reconsider adjacent children previously rejected by path-dependent
   danger. Fold this into F300's repair boundary: changed CLOSED state may require
   re-expansion, not merely direct-child revalidation.

3. The old canReuseInitialPathData warning about movement changes is not itself a
   current tech-bonus bug. A domain +move tech changes maxMoves(), therefore also
   movesLeft = maxMoves - movesUsed; the start-node reuse check sees the mismatch
   and resets.

4. Engineering/route-speed changes remain a stale-cache control, not a finding.
   Route movement cost can change without movesLeft changing, and processTech /
   changeRouteChange has no obvious pathfinder reset. However no normal current
   same-AI-group reuse sequence across that state transition has yet been proven.
   Human final movement uses the cleared execution finder. Do not allocate F302.

F302 CANDIDATE — iWorstMovesLeft overwritten by highest-cost unit
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Current GroupStepMetric::cost computes two logically distinct aggregates inside
FOR_EACH_UNIT_IN:

    iWorstMovesLeft = min(iWorstMovesLeft, iMovesLeft);

then, if this unit has the largest movement-cost contribution:

    if (iCost > iWorstCost)
    {
        iWorstCost = iCost;
        iWorstMovesLeft = iMovesLeft;
    }

The second assignment destroys the true minimum remaining movement whenever the
unit with the largest weighted movement cost is not the unit with the least
moves remaining. Yet the later `if (iWorstMovesLeft <= 0)` block is supposed to
mean "the GROUP ends its turn on kTo". updatePathData independently calculates
true group remaining moves and retains the minimum, so cost and path data can
classify the same node differently.

CURRENT-SAS NUMERIC STATE
-------------------------
Current UNIT_GERMAN_HUSSAR:
  * iMoves=3;
  * UNITCOMBAT_MOUNTED_RANGED;
  * DefaultUnitAI=UNITAI_ATTACK;
  * free PROMOTION_RETREAT1.
PROMOTION_RETREAT2 is available from Retreat I, and PROMOTION_MOBILITY_COST is
available from Retreat II to UNITCOMBAT_MOUNTED_RANGED; it supplies
`iMoveDiscountChange=1`.

On a terrain/feature step with nominal movement cost 3 and no route:
  * an ordinary 1-move unit pays its capped 60 points, has 0 left and movement
    weight 60*1024 = 61,440;
  * the 3-move Hussar with Mobility (Cost) reduces raw cost 3->2, pays 120 of
    180 points, has 60 left, and movement weight 120*1024 = 122,880.

If the exhausted slow member is encountered first, iWorstMovesLeft correctly
becomes 0. When the Hussar is then processed, its larger iCost wins and the code
incorrectly overwrites iWorstMovesLeft back to 60. The later end-turn block is
therefore skipped even though updatePathData correctly stores group moves=0.

ORDERING REACHABILITY — FIRST GATE PASSED
-----------------------------------------
This does NOT depend on arbitrary insertion order. CvSelectionGroup::addUnit
keeps m_units sorted descending by CvUnitAI::AI_groupFirstVal and then
AI_groupSecondVal. FOR_EACH_UNIT_IN walks that stored order from head to tail.

A normal 1-move siege unit assigned UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY with bombardRate>0 gets
AI_groupFirstVal() = 19. The German Hussar assigned UNITAI_ATTACK has withdrawal
and gets AI_groupFirstVal() = 14. Therefore the slow bombard siege unit is
naturally before the Hussar in the exact iteration order needed by the numeric
counterexample.

Current examples include 1-move Catapult/Trebuchet/Cannon-style attack-city
siege classes and the 3-move German Hussar. Still prove actual grouping behavior
rather than assuming any two compatible land units will normally share a group.

POTENTIAL CONSEQUENCE BOUNDARY
------------------------------
When the overwrite changes 0 -> positive, GroupStepMetric::cost skips the whole
end-turn section, including:
  * PATH_TERRITORY_WEIGHT;
  * feature/plot extra-cost damage weighting when enabled;
  * defense-position preferences;
  * enemy-territory aggregate defense penalties;
  * MOVE_AVOID_ENEMY_WEIGHT_2 / _3 ending-turn and adjacent-enemy multipliers.

This can therefore change route ordering substantially, not merely a tiny tie.
But F302 remains UNUSED until a normal current group/caller and actual route
choice/evaluation consequence are demonstrated, followed by ancestry comparison.

CORRECTION TO WIP05 F302 CANDIDATE
----------------------------------
The WIP05 numeric description omitted an important precondition. In
GroupStepMetric::cost:

    int const iMaxMoves = (iCurrMoves > 0 ? iCurrMoves : pGroupUnit->maxMoves());

Therefore mixed units do NOT receive their individual maxMoves while the parent
node still has positive GROUP moves; they all use the same iCurrMoves then. The
0 -> positive overwrite demonstrated below occurs specifically when the parent
node has group moves == 0, i.e. on the first step of a newly simulated turn.
That state is ordinary on any multi-turn mixed-stack path. The candidate survives
with that narrower and correct statement.

F302 / KI#625 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------
Title: GroupStepMetric::cost can erase the group's true minimum moves-left and
skip end-turn danger/defense costs for mixed-mobility stacks

CURRENT ROOT
------------
Current SAS does this inside the per-unit cost loop:

    iWorstMovesLeft = std::min(iWorstMovesLeft, iMovesLeft);

    ...

    if (iCost > iWorstCost)
    {
        iWorstCost = iCost;
        iWorstMovesLeft = iMovesLeft;
    }

The first assignment has group semantics: `iWorstMovesLeft` becomes the minimum
remaining movement of ANY member, which is what determines whether the GROUP
must end its turn on kTo. The second assignment silently changes the meaning to
the remaining movement of whichever member happens to have the largest weighted
movement cost.

Those need not be the same member. When a slow member is exhausted but a faster
member has a larger movement-cost contribution and still has movement left, the
second assignment changes `iWorstMovesLeft` from 0 back to a positive value.
The later `if (iWorstMovesLeft <= 0)` then skips every cost that is supposed to
apply when the group ends the turn on kTo.

`updatePathData` does not make this mistake. In the non-uniform-cost branch it
reconstructs the current turn separately for every unit and stores the minimum
remaining movement. Thus the path node can correctly say `moves == 0` while the
cost function that created that step has incorrectly treated it as a non-end-turn
step.

CURRENT NORMAL MIXED-GROUP STATE
--------------------------------
A current German Hussar is a particularly clear shipped exposure:
  * UNIT_GERMAN_HUSSAR has iMoves=3, DefaultUnitAI=UNITAI_ATTACK,
    UNITCOMBAT_MOUNTED_RANGED and free PROMOTION_RETREAT1;
  * PROMOTION_RETREAT2 is normally reachable from Retreat I;
  * PROMOTION_MOBILITY_COST is normally reachable from Retreat II for
    UNITCOMBAT_MOUNTED_RANGED and has iMoveDiscountChange=1.

A normal one-move bombard siege member such as a Catapult can lead the same
city-assault selection group. The required iteration order is NOT synthetic:
`CvSelectionGroup::addUnit` sorts members by descending `AI_groupFirstVal` and
then `AI_groupSecondVal`, and FOR_EACH_UNIT_IN walks that stored order.
  * bombard-capable UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY -> groupFirst 19;
  * ordinary UNITAI_ATTACK German Hussar -> groupFirst 14 with withdrawal,
    otherwise 13.
So the slow siege member naturally precedes the Hussar.

Nor is the mixed group itself script-only. UNITAI_ATTACK movement normally calls
`AI_omniGroup(UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY, ...)` in the relevant war movement logic and
can merge into a city-assault stack; the attack-city head retains the higher
priority after the merge.

EXACT MOVEMENT DIVERGENCE AT A SIMULATED TURN BOUNDARY
-------------------------------------------------------
At a parent node whose stored group moves are 0, consider moving onto a revealed
jungle hill without a usable incoming route. Current movement denominator is 60.
The feature costs 2 and hills add 1, so raw terrain cost is 3.

One-move siege:
  base/max movement = 60;
  regular cost caps at baseMoves=1 -> 60;
  moves left = 0;
  movement weight = 60 * 1024 = 61,440.

Three-move Hussar with Mobility Cost:
  raw terrain cost 3 -> 2 after iMoveDiscountChange=1;
  movement cost = 120;
  max movement = 180;
  moves left = 60;
  movement weight = 120 * 1024 = 122,880.

Iteration therefore does:
  1. slow siege: `iWorstMovesLeft` becomes 0;
  2. Hussar: its larger `iCost` wins and the nested assignment overwrites
     `iWorstMovesLeft` back to 60.

The path node produced by updatePathData correctly stores group moves=0.
GroupStepMetric::cost nevertheless behaves as if the group still has movement.

EXACT CURRENT ROUTE-CHOICE INVERSION
------------------------------------
This can reverse the A* path choice, not merely omit a cosmetic preference.
A legal local corridor can be built from ordinary map states; all non-corridor
exits may simply be impassable peaks. Shifted coordinates used for exact current
AI symmetry weights:

  current source S = (11,10)
  common boundary P = (10,10)

  dangerous branch:
    D1=(9,9) jungle hill, own railroad, adjacent to one enemy-at-war owned plot
    D2=(8,8) railroad
    T =(7,9) railroad destination

  safe branch:
    A=(9,11) ordinary flat, no route
    B=(8,11) railroad
    C=(7,10) railroad
    T=(7,9)

The graph geometry has no unintended cross-edge among the two branches; other
exits can be peaks. S->P is one ordinary common step that exhausts the 1-move
siege and gives P stored group moves=0. Thus the bug is live on the next step.
All plots are revealed and this is non-exploration AI movement.

Current exact constants used:
  PATH_MOVEMENT_WEIGHT=1024
  PATH_STEP_WEIGHT=7
  PATH_STRAIGHT_WEIGHT=2
  PATH_NOROUTE_WEIGHT=2
  PATH_DEFENSE_WEIGHT=7
  railroad movement=20, flat movement=6
  both example units can fight; with no defensive bonus on the relevant tile,
  the two-unit end-turn defense term is 1,400.

For P->D1:
  buggy movement + exact symmetry = 122,891;
  because the overwrite leaves `iWorstMovesLeft=60`, the entire end-turn block
  is skipped.

With the overwrite removed, the true group minimum remains 0:
  122,891 + 1,400 defense = 124,291;
  D1 is adjacent to one enemy-at-war owned plot and
  MOVE_AVOID_ENEMY_WEIGHT_2 applies 4/3;
  exact integer result = 165,721.

The two following railroad steps cost 18,444 each (movement plus exact current
symmetry), giving:
  BUGGY dangerous branch P->D1->D2->T = 159,779
  CORRECT dangerous branch             = 202,609

Safe branch exact current costs:
  P->A ordinary end-turn step = 62,852
  A->B ordinary end-turn step = 62,850
  B->C railroad step          = 18,444
  C->T railroad step          = 18,442
  total safe branch           = 162,588

Therefore current buggy code chooses the dangerous branch:
  159,779 < 162,588.
With correct group end-turn accounting it chooses the safe branch instead:
  162,588 < 202,609.

The common S->P prefix costs 62,850 and does not affect the inversion:
  full BUGGY dangerous path = 222,629
  full safe path            = 225,438
  full CORRECT dangerous    = 265,459.

The corresponding path lengths are 3 turns for the buggy dangerous route and
4 turns for the safe route. `updatePathData` supplies those turn counts using the
true group movement state.

CURRENT SHIPPED DECISION CONSEQUENCE
------------------------------------
This does not require claiming that the stack blindly follows the stale route on
a later turn. Current ATTACK_CITY AI consumes the result as an evaluator before
movement:

  * AI_attackCityMove uses MOVE_AVOID_ENEMY_WEIGHT_2 consistently in eMoveFlags;
  * it calls AI_pickTargetCity(eMoveFlags, ...);
  * AI_pickTargetCity scans candidate enemy cities with `generatePath` and the
    returned `iPathTurns`;
  * iPathTurns affects several target filters/strength calculations and, most
    directly, city score is divided by `8 + SQR(iPathTurns)`.

Thus the exact route inversion above changes one candidate from the correct
4-turn travel estimate to a buggy 3-turn estimate. The final denominator changes
from 24 to 17, a ~41% relative scoring swing before considering the other
path-turn-dependent branches. Two otherwise close city candidates can therefore
be ranked differently solely because the cost function failed to recognize that
one mixed-stack member ends its turn on D1.

This is a current AI decision consequence. Later mission movement can recalculate
its route; no claim of guaranteed unit death or guaranteed entry onto D1 is
needed or justified.

ANCESTRY / ORIGIN
-----------------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 still contains the same contradictory assignment in
GroupPathFinder.cpp. Current K-Mod 1.46 contains the same root in pathCost in
CvGameCoreUtils.cpp.

The local K-Mod history makes the origin unusually clear:

  * K-Mod practical 237 changed the path-cost unit selector from the old
    `iCost < iWorstCost` / minimum-cost logic to `iCost > iWorstCost`, retaining
    the coupled assignments of `iWorstCost` and `iWorstMovesLeft`.
  * K-Mod practical 238 then refactored movement accounting and explicitly added
    `iWorstMovesLeft = std::min(iWorstMovesLeft, iMovesLeft)` before the
    max-iCost selector, but retained the older nested
    `iWorstMovesLeft = iMovesLeft` inside that selector.

Practical 238 is therefore the clearest point where the present contradiction
became explicit: calculate the true group minimum, then overwrite it with the
moves of the highest-cost unit.

Stock BtS/Civ4CE has an older, materially different pathCost selection scheme;
the exact current root should be classified as inherited K-Mod behavior rather
than a Firaxis/Civ4CE defect. SAS movement/unit changes make a concrete exposure
easy to construct but did not introduce the code root.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Unlike F300/F301, this root appears locally repairable. The later end-turn block
needs the GROUP minimum, and that minimum has already been accumulated by:

    iWorstMovesLeft = std::min(iWorstMovesLeft, iMovesLeft);

`iWorstCost` independently needs the largest per-unit weighted movement cost.
There is no reason for selecting a new iWorstCost to change the already-computed
group minimum. The minimal candidate repair is therefore to remove only:

    iWorstMovesLeft = iMovesLeft;

from the `if (iCost > iWorstCost)` block.

Do not remove the preceding std::min accumulation. Current `iWorstMaxMoves` has
already been retired/commented out in AdvCiv, so no paired max-moves state needs
to be preserved in current SAS. A review/test should still compare path costs for
uniform groups, mixed 1-/3-move stacks on terrain and railroad, and AI avoid-enemy
routing before implementation is considered complete.

-------------
All promotion gates now pass:

  [x] Base/K-Mod ancestry and local historical origin;
