F303 / KI#626 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------
Title: GroupStepMetric::cost uses the group's minimum moves as every unit's
remaining moves and can invent premature end-turn penalties for mixed-speed
stacks

INDEPENDENCE FROM F302
----------------------
F302 is the nested assignment that destroys the true minimum after it has been
computed. Removing that one line does NOT fix this finding.

F303 occurs earlier. Whenever the parent node has positive group movement,
GroupStepMetric::cost does:

    int const iMaxMoves = (iCurrMoves > 0 ? iCurrMoves : pGroupUnit->maxMoves());

`iCurrMoves` is only the movement remaining to the SLOWEST / limiting group
member. It is not the actual remaining movement of every unit. Thus a faster
member can be evaluated as if it has far fewer moves left than it really has.

Current `updatePathData` explicitly knows that this shortcut is wrong for mixed
movement costs. Its non-uniform branch reconstructs the current turn for each
unit separately and stores the actual group minimum. The path node can therefore
carry correct movement/path-turn data while the cost function uses fictitious
per-unit movement state for the same step.

SIMPLE CURRENT RAILROAD EXPOSURE
--------------------------------
No special promotion is needed. A normal mixed stack containing:
  * a 1-move bombard siege member (e.g. Catapult), and
  * current UNIT_GERMAN_HUSSAR with iMoves=3
is enough. Such ATTACK units can normally merge into an ATTACK_CITY stack, as
already proven in the F302 grouping pass.

On current Railroad:
  * one-move unit: flat route cost min(20, 6*1) = 6 movement points;
  * three-move Hussar: flat route cost min(20, 6*3) = 18 movement points.
With full movement they have 60 and 180 points respectively, so BOTH can move
exactly ten railroad tiles in one turn.

`updatePathData` reconstructs that correctly.

But after each step the node stores only the group minimum, which is controlled
by the one-move unit: 54, 48, 42, 36, 30, 24, 18, 12, 6, 0.
`cost` reuses each of those values as the Hussar's own `iMaxMoves`.
Consequences in current cost:
  * on rail step 8, parent group moves=18; Hussar is falsely treated as having
    only 18, pays 18 and is computed at 0 although it actually has 54 before the
    step and 36 afterward;
  * step 9 starts from group moves=12, so Hussar movement weight is further
    reduced to 12*1024 even though its real step contribution remains 18*1024;
  * step 10 starts from group moves=6 and similarly uses only 6*1024.

Hence step 8 and 9 are falsely classified as group end-turn steps; step 10 is the
real end of the slow unit's turn. This remains true after the F302 overwrite is
removed because the per-unit `iMovesLeft` inputs themselves are already wrong.

EXACT CURRENT ROUTE INVERSION
-----------------------------
A current, ordinary railroad corridor can turn that approximation into the
opposite route choice. Non-corridor exits may be impassable peaks, so no synthetic
API behavior is needed.

Coordinates (all corridor plots are own revealed railroad):

Direct 9-step route:
  S=(10,10)
  (10,9) -> (10,8) -> (9,7) -> (10,6) -> (11,6) -> (12,7) ->
  (13,8) -> D=(14,9) -> T=(15,10)

Safe 11-step detour:
  S=(10,10)
  (11,11) -> (10,12) -> (9,12) -> (8,12) -> (9,13) -> (10,13) ->
  (11,12) -> (12,12) -> (13,12) -> (14,11) -> T=(15,10)

The two internal corridors have no cross-adjacency. Let D, the eighth direct
rail tile, be adjacent to three enemy-at-war owned off-corridor plots (they can
be owned peaks). The safe false-end tiles are not adjacent to enemy territory.
T is an own staging city. All other setup is ordinary and revealed.

Use current `AI_moveToStagingCity` flags: MOVE_AVOID_ENEMY_WEIGHT_3.
Exact current AI symmetry weights are included below.

TRUE PER-UNIT MOVEMENT COSTING:
  direct 9 rails, no real end turn yet = 165,992;
  safe 11 rails, with real end turn on rail 10 = 204,272.
So the intended movement/end-turn logic strongly prefers the 9-step direct path.
It reaches T in path turn 1 with 6 group movement points left.

CURRENT BUGGY COSTING:
  direct exact edge costs =
    18,442 + 18,441 + 18,444 + 18,444 + 18,440 + 18,446 + 18,445 +
    66,973 + 13,702
    = 209,777.

The 66,973 step is the falsely exhausted eighth railroad tile after the normal
1,400 two-unit defense end-turn term and three successive x3/2 adjacent-enemy
weights. The ninth step is also falsely treated as an end turn and, because the
shared group minimum is only 12, its movement component is underweighted.

  safe exact current edge costs =
    18,444 + 18,444 + 18,441 + 18,440 + 18,444 + 18,440 + 18,444 +
    19,841 + 13,698 + 7,558 + 18,446
    = 188,640.

Thus current code chooses the 11-step detour:
  188,640 < 209,777,
while correct per-unit state chooses the 9-step direct route:
  165,992 < 204,272.

CURRENT SHIPPED AI CONSEQUENCE
------------------------------
`AI_moveToStagingCity` is a normal current ATTACK_CITY path. It:
  * scans own cities;
  * calls `generatePath(city, MOVE_AVOID_ENEMY_WEIGHT_3, ..., &iPathTurns)`;
  * divides city value by `5 + iPathTurns`;
  * stores `getPathEndTurnPlot()` for the selected city;
  * pushes a group move with the same MOVE_AVOID_ENEMY_WEIGHT_3 flags.

`AI_attackCityMove` reaches AI_moveToStagingCity through several ordinary paths,
including while waiting for joiners and later staging/retreat logic.

For the concrete corridor:
  * correct direct route is pathTurns=1 and reaches staging city T this turn;
  * buggy selected detour is pathTurns=2 because its tenth railroad step really
    exhausts the slow unit and step 11 starts a new turn;
  * staging-city score is therefore divided by 7 instead of 6;
  * getPathEndTurnPlot returns the detour's tenth tile instead of T;
  * the mission push uses the same flags/path-cost rule, so the group can spend
    the turn following that longer detour and stop short of a city it could have
    reached during the current turn.

This is a direct current AI routing and decision consequence, not merely a
slightly inaccurate internal cost estimate.

ANCESTRY / HISTORY
------------------
Current K-Mod 1.46 has the same shared-parent-moves pathCost calculation. Base
AdvCiv 1.14 inherits it. Current SAS did not introduce this root.

K-Mod practical 1017 is particularly revealing. Its title is:
  "Fixed a BtS pathfinding bug which caused inaccurate path turns."
It changes pathAdd/update-path-data specifically because the old shared group
movement shortcut is wrong for groups where one unit has more moves and a higher
movement cost, explicitly naming mixed 1-/2-move railroad groups as the obvious
example. It reconstructs each unit's moves through the current turn to fix path
turns.

But practical 1017 does not make the equivalent correction in pathCost. Thus the
current finder has accurate path data from the K-Mod fix while its step-cost
function still reasons from the older shared-minimum approximation. AdvCiv later
ported/refactored both pieces without reconciling that mismatch.

Stock BtS/Civ4CE uses the older pathCost/pathAdd family; its path-data behavior is
materially different. The current mismatch is best classified as an inherited
K-Mod incomplete-fix boundary rather than a SAS regression.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
This is not safely repaired by only changing an end-turn `if` or by F302's
one-line deletion. The cost function also underweights the fast unit's movement
component on later railroad steps (12*1024, 6*1024 in the example). It needs the
actual per-unit movement available at kFrom.

The information cannot in general be recovered from `iCurrMoves` alone; that node
field intentionally stores only the group's minimum. A robust repair therefore
needs one of:
  * reconstruct each unit's movement since the current turn boundary, sharing or
    refactoring the non-uniform logic already used by updatePathData;
  * cache sufficient per-unit/current-turn state in path nodes; or
  * restructure processChild so cost can evaluate against prospective exact path
    data without breaking reparent handling.

Be careful with the third option: for an existing node being considered through a
new parent, its currently stored path data belongs to the OLD parent until after
`iNewCost` wins. Simply reading kChild's existing moves from cost would therefore
be wrong for reparent candidates.

Performance matters because GroupStepMetric::cost is hot. A practical repair may
want a fast uniform-cost path and only reconstruct when group members' movement
costs/max movement can diverge, analogous to updatePathData's existing fast path.

F303 DECISION
-------------
All finding gates pass:
  [x] exact independent source invariant;
  [x] ordinary current mixed-speed group with no special promotion required;
  [x] exact railroad movement-state divergence;
  [x] exact current route-cost inversion;
  [x] current ATTACK_CITY staging caller with changed pathTurns/end-turn plot;
  [x] Base/K-Mod ancestry and the upstream incomplete-fix history;
  [x] repair boundary distinguished from F302.

Promote as F303 / KI#626.

POST-WIP07 SATURATION / CONTROL LEDGER
--------------------------------------
No new finding is allocated in this checkpoint. The following candidates were
challenged specifically to avoid manufacturing F304.

1. SIGNED-INT PATH-COST OVERFLOW — OPEN BUT CURRENTLY WEAK
----------------------------------------------------------
The ordinary movement terms are far below signed-int range. MOVE_ATTACK_STACK is
the dominant one-step term: at the current attack-ratio floor its raw combat-ratio
penalty is on the order of 2.4 million before the remaining step terms. Even eight
successive MOVE_AVOID_ENEMY_WEIGHT_3 adjacent-enemy multipliers leave a worst
single step on the order of 60 million, below INT_MAX.

Cumulative known-cost overflow is mathematically possible after many such extreme
steps, because the generic finder stores known/total costs in signed int and does
not saturate addition. That is not yet a current finding: the proof currently
requires a long succession of maximally hostile / defended enemy plots. The live
MOVE_ATTACK_STACK producers are being checked for iMaxPath bounds and practical
search topology before deciding whether this is reachable enough to matter.

2. ENGINEERING / ROUTE-SPEED CACHE INVALIDATION — CONTROL SO FAR
----------------------------------------------------------------
Engineering changes road movement cost through processTech -> changeRouteChange
without changing a group's current movesLeft value and without an obvious direct
GroupPathFinder reset. In isolation this is a real cache-generation blind spot:
canReuseInitialPathData watches start/group movement state rather than global
route-speed generation.

Two plausible same-turn triggers were tested and rejected:

* Goody-hut Engineering:
  Engineering can receive goody research in current SAS and can in principle be
  completed from the hut when sufficiently close to completion. However, the unit
  must first MOVE onto the hut. The next reusable group-path call therefore has a
  different start plot, which makes setGroup / initial-data reuse reset the node
  tree. Execution movement also uses the always-cleared alternate finder.

* Pillaging a route:
  AI pillaging can execute synchronously and return to AI_update while the group
  remains on the same plot, so this is a better world-mutation shape. But pillage
  consumes one full movement denominator. On the next reusable-path call the
  cached start-node moves no longer equal the group's actual moves, and
  canReuseInitialPathData resets the node tree.

Thus the abstract invalidation gap remains documented, but neither current trigger
produces a stale same-group/same-start/same-moves reuse sequence. No F304.

3. EXPLICIT HEURISTIC-WEIGHT REUSE — CURRENT-CALLER CONTROL
-----------------------------------------------------------
KmodPathFinder::setGroup does not compare iHeuristicWeight when deciding whether
cached nodes may remain, and generatePath only recomputes OPEN-node heuristics when
the destination changes. A hypothetical same-group/same-destination caller that
changes only the explicit heuristic weight could therefore retain stale heuristic
values.

Current call-site sweep does not expose that API weakness:
  * explicit non-default weights are used with freshly constructed/local or
    always-cleared finders and remain constant for that finder;
  * the reusable AI GroupPathFinder uses the default derived heuristic.

So this is generic future-mod/API debt, not a shipped F304.

4. setGroup MUTABLE-INPUT LEDGER
--------------------------------
The four important mutable dimensions have now been challenged independently:
  * group identity / start data — normal reset/reuse boundary works, including the
    current SAS KI#475 membership invalidations;
  * move flags — relevant semantic changes are either stripped because the metric
    does not consume them, trigger reset, or (MOVE_DECLARE_WAR special case) are
    safe under current OWN_EXCLUSIVE_RADIUS=0 configuration;
  * max path — NOT safe; this is already F301;
  * explicit heuristic weight — generic API weakness, but current callers safe as
    described above.

5. DESTINATION / CLOSED DEAD-END BEHAVIOR — INTENTIONAL CONTROL
---------------------------------------------------------------
A node that was CLOSED because it could not be used as an intermediate step may
later be attached when that same plot becomes the destination. This initially
looks suspicious, but it matches the interface split:
  * canStepThrough controls intermediate traversal;
  * isValidDest is freshly checked for the requested destination.
The destination may therefore legally be entered even when traversal beyond it is
forbidden. No finding.

6. DECLARATION-OF-WAR WORLD MUTATION — RESET PRESENT
----------------------------------------------------
Actual declaration of war explicitly resets the global selection-group pathfinder
before post-DOW pathing. Therefore the most important diplomacy transition that
changes enemy-territory legality/cost does not preserve stale reusable nodes.
The earlier Open-Borders invalidation theory remains an architectural control but
still lacks a normal same-group reuse sequence.

7. OPEN/CLOSED / FORWARD-PROPAGATION FOLLOW-UP
----------------------------------------------
The generic finder explicitly admits that forwardPropagate can produce a POSITIVE
cost delta in descendants even though the reparented node itself received a
cheaper parent. Path-history-dependent end-turn / defensive / territorial costs
can make a descendant's continuation worse under the new movement state.

This is being challenged as a possible deeper plot-only-state compression issue:
reparenting one plot discards its old movement/path-history state, and descendants
are recomputed only through the retained child tree rather than reopening every
alternative edge. For danger legality, this is already part of F300's repair
boundary. It should NOT receive F304 unless an independent current cost/result
failure can be demonstrated without relying on F300 or F303.

NEXT CURSOR
-----------
F304 / provisional KI#627 remains UNUSED.
Continue:
  * bound every live MOVE_ATTACK_STACK producer before closing overflow;
  * try to prove or reject an independent positive-forward-propagation / plot-state
    result failure using current GroupStepMetric values and a shipped caller;
  * finish remaining K-Mod/AdvCiv history and arithmetic/sentinel checks;
  * merge any shared-movement consequences into F302/F303 rather than duplicating;
  * only then decide queue-054 saturation/closure.

No repository source files modified.

F304 / KI#627 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------
Title: MOVE_DECLARE_WAR route simulation ignores only the destination endpoint,
so pre-war AI pathing can count a future-enemy route when moving OUT of enemy
territory and underestimate invasion travel time

ROOT / EXACT SOURCE DEFECT
--------------------------
AdvCiv practical 4277 (`aa6bef8e31`, title "AI war-declaring moves anticipate
loss of Open Borders") added `bIgnoreRoutes` to GroupStepMetric::cost and
updatePathData so that a path computed before a declaration of war would not rely
on the prospective enemy's roads.

Current SAS / Base AdvCiv cost logic decides this only from `kTo`:

    TeamTypes const eToPlotTeam = kTo.getTeam();
    bool const bIgnoreRoutes = ((eFlags & MOVE_DECLARE_WAR) &&
            eToPlotTeam != NO_TEAM &&
            GET_TEAM(eTeam).AI_isSneakAttackReady(eToPlotTeam));

and then passes that single bool to:

    kTo.movementCost(*pGroupUnit, kFrom, false, bIgnoreRoutes)

The same destination-only rule is used by updatePathData, both in the uniform
cost path and in its per-unit reconstruction loop.

But CvPlot::movementCost can use a route only when BOTH endpoints have a valid
route:

    if (kFrom.isValidRoute(&kUnit, ...) &&
        isValidRoute(&kUnit, ...) &&
        ... && !bIgnoresRoute)

Before war, a prospective enemy's route can still be valid through Open Borders.
Therefore a step whose FROM plot belongs to the future war target but whose TO
plot belongs to a friendly / neutral-access team is not ignored by advc.001t.
The route segment is counted cheaply even though the FROM endpoint becomes an
enemy route immediately after the very DOW that MOVE_DECLARE_WAR is simulating.

This is directional: target-owned kTo is handled; target-owned kFrom is not.

SIMPLE CURRENT ONE-MOVE REPRODUCTION
------------------------------------
No SAS-only unit or unusual promotion is needed. Current Catapult, Trebuchet and
Cannon are 1-move UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY defaults, and ordinary attack-city stacks
can consist entirely of 1-move non-enemy-route land units.

Use a normal revealed road corridor:

    S -> E -> N -> C

where:
  * E is owned by prospective war target team A and has a Road;
  * N is a routed plot owned by us or a third party whose route is currently
    usable to us;
  * C is the target city of team A;
  * the team is sneak-attack ready against A;
  * the path is evaluated before war with MOVE_DECLARE_WAR;
  * no unit in the group has isEnemyRoute().

Current Road movement is 30 movement points before Engineering; one base land
move is 60 movement points.

PRE-DOW PATHFINDER ESTIMATE:
  1. S -> E:
     kTo is target-owned A, so bIgnoreRoutes=true. Ordinary movement consumes the
     full 60. Stored group moves become 0. Path turn 1 ends at E.

  2. E -> N:
     kTo is not A, so bIgnoreRoutes=false. Before war, E's A-owned route is still
     valid under current diplomatic access and N's route is valid too. movementCost
     therefore uses the Road cost 30. A new simulated turn starts with 60 and
     leaves 30 movement.

  3. N -> C:
     kTo is target-owned A, so bIgnoreRoutes=true. Ordinary movement cost is 60;
     the remaining 30 are exhausted/clamped to 0, but the step still belongs to
     the same simulated turn. Pathfinder result: C is reached in PATH TURN 2.

POST-DOW REAL MOVEMENT:
  * AI_considerPathDOW declares war before the group executes the invasion path;
  * after war, E is enemy-owned;
  * for ordinary units `CvPlot::isValidRoute` now rejects E's route;
  * E -> N therefore costs the full 60 and consumes all of turn 2;
  * N -> C cannot occur until turn 3.

Thus the exact pre-war route evaluation says 2 turns for a path that becomes
3 turns as soon as its predicted DOW actually occurs.

This is not merely a different aesthetic path preference. It directly violates
the stated purpose of practical 4277: anticipating the loss of Open Borders in
war-declaring movement.

CURRENT SHIPPED PRODUCER
------------------------
CvUnitAI::AI_attackCityMove builds:

    MOVE_AVOID_ENEMY_WEIGHT_2 |
    (bReadyToAttack ? (MOVE_ATTACK_STACK | MOVE_DECLARE_WAR) : 0)

for a ready city-assault stack and passes those flags to AI_pickTargetCity.
AI_pickTargetCity considers players whose teams satisfy `AI_mayAttack`, including
prospective targets before the actual DOW, and calls generatePath with those
flags.

Therefore the exact pre-war state above is a normal current evaluator path, not a
script/force-only call.

CURRENT DECISION CONSEQUENCE
----------------------------
AI_pickTargetCity consumes `iPathTurns` repeatedly:
  * AI_cityTargetStrengthByPath(..., iPathTurns);
  * visible-defense radius/logic changes with path time;
  * the `iPathTurns > 2` enough-offence-en-route branch changes exactly across
    this 2 -> 3 error;
  * most directly, final city target value is divided by:

        8 + SQR(iPathTurns)

A false 2-turn estimate uses denominator 12. The real 3-turn post-DOW route uses
17. Holding the preceding factors equal, the bad estimate therefore values that
city by 17/12 ~= 1.417 times the intended distance-adjusted value: about 41.7%
higher.

This is enough to change which prospective enemy city a ready assault stack
selects.

POST-DOW REPATH DOES NOT REPAIR TARGET SELECTION
------------------------------------------------
AI_goToTargetCity later calls AI_considerPathDOW. If that declares war, the code
explicitly regenerates the movement path after the DOW but comments:

    "but don't bother recalculating the best destination"

So execution can discover the slower post-war route only AFTER AI_pickTargetCity
has already ranked/selected the target using the underestimated pre-war path
turns. Repathing movement does not undo the target-selection consequence.

ANCESTRY / HISTORY
------------------
K-Mod's generic pathfinder does not contain this anticipatory enemy-route
suppression at all; it has the broader older pre-DOW route-assumption behavior.

AdvCiv practical 4277 (`aa6bef8e31`, 2025-01-10 in the reachable history) added:
  * the bIgnoreRoutes parameter to CvPlot::movementCost;
  * the destination-team-only route suppression in GroupStepMetric::cost;
  * matching destination-team-only suppression in updatePathData;
  * post-DOW path regeneration changes in AI_goToTargetCity.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains that exact destination-only implementation. Current SAS
inherits it. The precise F304 root is therefore best classified as an incomplete
Base AdvCiv repair of the older K-Mod behavior, not a SAS regression.

SAS-SPECIFIC REPAIR AMPLIFIER: `isEnemyRoute`
----------------------------------------------
Practical 4277 left this source comment:

    "Not bothering with CvUnit::isEnemyRoute. AI won't have a DoW group of those."

That assumption is no longer safe in current SAS.

Current `PROMOTION_LOGISTICS`:
  * has `<bEnemyRoute>1`;
  * requires only Combat I OR City Raider I;
  * has TechPrereq TECH_THE_WHEEL;
  * is available to UNITCOMBAT_GUN (among other combat classes).

Current Musketman, for example, is UNITCOMBAT_GUN and explicitly allows
UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY. Current promotion AI valuation also gives an enemy-route
promotion +20 value for UNITAI_ATTACK and UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY.

CvPlot::isValidRoute itself says:

    if (!isOwned() || pUnit->isEnemyRoute())
        return true;

Thus current SAS really can produce prospective-DOW attack-city units whose enemy
route remains usable after war.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
A naive patch such as:

    ignore routes if futureEnemy(kFrom) || futureEnemy(kTo)

would fix the ordinary-unit underestimation above, but it would create the
opposite error for Logistics / other `isEnemyRoute()` units that legitimately can
use those routes after war.

The robust semantic question is per UNIT and per ENDPOINT:

  "Would this unit be able to use the route on BOTH kFrom and kTo after the
   prospective MOVE_DECLARE_WAR diplomacy transition?"

Both GroupStepMetric::cost and updatePathData must use the same simulated
post-DOW rule. In particular, updatePathData's non-uniform per-unit reconstruction
must not use one group-global ignore bool if units in a mixed stack differ in
`isEnemyRoute()` capability.

A repair should preferably centralize the predicted-post-DOW route-validity rule
so path cost and movement/path-turn reconstruction cannot diverge. It should test:
  * ordinary non-enemy-route units crossing A -> friendly/third-party routes;
  * ordinary entry into A territory;
  * Logistics/isEnemyRoute units;
  * mixed groups where only some members have enemy-route access;
  * one-move and multi-move groups;
  * post-DOW regenerated path turns against pre-DOW MOVE_DECLARE_WAR estimates.

F304 DECISION
-------------
All promotion gates now pass:
  [x] exact endpoint-asymmetric source defect;
  [x] ordinary current 1-move attack-city stack state;
  [x] exact 2-turn pre-DOW vs 3-turn post-DOW reproduction;
  [x] current MOVE_DECLARE_WAR producer before target selection;
  [x] direct current target-value/path-strength consequence;
  [x] post-DOW movement repath shown not to recompute target selection;
  [x] precise K-Mod -> AdvCiv practical 4277 -> Base 1.14 -> SAS ancestry;
  [x] repair boundary checked against current SAS Logistics/isEnemyRoute.

Promote as F304 / KI#627.

POST-WIP08 SATURATION CONTROLS / CORRECTIONS
--------------------------------------------
1. Signed-int path-cost overflow remains UNNUMBERED.
   One extreme MOVE_ATTACK_STACK step remains below INT_MAX. Cumulative overflow
   lacks saturation protection in principle, and unbounded target-city searches
   exist, but a current construction still requires pathological chains of
   maximally overdefended / enemy-adjacent plots or absurd group-strength totals.
   That is insufficient for F305 under the current audit standard.

2. Positive forwardPropagate / plot-only path-state compression remains bounded
   as known upstream debt unless a sharper independent current failure is found.
   K-Mod source already acknowledges that a cheaper reparent can make descendant
   continuation cost increase; current AdvCiv documentation likewise records
   remaining path-data-dependent / cache-order suboptimality. Danger legality is
   already inside F300's repair boundary; hard max-path overwrite is F301; mixed
   movement cost errors are F302/F303. Do not duplicate these as F305.

3. Engineering route-speed stale-cache theory remains a control. Goody completion
   changes the start plot before reuse; pillaging changes moves-left before reuse.
   Neither preserves the required same-group/same-start/same-moves stale tree.

4. Explicit heuristic-weight reuse remains generic API debt only. Current reusable
   AI finder calls do not change only the heuristic weight for the same cached
   group/destination.

C027-WIP11 ADDENDUM -- QUEUE 054 `GroupPathFinder.cpp`
F305 / KI#628 CONFIRMED -- CORRECTED PRODUCER/DESTINATION PROOF

CORRECTION TO THE SUPERSEDED WIP10 PROOF
----------------------------------------
WIP10 used an unrevealed sea destination D when describing AI_explore as the
current producer. That destination shape is NOT valid for CvUnitAI::AI_explore:
AI_plotValid on DOMAIN_SEA calls CvUnit::isRevealedValidDomain, which returns
false for an unrevealed plot. Therefore the WIP10 producer wording was too broad.

Do not use WIP10's unrevealed-D reproduction as the durable F305 proof.

The underlying heuristic defect survives without that assumption. The corrected
current producer uses a REVEALED sea destination at the explored/fog boundary and
unrevealed intermediate water on the cheaper alternative route. The full exact
A* failure remains and is documented below.

F305 / KI#628 -- SEA-EXPLORER HEURISTIC OVERSTATES DISCOUNTED FOG STEPS,
SO A* CAN TERMINATE ON A MORE EXPENSIVE REVEALED-WATER PATH
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: CONFIRMED
CLASSIFICATION: inherited K-Mod pathfinder defect; present in Base AdvCiv 1.14
and current SAS. K-Mod practical 1188 made the pre-existing full-denominator sea
heuristic inadmissible when it introduced the 2/3 exploration discount.

ROOT
----
GroupPathFinder::setGroup chooses the default sea heuristic weight as one full
movement denominator:

    if (kGroup.getDomainType() == DOMAIN_SEA)
        iHeuristicWeight = GC.getMOVE_DENOMINATOR(); // 60

GroupStepMetric::heuristicCost therefore estimates:

    stepDistance * PATH_MOVEMENT_WEIGHT * 60

or 61,440 per remaining geometric step at PATH_MOVEMENT_WEIGHT=1024.

GroupStepMetric::cost, however, applies K-Mod's exploration modifier to every
step whose DESTINATION is unrevealed when the group is AUTOMATE_EXPLORE or an AI
UNITAI_EXPLORE / UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA group:

    iExploreModifier = 2; // thirds
    ...
    iCost = (iCost * iExploreModifier) / 3;

CvPlot::movementCost deliberately returns one movement denominator (60) for an
unrevealed destination when the pathfinder does not assume revelation. Therefore
an ordinary sea-explorer step into fog has movement component:

    60 * 1024 * 2 / 3 = 40,960

plus small positive step/symmetry/no-route terms. The heuristic still assumes
61,440 for the same geometric step. It overestimates future path cost by roughly
50% on such steps and is inadmissible.

KmodPathFinder::processNode relies on admissibility for early stopping. Once the
destination has a finite known cost it processes only OPEN nodes satisfying:

    node.m_iKnownCost + node.m_iHeuristicCost < destination.m_iKnownCost

An overestimated heuristic can therefore hide a cheaper path behind an OPEN node
and cause the search to terminate on a more expensive route.

CURRENT LIVE SEA-EXPLORER CONTENT
---------------------------------
Current SAS explicitly permits UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA for:
  * UNIT_GALLEY -- 3 moves;
  * UNIT_GALLEON -- 4 moves;
  * UNIT_TRIREME -- 3 moves;
  * UNIT_FRIGATE -- 5 moves;
  * UNIT_DESTROYER -- 8 moves;
  * UNIT_ATTACK_SUBMARINE -- 6 moves.

Thus the discounted cost is live in normal AI naval exploration.

CORRECTED EXACT CURRENT GALLEY COUNTEREXAMPLE
---------------------------------------------
Use one ordinary unpromoted 3-move Galley with UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA. No enemies,
features, routes or special movement modifiers are required. Use ordinary
zero-defence unowned water.

Choose start S=(10,20) and REVEALED water destination D=(40,20) on a sufficiently
wide local region. D is an exploration-edge plot: at least one adjacent detour
water tile remains unrevealed, so AI_explore can give D exploration value even
though D itself is revealed.

Provide two cardinal water corridors:

Direct corridor:
  * 30 eastward water steps along y=20;
  * every direct tile, including D, is revealed.

Detour corridor:
  * S -> (10,19) -> (10,18);
  * east along y=18 to (40,18);
  * then (40,19) -> D;
  * 34 total steps;
  * the first 15 detour tiles are revealed;
  * the deeper middle/far detour tiles are unrevealed;
  * D itself is revealed.

All steps are cardinal, so the sea-isthmus diagonal restriction is irrelevant.
The two horizontal corridors are two rows apart. The exact simulation also
included their normal diagonal adjacency at the vertical arms; those extra
neighbors do not rescue the search.

The first unrevealed detour tile is (24,18), Chebyshev distance 14 from S. A
3-move sea unit has:

    AI_searchRange(4) = 4 * baseMoves = 12

so the local region through distance 13 can already be explored and
AI_exploreSeaMove's earlier AI_exploreRange(4) pass can legitimately find nothing
new before the later map-wide AI_explore call. This is compatible with normal
current visibility; the proof does not require fog adjacent to the Galley.

Exact current GroupStepMetric totals are:

    direct 30-step fully-revealed corridor = 1,857,620
    detour 34-step partly-fog corridor      = 1,727,738

The longer detour is cheaper by 129,882 according to the pathfinder's OWN metric.

A* ORDER / EARLY-STOP FAILURE
-----------------------------
The first detour node is revealed, with:

    known g     = 61,450
    heuristic h = 30 * 61,440 = 1,843,200
    total f     = 1,904,650

The direct corridor OPEN nodes stay below that. The largest f-cost of a direct
node before D is only 1,856,200.

The custom pathfinder therefore expands the full direct corridor first. It then
discovers D through that route at known cost 1,857,620. At the next processNode,
the destination cost becomes the stopping ceiling. The first detour node is still
OPEN at f=1,904,650, which is above the ceiling, so the search terminates without
expanding any detour node.

A direct simulation of current KmodPathFinder processNode/processChild behavior on
this exact corridor graph produced:

    returned destination known cost = 1,857,620
    returned route length           = 30 steps
    direct nodes processed          = 30
    detour nodes processed          = 0
    first detour node state         = OPEN

Yet independently evaluating the valid detour with the same current cost function
gives 1,727,738.

This is a direct A* optimality failure, not tie-breaking and not merely a different
path-turn preference.

CURRENT PRODUCER
----------------
CvUnitAI::AI_exploreSeaMove is the normal move routine for UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA.
It tries AI_exploreRange(4) and later AI_explore.

AI_explore only path-targets sea plots accepted by AI_plotValid; for DOMAIN_SEA
that means a revealed-valid-domain destination. The corrected D satisfies that.
D also has exploration value because an adjacent water plot remains unrevealed.
The ordinary 1-in-4 sampling gate for otherwise non-goody explore candidates can
therefore cause AI_explore to call generatePath(D, AI_exploreFlags(), ...).

For an AI UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA head, GroupStepMetric::cost automatically applies the
2/3 modifier on the unrevealed intermediate detour steps. Thus the corrected
revealed-D state is a current shipped producer of the faulty A* comparison.

CURRENT EXECUTION CONSEQUENCE
-----------------------------
If D is selected as the exploration target, AI_explore queues MISSION_MOVE_TO D.
CvSelectionGroup::groupPathTo does not trust/reuse the evaluator tree; it obtains
the CLEARED alternate GroupPathFinder, sets the same group/flags, and generates a
fresh execution path.

That fresh finder receives the same default sea heuristic and reproduces the same
optimality failure. At the current state it therefore chooses the 1,857,620
revealed corridor instead of the 1,727,738 partly-fog corridor that
GroupStepMetric itself says is preferable.

Subsequent movement can reveal new tiles and trigger later replanning, but the
current path/next-step decision has already been made from a nonminimum route. In
addition, AI_explore uses the path turns returned by this nonminimum tree in its
target-value denominator, so the defect can affect target ranking as well as route
selection.

ANCESTRY / HISTORY
------------------
K-Mod practical 366 (`f6aac75c78`) introduced XML-derived admissible heuristic
weights. Sea groups retained one full movement denominator:

    iHeuristicWeight = GC.getMOVE_DENOMINATOR();

with an assumption only about no sea roads / no promotions reducing sea movement
cost. At that point K-Mod had not yet added this exploration discount.

K-Mod practical 1188 (`caebff59e1`), titled:

    "Adjusted pathfinding cost for exploring units."

later introduced `iExploreModifier = 2` for unrevealed exploration steps and
multiplied path movement cost by it. It simultaneously standardized unrevealed
CvPlot movement cost to one denominator so pathCost could apply the weighting.
It did NOT lower/rederive the already-existing sea heuristic.

Current K-Mod retains both pieces. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the same
combination. Therefore practical 1188 is the precise inherited root: a legitimate
new cost reduction broke the heuristic lower-bound invariant.

The current generic StepMetricBase comment explicitly warns that the custom
pathfinder may not cope with an inadmissible heuristic. F305 provides an exact
current case where early stopping indeed returns a nonminimum path.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Under current SAS rules there are no sea routes and no promotion that reduces raw
water movement cost. A sea-explorer fog step can therefore have movement weight
as low as:

    60 * 2 / 3 = 40

before positive small weights. The default heuristic for an exploring sea group
must be <= 40 per geometric step to preserve admissibility.

Safe approaches include:
  * conservative/simple: use 40 as the default sea heuristic weight for ALL sea
    groups. This sacrifices some search efficiency for non-explorers but avoids
    mode-transition/cache complications;
  * role-sensitive: use 40 for AUTOMATE_EXPLORE / AI UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA and 60
    otherwise, but then changing the derived heuristic weight on a reused finder
    must force reset/recalculation. Queue-054 saturation already proved that a
    same-destination generatePath call does not automatically recompute cached OPEN
    heuristics merely because m_stepMetric receives a different weight.

Any future sea route or sea movement-cost discount must be included in the lower
bound as well.

F305 DECISION
-------------
All promotion gates pass after the destination correction:
  [x] exact sea heuristic-overestimate invariant violation;
  [x] live current UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA units;
  [x] realistic revealed sea destination accepted by AI_plotValid;
  [x] nearest fog placed beyond the earlier AI_exploreRange(4) search boundary;
  [x] exact all-cardinal current cost counterexample;
  [x] direct simulation of current A* returning the more expensive path;
  [x] current AI_explore producer;
  [x] fresh execution finder uses the same faulty heuristic;
  [x] K-Mod practical 366 -> 1188 ancestry;
  [x] Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the defect;
  [x] repair boundary checked against heuristic-weight cache behavior.

F305 / KI#628 remains CONFIRMED.

POST-F305 SATURATION CONTROLS
-----------------------------
1. Land exploration does not share this current lower-bound failure. The land
   heuristic uses the globally conservative route-derived minimum step cost
   (railroad-scale), far below a 2/3 unrevealed normal-terrain movement step.

2. AdvCiv's OWN_EXCLUSIVE_RADIUS flip modifier is another cost-reducing modifier,
   but the feature is disabled in current SAS. Its revealed-tile branch is also
   mutually exclusive with the unrevealed-explorer branch. No current F306 from
   that feature.

3. GroupPathFinder::getPathEndTurnPlot is release-unsafe if called without a valid
   m_pEndNode because it dereferences before its later null assertion. Current
   shipped C++ callers sampled in this saturation pass are guarded by successful
   generatePath paths, and current shipped Python contains no use of the exposed
   wrapper. Keep as API robustness debt unless a current unguarded producer is
   proven.

CONTROL 1 — MOVE_SAFE_TERRITORY / MOVE_NO_ENEMY_TERRITORY DESTINATION EXCEPTION
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current GroupStepMetric::canStepThrough applies MOVE_SAFE_TERRITORY and
MOVE_NO_ENEMY_TERRITORY to plots that are treated as intermediate/transit plots.
GroupStepMetric::isValidDest does not repeat those tests and instead validates the
final plot through canMoveOrAttackInto (plus the separate destination danger and
area rules).

That shape initially looked like a possible policy leak: a plot forbidden as an
intermediate can still be accepted when it is the destination. The deeper contract
and ancestry pass instead support intentional transit semantics:

* KmodPathFinder StepMetricBase explicitly specifies that canStepThrough should
  check whether a plot can be entered assuming it is NOT the destination, whereas
  destination validity is a separate isValidDest contract. The same distinction is
  important for cross-destination node caching.
* Stock BtS's legacy path-validity design applies these movement flags from the
  source/intermediate side of a step and keeps pathDestValid separate. K-Mod and
  AdvCiv preserve that conceptual split.
* Current AdvCiv's CvUnitAI::AI_settleMove source comment describes the old BtS
  MOVE_SAFE_TERRITORY behavior as preventing "passage through foreign (open)
  borders". That wording describes transit, not a hard final-destination ownership
  rule.
* K-Mod/current exploration deliberately combines MOVE_NO_ENEMY_TERRITORY with
  ordinary destination evaluation. Its diplomacy fixes focus on avoiding accidental
  declarations while traversing toward a target; they do not establish a rule that
  a combat-capable explorer already at war may never finish a move on an empty
  enemy-owned endpoint.

Therefore the endpoint exception is internally consistent with the inherited
movement-flag contract. Do not "fix" it merely because the flag name sounds global.
No F306.

CONTROL 2 — getPathEndTurnPlot RELEASE NULL ROBUSTNESS
------------------------------------------------------
Current AdvCiv/SAS GroupPathFinder::getPathEndTurnPlot starts with:

    GroupPathNode* pNode = m_pEndNode;
    FAssert(pNode->getPathLength() == 1 || pNode->m_pParent != NULL);

so a caller that invokes the accessor without a successful path can dereference
NULL in a release build before the later pNode != NULL assertion/check loop.
K-Mod's older pointer-return implementation was more forgiving because its first
assert guarded `!node` and its return expression could yield NULL.

This is genuine API-hardening debt, but the shipped-consequence gate has not been
met:

* Current shipped Python contains no call to the exposed getPathEndTurnPlot
  wrapper.
* Current C++ call sites sampled in the full sweep are inside successful
  generatePath branches, boolean-success conditions, or loops whose candidate was
  admitted only after generatePath succeeded.
* getFinalMoves already handles a missing end node explicitly; getEndNode's current
  use in AI_considerPathDOW follows a successful generatePath.
* Current SAS has additionally added a release guard to the no-from-argument
  GroupPathFinder::generatePath overload when no group has been set, preventing a
  separate null-group crash path that Base AdvCiv still relies on an assertion for.

Without a shipped unguarded producer, keep this as API robustness debt rather than
F306.

CONTROL 3 — ROUTE / WORLD-STATE CACHE INVALIDATION BLIND SPOTS
--------------------------------------------------------------
The reusable pathfinder cannot intrinsically detect every world-state change that
alters movement cost while leaving group/start/flags/moves unchanged. Several such
shapes were challenged, but no normal current producer survived:

* Engineering changes road movement cost through route-change tech processing and
  does not itself reset the group finder. Ordinary research/trade turn sequencing
  did not yield same-group/same-start/same-moves reuse across the change.
* A goody hut can contribute enough research to complete Engineering mid-unit
  action, but acquiring the hut requires the unit to move onto it first. The next
  path query therefore has a different start plot and the reusable tree resets.
* Pillaging a route can mutate movement cost synchronously on the same plot and AI
  can loop into another update, but pillaging consumes a full movement denominator.
  The cached start-node moves no longer match the group's current moves, so
  canReuseInitialPathData resets the tree before reuse.
* Open Borders similarly lacks an explicit generic pathfinder invalidation, but
  sequential/simultaneous diplomacy and unit-turn ordering did not produce a
  normal same-group cache-reuse sequence before another reset boundary.

These remain architectural invalidation limitations to keep in mind, but no F306
without a current producer/consequence.

CONTROL 4 — EXPLICIT HEURISTIC-WEIGHT CACHE INPUT
--------------------------------------------------
setGroup can receive an explicit heuristic weight, but heuristic weight is not one
of the values used to decide whether cached nodes must be reset. A same-group,
same-destination future API caller could therefore reuse OPEN nodes with stale
heuristics if only that weight changes.

Current shipped call sites do not exercise that unsafe combination: explicit
non-default weights are used by fresh/local/cleared finders or remain constant for
that finder, while the reusable AI group finder uses the default derived weight.
Thus generic API debt only. F301 already covers the max-path input, which DOES have
an actual current reuse/commit failure.

CONTROL 5 — SIGNED-INT / MAX_INT ARITHMETIC
-------------------------------------------
No credible current signed-int overflow has been proven.

* Ordinary one-step movement terms are far below INT_MAX.
* Even the dominant current MOVE_ATTACK_STACK ratio penalty plus all eight possible
  adjacent-enemy multipliers remains only in the low tens of millions for one
  step, below signed 32-bit overflow.
* Cumulative overflow is mathematically possible only after long chains of those
  near-worst combat-cost plots; the shortest constructions found require dozens of
  consecutively massively overdefended hostile tiles, or equivalently absurd group
  strength/unit-count intermediates. This is not a credible shipped scenario under
  the audit's consequence standard.
* A newly initialized node's `iNewCost - MAX_INT` delta stays within signed range
  for the positive current step costs, and a newly created node has no descendants
  to propagate that sentinel delta through.
* Current largest declared SAS map dimensions (99 x 70 = 6,930 plots) do not create
  a NodeMap allocation/indexing overflow issue.

The code lacks formal saturating arithmetic, so retain this as robustness debt,
not F306 unless a substantially shorter normal producer is found.

CONTROL 6 — BROAD PATH-HISTORY / forwardPropagate LIMITATION
-------------------------------------------------------------
K-Mod's generic finder and AdvCiv's documentation already acknowledge that the path
cost function depends on path data and that reparenting / cached query order can
occasionally produce suboptimal paths. K-Mod source explicitly notes that a cheaper
parent can, counterintuitively, make a descendant more expensive and that there was
no obvious generic solution.

Do not allocate F306 merely by rediscovering that broad known limitation. The
numbered findings F300, F301 and F303 are narrower because they prove sharper
current contract failures (danger legality, hard max-path loss, and concrete mixed
movement cost reconstruction). A new finding here would need a similarly distinct
current failure, not another generic manifestation of the known compression issue.

OTHER CURRENT CONTROLS
----------------------
* Land exploration heuristic remains conservative despite the 2/3 fog discount;
  its route-derived minimum is railroad-scale and still below a fog step.
* OWN_EXCLUSIVE_RADIUS can lower cost but is disabled in current SAS; no live
  heuristic violation from it.
* Actual declaration of war resets the group pathfinder, so stale post-DOW cache is
  not the root of F304; F304 is specifically the pre-DOW simulation's endpoint
  asymmetry.
* Promotions reset group paths; current SAS KI#475 additionally invalidates the
  main finder across group membership changes.
* Domain +move technology changes alter maxMoves and therefore movesLeft, which the
  initial-data reuse check notices and resets.

CONTROL 7 — AUTOMATION / UnitAI STATE IS NOT A CURRENT CACHE ROOT
-----------------------------------------------------------------
GroupStepMetric cost/legality depends on group automation and UnitAI role, while
those values are not explicit fields in GroupPathFinder::setGroup's cache identity.
The transition paths were therefore traced rather than assumed safe.

* CvUnitAI::AI_setUnitAIType changes the role and then calls joinGroup(NULL). Current
  SAS KI#475 invalidates the reusable finder on selection-group membership change;
  any resulting new group also has a different group pointer and forces reset.
* CvSelectionGroup::setAutomateType itself does not reset the pathfinder, and
  CvUnit::automate can immediately call AI_update on the same group. Structurally
  this is therefore a state mutation that the cache identity does not encode.
* However, a normal nonautomated human group does not populate the reusable main
  finder in the live pre-automation paths inspected. The current MOVE_MAX_MOVES
  uses that can serve human-side evaluation use a temporary/cleared finder.
* Automation-type transitions that can reuse the main finder either preserve the
  same Explore cost semantics or cause the next query to use movement flags that
  differ from the previous automation's query, which makes setGroup reset.

Thus the generic cache key is not a complete value-function key, but no current
producer/consequence was established for automation or UnitAI changes. No F306.

CONTROL 8 — MAIN GROUP FINDER IS GLOBAL/STATIC, NOT PER GROUP
-------------------------------------------------------------
CvSelectionGroup::m_pPathFinder is one shared static reusable GroupPathFinder.
setGroup resets its nodes whenever the group pointer differs. Consequently a large
class of stale-world-state scenarios cannot survive ordinary inter-group AI work:
when another selection group queries the main finder, the previous group's tree is
discarded.

The meaningful reuse surface is therefore primarily repeated queries by the SAME
group (multi-target evaluators, same-group follow-up queries, same group/flags with
changed destination). This structural fact is important context for F300/F301 and
for rejecting several speculative stale-world-state candidates.

CONTROL 9 — STATIC DEAD-END NODE LATER USED AS DESTINATION IS INTENTIONAL AND SAFE
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A tempting candidate was that a plot first encountered as an illegal intermediate
might become CLOSED with no path, then be mistaken for an already-reached endpoint
on a later cached query because generatePath assigns m_pEndNode for any initialized
destination node.

Exact KmodPathFinder::processChild ordering disproves that candidate for the static
canStepThrough case:

1. updatePathData initializes the candidate path data.
2. New node known cost is initially MAX_INT.
3. If StepMetric::canStepThrough(kChildPlot) is false, state is set CLOSED so the
   node will never be expanded THROUGH as an intermediate.
4. Execution intentionally CONTINUES. processChild computes the finite candidate
   cost, installs the parent link, updates known cost, and links the child into the
   parent's child list.

That is exactly the intended cross-destination contract: a defended/otherwise
transit-forbidden plot may have a valid path TO it even though it may not be
expanded beyond. When a later cached query makes it the destination, its cached
parent chain and finite cost are legitimate.

The path-dependent danger check is different: failure there returns before the node
is opened/closed and leaves the node UNINITIALIZED. Such a parentless MAX_INT node
therefore is not mistaken for a cached endpoint by generatePath.

The initially plausible false-success / getPathEndTurnPlot crash sequence is thus
rejected. No F306.

CONTROL 10 — MOVE_DECLARE_WAR FLAG-ONLY CACHE OPTIMIZATION IS ENFORCED BELOW
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
GroupPathFinder::setGroup deliberately avoids a reset when only MOVE_DECLARE_WAR
changes and the acting team is not AI_isSneakAttackReady. The comment says that in
that state the flag is effectively no different.

Lower-level tracing confirms this is not merely an assumption: AI
CvUnit::canMoveInto/canMoveOrAttackInto with bDeclareWar=true still requires the
team to be sneak-attack ready (and the group's AI_isDeclareWar predicate) before
future-enemy traversal becomes legal. Therefore adding MOVE_DECLARE_WAR while the
team is not sneak-ready does not change AI intermediate legality. No stale-CLOSED
root from this optimization.

CONTROL 11 — HUMAN DIRECT-ATTACK TINY COST CANNOT BE AN INTERMEDIATE HEURISTIC EDGE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The human direct-attack fast path can return PATH_STEP_WEIGHT (7), far below the
normal GroupPathFinder heuristic lower bound. This is nevertheless safe for current
path structure: the special edge is restricted to the initial adjacent visible
attack, canStepThrough rejects a defended enemy plot as an ordinary intermediate,
and non-air groupAttack does not use such an attack edge as part of a longer route.
It can therefore only be the destination edge and does not invalidate A* lower-bound
reasoning for remaining path steps.

CONTROL 12 — SPEND_ALL_MOVES_ON_INVASION SIMULATION HAZARD IS DORMANT
---------------------------------------------------------------------
CvPlot::movementCost has an optional SPEND_ALL_MOVES_ON_INVASION branch that uses
the LIVE unit's current movesLeft. That would be suspect when GroupPathFinder is
simulating an invasion step on a future turn, because simulated remaining movement
can differ from the live unit object. Current SAS and Base AdvCiv both configure
SPEND_ALL_MOVES_ON_INVASION = 0, so this branch is dormant in the shipped rules.
Retain as configuration-sensitive debt only.

CROSS-FILE SIDE NOTE — SAS SETTLER LEVEL-2 LOGGING CAN USE STALE/NULL PATH END
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
The full getPathEndTurnPlot caller inventory found a real SAS diagnostic hazard,
but not a GroupPathFinder gameplay root suitable for F306.

SAS_shouldDelayFoundInPlaceForBetterReachableSite repeatedly calls generatePath for
candidate sites and stores the best site's plot/value/path-turn scalar data, but it
does not preserve that best query's pathfinder tree/end-node. A later candidate can
replace the current end-node with another site's path or can fail and leave no end
node, while the helper can still return true because an EARLIER best site exists.
Three level-2 Settler diagnostic lines then call getPathEndTurnPlot on the current
finder state. With SAS_BBAI_SETTLER_LOG_LEVEL >= 2 this can therefore log the wrong
candidate's end-turn plot, or hit GroupPathFinder's release-unsafe null dereference
if the final later query failed.

The default log level is 0 and gameplay behavior already uses the stored best-site
values rather than that diagnostic endpoint. Preserve for the appropriate SAS
CvUnitAI/Settler logging review; do not allocate F306 in queue 054 for it.

CONTROL 13 — CLOSED-NODE NON-REOPEN DOES NOT JUSTIFY A NEW ROOT BY ITSELF
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
The final generic KmodPathFinder sweep challenged a CLOSED node receiving a cheaper
parent without being reopened for fresh neighbor expansion. This is potentially
harmful only when the step metric depends on path history/state (or when the
heuristic is inadmissible), because ordinary path-independent A* with the remaining
current lower-bound assumptions should not discover a genuinely better route to an
already processed node later.

That exceptional family is already explicitly acknowledged by upstream code/history:
* KmodPathFinder::forwardPropagate says that a cheaper path to a parent can make a
  descendant more expensive because GroupStepMetric cost depends on path history,
  and says there is no obvious generic solution.
* AdvCiv practical 4196, "Fix danger avoidance checks in pathfinder", explicitly
  says rare failures may remain because GroupStepMetric uses path data and notes
  that further paths reaching a child may have to be reconsidered.

The sharper current consequences from this state-compression family are already
numbered as F300 (path-dependent danger legality is not revalidated/re-expanded
across reparent/propagation) and F303 (cost uses the wrong per-unit movement state).
F305 is the separate current inadmissible-heuristic root. Do not allocate F306 merely
for the broad CLOSED/non-reopen limitation already described by those roots/history.

CONTROL 14 — NAVAL MOVEMENT HAS NO SECOND LIVE SUB-HEURISTIC COST CHANNEL
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
F305 prompted a full check of current naval movement-cost reducers, not only raw
MoveDiscountChange.
* Current nonempty promotion FeatureDoubleMoves belongs to Woodsman-style land use.
* Current HillsDoubleMove belongs to a land archer/recon promotion.
* No current naval combat-class promotion grants terrain/feature double movement.
* The current raw move-discount promotion is restricted to land combat classes.
* There are no water routes and current unit XML has no nonempty SpeedBonuses.

Therefore ordinary sea movement cannot fall below one movement denominator through
another current movement ability. The live sea heuristic violation remains narrowly
the 2/3 unrevealed exploration discount recorded in F305 (plus optional disabled
rule configurations already controlled elsewhere). No F306.

CONTROL 15 — OLD baseMoves / maxMoves CACHE COMMENT HAS NO CURRENT SHIPPED ROOT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
GroupStepMetric::canReuseInitialPathData compares only initial moves, while an old
K-Mod comment worries that max/base moves may also need explicit checking.
Current state transitions were traced:
* domain +move technology and circumnavigation change maxMoves and therefore
  movesLeft (CvUnit::movesLeft = maxMoves - moves used), so initial-data reuse
  detects the difference and resets;
* promotions that alter unit movement explicitly reset the group pathfinder;
* current unit XML has no SpeedBonuses that could make baseMoves vary with local
  bonus availability while leaving group moves unchanged;
* the shipped debug CyTeam.changeExtraMoves path likewise changes maxMoves and hence
  movesLeft, which triggers the same start-data reset.

No normal current transition was established where the group's heuristic-relevant
baseMoves changes while same-group/same-start initial moves remain equal and cached
nodes are reused. Retain the comment as generic modding/API caution, not F306.

CONTROL 16 — PATH INFORMATION ACCESSORS / SHIPPED CALLERS
---------------------------------------------------------
The remaining path information interface was inventoried after the earlier
getPathEndTurnPlot control.
* AI_considerPathDOW calls getEndNode only after its own successful generatePath.
* Main C++ getPathFirstPlot/getPathEndTurnPlot/getFinalMoves uses are attached to
  successful generatePath branches or saved success booleans in the paths inspected.
* CyUnit/CySelectionGroup expose path plot accessors to Python, but current shipped
  SAS Python has no caller of these accessors.

The accessor implementation remains fragile as an API contract (especially
getPathEndTurnPlot's release null dereference), but the only concrete current SAS
unguarded/stale use found is the level-2 Settler diagnostic side note already
recorded in WIP13. No GroupPathFinder gameplay F306 from the accessor surface.

CONTROL 17 — ALTERNATE PATHFINDER LIFETIME/RESET CONTRACT HOLDS
---------------------------------------------------------------
CvSelectionGroup::m_pAltPathFinder is intentionally shared as allocation-saving
scratch state. getClearPathFinder unconditionally calls reset() before returning it.
Normal group death calls invalidateGroupPaths(), invalidating both main and alternate
finder group pointers. SAS clearUnits intentionally invalidates only the main finder
while a live groupMove may still consult its alternate execution path; if the group
then dies, kill() performs the two-finder invalidation before deletion.

Thus the deliberate KI#475 alternate-finder exception does not leave a stale group
pointer available on the next scratch-finder use. No F306.

CONTROL 18 — STRUCTURAL NODE / OPEN-LIST BOUNDS
-----------------------------------------------
* Current largest declared SAS map is 99 x 70 = 6,930 plots, far below PlotNumTypes
  and allocation arithmetic limits used by NodeMap.
* A plot has at most NUM_DIRECTION_TYPES (8) adjacent children; m_apChildren is
  exactly that size and m_iNumChildren is ample.
* OpenList::open is reached only for a newly UNINITIALIZED valid node; an existing
  OPEN/CLOSED node is not opened a second time, so the vector does not acquire
  duplicate node entries through normal processChild flow.
* Positive step costs and the strict cheaper-parent relation maintain an acyclic
  parent tree. Consequently path length is bounded by the finite plot set and does
  not threaten its int storage.
* Recursive forwardPropagate can be deep in theory, but a credible current crash
  would require an extremely pathological many-thousand-node descendant chain and
  late reparent; no shipped construction survived the consequence standard.

No F306 from structural storage/recursion bounds.

CONTROL 19 — IGNORED CACHE FLAGS ARE REALLY PATHFINDER-IRRELEVANT
-----------------------------------------------------------------
setGroup ignores differences in MOVE_DIRECT_ATTACK, MOVE_SINGLE_ATTACK and
MOVE_NO_ATTACK when comparing flags. A full GroupStepMetric search confirms none of
those flags participates in isValidStep, canStepThrough, isValidDest, cost,
updatePathData or heuristic calculation. They affect later mission/execution logic.
Excluding them from the reusable path tree's cache identity is therefore sound.

FINAL FINDING SET
-----------------
F300 / KI#623 — PATH-DEPENDENT DANGER IS NOT REVALIDATED AFTER REPARENT / PROPAGATION
  Reparenting changes GroupPathNode movement/path-turn state through updatePathData,
  but the path-dependent danger predicate is not rerun. forwardPropagate can change
  the same state recursively in descendants, and CLOSED nodes are not reopened for
  fresh expansion after such state mutation. A concrete current noncombat-worker
  case proves generatePath/path-turn evaluation can consume a route that no longer
  satisfies its own danger rule. Inherited from K-Mod; AdvCiv practical 4196 fixed
  the first-arrival form but explicitly left residual path-data concerns. Repair
  must preserve an older valid parent when a prospective reparent is invalid and
  account for descendant/CLOSED-node revalidation or rediscovery.

F301 / KI#624 — MAX-PATH BOUND IS NOT ENFORCED WHEN CHILD/PARENT STATE IS COMMITTED
  KmodPathFinder may initialize or reparent a destination through a path longer than
  iMaxPath. A valid bounded parent/path can then be overwritten by a cheaper
  over-limit route; the final length check returns false even though a legal bounded
  route had already existed. Current attack-city/mobile-artillery AI_choke(1) gives
  a shipped bounded producer. Inherited K-Mod generic-pathfinder root.

F302 / KI#625 — MAX-COST UNIT OVERWRITES TRUE GROUP MINIMUM MOVES LEFT
  GroupStepMetric::cost first computes iWorstMovesLeft as the minimum across group
  members, then overwrites it with iMovesLeft whenever a later unit sets iWorstCost.
  Mixed-speed/mixed-cost stacks can therefore skip real end-turn territory/defense/
  danger weights. Exact current siege + German Hussar route math reverses path
  choice and changes AI_pickTargetCity scoring. K-Mod practical 237/238 ancestry.
  Local repair: keep the independent group-minimum accumulation and remove the
  coupled iWorstMovesLeft assignment inside the max-cost branch.

F303 / KI#626 — COST FABRICATES PER-UNIT REMAINING MOVES FROM SHARED GROUP MINIMUM
  On parent nodes with positive group moves, GroupStepMetric::cost feeds the same
  iCurrMoves to every unit even when their true per-unit remaining movement differs
  because movement costs are non-uniform. updatePathData already contains K-Mod's
  practical-1017 per-unit replay to avoid exactly this movement-state error. A
  current siege + 3-move Hussar railroad case reverses a staging route and can make
  AI_moveToStagingCity spend an extra turn instead of reaching the city immediately.
  Independent of F302; repair needs real per-unit turn movement reconstruction or
  richer cached node state.

F304 / KI#627 — PRE-DOW ROUTE SIMULATION CHECKS ONLY THE DESTINATION ENDPOINT
  AdvCiv practical 4277 tries to anticipate loss of Open Borders when a path will
  declare war, but bIgnoreRoutes is derived only from kTo's team. A step from a
  future-enemy road out to a friendly/third-party road can therefore use the enemy
  route before war even though it will be unusable after the declaration. A normal
  1-move attack-city stack can be scored as 2 path turns when execution becomes 3,
  materially overvaluing AI_pickTargetCity. Base AdvCiv 1.14 inherits this incomplete
  repair. SAS also has AI-usable PROMOTION_LOGISTICS enemy-route capability, so a
  robust fix must simulate post-DOW route validity per unit at BOTH endpoints rather
  than blindly ignoring all prospective-enemy routes.

F305 / KI#628 — SEA EXPLORATION HEURISTIC OVERESTIMATES DISCOUNTED FOG STEPS
  Sea groups default to one full movement denominator as the A* heuristic weight,
  but K-Mod practical 1188 later made unrevealed exploration steps cost only 2/3.
  The resulting sea heuristic is inadmissible for UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA/
  AUTOMATE_EXPLORE. Corrected current reproduction uses a REVEALED edge destination
  (sea AI cannot choose an unrevealed destination): exact A* simulation returns a
  more expensive revealed route while leaving the genuinely cheaper partially-fog
  detour unexpanded. Physical groupPathTo uses a freshly cleared finder with the same
  heuristic, so execution reproduces the suboptimal route. K-Mod practical 366 +
  1188 ancestry; current K-Mod, Base AdvCiv and SAS all inherit it.

WHY F306 REMAINS UNUSED
-----------------------
The final saturation pass challenged, among other things:
* static dead-end nodes later becoming destinations;
* CLOSED-node cheaper-parent/non-reopen behavior;
* MOVE_SAFE_TERRITORY / MOVE_NO_ENEMY_TERRITORY destination semantics;
* ignored cache flags (DIRECT_ATTACK / SINGLE_ATTACK / NO_ATTACK);
* MOVE_DECLARE_WAR-only cache changes;
* automation and UnitAI changes;
* max/base movement changes and old canReuseInitialPathData caveat;
* Engineering / Open-Borders / pillage / route-world-state mutation;
* explicit heuristic-weight reuse;
* alternate scratch-finder lifetime;
* getPathEndTurnPlot/getEndNode/getPathFirstPlot caller contracts;
* sea raw discounts plus terrain/feature double-move promotion channels;
* dormant SPEND_ALL_MOVES_ON_INVASION;
* signed-int path-cost overflow;
* NodeMap sizing, child capacity, OPEN-list uniqueness, parent cycles and recursion;
* normalized SAS-vs-Base semantic deltas and all modern upstream pathfinder commits.

These checks either close cleanly under current callers/configuration, are generic
API/modding hardening only, require pathological unsupported states, are disabled by
current configuration, or fall into the already-documented path-history/state
compression family represented more sharply by F300/F303. None justified a
separate current shipped F306.

SCOPE / ANCESTRY START
----------------------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 BBAILog.cpp contains the inherited fixed 2048-byte formatter,
network-player/fixed BBAI filename logic and deal-cancel helper. Current SAS adds
XML-backed category levels, timestamped per-new/load filenames, new/load/game-state

per-new/load metadata/session rollover was added; it is not a Base AdvCiv/K-Mod
behavioral root.

F306 / KI#629 — FIXED-NAME BBAI MODE REUSES STALE FIRST-SESSION UTC METADATA
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current state:
  g_szSASBBAILogTimestamp is lazy/cached process-global state.
  getSASBBAILogTimestamp() creates it only while empty.

rollSASBBAILog(szContext) refreshes that timestamp ONLY inside:
  if (isSASBBAILogTimestampedFilenameEnabled())

But the supported XML mode SAS_BBAI_LOG_USE_TIMESTAMPED_FILENAME=0 is documented as
preserving fixed-name BBAI.log behavior; the new/load metadata rows still advertise
UTC identity in that mode:
  BBAI_NEW_GAME_INITIALIZING utc=...
  BBAI_NEW_GAME_STARTED utc=...
  BBAI_SAVE_LOADED utc=...

Concrete process sequence with BBAI logging enabled and timestamped filename=0:
  1. First new/load calls rollSASBBAILog, which does nothing.
  2. First metadata call lazily creates timestamp T1.
  3. A later load/new in the SAME Civ4 process again calls rollSASBBAILog, which
     still does nothing.
  4. getSASBBAILogTimestamp returns cached T1, not the actual new/load time T2.

Thus subsequent session headers appended to fixed BBAI.log carry stale UTC from the
first logged state in the process. This directly contradicts the practical-6011
new/load identification purpose: startSASBBAILogForLoadedSave explicitly says the
loaded state is identified through UTC, and the XML option describes only the
filename choice, not a metadata-freshness opt-out.

Ancestry/history:
* Pre-SAS/Base fixed-name BBAI had no per-session UTC row, so there was no stale-UTC
  metadata contract to violate.
* SAS practical 6011 (f544db1d5e) introduced rollSASBBAILog, per-new/load metadata,
  and the current conditional timestamp refresh together. This is the root.
* Current SASGameRecordLog demonstrates the intended separation: its roll helper
  ALWAYS refreshes the session timestamp, while only sequence/context filename state
  is conditional on SAS_GAME_RECORD_LOG_USE_TIMESTAMPED_FILENAME.

Impact / severity boundary:
* Diagnostic/report correctness only; no gameplay-state corruption.
* Default timestamped mode=1 is correct. The bug affects the explicitly supported
  fixed-name opt-out mode=0, especially repeated save/new tests without restarting
  Civ4—the exact workflow practical 6011 sought to identify reliably.
* The wrong UTC can make later fixed-file sessions look as if they began at the
  first session's time and undermines chronology when BBAI.log contains many runs.

Repair boundary:
Always refresh g_szSASBBAILogTimestamp at every roll/new/load. Keep filename
sequence/context conditional if fixed-name behavior must remain BBAI.log/BBAI%d.log.
In outline:
  g_szSASBBAILogTimestamp = createSASBBAILogTimestamp();
  if (isSASBBAILogTimestampedFilenameEnabled()) { ++sequence; set context; }
Optionally clear stale context when fixed-name mode is selected, though the static
filename branch ignores it today. No save format change is needed.

CONTROL 1 — CATEGORY MASTER-ENABLE COMPLETENESS IS CLEAN
---------------------------------------------------------
Mechanical current-source reconciliation found 17 BBAI log-level getters and all 17
appear in isSASBBAILogEnabled(). Every g*LogLevel macro in BBAILog.h maps to the
expected getter. Therefore newly separated WAR / MILITARY_PRODUCTION /
OVERSEAS_TRANSPORT / GREAT_GENERAL / SETTLER / WORKER / WORKER_SEA etc. categories
cannot be silently suppressed merely because their getter was omitted from the
master OR.

CONTROL 2 — XML SETTING CACHE IS INTENTIONAL
---------------------------------------------
The XML-backed getters are static-cached on first use. The current GlobalDefines SAS
documentation explicitly tells users to restart Civ4 after changing these BBAI
settings, so lack of hot reload is intentional rather than a stale-setting bug.

OPEN CONTROL — FIXED 2048-BYTE logBBAI FORMATTER
-------------------------------------------------
KI#161.2 correctly forces a terminator after MSVC 7.1 _vsnprintf truncation, but the
sink still silently loses content beyond 2047 bytes. This is not yet a numbered
finding in queue 092:
* longest current static structured format literals are large (~1.2 KB) but do not
  alone prove overflow;
* several dynamic list producers are deliberately capped (e.g. Settler escort pool
  logs at most 10 units);
* potentially unbounded wide strings remain to be proven, notably deal text and
  other CvWStringBuffer output.
Promote only if a current normal producer can exceed the sink with a meaningful
logging consequence; otherwise retain as known formatter debt already bounded by
KI#161.2.

CROSS-FILE CONTROL — INHERITED CvWStringBuffer VARARGS ODDITY
-------------------------------------------------------------
CvPlayer::onTurnLogging contains inherited `logBBAI("%S", szBuffer)` even though
CvWStringBuffer has no conversion operator; a nearby later call correctly uses
`szBuffer.getCString()`. K-Mod and Base AdvCiv contain the same direct-object call.
On Civ4's 32-bit MSVC ABI it appears to work accidentally because the first object
member is the wchar buffer pointer and it is the only variadic argument, but this is
non-portable / undefined C++ rather than a clean `%S` contract. Preserve as
cross-file/portability debt; no current shipped failure has been established, so do
not allocate F307 merely from the source shape.

C028-WIP02 — QUEUE 092 BBAILOG.CPP — FORMAT/LIFECYCLE/HISTORY SATURATION

Checkpoint status:

F306 STATUS
-----------
F306 remains unchanged and fully confirmed: supported fixed-name mode
SAS_BBAI_LOG_USE_TIMESTAMPED_FILENAME=0 refreshes neither
`g_szSASBBAILogTimestamp` nor session context in `rollSASBBAILog`, so later new/load
headers in the same Civ4 process retain the first logged session's UTC. Current
SASGameRecordLog provides the internal control: it refreshes UTC unconditionally
and gates only filename sequence/context on timestamped-filename mode.

CONTROL 3 — 2048-BYTE FORMATTER CEILING HAS NO CURRENT NORMAL >2047 PRODUCER
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
KI#161.2's fixed 2048-byte `_vsnprintf` sink still silently truncates a row longer
than 2047 bytes, but a current-source producer sweep did not establish a normal
BBAI row that reaches the ceiling:
* the longest structured format literal is about 1.2 KB; pessimistic numeric-width
  expansion remains below the sink before bounded string fields;
* the current BBAI_GAME_SETTINGS row remains about 1,050 bytes even under a deliberately
  pessimistic construction with all 28 current GAMEOPTION_* type names enabled and a
  100-character map-script name (current longest map-script filename is only 27);
* score help is one fixed localized score-breakdown structure rather than an
  inventory/list whose size scales without a small bound;
* the player team/met/vassal/war status buffer only enumerates MAX_CIV_TEAMS IDs;
* persisted CvDeal lists retain only ongoing trade items (resource/GPT and treaty/
  relationship items), not arbitrary lists of every technology/city/map/gold item,
  so deal-cancel text cannot scale with all one-shot tradeables;
* large SAS diagnostic lists examined in the current tree frequently impose their
  own small caps (e.g. Settler escort-pool diagnostic lists).

Therefore keep the fixed sink as formatter robustness/technical debt. KI#161.2
correctly prevents unterminated-truncation crashes; there is no evidence gate for a
separate current F307 based only on possible silent truncation. The independent
SASGameRecord formatter's later KI#375 dynamic grow-and-retry repair does not by
itself prove the same practical overflow exists in BBAI.

CONTROL 4 — LITERAL FORMAT/ARGUMENT COUNT SWEEP IS CLEAN
---------------------------------------------------------
A mechanical current-source sweep initially appeared to find one sea-spy call with
three conversions and ten arguments, but that was a parser false positive caused by
parentheses/apostrophes in a trailing `//` comment confusing the call boundary.
After stripping comments while preserving strings and source structure, the sweep
reconciled 816 literal-format `logBBAI` calls with ZERO conversion-count mismatches.
Record the corrected result, not the discarded false positive.

CONTROL 5 — LOAD HEADER ORDERING IS VALID FOR CHECKED METADATA
--------------------------------------------------------------
`startSASBBAILogForLoadedSave()` runs at the top of `CvGame::onAllGameDataRead`, so
several apparently-late compatibility/cache states were challenged explicitly:
* playersEverAlive: BBAI calls `countCivPlayersEverAlive()`, which rescans loaded
  player `isEverAlive()` state; it does NOT read the immediately-afterward repaired
  `m_iCivPlayersEverAlive` cache. The old-save compatibility assignment therefore
  does not make the header report zero/stale player history.
* map heaviness: `m_bLandHeavyMapname` and `m_bNavalHeavyMapname` are serialized
  directly in `CvGame::read` and written in `CvGame::write`. Supported current saves
  therefore already contain the actual cached DLL classification when the early
  BBAI_SAVE_LOADED row is emitted; no post-load recomputation is required.
* map dimensions, game setup enums and player data are already part of the loaded
  state at onAllGameDataRead. No current delayed-finalization dependency was found.

Do not manufacture a BBAI ordering bug from truly old pre-field saves whose overall
CvGame serialization layout is no longer a supported current uiFlag format.

CONTROL 6 — RNG IDENTITY ROW IS READ-ONLY
------------------------------------------
`BBAI_GAME_RNG` calls `CvRandom::getSeed()` on map and sync RNGs. The getter simply
returns `m_uiRandomSeed`; it neither advances nor reseeds the generator. Logging RNG
identity therefore cannot perturb deterministic game state.

CONTROL 7 — SESSION ROLLOVER BOUNDARY HAS NO PRE-ROLL BBAI PRODUCER FOUND
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
New game starts the BBAI session after `CvGame::reset` and before map generation;
loaded games roll after serialized data is read. A current source sweep found no
BBAI producer inside reset/uninit/save-read paths that can lazily create a timestamp
and context-less log before the intended roll. ReproTest's `ReproTest: reloading`
line belongs to the quick-load control flow and does not establish a serialization-
time pre-roll writer.

CONTROL 8 — logBBAICancel CALLER CONTRACT IS CLEAN
--------------------------------------------------
All five current callers are within CvPlayerAI deal-cancellation/overdraft logic and
pass `getID()` after the surrounding contract has established that the deal is
between this player and the counterpart. Logging occurs while the deal is live and,
where the deal is then killed, before `kill()`. No NO_PLAYER or post-destruction
lifetime path was found.

CONTROL 9 — INHERITED CvWStringBuffer ELLIPSIS PASS REMAINS PORTABILITY DEBT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CvPlayer::onTurnLogging still contains inherited `logBBAI("%S", szBuffer)` for a
`CvWStringBuffer` object. `CvWStringBuffer` is a non-trivial 12-byte class on the
Civ4 ABI, has no conversion operator, and its first member is the backing `wchar*`.
Passing such an object through C-style ellipsis is not a clean portable C++ contract.
K-Mod and Base AdvCiv ship the same call, while a nearby later call correctly uses
`szBuffer.getCString()`.

The Civ4 32-bit MSVC ABI/layout plausibly explains why the inherited call works in
practice (the first object word is the expected wide-string pointer), and no current
wrong-output/crash evidence was established. Keep as portability/undefined-behavior
debt for the CvPlayer/BBAI call-site review rather than allocating F307 from source
shape alone. A local cleanup to `.getCString()` would nevertheless be prudent.

C028-WIP03 ADDENDUM — QUEUE 092 CATEGORY-ISOLATION MATRIX / F307 STILL UNUSED
