CATEGORY-ISOLATION CONTRACT
---------------------------
SAS split the inherited monolithic BBAI logging into independently configurable
PLAYER/TEAM/WAR/CITY/MILITARY_PRODUCTION/CITIZEN/UNIT/OVERSEAS_TRANSPORT/
GREAT_GENERAL/SETTLER/FOUND/EVACUATION/WORKER/WORKER_SEA/MAP/DEAL_CANCEL/CULTURE
levels. `logBBAI()` itself only performs the global "any BBAI category enabled"
sink gate, so category-specific callers/helpers must own their individual level
checks. Current CvPlayerAI conquest/raze comments explicitly recognize this rule.

A raw grep for helpers with direct `logBBAI` calls is NOT evidence of leakage:
many helper bodies are intentionally unguarded and every entry point is caller-
gated. The current caller-chain matrix was therefore traced rather than counted.

CONTROL 10 — CvUnitAI HELPER/CALLER CATEGORY MATRIX IS CLEAN
------------------------------------------------------------
The remaining apparently-unguarded UnitAI helper bodies all resolve to explicit
category gates:
* `logSASRetreatUnitResult` -> `bLogRetreatResult`, derived from Evacuation level;
* `logSASSafetyUnitResult` -> Evacuation >= 3;
* `SAS_logSettlerMissionDecision` -> Settler >= 2 at every action path; calls that
  look bare in grep output sit inside enclosing Settler >= 2 blocks;
* `logSASEvacuationUnitDecision` -> Evacuation >= 2;
* `logSASWorkerSeaMoveDetail` -> Worker Sea >= 2 for work-boat decisions, or
  Evacuation >= 3 for the intentionally shared retreat/safety diagnostics;
* `logSASCultureGreatArtistDecision` -> `bLogCultureGreatArtistDecision`, which is
  Culture >= 3 and UNITAI_GREAT_ARTIST;
* first-city BFC diagnostics -> `bLogSettlerAILevel3` = Settler >= 3;
* missing-war-city expedition diagnostic -> Unit >= 2 before helper entry;
* attack-defense reinforcement diagnostic -> direct gameplay call is Unit >= 2;
  the second apparently bare call is nested inside `SAS_logAttackCityParking`, and
  all parking helper calls are under `bLogAttackCityParking` = Unit >= 2 plus the
  intended parking context;
* barbarian attack-city opportunity -> `(Unit >= 2 || Player >= 2)` intentionally;
* large attack-city stack -> `bLogLargeAttackCityStack` = Unit >= 2;
* crowded peaceful attack-city diagnostics -> Unit >= 2;
* assault-transport failure -> Overseas Transport >= 2;
* Great-General join diagnostics -> Great General >= 1/2/3 as appropriate.
No normal UnitAI helper was found that can execute solely because an unrelated BBAI
category turns on the global sink.

CONTROL 14 — CvPlayer / CvPlayerAI INHERITED LOGGING REMAINS PLAYER/CULTURE/WORKER-SEA GATED
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
* `CvPlayer::onTurnLogging` is wholly partitioned by Player > 0 / Player >= 2;
  the inherited score-help varargs wart therefore does not bypass the Player category.
* strategy-change macros explicitly require Player >= 2.
* crush/attack-city conversion rows require Player >= 2.
* civic decision/candidate diagnostics derive from Player >= 2/3.
* culture stage and Great-Person-weight diagnostics derive from Culture levels.
* `AI_logWorkerSeaAudit` has an unguarded helper body but both normal and Barbarian
  callers invoke it only at Worker Sea >= 3.
* conquest/raze/liberation rows use the explicit player-category boolean introduced
  after SAS's category split.
No current PlayerAI category leak survived caller tracing.

CONTROL 15 — DEBUG/GLOBAL DIAGNOSTICS ARE NOT A NORMAL CATEGORY LEAK
--------------------------------------------------------------------
ReproTest BBAI output is compile-time `ENABLE_REPRO_TEST` instrumentation and uses the
legacy/global diagnostic gate intentionally. It is not a normal release gameplay
category producer and is not used to manufacture F307.

CONTROL 16 — NEW-GAME COMPLETE MAP METADATA IS EMITTED AT THE LATE HEADER
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
`startSASBBAILogForNewGame()` intentionally logs only `BBAI_NEW_GAME_INITIALIZING`
plus mod/settings before map generation. It does NOT call the complete game-state
row there. `logSASBBAINewGameStarted()` is emitted from the exported gameStart event
and calls `logSASBBAIGameState` only after generated state exists. Map heaviness is
recomputed after map generation and again in `initFreeUnits` after starting plots so
script-list and dynamic start-area classifications are finalized before gameplay.
The source comments explicitly define this two-stage contract. Thus the initial
pre-map false/default heaviness cache is not logged as complete new-game metadata.

CATEGORY-ISOLATION RESULT
-------------------------
No shipped normal caller has yet been found that emits an unrelated category solely
because `logBBAI`'s global "any category enabled" gate is true. The SAS category split
therefore survives the completed helper/caller matrix. Keep F307 / KI#630 UNUSED.

FINAL STATUS

CONFIRMED ROOT
--------------
F306 / KI#629 — fixed-name BBAI mode reuses stale first-session UTC metadata.

`rollSASBBAILog` refreshes `g_szSASBBAILogTimestamp` only when
`SAS_BBAI_LOG_USE_TIMESTAMPED_FILENAME` is enabled. In the explicitly supported
fixed-name mode (`=0`), later new games and loaded saves continue appending to the
fixed BBAI filename as intended, but their `BBAI_NEW_GAME_INITIALIZING` /
`BBAI_NEW_GAME_STARTED` / `BBAI_SAVE_LOADED` identity rows obtain UTC from the
cached first session instead of the session currently being identified.

This is SAS-specific lifecycle behavior introduced with the per-new/load identity
metadata/session rollover work (practical 6011). The newer SASGameRecord rollover
provides the clean precedent: sample/refresh the session UTC on every roll and gate
only filename context/sequence on the timestamped-filename option. The BBAI repair
should follow that separation.

FINAL SATURATION / CONTROL LEDGER
---------------------------------
The following suspicious boundaries were explicitly challenged and did not justify
F307:

1. CATEGORY ISOLATION
   The 17 independently configurable SAS BBAI categories all participate in the
   master `isSASBBAILogEnabled` OR. A full helper/caller matrix found no normal
   shipped category-specific row that leaks merely because an unrelated category is
   enabled. Apparently bare helper bodies are caller-gated; intentional shared rows
   (e.g. Player-or-Found Barbarian-city context) remain shared by design.

2. XML SETTING LIFETIME
   BBAI master/level/interval/filename getters intentionally cache their XML values.
   `GlobalDefines_advciv_sas.xml` explicitly documents: "restart Civ4 to apply
   changes." Current shipped Python never writes `SAS_BBAI_*` defines through the
   generic `setDefine*` API. The static caches therefore match the supported config
   contract rather than defeating runtime settings.

3. SESSION/FILENAME UNIQUENESS
   Timestamped mode uses a process-local monotonically increasing `newN` / `loadN`
   context in addition to second-resolution UTC, so repeated rolls within the same
   Civ4 process remain distinct even in the same second. A collision would require
   separate OS processes producing the same player/timestamp/context tuple; that is
   external multi-process filename debt, not a normal queue-092 gameplay/logging
   failure.

4. NETWORK ACTIVE-PLAYER SUFFIX
   The inherited `BBAI<activePlayer>` network filename is intended for OOS debugging
   on one PC. The active network slot lives in CvInitCore and survives CvGame reset;
   ordinary network turns do not rotate active player like Hotseat/PBEM. The active-
   player-changing paths found are Hotseat/PBEM handoff, single-player reload,
   Rise&Fall/control transfer, AI Auto Play/debug-style transitions, or human-player
   conversion rather than normal network progression. No supported ordinary network
   sequence was established that silently splits one BBAI session across suffixes.

5. NEW/LOAD HEADER ORDERING
   New-game rollover intentionally occurs before map generation and emits only the
   initializing/settings/mod rows; complete game-state metadata is delayed until
   `gameStart`, after map/player initialization and map-heaviness recomputation.
   Load rollover occurs after deserialization. `playersEverAlive` is obtained by the
   live counting getter, and cached land/naval map classifications are serialized.
   No stale/default header field survived the ordering audit.

6. RNG OBSERVATION
   Header RNG calls use `CvRandom::getSeed`, a read-only getter. Logging session
   identity does not perturb deterministic RNG state.

7. FIXED 2048-BYTE FORMATTER
   KI#161.2 correctly guarantees a trailing NUL after MSVC 7.1 `_vsnprintf`
   truncation. Silent truncation remains possible in principle, but no credible
   current BBAI producer exceeding 2047 bytes was proven. Pessimistic all-current-
   game-options settings rows stay around ~1.05 KB; persisted deal text is limited to
   saveable ongoing trade items; other whole dynamic buffers are bounded. Keep as
   formatter ceiling/debt rather than F307.

8. FORMAT CONTRACT SWEEP
   A comments-stripped mechanical pass reconciled 816 current literal-format
   `logBBAI` calls with zero conversion-count mismatches. The initial sea-spy apparent
   mismatch was a parser false positive caused by a trailing comment and was
   explicitly rejected.

9. INHERITED CvWStringBuffer VARARGS CALL
   One inherited score logger passes a `CvWStringBuffer` object through C-style
   ellipsis where `%S` expects a wide-string pointer; standard C++ does not make that
   portable, while Civ4's fixed 32-bit MSVC ABI/layout plausibly explains why it has
   shipped working from K-Mod/Base AdvCiv. No current wrong-output/crash evidence was
   established. Preserve as portability/UB debt, not F307.

10. logBBAICancel CONTRACT
    Every current caller supplies a real canceling player and logs before deal kill
    where applicable. Temporary wide strings live through the synchronous formatter
    call. No NO_PLAYER or stale-object path survived.

11. STRING/OWNERSHIP / THREADING BOUNDARIES
    Mod/type strings come from stable owned storage; temporary CvString pointers are
    consumed within the same full expression. BBAI logging is game-thread diagnostic
    code; the static formatter buffer and C runtime `gmtime` use do not gain a current
    concurrent producer in the shipped DLL. Raw mod-context escaping remains less
    parser-robust than SASGameRecord but current Windows path constraints/current
    branded values do not establish a shipped ambiguity.

12. HISTORY / ANCESTRY
    Older AdvCiv logger behavior remains intact: deal cancellation (1577), no EXE
    log timestamps (2269), per-active-player network filename (2690), and corrected
    `BBAI.log` spelling (3579). SAS changes 5903/5925/5981/6011/6019/6326 and later
    category additions were individually reconciled. No later upstream safety repair
    was found missing from current SAS.

ROOT-MERGING / CLOSURE
----------------------
The remaining irregularities are controls, portability debt, optional-configuration
concerns, or external multi-process limitations. None supplies an independent
current producer -> violated contract -> shipped consequence chain strong enough for
F307. Queue 092 therefore closes with F306 as its sole numbered root.

KI#5383 ACTION-GUARD CHALLENGE -- REJECTED
------------------------------------------
A potentially serious SAS-local concern was tested: the null-selection-list guard
added after the CvSelectionGroup::plot crash might have disabled control-only
ActionInfo entries (advisor hotkeys, options, save/load) whenever no unit group is
selected.

The current ordering disproves this. canHandleAction first performs:

    if (kAction.getControlType() != NO_CONTROL && canDoControl(...))
        return true;

Only after that does it require a head selected unit and selection list for
mission/command/interface-mode actions. Therefore control-only actions never reach
the new selection-list null guard. handleAction likewise executes doControl before
checking the selection list for interface-mode processing. The KI#5383 guard is
narrowly placed around unit-group-dependent behavior; no regression established.

CIV4CE INDEPENDENT COMPARATOR PASS
----------------------------------
Civ4CE's BtS CvGameInterface.cpp was compared specifically on the exported/tail
contracts being challenged. It does not supply an independent modern guard that
would overturn current classifications:
* city-screen double click preserves stock's pCity!=NULL outer guard;
* neighboring city callbacks retain stock-style checks;
* soundtrack, initSelection, canDoPing, minimap/display callbacks keep the same
  ordinary active-player/team assumptions as stock BtS;
* its getEndTurnState is stock-like and lacks K-Mod's later PitBoss repair.

This supports two separate conclusions:
1. K-Mod's explicit PitBoss guard is a targeted observed engine-state repair and
   remains a better lifecycle oracle than speculative null guarding everywhere.
2. AdvCiv practical 2741 really did weaken the stock/K-Mod double-click null shape,
   but current local material still does not prove the EXE invokes that export with
   pCity==NULL and pPlot!=NULL during normal play. Keep as hardening debt, not F307.

NUKE AOE VISUAL-STATE CHALLENGE -- OPEN CONTROL, NO FINDING
-----------------------------------------------------------
AdvCiv practical 3685 introduced AREA_BORDER_LAYER_NUKE. updateNukeAreaOfEffect
returns before clearing that layer when no selected nuke exists; the only explicit
clear of AREA_BORDER_LAYER_NUKE in current source is inside this function after the
selected-nuke check. This creates a theoretical stale-overlay concern if selection
changes before the interface invokes the usual "still-selected nuke + null center"
clear path.

No normal UI transition ordering proving such a stale overlay has yet been found.
The common interface-mode transition can call getNewHighlightPlot/updateNukeArea-
OfEffect while the nuke remains selected, which clears the layer. Therefore this
remains an inherited visualization control unless a reproducible selection/mode
sequence is established.

SAS made SHOW_UNIT_LAYER_OPTIONS and VICTORY_SOUNDTRACK_AVAILABLE function-local
statics and similarly cached the two SAS city-camera percentage defines. Current
source contains no runtime setter for those defines, and the relevant values are
XML/configuration policy rather than BUG options advertised as live toggles. The
BUG EnlargeHUD choice remains queried dynamically. No supported live-setting
contract is currently violated.

CvGlobals::SetGraphicsInitialized(true) immediately calls

DOW / SELECTION-LIST MESSAGE EDGE PASS -- CONTROL CLOSED
--------------------------------------------------------
selectionListMove and selectionListGameNetMessage were reread together with the
BUTTONPOPUP_DECLAREWARMOVE reply path in CvDLLButtonPopup.cpp solely to close the
queue-018 continuation contract (not to pre-audit queue 019).

Current protections:
* selectionListMove requires a current head unit owned by the active player.
* selectionListGameNetMessage repeats that head-unit/ownership precondition.
* the initial DOW popup stores coordinates from an already-resolved current map plot.
* on popup reply, CvDLLButtonPopup re-resolves the current head unit; if it is gone,
  the move is not replayed.
* the replay then returns through selectionListGameNetMessage with MOVE_DECLARE_WAR,
  so the current selection is checked again rather than retaining an old unit
  pointer from popup construction time.

The coordinates remain valid because map dimensions do not change while this popup
is pending. No current stale-pointer / invalid-plot consequence survives here.
Popup-specific diplomacy/state assumptions remain for the full queue-019 audit.

NUKE AOE LAYER -- STRUCTURALLY PLAUSIBLE, STILL UNNUMBERED
----------------------------------------------------------
The deeper pass strengthens the shape but still does not prove the EXE ordering.

Current asymmetry:
* updateSeaPatrolColors clears AREA_BORDER_LAYER_PATROLLED before checking whether
  the selected unit is currently patrolling, and updateSelectionList explicitly
  clears that layer when all units become unselected.
* updateNukeAreaOfEffect first obtains the head selected unit and returns immediately
  when it is NULL or no longer a nuke; only after that does it clear
  AREA_BORDER_LAYER_NUKE.
* AREA_BORDER_LAYER_NUKE has no other explicit clear site in current C++.

Current NUKE InterfaceMode XML has bHighlightPlot=1. While the nuke remains selected,
leaving the targeting mode can reach a non-highlight-mode getNewHighlightPlot call
and clear the layer. The dangerous ordering would instead be:
    nuke radius painted -> selection changes to NULL/non-nuke first -> cleanup call
at which point updateNukeAreaOfEffect returns before clearing.

The DLL itself allows unit-cycle controls while not focused and those controls call
UI.selectUnit without an explicit DLL-side interface-mode reset. That makes the
ordering worth a practical UI test, but selectUnit and interface-mode transition
ordering live in the EXE-facing interface; local source still cannot establish
whether the EXE resets the mode / requests cleanup before or after changing the head
unit.

Therefore this remains a strong visualization-hardening candidate, not F307.
A robust local hardening would simply clear AREA_BORDER_LAYER_NUKE before the
selected-nuke early return. Suggested manual reproduction if desired later:
1. select a nuclear unit;
2. enter Nuke mode and hover a legal target until the yellow AOE is painted;
3. cycle/select a different unit (and separately test firing/consuming the nuke);
4. observe whether the yellow AOE ever remains stuck afterward.

CITY-SCREEN DOUBLE/RIGHT-CLICK LIFECYCLE -- STATUS UNCHANGED
-------------------------------------------------------------
The strongest crash-shaped candidate remains AdvCiv practical 2741's double-click
callback:

    if (pCity != NULL && pCity->plot() == pPlot) ...
    else if (pPlot != NULL && pCity->getCityPlotIndex(*pPlot) == NO_CITYPLOT) ...

Stock/K-Mod/Civ4CE guard pCity, and practical 2416 explicitly hardened the adjacent
single/right-click callbacks before practical 2741 added this new branch without the
equivalent guard. A pCity==NULL, pPlot!=NULL callback would therefore crash.

The final local lifecycle pass still does not establish such an EXE producer. The
callback's semantics identify pCity as the city currently being worked/viewed, and
normal city-screen operation pairs that callback with a selected city. CvCity::kill
clears selected cities before destruction, but no evidence shows the EXE then emits
this city-screen callback with the old screen context but null pCity.

The right-click callback's
    isCityScreenUp() ? getHeadSelectedCity()->plot() : NULL
has the same unsupported teardown-state dependency. It could cheaply use pCity->plot()
after the existing pCity guard, but no normal screen-up/no-head-city producer was
proven.

Both remain worthwhile defensive hardening, neither is numbered under the current
producer+contract+consequence standard.

UNNUMBERED CONTROL A -- CITY-SCREEN DOUBLE-CLICK NULL HARDENING
---------------------------------------------------------------
Current AdvCiv/SAS handleCityScreenPlotDoublePicked can dereference pCity in the
second branch when pCity == NULL and pPlot != NULL.  Stock/K-Mod/Civ4CE guard
pCity, and AdvCiv practical 2416 tightened the neighboring city-screen callbacks
before practical 2741 re-enabled double-click behavior without carrying an
analogous guard forward.

That ancestry makes a defensive guard attractive, for example rejecting either
NULL input before entering the body.  The missing audit fact is still the EXE
producer: local source/history does not demonstrate that normal play can invoke
this exported callback with a live plot and no city after city-screen selection
teardown.  Therefore this remains hardening debt, not F307.

UNNUMBERED CONTROL B -- NUKE AOE BORDER-LAYER CLEANUP ORDER
-----------------------------------------------------------
updateNukeAreaOfEffect obtains the selected unit and returns when no nuke is
selected before it clears AREA_BORDER_LAYER_NUKE.  updateSeaPatrolColors has the
stronger cleanup pattern: clear its layer first, then decide whether anything
should be repainted.  No other explicit Nuke-layer clear was found in current
C++.

The asymmetry is real and inherited from AdvCiv's introduction of the feature;
current SAS color/cache edits did not create it.  A stale yellow radius is
structurally possible only if the engine changes selection/interface state and
then invokes this callback after the selected nuke has disappeared or ceased to
be the head unit, without another engine-level layer clear first.  That event
ordering cannot be established from the available DLL/Python source.

Useful empirical test retained for later if desired:
- select a nuke;
- enter its nuke targeting mode and hover a legal target so the yellow radius is
  visibly painted;
- switch/cycle directly to a non-nuke or consume/fire the nuke;
- observe whether the old yellow radius remains until another redraw/mode
  transition.
A reproducible persistent overlay would supply the missing current producer /
consequence evidence and justify reopening this control.  Without it, do not
spend F307.

OPENING SURFACE / DELTA MAP
---------------------------
Current SAS CvDLLButtonPopup.cpp contains 43 CvDLLButtonPopup:: definitions.  Base
AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same 43-function surface.  K-Mod has the same functional
surface plus its older launchPythonScreen helper, which AdvCiv later folded away.

After stripping comments and whitespace, only six current SAS functions differ
semantically from Base AdvCiv 1.14:
  * OnOkClicked
  * launchButtonPopup
  * launchRazeCityPopup
  * launchDoEspionagePopup
  * launchDoEspionageTargetPopup
  * launchEventPopup

The first-pass classification of those six is deliberately narrow:
  * OnOkClicked: PolicyAdvisorScreen rename for the Civics/policy UI path.
  * launchButtonPopup: KI#203 optional AI-Auto-Play suppression of only
    BUTTONPOPUP_TEXT while autoplay is active.
  * launchRazeCityPopup: static cache of PLAYER_ALWAYS_RAZES_CITIES.
  * launchDoEspionagePopup / launchDoEspionageTargetPopup: KI#398 fix that resolves
    the eligible selected Spy rather than assuming the arbitrary selection head is
    the Spy.
  * launchEventPopup: static warning-color cache only on the SAS-vs-Base delta;
    however the inherited Base AdvCiv body contains the new F307 root below.

The Auto Play BUTTONPOPUP_TEXT branch survives its opening challenge: the
OnOkClicked BUTTONPOPUP_TEXT case performs no gameplay/session action, current
producers use it as informational notices, and no shipped runtime setter changes
SAS_AIAUTOPLAY_AUTO_DISMISS_INFORMATIONAL_POPUPS_ENABLE after its static cache has
been initialized.  Do not reopen KI#203 merely because the popup is skipped.

F307 / KI#630 -- EVENT-POPUP "REVALIDATION" RE-RANDOMIZES AND LEAKS A SECOND TRIGGER RECORD
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
~~~~
Current Base AdvCiv / SAS launchEventPopup begins with the already-existing human
EventTriggeredData selected at the end of the previous turn:

    EventTriggeredData* pTriggeredData =
        kActivePlayer.getEventTriggered(info.getData1());

It then tries to "Double-check trigger conditions" through:

    if (kActivePlayer.initTriggeredData(pTriggeredData->m_eTrigger) == NULL)
    {
        kActivePlayer.deleteEventTriggered(pTriggeredData->getID());
        ...
        return false;
    }

initTriggeredData is NOT a pure predicate.  It is the constructor/randomizer used by
CvPlayer::doEvents to create a fresh candidate trigger.  On a successful call it:
  * may choose religion, corporation, plot, building and other-player context with
    SyncRandNum;
  * calls addEventTriggered(), inserting a NEW live record into m_eventsTriggered;
  * calls the trigger's Python doEventTrigger/can-do hook on that new record;
  * may consume additional SyncRandNum for trigger text and world-news text;
  * returns the newly inserted EventTriggeredData pointer.

The current function contains seven distinct SyncRandNum call sites before/after
allocation depending on trigger shape.  launchEventPopup tests only whether that
returned pointer is NULL and immediately discards the pointer when it is non-NULL.
It never deletes the newly-created validation record.

CURRENT PRODUCER
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The producer is ordinary shipped random-event flow, not a hypothetical caller:
  1. CvPlayer::doEvents creates candidate EventTriggeredData through
     initTriggeredData.
  2. For the selected human event, CvPlayer::trigger(const EventTriggeredData&)
     queues BUTTONPOPUP_EVENT carrying kData.getID().
  3. Human event choice is deliberately delayed until the popup is shown (often the
     next player turn).
  4. The EXE asks CvDLLButtonPopup::launchButtonPopup to render BUTTONPOPUP_EVENT,
     which dispatches launchEventPopup.
  5. launchEventPopup retrieves the original record by the queued ID and then calls
     initTriggeredData a second time merely to decide whether the old popup should
     still be shown.

Thus every successfully revalidated human random-event popup reaches the root.

CONCRETE CURRENT CONSEQUENCES
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
A. Persistent logical-state leak in single-player too

On successful revalidation, the second EventTriggeredData remains in
CvPlayer::m_eventsTriggered.  This is an FFreeListTrashArray game-state container,
not a temporary heap object owned by launchEventPopup.  The normal doEvents candidate
cleanup deletes only the candidate pointers that doEvents itself retained in its
local vector.  There is no generic sweep of anonymous m_eventsTriggered entries.
The orphan therefore survives until an explicit delete by ID or player reset; no
such ID is retained here.

m_eventsTriggered is serialized by CvPlayer::write / restored by CvPlayer::read, so
these validation records persist into saves.  This is a logical game-state/save
leak, not merely a lost C++ pointer.

B. Rendering a UI popup mutates synchronized event/RNG state

initTriggeredData can consume synchronized random numbers while selecting trigger
context and text.  It also runs the trigger's Python predicate on the newly-created
record.  A delayed popup launch should be a validation/display operation, but the
current code can therefore advance gameplay RNG and execute trigger-construction
logic merely because the popup is being rendered.

C. Multiplayer desynchronization risk is structural, not just theoretical API debt

Most shipped event triggers are allowed in multiplayer: current XML has 197
EventTriggerInfo entries, of which 184 have bSinglePlayer=0.  The revalidation is in
CvDLLButtonPopup, i.e. the local UI popup-launch path, while the state it modifies
(m_eventsTriggered and SyncRand) is gameplay/synchronized state.  CvPlayer's own
save code explicitly treats displayed popups as potentially different between
network machines.  Therefore invoking synchronized random/event construction from
this UI-local renderer creates a direct OOS hazard: the client that renders its
human player's event can advance/add state that another peer has no reason to
construct at that moment.

The single-player orphan-record consequence already proves F307 even without an
empirical OOS reproduction; the network consequence raises the repair priority.

D. The supposed check does not actually validate the original event instance

The revalidation call passes only pTriggeredData->m_eTrigger and leaves all context
parameters at their defaults.  initTriggeredData is therefore free to pick a NEW
city/plot/unit/religion/corporation/other-player instance.  Success means "some new
instance of this trigger can be constructed now," not necessarily "the original
queued event instance is still valid."  launchEventPopup later tests event choices
against the old pTriggeredData, which catches some stale cases, but the advertised
trigger-condition recheck is semantically mismatched even apart from the leak/RNG
mutation.

ANCESTRY
~~~~~~~~
This is inherited from Base AdvCiv, not a SAS regression.

* K-Mod and Civ4CE/BtS launchEventPopup do not call initTriggeredData while rendering
  the event popup.
* Pre-SAS AdvCiv practical 4304 / commit 154ae6bd22 (2025-01-26), titled
  "Cancel random event popup if trigger conditions no longer met," introduced the
  exact call.
* The commit message explains the legitimate motivation: random events trigger at
  the end of a human player's turn, but the choice popup may not be handled until
  the next turn, so trigger conditions can become stale meanwhile.  It explicitly
  describes the new operation as "re-checking" conditions.
* Current Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS both retain the side-effectful
  implementation.

The root is therefore the use of a state-creating/randomizing initializer as a
predicate in the UI renderer, not the valid goal of stale-event revalidation.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Preferred repair: launchEventPopup must use a side-effect-free validation path for
the ORIGINAL pTriggeredData.  Refactor the relevant condition checks out of
initTriggeredData into a pure helper (or introduce a dedicated
canStillTrigger(EventTriggeredData const&) style helper) that:
  * does not allocate/add EventTriggeredData;
  * does not consume SyncRandNum;
  * does not reroll city/plot/unit/religion/corporation/player context;
  * does not invoke a construction-time Python hook merely to display the popup;
  * evaluates the old queued instance where instance-specific context matters.

A minimal containment patch that merely stores the new pointer and immediately
calls deleteEventTriggered(newId) would stop the persistent orphan, but it is NOT a
complete repair: it would still consume synchronized RNG / call trigger Python and
would still validate a freshly rerolled instance instead of the queued one.

If a pure refactor is undesirable in the first implementation pass, removing the
4304 reinitialization check and relying on the existing per-event canDoEvent(old
pTriggeredData) availability pass is safer for state/RNG integrity than retaining a
UI-local randomized constructor.  That fallback gives up some of 4304's intended
trigger-level stale-condition coverage, so a pure old-instance validator remains the
better final design.

FAST EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION (OPTIONAL, NOT REQUIRED FOR ROOT PROOF)
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
For a human random event, log/getNumEventsTriggered immediately before and after
launchEventPopup.  With successful 4304 revalidation, the count should increase by
one before the player has chosen any event outcome.  Saving immediately after the
popup is shown should preserve that extra record because m_eventsTriggered is in the
player save stream.

For MP/OOS validation, a two-human network test with random events enabled can log
m_eventsTriggered count and SyncRand seed/call state per peer around the first human
event popup.  The source already establishes the state mutation; this test would
only measure how quickly the divergence becomes externally visible.

NUMBERING / DOC NOTE
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
F307 is now CONFIRMED and consumes provisional KI#630.  The current repository
README_Known_Issues.md still contains the earlier provisional KI#630 text saying
F307 was unassigned during queue 018.  That source document was intentionally not
modified during the audit; implementation/reconciliation should replace that stale

TIME-GAP / RECEIVER CONTROLS CLOSED SO FAR
------------------------------------------
The launcher/reply pass has eliminated several tempting stale-popup candidates:

* Vassal tribute: the master popup lists a currently tradeable resource and the
  human-vassal grant popup can be delayed, but the eventual implement-deal path
  reaches CvDeal::addTradeItems(..., bCheckAllowed=true), which re-runs
  canTradeItem before applying the deal.  Losing/trading the resource while the
  popup is outstanding therefore rejects the stale deal instead of creating an
  invalid resource agreement.

* Diplomatic vote: a stale vote ID is rejected by the receiver when the
  VoteTriggeredData no longer exists.  The popup does not retain a raw pointer.

* Free colony: positive popup buttons carry an area ID, and CvPlayer::splitEmpire
  resolves the area again and rechecks both canSplitEmpire() and canSplitArea()
  before mutating the empire.  A stale area choice is therefore receiver-safe.

* Spaceship launch: K-Mod's old protection remains in launchLaunchPopup
  (!kTeam.canLaunch(eVictory) => cancel); CvPlayer::launch independently repeats
  canLaunch at execution.  The old K-Mod "launch popup after launch became
  impossible" defect has not regressed.

* Raze city: the old AdvCiv crash repair remains present.  When keeping a captured
  city would change its liberation target, eFutureLiberationPlayer is explicitly
  checked for NO_PLAYER before GET_PLAYER dereference.  The launcher also resolves
  the captured city ID afresh before use.

* Popup sound/relaunch tracking from AdvCiv practical 2453 remains structurally
  intact: only a successful launch plays AS2D_IF_BUTTONPOPUP_UP, while every launch
  attempt reports ButtonPopupLaunched so CvPlayer can distinguish relaunches.  No
  SAS delta was found in this ownership/lifecycle contract.

LOADUNIT / LEADUNIT ORDINAL TIME-GAP NOTE
-----------------------------------------
Both popups historically encode a displayed choice as an ordinal (1st eligible,
2nd eligible, ...), then re-enumerate the current plot when the player clicks.
That is weaker than storing a stable ID.  For LOADUNIT, however, the actual command
includes both transport owner and ID and the popup is an immediate modal choice;
no ordinary local mutation path was found that changes the active player's own
candidate ordering while the popup is open.  A same-team remote transport can move
in simultaneous multiplayer, but that presently establishes only a narrow stale
ordinal/no-op-or-retarget race, not a stronger general root.  Keep as hardening
unless runtime evidence makes it important.  A stable owner+unit-ID button payload
would be cleaner.

The LEADUNIT path has a separate, fully proved cross-player alias root below; do not
merge that with the generic ordinal observation.

F308 / KI#631 -- LEAD-UNIT POPUP CAN LIST TEAMMATE UNITS AND RESOLVE THEIR PLAYER-LOCAL ID AS A DIFFERENT OWN UNIT
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
~~~~
The Great General / Warlord action already defines its candidate-owner invariant in
CvUnit::canLead(pPlot, -1):

    if (pUnit != this && pUnit->getOwner() == getOwner() &&
        pUnit->canPromote(leaderPromotion, getID()))
    {
        iUnits++;
    }

Only SAME-OWNER units are therefore legitimate targets of this Great General.

CvDLLButtonPopup::launchLeadUnitPopup does not preserve that invariant.  It walks
EVERY unit on the selected group's plot and accepts solely:

    if (pUnit->canPromote((PromotionTypes)info.getData1(), info.getData2()))

The BUTTONPOPUP_LEADUNIT OnOk handler repeats the same owner-blind enumeration.
FOR_EACH_UNIT_VAR_IN on a CvPlot resolves the plot's full IDInfo unit list; it does
not filter by player.

WHY canPromote DOES NOT SAVE THIS
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
For a leader promotion, CvUnit::canPromote(ePromotion, iLeaderUnitId) resolves the
leader through the CANDIDATE unit's owner:

    CvUnit* pWarlord = GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).getUnit(iLeaderUnitId);
    ...
    return pWarlord->getUnitInfo().getLeaderPromotion() == ePromotion;

Civ4 unit IDs are player-local.  CvPlayer::getUnit(int iID) is simply
m_units.getAt(iID), and each CvPlayer owns its own m_units array.

Therefore info.getData2() -- the active player's Great General ID -- has a different
meaning when canPromote is invoked on a teammate's unit.  If the teammate happens
to own its own Great General / Warlord at the same numeric player-local ID, then a
teammate combat unit on the shared plot can pass canPromote and appear as a legal
button even though the active Great General cannot legitimately lead that unit.

This is not an invented hostile-input scenario.  Team/Permanent-Alliance players
can normally stack units on the same plot, and independent per-player unit ID
sequences naturally overlap.  The action itself proves that foreign targets are
not intended because CvUnit::canLead(..., -1) explicitly filters to getOwner().

CLICK-TIME ID ALIAS / CONSEQUENCE
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The popup button is only an ordinal.  Once that ordinal reaches the foreign
teammate unit, OnOk sends:

    selectionListGameNetMessage(..., MISSION_LEAD, pUnit->getID());

MISSION_LEAD carries ONLY the numeric unit ID -- no owner.  The selected active
Great General eventually executes CvUnit::lead(iData1), whose explicit target path
resolves:

    CvUnit* pUnit = GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).getUnit(iUnitId);

That is now the ACTIVE GREAT GENERAL OWNER'S namespace, not the teammate namespace
whose unit generated the button.

The receiver-side invariant is weaker than it should be too.  CvUnit::canLead(pPlot,
explicitId) gets the same-owner unit by ID and tests canPromote, but does NOT verify
that the target is actually at pPlot.  CvUnit::lead then promotes that resolved own
unit and kills the Great General.

Concrete outcomes after clicking a falsely-listed teammate button are therefore:
  * if the active player has no unit with that numeric ID, the command silently
    fails;
  * if that ID resolves to an ineligible own unit, it silently fails;
  * if that ID resolves to an eligible own unit, the Great General can be attached
    to the WRONG own unit; because explicit canLead lacks an at-plot test, that own
    unit may even be somewhere else on the map.

A normal shared-team setup can therefore turn a UI target described as teammate
unit X into a mission against unrelated active-player unit Y solely because their
player-local integer IDs coincide.

CURRENT PRODUCER / REACHABILITY
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
A normal supported sequence is sufficient:
  1. Human A and teammate B (multiplayer team, Permanent Alliance, etc.) have units
     on the same plot.
  2. A has a Great General with local unit ID L and at least one legitimate own
     lead target on that plot, so the Lead action is enabled through the correct
     canLead(...,-1) owner-filtered test.
  3. B independently has a Warlord/Great-General-type unit whose player-local ID is
     also L.  Player-local ID overlap is valid and expected.
  4. A teammate combat unit on the shared plot calls canPromote(..., L); because its
     getOwner() is B, it resolves B's Warlord L and can pass the leader-promotion
     test.
  5. launchLeadUnitPopup therefore displays B's unit alongside A's own legitimate
     targets.
  6. Clicking B's displayed unit sends only B-target numeric ID T.
  7. A's Great General resolves T as A.getUnit(T), potentially acting on a different
     unit.

No EXE timing assumption, malformed network packet or unsupported mod configuration
is needed.

ANCESTRY
~~~~~~~~
This is inherited Firaxis BtS behavior retained by Civ4CE, K-Mod, Base AdvCiv 1.14
and current AdvCiv-SAS.  The supplied Civ4CE BtS and K-Mod launchLeadUnitPopup and
BUTTONPOPUP_LEADUNIT reply code have the same owner-blind canPromote scan.  The
same-generation CvUnit::canLead(...,-1) already contains the intended same-owner
filter, so the inconsistency is historical rather than a SAS design choice.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Minimal current-producer repair:
  * in BOTH launchLeadUnitPopup and the BUTTONPOPUP_LEADUNIT OnOk re-enumeration,
    reject candidates whose owner is not the selected/active Great General owner
    before calling canPromote.
  * preferably resolve the intended Great General by active-player + info.getData2()
    first and use its owner as the authoritative owner boundary.

Stronger UI repair:
  * stop encoding lead targets as ordinals; store a stable same-owner target unit ID
    (e.g. ID+1 if button 0 must remain Cancel), resolve it afresh on click and
    revalidate owner/promotion/co-location.  This also removes the generic ordinal
    time-gap weakness.

Defense-in-depth outside this queue:
  * CvUnit::canLead(pPlot, explicitId) should require the resolved target to be at
    pPlot.  That makes the mission receiver uphold the spatial contract even if a
    stale/malformed UI mission supplies a wrong same-owner ID.  The ordinary AI/UI
    callers already choose co-located targets, so this should be a contract guard,
    not a gameplay-policy change.

NUMBERING
~~~~~~~~~
F308 is CONFIRMED and consumes provisional KI#631.  F309 / provisional KI#632 is
now the next unused root slot.

F307 REPRODUCIBILITY STRENGTHENING
----------------------------------
The event leak is repeatable more than once for the same original event.  For
pick-city triggers, the event popup can include "Examine City".  Its OnOk path
selects the city and queues a fresh BUTTONPOPUP_EVENT containing the SAME original
trigger ID.  Relaunching that popup re-enters launchEventPopup and calls
initTriggeredData again, creating another anonymous validation EventTriggeredData
and consuming another construction/randomization pass.  Repeated Examine City
round-trips can therefore increase m_eventsTriggered repeatedly before the player
chooses an event result.  This is useful for a fast WorldBuilder/debug confirmation
of F307 and further confirms that the leaked record is tied to rendering/relaunch,
not to one-time event generation.

C030-WIP03 APPEND -- QUEUE 019 DEEPER DELAYED-POPUP / VOTE-LIFETIME PASS

DORMANT SDK DEFECT -- DESTROY-UNIT ESPIONAGE POPUP PASSES UNIT TYPE WHERE UNIT ID IS REQUIRED (NOT NUMBERED)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A source-contract mismatch in launchDoEspionageTargetPopup initially looked strong:
for missions with getDestroyUnitCostFactor() > 0, the popup enumerates a concrete
pTargetUnit but calls canDoEspionageMission and getEspionageMissionCost with
pTargetUnit->getUnitType() as iExtraData.  Downstream CvPlayer espionage code treats
that same iExtraData as a TARGET PLAYER-LOCAL UNIT ID.  The actual popup button, by
contrast, correctly carries pTargetUnit->getID().

That generic SDK code is therefore inconsistent and could display the wrong
eligibility/cost (or alias another target-player unit ID) in a mod that enables a
Destroy Unit espionage mission.  The shape is inherited unchanged from Firaxis BtS
through Civ4CE, K-Mod, Base AdvCiv and current SAS.

It does NOT meet the current-tree producer standard, however.  Current shipped SAS
CIV4EspionageMissionInfo.xml explicitly sets iDestroyUnitCostFactor=0 and
iBuyUnitCostFactor=0 for every EspionageMissionInfo.  CvEspionageMissionInfo also
initializes both fields to 0 before XML loading.  Base AdvCiv and the supplied
Civ4CE data likewise have no nonzero Destroy Unit mission.  Therefore the branch
cannot currently be selected from shipped data.  Keep this as dormant generic SDK
repair debt; do NOT assign F309 to it.

F309 / KI#632 -- HUMAN "NONE" ELECTION CHOICE LEAKS VoteSelectionData FOREVER
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
~~~~
CvGame::doVoteSelection creates a VoteSelectionData in m_voteSelections whenever a
human Secretary-General is asked which UN/AP resolution to propose, and queues a
BUTTONPOPUP_CHOOSEELECTION carrying that selection's ID.

launchChooseElectionPopup adds one button for every current aVoteOptions entry and
then a final "None" button.  Current AdvCiv conditionally labels that final button
"None (causes an early election)", making the no-proposal path explicit.  Its button
ID is GC.getNumVoteInfos(), deliberately outside the 0..aVoteOptions.size()-1 choice
range.

BUTTONPOPUP_CHOOSEELECTION OnOk does this:

    VoteSelectionData* pData = kGame.getVoteSelection(info.getData1());
    if (pData != NULL &&
        pPopupReturn->getButtonClicked() < (int)pData->aVoteOptions.size())
    {
        sendChooseElection(pPopupReturn->getButtonClicked(), info.getData1());
    }

Thus an ordinary resolution choice sends the synchronized CvNetChooseElection
message.  The "None" button fails the range test and sends NOTHING.

OWNERSHIP / LIFETIME CONSEQUENCE
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
CvNetChooseElection::Execute calls CvGame::setVoteChosen(iSelection, iVoteId).
That routine is also the normal owner cleanup path:

    VoteSelectionData* pVoteSelectionData = getVoteSelection(iVoteId);
    if (pVoteSelectionData != NULL)
        addVoteTriggered(*pVoteSelectionData, iSelection);
    deleteVoteSelection(iVoteId);

Repository-wide current-source search found no other ordinary deletion/consumer for
an already-created human VoteSelectionData.  deleteVoteSelection is called when
addVoteSelection itself produces no options, and by setVoteChosen after a response;
there is no later vote-cycle sweep of abandoned selection objects.

So clicking the supported "None" button leaves its VoteSelectionData live in
m_voteSelections indefinitely.  Each later no-proposal election can add another
one.

This is persistent rather than a transient heap allocation.  m_voteSelections is
an FFreeListTrashArray: live entries remain occupied until removeAt/delete is called.
CvGame::write serializes m_voteSelections through
WriteStreamableFFreeListTrashArray, which writes flist.getCount() and invokes
VoteSelectionData::write for every live entry.  CvGame::read reconstructs those
entries.  Every skipped proposal therefore accumulates runtime state and permanent
save payload until game reset.

CURRENT PRODUCER / REACHABILITY
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
No unusual timing or malformed UI input is required:
  1. A normal UN/AP vote-source cycle reaches doVoteSelection with a human
     Secretary-General and at least one valid proposal.
  2. addVoteSelection creates a live VoteSelectionData and the engine displays the
     CHOOSEELECTION popup.
  3. The human clicks the shipped "None" / "None (causes an early election)" button.
  4. OnOk deliberately suppresses sendChooseElection because that button ID is
     outside aVoteOptions.size().
  5. The selection has no remaining owner/cleanup path and remains serialized.

The behavior can repeat every applicable vote cycle.  AdvCiv's own advc.178 UI text
explicitly documents "None" as an intended gameplay choice, so this is not an
unsupported close/cancel state.

ANCESTRY
~~~~~~~~
The same out-of-range "None" button plus range-gated OnOk structure is present in
the supplied Civ4CE BtS source and K-Mod and survives in Base AdvCiv/current SAS.
The leak is therefore inherited Firaxis/BtS behavior, not a SAS regression.
AdvCiv practical advc.178 later clarified the gameplay meaning by relabeling the
button "None (causes an early election)" when applicable, but did not add cleanup.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Do NOT simply call deleteVoteSelection locally from CvDLLButtonPopup::OnOk in a
network game: m_voteSelections is synchronized serialized game state, so a UI-local
mutation risks OOS.

The existing synchronized receiver already supports a clean no-choice sentinel:
CvGame::addVoteTriggered(kData, iChoice) returns NULL when iChoice == -1, while
CvGame::setVoteChosen still unconditionally deleteVoteSelection(iVoteId).
Therefore the narrow repair is to send the ordinary choose-election network message
with selection -1 when the final None/Early-Election button is clicked.  All peers
then execute the same no-resolution cleanup through setVoteChosen.

For robustness, OnOk should distinguish valid proposal indices, the dedicated
None-button ID, and malformed/negative values explicitly rather than relying only on
"button < vector size".

NUMBERING
~~~~~~~~~

F310 / provisional KI#633 is now the next unused root slot.

VOTE STALE-ID CONTROL
---------------------
BUTTONPOPUP_DIPLOVOTE sends a vote-trigger ID that can in principle become stale
while a popup is delayed.  The receiver CvGame::castVote first resolves
getVoteTriggered(iVote) and immediately returns if the object no longer exists.
This path is therefore receiver-safe against deletion of a stale vote object.  A
normal vote writes through setPlayerVote only after the trigger has been resolved.

  constructor. It can consume SyncRandNum while selecting religion, corporation,

  EventTriggeredData; the Python doEventTrigger hook runs on it. launchEventPopup

  confirmed.

F310 / KI#633 -- STALE TEAM-VOTE BALLOTS CAN ELECT A TEAM THAT IS NO LONGER ELIGIBLE
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
~~~~
BUTTONPOPUP_DIPLOVOTE builds a team-vote ballot from the CURRENT eligibility set:

    if (!GC.getGame().isTeamVoteEligible(itTeam->getID(), eVoteSource))
        continue;
    popupAddGenericButton(..., itTeam->getID(), ...);

The button payload is therefore a TeamTypes value that was eligible when that local
popup was rendered. On reply, however, CvDLLButtonPopup::OnOkClicked sends that
stored team ID without any current eligibility check:

    sendDiploVote(info.getData1(),
        (PlayerVoteTypes)pPopupReturn->getButtonClicked());

CvNetDiploVote::Execute forwards it to CvGame::castVote. castVote does safely reject
a deleted vote-trigger ID, but for a still-live team vote it accepts any positive
team-shaped PlayerVoteTypes and writes it with setPlayerVote. It does NOT call
isTeamVoteEligible for the chosen team.

The final result path has the same gap. CvGame::findHighestVoteTeam iterates every
alive civ team and simply counts votes whose stored value equals that team ID. It
does not skip teams that have ceased to satisfy isTeamVoteEligible. Thus even votes
cast before the state change remain capable of making an ineligible team the winner.

CURRENT PRODUCER / DELAY WINDOW
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
This does not depend on an invented EXE callback race.

CvGame::doTurn increments the game turn and then calls doDiploVote BEFORE activating
players for the new round in simultaneous-turn multiplayer. doDiploVote first
processes old results and then creates the next vote selection/trigger. Human voters
receive BUTTONPOPUP_DIPLOVOTE at that point.

Current doVoteResults deliberately gives missing human voters a full grace turn:
first-pass NO_PLAYER_VOTE entries become NO_PLAYER_VOTE_CHECKED and result processing
continues only on a later turn. Therefore a live VoteTriggeredData and unanswered
human ballot are explicitly designed to survive while ordinary gameplay continues.
Candidate state can change during that supported interval.

Two concrete eligibility transitions are available in current gameplay:

1. Apostolic Palace/full-membership change

isTeamVoteEligible rejects a non-force candidate that is no longer a full member.
CvTeam::isFullMember in turn requires every member player to remain a full member;
CvPlayer::isFullMember depends on the vote-source state religion/civic and loyal
membership. A candidate team that changes out of the required state religion/civic,
or otherwise loses full membership, therefore ceases to be a valid candidate while
already-issued ballots can still contain its team ID.

2. Capitulation -- particularly explicit in AdvCiv

advc.014 modifies isTeamVoteEligible so that, when compared with a non-capitulated
full-member alternative, a capitulated candidate's ranking votes are treated as 0.
CvTeam::setVassal also calls CvGame::updateSecretaryGeneral when capitulation occurs,
with the explicit comment "Early re-election if vote source owner capitulates".
updateSecretaryGeneral clears an incumbent Secretary General if it is capitulated.

So AdvCiv expressly intends capitulation to invalidate/replace that team in the
normal candidate machinery. A team can nevertheless capitulate after the ballot is
created, remain alive, and then be selected through an old popup or retain already
cast votes. findHighestVoteTeam will still count those votes because it tests only
alive-team identity, not current eligibility.

CONSEQUENCES
~~~~~~~~~~~~
A. Secretary-General election can undo AdvCiv's immediate capitulation cleanup

If the incumbent/candidate capitulates, advc.014 may clear its old Secretary General
outcome immediately. The still-live election can later choose the same now-ineligible
team through stale votes; doVoteResults then sets the team-vote outcome back to that
team. CvGame::getSecretaryGeneral only requires the passed outcome team to be alive,
so the stale result can restore the capitulated team as Secretary General until some
later updateSecretaryGeneral trigger clears it again.

B. Diplomatic-victory vote can award victory to an ineligible candidate

Team-vote result processing uses findHighestVoteTeam and the ordinary vote threshold.
CvGame::testVictory's diplomatic-vote condition accepts a team when a victory vote's
stored outcome equals that team. There is no final isTeamVoteEligible filter there.
Consequently a stale candidate that receives enough old/stale votes can satisfy the
vote-victory outcome even though it would not appear on a freshly generated ballot.

C. The problem is not limited to a voter clicking an old button

Even if every voter answered before the eligibility transition, those stored team
IDs are not normalized or invalidated when the candidate later becomes ineligible.
The result aggregator itself therefore needs a current-eligibility guard; UI-only
revalidation is insufficient.

ANCESTRY
~~~~~~~~
The result-side shape is inherited rather than SAS-local. K-Mod already combines an
isTeamVoteEligible candidate filter (including full-membership eligibility) with a
findHighestVoteTeam that counts every alive team and does not recheck eligibility.
Base AdvCiv/current SAS retain that architecture.

AdvCiv's advc.014 later added the capitulation-specific candidate-ranking rule and
immediate Secretary-General cleanup without adding reply/result revalidation. That
makes the stale-state contradiction especially explicit in AdvCiv, but the broader
"eligibility can change while a vote is live" architecture predates SAS.

This is distinct from:
  * F022 / KI#343, which concerns how missing simultaneous voters receive their grace
    turn; and
  * F032 / KI#353, which concerns AI_diploVoteCounterCandidate comparing a vote count
    with a team ID.
Neither existing root covers stale candidate eligibility at reply/result time.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The authoritative fix belongs in synchronized game-state handling, not only in the
local popup renderer.

1. Result aggregation: findHighestVoteTeam (or an equivalent team-vote result pass)
   should ignore teams that are no longer isTeamVoteEligible for the vote source.
   This is essential because votes cast while the team was eligible can outlive the
   eligibility transition.

2. Receiver hardening: CvGame::castVote should reject or convert to abstention a
   positive team-vote choice that is no longer an eligible team for the trigger's
   vote source. This prevents a stale local popup/network message from injecting a
   newly invalid choice.

3. UI defense-in-depth: launch/focus/reply can refresh or suppress stale team choices,
   but this is not sufficient on its own because eligibility can change after some
   votes have already been recorded.

Care is needed for the existing vassal-master auto-vote behavior in addVoteTriggered:
that path intentionally calls AI_diploVote for a capitulated human vassal when the
master is eligible and the vassal team itself is not. Receiver validation should
therefore validate the CHOSEN candidate team, not require the voter's own team to be
eligible.

NUMBERING
~~~~~~~~~
F310 is CONFIRMED and consumes provisional KI#633.
F311 / provisional KI#634 is now the next unused root slot.

The earlier vassal-tribute delayed-popup concern remains worth retaining, but F310

existing vassals through CvTeam::setVassal.

However, the exact local popup/modal scheduling needed to demonstrate the stale No
button in a supported human-vassal sequence is less direct than the team-vote grace
window above. Keep this as a delayed-state hardening candidate/control and do not
manufacture F311 from it without a concrete scheduling/reproduction chain.

F311 / KI#634 -- STALE HUMAN VASSAL-TRIBUTE POPUP CAN DECLARE WAR AFTER THE VASSAL RELATION HAS ENDED
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
~~~~
launchVassalGrantTributePopup correctly checks the relationship when the popup is
first rendered:

    CvPlayer& kMaster = GET_PLAYER((PlayerTypes)info.getData1());
    if (!GET_TEAM(getActiveTeam()).isVassal(kMaster.getTeam()))
        return false;

It then presents Yes / No. BUTTONPOPUP_VASSAL_GRANT_TRIBUTE OnOk does not repeat
that relationship check.

Yes builds a one-sided TRADE_RESOURCES offer and sends implementDeal to the old
master. No does this unconditionally:

    sendChangeWar(TEAMID((PlayerTypes)info.getData1()), true);

The popup therefore stores the semantic proposition "this player is my master and
is currently demanding tribute" only at launch time. Reply-time code treats that
relationship as immutable while the popup is visible.

SUPPORTED CURRENT PRODUCER -- SIMULTANEOUS MULTIPLAYER
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The missing transition is available through the ordinary AI diplomacy loop, not a
contrived direct setVassal call.

CvPlayerAI::AI_doDiplo is a two-pass contact loop: AI targets are processed first,
human targets second. Current AdvCiv/SAS shuffles the target order inside each pass.
For a human vassal H of AI master A, the human pass can execute this shipped branch:

    if (GET_TEAM(ePlayer).isVassal(getTeam()) ...)
        ...
        addPopup(BUTTONPOPUP_VASSAL_GRANT_TRIBUTE, getID(), eBestGiveBonus)

So A can place a live tribute demand on H's UI.

Later in the SAME human-target pass, a different human C can be processed. A is
allowed to offer itself as a voluntary vassal through TRADE_VASSAL when the usual
AI_vassalTrade checks succeed. Neither canPossiblyTradeItem(TRADE_VASSAL) nor
AI_vassalTrade forbids A merely because A currently has vassals of its own.

If H precedes C in the shuffled human order, A can therefore create H's tribute
popup and then open an OFFER_VASSAL negotiation with C. In simultaneous network
multiplayer H and C have independent local UI: H's immediate popup can remain open
while C accepts A's offer.

The accepted TRADE_VASSAL is synchronized through ordinary deal execution.
CvDeal::startTrade calls:

    GET_TEAM(eFromPlayer).setVassal(kToPlayer.getTeam(), true, false);

for A becoming C's vassal. CvTeam::setVassal expressly iterates A's existing
vassals and calls freeVassal on each of them before aligning the new master relation.
H therefore ceases to be A's vassal while H's already-launched popup still carries
A and the old bonus IDs.

There is no OnFocus handler for either vassal-tribute popup and no relation-change
hook that invalidates an already-displayed BUTTONPOPUP_VASSAL_GRANT_TRIBUTE. The
launch-time guard cannot help once the popup is already on H's client.

CONCRETE CONSEQUENCES
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
A. Stale No starts a war that the current UI would never offer as "refusing tribute"

CvNetChangeWar::Execute forwards the message directly to:

    GET_TEAM(m_ePlayer).declareWar(m_eRivalTeam, false, NO_WARPLAN);

CvTeam::declareWar does NOT rerun canDeclareWar. It returns only if the teams are
already at war and then performs the full war transition, including deal killing,
war-state changes and vassal/defensive-pact cascades.

Thus H can click "No" on a demand from a civilization that is no longer H's master
and thereby declare war on former master A (and potentially A's new master coalition)
under a popup whose gameplay premise has disappeared. A freshly launched tribute
popup would have been rejected by launchVassalGrantTributePopup instead.

This is not merely a stale label: a high-impact synchronized state transition is
executed from obsolete relationship state.

B. Stale Yes can become an ordinary gift or a false acceptance message

The Yes path sends a resource deal to old master A without checking current
vassalage. CvGame/CvDeal does revalidate trade legality, which limits corruption:
if the resource trade is no longer legal, the deal can fail. But if an ordinary
resource gift remains legal after independence, the stale demand becomes a free
voluntary gift to the ex-master.

Additionally, OnOk immediately posts TXT_KEY_VASSAL_GRANT_TRIBUTE_ACCEPTED to A
regardless of whether synchronized deal validation ultimately accepts the trade.
So stale Yes can also produce an acceptance message for a deal that was rejected.
The forced stale-war path is the stronger root consequence.

WHY THE EXISTING LAUNCH GUARD IS NOT ENOUGH
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
If the relationship changes BEFORE H's popup is rendered, the launcher safely
returns false. F311 concerns the supported simultaneous-network ordering where the
popup has already been rendered on H's client and a different human client then
causes the synchronized vassal transition. Per-client immediate UI does not freeze
remote human diplomacy/game-state changes.

The same broader risk can arise from other synchronized master/vassal restructuring,
but the AI A / human H / human C sequence above is sufficient current producer proof.

ANCESTRY
~~~~~~~~
This is inherited from K-Mod / Base AdvCiv, not SAS-local.

The supplied K-Mod source already contains:
  * the two-pass AI_doDiplo human-contact machinery;
  * the AI-master BUTTONPOPUP_VASSAL_GRANT_TRIBUTE producer;
  * the launch-time isVassal guard;
  * an OnOk No branch that sends change-war without revalidation; and
  * voluntary-vassal offers in the same human-contact pass.

Base AdvCiv/current SAS retain that interaction, with later refactors but no
reply-time relationship check. Current SAS changes in queue 019 did not create it.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1. BUTTONPOPUP_VASSAL_GRANT_TRIBUTE OnOk must re-resolve the stored master player and
   require the active team to STILL be that master's vassal before either Yes or No
   has gameplay effect. If the relation is stale, dismiss silently (or show a
   neutral "demand no longer applies" notice).

2. Recheck the stored bonus/trade item before the Yes path's success message. The
   authoritative synchronized implementDeal validation should remain in place, but
   local UI should not announce acceptance before knowing the premise still holds.

3. Defense-in-depth: CvNetChangeWar / its higher-level user-input producer should not
   be treated as a general permission bypass. Rechecking canDeclareWar for ordinary
   user-initiated declaration messages would contain stale/malformed UI sources,
   provided special forced-war callers that intentionally bypass normal permission
   are kept on an explicit separate path/cause.

The narrow queue-019 fix is the reply-time isVassal revalidation; broader network
war-command hardening belongs to the message/team audit if pursued.

NUMBERING
~~~~~~~~~
F311 is CONFIRMED and consumes provisional KI#634.
F312 / provisional KI#635 is now the next unused root slot.

supported way for a relationship to change AFTER the popup had actually launched.
The AI_doDiplo two-human simultaneous-network sequence above supplies that missing
producer. Therefore this WIP supersedes WIP04's "hardening candidate" status and
promotes the same root to F311; it is not a second tribute issue.

C030-WIP06 -- QUEUE 019 LOADUNIT RETARGET ROOT + RELAUNCH CONTROL
======================================================================

STATUS AT THIS CHECKPOINT
-------------------------
Queue 019 CvGameCoreDLL/CvDLLButtonPopup.cpp remains OPEN.
Files complete remain 29 / 169.

This WIP supersedes the earlier generic LOADUNIT hardening note in WIP05. The
missing ingredient there was a deterministic current candidate-order mutation,
not merely the abstract fact that a teammate can move while the popup is open.
The plot's actual insertion order now supplies that proof.

AUTO-PLAY BUTTONPOPUP_TEXT / POPUP-RELAUNCH COUNTER CONTROL
-----------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS has an early launchButtonPopup return while AI Auto Play is active:

    if (bSASAutoDismissAutoPlayInformationalPopups &&
        kGame.getAIAutoPlay() > 0 && eType == BUTTONPOPUP_TEXT)
    {
        ...
        return false;
    }

AdvCiv's normal launch tail always calls:

    kPlayer.reportButtonPopupLaunched();

whether or not the popup actually launches. CvPlayer::killAll uses this callback
to count down m_iButtonPopupsRelaunching, whose only purpose is suppressing the
popup-up sound while already displayed popups are recreated. Thus the SAS early
return is structurally asymmetric: if a BUTTONPOPUP_TEXT were itself one of the
already displayed popups being relaunched, its attempt would not decrement the
counter.

Do NOT promote this to a numbered root at present:

* new BUTTONPOPUP_TEXT popups created while Auto Play is already running are
  rejected by this same early branch before becoming displayed relaunch entries;
* the remaining producer would require a text popup already displayed before Auto
  Play becomes active and then a killAll-triggering civic/religion/research change
  while it remains in the displayed set; that normal UI sequence has not been
  established locally;
* even if reproduced, the counter only gates popup audio. One leaked count would
  suppress the next popup-up sound and then the next ordinary launch report would
  decrement the counter again. No gameplay state or popup decision is lost.

This is worth a tiny robustness cleanup -- report the skipped launch, or move the
Auto Play suppression through the common tail -- but it does not meet the album's
root threshold without a stronger producer/consequence.

F312 / KI#635 -- LOAD-TRANSPORT POPUP ORDINAL CAN RETARGET TO A NEW TEAMMATE TRANSPORT IN SIMULTANEOUS MP
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
~~~~
BUTTONPOPUP_LOADUNIT does not encode the transport that each displayed button
represents. The launcher enumerates the currently eligible transports and stores
only an ordinal 1, 2, 3, ... as the button ID:

    int iCount = 1;
    FOR_EACH_UNIT_VAR_IN(pUnit, *pPlot)
    {
        if (!pSelectionGroup->canDoCommand(COMMAND_LOAD_UNIT,
            pUnit->getOwner(), pUnit->getID()))
        {
            continue;
        }
        ...
        popupAddGenericButton(..., iCount, WIDGET_GENERAL);
        iCount++;
    }

When the human later clicks, OnOkClicked does not resolve a stored owner+unit ID.
It enumerates the CURRENT plot again, decrements the old ordinal, and sends the
load command for whichever transport now occupies that position:

    int iCount = pPopupReturn->getButtonClicked();
    FOR_EACH_UNIT_VAR_IN(pUnit, pSelectionGroup->getPlot())
    {
        if (pSelectionGroup->canDoCommand(COMMAND_LOAD_UNIT,
            pUnit->getOwner(), pUnit->getID()))
        {
            iCount--;
            if (iCount == 0)
            {
                selectionListGameNetMessage(... COMMAND_LOAD_UNIT,
                    pUnit->getOwner(), pUnit->getID());
                break;
            }
        }
    }

WIP05 had already established that this is weaker than a stable-ID design and that
a same-team remote transport can change the candidate set while the local modal
popup remains open. What had not yet been proved was a deterministic RETARGET,
rather than merely a stale ordinal becoming a no-op.

CURRENT PRODUCER / ORDERING PROOF
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The missing ordering fact is in CvPlot::addUnit. Plot units are not append-only.
A newly arriving unit is inserted at the first point where isBeforeUnitCycle says
it belongs:

    CvUnit const& kLoopUnit = *::getUnit(pUnitNode->m_data);
    if (!kLoopUnit.isBeforeUnitCycle(kUnit))
        break;
    ...
    m_units.insertBefore(kUnit.getIDInfo(), pUnitNode);

CvUnit::isBeforeUnitCycle's FIRST ordering key is owner ID:

    if (getOwner() != kOther.getOwner())
        return (getOwner() < kOther.getOwner());

CvUnit::canLoadOnto explicitly allows a transport owned by another player on the
same team:

    if (kUnit.getTeam() != getTeam())
        return false;

There is no same-player ownership requirement.

Therefore a fully current supported simultaneous-MP sequence is:

1. Human P selects cargo units on plot X. Two valid transports A and B are on X,
   so CvGame::handleAction creates BUTTONPOPUP_LOADUNIT and the launcher displays,
   for example, A as button ordinal 1 and B as ordinal 2.
2. The popup is immediate/modal only on P's client. With simultaneous turns, a
   teammate Q can continue issuing moves on another client while P is deciding.
3. Let Q have a lower PlayerTypes ID than P. Q moves valid same-team transport C
   onto X.
4. CvPlot::addUnit inserts C ahead of P's A/B because owner ID is the first cycle
   sort key. The current eligible order is now C, A, B.
5. P clicks the still-visible button labelled/described as A (old ordinal 1).
6. OnOkClicked re-enumerates current plot units. Ordinal 1 now resolves C.
7. canDoCommand(COMMAND_LOAD_UNIT, Q, C-ID) succeeds because C is same-team and
   otherwise load-compatible; the sent command therefore loads P's selected units
   onto C, not onto the transport P chose from the popup.

This does not require stale object memory, ID aliasing, or malformed packets. Both
old and new transports are legitimate current objects; the defect is that UI
identity is represented by a mutable ordinal.

CONSEQUENCE
~~~~~~~~~~~
The player's explicit popup choice can execute against the wrong transport. In
cooperative simultaneous multiplayer this can transfer/load the selected cargo
onto a teammate-owned transport that arrived only after the choice list was
rendered. Downstream command validation cannot repair the semantic mismatch because
the newly resolved transport is itself a legal target.

Severity is lower than F308's cross-player Great-General alias/crash-risk family,
but this is still a concrete wrong-action UI/network race with a supported producer,
not merely defensive hardening.

ANCESTRY
~~~~~~~~
The ordinal-at-launch / re-enumerate-at-reply design is inherited. Supplied K-Mod,
Base AdvCiv and Civ4CE all use the same conceptual scheme for BUTTONPOPUP_LOADUNIT.
Current AdvCiv/SAS added useful null checks and a single-transport auto-load path,
but retained ordinal identity for the multi-choice popup.

FIX DIRECTION
~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Do not identify transports by list position. Each displayed button needs a stable
transport identity containing BOTH owner and player-local unit ID, because unit ID
alone is not globally unique.

Possible approaches:

* encode owner + unit ID in popup button payload/data if the popup interface has two
  stable integer fields available per choice;
* maintain a popup-owned mapping from button ID to IDInfo and re-resolve that exact
  unit on reply;
* or introduce a network/UI helper whose choice token is an IDInfo-equivalent.

On reply, re-resolve the stored transport and repeat canDoCommand before sending the
command. If the exact chosen transport disappeared or became illegal, do nothing or
refresh the popup; never silently substitute another current ordinal.

NUMBERING
~~~~~~~~~
F312 is CONFIRMED and consumes provisional KI#635.
F313 / provisional KI#636 is now the next unused root slot.

RECONCILIATION WITH WIP05
-------------------------
WIP05 said the generic LOADUNIT ordinal observation should remain hardening unless
runtime/source evidence made the retarget important. The new CvPlot::addUnit /
isBeforeUnitCycle proof supplies exactly that missing evidence and deterministically
constructs a wrong-target sequence. The earlier note is therefore promoted, not
counted as a separate issue.

C030-WIP07 -- QUEUE 019 FREE-TECH STALE-CHOICE ROOT + SESSION/RF CONTROLS

STATUS AT THIS CHECKPOINT
