SESSION / PYTHON / RISE-&-FALL CONTROL PASS
-------------------------------------------
The remaining generic callback/session popup families were paired with their reply
identity rather than judged from launcher code alone.

* BUTTONPOPUP_PYTHON: each button ID is simply the index into the same CvPopupInfo
  Python-button array whose callback name/data are retained by the popup info. The
  generic layer intentionally delegates semantic validation to the Python callback;
  no mutable game-object ordinal is reconstructed in C++.

* BUTTONPOPUP_DETAILS: launch and reply both refer to the local runtime active
  player. PBEM sends the turn only AFTER applying the edited player details. A
  normal Hotseat/PBEM active-player handoff cannot occur behind a still-unanswered
  local modal details popup. No independent remote producer was found that changes
  the client's active-player slot while this popup is live.

* ADMIN / ADMIN_PASSWORD carry game-global settings and the current runtime
  ControlTypes value. The password reply only dispatches the two controls for which
  this popup is created (World Builder/Admin Details); no stale object pointer or
  player-local ID is retained.

* ADDBUDDY / forced-disconnect / PitBoss-disconnect / kicked are session-service
  prompts with copied text/IDs or an unconditional exit-to-menu action. Their state
  is not reconstructed by mutable gameplay list position.

* Rise & Fall civ selection is stronger than the ordinary LOADUNIT/LEADUNIT popup
  design: each displayed civilization uses WIDGET_RF_CIV_CHOICE with the actual
  PlayerTypes as widget data, and CvDLLWidgetData forwards that stable player ID to
  RiseFall::handleCivSelection. Defeat/retire use chapter/button state owned by the
  local Rise & Fall controller. Rise & Fall is a local-control game mode; no
  simultaneous remote-client producer was established that can rewrite the eligible
  civ set behind this modal choice.

These families remain controls, not F314 candidates.

F311 BROADENING -- MASTER-SIDE VASSAL-DEMAND POPUP HAS THE SAME REPLY-TIME RELATIONSHIP GAP
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F311 was initially proved through BUTTONPOPUP_VASSAL_GRANT_TRIBUTE on the human
vassal's client. The inverse BUTTONPOPUP_VASSAL_DEMAND_TRIBUTE path belongs to the
same root and should be repaired at the same boundary.

The master-side launcher checks at display time:

    if (!GET_TEAM(kVassal.getTeam()).isVassal(getActiveTeam()))
        return false;

but OnOkClicked immediately trusts info.data1 as the old vassal and contains no
current isVassal check. For an AI vassal, a rejected `AI_considerOffer` flows
straight to sendChangeWar(TEAMID(eVassal), true), i.e. the same un-revalidated war
message family as the already proved human-vassal Refuse path.

A supported remote transition exists in cooperative simultaneous team play: human
master M can have another human teammate T on the same team. While M's locally
modal demand popup against AI vassal V remains open, T can negotiate team-wide
voluntary vassalage to a third HUMAN player/team C. TRADE_VASSAL is team-wide and
CvDeal::startTrade -> CvTeam::setVassal makes M/T's team a vassal; setVassal then
frees that team's existing vassals, including V. M's already rendered demand popup
has no OnFocus relation check or invalidation hook. A stale resource click can
therefore continue into AI consideration and, on rejection, the direct declaration
path against a civilization that is no longer the team's vassal.

This is NOT a new number. It strengthens F311's root from "grant tribute reply does
not revalidate the relationship" to the broader contract:

    both vassal-tribute reply handlers trust launch-time vassalage after a modal
    time gap and can reach a direct war path after that relationship has ended.

The narrow repair should re-resolve and verify the current master/vassal
relationship in BOTH BUTTONPOPUP_VASSAL_DEMAND_TRIBUTE and
BUTTONPOPUP_VASSAL_GRANT_TRIBUTE before any response action.

F313 / KI#636 -- STALE FREE-TECH POPUP CAN CONSUME THE FREE CHOICE ON A TECHNOLOGY A TEAMMATE ACQUIRED WHILE IT WAS OPEN
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
~~~~
BUTTONPOPUP_CHOOSETECH uses current research eligibility when constructing its
buttons. For a free technology (info.data1 / iDiscover > 0), each displayed tech is
added only after:

    if (!kActivePlayer.canResearch(eTech))
        continue;

and the button carries the stable technology ID through WIDGET_RESEARCH together
with iDiscover. Stable ID identity is good, but eligibility is not revalidated at
the point that consumes the free entitlement.

The K-Mod OnFocus code itself documents the stale-list concern:

    // K-Mod todo: Perhaps we should cancel this popup and create a new one
    // on-the-fly so that we can be sure the tech-list is up-to-date.

For ordinary research (iDiscover == 0), OnFocus cancels after current research is
set or game over. For the free-tech branch it only does:

    else if (!GET_PLAYER(getActivePlayer()).isChoosingFreeTech())
        popupSetAsCancelled(...);

It does NOT rebuild/cancel merely because one displayed technology has become known
or otherwise unresearchable.

The click path then consumes the local free-tech-choice count BEFORE sending the
research message:

    if (widgetDataStruct.m_iData2 > 0)
    {
        if (!kActivePlayer.isChoosingFreeTech()) ...
        else kActivePlayer.changeChoosingFreeTechCount(-1);
    }
    sendResearch(eNewActiveResearch, widgetDataStruct.m_iData2, bShift);

On synchronized execution, CvNetResearch treats m_iDiscover > 0 as an unconditional
free-tech grant:

    GET_TEAM(kPlayer.getTeam()).setHasTech(m_eTech, true, ...);

There is no current `canResearch` / `!isHasTech` guard on that free-tech branch.
CvTeam::setHasTech immediately returns when the team already has the technology:

    if (isHasTech(eTech) == bNewValue)
        return;

Thus a stale but valid TechTypes ID can consume the free choice without granting
anything.

SUPPORTED SIMULTANEOUS-TEAM PRODUCER
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1. Human P receives one free-tech choice and BUTTONPOPUP_CHOOSETECH displays tech T,
   which is currently researchable and not yet known by P's team.
2. P has human teammate Q in a simultaneous multiplayer game. The popup is modal on
   P's client only; Q continues acting on another client.
3. While P is deciding, Q causes the shared team to acquire T -- e.g. through an
   accepted technology trade with another team. Technology ownership is team-wide.
4. P's already-rendered free-tech popup is not rebuilt merely because T became
   known. Its T button still exists.
5. P clicks T. CvDLLWidgetData::doResearch sees a free-tech click and decrements
   P's choosing-free-tech count.
6. CvNetResearch::Execute calls setHasTech(T, true). Since the team already owns T,
   setHasTech returns immediately.
7. For a one-tech entitlement (iDiscover == 1), no replacement chooseTech call is
   made. The entitlement is gone and P receives no technology from it.

The producer does not depend on object deletion, enum aliasing, malformed packets,
or an EXE timing guess. Simultaneous remote teammate actions are precisely the kind
of state change a local modal popup cannot freeze.

CONSEQUENCE
~~~~~~~~~~~
A legitimate free technology can be silently lost. The user clicked the technology
that the still-visible popup offered, but by execution time it is already team-owned;
the grant becomes a no-op after the free-choice state has been consumed.

For iDiscover > 1, the next free-tech popup is still created with iDiscover-1, so
one of the multiple free choices is likewise lost.

ANCESTRY
~~~~~~~~
The relevant architecture is inherited from K-Mod / Base AdvCiv. Supplied K-Mod
contains both:

* the OnFocus TODO acknowledging that the tech list may be stale;
* the free-tech widget-side decrement followed by CvNetResearch's unconditional
  setHasTech branch.

Current SAS retains those contracts. This is not introduced by the recent SAS popup
changes.

FIX DIRECTION
~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The free entitlement must be consumed only after the chosen technology is still a
valid current free-tech target.

At minimum:

1. Before decrementing the free-tech-choice state in CvDLLWidgetData::doResearch,
   recheck that the exact selected TechTypes is still researchable/not already
   known. If stale, do not consume the entitlement; refresh/reopen the choice.
2. Defense-in-depth at CvNetResearch::Execute: for m_iDiscover > 0, reject an
   already-known or otherwise invalid free-tech target rather than silently treating
   setHasTech's no-op as a successful consumption. The target player's local client
   should be given/reopened the same remaining free-tech choice.
3. Rebuilding/canceling the free-tech popup when relevant team tech state changes
   would improve UX, but receiver-side validation is still required for network
   latency between click and execution.

Care is needed because m_iChoosingFreeTechCount is UI/control state with historical
K-Mod multiplayer handling; the repair should preserve the entitlement exactly once
rather than merely adding another unconditional chooseTech increment on every
client.

DISTINCTNESS
~~~~~~~~~~~~
This is not F312: F312 resolves a mutable ordinal to the WRONG legal transport.
F313 carries the correct stable TechTypes but fails to revalidate its changed
eligibility before consuming a one-shot entitlement.

It is also unrelated to F020/KI#341, which concerns initial-score normalization of
civilization free starting technologies.

NUMBERING
~~~~~~~~~
F313 is CONFIRMED and consumes provisional KI#636.
F314 / provisional KI#637 is now the next unused root slot.

C030-WIP08 -- QUEUE 019 STALE SECRETARY-GENERAL SELECTION / MIN-VOTER ROOT
======================================================================

STATUS AT THIS CHECKPOINT

F314 / KI#637 -- STALE SECRETARY-GENERAL RESOLUTION POPUP CAN BYPASS THE CURRENT MINIMUM-VOTER RULE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
~~~~
Human Secretary-General resolution selection is a two-stage delayed contract:

1. CvGame::addVoteSelection(eVoteSource) snapshots the currently valid resolution
   options into VoteSelectionData.
2. CvDLLButtonPopup displays those copied options in BUTTONPOPUP_CHOOSEELECTION.
3. A later human click sends only the stored selection ID + option ordinal.
4. CvGame::setVoteChosen turns that old snapshot into a live VoteTriggeredData.

K-Mod deliberately strengthened stage 1 by replacing the generic resolution test:

    //if (canDoResolution(eVoteSource, kData))
    if (isValidVoteSelection(eVoteSource, kData)) // K-Mod (zomg!)

isValidVoteSelection contains validity that is NOT part of canDoResolution. Most
importantly, it counts the CURRENT eligible voting teams and rejects the proposal
when they fall below CvVoteInfo::getMinVoters():

    int iVoters = 0;
    ...
    if (iVoters < GC.getInfo(kData.eVote).getMinVoters())
        return false;

Current shipped CIV4VoteInfo.xml sets iMinVoters=3 for the vote definitions checked
in this pass, including ordinary choose-election resolutions.

The delayed human reply does not re-run that strengthened validity contract.
CvDLLButtonPopup::OnOkClicked merely verifies that the old VoteSelectionData still
exists and that the old ordinal is in range:

    VoteSelectionData* pData = kGame.getVoteSelection(info.getData1());
    if (pData != NULL &&
        pPopupReturn->getButtonClicked() < (int)pData->aVoteOptions.size())
    {
        sendChooseElection((VoteTypes)pPopupReturn->getButtonClicked(),
                info.getData1());
    }

(The sendChooseElection parameter type/name is historical; this value is the option
ordinal, not the option's VoteTypes.)

The synchronized receiver then trusts the snapshot:

    void CvGame::setVoteChosen(int iSelection, int iVoteId)
    {
        VoteSelectionData* pVoteSelectionData = getVoteSelection(iVoteId);
        if (pVoteSelectionData != NULL)
            addVoteTriggered(*pVoteSelectionData, iSelection);
        deleteVoteSelection(iVoteId);
    }

addVoteTriggered(VoteSelectionData,int) only checks ordinal bounds and copies the old
VoteSelectionSubData. It does not call isValidVoteSelection.

The later result-time cancellation is also insufficient. CvGame::doVoteResults calls
canDoResolution(eVoteSource, subdata), not isValidVoteSelection. canDoResolution
checks whether the resolution remains semantically executable by current members,
but contains no getMinVoters check. Thus the exact validity K-Mod added at proposal
construction can disappear while the human popup is pending and never be checked
again.

SUPPORTED CURRENT PRODUCER
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
This does not rely on an imagined EXE race. Current turn ordering exposes a normal
simultaneous-multiplayer time gap:

    incrementGameTurn();
    ...
    doDiploVote();
    if (isMPOption(MPOPTION_SIMULTANEOUS_TURNS))
    {
        ...
        kLoopPlayer.setTurnActive(true);
    }

CvGame::doDiploVote -> doVoteSelection therefore creates the human Secretary-
General's VoteSelectionData and queues BUTTONPOPUP_CHOOSEELECTION before the new
turn's simultaneous players are activated. The popup is immediate/modal only on the
Secretary-General player's local client; other human clients can act independently
once their turns are activated.

A concrete current sequence is:

1. Vote source V has exactly three eligible voting teams. Human Secretary General S
   receives a resolution-selection popup. An ordinary non-targeted proposal such as
   Free Trade is included because isValidVoteSelection sees iVoters == 3 and current
   semantic requirements are satisfied.
2. While S leaves that popup unanswered, another simultaneous human client acts.
   One of the three voting civilizations/teams is eliminated, or otherwise loses
   all vote-source voting membership, leaving only two current voting teams.
3. A fresh isValidVoteSelection for the displayed resolution now returns false:
   current iVoters == 2 < shipped iMinVoters == 3.
4. S clicks the still-visible old resolution button. CHOOSEELECTION has no OnFocus
   refresh beyond cancelling when GAMESTATE_OVER, so the stale option remains.
5. setVoteChosen copies the old option into a live VoteTriggeredData without the
   current isValidVoteSelection check.
6. doVoteResults later calls canDoResolution, which can still return true for an
   ordinary resolution whose remaining two members can comply.
7. Vote threshold is recomputed from current vote population by getVoteRequired;
   there is no separate minimum-team floor there. The remaining voters can therefore
   meet the percentage threshold and pass the ballot.
8. setVoteOutcome/processVote applies a real resolution effect -- e.g. Free Trade
   changes the global free-trade count; other generic resolutions can similarly
   alter no-nukes/forced-civic/trade-route state -- despite the current electorate
   being below the minimum required to propose that resolution.

The producer requires neither stale object memory nor malformed network input. It is
ordinary asynchronous human decision time in supported simultaneous multiplayer,
combined with a membership-changing game event on another client.

CONSEQUENCE
~~~~~~~~~~~
A resolution can be proposed and enacted with fewer current voting teams than XML
explicitly requires. This is a semantic rules bypass, not merely stale popup text.
The current game state itself says the option is invalid under isValidVoteSelection,
but the delayed human-selection path converts the historical snapshot into a live
ballot anyway.

ANCESTRY / ROOT CAUSE
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The important split is inherited from K-Mod:

* Civ4CE/BtS's generic non-targeted branch used canDoResolution when building the
  Secretary-General choice list.
* K-Mod explicitly changed that branch to isValidVoteSelection, thereby making
  minimum voter count and the rest of that stronger predicate part of proposal
  validity.
* K-Mod left setVoteChosen/addVoteTriggered unchanged and left result-time
  cancellation on canDoResolution.
* Base AdvCiv and current SAS inherit the same split.

So this is best understood as an incomplete K-Mod strengthening: proposal creation
learned a stronger validity predicate, but delayed human acceptance and result
validation were not brought onto the same contract.

DISTINCTNESS
~~~~~~~~~~~~
This is distinct from the other queue-019 vote roots:

* F309 is ownership/lifetime: choosing None/Early Election fails to run the normal
  setVoteChosen cleanup and leaks VoteSelectionData.
* F310 is candidate validity during an already-created TEAM VOTE: stale candidate
  team IDs are accepted/counted after eligibility changes.
* F314 is resolution-option validity BEFORE a ballot exists: a stale Secretary-
  General proposal snapshot bypasses current isValidVoteSelection, specifically
  including K-Mod's minimum-voter rule, and creates a ballot that should no longer
  be creatable.

No prior album finding mentioning iMinVoters or this setVoteChosen validity split was
found during duplicate reconciliation.

FIX DIRECTION
~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The synchronized transition from VoteSelectionData to VoteTriggeredData needs to
revalidate the exact stored VoteSelectionSubData against CURRENT game state before
creating the ballot.

A narrow repair is conceptually:

    VoteSelectionData* pData = getVoteSelection(iVoteId);
    if (pData != NULL && iSelection >= 0 &&
        iSelection < (int)pData->aVoteOptions.size() &&
        isValidVoteSelection(pData->eVoteSource,
            pData->aVoteOptions[iSelection]))
    {
        addVoteTriggered(*pData, iSelection);
    }
    deleteVoteSelection(iVoteId);

The normal cleanup should still happen even when the old choice is now invalid.
For UX, the Secretary General could be offered a fresh current selection rather than
silently losing the proposal opportunity, but synchronized validity belongs at this
transition regardless of UI refresh.

Defense-in-depth could also make doVoteResults cancel any live vote whose current
selection-level validity no longer holds. That requires care: some targeted
resolution conditions are intentionally re-evaluated differently after voting has
begun, so blindly replacing canDoResolution with isValidVoteSelection at result time
could alter legitimate semantics. The safest primary boundary is setVoteChosen,
where a ballot has not yet been created and proposal validity is exactly the relevant
contract.

NUMBERING
~~~~~~~~~
F314 is CONFIRMED and consumes provisional KI#637.
F315 / provisional KI#638 is now the next unused root slot.

----------------------------

    dormant shipped-XML branches separate from live paths;

C030-WIP09 -- QUEUE 019 CONFIRM-DELETE SELECTION-REBIND ROOT
======================================================================

STATUS AT THIS CHECKPOINT
-------------------------
Queue 019 CvGameCoreDLL/CvDLLButtonPopup.cpp remains OPEN.
Files complete remain 29 / 169.
F307-F315 are CONFIRMED in queue 019.
F316 / provisional KI#639 is UNUSED.

F315 / KI#638 -- DELETE CONFIRMATION CAN REBIND TO AN UNRELATED UNIT GROUP AFTER RAPID CYCLING DURING THE MODAL POPUP
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
~~~~
BUTTONPOPUP_CONFIRMCOMMAND preserves which ActionInfo the player asked to confirm,
but it does NOT preserve the selected units/group that the confirmation described.
The producer in CvGame::handleAction stores only:

    pInfo->setData1(iAction);
    pInfo->setOption1(bAlt);

The popup text is therefore effectively "Are you sure you want to perform this
ACTION?" against the selection that existed at construction time. On Yes,
CvDLLButtonPopup::OnOkClicked sends that action to whatever selection happens to be
CURRENT at reply time:

    int iAction = info.getData1();
    kGame.selectionListGameNetMessage(GAMEMESSAGE_DO_COMMAND,
            GC.getActionInfo(iAction).getCommandType(),
            GC.getActionInfo(iAction).getCommandData(), -1, 0,
            info.getOption1());

selectionListGameNetMessage then enumerates the current UI selection and sends one
CvNetDoCommand per currently selected unit. There is no launch-time unit/group
identity in the popup to compare against.

CURRENT SHIPPED SCOPE
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The broad shape is narrowed by XML: current shipped CIV4CommandInfos.xml has
bConfirmCommand=1 only for COMMAND_DELETE. Thus the live consequence is not an
arbitrary command being retargeted; it is specifically a confirmed unit deletion /
scrap action being applied to a replacement selection.

SUPPORTED PRODUCER -- REMOTE DEATH + RAPID UNIT CYCLING
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
A deterministic supported path exists in simultaneous multiplayer when the shipped
BUG option "Rapid Unit Cycling" is enabled.

CvUnit::kill contains special handling for the last selected unit:

    if (IsSelected())
    {
        if (gDLL->UI().getLengthSelectionList() == 1)
        {
            if (!gDLL->UI().isFocused() &&
                !gDLL->UI().isCitySelection() &&
                !gDLL->UI().isDiploOrPopupWaiting())
            {
                GC.getGame().updateSelectionList();
            }
            if (IsSelected())
                GC.getGame().cycleSelectionGroups_delayed(1, false);
            ...
        }
    }
    gDLL->UI().removeFromSelectionList(this);

The popup-waiting test protects only the immediate updateSelectionList call. It does
NOT protect the following cycleSelectionGroups_delayed call.

K-Mod's cycleSelectionGroups_delayed supports the user-visible BUG option:

    BUGOption::isEnabled("MainInterface__RapidUnitCycling", false)

When enabled and the camera is not locked, the helper directly executes:

    cycleSelectionGroups(true);

rather than merely arming the delayed engine counter. cycleSelectionGroups can call:

    gDLL->UI().selectUnit(pNextSelectionGroup->getHeadUnit(), bClear);

and therefore replace the old selected unit with another ready selection immediately.
There is no isDiploOrPopupWaiting guard in this rapid path.

A concrete sequence is:

1. Human P selects scrap-eligible unit/group A and invokes COMMAND_DELETE.
2. Because COMMAND_DELETE has bConfirmCommand=1, the game opens
   BUTTONPOPUP_CONFIRMCOMMAND. The popup stores only the Delete ActionInfo; A's
   ID/group identity is not stored.
3. P leaves the modal popup unanswered. In simultaneous multiplayer, enemy human Q
   continues acting on another client and attacks A.
4. Q destroys P's LAST currently selected unit while the confirmation popup is still
   waiting on P's client. Network/game-state processing continues despite the local
   modal decision.
5. CvUnit::kill sees isDiploOrPopupWaiting and therefore skips updateSelectionList,
   but A is still selected at that point, so it calls cycleSelectionGroups_delayed.
6. With Rapid Unit Cycling enabled, that helper immediately runs
   cycleSelectionGroups(true) and selects another ready P group B before the old
   unit is removed from the selection list.
7. P's old "Are you sure?" popup is still visible. P clicks Yes believing it refers
   to A.
8. OnOkClicked resolves no old unit identity; it sends COMMAND_DELETE to the CURRENT
   selection B.
9. CvNetDoCommand/CvUnit::doCommand revalidate COMMAND_DELETE through canScrap, but
   if B is itself scrap-eligible that validation succeeds. B is deleted.

Thus ordinary receiver legality checks cannot repair the semantic mismatch: B is a
perfectly legal unit to scrap; it is simply not the unit/group whose deletion the
player confirmed.

CONSEQUENCE
~~~~~~~~~~~
A local confirmation dialog can delete an unrelated replacement unit/group selected
automatically after the original selection dies. This is direct unintended loss of
player units caused by stale popup target identity.

The scenario is configuration-dependent because Rapid Unit Cycling defaults to
False, but it is a shipped, exposed BUG option with normal gameplay support. The
audit does not treat an explicitly supported user option as an unsupported/pathological
configuration.

ANCESTRY / ROOT CAUSE
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The popup's "remember action, use current selection later" design is inherited from
BtS/Civ4CE.

The concrete immediate-rebind producer is introduced by K-Mod's Rapid Unit Cycling
work. K-Mod commit 280 changed CvUnit::kill from:

    setCycleSelectionCounter(1);

to:

    cycleSelectionGroups_delayed(1, false);

and introduced the new helper/option whose rapid branch directly calls
cycleSelectionGroups(true). The pre-existing kill code's isDiploOrPopupWaiting guard
remained around updateSelectionList only. K-Mod therefore turned what had been an
engine-delayed cycle request into a possible immediate selection replacement inside
the popup-waiting death path without changing CONFIRMCOMMAND to retain its original
target.

Base AdvCiv and current SAS inherit both halves unchanged in substance.

DISTINCTNESS
~~~~~~~~~~~~
This is distinct from F312:

* F312 stores a mutable ORDINAL for a transport choice and later resolves that
  ordinal to the wrong legal transport.
* F315 stores the correct stable ACTION (Delete), but no target identity at all;
  K-Mod rapid cycling changes the current selection while the confirmation is still
  open, so the action is executed on the wrong legal selected group.

No prior album root for BUTTONPOPUP_CONFIRMCOMMAND / COMMAND_DELETE target rebinding
was found in duplicate search.

FIX DIRECTION
~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The strongest fix is to bind the confirmation to the selection it describes rather
than whatever happens to be selected later.

Possible approaches:

1. Store stable IDInfo identities for the units being confirmed and, on Yes,
   re-resolve exactly those surviving units and issue COMMAND_DELETE only to them.
   If all original units disappeared, the confirmation becomes a no-op.
2. For the currently shipped scope (only COMMAND_DELETE), a narrower popup-specific
   snapshot of the selected player-local unit IDs can be sufficient if ownership is
   implicit and unchanged; IDInfo is safer/general if the mechanism is later reused.
3. Defense-in-depth: cancel BUTTONPOPUP_CONFIRMCOMMAND when its original selection
   disappears/changes, or suppress rapid selection cycling while such a popup is
   outstanding. This improves UX but target identity at reply remains the robust
   contract.

Do NOT simply add canDoCommand at OnOk: the wrong replacement unit B can legitimately
pass canScrap, which is why receiver validation cannot detect the stale confirmation.

NUMBERING
~~~~~~~~~
F315 is CONFIRMED and consumes provisional KI#638.
F316 / provisional KI#639 is now the next unused root slot.

C030-WIP10 -- QUEUE 019 F315 BROADENING / SELECTION-BOUND MODAL TARGET IDENTITY
======================================================================

STATUS AT THIS CHECKPOINT
-------------------------
Queue 019 CvGameCoreDLL/CvDLLButtonPopup.cpp remains OPEN.
Files complete remain 29 / 169.
F307-F315 are CONFIRMED in queue 019.
F316 / provisional KI#639 remains UNUSED.

This checkpoint BROADENS the already-confirmed F315 from C030-WIP09. It does not
allocate another root number. The narrower WIP09 title focused on CONFIRMCOMMAND /
COMMAND_DELETE because that was the first fully proven manifestation. The same
underlying missing target-identity contract also affects other selection-bound modal
popups once K-Mod Rapid Unit Cycling replaces the launch-time selection while the
modal is still open.

F315 / KI#638 -- SELECTION-BOUND MODAL POPUPS CAN REBIND TO AN UNRELATED UNIT GROUP AFTER K-MOD RAPID CYCLING
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
GENERAL ROOT
~~~~~~~~~~~~
Several popup families are constructed from the CURRENT selected unit/group, but the
popup stores only the requested action/mission/auxiliary choice. It does not retain
stable identity for the unit/group/plot whose state the popup described. At reply,
CvDLLButtonPopup::OnOkClicked sends the stored action to whatever selection is
CURRENT then.

Normally that historical design relies on a practical UI invariant: the selected
unit/group does not silently change beneath an unanswered selection-bound modal.
K-Mod's Rapid Unit Cycling breaks that invariant in one supported path. When the
last selected unit dies while a popup is waiting, CvUnit::kill deliberately skips
updateSelectionList because isDiploOrPopupWaiting() is true, but still calls:

    GC.getGame().cycleSelectionGroups_delayed(1, false);

if the dying unit remains selected. With the user-visible BUG option
MainInterface__RapidUnitCycling enabled, cycleSelectionGroups_delayed can immediately
call cycleSelectionGroups(true) when the camera is not locked. There is no
isDiploOrPopupWaiting guard around that rapid path. A different ready group can
therefore become current before the old modal is answered.

The receiver-side legality checks then validate the REPLACEMENT selection. They
cannot determine that the popup text/options were generated for another unit/plot.

MANIFESTATION A -- CONFIRMCOMMAND / COMMAND_DELETE
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
This is the original C030-WIP09 proof and remains the simplest destructive example.
Current shipped XML sets bConfirmCommand=1 only for COMMAND_DELETE. The popup stores
the ActionInfo but no launch-time unit/group identity. If original selected unit A
dies while the modal waits and Rapid Unit Cycling selects scrap-eligible unit/group
B, clicking the old Yes sends Delete to current selection B. B passes normal
canScrap validation and is deleted even though the confirmation described A.

MANIFESTATION B -- ONE-PHASE ESPIONAGE POPUP CAN EXECUTE AT A DIFFERENT ENEMY CITY
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
launchDoEspionagePopup resolves an eligible selected Spy and builds mission buttons
from THAT spy's current plot and target player:

    CvSelectionGroup const* pSelectionGroup = m_kUI.getSelectionList();
    CvUnit const* pUnit = (pSelectionGroup == NULL ? NULL :
            pSelectionGroup->getEspionageUnit());
    CvPlot const* pPlot = pUnit->plot();
    ... canDoEspionageMission(eLoopMission, pPlot->getOwner(), pPlot, -1, pUnit) ...

The popup does not retain pUnit or pPlot. On reply, BUTTONPOPUP_DOESPIONAGE simply
sends:

    selectionListGameNetMessage(GAMEMESSAGE_PUSH_MISSION,
            MISSION_ESPIONAGE, clickedMission);

against the CURRENT selection.

Current shipped espionage XML supplies especially clean direct examples:

* ESPIONAGEMISSION_CITY_POISON_WATER has bIsTwoPhases=0;
* ESPIONAGEMISSION_CITY_UNHAPPINESS has bIsTwoPhases=0;
* ESPIONAGEMISSION_CITY_REVOLT has bIsTwoPhases=0.

Therefore no second target popup refresh intervenes. A supported sequence is:

1. Human P has selected Spy A on enemy city X and opens the espionage mission popup.
   The popup lists Poison Water because that mission is legal for A at X.
2. P leaves the modal unanswered. In simultaneous multiplayer, remote player Q
   kills A.
3. CvUnit::kill runs while the modal is waiting. With Rapid Unit Cycling enabled,
   cycleSelectionGroups_delayed immediately selects ready Spy B elsewhere.
4. Assume B is on enemy city Y where Poison Water is also legal -- an ordinary state
   for two active spies.
5. P clicks the still-visible Poison Water button generated from A/X.
6. OnOkClicked sends MISSION_ESPIONAGE to current selection B. CvUnit::espionage
   derives the target player and mission plot from B's CURRENT plot, and
   CvPlayer::doEspionageMission revalidates legality for B/Y.
7. Because Poison Water is legal there, it succeeds at Y.

The synchronized legality check is therefore not a repair: Y is a legal target, but
it is not the city whose popup the human answered.

MANIFESTATION C -- TWO-PHASE ESPIONAGE TARGET POPUP HAS THE SAME IDENTITY GAP
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
launchDoEspionageTargetPopup likewise derives its button list from the currently
selected eligible Spy and that spy's current plot/player. The popup retains only the
EspionageMissionTypes in info.data1 and the clicked extra-data value (building,
project, technology, civic, religion, etc.). It retains no original Spy IDInfo,
plot coordinates or target player.

On reply:

    selectionListGameNetMessage(GAMEMESSAGE_PUSH_MISSION, MISSION_ESPIONAGE,
            (EspionageMissionTypes)info.getData1(), clickedExtraData);

again targets the CURRENT selection. If original Spy A dies and Rapid Unit Cycling
selects Spy B at a different enemy city/player, the stale target choice can execute
there whenever the same stable extra-data is legal for B's current target. Examples
include the same technology being stealable from a different rival or the same
building type existing in a different city. If the old choice is not legal there,
receiver validation safely no-ops; when it IS legal, it cannot know that the popup
was built for A's target.

Current shipped XML has active two-phase Destroy Building, Destroy Project, Buy Tech,
Switch Civic and Switch Religion missions, so this is not dependent on dormant XML.
The Destroy Unit branch remains a separate dormant hardening note because current
shipped XML has no active iDestroyUnitCostFactor; do not allocate a root for that
branch merely from source shape.

MANIFESTATION D -- DECLAREWARMOVE CAN REPLAY THE OLD DESTINATION WITH A REPLACEMENT SELECTION
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
BUTTONPOPUP_DECLAREWARMOVE stores rival team and the intended destination/flags, but
not the moving selection that triggered the confirmation. After Yes, it gets the
CURRENT head-selected unit for its local tile-flip check and then sends the stored
MISSION_MOVE_TO coordinates to the CURRENT selection.

Thus the same original-selection-death + Rapid Unit Cycling producer can cause a
replacement group B to receive A's old move destination after the human answers A's
war/move popup. Current move legality/path handling may reject some replacements;
when B can legally perform the replayed move, the popup has silently rebound its
movement consequence to the wrong group.

COMPOUNDING WITH F312 AND F308 -- DO NOT MERGE ROOTS
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
LOADUNIT and LEADUNIT are also selection-bound at reply time and can therefore be
compounded by F315 when the original selected group disappears and rapid cycling
selects another group.

Keep their existing independent roots distinct:

* F312 is the LOADUNIT mutable-ORDINAL bug. It can retarget the chosen transport even
  when the original cargo selection stays stable.
* F308 is the LEADUNIT cross-player unit-ID alias. It can resolve a displayed
  teammate unit to a different own unit even when the Great General selection stays
  stable.
* F315 is the missing launch-time SELECTION identity. It changes which group receives
  the popup action/mission after automatic rapid cycling.

ANCESTRY / ROOT CAUSE
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The popup pattern of storing action/mission data while relying on the current UI
selection at reply is inherited from BtS/Civ4CE. Stock's selected-unit death path
requested an engine-delayed cycle with setCycleSelectionCounter(1).

K-Mod commit 280 introduced Rapid Unit Cycling and replaced that path with
cycleSelectionGroups_delayed(1, false). Its rapid branch can call
cycleSelectionGroups(true) immediately. The older isDiploOrPopupWaiting guard was
left around updateSelectionList only, so K-Mod introduced a supported way for the
current selection to change inside the very popup-waiting state that the old code
had treated specially.

Base AdvCiv and current SAS inherit this interaction. Current SAS's KI#398 espionage
launcher repair correctly chooses an eligible selected Spy instead of an arbitrary
selection head when CONSTRUCTING the espionage popup; it does not and cannot repair
the later missing launch-time identity at popup reply.

CONSEQUENCE
~~~~~~~~~~~
Depending on popup family, the player can:

* delete an unrelated replacement unit/group;
* execute a one-phase espionage mission at a different enemy city/player;
* apply a stale two-phase espionage target choice to another legal target;
* replay a declaration-of-war move destination using another selected group;
* compound LOADUNIT / LEADUNIT's separate target-resolution bugs.

The common semantic defect is that a modal decision created for selection A can
silently become a command for automatically selected B without any user action to
change the decision target.

FIX DIRECTION
~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Robust repair should bind selection-dependent popup decisions to their launch-time
target identity.

* Store stable IDInfo/unit identities (or an exact group/member snapshot appropriate
  to the popup) and re-resolve them on reply.
* For espionage, retain the launch-time Spy IDInfo and verify the same Spy/plot/target
  context before executing; cancel or rebuild if it changed.
* For DECLAREWARMOVE, retain the initiating unit/group identity before replaying the
  stored destination.
* Defense-in-depth: do not perform Rapid Unit Cycling while a selection-bound modal
  popup is outstanding, or cancel/rebuild those popups when the original selection
  disappears. This is useful UX protection, but reply-time identity validation is
  the stronger contract.

Do not rely only on current canDoCommand/canDoEspionageMission/path legality: the
wrong replacement selection may be perfectly legal, which is exactly why the
semantic retarget survives those checks.

NUMBERING
~~~~~~~~~
F315 / KI#638 remains one CONFIRMED generalized root.
F316 / provisional KI#639 remains UNUSED.

======================================================================
C030-WIP11 -- QUEUE 019 PLAYER-0 CONQUEST-LIBERATION BOOLEAN COLLISION
======================================================================

STATUS AT THIS CHECKPOINT
-------------------------
Queue 019 CvGameCoreDLL/CvDLLButtonPopup.cpp remains OPEN.
Files complete remain 29 / 169.
F307-F316 are CONFIRMED in queue 019.
F317 / provisional KI#640 is UNUSED.

F316 / KI#639 -- RETURN-CAPTURED-CITY MISROUTES PLAYER 0 THROUGH A PLAYER-ID-AS-BOOLEAN COLLISION
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
~~~~
AdvCiv's conquest-city popup deliberately distinguishes the special
bConquest=true liberation target from the normal liberation target. CvPlayer::acquireCity
computes:

    PlayerTypes eLiberationPlayer = kNewCity.getLiberationPlayer(true);
    ...
    pInfo->setData2(bGift ? eLiberationPlayer : NO_PLAYER);

launchRazeCityPopup uses info.data2 as that PlayerTypes and labels the button for the
stored liberation civilization.

On click, however, CvDLLButtonPopup::OnOkClicked sends that PLAYER ID as TASK_LIBERATE's
first integer payload:

    sendDoTask(info.getData1(), TASK_LIBERATE,
            info.getData2(), -1, false, false, false, false);

CvCity::doTask does not interpret the payload as a PlayerTypes. It converts it to a
BOOLEAN:

    case TASK_LIBERATE:
        liberate(iData1 != 0);
        break;

CvCity::liberate(bool bConquest) then recomputes the recipient using:

    PlayerTypes ePlayer = getLiberationPlayer(bConquest);

Thus every nonzero player ID happens to mean bConquest=true, while the perfectly
valid player ID 0 means bConquest=false.

PLAYER-0 COLLISION
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
PlayerTypes uses NO_PLAYER=-1 and valid major-player slots are integer IDs beginning
at 0. Therefore a conquest liberation whose intended stored target is player slot 0
passes exactly 0 into TASK_LIBERATE and becomes:

    liberate(false)

instead of the intended:

    liberate(true)

This is not merely a type-cleanliness concern. The two modes can select different
recipients by design.

WHY TRUE AND FALSE CAN DIFFER
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
CvCity::getLiberationPlayer has an explicit conquest-only bonus:

    if (bConquest && kLoopPlayer.getID() == getOriginalOwner())
    {
        iCultureScore *= 3;
        iCultureScore /= 2;
    }

The original owner receives a 50% score bonus only for conquest liberation. All
other candidate scoring continues normally. Therefore for a city that has been owned
by/cultured by multiple eligible civilizations, it is entirely possible for:

    getLiberationPlayer(true)  == PLAYER_0
    getLiberationPlayer(false) == PLAYER_X

For example, holding other multipliers equal, an original-owner score of 100 and
another eligible former owner's score of 140 gives PLAYER_0 a conquest score of 150
but a normal score of only 100. The conquest popup correctly chooses PLAYER_0; the
reply's false conversion then recomputes PLAYER_X instead.

The alternative normal result may also be NO_PLAYER depending on current owner and
candidate scores. In that case CvCity::liberate(false) simply returns without
transferring the city.

SUPPORTED SEQUENCE / CONSEQUENCE
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1. A human-controlled conqueror in any supported setup where its player slot is not
   0 captures a city whose original owner is alive PLAYER_0.
2. The city has enough competing eligible former-owner/culture state that the
   conquest-only 50% original-owner bonus makes PLAYER_0 the best liberation target,
   while normal liberation would choose another player (or no player).
3. CvPlayer::acquireCity computes getLiberationPlayer(true)==PLAYER_0, verifies that
   the city can legally be returned, and creates BUTTONPOPUP_RAZECITY with data2=0.
4. launchRazeCityPopup displays the Return/Liberate button naming PLAYER_0.
5. Human clicks that button.
6. OnOkClicked sends TASK_LIBERATE with iData1=0.
7. CvCity::doTask converts 0 to false and calls liberate(false).
8. The city is transferred to the normal liberation target rather than the
   civilization named by the conquest popup, or is not transferred at all.

This can therefore make an explicit human "Return city to civilization A" decision
give the city to civilization B. No simultaneous-turn race is required.

REACHABILITY / PLAYER 0
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The active human need only occupy a nonzero player slot while PLAYER_0 is the intended
return target. This is a normal supported state in multiplayer/hotseat/scenarios and
other control arrangements; player slot 0 is not a sentinel. The defect is therefore
configuration-dependent only in the ordinary sense that the target has to be the
first player slot.

ANCESTRY / INTENT EVIDENCE
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
This is an AdvCiv regression introduced in pre-SAS AdvCiv practical commit 1719
(7bc68e5a42b54474b646a84cb64d5077bab8f9b6), titled:

    Tweak/ refactor conditions for city trade and liberation

That patch changed the conquest popup to use eLiberationPlayer and replaced K-Mod's
TASK_GIFT path with TASK_LIBERATE. The added source comment explicitly explains the
reason:

    TASK_GIFT doesn't call CvCity::liberate if the
    bConquest=true liberation player differs from the normal
    liberation player

But the same patch passed `info.getData2()` -- the PlayerTypes value -- into the
existing TASK_LIBERATE payload whose receiver interprets nonzero as the bConquest
boolean. The intended distinction was therefore implemented correctly for player
slots 1+ but accidentally collapses for player slot 0.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain this code in substance. K-Mod used TASK_GIFT
here and therefore does not contain this specific PlayerTypes-as-bool regression.

DISTINCTNESS
~~~~~~~~~~~~
No prior album root for TASK_LIBERATE / player-slot-0 conquest-return misrouting was
found. This is independent of queue-019 stale-popup findings: the wrong behavior can
occur immediately after popup construction with no state change while the modal is
open.

It also explains why merely proving generational city IDs safe was insufficient for
this branch: the city object can be exactly the correct live city while the task
payload changes the meaning of the requested liberation mode.

FIX DIRECTION
~~~~~~~~~~~~~
For this conquest-popup button, send the boolean mode that TASK_LIBERATE actually
expects, not the recipient PlayerTypes:

    sendDoTask(info.getData1(), TASK_LIBERATE,
            1, -1, false, false, false, false);

CvCity::liberate(true) deliberately recomputes the current conquest liberation
recipient. If the intended contract instead requires binding the exact player named
by the popup, then TASK_LIBERATE would need a separate explicit recipient field or a
new task contract; simply passing the PlayerTypes in the boolean slot is invalid.

As defense-in-depth for delayed replies, the popup may also want to verify that the
current `getLiberationPlayer(true)` still matches the named/stored target before
executing. That is a separate stale-state policy question; it is not needed to fix
the deterministic PLAYER_0 collision.

NUMBERING
~~~~~~~~~
F316 is CONFIRMED and consumes KI#639.
F317 / provisional KI#640 is now the next unused root slot.

RELATED RAZE/DISBAND CONTROL
----------------------------
The ordinary Raze button itself does NOT have the same missing receiver-validation
problem: TASK_RAZE reaches CvPlayer::raze, which begins with `if (!canRaze(kCity))
return;`. A stale Raze button therefore rechecks current raze legality.

The city ID is also generational/player-local, so destruction/capture of the old city
cannot silently retarget the task to a newer city reusing the raw slot. The newly
confirmed F316 is specifically the liberation-mode payload collision, not a generic
city-ID problem.

C030-WIP12 -- QUEUE 019 STALE LIBERATION-RECIPIENT REBIND ROOT
======================================================================

STATUS AT THIS CHECKPOINT
-------------------------
Queue 019 CvGameCoreDLL/CvDLLButtonPopup.cpp remains OPEN.
Files complete remain 29 / 169.
F307-F317 are CONFIRMED in queue 019.
F318 / provisional KI#641 is UNUSED.

F317 / KI#640 -- LIBERATION POPUPS CAN GIVE A CITY TO A DIFFERENT CIVILIZATION THAN THE BUTTON NAMES
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
~~~~
Liberation UI text is built from a concrete recipient at popup-construction time,
but the reply does not bind that recipient. Instead it sends TASK_LIBERATE with only
the city ID and a conquest/non-conquest boolean. CvCity::liberate then recomputes the
best liberation player from CURRENT game state.

Thus the city identity can remain perfectly stable while the semantic target named
by the button changes underneath an unanswered modal popup.

MANIFESTATION A -- FREE COLONY / LIBERATE CITY
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
launchFreeColonyPopup iterates the active player's cities and computes:

    PlayerTypes eLibPlayer = pLoopCity->getLiberationPlayer();

It uses that exact player to build text such as "Liberate <city> to <civilization>",
but the button ID stores only:

    -pLoopCity->getID()

No recipient identity is preserved.

On reply, BUTTONPOPUP_FREE_COLONY sends:

    sendDoTask(-clickedButton, TASK_LIBERATE,
            0, -1, false, false, false, false);

CvCity::doTask turns this into:

    liberate(false);

and CvCity::liberate starts by recomputing:

    PlayerTypes ePlayer = getLiberationPlayer(false);

The civilization named by the button is therefore not part of the synchronized
request at all.

SUPPORTED SIMULTANEOUS PRODUCER
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
getLiberationPlayer(false) depends on live state: only alive/city-trade-eligible
players are considered; current capitals and capital distance matter; culture,
plot-team culture and current team/vassal relationships affect the score.

A particularly clean supported transition is elimination of the displayed recipient:

1. Human P owns city C, which has multiple eligible former owners/culture candidates.
2. P opens the Free Colony popup. At construction, X is alive and is the best
   liberation player, so the popup displays "Liberate C to X".
3. P leaves the modal unanswered during a simultaneous multiplayer turn.
4. Remote human Q captures/destroys X's last city. X is eliminated while P's local
   popup remains visible.
5. C itself is unchanged and still belongs to P. Another eligible former owner Y
   remains alive.
6. A fresh getLiberationPlayer(false) for C now cannot select X because
   PlayerIter<CIV_ALIVE> excludes it; suppose Y is now the best remaining candidate.
7. P clicks the still-visible "Liberate C to X" button.
8. The reply sends only C's city ID + false. CvCity::liberate(false) recomputes Y and
   transfers C to Y.

Receiver legality/state freshness therefore does not fix the problem. It is exactly
what causes the semantic retarget: the receiver intentionally uses the fresh best
recipient, but the human was asked to approve a different named recipient.

If no current liberation player remains, the stale click can instead become a no-op.
The wrong-recipient Y case is the stronger consequence.

MANIFESTATION B -- CAPTURED-CITY RETURN/LIBERATE BUTTON
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
AdvCiv's BUTTONPOPUP_RAZECITY construction stores the conquest liberation player in
info.data2 and labels the Return/Liberate button for that player. But its reply sends
TASK_LIBERATE rather than an explicit target, and CvCity::liberate(true) recomputes
the current conquest liberation player.

Therefore even after F316's PLAYER_0 boolean collision is repaired, a delayed
captured-city popup can still say "Return to X" and transfer to current Y if the
liberation ranking/eligibility changes before reply.

F316 and F317 are distinct:

* F316 is deterministic PlayerTypes-as-bool corruption for target PLAYER_0. It can
  misroute immediately with no game-state change.
* F317 is missing RECIPIENT identity across popup lifetime. It affects any player ID
  when the valid/best liberation target changes while the modal remains open.

ANCESTRY
~~~~~~~~
The Free Colony manifestation is inherited from stock BtS/Civ4CE. BtS builds the
button from getLiberationPlayer(false), stores only negative city ID, and replies
with TASK_LIBERATE,0. The Unofficial Patch/K-Mod adds a war check at construction but
retains the same target-less reply. Base AdvCiv and current SAS inherit it.

K-Mod's captured-city popup used TASK_GIFT with the explicit target player ID, so it
did not have this exact recompute-on-reply behavior there. AdvCiv practical commit
1719 switched that branch to TASK_LIBERATE in order to honor conquest-specific
liberation semantics, thereby extending the general target-rebinding issue to the
captured-city Return button as well.

ONFOCUS / REFRESH CHECK
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
There is no refresh that repairs this before click:

* BUTTONPOPUP_FREE_COLONY has no dedicated OnFocus revalidation branch.
* RAZECITY OnFocus checks only that the city still exists and looks at it; it does
  not verify that the stored/named liberation player is still the current
  getLiberationPlayer(true).
* launchRazeCityPopup itself treats info.data2 as the named immediate liberation
  target; its separate eFutureLiberationPlayer calculation is only explanatory text
  about what would happen if the player KEEPS the city and liberates later.

CONSEQUENCE
~~~~~~~~~~~
A human can explicitly click a button naming civilization X and have the city ceded
to civilization Y. This is a direct wrong-recipient gameplay action, not merely stale
text or a harmless failed command.

FIX DIRECTION
~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Bind the recipient shown by the popup and verify that exact recipient at reply.
Possible designs:

1. Store a stable PlayerTypes recipient alongside each liberation choice and send an
   explicit liberation/gift request for that player after current legality checks.
2. If the design intentionally wants `CvCity::liberate` to choose the current best
   recipient, then on reply compare current getLiberationPlayer(bConquest) against
   the launch-time named recipient. If they differ, cancel/rebuild the popup and ask
   the human again rather than silently redirecting.
3. RAZECITY already has its launch-time target in info.data2, so after fixing F316 it
   can directly compare current getLiberationPlayer(true) to that stored target.
4. FREE_COLONY needs to preserve the per-button target somehow; negative city ID alone
   is insufficient. A popup-side mapping or explicit message payload can carry both
   city and recipient.

Do not regard generational city IDs as sufficient: they solve stale city-object
identity, not stale recipient identity.

NUMBERING
~~~~~~~~~
F317 is CONFIRMED and consumes KI#640.
F318 / provisional KI#641 is now the next unused root slot.

----------------------------

C030-WIP13 -- QUEUE 019 FORMER-VOTER STALE DEFY ROOT + RESEARCH NOTE
======================================================================

STATUS AT THIS CHECKPOINT

F318 / KI#641 -- FORMER VOTING MEMBER CAN USE A STALE DEFY BALLOT TO VETO A RESOLUTION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
~~~~
BUTTONPOPUP_DIPLOVOTE is constructed only for players who are voting members at the
moment CvGame::addVoteTriggered creates the ballot. For an ordinary non-team
resolution, launchDiploVotePopup offers the Defy Resolution button whenever:

    GET_PLAYER(getActivePlayer()).canDefyResolution(eVoteSource,
            pVoteTriggered->kVoteOption)

returns true.

The popup can remain unanswered across a simultaneous multiplayer turn, but neither
the popup reply nor CvGame::castVote requires the voter still to be a CURRENT voting
member when the delayed choice arrives:

    case BUTTONPOPUP_DIPLOVOTE:
        sendDiploVote(info.getData1(), clickedVote);

    CvNetDiploVote::Execute()
    {
        GC.getGame().castVote(m_ePlayer, m_iVoteId, m_eChoice);
    }

    CvGame::castVote(...)
    {
        ...
        setPlayerVote(eVoter, iVote, ePlayerVote);
    }

There is no `isVotingMember` rejection in that path.

Ordinary vote WEIGHT mostly self-corrects because countVote asks getVotes from
current state. The dangerous exception is `PLAYER_VOTE_NEVER` (Defy Resolution).
When the resolution would otherwise pass, doVoteResults scans ALL major players,
not merely current voting members:

    if (getPlayerVote(itPlayer->getID(), voteID) == PLAYER_VOTE_NEVER &&
        itPlayer->canDefyResolution(eVoteSource, subdata))
    {
        bPassed = false;
        itPlayer->setDefiedResolution(eVoteSource, subdata);
    }

So a stale former-member Defy can still veto the entire resolution whenever
`canDefyResolution` remains true after membership was lost.

CURRENT-SAS XML / RULE PROOF
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
This is reachable with shipped Apostolic Palace data, not merely a hypothetical
VoteInfo configuration.

* DIPLOVOTE_POPE is religion-based.
* `CvPlayer::isVotingMember(eVoteSource)` is exactly
  `getVotes(NO_VOTE,eVoteSource) > 0`.
* For a religious vote source, `getVotes(NO_VOTE,...)` is the player's current
  population in cities containing the vote-source religion. Thus an alive player
  immediately ceases to be an AP voting member after losing the final owned city
  containing the AP religion.
* Current CIV4VoteInfo.xml includes `VOTE_FORCE_NO_TRADE` for DIPLOVOTE_POPE with
  iMinVoters=3.
* `CvPlayer::canDefyResolution` handles Force No Trade as an unconditional
  `return true` after only the general Secretary-General / vassal exclusions. It
  does NOT require current `isVotingMember` or `isFullMember` there.

Therefore there is a shipped AP resolution whose stale Defy remains result-time
legal according to the existing canDefyResolution predicate even after the player
has left the voting body.

SUPPORTED SIMULTANEOUS PRODUCER
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
A clean sequence uses at least four AP voting civilizations initially so that the
resolution can remain valid after one voter leaves:

1. Human P owns at least one city with the AP religion and is a current AP voting
   member. A non-team AP `VOTE_FORCE_NO_TRADE` ballot is created for P, and the popup
   includes Defy Resolution.
2. P leaves the modal unanswered.
3. CvGame::doTurn creates/processes diplomatic-vote state BEFORE simultaneous
   players are activated for the new game turn. Remote clients therefore act after
   the already-created ballot exists.
4. During that simultaneous turn, remote player Q captures P's final city containing
   the AP religion. P remains alive through other cities, but P's AP religion
   population becomes 0 and `P.isVotingMember(DIPLOVOTE_POPE)` becomes false.
5. At least three other AP voters remain, so the vote source still satisfies the
   shipped iMinVoters=3 rule and the Force No Trade resolution can remain otherwise
   valid.
6. P's already-rendered BUTTONPOPUP_DIPLOVOTE is not cancelled or rebuilt on loss of
   voting membership. Its OnFocus case checks only GAMESTATE_OVER.
7. P clicks the still-visible Defy Resolution button.
8. CvNetDiploVote -> castVote stores PLAYER_VOTE_NEVER without checking current
   membership.
9. At doVoteResults, P is correctly ignored for ordinary voting weight and for the
   normal result text because P is no longer a voting member. But the Defy scan does
   not have that membership guard. `canDefyResolution` still returns true for Force
   No Trade, so P sets `bPassed=false` and vetoes the resolution.

The built-in missing-vote/grace handling is not needed to invent timing here; the
normal ballot lives until results processing, and simultaneous remote actions can
change the membership state during that interval. If P submits the stale Defy before
results are processed, it is retained in the VoteTriggeredData/player vote state.

CONSEQUENCE
~~~~~~~~~~~
A civilization with zero current AP voting membership can veto an Apostolic Palace
resolution. Its numerical votes are zero, yet its stale Defy choice has stronger
than numerical effect: it unconditionally turns an otherwise-passing resolution
into failure.

`setDefiedResolution` also marks the former voter non-loyal and applies defiance
anger to any qualifying current cities. In the clean producer above P has no current
AP-religion city, so the main demonstrated consequence is the unauthorized veto;
the membership/loyalty side effect is secondary.

The results display then hides P from the listed vote breakdown because that display
DOES check current `isVotingMember`, making the veto particularly opaque: the
resolution can fail due to a former member whose Defy is not shown among current
voters.

ANCESTRY
~~~~~~~~
The underlying delayed-voter contract is inherited from stock BtS/Civ4CE:

* stock launch code offers Defy based on launch-time canDefyResolution;
* stock castVote stores the delayed choice without rechecking voting membership;
* stock doVoteResults scans every player with PLAYER_VOTE_NEVER and immediately
  vetoes, with no current membership check at all.

K-Mod retains that architecture.

AdvCiv improves the result-time Defy loop by re-running `canDefyResolution` (comment:
"May e.g. have become a vassal"), which prevents some stale Defy states. However,
`canDefyResolution` is not itself a membership predicate and intentionally contains
branches such as Force No Trade that remain true for a former voter. Base AdvCiv and
current SAS therefore inherit a partial stale-state repair that does not cover loss
of voting membership.

DISTINCTNESS
~~~~~~~~~~~~
F318 is separate from the other queue-019 diplomatic-vote roots:

* F309 concerns selection/proposal ownership/visibility state.
* F310 concerns a TEAM-VOTE CANDIDATE becoming ineligible while the ballot is live.
* F314 concerns a Secretary-General RESOLUTION OPTION becoming invalid before the
  human chooses it (notably iMinVoters).
* F318 concerns the VOTER who already received a live ballot ceasing to be a voting
  member, while a stale PLAYER_VOTE_NEVER retains veto power.

The same broad delayed-popup theme is present, but the violated identity/eligibility
invariant and receiver path are different.

FIX DIRECTION
~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The synchronized vote receiver/result processing should enforce current voter
eligibility, rather than relying only on launch-time popup eligibility.

A narrow robust direction is:

1. In `CvGame::castVote`, after resolving VoteTriggeredData, reject a voter who is no
   longer `isVotingMember(pTriggeredData->eVoteSource)`. This prevents stale former-
   member choices from entering vote state at all.
2. Defense-in-depth in doVoteResults: require current `isVotingMember(eVoteSource)`
   before honoring PLAYER_VOTE_NEVER, in addition to current canDefyResolution.
3. OnFocus for BUTTONPOPUP_DIPLOVOTE can cancel a ballot when the active player is no
   longer a voting member, improving UI clarity; this is not sufficient by itself
   because network state can change between focus/click and synchronized execution.
4. Preserve the existing `canDefyResolution` recheck as well, because membership can
   remain valid while other Defy-specific legality changes (e.g. vassalization).

Do not "fix" this by changing countVote alone. Defy is processed outside the numeric
vote-count path.

NUMBERING
~~~~~~~~~
F318 is CONFIRMED and consumes KI#641.
F319 / provisional KI#642 is now the next unused root slot.

F313 EXTENSION -- ORDINARY CHOOSE-RESEARCH POPUP SHARES THE STALE TECH-LIST GAP
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The stale technology-list architecture documented by F313 is not limited to free
technology awards. For the ordinary choose-research popup (`iDiscover == 0`), a
teammate can likewise acquire displayed technology T after the popup is rendered.
The ordinary OnFocus path does not rebuild the list merely because T became known;
it cancels when the active player has a current research target or the game ends.

If P still has NO_TECH selected and clicks stale T after teammate Q acquired it,
CvNetResearch::Execute sees T already team-known. With Shift not held it clears the
research queue and calls `pushResearch(T, true)`. pushResearch immediately returns
because the team already owns T, so T is not selected.

This is a LOWER-SEVERITY manifestation than F313's free-tech loss:

* the ordinary branch does not consume a one-shot free-tech entitlement;
* if the player reaches research processing without a valid target, current SAS
  stores the turn's research as overflow rather than dropping the beakers;
* the player can be prompted/choose again.

So do NOT allocate another root number from this ordinary-research case. It supports
F313's broader diagnosis that CHOOSETECH is a delayed snapshot that can become stale,
while the confirmed high-severity F313 consequence remains the free-tech entitlement
being consumed before the stale target's no-op is discovered.

C030-WIP14 APPEND -- QUEUE 019 CHOOSEELECTION SENTINEL COLLISION / F309 BROADENING
==================================================================================
Physical continuation from C030-WIP13. No repository source file was modified.
Queue 019 remains OPEN; files complete remain 29 / 169.

STATUS
------
F307-F318 remain confirmed.
F319 / provisional KI#642 remains UNUSED.

F309 BROADENING -- "NONE / EARLY ELECTION" PSEUDO-SENTINEL CAN COLLIDE WITH A REAL RESOLUTION ORDINAL
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The final 43-function reconciliation challenged a premise in the original F309 write-up.
F309 correctly identified that BUTTONPOPUP_CHOOSEELECTION does not have an explicit
synchronized branch for the final "None" / "Early Election" button.  However, the
original note described its button ID `GC.getNumVoteInfos()` as deliberately outside
`0..aVoteOptions.size()-1`.  That is NOT a valid invariant.

CURRENT CODE CONTRACT
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
launchChooseElectionPopup assigns every real proposal its VECTOR ORDINAL:

    for (int iI = 0; iI < (int)pVoteSelectionData->aVoteOptions.size(); iI++)
        popupAddGenericButton(..., iI, WIDGET_GENERAL);

and assigns the special no-proposal button:

    popupAddGenericButton(...,
        bEarlyElection ? TXT_KEY_EARLY_ELECTION : TXT_KEY_NONE,
        ..., GC.getNumVoteInfos(), WIDGET_GENERAL);

OnOk does not identify that special button semantically.  It merely tests:

    if (pData != NULL &&
        clicked < (int)pData->aVoteOptions.size())
    {
        sendChooseElection(clicked, selectionID);
    }

The synchronized receiver also treats `clicked` purely as an OPTION ORDINAL:

    CvNetChooseElection::Execute -> CvGame::setVoteChosen(iSelection, iVoteId)
    -> addVoteTriggered(kSelection, iSelection)
    -> kSelection.aVoteOptions[iSelection]

There is no downstream recognition of `GC.getNumVoteInfos()` as a special sentinel.

WHY THE VECTOR IS NOT BOUNDED BY getNumVoteInfos()
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Current SAS has 22 `<VoteInfo>` definitions, so the special button ID is 22.
But `CvGame::addVoteSelection` can append MORE THAN ONE `VoteSelectionSubData` for a
single VoteInfo:

* Force Peace appends one option per valid target major team.
* Force No Trade appends one option per valid target major team.
* Force War appends one option per valid target major team.
* Assign City can append one option per valid city/recipient combination.

The vector therefore counts concrete proposal INSTANCES, not VoteInfo definitions.
`GC.getNumVoteInfos()` cannot be a safe upper-bound sentinel for it.

CURRENT-SAS REACHABILITY -- ONE SHIPPED RESOLUTION IS ENOUGH
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
This is especially easy to reach in current AdvCiv-SAS because CvEnums.h compiles:

    MAX_CIV_PLAYERS = 48
    MAX_CIV_TEAMS   = 48

Current shipped CIV4VoteInfo.xml has 22 VoteInfo blocks and includes Apostolic Palace
`VOTE_FORCE_NO_TRADE` (`bForceNoTrade=1`, DIPLOVOTE_POPE, iMinVoters=3).

For that one VoteInfo, addVoteSelection loops every alive major team.  A target is
valid when it is not a full AP member and at least one other AP full-member player can
stop trading with that target.  A perfectly supported large SAS game can therefore
have, for example:

* at least 3 full Apostolic Palace member teams, satisfying iMinVoters=3; and
* at least 23 other alive major teams that are not full members and have a qualifying
  trade relation with one of those full members.

Those 23 targets alone can append at least 23 Force No Trade proposal instances.
Thus `aVoteOptions.size() > 22` is reachable without relying on Assign City or on a
sum of several resolution families.

CONSEQUENCE
~~~~~~~~~~~
When the vector has more than 22 entries, the final visible "None" / "Early Election"
button has ID 22, and 22 now satisfies:

    22 < aVoteOptions.size()

Clicking the button therefore sends `CvNetChooseElection(selection=22, voteId)`.
`setVoteChosen` creates a live ballot from `aVoteOptions[22]` and deletes the selection.
The human explicitly chose NO proposal (or Early Election), yet an unrelated real
resolution at vector ordinal 22 is proposed instead.

This is stronger than the original F309 leak consequence and is deterministic once
such an option vector exists; no delayed-state race is required.

RELATION TO THE ORIGINAL F309 CONSEQUENCE
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Do NOT allocate F319.  Both behaviors come from the SAME line-level encoding defect:
the special no-proposal action is represented by a pseudo-sentinel derived from the
number of VoteInfo definitions, while OnOk has no explicit semantic branch for it.

The two size regimes merely expose different consequences:

* `aVoteOptions.size() <= GC.getNumVoteInfos()`:
  the special ID fails the `< size` test, no synchronized message is sent, and the
  VoteSelectionData leaks indefinitely (original F309 consequence).
* `aVoteOptions.size() > GC.getNumVoteInfos()`:
  the special ID PASSES the `< size` test and aliases a real option ordinal, so the
  wrong resolution is proposed (this WIP14 consequence).

At exactly size == 22 the button is still out of range (`22 < 22` is false), so the
original leak applies.  The wrong-resolution branch starts at size 23.

ANCESTRY
~~~~~~~~
The same pseudo-sentinel plus range-only OnOk structure is present in supplied
Civ4CE/BtS and K-Mod and survives Base AdvCiv/current SAS. AdvCiv advc.178 only changes
the special button's label to "Early Election" in the relevant state; it retains the
same ID and dispatch contract.

Current SAS's 48-civ capacity makes a collision particularly easy to prove with one
shipped target-expanded resolution, but the architectural mistake is inherited.

REPAIR BOUNDARY -- SAME REPAIR AS F309
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The original F309 repair direction remains correct and now fixes BOTH consequences:

1. Give the special UI action an explicit semantic branch; do not infer it from a
   numeric value presumed to lie beyond the dynamic vector.
2. When the human clicks None/Early Election, send the synchronized choose-election
   message with the receiver-supported no-choice value `-1`.
3. `CvGame::setVoteChosen` then calls `addVoteTriggered(...,-1)` (which returns NULL)
   and still deletes the VoteSelectionData on every peer.
4. Validate ordinary proposal indices explicitly as `0 <= clicked < size`.

Using `GC.getNumVoteInfos()` as a UI button ID can be retained only if OnOk tests that
ID BEFORE interpreting ordinary ordinals, but a dedicated negative/special ID would
make the contract clearer and avoid future collisions entirely.

BOOKKEEPING CORRECTION
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The original F309 text saying the special ID is "deliberately outside the
0..aVoteOptions.size()-1 choice range" should be corrected to say that the CODE
INTENDS it as an out-of-band pseudo-sentinel, but the intended invariant is false
because aVoteOptions is a target-expanded vector.

F309 / KI#632 remains one confirmed root, now with TWO demonstrated consequences:
selection-state leak and wrong-resolution aliasing.
F319 / provisional KI#642 remains UNUSED.

43/43 MATRIX PROGRESS
---------------------
The explicit member-definition pass is still in progress.  This WIP freezes the
sentinel-collision correction before continuing so that the new proof is not left
only in chat state.

Already reconciled/closed in this final pass include singleton lifetime helpers,
production, civic/religion, disband-city identity, diplomacy/contact, spaceship
launch, found-religion, event, free-colony/liberation, vassal tribute, LOADUNIT,
LEADUNIT, espionage, confirm-command, declaration-war-move, details/admin/Python,
Rise & Fall, and most main-menu/session branches, subject to their already-numbered
roots where applicable.

Continue with F319 UNUSED through the remaining OnAltExecute/OnFocus/relaunch/session
bookkeeping, final six-family SAS semantic-delta reconciliation, and final
Base/K-Mod/Civ4CE history + duplicate saturation before closing queue 019.

END C030-WIP14


C030-WIP15 APPEND -- QUEUE 019 EXTENDED-GAME DEAD-RECIPIENT UI CONTRACT
========================================================================
Physical continuation from C030-WIP14. No repository source file was modified.
Queue 019 remains OPEN; files complete remain 29 / 169.

STATUS
------
F307-F319 are now confirmed.
F320 / provisional KI#643 is UNUSED.

F319 / KI#642 -- DEAD MULTIPLAYER HUMAN CAN RECEIVE AN INERT "ONE MORE TURN" BUTTON
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
~~~~
When the game enters GAMESTATE_OVER, CvGame::setGameState queues
BUTTONPOPUP_EXTENDED_GAME to EVERY ever-alive human, including eliminated humans.
Current AdvCiv/SAS even documents the intended special case immediately above that
loop:

    // advc (note): For dead humans, the popup will only lead to the opening menu.

CvPlayer::addPopup does not suppress the popup for dead humans; it rejects only
non-human recipients. Thus an eliminated human really can retain/receive this popup.

However, launchExtendedGamePopup decides whether to add the affirmative button from
GLOBAL state:

    if (GC.getGame().countHumanPlayersAlive() > 0)
        popupAddGenericButton(... TXT_KEY_EXTENDED_GAME_YES ..., 0, ...);

This asks only whether ANY human civilization remains alive, not whether the ACTIVE
RECIPIENT of this popup is alive.

SUPPORTED CURRENT PRODUCER
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
A normal multiplayer game is sufficient:

1. Human D has been eliminated but remains a human/ever-alive player/client.
2. At least one other human A remains alive when a victory ends the game.
3. CvGame::setGameState(GAMESTATE_OVER) queues BUTTONPOPUP_EXTENDED_GAME for D as
   well as A. The source explicitly anticipates dead-human recipients.
4. `countHumanPlayersAlive() > 0` is true because A is alive, so D's popup contains
   the same "One More Turn" / Extended Game Yes button as a living player.
5. D clicks Yes.

RECEIVER / CONSEQUENCE
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
In network multiplayer, OnOk sends CvNetExtendedGame for the active player. Its
receiver simply calls:

    GET_PLAYER(m_ePlayer).makeExtendedGame();

which sets D's `m_bExtendedGame = true` even though D is dead.

But CvGame::testExtendedGame intentionally counts only LIVING human players. In
stock/K-Mod this is spelled out as `isAlive() && isHuman()`; current AdvCiv/SAS uses
`PlayerIter<HUMAN>`, whose HUMAN status predicate explicitly requires both
`kAgent.isHuman()` and `isAlive(kAgent)`.

Therefore D's affirmative choice cannot cause GAMESTATE_OVER -> GAMESTATE_EXTENDED.
If no living human chooses Yes, D clicks a button labelled as continuing the game,
the popup closes, and the game remains over. D's choice is semantically inert.

This directly contradicts the current AdvCiv comment that a dead human's popup
"will only lead to the opening menu": the launcher's global test can expose a second,
nonfunctional path whenever another human survives.

SEVERITY
~~~~~~~~
LOW. This does not corrupt synchronized gameplay state and does not let an eliminated
player force continuation; `testExtendedGame` correctly ignores dead players. The
bug is a concrete multiplayer UI/action-contract mismatch: a supported button is
shown to a recipient for whom its action cannot have the promised effect.

ANCESTRY
~~~~~~~~
The mismatch is inherited from Firaxis BtS/Civ4CE:

* stock setGameState queues the Extended Game popup to every human player;
* stock launchExtendedGamePopup uses global `countHumanPlayersAlive() > 0`;
* stock testExtendedGame accepts the flag only from `isAlive() && isHuman()` players.

K-Mod retains the same three-part contract. AdvCiv refactors the loops to AgentIter
and adds the explicit dead-human/opening-menu comment, but keeps the launcher's global
alive-human gate unchanged. Base AdvCiv and current SAS therefore retain the defect.

FIX DIRECTION
~~~~~~~~~~~~~
At launch time, the affirmative button should be based on the recipient:

    if (getActivePlayer() != NO_PLAYER &&
        GET_PLAYER(getActivePlayer()).isAlive())
    {
        // add One More Turn / Yes
    }

The global count is unnecessary for a displayed active-player popup once recipient
liveness is known.

Defense-in-depth in CvNetExtendedGame::Execute (or CvPlayer::makeExtendedGame) could
also reject a dead player, matching the invariant already enforced by
testExtendedGame. The important user-facing repair is to avoid advertising the
inapplicable action in the first place.

NUMBERING
~~~~~~~~~
F319 is CONFIRMED and consumes KI#642.
F320 / provisional KI#643 becomes the next unused slot.

------------------------------

* OnAltExecute relaunch semantics and whether it creates any independent ownership
  defect beyond already-numbered delayed-popup roots;

  informational-popup early return already held below the root bar;

* final main-menu/admin/disconnect/session cleanup checks;
* targeted stock/K-Mod/AdvCiv history and duplicate sweep;
* final explicit 43/43 matrix and durable queue-019 closure if saturated.

Do not move to queue 020 after closure. The protected route is queue 019 -> queue 001
and then the deep-method 001-009 re-audit.
