C030-WIP16 APPEND -- QUEUE 019 PICK-RELIGION RESERVED-SLOT LOSS ON FOUNDER ELIMINATION
=====================================================================================
Physical continuation from C030-WIP15. No repository source file was modified.
Queue 019 remains OPEN; files complete remain 29 / 169.

STATUS
------
F307-F320 are now confirmed.
F321 / provisional KI#644 is UNUSED.

F320 / KI#643 -- PICK-RELIGION SLOT CAN BE PERMANENTLY RESERVED IF THE HUMAN FOUNDER DIES BEFORE CHOOSING
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
~~~~
The first-discovery religion path reserves the RELIGION SLOT before a human has
actually selected/founded a religion.

In CvTeam::setHasTech, after choosing eBestPlayer for the first-to-discover reward:

    kGame.setReligionSlotTaken(eLoopReligion, true);
    if (kGame.isOption(GAMEOPTION_PICK_RELIGION))
    {
        if (GET_PLAYER(eBestPlayer).isHuman())
        {
            CvPopupInfo* pInfo =
                new CvPopupInfo(BUTTONPOPUP_FOUND_RELIGION, eLoopReligion);
            ... addPopup(pInfo, eBestPlayer);
        }
        ...
    }

Thus the synchronized global slot reservation exists while the actual entitlement is
represented only by a human popup.

NORMAL SUCCESS PATH
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
BUTTONPOPUP_FOUND_RELIGION sends the chosen religion and reserved slot through
CvNetFoundReligion. CvPlayer::foundReligion then creates the Holy City (or reprompts
if the selected religion was taken first). The slot remains taken, now correctly
representing a consumed founding opportunity.

ELIMINATION PATH LOSES THE ONLY OWNER OF THE PENDING CHOICE
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Current player elimination removes the popup but does not release/reassign the slot:

* CvPlayer::setAlive(false) calls `clearPopups()`, deleting queued CvPopupInfo objects.
* It then calls `setTurnActive(false)`; for the local active player that calls the UI's
  `clearQueuedPopups()`, covering the displayed/EXE-owned popup side as well.
* No religion-slot cleanup accompanies either operation.

Repository-wide current-source search finds no ordinary
`setReligionSlotTaken(eReligion, false)` call at all. The only other state transition
is reset/deserialize. Once a slot is true during a running game, it is never released.

CvGame::doHolyCity cannot recover the reward either:

    if (isReligionSlotTaken(eReligion))
        continue;

so the global fallback deliberately skips the orphaned reservation forever.

SUPPORTED SIMULTANEOUS PRODUCER
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
No malformed popup or debug action is required:

1. GAMEOPTION_PICK_RELIGION is enabled.
2. Human P is selected as the best player when P's team is first to discover a
   religion-founding technology.
3. CvTeam::setHasTech immediately reserves that XML religion slot and queues
   BUTTONPOPUP_FOUND_RELIGION for P.
4. P leaves the modal unanswered.
5. In simultaneous multiplayer, remote player Q can continue acting while P's modal
   is open and eliminates P before P chooses a religion.
6. P's synchronized death clears P's queued/displayed popup state.
7. The reserved slot remains globally `true`; no CvNetFoundReligion response will
   ever arrive for it.
8. doHolyCity and later founding checks skip that slot permanently.

The producer is especially natural in simultaneous turns because technology can be
acquired while multiple players are active (trade/other synchronized acquisition),
and ordinary turn-start team research processing has completed before players are
left free to act. The modal blocks P's local decisions, not Q's remote military
execution.

CONSEQUENCE
~~~~~~~~~~~
One religion-founding opportunity is permanently lost from the running game. The
reserved slot remains serialized and blocks the fallback founder indefinitely even
though no religion was actually founded from that entitlement.

With Pick Religion, slot identity and actual founded-religion identity are decoupled:
a Buddhism XML slot can be used to choose/found another unfounded religion. Therefore
recovery cannot safely infer an orphan merely from
`slotTaken(slot) && !isReligionFounded(slot)`. That condition can be legitimate after
a successfully resolved Pick Religion choice.

A later founding slot may choose the religion that would otherwise have been chosen,
but the TOTAL number of founding opportunities has still dropped by one. Eventually
one religion can remain unfounded with all available slots already consumed/reserved.

ANCESTRY
~~~~~~~~
The core reservation-before-human-choice architecture is inherited unchanged from
Firaxis BtS/Civ4CE through K-Mod and Base AdvCiv:

* setReligionSlotTaken(slot,true) is performed before queuing FOUND_RELIGION;
* the human popup is the deferred owner of the choice;
* no normal false/reset path exists for an abandoned pending entitlement.

AdvCiv's popup/lifecycle refactors do not add synchronized pending-religion ownership,
so current SAS retains the architecture.

DISTINCTNESS
~~~~~~~~~~~~
F320 is not F313 despite the shared one-shot-choice theme.

* F313: a stale CHOOSETECH target is clicked and the free-tech counter is consumed
  before the already-known target no-ops.
* F320: no click occurs at all. The entitlement is reserved globally BEFORE popup
  response, then its only pending human owner disappears during elimination cleanup.

It is also separate from F307 event-popup construction and from the vote-selection
ownership roots.

FIX BOUNDARY
~~~~~~~~~~~~
A robust repair should not derive synchronized religion-slot state from local popup
inventory; network clients do not have identical displayed-popup ownership.

The architectural fix is to represent a pending Pick Religion entitlement in
synchronized game/player state, including at least:

* reserved slot;
* pending owning player/team (or another deterministic claimant);
* resolved/unresolved state.

Then player elimination can deterministically transfer the pending choice to another
eligible living team member, resolve it automatically, or release the reservation
according to an explicit policy.

A smaller but still synchronized design could reserve the slot with a tracked owner
field and, during `setAlive(false)`, resolve/reassign every pending slot owned by that
player BEFORE popup cleanup. Do not inspect only local displayed popups to decide
whether to mutate `m_abReligionSlotTaken`; that would risk OOS.

Simply rejecting CvNetFoundReligion for dead players is not a fix: the important
failure occurs because no response arrives after the popup is destroyed.

NUMBERING
~~~~~~~~~
F320 is CONFIRMED and consumes KI#643.
F321 / provisional KI#644 becomes the next unused slot.

43/43 MATRIX NOTE
-----------------
The initial alternative suspicion -- clicking FOUND_RELIGION after the player has no
city could mark the slot and then return with no Holy City -- is NOT the primary root:
normal first-discovery code has already marked the slot before the popup. Moreover,
ordinary elimination clears the popup. The durable defect is the orphaned pre-reserved
slot itself, documented above.

Continue final queue-019 saturation with F321 UNUSED.

END C030-WIP16

LATE CONTROL: EVENT TRIGGER RECORDS SURVIVING PLAYER DEATH ARE NOT A CURRENT GAMEPLAY ROOT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Player elimination clears queued/displayed popups but does not explicitly call
`m_eventsTriggered.removeAll()`. A pending BUTTONPOPUP_EVENT can therefore leave its
EventTriggeredData object in the eliminated player's private free-list.

That shape is not sufficient for a numbered finding:

* the destroyed popup no longer owns an action capable of applying the pending event;
* `CvPlayer::doEvents` creates fresh trigger candidates and does not redisplay arbitrary
  old pending EventTriggeredData objects;
* the synchronized `applyEvent` path re-resolves the trigger id and re-runs
  `canDoEvent` before mutating state;
* revival by itself does not requeue the abandoned pending popup.

No gameplay consumer or state mutation has been established. At most this is stale
private/serialized bookkeeping for a dead player. Under the album standard it remains
cleanup debt, not F321.

LATE CONTROL / F311 EXTENSION: STALE TRIBUTE RESOURCE AVAILABILITY IS RECEIVER-VALIDATED
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The human vassal's Grant reply constructs a TRADE_RESOURCES bundle without rechecking
that the demanded resource is still tradeable. This is another delayed-state weakness,
but the actual deal implementation is safer than the popup code suggests:

* `CvGame::implementDeal(..., bForce=false)` calls `implementAndReturnDeal`;
* this passes `bCheckAllowed=true` to `CvDeal::addTradeItems`;
* `addTradeItems` re-runs `CvPlayer::canTradeItem` for every item before calling
  `startTrade`.

Therefore a resource that was lost/pillaged/traded away while the popup remained open
cannot create an impossible export through this path. The popup handler can still emit
its immediate `TXT_KEY_VASSAL_GRANT_TRIBUTE_ACCEPTED` message after sending a request
that the synchronized deal layer rejects, so stale availability can produce misleading
feedback. This is a lower-severity manifestation of the same delayed tribute contract
already represented by F311, not an independent F321.

FINAL RELAUNCH / POPUP-SOUND RECONCILIATION
--------------------------------------------
The remaining C030-WIP17 question was whether an early return from
CvDLLButtonPopup::launchButtonPopup can strand CvPlayer::m_iButtonPopupsRelaunching,
causing later popup sounds to be suppressed.

The shape is real: normal launchButtonPopup attempts reach
CvPlayer::reportButtonPopupLaunched() at the common footer, whereas these branches
return earlier:

* SAS optional BUTTONPOPUP_TEXT suppression during AI Auto Play;
* Rise & Fall RF_CHOOSECIV / RF_DEFEAT / RF_RETIRE dispatch;
* Rise & Fall CvPlot::isAllFog() suppression;
* Rise & Fall chapter-start CHOOSEPRODUCTION / CHOOSETECH suppression through
  RiseFall::isBlockPopups().

However, no supported current producer was established that combines one of those
returns with a live relaunch counter:

1. AI Auto Play cannot normally arm CvPlayer::killAll's counter.
   Starting Auto Play calls CvGame::setAIAutoPlay(..., bChangePlayerStatus=true),
   which calls CvPlayer::setHumanDisabled(true). updateHuman then makes isHuman()
   false. CvPlayer::killAll immediately returns unless the active player is human.
   Countdown calls use bChangePlayerStatus=false only after that status transition.
   Therefore SAS's Auto-Play BUTTONPOPUP_TEXT early return does not intersect a
   newly armed killAll relaunch batch under the supported path.

2. Rise & Fall all-fog/interlude state likewise cannot normally arm the counter.
   RiseFall::setPlayerControl(..., false) clears the EXE popup queue and changes the
   former human civilization back to AI control before/while the map is hidden.
   Once isHuman()==false, killAll returns. On resuming human control, the popup queue
   is cleared before the AI civilization is handed to the human, and all-fog is then
   removed.

3. RiseFall::isBlockPopups is true only on the first turn of a later chapter
   (getCurrentChapter() >= 1). The selected civilization is still AI-controlled when
   setPlayerControl(..., true) begins, so the EXE popup queue is cleared before the
   human takeover. Any Choose Production / Choose Tech popup newly attempted during
   that blocked turn returns false before it can become a displayed popup. It cannot
   therefore later be one of killAll's relaunchDisplayed entries. The first chapter
   has isBlockPopups()==false.

4. RF_CHOOSECIV, RF_DEFEAT and RF_RETIRE are modal control-transition popups. No
   source-visible path was found that arms killAll and then relaunches one of these
   special popups as a preserved displayed entry before the counter drains.

A theoretical asynchronous edge remains possible in principle if a relaunch counter
survived an abrupt control/lifecycle transition before the EXE had consumed the
relaunch queue. The local source does not establish such a producer, and the only
established consequence is transient missing popup audio. Under the album standard
this remains defensive bookkeeping debt, not F321.

* F318 is inherited delayed diplomatic-vote state combined with AdvCiv's Defy/result

* F319 is inherited Extended Game UI logic: the button is gated by a global count of

* F320 is inherited Pick Religion reservation ownership: the religion slot is marked
  taken before the human chooses, elimination destroys the popup, and no runtime path
  releases the orphaned slot.

C031-WIP02 - F321 / KI#644: AI_bonusTradeVal uses pre-change strategic holdings

F321 / provisional KI#644 - CONFIRMED CURRENT SAS MARGINAL-VALUATION DEFECT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Title:
AI_bonusTradeVal strategic substitute multipliers ignore iChange and can undervalue
cancellation of the buyer's last imported key resource.

Birth / scope:
SAS-local. The relative strategic-resource valuation block was introduced by the
2025-09-30 AdvCiv-SAS work that added era/substitute-aware Iron/Copper/Horse/Camel/
Elephant pricing. Base AdvCiv does not contain this block.

Current supported configuration:
SAS_AI_BONUS_TRADE_VAL_VALUE_MORE_IRON_COPPER_HORSE_CAMEL_RELATIVELY = 1 in the
current GlobalDefines_advciv_sas.xml. The individual percentages are active current
balance values, e.g. Renaissance Iron with mounts and no Iron = 200%.

Root contract:
AI_bonusTradeVal(eBonus, eFromPlayer, iChange, ...) is not acquisition-only. AdvCiv's
advc.036 contract uses iChange prospectively; AI_considerOffer passes iChange=-1 while
checking whether an existing deal should be canceled/renegotiated. The inherited
AI_bonusVal call therefore evaluates the marginal state after loss.

The SAS strategic block instead builds its substitute state solely from the current
live inventory:
  bHaveCopper    = getNumAvailableBonuses(Copper) > 0
  bHaveIron      = getNumAvailableBonuses(Iron) > 0
  bHaveHorse     = getNumAvailableBonuses(Horse) > 0
  bHaveCamel     = getNumAvailableBonuses(Camel) > 0
  bHaveElephants = getNumAvailableBonuses(Elephants) > 0
It never adjusts the bonus being evaluated by iChange.

Supported reproduction:
1. Renaissance AI P has Horse/Camel but no Iron.
2. P considers buying its first/only Iron from outsider Q.
3. Before the deal, bHaveIron=false, so current configured logic applies
   SAS_AI_BONUS_TRADE_VAL_RELATIVE_BONUSES_REN_NO_IRON_WITH_MOUNT_IRON_PCT = 200.
   That high marginal value can help justify the purchase.
4. The deal starts; the imported Iron is now included in P's current
   getNumAvailableBonuses(Iron), so bHaveIron=true.
5. Once the deal is cancelable, AI_checkCancel calls
   AI_considerOffer(..., iChange=-1). The resource received from Q reaches
   P.AI_bonusTradeVal(Iron, Q, -1, ...).
6. Base/marginal valuation correctly treats this as losing a copy, but the SAS
   substitute block sees the pre-change live import and therefore concludes P already
   has Iron. The intended "no Iron, but mounts" 200% branch is skipped and the relative
   multiplier remains 100%.
7. AI_considerOffer can therefore value the same still-critical import at roughly
   half of the relative strategic value that caused it to be bought and can return
   false, making AI_checkCancel return RENEGOTIATE. AI-AI handling then kills the deal
   and may repropose; AI-human handling can cancel/renegotiate through its existing
   path. Once the import is gone, a fresh acquisition valuation again sees no Iron and
   restores the high multiplier, permitting oscillatory "valuable to buy, cheap to
   lose" behavior.

The same root affects other substitute-state rules whenever the evaluated -1 change
removes the last currently available configured resource: Horse/Camel/Elephants in
relevant eras and pre-Medieval metal/mount group tests. Losing one of multiple copies
correctly leaves the boolean true; the defect is specifically that the prospective
availability is not computed at all.

Why this is not KI#239 / KI#240:
* KI#239 concerned a hard AI-buy DENIAL leaking onto human recipients.
* KI#240 concerned the hard dominated-Copper denial overriding live strategic and
  corporation usefulness.
* F321 is in the price/marginal-value path after legality. It exists even with those
  denial fixes and is driven by current-vs-post-change inventory state.

Why this is not merely tuning:
The XML percentages themselves are balance choices. The defect is applying those
choices to a state different from the state that the function's iChange argument is
explicitly evaluating. Acquisition and cancellation of the same last imported copy
therefore use inconsistent substitute predicates.

Narrow repair direction:
Compute prospective availability for each configured resource, applying iChange only
to the resource currently being valued, e.g. conceptually:
  availableAfter(B) = getNumAvailableBonuses(B) + (eBonus == B ? iChange : 0) > 0
Then derive bHaveIron/bHaveHorse/etc. and grouped predicates from that prospective
state. Preserve all current era percentages, master/vassal-locus exemption and
ordinary AI_bonusVal behavior.

* the feature is enabled by default;
* current SPECIALBUILDING_TEMPLE and SPECIALBUILDING_MONASTERY have their own
  SpecialBuildingInfo technology gates, but no current Temple/Monastery building in
  CIV4BuildingInfos carries a nonzero BonusHealthChange/BonusHappinessChange, so the
  function's omission of SpecialBuildingInfo tech-gate checks does not currently
  create a bonus-price error through those two budget branches;
* ordinary nonreligious bonus-effect buildings remain deliberate approximate
  coverage valuation rather than a canConstruct simulation. Missing city-specific
  prerequisites/location coverage alone is therefore not promoted without a current
  contradiction/consequence.

The overloaded GET_TEAM(eFromPlayer) shape was also rechecked against rejected KI#311
/ KI#387: AdvCiv deliberately overloads GET_TEAM(PlayerTypes) through TEAMID, so there
is no player-ID-as-team-ID defect here.

C031-WIP03 - F322 / KI#645: KI#66 building-synergy gate ignores additional AND techs

F322 / provisional KI#645 - CONFIRMED CURRENT SAS TECH-GATE DEFECT
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Title:
AI_bonusTradeVal's KI#66 multi-effect building-synergy pre-check tests only the
building's primary prerequisite tech, so bonuses can receive building-effect price
markup before all of that building's required AND technologies are actually known.

Birth / lineage:
SAS-local. The KI#66 multi-effect bonus valuation block was introduced at practical
commit 4997, fce68b70e9161e7428339b593c29c3817ec79fe7, titled:
"(Fixed and greatly enhanced) AI valuing for example pig (+1 health) at the same value
than maize ..."
Base AdvCiv does not contain this extra rBoost pass. The original implementation and
current source both use only kB.getPrereqAndTech() for the building-tech gate.

Current supported configuration:
SAS_AI_BONUS_TRADE_VAL_VALUE_MORE_MULTI_EFFECT_BONUSES = 1 in current
GlobalDefines_advciv_sas.xml. KI#66 and the source comments explicitly describe the
rule as applying the extra bonus valuation once the buyer has the tech required to
build the relevant building.

Engine construction contract:
CvPlayer::canConstruct does not treat CvBuildingInfo::getPrereqAndTech() as the whole
technology requirement. Unless bIgnoreTech is requested, it requires:
  1. kBuilding.getPrereqAndTech(), AND
  2. every entry in kBuilding.getPrereqAndTechs(i).
CvBuildingInfo::isTechRequired likewise recognizes both the primary prerequisite and
every additional getPrereqAndTechs entry (and also a SpecialBuilding tech gate).
These are genuine AND requirements, not merely Pedia annotations.

Current KI#66 pricing code instead does only:
  TechTypes const eReq = (TechTypes)kB.getPrereqAndTech();
  if (eReq != NO_TECH && !kOurTeam.isHasTech(eReq))
      continue;
It never tests kB.getNumPrereqAndTechs()/getPrereqAndTechs(i) before adding that
building's BonusHealthChanges/BonusHappinessChanges to rBoost.

Concrete current-data reproduction - ordinary Grocer:
Current CIV4BuildingInfos.xml has:
  BUILDING_GROCER
    primary PrereqTech = TECH_MATHEMATICS
    additional AND tech = TECH_CURRENCY
    bonus effects include +1 for Spices/Banana/Grapes/Sugar.
Current CIV4TechInfos.xml does not make Currency a prerequisite of Mathematics:
  Mathematics requires Writing plus one of its own OR prerequisites;
  Currency instead requires Code of Laws plus its own OR prerequisite.
Therefore a perfectly normal current game state can have Mathematics while Currency
is still unknown.

In that state:
1. Buyer P has Mathematics but not Currency.
2. P cannot construct a Grocer; CvPlayer::canConstruct rejects it on the missing
   additional TECH_CURRENCY prerequisite.
3. AI_bonusTradeVal nevertheless passes its sole primary-tech test because P has
   Mathematics.
4. For Banana/Spices/Grapes/Sugar, the Grocer's positive bonus effect is added to
   rBoost as though the building were already technology-enabled.
5. For an ordinary non-water +1 effect, rBoost changes from 1 to 2 before the block's
   final 0.75 damping, i.e. this building alone materially raises the KI#66 multiplier
   while the building remains unavailable for a missing required technology.
6. The AI can consequently offer/pay a higher bonus price during a real Classical-era
   interval than the KI#66 rule says it should.

Additional current examples:
* BUILDING_PERSIAN_APOTHECARY, BUILDING_CARTHAGE_PUNIC_AGORA and
  BUILDING_PORTUGAL_PEIXARIA have the same Mathematics + Currency requirement and
  positive bonus effects, so their buyer-civilization substitutions inherit the same
  premature valuation.
* BUILDING_OTTOMAN_HAMMAM and BUILDING_IRELAND_MUILEANN_UISCE require Mathematics plus
  the additional AND tech Masonry. Their Marble/Wheat effects are likewise counted
  after Mathematics alone even when Masonry is still unknown.

Why this is a contract defect rather than a tuning disagreement:
KI#66's simplifying heuristic is intentionally generous: once the building is
technology-enabled, treat it approximately as broadly available without simulating
city-by-city construction. That approximation is not the defect. The defect occurs
one stage earlier: the code says a building is technology-enabled after checking only
one member of a multi-tech AND requirement. Current construction code and XML both
make the omitted prerequisites mandatory, and KI#66's own documentation says "if we
have their required tech" / "as soon as the buyer has the tech required to build these
buildings." The pricing code therefore violates its stated gate in current data.

Why this is independent from F321:
F321 concerns prospective iChange state in the later strategic-substitute multiplier,
especially cancellation of the last imported strategic resource. F322 concerns the
earlier building-synergy rBoost and exists on ordinary acquisition pricing even with
no cancellation and no Iron/Horse/Camel substitute logic.

Why existing AdvCiv AI_baseBonusBuildingVal does not rescue it:
AI_baseBonusBuildingVal elsewhere in this same file explicitly constructs
bHasTechForBuilding by checking both getPrereqAndTech() and every
getPrereqAndTechs(i). That demonstrates that the codebase already knows the complete
building-tech contract, but the newer KI#66 pass independently reimplemented only the
primary check.

Current-data SpecialBuilding note:
CvPlayer::canConstruct also checks a SpecialBuildingInfo technology prerequisite.
The KI#66 pass does not. Current bonus-effect cathedrals are deliberately skipped, and
current Temple/Monastery buildings have no nonzero bonus health/happiness effects, so
that omission does not supply an additional current F322 reproduction. It is sensible
defense-in-depth to use the complete technology gate, but this finding does not rely
on speculative future XML.

Narrow repair direction:
Before counting kB's bonus effect, require every building technology prerequisite,
not only getPrereqAndTech(). The smallest behavior-preserving repair is conceptually:
  if (eReq != NO_TECH && !kOurTeam.isHasTech(eReq))
      continue;
  bool bMissingAndTech = false;
  for (int i = 0; i < kB.getNumPrereqAndTechs(); i++)
      if (!kOurTeam.isHasTech(kB.getPrereqAndTechs(i))) ...
  if (bMissingAndTech)
      continue;
Optionally include the SpecialBuilding tech prerequisite for future XML robustness.
Do not replace the KI#66 heuristic with full canConstruct: city/religion/resource/
location requirements were intentionally abstracted away and doing so would change
its design rather than fix this specific gate.

DUPLICATE / HISTORY CHECK
-------------------------
The current reconciled album has no existing root for missing secondary
CvBuildingInfo technology prerequisites in AI_bonusTradeVal/KI#66. Existing KI#66 is
the enhancement being audited, not a prior report of this defect. F321 is a separate
prospective-resource-state root. The initial commit diff confirms the incomplete
single-tech check was present when the KI#66 feature was introduced rather than being
a later accidental formatting/refactor regression.

AI_bonusTradeVal - CURRENT CONTINUATION
---------------------------------------

but the function is not saturated yet. Continue through:
* human-information/fairness substitution (bUseOurBonusVal) versus buyer-specific
  building and strategic multipliers;
* whether the generic AIObjective multiplier is intentionally outside the
  master/vassal-cluster exemption or contradicts current docs/defines;
* seller/vassal and market-value tail behavior;
* remaining current XML/data assumptions in the building-synergy block, separating
  deliberate approximation from actual prerequisite/data-contract errors.
Then continue to AI_updateGreatPersonWeights and the remaining largest semantic
CvPlayerAI deltas. F323 remains unused until another independent root survives the
same producer/contract/consequence and duplicate standard.

C031-WIP04 - F323 / KI#646: AI_doCivics last-pass flag can bypass paid-anarchy safeguards

F323 / provisional KI#646 - CONFIRMED CURRENT SAS CONTROL-STATE DEFECT
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Title:
AI_doCivics uses the final recheck pass's bWillSwitch flag as though it described the
accumulated revolution bundle, so the SAS anti-flip-flop recheck can bypass the
near-future-civic and low-treasury safeguards for an already accepted paid-anarchy
switch.

Birth / lineage:
The multi-pass bWillSwitch/bWantSwitch loop is inherited from K-Mod and Base AdvCiv,
but its original thresholds preserve an important coupling: a rejected candidate sets
bWantSwitch only when its value is roughly >20% better, while the recheck lowers the
extra-anarchy threshold to 20%. Thus a candidate strong enough to request the recheck
is normally strong enough to be accepted on that recheck, keeping the final
bWillSwitch state aligned with the nonempty proposed bundle.

AdvCiv-SAS's anti-flip-flop work changed that contract. Current source says:
  bWouldLikeSwitch = (iBestValue > iCurrent);
  if (bWouldLikeSwitch)
      bWantSwitch = true;
but acceptance additionally requires BOTH the inherited percent test and the SAS
absolute-slack test. Current XML enables a 20% absolute slack of |current value|
(SAS_AI_DO_CIVICS_SWITCH_SLACK_PERCENT=20, minimum 5), with still larger slack for a
candidate that adds paid anarchy. Therefore a candidate can now request another pass
while being intentionally unable to pass that next pass.

Root state mismatch:
* aeBestCivic and iAnarchyLength accumulate accepted switches across passes.
* bWillSwitch and bWantSwitch are reset to false at the start of EVERY pass.
* The loop continues while the PREVIOUS pass ended with both true.
* After the loop, the near-future-civic and treasury safeguards are guarded by:
    if (iAnarchyLength > 0 && bWillSwitch)
  Here bWillSwitch describes only whether the FINAL pass accepted something, not
  whether aeBestCivic still contains a switch accepted in an earlier pass.
* canRevolution(aeBestCivic) later tests the actual accumulated bundle and can return
  true even when final-pass bWillSwitch is false. CvPlayer::revolution likewise only
  re-runs canRevolution; neither function repeats the AI wait/treasury safeguards.

Concrete current-configuration control-flow reproduction:
Assume two civic options A and B are encountered in that order, with the empire not
currently in anarchy and eligible to revolution.

1. Pass 1 accepts A. Let A require paid anarchy; iAnarchyLength becomes 2,
   aeBestCivic[A] becomes A-new, and bWillSwitch=true.
2. Later in pass 1, B's current AI value is 100 and its best alternative is 110. If B
   adds no more anarchy to A's existing bundle, the percent threshold is only 5%, so
   110 passes the inherited percent test.
3. Current SAS absolute slack is max(5, 20% of 100)=20. The +10 improvement fails
   bPassSlack because 10 is not >20. B is rejected, but because 110>100 the SAS branch
   still sets bWantSwitch=true.
4. Pass 1 therefore ends with bWillSwitch=true && bWantSwitch=true, entering pass 2.
5. At the start of pass 2 both booleans are reset. Option A is skipped because the
   accumulated aeBestCivic already contains the same best civic A-new.
6. B is evaluated again against the live civic state: AI_bestCivic calls
   AI_civicValue directly and does not install aeBestCivic's local A change into the
   player. B still has 110 vs 100 and still fails the same 20-point absolute slack.
   It sets bWantSwitch=true but never sets bWillSwitch=true.
7. The loop exits because final-pass bWillSwitch=false. aeBestCivic still contains A
   and iAnarchyLength is still 2.
8. The block guarded by `iAnarchyLength > 0 && bWillSwitch` is skipped entirely.
9. `canRevolution(aeBestCivic)` sees that A differs from the live civic and returns
   true; the revolution executes and pays the 2 turns of anarchy.

Concrete skipped consequences:
A) AdvCiv low-treasury protection (advc.131):
The skipped block contains the explicit test intended to avoid paid anarchy when the
AI lacks enough treasury for its negative gold rate. For example, with 2-turn anarchy,
0 strike turns, gold=20 and gold-per-turn=-30, the normal test can return before the
revolution. Under the state mismatch above it is never reached, so the AI can enter
anarchy despite failing AdvCiv's own affordability rule.

B) Near-future civic wait:
The same skipped block checks whether current research will shortly unlock another
valuable civic that can be bundled without increasing the current anarchy length.
When the state mismatch occurs, this intended delay is bypassed too; the AI can pay
anarchy now and then reconsider after the newly researched civic arrives.

Why this is distinct from existing KI#159:
KI#159 diagnosed/tuned excessive paid-anarchy civic churn and direct reversals. Its
implemented fixes deliberately add larger acceptance slack for anarchy-increasing
candidates and a longer post-anarchy civic timer. F323 is a control-flow defect in that
new hysteresis interaction: the broadened `bWantSwitch = any positive improvement`
can make a recheck pass accept nothing, which causes an older last-pass flag to hide an
already accepted bundle from the safeguards below. Fixing F323 does not change the
KI#159 tuning values; it makes those values coexist correctly with the existing
AdvCiv safeguards.

Why this is not simply an inherited K-Mod bug:
The potentially fragile use of final-pass bWillSwitch is inherited, but K-Mod's own
recheck trigger is tied to a >20% rejected improvement and its recheck acceptance
threshold is 20%. SAS explicitly replaced that trigger with any `iBestValue > iCurrent`
while adding an independent absolute-slack requirement that remains active on the
recheck. This breaks the threshold coupling on which the inherited control structure
relied and provides the current supported reproduction above. Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains
the K-Mod-style 20% bWantSwitch trigger and does not contain the SAS absolute slack.

Narrow repair direction:
Do not use final-pass bWillSwitch as a proxy for "the accumulated bundle contains a
paid-anarchy switch." The smallest repair for the two safeguards is to key them on the
accumulated state, e.g. `if (iAnarchyLength > 0)` (or an explicit persistent
`bAnySwitch`/bundle-diff flag), rather than on bWillSwitch from the last pass.
Separately, bWantSwitch could be restored to a predicate that guarantees the recheck
has some chance to pass, but that is a tuning/efficiency choice; the correctness fix is
to make the post-loop safeguards describe the accumulated bundle.

DUPLICATE / HISTORY CHECK
-------------------------
The reconciled album has no earlier numbered root for AI_doCivics's final-pass
bWillSwitch masking an accumulated civic bundle. KI#159 is a tuning/improvement entry
for churn and paid-anarchy damping, not this safeguard-bypass diagnosis. Current
CvPlayer::canRevolution / revolution confirm there is no downstream affordability or
near-future-civic revalidation that would neutralize the bug.

QUEUE-001 CONTINUATION
----------------------
AI_doCivics remains open beyond F323. Continue through:
* the remainder of the current SAS logging/timer changes and any interaction between
  iFinalAnarchyLength, getMaxAnarchyTurns and no-anarchy civic switches;
* AI_civicValue's large SAS specialist/valuation changes, reconciling current XML and
  civic data rather than treating heuristic disagreements as bugs;
* then continue the current semantic-delta priority list (AI_doDiplo,
  AI_barbarianTargetCityScore / AI_religionValue, AI_doMilitary, AI_doCommerce, etc.)
  before the inherited whole-file saturation pass.
F324 remains unused until an independent producer/contract/consequence chain survives
current-data and duplicate checks.

F324 / provisional KI#647 - CONFIRMED CURRENT SAS CAPACITY DOUBLE COUNT
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Title:
AI_civicValue's generalized unlimited-specialist estimator reuses the same finite
citywide specialist-capable population independently for every specialist type a civic
unlocks, so Caste System can value one citizen as several simultaneous specialists.

Birth / lineage:
SAS-local, in the generalized unlimited-specialist civic valuation introduced for
existing KI#76. Base AdvCiv/K-Mod do not contain this per-specialist capacity/output
estimator. Later KI#315 and KI#316 repaired the sign and baseline-GPP treatment of the
same block but intentionally left its capacity estimate unchanged.

Current code contract:
For every specialist type where `kCivic.isSpecialistValid(eLoopSpecialist)`, current
AI_civicValue loops every city and computes:

  iSpecialistNow = max(0,
      population - workingPopulation - angryPopulation)
  iFoodSlackSpecs = (foodDifference() >= 2 ? 1 : 0)
  iSurplus = iSpecialistNow + iFoodSlackSpecs
  iOpen = max(0, maxSlotsForThisType - assignedCountForThisType)
  iNeed = max(0, iSurplus - iOpen)
  iPotential += min(iNeed, softCap)

It then multiplies that iPotential by the output value of THIS specialist and adds the
result to iTotal before repeating the entire city-capacity calculation for the next
unlimited specialist type.

The population term is explicitly a shared finite pool, not a per-specialist-type
resource. CvCity::visiblePopulation() is defined by the same expression:
  getPopulation() - angryPopulation() - getWorkingPopulation().
Assigned specialist counts change the city's specialist population; one population
point cannot be an Artist and a Scientist and a Merchant at the same time.

Concrete current-data reproduction:
Current CIV4CivicInfos.xml has exactly one multi-type unlimited-specialist civic:
  CIVIC_CASTE_SYSTEM -> SPECIALIST_ARTIST,
                        SPECIALIST_SCIENTIST,
                        SPECIALIST_MERCHANT.
The other current unlimited-specialist civics unlock only one type each (Police State
Spy, Wage Labor Engineer, Trade Bloc Merchant, Organized Religion Priest), so the
shared-capacity duplication specifically biases Caste in current data.

Minimal one-city case:
1. P is evaluating Caste System while not currently running it.
2. City C has zero currently assigned specialists, no open Artist/Scientist/Merchant
   slots, no angry population, and `foodDifference() >= 2`.
3. For Artist, iSpecialistNow=0 and iFoodSlackSpecs=1, so iNeed/iPotential gain 1.
4. The entire same city calculation is repeated for Scientist: the SAME one-person
   food-slack capacity is again counted as iPotential=1.
5. It repeats again for Merchant.
6. iTotal therefore prices one plausible extra citizen as one Artist PLUS one Scientist
   PLUS one Merchant. All three current specialist types have positive commerce and/or
   GPP output, so all three impossible simultaneous assignments add positive civic
   value.

Existing-specialist case is stronger:
If a city has, for example, three non-angry specialist citizens and no open slots for
Caste's three types, the shared iSpecialistNow pool can contribute up to three Artists,
three Scientists and three Merchants before the soft caps - nine valued specialist
assignments from three people. The per-type current-slot subtraction does not make the
pools independent; it only changes how much of the SAME population each type appears
to need.

Consequence / why this is a defect rather than ordinary heuristic tuning:
The block's own comment says it estimates "How many extra of this specialist could we
plausibly run empire-wide?" and "the marginal need this civic actually unlocks." Its
soft cap and food-slack approximation are tuning choices. Reusing the same people as
productive specialists several times is a capacity-accounting contradiction: the
outputs summed into iTotal cannot coexist. Because Caste is the only current civic
unlocking three types, this systematically inflates Caste relative to the one-type
unlimited-specialist civics the KI#76 rewrite was intended to compare more fairly.
It can also make active Caste unusually sticky: existing specialist population is
reused for each of its three valid specialist types when its absolute civic score is
recomputed.

Why this is distinct from KI#76 / KI#315 / KI#316:
* KI#76 broadly rewrote and tuned unlimited-specialist valuation because inherited
  logic overfavored Caste and failed to value Engineer-like alternatives well.
* KI#315 fixed an active-civic sign error in this block.
* KI#316 restored baseline GPP value.
* F324 is independent shared-capacity arithmetic: even with those repairs, one finite
  population pool is still multiplied across every unlocked type.

Narrow repair direction:
Compute each city's marginal unrestricted-specialist capacity once, then allocate that
finite capacity across the specialist types the civic unlocks. A conservative heuristic
could value each marginal citizen at the best currently useful unlocked specialist (or
allocate by the same specialist-value ranking used by citizen assignment) rather than
summing a full copy of the capacity for every type. If specialist-type flexibility is
intended to carry extra value, add a bounded diversity/flexibility premium separately;
do not represent flexibility as simultaneous duplicate citizens.

DUPLICATE CHECK
---------------
No existing reconciled album root or current Known Issues entry diagnoses reuse of the
same citywide specialist-capacity pool across multiple `SpecialistValid` types. KI#76
is the feature/tuning history and KI#315/#316 are different arithmetic defects within
the block. Current XML provides a direct three-type Caste reproduction, so this is not
future moddability-only debt.

AI_doCivics FINAL TAIL CONTROL
------------------------------
After F323, the rest of AI_doCivics was rechecked before moving into AI_civicValue:
* iFinalAnarchyLength is recomputed from the actual accumulated aeBestCivic bundle,
  so the KI#159 extra civic timer uses the final bundle rather than stale iAnarchyLength.
* no-anarchy switches receive no per-anarchy extra timer; the inherited base timer
  choice still distinguishes players whose maximum anarchy is zero.
* the structured logging caches are diagnostic-only and do not alter civic choice.
No independent F324 arose from the timer/log tail.

----------------------
Continue AI_civicValue through the other SAS semantic additions:
* current civic-percent-anger replacement (reconcile against repaired KI#317);
* specialist-commerce weighting / toned multiplier and its define contracts;
* unlimited-specialist per-output/anarchy scaling beyond the shared-capacity root;
* current civic XML cases and any state-dependent iS behavior.
Then continue to AI_doDiplo and the next high-delta functions before inherited whole-
file saturation. F325 remains unused until an independent current root survives.

F325 / provisional KI#648 - CONFIRMED CURRENT SAS DIRECTION/SIGN DEFECT
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Title:
AI_civicValue's city-level CivicPercentAnger replacement adds the hypothetical welfare
change directly to the civic's absolute score; when the pressure civic is already
active, the modeled harm of dropping it therefore becomes negative value for KEEPING
the civic.

Birth / lineage:
SAS-local in the KI#75 replacement of K-Mod's broad civic-pressure estimate with a
city-level actual-angry-citizen model. Current KI#317 later fixed the city-selection
logic so happy cities that would become unhappy are no longer skipped, but retained
the direction/sign calculation examined here.

Relevant AI_civicValue contract:
`iS` is the inherited K-Mod sign identifying the direction of the hypothetical change:
  iS = +1 if eCivic is not currently active (evaluate gaining/adopting its effects)
  iS = -1 if eCivic is currently active (evaluate losing/dropping its effects).
Surrounding state-dependent civic components use that sign so the marginal welfare
change is converted into positive absolute value for a beneficial civic in either
state.

Current pressure block instead computes:
  iPermilDelta = -iS * iPermilIfWeDont
  iAngryCitizenChange = changedAngry - currentAngry
  iCityVal = -12 * iAngryCitizenChange
  iValue += scaled iCityVal
The first two lines correctly model the hypothetical direction. The final value is
then the welfare change of MAKING that hypothetical switch, not yet the absolute value
of eCivic. For iS=-1 the code fails to reverse the drop result back to the value of
keeping the active civic.

Current-data reachability:
Current CIV4CivicInfos.xml gives CIVIC_THEOCRACY `iCivicPercentAnger=200`; it is the
current nonzero CivicPercentAnger civic. Current XML also enables both city-level
pressure scales:
  SAS_AI_CIVIC_VALUE_ANGER_PRESSURE_SCALE_PERCENT_IF_A_CITY_IS_UNHAPPY = 150
  SAS_AI_CIVIC_VALUE_ANGER_PRESSURE_SCALE_PERCENT_IF_A_CITY_IS_HAPPY = 100.
Therefore this is live current gameplay logic whenever known rivals running Theocracy
create enough pressure to change actual angry-citizen counts.

Concrete direction reproduction:
Assume P is not running Theocracy, rivals create enough Theocracy pressure that city C
has two angry citizens attributable to that pressure, and adopting Theocracy removes
those two angry citizens.

Before adoption:
1. iS=+1.
2. iPermilDelta is negative, modeling removal of pressure.
3. changedAngry-currentAngry = -2.
4. iCityVal = -12 * -2 = +24 before the configured scale.
5. The pressure relief correctly makes Theocracy more attractive to adopt.

After adoption, with the same rivals still running Theocracy:
1. AI_civicValue evaluates active Theocracy with iS=-1.
2. `getCivicPercentAnger(eCivic,true)` still reports the rival pressure that would
   return if P stopped running the civic.
3. iPermilDelta is now positive, correctly modeling the hypothetical DROP.
4. If dropping would restore two angry citizens, iAngryCitizenChange=+2.
5. iCityVal becomes -24 and is added directly to THE ACTIVE THEOCRACY'S score.
Thus the very anger that Theocracy is currently preventing LOWERS its active civic
value instead of raising it.

The same logic can produce a pick-then-drop discontinuity: the component is positive
while considering adoption and negative after adoption, even though the underlying
rival pressure has not changed. Safely happy cities that would remain happy contribute
zero as intended; the defect concerns cities where the civic actually changes angry
population.

Why this is a sign/contract bug rather than civic tuning:
The KI#75 design explicitly says to value the pressure civic when it actually benefits
our cities. If keeping an active civic prevents angry citizens, that is the same
benefit as adopting it to remove those citizens. Current code instead treats the harm
of a hypothetical drop as evidence against the active civic. This is a direction
conversion error independent of the chosen 12-point base or 100/150% scales.

Why this is distinct from KI#315 and KI#317:
* KI#315 fixed a sign bug in the separate unlimited-specialist intrinsic-value block,
  where active civics subtracted their own specialist benefit.
* KI#317 fixed the pressure block's pre/post-happiness filtering so cities crossing the
  happiness cap are counted.
* F325 is the remaining directional normalization of the pressure welfare delta. The
  KI#317 city set can now be exactly correct while the resulting active-civic value is
  still sign-inverted.

Narrow repair direction:
Convert the hypothetical welfare change back into the absolute value of eCivic using
`iS`, conceptually e.g.:
  iCityVal = -12 * iAngryCitizenChange * iS;
This leaves the current pressure calculation, current/post-change angry counts and XML
scales intact:
* inactive/adopt: -angry change * +1 stays positive for relief;
* active/drop: harm is negative marginal welfare, then * -1 becomes positive value for
  retaining the civic.
Recheck the intended post-change pressure-scale asymmetry separately as tuning; it is
not necessary to change it to fix this sign defect.

---------------------------------

the feature/tuning history; KI#317 owns the city-crossing/filter repair; KI#315 is a
different sign regression in the specialist component. Current Theocracy and current
pressure defines provide a shipped reproduction rather than future-mod data only.

F326 / provisional KI#649 - CONFIRMED CURRENT SAS FORMULA/CONTRACT REGRESSION
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Title:
AI_civicValue's specialist-extra-commerce tuning also replaced K-Mod's structural
AI_averageCommerceMultiplier divisor for ordinary civic percentage-commerce modifiers;
the custom preference weight then cancels against its own toned divisor and existing
empire commerce multipliers are no longer backed out.

Birth / lineage:
SAS-local. Commit 59d8c92c41f71d9698bfd1cf8b909eb1706f203b is titled:
  "Fix the issue of civics that give specialist extra commerce ... by valuing commerce
   per specialist more"
and names CIVIC_REPRESENTATION's specialist beaker/gold/culture output as the target.
The patch generalized custom SAS commerce weights across the shared commerce loop,
including the ordinary `kCivic.getCommerceModifier` branch which is a structurally
different effect and was not the stated specialist-extra-commerce problem.

Inherited K-Mod / Base AdvCiv contract:
For ordinary civic percentage-commerce modifiers Base AdvCiv retains K-Mod's:
  iTempValue += (kCivic.getCommerceModifier(eCommerce) *
      100 * getCommerceRate(eCommerce)) /
      AI_averageCommerceMultiplier(eCommerce);
...
  iTempValue /= 100;
  iTempValue *= AI_commerceWeight(eCommerce);
  iTempValue /= 100;

`CvPlayer::getCommerceRate` is the cached sum of actual city commerce rates.
`CvCity::updateCommerce` computes those actual rates by multiplying each city's
`getBaseCommerceRateTimes100` by `getTotalCommerceRateModifier(eCommerce)`.
`AI_averageCommerceMultiplier` is independently cached as the population-weighted
average of those same city total-commerce-rate modifiers.

Therefore the inherited division is not merely a taste/priority coefficient. It backs
out the empire's already-applied current commerce multiplier before estimating the
incremental output of an additional civic percentage modifier. Only after that
structural normalization does K-Mod apply `AI_commerceWeight` as the AI preference for
the resulting commerce type.

Current SAS formula:
Current SAS replaces the divisor with:
  iSASCommerceWeight = SAS_SpecCommerceBaseWeight(...)
  iSASCommerceTonedDownMult =
      iSASCommerceWeight * SAS_AI_CIVIC_VALUE_SPEC_COMMERCE_WEIGHT_TO_MULT_TONING_DOWN_PERCENT / 100
and then still multiplies the final iTempValue by iSASCommerceWeight.
The shipped toning percentage is 45.

Ignoring only integer truncation, the ordinary modifier term becomes:
  M * 100 * Rate / (W * 45/100)
  then /100
  then *W/100
  = M * Rate / 45.
Thus the very custom commerce weight W that is supposed to encode the hierarchy
cancels from this ordinary-modifier term. With current base weights:
  research 300 -> toned divisor 135 -> effective post-weight divisor 45
  gold     300 -> toned divisor 135 -> effective post-weight divisor 45
  culture  100 -> toned divisor  45 -> effective post-weight divisor 45
  espionage200 -> toned divisor  90 -> effective post-weight divisor 45.
At the same time the actual `AI_averageCommerceMultiplier` no longer participates, so
an empire with 100%, 150% or 250% existing city commerce multipliers is normalized as
though those were the same.

Current-data reachability:
This branch is live in shipped CIV4CivicInfos.xml independently of Representation:
* CIVIC_FREE_SPEECH has CommerceModifiers [0, 0, 50] (+50% culture).
* CIVIC_FREE_RELIGION has CommerceModifiers [0, 10, 0] (+10% research).
Current specialist-extra-commerce civics are different effects:
* CIVIC_REPRESENTATION has SpecialistExtraCommerces [1,1,1,0].
* CIVIC_FREE_MARKET has SpecialistExtraCommerces [1,0,0,0].
So the specialist-targeted formula change currently changes the valuation of two
ordinary percentage-modifier civics as well.

Intent / documentation evidence:
Long Comment #168 describes the new value explicitly as a toned-down commerce
"multiplier" derived from the SAS specialist commerce weights, with the example
300 * 50% = 150, and explains that the purpose is to stop Representation from moving
from underpicked to overpicked after strengthening its specialist commerce.
The introducing commit likewise says the issue is civics "that give specialist extra
commerce" and that the formula is being strengthened so specialist extra commerce is
valued more. Neither describes replacing the inherited normalization for already-
modified ordinary player commerce.

Why this is a formula bug rather than merely different AI tuning:
A tuning change may intentionally make research or culture more/less important. Here:
1. the configured commerce preference weight algebraically cancels for the ordinary
   `% commerce` effect despite that weight being deliberately different by commerce;
2. an actual state variable needed to avoid double-applying existing city multipliers
   (`AI_averageCommerceMultiplier`) is replaced with that preference value; and
3. the change was introduced for the separate specialist-extra-commerce component.
The resulting formula therefore violates both the inherited marginal-output structure
and the stated scope/meaning of the new knob.

Narrow repair direction:
Keep K-Mod's structural divisor for `kCivic.getCommerceModifier`:
  ... / AI_averageCommerceMultiplier(eCommerce)
Then decide independently which final preference weight SAS wants for that ordinary
commerce output (`AI_commerceWeight` or the deliberate SAS replacement).
Keep the toned SAS multiplier on `kCivic.getSpecialistExtraCommerce`, where the
introducing commit and Long Comment #168 actually intend stronger specialist-commerce
valuation. Do not reuse a preference weight as a substitute for the empire's current
commerce-rate multiplier.

---------------

modifier denominator/weight cancellation. KI#76 concerns unlimited specialist slots;
KI#315/#316 are later specialist sign/GPP repairs. F326 concerns the older shared
commerce loop and is independently reachable through Free Speech and Free Religion.

AI_civicValue CONTINUATION
--------------------------
Continue with F327 unused through:
* define-boundary / integer-zero behavior around the toned specialist multiplier,
  distinguishing current shipped configuration from optional hardening;
* the remaining unlimited-specialist anarchy/output scaling after F324;
* inherited high-risk civic valuation components beyond the SAS delta slice.
Then continue queue-001 high-delta functions and ultimately whole-file saturation.

F327 / provisional KI#650 - CONFIRMED INHERITED K-MOD WRONG-VARIABLE REGRESSION
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Title:
AI_civicValue's K-Mod war-weariness happiness component guards on the candidate civic's
WarWearinessModifier but computes the happiness change from the PLAYER'S CURRENT
aggregate war-weariness modifier; inactive candidates can therefore receive the
magnitude or even the sign of the civic currently being run instead of their own
prospective effect.

Current SAS code:
  if (kCivic.getWarWearinessModifier() != 0) // K-Mod. (original code deleted)
  {
      iValue += (12 * iCities * iS * AI_getHappinessWeight(
          iS * intdiv::round(
          getWarWearinessPercentAnger() * -getWarWearinessModifier(),
          GC.getPERCENT_ANGER_DIVISOR()), 1, true)) / 100;
  }

The outer guard is explicitly about `kCivic`, but the magnitude inside the hypothetical
happiness delta is `getWarWearinessModifier()` on CvPlayerAI. That getter is the current
aggregate player state, not the candidate civic being evaluated.

Mechanics / contract proof:
`CvPlayer::updateWarWearinessPercentAnger` computes and caches the player's BASE war-
weariness anger from team war-weariness plus game/world/handicap modifiers. It does not
apply the player's civic WarWearinessModifier there.

The civic/player modifier is applied later at the city level. `CvCity` takes the
player's base `getWarWearinessPercentAnger()` and multiplies it by roughly:
  100 + cityWarWearinessModifier + playerWarWearinessModifier.
`CvPlayer::processCivics` changes the player aggregate by exactly
`kCivic.getWarWearinessModifier() * iChange`.

Therefore the prospective happiness effect of THIS civic is structurally based on
`kCivic.getWarWearinessModifier()` (with `iS` converting adopt/drop direction), not on
whatever modifier the player happens to have before the hypothetical change.

Stock / K-Mod / AdvCiv lineage:
Civ4CE / stock BtS uses the candidate civic correctly. Its corresponding block is:
  if (kCivic.getWarWearinessModifier() != 0)
  {
      int iAngerPercent = getWarWearinessPercentAnger();
      int iPopulation = 3 + getTotalPopulation()/max(1,getNumCities());
      int iTempValue = (-kCivic.getWarWearinessModifier() *
          iAngerPercent * iPopulation) /
          (GC.getPERCENT_ANGER_DIVISOR() * 100);
      if (iTempValue != 0)
          iValue += ... AI_getHappinessWeight(
              isCivic(eCivic) ? -iTempValue : iTempValue, 1) ...;
  }

K-Mod replaced this with its newer city-happiness estimator and introduced the wrong
getter:
  getWarWearinessPercentAnger() * -getWarWearinessModifier()
while still guarding on `kCivic.getWarWearinessModifier() != 0`.
Base AdvCiv and current SAS retain the exact K-Mod variable choice unchanged.
Thus this is an inherited K-Mod regression, not a SAS-local tuning change.

Current-data reachability:
Current SAS has several live nonzero civic modifiers, including:
* Hereditary Rule: -25
* Universal Suffrage: +25
* Police State: -50
* Theocracy: -25
* Free Religion: +25.
Government therefore supplies especially clean same-option reproductions.

Concrete wrong-direction reproduction:
Assume P currently runs Hereditary Rule (-25), has nonzero war-weariness anger, and is
evaluating inactive Universal Suffrage (+25).

Actual prospective effect:
* Universal Suffrage increases the player's WW multiplier by +25 compared with its own
  absolute civic effect; this civic's WW happiness component should be harmful / have
  a negative sign.

Current K-Mod/SAS happiness block:
1. Guard passes because candidate Universal Suffrage has +25.
2. iS=+1 because Universal Suffrage is inactive.
3. Inner expression ignores +25 and reads P's CURRENT aggregate -25.
4. Negating current -25 produces +25.
5. `AI_getHappinessWeight(...,+change, bPercent=true)` is therefore asked to value a
   happiness IMPROVEMENT.
The candidate's +25 war-weariness penalty can consequently receive a positive
happiness contribution solely because the currently active civic has -25.

Magnitude loss / zero-current reproduction:
Assume instead P currently runs Representation (0) with no other global player WW
modifier. Evaluating inactive Police State (-50) and Universal Suffrage (+25):
* both candidate guards pass;
* current `getWarWearinessModifier()` is 0 for BOTH;
* the candidate -50 versus +25 magnitude and sign disappear entirely from this block.
Moreover `AI_getHappinessWeight` explicitly coerces an input of 0 to +1, so this caller
can give both candidates the same small positive phantom happiness contribution rather
than zero. This is especially perverse for Universal Suffrage, whose +25 actually
worsens war weariness.

The earlier cdtw.4 urgency block DOES use `kCivic.getWarWearinessModifier()` and can
partly offset these errors, but that block explicitly says the city-happiness effect is
also valued below and intentionally double-counts high urgency. A correct first block
does not make a wrong-variable second block harmless; the latter is intended to value
the actual city happiness consequences and currently does not.

Active-civic nuance:
When the current aggregate happens to equal the active candidate civic's modifier and
there are no other player-level sources, the erroneous getter can accidentally produce
a plausible drop-direction delta for the active civic. This does not rescue inactive
candidate comparison: every alternative is still evaluated through the active/current
modifier rather than its own. Additional aggregate WW sources also break that accidental
identity.

Zero-delta caller issue:
Even after replacing the wrong getter, the rounded candidate happiness delta can be 0
at sufficiently low war weariness. `AI_getHappinessWeight` intentionally maps iHappy=0
to 1. Stock's old block explicitly skipped the helper when `iTempValue == 0`; the K-Mod
replacement lost that guard. This is best fixed in the same block while repairing the
wrong-variable contract: calculate the prospective `iHappy` first and call
AI_getHappinessWeight only when it is nonzero. It is a closely coupled consequence of
the same replacement rather than a separate F328 at this checkpoint.

Narrow repair direction:
Compute the hypothetical percentage-happiness delta from the candidate civic, e.g.
conceptually:
  int iHappy = iS * intdiv::round(
      getWarWearinessPercentAnger() * -kCivic.getWarWearinessModifier(),
      GC.getPERCENT_ANGER_DIVISOR());
  if (iHappy != 0)
      iValue += 12 * iCities * iS *
          AI_getHappinessWeight(iHappy, 1, true) / 100;
Preserve the surrounding K-Mod scaling unless empirical tuning says otherwise. The
important contract repair is candidate modifier + adopt/drop direction, not current
aggregate state; the nonzero guard preserves the stock behavior that a rounded zero
change has zero value.

the candidate civic's modifier is required.

F328 / provisional KI#651 - CONFIRMED INHERITED SATURATION / NON-INVERTIBLE-STATE DEFECT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Title:
AI_civicValue reconstructs pre-civic maintenance by dividing CURRENT maintenance by
`100 + current player modifier`; at the legitimate -100% boundary current maintenance
has already saturated to zero, so the lost base cannot be reconstructed and a civic
that abolishes that maintenance category loses its own active valuation.

Relevant AI_civicValue pattern (distance; colony is analogous):
  if (kCivic.getDistanceMaintenanceModifier() != 0)
  {
      int iTemp = 0;
      FOR_EACH_CITY(pLoopCity, *this)
      {
          iTemp += pLoopCity->calculateDistanceMaintenanceTimes100() *
              (pLoopCity->getMaintenanceModifier() + 100) / 100;
      }
      iTemp *= 100;
      iTemp /= std::max(1, getDistanceMaintenanceModifier() + 100);
      ...
      iValue -= iTemp * kCivic.getDistanceMaintenanceModifier() / 10000;
  }

This is intended to back the player's CURRENT modifier out of measured current city
maintenance and then apply the candidate civic's modifier to that recovered base.
That inversion works only while the current multiplier is nonzero.

Actual distance-maintenance mechanics:
`CvCity::calculateDistanceMaintenanceTimes100(..., bNoPlayerModifiers=false)` computes
its base and then applies:
  iTempMaintenance *= std::max(0,
      GET_PLAYER(eOwner).getDistanceMaintenanceModifier() + 100);
  iTempMaintenance /= 100;
Thus a current player distance modifier of -100 makes the returned distance-maintenance
component exactly zero before AI_civicValue sees it.

Current-data State Property reproduction:
Current CIV4CivicInfos.xml has:
  CIVIC_STATE_PROPERTY
  iDistanceMaintenanceModifier = -100.
`CvPlayer::processCivics` applies that value directly through
`changeDistanceMaintenanceModifier(... * iChange)`, and this modifier has no other
current source in CvPlayer.cpp; State Property therefore sets the relevant aggregate to
exactly -100 in the normal case.

Before adoption:
1. current distance modifier is normally 0;
2. city distance maintenance is positive where distance costs exist;
3. AI_civicValue divides by 100 and applies candidate -100;
4. State Property correctly receives a positive value for abolishing distance cost.

After adoption:
1. current distance modifier is -100;
2. each `calculateDistanceMaintenanceTimes100()` already returns 0 because of
   `max(0,100-100)`;
3. the evaluator multiplies that 0 by the city maintenance modifier and sums 0;
4. it attempts to divide the state back out by
   `max(1, getDistanceMaintenanceModifier()+100) = max(1,0) = 1`;
5. zero remains zero;
6. applying State Property's candidate -100 to that recovered value still gives 0.
The exact economic benefit that made State Property attractive before adoption therefore
disappears from its own active civic score merely because the civic successfully reduced
the measured cost to zero.

Current-data colony manifestation:
Current SAS Vassalage has:
  iNumCitiesMaintenanceModifier = -25
  iColonyMaintenanceModifier = -100.
AdvCiv's `calculateColonyMaintenanceTimes100` applies the player colony modifier to the
maintenance cap:
  iMaintenanceCap *= max(0, getColonyMaintenanceModifier()+100) / 100;
so active Vassalage's -100 makes the colony-maintenance cap and resulting colony
maintenance zero.

AdvCiv's later `AI_civicValue` colony block copied the same inverse-current-state pattern:
  current colony maintenance -> divide by max(1,current modifier+100) -> apply candidate.
At current -100 it has the same information-loss failure: Vassalage's abolition of
colony maintenance is valued before adoption but not recoverable once active. Its -25%
num-cities-maintenance effect remains separately valued; F328 concerns the saturated
-100 component.

Why `std::max(1, ...)` is not a valid repair:
The guard avoids division by zero, but zero current output contains no information about
the suppressed pre-modifier base. Replacing denominator 0 with 1 merely converts an
undefined inverse into a defined but wrong zero estimate. This is a mathematical
non-invertibility at a valid gameplay boundary, not optional XML misconfiguration.

Stock / K-Mod / AdvCiv lineage:
* Civ4CE / stock BtS used a rough direct candidate formula for distance and num-cities
  maintenance, e.g. `-kCivic.getDistanceMaintenanceModifier() * cityCount / ...`; it
  did not derive candidate value by inverting current maintenance and therefore did not
  lose the benefit simply because the candidate was active.
* K-Mod introduced the more accurate current-maintenance reconstruction for distance
  and num-cities maintenance. Stock State Property already has the -100 distance effect,
  so the saturation boundary exists in K-Mod's improved formula.
* Base AdvCiv inherits that distance pattern and `advc.912g` extends the same pattern to
  ColonyMaintenanceModifier.
* Current SAS retains both and additionally has a live -100 colony modifier on
  Vassalage.
Thus the distance root is inherited from K-Mod; the colony manifestation is the same
formula assumption extended by AdvCiv and reached by current SAS data.

Gameplay consequence:
`AI_civicValue` compares absolute civic scores. An intrinsic economic saving should not
vanish from the score merely because the evaluated civic is currently active. The
current discontinuity can therefore cause pick-then-drop pressure: State Property can
score highly while inactive because it abolishes substantial distance maintenance, then
lose that entire component immediately after adoption while competing Economy civics
retain their intrinsic benefits. Vassalage can similarly lose its colony-maintenance
component after adoption.

Narrow repair direction:
Do not infer the pre-modifier maintenance base by dividing an already-saturated current
value at -100. Available robust directions include:
* use the maintenance calculation's existing ability to skip player modifiers / expose
  a base component where available (distance already has `bNoPlayerModifiers=true` in
  its static helper), then apply the candidate modifier explicitly;
* add/use an analogous base calculation for colony maintenance; or
* simulate the candidate state from an unsaturated base rather than algebraically
  inverting current state.
Preserve city/handicap/world/local maintenance modifiers as appropriate. The key is that
-100 must be valued from a pre-player-modifier base, not from current zero output.

DUPLICATE CHECK
---------------
No reconciled album or current Known Issues entry diagnoses this active-civic -100%
maintenance inversion. Existing maintenance findings concern different domains. F328
is specifically the `AI_civicValue` current-state reconstruction becoming non-invertible
at a valid -100% civic modifier.

--------------------------

AI_religionValue - INTENTIONAL LARGE POWER-BLOC AMPLIFICATION
--------------------------------------------------------------
The repaired KI#309 player-by-player power accumulation is coherent: it now weights the

The resulting diplomatic religion multiplier can be extremely large (including values
above 10,000% for a strong known power bloc and low ReligionFlavor), but this is NOT a
missing /100 bug. Long Comment #107 explicitly documents the percentage-scale formula:
  Modifier = [MULT * Base * PowerBlocPercent + ADD] /
             [DIVIDER_MULT * ReligionFlavor + ADD]
and works through an example Base 75, power bloc 70%, ReligionFlavor 5 -> 10,500%,
explicitly describing the resulting boost as huge and intentionally left for autoplay /
tuning. Therefore this is deliberate design, not F329.

AI_doMilitary - KI#331 REPAIR VERIFIED
--------------------------------------
The current SAS repair to routine financial scrapping survives the deeper pass.

Candidate construction:
* AI_disbandValue still supplies the ordered desirability metric.
* candidates now enter the quota-indexed vector only if canScrap() currently permits
  routine removal;
* an independent iDisbandCandidateIndex traverses candidates;
* iDisbandCount increments only after scrap() returns success.
This repairs the old KI#331 contract where a restrictive SAS canScrap veto could consume
quota / be reported as though removal succeeded.

Lifetime/index check:
* unit_values stores stable player-unit IDs, not dense positional indices;
* removing one unit does not renumber later unit IDs;
* scrap() calls scrapInternal -> kill(true), starting delayed death for that same unit;
* the caller immediately calls doDelayedDeath() after a successful scrap and never uses
  that unit pointer afterward;
* killing that candidate does not normally delete the unrelated units whose stable IDs
  are still present later in unit_values.
Thus the separated candidate index does not introduce an index-shift/use-after-free loop.

Budget/quota check:
* iCost is recalculated after each successful scrap;
* the loop stops as soon as the actual budget condition clears;
* the inherited per-turn disband quota still applies outside strike;
* strike deliberately retains the inherited ability to continue beyond that quota while
  financial pressure persists.
The SAS extra-unit tolerance derives a rough average per-unit cost from
max(1, iCost / getNumUnits()) and raises iMaxCost by an era-scaled number of units. This
is approximate tuning, not a legality/accounting contract: the real cost/gold condition
is still recomputed after every removal. No F329 here.

AI_doCommerce - SAS DELTA CONTROL
---------------------------------
The SAS-vs-Base executable delta is logging/performance-only in current behavior:
* culture-slider intermediate values are captured for CULTURE_SLIDER_DECISION logging;
* AI_averageCulturePressure() is called once, stored, and reused for the two inherited
  calculations instead of being called twice;
* ESPIONAGE_EACH_TURN_UNIT_COST_DECREASE is restart-cached in a static const;
* final slider state is logged after verifyGoldCommercePercent().

The potentially semantic-looking culture-pressure cache is exactly equivalent:
AI_averageCulturePressure() is a const accessor that simply returns the turn-cached
m_iAverageCulturePressure member; it performs no calculation, random draw, cache refresh
or mutation. Reusing one local value therefore cannot change the inherited decision.
The new diagnostic locals are written/read only for logging and do not feed any slider
calculation. No F329 here.

The SAS rewrite deliberately makes XML production cost dominant, removes SyncRand jitter,

AI_neededWorkers / SAS_minimumAreaWorkerFloor - CURRENT POLICY COHERENT

The KI#192/KI#198 repair chain was rechecked through the shared helper and main callers.

Controls:

C031-WIP12 ADDENDUM - QUEUE 001 DEEP RE-AUDIT CONTINUES
================================================================================

F329 / provisional KI#652 - CONFIRMED
-------------------------------------
AI_isSASCityLikelyToBenefitUsLongTerm checks active World Wonders using the city's CURRENT
owner/team even when its callers are explicitly evaluating the city for a DIFFERENT
prospective recipient.

Current helper:
    bool const bIntrinsicSiteProtectedByActiveWorldWonder =
        (bDistanceOverrideActiveWorldWonder && kCity.hasActiveWorldWonder());

CvCity::hasActiveWorldWonder() calls getNumActiveWorldWonders(1) with the default
`eOwner=NO_PLAYER`, so obsolescence is tested against kCity.getTeam(). Yet AdvCiv already
provides exactly the needed prospective-owner API:
    int CvCity::getNumActiveWorldWonders(..., PlayerTypes eOwner) const;
and labels eOwner "Hypothetical owner". The implementation selects the obsolescence team as
TEAMID(eOwner) when one is supplied.

This mismatch is harmless in AI_conquerCity after acquisition, because the captured city is
already owned by `this`. It is live in the other behavioral callers:
* AI_cityTrade asks the RECIPIENT player whether the still-seller-owned city is likely to
  benefit that recipient long-term. A false result is an absolute DENIAL_UNKNOWN before
  AI_cityTradeVal can value the developed city.
* SAS_findNearbyOverseasConquestTarget evaluates still-foreign cities and skips a target
  entirely when this helper returns false, before AI_targetCityValue.
* SAS_isDistantDisposableBarbarianTarget likewise evaluates a still-Barbarian city for its
  prospective conqueror and can reject a distant expedition on the result.
The overseas logging caller inherits the same displayed misclassification, though its log is
not itself a separate behavioral root.

Current XML proves owner-team obsolescence can differ for real World Wonders. Seven shipped
World Wonders have an ObsoleteTech:
* Great Lighthouse -> Astronomy
* Colossus -> Democracy
* Oracle -> Broader Education
* Temple of Kukulcan -> Chemistry
* Temple of Artemis -> Broader Education
* Great Wall -> Gunpowder
* Apostolic Palace -> Mass Media

Concrete current reproduction direction:
1. Seller/foreign owner S owns a poor-intrinsic-site city containing the Great Lighthouse.
2. S's team has Astronomy, so kCity.hasActiveWorldWonder() returns false.
3. Prospective AI recipient/attacker B does NOT have Astronomy. On transfer/capture the World
   Wonder building is preserved, and it is active for B.
4. KI#186's helper nevertheless evaluates S's obsolescence state and can reject the city as
   unlikely to benefit B long-term.
5. The later AdvCiv target valuation would have handled this correctly: AI_targetCityValue
   already uses `c.getNumActiveWorldWonders(MAX_INT, getID())`, explicitly evaluating active
   Wonder count for the prospective attacker. The KI#186 filter can prevent reaching that
   correct broader valuation.

The reverse asymmetry is also wrong: if S lacks the obsoleting tech but B already has it, the
helper can protect an intrinsically poor site because the Wonder is active for S even though
it becomes obsolete for B immediately upon acquisition.

This contradicts KI#186's documented question - whether ACQUIRING the city is likely to
benefit the RECIPIENT long-term - and KI#186.2's rule that an ACTIVE World Wonder protects
intrinsic site quality. The define is enabled by default. The error was introduced by SAS's
KI#186/KI#186.2 helper; Base AdvCiv's hypothetical-owner World-Wonder API already exists.

Narrow repair direction:
* Inside AI_isSASCityLikelyToBenefitUsLongTerm, evaluate the protection as e.g.
  `kCity.getNumActiveWorldWonders(1, getID()) > 0` rather than `kCity.hasActiveWorldWonder()`.
  This automatically remains equivalent for the post-conquest self-owned caller while
  becoming correct for trade and pre-conquest target callers.
* Keep AI_conquerCity's separate outer `bActiveWorldWonder` check as current-owner state; at
  that point acquisition has already happened and current owner == evaluator.
* Add an autoplay/unit-style diagnostic case with different obsolescence tech state between
  city owner and prospective recipient (Great Lighthouse/Astronomy is a simple fixture).

Severity: MEDIUM AI acquisition/target-selection correctness. Can veto a city whose Wonder
would be active for the recipient, or admit/protect a site based on a Wonder that will be
obsolete for the recipient. Current city-trade and overseas-conquest filters make the
consequence behavioral, not cosmetic.

Duplicate check: no earlier album/Known-Issues root was found for hypothetical-owner World
Wonder obsolescence in this helper. KI#186/KI#186.2 are the introducing/fixed-feature family,
not an already-diagnosed instance of this recipient-state mismatch.
