===============================================================================
F346 / provisional KI#669 — AI_neededCityAttackers mistakes legitimate Ancient-era
war targets for "no targets" and contaminates their mean era with Barbarian era
===============================================================================

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited AdvCiv `advc.104p` value/sentinel collision introduced by the
feature that changed city-attack stack sizing from own/game era to target era; still
present unchanged in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_neededCityAttackers` intentionally estimates stack size from the mean
current era of civilizations against which this team has a war plan:

    scaled rMeanTargetEra;
    int iEnemies = 0;
    ...
    if (kOurTeam.AI_getWarPlan(itEnemy->getTeam()) != NO_WARPLAN)
    {
        rMeanTargetEra += itEnemy->getCurrentEra();
        iEnemies++;
    }

If no such target exists, the function wants a fallback era so that the calculation is
still defined. But it tests the accumulated *value* instead of whether any enemy was
found:

    if (rMeanTargetEra == 0)
    {
        rMeanTargetEra += GET_PLAYER(BARBARIAN_PLAYER).getCurrentEra();
        iEnemies++;
    }
    rMeanTargetEra /= iEnemies;

Era 0 is a legitimate civilization era. Therefore one or more real war-plan targets
can be present (`iEnemies > 0`) while `rMeanTargetEra == 0` simply because every target
is Ancient. Those targets are then treated as though none had been found: the Barbarian
player's era is injected and the divisor is incremented.

The correct sentinel already exists independently as `iEnemies`.

SUPPORTED REPRODUCTION
----------------------
Let an AI have exactly one known war-plan target T and let T still be in
`ERA_ANCIENT` (current-era index 0). Let the Barbarian player meanwhile have reached,
for example, era 4 through the ordinary AdvCiv Barbarian catch-up system.

The intended mean target era is:

    0 / 1 = 0

Current code executes the fallback because the sum is numerically zero:

    (0 + 4) / (1 + 1) = 2

So a real Ancient target is evaluated as though its era were 2 solely because unrelated
Barbarian technological progress exists elsewhere in the game.

With several Ancient targets the same collision remains: their summed era is still
zero, so the Barbarian era is added once and divided across `iEnemies + 1`.

CURRENT FORMULA CONSEQUENCE
---------------------------
The contaminated mean is not informational only. It feeds both deterministic and
random stack-size terms:

    scaled rEraRatio = (rMeanTargetEra + 1) / GC.getNumEraInfos();
    iModulus = round(strategyBase + rEraRatio * iFlavourExtra +
            rMeanTargetEra / 2);
    iR = floor(rMeanTargetEra / 2) + 4 + (hash % iModulus);

Current SAS has seven eras. For an ordinary military-flavoured AI, raising the mean
from 0 to 2 increases both the fixed term and the randomization range. For some
birthmarks the requested stack can jump by several units even before training-speed,
assault-area and colonial multipliers are applied.

The current SAS `SAS_MIN_ATTACK_CITY_STACK_UNITS = 9` can mask low-end differences in
one readiness comparison, but it does not neutralize the root:

* sufficiently high Barbarian-era contamination can make `AI_neededCityAttackers`
  exceed that floor;
* `AI_stackOfDoomExtra()` is also used directly as the target size for regrouping;
* assault transports use it directly to derive reinforcement and invasion cargo
  thresholds, without the SAS 9-unit city-attack readiness floor.

LIVE CONSUMERS
--------------
The main current `UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY` movement path obtains:

    iWarStackNeeded = AI_stackOfDoomExtra();

and requires a non-Barbarian real-war stack to meet `iWarStackNeeded` (plus the SAS
minimum) before setting `bReadyToAttack`. The same helper is used while under-sized
city-assault groups wait for or join other groups, including an `AI_omniGroup` target
of roughly twice `AI_stackOfDoomExtra()`.

`UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA` also derives:

    rTargetReinforcementSize = AI_stackOfDoomExtra();
    rTargetInvasionSize = 2 * rTargetReinforcementSize;

so the false target-era increase can make naval invasion transports wait for more land
cargo even though the actual civilization target remains Ancient.

The result therefore affects real army assembly/readiness and amphibious launch
thresholds rather than merely a debug or advisory value.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod's older stack-size formula scaled from the current/game era and therefore did not
have this particular value/sentinel collision.

AdvCiv practical commit 2710 (`168c4a2c799cef88f0461ed850ff1eaa34faa6a6`), titled:

    Tweak to AI the target size of AI city attack stacks

introduced the target-era calculation. The introducing diff explicitly says:

    We don't need more units as _we_ become more advanced.
    Instead check what era our potential targets are in.

and in that same new block adds:

    if (rMeanTargetEra == 0)
    {
        rMeanTargetEra += GET_PLAYER(BARBARIAN_PLAYER).getCurrentEra();
        iEnemies++;
    }

Thus the bug is present at the feature's introduction: zero was simultaneously made a
valid target-era result and used as the "no target" sentinel.

AdvCiv later moved this body from `CvUnitAI::AI_stackOfDoomExtra` into
`CvPlayerAI::AI_neededCityAttackers` (practical commit 3959, refactor only). Base
AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same `rMeanTargetEra == 0` condition verbatim, and current SAS
retains it too.

This is therefore inherited AdvCiv, not SAS-local.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
F346 is not about Barbarian-city expedition sizing; current SAS has a separate
`AI_neededCityAttackersVsBarbarians()` path for deliberate Barbarian-city attacks.
Here the actual intended target is a normal civilization, and the Barbarian player's
technological era leaks into that civilization-war stack estimate only because Ancient
has index 0.

It is also separate from earlier Barbarian-research findings such as KI#408/F086. Those
can affect how quickly Barbarians advance, but F346 remains a deterministic
misclassification whenever the Barbarian era is nonzero and all real war-plan targets
sum to era zero.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Use the actual presence/count sentinel:

    if (iEnemies == 0)
    {
        rMeanTargetEra = GET_PLAYER(BARBARIAN_PLAYER).getCurrentEra();
        iEnemies = 1;
    }

or equivalently retain the addition form while testing `iEnemies <= 0`.

This preserves the intended fallback when no civilization target exists while allowing
one or many legitimate Ancient targets to produce a mean era of exactly zero.

No retuning of stack-size coefficients is required; the repair only restores the
feature's stated target-era contract.

------------------------------

===============================================================================
F347 / provisional KI#670 — failed bounded path in AI_unitTargetMissionAIs can
MAX_INT++ into a negative "nearby" distance and count far joiners as imminent
===============================================================================

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited K-Mod bounded-mission-census failure-path bug; retained by
AdvCiv and current SAS. Vanilla BtS/Civ4CE does not contain the bounded path-turn
extension that creates this root.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_unitTargetMissionAIs` optionally counts only groups that can reach the
specified target unit within `iMaxPathTurns`:

    int iPathTurns = MAX_INT;
    if (iMaxPathTurns >= 0 && kUnit.plot() != NULL &&
        pLoopSelectionGroup->plot() != NULL)
    {
        pLoopSelectionGroup->generatePath(..., &iPathTurns,
                iMaxPathTurns);
        if (!pLoopSelectionGroup->canAllMove())
            iPathTurns++;
    }
    ...
    if (iMaxPathTurns < 0 || iPathTurns <= iMaxPathTurns)
        iCount += pLoopSelectionGroup->getNumUnits();

The return value of `generatePath` is ignored.

`CvSelectionGroup::generatePath` explicitly defines its output contract as:

    if (piPathTurns != NULL)
    {
        *piPathTurns = MAX_INT;
        if (bSuccess)
            *piPathTurns = kPathFinder.getPathTurns();
    }
    return bSuccess;

Therefore a path that does not exist *within the requested maximum* leaves
`iPathTurns == MAX_INT` by design.

The caller then increments that failure sentinel whenever the joining group cannot all
move. On Civ4's supported 32-bit MSVC/x86 runtime, incrementing `INT_MAX` wraps to the
negative signed endpoint. That negative value trivially satisfies every ordinary
nonnegative path window such as `<= 2` or `<= 3`.

So the exact branch intended to exclude a distant/unreachable group can instead count
it as nearby whenever that group has already spent movement this turn.

SUPPORTED REPRODUCTION
----------------------
No permanent physical disconnection is needed.

1. City-assault group A is the target group.
2. A second group B has an ordinary `MISSIONAI_GROUP` mission targeting A's head unit.
   Current `AI_omniGroup` producers can create such grouping missions with a maximum
   path of 10 turns, so B may legitimately be, for example, 5 turns away.
3. B acts earlier in the player turn and moves toward A. It therefore still has the
   same grouping target but `canAllMove()` is now false.
4. A later runs its city-assault movement and asks only for imminent joiners, e.g.:

       AI_unitTargetMissionAIs(*this, &eMissionAIType, 1,
               getGroup(), 2)

5. The helper asks B's group for a path capped at 2 turns. Because B is still about
   4 turns away, `generatePath` returns false and writes `MAX_INT`.
6. Because B has already moved, the helper executes `iPathTurns++` on that sentinel.
7. The wrapped negative value passes `iPathTurns <= 2`, and every unit in B is counted
   as a nearby joiner.

The same shape can arise from a truly unreachable target, but the ordinary
"longer than this caller's local wait window" case is sufficient and considerably
more common.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE
----------------
The main `UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY` path uses bounded mission counts specifically to decide
whether a stack should wait for backup.

For a ready attack stack, K-Mod/AdvCiv calculates a short `iMaxWaitTurns` (often 1-3)
and obtains:

    int iJoiners = AI_unitTargetMissionAIs(..., iMaxWaitTurns);

It can then `MISSION_SKIP` when the supposedly imminent joiners are large enough.

A concrete current shape is a 6-unit ready stack A and a 2-unit B group still more than
2 turns away. Correct bounded counting returns 0. With the failure-sentinel overflow,
B contributes 2 and the readiness check can become:

    2 * 5 > 6

causing A to wait despite the backup being explicitly outside the 2-turn horizon.

The not-yet-ready and nearby-joiner branches likewise use 2-turn bounded calls, so the
same false-positive census can make attack stacks park or avoid regrouping decisions
for distant groups.

This is a gameplay control-flow consequence, not merely an inaccurate diagnostic
count.

PRODUCER CONTRACT
-----------------
`MISSIONAI_GROUP` groups farther than the bounded query window are normal supported
state. `AI_omniGroup` selects a candidate after a successful path search using its own
caller-supplied maximum, and then pushes:

    MISSION_MOVE_TO_UNIT ... MISSIONAI_GROUP ... pBestUnit

Several attack-city grouping calls permit paths up to roughly 10 turns. The later
`AI_unitTargetMissionAIs(..., 2)` query is deliberately a *narrower* question:
"which of those joiners are close enough that we should wait now?"

Thus a 5-10-turn grouping mission presented to a 2-turn census is not stale or invalid
state; it is exactly why the helper has an `iMaxPathTurns` parameter.

Likewise `canAllMove()==false` is ordinary after B has already taken its movement for
the current turn. The function even contains the increment specifically to account for
that state on successful paths.

ANCESTRY
--------
Civ4CE/BtS `AI_unitTargetMissionAIs` has no path-turn filtering at all; it simply counts
groups whose MissionAI unit/type match. Therefore this particular failure sentinel does
not exist there.

K-Mod 1.46 adds the `iMaxPathTurns` overload. Its implementation already contains the
same sequence:

    int iPathTurns = MAX_INT;
    generatePath(..., &iPathTurns);
    if (!pLoopSelectionGroup->canAllMove())
        iPathTurns++;
    if (iMaxPathTurns == -1 || iPathTurns <= iMaxPathTurns)
        count ...

AdvCiv retained that logic while optimizing mission-type checks, passing the max path
directly to the newer pathfinder, adding the cargo-load kludge and adding `iMaxCount`.
Those changes do not repair the ignored failure return plus sentinel increment.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the root. This is therefore inherited from
K-Mod/BBAI-era mission-count logic, not SAS-local.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
Earlier mission-census findings KI#534/F206 and KI#544/F221 concern empty-group
lifecycle and double-counted loaded cargo in `AI_enemyTargetMissions`. F347 is a
separate helper and a separate invariant: a failed bounded path is converted into a
small/negative path-turn result before the distance filter.

The previously closed multi-MissionAI-array concern is also unrelated; F347 reproduces
with the ordinary single `MISSIONAI_GROUP` request used by live attack-city callers.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Honor path failure before adjusting turns:

    if (iMaxPathTurns >= 0 && ...)
    {
        if (!pLoopSelectionGroup->generatePath(..., &iPathTurns,
                iMaxPathTurns))
            continue;
        if (!pLoopSelectionGroup->canAllMove())
            iPathTurns++;
    }

Alternatively guard the increment/result explicitly against `MAX_INT`, but using the
boolean return is clearer and preserves the pathfinder's contract.

If the "already moved" adjustment can push a successful path from the maximum to one
turn beyond it, the existing final `iPathTurns <= iMaxPathTurns` check correctly rejects
that group; no additional tuning change is required.

===============================================================================
C031-WIP36 — F348 / provisional KI#671 CONFIRMED
AI_espionageVal Counterespionage era-0 normalization can divide by zero for a
supported WorldBuilder/scenario Ancient Spy
===============================================================================

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED, but deliberately bounded to supported scenario / WorldBuilder state.
This is not an ordinary current-SAS random-game crash because the only normal
`UNITAI_SPY` unit requires Classical-era Monarchy.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_espionageVal` values Counterespionage with:

    int const iEra = getCurrentEra();
    ...
    iCounterValue /= std::max(1, 50 * iEra * (iEra + 1) +
            GET_TEAM(getTeam()).getEspionagePointsAgainstTeam(eTargetTeam)) / 2;

The intended normalization floor is defeated by integer arithmetic. The divisor is
not:

    std::max(1, (...)/2)

but rather:

    std::max(1, X) / 2

because `/` is evaluated on the right-hand side before the compound assignment.
When `X` is 0 or 1, `std::max(1, X)` is 1 and integer `1 / 2` is 0. The subsequent
integer division is therefore a divide-by-zero fault.

At era 0:

    X = own espionage points against the target team

so an Ancient player with 0 or 1 EP against the target reaches the zero divisor.

WHY ORDINARY CURRENT-SAS TRAINING DOES NOT REPRODUCE
-----------------------------------------------------
Current SAS has exactly one unit that uses `UNITAI_SPY`: `UNIT_SPY`.
Its current XML has:

    <DefaultUnitAI>UNITAI_SPY</DefaultUnitAI>
    <bSpy>1</bSpy>
    <PrereqTech>TECH_MONARCHY</PrereqTech>

and current Monarchy belongs to the Classical era. Therefore a normally trained
current-SAS Spy has `iEra >= 1`; the era term alone makes the normalization quantity
at least 100 and the zero-divisor case disappears.

`UNIT_GREAT_SPY` does not supply a hidden normal-game producer. Current XML gives it
`bSpy=0` and `UNITAI_GREAT_SPY`; the UnitAI dispatcher sends it through
`AI_greatPersonMove`, not `AI_spyMove` / `AI_espionageSpy`.

SUPPORTED SCENARIO / WORLDBUILDER PRODUCER
------------------------------------------
The WorldBuilder save loader does not reconstruct units through `canTrain`. In
`Assets/Python/pyWB/CvWBDesc.py`, `CvUnitDesc.apply` resolves the serialized
`UnitType` and directly calls:

    player.initUnit(unitTypeNum, self.plotX, self.plotY,
            UnitAITypes(eUnitAI), self.facingDirection)

If the save leaves `UnitAIType` unspecified, it passes `NO_UNITAI`; `CvPlayer::initUnit`
then deliberately substitutes the unit XML's default UnitAI. Thus a WB scenario can
legitimately define an Ancient AI-owned `UNIT_SPY` and obtain `UNITAI_SPY` without the
player knowing Monarchy.

The same WB format independently serializes/sets the player's starting era, so
`ERA_ANCIENT + UNIT_SPY` is an ordinary supported scenario combination rather than
memory corruption or an invalid direct DLL call.

LIVE CRASH CHAIN
----------------
A minimal supported reproduction is:

1. WorldBuilder/scenario player A is AI-controlled and has current era Ancient.
2. A owns a normal `UNIT_SPY` / `UNITAI_SPY`, e.g. serialized directly in or moved to
   a city owned by major-civ player B.
3. A has 0 (or 1) espionage point against B.
4. On the AI turn, the Spy reaches the ordinary `AI_spyMove` city handling and invokes
   `AI_espionageSpy` once its normal mission-selection conditions are met (placing it
   already fortified in the target city makes this easy to reproduce).
5. `AI_espionageSpy` calls `AI_bestPlotEspionage`.
6. Current Counterespionage XML has no technology prerequisite, costs 100 EP and has
   `iCounterespionageNumTurns=10`.
7. `AI_bestPlotEspionage` deliberately evaluates missions that are unaffordable due
   only to insufficient EP so the AI can decide whether they are worth saving points
   for. Its guard is:

       if (iCost < 0 ||
           (iCost <= iEspPoints && !canDoEspionageMission(...)))
           continue;

   With cost 100 and current EP 0, the second condition is false; valuation proceeds
   even though the mission cannot yet be executed.
8. `AI_espionageVal` enters the Counterespionage branch because its duration is 10.
   At era 0 and own EP 0:

       std::max(1, 0) / 2 == 1 / 2 == 0

9. `iCounterValue /= 0` executes. On Civ4's supported 32-bit MSVC/x86 runtime this is
   an integer divide-by-zero exception / crash.

The mission does not need to be affordable; that is precisely why the valuation path
can encounter the low-EP state.

ANCESTRY
--------
Vanilla BtS / Civ4CE contains the Counterespionage branch but leaves it effectively
empty apart from the old commented attitude line. It therefore does not contain this
arithmetic crash.

K-Mod commit 161 (`f9e8a3c4ceeab74d8d33f1fe8a0323ac5d1bc5be`) introduced an actual
Counterespionage value. Its first normalization form used:

    iCounterValue /= std::max(1, 50*iEra*iEra + ownEP);

which retained a valid denominator floor.

K-Mod commit 162 changed the era scaling to `50*iEra*(iEra+1)` but still kept the
whole denominator inside `std::max`, so it remained safe.

K-Mod practical commit 228 (`285f6c4323e98fe3527a9f6659fcd9a05af9b83c`) changed the formula to the
current half-scale form:

    iCounterValue *= (...)/2 + targetEP;
    iCounterValue /= std::max(1, ... + ownEP)/2;

Moving `/2` *outside* the `std::max` introduced the zero-divisor state for a floored
value of 1. AdvCiv inherited that exact arithmetic; later AdvCiv changes to victory
strategy and memory weighting did not repair the divisor. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current
SAS retain it.

This is therefore an inherited K-Mod regression, absent from vanilla BtS.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
The earlier team-lifecycle Counterespionage findings in the album concern migration or
persistence of Counterespionage turns/modifiers across team changes. F348 is unrelated:
it is a local arithmetic failure during AI mission valuation before any mission is
performed.

The `GET_PLAYER(eTargetPlayer)`-before-`NO_PLAYER` ordering at the top of
`AI_espionageVal` is also separate and is not being numbered here; the sole current
gameplay caller rejects unowned plots before calling this helper.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Keep the intended half-scale normalization but floor the *actual divisor*, e.g.:

    int const iCounterDivisor = std::max(1,
            (50 * iEra * (iEra + 1) +
             GET_TEAM(getTeam()).getEspionagePointsAgainstTeam(eTargetTeam)) / 2);
    iCounterValue /= iCounterDivisor;

Equivalently, if the historical intent was to halve after flooring but never below 1:

    iCounterValue /= std::max(1,
            std::max(1, 50 * iEra * (iEra + 1) + ownEP) / 2);

The first form is simpler. This repair only restores denominator safety; it does not
retune normal Classical+ Counterespionage valuation.

===============================================================================
C031-WIP37 — CORRECTION: WIP36 F348 RETRACTED; F348 UNUSED AGAIN
===============================================================================

STATUS
------
WIP36's F348 promotion is RETRACTED after tracing the inner
`AI_espionageVal -> canDoEspionageMission` legality gate and the minimum reachable
Counterespionage mission cost. Do not treat the WIP36 scenario crash as a confirmed
finding.

The arithmetic expression remains unsafe in isolation, but the current supported
producer chain does not reach it with the only EP values that make the divisor zero.
This is therefore latent hardening debt, not a numbered current root under the album's
producer -> contract -> consequence standard.

WHAT WIP36 MISSED
-----------------
`CvUnitAI::AI_bestPlotEspionage` deliberately considers an espionage mission even when
it is currently unaffordable, so that the AI can decide whether saving EP is worthwhile.
That outer behavior initially appeared to make an Ancient WB-created Spy with 0-1 EP a
producer for the Counterespionage divisor.

However, `AI_espionageVal` itself begins with:

    TeamTypes eTargetTeam = GET_PLAYER(eTargetPlayer).getTeam();
    if (eTargetPlayer == NO_PLAYER ||
        !canDoEspionageMission(eMission, eTargetPlayer, &kPlot, iData, NULL))
    {
        return 0;
    }

`canDoEspionageMission` defaults `bCheckPoints=true` and ends with:

    return (iEspionagePoints >= iCost && iEspionagePoints > 0);

Therefore an unaffordable mission never reaches the valuation body. The outer
save-for-later path does not bypass this inner gate.

WHY EP=0 CANNOT REACH THE DIVISOR
---------------------------------
The inner gate explicitly requires:

    iEspionagePoints > 0

So the era-0 `ownEP == 0` zero-divisor case cannot enter `AI_espionageVal`'s mission
body through its current gameplay caller.

WHY EP=1 ALSO FAILS UNDER CURRENT SUPPORTED DATA
-------------------------------------------------
At era 0 the dangerous denominator is:

    std::max(1, ownEP) / 2

which is zero for ownEP 0 or 1. Since 0 is excluded above, a live producer would need
a Counterespionage mission cost of at most 1 EP.

The inner legality check passes `pUnit=NULL`. This matters: unlike the outer
unit-specific mission cost, the inner cost does NOT receive the Spy's fortification /
stationary discount. Consequently the strongest normal current-data cost reductions
for a city-target Counterespionage mission are bounded approximately by:

    trade route                 80%
    our state religion + holy   60%
    plot-culture modifier       50%
    distance                    >=100%   (cannot reduce below the base)
    espionage-points modifier   >=50%
    city espionage defense      >=100% in current XML
    target counterespionage     >=100% in ordinary current state

Population is neutral under the current default define. Multiplying the reducing
terms gives a floor of about 12% before team-size adjustment. The omitted stationary
50% discount is exactly what would otherwise have made the first WIP36 lower-bound
argument too optimistic.

`adjustMissionCostToTeamSize` can reduce the Counterespionage base cost before the
modifier when the target team is much larger than the acting team. Current
`TECH_COST_EXTRA_TEAM_MEMBER_MODIFIER` is 50. Even an extreme supported 48-civ setup
with one acting civ and 47 members on the target team gives approximately:

    adjusted base = floor(100 * sqrt(1 / (1 + 0.5 * 46)))
                  = about 20

Applying the approximately 12% minimum inner modifier leaves a mission cost of at
least 2 EP after integer arithmetic. Smaller target teams cost more.

Thus current supported WB/team setups cannot satisfy both required conditions:

    ownEP <= 1        (needed for zero divisor)
    ownEP >= mission cost > 0   (needed to pass the inner legality gate)

The dangerous arithmetic is unreachable under the current rules/data examined.

WHY ARBITRARY PYTHON/API STATE DOES NOT RESCUE THE FINDING
----------------------------------------------------------
Python exposes setters capable of constructing nonstandard state (for example a
negative Counterespionage modifier could artificially drive mission cost to zero),
but such arbitrary scripted mutation is not a current gameplay/scenario producer and
would reduce the standard to API misuse. The normal WB serializer does not establish
that state.

The supported WB ability to create an Ancient `UNIT_SPY` remains real, but it is not
enough by itself because the inner cost/EP gate blocks the divisor.

ANCESTRY NOTE RETAINED AS HARDENING EVIDENCE
---------------------------------------------
The arithmetic hazard itself still entered in K-Mod practical commit 228
(`285f6c4323e98fe3527a9f6659fcd9a05af9b83c`) when `/2` was moved outside the
`std::max(1, ...)` denominator floor. Vanilla BtS lacks the valuation arithmetic and
earlier K-Mod forms kept the whole denominator inside the floor.

That remains a worthwhile defensive cleanup:

    iCounterValue /= std::max(1, (...)/2);

would express the intended nonzero-divisor invariant directly. But without a current
supported producer, it does not earn F348.

===============================================================================
C031-WIP38 — F348 CONFIRMED (reused after WIP36 retraction)
===============================================================================

F348 / provisional KI#671 — AI_espionageVal's unitless current-EP gate defeats
K-Mod's save-for-later mission valuation and can suppress missions affordable only
through the acting Spy's stationary discount

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED current inherited root.

This is NOT WIP36's retracted Counterespionage divide-by-zero claim. WIP37 remains the
correction for that false producer. F348 is now reused for an independent, fully
supported mission-selection contract bug found while continuing through the same
`AI_espionageVal` entry gate.

ROOT
----
Current `CvUnitAI::AI_bestPlotEspionage` is deliberately unit-aware. For every candidate
mission it obtains the cost with the ACTUAL Spy:

    int iCost = kOwner.getEspionageMissionCost(
            eMission, eTargetPlayer, &kSpyPlot, iTestData, this);

and, when that cost is currently affordable, validates the mission with the same Spy:

    if (iCost < 0 || (iCost <= iEspPoints &&
        !kOwner.canDoEspionageMission(
            eMission, eTargetPlayer, &kSpyPlot, iTestData, this)))
    {
        continue;
    }

The intentional K-Mod contract is broader than "only value what is affordable now".
Immediately after valuation the caller explicitly handles an unaffordable mission:

    /* If we can't do the mission yet, don't completely give up.
       It might be worth saving points for. */
    if (!kOwner.canDoEspionageMission(
        eMission, eTargetPlayer, &kSpyPlot, iTestData, this))
    {
        ...
        iValue *= 3;
        iValue /= iTurns + 3;
    }

However the only value helper call in between is:

    int iValue = kOwner.AI_espionageVal(
            eTargetPlayer, eMission, kSpyPlot, iTestData);

and `AI_espionageVal` still begins with the old player-level gate:

    if (eTargetPlayer == NO_PLAYER ||
        !canDoEspionageMission(
            eMission, eTargetPlayer, &kPlot, iData, NULL))
    {
        return 0;
    }

`canDoEspionageMission` defaults `bCheckPoints=true`. It computes the mission cost and
then requires:

    iEspionagePoints >= iCost && iEspionagePoints > 0

Thus the value helper is enforcing CURRENT affordability even though its caller
explicitly needs a value before current affordability has been reached.

CONSEQUENCE A — THE SAVE-FOR-LATER BRANCH IS EFFECTIVELY DEAD
--------------------------------------------------------------
Take any otherwise legal mission whose actual Spy-specific cost is 200 EP while the
team currently has 150 EP.

`AI_bestPlotEspionage` sees:

    iCost = 200
    iEspPoints = 150

The early `continue` deliberately does NOT fire because `iCost > iEspPoints`; K-Mod
wants to value the mission and decide whether it is worth saving for.

But `AI_espionageVal` immediately calls `canDoEspionageMission(..., NULL)` with points
checking enabled. Its no-unit cost cannot be lower through the stationary-Spy mechanic,
and in the ordinary unfortified case it is the same 200 EP. Since 150 < 200, the helper
returns 0 before evaluating any mission benefit.

Back in `AI_bestPlotEspionage`, the intended save-for-later branch runs and scales that
zero value according to the estimated wait:

    iValue *= 3;
    iValue /= iTurns + 3;

Zero remains zero. Risk/escape overhead can then make the candidate negative. Since
`iBestValue` starts at zero, the mission cannot become the selected future target.

This does not require a special mission, scenario state, stationary Spy, or unusual XML.
For every currently unaffordable candidate admitted specifically for K-Mod's
save-for-later logic, the inner current-EP gate prevents the mission's positive value
from ever reaching that logic.

CONSEQUENCE B — A FULLY FORTIFIED SPY CAN AFFORD A MISSION THAT VALUATION REJECTS
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The same root also creates a direct current-action mismatch.

`CvPlayer::getEspionageMissionCostModifier` applies the stationary discount only when an
actual Spy pointer is supplied:

    if (pSpyUnit != NULL)
    {
        iModifier *= 100 - pSpyUnit->getFortifyTurns() *
                ESPIONAGE_EACH_TURN_UNIT_COST_DECREASE;
        iModifier /= 100;
    }

Current BtS/SAS defaults are:

    MAX_FORTIFY_TURNS = 5
    ESPIONAGE_EACH_TURN_UNIT_COST_DECREASE = 10

so a Spy that has waited the normal five turns receives a 50% cost modifier at this
stage.

`AI_spyMove` deliberately calls `AI_espionageSpy()` once the Spy reaches that exact
maximum fortification state, making this ordinary AI gameplay rather than a constructed
API state.

Let a candidate have:

    G = its mission cost when no Spy is supplied
    A = its cost for the fully stationary acting Spy (approximately half G)

Choose an ordinary accumulated-EP state with:

    A <= current EP < G

The outer selector computes A with `this`, and `canDoEspionageMission(..., this)` says
the mission is executable NOW. `AI_espionageVal`, however, recomputes legality with
`pUnit=NULL`, loses the stationary discount, sees cost G > current EP, and returns 0.
The later current-action check again uses the actual Spy and would pass, but the positive
mission value has already been erased.

NORMAL CURRENT-DATA REPRODUCTION — SPACESHIP COMPONENT SABOTAGE
---------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS keeps `ESPIONAGEMISSION_DESTROY_PROJECT` enabled with:

    iCost = 0
    iDestroyProjectCostFactor = 500
    TechPrereq = NONE

and current spaceship components include e.g. `PROJECT_SS_COCKPIT` with XML cost 1000,
along with Life Support, Stasis Chamber, Docking Bay, Engine, Casing and Thrusters.

`getEspionageMissionBaseCost` prices destroy-project at:

    base mission cost + (100 + 500)% * getProductionNeeded(project)

so component sabotage has a large positive generic cost and therefore a large interval
between the fully stationary actual-Spy cost and the NULL-unit cost.

Before launch, `canSpyDestroyProject` accepts completed non-world spaceship components.
For a malicious target, `AI_espionageVal` would value the destruction at:

    getProductionNeeded(project) *
        (maxTeamInstances == 1 ? 8 : 6)

which is thousands of value points for current components. Thus this is not a marginal
mission whose zeroing is likely irrelevant: a high-value, immediately executable
spaceship sabotage can be omitted from selection solely because the value helper
rechecks affordability without the acting Spy.

A war-plan target is sufficient to satisfy current `AI_isMaliciousEspionageTarget`.
Final `AI_espionageSpy` execution again calls `canDoEspionageMission(..., this)`, so both
ends of the live chain agree that the fortified Spy can perform the mission. The middle
value helper is the inconsistent layer.

CALLER / CONTRACT RECONCILIATION
--------------------------------
Current SAS has exactly one gameplay caller of `AI_espionageVal`:

    CvUnitAI::AI_bestPlotEspionage

So there is no competing current caller that requires `AI_espionageVal` itself to reject
missions solely because the team does not yet have enough EP.

The caller already owns:
- actual-Spy mission cost,
- actual-Spy current legality,
- the explicit save-for-later policy,
- wait-time discounting,
- risk/escape overhead,
- final actual-Spy execution validation.

The player-level value helper's second current-affordability gate is therefore both
redundant for immediately executable missions and directly incompatible with the
future-value contract.

ANCESTRY
--------
Vanilla BtS/Civ4CE already has the old player-level `AI_espionageVal` affordability
check using `pUnit=NULL`. Its old `CvPlayerAI::AI_bestPlotEspionage` is also player-level
and simply asks the value helper for missions; consequently vanilla selection already
does not make proper use of an acting Spy's stationary cost discount.

K-Mod then moved/reworked `AI_bestPlotEspionage` into `CvUnitAI` (the practical commit
around `f17786fc36db621009675c2a005fdd2c88f5559b`, which reworked Spy mission selection).
The new selector became explicitly unit-aware:
- mission cost is computed with `this`,
- actual legality is checked with `this`,
- final execution is checked with `this`, and
- currently unaffordable missions are intentionally retained so the AI can decide to
  save EP for them.

But K-Mod retained the old BtS `AI_espionageVal(... canDoEspionageMission(..., NULL))`
affordability gate. Current K-Mod source therefore already contains the contradiction,
and AdvCiv/SAS inherit it.

The most useful attribution is therefore:
- old stationary-discount blindness is inherited from BtS;
- K-Mod's unit-aware/save-for-later rework failed to remove the old unitless current-EP
  gate, making the intended future-value branch internally self-defeating;
- AdvCiv and current SAS inherit that integration defect.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
This is separate from F055 / KI#376. F055 concerns a diagnostic/preparation metric that
counts fortified states which do not represent a usable stationary espionage discount.
F348 concerns ACTUAL mission selection: even a real ordinary Spy fortified in the
correct foreign target city can have a legal discounted mission valued at zero.

It is also separate from WIP36's retracted Counterespionage divisor claim. WIP37 remains
the authoritative correction for that failed producer. The F348 number is reused here
only after that retraction, exactly as earlier retracted numbers in the album have been
reused for independent confirmed roots.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Do not fix only the stationary example by passing a Spy pointer while leaving current
EP checking enabled; that would still keep K-Mod's save-for-later branch dead.

The value helper needs STRUCTURAL mission legality without requiring current EP.
Since its only current caller has the acting Spy, a clean direction is to make that
context explicit, for example:

    int AI_espionageVal(..., CvUnit const* pSpyUnit) const;

and gate with:

    if (eTargetPlayer == NO_PLAYER ||
        !canDoEspionageMission(
            eMission, eTargetPlayer, &kPlot, iData, pSpyUnit, false))
    {
        return 0;
    }

where `false` is `bCheckPoints`.

That preserves structural/unit legality and the actual Spy context while leaving EP
affordability to `AI_bestPlotEspionage`, which already has the dedicated current-vs-
future logic.

A smaller repair could remove/relax the current-points gate in `AI_espionageVal`, but
passing the acting Spy is preferable because it keeps unit-sensitive legality coherent
with the sole caller and future-proofs any additional unit-dependent mission rules.

===============================================================================
C031-WIP39 — F349 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F349 / provisional KI#672 — AI_doCommerce reuses one tech-theft accumulator across
rivals, so the "at least two stealable techs" gate both misses real targets and can
combine unrelated one-tech targets into a false cheap-tech-steal strategy

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited K-Mod espionage-target state/accumulator bug retained by AdvCiv
and current SAS. Civ4CE/BtS does not contain this K-Mod cheap-tech-steal target block.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_doCommerce` declares these once before iterating rival teams and their
members:

    int iMinModifier = MAX_INT;
    int iApproxTechCost = 0;
    TeamTypes eMinModTeam = NO_TEAM;

For each rival member, the code then tries to establish that the target has at least
TWO technologies worth stealing:

    bool bValid = false;
    FOR_EACH_ENUM(Tech)
    {
        if (canStealTech(kRivalMember.getID(), eLoopTech))
        {
            // don't set it true unless there are at least 2 stealable techs.
            bValid = iApproxTechCost > 0;
            iApproxTechCost = (kOurTeam.getResearchCost(eLoopTech) +
                    iApproxTechCost) / (iApproxTechCost != 0 ? 2 : 1);
            break;
        }
    }

There are two incompatible contracts packed into `iApproxTechCost`:

1. `bValid = iApproxTechCost > 0` treats it as a PER-TARGET "already found one tech"
   sentinel.
2. The later `bCheapTechSteal` logic treats it as the approximate cost of the selected
   tech-theft opportunity.

But the variable is never reset for a new rival/member, and the loop `break`s after the
first stealable tech. Therefore the intended per-target "two techs" test cannot work.

FAILURE A — REAL MULTI-TECH TARGET MISSED
-----------------------------------------
A normal singleton rival can have two, five or ten stealable technologies. On that
player's scan:

- the first stealable tech enters the branch;
- `iApproxTechCost` was 0, so `bValid` is false;
- the cost is stored;
- `break` exits the entire technology loop immediately.

No second technology belonging to that same target is ever inspected. If there is no
previous rival/member to have seeded `iApproxTechCost`, `bValid` therefore remains
false and the target cannot become `eMinModTeam` at all.

This directly contradicts the source comment "don't set it true unless there are at
least 2 stealable techs." In the common one-rival/single-member shape, having multiple
stealable technologies is insufficient to satisfy the gate.

FAILURE B — UNRELATED ONE-TECH TARGETS COMBINE
----------------------------------------------
Now take two singleton rival teams A and B, each with exactly one stealable tech.

A is scanned first:

    iApproxTechCost = cost(A.tech)
    bValid = false

B is scanned next. Before B's first (and only) stealable tech is processed,
`iApproxTechCost` is still nonzero from A. Thus:

    bValid = true

and B is admitted as though B itself had at least two stealable technologies.
`iApproxTechCost` simultaneously becomes an average mixing A's tech cost with B's tech
cost.

So the same leak causes the opposite false positive: one tech on A plus one unrelated
tech on B satisfies a gate documented as requiring at least two stealable techs from
the candidate target.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE
----------------
When `bValid` is true, the candidate can set `eMinModTeam` based on its low espionage
cost modifier and is added to `potentialTechTargets`. After all rivals are scanned,
`eMinModTeam` drives `bCheapTechSteal`.

A cheap-tech-steal result is not cosmetic. Current K-Mod/AdvCiv/SAS logic then:

- adds `iApproxTechCost / 10` to that team's espionage target and to the global target
  rate;
- gives `eMinModTeam` a 50% spending-weight boost;
- halves other teams' weights (and can halve them again in the espionage-economy
  strategy when they are not in `potentialTechTargets`);
- skips the normal gold-based reduction of the target espionage rate;
- raises the espionage commerce cap by 50 percentage points; and
- disables the normal research-vs-espionage ratio brake while increasing the slider.

Thus Failure A can suppress an intended espionage-economy opportunity even when the
only rival has many technologies available to steal. Failure B can activate and focus
the same strategy on a rival with only one stealable technology, while using a cost
estimate partly inherited from a different rival.

The false-positive and false-negative are one root: per-target scan state was made
player-global within the function.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod 1.46 contains the same structure: `iApproxTechCost` is declared once before the
rival loop, the first stealable tech assigns `bValid = iApproxTechCost > 0`, updates the
same accumulator and immediately breaks. AdvCiv 1.14 retains it while adapting team
iteration and later targeting details; current SAS retains the root.

Civ4CE/BtS does not contain this K-Mod cheap-tech-steal targeting implementation, so the
root is inherited from K-Mod rather than vanilla BtS or SAS-local changes.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Separate PER-TARGET discovery state from any aggregate cost estimate. For each rival
member/team, scan enough technologies to count at least two genuinely stealable techs
and compute an estimate from that target only. For example:

    int iTargetStealable = 0;
    int iTargetApproxCost = 0;
    FOR_EACH_ENUM(Tech)
    {
        if (!canStealTech(kRivalMember.getID(), eLoopTech))
            continue;
        ... accumulate this target's cost ...
        if (++iTargetStealable >= 2)
            ... // target is valid; may stop once the intended sample is obtained
    }

If a team can have multiple members, avoid treating the same team technology as a new
independent stealable technology merely because another member is iterated; the gate is
about stealable technologies, not player entries.

Whichever target wins `iMinModifier` should carry its OWN approximate technology cost
alongside it (e.g. `iMinModApproxTechCost`) so the later `bCheapTechSteal` target-rate
boost cannot inherit costs from another rival.

===============================================================================
C031-WIP40 — F350 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F350 / provisional KI#673 — AI_doCounter decays cash-trade memory only while a
qualifying resource import is actively increasing Bonus-Trade attitude, so ordinary
gold-trade memory can remain permanent despite AdvCiv's explicit decay contract

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited AdvCiv `advc.036` control-flow bug retained by AdvCiv 1.14 and
current SAS. K-Mod/BtS keep the older non-decaying gold-traded state and therefore do
not contain AdvCiv's attempted decay implementation.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_doCounter` first updates the resource-trade attitude counter for each
known major rival. Current AdvCiv/SAS structure is:

    scaled rBonusVal = AI_bonusImportValue(ePlayer);
    int iBonusTrade = AI_getBonusTradeCounter(ePlayer);
    if (rBonusVal <= iBonusTrade / (fixp(1.2) * iAttitudeDiv))
    {
        AI_setBonusTradeCounter(... decay ...);
    }
    else
    {
        ... increase BonusTradeCounter ...

        // <advc.036>
        {
            int iOldGoldTraded = AI_getGoldTradedTo(ePlayer);
            int iNewGoldTraded = (rDecayFactor * iOldGoldTraded).floor();
            AI_changeGoldTradedTo(ePlayer, iNewGoldTraded - iOldGoldTraded);
        }
        // </advc.036>
    }

The cash-memory decay is therefore not a general per-turn decay. It runs only when the
resource-import value is high enough to enter the *increase* branch of the unrelated
Bonus-Trade attitude counter.

The simplest ordinary case demonstrates the defect immediately:

- AI A has previously paid player B a lump sum, so `AI_getGoldTradedTo(B) > 0`.
- B is not currently exporting any resource to A.
- `AI_bonusImportValue(B)` is therefore 0.
- With the normal nonnegative BonusTradeCounter, the `rBonusVal <= ...` condition is
  true.
- A's BonusTradeCounter may decay, but `AI_getGoldTradedTo(B)` is untouched.

The same happens whenever imported-resource utility is too small to outrun the current
BonusTrade counter. Cash memory therefore ages only as a side effect of sufficiently
valuable resource imports from that same player.

EXPLICIT DESIGN CONTRACT
------------------------
The AdvCiv manual's change-036 section states, independently of resource-attitude
memory:

    "AI memory about cash traded to other civs decays."

It then explains the exact reason:

    "The AI keeps track of how much gold it has traded to every other civ. That
    amount is subtracted from the cash that the AI is willing to trade to another
    civ. ... The amount of gold that a civ is willing to trade (prior to subtracting
    gold-traded memory) can stagnate, and then the BtS AI can stay unwilling to trade
    any gold indefinitely. Also, pretty much all other AI memory decays in AdvCiv."

So the present resource-dependent decay is not merely an alternative tuning policy; it
recreates exactly the indefinite-memory failure that `advc.036` says it is fixing.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE
----------------
`CvDeal::startTrade` increments the giver's `AI_changeGoldTradedTo(eToPlayer, gold)`
when lump-sum gold changes hands. `AI_maxGoldTrade` later computes the AI's current
cash budget and subtracts:

    iMaxGold -= AI_getGoldTradedTo(ePlayer);

before clamping the amount available for trade.

Therefore, for example, if A has previously traded 100 gold to B and A's pre-memory
cash budget later stabilizes around 100 gold or less, A can remain at zero available
cash toward B indefinitely so long as B does not provide a sufficiently valuable
resource import. No additional gold trade is needed to maintain the lockout; the
supposedly decaying memory itself is simply never visited.

An unrelated resource deal with B can suddenly start shrinking the old cash memory,
which also demonstrates the wrong dependency: B exporting a useful resource to A
changes how quickly A forgets an old lump-sum cash payment, although the manual defines
cash-trade memory and resource-trade appreciation as separate mechanisms.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod retains the BtS-style `m_aiGoldTradedTo` cap but contains no per-turn decay in
`AI_doCounter`. AdvCiv `advc.036` explicitly adds both the changed cash-trade budget and
the decay block. AdvCiv 1.14 already has the decay nested inside the Bonus-Trade
increase branch exactly as current SAS does.

Civ4CE/BtS contains neither AdvCiv's decay contract nor this attempted implementation.
Thus this is an AdvCiv-introduced control-flow bug, not a SAS-local regression.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Make cash-memory decay an unconditional per-rival `AI_doCounter` operation, independent
of resource-trade attitude state. For example, perform:

    int const iOldGoldTraded = AI_getGoldTradedTo(ePlayer);
    int const iNewGoldTraded = (rDecayFactor * iOldGoldTraded).floor();
    AI_changeGoldTradedTo(ePlayer, iNewGoldTraded - iOldGoldTraded);

once per eligible rival outside the `rBonusVal` if/else.

Prefer placing it before the BonusTradeAttitudeDivisor early `continue` as well. A
leader/personality with no Bonus-Trade attitude mechanism should not thereby disable
cash-memory decay; the manual describes the latter as a general cash-trade rule.

Do not tie the fix to whether there is a current resource deal, and do not reset the
memory abruptly: AdvCiv deliberately chose exponential diplomatic decay through
`rDecayFactor`.

------------------------------

C031-WIP41 — F351 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F351 / provisional KI#674 — AI_proposeWarTrade city-for-war fallback ignores a
failed AI_counterPropose result and unconditionally implements the original deal,
allowing a separately legal but AI-rejected/unbalanced city-for-war trade to execute

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — AdvCiv-introduced `advc.ctr` control-flow bug retained by AdvCiv 1.14 and
current SAS. The city-for-war fallback does not exist in K-Mod 1.46 or Civ4CE/BtS.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_proposeWarTrade` has an AdvCiv `advc.ctr` fallback for a sponsor that
has no suitable tech payment (or would otherwise need two techs). If the war is going
badly enough, it searches for a city to offer to an AI hireling in exchange for a
`TRADE_WAR` declaration.

After selecting the city, current AdvCiv/SAS does:

    CLinkList<TradeData> weGive;
    weGive.insertAtEnd(TradeData(TRADE_CITIES, pBestCity->getID()));
    CLinkList<TradeData> hirelingGives;
    hirelingGives.insertAtEnd(TradeData(TRADE_WAR, eBestTarget));
    AI_counterPropose(eHireling, hirelingGives, weGive, true, true);
    kGame.implementDeal(getID(), eHireling, weGive, hirelingGives);
    return;

The return value of `AI_counterPropose` is discarded.

That boolean is not advisory. The AI-initiated wrapper builds separate `ourCounter`
and `theirCounter` lists and concatenates them into the caller's original lists only
when the underlying balancing function returns true:

    if (AI_counterPropose(..., theirCounter, ourCounter, rLeniency))
    {
        kWeGive.concatenate(ourCounter);
        kTheyGive.concatenate(theirCounter);
        return true;
    }
    return false;

Thus, if balancing fails, `weGive` still contains only the selected city and
`hirelingGives` still contains only the declaration-of-war item. The caller then
implements precisely that rejected original package.

WHY AI_counterPropose CAN LEGITIMATELY FAIL HERE
------------------------------------------------
The selected city is not chosen by comparing its deal value with the hireling's war
price. The city search deliberately uses city keep/acquisition fitness and the
sponsor's war-success rating. This is useful for finding a strategically sensible city
to cede, but it does not establish trade-value balance.

The surrounding function separately computed the target war price for the ordinary
tech/gold path (`iBestTeamPrice`), but the city fallback does not require the chosen
city's value to approximate that price.

`AI_counterPropose` therefore has real work to do. It evaluates both sides, tries to
add balancing items and can return false when no acceptable package can be constructed.
For an AI-AI deal its final fairness checks require each side's received value to meet
that side's `AI_tradeAcceptabilityThreshold` fraction of what it gives. A large enough
mismatch — e.g. a roughly 5:1 value gap with no usable sweeteners — cleanly fails those
checks.

The wrapper does not partially mutate the original lists on such a failure: its extra
items are kept in separate local counter lists and only concatenated after success.

LIVE PRODUCER / CONSEQUENCE
---------------------------
This path has ordinary shipped producers:

- `AI_doDiplo` calls `AI_proposeWarTrade` for an AI sponsor and an eligible AI
  hireling while the sponsor is already at war.
- The city fallback is reached when there is no suitable tech to give, or when two
  techs would otherwise be needed, and the sponsor's war-success rating is poor enough.
- The selected city and requested `TRADE_WAR` item have already passed individual
  `canTradeItem(..., true)` / denial legality checks.

A clean supported example is therefore:

1. AI A is losing a war against T and asks AI H to join.
2. A has no suitable tradable techs and owns a city that the `advc.ctr` city-fitness
   test allows it to cede.
3. H's price for declaring war on T is far from the trade value of that city.
4. Neither side has legal/appropriate extra items sufficient to close the value gap.
5. `AI_counterPropose` returns false because it cannot construct a mutually acceptable
   AI-AI package.
6. `AI_proposeWarTrade` ignores false and calls `implementDeal` on the untouched
   city-for-war lists anyway.

Depending on the direction of the mismatch, H can be forced into a war for compensation
it would not accept, or A can give away a city for military help whose value does not
justify it. Both are manifestations of the same ignored balancing result.

NO DOWNSTREAM FAIRNESS SAFETY NET
---------------------------------
`CvGame::implementDeal` forwards directly to `implementAndReturnDeal`. The latter
creates a `CvDeal` and calls `CvDeal::addTradeItems(..., bCheckAllowed=true)`.

That final check verifies each item's `canTradeItem` legality. It does not rerun
`AI_counterPropose`, `AI_considerOffer` or the bilateral AI trade-value thresholds.
The city and war items were already selected as individually legal, so a failed
*package-balance* decision is not recovered at implementation time.

EXPLICIT ADVCIV DESIGN CONTRACT
-------------------------------
The AdvCiv manual's sponsored-war section explicitly describes the feature:

- when two AI civs negotiate a joint war, the civ already at war may offer a city in
  exchange for the declaration of war;
- the rationale is the possibility of a seemingly doomed AI bringing in a powerful
  neighbor by ceding a city;
- the manual's Tbd. note says such trades would work through the changes to
  `CvPlayerAI::AI_counterPropose` and suggests that function should be used for war
  trades.

The source comment around the `advc.ctr` fallback likewise says it considers giving a
city "instead (through AI_counterPropose)" and describes the deal as "city ceded in
exchange for help in a war."

So `AI_counterPropose` is the intended package-balancing contract here, not a best-effort
side calculation whose failure may be ignored.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod 1.46 and Civ4CE/BtS do not contain this `advc.ctr` city-for-war fallback or its
call to `AI_counterPropose`. AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same ignored-return sequence as
current SAS. This is therefore an AdvCiv-introduced control-flow defect, not a SAS-local
regression.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Honor the balancing result:

    if (AI_counterPropose(eHireling, hirelingGives, weGive, true, true))
    {
        kGame.implementDeal(getID(), eHireling, weGive, hirelingGives);
        return;
    }

If balancing fails, do not implement the original city-for-war package. The function
can fall through to its existing ordinary tech/gold logic (where applicable) or simply
abandon this proposal attempt. Do not try to duplicate the counterproposal fairness
logic locally; the whole purpose of `advc.ctr` is to delegate package construction to
`AI_counterPropose`.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
This is independent of the earlier `AI_proposeWarTrade` KI#372/F051 legacy
`iBestTeamPrice == -1` defect. KI#372 concerns the ordinary legacy target-selection
branch feeding a bad price into later tech/gold balancing. F351 occurs inside the
separate AdvCiv city fallback and remains possible with a fully correct positive war
price.

It is also independent of the previously rejected city-value orientation suspicion:
`kHireling.AI_cityTradeVal(*pCity, kHireling.getID())` is the correct acquiring-player
contract. F351 is about ignoring the package balancer's failure after a city has been
legitimately selected.

C031-WIP42 — F352 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F352 / provisional KI#675 — AI_bestRequestCity says liberation takes precedence but
its numeric-best comparison can let an earlier non-liberation city block every later
liberation city, making help/tribute city requests depend on city iteration order

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — AdvCiv-introduced `advc.ctr` selection-order bug retained by AdvCiv 1.14
and current SAS. The helper and city-request feature do not exist in K-Mod/BtS.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_bestRequestCity` explicitly establishes a two-level preference:

    bool bBestLiberate = false;
    ...
    bool bLiberate = (pCity->getLiberationPlayer() == getID());
    if (bBestLiberate && !bLiberate)
        continue; // Liberation takes precedence

After all eligibility/value checks, however, the actual replacement condition is only:

    int iValue = 3 * iOwnerValue - iOurValue;
    if (iValue < iBestValue &&
        kOwner.AI_cityTrade(*pCity, getID()) == NO_DENIAL)
    {
        iBestValue = iValue;
        pBestCity = pCity;
        bBestLiberate = bLiberate;
    }

That makes the supposed precedence one-sided:

- Once a liberation city has become `pBestCity`, later non-liberation cities are
  correctly skipped.
- But before that happens, an eligible non-liberation city may establish a low
  `iBestValue`.
- A later liberation city is then accepted only if its ordinary numeric score is even
  lower than that non-liberation score.

Therefore liberation does not take precedence; it takes precedence only if encountered
early enough or if it independently wins the secondary score.

ORDER-DEPENDENT REPRODUCTION
----------------------------
Nothing sorts `FOR_EACH_CITYAI(pCity, kOwner)` by liberation status. Ordinary city-list
order can therefore expose the defect.

For a help request (`rMinRatio = 5/3`), consider two separately legal human cities:

- N: non-liberation city, `iOurValue = 200`, `iOwnerValue = 100`.
  Ratio = 2, so it passes; score = `3*100 - 200 = 100`.
- L: liberation city, `iOurValue = 250`, `iOwnerValue = 150`.
  Ratio = 5/3, so it also passes; score = `3*150 - 250 = 200`.

If N is encountered first, it becomes best with score 100. When L is encountered,
`bBestLiberate` is still false, so the early precedence guard does not skip anything;
but `200 < 100` is false. L therefore cannot become best despite being a liberation
city.

If the same two cities are encountered in the opposite order, L becomes best first and
then N is skipped by `if (bBestLiberate && !bLiberate)`. The diplomatic request thus
changes merely with city iteration order.

The exact numbers are illustrative; the root only requires both cities to pass the
caller's value/ratio constraints while the liberation city's secondary score is not
lower than an earlier non-liberation candidate.

LIVE PRODUCERS / CONSEQUENCE
----------------------------
The helper has two current shipped diplomacy consumers:

1. `AI_askHelp(eHuman)` calls

       AI_bestRequestCity(eHuman, 1, 5/3)

   and may ask for the returned city instead of a technology.

2. `AI_demandTribute(eHuman, DEMAND_CITY)` calls

       AI_bestRequestCity(eHuman, rMinVal, 0.5)

   and places the returned city in the tribute demand.

So the bug is visible policy, not merely an internal ranking detail. The AI can ask a
human to hand over an unrelated non-liberation city even though an eligible city that
would be liberated to that AI is available and the source says liberation has
precedence. For tribute, this can make the demand unnecessarily intrusive; for help,
it directly undermines the intended liberation-oriented request behavior.

EXPLICIT DESIGN CONTRACT / ARCHAEOLOGY
--------------------------------------
The bug is present in the exact feature-introducing diff:

Practical commit 2075 / `3d9219cb2d...` (2020-03-29),
"AI asks for city as tribute/help; tweak city trade eval." [advc.ctr]

adds `AI_bestRequestCity` with the unchanged lines:

    if (bBestLiberate && !bLiberate)
        continue; // Liberation takes precedence

followed later by the plain `iValue < iBestValue` replacement condition. This is not a
later SAS refactor or a lost comment copied from unrelated code; the intended precedence
and the faulty comparator were introduced together.

The AdvCiv manual says that help requests may ask for cities that are significantly
more useful to the AI than to the human, and gives as part of the rationale:

    "To incentivize liberating AI cities"

It separately allows cities as tribute for variety and to give technologically lagging
players another way to avert war. Choosing a non-liberation city because it happened
to enter the list first is contrary to both the source's explicit precedence comment
and the liberation rationale.

AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the introduction logic. K-Mod 1.46 and Civ4CE/BtS
do not have `AI_bestRequestCity` or these AdvCiv city help/tribute requests.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Make the ranking lexicographic: liberation status first, then the existing `iValue`
score among candidates of equal liberation status.

For example, after the existing eligibility/denial checks, replacement can use the
conceptual condition:

    if ((!bBestLiberate && bLiberate) || iValue < iBestValue)

while retaining the earlier guard that skips non-liberation candidates once a
liberation best has been selected.

An even clearer formulation is to compare `(bLiberate, -iValue)` lexicographically or
write the two priority levels explicitly. The important part is that the *first*
eligible liberation candidate must be able to replace a non-liberation best regardless
of its secondary numeric score; subsequent liberation candidates can again use
`iValue` to choose the least painful/best request.

Do not simply sort the city list: iteration order is not the policy, and future callers
or city-list changes should not be able to alter liberation precedence.

CONTROL / ROOT SEPARATION
-------------------------
The earlier `AI_proposeResourceTrade` list-reuse/comment discrepancy remains a control,
not F352. Its failed first anchor can often be transformed by `AI_counterPropose` into a
valid resource-for-resource/GPT package, so no independent harmful consequence has yet
been established there.

F352 is also independent of F337's `AI_proposeCityTrade` leniency bug and F351's
city-for-war ignored-return bug. This root is confined to selecting which HUMAN-owned
city the AI asks for as help or tribute.

C031-WIP43 — F353 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F353 / provisional KI#676 — AI_eventValue values BonusRevealed through the unrelated
BonusType field, so the shipped "A Man Named Jed" Oil-reveal option receives zero
resource-reveal value and AI event choice can ignore the benefit it actually applies

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited BtS event-valuation field mix-up retained by Civ4CE/BtS,
K-Mod 1.46, AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS. Current shipped Event XML contains the exact
producer required for the defect.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_eventValue` computes one local bonus value only from the event's
ordinary plot-bonus field:

    int iBonusValue = 0;
    if (NO_BONUS != kEvent.getBonus())
        iBonusValue = AI_bonusVal((BonusTypes)kEvent.getBonus(), 0, true);

That value is then correctly reused for `getBonusChange`, because BonusChange changes
that same `BonusType` on the event plot.

Later, however, the separate reveal effect is evaluated with the same variable:

    if (kEvent.getBonusRevealed() != NO_BONUS)
        iValue += (iBonusValue * 10 * iGameSpeedPercent) / 100;

`BonusRevealed` is an independent EventInfo field. Nothing requires it to equal
`BonusType`, and the shipped data demonstrates that they are independent.

CURRENT-DATA PRODUCER — A MAN NAMED JED
---------------------------------------
Current SAS `CIV4EventTriggerInfos.xml` contains the active global trigger
`EVENTTRIGGER_MAN_NAMED_JED`:

- `iPercentGamesActive = 75`
- `iWeight = 5000`
- requires a Scout or Explorer on a plot with `BONUS_OIL`
- presents two choices, `EVENT_MAN_NAMED_JED_1` and `EVENT_MAN_NAMED_JED_2`

The second event is exactly the mismatched-field shape:

    <Type>EVENT_MAN_NAMED_JED_2</Type>
    <iGold>-10</iGold>
    ...
    <BonusType>NONE</BonusType>
    <iBonusChange>0</iBonusChange>
    ...
    <BonusRevealed>BONUS_OIL</BonusRevealed>
    ...
    <iAIValue>1000</iAIValue>

Thus `kEvent.getBonus() == NO_BONUS`, so `iBonusValue` remains 0. The later
`BonusRevealed` branch adds exactly zero for revealing Oil.

The first choice has no Oil reveal, no gold cost and the same `iAIValue = 1000`.
Consequently the intended differentiating benefit of option 2 is absent from AI
valuation; option 2 is instead slightly penalized by its 10-gold cost while both
choices retain their independent random AIValue component.

LIVE EFFECT / CONTRACT
----------------------
This is not dead XML and the reveal is not cosmetic.

`CvPlayer::canDoEvent` allows a BonusRevealed event only while the team lacks the
bonus's normal reveal technology and the bonus has not already been force-revealed.
For Oil in current SAS, `TechReveal = TECH_COMBUSTION`.

When the event is applied, `CvPlayer::applyEvent` executes:

    GET_TEAM(getTeam()).setForceRevealedBonus(
            (BonusTypes)kEvent.getBonusRevealed(), true);

So the selected option genuinely reveals Oil before Combustion.

Oil also has substantial current strategic use: current SAS has numerous Oil-requiring
units (Gunship, Tank, Modern Tank, Mobile SAM, Self-Propelled Artillery, Transport,
Destroyer, Battleship, Missile Cruiser, Attack Submarine, Carrier, Fighter, Jet
Fighter, Bomber and Stealth Bomber) and Oil-dependent building effects. The function's
own intended contract makes this even more direct: `AI_bonusVal(..., 0, true)` is the
resource-value routine that the surrounding event code uses for bonus creation/removal.
The omitted term is therefore not an abstract UI preference; it is the exact resource
value the source intended to add for early knowledge of Oil.

`AI_chooseEvent` loops every legal choice and chooses the largest `AI_eventValue`, so
the missing reveal value directly affects which event option an AI selects.

ANCESTRY
--------
The same field coupling is present throughout all supplied lineages:

- Civ4CE/BtS initializes `iBonusValue` from `kEvent.getBonus()` and later uses it for
  `getBonusRevealed()`.
- K-Mod retains the structure (changing the bonus-value call to its newer signature).
- AdvCiv 1.14 retains the K-Mod structure.
- Current SAS retains the same coupling.

The shipped `EVENT_MAN_NAMED_JED_2` producer is likewise present in Civ4CE/BtS,
K-Mod, AdvCiv and current SAS with `BonusType=NONE` / `BonusRevealed=BONUS_OIL`.
This is therefore a stock BtS inherited root, not a SAS regression.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
For "A Man Named Jed," the AI can fail to prefer paying 10 gold to reveal Oil early
because the Oil knowledge itself contributes zero to the choice score. More generally,
any EventInfo whose `BonusRevealed` differs from `BonusType` is evaluated using the
wrong resource; if `BonusType` is NONE the reveal is worth zero, and if the two fields
name different bonuses then the reveal is valued as the wrong bonus entirely.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Value the reveal field independently, e.g. conceptually:

    if (kEvent.getBonusRevealed() != NO_BONUS)
    {
        int iRevealedBonusValue = AI_bonusVal(
                (BonusTypes)kEvent.getBonusRevealed(), 0, true);
        iValue += (iRevealedBonusValue * 10 * iGameSpeedPercent) / 100;
    }

Keep the existing `iBonusValue` based on `kEvent.getBonus()` for `BonusChange`; those
are separate EventInfo effects and should not share identity state.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
The earlier album control on `AI_eventValue` recursion is unrelated: the current event
graph has no non-self recursion cycle. F353 is a direct field-identity bug on a shipped
choice.

KI#46 (deliberately unsupported old-save compatibility) is also unrelated. That was
checked immediately before entering the event block and remains an intentional project
policy, not a numbered root.

C031-WIP44 — F354 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F354 / provisional KI#677 — non-city EventInfo building yield/commerce changes are
collected by AI_eventValue but never consumed, so shipped multi-choice events can make
permanent building bonuses while the AI chooses as though those bonuses did not exist

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited BtS event-valuation omission retained by Civ4CE/BtS, K-Mod,
AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS. Multiple current multi-choice EventInfos exercise the
omitted path; `EVENTTRIGGER_TOO_CLOSE_TO_CALL` gives a particularly clean reproduction.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_eventValue` first aggregates every EventInfo building yield and commerce
change:

    FOR_EACH_NON_DEFAULT_PAIR(kEvent.getBuildingYieldChange(), ...)
        aiYields.add(...);

    FOR_EACH_NON_DEFAULT_PAIR(kEvent.getBuildingCommerceChange(), ...)
        aiCommerces.add(...);

For `kEvent.isCityEffect()`, those accumulators are then valued through
`iCityTurnValue`.

But the non-city branch only consumes happiness/health and the generic event fields:

    else if (!kEvent.isOtherPlayerCityEffect())
    {
        int iPerTurnValue = 0;
        iPerTurnValue += iNumCities * ((iHappy * 4) + ...);
        iPerTurnValue += iNumCities * ((iHealth * 3) + ...);
        ...
    }

There is no use of `aiYields` or `aiCommerces` in this branch. Therefore every
non-city building-specific yield or commerce effect contributes exactly zero to the AI
score despite the code having just parsed it.

CURRENT-DATA REPRODUCTION — TOO CLOSE TO CALL
---------------------------------------------
`EVENTTRIGGER_TOO_CLOSE_TO_CALL` is an active two-choice random event. Both choices are
non-city effects (`bPickCity=0`, `bPickOtherPlayerCity=0`) and both have
`iAIValue=1000` with no gold, tech, population, diplomacy or other differentiating
field.

Choice 1 contains only this material effect:

    BUILDINGCLASS_COURTHOUSE
    COMMERCE_GOLD +1

Choice 2 contains only this material effect:

    BUILDINGCLASS_COURTHOUSE
    COMMERCE_CULTURE +3

Because neither event is a city effect, `AI_eventValue` stores those values in
`aiCommerces` and then never reads them. The two options therefore reach the final
random multiplier with the same base valuation. The AI chooses between a permanent
+1-gold-per-Courthouse effect and a permanent +3-culture-per-Courthouse effect solely
through the generic random `iAIValue` noise rather than its economic/cultural needs or
the number of affected Courthouses.

LIVE EFFECT / PRODUCER
----------------------
`CvPlayer::applyEvent` confirms that these XML fields are real gameplay state. For
non-city events it iterates every current city and executes:

    pLoopCity->changeBuildingCommerceChange(
            perBuildingClassVal.first,
            perCommerceVal.first,
            perCommerceVal.second);

The analogous building-yield path calls `changeBuildingYieldChange` for every current
city. Building-specific happiness and health are also applied through dedicated
player modifiers.

Thus the valuation omission is not compensated at application time. The event really
changes Courthouse output while the AI selection logic assigns that output zero value.

The defect is broader than this one trigger. Current SAS has numerous multi-choice
non-city events with `BuildingExtraYields` or `BuildingExtraCommerces`, including
Horse Whispering completion, Harbormaster completion, Best Defense completion,
Sports League completion, Crisis in the Senate, Warships completion, Overwhelm,
Civ Game, Better Coal, Rogue Station and others. F354 is the shared valuation root;
those are downstream producers rather than separate findings.

ANCESTRY
--------
Civ4CE/BtS already has the same structure: building yield/commerce arrays are summed
before the city/non-city split and used only by the city-effect calculation. K-Mod
retains it (with revised specialist/commerce weights), AdvCiv retains it while
refactoring the containers to EnumMaps, and current SAS retains that logic.

This is therefore an inherited stock BtS omission, not a SAS regression.

CONTROL — SPACE PRODUCTION MODIFIER
-----------------------------------
The adjacent block contains another clear source-level field mistake:

    if (kEvent.getSpaceProductionModifier() != 0)
        iValue += ((20 + iNumCities) * getSpaceProductionModifier() * ...) / 100;

It tests the EventInfo modifier but values the player's *current* modifier instead of
`kEvent.getSpaceProductionModifier()`. The only current producer is
`EVENT_COMET_FRAGMENT_1` (`iSpaceProductionMod=5`). However that trigger has only one
choice and no other EventInfo references Comet Fragment through Additional/Clear event
valuation. Therefore the wrong number cannot alter current AI choice behavior and is
kept as dormant valuation debt rather than receiving its own finding number.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
The AI can choose materially inferior random-event rewards because permanent
building-class yield/commerce bonuses are invisible to `AI_chooseEvent` whenever the
EventInfo is non-city. In the clean Too Close to Call pair, the source supplies no
other deterministic distinction, so the omitted field is exactly what the AI should
be comparing.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Value non-city building yield/commerce effects in the non-city branch instead of
throwing away the already-collected accumulators.

A robust repair should preserve building-class identity rather than only summing by
Yield/Commerce, because the number of affected/owned buildings matters. At minimum,
for each BuildingClass change, map the class to this civilization's BuildingType and
weight the permanent yield/commerce effect by the cities/buildings to which it can
actually apply. Current buildings are the safest baseline; a modest future-building
allowance can be considered separately if desired because `applyEvent` stores the
change on every current city.

Do not simply multiply the aggregated `aiCommerces` by `iNumCities`: that would value a
Courthouse bonus as though every city necessarily had a Courthouse and would preserve
the existing loss of BuildingClass identity.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
F353 concerns `BonusRevealed` reading the wrong resource field. F354 is independent:
it concerns building yield/commerce data that is parsed correctly but dropped by the
non-city valuation branch.

KI#206 (already repaired in current SAS) concerns the missing `/100` after
ConstructPercent when valuing direct `BuildingChange`; it does not cover
`BuildingExtraYield` / `BuildingExtraCommerce`.
