C031-WIP59 — F369 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F369 / provisional KI#692 — advc.079 stores one randomized "best attack unit" as the
last unit bragged about, but the diplomacy text independently reruns the randomized
selection when expanding [OUR_BEST_UNIT], so the remembered unit and the unit actually
shown to the player can differ

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — AdvCiv regression introduced by practical commit 1439
`65a1472094e89d913ccf565c76687027a530a30d` ("Changes to AI greetings"). The underlying
`getBestAttackUnitKey` / asynchronous unit-selection randomness is inherited from BtS /
K-Mod; advc.079 newly made the selected UnitType persistent state without carrying that
same selection into text rendering.

ROOT
----
The advc.079 greeting code now asks for a candidate and stores it:

    UnitTypes eBragUnit = AI_getBestAttackUnit();
    ...
    if (eBragUnit != m_aeLastBrag[ePlayer])
    {
        m_aeLastBrag[ePlayer] = eBragUnit;
        return GC.getAIDiploCommentType("UNIT_BRAG");
    }

But none of the returned diplomacy state carries `eBragUnit`. The selected XML text
contains `[OUR_BEST_UNIT]`, e.g.:

    Our numberless [OUR_BEST_UNIT] shall crush ...

and `CvDllTranslator::replaceOur` resolves that token later by calling:

    kPlayer.getBestAttackUnitName(iForm)
      -> getBestAttackUnitKey()
      -> AI().AI_getBestAttackUnit()

This is a fresh, independent second evaluation.

The evaluation is intentionally asynchronous/randomized. `AI_getBestAttackUnit` calls
`CvCityAI::AI_bestUnitAI(UNITAI_ATTACK, true)`, and `AI_bestUnitAI` multiplies every
surviving candidate by an independent asynchronous random factor:

    if (bAsync)
    {
        iValue *= (GC.getASyncRand().get(50, "AI Best Unit ASYNC") + 100);
        iValue /= 100;
    }

Thus there is no invariant that the second text-rendering call returns the UnitType
stored by the first greeting-selection call.

CURRENT-DATA REACHABILITY
-------------------------
Current SAS has many simultaneously trainable `UNITAI_ATTACK` alternatives. A simple
early example is Axeman (strength 5) and Swordsman (strength 6) when the civ has both
required resources/technologies. Before the async multiplier, candidates below 2/3 of
the best are discarded, so these close alternatives both survive. A 100..149% random
multiplier is then easily large enough to reverse their ordering between two calls.

The same structural possibility occurs throughout the unit tree; this does not depend
on a scenario-only unit.

LIVE CONSEQUENCES
-----------------
1. The player can literally be shown a different unit from the one that advc.079 records
   as having just been bragged about.

   Example shape:

       greeting-selection call -> Axeman
       m_aeLastBrag[human] = Axeman
       text-rendering call      -> Swordsman
       visible line says        -> Swordsman

2. On the next contact, another randomized selection can return Swordsman. The new
   advc.079 test then sees:

       Swordsman != m_aeLastBrag[human] (Axeman)

   and treats this as a "new best unit", immediately producing another brag despite no
   technology, resource or trainability change at all.

3. Conversely, a real change in the best-unit set can be hidden or delayed if the
   randomized identity happens to equal the stored previous candidate.

This directly defeats the introducing commit's stated purpose: "When a braggart AI has
a new best unit, it brags about that unit at the first opportunity" and the memory is
supposed to reduce repeated greetings rather than create them from renderer randomness.

ANCESTRY / ROOT SEPARATION
--------------------------
BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod already use the capital-first `AI_bestUnitAI(UNITAI_ATTACK, true)`
logic for the `[OUR_BEST_UNIT]` text. That can make the phrase "best" somewhat noisy,
but there is no persistent `last brag` identity to contradict.

advc.079 refactored that old computation into `AI_getBestAttackUnit`, added
`m_aeLastBrag`, and calls the helper while deciding whether a unit is new. The existing
text token remained dynamic and calls the same helper again. F369 is therefore the new
state/display mismatch created when a randomized display helper was reused as stable
memory identity.

This finding does NOT currently promote the separate inherited question that
`AI_getBestAttackUnit` returns the first capital-trainable attacker rather than searching
for a global maximum. That may make the textual notion of "best" inaccurate in some
city-local prerequisite states, but it is a separate contract and remains unnumbered.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Do not rerun a randomized selector when expanding the brag that has just been chosen.
Preserve the exact `eBragUnit` for the active greeting and feed that UnitType to the
rendered line, or otherwise make the identity used by `m_aeLastBrag` and
`[OUR_BEST_UNIT]` come from one evaluation.

A second possible cleanup would make the selector deterministic when used as persistent
identity, but that is broader: BtS deliberately used asynchronous selection for this
UI-facing helper. The minimal advc.079 repair is simply to keep selection and display
atomic.

CONTROLS CLOSED BEFORE F369
---------------------------
- Sibling-vassal Privateer targeting is deliberate. AdvCiv's manual explicitly says
  that the vassal/master Privateer restrictions do not apply to vassals of the same
  master.
- `AI_isUnitNeedingOpenBorders` may inspect the group's head unit for domain, but
  `CvUnit::canJoinGroup` enforces a single domain for all units in a selection group;
  there is no mixed-domain producer.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F370 / provisional KI#693 — Advanced Start city setup counts a failed
improvement purchase as successful, then can buy population against phantom
improved plots
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_advancedStartPlaceCity` chooses the plot with the highest
`AI_getBestBuildValue`, calls the void Advanced Start action, and then increments
`iPlotsImproved` unconditionally:

    doAdvancedStartAction(ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_IMPROVEMENT,
            pBestPlot->getX(), pBestPlot->getY(), eBestImprovement, true);
    iPlotsImproved++;

There is no Advanced Start affordability check in the candidate loop and no
post-action verification that `pBestPlot` actually received `eBestImprovement`.

`CvPlayer::doAdvancedStartAction`, however, explicitly permits the action to fail
silently. For `ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_IMPROVEMENT` it computes
`getAdvancedStartImprovementCost`; if the action is legal but the player lacks
that many points, the function simply leaves the plot unchanged and returns to
the caller. Its return type is `void`, so success is not communicated.

The local counter therefore changes even when the game state does not.

SUPPORTED PRODUCER
------------------
This is reachable through ordinary AI Advanced Start. `AI_doAdvancedStart`
checks whether it can afford the city itself before calling
`AI_advancedStartPlaceCity`, but it does not reserve enough points for that
helper's preferred culture/improvements/population package. Later cities in the
city-budget loop can therefore enter the helper with only a small remainder.

Current SAS data makes an affordability split easy to construct. For example:

* `IMPROVEMENT_FARM` has `iAdvancedStartCost = 30`;
* SAS `ADVANCED_START_WORKER_BUILD_MODIFIER = 67`, so the base Farm portion is
  about 20 points at Normal build speed;
* removing `FEATURE_JUNGLE` adds its current Advanced Start removal cost of 40,
  making that Farm roughly 60 points before other speed adjustment;
* population is bought through the independent Advanced Start population-cost
  formula (BtS default `ADVANCED_START_POPULATION_COST = 150`). On ordinary
  Normal-speed/100%-growth settings, population 1 has a growth threshold of
  `20 + 2 = 22`, hence the next population point costs about 33.

A late Advanced Start city with, for example, a remainder between those costs
can therefore afford population but not the AI's highest-valued Jungle Farm.
The exact numeric remainder is not an exotic API state: `AI_doAdvancedStart`
spends the common point pool incrementally on cities, techs, visibility and the
city helper's own actions.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
Suppose the city has no improved plots and the Jungle Farm is its current
highest `AI_getBestBuildValue` target, but the remaining points are below that
Farm's Advanced Start cost.

1. The improvement action is attempted and silently fails.
2. `iPlotsImproved` nevertheless rises from 0 to 1.
3. On the next pass the same still-unimproved high-value plot remains the best
   target. The action can fail again and `iPlotsImproved` rises again.
4. Once the phantom count exceeds city population, the helper's final loop uses
   the real city plot and can spend any still-affordable points on population:

       while (iPlotsImproved > pCity->getPopulation())
       {
           int iPopCost = getAdvancedStartPopCost(true, pCity);
           ...
           doAdvancedStartAction(ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_POP,
                   pPlot->getX(), pPlot->getY(), -1, true);
       }

The AI can therefore grow a city because of improvements that do not exist.
Because candidate selection is based on build value rather than purchasability,
it can also keep retrying the same unaffordable high-value improvement while a
cheaper lower-valued improvement could actually have been bought with the
remaining points.

This is a genuine execution-state mismatch, not merely a subjective Advanced
Start allocation heuristic: the loop variable is explicitly named/counting
`iPlotsImproved`, and the runtime plot remains unimproved.

ANCESTRY
--------
The same unconditional post-action `iPlotsImproved++` structure is present in
BtS/Civ4CE, K-Mod, Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS. AdvCiv modernized iterators
and Advanced Start costs but preserved this state assumption. Classification:
inherited BtS Advanced Start execution-vs-assumed-success defect.

No existing current KI/F321-F369 root found for this behavior. Earlier Advanced
Start album items concern tech-refund reachability/cache effects, first-city
callbacks, or F366's forced land `UNITAI_EXPLORE` assignment; none owns failed
improvement purchases being counted as successful.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The stronger repair is to make the candidate/action state coherent rather than
merely patch the later population loop:

* before selecting/attempting an improvement, require
  `getAdvancedStartImprovementCost(eImprovement, true, pLoopPlot)` to be
  nonnegative and no greater than the current Advanced Start points; and/or
* after the action, increment `iPlotsImproved` only if the plot now actually has
  `eBestImprovement`.

Skipping unaffordable candidates is preferable because it lets the AI consider
a cheaper second-best improvement instead of repeatedly retrying an action that
cannot execute. A post-action verification remains useful defensive hardening
because `doAdvancedStartAction` is void and can reject actions for other
legality/state reasons.

CONTROL NOTE
------------
The immediate population action inside the improvement loop uses the improved
plot coordinates rather than the city plot, so it is normally a no-op when that
plot is not itself a city. The later `while (iPlotsImproved > population)` loop
uses the city plot correctly. That oddity does not rescue F370; it makes the
phantom count survive until the later real population-purchase loop.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F371 / provisional KI#694 — Advanced Start building phase treats one
unaffordable selected building as a global "done" state, so it can terminate
before later passes expose cheaper affordable buildings
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_doAdvancedStart` uses `bDoneBuildings` both as the outer-loop
termination condition and as a per-city affordability result:

    bool bDoneBuildings =
            (iLastPointsTotal - getAdvancedStartPoints() > iCityPoints);

    for (int iPass = 0; iPass < 10 && !bDoneBuildings; ++iPass)
    {
        FOR_EACH_CITYAI(pLoopCity, *this)
        {
            BuildingTypes const eBuilding =
                    pLoopCity->AI_bestAdvancedStartBuilding(iPass);
            if (eBuilding != NO_BUILDING)
            {
                bDoneBuildings = (iCityPoints < iLastPointsTotal -
                        (getAdvancedStartPoints() -
                        getAdvancedStartBuildingCost(
                                eBuilding, true, pLoopCity)));

                if (!bDoneBuildings)
                {
                    doAdvancedStartAction(
                            ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_BUILDING,
                            pLoopCity->getX(), pLoopCity->getY(),
                            eBuilding, true);
                }
                else
                {
                    //continue. there might be cheaper buildings
                    //in other cities we can afford
                }
            }
        }
    }

The condition itself is a valid projected-budget test for that particular
building. The defect is storing the result in the global phase-termination
flag.

`CvCityAI::AI_bestAdvancedStartBuilding(iPass)` deliberately changes what it is
willing to select across passes:

    pass 0: FOOD
    pass 1: + PRODUCTION
    pass 2: + EXPERIENCE
    pass 3: + HAPPY | HEALTHY
    pass 4+: + GOLD | RESEARCH | MAINTENANCE | (normally) ESPIONAGE

The threshold also falls from 20 to 0 across passes.

Therefore, "the selected building for this city on this pass exceeds the
remaining city budget" does not imply "no later-pass building is affordable."
Yet if that unaffordable candidate leaves `bDoneBuildings == true` at the end
of the city traversal, the outer loop terminates and those later selector
passes are never run.

The source comment already acknowledges the missing implication -- "there
might be cheaper buildings ... we can afford" -- but only continues the
current city traversal. It does not protect the next `iPass`.

SUPPORTED CURRENT-DATA SHAPE
----------------------------
Current SAS has an ordinary generic cost/focus split that demonstrates the
problem without relying on a mod-mod edge case:

* `BUILDING_COLOSSEUM`
  - production cost 90
  - Advanced Start cost percent 100
  - +1 happiness
  - prerequisite `TECH_CONSTRUCTION`

* `BUILDING_LIBRARY`
  - production cost 80
  - Advanced Start cost percent 100
  - +25% research
  - prerequisite `TECH_WRITING`
  - not a free start-era building until the Renaissance

`CvPlayer::getAdvancedStartBuildingCost` starts from production cost times the
building's Advanced Start percent and then applies AdvCiv's 1.5 multiplier.
On Normal speed, absent a city-specific production modifier, these are about:

    Colosseum: 90 * 1.5 = 135 points
    Library:   80 * 1.5 = 120 points

A pre-Renaissance Advanced Start city that knows both prerequisite techs and
currently values happiness can therefore reach the building phase with a
remaining city-budget allowance between 120 and 134 points.

On pass 3, the happiness/health focus can select the Colosseum. Its projected
135-point purchase exceeds the remaining city budget, so the code assigns
`bDoneBuildings = true` and does not buy it.

Pass 4 is exactly where RESEARCH is added to the selector. A 120-point Library
could be legal and affordable there, but pass 4 never executes because the
outer loop sees the `true` value left by the unaffordable pass-3 candidate.

The exact remainder does not require a special API state. `AI_doAdvancedStart`
uses one shared point pool and reaches the building phase only after incremental
spending on cities, improvements/population, visibility, technology, explorers
and routes. The city-budget remainder is not constrained to building-cost
multiples.

MULTI-CITY ORDER DEPENDENCE
---------------------------
The same variable is overwritten for every city that returns a building
candidate:

    bDoneBuildings = projectedPurchaseExceedsBudget;

Consequently, in a multi-city empire the decision to run the next building
pass can depend on which candidate-bearing city happens to be visited last.

For example, on the same pass:

* City A's selected building is affordable -> `bDoneBuildings = false`;
* City B's selected building is unaffordable -> `bDoneBuildings = true`.

If B is the last relevant city, the whole building phase stops after the pass.
If a later city instead has an affordable candidate, that later assignment can
reset the flag to false and the next pass runs.

Thus the flag is neither a monotonic "budget exhausted" state nor an
all-cities affordability result. It is effectively the affordability result of
the last candidate that happened to overwrite it.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
The AI can leave Advanced Start points unspent on useful buildings even though
a later focus pass would identify an affordable legal building.

This is not merely a disagreement with building valuation. The ten-pass design
explicitly broadens the candidate set over time; F371 can prevent those
designed passes from executing at all based on the cost of one earlier selected
candidate.

The effect is strongest near the end of the city/economic budget, where an
expensive happiness/health building can block a cheaper research, maintenance
or espionage building that only becomes eligible on the next pass.

ANCESTRY
--------
The same `bDoneBuildings` structure and the same explanatory comment are present
in BtS/Civ4CE, K-Mod, Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS. AdvCiv reformatted the
condition but preserved the control flow.

Classification: inherited BtS Advanced Start budget/control-flow defect.

This is independent of F370. F370 is an execution-state mismatch inside
`AI_advancedStartPlaceCity` where a failed improvement purchase increments
`iPlotsImproved`. F371 is a separate building-phase termination error even when
every attempted building action succeeds exactly as requested.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Do not use one candidate's affordability as the global outer-loop done flag.

A conservative repair is:

1. Keep the initial "city budget already exhausted" test if desired.
2. For each selected building, compute the projected city-budget spending.
3. If that particular building would exceed the budget, `continue` to the next
   city/candidate instead of setting a persistent phase-done state.
4. Allow the bounded later passes to run so that their broader focus flags can
   expose cheaper alternatives.

For example, conceptually:

    if (projectedCitySpending > iCityPoints)
        continue;

    doAdvancedStartAction(...);

Because the loop already has a hard ten-pass bound, no global "one selected
building was too expensive" flag is needed to prevent an infinite loop.

A stronger cleanup could track whether any building was purchased in a pass,
but "nothing was bought on pass N" still should not automatically terminate
before pass N+1 while the selector is intentionally gaining new focus flags.
Any early-exit optimization therefore needs a real proof that no later pass can
introduce a new affordable candidate.

CONTROLS CLOSED DURING THIS SLICE
---------------------------------
* The other void Advanced Start actions do not all share F370's false-state
  consequence. In particular, the final tech loop and the building action's
  projected-budget inequality imply affordability before execution; the
  earlier/interleaved tech attempts can fail when the common point pool is
  depleted, but the local variables changed afterward are allocation
  heuristics rather than a false representation of purchased game state. No
  independent F372 was assigned there in this slice.

* `AI_bestAreaUnitAIValue` does select only one representative city for a
  non-null area and can therefore miss a unit with a city-local prerequisite
  that is trainable elsewhere in the same area. Current SAS has Factory-gated
  Tanks that make the general hazard real, but the area-scoped sea/air cleanup
  consumers do not currently intersect such a local prerequisite. The only
  current-data intersection established here is K-Mod's gifted combat-unit
  valuation. That remains an inherited approximation / mod-mod hazard, not a
  numbered root at this checkpoint.

* `AI_getRankDifferenceAttitude`'s `iMajorCivsAlive - 1` denominator is protected
  on its live cached-attitude path: `AI_updateAttitude` asserts both participants
  are major civs and requires both to be alive before the rank helper is
  reached. No zero-divisor producer was established.

STATUS

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F372 / provisional KI#695 — AdvCiv made BtS's unused Advanced Start `bDone`
flag terminate the entire unit-buying phase when one selected unit is
unaffordable, even though the next role/pass can contain a cheaper affordable
unit
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
The Advanced Start unit phase cycles through four roles:

    CITY_DEFENSE
    WORKER
    RESERVE
    COUNTER

and, for each pass/city, asks `AI_bestAdvancedStartUnitAI` for the preferred
unit of that role.

BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod contain this affordability branch:

    bool bDone = false;
    for (int iPass = 0; iPass < 10; ++iPass)
    {
        ...
        if (getAdvancedStartUnitCost(eBestUnit, true, pUnitPlot) >
            getAdvancedStartPoints())
        {
            bDone = true;
            break;
        }
        ...
    }

`bDone` is written but never read. Therefore an unaffordable selected unit
breaks the current city traversal, but the outer loop continues to the next
`iPass` and thus to the next UnitAI role.

AdvCiv changed the outer loop to:

    for (int iPass = 0; iPass < 10 &&
        !bDone; // advc.001: bDone was never read. This is probably its intended use.
        iPass++)

Current SAS inherits that change unchanged.

This converts a dead/unused flag into a global phase-termination condition.
The implicit assertion is now:

    selected unit for current role is unaffordable
        =>
    no useful unit in any later role/pass is affordable

That implication is false.

CURRENT-SAS COUNTEREXAMPLE
--------------------------
The current unit data gives a simple one-city, generic-civilization example.

`UNIT_WORKER`:
* production cost 60
* Advanced Start cost percent 100
* no tech prerequisite
* no obsolete tech
* supports `UNITAI_WORKER`

The generic city-defense chain includes:

`UNIT_ARCHER`
* production cost 25
* obsolete at Construction

`UNIT_LONGBOWMAN`
* production cost 40
* obsolete at Firearms

`UNIT_MUSKETMAN`
* production cost 100
* prerequisite Firearms
* obsolete at Military Tradition
* explicitly supports `UNITAI_CITY_DEFENSE`

`UNIT_RIFLEMAN`
* production cost 120
* prerequisite Military Tradition (+ Firearms)
* obsolete at Fascism
* explicitly supports `UNITAI_CITY_DEFENSE`

`getAdvancedStartUnitCost` begins from `getProductionNeeded(eUnit)` multiplied
by 3 * AdvancedStartCost / 200, i.e. a 1.5 multiplier for the ordinary
100-percent units, then applies the same game-speed point normalization (plus
any applicable production modifier).

Consequently, in an otherwise ordinary Firearms / pre-Military-Tradition
state without a special unit-production modifier:

    Musketman nominal AS cost ~= 150 points
    Worker nominal AS cost     ~=  90 points

The exact absolute values scale with game/start speed, but the generic
Musketman remains substantially more expensive than the Worker.

The point pool reaches the unit phase only after many incremental Advanced
Start purchases (cities, improvements/population, visibility, technology,
explorers, routes, buildings), so a remainder in the interval where the Worker
is affordable but the Musketman is not is entirely ordinary.

At Firearms, the earlier Archer/Longbow city defenders are obsolete. Therefore
for a generic civilization `AI_bestAdvancedStartUnitAI(...,
UNITAI_CITY_DEFENSE)` can select the Musketman on pass 0.

With, for example, enough points for a Worker but not for that Musketman:

1. pass 0 selects the Musketman;
2. the cost test sees `Musketman cost > remaining points`;
3. `bDone = true`;
4. the city loop breaks;
5. AdvCiv's added `!bDone` prevents pass 1 from running;
6. `UNITAI_WORKER` is never considered despite an affordable Worker.

The same class of failure exists in later eras (e.g. Rifleman vs Worker), and
city-local production modifiers can add further city-order cases because
`getAdvancedStartUnitCost(..., &kCityPlot)` explicitly applies the city's unit
production modifier.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
AdvCiv/SAS can prematurely stop the Advanced Start military/worker purchase
phase and leave points that could still buy a useful unit.

This is stronger than merely choosing the wrong military unit: the code's
four-role round-robin is explicitly designed to move from CITY_DEFENSE to
WORKER/RESERVE/COUNTER, but the AdvCiv outer-loop change can prevent those roles
from being reached at all.

ANCESTRY
--------
* BtS/Civ4CE: `bDone` is assigned but never used by the outer loop.
* K-Mod 1.46: same as BtS.
* Base AdvCiv 1.14: adds `&& !bDone` and the comment
  `"bDone was never read. This is probably its intended use."`
* Current AdvCiv-SAS: inherits the AdvCiv behavior.

Classification: AdvCiv regression / speculative cleanup of dead BtS state that
made behavior strictly less robust.

This is related in pattern to F371 but is an independent code root and ancestry:
F371 is the inherited building-pass flag being overwritten by one building's
affordability. F372 is AdvCiv newly making BtS's formerly-unused unit flag
terminate all later role passes.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The safest minimal repair is to remove `!bDone` from the outer loop, restoring
the BtS/K-Mod behavior, and preferably remove/rename the dead flag as part of
the cleanup:

    for (int iPass = 0; iPass < 10; iPass++)
    {
        ...
        if (selectedCost > getAdvancedStartPoints())
            break; // only stop this city's/current pass traversal
    }

An even better policy would skip only the unaffordable candidate/city and keep
examining other cities on the same pass, because city-local production
modifiers can make another city's candidate cheaper.

If global early termination is desired for performance, it needs a real
"nothing remaining can be afforded" proof, e.g. the minimum legal cost across
the remaining roles/cities, not the cost of one selected candidate.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F373 / provisional KI#696 — SAS Culture competing-victory gate can never see
the CURRENT Diplomacy victory stage during the normal victory-hash update
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
Current SAS added a Culture-stage behavior gate intended to postpone expensive
Culture 2 investment when another victory route is already advanced:

    static int const iMinCompetingVictoryStage =
            range(GC.getDefineINT(
                "SAS_AI_CULTURE_VICTORY_COMPETING_VICTORY_MIN_STAGE"),
                0, 4);

    if (!isHuman() && iMinCompetingVictoryStage > 0 &&
        iHighCultureCount < iVictoryCities)
    {
        AIVictoryStage const eVictoryStageHash = AI_getVictoryStageHash();
        int const iSpaceStage = ...
        int const iConquestStage = ...
        int const iDominationStage = ...
        int const iDiplomacyStage =
                getSASDiplomacyVictoryStageLevel(eVictoryStageHash);

        int const iMostAdvancedCompetingStage =
                max(space, conquest, domination, diplomacy);

        if (iMostAdvancedCompetingStage >= iMinCompetingVictoryStage)
            return 1;
    }

The XML contract explicitly describes the default stage-3 gate as preventing an
unready Culture 2 hedge from diverting resources from an advanced:

    "Space, Conquest, Domination, or Diplomatic pursuit"

However, normal cached victory-stage construction is ordered as follows in
`CvPlayerAI::AI_updateVictoryStageHash`:

    m_eVictoryStageHash = AI_DEFAULT_VICTORY_STAGE;

    AI_calculateSpaceVictoryStage();
        -> add SPACE bits

    AI_calculateConquestVictoryStage();
        -> add CONQUEST bits

    AI_calculateDominationVictoryStage();
        -> add DOMINATION bits

    AI_calculateCultureVictoryStage();
        -> Culture reads AI_getVictoryStageHash()

    AI_calculateDiplomacyVictoryStage();
        -> only now add DIPLOMACY bits

The source even retains K-Mod's order comment immediately before Culture:

    "AI_calculateCultureVictoryStage now checks
     some of the other victory strategies,
     so it is important that they are set first."

SAS expanded the set of strategies Culture checks to include Diplomacy without
moving Diplomacy before Culture.

WHY NO CACHE/LATE-EVALUATION ESCAPE EXISTS
------------------------------------------
`CvPlayerAI.h` defines:

    AIVictoryStage AI_getVictoryStageHash() const
    {
        return m_eVictoryStageHash;
    }

It is not a lazy getter and performs no recomputation.

`AI_updateVictoryStageHash` resets `m_eVictoryStageHash` to
`AI_DEFAULT_VICTORY_STAGE` before rebuilding the individual strategy bits.
Therefore the Culture call during this normal update cannot even see a previous
turn's Diplomacy stage. The current Diplomacy bits simply do not exist yet.

The call path is live and routine:

    CvPlayerAI::AI_updateCacheData()
        -> AI_updateVictoryStageHash()
            -> reset hash
            -> Space
            -> Conquest
            -> Domination
            -> Culture
            -> Diplomacy

Thus, in the ordinary cached-strategy update, `iDiplomacyStage` inside the new
Culture competing-victory gate is necessarily 0 regardless of what
`AI_calculateDiplomacyVictoryStage()` will return a few statements later.

CONCRETE CONSEQUENCE
--------------------
With the default XML value:

    SAS_AI_CULTURE_VICTORY_COMPETING_VICTORY_MIN_STAGE = 3

an AI that is genuinely at Diplomacy stage 3 or 4, while Space/Conquest/
Domination are below stage 3, does NOT receive the intended competing-victory
Culture downgrade.

If the remaining Culture conditions permit Culture 2, the AI can therefore
continue diverting production, specialists and commerce toward an unready
cultural hedge even though the exact SAS policy says an advanced Diplomatic
pursuit should suppress it.

On the same turn, `AI_updateVictoryStageHash` subsequently calls
`AI_calculateDiplomacyVictoryStage` and stores DIPLOMACY3/4 correctly. Other
consumers later in the turn can see those bits; the Culture calculation that
needed them has already finished.

This is a deterministic state-order omission, not random disagreement between
two strategy estimates.

SECONDARY DIAGNOSTIC EFFECT
---------------------------
The level-2 Culture-4 diagnostic probe later in
`AI_calculateCultureVictoryStage` also reads `AI_getVictoryStageHash()` and
logs `diplomacyStage` / `competingVictoryPressure`. During normal victory-hash
construction it has the same partial-hash limitation, so diagnostics can report
Diplomacy stage 0 even though the immediately following Diplomacy calculation
will establish stage 3/4.

The numbered gameplay root is the competing-victory behavior gate; the
diagnostic mismatch is a downstream symptom of the same ordering.

ANCESTRY
--------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 already uses the inherited K-Mod ordering:

    Space -> Conquest -> Domination -> Culture -> Diplomacy

That ordering was coherent with the pre-SAS Culture function because the
existing Culture logic checks strategy bits that have already been established
before it.

SAS later added `SAS_AI_CULTURE_VICTORY_COMPETING_VICTORY_MIN_STAGE` and
explicitly included Diplomacy in the competing-stage maximum, but retained the
old update order.

Classification: SAS-local state-order regression introduced by the new Culture
competing-victory gate.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Make Diplomacy's current stage available before Culture consumes competing
victory stages.

The cleanest structural repair is likely to compute/store Diplomacy before
Culture in `AI_updateVictoryStageHash`, provided the diplomacy-stage calculator
is kept independent of Culture-stage bits. The current
`AI_calculateDiplomacyVictoryStage` does not call `AI_atVictoryStage`, so the
direct dependency is one-way and this reorder is naturally compatible with the
new SAS gate:

    Space
    Conquest
    Domination
    Diplomacy
    Culture

Then the existing Culture code can read one coherent current-turn hash.

An alternative is to compute the Diplomacy stage explicitly before the Culture
gate and pass/use that value, but that duplicates a nontrivial calculation and
the later hash update unless the update function is refactored to preserve the
result.

Do not "fix" this by retaining a previous-turn Diplomacy hash during rebuild;
that would merely replace a deterministic missing dependency with stale-state
behavior.

CLOSURE-RECONCILIATION CONTROL — AI_localAttackStrength / KI#593 REPAIR
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The current SAS-local KI#593 repair in `AI_localAttackStrength` was deliberately
reopened against the original F270 finding and the current
`estimateCollateralWeight` contract.

No independent F374 has been established there.

The repair now derives collateral roles as follows:

* explicit/default hostile-strength queries:
  - attacker = requested enemy team, or `NO_TEAM` for the intentionally generic
    multiple-hostile mode;
  - defender = evaluating player's team;

* explicit own-offense queries:
  - attacker = evaluating player's own team;
  - defender = opposing target-plot team when known;
  - if target plot is our own team, defender remains generic rather than
    falsely treating our team as both sides.

This matches F270's repair boundary: the original bug was hard-wiring
`getTeam()` as the collateral ATTACKER even when `AI_localAttackStrength`
was counting enemy units. The current code no longer does that, while preserving
`NO_TEAM` when the query aggregates multiple hostile teams and therefore has no
single truthful attacker identity.

Representative caller classes were reopened:
* city safety / enemy offense (`NO_TEAM`);
* explicit enemy-team recapture/raze risk;
* own local offense against a target plot;
* spy/city-attack and stack-vs-stack tactical comparisons;
* city-trade third-party danger.

No supported caller was found in this slice that inverts the new role mapping.
The remaining approximation for genuinely mixed hostile teams is inherent in a
single aggregate collateral scalar and was explicitly anticipated by F270; it
is not a new root.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F374 / provisional KI#697 — Culture victory strategy is player-local even
though the actual Cultural victory city requirement is TEAM-wide; SAS's new
deadline gate can now force cooperating teammates back to Culture 1
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
The actual game victory test counts Legendary/high-enough culture cities across
ALL members of the winning team.

Current `CvGame::testVictory`:

    int iCount = 0;
    for (MemberIter itMember(eTeam); itMember.hasNext(); ++itMember)
    {
        FOR_EACH_CITY(pCity, *itMember)
        {
            if (pCity->getCultureLevel() >=
                culturalVictoryCultureLevel())
            {
                iCount++;
            }
        }
    }

    if (iCount < kVictory.getNumCultureCities())
        return false;

K-Mod and BtS/Civ4CE use the same team-wide victory semantics (with older
explicit player loops).

By contrast, `CvPlayerAI::AI_calculateCultureVictoryStage` evaluates Cultural
victory entirely from the current player's own cities:

    FOR_EACH_CITY(pLoopCity, *this)
    {
        ...
        countdownList.push_back(iCountdown);
        if (iCountdown < iHighCultureMark)
            iHighCultureCount++;
        ...
    }

The required count remains the GAME/TEAM victory requirement:

    int iVictoryCities = kGame.culturalVictoryNumCultureCities();

but all of:

    iHighCultureCount
    iCloseToLegendaryCount
    iLegendaryCount
    countdownList
    iWinningCountdown

describe only `*this` player's cities.

The decisive Stage-3 condition is therefore:

    if (iHighCultureCount >= iVictoryCities)
        bAt3 = true;

rather than asking whether this player's TEAM has the required number of
credible cultural candidates.

SUPPORTED TEAM COUNTEREXAMPLE
-----------------------------
Assume the ordinary Cultural-victory requirement is three cities and a
two-player permanent team has:

    Player A: 2 strong near-Legendary/high-countdown culture cities
    Player B: 1 strong near-Legendary/high-countdown culture city

The actual victory engine sees three team cities. This is a complete collective
set of candidates; once those three reach Legendary, the team wins.

The AI strategy calculators see:

    Player A:
        iHighCultureCount <= 2
        countdownList.size() <= 2
        iWinningCountdown = MAX_INT

    Player B:
        iHighCultureCount <= 1
        countdownList.size() <= 1
        iWinningCountdown = MAX_INT

Neither player can satisfy:

    iHighCultureCount >= iVictoryCities /* 3 */

so neither can enter the normal Stage-3/Stage-4 cultural sprint on the strength
of the team's actual three-city path.

This is not merely a display mismatch. Culture victory stages affect
player-level commerce, specialists, buildings, production and other strategic
choices, so failing to recognize teammates' candidate cities can stop the
players from making the final coordinated push that their team victory
condition requires.

SAS DEADLINE GATE MAKES THE INHERITED GAP STRICTER
--------------------------------------------------
Current SAS adds:

    bool const bLateCultureRace = ...;

    if (!isHuman() && kGame.culturalVictoryValid() &&
        (bLateCultureRace || iWinningCountdown < MAX_INT))
    {
        ...
        bool const bWinningCountdownAvailable =
                (iWinningCountdown < MAX_INT);

        if (!bWinningCountdownAvailable || deadlineMiss)
            return 1;
    }

In the 2+1 team example, neither player has three qualifying OWN cities, so
neither can produce an Nth-city `iWinningCountdown`.

Once the late-race condition becomes true, SAS therefore does not merely fail
to promote the team path to Culture 3. It explicitly returns Culture 1 for both
players because each individual's complete three-city projection is missing.

Thus a team can collectively have exactly the required three credible culture
cities while the current SAS strategy logic treats BOTH members as lacking a
complete Cultural-victory projection.

The same mismatch also affects the new foundation/race helpers:
`getSASCultureVictoryNthCityCulture(*this, ...)` and rival countdowns are
computed per player, whereas the victory being ranked is achieved by teams.

ANCESTRY
--------
The actual Cultural-victory city test is team-wide in Civ4CE/BtS, K-Mod,
Base AdvCiv and current SAS.

K-Mod's `AI_calculateCultureVictoryStage` already loops only over the current
player's cities and compares those counts against the full victory-city
requirement. Base AdvCiv inherits that structure.

Current SAS inherits the player-local foundation and adds additional
player-local foundation/race/deadline gates; the new deadline gate makes the
late-team failure deterministic whenever the team distributes the required
candidates across members and no individual member owns a full required set.

Classification:
* root: inherited K-Mod/BBAI-style player-vs-team Cultural strategy mismatch;
* aggravating current behavior: SAS-local deadline/foundation/race logic
  preserves the same scope mismatch and can force Stage 1.

This is independent of F373. F373 is a current-turn ordering defect that hides
Diplomacy stage from the competing-victory gate. F374 is the object-scope
mismatch between a player strategy calculator and a team-wide victory
condition.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
A correct team-game implementation needs to separate two questions:

1. What is the TEAM's Cultural-victory position?
2. What should THIS PLAYER contribute to that team plan?

The first must aggregate candidate culture/countdowns across `MemberIter`
rather than requiring every player independently to own `iVictoryCities`
candidates.

For team-level feasibility/race/deadline checks, build one combined list from
all team members' cities and take the team's Nth-best required candidate.

The second can remain player-local for deciding which player's slider,
specialists and production should contribute, but it should use the team's
collective race state and then recognize whether this player owns one or more
of the team's selected Cultural candidates.

Do not simply make every teammate enter Culture 4 whenever the team has three
candidates; that could waste the slider of a teammate who owns none of them.
The minimal correctness boundary is:
* team aggregation for victory feasibility/stage/race;
* player ownership for contribution intensity.

ADDITIONAL CULTURE-STAGE CONTROLS CLOSED IN THIS SLICE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

* `SAS_AI_CULTURE_VICTORY_MAX_DEADLINE_PERCENT`
  - the default is 125 and its XML contract describes an estimated-game-length
    strategic deadline, not a 0-to-disable switch.
  - `CvGame::gameTurnProgress` explicitly documents the inherited design
    assumption that even with Time victory disabled the AI does not expect the
    game to last beyond the estimated end. Therefore using
    `getEstimateEndTurn()` as a strategic horizon is aggressive policy, not by
    itself a new F375.

* Culture logging levels:
  - the diagnostic-only foundation/race calculations are guarded so disabled
    behavior limits are checked explicitly before affecting strategy.
  - the Culture-4 candidate probe is enclosed in logging conditions and only
    computes/logs diagnostics.
  - no independent "turn logging on, strategy changes" F375 was established.

* `iOwnVictoryCountdown` comparison:
  - a real active team victory countdown is intentionally preferred over the
    projected Cultural finish when shorter. No independent sentinel inversion
    was established.

LATE CLOSURE FINDINGS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The final reconciliation materially improved Queue 001 rather than merely
rubber-stamping it. Its last confirmed roots were:

F367
    `AI_getHappinessWeight` / `AI_getHealthWeight` mutate the shared
    `iExtraPop` argument inside the city loop, making later-city valuation
    depend on city iteration order.

F368
    `AI_getPlotAirbaseValue` increments `iOtherCityCount` only when a newly
    visited base/city sets a new minimum distance, so it counts traversal
    record-minima rather than nearby bases.

F369
    AdvCiv's persistent unit-brag state stores one randomized
    `AI_getBestAttackUnit()` result while diplomacy text independently rolls
    the randomized selector again, allowing remembered unit A and displayed
    unit B.

F370
    `AI_advancedStartPlaceCity` increments `iPlotsImproved` after a void
    improvement purchase that can silently fail, producing phantom
    improvements that can drive real population spending.

F371
    Advanced Start building selection stores one candidate building's
    affordability result in the global `bDoneBuildings` outer-loop flag,
    preventing later focus passes from exposing cheaper affordable buildings.

F372
    AdvCiv changed BtS/K-Mod's formerly unread Advanced Start unit `bDone`
    flag into an outer-loop terminator. One unaffordable CITY_DEFENSE unit can
    therefore prevent the next WORKER/RESERVE/COUNTER role pass even when a
    cheaper unit is affordable.

F373
    SAS's new Culture competing-victory gate checks Diplomacy stage from
    `m_eVictoryStageHash` while the normal hash rebuild computes Diplomacy only
    AFTER Culture. The current Diplomacy arm of the gate is therefore absent
    during the ordinary strategy update.

F374
    `AI_calculateCultureVictoryStage` evaluates only the current player's
    culture cities even though the real Cultural-victory city test aggregates
    every member of the team. Current SAS's late deadline gate further forces
    Stage 1 when no individual teammate owns a full N-city projection, even
    when the team collectively has the required candidate set.

These late roots justify the function-range and pattern reconciliation: several
would not have been found by merely stopping when the earlier linear walk
reached the bottom of the file.

FINAL F375 CONTROLS — NO NUMBER ALLOCATED

No independent F375 survived the final closure slice.

`AI_localAttackStrength` / KI#593 repair
---------------------------------------
The current SAS repair correctly stopped hard-wiring the evaluating team as the
collateral attacker. Representative enemy/default, explicit-enemy, own-offense,
city-safety, trade-danger and tactical callers were rechecked against
`estimateCollateralWeight`. Remaining mixed-hostile approximation is inherent
in a single aggregate scalar and was already part of F270's repair boundary.

Culture rival visibility
------------------------
The new foundation/projected race scans use all alive major players and can
therefore consult exact data for unmet rivals. That is genuine omniscient
information use, but the current feature is explicitly a global race-ranking
heuristic and the source/XML contract does not promise a known-rivals-only
scope. Civ4 AI contains other deliberate information advantages. Without a
stronger fairness/knowledge contract, this remains design debt / a possible
policy improvement rather than F375. Same-team competition is NOT discarded:
the materially incorrect player-vs-team victory scope is already captured by
F374.

Culture deadline horizon
------------------------
Using `getEstimateEndTurn()` even when Time victory is disabled can aggressively
reject very late cultural plans, but AdvCiv's own `gameTurnProgress` contract
explicitly states that the AI does not expect the game to last beyond the
estimated end even with Time victory disabled. This is strategic policy, not a
new arithmetic bug.

Culture logging
---------------
The logging-only foundation/race/C4 probes were checked for feedback into
strategy. Behavior gates explicitly test their XML enable values, and diagnostic
vectors/counters do not alter decisions. No log-level-dependent strategy root
was established.

Great-Person weights
--------------------
The SAS Culture/corporation damping rewrite was reopened:
* `AI_permanentSpecialistValue` initializes all optional diagnostic outputs;
* logging-only maps/vectors do not feed the chosen weights back;
* the Culture-stage dependency reads a refreshed per-turn victory hash before
  the three-turn GP-weight update in the ordinary turn lifecycle;
* corporation-founder and Join-City damping are intentional policy according
  to the current XML/source comments.
The inherited three-turn refresh cadence can make any GP input stale briefly,
but it predates these changes and is an explicit performance tradeoff.

`AI_updateStrategyHash`
-----------------------
The current-vs-Base behavioral delta in the reopened strategy hash is only the
restart-cached `BBAI_TURTLE_ENEMY_POWER_RATIO` read. No runtime writer was
established and behavior is unchanged.

Advanced Start tech attempts
----------------------------
The early/interleaved void tech actions can fail after selection while local
tech-allocation heuristics still advance. This is a weaker sibling of F370.
The false state is confined to the current Advanced Start allocation heuristic
rather than representing a purchased object or consuming a hard success quota,
and the stronger independent building/unit termination defects are already
F371/F372. It remains documented control/debt rather than manufacturing F375.

Capital-first `AI_getBestAttackUnit`
------------------------------------
A Factory-less capital can miss a stronger Factory-gated attacker trainable in
another city. The demonstrated impact remains mostly presentation/brag
semantics and overlaps F369; no independent gameplay consequence strong enough
for F375 was established.

`AI_calculateStolenCityRadiusPlots`
-----------------------------------
AdvCiv's per-city-radius rewrite can count one physical foreign-owned plot more
than once when it affects multiple cities, but the rewrite is explicitly a
per-city capped border-grievance model and one plot can deny workable space to
multiple cities. No unique-physical-plot contract was established.

`AI_calculateUnitAIViability`
-----------------------------
Default UnitClass units can differ from civilization-specific UUs in UnitAI
availability. Current gameplay callers requiring the relevant discrepancy are
sea-role callers, and current SAS has no naval UU producing it. This remains a
mod-mod hazard, not a current root.

OPENING RECONCILIATION — OLD F002 / KI#331
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The old cross-file `scrap()` contract root is materially repaired in CURRENT
source and should not be rediscovered as F375.

Current `CvUnit::scrap()` now returns explicit success:

    bool CvUnit::scrap()
    {
        if (!canScrap())
            return false;
        scrapInternal();
        return true;
    }

The previously broadened Queue-002 callers now respect that contract:

* Worker discretionary cleanup:
      if (SyncRandSuccess(rScrapProb) && scrap())
          return;
  A restrictive SAS veto now falls through to ordinary Worker fallback.

* Excess land Explorer:
      if (scrap()) return;
  Failed cleanup continues into stranded/patrol/safety handling.

* Trapped Barbarian ship:
      if (bScrap && scrap()) return;

* Escort Sea cleanup:
      if (scrap()) return;

* obsolete/excess Explore Sea cleanup:
      if (scrap()) return;
  Both relevant inherited branches now continue if cargo-capacity protection
  vetoes the removal.

The two contexts that genuinely require removal after caller-specific safety
checks use the explicit forced path:

* retired inferior Settler transport after unloading:
      if (scrapForced()) return;

* doomed-city scorched-earth evacuation:
      if (scrapForced()) return true;

No remaining active `scrap(); return;` pattern from the original Queue-002
KI#331 expansion was found in the opening current-source grep. The idle
Barbarian Worker branch checks `canScrap()` before calling `scrap()`, and
`AI_scrapSettlerWithNoValidSite` deliberately uses its own guarded
`scrapInternal()` mandatory-cleanup operation.

Conclusion:
old F002 / KI#331 remains historical evidence and a cross-file contract lesson,
but its Queue-002 caller set is currently repaired/saturated. Do not allocate a
new finding merely for those old sites.

OPENING RECONCILIATION — EXISTING KI#213 STILL SURVIVES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The known city-cache / Worker-policy architecture split is still present and
must be retained as an EXISTING cross-file root, not duplicated as F375.

Current `CvCityAI::AI_getImprovementValue` explicitly disables the legacy
evaluator for every land plot:

    if (!kPlot.isWater())
    {
        if (peBestBuild)
            *peBestBuild = NO_BUILD;
        return 0;
    }

Current land Workers instead use the large custom
`CvUnitAI::AI_bestCityBuild`, which explicitly understands ordinary no-bonus
land terrain/features, including dedicated Flood Plains branches and the
current XML-driven build picker.

Several city/player consumers still ask the intentionally empty legacy cache.

A) Advanced Start remains structurally disconnected
----------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayerAI::AI_advancedStartPlaceCity` calls:

    pCity->AI_updateBestBuild();

and then searches ordinary city plots solely through:

    pCity->AI_getBestBuildValue(ePlot)
    pCity->AI_getBestBuild(ePlot)

before purchasing `ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_IMPROVEMENT`.

Because the city evaluator returns 0 / NO_BUILD for ordinary land, the custom
Worker policy that knows how to Farm/Mine/Cottage/etc. those plots is invisible
to this land-improvement purchase loop.

This is separate from F370's phantom-success bookkeeping: even after F370 is
repaired, Advanced Start still lacks the land candidate source that ordinary
Workers use.

B) Worker-demand workaround still has a feature-land hole
----------------------------------------------------------
`CvCityAI::AI_updateWorkersHaveAndNeeded` contains a current SAS workaround:

    bool const bSASWorkedLandDemand =
        (!kPlot.isWater() && !kPlot.isFeature() &&
         kPlot.getOwner() == getOwner());

For a worked unimproved plot it counts Worker demand when either the legacy
cache has a build or this featureless-land fallback is true.

That deliberately excludes FEATURE land. Yet `AI_bestCityBuild` explicitly has
valid custom no-bonus feature branches, including `FEATURE_FLOOD_PLAINS`, and
ordinary Forest/Jungle removal/build-followup policy.

Thus a currently worked improvable land plot can still be classified as
`iWorkedUnimprovableCount` solely because it has a feature and the city-side
cache is intentionally empty.

For unworked land, the mismatch is broader: the future-work count still
requires `AI_getBestBuild(ePlot) != NO_BUILD`, so ordinary custom land jobs are
invisible to that cache-derived path.

Existing classification:
KI#213 — pending cross-file architecture root.
Do not assign F375 for these rediscovered consequences.

Repair boundary remains architectural:
share the pure city/plot/build policy between city-side consumers and
`AI_bestCityBuild`; keep unit-specific pathing, danger, reservations and
mission execution in CvUnitAI.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F375 / provisional KI#698 — SAS `countImprovedTiles` counts improvements this
city cannot work, so foreign/shared BFC improvements can make an
underdeveloped city look worker-ready
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
Current SAS added the file-local helper:

    static int countImprovedTiles(CvCity const* pCity)
    {
        int iCount = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < NUM_CITY_PLOTS; ++i)
        {
            CvPlot* pPlot = plotCity(...);
            if (pPlot == NULL)
                continue;

            const ImprovementTypes eImp = pPlot->getImprovementType();
            if (eImp != NO_IMPROVEMENT)
                ++iCount;
        }
        return iCount;
    }

The accompanying history comment is particularly useful: an earlier version
filtered by

    getWorkingCity() == pCity

but SAS deliberately removed that filter in order to make the tile count
"tolerant of overlap."

That broadening crossed the actual worker/city contract.

`WorkablePlotIter(kCity)`, used by current `AI_bestCityBuild`, explicitly skips
a city-radius plot when:

    m_pNext->getWorkingCity() != m_pCity

and `CvCity::canWork` begins with the same condition:

    if (kPlot.getWorkingCity() != this)
        return false;

`CvPlot::updateWorkingCity` also establishes why ownership matters. If a plot
is not owned, it receives no default working city. For owned overlap, one
specific same-owner city is selected as the working city (or an override is
used).

Therefore "has an improvement somewhere inside the geometric 21-tile BFC" is
not equivalent to "is an improved plot available to this city."

CURRENT BEHAVIORAL CONSUMERS
----------------------------
The incorrect count feeds two live SAS worker decisions.

A) Small-city "improved enough" early departure
------------------------------------------------
`AI_workerMove` currently performs:

    if (maxPopDefine > 0 &&
        cityPopulation <= maxPopDefine &&
        countImprovedTiles(pCity) >=
            cityPopulation + buffer + smallCityExtra)
    {
        ...
        if (AI_nextCityToImprove(pCity))
            return;
    }

The current XML default is:

    SAS_AI_WORKER_OVERIMPROVE_SKIP_MAX_CITY_POPULATION = 5

and the C++ buffers are:

    iBufferForAllCities = 2
    iBufferExtraForSmallCities = 3 when population <= 4

Thus a size-5 city is declared geometrically "improved enough" at 7 counted
improvements.

Those seven improvements need not be seven usable improvements for that city.
They can include:
* improvements on tiles now owned by a rival;
* pre-existing improvements on currently unowned plots;
* same-owner overlap plots whose `getWorkingCity()` is another city.

The keep-current-plot safeguard does not repair the count. It only prevents
departure when the Worker happens already to stand on this city's own
currently-workable best local plot. In every other case the inflated count can
send it to another city.

B) Cross-city Worker readiness ranking
---------------------------------------
`AI_nextCityToImprove` computes:

    iImprovedPlots = countImprovedTiles(pLoopCity);
    iEffectiveImprovedPlots = iImprovedPlots + iAssignedWorkers;
    iReadinessPercent =
        max(100,
            100 * (population + 1) /
            (iEffectiveImprovedPlots + 1));

    score = iBuildValue * iReadinessPercent / 100;

This consumer is not limited to population <= 5.

A city with few genuinely usable completed improvements is supposed to receive
a multiplier above 100%. Every foreign/unassigned improvement counted by the
helper enlarges the denominator and suppresses that boost.

A simple shape demonstrates the magnitude. For a size-4 city with no completed
usable improvements and no assigned Worker, the intended readiness term would
be:

    100 * (4 + 1) / (0 + 1) = 500%

If four physically improved BFC plots belong to a rival or are assigned to
another city, the current helper reports four and the same city receives:

    100 * 5 / 5 = 100%

Its genuine `AI_bestCityBuild` candidate is still selected only from
`WorkablePlotIter(kCity)`, so those four counted plots are not part of the
candidate set whose shortage the readiness multiplier is meant to describe.

This can cause a genuinely underdeveloped border/overlap city to lose Worker
priority to a better-looking city elsewhere.

WHY THE OVERLAP CHANGE DOES NOT ESTABLISH SAFETY
------------------------------------------------
The historical rationale says to count overlapping improvements even when
`getWorkingCity() != pCity`.

That can be a reasonable *separate* measure of potential same-owner tile
flexibility, but the current consumers treat the number as completed
improvement capacity of this specific city.

Most importantly, the helper does not distinguish same-owner overlap from
foreign/unowned plots at all. A rival Mine inside the geometric BFC and a
currently usable city Mine both add exactly 1.

Even for friendly overlap, current `AI_bestCityBuild` itself cannot use the
shared plot while its `getWorkingCity()` points at the other city. Counting it
as completed capacity while excluding it from the job/candidate set makes the
readiness numerator and denominator describe different plot populations.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
Current SAS can:
* move a Worker out of a small city earlier than the city's own workable
  improvements justify;
* underweight that city in `AI_nextCityToImprove`;
* preserve the exact type of edge-city underdevelopment the custom cross-city
  Worker rewrite was intended to solve, especially around contested borders
  and overlapping BFCs.

This is independent of KI#213. KI#213 is the architectural split where city
consumers read the intentionally-empty legacy land `AI_getBestBuild` cache
instead of the custom `AI_bestCityBuild` policy.

F375 is entirely inside the new SAS Worker policy: its completed-improvement
counter and its actual custom candidate iterator disagree about which plots
belong to the city.

ANCESTRY
--------
Base AdvCiv 1.14, K-Mod and BtS/Civ4CE do not contain this SAS
`countImprovedTiles` helper or the current cross-city readiness formula.

Classification: SAS-local worker-allocation scope regression.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
At minimum, never count foreign or unowned plots as completed capacity for the
city.

The most contract-consistent conservative repair is to count the same plot
population that the actual city Worker selector can currently act for:

    if (pPlot->getWorkingCity() != pCity)
        continue;

before counting the improvement.

If SAS deliberately wants friendly overlap to count as *potentially
reassignable* capacity, that should be modeled separately and must at least
require same ownership. It should not be mixed one-for-one into the
`iImprovedPlots` term unless the corresponding candidate/job logic can also
treat those overlap plots as available to this city.

A useful split would be:
* `iUsableImprovedPlots`: `getWorkingCity() == pCity`;
* optional `iFriendlyOverlapImprovedPlots`: same owner, another working city,
  with a reduced/tunable contribution if desired.

Foreign/unowned improvements should contribute zero.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F376 / provisional KI#699 — AdvCiv `AI_plotValid` optimization inverted the
`AI_connectBonus` area test into a tautology, making the helper always return
false
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
Current SAS and Base AdvCiv 1.14 contain:

    bool CvUnitAI::AI_connectBonus(bool bTestTrade)
    {
        ...
        for (int iI = 0; iI < GC.getMap().numPlots(); iI++)
        {
            CvPlot const& kPlot = GC.getMap().getPlotByIndex(iI);
            if (kPlot.getOwner() != getOwner() || // XXX team???
                /*!AI_plotValid(kPlot)*/kPlot.isArea(kPlot.getArea())) // advc.opt
            {
                continue;
            }

            ...
        }
        return false;
    }

The second rejection term is always true for a valid plot.

`CvPlot.h` defines:

    bool isArea(CvArea const& kArea) const
    {
        return (area() == &kArea);
    }

and `kPlot.getArea()` is, by definition, that same plot's area. Therefore:

    kPlot.isArea(kPlot.getArea()) == true

for every ordinary map plot.

The `if` therefore reduces to:

    if (anything || true)
        continue;

Every loop iteration is skipped. No bonus can reach the subsequent
non-obsolete-bonus, capital-connection or `AI_connectPlot` logic, and the
function deterministically falls through to:

    return false;

ANCESTRY / INTRODUCING CHANGE
-----------------------------
Civ4CE/BtS and K-Mod use the meaningful original gate:

    if (AI_plotValid(pLoopPlot))
    {
        if (pLoopPlot->getOwner() == getOwner())
        {
            ...
        }
    }

The reachable AdvCiv history pinpoints the regression to pre-SAS AdvCiv commit:

    practical commit 1925
    e4ff624d23ec90298119911fa182fa0e4c870d5a
    "Remove or replace unnecessary AI_plotValid calls"

Immediately before that commit, AdvCiv had:

    if (!AI_plotValid(kPlot) || kPlot.getOwner() != getOwner())
        continue;

The commit changed it to:

    if (kPlot.getOwner() != getOwner() ||
        /*!AI_plotValid(kPlot)*/kPlot.isArea(kPlot.getArea()))
    {
        continue;
    }

The surrounding changes show the intended same-area replacement pattern
elsewhere in the same commit. For example, `AI_improveBonus` changes:

    !AI_plotValid(kPlot)

to:

    !isArea(kPlot.getArea())

and nearby `AI_routeTerritory` likewise uses:

    /*!AI_plotValid(kPlot)*/ !isArea(kPlot.getArea())

The `AI_connectBonus` replacement alone lost the negation and, additionally,
asks the plot whether it belongs to its own area instead of asking the unit
whether the plot belongs to the unit's area.

Classification: inherited AdvCiv optimization regression, introduced while
replacing `AI_plotValid`.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE
----------------
This is not dead source. Current SAS has three live calls.

A) Normal land Worker fallback in `AI_workerMove`
--------------------------------------------------
After city/local improvement, next-city reassignment and
`AI_routeTerritory(true)`, a route-capable Worker executes:

    if (AI_connectBonus(false))
        return;

That pass is intended to connect an owned bonus even without requiring its
current improvement to be the connecting improvement.

Because F376 makes the helper always false, this dedicated fallback never
pushes such a mission.

B) `AI_networkAutomated` first bonus-connection pass
----------------------------------------------------
After `AI_improveBonus()`:

    if (AI_connectBonus())
        return;

This is the stricter trade-ready form. It is dead at runtime because of F376.

C) `AI_networkAutomated` second bonus-connection pass
-----------------------------------------------------
After `AI_connectCity()` and `AI_routeTerritory(true)`:

    if (AI_connectBonus(false))
        return;

This broader connection pass is also dead.

Other Worker/route functions can sometimes connect the same resources by
different routes, so the consequence is NOT "the AI can never connect a
bonus." The precise defect is stronger and cleaner: every caller of this
dedicated helper is guaranteed to receive false, and all strategy encoded
inside the helper is unreachable.

This especially matters for fallback cases for which the ordinary local-city
improvement pipeline has no currently selected route job, including resources
outside ordinary city work assignments and network-automation behavior.

WHY THIS IS NOT KI#213 OR F375
------------------------------
KI#213 concerns the intentionally empty city-side land best-build cache versus
the custom SAS Worker selector.

F375 concerns SAS `countImprovedTiles` using a broader physical BFC population
than the actual workable candidate iterator.

F376 is independent and much older: the entire inherited bonus-connection
helper is disabled by a boolean typo before any cache, candidate valuation or
SAS Worker policy is reached.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
At minimum restore the intended negative same-area test for the land-Worker
optimization, consistent with the neighboring AdvCiv replacements:

    if (kPlot.getOwner() != getOwner() ||
        /*!AI_plotValid(kPlot)*/ !isArea(kPlot.getArea()))
    {
        continue;
    }

If preserving the full modern `AI_plotValid` semantics is desired for unusual
can-move-impassable / all-terrain units, simply restore:

    if (kPlot.getOwner() != getOwner() || !AI_plotValid(kPlot))
        continue;

The second form most directly restores the pre-regression contract; the first
matches the performance-oriented intent of the introducing AdvCiv commit for
ordinary land Workers.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NAVAL / TRANSPORT CONTROL WORK COMPLETED BEFORE F376
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The new destination-aware Settler cargo helper was traced end to end.

`AI_unloadSettlerCargoForDestination`
-------------------------------------
The helper's main accounting is internally coherent:

* before the founding voyage, it computes the destination area's Worker
  deficit and keeps that many cargo Workers aboard while unloading true excess
  only when still in an owned origin city and before a `MISSIONAI_FOUND`
  assignment exists;

* at the destination, cargo Workers can already be included in
  `AI_totalAreaUnitAIs(destination, UNITAI_WORKER)` because the transport is
  physically on the destination land area; the helper explicitly subtracts
  those cargo Workers before computing the shortage, preventing self-counting;

* it unloads Settlers/defenders at the destination while allowing excess
  Workers to remain aboard for reuse.

No selected-vs-executed or false-success state root was established in the
helper itself.

`AI_findTransport` Worker reload gate
-------------------------------------
The new gate rejects a Worker from rejoining a Settler transport already on
`MISSIONAI_FOUND` when the destination area's existing Worker count already
meets demand.

One subtle limitation was traced: while a transport is still outside the
destination area, Workers already aboard are not represented in
`AI_totalAreaUnitAIs(destination, UNITAI_WORKER)`. A capacity-four Settler
transport can therefore temporarily accept a second Worker for a destination
whose deficit is only one.

However:
* the existing Settler-transport cargo-space guard prevents the analogous
  duplicate on the common tighter capacities once only two non-Worker slots
  remain;
* before the initial voyage, the destination-aware unload helper removes
  excess Workers;
* after departure, any excess that does remain is retained aboard at the
  destination rather than dumped into a zero-demand colony.

This can waste a cargo slot in a narrow timing/capacity case, but no sufficiently
independent strategic consequence crossed the F377 threshold in this slice.

`AI_pickupStranded`
-------------------
The new completed-area Worker coordination gate merely prevents two empty
transports being dispatched to the same zero-demand Worker group. Ordinary
stranded groups retain Base AdvCiv's capacity-based coordination. No root was
established.

`AI_assaultSeaMove`
-------------------
The new below-threshold opportunistic launch still calls the existing
target-specific `AI_assaultSeaTransport` after the earlier safety, escort and
imminent-loading waits. No independent target-strength bypass was established.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F377 / provisional KI#700 — SAS `AI_betterPlotBuild` reversed its feature-
removal predicate, so a legal improvement that preserves Forest/Jungle can be
replaced with a pure chop
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
Current SAS `CvUnitAI::AI_betterPlotBuild` says:

    // High-Priority Override 1: Clear Feature
    // Check if the originally planned improvement requires a feature
    // to be removed first

but executes:

    if (!kOriginalBuildInfo.isFeatureRemove(eFeature))
    {
        if (eFeature == eFeatureForest)
        {
            if (canBuild(kPlot, eBuildRemoveForest))
                return eBuildRemoveForest;
        }
        else if (eFeature == eFeatureJungle)
        {
            if (canBuild(kPlot, eBuildRemoveJungle))
                return eBuildRemoveJungle;
        }
        ...
    }

The condition has the opposite meaning from the comment and from the safe
contract.

`isFeatureRemove(eFeature) == false` means the original build does NOT remove
that feature. The helper therefore substitutes a dedicated removal build
precisely when the selected build preserves the feature.

CURRENT-SAS CONCRETE CASE: FOREST CAMP
--------------------------------------
Current XML supplies an ordinary supported example.

`BUILD_CAMP`:
* prerequisite Hunting;
* builds `IMPROVEMENT_CAMP`;
* its `FeatureStructs` contain Fallout removal only;
* it has NO `FEATURE_FOREST` removal entry.

Therefore:

    GC.getInfo(BUILD_CAMP).isFeatureRemove(FEATURE_FOREST) == false.

`BONUS_DEER`:
* can occur on `FEATURE_FOREST`;
* is valid on Tundra / Forest configurations.

`BONUS_FUR`:
* can occur on `FEATURE_FOREST`;
* is valid on Tundra/Snow Forest configurations.

`IMPROVEMENT_CAMP`:
* explicitly connects Deer and Fur;
* those bonus entries make Camp valid on the resource.

`BUILD_REMOVE_FOREST`:
* becomes legal through its Forest `FeatureStruct` at Masonry;
* removes `FEATURE_FOREST`.

Thus after Masonry a Worker can legally be assigned `BUILD_CAMP` on a Forest
Deer/Fur tile while `BUILD_REMOVE_FOREST` is also legal.

LIVE CALLER PROOF
-----------------
The important live path is `CvUnitAI::AI_improveBonus`.

For a land bonus in a working city, current SAS first obtains its
bonus-specific build:

    eBuild = kPlot.SAS_getBonusSpecificBuild(eNonObsoleteBonus);

It then requires all of:

    eBuild != NO_BUILD

    kOwner.doesImprovementConnectBonus(
        GC.getInfo(eBuild).getImprovement(),
        eNonObsoleteBonus)

    canBuild(kPlot, eBuild)

before accepting it as `eBestTempBuild`.

For Forest Deer/Fur this can establish `BUILD_CAMP` as the selected build.
The caller later queues movement toward the exact target and only then runs:

    eBestBuild = AI_betterPlotBuild(*pBestPlot, eBestBuild);

At this point the caller has already proved:

    canBuild(Forest Deer/Fur, BUILD_CAMP) == true.

That fact is decisive. The Forest does not need to be cleared in order to
execute the planned Camp.

Nevertheless the current postprocessor evaluates:

    !BUILD_CAMP.isFeatureRemove(FEATURE_FOREST) == true

and, when Forest removal is legal, returns:

    BUILD_REMOVE_FOREST

instead of `BUILD_CAMP`.

The Worker therefore performs a pure chop rather than the already-selected
resource improvement.

The custom `AI_bestCityBuild` execution paths now intentionally bypass
`AI_betterPlotBuild`, so they do not reproduce this mismatch. That does not
make F377 dormant because `AI_improveBonus` remains a live land-Worker fallback
and executes the postprocessor exactly as above.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
The AI can:
* spend an extra Worker action chopping a Forest before constructing a Camp
  that was already legal without the chop;
* destroy a feature that the resource improvement can coexist with;
* delay connecting the Deer/Fur resource that `AI_improveBonus` explicitly
  selected;
* replace a caller-validated exact improvement choice with a different action
  whose prerequisite rationale is false.

The immediate chop production may sometimes be strategically useful, but that
does not repair the contract. The helper is not evaluating chop value here;
it claims to clear a feature only when required by the planned improvement,
and the caller has already proved the improvement is legal on the feature.

The same inverted class can affect any current/future Forest/Jungle-preserving
build for which the dedicated removal build is legal.

ANCESTRY / INTRODUCING CHANGE
-----------------------------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and K-Mod retain the older `bClearFeature` logic. They only
consider a feature-clearing override when the ORIGINAL build itself removes
the feature:

    if (kOriginalBuildInfo.isFeatureRemove(eFeature))
        ...

SAS practical commit 4921
`cc59407b55267151ae1cad01472a3625b83fa9bb`
rewrote/simplified `AI_betterPlotBuild` and still preserved the correct sense:

    if (eFeature != NO_FEATURE &&
        kOriginalBuildInfo.isFeatureRemove(eFeature))
    {
        // find a build that removes the feature
    }

The very next reachable practical commit 4922
`7e7a475897...`
changed that condition to:

    if (!kOriginalBuildInfo.isFeatureRemove(eFeature))

while adding hardcoded Forest/Jungle removal builds.

The surrounding prose still says this is a safeguard for cases where a
"specific build to remove feature" may have been missed, but the inversion
means it now fires for builds that explicitly do NOT remove the feature.

Classification: SAS-local regression introduced in practical commit 4922.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The minimum correctness repair is to restore the positive predicate:

    if (eFeature != NO_FEATURE &&
        kOriginalBuildInfo.isFeatureRemove(eFeature))
    {
        ...
    }

However, given current SAS's stronger exact Worker/build selection, an even
safer conservative policy is to avoid replacing a caller-validated improvement
at all unless there is a demonstrated sequencing reason.

In particular, `AI_improveBonus` has already checked `canBuild(kPlot, eBuild)`.
If that succeeds, no prerequisite feature-clearing action is required.

If SAS wants intentional chop-before-improvement behavior, that should be a
separate value decision that explicitly weighs the feature/chop yield and
preservation value; it should not masquerade as a prerequisite repair.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTROLS CLOSED WHILE PROVING F377
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

* The main current custom `AI_bestCityBuild` / `AI_improveCity` paths no longer
  pass their exact chosen build through `AI_betterPlotBuild`, specifically to
  avoid postprocessing replacing a scored/reserved Worker job. That prior
  repair is effective.

* `AI_improvePlot` still calls `AI_betterPlotBuild`, but the source itself
  labels `AI_improvePlot` as not currently used after K-Mod changes. It was not
  needed for the F377 live proof.

* The Forest/Camp proof does not depend on the legacy city best-build cache and
  is therefore independent of existing KI#213.
