-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F378 / provisional KI#701 — `AI_guardCity` selects the unit to detach using
the SOURCE plot's defensive value instead of the DESTINATION city it is being
sent to defend
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
After `AI_guardCity` searches for a city that needs reinforcement, it stores:

    pBestGuardPlot = pLoopCity->plot();

and the path/end-turn plot for movement toward that city.

Current SAS then chooses which member of the donor group to detach with:

    CvPlot* pSourcePlot = plot();
    ...
    CvUnit* pEjectedUnit =
            pOldGroup->AI_ejectBestDefender(pSourcePlot);

The detached unit is immediately assigned to `pBestGuardPlot`:

    pEjectedUnit->pushGroupMoveTo(
            *pEndTurnPlot, eFlags, false, false,
            eMissionAI, pBestGuardPlot);

Thus candidate selection asks "which unit defends the source plot best?" while
execution asks that selected unit to defend a different target city.

The selection helper is explicitly plot-sensitive.

`CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_ejectBestDefender(CvPlot* pDefendPlot)` begins with:

    int iValue = pUnit->AI_currEffectiveStr(pDefendPlot) * 20;

and, if the supplied plot is a city-defense plot:

    iValue *= 100 + pUnit->cityDefenseModifier();
    iValue /= 100;

`AI_currEffectiveStr(pDefendPlot)` itself reaches `CvUnit::maxCombatStr` and
therefore applies the supplied plot's:
* plot/city defense;
* city-defense modifier;
* hill defense;
* feature/terrain defense;
* other relevant defensive combat modifiers.

The public/group interface names the same argument `pTargetPlot`.

Therefore the plot argument is not an incidental non-null context; it controls
the exact ranking of which group member is the "best defender."

CURRENT-SAS RANK-REVERSAL PROOF
-------------------------------
Current XML provides a simple same-unit/same-level pair.

`UNIT_ARCHER`:
* `UNITCOMBAT_ARCHER_BOW_SHORT`;
* base combat 2;
* +50% city defense;
* 1 first strike + 1 chance first strike;
* accepts both Combat and City Garrison promotions.

`PROMOTION_COMBAT1`:
* +10% combat;
* valid for short-bow Archers.

`PROMOTION_CITY_GARRISON1`:
* +25% city defense;
* valid for short-bow Archers.

Take two otherwise-identical, full-health, same-level Archers in one donor
group:

    Archer A: Combat I
    Archer B: City Garrison I

On an ordinary flat non-city source plot, City Garrison contributes nothing to
`currEffectiveStr`, while Combat I contributes +10% general combat.

The remaining `AI_ejectBestDefender` factors are identical for these two
otherwise-identical units. Therefore the SOURCE-plot call prefers:

    Archer A (Combat I).

Now evaluate the same pair for the destination city.

Ignoring common city/terrain defense terms for clarity:

    Combat-I Archer:
        +50% built-in city defense
        +10% Combat

    CG-I Archer:
        +50% built-in city defense
        +25% City Garrison

So `AI_currEffectiveStr(destinationCity)` already favors City Garrison I.

The helper then applies ANOTHER explicit city-defense weighting:

    * (100 + cityDefenseModifier) / 100

which is:

    Combat-I Archer: * 150 / 100
    CG-I Archer:     * 175 / 100

The target-city ranking therefore favors:

    Archer B (City Garrison I).

This is a true rank reversal:
* source open terrain -> Combat I selected;
* target city -> City Garrison I selected.

The current call detaches the former and sends it to the city while leaving the
more city-specialized defender in the donor group.

The proof does not depend on unusual unique units, damage, or different unit
levels. Two copies of one ordinary current unit with one ordinary promotion
each suffice.

LIVE OFF-CITY PATH
------------------
`AI_guardCity` is not restricted to a group already standing in the target
city.

Its search explicitly requires a path to another city and stores a remote
`pBestGuardPlot`. Current SAS calls the search form from many mobile UnitAI
moves. In particular:

* `AI_attackMove` calls `AI_guardCity(false, true, 1)` for nearby colony/city
  defense;
* the SAS threatened-city response calls
  `AI_guardCity(false, true, 3, ..., bDangerOnly=true, bFillShortfall=true)`;
* the central continuation of a targeted `MISSIONAI_GUARD_CITY` calls the same
  search while the reinforcing group is between source and destination;
* the early city-to-city garrison rebalance can detach a defender from a donor
  group and send it several path turns away.

Therefore source != destination is an ordinary supported state, not a
hypothetical API misuse.

The current SAS `bFillShortfall` extension can repeat
`AI_ejectBestDefender(pSourcePlot)` several times, so a threatened-city rescue
can detach multiple units according to the wrong terrain/city context.

ANCESTRY
--------
The root predates SAS.

Civ4CE/BtS search-mode `AI_guardCity`:
* finds `pBestGuardPlot`;
* calls `getGroup()->AI_ejectBestDefender(pPlot)`, where `pPlot` is the current
  source plot;
* sends the returned unit toward the remote guard city.

K-Mod preserves the same source-plot call.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 preserves it as:

    AI_getGroup()->AI_ejectBestDefender(plot());

Current SAS names the source explicitly but preserves the inherited semantics:

    pOldGroup->AI_ejectBestDefender(pSourcePlot);

The selection helper itself has always treated its argument as the plot being
defended, and the interface calls it `pTargetPlot`.

Classification: inherited BtS/BBAI guard-city target-context defect.

WHY THIS IS NOT MERELY A HEURISTIC PREFERENCE
---------------------------------------------
The caller first makes a separate strategic decision about WHICH CITY needs a
defender. It then invokes a helper specifically designed to identify the
group's best defender for a supplied plot.

Passing the source plot causes that helper to answer a different question from
the mission that immediately follows.

This can systematically send:
* generic Combat-promoted units instead of City Garrison specialists from open
  terrain;
* hill/feature specialists favored by the source terrain instead of units best
  suited to the city;
* analogous source-specific defensive specialists whose bonuses disappear at
  the destination.

The distinction is particularly relevant to the SAS emergency shortfall mode,
whose purpose is explicitly to detach "suitable defenders" for a threatened
city.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Use the selected guard destination when ranking the detached defender:

    CvUnit* pEjectedUnit =
            pOldGroup->AI_ejectBestDefender(
                    const_cast<CvPlot*>(pBestGuardPlot));

or, preferably, make the helper parameter const-correct and pass
`pBestGuardPlot` directly.

When the group is already standing in the city being defended,
`pBestGuardPlot == source`, so this produces no behavioral change.

When reinforcing a remote city, the selected unit is then ranked for the plot
it is actually being sent to defend.

If SAS intentionally wants to consider the cost of weakening the donor/source
stack as well, that is a legitimate additional optimization, but it should be
modeled explicitly as a source-retention term rather than substituting the
source plot for the destination in a helper whose result is the unit sent away.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTROL CLOSED — `AI_betterPlotBuild` "ROAD IMPROVED BONUSES"
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The separate post-F377 suspicion around this block was not promoted:

    if (doesImprovementConnectBonus(...))
        bNeedsRoad = false;

The comment's interpretation is misleading. K-Mod's
`doesImprovementConnectBonus` answers whether the improvement is a valid
bonus-trading improvement / acts as a city under the relevant technology; it
does not prove that the land plot has a route to the capital.

However, the current live disconnected-bonus path in `AI_improveBonus`
handles an already-correct resource improvement through its explicit route
branch and `AI_connectPlot`, rather than relying on this postprocessor block.

The other relevant land-cache path remains subsumed by existing KI#213, and
`AI_improvePlot` is documented as not currently used.

So the semantic/comment mismatch is retained as robustness/design debt, not
manufactured into an independent F379.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F379 / provisional KI#702 — SAS central guard-mission continuation treats every
targeted `MISSIONAI_GUARD_CITY` as an emergency/danger-only assignment, so the
older six-turn SAFE-city garrison rebalance can lose its destination after one
movement turn
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
Current SAS contains two independent targeted guard-city systems.

A) Early ordinary city-to-city garrison rebalance
-------------------------------------------------
Near the top of `CvUnitAI::AI_update`, during the early-game window, many land
combat UnitAI types in an overstocked owned city may call:

    AI_guardCity(
        false, true,
        /*iMaxPath*/ 6,
        MOVE_SAFE_TERRITORY | MOVE_AVOID_ENEMY_WEIGHT_3,
        /*iExtraDefenders*/ 2)

This call has:

    bDangerOnly = false
    bFillShortfall = false

by default.

Its explicit purpose is to push surplus defenders toward weaker cities even
when those cities are not currently endangered.

When a remote city is selected, `AI_guardCity` queues movement with:

    MISSIONAI_GUARD_CITY
    missionAIPlot = pBestGuardPlot

B) Later emergency/endangered-city continuation
-----------------------------------------------
Current SAS also added, before UnitAI-specific movement:

    if (getDomainType() == DOMAIN_LAND &&
        !isBarbarian() &&
        AI_getGroup()->AI_getMissionAIType() == MISSIONAI_GUARD_CITY &&
        AI_getGroup()->AI_getMissionAIPlot() != NULL &&
        AI_guardCity(
            false, true, 3,
            MOVE_AVOID_ENEMY_WEIGHT_2,
            0,
            /*bDangerOnly*/ true,
            /*bFillShortfall*/ true))
    {
        return false;
    }

The comment correctly describes its original purpose:

    "Targeted emergency city reinforcements ..."

but the outer condition does not identify an emergency assignment.

It catches EVERY targeted `MISSIONAI_GUARD_CITY`, including the older safe-city
rebalance mission.

The continuation call then hardcodes:

    bDangerOnly = true

and `AI_guardCity` immediately excludes each safe city with:

    if (bDangerOnly && !pLoopCity->AI_isDanger())
        continue;

Therefore a still-valid SAFE rebalance target cannot be continued by this
central mission-preservation hook.

CONCRETE CURRENT-SAS FAILURE
----------------------------
A straightforward current path uses `UNITAI_ATTACK`.

Assume:
* early-game rebalance window is active;
* City A has more defend-capable units than its own minimum;
* City B is safe but underdefended enough to win the rebalance score;
* an ordinary one-move Archer/other `UNITAI_ATTACK` unit can reach B in six
  path turns over safe unroaded territory.

Turn N:
1. Unit is in City A.
2. early rebalance runs before `AI_attackMove`;
3. `AI_guardCity(... iMaxPath=6, iExtraDefenders=2)` selects City B;
4. the unit/group receives targeted `MISSIONAI_GUARD_CITY` for City B;
5. movement goes only to that turn's path end.

Turn N+1:
1. the group still carries a targeted `MISSIONAI_GUARD_CITY`;
2. City B is still safe and still underdefended;
3. central continuation recognizes the mission type/target;
4. it calls `AI_guardCity(... bDangerOnly=true ...)`;
5. City B is rejected solely because `AI_isDanger()==false`;
6. with no endangered replacement city, the continuation returns false;
7. normal `AI_attackMove` now runs.

The ordinary `UNITAI_ATTACK` guard searches do not preserve the original
six-turn reach:
* nearby guard search: 1 turn;
* colony/search paths: 3 turns in relevant branches;
* later general guard search: 3 turns.

After one ordinary movement turn from an initial six-turn target, an unroaded
one-move unit can still be five turns away.

Therefore the exact still-valid City-B assignment cannot be rediscovered by
those searches. The unit proceeds into offensive/grouping/other role logic and
can overwrite/abandon the previous guard mission.

The nominal six-turn rebalance radius consequently does not imply a six-turn
commitment for `UNITAI_ATTACK` and several other donor roles.

This is not limited to Attack units. The early exporter includes:

    UNITAI_ATTACK
    UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY
    UNITAI_COLLATERAL
    UNITAI_PILLAGE
    UNITAI_RESERVE
    UNITAI_COUNTER
    UNITAI_CITY_DEFENSE
    UNITAI_CITY_COUNTER
    UNITAI_CITY_SPECIAL

Their ordinary guard-search ranges differ. Some, such as City Defense, can
eventually perform broad searches and may rediscover the target; others use
shorter ranges and can lose a long-distance safe-city assignment.

The defect is therefore role-dependent, which also makes the apparent
six-turn rebalance behavior inconsistent across otherwise eligible donors.

WHY MISSIONAI STATE DOES NOT SAVE IT
------------------------------------
The queued movement is to the current turn's `pEndTurnPlot`, not an indefinitely
executing full multi-turn path. On the next AI update the role logic can choose
again.

The new practical-6049 central continuation exists precisely because targeted
emergency defenders were observed to "immediately rejoin offensive groups and
receive another assignment before reaching their city." That is direct history
evidence that carrying `MISSIONAI_GUARD_CITY` alone does not force completion.

The same lifecycle applies to the older targeted safe-city rebalance.

ANCESTRY / INTERACTION HISTORY
------------------------------
This is SAS-local.

Practical commit 4953
    `0704fd52d2...`

introduced the early city-to-city rebalance in `AI_update`, including the
six-turn search and ordinary `AI_guardCity` semantics.

Practical commit 6049
    `c89861b618e8512ea2731d1cfd832b33ec060970`

later fixed KI#188.2 emergency reinforcement persistence by adding the central
targeted-guard continuation. Its commit title is:

    "(Fixed/Improved) Base AdvCiv/K-Mod issue: offensive armies could ignore
     nearby endangered cities instead of going back to try to help defending
     them"

and its new comment explicitly scopes the hook to "Targeted emergency city
reinforcements."

However, the code distinguishes targeted vs targetless guard missions, not
emergency vs ordinary targeted guard missions. The older 4953 rebalance also
uses a target plot, so it is intercepted by 6049's emergency-only continuation
and then rejected when its city is safe.

Classification: SAS-local interaction/state-lifetime regression between the
ordinary garrison-rebalance feature and the later emergency continuation.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
The AI can:
* export a surplus defender toward a safe weak city;
* spend one turn moving it there;
* discard the still-valid assignment on the following turn;
* resume offensive/grouping work before reaching the city.

This weakens the exact purpose of the early rebalance: spreading real existing
defensive capacity from overstocked core cities toward weak secondary cities.

It also wastes movement turns and can create role-dependent "starts to
reinforce, then changes its mind" behavior.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Preserve the semantic type of the targeted guard assignment.

Several conservative designs are possible.

1. Distinguish emergency targeted guard missions from ordinary guard-city
   rebalance missions with an explicit mission/state marker, then:
   * emergency -> continue with `bDangerOnly=true`, `bFillShortfall=true`,
     3-turn emergency policy;
   * ordinary rebalance -> continue toward its existing safe underdefended
     target under the original rebalance policy/range.

2. If adding a state bit is undesirable, inspect the existing mission target
   first:
   * if it is endangered, use the emergency continuation;
   * otherwise validate that the same target still needs the ordinary garrison
     reinforcement and continue toward that exact target rather than globally
     rerunning danger-only search.

3. Alternatively make all targeted guard-city movement directly persistent
   until its target becomes invalid/satisfied, with the target's current
   shortage/danger deciding when to release it.

Do not simply change the central call to `bDangerOnly=false` while retaining
`bFillShortfall=true`; that would merge two policies and could cause ordinary
safe-city shortages to detach emergency-sized fractions of offensive groups.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTROLS / RELATED BEHAVIOR
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

* The existing central continuation correctly improves the practical-6049
  emergency case. F379 does not argue that it should be removed.

* City-Defense donors often have broader ordinary guard fallbacks and can
  rediscover a safe destination; this does not repair the cross-role contract
  because the early exporter intentionally includes many UnitAI types whose
  normal ranges are much shorter than six turns.

* A safe target becoming genuinely endangered naturally transitions into the
  emergency continuation and is then preserved. The defect concerns the
  ordinary, still-needed, still-safe garrison redistribution that practical
  4953 explicitly introduced.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F380 / provisional KI#703 — SAS early garrison rebalance says it counts every
defend-capable unit but actually counts only defend-capable GROUP HEADS, so a
large stacked military concentration can fail the source-surplus gate
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
Current SAS practical-4953 city-to-city garrison redistribution contains:

    // Count any unit that can defend, not just GUARD_CITY mission
    const int iHave =
        pHere->getPlot().plotCount(
            PUF_canDefendGroupHead,
            -1, -1, getOwner());

    const int iMinHere = pHere->AI_minDefenders();

    if (iHave > iMinHere)
    {
        if (AI_guardCity(...))
            ...
    }

The implementation does not match the stated population.

`CvGameCoreUtils.cpp` defines:

    bool PUF_canDefendGroupHead(CvUnit const* pUnit, ...)
    {
        return (PUF_canDefend(pUnit, ...) &&
                PUF_isGroupHead(pUnit, ...));
    }

Therefore the source count is:

    number of defend-capable SELECTION GROUP HEADS

not:

    number of defend-capable UNITS.

A multi-unit selection group contributes exactly one to `iHave`.

WHY GROUP-HEAD COUNTING IS WRONG FOR THIS SAS ACTION
----------------------------------------------------
The rebalance is not about moving an indivisible group.

When it decides the city has surplus, it calls `AI_guardCity`. That function
uses:

    AI_ejectBestDefender(...)

which can detach one selected unit from a multi-unit donor group and send only
that unit toward the weak city.

Current SAS's threat-shortfall extension can detach multiple selected
defenders, but the ordinary early rebalance still deliberately supports
splitting one defender away while leaving the rest of the donor group intact.

Thus the source-surplus test treats a ten-unit stack as one indivisible
defensive object, while the action it gates is explicitly capable of treating
that stack as ten individual defender candidates and exporting only one.

CONCRETE FAILURE SHAPE
----------------------
Suppose City A has:

    one 8-unit defend-capable ATTACK stack
    one separate CITY_DEFENSE garrison group

and:

    AI_minDefenders(City A) == 2.

Actual defend-capable land units physically available in the city:

    9

Current practical-4953 `iHave`:

    2 group heads

so:

    iHave > iMinHere
    2 > 2
    false

The early redistribution does not even call `AI_guardCity`.

Yet the intended action could safely detach one suitable defender from the
8-unit stack and still leave seven members of that stack plus the dedicated
garrison in City A.

The mismatch becomes even sharper for one large stack plus one minimum
garrison: adding more and more members to the same stack never increases
`iHave` at all.

This directly undercuts the feature's documented motivation: recognizing
overstocked cities and exporting their excess military to weaker cities.
Large ATTACK/ATTACK_CITY/RESERVE/COUNTER stacks are exactly the type of
concentration most likely to be grouped.

INTRODUCING HISTORY
-------------------
Practical commit 4953:

    0704fd52d2...

introduced both the comment and the predicate together:

    // Count any unit that can defend, not just GUARD_CITY mission
    plotCount(PUF_canDefendGroupHead, ...)

So this is not an inherited BtS/K-Mod convention accidentally exposed later.
The new SAS feature stated an individual-unit contract while selecting the
older group-head predicate.

Classification: SAS-local garrison-rebalance counting regression.

RELATION TO F379
----------------
F379 is the later state-lifetime defect: a long-range safe-city rebalance
mission can be abandoned after one movement turn because the practical-6049
central continuation only preserves endangered-city assignments.

F380 happens BEFORE an assignment is created. It can prevent the source city
from being considered surplus at all when its excess military is stacked.

The two therefore independently reduce the same feature:
* F380: some valid donors never dispatch;
* F379: some dispatched safe reinforcements do not persist.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Count individual defenders that are actually available to detach.

A naive:

    plotCount(PUF_canDefend, ...)

matches the unit-vs-group dimension, but the final repair should explicitly
consider cargo and any other units physically represented on the plot but not
available as city defenders/donors.

The safest implementation is likely a small explicit unit loop with conditions
such as:

    owner == getOwner()
    canDefend()
    !isCargo()

plus any intended immobility/special-unit exclusions.

Alternatively add/use a precise predicate for "defend-capable, non-cargo
individual unit."

Do NOT change the general semantics of `PUF_canDefendGroupHead`; many inherited
callers deliberately use group-head counting for mission/group accounting.
The defect is the practical-4953 choice of that predicate for this new
individual-unit surplus feature.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ADDITIONAL CONTROL
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The broader inherited `AI_guardCity` logic also uses
`PUF_canDefendGroupHead` in several places. That is older mission/group
accounting and was not automatically folded into F380.

F380 is deliberately scoped to the new SAS source-surplus gate because:
* its own comment explicitly says "any unit";
* its purpose is to detect military concentration;
* its subsequent action can split one unit out of a group.

No claim is made here that every historical group-head defender count should be
converted to an individual-unit count.

WHY WIP72'S OUTER-GATE F380 DOES NOT SURVIVE AS AN INDEPENDENT ROOT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

WIP72 correctly established this local mismatch in practical-4953's early
garrison rebalance:

    // Count any unit that can defend, not just GUARD_CITY mission
    const int iHave =
        pHere->getPlot().plotCount(PUF_canDefendGroupHead, ...);

and correctly established that `PUF_canDefendGroupHead` counts only
defend-capable GROUP HEADS.

However, the deeper downstream proof found that changing this OUTER gate alone
does not make the clean stacked-donor example dispatch a unit.

Immediately after the gate, the feature calls:

    AI_guardCity(false, true, 6, ..., iExtraDefenders)

and `AI_guardCity` performs its own source-city retention check:

    int const iHave =
        kPlot.plotCount(
            PUF_canDefendGroupHead,
            ...,
            AI_isCityAIType() ? PUF_isCityAIType : NULL)
        - 1;

    int iNeed = pCity->AI_neededDefenders() + iExtra;

    if (iHave < iNeed)
    {
        bSearch = false;
        pBestGuardPlot = &kPlot;
        ...
    }

For the WIP72 example:

    one large ATTACK stack
    + one dedicated garrison group
    AI_minDefenders / needed defenders ~= 2

the outer practical-4953 gate counts two group heads and rejects the call.

If that outer gate were changed to count all nine individual defenders, the
call would proceed -- but the inner inherited `AI_guardCity` check would count
the two group heads, subtract the current group head, see only one remaining
defender-group against a need of about two, and force the current group to stay
in the source city.

Therefore the WIP72 outer predicate is genuinely inconsistent with its comment,
but the clean demonstrated behavior is already blocked by the downstream
`AI_guardCity` contract.

Under the audit's root standard, that means the outer-only issue is not an
independent F380.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
BROADER INHERITED QUESTION — DELIBERATELY REOPENED, NOT YET NUMBERED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The downstream result exposes a potentially more fundamental inherited
question:

`AI_guardCity` compares group-head counts against `AI_neededDefenders` and, for
the current source group, effectively removes that entire group from the
available-defender count even though successful remote guard assignment later
calls:

    AI_ejectBestDefender(...)

and sends only ONE selected unit from the group.

For a multi-unit donor group, this can be very conservative: the source check
can behave as though all members of the current group leave even though
N-1 members remain after one-unit ejection.

K-Mod's rewritten `AI_guardCity` already contains the group-head accounting,
and Base AdvCiv/current SAS inherit it. K-Mod's city-level
`AI_isDefended`/AdvCiv `AI_countExcessDefenders` also use group-head counting,
so this may reflect a broader deliberate "defensive groups, not units" model
rather than a simple typo.

That broader question therefore needs:
* source-city multi-unit group proof;
* comparison with intended city-defense/group semantics;
* caller behavior when the ejected unit is or is not the group head;
* confirmation that individual remaining group members really remain usable
  city defenders after the split;
* ancestry/design comments.

Until that survives, do NOT relabel it F380 merely to preserve the number.

AUDIT METHODOLOGY NOTE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This retraction is intentional evidence that the deeper audit is not treating
every local mismatch as a finding.

The provisional claim passed:
* local source inspection;
* explicit predicate-definition proof;
* feature-comment comparison;

but failed the stronger:
* "would repairing this root change supported runtime behavior?"
downstream-consumer test.

That is sufficient reason to remove it from the confirmed set.

C031-WIP72 remains historical investigation context only; its F380 section is
superseded by this correction.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F380 / provisional KI#703 — AdvCiv SquareIterator rewrite dropped `!` from the
enemy/vassal test in `AI_airOffenseBaseValue`, so enemy border danger is
ignored while friendly vassal territory is treated as dangerous
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
Current SAS / Base AdvCiv 1.14:

    // Consider threat from nearby enemy territory
    int iBorderDanger = 0;
    for (SquareIter it(kPlot, 1); it.hasNext(); ++it)
    {
        CvPlot const& p = *it;
        if (p.sameArea(kPlot) && p.isOwned())
        {
            if (!p.isRevealed(getTeam()))
                continue;

            if (p.getTeam() != getTeam() &&
                GET_TEAM(p.getTeam()).isVassal(getTeam()))
            {
                int const iDistance = it.currStepDist();

                if (iDistance == 1)
                    iBorderDanger++;

                if (::atWar(p.getTeam(), getTeam()))
                {
                    if (iDistance == 1)
                        iBorderDanger += 2;
                    ...
                }
            }
        }
    }

    iDefenders -= std::min(2, (iBorderDanger + 1) / 3);

The comment says this is "threat from nearby enemy territory."

But the condition enters only when the neighboring team IS a vassal of our
team:

    GET_TEAM(p.getTeam()).isVassal(getTeam())

That is the opposite of the inherited test.

K-Mod:

    if (pLoopPlot->getTeam() != getTeam() &&
        !(GET_TEAM(pLoopPlot->getTeam()).isVassal(getTeam())))

Pre-regression AdvCiv likewise had:

    if (pLoopPlot->getTeam() != getTeam() &&
        !GET_TEAM(pLoopPlot->getTeam()).isVassal(getTeam()))

Thus the intended population is:
    other-team territory that is NOT our vassal

whereas current AdvCiv/SAS uses:
    other-team territory that IS our vassal.

Two semantic inversions follow immediately.

A) Ordinary hostile/non-vassal borders contribute zero
-------------------------------------------------------
A normal enemy team at war with us is not our vassal.

Therefore current code fails the vassal predicate before it can execute either:

    iBorderDanger++;

or the stronger wartime:

    iBorderDanger += 2;

So the dedicated nearby-enemy-territory risk term ignores the normal enemy
border case it was written to measure.

B) Friendly vassal borders contribute danger
---------------------------------------------
A vassal of our team satisfies the current predicate and therefore contributes
the basic adjacency danger:

    if (iDistance == 1)
        iBorderDanger++;

The nested:

    atWar(vassalTeam, ourTeam)

branch is normally contradictory to the vassal relationship itself and is a
useful diagnostic sign of the lost negation. The meaningful current effect is
the basic false-positive border penalty on friendly-vassal territory.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE
----------------
`AI_airOffenseBaseValue` is a live magnitude selector for offensive air-unit
basing.

`AI_airOffensiveCity` scans revealed air bases, calls:

    int iValue = AI_airOffenseBaseValue(kPlot);

and moves to the highest-valued base.

Inside `AI_airOffenseBaseValue`, `iBorderDanger` directly reduces the effective
land-defender count:

    iDefenders -= std::min(2, (iBorderDanger + 1) / 3);

The function then rejects a base entirely when:

    if (iAttackAirCount >= iDefenders || iDefenders <= 0)
        return 0;

and later scales its offensive value by local defense versus enemy offense.

So the lost negation can affect both:
* whether a candidate air base is considered usable at all;
* its value relative to safer alternative bases.

A wartime adjacent-enemy example is particularly direct.

Under K-Mod / correct logic, one adjacent at-war enemy-owned plot contributes:

    +1 basic foreign-border danger
    +2 wartime adjacency danger
    = 3

and therefore:

    (3 + 1) / 3 = 1

effective defender is removed.

Current AdvCiv/SAS sees the enemy as a non-vassal, fails the predicate, and
removes zero defenders from this term.

Conversely, enough adjacent friendly-vassal plots can lower the effective
defender count even though they are not enemy territory.

This is not merely a stale comment: the predicate reversal changes actual air
relocation/base ranking.

ANCESTRY / INTRODUCING CHANGE
-----------------------------
Civ4/K-Mod has the negated vassal test.

Reachable AdvCiv history shows the negation still present immediately before
practical commit:

    practical commit 1916
    085ab2c9b697b5690ba398ef31899cb27e2a8a77
    Title: `"SquareIterator" for loops over tiles within movement range`

That commit mechanically rewrote the old nested coordinate loops into
`SquareIter`.

The exact diff changes:

    if (pLoopPlot->getTeam() != getTeam() &&
        !GET_TEAM(pLoopPlot->getTeam()).isVassal(getTeam()))

to:

    if (p.getTeam() != getTeam() &&
        GET_TEAM(p.getTeam()).isVassal(getTeam()))

The only semantic change needed to create the defect is the missing `!`; it is
not part of the iterator abstraction itself.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains that regression, and current SAS inherits it
unchanged.

Classification:
    inherited AdvCiv iterator-refactor regression.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Restore the negation:

    if (p.getTeam() != getTeam() &&
        !GET_TEAM(p.getTeam()).isVassal(getTeam()))

This matches:
* the function's "enemy territory" comment;
* K-Mod;
* pre-1916 AdvCiv;
* the nested wartime branch.

A later cleanup could separately review whether current diplomacy/team
relations warrant treating other friendly relationships similarly, but that is
policy beyond the regression repair.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTROL CLOSED — RETRACTED WIP72 GARRISON SURPLUS CLAIM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The broader inherited `AI_guardCity` group-head accounting question was also
finished after WIP73.

Although `AI_guardCity` may eject only one defender toward a remote city, the
N-1 members remaining in the donor group are not thereby committed to defend
the source city. The remainder selection group continues its own UnitAI logic
and can leave on the same/later update.

BtS already uses the same lifecycle principle: when a city actually needs one
unit to stay, `AI_guardCity` ejects a defender into a separate staying group
while leaving the remainder group free to continue.

Therefore source retention expressed in group-head / current-group terms is a
conservative group-lifecycle model, not a demonstrated individual-unit-count
bug.

F380 remains correctly retracted for the WIP72 claim and is allocated only to
the independent air-base regression above.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F381 / provisional KI#704 — K-Mod `AI_load` scans an enemy coastal target but
tests transport pathing to water beside the PASSENGER instead of beside that
enemy target, breaking the long-distance boat-shortcut test
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvUnitAI::AI_load` has a special `iMaxTransportPath` check whose own comment
states the contract:

    // Can transport reach enemy in requested time

The current code first selects a transport `pBestUnit`, initializes a transport
pathfinder from that transport group, and scans plots around the TRANSPORT:

    for (SquareIter it(*pBestUnit,
        iMaxTransportPath * pBestUnit->baseMoves());
        !bFoundEnemyPlotInRange && it.hasNext(); ++it)
    {
        CvPlot const& p = *it;

        if (p.isCoastalLand() && p.isOwned() &&
            kOurTeam.AI_mayAttack(p.getTeam()) &&
            p.getArea().getCitiesPerPlayer(p.getOwner()) > 0)
        {
            ...
        }
    }

So `p` is the candidate enemy coastal land plot whose reachability should be
tested.

But inside that exact branch current SAS does:

    FOR_EACH_ADJ_PLOT(getPlot())
    {
        if (!pAdj->isWater())
            continue;

        if (tempFinder.generatePath(*pAdj))
        {
            ...
            if (iPathTurns <= iMaxTransportPath)
                bFoundEnemyPlotInRange = true;
        }
    }

`getPlot()` here is the CURRENT PASSENGER UNIT'S plot (`this`), not the scanned
enemy plot `p`.

Therefore the algorithm asks:

    "Does the selected transport have a short path to water beside the
     passenger's current location?"

while claiming to answer:

    "Can the selected transport reach the scanned enemy coast in time?"

The candidate enemy plot is used only as a boolean existence trigger. Its
actual adjacent sea tiles are never path-tested.

FALSE-NEGATIVE CLASS — INLAND ATTACK STACK
------------------------------------------
This produces a deterministic failure for the most useful boat-shortcut shape.

If the attack stack currently stands on inland land with no adjacent water:

    FOR_EACH_ADJ_PLOT(getPlot())

contains no water tile.

Therefore `bFoundEnemyPlotInRange` stays false regardless of:
* which assault transport `AI_findTransport` selected;
* whether the passenger can walk to that transport within `iMaxPath`;
* whether that transport can reach the target enemy coast within
  `iMaxTransportPath`.

The function then executes:

    if (!bFoundEnemyPlotInRange)
        return false;

and refuses the loading plan.

This is not rescued by `AI_findTransport`.

`AI_findTransport` independently verifies that the passenger can reach the
transport within its allowed loading path:

    generatePath(pTransport->getPlot(), eFlags, true,
        &iPathTurns, iMaxPath)

A land stack can therefore have a valid short walk to a coastal transport even
when its CURRENT tile itself has no adjacent water. The later
`iMaxTransportPath` branch throws that valid candidate away solely because it
looks for water around the passenger's old location.

LIVE CURRENT CALLER
-------------------
Current SAS has one genuine external call that supplies finite
`iMaxTransportPath`: `AI_attackCityMove`.

After selecting `pTargetCity`, it first estimates the ordinary land route:

    generatePath(pTargetCity->getPlot(), eMoveFlags, true, &iPathTurns)

When that route is longer than five turns, it tries to see whether a boat is
faster:

    int iLoadTurns =
        std::max(3, iPathTurns / 3 - 1);

    int iMaxTransportTurns =
        iPathTurns - iLoadTurns - 2;

    if (AI_load(
        UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA,
        MISSIONAI_LOAD_ASSAULT,
        NO_UNITAI,
        -1, -1, -1, -1,
        eMoveFlags,
        iLoadTurns,
        iMaxTransportTurns))
    {
        return;
    }

A simple supported geometry is:

    land path to target city = 12 turns
    allowed walk/load time   = 3 turns
    allowed transport time   = 7 turns

Suppose:
* the attacking stack is currently one or two inland tiles from the coast;
* a valid assault transport is reachable by the stack within those three
  loading turns;
* after pickup, that transport can reach water adjacent to the enemy target
  coast within seven turns.

That is precisely the type of route the caller is trying to discover.

`AI_findTransport` can select the transport because the land group can reach it
within `iLoadTurns`.

F381 then rejects it deterministically if the attacker's CURRENT plot itself
has no adjacent water. The actual enemy coast is never passed to the transport
pathfinder.

FALSE-POSITIVE CLASS — WRONG COAST / SEA ACCESS
-----------------------------------------------
The same source-vs-target error can also accept a route it did not prove.

For a passenger already on coastal land:
* the scan can encounter an enemy coastal plot `p` within the transport's
  geometric SquareIterator radius;
* instead of testing water adjacent to `p`, the code tests water adjacent to
  the passenger;
* the selected transport is usually already near/reachable from that passenger
  coast, so this local path can succeed quickly.

`bFoundEnemyPlotInRange` can therefore become true without any path to the
scanned enemy coast having been established.

This matters around:
* separate seas;
* peninsulas/isthmuses;
* blocked water routes;
* other geometries where geometric proximity does not imply transport-path
  reachability.

The temp pathfinder was added specifically to distinguish actual transport
reachability from geometric range, but the final destination supplied to it is
the wrong end of the trip.

ANCESTRY
--------
BtS/Civ4CE does not have this `iMaxTransportPath` mechanism in `AI_load`.

K-Mod adds the extra transport-range parameter and the long-distance
`AI_attackCityMove` loading calculation.

K-Mod correctly fixed one nearby BtS error by centering the enemy search on the
selected transport:

    // BtS had used plotXY(getX(), getY(), ...)
    pLoopPlot = plotXY(
        pBestUnit->getX(), pBestUnit->getY(), ...);

However, once a candidate enemy coastal `pLoopPlot` is found, K-Mod still uses:

    pAdjacentPlot =
        plotDirection(getX(), getY(), ...);

rather than coordinates from `pLoopPlot`.

Base AdvCiv preserves that source/target mix-up while converting the outer scan
to `SquareIter`.

Current SAS inherits it unchanged.

Classification:
    inherited K-Mod/BBAI transport-target context bug.

WHY THIS IS NOT A MERE HEURISTIC APPROXIMATION
----------------------------------------------
The code already:
* identifies a specific candidate enemy coastal plot;
* creates a real group pathfinder for the selected transport;
* gives that pathfinder the exact requested maximum transport turns.

There is no approximation requirement forcing it to use the passenger's
location. Passing the passenger-adjacent water simply asks the pathfinder the
wrong spatial question.

The function's comment, caller arithmetic and temporary pathfinder all agree
that the destination should represent the enemy coast.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
Current SAS can:
* miss faster naval shortcuts for inland attack stacks;
* force a long overland march despite a nearby assault transport and reachable
  enemy coast;
* accept geometrically-near enemy coast candidates whose actual water approach
  was never path-checked;
* make the K-Mod "boat faster than walking" branch strongly dependent on
  whether the stack happens to be standing directly on the coast at the moment
  of evaluation.

This can also help explain route-selection inconsistency where otherwise
similar attack stacks choose sea transport from coastal staging tiles but fail
to do so from nearby inland tiles.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Path-test water adjacent to the candidate enemy coastal plot `p`, not the
passenger:

    FOR_EACH_ADJ_PLOT(p)
    {
        if (!pAdj->isWater())
            continue;

        if (tempFinder.generatePath(*pAdj))
        {
            int iPathTurns = tempFinder.getPathTurns();
            if (tempFinder.getFinalMoves() == 0)
                iPathTurns++;

            if (iPathTurns <= iMaxTransportPath)
            {
                bFoundEnemyPlotInRange = true;
                break;
            }
        }
    }

The exact macro syntax may need the local const/non-const form supported by the
codebase, but the semantic target must be `p`.

That single change fixes both directions:
* inland passengers no longer require water beside themselves;
* coastal passengers no longer prove enemy reachability by pathing only back
  toward their own coast.

A stronger future cleanup could pass `pTargetCity` / an explicit intended
transport destination from `AI_attackCityMove` rather than scanning for any
attackable coastal city in range. That is a separate precision improvement;
the minimum F381 repair is simply to path toward the candidate enemy coast the
current helper already selected.

CONTROL CLOSED — AI_travelToUpgradeCity ALTERNATIVE-UPGRADE CONCERN
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The current SAS KI#188.3.3 repair asks `getUpgradeCity(true, &eUpgradeUnit)` for
one selected upgrade and then rejects travel if that exact upgrade fails the
real economic `canUpgrade` checks.

Because `getUpgradeCity` can return an early close candidate, it was reasonable
to test whether:
    first upgrade fails ROI
    later upgrade passes ROI
could make the new gate return false without trying the valid alternative.

A tempting current-data branch is:

    Grenadier
        -> Bazooka
        -> Machine Gun

At 0 XP under current SAS prices/ROI gates, Bazooka can be expensive enough to
fail while Machine Gun can be cheap/strong enough to pass.

However the LIVE caller/UnitAI contract kills that example.

Land movement roles that call `AI_travelToUpgradeCity` include:
    UNITAI_ATTACK
    UNITAI_PILLAGE
    UNITAI_EXPLORE

`UNIT_MACHINE_GUN` has:
    bOnlyDefensive = 1

and therefore is not a valid positive-value ATTACK/PILLAGE alternative in
`AI_unitValue` for the relevant travel path.

The defensive Grenadier roles for which Machine Gun is meaningful
(CITY_DEFENSE/CITY_COUNTER etc.) do not use the same travel helper.

Other current branching upgrade chains inspected so far either:
* have equal/similar alternatives;
* present the cheaper/better candidate first;
* or fail to provide two live alternatives for one role that actually calls
  `AI_travelToUpgradeCity`.

So the structural completeness concern remains worth remembering if future XML
adds another branching upgrade graph, but no supported current F382 was
established.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTROL CLOSED — LAUNCHED SPACE CAPITAL TARGET
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The unfinished C031-WIP74 launched-Space-capital concern was also closed.

`CvCity::kill` records whether the destroyed city was the owner's current
capital. After city removal / capital reassignment, if it was the capital it
calls:

    GET_TEAM(eOwner).resetVictoryProgress();

`CvTeam::resetVictoryProgress` clears active victory countdowns and removes the
team's victory projects.

Thus capturing/destroying ANY team member's current capital resets that team's
Space-victory progress at the game-engine boundary.

`AI_pickTargetCity` scans enemy players' current capitals while consulting the
target TEAM's active Space victory countdown, matching that team-wide reset
contract.

The `AI_attackCityMove` emergency check:

    iPathTurns <= iSpaceVictoryCountdown

and its "must attack now" boundary:

    iPathTurns >= iSpaceVictoryCountdown

were traced against the ordinary countdown decrement / victory resolution
lifecycle. No supported off-by-one was established.

No F382 allocated there.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F382 / provisional KI#705 — AdvCiv `AI_pickup` restructuring inverted K-Mod's
city-danger test, so transports reject SAFE remote pickup cities and travel
only toward DANGEROUS ones
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvUnitAI::AI_pickup` has two major cases:

1. if the transport is already in a suitable pickup city, it can wait there
   with `MISSIONAI_PICKUP`;
2. otherwise, it scans the owner's cities and chooses a remote city to travel
   toward for pickup.

The current remote-city branch contains:

    if (GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).AI_plotTargetMissionAIs(
        pLoopCity->getPlot(), MISSIONAI_PICKUP, getGroup()) <
        (iCount + cargoSpace() - 1) / cargoSpace())
    {
        if (!pLoopCity->AI_isDanger())
            continue;

        int iPathTurns;
        if (atPlot(pLoopCity->plot()) ||
            !generatePath(pLoopCity->getPlot(),
                MOVE_AVOID_ENEMY_WEIGHT_3,
                true, &iPathTurns))
        {
            continue;
        }

        ...
        pBestPickupPlot = pLoopCity->plot();
    }

This explicitly discards a remote city when it is NOT in danger.

Therefore the only remote cities allowed through this gate are cities for
which:

    pLoopCity->AI_isDanger() == true.

That is the opposite of the inherited K-Mod behavior and the opposite of the
obvious naval-pickup safety policy.

K-MOD CONTROL
-------------
K-Mod's same branch is:

    if (AI_plotTargetMissionAIs(...) < ...)
    {
        if (!(pLoopCity->AI_isDanger()))
        {
            if (!atPlot(pLoopCity->plot()) &&
                generatePath(pLoopCity->plot(),
                    MOVE_AVOID_ENEMY_WEIGHT_3,
                    true, &iPathTurns))
            {
                ...
                pBestPickupPlot = pLoopCity->plot();
            }
        }
    }

So K-Mod travels toward the pickup city only when:

    !pLoopCity->AI_isDanger()

Current AdvCiv/SAS does the precise complement.

This is not a change in the meaning of `AI_isDanger`; the two code versions
surround the same pathing/value logic and use the same city object.

ASYMMETRY WITH THE CURRENT-CITY BRANCH
--------------------------------------
The error produces a particularly clean behavioral contradiction inside one
function.

At the beginning of `AI_pickup`, if the transport is ALREADY in an owned,
suitable city, the code can execute:

    getGroup()->pushMission(
        MISSION_SKIP,
        ...,
        MISSIONAI_PICKUP,
        pCity->plot());

and wait for units there.

That current-city branch does NOT require the city to be dangerous.

Therefore:

    safe City A + transport already at City A
        -> transport may wait and pick units up there

while:

    same safe City A + transport one or more turns away
        -> remote scan executes
           if (!CityA.AI_isDanger()) continue;
        -> transport refuses to travel there.

The city is considered a valid pickup location only after the transport
somehow reaches it by another mechanism.

LIVE CALLERS
------------
Current SAS uses `AI_pickup` broadly.

Assault transports:
* `AI_pickup(UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY, true, 5)`
* `AI_pickup(UNITAI_ATTACK, true, 5)`
* later ATTACK_CITY / ATTACK / COUNTER pickup searches with ranges commonly
  3 or 7 turns

Settler transports:
* `AI_pickup(UNITAI_CITY_DEFENSE)`
* `AI_pickup(UNITAI_SETTLE, true)`
* `AI_pickup(UNITAI_WORKER)`

Special transports:
* Missionary pickup
* Spy pickup
* Missile-air pickup

Thus this is not a dormant helper or a single unusual role.

A routine assault example is enough:

1. a safe rear/coastal city has several available `UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY` units;
2. an empty Assault transport is a few turns away;
3. no other pickup group has already claimed enough capacity;
4. `AI_considerPickup` accepts the city;
5. `iCount > 0`;
6. the city is safe, so current AdvCiv/SAS executes:

       if (!pLoopCity->AI_isDanger())
           continue;

7. the transport never even pathfinds toward that staging city.

If the same transport later happens to enter that city, the current-city branch
can immediately wait for those same units.

DANGEROUS-CITY FALSE POSITIVE
-----------------------------
The inversion is two-sided.

After the earlier acquisition/enemy-power filter, a sufficiently established
city that is currently dangerous can reach the pathfinding branch.

For Assault transports, `AI_considerPickup` can still accept a dangerous city
when it considers the city adequately defended.

Current code then permits the transport to path toward that dangerous city,
using `MOVE_AVOID_ENEMY_WEIGHT_3` but not rejecting the city itself.

K-Mod did the opposite: danger prevented the remote pickup trip.

So the regression both:
* suppresses ordinary safe logistical pickup;
* enables precisely the endangered destination K-Mod tried to avoid.

The outer condition:

    city age > 15 OR enemy power in area == 0

does not repair the inversion. Any older city passes the first arm regardless
of current area enemy power.

ANCESTRY / INTRODUCING CHANGE
-----------------------------
BtS/BBAI/K-Mod history already contains the safe-city policy.

The reachable AdvCiv history identifies the regression precisely:

    practical commit 1583
    715fa87579778a04e8da1adb5a6f1170f141aed5
    "Several improvements to AI worker production and assignment"

That commit substantially flattened/reformatted `AI_pickup`.

Before the rewrite, the inherited logic was:

    if (!(pLoopCity->AI_isDanger()))
    {
        if (... generatePath ...)
        {
            ...
        }
    }

The rewrite transformed that into early-continue style:

    if (!pLoopCity->AI_isDanger())
        continue;

    if (... !generatePath ...)
        continue;

The early-continue conversion failed to negate the old enclosing condition.
To preserve:

    if (SAFE) { body }

the equivalent guard is:

    if (DANGER) continue;

but the commit emitted:

    if (SAFE) continue.

This behavioral inversion is unrelated to the commit's advertised Worker
production/assignment changes.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the regression.
Current AdvCiv-SAS inherits it unchanged.

Classification:
    inherited AdvCiv control-flow-flattening regression.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
The AI can:
* leave Assault transports idle/elsewhere instead of collecting invasion
  troops from safe coastal staging cities;
* fail to collect Settlers, Workers or escorts from ordinary safe ports;
* fail to route special transports to safe Missionary/Spy/Missile staging
  cities;
* create inconsistent logistics where a port is valid for pickup if the ship
  is already there but invalid if the ship must travel there;
* preferentially allow remote pickup travel toward dangerous cities rather
  than safe ones.

This can directly reduce naval invasion assembly and island logistics.

The effect is particularly broad because `AI_pickup` is a shared transport
primitive rather than one role-specific heuristic.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Restore K-Mod's safe-city contract:

    if (pLoopCity->AI_isDanger())
        continue;

then retain the current early-continue structure for the path test.

Conceptually:

    if (targetPickupGroups < requiredPickupGroups)
    {
        if (pLoopCity->AI_isDanger())
            continue;

        int iPathTurns;
        if (atPlot(pLoopCity->plot()) ||
            !generatePath(...))
        {
            continue;
        }

        ...
    }

This is the exact logical translation of K-Mod's older:

    if (!AI_isDanger())
    {
        if (generatePath(...))
        {
            ...
        }
    }

No broader redesign is required.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F383 / provisional KI#706 — SAS `AI_ferryWorkers` hard area-capacity gate
counts its own cargo Worker as already delivered at the destination, so the
transport can reject the island immediately before the branch that unloads it
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
Current SAS practical-6060 added a hard landmass-capacity guard to
`CvUnitAI::AI_ferryWorkers`:

    int iAreaHave =
        kOwner.AI_totalAreaUnitAIs(
            pLoopCity->getArea(), UNITAI_WORKER);

    // advc.113: Don't count the workers in cargo as available
    if (!getPlot().isWater() &&
        pLoopCity->isArea(getArea()))
    {
        iAreaHave -= (2 * iWorkers) / 3;
        FAssert(iAreaHave >= 0);
    }

    int const iAreaNeeded =
        kOwner.AI_neededWorkers(pLoopCity->getArea());

    if (iAreaHave >= iAreaNeeded)
        continue;

The newly added `continue` happens BEFORE pathfinding, scoring and the eventual
arrival branch:

    if (atPlot(pBestPlot))
    {
        unloadAll();
        ...
        return true;
    }

The inherited `(2 * iWorkers) / 3` adjustment is not an exact exclusion of
cargo Workers.

For one cargo Worker:

    (2 * 1) / 3 == 0

so the transport subtracts nothing.

CARGO WORKERS REALLY ARE IN THE AREA COUNTER
--------------------------------------------
`CvPlayerAI::AI_totalAreaUnitAIs` is:

    return kArea.getNumTrainAIUnits(...) +
           kArea.getNumAIUnits(...);

`CvUnit::setXY` moves cargo units together with their transport:

    if (pLoopUnit->getTransportUnit() == this)
        pLoopUnit->setXY(iX, iY, ...);

and every moved UnitAI updates the new plot area's counter:

    pNewPlot->getArea().changeNumAIUnits(
        getOwner(), AI_getUnitAIType(), 1);

Therefore, when a Settler transport enters a destination CITY on an island, a
Worker still aboard that ship is counted by:

    AI_totalAreaUnitAIs(destinationArea, UNITAI_WORKER)

even though it has not unloaded and cannot work the island while remaining
cargo.

CURRENT ONE-WORKER FAILURE
--------------------------
Consider a destination island for which:

    AI_neededWorkers(destinationArea) == 1

and, before the ferry arrives:

    actual land Workers in destinationArea == 0.

A Settler transport carries one Worker to that city's port.

Before arrival, while the ship is still on water / another area:
* that cargo Worker is not counted as a Worker in the destination land area;
* `iAreaHave == 0`;
* `iAreaNeeded == 1`;
* the destination passes the new hard-capacity gate;
* `AI_ferryWorkers` can choose it and sail there.

After the ship reaches the destination city, the cargo Worker has moved with
the ship to that land plot and now contributes to the destination area's
UnitAI count.

On the next `AI_settlerSeaMove` update:

    iWorkerCount > 0
    iSettlerCount == 0

is already sufficient to call `AI_ferryWorkers`.

For the destination city:

    iAreaHave = 1   // includes the still-loaded Worker

The inherited correction does:

    iAreaHave -= (2 * 1) / 3
               = 0

so:

    iAreaHave == 1
    iAreaNeeded == 1

and the new practical-6060 test executes:

    if (iAreaHave >= iAreaNeeded)
        continue;

The destination is discarded before:

    if (atPlot(pLoopCity->plot()))
        ...

and therefore before the later:

    if (atPlot(pBestPlot))
        unloadAll();

which is the helper's ordinary delivery mechanism.

FALLBACK DOES NOT RE-DISCOVER LOCAL ISLAND WORK
-----------------------------------------------
If the city loop produces no other destination, the old advc.040 fallback may
scan individual plots.

But when the transport is in a city on the same destination landmass, the
fallback deliberately rejects those local-area plots through:

    if (kPlot.getArea().getCitiesPerPlayer(owner) > 0 ||
        AI_neededWorkers(kPlot.getArea()) <= 0 ||
        AI_totalAreaUnitAIs(kPlot.getArea(), UNITAI_WORKER) > 0)
    {
        bool bValid =
            (pCurrentCity != NULL &&
             !kPlot.isArea(getArea()));

        ...
        if (!bValid)
            continue;
    }

For the current island:

    kPlot.isArea(getArea()) == true

so `bValid` is false and the scan skips its plots.

Thus the second half of `AI_ferryWorkers` cannot compensate by noticing that
the still-loaded Worker has work on the island.

CALLER LIFECYCLE
----------------
`AI_settlerSeaMove` calls `AI_ferryWorkers` whenever:

    iWorkerCount > 0 &&
    no incoming LOAD_SETTLER mission &&
    (isFull() || iSettlerCount == 0)

A Worker-only Settler transport therefore re-enters this logic after reaching
the delivery city.

There is no generic automatic unload on arrival.

If `AI_ferryWorkers` returns false:
* the normal later pickup/role/retreat/safety logic runs;
* none of those branches guarantees unloading the Worker merely because its
  current landmass needs it;
* with no alternative target, the transport can skip with the needed Worker
  still aboard and reconsider again next turn.

The new hard capacity can therefore convert:
    "the Worker we just delivered fills the deficit"
into:
    "the area already has enough Workers, so do not deliver this Worker."

HISTORY PROVIDES AN INTERNAL CONFIRMING CONTROL
-----------------------------------------------
The ancestry is unusually strong because SAS itself discovered the same
counting problem in a neighboring new helper one practical commit later.

Practical commit 6060:
    71ff2a0ba7...
introduced:
* the hard `iAreaHave >= iAreaNeeded` rejection in `AI_ferryWorkers`;
* `AI_unloadSettlerCargoForDestination`.

The first version of the new destination helper likewise used:

    iWorkersExisting =
        AI_totalAreaUnitAIs(destinationArea, UNITAI_WORKER);

without excluding cargo Workers already physically at the destination.

Practical commit 6061:
    08cb9d272e...

explicitly fixed that neighboring bug:

    // Cargo Workers may already be included in the
    // destination-area count when the transport reaches its city.
    // Count them separately so the exact shortage below can exclude them.

It then counts ALL cargo Workers and, when at the destination, executes:

    iWorkersExisting =
        std::max(0,
            iWorkersExisting - iCargoWorkers);

That is exactly the missing semantic correction in `AI_ferryWorkers`.

However practical 6061 left the inherited:

    iAreaHave -= (2 * iWorkers) / 3;

unchanged in the ferry hard-capacity path.

So current source contains:
* one destination Worker-demand helper that correctly removes all onboard
  Workers from the "already existing" count;
* one adjacent destination Worker-demand helper that can remove zero of one
  onboard Worker before a hard rejection.

Classification:
    SAS-local practical-6060 worker-ferry regression, with a partial sibling
    repair in practical 6061 that did not reach `AI_ferryWorkers`.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
Current SAS can:
* transport the exact Worker an island needs;
* reach the correct destination;
* count that still-loaded Worker as evidence that the island no longer needs
  the Worker;
* refuse to execute its own arrival `unloadAll()` branch;
* leave the needed Worker aboard or redirect the ship elsewhere.

The one-Worker case is particularly important because secondary islands often
have an exact demand of one, and integer `(2 * iWorkers) / 3` provides no
correction at all there.

The same under-subtraction can affect larger cargo:
    2 cargo Workers -> subtract 1
    3 cargo Workers -> subtract 2

so one onboard Worker is systematically left in `iAreaHave` for every positive
cargo count under this formula.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
For the new HARD area-capacity test, cargo Workers on this transport must not be
counted as already delivered.

Use the same exact semantic correction already implemented in
`AI_unloadSettlerCargoForDestination`.

When the transport is physically in the candidate destination land area:

    iAreaHave = std::max(0, iAreaHave - iWorkers);

rather than:

    iAreaHave -= (2 * iWorkers) / 3;

At minimum this exact exclusion should govern the hard:

    iAreaHave >= iAreaNeeded

decision.

If the inherited two-thirds adjustment is still desired for the older SOFT
scoring heuristic, keep a separately named weighted count for that purpose.
Do not reuse a deliberately fractional availability estimate as an exact
capacity count.

A cleaner design would centralize "existing Workers excluding cargo on this
transport" so both:
* `AI_ferryWorkers`, and
* `AI_unloadSettlerCargoForDestination`
share the same definition.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F384 / provisional KI#707 — AdvCiv ProbabilityTypes refactor inverted the
Carrier's land-threat retreat condition: `!= PROBABILITY_REAL` instead of
`>= PROBABILITY_REAL`
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
Current SAS / Base AdvCiv 1.14:

    void CvUnitAI::AI_carrierSeaMove()
    {
        ...
        if (AI_isThreatenedFromLand() != PROBABILITY_REAL)
        {
            if (AI_retreatToCity(true))
                return;
            if (AI_retreatToCity())
                return;
            if (AI_safety())
                return;
        }
        ...
    }

This is the only analogous naval role using `!= PROBABILITY_REAL`.

Current nearby roles use the expected threshold:

    AI_attackSeaMove
    AI_reserveSeaMove
    AI_escortSeaMove
    AI_exploreSeaMove
    AI_assaultSeaMove
    AI_settlerSeaMove
    AI_missionarySeaMove
    AI_spySeaMove
    AI_missileCarrierSeaMove
        -> AI_isThreatenedFromLand() >= PROBABILITY_REAL

The helper's enum is ordered:

    NO_PROBABILITY      = -1
    PROBABILITY_LOW     = 0
    PROBABILITY_REAL    = 1
    PROBABILITY_HIGH    = 2

Therefore the Carrier test means:

    NO   -> run emergency retreat block
    LOW  -> run emergency retreat block
    REAL -> SKIP emergency retreat block
    HIGH -> run emergency retreat block

That is not a sensible threat threshold and is the exact complement of the
important ordinary-threat state.

LIVE HELPER CONTRACT
--------------------
`AI_isThreatenedFromLand()` returns:

    if water:
        NO_PROBABILITY

    if in city:
        if city evacuating:
            HIGH
        if city safe:
            NO
        otherwise:
            damaged ? LOW : REAL

    outside city:
        if enemyOffense * 2 > ourDefense:
            REAL
        else if enemyOffense * 4 > ourDefense:
            LOW
        else:
            NO

So an ordinary, full-health naval unit sitting in an owned city that
`AI_isSafe()` does NOT consider safe receives:

    PROBABILITY_REAL.

That is exactly the state current `AI_carrierSeaMove` excludes from its urgent
retreat/safety block.

The Carrier then proceeds into:
* healing;
* grouping;
* carrier transport movement;
* blockade;
* assault-transport shadowing;
* upgrade travel;

before the generic late retreat/safety fallbacks.

Thus the dedicated "threat from land" priority is defeated at the threat level
it was designed to catch.

ANCESTRY / INTRODUCING REFACTOR
--------------------------------
K-Mod's Carrier code did not use ProbabilityTypes. It directly computed local
land defense and enemy offense and entered the emergency retreat block when:

    iEnemyOffense > iOurDefense / 2

(with damaged units treated more cautiously by scaling defense).

AdvCiv later extracted duplicate naval threat code into
`AI_isThreatenedFromLand`.

Immediately before the ProbabilityTypes conversion, the Carrier had the same
boolean helper contract as the other naval roles:

    if (getPlot().isCity(true))
    {
        if (AI_isThreatenedFromLand())
        {
            retreat/safety...
        }
    }

Reachable pre-SAS AdvCiv practical commit 2612,
SHA:

    fc7640933b544f0f943f527e2edc08999da1dc00

changed the helper return type from:

    bool CvUnitAI::AI_isThreatenedFromLand() const

to:

    ProbabilityTypes CvUnitAI::AI_isThreatenedFromLand() const

and converted the call sites.

For Spy and the ordinary naval roles, the old boolean condition became:

    AI_isThreatenedFromLand() >= PROBABILITY_REAL

which preserves the helper's old strong-threat meaning while allowing
LOW to represent a deliberately weaker state.

The same patch converted the Carrier to:

    AI_isThreatenedFromLand() != PROBABILITY_REAL

instead.

The diff therefore gives an unusually strong introducing-control:
* same helper conversion;
* same retreat body;
* sibling callers converted to `>=`;
* Carrier alone converted to `!=`.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the Carrier condition.
Current AdvCiv-SAS inherits it unchanged.

Classification:
    inherited AdvCiv ProbabilityTypes/refactor regression.

CURRENT-SAS CONSEQUENCE
-----------------------
Take an undamaged Carrier in an owned city that is currently unsafe because
nearby enemy land offense is sufficiently threatening.

The helper returns:

    PROBABILITY_REAL.

Expected/K-Mod behavior:
    immediately prioritize retreat to a safer/primary city or safety plot.

Current AdvCiv/SAS behavior:
    `REAL != REAL` is false;
    skip the emergency retreat block;
    continue into ordinary Carrier logic.

A loaded/escorted Carrier can therefore proceed toward:
* a carrier-sea transport target;
* blockade behavior;
* shadowing an assault fleet;

instead of first responding to the land threat that the inherited naval safety
block was written to handle.

The inverse states are also diagnostic:
* `NO_PROBABILITY != REAL` is true, so a completely safe/no-threat state enters
  the emergency retreat code unnecessarily;
* `LOW != REAL` is true, so the weaker state that the ProbabilityTypes refactor
  created specifically to distinguish from a real threat also enters it.

Some of those false-positive calls can harmlessly fail and fall through, but
they confirm that the predicate is not expressing a threshold. The
false-negative `REAL` state is the direct gameplay defect.

`PROBABILITY_HIGH`, used for an evacuating city, correctly enters the block
under both `!= REAL` and the intended `>= REAL`; this does not rescue the
ordinary REAL case.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Make Carrier consistent with the extracted threat contract and the sibling
naval roles:

    if (AI_isThreatenedFromLand() >= PROBABILITY_REAL)

This:
* catches REAL ordinary threats;
* catches HIGH evacuating-city threats;
* ignores LOW/NO states;
* matches the semantic conversion used by the other naval callers.

No broader redesign is required.

F380 COMPANION REPAIR NOTE — LATENT REVEALED-ROUTE ENUM BOOLEAN
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The final F384 sweep found another genuine historical defect adjacent to F380,
but it is CURRENTLY MASKED BY F380 and therefore is deliberately NOT assigned
a separate finding number.

Inside the same `AI_airOffenseBaseValue` enemy-border branch:

    else if (iDistance == 2 && p.
        getRevealedRouteType(getTeam()))
    {
        iBorderDanger += 2;
    }

K-Mod used:

    pLoopPlot->isRoute()

AdvCiv practical commit 1396,
SHA beginning:

    662e020a...

("Tentative changes to make naval invasions easier to intercept")

replaced that with a revealed-route query but used the returned `RouteTypes`
enum directly as a C++ boolean.

Civ4 dynamic route enums use:

    NO_ROUTE = -1

and current route XML orders real routes as:

    ROAD     = 0
    RAILROAD = 1
    ...

So as a boolean:

    NO_ROUTE (-1) -> true
    ROAD      (0) -> false
    RAILROAD  (1) -> true

The intended test must be explicit, e.g.:

    p.getRevealedRouteType(getTeam()) != NO_ROUTE

or equivalent revealed-route semantics.

WHY NO SEPARATE F385
--------------------
Current F380's lost vassal negation prevents ordinary enemy territory from
entering the enclosing branch at all:

    current:
        other team && IS our vassal

rather than:

        other team && IS NOT our vassal.

The nested route test then additionally requires:

    atWar(p.getTeam(), getTeam())

A normal vassal/master pair cannot supply the ordinary hostile state the
border-danger code is meant to measure.

Thus F380 currently masks the route-enum inversion for the meaningful enemy
case. It has no independent current runtime consequence proven beyond F380.

However, repairing F380 by restoring the missing `!isVassal(...)` would
immediately expose this older route predicate:
* an enemy tile with NO route would be treated as routed;
* an enemy tile with a ROAD (route enum 0) would be treated as unrouted.

Therefore the F380 implementation review should fix BOTH predicates together.

This remains a mandatory companion repair / latent historical defect, not a
manufactured F385.

F385 / provisional KI#708 — AdvCiv `AI_guardCitySite` replaced K-Mod's exact
mission-target check with an adjacent-only check, so a defender targeting the
city-site tile itself does not prevent duplicate guards
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

K-Mod rejects a planned city site when another group already has
`MISSIONAI_GUARD_CITY` targeted at that exact site:

    AI_plotTargetMissionAIs(pLoopPlot, MISSIONAI_GUARD_CITY, getGroup()) == 0

AdvCiv advc.300 comments out that exact check and says:

    // Need to check the adjacent tiles too

but implements only an adjacent-plot loop. `FOR_EACH_ADJ_PLOT(kLoopPlot)`
enumerates the eight neighboring tiles, not `kLoopPlot` itself, and the mission
query uses range zero by default. An existing mission targeted at the exact
city-site tile is therefore invisible to the new duplicate check.

The same rewritten function can still create precisely that omitted state.
`pBetterGuardPlot` starts as the city-site tile and changes only if an adjacent
plot receives a strictly positive guard value. On an ordinary revealed flat
neighborhood with no defensive/visibility bonus, every adjacent candidate can
remain at zero and the queued `MISSIONAI_GUARD_CITY` target stays the exact city
site.

A second eligible group then scans only the eight adjacent tiles, fails to see
the first exact-site mission, and can be sent redundantly to the same planned
city site. Current live callers include ordinary combat-unit movement such as
`AI_collateralMove` and `AI_counterMove`, so multiple groups can reach the
state.

A second internal control reinforces the omission. Inside the adjacency-only
loop the rewrite contains:

    if (pAdj == pBestGuardPlot)
        iGuardValue += 1; // tie-breaker

At that point `pBestGuardPlot` is the center city-site tile and `pAdj` is
necessarily adjacent, so the comparison is unreachable. The rewrite's logic
thus treats the center as though it were in the candidate neighborhood while
the iterator excludes it.

ANCESTRY
--------
* K-Mod: exact planned city-site mission target checked.
* Base AdvCiv 1.14: advc.300 replaces it with adjacent-only coordination.
* Current AdvCiv-SAS: inherits the AdvCiv structure unchanged.

Classification: inherited AdvCiv advc.300 mission-target scope regression.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
The AI can send multiple defenders to the same future city site instead of
spreading them across separate sites, wasting fogbusting/anti-Barbarian
coverage and diverting extra defenders. Duplicate suppression depends on
whether the first guard happened to choose the exact site or an adjacent tile.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Check the center and adjacent plots. The conservative repair is to restore the
old exact-site mission check and then scan adjacent tiles. Alternatively, use
the existing mission-target helper with range 1 around the planned site if that
matches the intended area semantics. The unreachable center tie-breaker should
also be removed or the center explicitly included in position scoring.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CLEAN CONTROL — AI_assaultSeaReinforce MASTER-TEAM OPTIMIZATION
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

K-Mod enters its final "assist master in attacking" block only when:

    GET_TEAM(getTeam()).isAVassal()

and finds the master through a loop over `isVassal`.

AdvCiv replaces the loop with:

    TeamTypes eMasterTeam = GET_TEAM(getTeam()).getMasterTeam();
    if (eMasterTeam != NO_TEAM &&
        GET_TEAM(getTeam()).isOpenBorders(eMasterTeam))
    {
        ...
    }

`getMasterTeam()` deliberately returns the team's own ID when it is free, so
this initially looked as though the vassal-only policy had been broadened to
all civs.

The state contract closes the concern. `CvTeam::reset` clears every
`m_abOpenBorders` entry, including self. `isOpenBorders(eTeam)` is a direct
array lookup and no self-open-borders initialization was found. Therefore a
free team gets:

    eMasterTeam == getTeam()
    isOpenBorders(getTeam()) == false

and does not enter the assistance block. A real vassal returns its external
master and can pass the ordinary vassal/master open-borders state.

No F386.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CLEAN CONTROL — F385 / SETTLER EXACT-SITE SAFETY INTERACTION
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

F385 established that advc.300 city-site guards can stand on an adjacent
fogbusting tile while the duplicate-guard check accidentally omits the exact
center site.

A neighboring Settler check looked inconsistent because an undefended Settler
in `AI_found` recognizes `MISSIONAI_GUARD_CITY` only when the mission target is
the exact founding tile, not merely adjacent.

That stricter test is justified: an adjacent fogbuster does not physically
defend the Settler after it steps onto the founding tile. Treating an adjacent
mission as a valid on-tile escort would weaken Settler safety. This is therefore
not an F385 sibling.

NOT claim they are all saturated.

F380 COMPANION-REPAIR EXPANSION (NO NEW FINDING NUMBER)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The deeper inheritance sweep found a second latent problem inside the same
`AI_airOffenseBaseValue` branch already broken by F380.

K-Mod/current code contains a distance-2 wartime route term, but the surrounding
search radius is only 1. In current AdvCiv this is:

    for (SquareIter it(kPlot, 1); ...)
        ...
        else if (iDistance == 2 && ...)

so the distance-2 arm is unreachable.

This is older than the SquareIterator conversion: K-Mod's coordinate loop also
used `iRange = 1` while retaining the distance-2 arm.

Combined with the already-recorded bare revealed-route enum bug:

    p.getRevealedRouteType(getTeam())

(where `NO_ROUTE=-1` is truthy and ROAD=0 is false), a complete F380 repair
should review all three conditions together:
1. restore `!isVassal(...)` for normal hostile territory;
2. compare revealed route explicitly with `NO_ROUTE`;
3. if the inherited distance-2 route-danger policy is intended, use a search
   radius that can actually reach distance 2.

No separate F386 is allocated because current F380 prevents the ordinary enemy
state from reaching the nested wartime branch in the first place.

`AI_leaveAttack`

The inherited comparison between defend-capable group heads and the departing

The apparent state hazard where the helper queues movement toward a remote

`AI_nextCityToImproveAirlift`

This helper ranks candidate cities partly through `AI_totalBestBuildValue`,

cache while land Workers use the custom `CvUnitAI::AI_bestCityBuild` policy.
This is another live consequence of EXISTING KI#213, not a new F386.

AdvCiv removed some runtime legality checks from Great Work / Trade execution

`AI_spreadCorporationAirlift`

The airlift mission uses generic `MISSIONAI_SPREAD` while ordinary corporation
movement coordinates through `MISSIONAI_SPREAD_CORPORATION`. That tag mismatch

rejects a destination once the same executive unit type is physically there.

`AI_assaultSeaReinforce` master-team optimization
-------------------------------------------------
AdvCiv replaced K-Mod's explicit "team that we are a vassal of" search with

`isOpenBorders(eMasterTeam)` test prevents ordinary non-vassals from entering
the master-assistance branch. No F386.

F380 companion repair expansion
-------------------------------
The deeper inherited reconciliation found two additional defects inside the
nested wartime-border portion of `AI_airOffenseBaseValue`, both currently
masked by F380's enclosing lost-vassal-negation defect and therefore not given
independent finding numbers:

1. `getRevealedRouteType(getTeam())` is used as a raw boolean. Dynamic route

2. Current code iterates `SquareIter(kPlot, 1)` but still contains an
   `iDistance == 2` route-danger branch inherited from the older radius-2
   search. That branch is unreachable under the current iterator radius.

Fixing F380 should therefore review all three pieces together:
* restore `!isVassal(...)`;
* use explicit revealed-route presence semantics;
* restore/reconcile the distance-2 search radius if that term remains desired.

POST-WIP82 RECONCILIATION — ROUTE / MOVEMENT / LATE ACTION CONTROLS
