`AI_routeCity` / advc.121 midpoint behavior
-------------------------------------------
A potentially serious-looking queue shape was traced through the actual mission
engine before being judged.

When advc.121 decides a Worker may already be in the middle of an incomplete
city-to-city route, its comment says:

    Don't move to kLoopCity first then.

The function can nevertheless queue:

    MISSION_ROUTE_TO -> kLoopCity
    MISSION_ROUTE_TO -> pRouteToCity

This initially looked like an accidental backtrack to the first endpoint.
`CvSelectionGroup::MISSION_ROUTE_TO`, however, executes `groupRoadTo`, and
`groupRoadTo` first attempts the best route build on the Worker's CURRENT plot
before pathing toward the mission endpoint.

The advc.121 distinction is therefore between:
* a plain MOVE_TO back to kLoopCity, which would waste travel without completing
  the route; and
* a ROUTE_TO back toward kLoopCity, which builds/completes the unfinished half
  while moving.

The queued shape is consistent with finishing an incomplete connection from a
midpoint. No F386.

Movement-family inherited controls
----------------------------------
The previously unnamed movement members were deliberately reopened against
K-Mod/Base rather than assumed safe:

* `AI_animalMove`
  - advc.309's `bAttackAttempted` prevents a second random attack attempt while
    still allowing a cornered animal to attack after patrol failure.
  - the damage-scaled heal chance is explicit animal policy; no polarity bug.

* `AI_barbAttackMove`
  - advc.300 replaces coarse civilization-city thresholds with a deterministic
    birthmark/aggression curve and area-city context. The major branch changes
    are policy, not an execution-state or sentinel regression found here.

* `AI_paratrooperMove`
  - the hostile-state change from potential enemy to actual `atWar` matches the
    accompanying contract that the unit should not already occupy undeclared
    enemy territory. No live branch inversion established.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F386 / provisional KI#709 — advc.139 replaced Pirate city/fort-only healing
with a land-threat helper that returns NO threat on water, so lightly damaged
Privateers can stop and heal in open sea
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
K-Mod `AI_pirateSeaMove` only offers the early heal action when the Pirate is in
an actual city/fort-like naval base with friendly defense and no nearby danger:

    if (plot()->isCity(true) &&
        AI_localDefenceStrength(...) > 0 &&
        !AI_getAnyPlotDanger(...))
    {
        if (AI_heal())
            return;
    }

Base AdvCiv/current SAS retain the original explanatory comment:

    // heal in defended, unthreatened forts and cities

and show the immediately preceding city/base expression as commented code:

    /*if ((kPlot.isCity() && kPlot.AI_getPlotCity()->AI_isSafe()) ||
        (kPlot.isCity(true) && ...localDefence... && ...no danger...))*/
    // advc.139: Probably better than the above
    if (AI_isThreatenedFromLand() <= PROBABILITY_LOW)
    {
        if (AI_heal())
            return;
    }

The extracted helper's first live condition is:

    if (getPlot().isWater())
        return NO_PROBABILITY;

and the ProbabilityTypes ordering used by this file is:

    NO_PROBABILITY   = -1
    PROBABILITY_LOW  = 0
    PROBABILITY_REAL = 1
    PROBABILITY_HIGH = 2

Therefore every ordinary water tile satisfies:

    NO_PROBABILITY <= PROBABILITY_LOW

and enters the early Pirate healing branch.

This is a scope change, not merely a changed danger threshold. The old condition
required a defended city/fort; the new condition explicitly includes open sea.

RUNTIME PROOF — SINGLE PRIVATEER
--------------------------------
`AI_heal()` immediately delegates a one-unit group to:

    AI_singleUnitHeal()

whose default parameters are:

    iMaxTurnsExposed = 1
    iMaxTurnsOutsideCity = 3

For a non-Barbarian single unit outside city-heal territory,
`AI_singleUnitHeal` heals whenever:

    iHealTurns <= iMaxTurnsExposed

i.e. one exposed healing turn is sufficient.

`CvUnit::healRate` gives a non-friendly, non-enemy tile the standard neutral
heal rate:

    NEUTRAL_HEAL_RATE + getExtraNeutralHeal()

and the inherited BtS/Civ4CE GlobalDefines value is:

    NEUTRAL_HEAL_RATE = 10

Current SAS does not override that define in its supplied XML set.

So a routine single Privateer on neutral/open water with, for example, 10 HP of
damage has:

    healTurns() == 1

and the current call chain becomes:

    AI_pirateSeaMove
      -> AI_isThreatenedFromLand() == NO_PROBABILITY (because water)
      -> NO <= LOW, enter early heal branch
      -> AI_heal()
      -> AI_singleUnitHeal()
      -> push MISSION_HEAL
      -> return from AI_pirateSeaMove

K-Mod's old caller never reached `AI_heal()` on that open-water plot because
`plot()->isCity(true)` was false.

This exact one-turn exposed-heal behavior is not new to current SAS and does not
save the refactor: K-Mod's own single-unit `AI_heal` logic also allowed a
one-turn heal when called outside a city. The important protective contract was
the Pirate CALLER's city/fort gate, and advc.139 removed that gate.

INTERACTION WITH PIRATE-SPECIFIC DAMAGE LOGIC
---------------------------------------------
The broadening changes real action priority, not only which helper is queried.
Later in `AI_pirateSeaMove`, current SAS calls `AI_pirateBlockade`, whose damaged
open-sea logic says roughly:

    if not in immediate stronger-enemy danger and damaged and
       plot not owned and not adjacent owned:
        try AI_retreatToCity(...)
        otherwise skip

That logic is reached only after the new early `AI_heal` branch.

A lightly damaged single Pirate on remote neutral water can therefore now heal
in place and return BEFORE the Pirate-specific retreat/blockade logic has a
chance to route it toward a base or make the normal blockade decision.

For damage requiring more than one neutral turn, `AI_singleUnitHeal()` normally
returns false under its default exposed threshold and the later Pirate logic
still runs. The regression therefore has a clean ordinary boundary rather than
requiring an exotic state:

    <= 10 damage at standard neutral heal rate -> can heal in open sea early
    larger damage -> usually falls through to normal Pirate damage handling

Extra neutral-heal bonuses can widen the affected damage range.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod:
* Pirate early healing explicitly requires `plot()->isCity(true)` plus defense
  and no nearby danger.

AdvCiv advc.139:
* extracts duplicated naval land-threat tests into `AI_isThreatenedFromLand`;
* current source retains the old city/base expression immediately above the new
  helper call and the comment "heal in defended, unthreatened forts and cities";
* the helper deliberately returns `NO_PROBABILITY` for all water plots;
* Pirate uses the unique low-threat predicate `<= PROBABILITY_LOW`.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS inherit that extracted condition.

Classification:
    inherited AdvCiv helper-extraction scope regression.

RELATION TO F384
----------------
F384 is a different advc.139/ProbabilityTypes caller defect:
`AI_carrierSeaMove` uses `!= PROBABILITY_REAL` instead of the sibling naval
threshold `>= PROBABILITY_REAL`.

F386 is not that threshold typo. The Pirate's `<= LOW` sense is reasonable for
"heal only when land threat is low" once the location is appropriate. The bug
is that extraction also removed the old city/fort location requirement, while
the helper's water sentinel automatically satisfies the low-threat comparison.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Restore the location scope while retaining the extracted danger policy.

The closest translation of the retained comment/K-Mod contract is conceptually:

    if (getPlot().isCity(true) &&
        AI_isThreatenedFromLand() <= PROBABILITY_LOW)
    {
        if (AI_heal())
            return;
    }

If current AdvCiv's `isCity(true)` API has been replaced/deprecated, use the
modern team/base predicate that represents an actual naval city/fort heal base
(e.g. the same `isCityHeal`/base semantics used by current healing code), but do
not let ordinary water satisfy the early branch solely because
`AI_isThreatenedFromLand` returns `NO_PROBABILITY` there.

If intentionally allowing minor open-sea healing is desired as NEW Pirate
policy, it should be stated and valued explicitly; it should not arise as an
accidental consequence of a helper whose purpose is land-threat extraction and
whose retained caller comment still says city/fort only.

C031-WIP86 — PROTECTED QUEUE 002 CvUnitAI.cpp DEEP RELOOP — F387 CONFIRMED

STATUS

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F387 / provisional KI#710 — AdvCiv `AI_guardYield` recovers the guarded tile's
working city but centers its next "city plot" search on the GUARD UNIT instead,
allowing a high-yield guard to drift outside that city's radius and breaking
the function's own one-hop-to-city safety rationale
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
AdvCiv added `AI_guardYield` under advc.300 to:

    // Protect high-yield tiles from Barbarians

The helper starts by identifying the relevant owned city:

    CvCity const* pCity = getPlot().getPlotCity();

    // For now, only consider nearby city if already guarding bonus.
    if (pCity == NULL &&
        AI_getGroup()->AI_getMissionAIType() == MISSIONAI_GUARD_BONUS)
    {
        pCity = getPlot().getWorkingCity();
    }

    if (pCity == NULL || pCity->getOwner() != getOwner())
        return false;

So after a guard has reached an improved tile in a city radius, the function
explicitly recovers that tile's working city.

However, `pCity` is then not used to define the candidate population.

Current Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS execute:

    for (CityPlotIter it(getPlot()); it.hasNext(); ++it)
    {
        CvPlot& kLoopPlot = *it;
        ...
    }

This is not an iterator over `pCity`.

`CityPlotIterator.h` explicitly defines the `CvPlot` constructor as:

    "Iterator over the CvPlot instances in the city radius
     around a plot in the center."

and stores:

    m_iCenterX(kCenter.getX()),
    m_iCenterY(kCenter.getY())

Therefore:

    CityPlotIter(getPlot())

means the 21-tile city-radius SHAPE centered on the unit's current guard plot.

The function had already recovered `pCity`, but searches a different footprint.

WHY THE FIRST CALL LOOKS CORRECT
--------------------------------
The defect is easy to miss because the normal first invocation occurs while a
Reserve unit is in an owned city.

At that moment:

    getPlot() == pCity->plot()

so:

    CityPlotIter(getPlot())

and:

    CityPlotIter(*pCity)

would describe the same center.

The function can select a high-value improved tile and queues:

    MISSIONAI_GUARD_BONUS

for that tile.

Only after the unit arrives does `getPlot()` cease to be the city plot.

THE GUARD REALLY RE-EVALUATES AFTER ARRIVAL
-------------------------------------------
This is not a dormant second-call path.

When the guard is on its yield tile it normally fortifies/skips with:

    MISSIONAI_GUARD_BONUS

AI-controlled groups that are not executing `ACTIVITY_MISSION` are force-
updated at the turn boundary. `CvSelectionGroup::doTurn` sets:

    setForceUpdate(true);
    clearMissionQueue();

for such AI groups.

`clearMissionQueue()` removes mission queue entries but does NOT clear the
selection group's `m_eMissionAIType` / mission-AI plot.

`CvSelectionGroup::readyToMove()` explicitly treats:

    isForceUpdate()

as sufficient to re-enter AI updating even when the group had been sleeping.

Consequently the fortified yield guard re-enters `AI_reserveMove` and reaches
`AI_guardYield` on later turns while its `MISSIONAI_GUARD_BONUS` identity is
still available.

The branch:

    pCity = getPlot().getWorkingCity();

is therefore live exactly as its comment implies.

LIVE GEOMETRY — SEARCH FOOTPRINT DRIFTS OUTWARD
------------------------------------------------
Take city C and an improved outer-ring plot A that C can work.

The standard Civ4 city geometry includes radius-two positions such as:

    C = (0,0)
    A = (2,0)

Once the unit is guarding A:

    pCity == C

but the current loop is equivalent to a new city radius centered at:

    A = (2,0)

That shifted footprint contains positions such as:

    B = (3,0)

which are outside C's real city radius.

If B is:
* owned by the same player;
* improved;
* land;
* not a city;
* currently empty;
* high-yield enough;
* sufficiently near invisible terrain;
* reachable from A in one path turn;

then B can outrank A and become `pBestPlot`.

Nothing in `AI_guardYield` requires:

    B.getWorkingCity() == pCity

or even:

    B.getWorkingCity() != NULL.

The unit can therefore move from a genuine worked/working-city yield tile to an
improved plot that the recovered city cannot work at all.

On the following turn, if B lies outside every city assignment:

    getPlot().getPlotCity() == NULL
    getPlot().getWorkingCity() == NULL

so the same `AI_guardYield` function immediately returns false and the
high-yield guard assignment has effectively dissolved.

BROKEN "HURRY BACK TO THE CITY" CONTRACT
-----------------------------------------
The function explains its one-turn path restriction explicitly:

    /* Must be reachable in one hop, so that we can hurry back to the city
       when it's in danger. */

It checks:

    generatePath(kLoopPlot, ..., &iPathTurns)
    iPathTurns <= 1

But `generatePath` starts from THIS UNIT'S CURRENT position.

On the first call, while the unit is in C, that does mean:
    candidate is one path turn from the city.

On a later call from outer-ring A it only means:
    new candidate B is one path turn from A.

It provides no guarantee that B is one turn from C.

A guard can therefore chain one legal one-turn step outward and end at a plot
that takes more than one turn to return from, contradicting the exact safety
rationale used to justify the path bound.

This also interacts with `AI_reserveMove` ordering. The earlier general
`AI_guardCity(false, true, 2)` search has a two-turn limit. Once a guard drifts
far enough from its original city, the ordinary high-priority city-guard branch
is no longer guaranteed to rediscover that city when it becomes endangered.

UNUSED `pCity` IS AN INTERNAL CONTROL
-------------------------------------
After ownership validation, `pCity` is not used anywhere else in
`AI_guardYield`.

That is particularly revealing because the special post-arrival branch exists
solely to recover a city from the current guarded tile:

    pCity = getPlot().getWorkingCity();

If the intended candidate population were simply "a 21-tile neighborhood
around wherever the unit currently stands," there would be little reason to
recover the exact working city rather than only test that the current tile is
near/owned by a city.

The recovered object is exactly what `CityPlotIter` can accept directly:

    CityPlotIter(*pCity)

but the implementation passes:

    CityPlotIter(getPlot())

instead.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod 1.46 does not contain `AI_guardYield`.

Base AdvCiv adds it under advc.300, with:
* the "Protect high-yield tiles from Barbarians" caller comment;
* the explicit `pCity` / `getWorkingCity()` recovery;
* the "hurry back to the city" one-hop rationale;
* the current `CityPlotIter(getPlot())` center.

Current AdvCiv-SAS inherits that structural behavior unchanged.

Classification:
    inherited AdvCiv advc.300 state/scope regression.

WHY THIS IS STRONGER THAN THE WIP85 UNPROMOTED NOTE
----------------------------------------------------
C031-WIP85 deliberately left this unnumbered because a generic "protect nearby
improvements one hop at a time" policy was still plausible.

The final closure pass supplied the missing contracts:

1. `CityPlotIterator.h` proves that the CvPlot overload is literally centered
   on the current guard plot; it does not silently resolve the working city.

2. the AI group lifecycle proves the `MISSIONAI_GUARD_BONUS` reevaluation path
   executes after fortifying; it is not merely theoretical state.

3. the function's own one-hop comment states that the path restriction is
   supposed to preserve rapid return TO THE CITY. After the first move, current
   code measures the hop from the guard tile instead.

4. the shifted iterator admits candidates outside `pCity`'s radius, including
   candidates with no working city, after which the helper can stop applying
   entirely.

Together those establish a concrete state transition that contradicts the
function's stated safety invariant.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
At minimum, keep the candidate population tied to the recovered city:

    for (CityPlotIter it(*pCity); it.hasNext(); ++it)

rather than:

    for (CityPlotIter it(getPlot()); it.hasNext(); ++it)

If "high-yield tile" means an actually usable tile for that city, a stronger
version can use / require the corresponding working-city contract as
appropriate rather than counting arbitrary owned overlap plots.

The one-hop safety rule should also be made relative to `pCity`, not merely
relative to the guard's current location on subsequent reevaluations.

A conservative design would:
* validate that the current guarded tile is still a valid high-yield candidate
  for `pCity`;
* stay if so;
* otherwise choose another candidate from `pCity`'s real radius;
* ensure the chosen guard position remains within the intended rapid-return
  distance to `pCity`.

Do not allow repeated "one hop from where I am now" retargeting to substitute
for "one hop from the city."

FINAL-SWEEP CONTROLS CHECKED BEFORE F387

SAS file-local Worker / attack helpers
--------------------------------------
The remaining behavior helpers were deliberately reopened.

* `SAS_getImprovementUpgradeChainLevel`
  - bounded by `GC.getNumImprovementInfos()`, so malformed/cyclic XML upgrade
    chains cannot loop forever.

* `SAS_getWorkerGrowthImprovementLevel`
  - takes the maximum valid configured chain level; no cross-chain stale state.

* `SAS_getWorkerRecoveredFoodCostImprovementValue`
  - only rewards configured improvements once current plot/player modifiers
    make their food effect nonnegative; no reversed "partial recovery" bonus.

* `SAS_isWorkerBuildActivelyCommitted`
  - empty mission queues are safe because `getMissionType(0)` returns the
    mission sentinel when no node exists; stale build progress alone is not
    treated as active commitment.

* `SAS_findWorkerIrrigationChainStep`
  - KI#214's `(plot,steps)` state remains intact;
  - generation-stamped cost storage is reset on size change / unsigned
    generation wrap;
  - route outputs are initialized before search;
  - returned source-side build candidates remain owned, same-area, flat,
    potential-irrigation-valid and buildable.

* targetless peaceful ATTACK_CITY release
  - aggregate plot counts are recomputed after role conversion;
  - `AI_setUnitAIType()` detaches converted units through `joinGroup(NULL)`,
    so the release is not merely a label change inside the old stack.

No independent F388 emerged from those helpers in this slice.

`AI_canRouteThroughSafeTerritory`
---------------------------------
The helper ignores the bool return from its first ordinary `generatePath` and
stores `iOriginalPathTurns` through an output parameter.

That looks like a possible uninitialized read in isolation.

Its live callers, however, reach it only for candidate destinations already
path-tested by the corresponding Worker selection path (`AI_bestCityBuild`,
`AI_improveBonus`, or the legacy local candidate path).

Moreover, the second path is strictly more restrictive (`MOVE_SAFE_TERRITORY`);
a successful safe path with no ordinary path is not a supported state under
the current movement contract.

No live uninitialized-path consequence was established; no F388.

`AI_tradeMissionValue`
----------------------
The initial comparison contains:

    iBestPathTurns = MAX_INT
    4 + iBestPathTurns

which overflows signed 32-bit arithmetic on the legacy compiler model.

At that initial state the paired `iBestValue` numerator is zero, and the
comparison still supplies the intended zero baseline on the actual Civ4
toolchain. No current city ranking mis-selection was established.

This remains worthwhile numeric cleanup / hardening, not F388.

Raw enum / area predicate sweep
-------------------------------
The whole-file scan reconfirmed the known strong cases rather than finding a
new sibling:

* F376:
    `kPlot.isArea(kPlot.getArea())` tautology in `AI_connectBonus`.

* F380 companion:
    raw `getRevealedRouteType(getTeam())` boolean in
    `AI_airOffenseBaseValue`.

Other current `getRevealedRouteType` uses in CvUnitAI explicitly compare with
`NO_ROUTE`.

No additional live raw-enum-as-bool or self-area predicate crossed the F388
threshold in this slice.

6. Pathfinder-state reconciliation
-----------------------------------
All uses of:
* `getPathEndTurnPlot()`;
* `getPathFinder().getPathTurns()`;
* `getPathFinder().getFinalMoves()`;
* `getPathLastNode()`

were mechanically inventoried and the potentially nonlocal cases were
inspected for stale shared-pathfinder state.

The final pass specifically challenged cases where:
* a candidate path is generated;
* other AI/value/helper calls occur;
* path metrics or end-turn state are consumed later.

No independent F388 survived.

Important controls:
* stored `CvPlot*` / references returned from `getPathEndTurnPlot()` point to
  stable map plots; later path searches do not invalidate those plot objects;
* candidate scoring calls such as city value, local attack/defense value,
  mission-count queries and weighted combat odds do not regenerate this
  unit group's movement path before the saved path metrics are consumed;
* `AI_solveBlockageProblem` looks vulnerable because `AI_goToTargetCity` can
  regenerate paths, but that branch is returned immediately, so execution
  cannot fall through and consume the old blockage path afterward;
* the unchecked first `generatePath` in `AI_canRouteThroughSafeTerritory`
  remains a robustness smell, but its live callers have already established
  ordinary pathability and the second safe-territory path is more restrictive;
  no supported successful-safe / failed-ordinary state was established.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F388 / provisional KI#711 — SAS tech-tree obsolete-unit consolidation ignores
civilization context and globally lists every civilization's UU
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
Current SAS added an obsolete-unit consolidation block to
`CvGameTextMgr::setTechTradeHelp`:

    if (!bCivilopediaText)
    {
        ...
        if (!bTreeInfo)
        {
            CvWString szObsoleteUnits;
            bool bAnyObsoleteUnits = false;

            FOR_EACH_ENUM(Unit)
            {
                CvUnitInfo const& kLoopUnitInfo =
                        GC.getInfo(eLoopUnit);

                if (kLoopUnitInfo.getObsoleteTech() == eTech)
                {
                    ...
                    szObsoleteUnits +=
                        kLoopUnitInfo.getDescription();
                }
            }

            if (bAnyObsoleteUnits)
                append TXT_KEY_TECH_OBSOLETES...
        }
    }

The code iterates every `UnitInfo` in the game.

It never asks:
* which UnitClass the active civilization can train;
* which UnitType that civilization maps the UnitClass to;
* whether the listed UnitType belongs to the active civilization at all.

This differs from the immediately preceding obsolete-BUILDING logic in the
same function.

That existing code iterates BuildingClasses and, in active-player context,
resolves each class through:

    kGame.getActiveCivilization()->getBuilding(eLoopBuildingClass)

before asking whether the resolved building is obsoleted by `eTech`.

The new Unit block therefore discarded the same civilization-resolution
contract for units.

LIVE CALLER — TECH TREE
-----------------------
This is not restricted to generic/no-player help.

`CvDLLWidgetData::parseTechTreeHelp` calls:

    GAMETEXT.setTechHelp(
        szBuffer,
        eTech,
        false,  // bCivilopediaText
        !GET_TEAM(getActiveTeam()).isHasTech(eTech),
        false,
        false); // bTreeInfo

`setTechHelp` forwards those values to `setTechTradeHelp`.

For an unresearched tech in the normal Tech Tree:
    bCivilopediaText = false
    bPlayerContext   = true
    bTreeInfo        = false

Therefore the new obsolete-unit block executes in an explicitly
active-player-context hover.

Despite that, it still lists all global UnitTypes.

CURRENT-DATA PROOF — CIVIL SERVICE
----------------------------------
Current SAS Unit XML has nine UnitInfos with:

    ObsoleteTech = TECH_CIVIL_SERVICE

They are:

Generic:
    UNIT_AXEMAN
    UNIT_SWORDSMAN

Civilization-specific:
    UNIT_SUMERIAN_VULTURE
    UNIT_NATIVE_AMERICA_DOG_SOLDIER
    UNIT_AZTEC_JAGUAR
    UNIT_CELTIC_GALLIC_WARRIOR
    UNIT_ROMAN_LEGIONARY
    UNIT_PERSIA_IMMORTAL
    UNIT_INCAN_QUECHUA

Take an Arabian active player.

Current `CIVILIZATION_ARABIA` has no Axeman- or Swordsman-class replacement;
its current unique-unit mapping in this portion of the tree is unrelated
(`UNITCLASS_CAMEL_KNIGHT -> UNIT_ARABIA_HAJJAN`).

When that player hovers unresearched Civil Service in the Tech Tree, the new
global Unit loop can therefore produce one comma-separated "Obsoletes" line
containing:
* Axeman;
* Swordsman;
* Vulture;
* Dog Soldier;
* Jaguar;
* Gallic Warrior;
* Legionary;
* Immortal;
* Quechua.

Seven of those are UUs belonging to other civilizations and can never be the
Arabian player's corresponding unit.

The same class repeats at other current techs.

For example current `TECH_FIREARMS` is the ObsoleteTech of sixteen UnitInfos:
generic Mace/Pike/Longbow/Crossbow/Knight/Camel-Knight units plus Samurai,
Viking, Skirmisher, Bowman, Cho-Ko-Nu, Benin Disciplined Crossbowman, Yeoman
Archer, Cataphract, Khishigten and Arabia's Hajjan.

A player-context hover therefore mixes:
* the player's real UnitClass mapping;
* generic defaults that may have been replaced;
* other civilizations' replacements.

WHY `bPlayerContext` DOES NOT SAVE IT
-------------------------------------
The outer function knows whether player context is active.

The obsolete-building branch uses that context to resolve civilization-specific
types.

The new obsolete-unit block never references `bPlayerContext`,
`eActivePlayer`, `getActiveCivilization()`, or UnitClass mappings.

So this is not merely a generic encyclopedia-style listing accidentally viewed
during play; the caller explicitly requested player-context help and the new
block ignores that contract.

WHY THE CIVILOPEDIA PANEL DOES NOT SAVE IT
-------------------------------------------
The new block is deliberately disabled when:

    bCivilopediaText == true

because current Sevopedia Tech has a dedicated Obsoletes panel.

F388 occurs in the non-Civilopedia Tech Tree hover, where that dedicated panel
does not replace the text being generated.

The suppression therefore makes the player-context hover itself the primary
surface for this new consolidated Unit line.

ANCESTRY
--------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 does not contain this global obsolete-Unit consolidation
block.

Its obsolete-building handling already performs civilization-class resolution,
while bonus/special-building obsolescence is naturally global.

Current SAS added the Unit block directly while consolidating obsolete prose.

Classification:
    SAS-local civilization-context UI regression.

This is conceptually related to the old F004/KI#332 leader-hover context bug,
but it is an independent current root:
* old F004: caller supplied the wrong civilization ID to trait help;
* F388: the current caller supplies active-player context correctly, but the
  newly added Unit loop ignores civilization context internally.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Mirror the existing BuildingClass pattern.

For player-context help, iterate UnitClasses and resolve each class through the
active civilization:

    UnitTypes eLoopUnit;

    if (eActivePlayer != NO_PLAYER)
        eLoopUnit =
            kGame.getActiveCivilization()->getUnit(eLoopUnitClass);
    else
        eLoopUnit =
            GC.getInfo(eLoopUnitClass).getDefaultUnit();

then test the resolved UnitType's `getObsoleteTech()`.

A generic/no-player help mode can use default units, consistent with the
building branch.

Do not globally enumerate every UnitInfo for a player-context Tech Tree hover.

If the intended UI instead wants an "all civilizations" encyclopedia list, it
needs to be explicitly limited to a generic context and clearly labeled as
such; it must not silently replace active-civilization semantics.

* Existing KI#21 still survives independently:
  live-unit map help prints raw Terrain/Feature impassability without applying

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F389 / provisional KI#712 — AdvCiv founding-health hover prints feature
unhealth instead of negative PLAYER extra health
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
AdvCiv's advc.004b `CvGameTextMgr::setFoundHealthHelp` computes surrounding
feature health first:

    int iGoodHealth = iGoodHealthPercent / 100;
    int iBadHealth = iBadHealthPercent / 100;

and later obtains the active player's global extra-health modifier:

    int iExtraHealth =
        GET_PLAYER(getActivePlayer()).getExtraHealth();

For positive extra health it correctly prints `iExtraHealth`:

    if (iExtraHealth > 0)
    {
        iIcon = gDLL->getSymbolID(HEALTHY_CHAR);
        szBuffer.append(
            CvWString::format(L"%d%c", iExtraHealth, iIcon));
    }

But the negative branch prints a different local variable:

    else
    {
        iIcon = gDLL->getSymbolID(UNHEALTHY_CHAR);
        szBuffer.append(
            CvWString::format(L"%d%c", iBadHealth, iIcon));
    }

`iBadHealth` is the number of rounded unhealthy points contributed by FEATURES
around the proposed city site.

It has no relation to the player's negative `iExtraHealth`.

The function therefore displays the local feature-unhealth value in the slot
that is explicitly meant to describe global player extra health.

LIVE CALLER
-----------
This is ordinary founding-mission UI, not dead Civilopedia code.

`CvDLLWidgetData` handles `MISSION_FOUND`.

When the selected Settler can found on the mission plot it calls:

    GAMETEXT.setFoundCostHelp(...)
    GAMETEXT.setHomePlotYieldHelp(...)
    GAMETEXT.setFoundHealthHelp(...)

before displaying the founding action help.

Current `UNIT_SETTLER`:
* has `bFound = 1`;
* has no prerequisite technology;
* has `ObsoleteTech = NONE`.

So this hover remains live throughout the game, including the Future Era.

NEGATIVE PLAYER EXTRA HEALTH IS LIVE IN CURRENT SAS
---------------------------------------------------
Current `CvPlayer::getExtraHealth()` is not constrained nonnegative.

Player-level health is modified by, among other sources:
* traits through `CvPlayer::processTraits`;
* civics through `CvPlayer::processCivics`;
* technologies through `CvTeam::processTech`;
* events.

In particular current SAS has:

    TECH_DEPOPULATION
        iHealth = -9

and `CvTeam::processTech` applies every technology's health directly to each
team member:

    kMember.changeExtraHealth(
        kTech.getHealth() * iChange);

The prerequisite graph gives an especially clean current-data state.

For `TECH_DEPOPULATION`:
* OR prerequisite: `TECH_COMPOSITES`;
* AND prerequisites:
  - `TECH_SATELLITES`;
  - `TECH_COMPUTERS`;
  - `TECH_ENVIRONMENTALISM`.

Among every technology reachable in the full prerequisite ancestry of
Depopulation, the only other nonzero health modifier is:

    TECH_ENVIRONMENTALISM
        iHealth = +1

The other current positive-health technologies
(Bioengineering, Alien Life, Genetics, AI, Transhumanism) are not required
ancestors of Depopulation; several are descendants/alternatives after it.

Therefore a player with:
* no health-changing trait;
* no health-changing civic;
* no health-changing event;
* only the technologies necessary to reach Depopulation,

has a technology-derived player extra-health total of:

    Environmentalism +1
    Depopulation     -9
    ------------------
    total            -8

So the `iExtraHealth < 0` branch is directly reachable in current SAS.

CONCRETE DISPLAY FAILURE
------------------------
Take that player after researching Depopulation and select a Settler over a
valid founding tile whose revealed city radius has no unhealthy feature
contribution.

Then:

    iExtraHealth = -8
    iBadHealth   = 0

`setFoundHealthHelp` executes:

    szBuffer.append(L"+");

then enters the negative extra-health branch and prints:

    iBadHealth == 0

with the unhealthy icon.

The result is effectively:

    +0 [unhealthy] "from trait"

despite the player actually carrying 8 points of global extra unhealth.

If the proposed site happens to have, for example, 2 unhealthy feature points,
the same player-global line instead prints 2 — still unrelated to the actual
-8 player modifier.

Thus the displayed number changes with the proposed site's feature health even
though the underlying `getExtraHealth()` value is global and unchanged.

INTERNAL FORMAT CONTROL
-----------------------
The ordinary city-health breakdown elsewhere in the same file already shows
the correct negative-player-health convention.

For an existing city:

    int iHealth =
        GET_PLAYER(kCity.getOwner()).getExtraHealth();

    if (iHealth < 0)
    {
        szBuffer.append(
            CvWString::format(L"%d%c ",
                -iHealth,
                gDLL->getSymbolID(UNHEALTHY_CHAR)));
        szBuffer.append(
            gDLL->getText("TXT_KEY_FROM_TRAIT"));
    }

So the intended negative branch is explicit:
* use `-iExtraHealth` as the positive magnitude;
* pair it with the unhealthy icon.

The founding helper's use of `iBadHealth` is not an alternative formatting
policy; it is a wrong-variable typo.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod 1.46 and Civ4CE/BtS do not contain `setFoundHealthHelp`.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same advc.004b helper and the same wrong-variable
negative branch:

    CvWString::format(L"%d%c", iBadHealth, iIcon)

Current SAS inherits that line unchanged.

Classification:
    inherited AdvCiv advc.004b UI wrong-variable defect.

REPAIR DIRECTION

Mirror the existing-city health formatting:

    else
    {
        iIcon = gDLL->getSymbolID(UNHEALTHY_CHAR);
        szBuffer.append(
            CvWString::format(
                L"%d%c",
                -iExtraHealth,

    }

The surrounding function already prepends `"+"` because healthy/unhealthy

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F390 / provisional KI#713 — AdvCiv relabeled aggregate PLAYER extra health as
"from Traits" even though the accumulator also contains civics, technologies
and events
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
Current city-health help uses the PLAYER-level aggregate:

    GET_PLAYER(kCity.getOwner()).getExtraHealth()

for both bad and good health.

AdvCiv advc.004g replaced K-Mod's neutral civilization-source text with:

    TXT_KEY_FROM_TRAIT

Current XML defines that key as:

    English: " from Traits"
    German:  "durch Merkmale des Herrschers"
             ("through leader traits")

So the UI explicitly attributes the complete `getExtraHealth()` value to
leader Traits.

That attribution does not match the data represented by `getExtraHealth()`.

CURRENT ACCUMULATOR SOURCES
---------------------------
`CvPlayer::m_iExtraHealth` is modified by several independent systems.

Traits:
    CvPlayer::processTraits
        changeExtraHealth(iChange * kTrait.getHealth());

Civics:
    CvPlayer::processCivics
        changeExtraHealth(
            GC.getInfo(eCivic).getExtraHealth() * iChange);

Technologies:
    CvTeam::processTech
        kMember.changeExtraHealth(
            kTech.getHealth() * iChange);

Events:
    CvPlayer::applyEvent
        changeExtraHealth(kEvent.getHealth());

Therefore:

    CvPlayer::getExtraHealth()

is a global player modifier accumulator, not a Trait accumulator.

CURRENT-DATA POSITIVE PROOF — ORGANIZED RELIGION
------------------------------------------------
Current SAS has:

    CIVIC_ORGANIZED_RELIGION
        iExtraHealth = +1

and:

    TRAIT_PROTECTIVE
        iHealth = +1

as the ordinary current health Trait.

Take a leader without Protective and adopt Organized Religion, with no other
player-level health modifier active.

Then:

    getExtraHealth() == +1

entirely because of the CIVIC.

Current city good-health help nevertheless executes:

    int iHealth =
        GET_PLAYER(kCity.getOwner()).getExtraHealth();

    if (iHealth > 0)
    {
        append "+1 [healthy]"
        append TXT_KEY_FROM_TRAIT;
    }

and displays the civic-derived health as:

    +1 [healthy] from Traits

despite no health Trait contributing anything.

CURRENT-DATA NEGATIVE PROOF — DEPOPULATION
------------------------------------------
F389 already established a particularly clean current technology state.

Current:

    TECH_ENVIRONMENTALISM  iHealth = +1
    TECH_DEPOPULATION      iHealth = -9

and Environmentalism is the only nonzero-health mandatory prerequisite in the
Depopulation ancestry.

A non-Protective player with no health civic/event can therefore have:

    getExtraHealth() == -8

from technology alone.

Existing-city bad-health help correctly prints the magnitude:

    8 [unhealthy]

but then appends:

    TXT_KEY_FROM_TRAIT

so the tech-derived penalty is presented as:

    8 [unhealthy] from Traits

This is independent of F389.

F389 is the wrong-variable numeric bug in `setFoundHealthHelp`, where the
negative founding preview prints local feature bad health instead of the
negative player extra-health magnitude.

F390 affects the SOURCE ATTRIBUTION of the aggregate value in:
* existing-city good-health breakdown;
* existing-city bad-health breakdown;
* founding-health preview once the numeric branch is repaired.

Even a correct F389 numeric repair would still display:
    8 unhealthy from Traits
for a technology-derived -8 state.

EVENTS PROVIDE ANOTHER LIVE SOURCE
----------------------------------
Current event XML also contains player events with positive `iHealth`
(e.g. +1, +2 and +3 values).

`CvPlayer::applyEvent` applies those directly through `changeExtraHealth`.

So the wrong attribution is not limited to one custom Civic or one Future Era
technology; the accumulator has always had a broader source contract.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod's city health breakdown uses:

    TXT_KEY_MISC_HEALTH_FROM_CIV
    TXT_KEY_MISC_GOOD_HEALTH_FROM_CIV

for negative/positive:

    GET_PLAYER(city.getOwner()).getExtraHealth()

That wording is broad enough for an aggregate civilization/player modifier.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 comments those neutral keys out under advc.004g and instead
formats the number/icon manually followed by:

    TXT_KEY_FROM_TRAIT

without changing `getExtraHealth()` or separating its contributing sources.

Current SAS inherits the same advc.004g source attribution.

Classification:
    inherited AdvCiv advc.004g UI source-attribution regression.

WHY THE SAME KEY IS NOT ALWAYS WRONG
------------------------------------
`TXT_KEY_FROM_TRAIT` also appears in current commerce/trade help.

Those uses were checked separately.

`CvPlayer::getFreeCityCommerce(eCommerce)` is changed in current C++ only by:

    CvPlayer::processTraits
        changeFreeCityCommerce(
            eCommerce,
            iChange * kTrait.getCommerceChange(eCommerce));

So "from Traits" is correct for that use.

The trade-yield modifier line explicitly iterates the player's actual Traits
and sums `getTradeYieldModifier`, also making the label correct there.

F390 is therefore not a complaint about the localization key itself. The bug is
using a Trait-specific key for the multi-source `getExtraHealth()` accumulator.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The minimal robust repair is to restore neutral aggregate wording for
`getExtraHealth()`.

For example, re-use/adapt the prior civilization/global-modifier text rather
than `TXT_KEY_FROM_TRAIT`.

A higher-fidelity UI could decompose the aggregate into known sources:
* Traits;
* current Civics;
* researched Technologies;
* persistent Events / other residual modifiers.

However events and other persistent mutations mean reconstructing every source
perfectly from current static configuration may require additional bookkeeping.

Therefore a neutral label such as:
    "from player modifiers"
or the former:
    "from civilization"
is safer than falsely attributing the aggregate to Traits.

The founding preview should use the same neutral aggregate label after F389's
numeric repair.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ADVCIV-ONLY HELPER CONTROL — SPEED BONUS RESOURCE MISMATCH IS DATA-DORMANT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The AdvCiv-only `setBonusExtraHelp(eBonus, ...)` contains a genuine dormant
source defect in its unit speed-bonus handling.

It loops a unit's speed-bonus entries:

    for (int j = 0; j < kUnit.getNumSpeedBonuses(); j++)
        iSpeed = kUnit.getExtraMoves(j);

but never checks:

    kUnit.getSpeedBonuses(j) == eBonus

before using `iSpeed` while generating help for the current bonus `eBonus`.

Semantically, a unit with a nonzero speed bonus for resource A could therefore
be listed as receiving that movement bonus in the help for unrelated resource
B.

`CvUnitInfo` stores these as explicit `(BonusType, ExtraMoves)` pairs, and the
actual movement logic checks ownership of the corresponding bonus, so the help
code's missing resource comparison is real.

Current SAS Unit XML, however, contains ZERO `<SpeedBonuses>` entries.

Therefore no current UnitType can trigger the erroneous help branch.

Classification for this checkpoint:
    dormant inherited AdvCiv helper defect / future XML hazard;
    NOT F391 under the current-data proof threshold.

  only `processTraits` calls `changeFreeCityCommerce`;
  Trait attribution is correct.

* trade-yield modifier:
  help explicitly sums actual Trait `getTradeYieldModifier`;
  Trait attribution is correct.

Thus the health source is the exceptional wrong use rather than a globally bad
key.

`setBonusExtraHelp` team overload
---------------------------------
A superficially suspicious `GET_TEAM(eActivePlayer)`-style call is safe in the
current CoreAI interface because `getTeam` is overloaded for `PlayerTypes` and
converts through the player's team ID.

No enum-domain F391.

`setFoodHelp`
-------------
`healthRate()` is nonpositive by contract for unhealth-food loss, so:

    iSpoiledFood = -healthRate();

has the expected nonnegative magnitude.

No sign inversion.

`setFoundCostHelp`
------------------
The founding mission target is the selected Settler's current plot; using that
plot's ownership for unit-supply cost is consistent with the MISSION_FOUND
execution surface.

No stale target context established.

`setDiscoverPathHelp`
---------------------
The temporary-tech exploration uses the purpose-built
`setHasTechTemporarily` mechanism and restores state. No persistent tech-side
effect was established.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F391 / provisional KI#714 — production-decay hover reports the wrong amount on
non-Normal game speeds because the BULL getter ignores game-speed scaling
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
The current unit/building hover path calls:

    setProductionDecayHelp(...,
        pCity->getUnitProductionDecay(eUnit), ...)

or:

    setProductionDecayHelp(...,
        pCity->getBuildingProductionDecay(eBuilding), ...)

and the text explicitly says, for example:

    "Will lose %d1[ICON_PRODUCTION] this turn"

or:

    "Will lose %d1[ICON_PRODUCTION] in %d2 turns"

The shared BULL getter generated in `CvCity.cpp` is:

    int CvCity::get##Order##ProductionDecay(...) const
    {
        int const iProduction = get##Order##Production(...);
        return iProduction -
            (iProduction *
            GC.getDefineINT(CvGlobals::ORDER##_PRODUCTION_DECAY_PERCENT)) / 100;
    }

That computes the decay amount as though the game-speed production percentage
were always 100.

The actual runtime decay in `CvCity::doDecay`, however, is:

    int const iGameSpeedPercent = ...getConstructPercent();
    ...
    setBuildingProduction(eBuilding, iProduction -
        (iProduction * (100 - iDecayPercent) +
         iGameSpeedPercent - 1) /
        iGameSpeedPercent);

and analogously uses `getTrainPercent()` for units.

Therefore the actual amount LOST is:

    ceil(iProduction * (100 - iDecayPercent) / iGameSpeedPercent)

whereas the UI getter effectively reports:

    ceil(iProduction * (100 - iDecayPercent) / 100)

The two agree only when the relevant game-speed percentage is 100 (or by
accidental integer rounding for a particular production amount).

CURRENT CONFIG / LIVE SURFACE
-----------------------------
The feature is not hidden behind a dormant option.

Current:

    Assets/Config/BUG City Screen.xml

sets:

    ProductionDecayQueue default="True"

and `setUnitHelp` / `setBuildingHelp` use that same option for the decay hover.

Current SAS has multiple non-100% game speeds:

    Nitro       Train/Construct = 33%
    Turbo       Train/Construct = 50%
    Quick       Train/Construct = 67%
    Normal      Train/Construct = 100%
    Epic        Train/Construct = 150%
    Marathon    Train/Construct = 200%
    Slow        Train/Construct = 300%
    Very Slow   Train/Construct = 400%

The inherited BtS production-decay defines are:

    BUILDING_PRODUCTION_DECAY_PERCENT = 99
    UNIT_PRODUCTION_DECAY_PERCENT     = 98

and current SAS has no override of those standard values in its modified XML
surface.

CONCRETE CURRENT EXAMPLES
-------------------------
Take 300 stored production in a building on Slow (ConstructPercent = 300).

UI getter:

    300 - floor(300 * 99 / 100)
    = 300 - 297
    = 3 production

Actual `doDecay` loss:

    ceil(300 * (100 - 99) / 300)
    = ceil(300 / 300)
    = 1 production

The hover can therefore say:

    Will lose 3 [production]

when the runtime will remove only 1.

For a unit with 300 stored production on Slow:

UI getter:

    300 - floor(300 * 98 / 100)
    = 6

Actual runtime loss:

    ceil(300 * 2 / 300)
    = 2

so the tooltip can report 6 when only 2 are lost.

The direction reverses on fast speeds. With 300 building production on Quick
(ConstructPercent = 67):

UI getter:

    3

Actual runtime loss:

    ceil(300 / 67)
    = 5

Thus this is not merely a conservative warning; it can either overstate or
understate the actual loss depending on game speed.

NORMAL-SPEED CONTROL
--------------------
At 100% speed the formulas coincide:

    ceil(P * (100 - decayPercent) / 100)

so a Normal-speed-only test would mask the defect. This likely explains why the
BULL-derived display can appear correct in ordinary testing.

ANCESTRY
--------
BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod already have the game-speed-scaled runtime `doDecay`
formula.

The production-decay warning getters and `CvGameTextMgr::setProductionDecayHelp`
were imported into AdvCiv by pre-SAS AdvCiv commit:

    0c4bd84a716240c6c6889acaa15b51a1d9ce5105
    "Production decay warnings from BULL"

The introducing diff added the getter with `/ 100` while leaving the existing
runtime decay calculation scaled by `iGameSpeedPercent`.

Classification:
    inherited AdvCiv/BULL UI calculation regression against the inherited BtS
    runtime decay formula.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Make `getBuildingProductionDecay` / `getUnitProductionDecay` mirror the actual
runtime formula, including the corresponding Construct/Train game-speed
percentage.

Conceptually:

    int const iGameSpeedPercent = ...get##Verb##Percent();
    int const iDecayPercent =
        GC.getDefineINT(CvGlobals::ORDER##_PRODUCTION_DECAY_PERCENT);
    return (iProduction * (100 - iDecayPercent) +
            iGameSpeedPercent - 1) /
           iGameSpeedPercent;

Ideally the runtime and preview should share one helper so the two formulas
cannot drift again.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F391 CONTROL — RESEARCH MODIFIER BREAKDOWN CAN HIDE A TERM, BUT CURRENT
GROUNDBREAKING ENABLES ARE OFF
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The previously open research-tooltip candidate is a real configurable display
hazard but does NOT qualify as a separate current-data finding.

`CvGameTextMgr::setResearchModifierHelp` obtains ordinary known-team / tech-
diffusion contribution in `iFromOtherKnown` and independently computes:

    iFromGroundbreaking = -groundbreakingPenalty(eTech);

It then intentionally groups those into one display slot and chooses which
label/value to show based on the sign of their SUM:

    bool const bShowOtherKnown =
        (iFromOtherKnown + iFromGroundbreaking > 0);

If both are nonzero, one real component is omitted from the breakdown even
though `calculateResearchModifier` applies both to the actual total.

However current SAS configuration has:

    TECH_DIFFUSION_ENABLE                    = 0
    AI_GROUNDBREAKING_PENALTY_ENABLE         = 0
    HUMAN_GROUNDBREAKING_PENALTY_ENABLE      = 0

The ordinary BtS known-team research bonus still exists while
`TECH_DIFFUSION_ENABLE = 0`, but `groundbreakingPenalty` returns 0 for both
human and AI players because both groundbreaking enable defines are 0.

Therefore the simultaneous positive-diffusion + negative-groundbreaking state
cannot occur under current configuration.

Current era XML does contain nonzero maximum groundbreaking penalties in
several eras, so enabling either groundbreaking define would immediately make
the hidden-component behavior reachable. The XML comment itself documents the
intentional "only the sum" UI policy.

Classification:
    configurable / dormant AdvCiv UI decomposition limitation;
    NOT an additional numbered finding under the current-data proof threshold.

production-time getter. F391 concerns the AMOUNT passed into the text, not the
turn countdown.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F392 / KI#715 — SETTLER FOUNDING-COST HOVER CHARGES NORMAL MAINTENANCE FOR
WLTKD CITIES THAT ACTUALLY CONTINUE PAYING ZERO MAINTENANCE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED current-data UI/state mismatch.

Current SAS `CvGameTextMgr::setFoundCostHelp` projects the expenses after
founding a new city. For each existing city it does:

    FOR_EACH_CITY (c, kPlayer)
    {
        if (c->isDisorder()) // Can't account for these
            continue;
        int iProjected =
                c->calculateDistanceMaintenanceTimes100() +
                c->calculateCorporationMaintenanceTimes100() +
                CvCity::calculateNumCitiesMaintenanceTimes100(..., 1) +
                CvCity::calculateColonyMaintenanceTimes100(..., 1);
        iProjPreInfl += (iProjected *
                std::max(0, c->getMaintenanceModifier() + 100)) / 100;
    }

It therefore treats every city that is not in `isDisorder()` as if its normal
post-founding maintenance will actually be charged.

That is not the runtime maintenance contract.

`CvCity::isDisorder()` is only:

    return (isOccupation() || GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).isAnarchy());

whereas actual maintenance suppression is controlled by:

    bool CvCity::isNoMaintenance() const
    {
        return (isDisorder() || isWeLoveTheKingDay() || getPopulation() <= 0);
    }

and `CvCity::updateMaintenance()` does:

    int iNewMaintenance = 0;
    if (!isNoMaintenance())
    {
        iNewMaintenance = calculateBaseMaintenanceTimes100() *
                std::max(0, getMaintenanceModifier() + 100) / 100;
    }

So a city celebrating We Love the King Day (WLTKD) is NOT in disorder, but it
pays exactly zero city maintenance.

WHY FOUNDING DOES NOT MAKE THE PROJECTION TRUE
----------------------------------------------
The mismatch survives the actual founding transition rather than merely
comparing the hover with a stale pre-action state.

During `CvCity::init`, after the new city increments the team/game city counts,
the owner immediately runs:

    kOwner.updateMaintenance();

`CvPlayer::updateMaintenance()` updates every city, and each old WLTKD city
again executes `CvCity::updateMaintenance()`. Its WLTKD flag is still set, so
`isNoMaintenance()` remains true and its actual maintenance remains 0.

Founding another city does not clear WLTKD. The flag is reconsidered in the
city's ordinary `doTurn` WLTKD logic, not as a side effect of founding a city
elsewhere.

Thus the preview is not validly anticipating that the celebration will end.
It includes maintenance that the runtime explicitly continues suppressing
immediately after the city is founded.

WHY THE DISPLAY OVERSTATES THE INCREMENT
----------------------------------------
After constructing the projected pre-inflation total, `setFoundCostHelp`
subtracts:

    kPlayer.calculateInflatedCosts();

Current actual inflated costs are based on:

    calculateUnitCost() + calculateUnitSupply() + getTotalMaintenance() +
    getCivicUpkeep() + extraExpenses

and `getTotalMaintenance()` already contains zero maintenance for each WLTKD
city.

For an existing WLTKD city, therefore:

    projected side: full normal projected city maintenance is added
    current side:   0 city maintenance is subtracted

instead of comparing 0 before with 0 after.

This can overstate the displayed incremental founding cost by approximately
the entire projected maintenance of every WLTKD city, after the same city and
inflation modifiers, rather than merely by a rounding unit.

LIVE CURRENT SAS SURFACE
------------------------
This is not merely an inherited dormant AdvCiv edge case.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 effectively disables celebrations through:

    WE_LOVE_THE_KING_POPULATION_MIN_POPULATION = 100

and explicitly documents values above 50 as effectively disabling WLTKD.

AdvCiv-SAS deliberately re-enabled the mechanic and currently sets:

    WE_LOVE_THE_KING_POPULATION_MIN_POPULATION = 5

The inherited BtS define remains:

    WE_LOVE_THE_KING_RAND = 1000

so an eligible healthy/non-angry/non-occupied city of population P >= 5 has
the standard P/1000 per-turn chance to enter WLTKD.

Current SAS maintenance factors are also positive across ordinary world sizes
and handicap levels, so an established WLTKD city can readily have positive
normal distance / number-of-cities / corporation / colony maintenance that is
suppressed to 0 by WLTKD. The error therefore has an ordinary live state under
current data.

USER-FACING CALLER
------------------
This is directly exposed in the Settler found-action hover.

`CvDLLWidgetData::parseActionHelp_Mission`, for `MISSION_FOUND`, calls:

    if (kUnitOwner.getNumCities() > 0)
        GAMETEXT.setFoundCostHelp(szBuffer, kMissionPlot);

and the localization says:

    TXT_KEY_PROJECTED_COST
    "Increases city cost by %s1_MaintNum [ICON_GOLD]"

So the wrong value is presented specifically as the incremental expense caused
by founding the proposed city.

ANCESTRY
--------
The founding-cost preview is an AdvCiv addition (`advc.004b`), not a BtS/K-Mod
UI feature.

The initial AdvCiv implementation already projected maintenance for existing
cities without excluding WLTKD. That older form primarily computed the change
in number-of-cities / colony maintenance, so the same conceptual omission was
present but its impact was narrower.

Pre-SAS AdvCiv commit:

    ef40cbb8b47a2b11e4b213076d0f1cad62ad13b1
    "Misc. tweaks (mostly UI)"

rewrote the projection into essentially the current form: it adds each
non-disorder city's FULL projected maintenance, then subtracts the player's
current aggregate inflated expenses. That rewrite introduced the especially
large current WLTKD error because the projected side includes full normal
maintenance while the current aggregate contains 0 for a celebrating city.

Later commits added corporation maintenance and moved/refactored the helper into
`CvGameTextMgr`, while preserving the `c->isDisorder()` guard.

Classification:
    inherited AdvCiv UI projection defect, mostly dormant in Base AdvCiv 1.14
    because AdvCiv disables WLTKD through XML; made live again by SAS's
    intentional re-enabling of WLTKD.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The smallest contract-aligned repair is for the existing-city projection to
skip cities whose runtime maintenance remains suppressed:

    if (c->isNoMaintenance())
        continue;

rather than only:

    if (c->isDisorder())
        continue;

That mirrors `CvCity::updateMaintenance()` for occupation/anarchy, WLTKD and
the zero-population guard in one place.

A still stronger long-term design would project the actual before/after city
maintenance through a shared helper rather than manually reproducing pieces of
`CvCity::updateMaintenance`, but replacing the guard with `isNoMaintenance()`
is the surgical fix for the demonstrated current bug.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTROL — APPARENT NO_IMPROVEMENT DEREFERENCE IN PLOT-HEALTH TRANCHE IS SAFE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
During the surrounding plot-health pass, a narrow source excerpt initially
made an improvement-upgrade lookup appear reachable when:

    ePlotImprovement == NO_IMPROVEMENT

A wider brace/context check disproved that suspicion. The upgrade lookup is
inside the pre-existing:

    if (ePlotImprovement != NO_IMPROVEMENT)

block. No invalid enum/info access exists there. This is explicitly retained as
a control rather than promoted into a finding.

C031-WIP94 — QUEUE 003 CONTINUATION FROM F393 UNUSED
===============================================================================

F393 / KI#716 — SAS SEVOPEDIA-ONLY UNIT-STAT SUPPRESSION LEAKS INTO PLE UPGRADE HOVERS BECAUSE `bCivilopediaText` IS NOT A SEVOPEDIA-ONLY CONTEXT FLAG
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: CONFIRMED — SAS-local UI regression / incomplete repair of an earlier SAS Sevopedia cleanup.

ROOT
----
Current SAS `CvGameTextMgr::setBasicUnitHelp` suppresses several static unit
ability families whenever:

    bCivilopediaText == true

because Sevopedia Unit now renders those values through dedicated button
panels instead of repeating them in `placeSpecial` text.

Examples include:

    city attack / city defense modifiers
    hill attack / hill defense modifiers
    terrain attack / terrain defense modifiers
    feature attack / feature defense modifiers
    UnitClass attack / defense modifiers
    UnitCombat modifiers
    free starting promotions (`Starts with ...`)

The relevant current code repeatedly uses:

    if (!bCivilopediaText)
    {
        ... ordinary static ability text ...
    }

and the SAS comments explicitly describe the reason as hiding duplicate rows
"in sevopedia" because Sevopedia has replacement button panels.

But `bCivilopediaText` is a formatting/mode parameter shared by other clients;
it is NOT an identity test for the Sevopedia Unit screen.

LIVE NON-SEVOPEDIA CONSUMER
---------------------------
The Plot List Enhancements (PLE) live map UI has an Upgrade grouping. It shows
buttons for actual upgrade targets and displays a custom information pane when
the mouse enters one of those target buttons.

`Assets/Python/Screens/PLE.py::showUpgradeInfoPane` still does:

    szSpecialText = mt.removeLinks(
        CyGameTextMgr().getUnitHelp(iUnitType, True, False, False, None)[1:]
    ) + "\n"

That `True` is `bCivilopediaText`.

PLE does NOT have the Sevopedia terrain / feature / hill / city / matchup
button panels that motivated the suppression. Therefore every static ability
removed solely by `bCivilopediaText` disappears from this live upgrade-target
hover.

This is a real supported UI route:

1. `Assets/Config/Plot List Enhancements.xml` exposes `PLE_Style` as a normal
   user option.
2. `CvMainInterface.py` selects the PLE draw method when
   `PleOpt.isPLE_Style()` is true.
3. PLE exposes `PLE_GRP_UPGRADE` as an interactive grouping mode.
4. In that mode, `displayUnitUpgrades` obtains candidate targets from:

       mt.getPossibleUpgrades(pUnit)

5. `MonkeyTools.getPossibleUpgrades` iterates UnitInfos and retains targets
   for which:

       pUnit.canUpgrade(i, true)

6. Each target is shown as an image button whose hover dispatch calls
   `showUpgradeInfoPane`.

The mode is optional and not the default (`PLE_Style` defaults false), but it
is a shipped, user-selectable interface path rather than dead/debug code.

SIMPLE CURRENT-DATA EXAMPLE
---------------------------
A generic Archer directly upgrades to the Longbowman class in current SAS:

    UNIT_ARCHER
        UnitClassUpgrade -> UNITCLASS_LONGBOWMAN

The generic current Longbowman has:

    iCityDefense = 25
    iHillsDefense = 20

In ordinary in-game unit help (`bCivilopediaText == false`), those are rendered
as the corresponding +25% city-defense and +20% hill-defense ability lines.

In Sevopedia (`bCivilopediaText == true`), hiding those rows is intentional
because the dedicated Sevopedia panels carry them.

In PLE's Archer -> Longbowman upgrade-target hover, however, PLE also passes
`true`, but supplies no replacement panels. The target preview therefore
omits both inherent Longbowman defensive modifiers even though they are
important properties of the unit the player is considering upgrading into.

This is broad rather than a one-off XML accident. A direct current UnitInfo
edge scan found 55 upgrade-target UnitTypes with at least one currently
suppressed city/hill/terrain/feature/UnitClass/UnitCombat modifier family.
Examples include Explorer, Axeman, Spearman, Pikeman, Longbowman, Crossbowman,
several UUs, Grenadier, many mounted lines, Tank and later units.

FREE-PROMOTION SUBCASE
----------------------
The same context leak also applies to the SAS block that hides:

    TXT_KEY_UNIT_STARTS_WITH

when `bCivilopediaText` is true. Sevopedia has its own Free Promotions panel;
PLE's upgrade hover does not. Upgrade targets with XML free promotions can
therefore lose that information through the same root.

ANCESTRY / WHY THIS IS A PARTIAL REPAIR
---------------------------------------
Base AdvCiv's `setBasicUnitHelp` emitted the city/hill/terrain/feature/class/
combat modifier text regardless of `bCivilopediaText`.

SAS commit:

    e82115dc5a...  (practical commit 4764)

commented those blocks out globally while building dedicated Sevopedia Unit
panels. Its own comments said the goal was to hide the cumbersome duplicate
data from Sevopedia, while still wanting it in-game.

That global suppression caused player-facing non-Sevopedia tooltips to lose
combat information.

SAS commit:

    9c01aa6e3f18c6826441cd77b84c7c160bb970b4
    2025-12-16
    "Fix some combat or other tooltips also being disabled outside sevopedia
     now instead of being disabled everywhere, they are only disabled in
     sevopedia."

re-enabled the blocks under:

    if (!bCivilopediaText)

The full commit message explicitly says the intended scope is "only in
sevopedia" and that the change fixes player feedback.

However the repair changed only `CvGameTextMgr.cpp`; PLE's pre-existing
upgrade-pane call still asks for `getUnitHelp(..., True, ...)`. Thus the repair
used a broader proxy (`bCivilopediaText`) than the actual intended scope
(Sevopedia Unit `placeSpecial`) and left this live side consumer suppressed.

A later comment/layout commit (`fb9054847f...`) preserved the same guard and
Sevopedia-only rationale.

CLASSIFICATION
--------------
SAS-local UI context-leak / partial-fix regression.

This is not a disagreement over whether Civ4 "Civilopedia text" should be
shorter. The source history explicitly states the desired policy: the rows
should be disabled ONLY in Sevopedia. PLE is a live main-interface upgrade
hover with no replacement presentation, and current data provides many
ordinary victims.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Do not use the generic `bCivilopediaText` parameter as a proxy for
"Sevopedia Unit has replacement buttons."

Best structural fix:

    introduce a dedicated Sevopedia-only suppression/context flag (or a
    dedicated help entry point) that SevoPediaUnit passes when it wants the
    replacement-panel version, while other `bCivilopediaText` consumers keep
    complete static ability help.

A smaller PLE-local repair may be possible by having `showUpgradeInfoPane`
request non-Civilopedia unit help, but that parameter controls more than these
specific rows and could alter unrelated formatting/content. It is therefore
less robust than separating the actual Sevopedia-only policy from the generic
Civilopedia formatting mode.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTROL — SUPPORTED BUT OPTIONAL PLE SURFACE DOES NOT MAKE THE ROOT DORMANT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`PLE_Style` defaults to False and the Upgrade grouping is user-selected, so
this is not a default-screen-every-turn defect. It is nevertheless a normal
shipped configuration path with active handlers, real upgrade candidates and
user-facing hover rendering. Unlike dormant XML/schema hazards retained
elsewhere in this audit, no hypothetical data edit or unsupported mod-mod
combination is needed to trigger F393.

C031-WIP95 — QUEUE 003 CONTINUATION FROM F394 UNUSED

F394 / KI#717 — VASSAL-ENABLING TECH HELP TESTS `NO_VASSAL_STATES` WITH THE WRONG POLARITY, HIDING THE EFFECT WHEN IT WORKS AND SHOWING IT WHEN THE OPTION DISABLES IT
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: CONFIRMED — inherited BtS UI/help logic bug, retained by K-Mod, Base AdvCiv and current SAS.

ROOT
----
Current `CvGameTextMgr::buildVassalStateString` contains:

    if (GC.getInfo(eTech).isVassalStateTrading() &&
        (!bPlayerContext ||
        (!GET_TEAM(getActiveTeam()).isVassalStateTrading() &&
        GC.getGame().isOption(GAMEOPTION_NO_VASSAL_STATES))))
    {
        if (bList)
            szBuffer.append(NEWLINE);
        szBuffer.append(gDLL->getText("TXT_KEY_MISC_ENABLES_VASSAL_STATES"));
    }

For player-context help, the final condition requires:

    GAMEOPTION_NO_VASSAL_STATES == true

before the tooltip says that the technology enables vassal states.

That is the opposite of the runtime contract.

RUNTIME CONTRACT
----------------
When a team gains a technology, `CvTeam::processTech` does:

    if (kTech.isVassalStateTrading())
        changeVassalTradingCount(iChange);

But the public capability queried by diplomacy is:

    bool CvTeam::isVassalStateTrading() const
    {
        return (!GC.getGame().isOption(GAMEOPTION_NO_VASSAL_STATES) &&
                getVassalTradingCount() > 0);
    }

and actual vassal/capitulation trading checks require the prospective master's
team to satisfy that capability. For example `CvPlayer::canTradeItem` rejects
`TRADE_VASSAL` / `TRADE_SURRENDER` when:

    !kToTeam.isVassalStateTrading()

Thus:

    No Vassal States OFF + enabling tech known -> capability can become TRUE.
    No Vassal States ON  + enabling tech known -> capability remains FALSE.

The help test is therefore exactly reversed with respect to whether the effect
can function.

CURRENT SAS DATA / ORDINARY EXAMPLE
-----------------------------------
Current SAS has:

    TECH_PHILOSOPHY
        <bVassalTrading>1</bVassalTrading>

and the visible game option:

    GAMEOPTION_NO_VASSAL_STATES
        <bDefault>0</bDefault>

So the default game is the simplest live example.

Before Philosophy is researched in a normal/default game:

    kTech.isVassalStateTrading()                         = true
    activeTeam.isVassalStateTrading()                    = false
    GAMEOPTION_NO_VASSAL_STATES                          = false

The player-context helper evaluates:

    true && (false || (true && false))
    -> false

and omits "Enables Vassal States" precisely while the player is evaluating a
technology whose acquisition really will enable the capability.

If the player instead starts a custom game WITH No Vassal States enabled:

    activeTeam.isVassalStateTrading()                    = false
    GAMEOPTION_NO_VASSAL_STATES                          = true

then the same pre-research helper evaluates true and advertises "Enables
Vassal States" even though runtime `CvTeam::isVassalStateTrading()` is forced
false by that option after the tech is acquired.

USER-FACING CALLERS
-------------------
The affected function is part of the ordinary technology-help effect list.
`setTechTradeHelp` calls:

    buildVassalStateString(szBuffer, eTech, true, bPlayerContext);

Player-context tech help is used by live research/technology UI, including
`CvDLLWidgetData::parseResearchHelp` and the unresearched-tech branch of
`parseTechTreeHelp`.

`parseTechTreeHelp` deliberately passes player context while the technology is
not yet known:

    GAMETEXT.setTechHelp(...,
        !GET_TEAM(getActiveTeam()).isHasTech(eTech), ...);

That is exactly the decision-time state in which F394 suppresses Philosophy's
real vassal-enabling effect in the default game.

After the tech is already known, that caller passes `bPlayerContext=false`, so
the static Civilopedia-style branch can display the line. This makes the
mismatch especially perverse: the effect is hidden while deciding whether to
research the tech and can reappear after the player already owns it.

ANCESTRY
--------
The same conditional, including the positive test of
`GAMEOPTION_NO_VASSAL_STATES`, is present in:

    Civ4CE/BtS
    K-Mod
    Base AdvCiv 1.14
    current AdvCiv-SAS

So this is an inherited BtS root rather than a SAS regression.

The unchanged ancestry is also a useful control against interpreting the SAS
technology-tree rework as the cause. SAS's current placement of the flag on
Philosophy merely supplies a live current example; the logic defect predates
it.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
For player-context help, the option predicate should match the runtime's
availability direction. The narrow correction is:

    if (GC.getInfo(eTech).isVassalStateTrading() &&
        (!bPlayerContext ||
        (!GET_TEAM(getActiveTeam()).isVassalStateTrading() &&
         !GC.getGame().isOption(GAMEOPTION_NO_VASSAL_STATES))))

That says to advertise the not-yet-active effect only when the game option
allows it to become active.

A shared/query-based future-proof form would be even safer if technology help
can project the post-tech capability without duplicating option gates, but the
single missing `!` is the demonstrated root.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTROL — NEW `buildBTradeString` / `buildBRepeatString` PLAYER-CONTEXT GATES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The two SAS-added technology helpers initially looked similar because they
also combine XML flags with `bPlayerContext` and current-team tech state.
Their current callers explain the shape:

* while a technology is unresearched, research/tree help passes player context;
* after it is known, the tech-tree caller passes non-player-context static
  help.

No analogous option-polarity contradiction was established there. Current SAS
also has no repeatable technology, so the repeat helper remains dormant under
current XML. These do not consume F395.

C031-WIP96 — QUEUE 003 CONTINUATION FROM F395 UNUSED
===============================================================================

F395 / KI#718 — `NO_TECH_TRADING` GAME OPTION DOES NOT SUPPRESS PLAYER-CONTEXT "ENABLES TECHNOLOGY TRADING" TECH HELP
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: CONFIRMED — inherited BtS player-context help bug, retained by K-Mod, Base AdvCiv and current SAS.

ROOT
----
Current `CvGameTextMgr::buildTechTradeString` says:

    if (GC.getInfo(eTech).isTechTrading() &&
        (!bPlayerContext || !GET_TEAM(getActiveTeam()).isTechTrading()))
    {
        if (bList)
            szBuffer.append(NEWLINE);
        szBuffer.append(gDLL->getText("TXT_KEY_MISC_ENABLES_TECH_TRADING"));
    }

Unlike the neighboring Permanent Alliance helper, and unlike the intended
(option-corrected) Vassal helper from F394, it never checks the game option
that globally disables the advertised action:

    GAMEOPTION_NO_TECH_TRADING

RUNTIME CONTRACT
----------------
The team-level technology flag is only a count:

    bool CvTeam::isTechTrading() const
    {
        return getTechTradingCount() > 0;
    }

so researching the enabling technology still raises that count even in a
No-Tech-Trading game.

But actual player trade legality explicitly gates the trade item:

    case TRADE_TECHNOLOGIES:
        return (!kGame.isOption(GAMEOPTION_NO_TECH_TRADING) &&
                (kOurTeam.isTechTrading() || kToTeam.isTechTrading()));

Thus when the option is enabled, no team can actually trade technologies even
if its technology-count flag says that the enabling technology is known.

CURRENT SAS DATA / LIVE EXAMPLE
-------------------------------
Current SAS has:

    TECH_WRITING
        <bTechTrading>1</bTechTrading>

and exposes the standard visible option:

    GAMEOPTION_NO_TECH_TRADING
        <bDefault>0</bDefault>
        <bVisible>1</bVisible>

In a supported Custom Game with No Tech Trading enabled, before Writing is
known:

    kTech.isTechTrading()             = true
    activeTeam.isTechTrading()        = false
    bPlayerContext                    = true

so `buildTechTradeString` displays:

    "Enables Technology Trading"

while acquiring Writing cannot make any `TRADE_TECHNOLOGIES` item legal
because the runtime option check always rejects it.

USER-FACING SURFACE
-------------------
As with F394, `setTechTradeHelp` invokes this helper in the ordinary technology
effect list. Live research and unresearched Tech Tree hovers use player
context, so this is specifically misleading decision-time help in the game
configuration where the advertised effect has been disabled.

This is not merely the static Civilopedia continuing to describe the XML
technology in isolation. The code has a distinct `bPlayerContext` mode and
neighboring helpers already use game-option state to contextualize effects.

ANCESTRY
--------
The same `buildTechTradeString` condition, without a
`GAMEOPTION_NO_TECH_TRADING` guard, is present in:

    Civ4CE/BtS
    K-Mod
    Base AdvCiv 1.14
    current AdvCiv-SAS

Classification: inherited BtS UI/help omission.

RELATION TO F394
----------------
F394 and F395 share a high-level theme but have different roots:

* F394: `buildVassalStateString` DOES test its disabling option but tests it
  with the wrong polarity, reversing the help state even in the default game.
* F395: `buildTechTradeString` never checks its disabling option at all, so the
  false advertisement occurs in the supported No Tech Trading configuration.

They require different local repairs and are retained as separate findings.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Preserve static/non-player-context description, but suppress the advertised
not-yet-active effect in player context when the option makes it unusable, e.g.
conceptually:

    if (kTech.isTechTrading() &&
        (!bPlayerContext ||
         (!kTeam.isTechTrading() &&
          !kGame.isOption(GAMEOPTION_NO_TECH_TRADING))))

This parallels the correct positive-option treatment already used for
Permanent Alliances.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTROL — PERMANENT ALLIANCE HELPER HAS THE EXPECTED OPTION POLARITY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`buildPermanentAllianceString` requires:

    GAMEOPTION_PERMANENT_ALLIANCES == true

for player-context "Enables Permanent Alliances" help, matching
`CvTeam::isPermanentAllianceTrading()`.

That neighboring implementation is a useful internal control: player-context
tech help is intended to take global option availability into account, and the
Vassal/Tech-Trading cases are not simply a policy of always describing raw XML
flags.
