C031-WIP97 — QUEUE 003 CONTINUATION FROM F396 UNUSED
===============================================================================

F396 / KI#719 — NO-SLAVERY PLAYER-CONTEXT TECH HELP STILL SAYS THE PREREQUISITE TECH "ENABLES" SLAVERY
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: CONFIRMED — inherited AdvCiv option/help omission (advc.912d), live in current SAS.

ROOT
----
Current `CvGameTextMgr::buildCivicRevealString` ignores both `bPlayerContext`
and the No Slavery game option when it lists civics unlocked by a technology:

    if (GC.getInfo(eCivic).getTechPrereq() == eTech)
    {
        ...
        setListHelp(szBuffer, gDLL->getText("TXT_KEY_MISC_ENABLES").c_str(),
                szTempBuffer, L", ", bFirst);
    }

The `bPlayerContext` parameter is accepted but unused. Consequently the live
research/Tech Tree help describes the raw XML prerequisite even when current
rules make adoption impossible for the active human.

RUNTIME CONTRACT
----------------
AdvCiv's `advc.912d` No Slavery option explicitly rejects any human civic that
allows population rushing:

    if (kGame.isOption(GAMEOPTION_NO_SLAVERY) && isHuman())
    {
        FOR_EACH_ENUM(Hurry)
        {
            if (GC.getInfo(eCivic).isHurry(eLoopHurry) &&
                GC.getInfo(eLoopHurry).getProductionPerPopulation() > 0)
            {
                return false;
            }
        }
    }

This is in `CvPlayer::canDoCivics`, i.e. the actual adoption legality path.
The same AdvCiv feature also taught `CvGameTextMgr::parseCivicInfo` to detect
this state and say explicitly that the civic cannot be adopted because of the
No Slavery option. It even suppresses the ordinary technology-requirement
message in that disabled state.

Thus the technology-side "Enables" line and the civic-side player-context help
contradict one another under the same supported game configuration.

CURRENT SAS DATA / LIVE EXAMPLE
-------------------------------
Current SAS exposes:

    GAMEOPTION_NO_SLAVERY
        bDefault = 0
        bVisible = 1

Current Slavery data is:

    CIVIC_SLAVERY
        TechPrereq = TECH_MASONRY
        HURRY_POPULATION = true

and HURRY_POPULATION has positive production-per-population, so the runtime
No-Slavery rejection applies.

Therefore, in a human Custom Game with No Slavery enabled, before Masonry is
known:

    * Masonry's player-context research/Tech Tree hover can say
      "Enables Slavery";
    * acquiring Masonry does not make Slavery adoptable;
    * hovering Slavery itself correctly reports that it cannot be adopted
      because of the No Slavery option.

USER-FACING CALLERS
-------------------
`setTechTradeHelp` calls `buildCivicRevealString` for every civic. The ordinary
research hover passes player context through `CvDLLWidgetData::parseResearchHelp`,
and an unresearched Tech Tree hover does the same through
`CvDLLWidgetData::parseTechTreeHelp`.

This is therefore decision-time in-game help, not merely static Civilopedia
text describing XML in isolation.

ANCESTRY
--------
The No Slavery option was introduced in AdvCiv commit:

    df5a03e743a64c58380ae91f2bdaf586c817f34f
    v0.92f: Changes to replays; "No Slavery" option

The introducing diff modified `CvPlayer` legality and `parseCivicInfo` so that
the civic's own player-context help understands the new option, but it did not
modify the pre-existing `buildCivicRevealString` technology-side "Enables"
list.

BtS/K-Mod cannot contain this exact root because they do not have AdvCiv's
No Slavery option. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the omission.
Classification: inherited AdvCiv UI/help integration bug.

RELATION TO F394/F395
---------------------
This belongs to the same closure family of option-sensitive technology help,
but has an independent origin and repair point:

* F394: BtS vassal helper tests its disabling option with reversed polarity.
* F395: BtS tech-trading helper omits its disabling option.
* F396: AdvCiv adds a new civic-disabling option and updates civic help/runtime,
  but leaves the technology-to-civic "Enables" helper context-blind.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Preserve static/non-player-context Civilopedia behavior, but in player context
omit a civic from the technology's "Enables" list when the active player is
not allowed to adopt it for a game-option reason. The narrow current repair can
mirror the `advc.912d` No-Slavery test; a more future-proof repair would share
an option-legality helper with `parseCivicInfo` rather than duplicate the rule.

Do not blindly use `canDoCivics(eCivic)` as the only predicate: player-context
technology help normally needs to list civics whose only missing condition is
the technology being hovered. The projection must ignore the technology
prerequisite while retaining independent blockers such as No Slavery.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTROL — `GET_TEAM(eActivePlayer)` IN `CvGameTextMgr.cpp` IS NOT A PLAYER/TEAM-ID MIXUP
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The whole-file active-context sweep initially made several calls such as:

    GET_TEAM(eActivePlayer).isHasTech(...)

look suspicious because `eActivePlayer` is `PlayerTypes`. In this translation
unit, however, `CoreAI.h` supplies an overload:

    getTeam(PlayerTypes ePlayer) { return CvTeamAI::AI_getTeam(TEAMID(ePlayer)); }

so the macro intentionally converts a player to that player's actual team.
This remains safe in team games where player and team numeric IDs differ and
does not consume F397.

F397 / provisional KI#720 — AdvCiv LuxuryModifier is omitted from BUG's
additional-building-happiness projection
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
The optional BUG/BULL city happiness hover uses:

    CvGameTextMgr::setBuildingAdditionalHappinessHelp
      -> CvCity::getAdditionalHappinessByBuilding

for every currently constructible building.

The inherited additional-happiness helper handles a building's resource-
conditional happiness by adding the raw XML values:

    FOR_EACH_NON_DEFAULT_PAIR(kBuilding.getBonusHappinessChanges(), Bonus, int)
    {
        if ((hasBonus(eLoopBonus) || kBuilding.getFreeBonus() == eLoopBonus) &&
            kBuilding.getNoBonus() != eLoopBonus)
        {
            addGoodOrBad(perBonusVal.second, iGood, iBad);
        }
    }

AdvCiv's advc.912c Hereditary-Rule rework, however, changed the runtime meaning
of positive bonus happiness. `CvCity::getBonusGoodHappiness()` now returns:

    r = m_iBonusGoodHappiness;
    r = r * (100 + GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).getLuxuryModifier()) / 100;

and `CvCity::happyLevel()` consumes that scaled getter.

Building processing adds positive `BonusHappinessChanges` into
`m_iBonusGoodHappiness`, so the effective happiness gained from a building is
not generally the raw sum that `getAdditionalHappinessByBuilding` reports.
The omission is especially visible because integer rounding is applied to the
whole bonus-happiness pool, not independently to each building entry.

CURRENT SAS DATA / CONCRETE EXAMPLE
-----------------------------------
Current SAS has:

    CIVIC_HEREDITARY_RULE
        iLuxuryModifier = 25

and many live buildings with positive resource-conditioned happiness. The
ordinary Forge alone has:

    Gemstones +1 happiness
    Gold      +1 happiness
    Silver    +1 happiness

Current Gemstones, Gold and Silver each also have base `iHappiness = 1`.

Take a city under Hereditary Rule connected to exactly those three luxury
resources and able to construct a Forge.

Before the Forge:

    raw m_iBonusGoodHappiness = 3
    runtime bonus happiness   = floor(3 * 125 / 100) = 3

After the Forge:

    raw m_iBonusGoodHappiness = 6
    runtime bonus happiness   = floor(6 * 125 / 100) = 7

Actual happiness change from constructing the Forge:

    +4 happiness

The additional-building-happiness helper instead adds the three raw Forge
entries and reports:

    +3 happiness

Its derived `getAdditionalAngryPopuplation(iGood, iBad)` value can therefore
also be wrong in a city near the happy/unhappy threshold.

LIVE USER-FACING CALLER
-----------------------
`CvDLLWidgetData::parseHappinessHelp` invokes this helper for the active-owned
selected city when either:

    MiscHover__BuildingAdditionalHappiness == true

or the player holds Alt while hovering the happiness display.

The BUG option defaults to false, but the Alt-key path makes the calculation
available in every ordinary current game without configuration editing.
This is therefore a live optional/modified-hover information defect, not a
dormant helper with no UI caller.

BREADTH
-------
Current SAS contains 32 BuildingInfos with at least one nonzero
`BonusHappinessChange`, including Forge, Market, Grocer and numerous UBs and
religious/cultural buildings. The defect is therefore not limited to one
custom building.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod already contains the BUG `getAdditionalHappinessByBuilding` raw
BonusHappinessChanges calculation, but it has no AdvCiv LuxuryModifier system.

AdvCiv commit/diff `AdvCivPreSAS_1287_ad5faf8aa2` introduced advc.912c:
* `iLuxuryModifier` in CivicInfo;
* Hereditary Rule `iLuxuryModifier = 25`;
* player LuxuryModifier state;
* the scaling in `CvCity::getBonusGoodHappiness`.

That introducing diff does not update `getAdditionalHappinessByBuilding`.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains both the LuxuryModifier scaling and the old raw BUG
projection, and its own current building data also has many positive
BonusHappinessChanges. Current SAS inherits the omission and expands the number
of affected buildings.

Classification:
    inherited AdvCiv integration defect between advc.912c and BUG's
    additional-building-happiness preview.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Do not simply multiply each building bonus-happiness entry by LuxuryModifier
independently; runtime rounds the whole positive bonus-happiness pool.

The projection should compare the effective before/after bonus-happiness
getter, e.g. conceptually:

    oldRaw = getBonusGoodHappiness(true);
    newRaw = oldRaw + raw positive bonus-happiness added by the building;
    oldEffective = oldRaw * (100 + luxuryMod) / 100;
    newEffective = newRaw * (100 + luxuryMod) / 100;
    iGood += newEffective - oldEffective;

while preserving separate handling of negative bonus happiness, which
`getBonusBadHappiness()` does not pass through LuxuryModifier.

A still stronger repair would centralize the projected building effect around
the same runtime transformation rather than duplicating the rounding rule.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTROL — `setHealthHappyBuildActionHelp` SIGN / ROUNDING RECONCILIATION
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The unfinished WIP97 comparison was completed before promoting F397.

The apparent sign oddities are intentional:
* surrounding bad happiness/health storage uses non-positive values;
* the UI flips bad-health/unhappiness deltas so "more bad" is shown as a
  positive amount beside the bad icon;
* percentage offsets are fed into `calculateSurroundingHealth` while the
  current feature/improvement is still physically present, correctly
  projecting feature removal and improvement replacement;
* good and bad health are rounded separately, matching the runtime storage
  contract.

Opposite-sign replacement and fractional Forest/Jungle cases were challenged;
no independent F397 root exists in this helper chain.

F398 / provisional KI#721 — BUG additional-production hover treats conditional
military/domain/space production modifiers as ordinary production yield
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
The optional production hover calls:

    CvGameTextMgr::setBuildingAdditionalYieldHelp(..., YIELD_PRODUCTION, ...)
      -> CvCity::getAdditionalYieldByBuilding
      -> CvCity::getAdditionalYieldRateModifierByBuilding

The helper contract says it returns the additional *yield* supplied by adding a
building. For `YIELD_PRODUCTION`, however, the inherited BUG helper adds:

    kBuilding.getMilitaryProductionModifier();
    kBuilding.getSpaceProductionModifier();
    kBuilding.getGlobalSpaceProductionModifier();
    max(kBuilding.getDomainProductionModifier(...));

into the city's projected ordinary base-yield modifier.

Those fields do not modify `CvCity::getYieldRate(YIELD_PRODUCTION)`.
Runtime applies them only to matching production orders:

* `CvCity::getProductionModifier(UnitTypes)` adds the city's domain modifier
  for the unit's actual domain and adds military production only when the unit
  is military production;
* `CvCity::getProductionModifier(ProjectTypes)` adds space production only for
  spaceship projects;
* building production uses neither military nor domain nor spaceship-only
  modifiers.

The preview therefore converts conditional order modifiers into generic hammer
output, and also loses the conditions by adding *all* families at once (using
only the largest DomainProductionModifier).

CURRENT SAS DATA / SIMPLE LIVE EXAMPLE
--------------------------------------
Current SAS `BUILDING_HEROIC_EPIC` has:

    iMilitaryProductionModifier = 50
    ordinary YieldModifier(PRODUCTION) = 0

Take an active-owned city with:

    base production yield = 10 hammers
    base yield modifier   = 100%
    Heroic Epic currently constructible

The additional-building-production calculation projects:

    10 * (100 + 50) / 100 - 10 * 100 / 100 = +5 hammers

and can therefore list approximately:

    Heroic Epic: +5 [production]

Yet once Heroic Epic exists, the city's ordinary production yield remains 10.
A building order still receives no Heroic-Epic modifier at all. Only qualifying
military-unit production receives the +50% order-specific bonus.

Current SAS provides another direct family example:

    BUILDING_DRYDOCK
        DomainProductionModifier(DOMAIN_SEA) = 50

The preview treats that as generic city production although runtime applies it
only when the actual unit being trained has DOMAIN_SEA.

LIVE USER-FACING CALLER
-----------------------
`CvGameTextMgr::setProductionHelp` enables the additional-building-yield block
when either:

    MiscHover__BuildingAdditionalProduction == true

or the player holds Alt. It then calls the helper for every visible/
constructible building in the active-owned selected city.

Thus the defect is reachable in an ordinary current game simply by holding Alt
on the production hover; the BUG option need not be permanently enabled.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod 1.46 already contains the same BUG `getAdditionalYieldRateModifierByBuilding`
logic, including unconditional addition of military/space/global-space and the
maximum domain production modifier for `YIELD_PRODUCTION`.

The Civ4CE/BtS core does not provide this BUG helper layer. Base AdvCiv 1.14
inherits the K-Mod/BUG code and current SAS retains it.

Classification:
    inherited BUG/K-Mod optional-hover calculation defect.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
If this helper is meant to honor its stated *yield* contract, remove
order-specific military/domain/space modifiers from
`getAdditionalYieldRateModifierByBuilding`; only modifiers that actually alter
`getBaseYieldRateModifier(YIELD_PRODUCTION)` belong there.

If the UI instead intends to answer "how much would this building change the
currently selected production order?", then it needs a different projection:
* inspect the current order type;
* for a unit, use that unit's actual Domain and military-production flag;
* for a project, apply space production only when it is a spaceship;
* for a building, omit those order-specific fields;
* compare the projected before/after `getCurrentProductionDifference`-style
  result rather than relabeling those modifiers as ordinary yield.

The current hybrid (all conditional modifiers -> generic production yield) is
not contract-correct under either interpretation.

with runtime before/after `unhealthyPopulation` for those reachable modifier
states, including the cap at -100%.

No F399 from that rounding path.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F399 / provisional KI#722 — BUG saved-maintenance hover omits government-center
maintenance savings entirely
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT / CONTRACT
---------------
The optional city maintenance hover calls:

    CvGameTextMgr::setBuildingSavedMaintenanceHelp
      -> CvCity::getSavedMaintenanceTimes100ByBuilding

The helper was introduced by K-Mod's BUG "actual building effect" integration
with the explicit contract:

    "Returns the total additional gold from saved maintenance times 100 that
     adding one of the given buildings will provide."

Yet the implementation considers only:

    int iModifier = kBuilding.getMaintenanceModifier();

and returns zero whenever that scalar percentage modifier is zero.

Government-center buildings reduce maintenance by an entirely different live
mechanism. `CvCity::processBuilding` calls:

    changeGovernmentCenterCount(kBuilding.isGovernmentCenter() ? iChange : 0);

and `changeGovernmentCenterCount` immediately calls:

    GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).updateMaintenance();

The player's cities then recompute distance maintenance. K-Mod's
`calculateMaintenanceDistance` explicitly uses the shortest distance to any
owned city for which `isGovernmentCenter()` is true.

CURRENT SAS DATA / SIMPLE LIVE PROOF
------------------------------------
Current SAS `BUILDING_FORBIDDEN_PALACE` has:

    bGovernmentCenter     = 1
    iMaintenanceModifier  = 0
    PrereqTech            = TECH_CONSTITUTION
    iCitiesPrereq         = 6

Therefore, whenever Forbidden Palace is currently constructible:

    getSavedMaintenanceTimes100ByBuilding(BUILDING_FORBIDDEN_PALACE)
        -> iModifier == 0
        -> returns 0

and `setBuildingSavedMaintenanceHelp` omits the building completely.

But take any eligible city that currently pays positive distance maintenance.
After Forbidden Palace completes there, that same city is itself a government
center. In `calculateMaintenanceDistance` the loop encounters the city at
plotDistance 0, so its shortest-government-center distance becomes 0 and its
positive distance-maintenance component disappears. The resulting maintenance
saving is real even before considering any other city.

The runtime effect can be larger still: because the government-center count
change triggers an owner-wide `updateMaintenance()`, other nearby cities can
also replace a farther Palace/government center with the new Forbidden Palace
as their shortest government center and reduce their distance maintenance.

Thus the helper can report zero saved gold for a building whose completion
immediately saves positive maintenance in the very city being hovered, and can
also save maintenance elsewhere in the empire.

LIVE USER-FACING CALLER
-----------------------
`CvDLLWidgetData::parseMaintenanceHelp` invokes the helper for an active-owned
selected city when either:

    MiscHover__BuildingSavedMaintenance == true

or the player holds Alt (`GC.altKey()`, AdvCiv advc.063).

The BUG option defaults to false, but the Alt path makes the defect ordinarily
reachable without changing configuration.

Static building help separately prints `TXT_KEY_BUILDING_REDUCES_MAINTENANCE`
for `isGovernmentCenter()`, so the government-center reduction is also
explicitly advertised as a maintenance effect; it is not an unrelated ability
outside the saved-maintenance concept.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod commit 8478443165fcaeca861fc9d2dbb725de7e94ca59,
"Implemented \"actual building effect\" mouse-over hover options from BUG",
introduced `getSavedMaintenanceTimes100ByBuilding` with the same percentage-
modifier-only algorithm and the quoted total-saved-gold contract.

Civ4CE/BtS does not contain this BUG helper layer. Base AdvCiv 1.14 inherits the
same omission, and current SAS retains it while current data provides the live
Forbidden Palace example above.

Classification:
    inherited BUG/K-Mod optional-hover calculation omission.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
A contract-correct projection cannot be based only on `iMaintenanceModifier`.
For an ordinary maintenance-modifier building, the current cheap calculation is
fine. For a hypothetical new government center, the projection must also
recalculate distance maintenance with the candidate city treated as a center.

If "total additional gold" is interpreted literally, the strongest repair is
to compare owner-wide maintenance before/after the hypothetical center, because
the new center can reduce maintenance in several cities. A narrower city-only
repair would at least project the hovered city's distance maintenance with a
zero-distance center and would fix the simplest Forbidden Palace false zero,
but would still understate the building's empire-wide saved gold.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTROL — GOVERNMENT-CENTER EFFECT IS NOT MERELY HIDDEN ELSEWHERE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Generic building help does tell the player that a government center "reduces
maintenance", but it does not calculate the current-state gold amount. The BUG
"Building Saved Maintenance" feature exists specifically to provide those
actual-state numerical projections. Therefore the static line is not a numeric
replacement that would make the false-zero projection intentional.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F400 / provisional KI#723 — Finance city-maintenance breakdown rounds its
components to a different total than the total it actually displays
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvGameTextMgr::buildFinanceCityMaintString` computes the displayed distance,
colony and corporation components at scaled precision and rounds each one.
It then derives the residual number-of-cities component from:

    (kPlayer.getTotalMaintenance() * rInflationFactor).round()

so the four displayed components are forced to add up to a *rounded* inflated
maintenance total.

But the fifth argument sent to `TXT_KEY_FINANCE_ADVISOR_CITY_MAINT_COST`—the
line's displayed total—is instead:

    (kPlayer.getTotalMaintenance() * iInflationFactorTimes100) / 100

which is integer division and therefore truncates.

The engine's normal inflated-cost calculation likewise multiplies the integer
pre-inflated cost and then divides by 100. Thus the helper uses two different
rounding contracts inside one breakdown: round-to-nearest to derive the
components, truncate for the displayed total.

EXACT CURRENT-SAS CONSTRUCTION
------------------------------
A fully current-data state can make the contradiction explicit.

Use:

    game speed       = Normal
    world size       = Standard
    handicap         = Noble
    civ players ever = 8 (the Standard recommended count)
    owned cities     = 6
    each population  = 8
    civic            = State Property
    all cities on capital's landmass
    no corporations
    no maintenance-modifier buildings

State Property has `iDistanceMaintenanceModifier = -100`, so distance
maintenance is zero. Same-area cities have zero colony maintenance, and no
corporations means zero corporation maintenance.

For Standard/Noble with the recommended-player crowdedness factor 1, current
number-of-cities maintenance per population-8 city is:

    maintenance cities       = 6
    population factor        = (8 + 17) / 18 = 25/18
    Standard city factor     = 30%
    Noble city factor        = 75%

    6 * 25/18 * 30% * 75% = 1.875 gold

`scaled::getPercent()` rounds this to 188 hundredths per city. Across six
cities, `m_iTotalMaintenance` is therefore 1128 hundredths and:

    getTotalMaintenance() = 1128 / 100 = 11

(the rules intentionally truncate only after city maintenance has been
aggregated).

On an ordinary Normal-speed game where game turn and elapsed turns are both
230, current inflation is exactly 50%:

    adjusted turns = 230 + (-90 Normal offset) = 140
    first term      = floor(140 * 30 / 100) = 42
    second term     = floor(140 * 139 * 30 * 30 / 2,000,000) = 8
    inflation       = 50%

With distance/colony/corporation components all zero, the helper computes:

    displayed number-of-cities component
      = round(11 * 1.50)
      = 17 gold

but passes as the displayed total:

    floor(11 * 150 / 100)
      = 16 gold

So the same Finance Advisor tooltip can effectively say:

    Number of Cities: 17 gold
    Total:            16 gold

with every other city-maintenance component equal to zero.

This is a direct internal contradiction, not merely a one-gold disagreement
with an external screen.

LIVE CALLER
-----------
`CvDLLWidgetData::parseFinanceCityMaint` calls
`buildFinanceCityMaintString` for the Finance Advisor city-maintenance widget
when its data flag is positive. The path is part of the ordinary Finance
Advisor hover UI.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod already derived `iNumCityMaint` with `ROUND_DIVIDE` but displayed the
maintenance total using truncating integer division, so the rounding split is
inherited from K-Mod.

AdvCiv commit 305e9a675013ef3e800526eee894c92864f05210,
"Refactor code for city maintenance breakdown", explicitly changed the three
named components to `scaled` precision and retained the split:

    iNumCityMaint = (... * rInflationFactor).round() - components

versus

    total = (... * iInflationFactorTimes100) / 100

The commit comment says the goal is to improve precision and notes that rules
round costs down only after adding components, but the residual component still
balances against a rounded rather than truncated total. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
current SAS retain that result.

Classification:
    inherited K-Mod finance-breakdown rounding defect, retained through
    AdvCiv's later precision refactor.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Use one target total consistently. Since the displayed/rules total uses integer
truncation, derive the residual component from that same integer:

    int iTotalMaint = (kPlayer.getTotalMaintenance() *
            iInflationFactorTimes100) / 100;

    int iNumCityMaint = iTotalMaint - iDistanceMaint -
            iColonyMaint - iCorpMaint;

and pass `iTotalMaint` as the final localization argument.

That guarantees the displayed breakdown sums to its displayed total. If the UI
instead intentionally wants a rounded presentation, then the total line must be
changed to that same rounded value; mixing both contracts is the root.

CONTROL — REMAINING BUG COMMERCE / GREAT-PEOPLE BUILDING PROJECTIONS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The adjacent BUG projections were challenged before moving into finance.

* Additional commerce uses the city's runtime base-commerce and total commerce
  modifier structure, including the No Espionage culture/espionage transfer.
* Additional Great People combines current base GPP with local and global GPP
  modifiers consistently with `getTotalGreatPeopleRateModifier`.
* AdvCiv advc.051 introduced a valid-civilization-GP-unit mapping guard in
  runtime base-GPP processing that the old BUG projection does not reproduce.
  Current playable civilizations, however, have the needed mappings; the
  obvious Barbarian mismatch is not reachable through the active-human hover
  caller. It remains a dormant mod-data hazard, not a supported F401.
* Finance unit-cost breakdown also leaves `iExtraCost` unscaled by inflation,
  but current SAS has zero UnitInfos with nonzero `iExtraCost`, so that inherited
  issue is data-dormant and not numbered.

C031-WIP102 — QUEUE 003 CONTINUATION FROM WIP101

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F401 / provisional KI#724 — Finance Advisor foreign-trade row can have a blank
hover when exactly one profitable foreign trade route exists
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvGameTextMgr::buildForeignTradeString` calculates the player's current
foreign trade yield and route count, but only assigns any hover text when:

    if(iForeignRoutes > 1)

The corresponding Finance Advisor row has a different visibility contract.
Current `CvDomesticAdvisor.py` obtains the trade yield through
`TradeUtil.calculateTradeRoutes(player)` and creates the Foreign Trade row
whenever:

    if iForeignTrade > 0:

Both the row label and its displayed amount use
`WIDGET_HELP_FINANCE_FOREIGN_TRADE`, so a positive one-route state produces a
visible interactive row whose C++ help builder returns an empty buffer.

CURRENT-DATA REACHABILITY
-------------------------
This does not require an exotic route-count distribution.

BtS `INITIAL_TRADE_ROUTES` is 1, and current SAS does not override that
inherited global define. `CvPlayer::initOtherData` applies that value through
`changeTradeRoutes`, and `CvCity::getTradeRoutes` starts from the player's
trade-route count.

A one-city player connected to a foreign civilization can therefore have one
available route slot filled by one foreign city and no second owned city whose
routes would inflate the empire-wide count. `CvCity::calculateTradeTotals`
counts every non-null foreign trade city independently, so this state gives:

    iForeignRoutes = 1

The route can ordinarily have positive commerce: `getBaseTradeProfit` clamps
base trade profit to at least 100 (hundredths), and the normal commerce trade
yield modifier is positive. Thus the Python Finance Advisor can simultaneously
have:

    iForeignTrade > 0     -> Foreign Trade row is shown
    iForeignRoutes == 1   -> C++ hover text is not assigned

The result is a visible, profitable Foreign Trade row with a blank tooltip.

DOMESTIC COMPANION
------------------
`buildDomesticTradeString` has the same `iDomesticRoutes > 1` predicate, while
the current Finance Advisor deliberately shows the domestic/trade row always
(`advc.086: "Always show this to avoid confusion"). Exactly-one-domestic-route
states therefore deserve the same treatment if reached. The foreign-route
construction above is already sufficient to establish the root without
needing to rely on domestic route symmetry or disruption edge cases.

TEXT CONTRACT
-------------
The localization keys currently read:

    "%d1[ICON_COMMERCE] from %d2 Domestic Trade Routes"
    "%d1[ICON_COMMERCE] from %d2 Foreign Trade Routes"

so the original `> 1` may have been intended to avoid a singular/plural grammar
issue. That does not make an empty hover on a visible Finance row correct. A
singular key, plural-aware localization, or simply displaying the count-1
summary would all preserve information better than suppressing the hover.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod's current `CvGameTextMgr.cpp` does not contain these two finance-summary
builders. They were added to AdvCiv in commit
4a65bf5c0fb187fd25d4908346abb462354a9172,
"Option for expanding scoreboard; BULL hover text".

The introducing diff explicitly shows the AdvCiv `advc.086` replacement:

    //buildTradeString(... false, true, false);
    // <advc.086> Replacing the above
    ...
    if(iForeignRoutes > 1) {
        szBuffer.assign(...);
    }

The same commit adds the Finance Advisor widget parsers and imports the BULL
hover subsystem. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the `> 1` gate.

Classification:
    AdvCiv/advc.086 Finance Advisor hover integration defect, retained by SAS.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Match the builder's visibility threshold to the data that makes the Finance
row meaningful:

    if(iForeignRoutes > 0)

and likewise for domestic trade if retaining these summary builders.

If English singular/plural grammar is important, use a dedicated count-1 text
key or a plural-aware text form rather than suppressing the only explanatory
hover.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

===============================================================================
C031-WIP103 — QUEUE 003 CvGameTextMgr.cpp CONTINUATION
F402 / provisional KI#725 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

Continuation basis
------------------
Resumed from C031-WIP102 with Queue 003 still open and F402 unused. This pass
continued the AdvCiv-only TextMgr-member reconciliation rather than revisiting
already saturated linear regions. The first targets were the city/bonus trade
perspective helpers, relation helpers, civic-reveal button path, combat-action
helpers and other previously low-mention AdvCiv additions.

Controls before F402
--------------------

1. setCityTradeHelp perspective/liberation logic survives.

The Foreign Advisor folds city owner and recipient into WIDGET_CITY_TRADE.
CvDLLWidgetData::parseCityTradeHelp reconstructs those exact two players.
setCityTradeHelp then chooses eOtherPlayer from the active-player perspective
and calls AI_cityTrade on the actual city owner. The initially odd:

    bool bLiberate = (eWhoTo == eOtherPlayer &&
                      kCity.getLiberationPlayer() == eWhoTo);

is correct for the relevant direction: it describes a city owned by the active
player that the rival recipient wants liberated. When the rival owns the city
and the active player is recipient, the owner is instead described as willing
to cede it. The Foreign Advisor's own column population uses canTradeItem and
getTradeDenial/AI_cityTrade consistently with this helper. No F402 here.

2. setBonusTradeHelp valuation direction survives.

For a rival exporting a resource to the active human, the helper's
pActivePlayer->AI_goldForBonus(eBonus, eTradePlayer) asks how much the human is
willing to pay for the rival's bonus in the rival's estimate, matching
AI_goldForBonus/AI_bonusTradeVal's documented eBonusOwner/eFromPlayer contract.
For the opposite (rival importing the active player's resource), the rival's
AI_goldForBonus(eBonus, eActivePlayer) correctly gives how much that rival will
pay. The Foreign Advisor's +1000 import-column encoding is decoded consistently.
No supported perspective inversion found.

3. parseSingleCivicRevealHelp has a live No-Slavery omission, but it is a
   companion consequence of F396 rather than a new root.

The Tech Tree's WIDGET_HELP_CIVIC_REVEAL calls parseSingleCivicRevealHelp.
That helper intentionally passes:

    parseCivicInfo(..., bCivilopediaText=true,
                   bPlayerContext=true, bSkipName=true)

in order to hide the civic's technology prerequisite. AdvCiv's No-Slavery
warning in parseCivicInfo is itself gated by !bCivilopediaText, so a Slavery
button revealed by Masonry also omits the "cannot adopt" warning under No
Slavery. This is the same AdvCiv option/help integration omission already
numbered F396 (tech help says Masonry enables an unavailable Slavery civic),
not an independent root.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F402 / provisional KI#725 — PAIR-SPECIFIC LEADER-RELATIONS HOVERS CAN LIST
UNRELATED THIRD-PARTY WARS / WORST-ENEMY RELATIONS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
File: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp
Primary functions:
    CvGameTextMgr::parseLeaderHeadRelationsHelp
    CvGameTextMgr::getOtherRelationsString(PlayerTypes, PlayerTypes)
    CvGameTextMgr::getOtherRelationsString(TeamTypes, TeamTypes, TeamTypes)
Live callers:
    CvDLLWidgetData::parseLeaderheadRelationsHelp
    WIDGET_LEADERHEAD_RELATIONS
    WIDGET_LH_GLANCE
    CvForeignAdvisor.py Glance matrix
    CvBUGMilitaryAdvisor.py relation icons
Classification:
    AdvCiv BULL/K-Mod leader-relations integration defect; retained by SAS.

ROOT
----
AdvCiv contains two incompatible contracts for the same relation helper chain.

The top-level pair hover explicitly says:

    // Displays the relations between two leaders only.
    // This is used by the F4:GLANCE and F5:SIT-REP tabs.

and, for a non-active-player pair, does:

    else getOtherRelationsString(szBuffer, eThisPlayer, eOtherPlayer);

The PlayerTypes overload converts that pair directly to:

    getOtherRelationsString(szString,
        TEAMID(eThisPlayer), TEAMID(eOtherPlayer), NO_TEAM);

The TeamTypes overload's own contract then says:

    If eOtherTeam is not NO_TEAM, only relations between it and
    eThisTeam are shown.

But current code explicitly marks eOtherTeam unused and comments out the only
predicate that would implement that contract:

    void CvGameTextMgr::getOtherRelationsString(...,
        TeamTypes eThisTeam,
        /* (advc: unused) */ TeamTypes eOtherTeam,
        TeamTypes eSkipTeam)
    {
        ...
        if (itThird->getID() == eSkipTeam)
            // || (eOtherTeam != NO_TEAM &&
            //     itThird->getID() != eOtherTeam)
            continue;
        ...
    }

Consequently, supplying eOtherTeam does not restrict anything. The iterator
walks every major civilization known to eThisTeam and visible to the active
team, and appends every matching war / worst-enemy relation it finds.

LIVE UI PATH
------------
Current CvForeignAdvisor.py Glance cells use either
WIDGET_LEADERHEAD_RELATIONS or WIDGET_LH_GLANCE, with the matrix's two player
IDs stored in data1/data2. Both widget parsers reach
parseLeaderHeadRelationsHelp(data1, data2).

Current CvBUGMilitaryAdvisor.py also uses WIDGET_LEADERHEAD_RELATIONS for
specific pair icons such as:

- current-war opponents,
- vassals,
- defensive pacts,
- possible war targets,
- possible embargo targets,
- worst enemy.

Thus this is not a dead helper or a generic leader tooltip only; it is directly
used on UI elements whose visible cell/icon identifies a particular pair.

CONCRETE STATE
--------------
Let the active human know all three AI civilizations A, B and C.

Suppose:

    A is at peace with B,
    A is at war with C.

Hover a Glance matrix cell representing the A/B pair (or another pair-specific
WIDGET_LEADERHEAD_RELATIONS icon involving A and B).

parseLeaderHeadRelationsHelp first shows A/B-specific material such as
attitude and active deals. Because B is not the active player, it then calls
getOtherRelationsString(A, B).

The intended eOtherTeam=B filter is disabled. The iterator reaches C, sees
that C is at war with A, and appends:

    "At war with C"

Even though C is not one of the two leaders represented by the hovered cell.
If another known AI has A as worst enemy, that unrelated civilization can be
appended as well.

The amount of unrelated output grows with the number of known third parties
and A's diplomatic state; this is not a one-off formatting discrepancy.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE GENERAL K-MOD LEADER-HOVER CONTRACT
-------------------------------------------------------
There is a legitimate separate caller with broader semantics:
parseLeaderHeadHelp (the ordinary leader tooltip) intentionally retains
K-Mod's behavior of showing a leader's relations with other civilizations.
That explains why simply deleting all third-party relation display would be
wrong.

The defect is the collision between that broad K-Mod behavior and the BULL
pair-specific helper. parseLeaderHeadRelationsHelp explicitly promises
"relations between two leaders only," while the shared PlayerTypes overload
currently routes it through the broad behavior.

ANCESTRY
--------
Civ4CE/BtS and K-Mod have only the older PlayerTypes
getOtherRelationsString. K-Mod deliberately broadened that old helper by
allowing the selected other player's team to appear among the leader's wider
relations (its comment: "show 'at war' even for the civ selected").

AdvCiv commit:

    4a65bf5c0fb187fd25d4908346abb462354a9172
    "Option for expanding scoreboard; BULL hover text"

introduced the BULL relation-hover subsystem, including:

- parseLeaderHeadRelationsHelp with the explicit two-leader-only contract,
- getAllRelationsString,
- getActiveTeamRelationsString,
- the TeamTypes getOtherRelationsString with eOtherTeam/eSkipTeam controls.

The introducing diff already contains the contradictory merge:

    /* advc: This BULL function replaces ... I've merged just one K-Mod
       change from the latter. */
    ...
    i == eSkipTeam /*|| (eOtherTeam != NO_TEAM && i != eOtherTeam)*/

and marks eOtherTeam unused. In other words, while importing BULL's
pair-filterable helper, AdvCiv applied K-Mod's broader old-helper behavior by
commenting out the new helper's eOtherTeam filter. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current
SAS retain that state.

This is therefore best classified as an AdvCiv BULL/K-Mod integration defect,
not a SAS-local regression and not a raw BtS bug.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The two contracts need to remain distinct.

For pair-specific relation help, honor eOtherTeam:

    if (itThird->getID() == eSkipTeam ||
        (eOtherTeam != NO_TEAM && itThird->getID() != eOtherTeam))
    {
        continue;
    }

But do not blindly narrow the ordinary K-Mod-style leader hover, which
intentionally wants broader third-party relations. One conservative structure
is:

- let pair-specific parseLeaderHeadRelationsHelp call the TeamTypes overload
  with eOtherTeam set, and honor the filter there;
- let broad parseLeaderHeadHelp call the TeamTypes overload with
  eOtherTeam=NO_TEAM (and an appropriate skip team if desired), preserving its
  broader relation summary.

Equivalently, split pair and broad modes explicitly so a PlayerTypes overload
cannot silently serve both incompatible purposes.

RELATED CONTROL
---------------
The TeamTypes helper also accumulates szPeace and szPact but currently never
prints them. That is suspicious against its "peace/war/enemy/pact" comment,
but direct pair peace/pact information is already covered by active-deal help,
and the historical merge needs a separate consumer/intent proof before this
should be numbered independently. It is therefore retained as closure debt,
not promoted as F403 here.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F403 / provisional KI#726 — THIRD-PARTY FORCE-PEACE AND DEFENSIVE-PACT STATES
ARE COMPUTED BUT NEVER RENDERED IN LEADER-RELATIONS HELP
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
File: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp
Primary functions:
    CvGameTextMgr::getAllRelationsString
    CvGameTextMgr::getActiveTeamRelationsString
    CvGameTextMgr::getOtherRelationsString(TeamTypes, TeamTypes, TeamTypes)
Live broad consumer:
    CvGameTextMgr::parseLeaderHeadHelp
    ordinary leader / scoreboard-style help through CvDLLWidgetData
Classification:
    AdvCiv BULL leader-relations integration omission; retained by SAS.

ROOT
----
The TeamTypes relation helper explicitly advertises four relation families:

    "peace/war/enemy/pact status"

and allocates / fills four corresponding strings:

    CvWString szWar, szPeace, szEnemy, szPact;

    if (itThird->isAtWar(eThisTeam))
        setListHelp(szWar, ...);
    else if (itThird->isForcePeace(eThisTeam))
        setListHelp(szPeace, ...);
    ...
    if (itThird->isDefensivePact(eThisTeam))
        setListHelp(szPact, ...);

But the function's output section renders only szWar and szEnemy. szPeace and
szPact are never appended to szString at all.

This is not harmless dead computation in the broad leader-hover path.
parseLeaderHeadHelp(eThisPlayer, eOtherPlayer) does:

    getActiveDealsString(szBuffer, eThisPlayer, eOtherPlayer);
    ...
    getOtherRelationsString(szBuffer, eThisPlayer, eOtherPlayer);

The active-deal call is strictly pair-specific: getActiveDealsString iterates
only deals for which pDeal->isBetween(eThisPlayer, eOtherPlayer). In the usual
leader hover eOtherPlayer is the active human. It therefore cannot render a
peace treaty or defensive pact between the hovered AI and some third AI.

CONCRETE LIVE STATE
-------------------
Let the active human H have met AI teams A and B, and let A and B have a
Defensive Pact.

Hover A through a normal leader-help consumer with H as the comparison player.
The pair-specific active-deal scan can display A<->H deals only. The subsequent
relation scan reaches B, verifies that the active team knows B, sees:

    B.isDefensivePact(A) == true

and appends B's name to szPact. But there is no later output block for szPact,
so the broader leader-relations help omits that known A<->B pact entirely.

The same omission applies to a known force-peace relation between A and B:
szPeace is populated but never rendered.

WHY THIS IS DISTINCT FROM F402
------------------------------
F402 is a filtering defect: pair-specific A/B hovers accidentally include
unrelated C/D war and worst-enemy information because eOtherTeam is ignored.

F403 is an output defect: even in the broad relation mode where third-party
relations are wanted, two relation families that the helper deliberately
collects are silently discarded.

Restoring the eOtherTeam filter for F402 does not repair F403, and rendering
szPeace/szPact does not repair F402. They therefore have independent roots and
repairs.

ACTIVE-PLAYER PAIR CONTROL
--------------------------
getActiveTeamRelationsString intentionally comments out force-peace and
Defensive Pact lines for relations directly involving the active player:

    // advc: Covered by active deals

That is a valid duplicate-suppression argument because getActiveDealsString can
show the direct A<->H treaty/pact. It does not apply to A<->B third-party
relations in parseLeaderHeadHelp, because that active-deal scan never examines
A<->B.

ANCESTRY
--------
Civ4CE/BtS and K-Mod contain only the older PlayerTypes relation helper and do
not contain this four-list BULL TeamTypes implementation.

AdvCiv commit:

    4a65bf5c0fb187fd25d4908346abb462354a9172
    "Option for expanding scoreboard; BULL hover text"

introduced the BULL relation subsystem. The introducing diff already creates,
populates, and then drops szPeace and szPact while rendering only szWar and
szEnemy. The same introducing code comments out the active-player peace/pact
lines specifically because active deals cover them, which strengthens the
contrast: no equivalent third-party deal consumer exists for the discarded
lists.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the omission unchanged.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
After the existing szWar output, render non-empty szPeace with the existing
TXT_KEY_PEACE_TREATY_WITH key; after the relevant relation output, render
non-empty szPact with TXT_KEY_DEFENSIVE_PACT_WITH. Preserve the direct
active-player duplicate suppression in getActiveTeamRelationsString.

When combined with F402's repair, pair-specific mode should honor eOtherTeam,
while broad mode should continue scanning all known third parties and actually
render all relation families it collects.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F404 / provisional KI#727 — ADVCIV FOUNDING HOVER OMITS GOLDEN-AGE YIELD FROM
THE PROJECTED CITY HOME TILE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
File: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp
Primary function: CvGameTextMgr::setHomePlotYieldHelp
Runtime comparator: CvPlot::calculateYield / CvPlot::calculateCityPlotYieldChange
Live consumer: CvDLLWidgetData MISSION_FOUND action help
Classification: inherited AdvCiv founding-help projection omission; retained by
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS.

ROOT
----
The Found mission hover labels a line as the projected home-tile yield, but
setHomePlotYieldHelp reconstructs only nature yield and the minimum city yield:

    int iYieldRate = kCityPlot.calculateNatureYield(
            eLoopYield, getActiveTeam(), true);
    CvYieldInfo const& kLoopYield = GC.getInfo(eLoopYield);
    iYieldRate = std::max(iYieldRate, kLoopYield.getMinCity());

Actual city-center yield does not stop there. CvPlot::calculateYield performs
its ordinary plot calculation and, once the plot has a city, applies
calculateCityPlotYieldChange. It then still applies player-level yield
thresholds and Golden Age yield:

    if (GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).isGoldenAge())
    {
        if (iYield >= GC.getInfo(eYield).getGoldenAgeYieldThreshold())
            iYield += GC.getInfo(eYield).getGoldenAgeYield();
    }

The founding helper never applies that Golden Age stage.

CONCRETE CURRENT-SAS STATE
--------------------------
Current Yield XML has:

    YIELD_FOOD:
        iMinCity = 2
        iGoldenAgeYield = 0

    YIELD_PRODUCTION:
        iMinCity = 1
        iGoldenAgeYieldThreshold = 1
        iGoldenAgeYield = 1

    YIELD_COMMERCE:
        iMinCity = 1
        iGoldenAgeYieldThreshold = 1
        iGoldenAgeYield = 1

Take an ordinary legal city site whose post-city minimum home-tile values are
2 food, 1 hammer and 1 commerce, and let the active player be in a Golden Age.
The founding hover reconstructs and displays:

    Home Tile Yield: 2 food, 1 hammer, 1 commerce

After founding, CvCity::init assigns the owner and calls kPlot.setPlotCity(this).
CvPlot::setPlotCity calls updateYield, so the new city plot immediately runs
CvPlot::calculateYield as a city tile while its owner is still in the same
Golden Age. The 1 hammer and 1 commerce both meet their threshold, producing:

    actual home tile: 2 food, 2 hammers, 2 commerce

Nothing about founding a city ends the player's Golden Age, and Settlers remain
ordinary live founding units in current SAS. This is therefore reachable
normal gameplay, not a hypothetical XML configuration.

BROADER CONTRACT
----------------
The root is slightly broader than Golden Ages: setHomePlotYieldHelp is a manual
partial reconstruction of CvPlot::calculateYield. Player-level extra-yield
thresholds are also evaluated after the city-plot stage at runtime and are not
reproduced by this helper. Golden Age yield is the clean current-data proof and
sufficient live consequence; no speculative extra case is needed for F404.

WHY THE PREVIEW REALLY MEANS POST-FOUNDING YIELD
------------------------------------------------
The helper is called only in the successful MISSION_FOUND action-help path,
alongside setFoundCostHelp and setFoundHealthHelp, and its localization label
is TXT_KEY_HOME_TILE_YIELD. It is explicitly a projection of the city that will
exist after the action, not merely a description of the terrain before the
city exists.

ANCESTRY
--------
This helper is not a BtS/K-Mod member. The founding preview was introduced by
AdvCiv's advc.004b work. Reachable-history commit:

    f6ff6a182f5187541fff6e5bbbe12f9573b3778c
    "Initial commit (cont.)"

already contains the original CvDLLWidgetData::getHomePlotYieldText with the
same nature-yield + MinCity reconstruction. AdvCiv commit:

    6f8d41a1ac548879d04f56ff9210e9a5e10aa975
    "Help text for feature health made more flexible, refactored."

later moved that logic into CvGameTextMgr::setHomePlotYieldHelp without changing
the calculation. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain it.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Avoid stopping at NatureYield + MinCity. The projection should mirror the
post-founding CvPlot::calculateYield stages that can be evaluated without
actually creating a city:

1. calculate nature yield for the active team;
2. apply the city-plot yield change/minimum for CvCity::initialPopulation();
3. apply the active player's normal and natural extra-yield thresholds;
4. apply Golden Age threshold/yield;
5. clamp as runtime does.

Prefer sharing/factoring the runtime city-plot/player-yield logic where
practical rather than maintaining a second partial formula that can drift
again. Current RouteInfos have no direct route yields, so the newly created
city route does not add another current-data discrepancy here.

CONTROL — TECH "CAN TRAIN/CREATE" UNDER GLOBAL BLOCKERS
--------------------------------------------------------
A neighboring candidate was deliberately rejected. Player-context tech help
can still list a unit/project whose tech prerequisite is eTech even when an
external condition such as No Nukes currently blocks construction. That
section already represents prerequisite relationships rather than immediate
eligibility: it likewise lists targets whose other AND-techs, resources,
projects, etc. are still missing. Therefore treating every external blocker as
a false "Can Train/Create" promise would overstate that UI contract. No F404
was spent on that path.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F405 / provisional KI#728 — CTRL+ALT PLOT DEBUG HELP REUSES ENEMY-CITY PATH
RESULTS FROM A DIFFERENT PLOT OWNED BY THE SAME TEAM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
File: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp
Primary function: CvGameTextMgr::setPlotHelpDebug_Ctrl
Runtime comparator: CvTeamAI::AI_isHasPathToEnemyCity overloads
Classification: inherited AdvCiv debug-UI stale-cache defect; retained by Base
AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS.

ROOT
----
For an owned non-city land plot under Ctrl+Alt debug help, the function caches
whether the plot owner's team has a path to enemy cities:

    static TeamTypes eCacheTeam = NO_TEAM;
    static bool bHasPath = false;
    static ArrayEnumMap<TeamTypes,bool> abHasPath;
    bool const bUpdCache = (kPlotTeam.getID() != eCacheTeam);
    eCacheTeam = kPlotTeam.getID();

    if (bUpdCache)
        bHasPath = kPlotTeam.AI_isHasPathToEnemyCity(kPlot);

and, for every target team:

    if (bUpdCache)
        abHasPath.set(itTarget->getID(),
            &kPlotTeam == &*itTarget ||
            kPlotTeam.AI_isHasPathToEnemyCity(kPlot, *itTarget));

The cache invalidation condition contains only TeamTypes. The queried source
`kPlot` is absent from the cache key.

The first hovered plot for a team therefore determines the displayed results
for every subsequently hovered eligible plot owned by that same team until a
plot owned by a different team happens to be inspected.

SOURCE PLOT IS SEMANTIC INPUT, NOT COSMETIC
-------------------------------------------
`CvTeamAI::AI_isHasPathToEnemyCity(CvPlot const& kFrom, CvTeam const& kEnemy)`
constructs a TeamPathFinder and, for each enemy city in the same area, calls:

    pathFinder.generatePath(kFrom, pCity->getPlot())

The aggregate overload likewise passes the supplied `kFrom` into the
per-enemy-team overload.

Thus two plots of the same owner can legitimately have different answers due
to geography, impassable boundaries, hostile borders and reachable city
locations. Team identity cannot substitute for the source plot.

CONCRETE REPRODUCTION SHAPE
---------------------------
Run with debug mode enabled and inspect owned, non-city, non-water tiles using
Ctrl+Alt.

Let A and B be two land plots owned by the same team where:

    AI_isHasPathToEnemyCity(A, enemy) == true
    AI_isHasPathToEnemyCity(B, enemy) == false

Hover A first. `eCacheTeam` changes to the owner's team and the cache stores
A's result. Hover B next. The team ID is unchanged, so `bUpdCache == false` and
neither `bHasPath` nor any entry in `abHasPath` is recomputed.

B's debug tooltip therefore reports A's reachability, including both:

    "Can reach an enemy city" / "No reachable enemy cities"

and each per-target-team "Can reach ... city" line.

The reverse hover order produces the reverse stale result, proving display
output depends on the previously inspected plot rather than only current game
state.

ANCESTRY
--------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same team-only cache.

Reachable-history commit:

    a936404e1b97a691e39e57a3dcb41f652796b0a0
    "Fix BBAI bug in PathToEnemyCity check"

introduced the static TeamTypes/bool/per-team cache while replacing the older
BBAI player-city path display. Its intent comment says not to recompute this
"over and over as the user inspects" the text.

The initial cache patch did not update `eCacheTeam`, which accidentally caused
the expensive path result to be recomputed every time and therefore avoided
this particular stale-plot behavior.

A later amendment:

    e7c8b9592e0dd30273950bde6c3746d85a97f0ed
    "Amend a minor bug in CvGameTextMgr"

added:

    eCacheTeam = kPlotTeam.getID();

making the cache persistent as intended, but still without adding the source
plot to the key. Current Base AdvCiv and SAS retain that state.

This is therefore an AdvCiv optimization/cache regression in debug help rather
than a raw BtS/K-Mod root.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
At minimum, key the cache by both team and source plot, e.g. team plus plot
index/coordinates (or the plot pointer while map storage is stable):

    bUpdCache = (eTeam != eCacheTeam || iPlot != iCachePlot);

A more robust debug cache should also consider invalidation when relevant game
state changes; a simple per-call computation is acceptable if this diagnostic
path is infrequent enough. The essential correctness requirement is that a
result computed from `kPlot A` must never be reused for `kPlot B` solely
because both share an owner team.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Continuation basis

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F406 / provisional KI#729 — CTRL+SHIFT TEAM-PATH DEBUG HELP CAN REUSE PATH
COST/LENGTH AFTER THE SAME SELECTED UNIT'S SOURCE PLOT HAS CHANGED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
File: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp
Primary function: CvGameTextMgr::setPlotHelpDebug_Ctrl
Classification: inherited AdvCiv debug-UI stale-cache defect; retained by Base
AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS; absent from K-Mod/Civ4CE because this TeamPath
 diagnostic was added by AdvCiv.

ROOT
----
The Ctrl+Shift TeamPath diagnostic avoids recomputation with:

    static CvPlot const* pOldPlot = NULL;
    static CvUnit const* pOldUnit = NULL;
    static int iCost = MAX_INT;
    static int iLength = MAX_INT;

    if (pPlot != pOldPlot || pUnit != pOldUnit)
    {
        pOldPlot = pPlot;
        pOldUnit = pUnit;
        ...
        CvPlot const& kStart = pUnit->getPlot();
        CvPlot const& kDest = *pPlot;
        ... generatePath(kStart, kDest) ...
    }

The cache key therefore contains the destination-plot pointer and selected-unit
pointer, but not the selected unit's current source plot. The cached value is a
function of that omitted source plot.

LIVE STALE-STATE SHAPE
----------------------
Keep one unit selected and inspect a destination plot D under the diagnostic.
The cache stores the TeamPath cost/length from the unit's current source A to D.
If that same unit subsequently moves to B while remaining the same CvUnit
object, then the semantic query becomes B -> D. If D remains/rebecomes the same
mouse-over CvPlot object, both cache keys still compare equal:

    pPlot == pOldPlot
    pUnit == pOldUnit

so no pathfinder is run and the text still prints A -> D's old cost/length.

This is not a mere formatting cache: the omitted input is read explicitly as
`pUnit->getPlot()` immediately before `generatePath`. Different source plots
can have different path lengths, route costs or even reachability.

The same underspecified key can also retain stale results when path-relevant
map/diplomatic state changes while both object pointers remain unchanged (for
example routes or war-access state). The moving-source case alone is sufficient
for the root.

ANCESTRY
--------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same cache. K-Mod and Civ4CE/BtS do not contain
this TeamPath debug display.

Reachable-history commit:

    147c51de866e5decea37cebabce251b5061bf574
    "TeamPathFinder with test code (CvGameTextMgr)"

introduced the diagnostic and initially cached only `pOldPlot`.

The follow-up:

    9294e00681e1f5307a4a3f81a35e53959a3c9aff
    "Test code ensuring symmetrical team path distances"

noticed another omitted input and added `pOldUnit`, changing the invalidation
condition to the current:

    pPlot != pOldPlot || pUnit != pOldUnit

but still did not include the unit's current source plot or other mutable path
state. Current Base AdvCiv and SAS retain that partial key.

DISTINCT FROM F405
------------------
F405 caches enemy-city reachability by owner TeamTypes while omitting the
queried source plot `kPlot`. F406 is a separate static cache in the TeamPath
cost/length diagnostic: it does include the destination plot and unit identity,
but omits mutable state of that same unit, most directly `pUnit->getPlot()`.
The caches have different producers, keys, values and visible stale-state
transitions.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
At minimum, include the source plot in cache invalidation, e.g. remember
`pUnit->plot()` / plot index alongside `pOldPlot` and `pOldUnit`.

For a diagnostic path whose correctness depends on routes, diplomacy and other
mutable traversal state, a turn/state stamp or simply recomputing on tooltip
refresh may be safer. The essential fix is not to treat object identity as a
complete representation of the path query's state.

POST-WIP107 CONTROLS — NO NEW NUMBER
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. UnitClass / BuildingClass civilization resolution
----------------------------------------------------
The current player-context help paths inspected generally resolve an actual
player/civilization's unit or building before falling back to the class default.
The remaining default-class uses do not produce a current-SAS UU/UB mismatch:

* The Great Artist/Scientist/Merchant/Engineer/Spy UnitClasses used by the
  building Great-Person/free-unit helpers only differ for the Barbarian
  civilization, where the mapping is NONE. The normal player-facing building
  callers do not reach that combination.
* Religion free-unit classes in current XML are missionary-specific and have
  no civilization replacement that can make the default disagree with a
  player's actual unit.
* No current live FreeBuildingClass case established an analogous UB mismatch.

So the class-resolution family is provisionally closed without F407.

2. appendCombatModifiers Barbarian-city-attack omission
-------------------------------------------------------
Runtime combat strength contains the attack-side Handicap
BarbarianCityAttackBonus when a Barbarian attacks a city, while
appendCombatModifiers does not print that term. This is a real helper-
completeness asymmetry, but the ordinary combat-odds callers obtain the
attacker from the active player's selected group. They therefore do not supply
a Barbarian attacker in normal player UI. Kept as an unreachable-orientation
control rather than F407.

3. setSpecialistLink singular/plural polarity
---------------------------------------------
One building-slot caller computes `bSingular` and passes it directly to the
helper parameter named `bPlural`, which is source-level opposite polarity.
The parameter mainly changes grammatical link-target syntax for Italian/
Spanish while the visible description is passed separately. Without a proven
broken visible link/text state in the current EXE/localization resolver, this
remains an unresolved low-level grammar/link hazard rather than a numbered
finding.

4. Sentinel / dead-path controls retained from the closure sweep
----------------------------------------------------------------
The sweep reconfirmed several genuine defensive/source oddities without a live
current-SAS consequence strong enough for a finding:

* a plot-resource branch compares ImprovementTypes against NULL rather than
  NO_IMPROVEMENT; current path/data short-circuits mask the sentinel collision;
* old setGoldStr negative-color formatting uses SETCOLR where ENDCOLR is
  required, but current BUG Main Interface no longer calls that inherited path;
* setResearchStr can reuse the repeat-tech ordinal buffer if research turns are
  negative, but current SAS has no repeatable technologies;
* parseSpecialistHelp retrieves GC.getInfo(eSpecialist) before its own
  NO_SPECIALIST guard, but all current UI callers traced supply a valid
  specialist or reject the sentinel first;
* eventGoldHelp has asymmetric sign handling for a randomized negative-gold
  range, but current event XML has no reachable negative randomized range.

These are worth preserving as future mod-mod/cleanup controls, but none consumes
F407 under the current audit threshold.

F407 / provisional KI#730 — CITY-BAR TEMPORARY-ANGER SUMMARY TAKES THE MAXIMUM
SOURCE INSTEAD OF ADDING SIMULTANEOUS HURRY, DRAFT AND DEFY ANGER
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
File: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp
Primary function: CvGameTextMgr::setCityBarHelp
Runtime comparison: CvCity::unhappyLevel, getHurryPercentAnger,
getConscriptPercentAnger, getDefyResolutionPercentAnger
Classification: AdvCiv BULL-integration aggregation/display defect; introduced
by AdvCiv city-bar hover integration and retained by Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
current SAS.

ROOT
----
The city-bar temporary-anger helper first takes the longest timer:

    int iAngerTimer = std::max(kCity.getHurryAngerTimer(),
            kCity.getConscriptAngerTimer());
    iAngerTimer = std::max(iAngerTimer,
            kCity.getDefyResolutionAngerTimer());

It then also takes only the greatest anger percentage:

    int iPercentAnger = std::max(kCity.getHurryPercentAnger(),
            kCity.getConscriptPercentAnger());
    iPercentAnger = std::max(iPercentAnger,
            kCity.getDefyResolutionPercentAnger());
    int iAngryPop = (iPercentAnger * kCity.getPopulation()) /
            GC.getPERCENT_ANGER_DIVISOR();

and formats:

    TXT_KEY_CITY_BAR_ANGER_TIMER
    "-%d1[ICON_UNHAPPY] in %d2 Turns"

Runtime city unhappiness does not choose one temporary-anger source. In
CvCity::unhappyLevel it ADDS all three before the one final population/divisor
conversion:

    iAngerPercent += getHurryPercentAnger(iExtra);
    iAngerPercent += getConscriptPercentAnger(iExtra);
    iAngerPercent += getDefyResolutionPercentAnger(iExtra);
    ...
    iUnhappiness = (iAngerPercent * (getPopulation() + iExtra)) /
            GC.getPERCENT_ANGER_DIVISOR();

Therefore simultaneous temporary anger is cumulative at runtime but mutually
exclusive in this city-bar display.

CURRENT-DATA REACHABILITY
-------------------------
This is ordinary current SAS gameplay, not an XML combination requiring a
custom scenario:

* CIVIC_SLAVERY is a Labor civic and enables HURRY_POPULATION.
* CIVIC_NATIONHOOD is a Legal civic and allows up to 3 conscriptions.
  The two civics can therefore be active simultaneously.
* Normal speed has iHurryConscriptAngerPercent = 100.
* BtS inherited defines used by current SAS are:

      HURRY_ANGER_DIVISOR = 10
      CONSCRIPT_ANGER_DIVISOR = 10
      HURRY_POP_ANGER = 1
      CONSCRIPT_POP_ANGER = 3
      PERCENT_ANGER_DIVISOR = 1000
      CONSCRIPT_POPULATION_PER_COST = 60

* Current UNIT_RIFLEMAN costs 120 production, so when it is the conscription
  unit getConscriptPopulation() returns max(1, 120 / 60) = 2.
* Current HURRY_POPULATION gives 27 production per population, so an ordinary
  already-started build with sufficiently little adjusted production remaining
  can be a one-pop whip.
* The CityScreen Anger Counter option controlling this city-bar line is enabled
  by default.

CONCRETE NUMERIC STATE
----------------------
On Normal speed, take an ordinary population-11 city running Slavery and
Nationhood in a state where Rifleman is its conscription unit.

1. Hurry an eligible build for 1 population.
   Population becomes 10 and hurry anger timer becomes 10.
2. Conscript the 120-production Rifleman for 2 population.
   Population becomes 8 and conscription anger timer becomes 10.

At final population 8 with one layer of each anger:

    hurry percent = 1 + (1 * 1 * 1000 / 8) = 126
    draft percent = 1 + (1 * 3 * 1000 / 8) = 376

Runtime temporary-anger contribution:

    (126 + 376) * 8 / 1000
    = 4016 / 1000
    = 4 unhappy citizens

City-bar helper:

    max(126, 376) * 8 / 1000
    = 3008 / 1000
    = 3 unhappy citizens

Thus the city-bar tooltip can print:

    -3 unhappy in 10 turns

while the same city's actual current unhappiness calculation contains 4 unhappy
citizens from those two temporary sources alone.

The issue is not limited to equal timers. With different source timers or
multiple stacked anger layers, the helper independently takes the maximum
percentage and maximum duration. Those maxima can come from different anger
sources, producing a displayed `(angry citizens, turns)` pair that corresponds
to no single underlying temporary-anger state.

ANCESTRY
--------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same max-based block. K-Mod/Civ4CE do not contain
AdvCiv's integrated C++ city-bar helper in this form.

Reachable-history commit:

    92202f546295e43857d6172e1b9c6665446e68a5
    "Overhaul city bar hover text (based on BULL)"

introduced this exact block into CvGameTextMgr::setCityBarHelp as advc.186.
The same patch notes that BULL had separate CityBar__HurryAnger and
CityBar__DraftAnger options, while AdvCiv ties the consolidated city-bar line to
CityScreen__Anger_Counter. The introduced consolidation uses max for both the
timer and anger amount. Later/current source also includes defy-resolution
anger in the same max aggregation.

This is therefore best classified as an AdvCiv BULL-integration aggregation
regression, retained by SAS, rather than a raw BtS/K-Mod runtime bug.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The minimum correction for the displayed CURRENT temporary-unhappiness amount
is to mirror CvCity::unhappyLevel's aggregation and convert only after summing:

    int iPercentAnger =
            kCity.getHurryPercentAnger() +
            kCity.getConscriptPercentAnger() +
            kCity.getDefyResolutionPercentAnger();

    int iAngryPop = (iPercentAnger * kCity.getPopulation()) /
            GC.getPERCENT_ANGER_DIVISOR();

Do not convert each source to citizens separately and add afterward; runtime
sums the percentages first, so one final conversion is required to preserve
its integer-rounding behavior.

Keeping `max(timer)` can still serve as an upper-bound "temporary anger fully
cleared by" duration, but it should not imply that the entire current summed
amount persists until that exact turn when sources have different timers. A
more precise UI would either label the amount as current temporary
unhappiness plus a maximum remaining duration, or report hurry/draft/defy
sources separately as BULL's original option structure suggests.

POST-WIP108 CONTROLS / CLEAN RESULTS
------------------------------------

1. Remainder of setCityBarHelp after F407 is provisionally clean.

- Production/process conversion uses the same yield/modifier units as runtime.
- CvCity::calculateTradeTotals explicitly returns in disorder, so the city-bar
  trade detail does not resurrect trade-route yield during disorder.
- CvCity::getGreatPeopleRate() explicitly returns 0 in disorder, matching the
  city-bar GP line.
- On city acquisition, non-Wonder foreign UBs are converted to the new owner's
  civilization-equivalent BuildingClass entry before the city-bar building list
  sees them; iterating the current civilization's buildings therefore does not
  silently lose retained captured UBs.
- Free buildings are intentionally omitted, and the controlling BUG option help
  explicitly documents that free buildings (e.g. Stonehenge Monuments) are never
  listed. This is not an accidental omission.

2. setRevoltHelp state ordering matches runtime.

Runtime CvCity::doRevolt first rolls probabilityOccupationDecrement(); on success
it decrements occupation and returns. Only if that fails does it roll
revoltProbability(). setRevoltHelp displays the effective revolt probability as:

    revoltProbability() * (1 - probabilityOccupationDecrement())

which matches that ordered runtime transition. CvDLLWidgetData's nationality help
uses the same effective probability. No F408 here.

3. Ordinary happiness breakdown remains internally reconciled after F407.

setHappyHelp accumulates the same positive source getters used by
CvCity::happyLevel(), and retains its final assertion against happyLevel(). The
F407 temporary-anger bug is in setCityBarHelp's separate consolidated anger
summary, not in setHappyHelp.

4. Ordinary health breakdown has a semantic split mismatch, but current SAS data
masks it.

CvCity::goodHealth()/badHealth() combine:

    GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).getExtraHealth() + getExtraHealth()

before clamping that sum to its positive or negative part. setGoodHealthHelp and
setBadHealthHelp instead print player-wide ExtraHealth and city-local ExtraHealth
as independent contributions. Opposite-signed sources could therefore make the
listed source lines disagree with runtime's combined clamp.

Current SAS does not provide the needed opposing signs in normal data paths:
player-wide ExtraHealth sources found are nonnegative (e.g. Protective and the
custom civic), while current event-driven CvCity ExtraHealth values are likewise
positive. No current-data F408 is promoted; retain as a mod-mod/defensive display
hazard.

5. Additional-building projection defects remain the already-numbered F397-F399
family; the ordinary health/happy breakdown pass did not establish a distinct new
root.


F408 / provisional KI#731 — CONFIRMED
--------------------------------------
TITLE:
FOOD-RATE HOVER IGNORES CITY DISORDER AND CAN DISPLAY GROWTH/STARVATION THAT
RUNTIME EXPLICITLY FREEZES AT ZERO

CLASSIFICATION:
Inherited BULL food-hover integration defect retained by AdvCiv and current SAS.
The runtime city-food rule itself is correct; the defect is in the displayed
breakdown.

CURRENT SAS DISPLAY PATH:
CvDLLWidgetData::parseFoodModHelp obtains the currently selected city and calls:

    GAMETEXT.setFoodHelp(szBuffer, *pCity);

CvMainInterface.py attaches WIDGET_FOOD_MOD_HELP to PopulationInputText even in
the disorder branch. In that branch the visible city-screen number itself uses
pHeadSelectedCity.getFoodDifference(), so it correctly displays 0 during
occupation/anarchy disorder, but hovering that same label still enters
setFoodHelp.

CURRENT SAS TOOLTIP CALCULATION:
CvGameTextMgr::setFoodHelp has no isDisorder() guard. It reconstructs production
from currently worked plots (the city center is always worked), trade,
specialists, corporations and buildings; subtracts ordinary population food
consumption plus spoiled food; then reports growing/shrinking/stagnant based on
that reconstructed net result.

RUNTIME CONTRACT:
CvCity::foodDifference begins with:

    if (isDisorder())
        return 0;

Thus stored city food does not grow or shrink while the city is in disorder.
CvCity::getYieldRate itself does not contain that disorder suppression; the
suppression belongs specifically to foodDifference(). Therefore rebuilding the
normal yield-minus-consumption arithmetic in the tooltip bypasses the rule.

LIVE CURRENT-SAS EXAMPLE:
Take an occupied captured city at population 3. WorkingPlotIter includes the city
center because the home plot is always worked. On an ordinary 2-food city-center
state, even if no other workable plots contribute and health is neutral,
setFoodHelp can reconstruct approximately:

    2 food produced
  - 6 food eaten (3 population * 2)
  = -4 food / shrinking

while CvCity::foodDifference() returns exactly 0 for the same city and stored food
is frozen. The city screen's primary food label therefore correctly shows 0, but
its hover can claim a negative food rate / shrinking state that cannot occur.
Other occupied-city yields merely change the wrong nonzero number; they do not
remove the root mismatch.

REACHABILITY:
This is not hidden behind an optional Alt-only projection. CvMainInterface.py
still attaches WIDGET_FOOD_MOD_HELP when the city is in disorder; its explicit
`else` branch for disorder/food-production sets PopulationInputText and gives it
that widget. Captured occupied cities are ordinary gameplay states.

ANCESTRY:
Reachable-history diff:

    LLM_Helpers/context/commit_diffs/AdvCivPreSAS_1481_4a65bf5c0f.diff

Commit:
    4a65bf5c0fb187fd25d4908346abb462354a9172
Title:
    "Option for expanding scoreboard; BULL hover text"

That AdvCiv integration imports the BULL Food Rate Hover path, including
parseFoodModHelp and setFoodHelp. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the
no-disorder tooltip arithmetic. This is therefore best classified as an inherited
BULL/AdvCiv UI integration defect, not a SAS runtime-rule regression.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR:
Mirror the runtime state contract at the top of setFoodHelp. For example, if the
city is in disorder, either return after showing an explicit "0 / no food change
in disorder" explanation, or build a dedicated disorder line. Do not run the
ordinary yield-minus-consumption breakdown and then label it as net growth/shrink.
At minimum:

    if (kCity.isDisorder())
    {
        // append a suitable zero/disorder explanation if desired
        return;
    }

A dedicated explanation is preferable to a blank tooltip because the widget is
visible and the main label is already showing the frozen 0-food state.

WHY THIS IS DISTINCT FROM F407:
F407 is a max-vs-sum aggregation error in temporary unhappiness. F408 is a
state-rule omission in the food hover: it applies normal food arithmetic in a
state where runtime bypasses that arithmetic entirely.
