F409 / provisional KI#732 — CONFIRMED
--------------------------------------
TITLE:
ALT / "BUILDING ADDITIONAL PRODUCTION" BYPASSES THE DISORDER ZERO-PRODUCTION
GUARD AND RECONSTRUCTS NONZERO PRODUCTION / OVERFLOW THAT RUNTIME CANNOT EARN

CLASSIFICATION:
Inherited K-Mod BUG "Actual Building Effects" integration defect retained by
AdvCiv and current SAS; AdvCiv additionally made the broken path directly
reachable through the Alt key even with the option disabled.

RUNTIME CONTRACT:
CvCity::getProductionDifference begins with:

    if (isDisorder() && !bForceFeatureProd)
        return 0;

and CvCity::isDisorder() is true for either occupation or owner anarchy:

    return (isOccupation() || GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).isAnarchy());

Thus ordinary current production is exactly zero throughout disorder. The city
screen follows that contract: CvMainInterface.py gets
getCurrentProductionDifference(True, True) and displays that value in
ProductionInputText, which is still attached to WIDGET_PRODUCTION_MOD_HELP.

BROKEN TOOLTIP PATH:
CvGameTextMgr::setProductionHelp normally uses the same zero result to return:

    bool bBuildingAdditionalYield =
        (BUGOption::isEnabled("MiscHover__BuildingAdditionalProduction", false) ||
         GC.altKey());

    if (kCity.getCurrentProductionDifference(false, true) == 0 &&
        !bBuildingAdditionalYield)
        return;

Holding Alt, or enabling the BUG option, therefore bypasses the return even when
the only reason production is zero is disorder.

After bypassing it, setProductionHelp does not switch to a dedicated hypothetical
"after disorder" mode. It runs the ordinary live-production reconstruction:

- setYieldHelp prints the city's normal base production and yield modifiers;
- iBaseProduction is rebuilt from getBaseYieldRate(YIELD_PRODUCTION);
- unit/building/project production modifiers are added;
- iModProduction is computed from those normal values;
- the tooltip appends TXT_KEY_MISC_HELP_PROD_FINAL_YIELD with iModProduction;
- if an order is queued, it can also compute/display iNewOverflow from that
  reconstructed production.

But runtime remains at exactly zero for the turn.

INTERNAL SELF-CHECK CONFIRMS THE MISMATCH:
The helper contains:

    FAssertMsg(iModProduction ==
        kCity.getCurrentProductionDifference(false, !bProcess) + ...,
        "Modified Production does not match actual value");

In an anarchy/occupation city with ordinary positive base production and a queued
order, the left side is positive while getCurrentProductionDifference is 0.
Therefore the Alt/option path can trip the helper's own assertion in a debug DLL;
in a release DLL it proceeds to show the wrong nonzero final production instead.

LIVE CURRENT-SAS EXAMPLE:
Use an ordinary city with a queued unit/building and 5 base hammers, then enter
civic or religious anarchy. The queue remains present but isDisorder() makes the
actual production difference 0, which the main city-screen production input
correctly displays.

Hover that same ProductionInputText while holding Alt:

    runtime/current-production display: 0 hammers
    setProductionHelp reconstruction:   5 hammers (before any order modifiers)

and the hover can label that reconstructed value as final production and even
project overflow that cannot be generated during the disorder turn. Any normal
positive production city supplies the mismatch; 5 hammers is only a simple
illustration.

REACHABILITY:
This is live even though the BUG menu option defaults to False in current SAS.
AdvCiv's advc.063 integration explicitly ORs the option with GC.altKey(), and Alt
is the documented shortcut for showing all "Actual Effects" information. The
production input label remains attached to WIDGET_PRODUCTION_MOD_HELP in disorder.

ANCESTRY:
K-Mod commit:
    8478443165fcaeca861fc9d2dbb725de7e94ca59
Title:
    "Implemented \"actual building effect\" mouse-over hover options from BUG."

Its diff changes the original unconditional zero-production return into:

    if (city.getCurrentProductionDifference(false, true) == 0 &&
        !bBuildingAdditionalYield)
        return;

so the defective bypass originates with the BUG/K-Mod integration.

AdvCiv commit:
    aa7146bdeef00ac4ce12198f795dc3ac0cb46770
Title:
    "Improved the integration of some UI conveniences; smarter Sentry mission"

advc.063 changes bBuildingAdditionalYield to include:

    || GC.altKey()

and its log explicitly says Alt now shows all Actual Effects info. Thus AdvCiv
makes the already-broken zero-production bypass directly reachable on demand,
even with the menu option disabled. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain it.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR:
Disorder must win over the Actual Effects toggle for the live-production portion.
For example, return (or show an explicit zero/disorder line) before the optional
building projections:

    if (kCity.isDisorder())
    {
        // optionally show "0 production during disorder"
        // optional building-effect projections may be shown separately,
        // but must not be labelled as current/final production.
        return;
    }

If keeping Alt building projections during disorder is desirable, separate them
from the current-production reconstruction rather than using the option to bypass
the runtime-zero guard.

WHY THIS IS DISTINCT FROM F408:

is used throughout disorder. F409 is a separate control-flow regression in
setProductionHelp: the helper does have a zero-production guard, but the BUG
Actual Effects option / Alt shortcut deliberately bypasses it and then continues

F410 / provisional KI#733 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------------------
TITLE:
Alt / "Building Additional Great People" bypasses disorder's zero-GPP contract,
so the Great Person hover can display a nonzero final rate (and trip its own
assertion) while occupation/anarchy actually generates 0 GPP.

CLASSIFICATION:
Inherited BUG/K-Mod UI-calculation defect; AdvCiv makes it directly reachable
through the Alt "Actual Effects" shortcut. Current SAS retains it.

RUNTIME CONTRACT:
CvCity::getGreatPeopleRate() explicitly returns zero in disorder:

    int CvCity::getGreatPeopleRate() const
    {
        if (isDisorder())
            return 0;
        return (getBaseGreatPeopleRate() * getTotalGreatPeopleRateModifier()) / 100;
    }

CvCity::doGreatPeople() independently enforces the same state transition:

    if (isDisorder())
        return;

    changeGreatPeopleProgress(getGreatPeopleRate());

So occupation or owner anarchy produces exactly 0 Great Person points for that
turn. This is not merely a display convention.

BROKEN TOOLTIP CONTROL FLOW:
CvGameTextMgr::parseGreatPeopleHelp first obtains the correct live value:

    int const iGPRate = kCity.getGreatPeopleRate();

but the BUG "Building Additional Great People" integration changes the normal
zero-rate return into:

    bool bBuildingAdditionalGreatPeople =
        (BUGOption::isEnabled("MiscHover__BuildingAdditionalGreatPeople", false) ||
         GC.altKey());

    if (iGPRate == 0 && !bBuildingAdditionalGreatPeople)
        return;

Thus Alt (or the option) bypasses the return even when iGPRate is zero solely
because the city is in disorder.

After bypassing it, the helper does not keep the live zero rate. It reconstructs
normal, non-disorder GPP from:

* specialists and free specialists;
* building GPP (including the SAS explicit obsolete-building line);
* base Great People rate;
* building/global GPP modifiers;
* civic/state-religion modifiers;
* trait modifiers;
* Golden Age modifier.

It then computes:

    int iModGreatPeople =
        (iModifier * kCity.getBaseGreatPeopleRate()) / 100;

and appends TXT_KEY_MISC_HELP_GREATPEOPLE_FINAL with that value.

INTERNAL SELF-CHECK PROVES THE STATE MISMATCH:
Immediately before displaying the final value, the helper has:

    FAssertMsg(iModGreatPeople == kCity.getGreatPeopleRate(),
        "Great person rate does not match actual value");

During disorder, getGreatPeopleRate() is 0. If the city has any normal positive
base GPP, Alt causes iModGreatPeople > 0, so a debug DLL can fire this assertion.
A release DLL proceeds and displays the wrong nonzero final rate.

LIVE CURRENT-SAS REACHABILITY:
The city-screen GreatPeopleBar is created with WIDGET_HELP_GREAT_PEOPLE and
CvDLLWidgetData::parseGreatPeopleHelp forwards that hover to this function.

CvMainInterface.py keeps the Great People bar visible when either:

    pHeadSelectedCity.getGreatPeopleProgress() > 0
    or pHeadSelectedCity.getGreatPeopleRate() > 0

Therefore disorder does NOT necessarily hide the widget: an established GP city
with any stored progress remains hoverable even though its current rate has
fallen to 0.

A simple supported state:

1. Have an ordinary city with stored Great Person progress and 3 base GPP/turn
   (e.g. from a specialist/building).
2. Enter civic or religious anarchy, or put the city in occupation.
3. Runtime `getGreatPeopleRate()` becomes 0 and doGreatPeople adds nothing.
4. The stored progress keeps GreatPeopleBar visible.
5. Hover normally: the zero-rate guard stops the detailed rate breakdown.
6. Hold Alt: the guard is bypassed; the helper reconstructs and labels the
   ordinary positive rate (e.g. 3 GPP/turn, before any modifiers) as Final.

So the same current city state is simultaneously:

    runtime/current GPP rate: 0
    Alt detailed-hover final: >0

and the debug assertion can fail for exactly that reason.

ANCESTRY:
K-Mod commit:
    8478443165fcaeca861fc9d2dbb725de7e94ca59
Title:
    "Implemented \"actual building effect\" mouse-over hover options from BUG."

That integration introduced BuildingAdditionalGreatPeople and replaced the old
zero-GPP return with the option-gated return, creating the state bypass.

AdvCiv commit:
    aa7146bdeef00ac4ce12198f795dc3ac0cb46770
Title:
    "Improved the integration of some UI conveniences; smarter Sentry mission"

advc.063 changes the option test to:

    BUG option || GC.altKey()

making the bad path directly reachable through the documented Alt "Actual
Effects" shortcut even though the menu option defaults to false. Base AdvCiv
1.14 and current SAS retain it.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR:
Disorder must remain authoritative for the live/final GPP-rate portion. E.g.:

    if (kCity.isDisorder())
    {
        // Optionally allow a separately-labelled hypothetical building-effect
        // section, but do not reconstruct or label a nonzero current/final rate.
        return;
    }

or preserve the building projections in a separate path while leaving
`iGPRate == 0` as an unconditional stop for the ordinary live-rate breakdown.

WHY F410 IS DISTINCT FROM F408/F409:
F408 is setFoodHelp's unconditional failure to mirror disorder.
F409 is setProductionHelp's Building Additional Production/Alt bypass of its
otherwise-correct zero-production guard.
F410 is a separate BUG feature/helper (`parseGreatPeopleHelp` and
BuildingAdditionalGreatPeople), separate runtime quantity and separate display
widget. It happens to repeat the same integration pattern as F409, which is
useful evidence that the BUG "Actual Effects" zero-rate bypass family should be
checked systematically.

F411 / provisional KI#734 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------------------
TITLE:
City corporation hover ignores disorder: it can display normal corporation
output and maintenance while occupation/anarchy suppresses those live effects.

CLASSIFICATION:
Inherited BtS city-hover/runtime-state defect; retained unchanged in K-Mod,
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

BROKEN DISPLAY CONTRACT:
CvGameTextMgr::setCorporationHelpCity determines:

    bool const bActive = (pCity->isActiveCorporation(eCorporation) ||
        (bForceCorporation && iNumResources > 0));

and, whenever bActive is true, reconstructs corporation yield/commerce from the
resource count and CorporationInfo values. It also reconstructs corporation
maintenance and inflation. There is no `pCity->isDisorder()` /
`pCity->isNoMaintenance()` check in this display path.

RUNTIME CONTRACT — CORPORATION OUTPUT:
CvCity::getCorporationYieldByCorporation and
CvCity::getCorporationCommerceByCorporation both require:

    if (isActiveCorporation(eCorporation) && !isDisorder())

before adding any output. In disorder they return 0.

`CvCity::isActiveCorporation` itself deliberately does NOT include disorder; it
checks possession, owner corporation policy and prerequisite resources. Thus the
TextMgr's bActive can remain true while the runtime-output functions explicitly
return zero.

RUNTIME CONTRACT — MAINTENANCE:
CvCity::isNoMaintenance() is:

    return (isDisorder() || isWeLoveTheKingDay() || getPopulation() <= 0);

and updateMaintenance sets current city maintenance to zero whenever
isNoMaintenance() is true. The corporation hover nevertheless computes its own
corporation-maintenance number when bActive is true, without that state guard.

LIVE CURRENT-SAS UI REACHABILITY:
CvMainInterface.py keeps corporation icons for corporations that the selected
city has, independent of disorder, and attaches
WIDGET_HELP_CORPORATION_CITY. CvDLLWidgetData::parseCorporationHelpCity passes the
selected city to setCorporationHelpCity(..., bCityScreen=true).

Therefore both player anarchy and captured-city occupation leave a normal live
hover path to the broken calculation.

CONCRETE CURRENT-DATA EXAMPLE:
Cereal Mills (CORPORATION_1) produces 100 food-hundredths per qualifying resource
and Standard world size has CorporationMaintenancePercent=100. A city with
Cereal Mills and one Wheat therefore ordinarily receives +1 food from that
corporation.

If the owner enters anarchy (or the city is occupied):

    runtime getCorporationYieldByCorporation(FOOD, Cereal Mills) = 0

but the corporation icon hover still reconstructs and prints +1 food because
`bActive` remains true. Any displayed corporation-maintenance amount is likewise
not the currently charged city maintenance, which is zero in disorder.

ANCESTRY:
The same missing disorder/no-maintenance guard is present in Civ4CE/BtS's
setCorporationHelpCity, K-Mod, Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS. K-Mod adds
inflation to the displayed maintenance but does not repair the state mismatch.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR:
For live city help, derive displayed corporation yield/commerce through the
runtime getters (getCorporationYieldByCorporation /
getCorporationCommerceByCorporation) or at minimum require `!pCity->isDisorder()`
for those values. Do not show a currently-paid corporation maintenance value when
`pCity->isNoMaintenance()` is true. Keep bForceCorporation hypothetical-preview
semantics separate if those callers intentionally want counterfactual output.

WHY DISTINCT FROM F408-F410:
F408 is the food-rate hover's missing disorder guard; F409 is production Actual
Effects/Alt bypass; F410 is Great-People Actual Effects/Alt bypass. F411 is a
separate corporation-icon helper with its own corporation output and maintenance
runtime contracts, and it is wrong without any modifier key or BUG option.

F412 / provisional KI#735 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------------------
TITLE:
Finance Advisor unit-cost / unit-supply hovers ignore player anarchy and can
itemize positive expenses while the visible/runtime expense rows are exactly 0.

CLASSIFICATION:
Inherited BUG/K-Mod Finance Advisor state mismatch; present in K-Mod and retained
by Base AdvCiv 1.14/current AdvCiv-SAS. Stock BtS/Civ4CE does not contain these
finance-breakdown TextMgr helpers.

RUNTIME OVERLOAD CONTRACT:
CvPlayer exposes ordinary unit-cost / supply functions and detailed breakdown
overloads.

The ordinary unit-cost path explicitly does:

    int CvPlayer::calculateUnitCost(int iExtraPop, int iExtraUnits) const
    {
        if (isAnarchy())
            return 0;
        ... detailed overload ...
    }

and ordinary unit supply similarly does:

    int CvPlayer::calculateUnitSupply(int iExtraOutsideUnits) const
    {
        if (isAnarchy())
            return 0;
        ... detailed overload ...
    }

The detailed overloads
`calculateUnitCost(iFreeUnits, ..., iExtraCost, ...)` and
`calculateUnitSupply(iPaidUnits, iBaseSupplyCost, ...)` do not perform the
anarchy test; they calculate the normal pre-anarchy support burden.

BROKEN TEXTMGR CONTRACT:
CvGameTextMgr::buildFinanceUnitCostString calls the detailed unit-cost overload
directly and then inflates / prints its components and total.
CvGameTextMgr::buildFinanceAwaySupplyString likewise calls the detailed supply
overload directly. Neither helper checks `kPlayer.isAnarchy()`.

LIVE CURRENT-SAS UI PROOF:
The Economics/Finance tab in CvDomesticAdvisor.py computes its displayed rows
through the ordinary Python-exposed runtime calls:

    totalUnitCost = player.calculateUnitCost() * inflation...
    totalUnitSupply = player.calculateUnitSupply() * inflation...

Thus both visible values are exactly 0 during anarchy.

The Unit Cost and Unit Supply labels are nevertheless always created and always
carry WIDGET_HELP_FINANCE_UNIT_COST / WIDGET_HELP_FINANCE_AWAY_SUPPLY with
m_iData2=1. CvDLLWidgetData consequently invokes buildFinanceUnitCostString and
buildFinanceAwaySupplyString for those zero-valued rows.

SUPPORTED STATE:
Take any ordinary empire with enough units to owe positive regular unit cost and
at least one paid outside unit for supply. Before a civic/religion switch its
Finance rows and hovers show positive costs. During the resulting player anarchy:

    visible Unit Cost row = 0
    visible Unit Supply row = 0
    runtime calculateUnitCost() = 0
    runtime calculateUnitSupply() = 0

but the hover helpers bypass those anarchy-aware wrappers and reconstruct the
normal positive support costs. A zero row can therefore have a tooltip whose own
itemized total says that the player is paying positive gold per turn.

ANCESTRY:
The detailed finance helpers and the same direct detailed-overload calls are
present in K-Mod and Base AdvCiv. They are absent from stock BtS/Civ4CE's
CvGameTextMgr, making this part of the inherited BUG/K-Mod Finance Advisor
integration rather than a stock-BtS root. Current SAS retains the behavior.

REPAIR DIRECTION:
Mirror the runtime state before constructing the breakdown. At minimum, when
`kPlayer.isAnarchy()` the unit-cost and away-supply helpers should report zero /
anarchy-suppressed cost rather than invoke the detailed overload as though the
state were normal. An alternative is to make the detailed breakdown API accept
or expose the same runtime suppression explicitly so the row and tooltip share
one source of truth.

NEIGHBORING EXTRA-COST CONTROL:
The unit-cost helper inflates iCost, iUnitCost and iMilitaryCost but does not
inflate `iExtraCost` before printing that component. That is structurally
suspicious, but current SAS UnitInfo XML has no nonzero iExtraCost values, so it
is data-dormant and is not promoted as F413 here.

F413 / provisional KI#736 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------------------
TITLE:
Random-event pillage ranges advertise an inclusive XML maximum that runtime can
never roll when MinPillage and MaxPillage differ.

CLASSIFICATION:
Inherited stock-BtS random-event off-by-one; present in Civ4CE/BtS, K-Mod,
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS. The defect is in the event execution
range calculation; CvGameTextMgr faithfully exposes the XML's stated min/max.

TEXT / DATA CONTRACT:
CvGameTextMgr::setEventHelp displays the two XML endpoints directly:

    TXT_KEY_EVENT_PILLAGE_RANGE_CITY(
        kEvent.getMinPillage(), kEvent.getMaxPillage(), city)

(or the non-city range key for empire-wide events).

The fields are named iMinPillage and iMaxPillage, and current SAS's Sevopedia
random-event page independently describes them as the "possible count range"
and formats unequal values as `min-max`. The stock BtS localization likewise
presents the two values as a range. There is no indication that iMaxPillage is
intended as an exclusive bound.

BROKEN RUNTIME CONTRACT:
Both CvCity::applyEvent (city / other-player-city events) and
CvPlayer::applyEvent (empire-wide events) choose the count with:

    iMinPillage + SyncRandNum(iMaxPillage - iMinPillage)

CvRandom::getInt(N) returns an integer in [0, N-1]. Therefore, when max > min,
the actual event range is:

    MinPillage ... MaxPillage-1

and the XML / tooltip maximum can never happen. When min==max, the current call
uses SyncRandNum(0), which happens to return 0 and therefore masks the same
missing-inclusive-endpoint issue.

LIVE CURRENT-SAS EXAMPLES:
Current CIV4EventInfos.xml contains ordinary reachable Looters outcomes:

    EVENT_LOOTERS_2: iMinPillage=2, iMaxPillage=4,
                     bPickOtherPlayerCity=1
    EVENT_LOOTERS_3: iMinPillage=3, iMaxPillage=5,
                     bPickOtherPlayerCity=1

CvEventInfo deliberately loads bPickOtherPlayerCity into
m_bOtherPlayerCityEffect, so these outcomes run through CvCity::applyEvent on
the selected other-player city and through the city-specific help text.

For Looters 2 the hover says 2-4 improvements may be destroyed, while runtime
computes `2 + Rand(2)` and can destroy only 2 or 3.
For Looters 3 the hover says 3-5, while runtime computes `3 + Rand(2)` and can
choose only 3 or 4.

This is therefore reachable with unmodified current SAS EventInfo data and does
not depend on a hypothetical mod-mod field.

ANCESTRY:
The same range display and the same `Rand(max-min)` execution formula are
present in stock BtS/Civ4CE. K-Mod and Base AdvCiv retain both, and current SAS
retains them as well. This is a stock-BtS inherited root rather than a SAS-local
regression.

REPAIR DIRECTION:
Make the execution range inclusive to match the XML field names and all player-
facing descriptions:

    MinPillage + SyncRandNum(MaxPillage - MinPillage + 1)

in both CvCity::applyEvent and CvPlayer::applyEvent. That also replaces the
min==max zero-outcome RNG call with the natural Rand(1) form.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

BROKEN TEXT / RUNTIME CONTRACT:
CvGameTextMgr::setEventHelp handles iUnitExperience with only:

    TXT_KEY_EVENT_UNIT_EXPERIENCE(
        kEvent.getUnitExperience(), szUnit)

whose stock English text is:

    "The [unit] receives N XP"

No healing effect is shown.

CvUnit::applyEvent, however, executes:

    if (kEvent.getUnitExperience() != 0)
    {
        setDamage(0);
        changeExperience(kEvent.getUnitExperience());
    }

Thus every XP event also restores the target to full health before granting the
advertised experience.

LIVE CURRENT-SAS DATA / REACHABILITY:
Current CIV4EventInfos.xml contains two nonzero iUnitExperience outcomes:

    EVENT_AT_THE_SWORD_1       iUnitExperience=3
    EVENT_FRIENDLY_LOCALS_1    iUnitExperience=1

Their corresponding trigger data both use:

    iUnitDamagedWeight=1

CvUnit::getTriggerValue has the explicit contract:

    if (getDamage() == 0 && kTrigger.getUnitDamagedWeight() > 0)
        return MIN_INT;

and then weights candidates by `getDamage() * iUnitDamagedWeight`.
Consequently, an undamaged unit is not merely unlikely for these triggers; it
is ineligible. Every reachable At the Sword / Friendly Locals XP event targets
a damaged unit, so the undisclosed `setDamage(0)` has a real effect on every
legal application.

SUPPORTED EXAMPLE:
A damaged Swordsman selected by At the Sword can be at any positive damage
amount permitted by the trigger. The event-choice help states only that the
unit receives +3 XP. Selecting the outcome also sets damage to 0 immediately,
fully healing the Swordsman. Friendly Locals behaves the same way for +1 XP.

ANCESTRY:
Stock BtS/Civ4CE CvUnit::applyEvent already performs `setDamage(0)` for any
nonzero UnitExperience event. Stock CvGameTextMgr::setEventHelp already prints
only TXT_KEY_EVENT_UNIT_EXPERIENCE. K-Mod, Base AdvCiv and current SAS retain
both sides unchanged in substance. This is therefore an inherited stock-BtS
help omission rather than a SAS-local regression.

REPAIR DIRECTION:
The conservative UI-side repair is to expose the healing that runtime already
performs, e.g. append a "fully heals [unit]" line when a UnitExperience event
has a damaged concrete target. A gameplay-side alternative would be to remove
the unconditional `setDamage(0)` if that hidden healing was never intended,
but that would deliberately alter longstanding event mechanics and therefore
requires a design decision rather than being the surgical compatibility fix.

F415 / provisional KI#738 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------------------
TITLE:
Empire-wide negative-population event help says every city loses population,
but runtime silently spares cities that would fall to population 0.

CLASSIFICATION:
Inherited stock-BtS random-event help/runtime mismatch; present in Civ4CE/BtS,
K-Mod, Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

BROKEN TEXT CONTRACT:
For a non-city event with nonzero PopulationChange, setEventHelp uses:

    TXT_KEY_EVENT_POPULATION_CHANGE(kEvent.getPopulationChange())

whose stock English text is:

    "N population in all cities"

There is no minimum-population qualification.

BROKEN RUNTIME MATCH:
CvPlayer::applyEvent handles empire-wide PopulationChange by iterating every
city but applies the change only when:

    pLoopCity->getPopulation() + kEvent.getPopulationChange() > 0

Cities that would be reduced to population 0 or below are skipped entirely.
Thus the runtime effect is conditional per city while the help states that it
applies to all cities.

LIVE CURRENT-SAS DATA / REACHABILITY:
Current EVENT_HEALING_PLANT_4 is a non-city event with:

    iPopulationChange=-1

It is an immediate additional outcome of both EVENT_HEALING_PLANT_2 and
EVENT_HEALING_PLANT_3, with 20% / 50% AdditionalEventChance respectively.
CvGameTextMgr::setEventHelp recursively expands immediate additional events and
therefore shows Healing Plant 4's `-1 population in all cities` consequence in
the parent choice help.

EVENTTRIGGER_HEALING_PLANT has no minimum-city-population restriction and no
picked city. An ordinary empire can therefore have, for example, one population-
1 city and one larger city when the event fires. If Healing Plant 4 occurs:

    larger city: population decreases by 1
    population-1 city: unchanged

although the displayed nested effect said the loss applied in all cities.

ANCESTRY:
Stock BtS/Civ4CE already uses the unconditional "population in all cities" help
key and the per-city `population + change > 0` runtime guard. K-Mod, Base AdvCiv
and current SAS retain both. This is an inherited stock-BtS display/runtime
mismatch rather than a SAS-local regression.

REPAIR DIRECTION:
Preserve the no-city-death runtime rule and make the player-facing text match it,
e.g. explain that the population loss applies to every city where the reduction
would leave at least population 1. A dynamic concrete count could be even more
precise when a triggered player is available, but the minimum requirement is to
stop promising a loss in cities that runtime explicitly exempts.

F416 / provisional KI#739 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------------------
TITLE:
Trade-route hover says there is no trade with a civilization in anarchy but
omits anarchy from its explanatory reasons.

CLASSIFICATION:
Inherited AdvCiv integration omission: AdvCiv advc.124 added the foreign-player
anarchy prohibition to trade-route eligibility after the BUG trade hover had
been integrated, but the hover's reason decomposition was not updated to cover
the new runtime blocker. Present in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS;
the underlying anarchy blocker is absent from K-Mod/BtS.

RUNTIME CONTRACT:
CvPlayer::canHaveTradeRoutesWith(PlayerTypes ePlayer) now contains:

    if (getID() != ePlayer && kOtherPlayer.isAnarchy())
        return false;

before its normal same-team / free-trade / civic checks. Thus, from player A's
perspective, ordinary foreign trade with B is unavailable while B is in anarchy.

BROKEN HELP DECOMPOSITION:
CvGameTextMgr::buildTradeString first uses that exact runtime predicate to choose
its heading and to enter the "cannot trade" explanation branch:

    if (bForeign && !kPlayer.canHaveTradeRoutesWith(eWithPlayer))

It then diagnoses only:

    - defeated player
    - no trade-network connection
    - no free-trade / Open Borders relationship
    - our no-foreign-trade civic state
    - their no-foreign-trade civic state
    - none of their cities known to us

There is no test for `kWithPlayer.isAnarchy()` and no anarchy explanation key.
If anarchy is the sole blocker, `bCanTrade` remains true, no explanatory bullet
is appended, and the function continues to a zero-route summary after already
printing the "No Trade with <player>" heading.

LIVE UI REACHABILITY:
This is not a dormant helper. CvDLLWidgetData::parseTradeRoutes routes
WIDGET_TRADE_ROUTES directly to buildTradeString(activePlayer, otherPlayer).
Current CvForeignAdvisor.py attaches that widget to both trade-route count and
trade-yield text for every shown civilization pair. Current SAS CvInfoScreen.py
also attaches WIDGET_TRADE_ROUTES to its trade column using the active/other
player IDs.

The Foreign Advisor's own pre-display test is additionally asymmetric here:
for a row about B it asks `B.canHaveTradeRoutesWith(activePlayer)`. If B is in
anarchy and the active player is not, that direction does not trip AdvCiv's
"other player is in anarchy" rule, so the row/widget remains naturally present
while the C++ hover, evaluated from the active player's direction, correctly
enters the no-trade branch and then fails to explain why.

SUPPORTED CURRENT STATE:
Take two living civilizations A (active) and B that:

    - have met and know at least one of B's cities,
    - have a valid trade-network connection,
    - satisfy free-trade/Open-Borders requirements,
    - neither has a no-foreign-trade civic restriction,
    - B is temporarily in civic/religious anarchy.

A.canHaveTradeRoutesWith(B) is false solely because B is in anarchy. Hovering
B's Trade field can therefore show:

    No Trade with B
    0 commerce from 0 Trade Routes

without any bullet that identifies the actual blocker.

ANCESTRY:
K-Mod's canHaveTradeRoutesWith has no foreign-player-anarchy rejection. Base
AdvCiv adds that check under advc.124. Base AdvCiv's integrated buildTradeString
already contains an advc.124 diagnostic addition for unknown foreign cities,
but it has no corresponding anarchy diagnostic. Current SAS retains both the
runtime prohibition and the incomplete decomposition. This is therefore best
classified as an AdvCiv integration omission rather than a stock-BtS root.

REPAIR DIRECTION:
Mirror the runtime predicate inside the explanation block, before the remaining
reasons, e.g. append a dedicated localized bullet when
`kWithPlayer.isAnarchy()`. Keep the direction explicit: the runtime restriction
is specifically on the *other* player being in anarchy from kPlayer's
`canHaveTradeRoutesWith(eWithPlayer)` perspective.

F417 / provisional KI#740 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------------------
TITLE:
Advanced Start hides the Visibility purchase control on slower game speeds when
the legal visibility cost rounds down to zero.

CLASSIFICATION:
AdvCiv regression/integration defect created by advc.250c cost normalization
interacting with an inherited BtS UI filter. Present in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
current AdvCiv-SAS; stock BtS's unscaled/higher visibility cost normally masked
the old `> 0` assumption.

BROKEN UI CONTRACT:
CvGameTextMgr::getVisibilityDataForAS obtains:

    int iCost = GET_PLAYER(getActivePlayer()).
            getAdvancedStartVisibilityCost(true);

Its own comment states that cost -1 means the action may not be purchased, but
it only exposes the Visibility entry when:

    if (iCost > 0)

Thus a valid zero-cost action is treated exactly like an unavailable action and
removed from the Advanced Start palette.

RUNTIME CONTRACT:
CvPlayer::doAdvancedStartAction(ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_VISIBILITY) obtains the
plot-specific cost and rejects only:

    if (iCost < 0)
        return;

For an add action it then performs the reveal whenever:

    getAdvancedStartPoints() >= iCost

A cost of 0 is therefore explicitly legal: the plot is revealed and zero start
points are deducted.

WHY CURRENT DATA REACHES ZERO:
Current AdvCiv/SAS GlobalDefines_advc.xml sets:

    ADVANCED_START_VISIBILITY_COST = 1

CvPlayer::getAdvancedStartVisibilityCost eventually returns:

    adjustAdvStartPtsToSpeed(iCost)

and advc.250c's helper performs:

    iPoints *= 100;
    return max(0, iPoints / GC.getGame().getSpeedPercent());

CvGame::getSpeedPercent() is the game speed's ResearchPercent. Current SAS has:

    Normal       100% -> 1 * 100 / 100 = 1
    Epic         150% -> 1 * 100 / 150 = 0
    Marathon     200% -> 0
    Slow         300% -> 0
    Very Slow    400% -> 0

Immediately after an Advanced Start city supplies the ordinary initial revealed
city area, the base visibility cost can therefore be exactly 0 on these slower
speeds. The runtime permits the free reveal, but the exported UI list contains
no Visibility tool with which the human can request it.

REACHABILITY / UI ROLE:
getVisibilityDataForAS is a DllExport whose sole purpose is to populate the
Advanced Start Visibility data list (CvWBData entry using the
INTERFACE_TECH_LOS button). Advanced Start actions dirty/rebuild the Advanced
Start interface when purchases change state. Once the player has a city, the
cost function is no longer blocked by its `getNumCities() <= 0` guard; the
positive-only list filter is then the remaining reason a legal zero-cost entry
is omitted.

ANCESTRY:
Stock BtS/Civ4CE already uses `if (iCost > 0)` in getVisibilityDataForAS, but
stock getAdvancedStartVisibilityCost simply returns its positive define-derived
cost without AdvCiv's game-speed division. AdvCiv advc.250c introduces
`adjustAdvStartPtsToSpeed` for this cost and also recommends/redefines
ADVANCED_START_VISIBILITY_COST to 1. Base AdvCiv retains the old `> 0` UI test,
and current SAS retains the same interaction while also adding very slow speed
settings that make the zero truncation common. Hence the live defect is best
classified as an AdvCiv integration regression, not an originally reachable
stock-BtS bug.

REPAIR DIRECTION:
Honor the cost API's documented sentinel and expose the control whenever
`iCost >= 0`, not only when positive. A zero-cost item should remain selectable;
its text can simply show the normal visibility action without a positive cost.
The same `> 0` vs `>= 0` assumption should be reviewed in the neighboring
Advanced Start list builders, but no additional current zero-cost category is
numbered without its own data/formula proof.

F418 / provisional KI#741 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------------------
TITLE:
Religion conversion help can say only "Cannot convert to <religion>" while
omitting the actual blocker: no-state-religion civics or absence of the target
religion from the player's cities.

CLASSIFICATION:
Inherited stock-BtS diagnostic/help omission. Present unchanged in BtS/Civ4CE,
K-Mod, Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

RUNTIME CONTRACT:
Current CvPlayer::canConvert(ReligionTypes eReligion) rejects conversion when:

    if (isBarbarian())
        return false;
    if (isAnarchy())
        return false;
    if (getConversionTimer() > 0)
        return false;
    if (!isStateReligion())
        return false;
    if (getLastStateReligion() == eReligion)
        return false;
    if (eReligion != NO_RELIGION && !canDoReligion(eReligion))
        return false;

and current canDoReligion is simply:

    getHasReligionCount(eReligion) > 0

Thus two ordinary non-Barbarian blockers are part of the executable contract:

    1. the current civic setup does not permit a state religion;
    2. the requested religion is absent from all of the player's cities.

BROKEN HELP DECOMPOSITION:
CvGameTextMgr::setConvertHelp always begins with:

    "Cannot convert to <religion>"

but only explains:

    - player is in anarchy;
    - requested religion is already the state religion;
    - conversion timer / recent revolution is still active.

It contains no branch corresponding to `!isStateReligion()` and no branch for
`!canDoReligion(eReligion)`. When either omitted condition is the sole blocker,
the help ends after the generic heading and gives the user no reason.

LIVE CURRENT-SAS CALLER:
Current Assets/Python/Screens/CvPolicyAdvisorScreen.py uses the DLL predicate
and the C++ help together. For the selected religion it tests its canConvert
wrapper, which calls:

    gc.getPlayer(self.iActivePlayer).canConvert(iConvertReligion)

and whenever conversion is unavailable it displays:

    CyGameTextMgr().setConvertHelp(self.iActivePlayer, iLinkReligion)

on the Policy Advisor Religion tab. Therefore the missing diagnostic is directly
player-facing and does not depend on a debug or unused API path.

SUPPORTED CURRENT STATE A — FREE RELIGION:
Current SAS CIV4CivicInfos.xml gives CIVIC_FREE_RELIGION:

    <CivicOptionType>CIVICOPTION_RELIGION</CivicOptionType>
    ...
    <bStateReligion>0</bStateReligion>

CvPlayer::isStateReligion() is `getStateReligionCount() > 0`, so under Free
Religion the runtime rejects conversion at `!isStateReligion()`. The player can
still have founded religions in their cities and select/hover them on the
Religion tab. Assuming no anarchy and no conversion timer, setConvertHelp then
has no matching branch and displays only the generic inability to convert.

SUPPORTED CURRENT STATE B — RELIGION ABSENT FROM OUR CITIES:
While using an ordinary state-religion civic, select a founded religion that
exists in the world but is present in none of our cities. canDoReligion returns
false because getHasReligionCount(eReligion) is zero, so canConvert rejects it.
setConvertHelp again has no branch for that reason and stops at the generic
"Cannot convert to <religion>" heading.

ANCESTRY:
The BtS/Civ4CE implementation of setConvertHelp is materially the same: it
handles anarchy, already-current religion and conversion timer only. BtS's own
canConvert already includes both `!isStateReligion()` and `!canDoReligion`.
K-Mod retains the same mismatch, and Base AdvCiv/current SAS retain it as well.
This is therefore a stock-BtS help omission, not an AdvCiv/SAS integration
regression.

REPAIR DIRECTION:
Mirror the remaining executable reasons in setConvertHelp. After the existing
anarchy/current-religion/timer handling (or in runtime-order if preferred), add
localized diagnostics for:

    - state religions are not permitted by the player's current civics;
    - the target religion is not present in any of the player's cities.

A dedicated localized key is preferable to reusing unrelated "requires state
religion" / spread text because this is a conversion-action explanation. Also
consider the NO_RELIGION case explicitly: when the current civic setup already
prohibits state religions, `canConvert(NO_RELIGION)` is false through the same
`!isStateReligion()` gate and should not fall back to an unexplained generic
heading.

F419 / provisional KI#742 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------------------
TITLE:
Found-city health preview prints nearby-feature unhealth instead of the
player-wide negative extra-health value.

CLASSIFICATION:
Inherited AdvCiv advc.004b TextMgr wrong-variable bug, present unchanged in
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS. The negative branch was latent under
older mostly/nonnegative data but is ordinarily live in current SAS because
TECH_DEPOPULATION applies negative player-wide health.

BROKEN SOURCE:
Current CvGameTextMgr::setFoundHealthHelp computes feature health first:

    int iGoodHealth = iGoodHealthPercent / 100;
    int iBadHealth = iBadHealthPercent / 100;

and later obtains the independent player-wide value:

    int iExtraHealth = GET_PLAYER(getActivePlayer()).getExtraHealth();

The positive branch prints the correct variable:

    if (iExtraHealth > 0)
        ... format("%d", iExtraHealth) ...

but the negative branch instead prints the unrelated earlier accumulator:

    else
    {
        iIcon = UNHEALTHY_CHAR;
        ... format("%d", iBadHealth) ...
    }

Thus the displayed magnitude is determined by nearby feature unhealth, not by
negative player-wide extra health.

LIVE CURRENT-SAS DATA:
Current TECH_DEPOPULATION is enabled Future-era content and has:

    <iHealth>-9</iHealth>
    <iHappiness>-9</iHappiness>
    <bDisable>0</bDisable>

Its prerequisites are current enabled technologies (OR Composites; AND
Satellites, Computers and Environmentalism), so the technology is an ordinary
reachable part of the current tree.

Current CvTeam::setHasTech applies technology health directly to every team
member's persistent player value:

    kMember.changeExtraHealth(kTech.getHealth() * iChange);

Therefore acquiring Depopulation can make CvPlayer::getExtraHealth() negative
(e.g. -9 for a player without offsetting positive extra-health sources).

RUNTIME CITY CONTRACT:
CvCity::goodHealth and CvCity::badHealth both combine the player-wide and
city-local values before taking positive/negative parts:

    GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).getExtraHealth() + getExtraHealth()

so the negative player value is a real health contribution inherited by a
newly founded city. It is not a cosmetic or unused technology statistic.

LIVE CALLER:
CvDLLWidgetData::parseActionHelp_Mission handles MISSION_FOUND. Whenever the
selected unit may legally found on the mission plot, it calls in sequence:

    GAMETEXT.setFoundCostHelp(...)
    GAMETEXT.setHomePlotYieldHelp(...)
    GAMETEXT.setFoundHealthHelp(...)

Thus an existing Settler after Depopulation can reach the defective preview on
any legal founding plot; no debug or dormant API path is required.

CONCRETE CURRENT STATE:
Take a player whose net player-wide extra health is -9 after Depopulation and a
legal feature-neutral founding plot with iBadHealth=0.

Runtime consequence for the future city:
    player-wide extra health contribution = -9

Founding hover consequence:
    negative branch enters because iExtraHealth != 0 and iExtraHealth < 0;
    it prints iBadHealth = 0 with the unhealthy icon.

So a real -9 unhealthy contribution can literally be previewed as +0 unhealthy.
On a site with e.g. two whole points of nearby feature unhealth, the same -9
player effect is instead mislabeled as 2, proving this is wrong-source variable
contamination rather than a mere sign/rounding issue.

ANCESTRY:
AdvCiv commit:

    6f8d41a1ac548879d04f56ff9210e9a5e10aa975
    "Help text for feature health made more flexible, refactored."

introduced setFoundHealthHelp as part of advc.004b and the introducing diff
already contains the erroneous `iBadHealth` reference in the negative
`iExtraHealth` branch. Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the line unchanged, as does
current SAS. Stock BtS/K-Mod do not have this AdvCiv helper in this form.

SAS ACTIVATION HISTORY:
SAS introduced negative health on Depopulation early in the Future-era work.
Commit 2a7f9e05e8 (practical 4895, "add initial future era techs ...") changed
Depopulation from iHealth=0 to iHealth=-5; later balance changes increased that
to -6, -8 and the current -9. Thus SAS content made an old AdvCiv negative-
branch typo an ordinary reachable player-facing defect.

REPAIR DIRECTION:
Use the actual negative player-wide value in the negative branch, e.g.:

    szBuffer.append(CvWString::format(L"%d%c", -iExtraHealth, iIcon));

(or an equivalent absolute-magnitude expression consistent with the helper's
existing `+<magnitude><healthy/unhealthy icon>` display convention).

The trailing TXT_KEY_FROM_TRAIT wording is also semantically incomplete because
CvPlayer::getExtraHealth can come from technologies, civics and other sources;
that is a secondary labeling concern, not the F419 root. The correctness repair
is first to stop substituting `iBadHealth` for `iExtraHealth`.

F420 / KI#743 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TITLE:
CITY HEALTH HOVER SPLITS PLAYER-WIDE AND CITY-LOCAL EXTRA HEALTH EVEN THOUGH
RUNTIME NETS THEM FIRST, SO OPPOSITE-SIGNED CURRENT SOURCES MISSTATE THE
COMPONENT TOTALS

CLASSIFICATION:
K-Mod-origin health-help integration mismatch retained by Base AdvCiv and current
SAS; latent under K-Mod/Base-AdvCiv normal data, made ordinarily live by SAS's
negative-health Depopulation technology together with an inherited positive
city-health random event.

WHY THIS IS DISTINCT FROM F389/F390:
F389/KI#712 concerns `setFoundHealthHelp` and a direct wrong-variable typo in a
future-city founding preview. F390/KI#713 concerns the aggregate player-health
source being mislabeled "from trait". F420 is instead in the ordinary selected-
city health breakdown (`setBadHealthHelp` / `setGoodHealthHelp`) and is caused by
splitting two operands that runtime deliberately combines before sign clamping.
It therefore has a separate caller, producer shape and repair contract.

PREVIOUS DORMANT CONTROL REACTIVATED:
An earlier whole-file sweep had already noticed the semantic seam and correctly
kept it unnumbered at that time:

    CvCity::goodHealth()/badHealth() combine
        GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).getExtraHealth() + getExtraHealth()
    before clamping, while TextMgr prints the two values independently.

That control was dismissed because the then-audited current data was believed to
provide no ordinary opposite-signed pair. The later F389 investigation proved
that assumption stale: current enabled `TECH_DEPOPULATION` has `iHealth = -9`
and feeds that value into `CvPlayer::changeExtraHealth` on acquisition.

RUNTIME CONTRACT:
Current `CvCity::goodHealth()` uses:

    iHealth += std::max(0,
            GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).getExtraHealth() + getExtraHealth());

Current `CvCity::badHealth()` analogously uses:

    iHealth += std::min(0,
            GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).getExtraHealth() + getExtraHealth());

Thus these are not two independent health buckets. They are one net ExtraHealth
contribution whose sign is determined only after player-wide and city-local
values have been added.

CURRENT TEXTMGR CONTRACT VIOLATION:
`setBadHealthHelp` independently checks and prints:

    GET_PLAYER(kCity.getOwner()).getExtraHealth()

when it is negative, then independently checks `kCity.getExtraHealth()` only
when that second value is negative.

`setGoodHealthHelp` does the mirror image, printing the player value if positive
and the city value if positive.

Therefore opposite signs are never allowed to cancel in the source lines even
though runtime cancels them before assigning anything to healthy/unhealthy.
Both helpers then print footers from the correct runtime totals (`goodHealth()` /
`badHealth()`), so the displayed components can visibly fail to add up to their
own footer.

LIVE CURRENT-SAS PLAYER-WIDE NEGATIVE SOURCE:
Current enabled Future-era `TECH_DEPOPULATION` has:

    <iHealth>-9</iHealth>
    <bDisable>0</bDisable>

and ordinary team-tech acquisition executes:

    kMember.changeExtraHealth(kTech.getHealth() * iChange);

Its current prerequisites are enabled (OR Composites; AND Satellites, Computers
and Environmentalism), so this is normal reachable tree content, not a hidden
option or debug-only state.

LIVE CURRENT-SAS CITY-LOCAL POSITIVE SOURCE:
Current inherited `EVENT_HORTICULTURE_3` has:

    <bPickCity>1</bPickCity>
    <iHealth>3</iHealth>

`CvEventInfo::isCityEffect()` is loaded directly from the XML `bPickCity` field,
and `CvCity::applyEvent` applies such event health through:

    changeExtraHealth(kEvent.getHealth());

The Horticulture trigger is ordinary current content:
- 80% games active;
- weight 200;
- Calendar prerequisite;
- normal owned Forest/Jungle plot requirement;
- `bPickCity=1`;
- no obsolete tech.

Its selectable `EVENT_HORTICULTURE_2` outcome has a 67% AdditionalEventChance for
`EVENT_HORTICULTURE_3`. The +3 city value is persistent state: `m_iExtraHealth`
is incremented by `changeExtraHealth`, serialized in city saves, and Horticulture
3 has no EventTimes/ClearEvents entry that later removes it.

Thus an ordinary Calendar-era city can permanently acquire +3 city-local health
and later survive into the Future era when its owner researches Depopulation.
No WorldBuilder, Python injection, custom scenario or mod-mod XML is needed.

CONCRETE CURRENT-SAS FAILURE:
Take such a Horticulture city after Depopulation, with no other player-wide
ExtraHealth offset for the simple example:

    CvPlayer::getExtraHealth() = -9
    CvCity::getExtraHealth()   = +3

Runtime nets them first:

    -9 + 3 = -6

so this pair contributes exactly 6 unhealth and 0 health.

But `setBadHealthHelp` prints the full player-wide 9 unhealth source because it
checks -9 independently. It does not print the +3 city value in the bad section
because +3 is positive. The helper's final `TOTAL_UNHEALTHY` footer, however,
uses `kCity.badHealth()` and therefore incorporates only the correct net -6.
Its listed components consequently overstate unhealth by 3.

The good-health side has the mirror semantic problem: when the city has any
other positive source causing `goodHealth()>0`, `setGoodHealthHelp` can list the
+3 city ExtraHealth line even though this +3 contributes zero to runtime good
health because it is consumed by the -9 player-wide value before clamping.

LIVE UI CALLER:
Current `CvMainInterface.py` attaches `WIDGET_HELP_HEALTH` to the ordinary city
screen `HealthText`. `CvDLLWidgetData::parseHealthHelp` then calls:

    GAMETEXT.setBadHealthHelp(szBuffer, *pHeadSelectedCity);
    ...
    GAMETEXT.setGoodHealthHelp(szBuffer, *pHeadSelectedCity);

This is the standard selected-city health hover, so the mismatch is directly
player-facing.

ANCESTRY:
The supplied stock-BtS/Civ4CE source has only player-wide ExtraHealth in both
runtime good/bad health and the matching TextMgr breakdown; it does not have the
city-local operand in this contract.

The supplied K-Mod source is the first point in the local lineage where runtime
uses:

    GET_PLAYER(...).getExtraHealth() + getExtraHealth()

while its TextMgr simultaneously displays player ExtraHealth and
`city.getExtraHealth()` as separate sign-filtered lines. Base AdvCiv retains the
same semantic split, as does current SAS (with AdvCiv wording/refactoring around
the individual lines).

K-Mod already has positive city-local event health such as Horticulture 3, but
its supplied stock data has no negative direct tech/event health source that
creates the opposing-sign player-wide side. Base AdvCiv likewise has no ordinary
negative player-wide direct health source in the checked event/tech/civic/trait
XML. Hence the mismatch remained data-masked there.

SAS's Future-era Depopulation health penalty removes that masking condition.
This makes F420 best classified as a latent K-Mod integration mismatch retained
through AdvCiv and activated by current SAS data.

REPAIR DIRECTION:
Make the ordinary health breakdown honor the same net ExtraHealth bucket as
runtime. The player-wide and city-local values should be combined before deciding
whether this source contributes to the good or bad section, e.g. conceptually:

    iExtraHealth = GET_PLAYER(kCity.getOwner()).getExtraHealth()
                 + kCity.getExtraHealth();

and then print only the positive net in `setGoodHealthHelp` and only the negative
net magnitude in `setBadHealthHelp`.

If source attribution is preserved, it must still reconcile to that net rather
than presenting the two operands as independent health buckets. F390 separately
covers the existing inaccurate "from trait" attribution of the aggregate player
value and should not be conflated with this arithmetic repair.

F421 / KI#744 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TITLE:
CORPORATION MAINTENANCE CACHE EMBEDS THE INVERSE OF THE INFLATION RATE BUT IS
NOT REFRESHED WHEN INFLATION CHANGES, SO STABLE CORPORATION CITIES CAN BE
SYSTEMATICALLY OVERCHARGED AS THE GAME ADVANCES

CLASSIFICATION:
Inherited stock-BtS runtime cache defect. Present in stock BtS/Civ4CE, later
explicitly recognized in K-Mod source as "obviously a bug", and retained by
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

HOW THIS SURFACED FROM THE TEXTMGR AUDIT:
The post-F420 pass reopened `setCorporationHelpCity` because that helper
recalculates corporation maintenance and then restores inflation for its displayed
corporation cost. A first lead concerned per-component versus aggregate rounding.
That weaker lead does not justify a new finding by itself: with a freshly updated
maintenance cache, the corporation icon has no independent aggregate total against
which its per-corporation allocation must sum exactly.

Tracing the helper back to the actual city-maintenance producer exposed a much
harder defect: the corporation-maintenance term stored in `m_iMaintenance` depends
on the current inflation rate, but inflation changing with game time does not
invalidate that cache.

RUNTIME CONTRACT:
Current `CvCity::calculateCorporationMaintenanceTimes100(eCorporation)` computes
normal corporation maintenance and then deliberately divides by inflation:

    int iInflation = GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).calculateInflationRate() + 100;
    if (iInflation > 0)
    {
        iMaintenance *= 100;
        iMaintenance /= iInflation;
    }

The reason for that inverse factor is that ordinary expenses later pass through
`CvPlayer::calculateInflatedCosts`:

    int iCosts = calculatePreInflatedCosts();
    iCosts *= std::max(0, calculateInflationRate() + 100);
    iCosts /= 100;

Thus, when recomputed at the same inflation rate, corporation maintenance is
intended to be approximately inflation-neutral: the inverse factor inside the
corporation component cancels the later general expense inflation.

CACHE CONTRACT:
`CvCity::updateMaintenance()` calculates:

    iNewMaintenance = calculateBaseMaintenanceTimes100() *
            max(0, getMaintenanceModifier() + 100) / 100;

and stores it in `m_iMaintenance`. `calculateBaseMaintenanceTimes100` includes
`calculateCorporationMaintenanceTimes100()`.

Therefore the inverse-inflation divisor used at the moment of a maintenance
refresh becomes embedded in the persistent city-maintenance cache.

But current `calculateInflationRate()` is a live calculation from game turn /
elapsed turns, game speed, handicap and modifiers. It increases as the game
advances without modifying any of the inputs that normally call
`updateMaintenance()`.

INVALIDATION FAILURE:
A complete source grep of current SAS maintenance refreshes finds updates for
specific state mutations such as:
- city creation/removal;
- population changes;
- government-center / maintenance-modifier changes;
- corporation/resource updates;
- relevant player modifiers, anarchy-state changes, religion/capital changes;
- a few Rise & Fall / vassal-state transitions.

There is no ordinary per-turn `CvPlayer::updateMaintenance()` and no hook that
refreshes city maintenance merely because `calculateInflationRate()` has advanced.
`CvCity::doTurn()` likewise does not refresh maintenance unconditionally.

Consequently a stagnant corporation city whose population, corporation/resource
network, maintenance modifiers and other invalidating state remain unchanged can
retain an inverse-inflation divisor from many turns earlier.

DIRECTION OF THE ERROR:
Suppose the cache was last refreshed at inflation I_old and the current inflation
has risen to I_new. Ignoring integer truncation for clarity, the corporation
portion stored in city maintenance is proportional to:

    nominal corporation maintenance * 100 / (100 + I_old)

but current general expenses multiply it by:

    (100 + I_new) / 100

so the final corporation burden becomes proportional to:

    nominal * (100 + I_new) / (100 + I_old)

rather than nominal.

Since ordinary inflation rises over time, a stale cache normally OVERCHARGES the
corporation. The longer the cache survives without an unrelated maintenance
refresh, the larger the drift can become.

CONCRETE CURRENT-SAS NUMERIC CONSTRUCTION:
Use current Normal speed, Standard world size and Noble handicap. Relevant XML:

    Normal iInflationPercent              = 30
    Normal iInflationOffset               = -90
    Standard CorporationMaintenancePercent = 100
    Noble CorporationMaintenancePercent    = 100

Use current Cereal Mills (`CORPORATION_1`), which has:

    iMaintenance = 100
    total HeadquarterCommerce = 4

Take a population-20 corporation city with ten qualifying connected grain
resources, no city maintenance modifier and no player corporation-maintenance
modifier.

Before the inverse-inflation step its corporation maintenance is:

    HQ term                 = 4 * 100 = 400 hundredths
    resource term           = 10 * 100 = 1000 hundredths
    subtotal                = 1400
    population factor       = (20 + 17) / 18
    floor(1400 * 37 / 18)   = 2877 hundredths

On an ordinary Normal-speed timeline with game turn == elapsed turns, current
SAS inflation is 48% at turn 224 and 59% at turn 250.

If the city's maintenance is refreshed at turn 224, the cached corporation term
becomes:

    floor(2877 * 100 / 148) = 1943 hundredths

A normal whole-player refresh can happen, for example, when anarchy ends;
`changeAnarchyTurns` calls `updateMaintenance()` when the anarchy state changes.

Now let the city remain stable through turn 250: no population change, resource
network change, corporation change, maintenance-modifier change or other refresh
producer. `CvCity::doTurn` does not itself refresh maintenance each turn.

At turn 250 the CORRECT freshly calculated inverse-inflation term would be:

    floor(2877 * 100 / 159) = 1809 hundredths

but the stored city cache still contains 1943. It is therefore already 134
hundredths (1.34 pre-inflated gold) too high for this one corporation city.

Applying the current 59% general inflation illustrates the intended cancellation
versus the stale result at component precision:

    fresh: floor(1809 * 159 / 100) = 2876 hundredths ~= 28.76 gold
    stale: floor(1943 * 159 / 100) = 3089 hundredths ~= 30.89 gold

The stale component is about 2.13 gold/turn above the inflation-neutral target
before the engine's later whole-expense aggregation/truncation.

This is not restricted to sub-gold noise. If ten otherwise stable corporation
cities have the same 134-hundredth stale excess, `m_iTotalMaintenance` is 1340
hundredths too high. Regardless of the unrelated maintenance fractional residue,
`getTotalMaintenance()` is then 13 or 14 whole pre-inflation gold too high; at
59% inflation that necessarily changes the final charged expenses by roughly
20+ gold/turn.

LIVE TEXTMGR CONSEQUENCE:
Current `setCorporationHelpCity` does NOT read the cached corporation portion.
It calls `calculateCorporationMaintenanceTimes100(eCorporation)` afresh using the
CURRENT inflation rate and then multiplies by the current inflation factor for
display (a K-Mod UI change).

Thus after the cache has gone stale the corporation icon can continue to show the
roughly inflation-neutral/current corporation maintenance while the player's
actual cached city maintenance is based on an older, larger inverse-inflation
term. The UI can therefore understate the maintenance actually feeding the
player's expenses. This is a symptom of the runtime cache root, not a separate
TextMgr finding.

ANCESTRY:
Stock BtS/Civ4CE already has all essential pieces:
- corporation maintenance divides by `calculateInflationRate() + 100`;
- city maintenance is cached through `m_iMaintenance` / `updateMaintenance()`;
- inflation is time-dependent;
- there is no per-turn maintenance refresh tied to inflation.

So the runtime root is stock BtS, not a K-Mod invention.

K-Mod later made inflation itself cached/updated per turn. In practical commit
1195, SHA `8c6e324ab4e02e1276b0f565d8746696d4f2ee51`, source commentary explicitly
states that because city maintenance is cached, the inverse inflation correction
can remain unchanged while inflation grows, making corporation maintenance too
high, and concludes:

    "This is obviously a bug; but I'm not going to worry about it right now."

That K-Mod commit documents rather than introduces the root.

K-Mod practical 1197 (`efe8a852fa0d6c56a7c3dd57af2eeced1a99b72c`) then changed
`setCorporationHelpCity` to include inflation when displaying costs, but did not
repair maintenance-cache invalidation.

AdvCiv's early import/refactor (`f6ff6a182f5187541fff6e5bbbe12f9573b3778c`)
removed K-Mod's stored `m_iInflationRate` / `updateInflationRate()` and returned
inflation to an on-demand `calculateInflationRate()` result. It retained the
inverse-inflation corporation-maintenance formula and still did not add a
maintenance refresh when time changes. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS therefore
retain the stock defect.

REPAIR DIRECTION:
The conservative repair is to keep the intended inflation-neutral corporation
rule but ensure that any cached maintenance containing the inverse inflation term
is rebuilt whenever the effective inflation rate changes, before that maintenance
is used for economic charging / UI totals.

Possible implementations include:
- track the inflation rate used for the maintenance cache and call
  `CvPlayer::updateMaintenance()` when the effective rate changes;
- refresh maintenance at a turn transition point that is guaranteed to precede
  all expense calculations for that inflation rate (ideally only when the rate
  actually changes, and potentially only for players with active corporations);
- architecturally remove the time-varying inverse-inflation term from persistent
  cached city maintenance and handle corporation inflation cancellation outside
  that cache.

Simply deleting the inverse-inflation division would make corporation maintenance
inflate normally and would therefore be a gameplay-rule change rather than the
minimal bug fix.

ROUNDING / DECOMPOSITION CONTROL THAT LED HERE:
With a freshly updated cache, `setCorporationHelpCity` applies city maintenance
modifier and inflation to one corporation separately, whereas actual city/player
expenses aggregate components and perform integer truncation at later stages.
This can create one-gold allocation differences. However the corporation hover
has no independently displayed aggregate total that its one-corporation number
must sum to, unlike F400's internally contradictory Finance Advisor breakdown.
Without a stronger semantic contract, keep that as presentation/decomposition
debt rather than creating a second finding. F421 is the independently provable
runtime cache defect.

F422 / provisional KI#745 — FRENCH CITY-BAR ANGER LOCALIZATION PRINTS THE ANGRY
POPULATION ARGUMENT TWICE, INSERTING AN EXTRA NUMBER BEFORE THE TURN COUNT NOUN
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
File family: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp + Assets/XML/Text/CIV4GameText_advc.xml
Primary function: CvGameTextMgr::setCityBarHelp
Classification: AdvCiv French localization typo introduced with advc.186 city-bar
hover integration; retained by Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS.

ROOT
----
The C++ contract is unambiguous:

    szString.append(gDLL->getText("TXT_KEY_CITY_BAR_ANGER_TIMER",
            iAngryPop, iAngerTimer));

There are exactly two arguments:

    %d1 = displayed angry population
    %d2 = displayed anger timer

The current English/German/Italian/Spanish strings use those two arguments once.
French instead contains:

    -%d1[ICON_UNHAPPY] pour %d2 %d1 [NUM2:tour:tours]

The second `%d1` has no grammatical role. It repeats the angry-population number
between the timer and the noun selected from argument 2.

For example, if the helper supplies `(3, 10)`, the French text structurally
contains:

    -3 unhappy pour 10 3 tours

rather than the intended equivalent of `-3 unhappy for 10 turns`.

CURRENT REACHABILITY
--------------------
This is an ordinary current-SAS path:

* `setCityBarHelp` executes this block for the active player's city when the BUG
  option `CityScreen__Anger_Counter` is enabled.
* Current `Assets/Config/BUG City Screen.xml` sets that option to `default="True"`.
* Any positive hurry, conscription or defy-resolution anger timer reaches the
  formatter.
* F407 already provides a fully current-data construction with simultaneous
  hurry/draft anger; no special scenario or custom XML is needed merely to
  reach the localization key.

DISTINCT FROM F407
------------------
F407 is the C++ arithmetic root in the same display: AdvCiv takes the maximum of
multiple temporary-anger sources where runtime adds them. F422 remains wrong even
if F407 is repaired perfectly, because it is an independent French XML format
string typo. Conversely, changing this French string does not repair F407.

ANCESTRY
--------
Reachable-history practical commit 3010:

    92202f546295e43857d6172e1b9c6665446e68a5
    "Overhaul city bar hover text (based on BULL)"

introduced both the C++ call and `TXT_KEY_CITY_BAR_ANGER_TIMER`. Its introducing
diff already contains the duplicate French `%d1`. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current
SAS retain it. This therefore belongs to AdvCiv's advc.186 integration rather
than stock BtS/K-Mod.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Remove the second `%d1` from the French localization, preserving argument 2 for
the `[NUM2:tour:tours]` grammar token, e.g. structurally:

    -%d1[ICON_UNHAPPY] pour %d2 [NUM2:tour:tours]

This is a localization-only repair; it should be made independently of F407's
C++ anger aggregation repair.

F423 / provisional KI#746 — STOCK CIV4 FRENCH STATE-RELIGION GREAT-PEOPLE CIVIC
HELP OMITS THE `%` BEFORE ARGUMENT 2 AND DISPLAYS `F2_Religion` AS LITERAL TEXT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
File family: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp + inherited Civ4 text XML
Primary function: CvGameTextMgr::parseCivicInfo
Classification: stock Civ4 French localization typo retained through BtS/K-Mod,
AdvCiv and current SAS.

ROOT
----
For a civic with a nonzero state-religion Great Person modifier, the generic /
non-player-context branch supplies two arguments:

    gDLL->getText("TXT_KEY_CIVIC_GREAT_PEOPLE_MOD_STATE_RELIGION",
            kCivic.getStateReligionGreatPeopleRateModifier(),
            gDLL->getSymbolID(RELIGION_CHAR));

The inherited key is:

English:
    ... State %F2_Religion
German/Italian/Spanish:
    ... %F2_Religion ...
French:
    ... religion d'etat : F2_Religion

French alone lacks the leading `%`. Therefore its second argument is never
interpreted as the religion glyph/formatter token; the user instead receives the
literal text `F2_Religion` at the end of the help line.

CURRENT REACHABILITY
--------------------
Current `CIVIC_PACIFISM` has:

    iStateReligionGreatPeopleRateModifier = 100

and is normal current content (currently unlocked at Medicine).

There are two ordinary current callers:

1. Policy Advisor:

       CyGameTextMgr().parseCivicInfo(iCivic, False, True, True)

   If the active player currently has no state religion, `parseCivicInfo` takes
   the `_STATE_RELIGION` branch.

2. Current SAS Sevopedia civic page:

       CyGameTextMgr().parseCivicInfo(self.iCivic, True, False, True)

   Here `bPlayerContext == false`, so Pacifism's pedia effects always use the
   `_STATE_RELIGION` key regardless of the active player's religion.

Thus merely opening Pacifism in the current Sevopedia while the game language is
French is sufficient to expose the malformed line.

ANCESTRY
--------
`TXT_KEY_CIVIC_GREAT_PEOPLE_MOD_STATE_RELIGION` is present in the stock Civ4 text
set represented by Civ4CE. Its English/German/Italian/Spanish entries contain
`%F2_Religion`; its French entry already contains bare `F2_Religion`.
No Warlords/BtS/SAS override repairs it. This is therefore a stock-Civ4 French
text defect inherited intact through the lineage rather than an AdvCiv/SAS
regression.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Change French `F2_Religion` to `%F2_Religion`. No C++ change is required.

F424 / provisional KI#747 — ADVCIV ESPIONAGE CIVIC/RELIGION COST WARNING PASSES
ONE ARGUMENT BUT FOUR NON-ENGLISH LOCALIZATIONS REQUEST `%s2`
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
File family: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp + Assets/XML/Text/CIV4GameText_advc.xml
Primary function: CvGameTextMgr::setEspionageCostHelp
Classification: AdvCiv advc.132 localization argument-index defect; introduced
with the warning feature and retained by Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS.
Affected current languages: French, German, Italian, Spanish.

ROOT
----
AdvCiv deliberately added a warning when a force-civic/force-religion espionage
mission remains legal even though the spying player does not itself practice the
chosen civic/religion. The formatter is called with exactly ONE argument:

    gDLL->getText("TXT_KEY_ESPIONAGE_CIVIC_RELIGION_MOD",
            kMission.getSwitchCivicCostFactor() > 0 ?
            GC.getInfo((CivicTypes)iExtraData).getTextKeyWide() :
            GC.getInfo((ReligionTypes)iExtraData).getTextKeyWide())

English correctly references:

    %s1_ReligionOrCivic

but French, German, Italian and Spanish all reference:

    %s2_ReligionOrCivic

There is no argument 2. This is a hard localization/C++ contract mismatch, not a
translation-style difference. Those four languages request an out-of-range
placeholder whenever this warning branch is used.

CURRENT REACHABILITY
--------------------
Current espionage XML retains both ordinary missions:

    ESPIONAGEMISSION_SWITCH_CIVIC
        iSwitchCivicCostFactor = 1000

    ESPIONAGEMISSION_SWITCH_RELIGION
        iSwitchReligionCostFactor = 1000

Both are active city-targeting missions with no tech prerequisite in current XML.

Current `CvPlayer::getEspionageMissionBaseCost` intentionally supports the exact
mismatch state that the warning describes. For force-civic cost it adds 100 to
the speed/anarchy modifier when the spying player is not using the candidate
civic; for force-religion it analogously adds 100 when the spying player's state
religion differs. In other words, mismatch does not invalidate the mission; it
increases its cost.

`CvDLLWidgetData::parseEspionageCostHelp` is the ordinary
`WIDGET_HELP_ESPIONAGE_COST` path. It obtains the selected eligible Spy and calls
`setEspionageCostHelp` with the mission, target plot/player and mission extra data.
Thus an ordinary spy mission button hover can enter this warning path.

ANCESTRY
--------
Reachable-history practical commit 4221:

    cd4282f9fb8bf792a353e416fdfc5abf4fae0f3d
    "Espionage cost breakdown warns when civic/religion not practised"

introduced the C++ warning and its new localization key together. The introducing
diff already has English `%s1` and FR/DE/IT/ES `%s2`. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current
SAS retain the mismatch.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Change `%s2_ReligionOrCivic` to `%s1_ReligionOrCivic` in French, German, Italian
and Spanish. The current C++ one-argument call is the intended contract and the
English entry already demonstrates it.

F425 / provisional KI#748 — SPANISH ZERO-ATTITUDE SUMMARY REQUESTS NONEXISTENT
ARGUMENT 3 EVEN THOUGH THE ZERO CASE PASSES ONLY ATTITUDE AND LEADER NAME
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
File family: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp + Assets/XML/Text/CIV4GameText_advc.xml
Primary function: CvGameTextMgr::getAttitudeString
Classification: early AdvCiv/advc.004q Spanish localization argument-index typo,
present in the earliest tracked AdvCiv import and retained by current SAS.

ROOT
----
The exact-zero Cautious branch calls:

    gDLL->getText("TXT_KEY_ZERO_ATTITUDE_TOWARDS",
            szAttitude, szTargetName)

so the contract is:

    %s1 = attitude description
    %s2 = target leader name

English/French/German/Italian all obey that contract. Spanish instead says:

    Actitud hacia %s3_leader: %s1_attitude (+/- 0)

There is no third argument in the zero branch.

The copy/paste origin is especially clear in the neighboring positive/negative
neutral-attitude keys. Those nonzero variants genuinely pass THREE arguments:
attitude, numeric total, leader name, and therefore correctly use `%s3_leader`.
The Spanish zero variant retained that third-argument index even though the zero
formatter omits the numeric middle argument.

CURRENT REACHABILITY
--------------------
This is an ordinary diplomacy/scoreboard state, not a rare XML branch:

* current `AI_getAttitudeFromValue` returns Cautious for totals not reaching the
  configured Friendly/Pleased/Annoyed/Furious thresholds;
* current thresholds are Friendly >= 9, Pleased >= 4, Annoyed <= -2,
  Furious <= -9, so an exact total of 0 is unambiguously Cautious;
* `getAttitudeString` therefore selects `TXT_KEY_ZERO_ATTITUDE_TOWARDS` whenever
  the visible summed attitude is exactly 0;
* current `CvDLLWidgetData` invokes `getAttitudeString` in normal player /
  scoreboard hover paths, and BUG `AttitudeUtil.py` also consumes the same DLL
  string.

Thus a Spanish game merely needs an AI relationship whose current visible total
is exactly zero, a normal early/intermediate diplomacy state.

ANCESTRY
--------
The key appears in reachable-history practical commit 1253:

    f6ff6a182f5187541fff6e5bbbe12f9573b3778c
    "Initial commit (cont.)"

inside the advc.004q attitude-summary text family. That earliest tracked entry
already has `%s3_leader` in Spanish while the other four languages use `%s2`.
A later attitude refactor retained the two-argument C++ call and did not repair
the Spanish key. K-Mod/Civ4CE do not contain this AdvCiv key family.

Because practical 1253 is an early history/import boundary, classify this as an
early-AdvCiv/advc.004q defect present in the earliest tracked AdvCiv form rather
than claiming that the import commit necessarily originated the typo historically.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Change the Spanish zero-case leader placeholder from `%s3_leader` to
`%s2_leader`. Leave the nonzero three-argument Spanish attitude keys at `%s3`.

FULL-SWEEP CONTROLS / NON-FINDINGS PRESERVED AFTER F422-F425
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. Already-known dormant negative-event-health key mismatch
------------------------------------------------------------
The corrected scanner flags `TXT_KEY_EVENT_UNHEALTH_CITY` because one current C++
negative-health branch supplies only the numeric health argument although the key
also expects `%s2_city`. This is the same already-recorded dormant event-health
city/global-key mismatch, not a new root. Current Event XML still supplies no
negative `iHealth`, so it remains data-dormant and consumes no number here.

2. `TXT_KEY_BUILDING_RELIGION_YIELD` German omits `%s1`
--------------------------------------------------------
Other languages name the building/religion argument. German instead uses a
self-contained description equivalent to "all religious buildings whose religion
matches this building." It does not require the argument to preserve the effect's
meaning. Treat as translation phrasing, not a contract bug.

3. `%d` vs `%D` language differences
------------------------------------
The scanner finds Spanish `TXT_KEY_EVENT_HURRY_ANGER` and French
`TXT_KEY_MISC_TOTAL_HEALTHY` differing in signed/unsigned-style placeholder code
from English. No current source/runtime contradiction was proven from that alone.
Do not promote without a concrete formatting failure.

4. Missing `TXT_KEY_CIVIC_COLONY_MAINT_MOD`
-------------------------------------------
Current C++ asks for `TXT_KEY_CIVIC_COLONY_MAINT_MOD`, while AdvCiv text defines
`TXT_KEY_CIVIC_COLONYE_MAINT_MOD` (extra E). This is a genuine AdvCiv key-name
typo, but current SAS's only nonzero `iColonyMaintenanceModifier` is Vassalage at
-100, which takes the separate "No Colonial Expenses" branch. The broken general
modifier branch remains current-data dormant.

5. Missing `TXT_KEY_CIV_UNKNOWN`
--------------------------------
`parseCivInfos(NO_CIVILIZATION, ...)` asks for `TXT_KEY_CIV_UNKNOWN`, and the
combined stock+SAS text search finds no effective key. The branch is inherited
from stock code. Known current Python callers pass concrete civilizations; an
EXE-side SimpleCivPicker/random-civilization path may call the sentinel branch,
but local source does not prove that. Preserve as an EXE-facing suspicion, not a
finding.

6. WorldBuilder Holy City / Headquarters extra arguments
---------------------------------------------------------
The stock WorldBuilder data helpers pass religion/corporation names into generic
keys whose shipped strings contain no placeholders. This may discard identifying
text, but the functions are EXE-facing `DllExport` palette records and local
source does not establish how the EXE displays those descriptions beside IDs /
icons. Keep below threshold.

7. Earlier partial scanner is superseded
-----------------------------------------
Do not reuse the earlier 529-key / 717-ish-call intermediate result. The
comment-aware corrected scan above (1252 active literal calls / 980 unique keys)
is authoritative for this tranche.

FALSE-POSITIVE FAMILY CLOSED — GET_TEAM(PlayerTypes) IS TYPE-AWARE
------------------------------------------------------------------
A mechanical player/team-domain scan made three current expressions look highly
suspicious:

    setResearchStr:
        GET_TEAM(ePlayer).getTechCount(...)

    getVassalInfoString:
        CvTeam const& kTeam = GET_TEAM(ePlayer);

    parseWarTradesHelp:
        GET_TEAM(eThisPlayer).isAtWar(...)
        GET_TEAM(eOtherPlayer).isHuman()
        GET_TEAM(eThisPlayer).AI_declareWarTrade(...)

The history makes the syntax especially deceptive: old AdvCiv often used the
TEAMREF(player) macro and practical 1679 mechanically changed many such calls to
GET_TEAM(player); K-Mod's getVassalInfoString explicitly used
GET_TEAM(GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).getTeam()), while AdvCiv practical 3062 later
simplified it to GET_TEAM(ePlayer).

These are nevertheless NOT player-ID-as-team-ID bugs. Current AdvCiv/SAS defines
GET_TEAM through an overloaded helper. In the gameplay layer:

    #define GET_TEAM(x) CvGamePlay::getTeam(x)

    __forceinline CvTeam& getTeam(TeamTypes eTeam)
    {
        return CvTeam::getTeam(eTeam);
    }

    __forceinline CvTeam& getTeam(PlayerTypes ePlayer)
    {
        return CvTeam::getTeam(TEAMID(ePlayer));
    }

and the CoreAI layer analogously defines:

    getTeam(PlayerTypes ePlayer)
    {
        return CvTeamAI::AI_getTeam(TEAMID(ePlayer));
    }

Therefore overload resolution preserves the PlayerTypes static type and converts
the player through that player's actual team. This is safe when player and team
numeric IDs differ, including team games / team reassignment.

This exact semantic trap was already preserved in Queue-003 WIP97 and elsewhere
in the album. The current recheck broadens that positive control explicitly to:

* setResearchStr;
* getVassalInfoString;
* parseWarTradesHelp.

Do not promote any of these merely because the source argument is named ePlayer.
The old F113/KI#436 player/team-ID hypothesis was likewise retracted after this
overload was traced. parseLeaderLineHelp has similar-looking calls but is already
explicit dead code; it remains a dead-path control.

The history remains useful for archaeology but does not change the runtime
contract:

* practical 1679 (`1c56cc6ac1...`, "GET_PLAYER, GET_TEAM macros outside of AI
  headers") converts TEAMREF(player) spellings to GET_TEAM(player) precisely as
  part of introducing the typed overload infrastructure;
* practical 3062 (`457122d485...`, "Misc. refactoring") simplifies K-Mod's
  explicit player->team chain in getVassalInfoString to that overloaded form.

No F426 is consumed.
