-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F426 / provisional KI#749 — FORCE-RELIGION ESPIONAGE HELP REUSES THE FORCE-CIVIC
TEXT KEY, SO GERMAN ORDINARY MISSION HELP CALLS THE CHOSEN RELIGION A CIVIC /
GOVERNMENT FORM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
File family: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp + stock BtS localization
Primary function: CvGameTextMgr::setEspionageCostHelp
Classification: stock-BtS localization/help integration defect retained by K-Mod,
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS; ordinary current German UI exposure.

ROOT
----
The force-civic and force-religion branches are distinct runtime effects, but
stock BtS uses the exact same help key for both:

    if (kMission.getSwitchCivicCostFactor() > 0)
    {
        ...
        gDLL->getText("TXT_KEY_ESPIONAGE_HELP_SWITCH_CIVIC",
                targetName, civicName)
    }

    if (kMission.getSwitchReligionCostFactor() > 0)
    {
        ...
        gDLL->getText("TXT_KEY_ESPIONAGE_HELP_SWITCH_CIVIC",
                targetName, religionName)
    }

There is no TXT_KEY_ESPIONAGE_HELP_SWITCH_RELIGION anywhere in the locally
available lineage.

The inherited BtS localization for the reused key is not language-neutral in
all supported languages. In particular German is:

    %s1_player zum Wechsel zur Staatsform %s2_civic verleiten

"Staatsform" means the civic/government form. Supplying a ReligionInfo text key
as argument 2 therefore produces a semantically false ordinary help sentence --
for example, a Buddhism choice is described as inducing the target to switch to
the civic/government form Buddhism.

English happens to mask the design error because its wording is generic:

    Induce %s1_player to switch to %s2_civic

Italian is similarly generic, and French "doctrine" is less categorical. The
German localization demonstrates a hard visible consequence of the shared-key
contract rather than a mere naming-style concern.

CURRENT SAS REACHABILITY
------------------------
Current CIV4EspionageMissionInfo.xml retains the normal two-phase mission:

    ESPIONAGEMISSION_SWITCH_RELIGION
        bIsTwoPhases = 1
        bTargetsCity = 1
        TechPrereq = NONE
        iSwitchReligionCostFactor = 1000

CvDLLButtonPopup::launchEspionageTargetPopup handles this mission by iterating
all religions. For every religion for which canDoEspionageMission succeeds, it
adds a normal selectable button with:

    WIDGET_HELP_ESPIONAGE_COST,
    eMission,
    eLoopReligion

Thus widget data2 is the actual chosen ReligionTypes value. The ordinary widget
parser finds the eligible selected Spy and calls:

    GAMETEXT.setEspionageCostHelp(...,
            widgetDataStruct.m_iData2, pUnit)

so hovering one of those legal religion choices enters the force-religion help
branch with exactly the religion selected by the popup. No debug mode, hidden
option, unsupported scenario or dormant XML value is required.

Runtime execution separately confirms the intended semantics: CvPlayer's
espionage execution branch for getSwitchReligionCostFactor sets the target's
last state religion to the chosen ReligionTypes and uses the religion-specific
TXT_KEY_ESPIONAGE_TARGET_SWITCH_RELIGION result key. The help line is therefore
the mismatched component, not ambiguous gameplay behavior.

ANCESTRY
--------
The Civ4CE BtS reference already contains both pieces of the defect:

* CvGameTextMgr::setEspionageCostHelp uses
  TXT_KEY_ESPIONAGE_HELP_SWITCH_CIVIC in the force-religion branch;
* CIV4GameText_BTS_FourthRoundTranslation.xml defines that key with the German
  word "Staatsform" and has no religion-specific sibling help key.

K-Mod retains the same reuse. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain it too.
Current SAS does not override the inherited help key. This is therefore a
stock-BtS help/localization integration defect rather than an AdvCiv/SAS
regression.

RELATION TO F424
----------------
F424 / KI#747 is independent. F424 concerns AdvCiv's later
TXT_KEY_ESPIONAGE_CIVIC_RELIGION_MOD warning and an out-of-range %s2 argument in
four non-English translations. F426 concerns the older primary mission-effect
line and reuse of a civic-specific text key for a ReligionTypes effect. Fixing
one does not repair the other.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Prefer a dedicated force-religion help key, e.g.
TXT_KEY_ESPIONAGE_HELP_SWITCH_RELIGION, and call it from the
getSwitchReligionCostFactor branch. Its translations should explicitly describe
a religion conversion rather than a civic/government-form switch.

A smaller alternative is to make the existing shared key semantically neutral
in every language and rename the placeholder concept, but the two runtime
branches already have separate mission/result localization families, so a
separate help key is clearer and less translation-fragile.

POST-F426 CONTROLS / CONTINUATION
--------------------------------
Before F426, the persistent-cache inventory was reconciled again:

* F405/F406 remain the two live underspecified debug caches already numbered.
* setPlotListHelp's static vectors are scratch storage and are explicitly
  cleared/rebuilt for the relevant call shapes.
* static define/info caches elsewhere in CvGameTextMgr are immutable settings or
  immutable XML identities for the lifetime of a loaded ruleset.
* getTechDataForAS's static localized help string is fixed-content UI text and no
  supported in-game language/ruleset mutation path was established.

The obvious happiness analogue of F420 was also explicitly disproved. Runtime
CvCity::happyLevel/unhappyLevel and TextMgr setHappyHelp/setAngerHelp both combine

    city.getExtraHappiness() + player.getExtraHappiness()

before sign splitting. The health mismatch does not have a parallel happiness
root.

F427 / provisional KI#750 — SABOTAGE-IMPROVEMENT ESPIONAGE HELP OMITS THE ROUTE
TARGET THAT THE SAME MISSION ACCEPTS AND DESTROYS ON A ROUTE-ONLY PLOT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
File family: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp + CvPlayer.cpp
Primary function: CvGameTextMgr::setEspionageCostHelp
Classification: stock-BtS espionage help/runtime branch omission retained by
K-Mod, Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS; ordinary current gameplay.

ROOT
----
The runtime contract of a mission with isDestroyImprovement() is explicitly
"improvement OR route".

Current CvPlayer::getEspionageMissionBaseCost permits the mission on any non-city
plot where either component exists:

    if (pPlot->isImproved() || pPlot->isRoute())
        iMissionCost = ...;

Current CvPlayer::doEspionageMission mirrors that exactly:

    if (pPlot->isImproved())
    {
        ... destroy/pillage improvement ...
    }
    else if (pPlot->isRoute())
    {
        ... report the route description ...
        pPlot->setRouteType(NO_ROUTE);
    }

But CvGameTextMgr::setEspionageCostHelp only implements the first half:

    if (kMission.isDestroyImprovement() && pPlot != NULL && pPlot->isImproved())
    {
        append TXT_KEY_ESPIONAGE_HELP_DESTROY_IMPROVEMENT(improvementName);
    }

There is no else-if route branch. Consequently the exact state in which runtime
will destroy a route because no improvement exists receives no target-effect
line in the detailed cost help.

CURRENT SAS REACHABILITY
------------------------
Current XML retains:

    ESPIONAGEMISSION_DESTROY_IMPROVEMENT
        iCost = 75
        bIsTwoPhases = 0
        bTargetsCity = 0
        bSelectPlot = 1
        TechPrereq = NONE
        bDestroyImprovement = 1

Current route XML retains ordinary ROUTE_ROAD and ROUTE_RAILROAD.

For a Spy on a legal foreign non-city tile that has a road/railroad but no
improvement, getEspionageMissionBaseCost returns a valid positive cost because
isRoute() is true. The first espionage popup therefore includes the ordinary
one-phase mission button and assigns WIDGET_HELP_ESPIONAGE_COST to it. Hovering
that button calls setEspionageCostHelp with the Spy's current plot.

Because pPlot->isImproved() is false, the specific sabotage line is skipped.
The rest of the help (base cost and modifiers) can still appear, but it never
names the Road/Railroad that execution is about to remove. Selecting the mission
then enters doEspionageMission's route branch and deletes that route.

This is therefore not an unsupported XML combination or a theoretical
CvRouteInfo capability. A route-only target is exactly one of the two plot states
accepted by the mission's normal runtime cost gate.

ANCESTRY
--------
The Civ4CE BtS reference already has the mismatch:

* getEspionageMissionBaseCost accepts
  `getImprovementType() != NO_IMPROVEMENT || getRouteType() != NO_ROUTE`;
* doEspionageMission destroys the improvement first and otherwise the route;
* setEspionageCostHelp only emits the specific line when
  `getImprovementType() != NO_IMPROVEMENT`.

K-Mod retains all three parts. Base AdvCiv modernizes the predicates to
isImproved()/isRoute() but retains the missing help sibling. Current SAS retains
that implementation. F427 is therefore inherited from stock BtS.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Mirror the runtime target selection in help. For example:

    if (kMission.isDestroyImprovement() && pPlot != NULL)
    {
        if (pPlot->isImproved())
            append sabotage-help with ImprovementInfo text key;
        else if (pPlot->isRoute())
            append sabotage-help with RouteInfo text key;
    }

The existing TXT_KEY_ESPIONAGE_HELP_DESTROY_IMPROVEMENT wording is "Sabotage
%s1..." in English and can accept a route description; a dedicated route key
would also be reasonable if any translation needs a different noun contract.

RELATION TO F426/F424
---------------------
F427 is a target-branch omission for the Sabotage mission. It is unrelated to
F426's force-religion/civic text-key reuse and F424's AdvCiv warning-placeholder
index bug. Each requires a different repair.

POST-F427 ESPIONAGE CLOSURE
---------------------------
The remaining active espionage cost-modifier arithmetic is guarded by exact
internal assertions against `getEspionageMissionCostModifier` and the final
mission cost. The remaining review therefore concentrated on effect-description
branches, where F426/F427 had both lived.

Destroy Production at zero accumulated production:
* `getEspionageMissionBaseCost` can technically return a zero base/final cost
  when the target city has zero current production, and `canDoEspionageMission`
  is permissive enough that the mission predicate itself can still succeed.
* The human first-phase espionage popup only creates one-phase mission buttons
  when `iCost > 0`, so the zero-cost/no-effect case is not exposed as a normal
  human action.
* `CvPlayerAI::AI_espionageVal` adds value for this mission only when the target
  city's production is greater than zero, so the normal AI selection path does
  not choose the zero-production no-op either.
Classification: harmless/current-caller structural looseness, not F428.

Insert Culture fractional precision:
* Runtime computes culture insertion in hundredths and can therefore apply a
  fractional remainder below one culture.
* Both TextMgr's displayed whole-culture amount and the mission base-cost
  calculation apply the same `/100` truncation, so the displayed integer and
  charged cost remain mutually consistent.
* Execution can still place a sub-1-culture remainder on plots, but that is UI
  precision rather than a contradictory gameplay contract.
Classification: low-value precision control, not F428.

Investigate City / counterespionage / return-to-capital:
* Current speed scaling leaves the active counterespionage duration positive.
* The help's return/no-return wording mirrors the actual post-mission relocation
  logic, including the existence of a capital.
* Passive missions do not use the active espionage-cost popup widget.
No further live root found.

Conclusion: the active `setEspionageCostHelp` subsystem is provisionally
saturated after F426 and F427. F428 remains unused.

WHOLE-FILE STATEFUL CONTROLS
----------------------------
`getWarWearinessString`:
* Reconciled target-specific and total values against the player/team war-
  weariness calculations.
* The helper intentionally reports natural/pre-city-modifier war-weariness
  units. Ordinary per-opponent integer decomposition can round independently,
  but no hard total/effect contradiction was established.
Classification: closed control.

`buildProcessInfoString`:
* `CvPlayer::canMaintain` is the same simple team-tech prerequisite described by
  the help path.
Classification: closed control.

`buildFoundCorporationString` / old tech-founded corporations:
* The apparently surprising "first to discover incorporates" behavior is real
  runtime behavior for corporations with a TechPrereq: `CvTeam::setHasTech`
  contains the first-discovery auto-founding path.
* Current SAS sets every corporation `TechPrereq=NONE`, so that old path/help is
  dormant rather than false.
Classification: dormant historical capability, not F428.

Population-unhealth modifier <= -100 wording:
* K-Mod's own caveat remains structurally valid if a -100 source could be offset
  by a positive population-unhealth modifier while help claims absolute
  immunity.
* Current SAS has National Park at -100 and Public Transportation at -20, with
  no positive civic/building population-unhealth modifier able to offset the
  -100 case.
Classification: current-data masked inherited hazard, not F428.

`setTerrainHelp` city-founding exception separator:
The code appends `TXT_KEY_OR` immediately after a coastal founding exception,
before testing whether a fresh-water exception actually exists. A terrain with:

    bFound = 0
    bFoundCoast = 1
    bFoundFreshWater = 0

would therefore end its founding help with a dangling "or".

Current SAS terrain XML activates no such exception: terrains with bFound=0
have both bFoundCoast=0 and bFoundFreshWater=0. Thus this is a genuine latent
branch-grammar defect but current-data dormant.
Classification: control, not F428.

Improvement/bonus connector multiplicity:
* The plot-help logic has comments/structure that are easiest to reason about
  when a bonus has a single connecting improvement.
* Current Oil is the notable multi-connector bonus (Well + Offshore Platform),
  but their land/water validity makes the alternatives mutually exclusive on a
  particular plot.
Classification: current-data safe.

BUILDING REQUIREMENT RECONCILIATION
-----------------------------------
`buildBuildingRequiresString` does not explicitly diagnose every predicate in
`CvCity::canConstruct`, notably `PrereqReligion`, `PrereqCorporation`,
`bPrereqReligion`, competing-corporation headquarters and government-center
exclusivity.

Current-data/caller proof prevents promotion:
* Current SAS has 28 live `PrereqReligion` buildings (the seven religion sets of
  temple/cathedral/monastery/shrine, including Paganism).
* However, the specific-religion rejection in `CvCity::canConstruct` occurs
  before its `bTestVisible` early return. `CvMainInterface.py` adds a production
  button only when `city.canConstruct(..., bTestVisible=true)` succeeds.
  Therefore a religious building whose religion is absent is hidden, not shown
  as a disabled production button that relies on this helper to explain why.
* Current `PrereqCorporation` and `bPrereqReligion` building fields are unused.
* Palace/Forbidden Palace use the live GovernmentCenter flag, but the
  already-government-center city rejection is likewise before bTestVisible and
  therefore filtered from the normal build palette.
* Current NumCitiesPrereq, UnitLevelPrereq, NumTeamsPrereq and VictoryPrereq are
  unused in building XML; the helper/runtime arithmetic for the generic fields
  was nevertheless checked.

The omission may still matter for generic Civilopedia/API completeness or
unusual mission/scenario data, but ordinary current production-button
reachability is not established. Do not promote as F428 without a stronger
caller/data state.

WORLD-SIZE PREREQUISITE RANGE CONTROL
-------------------------------------
The Civilopedia building-class prerequisite range uses the raw prerequisite as
its low end and the largest current world-size modifier for its high end.
Current SAS world-size BuildingClassPrereqModifier values are monotonic across
its extended sizes, so the resulting displayed range is valid. The analogous
conscription world-size modifier sequence is also monotonic.
Classification: closed control.

PURPOSE OF THIS CHECKPOINT
--------------------------
Continue from C031-WIP129 / F428 unused through the aggregate-vs-component
recomputation pass. This tranche broadens the already-confirmed F400 Finance
rounding root with two sibling live manifestations instead of manufacturing new
numbers from the same arithmetic contract, then establishes one genuinely
independent inherited free-specialist help omission as F428.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F400 / provisional KI#723 BROADENED — THE FINANCE INFLATION BREAKDOWN FAMILY
CAN ROUND COMPONENTS INDEPENDENTLY FROM ITS AGGREGATE TOTAL
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ORIGINAL ROOT RETAINED
----------------------
F400 was originally established in `buildFinanceCityMaintString`: named
maintenance components plus the residual number-of-cities component are made to
sum to a round-to-nearest inflated aggregate, while the line's displayed total
uses truncating integer division just like the engine. At 50% inflation an exact
current construction yields Number of Cities = 17 gold and Total = 16 gold.

The new whole-Finance aggregate pass shows that the same K-Mod inflation-help
integration pattern has two additional ordinary live manifestations. Keep these
under F400 rather than assigning new roots: in each case inflation is applied
and rounded separately to displayed components while the total is obtained by
applying inflation once to the already-summed pre-inflation runtime value.
Because rounding does not distribute over addition, the listed parts need not
sum to the listed total.

A. UNIT COST
------------
`buildFinanceUnitCostString` obtains the pre-inflation runtime decomposition:

    iCost = iUnitCost + iMilitaryCost + iExtraCost (+ residual handicap, if any)

and then independently does:

    iCost         = round(iCost * inflationFactor / 100)
    iUnitCost     = round(iUnitCost * inflationFactor / 100)
    iMilitaryCost = round(iMilitaryCost * inflationFactor / 100)

For an ordinary human current-SAS state the residual handicap component is zero,
and current Unit XML has `iExtraCost=0`, so ordinary unit and military support
alone are sufficient to expose non-additivity.

Exact current-data construction:

    game speed   = Normal
    world size   = Standard
    handicap     = Noble
    total pop    = 10
    civic        = Pacifism
    total units  = 13
    military     = 4
    inflation    = 50%

Current inherited/base support plus Noble gives:

    total-unit free allowance
      = Noble FreeUnits 6
      + INITIAL_BASE_FREE_UNITS 4
      + floor(10 * 24%)
      = 12

    military free allowance
      = INITIAL_BASE_FREE_MILITARY_UNITS 2
      + floor(10 * 12%)
      = 3

Normal/Standard/Noble gives a 100% ordinary unit-cost multiplier. Thus:

    paid ordinary units = 13 - 12 = 1
    iUnitCost            = 1 gold

Current Pacifism has `iGoldPerMilitaryUnit=100`, i.e. +1 gold per paid military
unit under the K-Mod percentage representation:

    paid military units = 4 - 3 = 1
    iMilitaryCost        = 1 gold

At 50% inflation the helper therefore displays:

    ordinary unit component = round(1 * 1.5) = 2
    military component      = round(1 * 1.5) = 2
    total                   = round(2 * 1.5) = 3

So one ordinary Finance hover can list 4 gold of components and then state a
3-gold total.

B. CIVIC UPKEEP
---------------
`buildFinanceCivicUpkeepString` applies the same pattern:

    each row = round(getSingleCivicUpkeep(civic) * inflationFactor / 100)
    total    = round(getCivicUpkeep() * inflationFactor / 100)

`getCivicUpkeep()` is exactly the sum of the five `getSingleCivicUpkeep` values
before inflation. Therefore the separately rounded rows are not guaranteed to
sum to the rounded total.

A small fully current construction on Noble at 50% inflation is one city with
population 15 using:

    Government: Police State       (HIGH upkeep)
    Legal:      Free Speech        (LOW upkeep)
    Labor:      Slavery            (LOW upkeep)
    Economy:    State Property     (LOW upkeep)
    Religion:   Organized Religion (HIGH upkeep)

With the inherited current upkeep offsets (-8 population, -1 city), the five
pre-inflation single-civic values are exactly:

    [1, 0, 0, 0, 1] gold

The helper displays the two nonzero rows as 2 gold each at 50% inflation, while
its rounded aggregate is only 3 gold:

    sum of displayed rows = 4
    displayed total       = 3

ANCESTRY / ROOT NORMALIZATION
-----------------------------
K-Mod already contains all three Finance inflation patterns: it introduced
ROUND_DIVIDE inflation treatment separately in Unit Cost, City Maintenance and
Civic Upkeep. Base AdvCiv retains them, replacing ROUND_DIVIDE with its corrected
`intdiv::round` and improving city-maintenance intermediate precision without
changing the aggregate/component contract. Current SAS retains the behavior.

These are not three independent gameplay rules. They are sibling manifestations
of the same Finance-breakdown presentation architecture: separately rounding
inflated parts while presenting an independently rounded/truncated aggregate.
Keep one F400 / KI#723 root and broaden its repair surface.

REPAIR DIRECTION (BROADENED)
----------------------------
Choose one additive display contract for every Finance breakdown.

For exact internal consistency, compute the authoritative displayed total using
the same rule as runtime, then either:

* derive one residual displayed component after the other components have been
  rounded; or
* preserve enough fractional precision for all components and perform a
  deterministic largest-remainder/allocation step so displayed integer parts
  sum exactly to the runtime total.

Do not independently round every component and also independently round the
aggregate unless the UI explicitly labels the components as approximate.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F428 / provisional KI#751 — COLLAPSED FREE-SPECIALIST HELP TOTALS YIELD,
COMMERCE AND XP BY COUNT BUT OMITS THE SPECIALISTS' GREAT-PERSON POINTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
File family: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp + CvDLLWidgetData.cpp +
Assets/Python/Screens/CvMainInterface.py + current specialist/building XML
Primary function: CvGameTextMgr::parseFreeSpecialistHelp
Classification: stock-BtS city-help omission retained by K-Mod, Base AdvCiv 1.14
and current SAS; ordinary current SAS can reach the collapsed UI from buildings
alone.

ROOT
----
`parseFreeSpecialistHelp` is the aggregate helper used when the city UI needs to
summarize its specific free specialists. For every SpecialistTypes entry with a
positive `getFreeSpecialistCount`, it prints a row headed by the specialist name
and count, then multiplies that count into:

* specialist yields;
* specialist commerce;
* specialist free unit experience.

It never displays or multiplies:

    CvSpecialistInfo::getGreatPeopleRateChange()

Yet ordinary `CvCity::processSpecialist` applies that exact field to both the
specialist-specific Great Person unit rate and the city's base Great Person rate
for every added free specialist. The omitted effect is gameplay state, not
pedia flavor.

The contrast with `parseSpecialistHelp` is direct. The ordinary one-specialist
helper explicitly prints `TXT_KEY_SPECIALIST_BIRTH_RATE` whenever
`getGreatPeopleRateChange()!=0`; the aggregate free-specialist helper simply
stops after yield/commerce/experience.

WHY THE CURRENT UI MAKES THIS A REAL TOTALING ERROR
---------------------------------------------------
Current `CvMainInterface.py` uses `MAX_CITIZEN_BUTTONS = 8`.

At eight or fewer specific free specialists, it can draw one icon per free
specialist and passes `WIDGET_FREE_CITIZEN(..., data2=-1)`. Hovering that icon
uses the ordinary one-specialist help, which does contain the specialist's GPP.

Above eight, `updateFreeSpecialistButtons` switches representation: it draws one
button per specialist TYPE with `data2=1`, regardless of how many free
specialists of that type are present. `CvDLLWidgetData::parseFreeCitizenHelp`
then appends `parseFreeSpecialistHelp` after the ordinary specialist header.
The aggregate rows are therefore the UI's mechanism for explaining the hidden
multiplicity. Yields, commerce and XP are multiplied by the displayed count;
GPP are not.

CURRENT-SAS BUILDING-ONLY REACHABILITY
--------------------------------------
Current XML can exceed the collapse threshold in one city without events,
debugging or unsupported data. The following currently non-obsolete buildings
can coexist and together supply ten *specific* free specialists:

    Custom House        +1 Merchant
    Industrial Park     +2 Engineers
    Laboratory          +1 Scientist
    Natya Shastra       +1 Artist
    Oxford University   +2 Scientists
    Statue of Liberty   +1 Merchant
    Cristo Redentor     +1 Priest
    Versailles          +1 Spy
                        ----------------
                        10 free specialists

All six ordinary specialist types involved currently have
`iGreatPeopleRateChange=3`:
Priest, Artist, Scientist, Merchant, Engineer and Spy.

Those ten free specialists therefore contribute exactly:

    10 * 3 = 30 base GPP/turn

through `CvCity::processSpecialist`.

For example, once collapsed, an Engineer button represents two free Engineers.
The ordinary header describes a single Engineer and can show +3 GPP. The
aggregate row says `Engineer (2)` and correctly doubles its yields, but omits the
corresponding +6 base GPP entirely. Across the ten-specialist construction the
aggregate section omits all 30 base GPP while totaling the other effects.

ANCESTRY
--------
Civ4CE stock BtS already contains `parseFreeSpecialistHelp` with the same
omission: it totals yield, commerce and specialist experience but never calls
`getGreatPeopleRateChange`.

K-Mod retains that structure (while fixing a neighboring separator typo).
Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains it, and current SAS retains it. Current SAS's richer
specific-free-specialist building data makes the >8 collapsed state especially
straightforward to reach, but the root is inherited stock BtS.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Include the count-scaled GPP contribution in each aggregate specialist row,
parallel to yield/commerce/XP, e.g. using the existing GREAT_PEOPLE_CHAR or an
appropriate short birth-rate text:

    iNumSpecialists * GC.getInfo(eSpecialist).getGreatPeopleRateChange()

This should describe the specialist contribution at the same base-effect level
as the ordinary `parseSpecialistHelp`; city-wide Great Person modifiers belong
in the separate Great People rate breakdown and need not be duplicated here.

===============================================================================
C031-WIP131 APPEND - F429 CONFIRMED / CORPORATION FORCE-PREVIEW RECONCILIATION
===============================================================================

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F429 / provisional KI#752 - FORCE-CORPORATION HELP COUNTS A COMPETING
CORPORATION'S PRODUCED RESOURCE EVEN THOUGH A SUCCESSFUL SPREAD REMOVES THAT
CORPORATION BEFORE THE NEW CORPORATION'S EFFECTS ARE CALCULATED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
File family: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp + CvCity.cpp + CvUnit.cpp +
current Corporation XML
Primary function: CvGameTextMgr::setCorporationHelpCity
Classification: inherited stock-BtS hypothetical-preview algorithm made
normally wrong by K-Mod's corporation-resource rework; retained by Base AdvCiv
1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

ROOT
----
The corporation spread mission asks:

    setCorporationHelpCity(..., bCityScreen=false, bForceCorporation=true)

for the prospective effects of successfully adding the corporation to the
mission city.

The helper first counts every CURRENT prerequisite resource through:

    iNumResources += pCity->getNumBonuses(kCorporation.getPrereqBonus(i));

and then uses that fixed current-state count for the incoming corporation's
prospective yields, commerce and maintenance.

However a successful corporation spread does not simply add the new corporation
on top of the current city state. `CvCity::setHasCorporation(..., true, ...)`
first removes every CURRENT corporation that competes with the incoming one.
Those recursive removals immediately call `updateCorporation()`, whose
`updateCorporationBonus()` rebuilds corporation-produced resources. Thus the
resource set on which the new corporation actually operates can differ from the
resource set that `setCorporationHelpCity` counted before the replacement.

CURRENT-SAS CONCRETE FAILURE - ALUMINUM CO -> MINING INC
--------------------------------------------------------
Current corporation data gives a direct ordinary case.

Aluminum Co (`CORPORATION_6`):

    prerequisite resources: Coal
    produced resource:       Aluminum

Mining Inc (`CORPORATION_5`):

    prerequisite resources: Coal, Iron, Copper, Uranium, Aluminum
    production output:       100 hundredths per prerequisite resource

The corporations compete because both consume Coal.

Take a normal non-HQ city with:

    one connected Coal;
    no natural/imported Aluminum;
    Aluminum Co active;
    the tech state needed for corporation-produced Aluminum to be usable;
    no civic/policy disabling either corporation.

`updateCorporationBonus` gives the active Aluminum Co one corporation-produced
Aluminum from that Coal. Therefore immediately before the Mining Inc spread:

    getNumBonuses(Coal)      = 1
    getNumBonuses(Aluminum)  = 1   // supplied by Aluminum Co

`setCorporationHelpCity(... Mining Inc ..., bForceCorporation=true)` therefore
counts two Mining Inc resources.

On current Standard world size, CorporationMaintenancePercent=100 and Mining
Inc produces 100 production-hundredths per qualifying resource, so the
prospective mission help reports:

    +2 production

and calculates Mining Inc maintenance from two qualifying resources.

But on a SUCCESSFUL spread, `CvCity::setHasCorporation(Mining Inc, true, ...)`
first sees Aluminum Co as competing and removes it. That removal immediately
runs `updateCorporationBonus`; Aluminum Co no longer exists in the city, so its
corporation-produced Aluminum disappears. Mining Inc is then installed and its
own corporation update sees only:

    Coal = 1
    Aluminum = 0

The actual incoming Mining Inc contribution is therefore only:

    +1 production

and its actual corporation maintenance is correspondingly based on one resource,
not the two counted by the pre-spread help.

This is not merely failure to itemize the LOSING corporation's effects. The
numeric effects attributed to the INCOMING corporation itself are calculated
from a resource that the incoming corporation's own successful replacement
removes before runtime evaluates those effects.

NORMAL CALLER / LEGALITY
------------------------
`CvDLLWidgetData`'s spread-corporation mission help calls
`setCorporationHelpCity(..., false, true)` for the mission city.

`CvUnit::canSpreadCorporation` permits the state above:
- the incoming corporation is active for both players;
- the city does not already have it;
- the city is not disordered;
- the corporation has at least one prerequisite bonus (Coal suffices);
- the target is not the headquarters of a competing corporation;
- ordinary territory/gold conditions hold.

The mission can fail probabilistically, but the force-help is explicitly the
prospective successful-spread effect. Whenever the supported state succeeds, the
reported two-resource Mining Inc result and the actual one-resource result
diverge deterministically.

ANCESTRY / ACTIVATION
---------------------
Stock BtS/Civ4CE already implements the force-corporation helper by counting the
city's CURRENT prerequisite bonuses before any replacement simulation. It also
already removes competing corporations during successful spread.

Stock corporation data, however, masks this particular resource-dependency
failure: stock Mining Inc consumes Coal/Iron/Copper/Gold/Silver and therefore
does not consume the Aluminum produced by Aluminum Co.

K-Mod changes Mining Inc's Gold/Silver prerequisites to Uranium/Aluminum (the
XML comment in Base AdvCiv explicitly records: `K-Mod: Gold, Silver replaced
with Uranium, Aluminum`) while Aluminum Co continues to consume Coal and produce
Aluminum. K-Mod retains the inherited force-preview algorithm unchanged, making
the previously latent replacement-state mismatch normally reachable.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains both K-Mod's corporation inputs and the inherited
preview algorithm. Current SAS retains them too.

RELATION TO EXISTING CORPORATION FINDINGS
-----------------------------------------
This is independent of:

* F411/KI#734: ordinary corporation city hover ignores disorder/no-maintenance
  state. F429 occurs in a normal non-disordered prospective spread and concerns
  replacement-state simulation.
* F421/KI#744: cached corporation maintenance embeds stale inverse inflation.
  F429 is wrong immediately even with a freshly updated cache because the
  preview uses a resource that successful execution removes.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
For `bForceCorporation`, derive the incoming corporation's effects from the
POST-SUCCESS hypothetical corporation/resource state rather than the current
city resource count.

A robust repair should account for the full corporation-produced-resource
fixpoint after every competing corporation that `setHasCorporation` would remove
has been removed. Merely subtracting one hardcoded Aluminum source is too narrow;
corporation-produced resources can form dependency chains and future data can
create additional replacement interactions.

Possible conservative approaches:
- factor a side-effect-free helper that computes corporation-produced resources
  for a hypothetical corporation membership set and use it for preview;
- or suppress exact force-preview yield/commerce/maintenance numbers when a
  competing-corporation removal changes any prerequisite resource, while still
  showing the existing `will eliminate corporation` warning.

Do not mutate the real city merely to obtain help text.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F430 / provisional KI#753 - ROUTE-ONLY BUILD ACTION HELP OMITS THE YIELD CHANGE
THAT THE NEW ROUTE CAUSES THROUGH AN EXISTING IMPROVEMENT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
Root file: CvGameCoreDLL/CvDLLWidgetData.cpp
Cross-files: CvPlot.cpp + current Build/Improvement XML
Audit accounting: Queue-012 closure correction discovered while Queue 003 traced
CvGameTextMgr improvement/build-help contracts. Queue 012 does not require a
full re-audit; amend its closure with this missed inherited root.
Classification: inherited stock-BtS action-help defect retained by K-Mod,
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

ROOT
----
`CvDLLWidgetData::parseActionHelp_Mission`, MISSION_BUILD, previews build yield
changes by looping yields and calculating a prospective improvement delta only
inside:

    if (eImprovement != NO_IMPROVEMENT)
    {
        iYield += kMissionPlot.calculateImprovementYieldChange(eImprovement, ...);
        if (kMissionPlot.isImproved())
            iYield -= kMissionPlot.calculateImprovementYieldChange(
                    kMissionPlot.getImprovementType(), ...);
    }

The build's route is read separately into `eRoute`, but it is used only by the
later route-prerequisite diagnostics. It never participates in the yield-delta
preview.

That is incomplete because an existing improvement can itself have
`RouteYieldChanges`. A route-only build can therefore change plot yield even
when it does not replace the improvement.

CURRENT-SAS CONCRETE FAILURE - RAILROAD ON MINE / LUMBERMILL
-------------------------------------------------------------
Current `BUILD_RAILROAD` is an ordinary route-only Worker build:

    PrereqTech       = TECH_STEAM_POWER
    ImprovementType  = NONE
    RouteType        = ROUTE_RAILROAD

Current Mine and Lumbermill each contain:

    RouteType ROUTE_RAILROAD
    production yield change +1

`CvPlot::calculateImprovementYieldChange` explicitly obtains the plot's
current/revealed route and adds:

    kImpr.getRouteYieldChanges(eRoute, eYield)

Thus, once a Railroad exists on a Mine or Lumbermill, that improvement's actual
production contribution is one hammer larger than before.

Normal execution confirms the state transition. `CvUnit::build` completes
through `CvPlot::changeBuildProgress`; when a build has a route, completion calls:

    setRouteType(kBuild.getRoute())

so a successful `BUILD_RAILROAD` immediately changes the plot to Railroad and
therefore activates the Mine/Lumbermill +1 production RouteYieldChange.

But for the same Railroad action hover:

    eImprovement == NO_IMPROVEMENT

so the action-help yield loop never calls `calculateImprovementYieldChange` at
all. With no feature-removal yield in the example, `iYield` remains zero and no
`, +1 production` effect is appended.

A Worker can therefore hover a fully legal Railroad build over an existing Mine
or Lumbermill, receive no yield-change preview, complete the build and gain +1
production on the tile.

This is not merely a missing direct RouteInfo yield. The live current effect is
stored on the EXISTING IMPROVEMENT's `RouteYieldChanges`, and the normal plot
yield path applies it through `calculateImprovementYieldChange`.

ANCESTRY
--------
Stock BtS/Civ4CE already contains the same MISSION_BUILD preview structure:
prospective yield calculation is conditional on the build having an
ImprovementType, while the route is not incorporated into the yield delta.

Stock BtS XML also already gives Mine and Lumbermill +1 production with
Railroad. Thus the defect is live in stock BtS data, not merely activated by a
later K-Mod/AdvCiv/SAS data change.

K-Mod retains both the action-help structure and the Railroad
RouteYieldChanges. Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains both. Current SAS retains both while
moving Railroad construction to Steam Power; that tech-tree change affects when
the ordinary state is reached, not the root itself.

RELATION TO PRIOR QUEUE-012 COVERAGE
------------------------------------
Queue 012 previously checked several MISSION_BUILD contracts, including:
- feature-tech sentinel handling;
- MAX_INT/zero-work ETA reachability;
- worker-count ETA double-counting;
- build-button data domains.

The reconciled album contains no prior MISSION_BUILD route-dependent yield
preview root. Searches for Railroad/RouteYieldChanges/action-hover equivalents
also found no existing Known Issue owning this defect. F430 therefore amends the
Queue-012 closure rather than duplicating a prior root.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
For MISSION_BUILD, calculate the yield delta from the full hypothetical
post-build plot state, not only from a prospective replacement improvement.

At minimum, when `eRoute != NO_ROUTE` and the plot already has an improvement,
include the change in that improvement's `RouteYieldChanges` between the current
route and `eRoute`. A general repair should also include direct RouteInfo yield
changes so future/current data do not require another special case.

Prefer one side-effect-free prospective-yield helper or a small calculation that
mirrors `CvPlot::calculateYield` under hypothetical improvement/route/feature
state, rather than independently reconstructing only whichever XML fields happen
to be nonzero today.

Do not mutate the real plot for help text.

C031-WIP133 APPEND - F431 CONFIRMED / ADVANCED-START PEACE COUNTDOWN
===============================================================================

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F431 / provisional KI#754 - ADVANCED-START TURN-TIMER STILL ANNOUNCES ZERO
TURNS OF FORCED PEACE AFTER ADVCIV HAS ALREADY EXPIRED THE SETUP PEACE DEALS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
Root file: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp
Cross-files: CvGame.cpp + CvDeal.cpp
Classification: stock-BtS countdown condition made wrong by AdvCiv advc.004's
faster peace-deal expiry; retained by Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

ROOT
----
`CvGameTextMgr::getTurnTimerText` displays the Advanced Start universal-peace
countdown while:

    kGame.getElapsedGameTurns() <= PEACE_TREATY_LENGTH

and formats:

    PEACE_TREATY_LENGTH - getElapsedGameTurns()

Ordinary Advanced Start creates reciprocal `TRADE_PEACE_TREATY` deals between
eligible major players during game initialization. A peace treaty becomes
cancelable when:

    initialGameTurn + PEACE_TREATY_LENGTH - currentGameTurn <= 0

Current AdvCiv/SAS then deliberately calls `verifyDeals()` immediately AFTER:

    incrementGameTurn();
    incrementElapsedGameTurns();

with the explicit comment:

    Already done in doDeals, but that's before incrementing the turn counter.
    Want to kill peace treaties asap.

`CvDeal::verify` kills a peace deal once it is cancelable. Therefore, when the
new elapsed-turn count first equals `PEACE_TREATY_LENGTH`, those setup peace
treaties have already reached zero remaining turns and have already been killed
before the new turn begins.

CURRENT-SAS CONCRETE TIMELINE
-----------------------------
With the normal 10-turn peace-treaty length and an initial setup deal created at
game turn 0:

    elapsed/game turn 9:  turnsToCancel = 1; treaty still enforces peace.

At the round boundary:

    incrementGameTurn()        -> 10
    incrementElapsedGameTurns()-> 10
    verifyDeals()              -> treaty is cancelable (10 + 0 - 10 == 0)
                                  and is killed immediately.

The new turn therefore begins with the Advanced-Start peace treaty gone.

But `getTurnTimerText` still evaluates:

    10 <= 10   // true

and prints `TXT_KEY_MISC_ADVANCED_START_PEACE_REMAINING` with value 0.

Thus the first turn on which the setup treaty no longer protects the players is
still labelled as having `0 turns` of Advanced Start peace remaining. Because
this branch precedes the normal victory/max-turn countdown branches, it can also
suppress a real competing countdown for that turn.

REACHABILITY
------------
This is the ordinary non-SPAH Advanced Start setup path, not a scenario-only or
hidden-option state:
- `CvGame::initDiplomacy` creates the reciprocal peace-treaty deals whenever
  GAMEOPTION_ADVANCED_START is active and GAMEOPTION_SPAH is not;
- `getTurnTimerText` is the normal interface turn/countdown text path;
- current SAS retains PEACE_TREATY_LENGTH and the inherited countdown display.

The `GAMEOPTION_ALWAYS_WAR` guard is unrelated to the demonstrated ordinary
Advanced Start state.

ANCESTRY
--------
Stock BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod already use the `<= PEACE_TREATY_LENGTH` countdown.
They also create the initial Advanced Start peace treaties.

However stock BtS/K-Mod do NOT perform the second post-increment `verifyDeals`
call. Their deal verification occurs before the turn counter increments, so a
peace treaty reaching zero can remain present through the newly incremented turn
until the next verification boundary. The inherited zero-count display therefore
matched that older delayed-expiry lifecycle much more closely.

AdvCiv practical 1363 (`advc.004`) added:

    incrementGameTurn();
    incrementElapsedGameTurns();
    verifyDeals();

specifically to "kill peace treaties asap." The inherited TextMgr `<=` condition
was not changed. Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains both the faster expiry and the old
countdown predicate; current SAS retains both.

This is therefore best classified as an AdvCiv integration regression between a
runtime lifecycle fix and unchanged stock UI timing, not as a pure stock-BtS
TextMgr typo.

DUPLICATE CHECK
---------------
The reconciled album and current Known-Issue documentation contain no existing
Advanced Start peace-countdown/off-by-one root. Existing Advanced Start findings
in Queue 003 concern zero-cost visibility (F417) and unrelated setup/UI
contracts. F431 is independent.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
For the current lifecycle, the minimal repair is to display the elapsed-based
setup countdown only while:

    getElapsedGameTurns() < PEACE_TREATY_LENGTH

so the branch disappears as soon as post-increment `verifyDeals` expires the
setup treaties.

A stronger future-proof implementation would derive the message from the actual
surviving Advanced-Start peace-deal / force-peace state and its real remaining
turns rather than duplicating lifetime arithmetic from elapsed game turns. That
would remain correct if start-turn/deal initialization semantics change again.

Queue 012 closure remains amended by F430.

POST-WIP133 CONTROL - GREAT-PERSON BASE-RATE SOURCE RECONCILIATION
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The unfinished Great Person breakdown check from WIP133 closes cleanly.

Current `CvCity::m_iBaseGreatPeopleRate` gameplay writers were traced through the

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F432 / provisional KI#755 - RELIGION-SPECIFIC CITY HELP OMITS THE CURRENT
NON-STATE-RELIGION HAPPINESS EFFECT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
Root file: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp
Cross-files/data: CvCity.cpp, CvPlayer.cpp, CvDLLWidgetData.cpp,
Assets/Python/Screens/CvMainInterface.py, CvPolicyAdvisorScreen.py,
CIV4CivicInfos.xml.
Classification: inherited stock-BtS religion-help omission, normally live in
stock BtS and current AdvCiv-SAS through Free Religion.

RUNTIME CONTRACT
----------------
`CvCity::getReligionHappiness(ReligionTypes eReligion)` applies a happiness
contribution for every religion actually present in the city:

    if (eReligion == owner.getStateReligion())
        iHappiness += owner.getStateReligionHappiness();
    else
        iHappiness += owner.getNonStateReligionHappiness();

`CvCity::updateReligionHappiness` loops every religion and accumulates those
values into the city's religion-good / religion-bad happiness state.

The player-side civic processing is live state, not merely descriptive XML:
`CvPlayer::processCivics` feeds `iNonStateReligionHappiness` through
`changeNonStateReligionHappiness`, which immediately calls
`updateReligionHappiness()` across the player's cities.

CURRENT DATA / ORDINARY REACHABILITY
------------------------------------
Current SAS `CIVIC_FREE_RELIGION` has:

    <bStateReligion>0</bStateReligion>
    <iStateReligionHappiness>0</iStateReligionHappiness>
    <iNonStateReligionHappiness>1</iNonStateReligionHappiness>

Therefore, while using Free Religion, every religion present in a city is a
non-state religion and contributes +1 happiness through the executable runtime
contract above.

Concrete ordinary state:

    city has Hinduism + Buddhism
    owner runs Free Religion

Runtime religion happiness is therefore:

    Hinduism  +1
    Buddhism  +1
    total     +2 happiness

The ordinary city happiness breakdown does correctly expose the aggregate
`getReligionGoodHappiness()` total through `TXT_KEY_HAPPY_RELIGIOUS_FREEDOM`, so
this finding should NOT claim that the two happiness points vanish from every
UI surface. The defect is more precise: the religion-specific city/help path
fails to attribute or preview the per-religion effect it is meant to describe.

BROKEN HELP CONTRACT
--------------------
Current `CvGameTextMgr::setReligionHelpCity` first derives the effective state
religion, then handles religion commerce. Its happiness/effect block is entered
only when:

    if (eStateReligion == eReligion)

Inside that block it prints:

    pCity->getStateReligionHappiness(eReligion)
        + owner.getStateReligionHappiness()

along with the state-religion production / XP / Great-Person modifiers.

There is no sibling branch for:

    owner.getNonStateReligionHappiness()

when the requested religion is present but is not the effective state religion.
Under Free Religion `eStateReligion == NO_RELIGION`, so the happiness block is
skipped for every religion icon even though every one of those religions is
actively contributing +1 happiness to the city.

LIVE CALLERS
------------
This is not a dormant TextMgr API.

1. Main city screen:
   Current `CvMainInterface.py` attaches `WIDGET_HELP_RELIGION_CITY` to every
   displayed city religion icon (and its Holy City overlay). The DLL widget
   parser calls:

       GAMETEXT.setReligionHelpCity(...,
           gDLL->UI().getHeadSelectedCity(), true)

   Thus hovering Hinduism or Buddhism in the concrete Free Religion city above
   reaches the incomplete helper directly and omits that religion's +1 happy.

2. Current Policy Advisor Religion tab:
   `CvPolicyAdvisorScreen.py` calls
   `CyGameTextMgr().getReligionHelpCity(...)` for the per-city religion help.
   The same missing non-state branch therefore affects that integrated current
   SAS screen as well.

The current Main Interface still contains the older commented Python-side
religion tooltip reconstruction using `pHeadSelectedCity.getReligionHappiness`
for each religion. That is supporting evidence for the per-religion semantic
contract, though the live DLL/runtime comparison above is sufficient by itself.

ANCESTRY
--------
Stock BtS/Civ4CE already has the mismatch:

- stock `CvCity::getReligionHappiness` applies
  `getNonStateReligionHappiness()` to present non-state religions;
- stock `setReligionHelpCity` only prints happiness inside its state-religion /
  forced-state block and has no non-state happiness counterpart;
- stock `CIVIC_FREE_RELIGION` already uses
  `<iNonStateReligionHappiness>1</iNonStateReligionHappiness>`.

So the omission was normally reachable in stock BtS itself. K-Mod retains the
same missing branch, Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains it through the advc.172 religion-
help refactor, and current SAS retains it.

This is therefore an inherited stock-BtS help omission rather than a SAS data
activation or AdvCiv integration regression.

DUPLICATE CHECK
---------------
The reconciled album contains no existing non-state-religion-happiness city-help
root.

F418/KI#741 also uses Free Religion as a current proof state, but it is a
different contract: `setConvertHelp` fails to explain why conversion is blocked
when current civics permit no state religion (and when the target religion is
absent from the player's cities). F432 concerns an actually applied city
happiness effect that `setReligionHelpCity` omits from the religion-specific
help. Keep the roots separate.

F429's neighboring forced-religion commerce-max control is likewise independent:
that control concerns max religion-commerce semantics during prospective spread;
F432 is the ordinary present-city happiness branch and needs no forced preview.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
After the existing effective `eStateReligion` calculation, mirror the runtime
happiness split:

- when `eReligion == eStateReligion`, retain the current state-religion
  happiness path, including city-specific state-religion building happiness;
- when the religion is present (or is being force-previewed as present) and is
  not the effective state religion, append
  `GET_PLAYER(owner).getNonStateReligionHappiness()` with the same correct
  happy/unhappy sign formatting.

Use the already-adjusted effective `eStateReligion` so advc.172's `bForceState`
preview semantics continue to work in both directions. Do not apply
`pCity->getStateReligionHappiness(eReligion)` to the non-state branch; runtime's
non-state religion happiness comes from the player-wide non-state value.

For `bForceReligion`, the same branch can also show the prospective non-state
happiness of spreading a religion while a no-state-religion civic is active.
That is a natural consequence of mirroring the runtime predicate rather than a
separate finding.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTROL — IMPROVEMENT CIVILOPEDIA PLACEMENT HELP IS SELECTIVE, BUT THE FARM
IRRIGATION OMISSION IS NOT PROMOTED AS F433
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlot::canHaveImprovement` enforces more placement semantics than
`CvGameTextMgr::setImprovementHelp(..., bCivilopediaText=true)` explicitly
lists. Current Farm is a concrete example:

    bRequiresIrrigation = 1
    bFreshWaterMakesValid = 1
    bRequiresFlatlands = 1
    PrereqNatureYields food = 1

The DLL Pedia helper lists the flatland restriction and "carries irrigation"
but has no direct `isRequiresIrrigation()` requirement line. Current custom
SevoPedia's Requires panel lists the Build's technology prerequisite and its
Most Yields panel links the irrigated-yield effect to the Irrigation concept;
it does not add a separate irrigation-placement requirement row.

However the actual rule is deliberately layered rather than an unconditional
"Farm requires irrigation" statement:
* fresh water itself satisfies `isIrrigationAvailable()`;
* a bonus for which Farm has BonusMakesValid returns true before the later
  irrigation gate;
* current `TECH_WATER_WHEEL` sets both `bIrrigation=1` and
  `bIgnoreIrrigation=1`, after which the team ignores that placement gate;
* the current custom Irrigation/Fresh Water concept text separately explains
  the Farm/irrigation relationship.

The action-help path on an actually blocked build also explicitly checks
`isRequiresIrrigation() && !isIrrigationAvailable()` and points to the
irrigation-enabling technology.

Classification: selective/static Pedia completeness and future UI-improvement
opportunity, not a crisp current runtime/help contradiction strong enough for
F433. A repair would need to express the exceptions/bypass coherently rather
than append an unconditional requirement sentence.

The same family contains other selectively represented placement fields such
as `RequiresFeature`, PrereqNatureYields and the various *MakesValid flags.
Their existence reinforces that `setImprovementHelp` is not currently a full
serialization of `canHaveImprovement`; no individual live contradiction was
promoted from that static-reference scope in this tranche.

CONTROL — AIR-BOMB / PARADROP TARGET HELP RECONCILES WITH CURRENT EXECUTION
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`getAirBombPlotHelp` was compared to `CvUnit::canAirBombAt`,
`getDestructibleStructureAt` and `CvUnit::airBomb` after F430's separate
Railroad build-action discovery.

* the helper asks the same mission executor for a target-eligible aircraft;
* city-defense damage uses the same `airBombDefenseDamage` calculation;
* route-vs-improvement priority uses the same `getDestructibleStructureAt`
  contract as execution;
* AirBombDefense < 0 structures are filtered by the same target resolver;
* the displayed success probability is mathematically the exact probability
  of runtime's two synchronized uniform dice rolls
  `SyncRandNum(attack) >= SyncRandNum(defense)`;
* paradrop interception help likewise delegates through the target-eligible
  mission-unit path.

No independent F433 survived this action-target reconciliation.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
MECHANICAL COVERAGE — CIVIC AND TRAIT RUNTIME FIELDS ARE REPRESENTED IN THEIR
STATIC HELPERS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A field-level comparison was made between `CvPlayer::processCivics` and
`CvGameTextMgr::parseCivicInfo`.

After accounting for array accessors (`getYieldModifierArray`,
`getCommerceModifierArray`, etc.) and explicit loops, every current CivicInfo
field that processCivics applies has a corresponding parseCivicInfo help branch:
health/happiness, maintenance, unit support, military support, state/non-state
religion effects, production/experience, yield/commerce arrays, building and
feature happiness/health, hurry/specialist/special-building permissions,
improvement yields and the remaining scalar effects.

The analogous `CvPlayer::processTraits` -> `CvGameTextMgr::parseTraits` field
comparison also has no runtime TraitInfo getter absent from the help helper.

This does not prove every wording/arithmetic branch correct (several numbered
findings already show integration mistakes despite field presence), but it
closes the broad "an entire current civic/trait runtime field is simply missing
from static help" hypothesis after F432.

C031-WIP136 — QUEUE 003 CONTINUATION — F433 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

STATUS
------
Queue 003 `CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp` remains OPEN.
Unique files complete: 32/169.
F433 / provisional KI#756 is CONFIRMED.
F434 / provisional KI#757 is UNUSED.
No repository source files were modified.

PURPOSE OF THIS CHECKPOINT
--------------------------
Preserve the post-WIP135 resource-layer cache investigation before continuing.
The candidate is a cross-file TextMgr/cache contract: the stale string is built
by `CvGameTextMgr::setBonusHelp` / `setBonusExtraHelp`, cached by
`CvPlayer::getResourceLayerColors`, and incorrectly invalidated from
`CvCity::processBuilding` when another civilization completes a World Wonder.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F433 / provisional KI#756 — WORLD-WONDER COMPLETION DIRTIES THE FOREIGN
BUILDER'S BONUS-HELP CACHE INSTEAD OF THE ACTIVE PLAYER'S CACHE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: NEW CURRENT INHERITED ADVCIV UI CACHE-INVALIDATION DEFECT ROOT;
ordinary current-data proof strong.

ROOT CONTRACT
-------------
AdvCiv caches the complete resource-indicator help string for each BonusType in
`CvPlayer::m_aszBonusHelp`. `CvPlayer::getResourceLayerColors` behaves as:

    if (m_aszBonusHelp[eLoopBonus] != NULL)
        szBuffer.append(*m_aszBonusHelp[eLoopBonus]);
    else
    {
        GAMETEXT.setBonusHelp(szTempBuffer, eLoopBonus, false);
        m_aszBonusHelp[eLoopBonus] = new CvWString(...);
    }

The cached string is stateful. `setBonusExtraHelp` decides whether to list
resource-related buildings and Wonders from current game/player state,
including global/player/team max-instance status through `CvGame::canConstruct`
and the class-max predicates.

For that reason `CvCity::processBuilding` contains an explicit resource-layer
invalidation block. Its comments state that it is updating the text generated
by `CvGameTextMgr::setBonusExtraHelp`.

The block correctly computes which player's cached help must be invalidated:

    PlayerTypes eDirtyPlayer = NO_PLAYER;
    if (kBuilding.isNationalWonder() && isActiveOwned())
        eDirtyPlayer = getOwner();
    else if (kBuilding.isWorldWonder())
        eDirtyPlayer = kGame.getActivePlayer();

For a World Wonder completed by another civilization, the active human's
resource help must be rebuilt because that Wonder can have disappeared from the
active human's future construction/resource-production options.

But after calculating `eDirtyPlayer`, current code executes:

    GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).setBonusHelpDirty();

instead of:

    GET_PLAYER(eDirtyPlayer).setBonusHelpDirty();

Thus the explicit target calculation is discarded. If a foreign player built
the Wonder, the code clears the foreign builder's cache and leaves the active
human's cache unchanged.

CURRENT-SAS CONCRETE PROOF — STONE / PYRAMIDS
---------------------------------------------
Current `BUILDING_PYRAMID` is a normal one-instance World Wonder and has:

    BuildingClass = BUILDINGCLASS_PYRAMID
    PrereqTech = TECH_MINING
    BonusProductionModifier:
        BONUS_STONE -> +25%

Take an ordinary Ancient-era active human who can see/use Stone and for whom
Pyramids has not yet been globally constructed. While the Globe resource layer
is open, hovering/creating the Stone resource indicator causes
`getResourceLayerColors` to call `setBonusHelp` and cache the resulting Stone
help in the human's `m_aszBonusHelp[BONUS_STONE]`.

`setBonusExtraHelp` sees Pyramids as still constructible. Pyramids is current-
era rather than a remote future Wonder, so the cached Stone string legitimately
contains its construction effect:

    +25% production for Pyramids

Now another civilization completes Pyramids while the human remains on the
resource layer.

`CvCity::processBuilding` reaches the World-Wonder invalidation branch:

    eDirtyPlayer = kGame.getActivePlayer();

and dirties `GlobeLayer_DIRTY_BIT`, so the layer is redrawn. However it then
calls `setBonusHelpDirty()` on `getOwner()`, i.e. the foreign Wonder builder.
The active human's cached Stone text survives.

On redraw `getResourceLayerColors` sees the human's non-NULL cached Stone string
and reuses it without calling `setBonusHelp` again. The resource indicator can
therefore continue advertising the now-impossible Pyramids +25% construction
bonus.

A freshly generated string differs deterministically. After Pyramids is
completed, `CvGame::canConstruct(BUILDING_PYRAMID, true, true)` fails because
`isBuildingClassMaxedOut(BUILDINGCLASS_PYRAMID)` is true. In
`setBonusExtraHelp`, `bCanEverConstruct` becomes false; because the active human
owns zero Pyramids, the building is skipped before its production-bonus line.
The stale cached and fresh authoritative texts therefore disagree.

INVALIDATION-LIFECYCLE CHECK
----------------------------
All current `setBonusHelpDirty()` call sites were enumerated. No independent
World-Wonder-completion path repairs the active human cache:

* `CvPlayer::updateActiveVisibility` / active-player changes invalidate the new
  active player's cache, but no active-player switch occurs in the concrete
  case above.
* active-owned religion changes can invalidate the active owner's cache because
  religion prerequisites affect `setBonusExtraHelp`; unrelated to Wonder
  completion.
* `CvCity::processBuilding` is the explicit building/Wonder invalidation path
  and contains the wrong-target call described here.
* ordinary `CvPlayer::changeBuildingClassCount` only changes the class counter;
  it does not invalidate `m_aszBonusHelp`.

Therefore the dirty Globe redraw does not rescue the string: it can redraw
using exactly the stale cache entry that should have been deleted.

SCOPE / OTHER BUILDINGS
-----------------------
Pyramids is only a compact current example. Current SAS has many World Wonders
with resource production modifiers (Stone/Marble/Copper/etc.). Completion of
any such foreign Wonder can make a previously listed active-player resource
construction perk disappear while this wrong-owner invalidation leaves the
corresponding resource help cached.

The National-Wonder branch is not the same failure when the active player owns
the city: `isActiveOwned()` implies `getOwner() == eDirtyPlayer`, so the wrong
expression happens to select the intended player there. The defect is exposed
specifically by the World-Wonder branch's deliberate cross-player target.

ANCESTRY
--------
Civ4CE/stock BtS and K-Mod do not contain AdvCiv's `m_aszBonusHelp` resource-
layer help cache / `setBonusHelpDirty` invalidation architecture.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same cache and the exact same code sequence:

    else if (kBuilding.isWorldWonder())
        eDirtyPlayer = kGame.getActivePlayer();
    ...
    GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).setBonusHelpDirty();

The code is annotated by AdvCiv's `advc.004w` resource-help work, with the cache
itself marked `advc.003p`. Current SAS retains the wrong-target call unchanged.

Classification: inherited AdvCiv resource-layer cache-invalidation defect,
retained by SAS; not a stock-BtS/K-Mod defect.

DUPLICATE CHECK
---------------
The reconciled album contains no prior root for `m_aszBonusHelp`,
`setBonusHelpDirty`, the `eDirtyPlayer` variable, or stale World-Wonder resource
help. Existing resource-layer/bonus findings concern different contracts.

This is also not F429: F429 is a corporation-spread prospective calculation
that uses pre-removal corporation-produced resources. F433 is a persistent UI
cache invalidation bug after a real World Wonder state change.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Use the target that the block already computed:

    GET_PLAYER(eDirtyPlayer).setBonusHelpDirty();

inside the `eDirtyPlayer != NO_PLAYER` branch.

That is the minimal local repair and matches the surrounding intent exactly.
The existing `GlobeLayer_DIRTY_BIT` redraw can remain; once the correct cache is
cleared, redraw will regenerate the active player's affected resource strings.

A broader robustness option would centralize resource-help-cache invalidation
inside state mutations that change `setBonusExtraHelp` eligibility rather than
requiring individual callers to remember both redraw and cache deletion, but
that is not necessary to fix this root.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
POST-F433 CONTROL — STATE-RELIGION BUILDING HAPPINESS / CURRENT DATA
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The unfinished neighboring state-religion building-happiness check from WIP134
was completed before F433. Current BuildingInfo XML has no nonzero
`iStateReligionHappiness`, so it does not activate a second F432-like omission.
No additional root is assigned.

PURPOSE OF THIS CHECKPOINT
--------------------------
Continue the resource-layer cache audit begun by F433. F433 is a wrong-target
bug inside an existing World-Wonder invalidation hook. F434 is a separate cache
contract: the complete resource help string contains several ordinary volatile
player/team values for which AdvCiv added no invalidation hook at all.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F434 / provisional KI#757 — RESOURCE-LAYER BONUS-HELP CACHE IS NOT INVALIDATED
WHEN ORDINARY RESOURCE / CORPORATION / TECHNOLOGY STATE CHANGES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: NEW CURRENT INHERITED ADVCIV UI CACHE-LIFETIME DEFECT ROOT; multiple
ordinary current gameplay proofs.

CACHE CONTRACT
--------------
`CvPlayer::getResourceLayerColors` caches the complete non-Civilopedia
`CvGameTextMgr::setBonusHelp` result per BonusType in `m_aszBonusHelp`.

That string is not static. In current code it directly contains or conditionally
selects text from live state including:

1. `CvPlayer::getNumAvailableBonuses(eBonus)` — current capital-network
   availability count;
2. active-player corporation ownership — corporation glyphs are appended when
   a corporation currently present in the player's empire consumes the bonus;
3. active-team bonus obsolescence — obsolete resources print `(Obsolete)` and
   suppress the ordinary perk block;
4. current era / team tech / constructibility state used by
   `setBonusExtraHelp` to decide which buildings, projects and units to list.

Yet all current `setBonusHelpDirty()` callers are limited to:

* active-player/civilization visibility changes;
* the special building/Wonder resource-layer hook (whose World-Wonder branch is
  independently wrong-targeted by F433);
* a first active-owned religion acquisition while the resource layer is open.

There is no cache invalidation in the ordinary mutation paths below.

CURRENT PROOF A — AVAILABLE RESOURCE COUNT CAN REMAIN STALE
-----------------------------------------------------------
`setBonusTradeHelp` always appends the active player's available count in the
resource-layer context (`pCity == NULL`), using:

    pActivePlayer->getNumAvailableBonuses(eBonus)

`getNumAvailableBonuses` reads the capital plot group's live bonus count.
Ordinary connection/trade changes update that count through
`CvPlotGroup::changeNumBonuses` / `CvPlot::updatePlotGroupBonus` and
`CvPlayer::changeBonusImport` / `changeBonusExport`.

None of those paths calls `setBonusHelpDirty()`.

Concrete current state:

1. Active human has one Iron in the capital network and opens the resource
   Globe layer. Iron help is generated and cached with `1 available`.
2. The human connects a second Iron or begins importing another Iron.
3. The capital plot group now reports 2 Iron, so a fresh `setBonusHelp` call
   would print `2 available`.
4. `m_aszBonusHelp[BONUS_IRON]` is still non-NULL. Reusing or reopening the
   resource layer therefore continues to use the cached `1 available` string
   until some unrelated cache-clear event happens.

This does not depend on a one-frame redraw race; the stale string is persistent
heap state and can survive later layer rebuilds because the cache entry itself
was never deleted.

CURRENT PROOF B — CORPORATION-USE GLYPHS CAN REMAIN STALE
---------------------------------------------------------
The cached string loops all corporations and appends a corporation's glyph when
both:

    pActivePlayer->getHasCorporationCount(eCorporation) > 0

and the hovered bonus is one of that corporation's prerequisite resources.

`CvCity::setHasCorporation` changes the owning player's corporation count and
updates corporation effects, but it does not call `setBonusHelpDirty()`.

Therefore a player can cache a resource string before acquiring their first
copy of a corporation, then have that corporation spread normally and continue
to see the old string without the newly relevant corporation glyph. Removal of
the last copy has the symmetric stale-glyph possibility.

CURRENT PROOF C — TECHNOLOGY / BONUS OBSOLESCENCE CAN REMAIN STALE
-----------------------------------------------------------------
`CvTeam::setHasTech` explicitly dirties `GlobeLayer_DIRTY_BIT` for the active
team, but does not clear the active player's `m_aszBonusHelp` cache.

Current SAS provides a very direct state transition:

    BONUS_FUR       iHappiness = +1
                    TechObsolete = TECH_ENVIRONMENTALISM
    BONUS_ELEPHANTS iHappiness = +1
                    TechObsolete = TECH_ENVIRONMENTALISM
    BONUS_WHALE     iHappiness = +1
                    TechObsolete = TECH_ENVIRONMENTALISM

Take an active human with cached Fur help immediately before completing
Environmentalism. The pre-tech string can show Fur's ordinary +1 happiness,
available count and eligible perk lines.

After the tech is acquired, runtime `isBonusObsolete(BONUS_FUR)` becomes true.
A fresh `setBonusHelp` would append `TXT_KEY_BONUS_OBSOLETE` and skip the normal
bonus-perk block. The tech-acquisition path redraws the Globe layer but leaves
the cached pre-tech string intact, so the redraw can display the stale
non-obsolete help.

The same missing tech invalidation can stale the era/tech-sensitive
building/project/unit shortlist inside `setBonusExtraHelp` even when no bonus
itself becomes obsolete.

WHY THIS IS NOT F433
--------------------
Both roots involve `m_aszBonusHelp`, but the implementation defects and repairs
are independent:

* F433: `CvCity::processBuilding` already knows a World Wonder changed the
  active player's cached help and computes `eDirtyPlayer = activePlayer`, but
  accidentally clears `getOwner()` instead. This is a wrong-target variable in
  an existing hook.
* F434: routine bonus-network, corporation and technology mutations have no
  cache-clear hook at all. Fixing F433's single expression does not repair any
  F434 state.

Keep separate roots unless a future repair deliberately replaces the whole
cache-invalidation architecture with one centralized dependency revision.

ANCESTRY
--------
Stock BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod recompute resource-layer bonus help and do not have
AdvCiv's `m_aszBonusHelp` / `setBonusHelpDirty` cache architecture.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 already contains:

* the `advc.003p` per-Bonus help cache;
* dynamic available-count / corporation / obsolescence content in the cached
  `setBonusHelp` string;
* the active-team tech path dirtying `GlobeLayer_DIRTY_BIT` without clearing
  the cache;
* no cache invalidation in the ordinary plot-group bonus-count,
  import/export, or corporation-count mutation paths.

Current SAS retains this cache lifetime unchanged. Classification: inherited
AdvCiv cache-dependency/invalidation defect, not stock BtS/K-Mod.

DUPLICATE CHECK
---------------
The reconciled album has no pre-F433/F434 root for `m_aszBonusHelp` lifetime or
stale resource-layer availability/corporation/tech text. F433 is deliberately
kept separate for the wrong-target World-Wonder hook as explained above.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The narrow repair is to invalidate the active player's bonus-help cache whenever
one of its semantic inputs changes, including at least:

* capital-network bonus counts / imports / exports;
* player corporation-presence transitions relevant to prerequisite resources;
* active-team technology changes that can obsolete bonuses or alter the
  building/project/unit shortlist;
* the already-existing building/Wonder transitions (with F433's target fix).

A safer architecture is preferable to proliferating hooks: cache either a
static-only portion of bonus help, or maintain a revision/generation counter for
resource-help semantic state and regenerate cached entries whenever the
revision changes. The current full-string cache is too dynamic for a handful of
ad hoc invalidation sites to be reliable.

PURPOSE OF THIS CHECKPOINT

Continue the low-mention stateful TextMgr pass after the F433/F434 resource-help
