the ordinary plot-resource hover: the prospective yield of the improvement that
would connect a resource is rebuilt from only two XML fields instead of using
the engine's authoritative improvement-yield calculation.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F435 / provisional KI#758 — RESOURCE HOVER'S PROSPECTIVE CONNECTING-IMPROVEMENT
YIELD OMITS LIVE TECH / CIVIC / IRRIGATION / ROUTE / TERRAIN-SIDE MODIFIERS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: NEW CURRENT INHERITED BTS UI/RUNTIME-YIELD CONTRACT DEFECT ROOT; ordinary
current SAS reproduction and full lineage proof.

ROOT
----
When `CvGameTextMgr::setPlotHelp` sees a visible, nonobsolete bonus that is not
currently connected by its required improvement, it finds the first legal
`isImprovementBonusTrade(eBonus)` improvement and previews the yield difference.

For the prospective NEW improvement, current SAS computes only:

    kImprovementInfo.getImprovementBonusYield(eBonus, eYield)
    + kImprovementInfo.getYieldChange(eYield)

If another improvement is already on the plot, AdvCiv subtracts that old
improvement through the authoritative:

    kPlot.calculateImprovementYieldChange(oldImprovement, ...)

The asymmetry is therefore explicit: the old side is evaluated with full live
plot/player/team state, while the proposed new side is only base improvement
XML + bonus-specific XML.

AUTHORITATIVE RUNTIME CONTRACT
------------------------------
`CvPlot::calculateImprovementYieldChange` is the engine path for the actual
improvement yield. In current SAS it includes, in addition to the two fields
used by the hover:

* RiverSideYieldChange;
* HillsYieldChange;
* IrrigatedYieldChange when irrigation is currently available;
* RouteYieldChanges for the plot's current/revealed route;
* player ImprovementYieldChange (including civic effects);
* team ImprovementYieldChange (including technology effects);
* the bonus-specific yield.

`CvTeam::processTech` feeds current technology improvement-yield changes into
that team accumulator through `changeImprovementYieldChange`.

CURRENT SAS DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION — MAIZE + BIOLOGY
--------------------------------------------------------
Current `IMPROVEMENT_FARM` data has:

    base YieldChanges:              +2 food
    BONUS_MAIZE YieldChanges:       +2 food
    TECH_BIOLOGY TechYieldChanges:  +1 food

Take an ordinary active-player Maize plot after Biology with no connecting
improvement (for example an unimproved or pillaged Farm resource tile) on which
a Farm is legal.

The resource hover's prospective Farm line computes:

    +2 base Farm food
    +2 Maize-specific Farm food
    = +4 food with Farm

But actually building the Farm causes plot yield to be evaluated through
`calculateImprovementYieldChange`. The active team already owns Biology, so the
Farm receives the additional +1 technology yield and its actual improvement
contribution is:

    +2 +2 +1 = +5 food

Thus the ordinary revealed-plot hover understates the result of the action it is
recommending by one food.

OTHER LIVE SHAPES OF THE SAME ROOT
----------------------------------
The missing set is broader than Biology alone. The same manual prospective
formula can omit currently active:

* Farm IrrigatedYieldChange;
* Mine/Lumbermill Railroad RouteYieldChanges;
* river-side or hill-specific improvement yields;
* civic/player improvement-yield modifiers;
* other technology/team improvement-yield modifiers.

These are manifestations of the same partial-reconstruction root and should not
receive separate finding numbers.

ORDINARY CALLER / VISIBILITY CONTRACT
-------------------------------------
This is not a dead Civilopedia helper. `CvGameTextMgr::getPlotHelp` calls
`setPlotHelp` for ordinary revealed mouse-over plots in both map and city-screen
contexts. The resource-improvement branch is therefore normal map help whenever
a visible nonobsolete bonus lacks its connecting improvement.

The reproduction does not require hidden information, unsupported XML, debug
mode, Python direct calls or a future/mod-mod configuration.

ANCESTRY
--------
Firaxis BtS/Civ4CE already computes the proposed improvement yield as exactly:

    getImprovementBonusYield(...) + getYieldChange(...)

K-Mod retains the same partial formula. Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains it as well;
`advc.047` improves the OLD-improvement subtraction by calling
`calculateImprovementYieldChange`, but leaves the proposed improvement side
partial. Current SAS inherits that asymmetry unchanged.

Classification: inherited stock-BtS help/runtime mismatch, not a SAS-local
regression.

DUPLICATE / RELATED-ROOT RECONCILIATION
---------------------------------------
F180 / KI#503 is related in coding smell but is NOT this root. F180 concerns the
SAS practical-5976 `SAS_getBonusImprovementFoodChange` helper used by the
first-city low-food evaluation; it independently omitted already-active
IrrigatedYieldChange from a gameplay AI score.

F435 is an older, separate `CvGameTextMgr::setPlotHelp` formula used by ordinary
player-facing resource hover and omits a broader set of live modifiers. Fixing
F180 does not affect F435 and vice versa.

F430 is also separate. F430 is `CvDLLWidgetData::parseActionHelp` failing to
preview an existing Mine/Lumbermill's Railroad `RouteYieldChanges` for the
route-only BUILD_RAILROAD action. F435 instead previews placing a resource-
connecting improvement and partially reconstructs that prospective
improvement's own yield. The code sites and repair surfaces are independent.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Do not manually rebuild the proposed improvement yield from base + bonus fields.
Use the same authoritative plot calculation already used for the old side, e.g.
conceptually:

    newYield = kPlot.calculateImprovementYieldChange(
        eLoopImprov, eLoopYield, eActivePlayer);
    oldYield = (no old improvement ? 0 :
        kPlot.calculateImprovementYieldChange(
            ePlotImprovement, eLoopYield, eActivePlayer));
    iYieldChange = newYield - oldYield;

That automatically follows current river/hill/irrigation/route/player/team/bonus
semantics and prevents later XML or civic/tech changes from creating new drift.
Preserve the surrounding revealed-owner/observer semantics already implemented
inside `calculateImprovementYieldChange` rather than duplicating them here.

POST-WIP137 CONTROL
-------------------
The earlier F434 cache audit remains separate. Project-max / capital-sensitive /
era-sensitive resource-help cache dependencies, where current, should broaden
F434's missing-invalidation family rather than be renumbered unless an
independent invalidation defect is proved.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F436 / provisional KI#759 — AVOID GROWTH HIDES THE CITY-BILLBOARD'S IMMINENT
STARVATION COUNTDOWN BECAUSE THE ONE-TURN SUPPRESSION USES abs(iTurns)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: NEW CURRENT INHERITED ADVCIV UI/LIFECYCLE CONTRACT DEFECT ROOT; ordinary
current-SAS reproduction and exact introducing-history proof.

ROOT
----
`CvCity::getFoodTurnsLeft()` has a signed contract in current AdvCiv/SAS:

    positive value  = turns to population growth
    negative value  = turns to starvation / population loss
    MAX_INT         = stagnant

For negative food difference it explicitly returns:

    return std::min(-1, -intdiv::uceil(getFood(), -iFoodDiff));

The city billboard deliberately displays the absolute number because the small
billboard suffix has no color/sign channel:

    int iTurns = pCity->getFoodTurnsLeft();
    if (abs(iTurns) > 1 || !pCity->AI().AI_isEmphasizeAvoidGrowth())
    {
        if (iTurns < MAX_INT)
            ... append abs(iTurns) ...
    }

The inherited Avoid Growth suppression therefore treats `+1` growth and `-1`
starvation as if Avoid Growth affected both. It does not.

AUTHORITATIVE RUNTIME CONTRACT
------------------------------
`CvCity::doGrowth()` applies Avoid Growth only after positive food has reached
the growth threshold:

    if (getFood() >= growthThreshold())
    {
        if (AI().AI_isEmphasizeAvoidGrowth())
            setFood(growthThreshold());
        else
            changePopulation(1);
    }
    else if (getFood() < 0)
    {
        ...
        if (getPopulation() > 1)
            changePopulation(-1);
    }

The starvation branch contains no Avoid Growth exemption. Thus Avoid Growth can
make a displayed `+1` growth estimate non-actionable, but it cannot prevent a
`-1` starvation estimate from becoming a real population loss.

CONCRETE CURRENT-SAS REPRODUCTION
---------------------------------
Take an ordinary selectable active-player city with population > 1, Avoid Growth
enabled, stored food = 1 and `foodDifference() = -2`.

`getFoodTurnsLeft()` computes:

    ceil(1 / 2) = 1
    => -1 turn to starvation

On the city turn, `doGrowth()` subtracts two food, reaches negative stored food,
and executes `changePopulation(-1)` despite Avoid Growth.

But the billboard test sees:

    abs(-1) > 1                         => false
    !AI_isEmphasizeAvoidGrowth()        => false

and therefore suppresses the `(1)` suffix entirely. The same city without Avoid
Growth shows the one-turn starvation countdown. Toggling an option that only
prevents positive growth thus hides an imminent negative-population event that
it does not prevent.

WHY THE POSITIVE +1 CASE IS DIFFERENT
-------------------------------------
The old one-turn suppression has a legitimate purpose for growth. When
`iTurns == +1` and Avoid Growth is active, the city can hit its growth threshold
this turn and then be clamped instead of gaining population. Showing `(1)` as a
growth countdown would therefore be misleading.

The defect is not the suppression itself; it is broadening that suppression to
`-1` through `abs(iTurns)` after starvation support was added.

ANCESTRY / BIRTH
----------------
Stock BtS/Civ4CE and the older AdvCiv code used the billboard suffix only for
positive food difference, so the Avoid Growth `iTurns > 1` suppression could not
hide starvation there.

AdvCiv practical 3000 / commit

    63477cec3fd52c882ef69b1e61e7c9213fa05df2
    "Show turns to starvation on city bar"

changed `CvCity::getFoodTurnsLeft()` to return negative starvation turns and
broadened `buildCityBillboardCityNameString` from growth-only to both signs. The
introducing diff changes:

    if (pCity->foodDifference() > 0)
        ... if (iTurns > 1 || !AvoidGrowth) ...

to:

    int iTurns = pCity->getFoodTurnsLeft();
    if (abs(iTurns) > 1 || !AvoidGrowth)
        ... append abs(iTurns) ...

That commit therefore introduces the regression directly: starvation became a
supported billboard state, but the growth-only Avoid Growth exception was made
sign-insensitive. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the same code.

DUPLICATE / CONTROL RECONCILIATION
----------------------------------
The reconciled Queue-003 album already contains F408's disorder-food hover bug
and later general billboard controls, but no prior root or control covers this
signed one-turn Avoid Growth suppression. F408 concerns reconstructing normal
food arithmetic while runtime freezes food in disorder; F436 concerns a normal
non-disorder city's imminent starvation countdown being hidden solely because
Avoid Growth is enabled. The code paths, states and repairs are independent.

The earlier broad billboard closure note after WIP111 is therefore refined, not
contradicted wholesale: production/GP/top-city billboard calculations remain
closed; this specific city-name food-turn sign branch had not been isolated.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Make the Avoid Growth exception sign-sensitive. Conceptually:

    if (iTurns < 0 || iTurns > 1 || !pCity->AI().AI_isEmphasizeAvoidGrowth())
        append abs(iTurns);

or equivalently suppress only the exact positive-growth case:

    if (!(iTurns == 1 && pCity->AI().AI_isEmphasizeAvoidGrowth()))
        ...

Preserve `abs(iTurns)` in the displayed suffix if the billboard cannot encode
negative/starvation color; the important fix is that `-1` must not be discarded
by a growth-only policy.

-------------------------

   Explicit active-player use in `setEspionageCostHelp`, `parseWarTradesHelp`,
   relation helpers and trade diagnostics corresponds to observer/actor state;
   no ordinary subject substitution mismatch survived caller review.

2. `setEventHelp` nested additional-event legality can still consult the actual
   global active player in one API shape, but current ordinary event widgets
   supply the active player and current quest/global/team data do not activate a
   distinct supported mismatch. Retain the earlier compatibility/API control.

3. `getTradeString` / disengagement and nuke-target helpers remain under the
   previously completed execution-contract controls; no new current root was

F437 / provisional KI#760 — FEATURE HELP DROPS ADVC.012'S CONDITIONAL RIVAL-DEFENSE FIELD, SO FOREST/JUNGLE PEDIA STATS DO NOT DESCRIBE THEIR ACTUAL DEFENSE RULE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: CONFIRMED — inherited AdvCiv UI/help integration omission; current SAS data and current Sevopedia caller make it ordinary-live.

ROOT
----
AdvCiv change advc.012 replaced BtS/K-Mod's single unconditional Forest/Jungle
feature-defense value with a two-part rule:

    ordinary feature defense       = CvFeatureInfo::getDefenseModifier()
    conditional rival defense      = CvFeatureInfo::getRivalDefenseModifier()

`CvPlot::defenseModifier` applies the second field when:

    eAttacker == NO_TEAM || getTeam() != eAttacker

For actual combat, the attacker team is supplied. Thus the intended player-facing
rule is the one stated by the AdvCiv manual: Forest and Jungle provide feature
defense except when the attacker owns the tile. The live plot-help implementation
also has explicit advc.012 code that computes and labels this conditional component.

Current SAS feature data makes the split concrete:

    FEATURE_FOREST:
        iDefense       =   0
        iRivalDefense  = +25

    FEATURE_JUNGLE:
        iDefense       = -25
        iRivalDefense  = +25

The SAS Jungle rework deliberately retains the inherited +25 rival-defense field
while changing the ordinary component to -25.

STATIC FEATURE-HELP OMISSION
----------------------------
`CvGameTextMgr::setFeatureHelp` still contains only the old single-field display:

    if (kFeature.getDefenseModifier() != 0)
        ... TXT_KEY_TERRAIN_DEFENSE_MODIFIER ...

There is no call to `getRivalDefenseModifier()` anywhere in setFeatureHelp and no
second static line describing the ownership-dependent feature defense.

This matters to current SAS's actual feature page. `SevoPediaFeature::placeSpecial`
constructs the Special Abilities text with:

    info.getHelp() + CyGameTextMgr().getFeatureHelp(self.iFeature, True)

so the omission is directly inherited by the custom Sevopedia Feature screen.
`WIDGET_PEDIA_JUMP_TO_FEATURE` hover help also routes through
`CvDLLWidgetData::parseFeatureHelp -> CvGameTextMgr::setFeatureHelp`.

CONCRETE CURRENT CONSEQUENCES
-----------------------------
1. Forest

   The Feature page sees `iDefense == 0`, so setFeatureHelp emits no defense line.
   A reader inspecting Forest itself therefore sees no feature-defense stat even
   though normal combat on a Forest tile receives +25% from iRivalDefense whenever
   the attacker does not own that tile.

2. Jungle

   Current SAS sets ordinary iDefense to -25 while retaining +25 iRivalDefense.
   setFeatureHelp therefore prints the -25% defense modifier but omits the +25%
   conditional component. In the common case where the attacker does not own the
   Jungle tile, the two feature components net to 0; the static feature page shows
   only the -25 half of that rule.

The live map plot help is better: advc.012 explicitly compares defense with and
without the ownership-conditioned component and emits TXT_KEY_FEATURE_RIVALDEF.
The omission is therefore specifically the static feature/widget contract, not a
claim that every combat hover is wrong.

DOCUMENTATION CONTROL
---------------------
AdvCiv's manual states the rule directly:

    Forest and Jungle provide only 25% defense, and none if the tile is owned by
    the attacker. 012

Current SAS also preserves this information in its Mods Info / K-Mod-to-AdvCiv
summary, and AdvCiv modified its combat concept/hints for the same rule. Those
separate documents reduce discoverability impact but do not make the feature's own
stat/helper correct. The Sevopedia Feature page is the canonical per-feature stat
surface and explicitly delegates Special Abilities to setFeatureHelp.

ANCESTRY
--------
Stock BtS/Civ4CE uses one unconditional `iDefense = 50` for both Forest and Jungle.
Its setFeatureHelp displays that one field, so there is no missing second defense
component in the stock data model.

K-Mod retains the same single-field 50% feature-defense data and corresponding
single-field help model.

AdvCiv change advc.012 changes Forest/Jungle ordinary iDefense from 50 to 0, adds
`iRivalDefense = 25`, extends CvFeatureInfo/XML, changes CvPlot::defenseModifier,
AI plot-defense consumers, live plot help, hints/manual/concept wording, etc. But
`setFeatureHelp` remains structurally the old single-field implementation. Base
AdvCiv 1.14 therefore already contains the omission; current SAS inherits it and
makes the Jungle presentation especially misleading through its -25 ordinary
component.

DUPLICATE RECONCILIATION
------------------------
No prior F/KI root or preserved Queue-003 control in the reconciled album covers
`getRivalDefenseModifier` being absent from setFeatureHelp. Existing promotion
feature-defense help concerns unit promotion modifiers, not the plot feature's
advc.012 ownership-conditioned base defense. Existing KI#21 concerns live-unit
Cannot Enter state, not feature-defense documentation.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Extend `setFeatureHelp` to represent `getRivalDefenseModifier()` explicitly rather
than folding it blindly into ordinary defense. The condition matters; a safe static
line should communicate the advc.012 rule (e.g. +25% defense except when attacked by
the tile owner / no feature defense against the tile owner), with localized wording.

Do not simply add iDefense + iRivalDefense into one unconditional number: that would
make Forest/Jungle look like permanent +25/0 and lose the ownership-dependent rule.
Reuse or adapt the existing advc.012 localization where semantically appropriate,
but note that `TXT_KEY_FEATURE_RIVALDEF` was designed for contextual plot help
("for tile owner") rather than a context-free Feature page.

POST-WIP140 CONTROLS BEFORE F437
--------------------------------
- parsePromotionHelp effect-field and acquisition-prerequisite reconciliation was
  completed. Every current runtime promotion effect has corresponding help; no
  promotion-help F437 sibling was established.
- Great-General progress help uses the same stored combat XP and
  `greatPeopleThreshold(true)` runtime threshold; no drift found.
- The low-mention live-helper classification found no new deal/trade or sentinel
  root before the feature-field comparison reached setFeatureHelp.

F438 / provisional KI#761 — FINANCE ADVISOR SPECIALIST-GOLD ROW USES BASE-ONLY
CITY SPECIALIST COMMERCE WHILE ITS OWN BULL HOVER AND RUNTIME INCLUDE PLAYER-
WIDE SPECIALIST-EXTRA GOLD
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
The current SAS Finance screen (`Assets/Python/Screens/CvDomesticAdvisor.py`)
computes the visible Specialists income row by summing, for every non-disorder
city:

    fCitySpecialists = city.getSpecialistCommerce(COMMERCE_GOLD)
    fSpecialists += fCitySpecialists

`CvCity::getSpecialistCommerce` is the city's stored specialist-info commerce.
`CvCity::processSpecialist` updates that store only from:

    CvSpecialistInfo::getCommerceChange

It does not contain the player-wide `getSpecialistExtraCommerce` contribution.

The exact widget attached to that same row is `WIDGET_HELP_FINANCE_SPECIALISTS`.
Its C++ path reaches `CvGameTextMgr::buildFinanceSpecialistGoldString`, which
counts assigned + free specialists in every non-disorder city and computes each
specialist's Gold through:

    kPlayer.specialistCommerce(eSpecialist, COMMERCE_GOLD)

`CvPlayer::specialistCommerce` is explicitly:

    SpecialistInfo base commerce + getSpecialistExtraCommerce(eCommerce)

Therefore the displayed row and its own tooltip use different definitions of
"specialist Gold".

RUNTIME CONTROL
---------------
The actual city commerce formula agrees with the tooltip, not with the Python
row. `CvCity::getBaseCommerceRateTimes100` adds:

    (getSpecialistPopulation() + getNumGreatPeople()) *
        owner.getSpecialistExtraCommerce(eCommerce)

separately from `getSpecialistCommerce(eCommerce)`.

The ordinary city commerce hover (`CvGameTextMgr::setCommerceHelp`) already uses
this same complete formula for its Specialists line:

    city.getSpecialistCommerce(eCommerce) +
    (city.getSpecialistPopulation() + city.getNumGreatPeople()) *
        owner.getSpecialistExtraCommerce(eCommerce)

This is an especially strong internal control: the authoritative runtime and an
existing TextMgr breakdown both include the component which the Finance row
omits.

CURRENT-DATA REACHABILITY
-------------------------
This latent split is live in current SAS because current data supplies
specialist-extra GOLD.

Current `CIV4CivicInfos.xml`:

    CIVIC_REPRESENTATION  SpecialistExtraCommerces = [1, 1, 1, 0]
    CIVIC_FREE_MARKET     SpecialistExtraCommerces = [1, 0, 0, 0]

Both feed `CvPlayer::changeSpecialistExtraCommerce` through `processCivics`.
The two civics belong to different civic-option categories and can therefore
stack, but either one is independently sufficient.

Current Specialist XML gives the simple controls:

    Scientist intrinsic Gold = 0
    Merchant  intrinsic Gold = 3

Ordinary one-Merchant reproduction under Representation:

    Finance visible Specialists row = 3
        because city.getSpecialistCommerce(GOLD) sees only intrinsic 3

    Hover on that exact row          = 4
        because player.specialistCommerce(Merchant, GOLD) sees 3 + 1

    Runtime base specialist Gold     = 4
        because CvCity adds the player-wide +1 per specialist

A more severe one-Scientist shape is possible. The Scientist has zero intrinsic
Gold, so the Finance loop leaves `fSpecialists == 0` and suppresses the
Specialists row entirely. Under Representation the same Scientist nevertheless
contributes +1 Gold to real city commerce. With Representation + Free Market,
it contributes +2 while the row still remains absent if no intrinsic-Gold
specialist is present.

FINANCE BREAKDOWN CONSEQUENCE
-----------------------------
The omission is broader than only the row label/hover number.

The Finance screen also computes each Gold-multiplier building's contribution
from:

    fCityTotel = fCityTaxes + fCityBuildings + fCityHeadquarters +
        fCityCorporations + fCitySpecialists

Because `fCitySpecialists` is base-only, any Gold multiplier contribution caused
by specialist-extra Gold is omitted from those multiplier rows too. The final
Income line is still based on the authoritative `player.getCommerceRate(GOLD)`,
so the total contains the missing specialist-extra output while the detailed
component rows fail to reconstruct it.

Replacing the base-only specialist quantity with the complete runtime quantity
would repair both the Specialist row and the multiplier base in the same place.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod's `Assets/Python/Screens/EconomicsAdvisor.py` already contains the
base-only row calculation:

    fCitySpecialists = city.getSpecialistCommerce(COMMERCE_GOLD)

and attaches a BUG/BULL specialist-help widget through `BugDll.widget`.
However the supplied K-Mod DLL source does not itself contain
`buildFinanceSpecialistGoldString` or the corresponding BULL widget enum/parser.

AdvCiv practical commit 1481,
4a65bf5c0fb187fd25d4908346abb462354a9172,
"Option for expanding scoreboard; BULL hover text", imports/enables the BULL
Finance hover subsystem in the DLL. The introducing diff adds
`CvGameTextMgr::buildFinanceSpecialistGoldString` using
`kPlayer.specialistCommerce(...)` and converts the existing Finance Specialist
row from optional `BugDll.widget(...)` plumbing to the concrete
`WIDGET_HELP_FINANCE_SPECIALISTS` enum. It does not change the inherited
base-only Python row calculation.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains that split, but its shipped data masks the GOLD case:
its nonzero specialist-extra-commerce sources are Research/Culture only
(Representation [0,3,0], Scientific Method [0,1,0], Sistine Chapel [0,0,2]).
The supplied K-Mod and stock BtS/Civ4CE data likewise have no nonzero first
(Gold) SpecialistExtraCommerce entry.

Current SAS data removes that masking condition. Representation is already
shown with +Gold specialist commerce in SAS history by practical commit 5109
(the commit removes only its former fourth/espionage +1, leaving [1,1,1,0]),
and current Free Market supplies another +1 Gold per specialist.

Classification:
    latent inherited K-Mod/BULL/AdvCiv Finance-definition split, data-masked in
    base AdvCiv's Gold channel but made directly live by current SAS civic data.

DUPLICATE RECONCILIATION
------------------------
The earlier Queue-003 control for `buildFinanceSpecialistGoldString` checked only
its exclusion of disorder cities and found that state handling correct. It did
not compare the helper's `player.specialistCommerce` quantity against the
Python row's `city.getSpecialistCommerce` quantity.

Existing Finance roots are distinct:

- F400/KI#723: separately rounded/truncated Finance cost decomposition.
- F401/KI#724: exactly-one profitable trade route can have a blank Finance hover.
- later Finance anarchy controls concern unit-cost/supply state.
- F326/KI#649 mentions current Representation/Free Market
  SpecialistExtraCommerces only in AI civic valuation; it does not cover the
  Finance Advisor display/hover contract.

No existing root in the reconciled album owns this row-vs-tooltip/runtime split.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Use the same complete specialist-commerce quantity that runtime and
`setCommerceHelp` already use when computing `fCitySpecialists`.

A narrow Python repair is conceptually:

    fCitySpecialists = city.getSpecialistCommerce(COMMERCE_GOLD)
    fCitySpecialists += (city.getSpecialistPopulation() +
            city.getNumGreatPeople()) * player.getSpecialistExtraCommerce(
                    COMMERCE_GOLD)

All three Python APIs are exposed in current SAS. This preserves the existing
assigned/free-specialist count contract, excludes disorder exactly where the
Finance screen already does, makes the row agree with its BULL hover/runtime,
and automatically lets the later multiplier computation include the extra
specialist Gold as part of its base.

An alternative per-specialist loop using `player.specialistCommerce` would also
match the BULL helper, but the compact formula above is already the formula used
by `CvCity::getBaseCommerceRateTimes100` and `CvGameTextMgr::setCommerceHelp`.

Do not "fix" the C++ hover by switching it down to `city.getSpecialistCommerce`:
that would make the tooltip agree with the buggy row by hiding real current
Gold output that the runtime actually grants.

C031-WIP144 APPEND - F439 / KI#762 confirmed; Nuke target help uses group head
===============================================================================

STATUS

F439 / provisional KI#762 — NUKE TARGETING IS GROUP-WIDE, BUT NUKE PLOT HELP
AND THE AOE RADIUS RENDERER USE ONLY THE HEAD-SELECTED UNIT; A FIGHTER-HEADED
TACTICAL-NUKE GROUP CAN LEGALLY LAUNCH WHILE ITS TARGET HELP/RADIUS USE THE
NON-NUKE FIGHTER
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvGameTextMgr::getPlotHelp` dispatches `INTERFACEMODE_NUKE` through:

    CvUnit* pHeadSelectedUnit = gDLL->UI().getHeadSelectedUnit();
    ...
    getNukePlotHelp(*pMouseOverPlot, *pHeadSelectedUnit, szTempBuffer);

`getNukePlotHelp` then treats that unit as `kNuke` for every nuke-specific
quantity:

- `canNukeAt`;
- `nukeInterceptionChance`;
- `nukeRange` for explored-tile checks;
- `isNukeVictim` and all detailed invalid-target explanations.

That actor choice does not match the interface-mode or mission contract.

`CvSelectionGroup::canDoInterfaceMode(INTERFACEMODE_NUKE)` iterates every group
member and returns true as soon as ANY unit can `canNuke`.

`CvSelectionGroup::canDoInterfaceModeAt(INTERFACEMODE_NUKE, pPlot)` likewise
iterates every member and returns true as soon as ANY unit can `canNukeAt` the
hovered plot.

`CvSelectionGroup::canDoMission(MISSION_NUKE, ...)` is also any-member logic,
and `CvSelectionGroup::startMission` iterates the group's units; each member is
asked to `nuke(iData1, iData2)`, so an ineligible earlier member simply returns
false and a later eligible nuke can execute the order.

The visible hover therefore reconstructs a group-wide action from the wrong,
head-only actor.

CURRENT DETERMINISTIC PRODUCER
------------------------------
Current SAS supplies an ordinary mixed group that makes the mismatch live:

    UNIT_TACTICAL_NUKE  Domain = DOMAIN_AIR
                         DefaultUnitAI = UNITAI_ICBM
                         iNukeRange = 1
                         iAirRange = 4

    UNIT_FIGHTER / UNIT_JET_FIGHTER
                         Domain = DOMAIN_AIR
                         non-nuclear, positive air combat

`CvUnit::canJoinGroup` permits the grouping: once the group is nonempty it
requires the same owner/plot and the same domain; it does not require the same
unit type or mission abilities. Thus a Tactical Nuke and Fighter on one plot can
be one human selection group.

The group ordering makes the non-nuke-head case stronger than mere user-order
speculation. `CvSelectionGroup::addUnit` orders members by
`AI_groupFirstVal`, then `AI_groupSecondVal`. Current `UNITAI_ICBM` and the air
combat roles all have first value 0, while `AI_groupSecondVal` for air units is
`airBaseCombatStr()`. A Fighter therefore sorts ahead of the zero-combat
Tactical Nuke and becomes group head.

The Nuke interface XML does not repair this by narrowing the selection:

    INTERFACEMODE_NUKE
        bSelectType = 0
        bSelectAll  = 0

So entering Nuke mode leaves the mixed group intact.

Concrete current reproduction:

1. Put a Fighter and Tactical Nuke of the same player on the same air-base plot.
2. Group them. The Fighter is the group head because of the air-combat group
   ordering above.
3. Enter Nuke mode. The action is available because the group-wide
   `canDoInterfaceMode` finds the Tactical Nuke.
4. Hover a target legal for the Tactical Nuke. The normal target-validity test
   is positive because `canDoInterfaceModeAt` finds that Tactical Nuke.
5. `getNukePlotHelp` nevertheless receives the Fighter and calls the Fighter's
   `canNukeAt`, `nukeRange`, victim checks and interception logic.
6. Clicking the legal target sends `MISSION_NUKE` to the selected group. The
   Fighter cannot nuke and does nothing; the Tactical Nuke reaches `CvUnit::nuke`
   and executes the strike.

Thus the UI can present a target which is genuinely legal and executable while
its Nuke-specific hover is based on a unit that cannot perform the action.

VISIBLE CONSEQUENCES
--------------------
On an otherwise legal target, the head Fighter fails `canNukeAt`, so the helper
never enters the valid-nuke branch that displays the real
`nukeInterceptionChance`. Its subsequent explanation scan also uses the
Fighter's `iNukeRange=-1` rather than the Tactical Nuke's radius 1; it therefore
cannot be relied upon to explain the same affected area or legality that the
actual mission uses.

There is a deterministic sibling manifestation in `CvGame::updateNukeAreaOfEffect`.
That renderer also starts with:

    CvUnit const* pNuke = gDLL->UI().getHeadSelectedUnit();
    if (pNuke == NULL || !pNuke->isNuke())
        return false;

For the Fighter-headed Tactical-Nuke group, `canDoInterfaceModeAt` can mark the
hovered target legal, but the yellow nuclear AOE radius is never painted because
the renderer rejects the Fighter head before resolving the group's actual nuke.

This is separate from the earlier Queue-018 UNNUMBERED control about possible
STALE AOE-layer cleanup ordering after selection changes. F439 needs no unknown
EXE transition ordering: the mixed Fighter/Tactical-Nuke group is a fully
source-proven current producer, and its no-radius/help mismatch occurs while the
selection is stable.

ANCESTRY
--------
The head-selected-unit assumption is inherited.

Stock BtS/Civ4CE `CvGameTextMgr::getNukePlotHelp` fetches
`getHeadSelectedUnit()` internally and calls `isNukeVictim` on that unit. K-Mod
retains the same structure. Their selection-group nuke target test is already
an any-member loop, so the basic actor mismatch predates AdvCiv.

AdvCiv practical 2784,
160fa499a896cf595f74bcbde68b7ce41bedc466,
"Show best visible enemy interceptor in tile hover", refactors plot-mode help and
passes the previously fetched `pHeadSelectedUnit` explicitly into
`getNukePlotHelp`; it preserves rather than fixes the inherited assumption.

Later AdvCiv changes make the wrong actor more consequential:

- practical 3096, f28226d0dd6a779876d9737699f8d2334fe4ddbc,
  "AI considers nuke interception chance, UI displays it", adds the valid-target
  interception percentage using the passed `kNuke`;
- practical 3770, b6fce2cedca0f66e226c10bad755f8ff248e88e5,
  "Can't nuke cities with >=10% friendly nationality", expands the detailed
  invalid-target explanations;
- practical 3776, eed5e3b09739596c7aec19f0965443dbc804aaab,
  "Can't nuke cities culturally owned by a neutral party", further aligns
  runtime target legality and its explanations with observer/fog-of-war state.

All of those still receive the arbitrary selection head rather than the
selected unit which can execute Nuke at the target.

DUPLICATE RECONCILIATION
------------------------
The album contains nuclear AI/valuation/report findings, but no existing
`getNukePlotHelp` or mixed-air-selection root.

The closest prior control is Queue 018's unnumbered Nuke AOE-layer cleanup
ordering question. That control asked whether a radius already painted by a
selected nuke can become STALE after the EXE changes selection before clearing
the border layer; it remained unnumbered because callback ordering could not be
proved locally. F439 is different: a stable mixed group has a non-nuke head from
the outset, while group-wide mode legality comes from its Tactical Nuke. The
same renderer consequently paints NO radius for an actually executable target.
No EXE teardown/callback ordering is needed.

No reconciled KI/F root owns the TextMgr head-vs-executor mismatch or this
stable mixed-group AOE symptom.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Do not make Nuke targeting head-only. The game deliberately defines the
interface mode and mission for any eligible selected/group member.

Resolve a target-eligible selected nuke first, then use that SAME unit for all
Nuke hover calculations. Conceptually, before calling `getNukePlotHelp`, scan
the current selection/group for a unit satisfying the execution gates, most
importantly:

    pUnit->canMove() &&
    pUnit->canNukeAt(pUnit->getPlot(), kPlot.getX(), kPlot.getY(),
            pUnit->getTeam())

and pass that unit into `getNukePlotHelp`.

For an invalid target, where no selected nuke passes `canNukeAt`, explanation
text still needs a real selected nuclear unit rather than an arbitrary Fighter;
resolve a selected `isNuke()` unit (preferably using the same selection/group
ordering that mission execution uses) and let that nuke explain why the target
is invalid.

The same resolver principle should be applied to
`CvGame::updateNukeAreaOfEffect`: obtain the selected target-eligible nuke (or a
real selected nuke as appropriate) rather than requiring the head-selected unit
to be nuclear.

The neighboring current Air Bomb / Paradrop help already demonstrates the
right architectural direction: it asks the current selection for a
mission-eligible unit instead of assuming that the selection head is the actor.
A small shared Nuke-selection helper would avoid letting TextMgr and the AOE
renderer drift independently.

C031-WIP145 APPEND - F440 / KI#763 confirmed; Advanced Start advertised
per-city military-unit cap is actually enforced only as an empire-wide average
===============================================================================

STATUS
------
Queue 003 `CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp` remains OPEN.

F440 / provisional KI#763 — ADVANCED START UNIT HELP SAYS "MAXIMUM N UNITS PER
CITY", BUT THE PURCHASE GATE ONLY CAPS TOTAL MILITARY UNITS AT N * CITY COUNT;
MULTIPLE CITIES LET THE PLAYER CONCENTRATE MORE THAN N UNITS IN ONE CITY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvGameTextMgr::getUnitDataForAS` appends the inherited Advanced Start warning
for every purchasable military-support unit:

    int iMaxUnitsPerCity = GC.getDefineINT("ADVANCED_START_MAX_UNITS_PER_CITY");
    if (iMaxUnitsPerCity >= 0 && GC.getInfo(eUnit).isMilitarySupport())
    {
        ...
        gDLL->getText("TXT_KEY_WB_AS_MAX_UNITS_PER_CITY", iMaxUnitsPerCity)
    }

The stock BtS text behind that key is explicit:

    "Maximum %d units per city"

The runtime gate in `CvPlayer::getAdvancedStartUnitCost`, however, does NOT
count units on the target city's plot. For an added military-support unit it
checks only:

    if (getNumMilitaryUnits() >= iMaxUnitsPerCity * getNumCities())
        return -1;

`getNumMilitaryUnits()` is player-wide. `getNumCities()` is player-wide. The
candidate `pPlot` / `pCity` is not used by this cap at all.

After this aggregate check, the city branch verifies only `pCity->canTrain(eUnit)`;
it does not impose any local unit-count limit. `CvPlayer::doAdvancedStartAction`
then calls this same cost function and, when the cost is nonnegative and points
are sufficient, directly creates the unit with `initUnit(eUnit, iX, iY, ...)`.
There is no later per-city cap.

CURRENT DETERMINISTIC PRODUCER
------------------------------
The base `ADVANCED_START_MAX_UNITS_PER_CITY` define is 2. Current SAS does not
override that define in its supplied XML, so the inherited value remains the
current configuration.

With two cities and zero military units, choose any military-support unit that
the target city can train and has enough Advanced Start points to buy.

The advertised rule says that the target city may contain at most 2 such units.
The actual checks for four consecutive purchases on the SAME city are:

    before purchase 1: 0 >= 2 * 2  -> false, allowed
    before purchase 2: 1 >= 2 * 2  -> false, allowed
    before purchase 3: 2 >= 2 * 2  -> false, allowed
    before purchase 4: 3 >= 2 * 2  -> false, allowed
    before purchase 5: 4 >= 2 * 2  -> true, denied

Thus one city can hold four purchased military units while every one of those
unit entries advertises "Maximum 2 units per city". With three cities, all six
may likewise be concentrated in a single city, and so on.

The runtime rule is therefore an empire-wide allowance equal to N times city
count — effectively N military units PER CITY ON AVERAGE — not a local maximum
of N units in each city.

CURRENT CONSEQUENCE
-------------------
This is player-visible and mechanically exploitable during Advanced Start.
The help claims a local placement restriction that the action does not enforce.
A player can therefore legally do exactly what the warning says is forbidden,
concentrating the whole empire allowance in one city.

The discrepancy is not a transient UI/cache issue. `doAdvancedStartAction`
revalidates through `getAdvancedStartUnitCost(..., pPlot)` immediately before
creating the unit, and that authoritative action-time check uses the same
aggregate formula.

ANCESTRY
--------
This mismatch is inherited from stock BtS rather than introduced by AdvCiv-SAS.

Civ4CE's reconstructed BtS source contains both halves unchanged:

* `CvPlayer::getAdvancedStartUnitCost` tests
  `getNumMilitaryUnits() >= iMaxUnitsPerCity * getNumCities()`;
* `CvGameTextMgr::getUnitDataForAS` displays
  `TXT_KEY_WB_AS_MAX_UNITS_PER_CITY`;
* stock BtS `CIV4GameText_BTS.xml` defines the English text as
  `Maximum %d units per city`;
* stock `GlobalDefines.xml` sets `ADVANCED_START_MAX_UNITS_PER_CITY` to 2.

K-Mod 1.46 retains the same aggregate runtime gate and the same TextMgr warning.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 also retains both pieces unchanged. Current SAS inherits the
same semantics; its recent change in this helper only caches/hoists the define
lookup and does not alter behavior.

Classification: inherited BtS Advanced Start rule/help mismatch, still live in
K-Mod, AdvCiv and current AdvCiv-SAS.

DUPLICATE RECONCILIATION
------------------------
The album contains several Advanced Start findings, especially the deep
`CvPlayerAI` automation roots F370-F372 and the later generic-cost/visibility
checks, but none owns this player-facing local-vs-global military-unit cap.

F372 concerns AI automation terminating later unit-role passes after one
unaffordable candidate. F440 concerns the authoritative human/AI purchase-cost
gate itself disagreeing with the static Advanced Start unit warning about the
spatial scope of the cap. They are independent code roots and consequences.

No existing reconciled KI/F entry describes `ADVANCED_START_MAX_UNITS_PER_CITY`,
`TXT_KEY_WB_AS_MAX_UNITS_PER_CITY`, or a per-city-vs-empire-wide military-unit
cap.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The correct repair depends on intended design; the current name and stock text
both strongly suggest that a true local per-city limit was intended, whereas
the implementation behaves like an empire-wide average allowance.

If the intended rule really is LOCAL "maximum N per city", enforce it on the
candidate plot/city in `getAdvancedStartUnitCost` by counting relevant existing
military units there and rejecting once that local count reaches N. The action
already has `pPlot`/`pCity`, so this can be authoritative at purchase time.

If the aggregate allowance is deliberate and should be preserved, then the
warning and define naming need to stop claiming a local cap. A conservative UI
repair would describe the actual rule as an empire maximum derived from city
count (e.g. "Maximum N military units per city on average" or, better, show the
current total allowance explicitly).

Do not merely change the TextMgr number from N to N * city count while retaining
"per city"; that would still misstate the spatial rule.

--------------------------------------------------------

C031-WIP146 APPEND - F441 / KI#764 confirmed; Advanced Start unit palette keeps
military entries after every placement target has become illegal at the cap
===============================================================================

CURRENT STONE
-------------

F441 / provisional KI#764 — ADVANCED START UNIT PALETTE USES A GENERIC COST
QUERY THAT SKIPS THE MILITARY CAP, SO THE REFRESHED PALETTE CAN ADVERTISE AN
ITEM THAT IS ILLEGAL ON EVERY ACTUAL TARGET
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvGameTextMgr::getUnitDataForAS`, the exported builder for the Advanced Start
unit palette, decides whether to include a civilization unit by asking:

    int iCost = kActivePlayer.getAdvancedStartUnitCost(eUnit, true);
    if (iCost > 0)
        mapUnitList.push_back(...);

The omitted plot argument means `pPlot == NULL`.

`CvPlayer::getAdvancedStartUnitCost` deliberately has separate generic and
plot-specific branches. In the generic (`pPlot == NULL`) add branch it only asks
whether at least one city can train the unit:

    bool bValid = false;
    FOR_EACH_CITY(pLoopCity, *this)
    {
        if (pLoopCity->canTrain(eUnit))
        {
            bValid = true;
            break;
        }
    }
    if (!bValid)
        return -1;

The Advanced Start military-unit cap is NOT checked there. It exists only in
the `pPlot != NULL` branch:

    if (bAdd)
    {
        int iMaxUnitsPerCity = ADVANCED_START_MAX_UNITS_PER_CITY;
        if (iMaxUnitsPerCity >= 0 &&
            GC.getInfo(eUnit).isMilitarySupport() &&
            getNumMilitaryUnits() >= iMaxUnitsPerCity * getNumCities())
        {
            return -1;
        }
        ...
    }

Thus the same cost API has the following reachable state:

    getAdvancedStartUnitCost(militaryUnit, true, NULL)  > 0
    getAdvancedStartUnitCost(militaryUnit, true, cityA) == -1
    getAdvancedStartUnitCost(militaryUnit, true, cityB) == -1
    ... for every legal city/plot target

CURRENT-SAS REPRODUCTION
------------------------
Current SAS inherits `ADVANCED_START_MAX_UNITS_PER_CITY = 2` from the stock
BtS global define (the SAS tree contains no XML override of that define).

Use an ordinary one-city Advanced Start position with a trainable military unit
and enough points. Buy two military units. At that point:

    getNumMilitaryUnits() == 2
    getNumCities() == 1
    cap threshold == 2 * 1 == 2

For any actual placement plot, the plot-specific cost reaches the cap test and
returns -1.

But the no-plot generic cost used by `getUnitDataForAS` does not execute that
check. The city can still `canTrain(eUnit)`, so the generic call returns its
normal positive cost and TextMgr re-adds the unit to `mapUnitList`.

With two cities the same shape occurs at four total military units, etc. This
finding does not depend on F440's separate question of whether that aggregate
formula should really be local per-city: under the CURRENT aggregate runtime
rule itself, reaching the threshold makes all new military placements illegal,
yet the generic palette query still reports them available.

UI / REFRESH PROOF FROM THE SUPPLIED BtS/Civ4CE MATERIAL
---------------------------------------------------------
The supplied Civ4CE/BtS `CvWorldBuilderScreen.py` confirms the two roles of the
cost API rather than leaving them as an EXE guess:

* `refreshASItemCost` asks `getAdvancedStartUnitCost(activeUnit, true,
  currentPlot)` for the selected map target;
* left-click handling again requires that same plot-specific call to be != -1
  before sending `ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_UNIT`;
* after a successful unit action, `CvPlayer::doAdvancedStartAction` sets
  `Advanced_Start_DIRTY_BIT` for the active player;
* `CvWorldBuilderScreen.updateScreen` responds to that dirty bit by calling
  `refreshAdvancedStartTabCtrl(true)`;
* `refreshAdvancedStartTabCtrl` reinitializes the Advanced Start control, whose
  exported unit data are supplied by `CvGameTextMgr::getUnitDataForAS`.

Therefore the cap is not merely reached while an old stale list remains on
screen. The purchase explicitly dirties and rebuilds the interface; the
rebuilt unit list still includes the capped military unit because its generic
cost remains positive. Moving/hovering over a real city then gives no purchase
cost, and clicking is rejected because the plot-specific cost is -1.

This is a concrete dead-palette state: an entry advertised by the refreshed
Advanced Start palette has no legal target anywhere.

RUNTIME ACTION CONTROL
----------------------
`CvPlayer::doAdvancedStartAction(ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_UNIT)` rechecks:

    int iCost = getAdvancedStartUnitCost(eUnit, bAdd, pPlot);
    if (bAdd && iCost < 0)
        return;

so the stale availability cannot accidentally bypass the cap. The defect is
UI/API availability disagreement, not an extra-unit purchase exploit.

ANCESTRY
--------
The split is inherited:

* BtS/Civ4CE: generic null-plot unit cost checks `canTrain`, while the max-unit
  check is inside the non-null plot branch; `getUnitDataForAS` uses the generic
  call.
* K-Mod 1.46: same structure.
* Base AdvCiv 1.14: same structure (with AdvCiv cost normalization changes,
  but not a repair of this availability split).
* Current AdvCiv-SAS: same semantic structure; recent SAS edits here only cache
  relevant defines / clean implementation details.

Classification: inherited BtS Advanced Start generic-vs-target availability
mismatch, retained by K-Mod, AdvCiv and SAS.

DUPLICATE RECONCILIATION
------------------------
No existing album root owns this contract.

* F417 is the opposite UI-filter shape: a legally zero-cost Visibility action is
  omitted because TextMgr tests `iCost > 0` instead of the API's -1 sentinel.
* F440 concerns the text "Maximum N units per city" contradicting the current
  aggregate runtime formula.
* Queue-001 F372 concerns AI Advanced Start stopping later unit-role passes after
  one selected unit is unaffordable.

F441 instead concerns `getUnitDataForAS` accepting the generic no-plot unit cost
as proof that SOME placement remains legal when the military cap is only tested
by plot-specific calls. Its reproduction persists even if the F440 wording is
changed to describe the aggregate cap accurately.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Under the current aggregate-cap policy, the minimal semantic fix is to make the
cap independent of `pPlot`: for an add of a military-support unit, reject the
cost once

    getNumMilitaryUnits() >= maxUnits * getNumCities()

before the generic/non-generic branch split (or perform the same check in the
null branch). Then `getUnitDataForAS` naturally stops exporting military entries
when no purchase can succeed anywhere.

If F440 is instead repaired by implementing a true local per-city cap, the
generic query cannot simply use the empire total. It should answer "available"
only when at least one eligible city both can train the unit AND has remaining
local military capacity. The important invariant is:

    generic add cost >= 0
        =>
    at least one current target can return a legal plot-specific add cost

for constraints that make the action globally impossible.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F442 / KI#765 — QUEUED BUILDING HOVER APPLIES THE "START ANOTHER" BUILDING-
CLASS PREREQUISITE FORMULA TO THE BUILDING THAT IS ALREADY CONTINUING
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
Primary file family: `CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp` +
`CvGameCoreDLL/CvDLLWidgetData.cpp` + `CvGameCoreDLL/CvPlayer.cpp` + city-screen
queue caller
Classification: K-Mod v1.39 UI integration regression retained by Base AdvCiv
1.14 and current SAS; ordinary current gameplay.

ROOT
----
K-Mod extended `CvPlayer::getBuildingClassPrereqBuilding` with an `iExtra`
argument so the requirement for a repeatable building class (most visibly a
Cathedral) can account for other buildings of that target class already under
construction.

Runtime deliberately distinguishes STARTING a new building from CONTINUING an
already accepted queue order. In `CvPlayer::canConstruct`:

    int iMaking = getBuildingClassMaking(eBuildingClass);
    ...
    getBuildingClassPrereqBuilding(
        eBuilding, ePrereqClass, bContinue ? 0 : iMaking)

Thus:

* starting a new Cathedral counts all Cathedrals currently making, because the
  new order must satisfy the requirement for one additional Cathedral;
* continuing a Cathedral already in the queue passes `iExtra = 0`, because that
  order has already passed its start gate and must not be reclassified as yet
  another Cathedral being started.

`buildBuildingRequiresString` has no corresponding continuation context. For
ordinary city help it always does:

    getBuildingClassPrereqBuilding(
        eBuilding, ePrereqClass,
        kPlayer.getBuildingClassMaking(targetBuildingClass))

(the Civilopedia path is a separate special case).

That is correct for a production-choice button representing a NEW order, but
wrong for an existing queue item.

CALLER PROOF
------------
The current city production queue is a direct ordinary caller:

* `CvMainInterface.py` renders every queued order row with
  `WIDGET_HELP_SELECTED` and passes its queue index;
* `CvDLLWidgetData::parseSelectedHelp` retrieves that exact order via
  `getOrderFromQueue`;
* for `ORDER_CONSTRUCT`, it calls
  `setBuildingHelpActual(..., pHeadSelectedCity)`;
* `setBuildingHelpActual` calls `buildBuildingRequiresString` without any flag
  saying that the hovered item is an already-accepted/continuing order.

Therefore the bad formula is not limited to Civilopedia/API use and does not
require an EXE-ordering assumption.

CURRENT SAS REPRODUCTION
------------------------
Current SAS Cathedrals are non-limited building classes with a raw requirement
of 2 Temples. On `WORLDSIZE_STANDARD`,
`iBuildingClassPrereqModifier = 38`, so the authoritative scaled prerequisite is:

    ceil(2 * 138 / 100) = 3 Temples per Cathedral step.

With zero completed Cathedrals and exactly 3 Temples:

1. Starting the first Cathedral is legal:

       getBuildingClassMaking(Cathedral) = 0
       required = 3 * (0 built + 0 making + 1) = 3

2. Once the order is pushed, `changeBuildingClassMaking(..., +1)` makes:

       getBuildingClassMaking(Cathedral) = 1

3. Runtime continuation still checks with `bContinue = true`, hence
   `iExtra = 0`, and continues to require only 3 Temples.

4. Hovering that queued Cathedral instead calls the TextMgr formula with
   `iExtra = getBuildingClassMaking(...) = 1`, producing:

       required = 3 * (0 built + 1 making + 1) = 6

The Unofficial Patch localization used by the helper is warning-coloured and
explicitly says:

    Requires Temple (3/6 Total)

although the same queued Cathedral is legal to continue with the 3 Temples the
player already has.

The discrepancy grows with simultaneous accepted orders. Runtime continuation
passes zero `iExtra` for each existing order, while the shared hover counts all
currently-making target buildings as though the hovered order were a fresh
additional start.

ANCESTRY / INTENT PROOF
-----------------------
Stock BtS did not have this exact regression: its TextMgr used the older
prerequisite calculation without K-Mod's under-construction `iExtra` extension.

K-Mod v1.39 explicitly introduced the relevant UI behaviour. Its changelog says:

    "The mouseover text for cathedrals will now include the number of cathedrals
     currently under construction when calculating the required number of
     temples. (ie. it will report how many temples are required to start the
     construction of another cathedral.)"

That stated intent is correct for a NEW production choice. The implementation
placed the calculation in the shared building-help path, which is also used for
an EXISTING queue entry, and did not carry the runtime `bContinue` distinction
through the UI call chain.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the K-Mod formula; current SAS retains it as well.

DUPLICATE RECONCILIATION
------------------------
The earlier Queue-003 Building Requirement reconciliation checked missing
`canConstruct` predicates, current production-button visibility, and the
Civilopedia world-size prerequisite range. It did not cover the separate
NEW-ORDER-vs-CONTINUING-ORDER arithmetic distinction.

No existing album root was found for Cathedral/building-class `iMaking` leaking
into an already-queued building's hover. This is therefore independent of the
previous building-help controls and the Actual Effects findings.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Carry an explicit continuation/queue-order context to the prerequisite helper.
The important arithmetic contract is:

* NEW production choice: pass current `getBuildingClassMaking(targetClass)`,
  matching `canConstruct(..., bContinue=false)`;
* EXISTING queue order: pass `0`, matching
  `canConstruct(..., bContinue=true)`;
* Civilopedia: preserve its existing context-free/base-requirement behaviour.

Do not merely subtract one from `getBuildingClassMaking`. Runtime continuation
ignores all currently-making siblings for the already accepted order; its exact
contract is `iExtra = 0`.

A narrow implementation would let `parseSelectedHelp` mark the
`ORDER_CONSTRUCT` help as continuing (it knows the row is an existing queue
order), thread that boolean through `setBuildingHelpActual` /
`buildBuildingRequiresString`, and select the same `iExtra` as runtime.

C031-WIP149 — QUEUED PRODUCTION-TURNS HOVER INDEX LOSS; F443 / KI#766 CONFIRMED

CONTINUATION ANCHOR

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F443 / KI#766 — PRODUCTION-QUEUE ROW HOVER DISCARDS THE ROW'S ACTUAL QUEUE
INDEX AND RECOMPUTES TURNS AS A HYPOTHETICAL FRONT/END INSERTION
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
Primary file family: `CvGameCoreDLL/CvDLLWidgetData.cpp` +
`CvGameCoreDLL/CvGameTextMgr.cpp` + `CvGameCoreDLL/CvCity.cpp` + city-screen
queue caller
Classification: inherited BtS UI integration defect retained by K-Mod, Base
AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS; ordinary current gameplay. AdvCiv's advc.064b
queued-overflow predictor increases the importance of the lost queue index but
did not introduce the root.

ROOT
----
The city production queue already knows the exact queue index of every row.
Current `CvMainInterface.py` uses that exact `i` when rendering its visible
turn count:

    getUnitProductionTurnsLeft(eUnit, i)
    getBuildingProductionTurnsLeft(eBuilding, i)
    getProjectProductionTurnsLeft(eProject, i)

The same row is assigned `WIDGET_HELP_SELECTED` with `iData1 = i`.
`CvDLLWidgetData::parseSelectedHelp` therefore receives the exact row index and
uses it to retrieve the exact `OrderData` through `getOrderFromQueue(i)`.

But after identifying the order, `parseSelectedHelp` discards the index and
calls the ordinary generic help functions:

    setUnitHelp(..., pHeadSelectedCity)
    setBuildingHelpActual(..., pHeadSelectedCity)
    setProjectHelp(..., pHeadSelectedCity)

Those generic functions were designed primarily for prospective production
choices. Their turns-left call chooses a simulated insertion position from the
keyboard state:

    pCity->getProductionTurnsLeft(eThing,
        (GC.ctrlKey() || !GC.shiftKey()) ? 0 :
        pCity->getOrderQueueLength())

Thus an ordinary no-modifier hover over an EXISTING queue row recomputes the
turns as though the item were a hypothetical order at queue position 0. Holding
Shift instead simulates an append at `getOrderQueueLength()`. Neither path uses
the actual existing row index which `WIDGET_HELP_SELECTED` already supplied.

WHY THE INDEX IS SEMANTIC
-------------------------
`CvCity::getProductionTurnsLeft(Unit/Building/Project, iNum)` does not treat
`iNum` as decorative UI data.

For each production kind it finds the first queued order of the same type and
only credits the city's stored production when either no such queued order
exists or that first occurrence is exactly `iNum`:

    if (iFirstBuildingOrder == -1 || iFirstBuildingOrder == iNum)
        iProduction += getBuildingProduction(eBuilding);

(and equivalently for Units and Projects).

This is correct: stored production belongs to the already-existing first queued
occurrence, not to a hypothetical duplicate inserted before it.

AdvCiv's advc.064b additionally makes queue position affect first-turn overflow
prediction:

* `iNum == 0` uses current-production overflow/feature-production semantics;
* `iNum == 1` can predict overflow from the head order when it is about to
  complete;
* later queued positions deliberately do not attempt that overflow prediction.

So the exact queue index is authoritative input to the displayed estimate.

ORDINARY CURRENT REPRODUCTION
-----------------------------
A particularly simple reproduction needs no unusual modifiers and no EXE
assumption:

1. Start a production item B and accumulate some production into it.
2. Switch the city to another item A. Civ4 retains B's invested production.
3. Queue B behind A.
4. The visible B queue row calls `get*ProductionTurnsLeft(B, 1)` and therefore
   recognises that B's first queued occurrence is index 1 and credits B's stored
   production.
5. Hover that same B row with no modifier keys. `parseSelectedHelp` identifies
   row 1, but the generic TextMgr helper calls
   `getProductionTurnsLeft(B, 0)`. Because B's first queued occurrence is 1,
   the index-0 hypothetical order receives none of B's stored production.

Illustrative current arithmetic with a 100-production item, 50 production
already stored and a steady 10 production/turn:

    queue row, real index 1:  5 turns
    row hover, simulated 0:  10 turns

Current SAS has ordinary 100-production buildings (e.g. Forge), so this shape
does not depend on a hypothetical XML cost. The exact numeric difference in a
real city follows that city's production modifiers/rate, but the source
mismatch is deterministic whenever enough stored production changes the
rounded estimate.

A second AdvCiv-specific manifestation can occur for the row immediately after
a head order that is about to finish: the exact `iNum == 1` row prediction can
include predicted head-order overflow, while the queue-row hover's generic
`iNum == 0` path instead treats the hovered item as current production.

CALLER / UI CONTRADICTION
-------------------------
This is unusually direct because the same visual queue row can expose both
values simultaneously:

* its right-side `(N)` is computed in Python using the exact queue index;
* hovering that row calls TextMgr through `WIDGET_HELP_SELECTED` and can show a
  different `N Turns` computed from index 0 / queue end.

The hover is therefore not merely less precise than runtime. It can contradict
the number printed next to the exact item being hovered.

ANCESTRY
--------
Stock BtS already has both halves of the root:

* `CvMainInterface.py` renders queue Unit/Building/Project turns using the exact
  row index `i`;
* `parseSelectedHelp` retrieves that row but calls the generic help functions;
* those generic TextMgr functions choose 0 or queue length from Ctrl/Shift
  state instead of the selected row index.

Stock BtS `CvCity::getProductionTurnsLeft(eThing, iNum)` already uses `iNum` to
decide which occurrence receives stored production, so the bug is live in the
original contract.

K-Mod retains that flow. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain it as well.
AdvCiv advc.064b improves queued-order prediction and adds special `iNum == 1`
overflow handling, but the `parseSelectedHelp` caller was never updated to pass
the row index into the generic help functions.

DUPLICATE RECONCILIATION
------------------------
The album contains prior production-turn and production-decay work, including
sentinel handling and the separate game-speed production-decay amount defect.
None covers an existing production queue row discarding its own queue index.

F442 is adjacent but independent:

* F442 concerns Building-class prerequisite arithmetic for an already accepted
  Building order (START another vs CONTINUE this one);
* F443 concerns the turns-left projection for Unit, Building and Project queue
  rows and the lost `iNum` argument.

No existing root was found for `parseSelectedHelp` / `WIDGET_HELP_SELECTED`
recomputing an existing queued item's turns at position 0 or queue end.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Preserve the generic production-button semantics, but let existing queue-row
help carry its actual queue index.

A narrow design is to add an optional queue-position argument (defaulting to a
sentinel meaning "prospective production choice") to the Unit / Building /
Project city-help path:

* production-choice buttons with no queue position continue using the existing
  Ctrl/Shift 0-vs-end insertion simulation;
* `parseSelectedHelp`, which already owns `widgetDataStruct.m_iData1`, passes
  that exact index for `ORDER_TRAIN`, `ORDER_CONSTRUCT` and `ORDER_CREATE`;
* the turns-left line then calls `getProductionTurnsLeft(eThing, iQueuePos)`
  for an existing order.

This should be coordinated with F442's queue/continuation context so that one
explicit "existing queue order" path can carry both the correct prerequisite
semantics and the correct turns position rather than adding unrelated ad-hoc
special cases.

F444 / provisional KI#767 - CONFIRMED CURRENT BASE ADVCIV ARITHMETIC/CACHE DEFECT
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Title:
`CvPlayer::updateCommerceRates` repeatedly awards every whole rounding correction to
the same commerce type because its advertised implicit selection sort never removes
or updates the selected fractional remainder.

Birth / lineage:
Base AdvCiv, change id `advc.157`, introduced by exact locally preserved commit:

    4e6fe9df58dfbce36a575aa24224e44030bd76fa
    2021-09-08
    "Redistribute rounding errors from non-binary research"

The introducing diff adds `updateCommerceRates` and already contains the defective loop
in exactly the relevant form. K-Mod / BtS do not have this redistribution/cache
algorithm; current Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS retain it unchanged in the
relevant logic.

Intended/documented contract:
The source immediately calls the loop:

    // Implicit selection sort (b/c the error is going to be small)

The AdvCiv manual for change 157 says that when accumulated rounding errors reach at
least 1 commerce, the integer correction is added to the commerce rate(s) that
contribute(s) the most to the total error. The purpose is to remove the systematic
penalty from non-binary commerce-slider positions.

Implemented contract:
For each CommerceTypes value, `updateCommerceRates` stores the signed fractional
remainder:

    iError = sign(iRate) * (abs(iRate) % 100)

and accumulates all remainders in `iTotalError`. It truncates every Times100 rate to an
integer, then performs `abs(iTotalError) / 100` correction iterations. Each iteration
searches `aiError` for the largest signed remainder and adds +/-1 to that commerce
rate.

However, after selecting `eArgMax`, the implementation only does:

    m_aiCommerceRate.add(eArgMax, iSign * 1);

It never reduces, clears, or otherwise updates `aiError[eArgMax]`.

Therefore, when at least two whole correction points are required, the next iteration
sees exactly the same maximum and selects exactly the same commerce type again. All
corrections go to the first maximum. The advertised selection sort never advances.

This is mathematically inconsistent with the residual after the first correction: if
an exact rate has remainder +90 and receives +1, its new residual is -10, not still
+90. It therefore cannot legitimately remain ahead of an uncorrected +80 remainder.

CURRENT SAS REACHABILITY - NO FUTURE/MODDED DATA REQUIRED
---------------------------------------------------------
The multi-correction branch is ordinary current-data gameplay, not a theoretical
edge case.

Current SAS Palace (`BUILDING_PALACE`) has:

    YieldChanges:          [0, 0, 8]  => +8 raw YIELD_COMMERCE
    CommerceChanges:       [0, 0, 0, 4] => +4 flat Espionage
    CommerceModifiers:     empty

Current `YIELD_COMMERCE` has `iMinCity = 1`; `CvPlot::calculateCityPlotYieldChange`
raises the city plot to that minimum. Thus a capital can have exactly 9 raw commerce
from the Palace's +8 plus the city plot's minimum +1 while avoiding extra worked-tile
commerce (e.g. use a specialist / zero-commerce worked configuration).

Current Tech XML makes the relevant slider state legal:

* `TECH_MONARCHY` has `CommerceFlexible [0,0,0,1]` -> Espionage slider flexible.
* `TECH_DRAMA` has `CommerceFlexible [0,0,1,0]` -> Culture slider flexible.

Gold/Research are the ordinary slider pair. Once Monarchy + Drama are known, a
30% Gold / 10% Research / 20% Culture / 40% Espionage split is legal.

For 9 raw commerce, before optional percentage-commerce modifiers:

    Gold:       9 * 30% = 2.70 -> 270
    Research:   9 * 10% = 0.90 ->  90
    Culture:    9 * 20% = 1.80 -> 180
    Espionage:  9 * 40% = 3.60 -> 360, plus Palace +4 = 760

The fractional remainders are therefore:

    Gold       70
    Research   90
    Culture    80
    Espionage  60
    ----------------
    total     300

`abs(iTotalError) / 100 == 3`, so the correction loop runs THREE times.

After initial truncation, special-commerce integer rates are:

    Gold 2, Research 0, Culture 1, Espionage 7

BROKEN RESULT:
The first scan selects Research (90). Because its stored 90 remainder never changes,
the second and third scans select Research again:

    Gold 2, Research 3, Culture 1, Espionage 7

(before AdvCiv's separate BASE_RESEARCH_RATE addition).

INTENDED SELECTION / LARGEST-REMAINDER RESULT:
After Research receives +1, its effective remainder is -10. The next largest
uncorrected remainder is Culture 80, then Gold 70:

    Gold 3, Research 1, Culture 2, Espionage 7

(before BASE_RESEARCH_RATE).

The bug therefore does not merely choose a different cosmetic tie-break. It can move
multiple whole commerce points between different commerce categories.

AUTHORITATIVE GAMEPLAY CONSUMERS
--------------------------------
The corrected `m_aiCommerceRate` cache is authoritative for normal player-level rates:

* `calculateGoldRate()` starts from `getCommerceRate(COMMERCE_GOLD)` and applies GPT /
  expenses; this feeds actual treasury changes.
* `calculateResearchRate()` starts from `getCommerceRate(COMMERCE_RESEARCH)` and applies
  the research modifier; `doResearch()` sends that rate into team research progress.
* `doEspionagePoints()` uses `getCommerceRate(COMMERCE_ESPIONAGE)` for actual EP-ever
  gain and `getEspionageSpending()` distributes the same integer budget against teams.

Thus an erroneous redistribution among these categories changes real Gold, Research,
and/or Espionage output. It is not confined to UI display.

Culture is a useful additional warning: player-wide Culture rate is much less
important because city culture is applied per city (the AdvCiv manual itself says
"total culture isn't really relevant"). A malformed correction can therefore also be
dumped into or withheld from a civ-wide Culture aggregate that does not symmetrically
substitute for lost Gold/Research/Espionage gameplay output.

WHY THIS IS A DEFECT, NOT AN ALTERNATIVE ROUNDING POLICY
--------------------------------------------------------
Several independent pieces agree:

1. the code names the algorithm an "Implicit selection sort";
2. the manual says correction goes to the rate(s) contributing most to the total
   error, not repeatedly to the first rate that happened to have the initial maximum;
3. after +1 is awarded to a +90 remainder, that rate's actual residual becomes -10,
   so treating it as +90 on the next pass is arithmetically stale;
4. the introducing commit's stated purpose is to redistribute accumulated rounding
   error from non-binary research, and the malformed repeated maximum can transfer
   multiple whole units to the wrong commerce category instead.

DUPLICATE / ALBUM CHECK
-----------------------
The reconciled album contains no prior `updateCommerceRates`, advc.157, non-binary-
research redistribution, or player-commerce-rounding root. F326 references
`getCommerceRate` only as an input to AI civic valuation and concerns removal of
`AI_averageCommerceMultiplier` normalization; it is unrelated. Queue-003 Finance /
commerce findings concern display decomposition and rounding of other components, not
this authoritative player cache.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
After awarding the +/-1 correction, update the selected stored residual before the
next scan. The mathematically direct form is conceptually:

    m_aiCommerceRate.add(eArgMax, iSign);
    aiError.add(eArgMax, -iSign * 100);

because giving +1 to a +90 hundredths residual changes the residual to -10, and giving
-1 to a -90 residual changes it to +10.

For currently nonnegative special-commerce rates, simply excluding each selected
candidate from subsequent passes would also produce the intended largest-remainder
selection because each original remainder has magnitude <100 and at most three whole
corrections can exist across four commerce types. Updating by +/-100 is preferable as
it directly preserves the residual arithmetic and the function's stated negative-rate
future-proofing intent.

A regression test should cover at least one `abs(iTotalError) / 100 >= 2` state, not
only the typical one-correction case; a 9-commerce four-slider state above is a compact
current-SAS fixture.

POST-F444 CONTROL TRANCHE
-------------------------
Several inherited state/cache candidates were chased through full transitions rather
than promoted on suspicious syntax alone.

1. CHANGELEADER / TRUE STARTS FREE-PROMOTION CONTROL — CLEAN FOR ORDINARY TRUE STARTS

`CvPlayer::changeLeader` removes old-trait processing and applies the new leader's
traits, while trait-granted unit free promotions themselves are normally installed by
`CvUnit::init`. That initially suggested that a True Starts leader swap could leave
already-created starting units with the old leader's promotions. The actual game-init
order closes the ordinary case: `TrueStarts::changeCivs()` runs before
`CvGame::initFreeUnits()` in `CvGame::setInitialItems`, so normal starting units are
created only after the final leader is installed. Scenario-authored pre-existing units
remain a scenario/robustness caveat rather than a proven generic current root.

2. PERMANENT-ALLIANCE TECHNOLOGY PROCESSING CONTROL — CLEAN

`CvTeam::addTeam` calls `shareItems(eTeam)` before moving absorbed players to the
surviving team. A partial trace suggested that survivor-only technologies might be
processed before absorbed players became members and therefore fail to install their
player-level effects. Full `shareItems` tracing rejects that: K-Mod/AdvCiv makes the
technology sharing bidirectional before reassignment. Each team receives the other's
missing technologies through `setHasTech` while its own players still belong to it;
therefore persistent player-level technology effects are processed for both sets of
players before `CvPlayer::setTeam` performs the merge.

3. `updateExtraYieldThresholds` NATURAL-THRESHOLD TYPO — REAL BUT CURRENTLY DATA-MASKED

The natural-yield branch contains an apparent inherited typo:

    if (iBestNaturalThresh == 0 || iBestNaturalThresh < iBestThresh)
        iBestNaturalThresh = iNaturalThresh;

The ordinary threshold branch correctly compares the candidate against the current
best ordinary threshold. The natural branch instead compares the existing natural
threshold against the unrelated ordinary `iBestThresh`, making multiple natural
threshold sources potentially trait-order dependent. Current SAS data masks the
fault: only Financial currently supplies a nonzero `ExtraYieldNaturalThreshold`
(Commerce 3), so no competing current natural thresholds exist. Preserve as
robustness/future-data debt; do not number as F445 without a current consequence.

4. `canStealTech` / `canSpyDestroyProject` APPARENT PLAYER->TEAM ENUM MISMATCH — REJECTED

Current source contains lines such as:

    GET_TEAM(eTarget).isHasTech(eTech)
    GET_TEAM(eTarget).getProjectCount(eProject)

where `eTarget` is declared `PlayerTypes`. Read without include context, these appear
to index the team table by player ID and would imply severe team-game espionage bugs.
That diagnosis is false.

`CvPlayer.cpp` includes `CoreAI.h`. `CoreAI.h` deliberately replaces the ordinary
`GET_TEAM` macro with an overloaded accessor:

    #define GET_TEAM(x) CoreAI::getTeam(x)

    getTeam(TeamTypes eTeam)     -> AI_getTeam(eTeam)
    getTeam(PlayerTypes ePlayer) -> AI_getTeam(TEAMID(ePlayer))

Therefore `GET_TEAM(eTarget)` resolves the target player's ACTUAL team even when
PlayerTypes and TeamTypes numeric IDs differ.

Lineage confirms intent. BtS and K-Mod spell the conversion explicitly as
`GET_TEAM(GET_PLAYER(eTarget).getTeam())`. An AdvCiv style/refactor stage first used
the player-aware `TEAMREF(eTarget)` helper; commit
`1c56cc6ac149d97c3a28eae56440f4f0ab0183bd`, titled
"GET_PLAYER, GET_TEAM macros outside of AI headers", then deliberately changed that
spelling to overloaded `GET_TEAM(eTarget)`. The active CoreAI overload preserves the
same semantics.

This independently revalidates the album's earlier KI#311 rejected-false-positive
methodology: apparent PlayerTypes/TeamTypes mismatches through `GET_TEAM` must be
resolved through the active include-context macro/overloads before diagnosis.

`canStealTech` does appear in the album under F349, but only as an input to the
separate `CvPlayerAI::AI_doCommerce` accumulator defect. There is no missing
`canStealTech` root here; F445 remains unused.

5. OTHER EARLY QUEUE-004 CONTROLS

* `canReceiveGoody` / `receiveGoody`: technology rewards are still protected by
  `isGoodyTech()->canResearch`; no current mismatch found. A bad goody with a
  BarbarianUnitClass plus `iMinBarbarians==0` would expose a latent division-by-zero
  shape, but current hostile goodies have positive minima.
* `disbandUnit`: preliminary forced-financial-disband scoring/eligibility review has
  not established a defect. Its behavior is intentionally distinct from voluntary
  scrapping and should not inherit the earlier SAS scrapping findings automatically.
* `changeCommerceFlexibleCount`, trade-route/anarchy transitions and the current
  stacked availability counters checked so far preserve their zero/nonzero transition
  invariants under current callers/data.
