F445 / KI#768 — `CvPlayer::setCapital` changes capital-only yield modifiers without invalidating cached city yield ranks
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvCity::getBaseYieldRateModifier(YieldTypes)` dynamically includes the owning
player's `getCapitalYieldRateModifier(eYield)` whenever `isCapital()` is true.
`CvCity::isCapital()` is itself dynamic and simply compares the city to
`GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).getCapital()`.

K-Mod's `CvCity::findYieldRateRank` caches yield-rate rankings. When one city asks for
a rank, it calculates the ordering for ALL of the player's cities and marks every
city's rank valid for that yield.

The source next to `getBaseYieldRateModifier` explicitly states the cache contract:

    // note: player->invalidateYieldRankCache() must be called for anything that is checked here

Capital status is one of the conditions checked there.

However, `CvPlayer::setCapital(CvCity* pNewCapital)` changes `m_iCapitalCityID` and
updates maintenance, trade routes and commerce for the old/new capitals, but never
calls `invalidateYieldRankCache`.

Therefore changing capital identity can change an old/new capital's actual Food /
Production / Commerce yield-rate modifier while a previously computed city-yield
ranking remains valid according to the cache flags.

CURRENT LIVE DATA / REPRODUCTION
--------------------------------
This is live in ordinary current SAS data. `CIVIC_BUREAUCRACY` has:

    CapitalYieldModifiers = [0, +50, +50]

so the capital receives +50% Production and +50% Commerce.

A simple deterministic shape is:

1. Player runs Bureaucracy and owns at least two cities A and B.
2. Before the capital move, actual production rates are such that A (the capital)
   ranks above B only because of Bureaucracy's +50% capital Production modifier; e.g.
   A base 10 -> 15, B base 11 -> 11.
3. Something calls `findYieldRateRank(YIELD_PRODUCTION)`. K-Mod computes and caches the
   complete ordering, e.g. A rank 1, B rank 2.
4. Complete a Palace in B, causing `CvPlayer::setCapital(B)`.
5. Actual rates immediately change dynamically: A loses the +50% and becomes 10;
   B gains it and becomes 16 (integer arithmetic), so the correct order is B rank 1,
   A rank 2.
6. `setCapital` does not invalidate `YIELD_PRODUCTION`, therefore the cached ordering
   can remain A rank 1 / B rank 2 until some unrelated Production-yield change later
   invalidates it.

PALACE SIDE-EFFECT CONTROL
--------------------------
The capital relocation path does not accidentally repair the missing Production-rank
invalidation. Current `BUILDING_PALACE` has base YieldChanges `[0, 0, +8]` — only
Commerce yield. `CvCity::processBuilding` therefore invalidates the Commerce-yield
rank through the Palace's base-commerce-yield change, but it performs no
Production-yield mutation that would invalidate `YIELD_PRODUCTION`.

The relevant capital-only Production modifier comes from the player's civic and changes
solely because `isCapital()` now points at a different city.

RUNTIME CONSEQUENCE
-------------------
The underlying Production yield itself is NOT stale; `getYieldRate()` consults
`isCapital()` dynamically, so actual production changes immediately. The stale object
is specifically the cached rank returned by `findYieldRateRank(YIELD_PRODUCTION)`.

That rank is gameplay-significant. Current SAS has multiple AI consumers in
`CvCityAI.cpp` / `CvPlayerAI.cpp` (plus additional logging/UI consumers) that use
Production rank when evaluating city roles, production choices and related decisions.
A capital move can therefore temporarily feed those AI decisions an ordering that no
longer corresponds to the actual Production yields.

ANCESTRY
--------
This omission is inherited. BtS `CvPlayer::setCapitalCity`, K-Mod
`CvPlayer::setCapitalCity`, Base AdvCiv 1.14 `CvPlayer::setCapital`, and current SAS all
perform the same capital-ID transition plus maintenance/trade/commerce refresh without
yield-rank invalidation.

BtS data already makes the state live: Bureaucracy carries the same +50% Production /
+50% Commerce `CapitalYieldModifiers`. K-Mod's later all-city rank-cache implementation
makes the stale state especially broad because one rank lookup marks all city ranks for
that yield valid together.

DUPLICATE / ALBUM CHECK
-----------------------
The reconciled album contains no prior `setCapital`, Bureaucracy capital-yield,
`findYieldRateRank`, capital-modifier or yield-rank-cache root. Existing capital,
Palace, commerce and rank mentions belong to unrelated systems.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
`CvPlayer::setCapital` should invalidate player city yield-rate ranks after changing
capital identity, at least for every yield whose `getCapitalYieldRateModifier` can be
nonzero. The simplest and safest repair is conceptually:

    invalidateYieldRankCache();

once the capital ID has changed (before or alongside the old/new UI/commerce refreshes).
This directly satisfies the maintenance contract documented beside
`CvCity::getBaseYieldRateModifier` and remains correct for XML/mod data that adds
capital-only Food or other yield modifiers later.

A regression test should first populate Production ranks under Bureaucracy, move the
Palace/capital to another city without otherwise changing Production yields, and verify
that a subsequent `findYieldRateRank(YIELD_PRODUCTION)` recomputes the new ordering.

POST-F445 CLEAN CONTROLS
------------------------
* `CvPlayer::setCommercePercent`: the apparently negative adjustment when total
  commerce is below 100 is intentional; subtracting a negative increases another
  flexible category. Player-level flexibility loss resets the newly inflexible
  category to its XML initial percent. No current broken 100%-sum transition proven.
* `changeHurryCount`: derived pop-/gold-rush counts add `iChange` on a zero/nonzero
  transition, but its gameplay caller `processCivics` supplies only -1/0/+1 per civic,
  so current data cannot create a multi-point transition mismatch.
* `changeFreeBuildingCount`: correctly applies/removes free buildings only on the
  zero-to-positive / positive-to-zero source-count boundaries.

F446 / KI#769 — `calculateUnitCost(..., iExtraUnits)` applies generic unit delta to military-unit count too
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
AdvCiv extends `CvPlayer::calculateUnitCost` with prospective-state parameters:

    int iExtraPop, int iExtraUnits

The implementation applies `iExtraUnits` to BOTH support populations:

    iPaidUnits = max(0, getNumUnits() - iFreeUnits + iExtraUnits);
    iPaidMilitaryUnits = max(0,
            getNumMilitaryUnits() - iFreeMilitaryUnits + iExtraUnits);

That silently assumes every prospective extra/removed unit is also a military-support
unit. The parameter itself is generic and live callers use it for explicitly civilian
units.

CURRENT LIVE CALLER 1 — CITY-FOUND COST HELP
---------------------------------------------
`CvGameTextMgr::setFoundCostHelp` projects expenses after founding a city. It correctly
accounts for the Settler disappearing by calling:

    kPlayer.calculateUnitCost(CvCity::initialPopulation(), -1)

Current `UNIT_SETTLER` has:

    bMilitarySupport = 0

and therefore does NOT contribute to `CvPlayer::getNumMilitaryUnits()` at runtime.
Founding a city removes one total unit but zero military units.

The projection nevertheless subtracts one from both populations through the shared
`iExtraUnits=-1` argument.

CURRENT DATA MAKES THE MILITARY-COST ERROR LIVE
-----------------------------------------------
Current `CIVIC_PACIFISM` has:

    iGoldPerMilitaryUnit = 100

(1 gold per paid military-support unit), and current civic data has no nonzero
`iBaseFreeMilitaryUnits` or `iFreeMilitaryUnitsPopulationPercent` source.

A compact ordinary reproduction is:

1. Human player runs Pacifism.
2. Player owns at least one military-support unit and a Settler.
3. Hover a legal city-found action.
4. Actual post-found state consumes the Settler but keeps the military-support unit;
   military upkeep therefore remains charged for that military unit.
5. `setFoundCostHelp` passes `iExtraUnits=-1`; the projection also decrements
   `iPaidMilitaryUnits`, reducing projected military cost by 1 gold/turn before
   inflation whenever the paid military count is positive.

The projected founding-cost delta is therefore understated. Inflation can scale the
visible error further.

CURRENT LIVE CALLER 2 — DELETE / SCRAP COMMAND HELP
----------------------------------------------------
`CvDLLWidgetData`'s `COMMAND_DELETE` help builds `iUnits` by subtracting every selected
unit and every carried cargo unit, without distinguishing military-support units. It
then calls:

    calculateUnitCost(0, iUnits)

for the projected expenses and again with further generic negative unit deltas when
estimating how many additional units would need deletion before expenses decrease.

Selecting/deleting a Worker, Settler or other `bMilitarySupport=0` unit therefore also
pretends to reduce the military-support population. Under Pacifism this can overstate
the gold savings from deleting civilian units and can distort the helper's "one more /
N more units" guidance.

RUNTIME CONTROL
---------------
Actual military-unit accounting is type-aware. `CvUnit::init` increments
`changeNumMilitaryUnits(1)` only when `m_pUnitInfo->isMilitarySupport()`; `CvUnit::kill`
symmetrically decrements only those units. Settlers are explicitly non-military-support.
The projection is therefore not mirroring runtime unit accounting.

ANCESTRY / INTRODUCING COMMIT
-----------------------------
This is an AdvCiv regression, not stock BtS/K-Mod unit-cost arithmetic.

K-Mod's ordinary `calculateUnitCost` has no prospective `iExtraUnits` parameter.
Before the relevant AdvCiv change, the founding-cost projection handled the Settler
specifically:

    iPaidUnits = max(0, getNumUnits() - iFreeUnits
            - (iExtraPop > 0 ? 1 : 0)); // The Settler is gone after founding
    iPaidMilitaryUnits = max(0, getNumMilitaryUnits() - iFreeMilitaryUnits);

That correctly removed the Settler from total-unit upkeep while leaving military-unit
upkeep untouched.

AdvCiv practical commit 1412, SHA `ef40cbb8b47a2b11e4b213076d0f1cad62ad13b1`,
titled "Misc. tweaks (mostly UI)", generalized the projection API to add
`iExtraUnits`. In the same introducing diff it replaced the Settler-specific total-unit
adjustment and added `+ iExtraUnits` to BOTH `iPaidUnits` and `iPaidMilitaryUnits`.
The same commit also introduced the Delete-command unit-cost projection that counts
selected units generically. Thus the wrong military delta is present in the
introducing change itself.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the generalized implementation.

DUPLICATE / ALBUM CHECK
-----------------------
The album already audits `setFoundCostHelp`, but its confirmed F392/KI#715 root is the
separate WLTKD maintenance projection mismatch. F412/KI#735 concerns Finance Advisor
unit-cost/supply hovers bypassing anarchy-aware wrappers. Neither covers prospective
civilian-unit deltas being applied to military-unit upkeep.

The album contains no prior root for `iExtraUnits`, prospective paid-military count, or
civilian Delete-command military-upkeep savings. F446 is independent.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
The prospective API needs distinct total-unit and military-unit deltas, e.g.
conceptually:

    calculateUnitCost(iExtraPop, iExtraUnits, iExtraMilitaryUnits)

with the detailed overload using:

    iPaidUnits         ... + iExtraUnits
    iPaidMilitaryUnits ... + iExtraMilitaryUnits

`setFoundCostHelp` should pass `-1` total units and `0` military units for the Settler.

The Delete-command helper should count both selected/cargo total units and selected /
cargo `isMilitarySupport()` units separately, then pass both deltas. Its iterative
"how many more deletions" prediction cannot know the military status of hypothetical
future deletions; that fallback should either state its assumption explicitly, use a
conservative model, or be refactored around actual candidate unit types rather than a
single generic unit count.

Regression tests should include Pacifism with one paid military unit plus a Settler /
Worker and verify that removing the civilian changes total-unit support only, not
military support.

F447 / KI#770 -- RECYCLING A DEFEATED PLAYER WHOSE OLD TEAM IS STILL ALIVE SKIPS COLONY INITIALIZATION, THEN REVIVES THE OLD PLAYER FROM THE TRANSFERRED CITIES
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvPlayer::getSplitEmpirePlayer` chooses a recycled slot according to PLAYER state:

    if (!itPlayer->isAlive())
        eNewPlayer = itPlayer->getID();

when no never-used player slot remains (AdvCiv restricts this fallback to human
splitters through `<kekm.24>`).

But `CvPlayer::splitEmpire` immediately decides whether that selected slot already
"exists" according to TEAM state instead:

    bool bPlayerExists = GET_TEAM(eNewPlayer).isAlive();
    FAssert(!bPlayerExists);

and performs all new-colony initialization only when that TEAM is dead:

    if (!bPlayerExists)
    {
        ... choose eBestLeader / eBestCiv ...
        kGame.addPlayer(eNewPlayer, eBestLeader, eBestCiv);
        GET_PLAYER(eNewPlayer).setParent(getID());
        ... inherit technologies ...
        GET_TEAM(getTeam()).assignVassal(TEAMID(eNewPlayer), false);
        ...
    }

A player can be dead while their team remains alive whenever another teammate
survives. In that supported state, `getSplitEmpirePlayer` selects the slot precisely
because the PLAYER is dead, but `splitEmpire` sees `bPlayerExists == true` precisely
because the TEAM is alive. The debug assertion fails and, in release builds, the
entire colony-initialization block is skipped.

The function does NOT abort after that mismatch. It proceeds to transfer cities,
culture and free defenders to the selected dead player.

DETERMINISTIC STATE / REPRODUCTION SHAPE
----------------------------------------
Use a team game or scenario with the following state:

1. All player slots have been ever-alive, so `getSplitEmpirePlayer` cannot find a
   `!isEverAlive()` slot.
2. Human player P can create a colony from an overseas area containing at least two
   P cities (the ordinary `canSplitArea` requirement for a dead recipient).
3. Player X was eliminated, but X had teammate Y and Y is still alive. Therefore:

       X.isAlive() == false
       GET_TEAM(X).isAlive() == true

4. X is the first dead ever-alive player found by the player iterator.
5. At least one valid civilization/leader combination has never been used, so
   `getSplitEmpireLeaders` allows colony creation.
6. P chooses "Create Colony" for the eligible area.

`getSplitEmpirePlayer` returns X. `splitEmpire` sets `bPlayerExists=true` from X's
still-alive team and skips `CvGame::addPlayer` and every new-colony setup step.
Nevertheless the later city loop executes:

    GET_PLAYER(eNewPlayer).acquireCity(...);

and the free-defender loop creates units in those transferred cities for X.

REVIVAL TIMING IS SOURCE-PROVEN
-------------------------------
Neither `CvPlayer::acquireCity` / `initCity` nor the free-defender creation in this
path makes the recipient player alive immediately. The split therefore finishes with
X still dead but now owning cities (and normally units).

The ordinary game-update path then executes:

    CvGame::updateUnprofiled()
        -> testAlive()
            -> GET_PLAYER(eLoopPlayer).verifyAlive()

`CvPlayer::verifyAlive` explicitly revives any dead player who now owns a city or unit:

    if (!isAlive())
    {
        if (getNumCities() > 0 || getNumUnits() > 0)
            setAlive(true);
        return;
    }

Thus the recycled old player is deterministically resurrected on the next normal
update from the possessions that `splitEmpire` just gave them.

WHAT IS SKIPPED / MALFORMED
---------------------------
Because `bPlayerExists` was true, the revived player never went through the intended
new-colony initialization:

* no `CvGame::addPlayer(eNewPlayer, eBestLeader, eBestCiv)`;
* no `CvPlayer::initInGame` reset/reinitialization performed by `addPlayer`;
* no new colony civilization/leader selection;
* no `setParent(getID())` for the splitting civilization;
* no inheritance of the parent's technologies / no-trade-tech flags;
* no `assignVassal(..., false)` establishing the intended colonial-vassal team;
* no new-player replay/message setup guarded by `!bPlayerExists`.

Instead X retains the old defeated player's persistent identity/state and remains a
member of X's old still-alive team. Once `verifyAlive` resurrects X, the supposed
"colony" is therefore an old civilization/player revived on its former team rather
than a freshly initialized colonial vassal of P.

Any old `parent` value also remains whatever the defeated player had; the intended
new parent is not installed.

CURRENT SAS REACHABILITY
------------------------
Current SAS has:

    MAX_CIV_PLAYERS = 48
    36 CivilizationInfos with bPlayable=1 and bAIPlayable=1
    55 unique leaders mapped to those playable civilizations

With an ordinary fully-random 48-player setup, AdvCiv's random assignment tends to
spread players across all available civilizations before duplicating them, which can
consume every civilization and leave no valid unused colony civ. That masks this
specific fallback in that common setup.

It does NOT establish an engine invariant. Scenario/custom initialization can reuse
civilizations; `CvInitCore::setCiv` simply installs the requested CivilizationTypes
and has no uniqueness check. Current WorldBuilder/scenario player data can therefore
use all 48 player slots while repeating some civilizations and leaving another
playable civilization plus at least one of its leaders unused.

Because SAS has 55 mapped playable leaders, it is straightforward to reserve a valid
leader for the unused civilization while populating the other 48 ever-alive slots.
After one member of a multi-player team is eliminated, the exact dead-player /
live-team state above is reachable and the colony command remains source-legal.

So this is not merely a hypothetical future-data condition; it is a supported
scenario/team-game lifecycle defect. It is rarer in ordinary random games under the
48-slot SAS configuration than it was under stock BtS's smaller player cap.

ANCESTRY
--------
The root predates AdvCiv.

Stock BtS/Civ4CE already does both halves:

* `getSplitEmpirePlayer` first searches never-alive players and then recycles any
  `!GET_PLAYER(i).isAlive()` slot;
* `splitEmpire` then computes:

      bool bPlayerExists =
          GET_TEAM(GET_PLAYER(eNewPlayer).getTeam()).isAlive();
      FAssert(!bPlayerExists);

  and only calls `addPlayer` / parent-tech-vassal setup when that TEAM is dead.

K-Mod 1.46 retains the same mismatch.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same split logic. Its `<kekm.24>` change does NOT
introduce the player/team mismatch; it merely recognizes that "Reusing a defeated
player might not work correctly" and restricts the fallback to human players so AI
players cannot trigger the risky recycling path automatically.

Current SAS retains that AdvCiv behavior.

DUPLICATE / ALBUM CHECK
-----------------------
The album's existing Free Colony finding F317/KI#640 is a different root: its popup
names a liberation recipient at launch but sends only a city/area action and later
recomputes the recipient, allowing stale UI approval to retarget to another civ.
That finding explicitly established that the `splitEmpire` receiver rechecks the area
and general split legality; it does not audit the lifecycle semantics of the recycled
player slot selected by `getSplitEmpirePlayer`.

No existing album root covers:

* dead PlayerTypes whose TeamTypes remains alive;
* `getSplitEmpirePlayer` player-state selection versus `splitEmpire` team-state
  `bPlayerExists`;
* skipped `addPlayer/initInGame` for a recycled colony slot;
* revival by `verifyAlive` after transferred cities are assigned to the dead slot.

F447 is therefore independent.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
The "new colony needs initialization" decision must be based on the PLAYER SLOT that
was selected for recycling, not merely on whether that slot's old team still happens
to have another living member.

The safest repair is probably to treat every selected `!isAlive()` recycled player as
requiring full recycled-player initialization, while also handling its old live-team
membership explicitly before `addPlayer/initInGame` rather than assuming a recycled
slot's team is dead.

At minimum, do NOT allow this sequence:

    dead player selected -> old team alive -> skip initialization -> transfer cities

Possible conservative policies include:

1. Reject dead-player recycling when `GET_TEAM(eNewPlayer).isAlive()` and return
   `NO_PLAYER` / disable the colony choice. This is narrow and avoids having to detach
   a recycled player from a still-active team.
2. If supporting such recycling is desirable, explicitly move/reset the slot onto a
   proper new colony team and run the same `addPlayer/initInGame`, parent, technology
   and vassal initialization as other recycled slots before any city transfer.

The existing `FAssert(!bPlayerExists)` is useful evidence of the intended invariant
but is not a release guard. Turn it into enforced runtime handling rather than
continuing with malformed state when the assertion condition fails.

Regression coverage should include a dead member of a still-alive team selected as
the first recyclable slot, followed by a human colony split. The result should either
be rejected cleanly or produce a fully initialized new colonial vassal; it must never
revive the old player/team identity from the transferred cities.

NUMBERING
---------

F448 / provisional KI#771 is the next unused root slot.

C031-WIP156 — QUEUE 004 CVPLAYER.CPP CONTINUATION — F448 / KI#771 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

POST-WIP155 CONTROL: `CvPlayer::setStartingPlot`
-------------------------------------------------
The second-pass low-coverage inventory first exposed a genuine mutation-order flaw in
`setStartingPlot` when `bUpdateStartDist` is true:

* while removing an old start, the function decrements the old area's start count;
* it then calls `GC.getMap().updateMinOriginalStartDist(oldArea)` BEFORE assigning
  `m_pStartingPlot = pNewValue`;
* the recalculation iterates current player `getStartingPlot()` values and therefore
  still sees/re-adds this player's old starting plot;
* after `m_pStartingPlot` changes, only the NEW area is recalculated.

Thus a cross-area start move can leave the old area's `MinOriginalStartDist` cache
stale.

This was NOT numbered. Current normal-game consumers are the Boreal, Highlands and
Rainforest map scripts, and their start-assignment loops assign each player's first
start from NULL. Current C++ start-moving callers use the default
`bUpdateStartDist=false`. No ordinary supported current gameplay consumer was found
that performs the problematic old-start -> different-area transition while asking for
this cache update. Keep as API/WorldBuilder robustness debt, not F448.


F448 / KI#771 — RISE & FALL HUMAN/AI CONTROL SWITCH LEAVES CACHED SETTLER
"NEW CITY" PRODUCTION COST PRICED FOR THE PREVIOUS CONTROLLER
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED. Current normal Rise & Fall chapter transitions reach the stale cache with
current SAS data. This is an inherited AdvCiv integration regression introduced when
advc.251 made the cached Settler surcharge depend on human/AI handicap modifiers.

ROOT
----
Founding units do not obtain their city-equivalent production surcharge dynamically.
`CvPlayer::resetCivTypeEffects` and `CvPlayer::processTraits` precompute it and store it
per unit class:

    if (GC.getInfo(eUnit).isFound())
        setUnitExtraCost(kCiv.unitClass(eUnit), getNewCityProductionValue());

`CvPlayer::getProductionNeeded(UnitTypes)` later adds that cached value directly:

    iProductionNeeded += getUnitExtraCost(eUnitClass);

Current SAS `UNIT_SETTLER` has XML `iCost = 0`, so in an Ancient normal start the
Settler's production cost is effectively this cached "new city" surcharge (subject to
any later Python modifier), rather than a nonzero XML base cost.

`getNewCityProductionValue()` is controller/handicap-sensitive. It includes:

* free-start-era building production costs through `getProductionNeeded(Building)`;
* Advanced Start city cost;
* population costs through `getGrowthThreshold`, whose AI branch applies the game
  handicap's `iAIGrowthPercent` when `!isHuman()`;
* finally half of `trainingModifierFromHandicap(false)`, which also applies game
  handicap AI production modifiers when `!isHuman()`.

Therefore `isHuman()` and the player's handicap are inputs of the cached value.

RISE & FALL CHANGES BOTH INPUTS WITHOUT REFRESHING THE CACHE
-------------------------------------------------------------
`RiseFall::setPlayerControl(civId, b)` does, in order:

    setPlayerHandicap(civId, b, b);
    if (b)
        g.changeHumanPlayer(civId);
    else
        civ.setIsHuman(false, true);

`setPlayerHandicap` writes the player's handicap and updates maintenance/AI work
assignment only. `CvPlayer::setIsHuman` changes slot/human/AI state and alert/leader
state only. Neither recomputes founding-unit extra cost.

A complete current-tree search finds the actual recomputation only in:

1. `CvPlayer::processTraits`, and
2. `CvPlayer::resetCivTypeEffects`.

Normal Rise & Fall chapter transitions call `setPlayerControl` directly when the old
chapter ends and when the next civilization becomes active. `RFChapter::start`, the
welcome path and the surrounding chapter-control code do not call either refresh
function. Hence the stale value persists into ordinary production calculations.

CURRENT SAS REPRODUCTION — ANCIENT / NORMAL / MONARCH
------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS makes the difference deterministic without traits or later-era free
buildings.

Relevant current/inherited values:

    UNIT_SETTLER iCost                         = 0
    Ancient FreePopulation                    = 0
    Normal research/speed percent             = 100
    BASE_CITY_GROWTH_THRESHOLD                = 20
    CITY_GROWTH_MULTIPLIER                    = 2
    ADVANCED_START_CITY_COST                  = 67
    ADVANCED_START_POPULATION_COST            = 150
    INITIAL_CITY_POPULATION                   = 1
    current RF_PLAYER_HANDICAP_ADJUSTMENT     = 0
    Monarch iAIGrowthPercent                  = 90
    Monarch iAITrainPercent                   = 90
    Monarch iAIConstructPercent               = 90
    human BaseGrowth/Train/Construct percents = 100

There are no Ancient `FreeStartEra` buildings in current SAS, so the simple Ancient
case begins with the city + population terms only.

Fresh HUMAN calculation on Monarch:

    growth threshold at pop 1 = 20 + 1*2 = 22
    population value          = 22 * 150% = 33
    city value                = 67
    subtotal                  = 100
    half-training adjustment  = 100%
    getNewCityProductionValue = 100

Fresh AI calculation on Monarch (AI player handicap Noble, game-handicap AI factors
90%):

    growth threshold at pop 1 = round(22 * 90%) = 20
    population value          = 20 * 150% = 30
    city value                = 67
    subtotal                  = 97
    training modifier         = 90%
    half-training factor      = 95%
    round(97 * 95%)           = 92
    getNewCityProductionValue = 92

Thus a normal Rise & Fall handoff can produce both directions:

AI -> HUMAN chapter start
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The civilization had its founding-unit surcharge cached as 92 while AI-controlled.
`setPlayerControl(..., true)` changes handicap/human status, but no refresh follows.
The now-human player can therefore continue to have:

    getProductionNeeded(UNIT_SETTLER) = 92

when the same current player state freshly evaluated should price the Settler at 100.

HUMAN -> AI chapter end
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The old chapter civilization can retain the human-priced 100 surcharge after becoming
AI-controlled, even though a fresh AI calculation is 92. Its AI Settlers can therefore
remain 8 production too expensive in this clean current example.

The exact numeric gap varies with handicap, game speed/start era and free-start-era
buildings, but the cache invariant is broken whenever the controller-sensitive inputs
change enough to alter `getNewCityProductionValue`.

The current SAS removal of the old human-only "round to multiples of 5" production
rounding does not mask the root; the current `.round()` path still yields the 100 vs
92 example above.

CALLER / GAMEPLAY SIGNIFICANCE
------------------------------
This is not a stale tooltip-only number. `CvPlayer::getProductionNeeded(UnitTypes)` is
the authoritative unit production-cost calculation used by cities/AI and directly
adds `getUnitExtraCost(eUnitClass)`.

Because the current Settler XML base production cost is zero, this cache is especially
important: the cached city-equivalent surcharge supplies the Settler's actual base
production requirement.

Normal Rise & Fall chapter progression repeatedly performs the relevant transitions:

* at a chapter end, `setPlayerControl(currentChapterCiv, false)`;
* when the chosen next civ becomes active, `setPlayerControl(nextCiv, true)`.

No debug/Civ-Changer path is needed for reproduction.

ANCESTRY / INTRODUCING CHANGE
-----------------------------
K-Mod 1.46 already caches `getNewCityProductionValue()` in `m_aUnitExtraCosts`, but
its `getNewCityProductionValue()` does NOT apply the later advc.251 human/AI training
adjustment. The cached value therefore did not acquire this controller-switch
invariant from K-Mod.

AdvCiv practical 1268 / commit:

    e11525d3039c7b1baf017b3f5a25a963a8abef50
    "v0.89rc ... New game option 'Rise & Fall' added ..."

introduced Rise & Fall and its civilization-control switching. At that point the
K-Mod-style new-city value was still not controller-sensitive in the later advc.251
way, so this specific root was not yet present.

AdvCiv practical 1407 / commit:

    bf48af8b3529f23c93ddbf21fde05e6b4ad8539a
    2019-01-21 — "Many misc. tweaks"

introduced the regression. Its commit message explicitly says:

    "Production modifiers from difficulty only apply half to Settler units."

and the introducing diff changes `getNewCityProductionValue()` by adding:

    iValue = roundToMultiple(iValue *
        (1 + 0.5 * (trainingModifierFromHandicap(false) - 1)),
        isHuman() ? 5 : 1);

while also moving the cached unit extra cost after the ordinary unit handicap
multiplier so this city-equivalent portion gets the special half modifier.

That commit touched `RiseFall.cpp` only for unrelated capital-coordinate visibility
text and added no cache refresh to `setPlayerControl`. Thus practical 1407 made an
existing cached value depend on exactly the human/AI state that Rise & Fall changes,
without adding the required invalidation/recompute step.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the controller-sensitive calculation and the missing Rise &
Fall refresh. Current SAS retains the same semantic structure (with later arithmetic
refactors/current handicap XML).

DUPLICATE / ALBUM CHECK
-----------------------
The album contains no prior Rise & Fall / Settler unit-extra-cost cache root.

The earlier literal "Finance unit extra cost" control in Queue 003 concerns
`UnitInfo::iExtraCost` XML scaling in Finance help and is explicitly data-dormant; it
is unrelated to the per-unit-class `m_aUnitExtraCosts` city-equivalent founding-unit
surcharge audited here.

No existing R&F finding covers production-cost cache refresh after human/AI chapter
control changes.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Centralize the founding-unit surcharge refresh rather than duplicating the current
loops. For example, a small `updateNewCityProductionValue()`/`updateFoundingUnitExtraCosts()`
helper can iterate the civilization's founding units and execute:

    setUnitExtraCost(unitClass, getNewCityProductionValue());

Then call it whenever an input of `getNewCityProductionValue()` changes outside the
existing trait/civilization reset paths.

For this root, the most important transition is AFTER the final human/AI state is
installed in `CvPlayer::setIsHuman`, because Rise & Fall deliberately changes the
handicap first and human status second. Recomputing after `setIsHuman` therefore sees
both final inputs.

For robustness, player-handicap changes that do not also change human status can alter
the same cached value. `RiseFall::setPlayerHandicap` currently even comments
"Further updates might be warranted." A dedicated refresh callable from both
handicap-change and human-state-change paths would make that dependency explicit and
also support nonzero `RF_PLAYER_HANDICAP_ADJUSTMENT` cleanly. Avoid unnecessary double
refresh in the paired Rise & Fall transition if desired by choosing one final
controller-switch hook or by structuring the helper/caller sequence accordingly.

Regression tests should cover both chapter directions at a difficulty where AI
production/growth modifiers differ from 100:

1. record a civ's `getUnitExtraCost(UNITCLASS_SETTLER)` while AI-controlled;
2. hand control to the human through normal R&F `setPlayerControl`;
3. assert cached extra cost equals a fresh `getNewCityProductionValue()`;
4. relinquish control and assert equality again under AI state.

On current Ancient/Normal/Monarch data, the clean expected fresh values are 92 for AI
and 100 for human.

NUMBERING
---------
F448 is CONFIRMED and consumes KI#771.
F449 / provisional KI#772 is the next unused root slot.

POST-WIP156 CLEAN CONTROLS

1. Great General / Great Person threshold counters
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
`CvPlayer::setCombatExperience` safely handles threshold overshoot: after spawning a
Great General it recursively calls itself with the remaining combat XP, so an input
large enough to cross more than one threshold can continue through successive
thresholds. Current combat awards are normally much smaller in any case.

The player+team Great Person / Great General threshold-modifier increments in

counter/double-count root was established there.

The Defensive Pact stale-offer check initially looked suspicious because it checks

F449 / KI#772 — GP BIRTH MESSAGE IS MUTATED BY ONE HIDDEN OBSERVER AND LEAKS THAT
FALLBACK INTO LATER VISIBLE OBSERVERS
===============================================================================

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED current inherited AdvCiv player-facing message-state defect.

Current SAS and Base AdvCiv 1.14 retain it. BtS/K-Mod do not have the defect in this
form. The regression is introduced by AdvCiv's advc.106 Great-Person birth-message
privacy integration and is already present in the reachable practical-1253 initial
AdvCiv history snapshot.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayer::createGreatPeople` constructs one detailed non-replay GP birth message
before iterating observers:

    CvWString szMessage;
    ...
    if (pCity != NULL)
        szMessage = TXT_KEY_MISC_GP_BORN(... city ...);
    else
        szMessage = TXT_KEY_MISC_GP_BORN_FIELD(...);

It then reuses that SAME mutable string for every observer:

    for (PlayerIter<MAJOR_CIV,KNOWN_TO> it(kGPOwner.getTeam()); it.hasNext(); ++it)
    {
        CvPlayer const& kObs = *it;
        bool const bRev = (... observer can see birth location ...);
        if (!bRev)
        {
            szMessage = gDLL->getText("TXT_KEY_MISC_GP_BORN_CIV", ...);
        }
        ...
        gDLL->UI().addMessage(kObs.getID(), ..., szMessage, ...,
                bRev ? kAt.getX() : -1, bRev ? kAt.getY() : -1, bRev, bRev);
    }

The hidden-observer branch permanently overwrites `szMessage` with the less-specific
"GP born in [civilization]" text. There is no corresponding branch that restores the
detailed city/field message when a LATER observer can reveal the location.

Consequently observer A's visibility state changes observer B's message text.

CURRENT CLEAN REPRODUCTION
--------------------------
No unusual XML, scenario scripting or EXE callback ordering is required.

Example:

* Player 2 owns the city in which the Great Person is born.
* Player 0 has met Player 2's team, so Player 0 belongs to the `KNOWN_TO` iterator,
  but Player 0 has not revealed the GP city / plot.
* Player 2 of course can reveal its own city and birth plot.

The cached major-alive player sequences are kept in ascending PlayerTypes order.
`PlayerIter<MAJOR_CIV,KNOWN_TO>` therefore visits the lower-ID Player 0 before the
higher-ID owner Player 2.

For Player 0:

    bRev == false

so the shared message is overwritten with `TXT_KEY_MISC_GP_BORN_CIV`.

Later, for Player 2:

    bRev == true

but the code does not reconstruct the detailed message. Player 2 therefore receives
the civ-only fallback text that was created for Player 0.

The inconsistency is especially visible because the SAME `addMessage` call still
passes the real birth coordinates and reveal/link booleans for Player 2:

    bRev ? kAt.getX() : -1
    bRev ? kAt.getY() : -1
    bRev
    bRev

Thus the owner can receive a location-enabled announcement whose text nevertheless
claims only the civilization-level location because an earlier observer could not see
the city.

The owner need not be the affected visible observer. Any later observer with location
visibility can inherit the fallback after an earlier hidden observer. Using the owner
simply gives the strongest deterministic visibility invariant.

ITERATOR / OWN-VISIBILITY PROOF
-------------------------------
`AgentPredicates.h` explicitly documents `KNOWN_TO` as:

    "Incl. the first agent's team (agents know themselves)"

so the GP owner's own team is part of this observer sequence.

`CvAgents` stores these player sequences ordered by player ID. `insertIntoVector`
walks until it encounters a greater ID and inserts before it, preserving ascending
`getID()` order. Normal `MAJOR_ALIVE` construction follows player-ID order as well.

A city also establishes sight for its owning team as part of ordinary city/plot
visibility processing. The detailed observer condition requires both the plot and,
when present, the city to be revealed; the owner satisfies that condition for its own
ordinary GP city. No speculative UI ordering is therefore involved in the repro.

ANCESTRY / INTRODUCING CHANGE
-----------------------------
BtS/K-Mod keep the detailed message immutable across observers. K-Mod's inherited
shape is:

    if (pPlot->isRevealed(observerTeam, false))
        addHumanMessage(... szReplayMessage ...);
    else
    {
        CvWString szMessage = TXT_KEY_MISC_GP_BORN_SOMEWHERE(...);
        addHumanMessage(... szMessage ...);
    }

The hidden fallback is a LOCAL string in the hidden branch. It cannot contaminate a
later visible observer.

AdvCiv practical 1253 / reachable initial-history commit:

    f6ff6a182f...

contains the advc.106 integration that introduces `TXT_KEY_MISC_GP_BORN_CIV` and,
critically, changes the observer loop to write that fallback directly into the shared
`szReplayMessage`:

    if (!isRev)
    {
        if (isMet)
            szReplayMessage = gDLL->getText("TXT_KEY_MISC_GP_BORN_CIV", ...);
        else continue;
    }
    ... addHumanMessage(... szReplayMessage ...);

That is the regression point visible in the reachable AdvCiv history: privacy was
improved from "somewhere" to civilization-level information for met observers, but
the fallback was no longer kept observer-local.

AdvCiv practical 1268 later renames/reuses the shared variable as `szMessage`; the
same mutation remains.

Most notably, practical 2188 / commit:

    66a705a7830c6df13301724d874f69ba792d054e
    "Fix minor info leak in GP birth messages"

changes the observer loop to `PlayerIter<MAJOR_CIV,KNOWN_TO>` and strengthens `bRev`
so a city birth requires the city itself to be revealed too. That privacy fix is
correct in isolation, but it retains:

    if (!bRev)
        szMessage = TXT_KEY_MISC_GP_BORN_CIV(...);

followed by unconditional reuse of `szMessage`. It therefore does not fix the
cross-observer state contamination; by creating more legitimate `bRev == false`
cases for partially revealed cities, it makes the importance of keeping the fallback
observer-local even clearer.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain this exact shared-mutation structure.

DUPLICATE / ALBUM CHECK
-----------------------
No prior album finding covers Great-Person birth-message cross-observer state.

The nearest literal observer-message material is an unrelated nuke hidden-nationality
information leak. That concerns identifying real unit civilizations in nuke messages,
not mutation/reuse of a GP observer-specific message string.

No prior `createGreatPeople`, GP-birth, or `TXT_KEY_MISC_GP_BORN*` root owns this
behavior.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Keep the detailed message immutable and choose an observer-specific message without
mutating shared state.

For example:

    CvWString const szDetailedMessage = ... city/field message ...;
    CvWString const szCivMessage = gDLL->getText(
            "TXT_KEY_MISC_GP_BORN_CIV", ...);

    for (... observers ...)
    {
        bool const bRev = ...;
        CvWString const& szObsMessage = (bRev ? szDetailedMessage : szCivMessage);
        gDLL->UI().addMessage(..., szObsMessage, ...);
    }

The exact implementation can avoid constructing the fallback until first needed if
that matters, but the important invariant is that one observer must never mutate the
message subsequently used for another observer.

Regression test:

1. lower-ID observer has met the GP owner but cannot reveal the GP birth city;
2. higher-ID GP owner can reveal its own city;
3. generate a city-born GP;
4. assert lower observer receives the civilization-only fallback and no coordinates;
5. assert owner receives the detailed city message and real coordinates.

Also test the inverse player-ID ordering to ensure each observer's text depends only
on that observer's own `bRev`, never on whoever happened to be visited earlier.

CONTROL — GOLDEN-AGE READINESS UNITCLASS VS CONSUMPTION UNITTYPE IS CURRENT-DATA MASKED
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
K-Mod intentionally changed `unitsGoldenAgeReady()` to require distinct Great Person
`UnitClassTypes`, but `killGoldenAgeUnits()` still records already-consumed kinds by
`UnitTypes`. In a mod with multiple Golden-Age-capable unit types mapped to the same
Great Person class, readiness and consumption could therefore disagree.

Current SAS data masks the mismatch: the Golden-Age-capable Great People are exactly
one unit type per Great Person class (Prophet, Artist, Scientist, Merchant, Engineer,
Spy), and current CivilizationInfos provides no alternate same-class Golden-Age unit
mapping. No current execution state was established in which the two definitions
diverge. Keep as latent robustness/data-extension debt; not F450.

CONTROL — TEAM EVENT PROPAGATION BRANCH IS A REAL ADVCIV REFACTOR REGRESSION, BUT DORMANT
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
`CvPlayer::setEventOccured` currently contains:

    else if (GC.getInfo(eEvent).isTeam())
    {
        for (MemberIter itOtherMember(getTeam()); itOtherMember.hasNext(); ++itOtherMember)
        {
            if (itOtherMember->getID() != getID())
                continue;
            itOtherMember->setEventOccured(..., false);
        }
    }

The predicate is inverted for propagation: it discards every teammate except self.
K-Mod's corresponding loop is correct (`i != getID()` -> propagate to other team
members). Reachable-history commit practical 2416, SHA
`b9b15b001b7f47a1bef8f264332988026f87dedb`, title "Use EnumMap in CvPlayer; and
other refactoring changes", introduced the MemberIter rewrite and the inverted
predicate directly.

However, current SAS EventInfo and EventTriggerInfo XML contains no `<bTeam>1</bTeam>`
entry at all. The broken EventInfo::isTeam branch therefore has no current data
producer. Preserve as a genuine dormant AdvCiv regression, but do not spend F450.

CONTROL — AI PLAYER-LEVEL WORK-RATE PREDICTOR CONTAINS DUPLICATE +100, NORMAL CALLERS MASK IT
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Current/Base AdvCiv `CvPlayer::getWorkRate(BuildTypes)` has an AI branch equivalent to

    iRate *= max(0, 100 + AIWorkRateModifier + 100);

whereas actual `CvUnit::workRate` and K-Mod use the normal single
`100 + AIWorkRateModifier`. Current handicap AIWorkRateModifier values are 0, so the
player-level helper would predict double ordinary AI worker rate if its AI branch were
used. Normal runtime worker progress uses unit workRate; the player helper's internal
uses are human-facing build prediction / a human selection-group finish check. No
ordinary shipped gameplay mismatch was established. AI-Auto-Play active-player UI is
a possible robustness edge still worth remembering, but not presently a numbered root.

LIVE LOW-SEVERITY CANDIDATE — POSTPROCESSMESSAGES DISCOUNTS ONE REAL MESSAGE WHEN NO TECH IS PERSISTENT
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
`CvPlayer::postProcessMessages` contains the advc.106b heuristic:

    // Finishing a tech should generate a message ... don't count it ...
    if (getCurrentResearch() == NO_TECH)
        m_iNewMessages--;

This was introduced in the initial advc.106b implementation (reachable history already
contains the line in practical 1253 / `f6ff6a182f...`). The condition is only a proxy
for "a technology just finished". A human can persistently have `NO_TECH` without a
new completion message — the cleanest current case is after all researchable
technologies are already known. `doResearch` then fails to choose a target and retains
NO_TECH, while unrelated INFO/MINOR/MAJOR interturn messages still increment
m_iNewMessages normally.

At the next active turn, postProcessMessages subtracts one anyway. Therefore exactly
`MessageLimit + 1` genuine qualifying messages are treated as only `MessageLimit` and
can fail the `m_iNewMessages > iLimit` auto-open test. The underlying Turn Log entries
are not lost; only the auto-open heuristic is wrong. This is current and deterministic
but low-severity/UI-only, so F450 is intentionally still unused while higher-value
state/arithmetic functions are audited.

---------------------
`CvPlayer::canTrigger` was reconciled with its caller in `initTriggeredData`: it is
invoked on each candidate OTHER player, with the originating player passed as ePlayer.
Thus its `OtherPlayerHasTech` test against `this->getTeam()` correctly refers to the
candidate other player's team; no actor/target inversion was established.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHY F445 DOES NOT SURVIVE THE CROSS-FILE INVALIDATION PROOF
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP153 correctly observed that capital status participates directly in
`CvCity::getBaseYieldRateModifier`:

    if (isCapital())
        iModifier += GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).getCapitalYieldRateModifier(eYield);

and correctly noted that Bureaucracy makes a capital relocation change current
Production yield in ordinary current data.

The earlier proof then incorrectly concluded that `CvPlayer::setCapital` refreshed
only commerce and therefore failed to invalidate cached Production-yield ranks.

The missing downstream step is the exact implementation of the refresh that
`setCapital` calls.

Current `CvPlayer::setCapital` does:

    if (pOldCapital != NULL)
        pOldCapital->updateCommerce();
    if (pNewCapital != NULL)
        pNewCapital->updateCommerce();

The no-argument `CvCity::updateCommerce()` begins with:

    GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).invalidateYieldRankCache();

before looping over commerce types.

That player-level invalidation reaches every city and invalidates both base-yield and
yield-rate rank caches for every YieldTypes value. Thus the capital transition itself
already satisfies the cache-maintenance contract that WIP153 thought was missing.

A Bureaucracy Palace relocation therefore behaves as follows:

1. capital identity changes;
2. old/new actual Production modifiers change dynamically through `isCapital()`;
3. `setCapital` calls `updateCommerce()` on the old capital;
4. that call invalidates the player's complete yield-rank cache;
5. the next `findYieldRateRank(YIELD_PRODUCTION)` recomputes the city ordering from
   the post-relocation rates.

There is no stale Production-rank window under this source path.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
HOW THE CORRECTION SURFACED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The F450 low-coverage pass reopened Golden-Age/base-yield updates and followed
`CvPlot::updateYield -> CvCity::changeBaseYieldRate -> setBaseYieldRate ->
updateCommerce()`. That exposed the otherwise easy-to-miss fact that the no-argument
commerce refresh is deliberately also a global yield-rank invalidation point.
Rechecking `setCapital` against that exact callee invalidated WIP153's root.

This is a useful cross-file methodology control: a setter's call-site name is not
sufficient evidence about what caches it refreshes; the complete callee body must be
traced before declaring a missing invalidation.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F450 / KI#773 — `CvPlayer::getUnitLayerColors` computes military Globe-layer
strength as HP / (maxHP * baseCombatStr) instead of (HP / maxHP) * baseCombatStr
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

CURRENT SAS CODE
----------------
In all three Globe unit-layer modes that accumulate a numeric military strength —
`SHOW_ALL_MILITARY`, `SHOW_TEAM_MILITARY`, and `SHOW_ENEMIES` — current SAS does:

    fPlotStrength += pUnit->currHitPoints() /
            (float)(pUnit->maxHitPoints() *
            pUnit->baseCombatStr());

The same code is present in Base AdvCiv 1.14.

K-Mod instead uses the expected expression:

    fPlotStrength += ((float)pUnit->currHitPoints() /
            (float)pUnit->maxHitPoints() *
            (float)pUnit->baseCombatStr());

The important difference is not cosmetic parenthesization. Current AdvCiv/SAS divide
by combat strength where the inherited calculation multiplies by it.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DETERMINISTIC CURRENT LAND-UNIT REPRODUCTION
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS XML gives ordinary live examples:

    UNIT_WARRIOR   iCombat = 3
    UNIT_TANK      iCombat = 30

At full health, the intended/K-Mod contribution is therefore:

    Warrior: (100 / 100) * 3  = 3
    Tank:    (100 / 100) * 30 = 30

Current AdvCiv/SAS instead computes:

    Warrior: 100 / (100 * 3)  = 1/3
    Tank:    100 / (100 * 30) = 1/30

So, for equal-health single-unit plots, the Globe layer considers the Warrior's
numeric plot strength ten times the Tank's. The ordering is exactly backwards.

The function then normalizes each visible plot against the global maximum:

    fAlpha = (fPlotStrength / fMaxPlotStrength * 0.75f + 0.25f) * 0.8f;

With one visible full-health Warrior plot and one full-health Tank plot:

    current bad formula:
        Warrior alpha = 0.80
        Tank alpha    = (0.1 * 0.75 + 0.25) * 0.8 = 0.26

    intended/K-Mod formula:
        Tank alpha    = 0.80
        Warrior alpha = (0.1 * 0.75 + 0.25) * 0.8 = 0.26

Thus the map visualization does not merely have an imprecise scale. It visually ranks
weaker land units/plots as stronger than stronger ones. Stacks likewise sum reciprocal
base strengths rather than actual damaged base strength.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
AIR-UNIT CONSEQUENCE / SECONDARY STRENGTHENING
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
AdvCiv's surrounding code deliberately classifies military units through:

    pUnit->canCombat();

and `CvUnit::canCombat()` is:

    return (baseCombatStr() > 0 || airBaseCombatStr() > 0 || isNuke());

Current SAS aircraft use the separate air-strength field and have zero ordinary
`baseCombatStr`. Verified current examples include:

    Fighter         iCombat = 0, iAirCombat = 12
    Jet Fighter     iCombat = 0, iAirCombat = 24
    Bomber          iCombat = 0, iAirCombat = 16
    Stealth Bomber  iCombat = 0, iAirCombat = 20

Those units therefore pass the `bMilitary` test but reach a denominator containing
`baseCombatStr() == 0` in the bad formula.

The land-unit inversion above is already sufficient to confirm F450 and does not rely
on platform floating-point divide-by-zero behavior. On the normal masked x86 floating
point environment, a positive float divided by zero may become infinity, which can
also poison `fMaxPlotStrength`/normalization; however that stronger platform-specific
manifestation is not needed for the root.

There is also an older independent design limitation in the pre-regression expression:
using only `baseCombatStr()` means aircraft contribute zero rather than their actual
air strength. The practical-2416 regression makes that old limitation worse by moving
zero into the denominator. Do not conflate fixing the introduced land arithmetic
regression with deciding whether the Globe layer should additionally use
`airBaseCombatStr()` for aircraft.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CALLER / PLAYER-VISIBLE REACHABILITY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This is the normal active-player Globe View path, not debug-only code:

    CvPlayer::getGlobeLayerColors(...)
        case GLOBE_LAYER_UNIT:
            getUnitLayerColors((GlobeLayerUnitOptionTypes)iOption, ...);

`getUnitLayerColors` fills the Globe-layer per-plot colors and unit indicators. The
wrong `fPlotStrength` directly determines the color alpha in the ordinary Unit Globe
layer for the affected modes.

No special scenario, AI-only path, future XML, assertion build, or uncommon team setup
is required. A visible Warrior and Tank are enough to produce the reversed intensity.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
INTRODUCTION / ANCESTRY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The exact regression is visible in the supplied AdvCiv practical-2416 diff:

    practical 2416
    SHA b9b15b001b7f47a1bef8f264332988026f87dedb
    "Use EnumMap in CvPlayer; and other refactoring changes."

Before that refactor, the expression was:

    fPlotStrength += ((float)pUnit->currHitPoints() /
            (float)pUnit->maxHitPoints() *
            (float)pUnit->baseCombatStr());

Practical 2416 rewrote it to:

    fPlotStrength += pUnit->currHitPoints() /
            (float)(pUnit->maxHitPoints() *
            pUnit->baseCombatStr());

The same edit was made in the `SHOW_ALL_MILITARY`, `SHOW_TEAM_MILITARY`, and
`SHOW_ENEMIES` branches. There is no corresponding gameplay-rule change that could
justify taking the reciprocal of combat strength; this sits inside a broad refactor
commit and is a straightforward parenthesization/arithmetic regression.

K-Mod retains the correct multiply-by-strength expression. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
current SAS retain the practical-2416 bad denominator unchanged.

The same practical-2416 audit also found the separate inverted `setEventOccured`
Team-event member predicate preserved in WIP158, but current SAS has no Team EventInfo
or Team EventTriggerInfo producer. F450 is different: the Globe-layer arithmetic is
live under current ordinary data and UI.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DUPLICATE / ALBUM RECONCILIATION
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A literal and semantic album search found no existing root for:

    getUnitLayerColors
    fPlotStrength
    Globe military/unit-layer strength normalization
    SHOW_ALL_MILITARY / SHOW_TEAM_MILITARY / SHOW_ENEMIES

Earlier album material involving aircraft/baseCombatStr belongs to different roots or
controls (AI effective-strength/debug/attack-order contracts and the mixed-group Nuke
help finding). None covers this Globe View reciprocal-strength arithmetic.

Therefore F450/KI#773 is independent.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
REPAIR DIRECTION
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The conservative regression repair is to restore the inherited/K-Mod multiplication:

    fPlotStrength += (float)pUnit->currHitPoints() /
            (float)pUnit->maxHitPoints() *
            (float)pUnit->baseCombatStr();

in all three strength-accumulating branches.

That repairs the confirmed land-unit inversion and removes the newly introduced
zero-denominator problem while preserving the pre-practical-2416 behavior exactly.

A separate optional follow-up can make the AdvCiv air-inclusive `canCombat()` change
internally consistent by selecting an appropriate air strength when
`baseCombatStr()==0` (for example using `airBaseCombatStr()` for true aircraft). That
would be a broader correctness improvement, not required to prove or minimally fix the
practical-2416 regression itself.

CURRENT STONE AFTER C031-WIP160

===============================================================================
C031-WIP161 — QUEUE 004 CvPlayer.cpp — POST-F450 PRACTICAL-2416 / EVENT CLEAN TRANCHE
===============================================================================
Date: 2026-08-31
Status: Queue 004 OPEN. F451 / provisional KI#774 remains UNUSED.
No repository source files modified.

This checkpoint preserves the first post-F450 closure tranche. Its purpose is not to
manufacture a finding after the strong practical-2416 Globe regression; it records
which nearby refactor-looking candidates were traced through full current semantics
and rejected, so they do not get rediscovered later.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PRACTICAL-2416 ACCESSOR RELOCATION CONTROL — BARBARIAN UNIT UPKEEP
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The practical-2416 refactor appears at first glance to have removed meaningful logic
when `CvPlayer::getGoldPerUnit()` and `getGoldPerMilitaryUnit()` were moved to raw
one-line member getters. Older code returned 0 directly for Barbarians.

The whole introducing hunk shows that this was intentional relocation, not semantic
loss. `CvPlayer::initOtherData()` now initializes the ordinary per-unit rate with:

    changeGoldPerUnit(isBarbarian() ? 0 : iINITIAL_GOLD_PER_UNIT);

The current source retains an explicit AdvCiv comment explaining that the former
Barbarian special case had been implemented in the getters and was moved here; it
also records that the analogous military getter guard was considered unnecessary.
Current Barbarian initialization leaves the stored rates at the intended zero values.

Therefore the raw current getters do not establish F451.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PRACTICAL-2416 HISTORICAL GLOBAL-BUILDING ITERATOR REGRESSION — ALREADY REPAIRED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The same large refactor historically contained a genuine iterator conversion defect
in global-building trigger counting: an initially converted expression used an
unqualified/current-player building count where the loop player's count was intended.
Current SAS no longer contains that form. Its trigger scan correctly calls the loop
player (`itPlayer->getBuildingClassCount(...)`).

This is useful refactor-lineage evidence but repaired history, not a present root.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
EVENT-EXPIRATION SUBJECT/HOLDER ASYMMETRY — CURRENT DATA MASKS IT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::checkExpireEvent` is internally asymmetric for quests copied between
players. Most quest-expiration predicates deliberately inspect the originating player
stored in `kTriggeredData.m_ePlayer` (`kPlayer`) — state religion, civic, city, unit,
other player/city. The obsolete-tech branch instead tests:

    GET_TEAM(getTeam()).isHasTech(...)

where `getTeam()` is the player object that currently holds the copied event record.
If a Quest EventInfo were also Global, two holders of the same originating event could
therefore expire it according to different teams' technology states.

Current XML masks the path cleanly: a mechanical EventInfo parse finds ZERO entries
with both:

    <bQuest>1</bQuest>
    <bGlobal>1</bGlobal>

Global EventInfos are non-quests and return from `checkExpireEvent` through the
short-lived non-quest branch before obsolete-tech processing. Current Quest EventInfos
are local, so holder and originator are the same player for the relevant state.

This remains an API/robustness asymmetry, not current F451.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TEAM EVENT PROPAGATION REGRESSION REMAINS DATA-DORMANT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The previously preserved practical-2416 inversion in `setEventOccured` remains real:
its MemberIter loop currently `continue`s when the member is NOT self, retaining only
the originating player instead of the teammates. K-Mod/pre-refactor behavior is the
opposite and correct.

Current SAS still has no EventInfo/TriggerInfo producer with `bTeam=1`, so this branch
is not a shipped gameplay path. Keep as latent refactor debt rather than F451.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
OTHER LOW-COVERAGE CONTROLS STARTED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
* `changeGoldenAgeTurns` still follows the inherited transition contract. On entering
  or leaving a Golden Age it calls player `updateYield`; changed worked-plot yields go
  through `CvCity::changeBaseYieldRate`, which performs the normal yield-rank/cache and
  dependent-commerce updates. No F445-style missing invalidation survives that callee
  chain.
* `calculatePollution` keeps K-Mod's explicit sign convention: bad-health components
  are negative except population, and the outer subtraction converts them into
  positive pollution weights. No arithmetic sign root found.
* `isValidTriggerCorporation` retains the K-Mod correction requiring actual
  corporation presence and then independently checks Headquarters ownership when
  requested.
* `getTradeLayerColors` and the early `getCultureLayerColors` pass are visual-state
  builders using revealed/visible ownership and plot-group/culture state directly;
  no current gameplay-state contradiction established in this tranche.

===============================================================================
F451 / provisional KI#774 — countReligionSpreadUnits counts missionaries being
trained on other land areas, so area-specific AI missionary valuation can suppress
needed local missionary production
===============================================================================

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — Better BTS AI 0.83 area-filter omission inherited through K-Mod and
AdvCiv, still live in current SAS. The recent KI#668 same-team missionary valuation
repair does not create this root; it exposes the same helper more broadly and makes
its intended area-local contract especially explicit.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayer::countReligionSpreadUnits(pArea, eReligion, bIncludeTraining)` correctly
filters already-existing spread units to `pArea`:

    FOR_EACH_UNIT(pLoopUnit, *this)
    {
        if (pLoopUnit->isArea(*pArea))
        {
            if (pLoopUnit->getUnitInfo().getReligionSpreads(eReligion) > 0)
                iCount++;
        }
    }

But the BBAI `bIncludeTraining` extension then counts every city currently training a
matching missionary, with no corresponding area condition:

    if (bIncludeTraining)
    {
        FOR_EACH_CITY(pLoopCity, *this)
        {
            UnitTypes eUnit = pLoopCity->getProductionUnit();
            if (eUnit != NO_UNIT)
            {
                if (GC.getInfo(eUnit).getReligionSpreads(eReligion) > 0)
                    iCount++;
            }
        }
    }

Thus the function's two halves use incompatible geography: completed missionaries are
area-local, while queued missionaries are empire-global.

The parallel corporation helper makes the intended contract unusually clear. Its
training loop explicitly uses:

    if (pArea == NULL || pLoopCity->isArea(*pArea))

before counting an executive in production. Religion has no analogous check.

CURRENT LIVE CONSUMER
---------------------
Current `CvPlayerAI::AI_missionaryValue(eReligion, pArea)` uses the helper with
`bIncludeTraining=true` in the area-specific internal-spread calculation. After the
KI#668 repair it sums the same area-local state for every living team member:

    for (MemberIter itMember(getTeam()); itMember.hasNext(); ++itMember)
    {
        iOurCitiesHave += pArea->countHasReligion(eReligion, itMember->getID()) +
                itMember->countReligionSpreadUnits(pArea, eReligion, true);
        iOurCitiesCount += pArea->getCitiesPerPlayer(itMember->getID());
    }

Then:

    if (iOurCitiesHave < iOurCitiesCount)
        ... positive internal spread value ...
    else
        iSpreadInternalValue = 0;

`CvCityAI::AI_bestSpreadUnit` calls this area-specific value for each religion the city
can spread. If the returned value is <= 0, that religion is skipped before the city
considers a missionary unit type.

DETERMINISTIC SINGLE-PLAYER REPRODUCTION
-----------------------------------------
No team-game interaction is needed.

Let one AI player have:

* Area A with two cities, P and T;
* P already has religion R and can train R's missionary;
* T lacks R;
* Area B with another city B that is currently training an R missionary.

For Area A, the real area-local accounting is:

    cities in Area A:                2
    cities already having R:        1
    R missionaries in Area A:       0
    R missionaries training in A:   0

So Area A still has one uncovered internal spread target.

Current code instead evaluates:

    pAreaA->countHasReligion(R, player)          = 1
    countReligionSpreadUnits(AreaA, R, true)     = 1
        (the +1 incorrectly comes from city B in Area B)
    iOurCitiesHave                               = 2
    iOurCitiesCount                              = 2

Therefore `AI_missionaryValue(R, AreaA)` sets `iSpreadInternalValue = 0`.
`AI_bestSpreadUnit` in producer P then skips religion R entirely, even though T in the
same land area still lacks R and the only missionary being trained is on another land
area.

Existing completed missionaries in Area B do NOT cause this suppression because the
first half of `countReligionSpreadUnits` filters them by `pArea`. The defect is specific
to the queued-unit extension.

CURRENT-DATA REACHABILITY
-------------------------
Current SAS has the ordinary seven religion-spreading missionary unit types:

    UNIT_PAGAN_MISSIONARY
    UNIT_HINDU_MISSIONARY
    UNIT_JEWISH_MISSIONARY
    UNIT_DAOIST_MISSIONARY
    UNIT_BUDDHIST_MISSIONARY
    UNIT_CHRISTIAN_MISSIONARY
    UNIT_ISLAMIC_MISSIONARY

Each has a live `ReligionSpreads` entry. Multi-land-area empires and simultaneous city
production are ordinary supported game states, so no special option, scenario-only
caller or future XML is required.

ANCESTRY
--------
Stock BtS/Civ4CE `countReligionSpreadUnits` contains only the completed-unit area-local
loop; it has no `bIncludeTraining` parameter.

Better BTS AI 0.83 introduced the extension. Its bundled changelog states both:

    "Cities now consider how many missionaries they already have plus those being
     trained when deciding whether to train another"

and:

    "Added option to CvPlayer::countReligionSpreadUnits and
     CvPlayer::countCorporationSpreadUnits to include units being trained"

K-Mod contains that BBAI religion extension unchanged: completed missionaries are
area-filtered, but its city-training loop has no `pArea` test. K-Mod's corporation
sibling, however, explicitly filters training cities with
`pArea == NULL || pLoopCity->area() == pArea`.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the same religion omission and corporation
area check. Thus the root is an inherited BBAI 0.83 implementation oversight, not a
SAS regression.

RELATION TO KI#668 / F345
-------------------------
F345/KI#668 diagnosed a different omission in `AI_missionaryValue`: before the SAS
repair, the area branch counted only the current player's cities and therefore dropped
reachable same-team cities entirely. Its repair direction explicitly called for
summing each team member's AREA-LOCAL cities and relevant missionaries so that
teammates do not independently train for the same missing target.

F451 is the lower-level geographic counting bug inside that helper. It already affected
single-player K-Mod/AdvCiv before KI#668: a missionary queued by the same player on
Area B could suppress production on Area A. The KI#668 team loop merely causes each
member's malformed training count to be included as well.

Therefore F451 is not a duplicate or consequence of F345. Fixing F345 does not fix
F451; fixing F451 remains necessary for the repaired F345 logic to actually be
area-local.

It is also separate from F340's missionary-sea carrier validation bug, which concerns
whether a naval transport can carry missionaries at all.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Make the religion training half obey the same `pArea` scope as the completed-unit half
and the corporation sibling. Conservatively:

    FOR_EACH_CITY(pLoopCity, *this)
    {
        if (!pLoopCity->isArea(*pArea))
            continue;
        UnitTypes eUnit = pLoopCity->getProductionUnit();
        ...
    }

Because the religion helper currently dereferences `pArea` unconditionally for its
existing-unit scan, preserving its current non-NULL contract is the narrowest change.
A broader NULL-compatible refactor analogous to the corporation helper is optional and
not required to repair F451.

The corrected function then consistently answers one question: how many matching
religion-spread units already exist OR are being trained in THIS requested area.

F452 / provisional KI#775 — Culture Globe layer can write a fifth culture color into
another plot's four-color storage (and one-past-end on the final plot)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

CURRENT CODE CONTRACT
---------------------
`CvPlayer::getCultureLayerColors` hardcodes:

    const int iColorsPerPlot = 4;
    aColors.resize(kMap.numPlots() * iColorsPerPlot, ...);

So the returned vector reserves exactly four `NiColorA` entries for every plot.

The same function builds `aieOwners` for each revealed owned plot. The territorial
owner is inserted unconditionally, then (when the plot is visible) every other
EVER_ALIVE player with at least 20% of total plot culture is appended.

The source itself explicitly acknowledges that this list can exceed the storage width:

    /* Ideally ==iColorsPerPlot, but my algorithm above can't guarantee that.
       Can be 1 greater than iColorsPerPlot because the territorial owner is
       always included. */
    FAssert(aieOwners.size() <= iColorsPerPlot + 1);

Thus size 5 is considered a supported outcome by the function itself.

The write loop nevertheless uses:

    for (int i = 0;
         i < std::max(iColorsPerPlot, (int)aieOwners.size()); i++)
    {
        ...
        aColors[iPlot * iColorsPerPlot + i] = kCurColor;
        ...
    }

When `aieOwners.size() == 5`, `i == 4` writes:

    aColors[iPlot * 4 + 4]

but the four slots belonging to plot `iPlot` are only offsets 0..3.

For any non-final plot this is the FIRST culture-color slot of plot `iPlot + 1`, so the
current plot can contaminate the next plot's Globe culture coloring. If the next plot
is skipped by the later loop (for example because its revealed owner is NO_PLAYER or
its total culture is zero), the foreign color can remain visible there.

If the five-owner state occurs on the map's final plot, the same write is exactly one
past `aColors.end()`. `operator[]` performs no bounds check, so this is an actual
out-of-bounds write / undefined behavior path. The gameplay/display corruption on
non-final plots establishes the defect without relying on any particular crash or heap
behavior from the final-plot case.

CURRENT REACHABILITY
--------------------
The five-entry case is reachable under current culture semantics; it does not require
future XML.

`CvPlot::calculateCulturalOwner` considers only ALIVE players for ordinary ownership.
`getCultureLayerColors`, deliberately under advc.099, includes EVER_ALIVE players so
culture from defeated civilizations remains represented.

`CvPlayer::setAlive(false)` kills units/cities/deals but does not clear the defeated
player's plot culture. This is consistent with the explicit culture-layer comment
"include defeated."

Therefore a visible tile can legitimately have, for example:

    current living territorial owner: 20 culture
    defeated civ A:                   20 culture
    defeated civ B:                   20 culture
    defeated civ C:                   20 culture
    defeated civ D:                   20 culture

The four defeated players are ignored as ownership candidates because they are dead;
the living player can remain the territorial owner. But the Globe layer inserts that
owner and then all four defeated EVER_ALIVE players, since each has at least 20% of
total culture. `aieOwners.size()` is therefore 5 and the bad fifth write executes.

The exact numbers need not be equal; defeated-player culture allows the territorial
owner to be below several historical culture contributors because only living players
compete for current ownership.

SHIPPED CALLER
--------------
`CvPlayer::getGlobeLayerColors(GLOBE_LAYER_CULTURE, ...)` directly calls
`getCultureLayerColors`. This is the normal active-player Culture Globe layer exposed
by `CvGameInterface`. There is no later DLL-side resizing or remapping that grants a
fifth slot per plot.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod's culture layer allocates four colors per plot and always writes exactly four:

    aColors.resize(numPlots * 4, ...);
    for (int i = 0; i < iColorsPerPlot; ++i)
        aColors[iPlot * iColorsPerPlot + i] = ...;

AdvCiv practical 2086 / commit
`1c5f39d8bebad59307fd420de2cba052a666760e`, titled:

    "Fix a minor (AdvCiv) issue with culture layer coloring"

explicitly changed the prior fixed four-write loop to the current
`std::max(iColorsPerPlot, plot_owners.size())` loop after documenting that the owner
list can contain five entries. The vector allocation remained four entries per plot.

Practical 2416 later only performed iterator/name refactoring in this block; Base
AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the practical-2086 storage/write mismatch.

DUPLICATE LEDGER
----------------
Album and current WIP searches found no prior root for `getCultureLayerColors`,
`iColorsPerPlot`, the five-owner list, or this cross-plot/out-of-bounds write.
F450 concerns the neighboring UNIT Globe layer's inverted strength arithmetic and is
independent.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Never write more than the four slots allocated for a plot.

The narrow safety repair is to restore the write bound to:

    i < iColorsPerPlot

If preserving the most relevant four identities when five contributors qualify is
desired, select/truncate the owner list BEFORE writing (e.g. always keep the
territorial owner and choose the three largest remaining culture contributors). That
is a presentation improvement; the correctness requirement is simply that no plot
writes outside its four-slot segment.
