F453 / KI#776 — `findPathLength` DOUBLE-COUNTS SHARED PREREQUISITES AND CAN MAKE
`pushResearch` CHOOSE A MORE EXPENSIVE OR-PREQUISITE PATH
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
~~~~
`CvPlayer::findPathLength` recursively sums every AND-prerequisite branch independently and
then adds the shortest OR-prerequisite branch:

    for each AND prereq:
        iPathLength += findPathLength(prereq)

    for each OR prereq:
        iNumSteps = findPathLength(prereq)
        keep the smallest

The source itself contains the inherited K-Mod warning:

    // k146 (note): This will double-count any shared AND-prepreqs.

That caveat is behaviorally significant because `CvPlayer::pushResearch` uses
`findPathLength` to decide WHICH OR prerequisite to queue when a future technology is
selected.

`pushResearch` itself does not double-add a shared prerequisite: after one prerequisite
branch has been pushed, `isResearchingTech` makes the later recursive branch return early.
Therefore the estimator and the queue builder can rank alternatives differently.

CURRENT SAS REPRODUCTION
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The current SAS technology tree contains a concrete reachable reversal.

One simple reproducible state is Carthage (starting Fishing + Pottery), with these additional
technologies legitimately acquired and no existing research queue:

    Mysticism
    Calendar
    Masonry
    Seafaring
    Sailing
    The Wheel
    Writing
    Code of Laws
    Construction
    Mathematics
    Monarchy
    Navigation
    Engineering
    Water Wheel
    Machinery

Together with Fishing + Pottery, that is 17 known technologies. This set is reachable through
ordinary prerequisite-legal research; it does not require an impossible WorldBuilder-only
knowledge combination.

Now select `TECH_LIBERALISM` directly as the future research target.

Liberalism has:

    AND prerequisite: Banking
    OR prerequisites: Naturalism, Democracy

`pushResearch` first recursively queues Banking's missing prerequisite path. At the moment it
then compares Liberalism's two OR alternatives, the relevant queued/researching Banking-side
technologies are already recognized by `findPathLength` and do not affect the comparison.

For the Naturalism alternative, the ACTUAL additional queue is:

    Polytheism          80
    Monotheism         425
    Drama              260
    Sacred Architecture 650
    Aesthetics          850
    Medicine           1100
    Naturalism         1700
                       ----
                       5065

For Democracy, the actual additional queue is:

    Polytheism          80
    Meditation         425
    Civil Service      650
    Feudalism          850
    Printing Press    1400
    Democracy         1700
                      ----
                      5105

So Naturalism is the genuinely cheaper remaining route by 40 beakers.

But `findPathLength(Naturalism)` returns 5145, not 5065. The extra 80 is Polytheism counted
TWICE inside the Sacred Architecture subtree:

* Sacred Architecture has Monotheism as an AND prerequisite and Drama as an OR route;
* Monotheism's path requires Polytheism;
* Drama's path also requires Polytheism;
* `findPathLength` evaluates those branches independently, so each recursion charges the same
  unknown Polytheism;
* real `pushResearch` pushes the Monotheism branch first, making Polytheism `isResearchingTech`,
  so the Drama branch correctly does not queue/pay for Polytheism a second time.

The resulting comparison seen by current code is therefore:

    estimated Naturalism = 5145   (wrong: +80 duplicate Polytheism)
    estimated Democracy  = 5105   (correct for this state)

and `pushResearch` chooses Democracy.

The real unique queue costs are:

    Naturalism = 5065
    Democracy  = 5105

so the automatic future-tech queue selects the MORE EXPENSIVE OR route.

DEFAULT-COST STABILITY
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
This reproduction does not rely on a hidden unusual cost option. Under the ordinary current
SAS Ancient-start / Normal-speed / Standard-world / Medium-sea setup, the relevant global
research-cost multipliers are 100%, current Era `iTechCostModifier` values are 0, and
TECH_COST_MODIFIER plus groundbreaking normalization are disabled/0. Thus the current XML
technology costs above are the corresponding team research costs for the ordinary one-member
human team (apart from any deliberately enabled special game-option modifiers).

SHIPPED CALLER / GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCE
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
This is the normal future-tech selection path, not a diagnostic helper.

`CvNetResearch::Execute` handles an ordinary technology click and calls:

    kPlayer.pushResearch(m_eTech, !m_bShift);

`pushResearch` recursively queues mandatory prerequisites and calls `findPathLength` to choose
the shortest OR branch. Therefore clicking a future technology in the normal Tech Chooser can
silently construct a higher-cost research queue than another legal OR path.

The effect is not that the player becomes unable to choose the cheaper technologies manually;
it is that Civ4's automatic prerequisite-queue construction fails its own "shortest path"
contract.

ANCESTRY
~~~~~~~~
This recursive algorithm is inherited from BtS. Civ4CE's reconstructed BtS source contains the
same independent AND-recursion / minimum-OR structure. K-Mod retains it and explicitly added
(or preserved in its source lineage) the warning that shared AND-preprequisites will be
counted twice. Base AdvCiv and current SAS retain the same algorithm.

The current SAS technology graph provides the concrete Liberalism reversal above, turning the
long-standing caveat into a shipped deterministic queue-selection defect.

DUPLICATE LEDGER
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Album searches for `findPathLength`, shared/double-counted prerequisites, shortest OR paths and
`pushResearch` found no prior numbered root covering cost-estimator double counting or
selection of a non-minimal prerequisite queue.

Earlier `pushResearch` findings concern different contracts (e.g. stale choose-tech snapshots
or Barbarian `canResearch` legality) and do not own this path-cost error.

REPAIR DIRECTION
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The path estimator must count each prospective technology at most once within one candidate
queue calculation, just as real `pushResearch` does through `isResearchingTech` after a tech is
queued.

A robust direction is an internal path-cost helper that carries a prospective "already
counted / already queued" tech set through AND branches. OR alternatives must be evaluated
with independent copies of that prospective set, and the chosen alternative's resulting set
must then be merged into the caller's path state. This avoids both shared-AND double counting
and accidental cross-contamination between alternatives.

Alternatively, factor the queue-building prerequisite traversal into a non-mutating simulator
and use the resulting unique queued technology set/cost for OR comparisons. The important
requirement is that `findPathLength` and `pushResearch` model the SAME deduplication semantics;
merely adjusting the Liberalism XML would only mask the generic defect.

F454 / KI#777 — THIRD-PARTY CIVIC/RELIGION ESPIONAGE ANNOUNCEMENTS LEAK AN
UNREVEALED TARGET CAPITAL THROUGH RAW MESSAGE COORDINATES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
~~~~
`CvPlayer::announceEspionageToThirdParties(EspionageMissionTypes eMission,
PlayerTypes eTarget)` builds the AdvCiv 120f announcement sent to third-party major civs
that know the espionage target.

It obtains the target capital once:

    int iX = -1, iY = -1;
    CvCity* pCapital = GET_PLAYER(eTarget).getCapital();
    if (pCapital != NULL)
    {
        iX = pCapital->getX();
        iY = pCapital->getY();
    }

and then sends those SAME raw coordinates to every eligible observer:

    for (PlayerIter<MAJOR_CIV,OTHER_KNOWN_TO> it(TEAMID(eTarget)); ...)
    {
        CvPlayer const& kObs = *it;
        if (kObs.getID() != getID())
            gDLL->UI().addMessage(kObs.getID(), ..., iX, iY);
    }

There is no `isRevealed(kObs.getTeam())` test and no observer-aware capital-coordinate
lookup. Merely knowing the target civilization is enough to receive the target capital's
exact current map coordinates.

CURRENT SHIPPED REACHABILITY
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Both affected mission families are enabled in current SAS
`CIV4EspionageMissionInfo.xml`:

    ESPIONAGEMISSION_SWITCH_CIVIC:
        iCost = 0
        iSwitchCivicCostFactor = 1000

    ESPIONAGEMISSION_SWITCH_RELIGION:
        iCost = 0
        iSwitchReligionCostFactor = 1000

`iCost == 0` is enabled; only `-1` disables a mission in
`getEspionageMissionBaseCost`.

Current `GlobalDefines_advc.xml` also enables the feature by default:

    ANNOUNCE_ESPIONAGE_REVOLUTION = 1

with the defining comment stating that third parties that know the target are notified.

A normal reproduction therefore needs only three major civilizations:

    A = spy owner
    B = espionage target
    C = third-party observer

C has met B but has never revealed B's capital. A successfully performs Switch Civic or
Switch Religion against B. `doEspionageMission` calls
`announceEspionageToThirdParties(eMission, B)` directly in both successful mission
branches. C is in `OTHER_KNOWN_TO(TEAMID(B))`, and unless C is A, C receives the message
with B's raw capital `(x,y)`.

The spy's mission target city need not be B's capital, so the mission itself does not
supply a reason for C to know those capital coordinates.

WHY THE COORDINATES ARE PLAYER-FACING INFORMATION
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
`CvDLLInterfaceIFaceBase::addMessage` forwards `iFlashX/iFlashY` into the EXE message
payload. Its AdvCiv comment explicitly notes that flash information is used for:

    "the text color and coordinates stored in the Turn Log -- not just
     for the (disabled) icon."

Thus the coordinates are not an unused implementation detail. They become message/Turn
Log location data, with the normal Civ4 message-location navigation behavior.

LOCAL CONTROL PROVES THE INTENDED VISIBILITY CONTRACT
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The neighboring ordinary religion-change announcement in
`CvPlayer::setLastStateReligion` already handles this exact problem correctly. It sends:

    getCapitalX(kObs.getTeam(), true),
    getCapitalY(kObs.getTeam(), true)

for each observer separately.

`CvPlayer::getCapitalX/Y(TeamTypes eObserver, bool bDebug)` return `-1` when the capital
has not been revealed to that observer. Therefore ordinary conversion news deliberately
avoids revealing a hidden capital, while the AdvCiv espionage-third-party helper bypasses
that observer-aware API and sends raw coordinates.

Other current announcement code likewise tests capital/city reveal state before attaching
coordinates. This makes the 120f behavior an integration omission rather than a necessary
property of Civ4 messages.

EXECUTION PATH
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
For Switch Civic:

    doEspionageMission
      -> announceEspionageToThirdParties(eMission, eTargetPlayer)
      -> target.setCivics(...)

For Switch Religion:

    doEspionageMission
      -> announceEspionageToThirdParties(eMission, eTargetPlayer)
      -> target.setLastStateReligion(...)

There is no subsequent observer-specific revalidation or coordinate replacement.

ANCESTRY
~~~~~~~~
The third-party announcement helper is an AdvCiv feature marked `advc.120f`. It is absent
from the supplied BtS reconstruction and K-Mod source; Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS
contain the same raw-capital-coordinate implementation. `GlobalDefines_advc.xml` identifies
120f as the feature that announces forced civic/religion espionage to third parties.

The exact local control (`setLastStateReligion` using observer-aware `getCapitalX/Y`) is
also present in current AdvCiv/SAS, so the omission survives in the feature that introduced
the extra announcement rather than being inherited from the stock message path.

DUPLICATE LEDGER
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Album searches for `announceEspionageToThirdParties`,
`ANNOUNCE_ESPIONAGE_REVOLUTION`, third-party espionage-capital coordinates, and hidden
capital/message-coordinate exposure found no prior numbered root.

The previously parked Global + PickPlayer World News visibility question is different:
it concerns whether a world-news TEXT string may identify an unmet picked civilization.
F454 is an unambiguous MAP-LOCATION leak against a local observer-aware coordinate API.

REPAIR DIRECTION
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Resolve message coordinates per observer, exactly like `setLastStateReligion`.
Conservatively, inside the observer loop use:

    int iX = GET_PLAYER(eTarget).getCapitalX(kObs.getTeam(), true);
    int iY = GET_PLAYER(eTarget).getCapitalY(kObs.getTeam(), true);

(or equivalently test `pCapital->isRevealed(kObs.getTeam(), true)` and pass `-1,-1` when
hidden).

Keep the third-party text itself unchanged; F454 concerns only attaching information the
observer has not revealed.

F455 / KI#778 — PERMANENT ALLIANCE TEAM REASSIGNMENT DOES NOT RECOUNT
CACHED MILITARY-HAPPINESS GARRISONS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED. Current shipped Permanent Alliances can change a stationary unit's
`CvUnit::isGarrisonInTeamCity()` / `isMilitaryHappiness()` result without updating the
city's cached `m_iMilitaryHappinessUnits`. A later move can even decrement a cache that
never received the corresponding increment, producing a negative count in release builds
(and tripping the debug assertion).

ROOT
----
Current AdvCiv/SAS military-happiness eligibility is relational rather than simply an XML
unit flag:

    bool CvUnit::isMilitaryHappiness() const
    {
        return (m_pUnitInfo->isMilitaryHappiness() &&
                isGarrisonInTeamCity());
    }

    bool CvUnit::isGarrisonInTeamCity() const
    {
        if (!getPlot().isCity())
            return false;
        CvTeam const& kCityTeam = GET_TEAM(getPlot().getTeam());
        if (isInvisible(kCityTeam.getID(), false))
            return false;
        return (kCityTeam.getID() == getTeam() ||
                kCityTeam.getMasterTeam() == getTeam() ||
                kCityTeam.getID() == GET_TEAM(getTeam()).getMasterTeam());
    }

`CvCity` does not derive its military-happiness unit count on demand. It stores
`m_iMilitaryHappinessUnits`, initialized/rebuilt by:

    CvCity::updateMilitaryHappinessUnits()
      -> plotCount(PUF_isMilitaryHappiness) - cached count

Ordinary unit movement maintains that cache incrementally in `CvUnit::setXY`:

    leaving city:  if (isMilitaryHappiness()) changeMilitaryHappinessUnits(-1);
    entering city: if (isMilitaryHappiness()) changeMilitaryHappinessUnits(+1);

This is only correct if every state transition that can change `isMilitaryHappiness()` for a
stationary unit performs a full recount.

PERMANENT ALLIANCE VIOLATES THAT CACHE CONTRACT
------------------------------------------------
`CvTeam::addTeam(eTeam)` absorbs every player on `eTeam` by calling:

    GET_PLAYER(...).setTeam(getID());

`CvPlayer::setTeam` updates team membership/alive/city/population/land counters and attitude
state, but never calls `updateMilitaryHappinessUnits`.

For stationary units and cities, changing the player's team can immediately change
`isGarrisonInTeamCity()`:

* an absorbed player's unit standing in a survivor-team city was not a same-team garrison
  before the alliance, but becomes one as soon as its owner is reassigned;
* a survivor-team unit standing in an absorbed player's city becomes a same-team garrison
  once the city owner is reassigned and the plot's cached team is refreshed.

`CvTeam::addTeam` later loops across all map plots and calls `kPlot.updateTeam()`, but that
function only assigns the cached plot team from its owner. It does not recount city military
happiness.

A complete current-tree caller search finds full military-happiness recounts only in:

* `CvCity::init` (city initialization), and
* `CvTeam::setVassal`, through `CvTeam::updateMilitaryHappinessUnits` for both sides.

There is no corresponding recount in `CvPlayer::setTeam` or the ordinary independent-team
Permanent Alliance path in `CvTeam::addTeam`.

DETERMINISTIC CURRENT REPRODUCTION
----------------------------------
Current SAS supports the full state without custom data:

* `GAMEOPTION_PERMANENT_ALLIANCES` is visible and supported (default off, user-selectable);
* current `TECH_GAME_THEORY` has `bPermanentAllianceTrading=1`;
* `CIVIC_HEREDITARY_RULE` has `iHappyPerMilitaryUnit=1`;
* ordinary military units such as Warrior, Archer and Rifleman have
  `bMilitaryHappiness=1`.

Example:

1. Player A / Team A owns City A and has no military-happiness unit counted there.
2. Player B / Team B has a Warrior stationed in City A under the pre-alliance diplomatic
   access. Because the teams are independent, `isGarrisonInTeamCity()` is false and City A's
   cached `m_iMilitaryHappinessUnits` correctly remains 0.
3. A and B form a Permanent Alliance; assume Team A survives the merge.
4. `CvTeam::addTeam` calls B's `setTeam(Team A)`. The stationary Warrior's
   `isGarrisonInTeamCity()` now becomes true immediately, but City A's cached count remains 0.
5. Under Hereditary Rule, City A therefore misses the +1 happiness that the now-same-team
   Warrior should provide.
6. If that Warrior subsequently moves out, `CvUnit::setXY` evaluates the CURRENT predicate,
   sees `isMilitaryHappiness()==true`, and executes `changeMilitaryHappinessUnits(-1)`.
   The stale cache goes 0 -> -1. `CvCity::changeMilitaryHappinessUnits` asserts that the count
   is nonnegative, so debug builds expose the invariant violation directly; release builds
   retain the invalid negative count.

The negative count is not merely cosmetic. `CvCity::getMilitaryHappiness()` multiplies the
cached count by the player's `getHappyPerMilitaryUnit`, and several happiness/anger/AI and
occupation checks consume either that result or `getMilitaryHappinessUnits()` directly.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod's `CvUnit::isMilitaryHappiness()` simply returned the XML military-happiness flag; its
city movement bookkeeping therefore did not have this same team-relation cache dependency.

AdvCiv commit `177701cd0a0f4a295a59b4c7bf2d1c8143853763` (2023-09-06,
"Allow vassal/ master to help suppress 3rd-party revolts", change `advc.184`) introduced
`isGarrisonInTeamCity()` and made military-happiness eligibility depend on team/master-vassal
relations.

AdvCiv commit `6c12950422223708a8ec4c1fe0a90834fc10b0cf` (2024-07-19,
"Fix a rare issue with counting of military happiness units") subsequently recognized the
cache-invalidation consequence. It introduced `CvCity::updateMilitaryHappinessUnits`, player
and team wrappers, and explicitly recounts BOTH teams whenever `CvTeam::setVassal` changes a
master/vassal relation.

That fix demonstrates the intended invariant: relational changes that alter
`isGarrisonInTeamCity()` require a full recount. The Permanent Alliance path changes the even
more fundamental same-team relation through `setTeam`, but no analogous recount was added.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain that omission.

DUPLICATE LEDGER
----------------
Album searches for `advc.184`, `updateMilitaryHappinessUnits`,
`isGarrisonInTeamCity`, military-happiness + Permanent Alliance, and garrison + alliance found
no prior numbered root. Earlier Permanent Alliance findings concern diplomacy/history,
espionage, research/project migration, visibility and other team-keyed state, not the city
military-happiness cache.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Perform a full military-happiness recount after the Permanent Alliance team reassignment and
after plot team caches have been refreshed.

The safest local placement is in `CvTeam::addTeam`, after the map loop that calls
`kPlot.updateTeam()`, because units in cities formerly owned by the absorbed team need those
plot-team caches to reflect the surviving team before `isGarrisonInTeamCity()` is reevaluated.
At that point the surviving team's `updateMilitaryHappinessUnits()` covers all cities now
owned by both sets of merged players.

Do not merely add an incremental adjustment in `CvPlayer::setTeam`: a team reassignment can
change eligibility for many stationary units in many cities at once, and for absorbed-team
cities the plot's cached team is not yet updated at the moment `setTeam` is called.

----------------------------------------------------------

a caller/API audit lead, not F456.

F456 / KI#779 -- Random Personalities: Missionary strategy still uses the hidden personality's favorite civic after advc.130n moved favorite ideology to the displayed leader
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT / CONTRACT
---------------
AdvCiv `advc.130n` deliberately centralized favorite-ideology semantics in `CvPlayer`:

    CivicTypes CvPlayer::getFavoriteCivic() const
    {
        return GC.getInfo(getLeaderType()).getFavoriteCivic();
    }

The accompanying source comment is explicit: the distinction matters for Random Personalities;
favorite ideologies are tied to the displayed leader type, while personality-specific numeric
attitude changes remain tied to the randomized hidden personality.

The 2022 commit converted many AI call sites from direct
`GC.getInfo(getPersonalityType()).getFavoriteCivic()` lookups to `getFavoriteCivic()`.
One live runtime lookup was missed in `CvPlayerAI::AI_updateStrategyHash`:

    CivicTypes eCivic = GC.getInfo(getPersonalityType()).getFavoriteCivic();
    if (eCivic != NO_CIVIC && GC.getInfo(eCivic).isNoNonStateReligionSpread())
        iMissionary += 20;

This is the only remaining current DLL runtime direct favorite-civic lookup through
`getPersonalityType()` found by the full-tree search. Therefore the Missionary-strategy score
still lets the SECRET randomized personality's favorite civic leak into a field that AdvCiv
explicitly moved back to the DISPLAYED leader.

CURRENT DATA / SUPPORTED PRODUCER
---------------------------------
`GAMEOPTION_RANDOM_PERSONALITIES` is visible and supported (default off). `changePersonalityType`
can assign any non-Barbarian leader personality, merely reducing the random weight of personalities
already in use; it does not require personality == displayed leader.

Current SAS gives:

- displayed Asoka: FavoriteCivic = `CIVIC_PACIFISM`;
- Isabella personality: FavoriteCivic = `CIVIC_THEOCRACY`;
- Isabella personality: FLAVOR_RELIGION = 10, no Gold/Culture flavor;
- current Theocracy: `bNoNonStateReligionSpread = 1`.

The surrounding flavor terms are correctly personality-driven by design:
`AI_getFlavorValue` reads `GC.getInfo(getPersonalityType()).getFlavorValue(...)`.
The favorite-civic term is the exceptional field whose semantics advc.130n deliberately changed.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION
--------------------------
Use Random Personalities and a displayed Asoka whose hidden personality is Isabella. Construct an
ordinary AI state with:

1. current state religion present;
2. the AI owns that state religion's Holy City plus one additional Holy City (`iHolyCityCount=2`);
3. exactly one met civilization in a two-civ game (so AdvCiv's lonely-flavor adjustment is false);
4. that known civilization can be peacefully entered and has the same state religion;
5. the AI is not close to a religious victory.

The fixed non-random score terms are then:

    Isabella Religion flavor: 10 * 6 = 60
    one extra Holy City:      (2 - 1) * 5 = 5
    one met civ:              1 * 7 = 7
    same-religion target:     10
    -----------------------------------
    intended displayed-favorite score = 82

Asoka's displayed favorite is Pacifism, which does NOT forbid non-state religion spread, so under
the intended `getFavoriteCivic()` semantics no +20 applies.

Current code instead reads hidden Isabella's favorite Theocracy and adds +20:

    current broken score = 102

The strategy random term is only `(AI_getStrategyRand(9) % 7) * 3`, i.e. 0..18. The activation
threshold is strictly `iMissionary > 100`.

Therefore:

    intended score: 82..100  -> Missionary strategy NEVER activates
    current score:  102..120 -> Missionary strategy ALWAYS activates

This proves a deterministic strategy-bit flip without depending on a lucky strategy RNG result.

GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCE
--------------------
`AI_STRATEGY_MISSIONARY` is not decorative. Current live consumers include:

- `AI_missionaryValue`: external-spread multiplier 60 when strategy active vs 25 otherwise;
- `CvCityAI::AI_bestSpreadUnit`: state-religion missionary chance is multiplied by 170% while
  other-religion spread is reduced to 65%;
- `AI_bestReligion`: Missionary strategy changes the acceptance path for the selected religion;
- strategy interactions elsewhere also avoid/alter competing strategy choices.

Thus Random Personalities can make the AI's religious expansion strategy depend on the hidden
personality's favorite civic even though favorite ideology is intentionally a displayed-leader
property throughout the rest of current AdvCiv/SAS.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod inherited the Missionary-strategy code with a direct personality favorite-civic lookup.

AdvCiv commit `cbb9fe7ef68b7e8ea9ee5dd3ab5eb9883a83273d` (2022-10-29,
"Fave civics based on displayed leader type", practical commit 3974 / `advc.130n`) introduced
`CvPlayer::getFavoriteCivic()` and systematically converted many AI/UI favorite-civic call sites
from personality/leader-info lookups to that central accessor. The commit's source comment states
the intended displayed-leader semantics explicitly.

The Missionary-strategy line was not converted by that commit. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS
still contain the inherited K-Mod direct `getPersonalityType()` lookup. A full current DLL search
finds no other live direct favorite-civic lookup through `getPersonalityType()`.

DUPLICATE LEDGER
----------------
Album searches for Random Personalities, favorite/favourite civic, `advc.130n`, Missionary strategy,
`AI_STRATEGY_MISSIONARY`, displayed leader and hidden personality found no prior numbered root for
this lookup. An earlier Queue-001 control notes an odd post-advc.130n incremental ideology-attitude
helper, but that concerns attitude-cache refresh and is explicitly not a finding. It does not own
this live strategy-scoring mismatch.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Replace the one stale Missionary-strategy lookup with the centralized accessor:

    CivicTypes eCivic = getFavoriteCivic();

Do NOT replace the surrounding `AI_getFlavorValue` calls: those are intentionally based on the
randomized personality and are part of what Random Personalities is supposed to randomize.
The repair should change only the favorite-ideology term, matching every other advc.130n-converted
AI use.

F457 / KI#780 -- Global PickPlayer trigger World News reveals an unmet picked civilization to observers; sibling event-news path was explicitly fixed in AdvCiv 2422
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT / CONTRACT
---------------
`CvPlayer::setTriggerFired` announces a trigger's pre-expanded `m_szGlobalText` to third-party
observers. For a trigger involving `m_eOtherPlayer`, current code hoists this test OUTSIDE the
observer loop:

    bool bMetOtherPlayer = (kTriggeredData.m_eOtherPlayer == NO_PLAYER ||
            GET_TEAM(kTriggeredData.m_eOtherPlayer).isHasMet(getTeam()));

and then sends the World News text to each living observer when:

    bMetOtherPlayer && observerTeam.isHasMet(getTeam())

The first predicate asks whether the PICKED OTHER PLAYER has met the EVENT OWNER. It does NOT ask
whether the current OBSERVER has met that picked player.

`initTriggeredData` has already expanded the World News string once, including:

    eOtherPlayer != NO_PLAYER ? GET_PLAYER(eOtherPlayer).getCivilizationAdjectiveKey() : L""

Therefore every accepted observer receives the picked civilization's actual adjective even when
that observer has never met the picked civilization.

CURRENT SHIPPED PRODUCER / DETERMINISTIC REPRO
----------------------------------------------
Current `EVENTTRIGGER_FUGITIVE` is:

    bGlobal     = 1
    bPickPlayer = 1
    WorldNews   = TXT_KEY_EVENTTRIGGER_FUGITIVE

The stock BtS text inherited by current SAS is:

    "%s1_civ_adjective authorities are rumored to have captured a fugitive fleeing from
     %s4_civ_adjective justice. No confirmation is available."

So both the event owner's civilization and the picked civilization are explicitly named.

Construct three living major civilizations:

1. A is the player whose Fugitive trigger fires.
2. B is the picked `m_eOtherPlayer`; A and B have met.
3. C has met A but has never met B.

This is a valid trigger state because `CvPlayer::canTrigger` requires the candidate picked player
B to have met the triggering player A:

    if (!GET_TEAM(B).isHasMet(A.team)) return false;

When `setTriggerFired` announces the trigger:

    bMetOtherPlayer = B.hasMet(A) = true
    C.hasMet(A)                    = true

so C receives the already-expanded Fugitive World News text and learns B's civilization adjective,
despite C never having met B.

Other current Global + PickPlayer trigger texts such as `EVENTTRIGGER_FAUX_PAS` and
`EVENTTRIGGER_TEA` also explicitly contain the picked civilization adjective. Fugitive alone is
sufficient for the root.

AUTHORITATIVE CURRENT SIBLING CONTROL
-------------------------------------
This is no longer an ambiguous question about whether "World News" is intentionally omniscient.
AdvCiv itself explicitly established the opposite information contract.

Commit `71a7af8cd9ddd50f5fbbbafd17bec46698339993` (practical 2422), titled:

    "Report random events involving two civs only if both known"

fixed the later `CvPlayer::applyEvent` World News observer loop. The old code checked the other
player against the event owner's team. The fix changed that check to the CURRENT OBSERVER'S team:

    if (pTriggeredData->m_eOtherPlayer != NO_PLAYER &&
        !GET_TEAM(pTriggeredData->m_eOtherPlayer).isHasMet(kObs.getTeam()))
    {
        continue;
    }

Current SAS retains that observer-specific check in `applyEvent`. Thus event-choice World News is
suppressed for C in the reproduction above, while the trigger-level World News emitted earlier by
`setTriggerFired` leaks B's identity.

ANCESTRY
--------
BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod already contain the flawed trigger-announcement condition: the observer must
know the event owner, but the picked-other-player test is against the event owner rather than the
observer.

An early AdvCiv refactor (practical 1648) hoisted the picked-player test out of the loop as
`bMetOtherPlayer`; practical 2416 corrected an unrelated `||`/`&&` mistake in the refactored
condition but retained the same wrong subject.

Practical 2422 later fixed the parallel event-choice World News path specifically so two-civ event
reports are shown only when BOTH civilizations are known to each observer. It did not apply the
same observer-specific correction to `setTriggerFired`'s trigger World News. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
current SAS retain this unfixed sibling.

DUPLICATE LEDGER
----------------
The Queue-004 audit had previously parked this exact Global + PickPlayer visibility behavior as an
ambiguous World-News policy question. No prior numbered root owns it. The newly traced practical
2422 history resolves that ambiguity by explicitly stating and implementing the observer-specific
"both known" contract in the sibling event-news path.

F454 is separate: it leaks a hidden target CAPITAL LOCATION through espionage third-party message
coordinates. F457 leaks the IDENTITY/adjective of an unmet picked civilization through random-event
trigger World News.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Do not hoist the picked-player contact check globally. Resolve it per observer, mirroring the
already-correct `applyEvent` path. Conceptually:

    observer knows event owner
    && (no picked player || observer knows picked player's team)

The existing `applyEvent` observer loop is the direct local repair model.

F458 / KI#781 -- Permanent Alliance team absorption leaves `m_iNumOutsideUnits` stale, so former allied-border units keep charging unit supply after becoming same-team units
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED. Current shipped Permanent Alliances can change stationary units from "outside borders"
to "inside borders" without updating the owning player's cached `m_iNumOutsideUnits`. The stale
count feeds authoritative unit-supply expenses, is serialized directly, and has no later full
recount that repairs it.

ROOT / CACHE CONTRACT
---------------------
`CvPlayer` stores the number of units outside friendly/vassal territory in the mutable cache:

    int m_iNumOutsideUnits;

The ordinary unit-supply calculation consumes that cache directly:

    iPaidUnits = std::max(0, getNumOutsideUnits()
            + iExtraOutsideUnits
            - iFreeOutsideUnits);

    iBaseSupplyCost = iPaidUnits * INITIAL_OUTSIDE_UNIT_GOLD_PERCENT;
    iBaseSupplyCost /= 100;

The count is not derived from all units when queried. Current-tree maintenance is entirely
incremental. `CvUnit::setXY` removes/adds one outside unit when leaving/entering a plot whose team
satisfies:

    plotTeam != unitTeam &&
    (plotTeam == NO_TEAM || !GET_TEAM(plotTeam).isVassal(unitTeam))

`CvPlot::setOwner` performs the analogous remove/re-add around an ownership/team change.

This establishes the invariant: any other state transition that changes that relational predicate
for stationary units must also adjust or recount `m_iNumOutsideUnits`.

AUTHORITATIVE SIBLING CONTROL: VASSALAGE ALREADY DOES THE REQUIRED RELATIONAL UPDATE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvTeam::setVassal` explicitly handles this exact dependency. Before changing master/vassal state,
it iterates the master's units and decrements `changeNumOutsideUnits(-1)` for units whose current
plots qualify under the old relation. After the relationship changes, it iterates again and adds
them back under the new relation.

That code is present already in stock BtS/Civ4CE, K-Mod, Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS. It proves
that "outside unit" is recognized as relationship-dependent cached player state rather than a
value that can safely be left to future movement.

PERMANENT ALLIANCE VIOLATES THE SAME CONTRACT
---------------------------------------------
`CvDeal` forms a Permanent Alliance by calling `CvTeam::addTeam`; the lower-numbered team survives.
The merge reassigns every absorbed player through:

    GET_PLAYER(...).setTeam(getID());

`CvPlayer::setTeam` updates team membership/alive/city/population/land counters and attitude state,
but does not touch `m_iNumOutsideUnits`.

Later in `CvTeam::addTeam`, every map plot runs:

    kPlot.updateTeam();

Current AdvCiv's `CvPlot::updateTeam` only refreshes the cached team from the plot owner:

    m_eTeam = (isOwned() ? TEAMID(getOwner()) : NO_TEAM);

It does not execute the remove/re-add outside-unit bookkeeping used by `CvPlot::setOwner`.
`CvTeam::addTeam` then updates plot groups, but no outside-unit recount occurs there either.

A complete current DLL reference search finds `changeNumOutsideUnits` only in:

* `CvUnit::setXY` -- ordinary unit movement / placement;
* `CvPlot::setOwner` -- ordinary plot owner change;
* `CvTeam::setVassal` -- explicit relationship transition repair;
* `CvPlayer::changeNumOutsideUnits` itself.

There is no full player/team `updateNumOutsideUnits` helper and no Permanent-Alliance correction.

DETERMINISTIC CURRENT REPRODUCTION
----------------------------------
The state is fully supported by current SAS data:

* `GAMEOPTION_PERMANENT_ALLIANCES` is a shipped game option;
* current `TECH_GAME_THEORY` has `bPermanentAllianceTrading=1`;
* standard BtS `INITIAL_FREE_OUTSIDE_UNITS` is 4, and current Normal speed adds
  `iExtraFreeOutsideUnits=0`;
* `INITIAL_OUTSIDE_UNIT_GOLD_PERCENT` is 50.

Example on Normal speed with no other outside units:

1. Player A / Team A and Player B / Team B are independent friendly civilizations able to form a
   Permanent Alliance.
2. A stations six ordinary units in B-owned territory (Open Borders is enough to allow the units
   to stand there; Open Borders does not make the territory "inside" for unit-supply counting).
3. Before the alliance, all six correctly satisfy the outside-unit predicate, so
   `A.m_iNumOutsideUnits == 6`.
4. A and B form a Permanent Alliance and Team A survives.
5. B's player is reassigned to Team A and B-owned plots are refreshed to Team A. Every one of A's
   six stationary units is now on SAME-TEAM territory and should no longer count as outside.
6. No outside-unit update runs. A's cache remains 6.
7. Runtime supply therefore still computes:

       paid units = max(0, 6 - 4) = 2
       base supply = 2 * 50 / 100 = 1 gold/turn

   even though the six units are now standing in the merged team's own territory.

The symmetric absorbed-player case is also reachable: B units standing in A territory cease being
outside as soon as B is reassigned to Team A, but B's player cache likewise receives no correction.

PERSISTENCE / WHY MOVEMENT DOES NOT SELF-HEAL
---------------------------------------------
This stale state is not tied to a pending per-unit flag that gets cleared later. Once the alliance
exists, an affected unit's current plot is same-team territory. Moving that unit between merged-team
plots performs neither the old-plot decrement nor the new-plot increment because the CURRENT
outside predicate is false on both sides.

Moving it out to genuinely foreign/unowned territory adds one and moving it back subtracts one,
returning to the same stale baseline. Killing/removing it while on merged-team territory likewise
does not subtract the old stale contribution.

`m_iNumOutsideUnits` is read and written directly by `CvPlayer::read` / `CvPlayer::write`; load does
not rebuild it from units. A save made after the alliance therefore preserves the incorrect supply
burden across sessions.

GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCE
--------------------
`CvPlayer::calculateUnitSupply` is the authoritative runtime supply expense and is included by
`calculatePreInflatedCosts`. Thus F458 is not merely a Finance-Advisor display mismatch: the player
actually pays excess supply from the stale count (subject to normal handicap/inflation handling).
AI economic state consumes the same player cost pipeline.

Even below the first whole-gold threshold, `getNumOutsideUnits` and Finance breakdown data remain
wrong; with six stale units on Normal the shipped values already produce a deterministic +1 base
gold/turn error.

ANCESTRY
--------
This is inherited core BtS behavior, not an AdvCiv-SAS regression.

Stock BtS/Civ4CE already has:

* incremental `changeNumOutsideUnits` maintenance in unit movement and plot owner change;
* the explicit two-pass outside-unit adjustment in `CvTeam::setVassal`;
* `CvTeam::addTeam` player reassignment for Permanent Alliances without an analogous outside-unit
  adjustment/recount.

K-Mod retains that omission. Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains it as well. AdvCiv later cached plot team in
`CvPlot::m_eTeam` and explicitly refreshes it during `addTeam`, but the refresh remains a bare cached
team assignment and still bypasses the outside-unit accounting.

F455 / KI#778 is a later AdvCiv-specific sibling caused by military-happiness eligibility becoming
team/vassal relational. F458 is older and independent: BtS itself already knew unit supply had to be
adjusted for vassal relationship changes, but Permanent Alliance absorption never received the same
cache maintenance.

DUPLICATE LEDGER
----------------
Full album searches for `outside unit`, `NumOutsideUnits`, `changeNumOutsideUnits`, `unit supply`,
Permanent Alliance + supply/outside, and related team-reassignment wording found no prior numbered
root for this cache corruption.

F412 / KI#735 is separate: the Finance Advisor's unit-cost/unit-supply HOVERS ignore anarchy and can
show positive itemized costs while runtime costs are zero. It does not alter `m_iNumOutsideUnits` or
runtime supply.

F455 / KI#778 is separate: Permanent Alliance reassignment leaves the CITY military-happiness cache
stale and can drive that city count negative on later movement. F458 concerns the PLAYER outside-unit
cache and authoritative supply expense.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Use a full recomputation after Permanent Alliance member reassignment AND after the map loop has
refreshed absorbed territory's plot-team cache.

A robust local design is a player helper that counts all on-map units using the same predicate as
`CvUnit::setXY`, then applies:

    changeNumOutsideUnits(recomputedCount - getNumOutsideUnits());

Call it for every surviving-team member in `CvTeam::addTeam` after all `kPlot.updateTeam()` calls.
That placement repairs both directions at once:

* survivor players with units in formerly absorbed territory;
* absorbed players with units in survivor territory.

Do not try to repair only inside `CvPlayer::setTeam`: at that point absorbed-player plot teams have
not yet all been refreshed, and survivor players whose own team ID never changes can still have
stationary units whose outside status changes when absorbed territory switches team.

IMMEDIATE RELATIONSHIP-CACHE SIBLING SWEEP
------------------------------------------
The neighboring `CvTeam::setVassal` transition list was rechecked after F458. The major relation-
dependent families it explicitly updates are city sight, master-unit outside status, war/war-plan
counters, military-happiness garrisons, culture and plot groups. Permanent-Alliance `addTeam`
already has dedicated visibility/contact/war/culture/plot-group/team-state migration for the latter
families, while F455 and F458 identify the two cached per-city/per-player relational counters that
were missing from that merge path. No third comparably direct current cache omission has yet been
established from this local list.

POST-WIP171 CLOSURE / CONTROL PASS
----------------------------------
The next tranche finished several candidates opened by the paired-counter and
relationship-dependent-cache inventory. None currently clears the numbered-root threshold.

CONTROL — TEAM COMMERCE-FLEXIBILITY REMOVAL HAS AN INVARIANT GAP, BUT SHIPPED TECH-REMOVAL PATHS MASK IT
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
`CvPlayer::changeCommerceFlexibleCount` resets a commerce slider to its XML initial percent
when the player's last flexibility source disappears. The corresponding team-level
`CvTeam::changeCommerceFlexibleCount` only mutates the team counter and dirties the UI; it
does not reset a now-illegal player slider.

In isolation, therefore, removing the last team source while Culture/Espionage is allocated
above its initial percentage can leave percentage assigned to a commerce type that
`CvPlayer::isCommerceFlexible` now reports as inflexible.

Current SAS does not establish a shipped normal-game producer for that bad transition:
team flexibility is tech-driven, ordinary gameplay does not remove known technologies,
the Advanced Start refund receiver exists but the shipped tech chooser exposes only tech
purchase (the same reachability control that rejected F084/F085/F088), and the main commerce
sliders are hidden while the interface is in Advanced Start. True Starts tech stripping is a
setup/regeneration operation before ordinary slider use. Preserve this as an API/robustness
asymmetry, not F459.

CONTROL — PROPAGATED EVENT EXPIRY MIXES RECIPIENT AND ORIGINAL TRIGGER OWNER, BUT CURRENT DATA DOES NOT REACH THE MISMATCH
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
`setEventOccured` propagates a Global occurrence by copying the same `EventTriggeredData`,
so recipient copies retain the original trigger owner's `m_ePlayer`. Some quest expiry tests
in `checkExpireEvent` combine state from `this` (the player storing the occurrence) with
`kTriggeredData.m_ePlayer` (the original trigger owner). That is structurally fragile for a
propagated Global/Team quest.

Current SAS event data contains no Quest event that is also Global or Team, so no shipped
occurrence reaches a state where the recipient/original-owner distinction changes the quest
expiry result. The already preserved practical-2416 Team-event propagation inversion is
likewise real source debt but remains dormant because current Event/EventTrigger data has no
Team producer. No F459.

CONTROL — SPY DESTROY/BRIBE UNIT TARGET VALIDATION IS DORMANT IN CURRENT MISSION DATA
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
`canSpyDestroyUnit(eTarget, kUnit)` does not itself establish that `kUnit.getOwner()` equals
`eTarget`; the generic plot fallback in espionage mission costing can iterate units belonging
to third parties. The analogous bribe path has the same family shape.

Current SAS `CIV4EspionageMissionInfo.xml` has every `iDestroyUnitCostFactor` and
`iBuyUnitCostFactor` set to 0, leaving these mission branches without a shipped data producer.
Keep as data-masked robustness debt, not F459.

CONTROL — WAR-WEARINESS MODIFIER MUTATOR DOES NOT NEED A PLAYER CACHE RECOUNT
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
`CvPlayer::changeWarWearinessModifier` initially looked like a missing recomputation because
it does not refresh `m_iWarWearinessPercentAnger`. Full consumer tracing closes that lead:
`CvCity::getWarWearinessPercentAnger` applies the current player + city war-weariness modifier
dynamically when converting the cached base anger percent into city anger. No stale-cache
root survives.

CONTROL — RESEARCH QUEUE FLAG MAINTENANCE CLOSES UNDER THE NORMAL ACQUISITION CALLER
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
`CvPlayer::popResearch(eTech)` clears `m_abResearchingTech[eTech]` even if its queue scan did
not find a node. The normal DLL acquisition path in `CvTeam::setHasTech` first checks
`kMember.isResearchingTech(eTech)` and calls `popResearch` only when that flag is true; queue
construction sets the flag exactly when inserting the node, while `clearResearchQueue`
resets all flags. No ordinary caller was found that desynchronizes node and flag state.
The Python wrapper can invoke the API more loosely, which is not enough for a current root.

CONTROL — `updateExtraYieldThresholds` CONTAINS A REAL ADVC.908a COMPARATOR TYPO, CURRENT TRAIT DATA MASKS IT
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The ordinary threshold branch correctly keeps the smallest positive threshold:

    if (iBestThresh == 0 || iThresh < iBestThresh)
        iBestThresh = iThresh;

The AdvCiv 908a natural-threshold sibling instead says:

    if (iBestNaturalThresh == 0 || iBestNaturalThresh < iBestThresh)
        iBestNaturalThresh = iNaturalThresh;

The second clause plainly compares the current NATURAL best against the unrelated ordinary
best rather than comparing `iNaturalThresh` with `iBestNaturalThresh`. With two active traits
providing different natural thresholds, iteration order can therefore select the wrong value.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS contain the same typo; K-Mod predates the natural-threshold
feature and therefore has only the original ordinary-threshold logic.

Current SAS XML masks the defect: only `TRAIT_FINANCIAL` has any positive
`ExtraYieldNaturalThreshold` (Commerce = 3), and there are no positive ordinary
`ExtraYieldThreshold` entries. With only one possible positive natural source, the first
`iBestNaturalThresh == 0` clause always installs the correct 3 and no competing source exists.
Preserve this as a clean latent AdvCiv/data-extension bug and worthwhile narrow cleanup, but
do not consume F459 under the album's current-data threshold.

RELATIONSHIP-CACHE SIBLING RECONCILIATION AFTER F458
----------------------------------------------------
A direct comparison of `CvTeam::setVassal` with the Permanent-Alliance `addTeam`/`setTeam`
path confirms why F455 (military happiness) and F458 (outside-unit supply) are special:
`setVassal` explicitly re-evaluates both relationship-dependent unit predicates across the
transition. The broader connectivity/economic updates are not omitted in the same way:
`addTeam` performs its plot-team refresh and then `CvGame::updatePlotGroups`, whose player
path also verifies production and updates trade routes. No third equally clean player cache
sibling has emerged from that relation transition yet.

Continuation anchor

Continued directly from C031-WIP172 with F459 / provisional KI#782 unused.  This
tranche deliberately emphasizes closure proof and invariant tracing; no numbered
root is promoted merely because code is unusual or because an API could be made
more defensive.

1. getBestRoute(NULL): Railroad resource prerequisite mismatch — CLOSED AS
   INTENTIONAL ABSTRACTION, NOT F459
------------------------------------------------------------
Current CvPlayer::getBestRoute distinguishes two meanings explicitly:

* with pPlot != NULL, the candidate Build must satisfy canBuild(*pPlot, eBuild),
  which re-enters the normal build/route legality path including resource
  prerequisites;
* with pPlot == NULL, the candidate only needs its Build tech prerequisite.

Railroad therefore can be the no-plot "best route" once Railroad's technology is
known even when the player does not currently have Coal/Oil.  This first looked
like a possible resource-legality leak because RouteInfo itself has those
resource prerequisites.

Full caller/ancestry reconciliation closes it.  Stock BtS/Civ4CE, K-Mod, base
AdvCiv and current SAS all retain the same deliberate no-plot behavior for
CvPlot::updateCityRoute and related abstract route valuation.  Worker route
selection uses the plot-aware form and therefore performs the missing resource
check.  AI technology valuation also has separate missing-resource handling.
Movement through a city tile does not turn an ordinary adjoining Road into
Railroad movement because route movement is constrained by the endpoint route
pair, and city tiles have no ordinary improvement whose RouteYieldChanges would
supply a broader resource bypass.  Treat no-plot getBestRoute as "best
technologically unlocked / automatic city route", not "a route a Worker can
construct on an arbitrary plot".

2. CvPlayer::canContact GET_TEAM(ePlayer) — FALSE POSITIVE RECLOSED
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Two expressions in canContact superficially look as if a PlayerTypes value were
being used as a TeamTypes value:

    GET_TEAM(ePlayer).isAtWar(getTeam())
    GET_TEAM(ePlayer).isAlwaysWar()

This is the same enum-overload trap already proven in earlier album controls.
In the active AdvCiv/SAS helper layer GET_TEAM is routed to overloaded getTeam
functions; a PlayerTypes argument resolves to the PlayerTypes overload and that
overload maps through TEAMID(ePlayer).  The expressions are therefore target
player -> target team, as intended.  Do not resurrect the previously retracted
"player index used as team index" family from this syntax alone.

3. Group-cycle stale-ID dereference lead — CLOSED UNDER LIFECYCLE INVARIANT
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CvPlayer::refreshGroupCycleList dereferences getSelectionGroup(pNode->m_data)
without a NULL check, and updateGroupCycle similarly assumes every stored ID
still names a live selection group.  The lifecycle chain maintains that
invariant:

* CvSelectionGroup::kill calls removeGroupCycle(getID()) before
  deleteSelectionGroup(getID());
* player teardown clears m_groupCycle before destroying/uninitializing the
  selection-group container;
* save loading reads the serialized group-cycle IDs and then the serialized
  selection-group array without invoking refreshGroupCycleList in between.

No live stale-ID producer was found.  A defensive NULL check could harden
corrupt/noncanonical state, but the current normal lifecycle does not establish
F459.

4. calculateTotalCommerce excludes culture/espionage — INTENTIONAL advc.004s
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
The name is broader than the current semantics: the function returns gold
commerce + gold-per-turn + research commerce, rather than summing all commerce
types.  This is not an accidental omission.  Base AdvCiv's advc.004s rewrite
explicitly replaced K-Mod's all-commerce calculation for Economy history, and
UWAI contains a dedicated comment acknowledging that culture/espionage are
excluded and that Big Espionage economies may therefore be underestimated.
This is known design, not a newly discovered regression.

5. Building-granted CivicOption loss — DEFERRED REVALIDATION, NOTE ONLY
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS has live building sources for CivicOption (including customized
Colossus -> Government, Mausoleum of Maussollos -> Economy, and Shwedagon Paya
-> Legal).  CvPlayer::processBuilding updates m_aiHasCivicOptionCount, while
changeHasCivicOptionCount itself does not immediately call verifyCivics when the
last source disappears.  Thus losing such a building can transiently leave the
player's current civic in a state that canDoCivics would no longer allow.

The higher-level turn lifecycle bounds this condition: CvPlayer::doTurn calls
verifyCivics every normal turn after city processing/anarchy updates, and
AdvCiv intentionally removed the older "skip verification during anarchy"
guard.  The state therefore does not persist indefinitely; at worst the source
supports a deferred turn-boundary cleanup.  Without stronger evidence that the
intended contract requires immediate invalidation (and given the mutation-heavy
city/building transition where deferral can be deliberate), retain this as a
timing/design robustness note rather than F459.

6. Reconfirmed existing controls encountered during this pass
--------------------------------------------------------------
* changeHurryCount's derived pop/gold-rush cache uses raw iChange across a
  zero/nonzero transition; all live processCivics callers change one civic
  source by +/-1, so the latent |iChange|>1 weakness remains unreachable in
  shipped gameplay.
* checkAlert uses > rather than >= against m_paAlerts.size(), but shipped alert
  IDs and internal loops remain in bounds; equality is API robustness only.
* Team-event propagation in setEventOccured retains the known inverted-member
  condition, but current event XML has no live Team event, so the already-known
  dormant issue is not promoted here.
* checkExpireEvent's boolean test uses bitwise '&' between bool-returning,
  side-effect-free predicates; both sides evaluating does not change gameplay.
* verifyStateReligion remains deliberately disabled in the inherited kekm.10
  path; state religion is represented dynamically through isStateReligion() and
  getLastStateReligion(), and no new current failure was established here.

1. Golden-Age UnitClass readiness vs UnitType consumption — PRIOR CONTROL RECONFIRMED,
   NOT A NEW ROOT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The low-coverage scan naturally rediscovered the mismatch between
`unitsGoldenAgeReady()` (distinct `UnitClassTypes`) and `killGoldenAgeUnits()`
(distinct `UnitTypes`). Full-album duplicate checking showed that C031-WIP158 already
classified this exact seam. K-Mod intentionally changed readiness from unit type to
unit class, but current SAS has exactly one Golden-Age-capable unit type for each Great
Person class and no CivilizationInfos alternate same-class Great Person mapping. Thus
current shipped data cannot make readiness and consumption disagree. Preserve the
existing latent extension/robustness note; do not duplicate it as F459.

2. setCurrentEra -> updateGraphicEra(..., eOldEra) — CLOSED AS EXE/INTERFACE CONTRACT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::setCurrentEra(eNewValue)` stores the old era, assigns the new era, then
updates every unit entity with:

    gDLL->getEntityIFace()->updateGraphicEra(pLoopUnit->getEntity(), eOldEra);

Passing the *old* era initially looks backwards. It is not a local SAS/AdvCiv mistake:

* `CvDLLEntityIFaceBase::updateGraphicEra` explicitly names its optional second
  parameter `eOldEra`;
* stock BtS in Civ4CE passes `eOldEra` from the same player-era transition;
* K-Mod retains that exact argument;
* Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain it as well.

The DLL is therefore supplying the era being left to an EXE-side graphics transition
whose current/new era is already available through player state. Changing this to
`eNewValue` would contradict the interface contract and stock ancestry. Not F459.

3. canHaveTradeRoutesWith anarchy asymmetry — CLOSED BY CALLER / CITY-DISORDER CHAIN
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current helper code rejects a *different* partner when that partner is in anarchy:

    if (getID() != ePlayer && kOtherPlayer.isAnarchy())
        return false;

but does not explicitly reject `this->isAnarchy()`. Read alone, that can look like an
asymmetric foreign-trade rule. The authoritative city caller closes the apparent gap.
`CvCity::updateTradeRoutes()` begins by clearing existing routes and only builds new
ones when the owner city is not in disorder. Anarchy puts the owner's cities in
disorder, so an anarchic player's own cities do not generate routes at all. From the
other direction, non-anarchic players call `canHaveTradeRoutesWith(anarchicPlayer)`
and are rejected by the partner-anarchy check. The resulting gameplay rule is
symmetric even though the helper only needs to test its argument.

The ancestry supports this purpose: advc.124 introduced the partner-anarchy check in
the trade-route eligibility path while also integrating city-disorder handling. The
related `changeNoForeignTradeCount` deferral until anarchy ends is consistent with
trade routes already being suppressed through disorder during the anarchic interval.
Not F459.

4. isValidTriggerReligion / isValidTriggerCorporation sibling comparison — CLEAN
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The event-trigger religion helper was checked because the neighboring corporation
helper carries an explicit K-Mod bugfix. The religion path already has the correct
positive-existence contract in both city and player-wide forms:

* with a selected city, that city must actually have the religion and, when requested,
  must be its Holy City;
* without a selected city, `getHasReligionCount(eReligion)` must be nonzero and the
  owned-Holy-City condition is then checked separately.

There is no analogue of the old corporation helper's inverted/incorrect terminal
logic. Current trigger data adds no contradictory special case. Close this sibling.

5. getProductionTraitModifier unit/building split — CLEAN
---------------------------------------------------------
The two overloads deliberately aggregate both object-specific trait production and,
where applicable, the associated SpecialUnit/SpecialBuilding trait production bonus.
This mirrors the data model rather than double-counting the same field: the direct
UnitInfo/BuildingInfo production-trait array and the special-category production-trait
array are distinct XML sources intended to stack. No current source maps one field
through the other, and ancestry preserves the same additive semantics. No root.

POST-WIP174 RESEARCH / ESPIONAGE CLOSURE TRANCHE
-------------------------------------------------
1. `getResearchTurnsLeftTimes100` teammate-overflow modifier mismatch is a real generic /
   config-dependent defect, but current SAS masks every live modifier difference.

   The function iterates team members and, for each included member, converts that member's
   normalized `getOverflowResearch()` with:

       kMember.getOverflowResearch() * calculateResearchModifier(eTech) / 100

   where the unqualified `calculateResearchModifier` belongs to the SUBJECT player rather
   than `kMember`. This matters conceptually because `doResearch()` stores overflow in
   normalized form and later applies it with EACH PLAYER'S own current research modifier.
   Therefore a faithful team turns-left estimate should likewise apply each member's own
   modifier.

   The prospective-tech path is genuinely callable: the human tech-choice popup calls
   `getResearchTurnsLeft(candidate,true)`, and an already-researching teammate can therefore
   contribute overflow while the subject has not yet selected that candidate. In generic
   AdvCiv configuration the advc.156 extra-team-member modifier can then differ between the
   subject and that teammate; groundbreaking penalties can also be player-specific.

   Current SAS, however, explicitly sets `RESEARCH_MODIFIER_EXTRA_TEAM_MEMBER` to 0, and the
   earlier audit established that both human and AI groundbreaking penalties are disabled.
   All remaining research-modifier components on this path are team/tech-wide. Consequently
   the wrong receiver expression is numerically masked in current shipped SAS gameplay.

   Classification: real latent/config-dependent source defect; no F459.
   Conservative cleanup if desired later: use `kMember.calculateResearchModifier(eTech)`.

2. `espionageNeededToSee` same-team/master-vassal concern closes at its only shipped caller.
   `canSeeIntel` deliberately grants direct visibility to same-team players and to the
   subject's vassals without requiring a passive espionage mission. In isolation,
   `espionageNeededToSee` would then search mission costs even though visibility came from
   that direct relationship. But the only compiled consumer is the scoreboard power-ratio
   hover, and it returns immediately when active player and subject have the same master
   team (`getMasterTeam()` equality), before calling `espionageNeededToSee` at all.
   Ordinary rival use therefore enters the intended passive-espionage case. No gameplay or
   current UI root survives.

3. The already-known `updateCommerceRates()` repeated largest-remainder correction was
   encountered while probing arithmetic helpers and was rejected immediately as a duplicate:
   it is F444 / KI#767, already fully confirmed in C031-WIP151. It is not a new F459 lead.

Continuation anchor

Continued directly from C031-WIP175 with F459 / provisional KI#782 unused. The

F459 / KI#782 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------
Title: Losing the final building-granted CivicOption can leave an unavailable civic
active through the player's next full turn and through that turn's economy/city
processing.

Root / invariant
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
`CvPlayer::canDoCivics` permits a civic when either the player currently has the
civic's CivicOption source OR the player's team has the civic's prerequisite tech:

    if (!isHasCivicOption(GC.getInfo(eCivic).getCivicOptionType()) &&
        !GET_TEAM(getTeam()).isHasTech(GC.getInfo(eCivic).getTechPrereq()))
        return false;

A building with `<CivicOption>` therefore intentionally lets its owner adopt civics
in that category before researching their individual prerequisite technologies.
`CvPlayer::processBuilding` changes `m_aiHasCivicOptionCount` when such a building is
added or removed, but neither `processBuilding` nor `changeHasCivicOptionCount`
revalidates the currently selected civic when the LAST source disappears.

The current civic is not computed dynamically through `canDoCivics`. `setCivics`
applies/removes its gameplay effects through `processCivics`, which changes stored
player modifiers/counters such as capital yield modifiers, commerce modifiers,
trade routes, free specialists, happiness, war weariness, improvement yields, etc.
Those processed effects therefore remain live until `setCivics` is actually called.

Current SAS reachability
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
This is not an API-only possibility. Current SAS deliberately has three live World
Wonder sources:

* `BUILDING_COLOSSUS` at Metal Casting -> `CIVICOPTION_GOVERNMENT`;
* `BUILDING_MAUSOLEUM_OF_MAUSSOLLOS` at Currency -> `CIVICOPTION_ECONOMY`;
* `BUILDING_SHWEDAGON_PAYA` at Meditation -> `CIVICOPTION_LEGAL`.

The latter two never obsolete. All three have `bNeverCapture=0` and
`iConquestProb=100` in current SAS data, so ordinary city loss is a supported source
removal path.

A particularly compact deterministic repro is Shwedagon Paya + Bureaucracy:

1. Player A owns Shwedagon Paya and has not researched Civil Service.
2. Shwedagon's Legal CivicOption makes `canDoCivics(CIVIC_BUREAUCRACY)` true despite
   the missing tech, so A can legitimately adopt Bureaucracy.
3. Current SAS Bureaucracy requires `TECH_CIVIL_SERVICE` and carries +50% capital
   production and +50% capital commerce yield through `CapitalYieldModifiers`.
4. During another player's turn, that player captures A's Shwedagon city.
5. `CvPlayer::acquireCity` calls `pOldCity->kill`; `CvCity::kill` sets every real
   building to zero; the normal `CvCity::processBuilding(...,-1)` ->
   `CvPlayer::processBuilding(...,-1)` chain therefore removes A's final Legal
   CivicOption source immediately.
6. At this point `A.canDoCivics(CIVIC_BUREAUCRACY)` is false, but A's selected civic
   remains Bureaucracy and its `processCivics` modifiers remain applied.

Full-turn consequence
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The old WIP173 classification treated this as a bounded deferred cleanup. The exact
turn lifecycle shows that the bound is nevertheless gameplay-significant.

For normal sequential human turns, `CvPlayer::setTurnActive(true)` does NOT call
`CvPlayer::doTurn`; it prepares the turn, runs team/start/unit work, and gives the
human control. There is no `verifyCivics` call in `acquireCity`, the building-removal
chain, or the normal human turn-activation path.

When that human finally ends the turn, `setTurnActive(false)` calls
`CvPlayer::doTurn()`. And `doTurn` performs, in this order:

    verifyGoldCommercePercent();
    doGold();
    doResearch();
    doEspionagePoints();
    every city -> doTurn();
    ...
    verifyCivics();

Therefore the player gets the ENTIRE following active turn while an objectively
unavailable civic remains selected, and even the end-of-turn economy and every city
turn are processed with that civic still active. Only afterward does
`verifyCivics()` switch the category to a legal civic and remove the stale
`processCivics` effects.

The same omission can also occur through a voluntary city trade during the player's
own active turn; in that case the illegal civic survives through the remainder of
that turn and its end-of-turn processing.

Ancestry / scope
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
This is inherited rather than a SAS-only C++ regression:

* stock BtS/Civ4CE changes the building CivicOption count without immediate civic
  verification and calls `verifyCivics()` only after gold/research/city processing;
* K-Mod retains the same lifecycle;
* AdvCiv 1.14 retains it (advc.004x adds the useful civic-change popup on gaining a
  source, but not loss-side revalidation);
* current SAS retains the code path and expands the practical exposure through its
  customized CivicOption wonders.

Stock BtS/AdvCiv also have building-granted CivicOptions (notably Pyramids ->
Government and Shwedagon Paya -> Religion), so the underlying root can affect base
lineage as well. SAS's current Colossus/Mausoleum/Shwedagon assignments make the
condition especially broad and easy to reach.

Duplicate check
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The full reconciled album contains the exact seam only as the C031-WIP173
"Building-granted CivicOption loss — DEFERRED REVALIDATION, NOTE ONLY" control.
That note explicitly left promotion open pending stronger timing/contract evidence.
No earlier numbered root covers the missing loss-side revalidation. F459 therefore
upgrades that prior control rather than duplicating another finding.

Fix direction (not implemented)
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The semantic fix is to ensure that crossing the final CivicOption source from
positive to zero revalidates a currently selected civic that no longer passes
`canDoCivics`. The most direct location is the loss-side zero transition in
`changeHasCivicOptionCount` / `processBuilding`. Because building removal may occur
inside `CvCity::kill`/city transfer, implementation should still check reentrancy of
an immediate `verifyCivics()`/`setCivics` call; if a deferred flag is safer, it must
be consumed before the player can act and before gold/research/city processing, not
at the current late end-of-turn location.

Additional closures in this tranche
-----------------------------------
1. `GET_TEAM(getID())` occurrences in free-unit initialization are not player/team
   index bugs. The active AdvCiv/SAS helper overload resolves a `PlayerTypes`
   argument through the player -> team mapping; this is the already-known enum
   overload trap and remains closed.

2. `getEspionageSpending` remainder allocation is inherited BtS/K-Mod behavior. It
   distributes integer leftovers to the highest-weight eligible targets after the
   proportional division. No arithmetic invariant failure was established.

3. `canReceiveGoody` / hostile-goody minimum handling retains the prior latent
   zero-minimum robustness note, but current hostile goody XML uses positive minima;
   no current F460 lead there.

Continued directly from C031-WIP176 with F460 / provisional KI#783 unused.  This

F460 / KI#783 — city-trade outer-ring culture conversion asks for the traded city's
working priority only after that city has been deleted, so documented full-radius
conversion is silently skipped on ordinary outer-ring plots
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — AdvCiv-introduced `advc.ctr` gameplay bug retained by AdvCiv 1.14 and
current AdvCiv-SAS.  The underlying full-radius conversion feature does not exist in
K-Mod 1.46 / stock BtS-Civ4CE; their older inner-ring-only transfer does not depend on
the deleted city's working priority and therefore does not contain this exact root.

DOCUMENTED ADVC.CTR CONTRACT
----------------------------
The AdvCiv manual's `ctr (cont.) Consequences of city trades` section explicitly says
that, when a city is traded:

* old-owner tile culture is decreased in the **full city radius (21 tiles)**;
* tiles contested by cities not belonging to the new owner are excluded **unless the
  traded city has the higher working priority**, based on distance and age;
* the new owner's tile culture increases by the amount removed from the old owner.

This is also exactly what the source comment in
`CvPlayer::cultureConvertedUponCityTrade` says for the outer circle:

    // Outer circle: Based on plot priority when contested
    CvCity const* pDefaultWorkingCity = kPlot.defaultWorkingCity();
    bConvert = (pDefaultWorkingCity != NULL &&
            /* Plot has to be assigned to the traded city or to
               a city of the new owner */
            (pDefaultWorkingCity->at(kCityPlot) ||
             pDefaultWorkingCity->getOwner() == eNewOwner));

`CvPlot::defaultWorkingCity` was itself factored out of `updateWorkingCity` with the
explicit note `advc: Cut from updateWorkingCity (for advc.ctr)`.  It selects the
highest-priority currently live nearby city, using city-plot priority and then
founding-time / city-ID tie-breakers.  Thus both documentation and code structure say
that the traded city is supposed to be a possible answer here.

ACTUAL ACQUIRECITY ORDER MAKES THAT HALF OF THE TEST IMPOSSIBLE
---------------------------------------------------------------
The ordinary current transfer path in `CvPlayer::acquireCity` is ordered as follows:

1. preserve the old city's data;
2. call

       pOldCity->kill(false, false);
       pOldCity = NULL;

3. only then, for `bTrade`, iterate `CityPlotIter(kCityPlot)` and call

       cultureConvertedUponCityTrade(kCityPlot, *it, eOldOwner, getID());

4. only after the culture-conversion loop call `initCity(...)` for the replacement
   city owned by the recipient.

This is not merely a dangling-pointer concern. `CvCity::kill` performs the decisive
lifecycle work before returning:

* `kPlot.setPlotCity(NULL)` removes the city from its plot;
* `kOwner.deleteCity(getID())` deletes it from the owner's live city container;
* after the ownership/culture updates it calls `GC.getMap().updateWorkingCity()`.

Consequently every plot's working-city assignment is recomputed without the traded
city in existence.  When `cultureConvertedUponCityTrade` subsequently calls
`kPlot.defaultWorkingCity()`, the documented candidate "the traded city" cannot be
returned.  The replacement city also cannot be returned because it has not yet been
created.

For an outer-ring plot (`adjacentOrSame == false`), the first intended condition

    pDefaultWorkingCity->at(kCityPlot)

is therefore dead on the actual transfer path.

DETERMINISTIC ORDINARY REPRODUCTION
-----------------------------------
A minimal source-supported example needs no unusual XML or API use:

1. Player A owns city C; player B is eligible to receive C through an ordinary city
   trade.  Current AdvCiv city-trade rules only require sufficient B city-tile culture,
   so this is normal gameplay.
2. Choose an outer-ring (distance-2) plot P that C can work and for which C is the
   default/highest-priority working city before the transfer.  Let no other A city be
   able to work P.
3. Give P, for example, 100 A tile culture and 40 B tile culture.  P remains owned by A
   across the deletion step, so after C is killed it has no live default working city.
4. Under the intended helper calculation, while C still exists, P qualifies because
   `defaultWorkingCity(P) == C`.  Current conversion arithmetic would therefore move

       min(100 / 2, 2 * 40) = 50

   culture points from A to B, leaving A=50 and B=90 on P.
5. In actual `acquireCity`, C is killed first. `GC.getMap().updateWorkingCity()` then
   removes C from P's assignment.  With no other A city in range,
   `P.defaultWorkingCity()` is NULL.
6. The later outer-ring helper returns 0; P remains A=100, B=40 instead of receiving
   the documented transfer.

The same failure also affects contested outer plots where another old-owner city
becomes the default only *after* deletion.  Even if C had the higher priority before
trade — exactly the case the manual says should convert — C is no longer available to
win that comparison.

The inner ring is not the problem: `adjacentOrSame(kPlot,kCityPlot)` makes those plots
convert without consulting a working city.  F460 is specifically the full-radius /
outer-ring extension introduced by AdvCiv.

LIVE CONSEQUENCES
-----------------
The immediate authoritative consequence is wrong persistent plot culture after a city
trade.  The recipient fails to receive culture that the documented AdvCiv rule says
belongs with the ceded city; the former owner retains it instead.  This can change plot
ownership/border shape, subsequent cultural pressure, workable-tile access and later
revolt/culture calculations.

There is also an AI/runtime mismatch in the same feature family.  `CvPlayerAI` uses
`cultureConvertedUponCityTrade(..., bIgnorePriority=true)` while valuing a peacefully
acquired city, which estimates conversion throughout the radius without depending on
the post-kill working-city state.  Some approximation is deliberate there, so that is
not a separate root; however the execution-order defect means the actual transfer can
systematically grant less outer-ring culture than the city-acquisition valuation is
built around.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod 1.46 and stock BtS/Civ4CE perform the old trade consequence *after* killing the
city too, but their rule only loops the inner 3x3 area and sets old-owner culture to
zero.  That operation needs no old-city priority, so the ordering is harmless there.

AdvCiv's `advc.ctr` replaces that old inner-ring loop with `CityPlotIter` plus
`cultureConvertedUponCityTrade`, explicitly expanding the policy to the full city
radius and introducing a dependence on whether the **traded city** is the
`defaultWorkingCity`.  The old post-kill placement was retained.  AdvCiv 1.14 and
current SAS have the same order and helper logic.

This is therefore an AdvCiv feature-integration/order bug rather than a stock-BtS root
or a SAS-local regression.

DUPLICATE CHECK
---------------
The reconciled album contains earlier `advc.ctr` findings in the diplomacy/AI city
trade family (including city-for-war balancing and request-city selection), but no
prior root for transfer-time tile-culture conversion, `cultureConvertedUponCityTrade`,
or the full-radius working-priority lifetime mismatch.  Full-album searches for the
helper, full-radius trade culture and outer-circle conversion were clean.  F460 is a
new root.

REPAIR DIRECTION — NOT IMPLEMENTED
----------------------------------
Preserve the conversion decision while the old city still exists, then apply the
culture changes at the existing safe point after deletion.  The most conservative
shape is:

* before `pOldCity->kill`, iterate the 21 city plots and snapshot each intended
  conversion amount by calling `cultureConvertedUponCityTrade` while
  `defaultWorkingCity()` can still return the traded city;
* after `kill`, apply those saved amounts to old/new player plot culture exactly where
  the current conversion loop lives;
* then initialize the new city as current code already does.

This avoids changing plot ownership/working assignments prematurely while the old city
is still alive, and it preserves the exact documented priority decision at the moment
when all of its required city objects exist.

Alternatively the helper would need enough pre-kill state passed explicitly to answer
"was the traded city the default working city here?" after deletion.  Simply calling
`defaultWorkingCity()` later cannot recover that information.

A regression test should use an outer-ring plot uniquely assigned to the ceded city,
with nonzero recipient culture, and verify the documented conversion amount survives
the `CvCity::kill`/recreate transfer sequence.  A second test should use an outer plot
contested by two old-owner cities and verify conversion occurs iff the ceded city had
higher pre-transfer priority.

------------------------

  semantics.  Movement denial and the team-wide spy-ejection hook use the same
  orientation; no reversed-player root survives.

  no current arithmetic/caller mismatch was established in this pass.
