  shape because AdvCiv introduced `BaseGrowthThresholdPercent`; no source/data contract
  establishes that the player-handicap component should multiply the population term
  too, so no root was manufactured.
* free-promotion event setters and `promoteFreeUnit` remain legal under current
  promotion data/canAcquirePromotion checks.  The latter's enum-order heuristic is
  fragile but no current data violation was proved.
* `CvPlayer::getEventTriggerWeight` retained the prior corrected handicap-difficulty
  logic; current building-multiply triggers fit the implementation.
* `doGold`, `doResearch`, `doEspionagePoints` and espionage-spending weight setters
  retain their normal bookkeeping contracts; previously classified research-overflow

CONTINUATION ANCHOR
-------------------
Continued Queue 004 `CvGameCoreDLL/CvPlayer.cpp` directly from C031-WIP177 with
F461 / provisional KI#784 unused.  The first pass reconciled capital yield/commerce
mutators against the earlier F445 retraction and then moved into genuinely
under-covered religion / espionage / persistent-visibility player state.  No
repository source files were modified.

CAPITAL-MUTATOR RECONCILIATION — CLEAN / F445 RETRACTION REMAINS AUTHORITATIVE
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
`changeCapitalYieldRateModifier` explicitly invalidates the exact affected yield-rank
cache and refreshes capital work assignment. `changeCapitalCommerceRateModifier`
refreshes the capital through `CvCity::updateCommerce()`, whose no-argument form also
invalidates the player's yield-rank caches. Thus the cross-file callee proof that
retracted F445 remains correct; no hidden capital-modifier sibling survives here.

F461 / KI#784 — `m_abEverSeenDemographics` IS LATCHED ONLY BY ESPIONAGE-POINT
CHANGES, SO FULL SCORE HISTORY CAN BECOME VISIBLE WITHOUT EVER BEING RECORDED AS
"EVER SEEN"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — AdvCiv-introduced `advc.091` persistent-information bug retained by
AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS. K-Mod supplies the population-sensitive
espionage-cost machinery, but it has no `m_abEverSeenDemographics` latch; this exact
root begins when AdvCiv adds the persistent "ever seen" state and updates it from an
incomplete set of threshold-changing transitions.

ADVC.091 CONTRACT IS EXPLICIT
-----------------------------
AdvCiv's Info Screen adds `m_abEverSeenDemographics` specifically to distinguish
players whose **full score history has ever been visible** from players whose full
history has never been visible.

The shipped BUG option text for `Partial Score Graphs` states:

    For players whose full score history has never been visible to you,
    display a score graph that only shows the player's game scores since
    the turn that you've first met.

`CvInfoScreen.showTotalScoreGraph` implements exactly that distinction:

    return ((gameTurn - hasMetTurn >= 5 and PartialScoreGraphs) or
            pActivePlayer.hasEverSeenDemographics(iPlayer))

and score-cache construction uses the same latch to decide whether pre-contact score
history must be hidden.

Therefore this boolean is not merely an optimization hint. Once the active player has
actually met the passive-demographics threshold and the full score history has been
shown, the bit is meant to remain true even if current espionage visibility is later
lost.

THE ONLY LIVE LATCH UPDATE IS TOO NARROW
----------------------------------------
Current `CvPlayer::updateEverSeenDemographics(TeamTypes eTargetTeam)` does the right
predicate test:

    if (!hasEverSeenDemographics(target) && canSeeDemographics(target))
        m_abEverSeenDemographics.set(target, true);

but a whole-tree caller search finds only one normal DLL updater:

    CvTeam::setEspionagePointsAgainstTeam
        -> each member.updateEverSeenDemographics(eIndex)

No call is made from the other state transitions that change
`canSeeDemographics()` / passive mission cost.

That is insufficient because `canSeeDemographics` is not a function solely of the
watcher's current espionage points. It calls `canDoEspionageMission`, which compares
those points against `getEspionageMissionCost`, and that cost includes several
mutable modifiers.

MOST DIRECT CURRENT PRODUCER: COUNTERESPIONAGE EXPIRY
-----------------------------------------------------
The shipped demographics passive mission is live and has:

    ESPIONAGEMISSION_SEE_DEMOGRAPHICS
    iCost = 30
    bIsPassive = 1
    bSeeDemographics = 1

The shipped Counterespionage mission is also live and has:

    iCounterespionageNumTurns = 10
    iCounterespionageMod = 100

K-Mod's mission-cost modifier multiplies passive mission cost by the target team's
counterespionage modifier against the spying team:

    iModifier *= 100 + max(-100,
            kTargetTeam.getCounterespionageModAgainstTeam(getTeam()));
    iModifier /= 100;

Thus the shipped +100 Counterespionage effect doubles the otherwise identical
passive-demographics cost.

The effect expires in `CvTeam::doTurn`:

    changeCounterespionageTurnsLeftAgainstTeam(eOther, -1);
    if (getCounterespionageTurnsLeftAgainstTeam(eOther) == 0)
        setCounterespionageModAgainstTeam(eOther, 0);

`setCounterespionageModAgainstTeam` only stores the new modifier and dirties the
Espionage Advisor. It does **not** call `updateEverSeenDemographics` for members of
the opposing team whose passive visibility may just have become affordable.

Likewise, changing population can alter K-Mod's `CvTeam::getEspionageModifier`, and
therefore the passive threshold, without changing current espionage points. The
Counterespionage expiry case is sufficient by itself and gives the cleanest current
reproduction.

DETERMINISTIC CURRENT-DATA REPRODUCTION
---------------------------------------
Use two met singleton major teams A and B with equal total population and arrange
equal team `getEspionagePointsEver()` values. This makes K-Mod's population/points
ratio modifier exactly 100. Arrange the current directional points so that:

* B currently has 0 EP against A (spent points do not reduce PointsEver);
* A currently has 50 EP against B;
* B has an active +100 Counterespionage modifier against A;
* A has never previously met the demographics threshold, so
  `A.hasEverSeenDemographics(B) == false`.

These values are ordinary reachable state: points-ever persists after active missions
spend current points, and the current Counterespionage mission creates the +100 timed
effect.

With equal team sizes and the setup above:

1. The base passive-demographics cost is 30. B's current EP against A is zero, so the
   passive base-cost term remains 30.
2. Equal population and equal PointsEver give an espionage ratio modifier of 100.
3. While B's Counterespionage is active, the final +100 modifier doubles the cost to
   60. A has only 50 EP, so `canSeeDemographics(B)` is false.
4. If A gains/reaches those 50 points while protection is active,
   `setEspionagePointsAgainstTeam` does call `updateEverSeenDemographics`, but the
   predicate is false and the latch correctly remains false at that moment.
5. B's Counterespionage timer later reaches zero in `CvTeam::doTurn`.
   `setCounterespionageModAgainstTeam(B->A, 0)` lowers A's demographics threshold
   from 60 to 30 without changing A's EP against B.
6. A can now see B's demographics and full Info Screen score history. Opening the
   Info Screen classifies B through the live `canSeeDemographics` check and really
   reveals that history.
7. No `updateEverSeenDemographics` call occurs on the counterespionage-expiry path,
   so `hasEverSeenDemographics(B)` incorrectly remains false despite the history
   having been visible.
8. If B later applies Counterespionage again, A's current visibility can disappear.
   With the default `Partial Score Graphs = False`, `showTotalScoreGraph(B)` now also
   returns false because the supposedly permanent "ever seen" bit was never latched.
   The full score history disappears as though A had never unlocked it.

The same missing latch can be reached whenever a non-EP cost dependency crosses the
threshold. K-Mod's `getEspionageModifier` depends on both teams' current population,
so population changes provide another ordinary source. Counterespionage expiry is the
simpler proof because the shipped +100 modifier creates a large deterministic
threshold change.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE
----------------
This is persistent-information state, not merely an Espionage Advisor redraw issue.
While the threshold is temporarily satisfied, the ordinary Info Screen uses
`canSeeDemographics()` and exposes the target's full graph/history information. Once
current visibility is lost, AdvCiv intends `hasEverSeenDemographics` to preserve the
fact that this history was already revealed. The missed latch can instead revoke the
full Total Score graph later and make partial/full history gating behave as if the
player had never seen it.

The default shipped BUG setting `Partial Score Graphs = False` makes the consequence
particularly direct: after visibility is lost again, a false ever-seen bit removes
the target's Total Score graph rather than falling back to the optional post-contact
partial graph.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod provides the population-sensitive `CvTeam::getEspionageModifier` and timed
Counterespionage cost effect, but does not have AdvCiv's persistent ever-seen score-
graph latch.

AdvCiv practical 2468 / SHA `f91c93bea834f12a3f5da1894d8afaa1a07b4cac`, which
introduced `advc.091` ("Show score graph (Info screen) regardless of espionage"),
added all of the following together:

* `m_abEverSeenDemographics`;
* `updateEverSeenDemographics`;
* Info Screen `hasEverSeenDemographics` graph gating;
* a call to the updater from `CvTeam::setEspionagePointsAgainstTeam`.

The introducing diff contains no updater on Counterespionage modifier/timer changes,
population changes, or a generic "current demographics just became visible" path.
The only later history change touching the call merely added the Barbarian guard
(practical 3437, "Fix minor issue with a failed assertion"). Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
current SAS retain the same incomplete updater set.

This is therefore an AdvCiv integration/invalidation omission: the new persistent
cache was wired to one input (`EspionagePointsAgainstTeam`) although its predicate
has additional mutable inputs inherited from K-Mod.

DUPLICATE CHECK
---------------
The album already contains F079/KI#401 in the same `advc.091` feature family:
Permanent Alliance resets `m_aiHasMetTurn`, which breaks first-contact dates used by
partial score graphs. That is a different stored field, transition and consequence.

The album also contains F078/KI#400 for Permanent Alliance dropping live
Counterespionage state. F461 does not depend on a Permanent Alliance and does not lose
a Counterespionage effect; it concerns the missing persistent-demographics latch when
a legitimate effect expires or another cost input changes.

Full-album searches for `m_abEverSeenDemographics`, `updateEverSeenDemographics`,
Counterespionage-driven demographics visibility and the full-history latch found no
prior root. F461 is distinct.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION — NOT IMPLEMENTED
-----------------------------------------------
The invariant to preserve is:

    whenever `canSeeDemographics(target)` becomes true for a player who has not
    previously latched it, set `m_abEverSeenDemographics[target] = true`.

A narrow repair should at minimum update opposing player members when a
Counterespionage modifier changes in a direction that can reduce their passive cost,
especially when the modifier expires. However, population-dependent espionage ratios
mean Counterespionage alone is not the complete dependency set.

The more robust design is to centralize/lazily latch this state at a normal place that
actually queries or refreshes demographics visibility, or to call a small updater
from every authoritative transition that can lower the passive-demographics cost.
Care is needed not to turn a read-only const query into surprising persistent mutation
without considering save/OOS behavior.

Regression tests should cover at least:

1. reach the demographics threshold through an EP change -> ever-seen becomes true
   (existing path/control);
2. remain below the protected threshold, let +100 Counterespionage expire without any
   EP change, become able to see demographics -> ever-seen must become true;
3. lose current visibility again -> full-score-history gating must still remember the
   prior reveal;
4. optionally, cross the threshold solely through a population-driven
   `getEspionageModifier` change.

-------------------------------------

  update chains; F445 remains retracted.
* religion conversion/anarchy helpers inspected in the immediate neighboring pass
  retain their inherited timer/update contracts; no separate F462 candidate was
  established before this checkpoint.
* the previously classified Golden-Age readiness UnitClass vs consumption UnitType
  mismatch remains current-data masked and is not duplicated here.

POST-F461 CONTROL — PERMANENT ALLIANCE TEAM-SIZE SCORE INPUT IS RECOMPUTED
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::getPopScore(true)` and `getLandScore(true)` divide the included vassal
contribution by `GET_TEAM(getTeam()).getNumMembers()`. A Permanent Alliance therefore
changes those dynamic score values when the absorbed players move onto the surviving
team, which initially looked like another relationship-cache sibling of F455/F458.

The merge path closes the invariant, however: `CvTeam::addTeam` finishes with an
unconditional `kGame.updateScore(true)` after the player/team reassignment work. The
global player scores and ranks are therefore recomputed using the new team-member
count. No stale-score root survives.

POST-F461 CONTROL — NO ANALOGOUS PERSISTENT "EVER SAW RESEARCH" LATCH
------------------------------------------------------------------------
The immediate intelligence sibling is isolated. AdvCiv stores persistent
`m_abEverSeenDemographics` specifically for score-graph history; research visibility
is queried from current `canSeeResearch` state and has no parallel persistent
"ever-seen research" field whose invalidation could share F461. No independent F462
candidate exists there.

CONTROL — DELAYED EVENT COUNTDOWN HAS A REAL USE-AFTER-ERASE, BUT CURRENT SAS DATA
DOES NOT PRODUCE COUNTDOWNS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::doEvents()` contains an unambiguous C++ lifetime defect for due delayed
events:

    EventTriggeredData const* pTriggeredData = getEventCountdown(eLoopEvent);
    ...
    applyEvent(eLoopEvent, pTriggeredData->m_iId);
    resetEventCountdown(eLoopEvent);          // std::map::erase of the node
    aCleanup.push_back(pTriggeredData->m_iId); // dereference after erase

`getEventCountdown` returns the address of the `m_mapEventCountdown` node value and
`resetEventCountdown` erases that node, so the final dereference is invalid. The same
ordering is inherited from stock BtS/Civ4CE through K-Mod and base AdvCiv 1.14.

Current SAS nevertheless does not establish an ordinary producer. Every shipped
`<EventTimes>` table in `CIV4EventInfos.xml` is empty, and `applyEvent` calls
`setEventCountdown` only when an AdditionalEvent time is nonzero. A whole-tree search
also finds no Python-facing `setEventCountdown` producer. Thus no shipped current game
creates one of these delayed-countdown map nodes through the event system.

Preserve as a real dormant robustness bug. The narrow lifetime repair is to save
`pTriggeredData->m_iId` into an integer before erasing the countdown and use that saved
ID afterward. F462 remains unused.

CONTROL — LIVE CIVILIZATION CHANGE DOES NOT LEAVE A CURRENT SAS FOUNDER-CLASS COST
ENTRY BEHIND
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::changeCiv` installs the new civilization and calls
`resetCivTypeEffects(false)`. That helper rewrites cached founding-unit extra cost for
founder UnitClasses present in the NEW civilization but does not explicitly erase
founder-class entries belonging only to the OLD civilization. In a more extensively
modded data set, changing between civilizations that use different founding UnitClasses
could therefore leave an old `m_aUnitExtraCosts` entry behind.

Current SAS masks that generic weakness completely: the entire Unit XML contains one
`bFound=1` unit, `UNIT_SETTLER`, and current civilization mappings use the same
`UNITCLASS_SETTLER`. `changeCiv` therefore rewrites the one relevant cache key rather
than leaving a distinct old founder class stale. True Starts uses `changeCiv`; the
Python ChangePlayer utility also reaches it, but neither changes that current-data
fact. No F462.

------------------------------

  F448 for the live Rise & Fall human/AI-control invalidation; do not rediscover it
  through civilization-change or handicap-adjacent passes.
* `checkAlert` still has the real `>` vs `>= m_paAlerts.size()` robustness typo, but
  all shipped alert IDs/internal loops remain 0..size-1; this was already preserved
  unnumbered in earlier Queue-004 work.
* `canStealTech`'s `GET_TEAM(eTarget)` remains the already-closed AdvCiv overload trap:
  the `PlayerTypes` overload resolves the target player's real team.
* `killGoldenAgeUnits` UnitType-vs-readiness-UnitClass mismatch remains current-data
  masked because SAS has only one Golden-Age unit type per relevant class.

CONTROL — `OtherPlayerHasTech` IS CHECKED ON THE CORRECT RECEIVER
-----------------------------------------------------------------
The trigger eligibility condition

    GET_TEAM(getTeam()).isHasTech(kTrigger.getOtherPlayerHasTech())

looks suspicious if `CvPlayer::canTrigger` is read as though `this` were the
trigger owner. Full caller orientation resolves it:

    itPlayer->canTrigger(..., getID(), ...)

is invoked on each candidate other player. Inside `canTrigger`, `this` is
therefore the candidate OTHER player and the explicit `ePlayer` argument is
the trigger owner. `GET_TEAM(getTeam())` consequently checks exactly the team
named by `OtherPlayerHasTech`. No defect.

  already-owned findings.

CONTROL — `changeHurryCount` RAW `iChange` UPDATE IS SAFE UNDER CURRENT CALLERS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`changeHurryCount` updates the derived pop-rush / gold-rush availability
counters by raw `iChange` when the source count crosses zero. In a generic API
this would be wrong if a single call crossed the boundary by magnitude > 1.

Current compiled callers constrain the delta: hurry availability is processed
through civic boolean sources using +/-1 transitions. The derived counter
therefore changes by exactly one whenever availability flips. No current root.

CONTROL — HOSTILE GOODY MIN-BARBARIAN DIVISION HAS A GENERIC CONFIGURATION
HOLE, BUT CURRENT SAS DATA MASKS IT
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
The hostile-unit block in `receiveGoody` contains:

    int iMinBarbs = max(kGoody.getMinBarbarians(),
        (kGoody.getMinBarbarians() * goodyHutEffectFactor(false)).sqrt().round());
    int iProb = (kGoody.getBarbarianUnitProb() * iMinBarbs) /
        kGoody.getMinBarbarians();

A bad goody configured to enter this block with `MinBarbarians == 0` could
therefore divide by zero.

Current shipped hostile goodies do not satisfy that malformed configuration:
the weak barbarian result has `MinBarbarians = 1`, the strong result has
`MinBarbarians = 2`. The other non-bad outcomes using
`BarbarianUnitProb` participate in AdvCiv's upgrade/additional-outcome logic,
not this zero-min hostile case. Preserve as robustness debt only; no F462.

CONTROL — ABSOLUTE GAME TURN IN ADVC.314 GOODY SCALING IS DESIGN-ALIGNED
------------------------------------------------------------------------
A later-era start begins with nonzero `getGameTurn()` while elapsed turns are
zero, so AdvCiv's absolute-turn checks can make early hut protections weaker
or already expired on turn 0 of Classical/Medieval starts. That initially
looked like an elapsed-vs-absolute-turn regression.

The surrounding feature points the other way. AdvCiv's `advc.314`
`goodyHutEffectFactor` itself deliberately scales from absolute world/game
turn, later-era starts receive correspondingly advanced starting packages,
and current Renaissance+ eras disable goodies entirely. The absolute-turn
tests are therefore coherent with the feature's overall world-age scaling,
not a proven stray substitution. Close; no F462.

TURN-CONTROL / SMALL STATE HELPERS
----------------------------------
`setAutoMoves`, `isTurnDone`, `setStrike`, `getReligionAnarchyLength`,
`setEspionageSpendingWeightAgainstTeam`, and nearby small state helpers were
rechecked through their ordinary callers. No new authoritative gameplay
contradiction has survived. Persistent strike-turn behavior is already
documented policy from earlier Queue-004 work rather than a fresh bug.

CONTROL — ORGANIZED RELIGION MONASTERY EXEMPTION DOES NOT LET INVALID
MISSIONARY PRODUCTION CONTINUE
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS uses the `SpecialBuildingNotRequired` civic mechanism in ordinary
gameplay: Organized Religion makes `SPECIALBUILDING_MONASTERY` unnecessary,
so missionaries whose normal prerequisite is a Monastery can legitimately be
queued without that building.

`setCivics` itself does not immediately call a city-production verifier, so a
queued missionary can remain temporarily present after switching away from
Organized Religion. The full city-turn lifecycle closes the apparent bypass:

* every `CvCity::doTurn()` begins with `doCheckProduction()`;
* `doCheckProduction()` reaches `checkCanContinueProduction(false)`;
* an order that no longer passes its unit/building prerequisites is popped
  with `bFinish=false`;
* this happens before the city can receive normal production for the turn,
  including through a period of civic anarchy.

Therefore loss of the civic exemption does not let an invalid missionary keep
accumulating normal production or complete. No F462.

CONTROL — LOSS OF PLAYER-WIDE SPECIALIST VALIDITY IS CLAMPED BEFORE THE NEXT
PRODUCTIVE TURN
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Organized Religion also grants player-wide Priest validity in current SAS.
Losing that civic can temporarily leave assigned Priests above the city's
ordinary slot count.

The player-level mutator dirties city work assignment. On the first
non-anarchy `CvPlayer::doTurn`, `AI_assignWorkingPlots()` reaches each city and
clamps assigned specialists that are no longer valid and exceed the restored
slot cap before gold, research and city processing. During civic anarchy the
cleanup is deferred, but the city is in disorder and gains no productive turn
from the stale assignment. No F462.

ROBUSTNESS NOTE — `canHurry` DOES NOT REVALIDATE THE CURRENT PRODUCTION ORDER
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
There is a real inherited timing/API hole adjacent to the preceding closure.

After a civic switch makes the current queued unit/building invalid,
`CvCity::canHurry` does not call `canContinueProduction`, `canTrain` or
`canConstruct` for the current order. A human can therefore hurry that stale
order before the end-turn `doCheckProduction()` cleanup.

The DLL accepts the action: population/gold is spent, hurry anger is applied
and hurry production is added. At the subsequent city turn, however,
`doCheckProduction()` removes the still-invalid order with `bFinish=false`;
the unit/building is not created. The accumulated per-type production remains
banked for a future legal build.

A current-data example is a Spiritual player using Organized Religion +
Slavery, queuing a missionary without its Monastery, switching away from
Organized Religion with zero civic anarchy and whipping the now-invalid queue
entry before ending the turn.

This is a genuine inherited action-validation/UX robustness defect, but it
does not bypass the prerequisite or produce the invalid unit/building. The
same player could also have hurried the valid order immediately before the
civic switch. Preserve below the numbered gameplay-root threshold; F462 stays
unused.

CONTROL — `processCivics` FIELD/CACHE RECONCILIATION
-----------------------------------------------------
A field-by-field pass compared civic effects against their mutators and live
consumers rather than assuming every zero-boundary counter needed an explicit
bulk refresh.

Important closures:

* distance, colony, number-of-cities and corporation maintenance modifiers
  call player-wide `updateMaintenance()`, which recomputes every city's
  cached maintenance and the player's total;
* trade-route modifiers refresh trade routes;
* yield/commerce modifiers invalidate or recompute the affected caches;
* happiness/health effects are dynamically queried or dirty city assignment;
* `NoCivicUpkeep` and `NoNonStateReligionSpread` are consumed dynamically;
* `BuildingOnlyHealthy` is dynamically reflected in city health and dirties
  assignment;
* `SpecialBuildingNotRequired` is enforced by the city production check above;
* `SpecialistValid` is clamped through dirty work assignment as described
  above.

No additional stale-economy sibling of F459 was established.

CONTROL — STATIC LOCAL GLOBALDEFINE CACHES ALREADY MECHANICALLY AUDITED
------------------------------------------------------------------------
A fresh SAS-specific scan considered whether local `static const` performance
caches could retain game-dependent values across multiple games in one Civ4
process.

Album reconciliation shows that this exact class was already mechanically
closed in the earlier File-004 control pass: 103 GlobalDefine names read by
current `CvPlayer.cpp` were compared against runtime `setDefineINT`,
`setDefineFLOAT` and `setDefineSTRING` mutation sites in C++ and Python/map
scripts, with no overlap. The current local static values in this file are
overwhelmingly such GlobalDefines, color/info-type lookups and fixed text
lookups rather than player/world/game-speed expressions.

Do not duplicate this as a new investigation root unless a genuinely
game-state-dependent static expression is found.

* state-religion unit/building production modifiers are queried dynamically;
* state-religion free experience is applied from current player state at unit

* upkeep, level-experience, city-defense and feature-production modifiers are

POST-WIP181 BUILDING / CIVILIZATION-CHANGE CONTROLS
----------------------------------------------------
The first continuation tranche closed several player-building lifecycle concerns before
F462 surfaced.

1. Building obsolescence player effects are symmetrically processed.

`CvTeam::changeObsoleteBuildingCount` detects the zero/nonzero obsolete-state transition
and calls each affected city's `processBuilding` with `bObsolete=true`, subtracting the
same active city/player/team/game effects when obsolescence begins and adding them back
if obsolescence is removed. No generic "obsolete wonder retains player bonus" root was
established.

2. Runtime civilization-change concrete-building mappings are a real debug/API caveat,
not an ordinary True Starts root.

Some `CvPlayer::processBuilding` effects are stored against the current civilization's
concrete building mapping, e.g. a wonder's `FreeBuildingClass` and
`BuildingHappinessChanges`. `changeCiv` does not reprocess already-existing buildings,
so an already-developed player changed through the cheat ChangePlayer utility can retain
old-civilization concrete-building caches/free-building state.

Current ordinary True Starts does not expose that state:
* `TrueStarts::changeCivs()` runs before `initFreeCivState` / `initFreeUnits` and before
  normal cities/buildings are created;
* scenario True Starts only performs the replacement when the scenario contains no
  cities;
* the Python ChangePlayer UI itself is gated behind cheats.

Preserve as runtime-change/debug robustness debt. It does not consume F462.

3. Permanent Alliance TeamShare-building replay is explicitly handled and current data
masks it anyway.

K-Mod/AdvCiv `CvTeam::shareItems` walks each constituent side's existing cities before
team reassignment. For `isTeamShare()` buildings it replays `CvPlayer::processBuilding`
onto the other side's players in both directions, and processes team building state as
well. Current SAS additionally has no `<bTeamShare>1</bTeamShare>` BuildingInfo entries.
No PA team-shared-building sibling of F455/F458.

4. AdvCiv's shrine cache key is internally consistent under current data.

`CvCity::processBuilding` detects shrine buildings through `getHolyCity()!=NO_RELIGION`
but indexes `m_aiShrine` with `getReligionType()`. All seven current shrine BuildingInfos
set `HolyCity` and `ReligionType` to the same religion, and `CvCity::hasShrine` reads the
cache by that religion. No current wrong-key root.


F462 / KI#785 — FORCE-CIVIC ESPIONAGE USES THE SPY OWNER'S REVOLUTION-COOLDOWN
MODIFIER INSTEAD OF THE TARGET PLAYER'S
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED. Ordinary current espionage reaches the defect. This is an AdvCiv refactor
regression: stock BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod use the target player's modifier explicitly;
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS call the new helper on the wrong `CvPlayer` receiver.

ROOT
----
On a successful Force Civic espionage mission, current SAS does:

    GET_PLAYER(eTargetPlayer).setCivics(
            GC.getInfo(eCivic).getCivicOptionType(), eCivic);

    GET_PLAYER(eTargetPlayer).setRevolutionTimer(
            getMinTurnsBetweenRevolutions());

The target of the setter is correct, but the unqualified
`getMinTurnsBetweenRevolutions()` is invoked on `this` — the spying player.

The helper is player-specific:

    int getMinTurnsBetweenRevolutions() const
    {
        return std::max(1,
                ((100 + getAnarchyModifier()) *
                MIN_REVOLUTION_TURNS) / 100);
    }

Therefore the victim's post-mission civic cooldown is computed from the SPY OWNER's
`getAnarchyModifier()`.

The immediately neighboring Force Religion branch provides a useful internal control.
It sets the target's conversion timer from:

    GET_PLAYER(eTargetPlayer).getAnarchyModifier()

rather than the spy owner's modifier.

CURRENT SHIPPED REACHABILITY
----------------------------
Current `CIV4EspionageMissionInfo.xml` enables both ideology-changing mission families:

    ESPIONAGEMISSION_SWITCH_CIVIC
        iSwitchCivicCostFactor = 1000
        TechPrereq = NONE

    ESPIONAGEMISSION_SWITCH_RELIGION
        iSwitchReligionCostFactor = 1000
        TechPrereq = NONE

`canForceCivics` permits an ordinary eligible different civic when the target can use
it and either the spy is already using it or the civic's AdvCiv `canAlwaysForce` flag
allows it. The successful mission reaches the code above directly.

The revolution timer is authoritative gameplay state. `CvPlayer::canRevolution` and
`canDoAnyRevolution` both reject civic changes while `getRevolutionTimer() > 0`, and
the timer is decremented through the normal player-turn path.

CURRENT SAS NUMERIC REPRODUCTION
--------------------------------
The inherited current value is:

    MIN_REVOLUTION_TURNS = 5

Current SAS also has ordinary player-level sources of a different anarchy modifier:

    BUILDING_PYRAMID       iAnarchyModifier = -100
    BUILDING_VERSAILLES    iAnarchyModifier = -100

Both have no obsolete technology and 100% conquest retention in current data.

Thus two simple ordinary cases produce deterministic wrong cooldowns.

Case A — spy has Pyramids, target has no anarchy modifier:

    spy getMinTurnsBetweenRevolutions()
        = max(1, (100 - 100) * 5 / 100)
        = 1

    target's correct value
        = max(1, 100 * 5 / 100)
        = 5

Current code forces the target civic and gives the victim a revolution timer of 1
instead of 5. The victim can undo/change civics four turns earlier than its own rules
permit, weakening the espionage effect.

Case B — spy has no modifier, target has Pyramids:

    spy helper = 5
    target helper = 1

Current code gives the victim 5 instead of 1, locking the target out of voluntary
civic changes four turns longer than the target's own anarchy/cooldown modifier says.

No malformed setup, scenario-only state or disabled XML is required.

ANCESTRY
--------
The supplied stock BtS/Civ4CE implementation sets:

    GET_PLAYER(eTargetPlayer).setRevolutionTimer(
        std::max(1,
            ((100 + GET_PLAYER(eTargetPlayer).getAnarchyModifier()) *
            MIN_REVOLUTION_TURNS) / 100));

K-Mod 1.46 retains that target-explicit expression.

AdvCiv introduces/uses the player helper `getMinTurnsBetweenRevolutions()` and replaces
the duplicated arithmetic in this branch with:

    GET_PLAYER(eTargetPlayer).setRevolutionTimer(
        getMinTurnsBetweenRevolutions());

but omits the target receiver. Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the wrong receiver, and current
SAS inherits it.

This is therefore not a disagreement over espionage policy. The pre-refactor lineage
and the neighboring Force Religion branch both identify the target player as the
intended modifier subject.

DUPLICATE / ALBUM CHECK
-----------------------
The reconciled album contains multiple force-civic/religion espionage findings, but
they concern different contracts:
* localization argument/key defects in Queue 003;
* F454's third-party capital-coordinate information leak;
* dormant destroy/bribe unit ownership / popup-ID issues.

No existing root covers the post-Force-Civic revolution timer being computed from the
spying player's anarchy modifier. F462 is independent.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR
-------------------
Call the helper on the player whose timer is being set:

    CvPlayer& kTarget = GET_PLAYER(eTargetPlayer);
    kTarget.setCivics(GC.getInfo(eCivic).getCivicOptionType(), eCivic);
    kTarget.setRevolutionTimer(kTarget.getMinTurnsBetweenRevolutions());

or retain the existing spelling and qualify only the helper call:

    GET_PLAYER(eTargetPlayer).setRevolutionTimer(
            GET_PLAYER(eTargetPlayer).getMinTurnsBetweenRevolutions());

A regression test should use different spy/target anarchy modifiers and verify that
changing only the SPY's modifier does not change the victim's timer, while changing
the TARGET's modifier does.

---------

F463 / provisional KI#786 is the next unused root.

F463 / KI#786 — K-MOD'S POST-SABOTAGE AI PRODUCTION-RECONSIDERATION HOOKS
TEST THE SPY OWNER'S HUMAN STATUS INSTEAD OF THE SABOTAGED CITY OWNER
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED. Both affected espionage mission families are enabled in current SAS and
ordinary human-vs-AI espionage reaches the wrong branch decision.

ROOT
----
K-Mod added production-choice invalidation after building/production sabotage so an AI
city can reconsider its current build after the sabotage changes the city's state.

Current SAS inherits these two branches in `CvPlayer::doEspionageMission`:

    if (kMission.getDestroyBuildingCostFactor() > 0 && pCity != NULL)
    {
        ...
        pCity->setNumRealBuilding(... - 1);
        ...
        if (!isHuman() || pCity->isProductionAutomated())
            pCity->setChooseProductionDirty(true);
    }

and:

    if (kMission.getDestroyProductionCostFactor() > 0 && pCity != NULL)
    {
        ...
        pCity->setProduction(0);
        ...
        if (!isHuman())
            pCity->setChooseProductionDirty(true);
    }

`CvPlayer::doEspionageMission` is invoked on the SPY OWNER. The unqualified
`isHuman()` therefore asks whether the attacker is human.

The city being marked dirty belongs to the espionage target. Whether that TARGET city
is AI-controlled is the relevant condition for K-Mod's production replanning.

WHY THE BAD SUBJECT IS NOT REPAIRED ELSEWHERE
----------------------------------------------
`CvCity::setNumRealBuilding` updates the real-building count and processes the
building's city/player/team/game effects, but it does not set
`ChooseProductionDirty`.

`CvCity::setProduction(0)` likewise resets the current order's stored production
without removing the order or forcing a fresh choice.

At the target city's later `doProduction()`:

    if (!isHuman() || isProductionAutomated())
    {
        if (!isProduction() || isProductionProcess() ||
            isChooseProductionDirty())
        {
            AI().AI_chooseProduction();
        }
    }

An AI target with an existing valid production order therefore re-runs
`AI_chooseProduction()` after sabotage only when the dirty bit was set. If the bit is
missing, it simply continues the existing order (with the sabotaged production amount
or changed building environment).

For a building whose destruction makes the current order outright illegal,
`doCheckProduction` can independently remove that illegal order. That does not close
this root: K-Mod's hook deliberately asks the AI to reconsider even when the current
order remains legal, and Destroy Production normally leaves the current order legal.

AUTHORITATIVE K-MOD INTENT
--------------------------
The supplied K-Mod 1.46 changelog explicitly states:

    "The AI will now reconsider its current city production after a building is
     sabotaged."

The corresponding K-Mod source introduces:

    if (!isHuman() || pCity->isProductionAutomated())
        pCity->AI_setChooseProductionDirty(true);

inside the attacker's `CvPlayer::doEspionageMission`, making the receiver mix-up part
of the original K-Mod implementation rather than an AdvCiv/SAS semantic choice.

The Destroy Production branch contains the same attacker-side `!isHuman()` pattern.

CURRENT SAS REACHABILITY
------------------------
Current `CIV4EspionageMissionInfo.xml` enables both affected active missions:

    ESPIONAGEMISSION_DESTROY_BUILDING
        iDestroyBuildingCostFactor = 500
        bIsTwoPhases = 1
        bTargetsCity = 1

    ESPIONAGEMISSION_DESTROY_PRODUCTION
        iDestroyProductionCostFactor = 500
        bTargetsCity = 1

A normal human player can therefore perform either mission against an AI city.

Deterministic control-flow reproduction:

1. AI player B owns a city that currently has a valid production order.
2. Human player A performs Destroy Production against that city.
3. `this == A`, so `!isHuman()` is false.
4. The city's production becomes 0 but `ChooseProductionDirty` is not set.
5. On B's city turn, the order still exists and is valid, so `doProduction` does not
   call `AI_chooseProduction`; B simply continues that pre-sabotage order.

Perform the same mission against the same AI city from an AI-controlled attacker:

1. `this` is now AI, so `!isHuman()` is true.
2. The target city is marked dirty.
3. Its next `doProduction` calls `AI_chooseProduction()` and re-evaluates the build.

The victim's AI behavior therefore changes solely with the controller type of the
ATTACKER, even though the target city and sabotage result are otherwise identical.

Destroy Building has the same subject asymmetry; a human spy suppresses the explicit
K-Mod production-reconsideration hook for an AI target unless the target city happens
to be production-automated.

ANCESTRY
--------
Stock BtS/Civ4CE does not contain these K-Mod production-reconsideration additions.

K-Mod 1.46 adds the two dirtying hooks with the attacker-side `isHuman()` spelling.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains them (renaming `AI_setChooseProductionDirty` to the current
setter where appropriate), and current SAS retains the same receiver logic.

This is therefore best classified as an inherited K-Mod wrong-subject integration bug.

DUPLICATE / ALBUM CHECK
-----------------------
No reconciled album root covers attacker human status controlling the target AI city's
post-espionage production replanning. Existing espionage roots cover visibility leaks,
localization/help, Force Civic cooldown subject (F462), and dormant target-unit
ownership/ID issues. F463 is independent.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR
-------------------
Base the condition on the sabotaged city's owner, not on the spy owner. For example:

    CvPlayer const& kTargetOwner = GET_PLAYER(pCity->getOwner());

    if (!kTargetOwner.isHuman() || pCity->isProductionAutomated())
        pCity->setChooseProductionDirty(true);

Use the same target-owner test in both Destroy Building and Destroy Production
branches. For Destroy Production, including `pCity->isProductionAutomated()` gives the
same sensible human-city automation handling as the building branch.

A regression test should sabotage the same AI city from a human attacker and an AI
attacker and verify that the target city receives identical production-dirty state.

NUMBERING
---------

F464 / provisional KI#787 is the next unused root.

RECONCILIATION / CORRECTION — WIP181 TEAMSHARE XML SENTENCE WAS FACTUALLY WRONG
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP181 included the statement that current SAS had no `<bTeamShare>1</bTeamShare>`
BuildingInfo entries. That sentence is incorrect and must not be carried forward.

Current `CIV4BuildingInfos.xml` does contain TeamShare buildings, including the Three
Gorges Dam and Great Wall family inspected during the Permanent-Alliance area-effect
sweep.

The substantive PA closure survives the correction: `CvTeam::shareItems` explicitly
walks existing cities and replays `CvPlayer::processBuilding` for TeamShare buildings
in both directions before absorbed players are reassigned by `setTeam`. Therefore the
earlier conclusion did not rely on the false "no current TeamShare buildings" premise.

A count-weighting robustness wrinkle remains: TeamShare area counters are incremented
per player, so changing team membership can leave noncanonical signed counts when a
shared building is later removed. Clean Power's zero/nonzero transition logic still
flips correctly. Border-obstacle reactivation would be more fragile after a negative
count, but current Great Wall obsoletes at Gunpowder, well before ordinary Permanent
Alliance timing. Preserve as a PA/cache robustness note, not a numbered current root.

DUPLICATE CONTROL — RELIGION SPREAD UNIT AREA-TRAINING BUG IS ALREADY F451 / KI#774
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A fresh pass rediscovered that `countReligionSpreadUnits(pArea, ..., true)` limits
existing missionaries to `pArea` but counts missionaries currently being trained in
all cities on the map, unlike its corporation sibling which applies the area filter to
both existing and training units.

Album reconciliation caught this before renumbering: this is already the confirmed
F451 / KI#774 root, including the ordinary `AI_missionaryValue` area-scoped consumer.
Do not duplicate it as F464.

CONTROL — PERMANENT-ALLIANCE STALE ESPIONAGE WEIGHTS ARE EXCLUDED FROM ALLOCATION
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`m_aiEspionageSpendingWeightAgainstTeam` is player state indexed by TeamTypes and is
not remapped when Permanent Alliance `setTeam` changes a player's team. That creates
stale array entries toward the absorbed/surviving team IDs.

The live allocator closes the concern:

    CvPlayer::getEspionageSpending
      -> TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE,OTHER_KNOWN_TO>(getTeam())

Both the denominator and remainder loops iterate only alive OTHER teams. After
absorption the old team loses its alive members and is excluded; the surviving team is
now the player's own team and is likewise excluded. The stale slots therefore do not
consume current espionage commerce. No F464 from this state family.

CONTROL — SABOTAGE PRODUCTION COST SUBJECT ASYMMETRY REMAINS POLICY-AMBIGUOUS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Destroy Building / Destroy Project mission pricing calls the SPY OWNER's
`getProductionNeeded(Building/Project)`, whose AdvCiv implementation includes
player-specific handicap / AI production-cost adjustments. Thus two attackers can in
principle receive different EP prices for sabotaging the same target object.

BtS and K-Mod already use the acting player's production-cost helper. No local help,
manual or AI valuation contract found in this tranche establishes that the victim's
effective cost is intended instead. Difficulty-normalized espionage pricing is
plausible inherited policy. Preserve the asymmetry as an observation; do not promote it
without an authoritative semantic contradiction.

------------------------------------------------------------------
The remaining enabled `doEspionageMission` branches were compared side by side after
the F462/F463 wrong-subject pair.

No further independent wrong-player root was established:
* poison / unhappiness / revolt mutate the target city;

* tech theft grants the spying team;
* Force Religion explicitly uses the target player's anarchy modifier;
* counterespionage is stored on the spying team against the target team;
* the attacker-humanity check in the revolt branch is diagnostic logging only.

The apparent `GET_TEAM(eTarget)` syntax in project sabotage is also an already-recorded
false positive: current `CvPlayer.cpp` includes `CoreAI.h`, whose overloaded
`GET_TEAM(PlayerTypes)` resolves the player to its actual team.


F464 / KI#787 — ADVC SPACESHIP-LAUNCH MESSAGE COORDINATES LEAK FROM ONE OBSERVER
TO ALL LATER OBSERVERS IN THE PLAYER ITERATION
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED. Ordinary current Space Race launch reaches the defect. This is an AdvCiv
`advc.106` refactor regression. Stock BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod reset the capital coordinates
for each observer; Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS carry them across observers.

ROOT
----
Current SAS `CvPlayer::launch` does:

    CvCity const* pCapital = getCapital();
    CvWString szMsg(...);
    int iPlotX = -1;
    int iPlotY = -1;

    for (PlayerIter<MAJOR_CIV> it; it.hasNext(); ++it)
    {
        CvPlayer const& kObs = *it;
        if (pCapital != NULL && pCapital->isRevealed(kObs.getTeam()))
        {
            iPlotX = pCapital->getX();
            iPlotY = pCapital->getY();
        }

        ...
        gDLL->UI().addMessage(kObs.getID(), ..., iPlotX, iPlotY, true, true);
    }

The coordinate variables are initialized only once. If observer A has revealed the
launching capital, the pair becomes the true capital `(x,y)`. For a later observer B
whose team has NOT revealed the capital, the `if` body is skipped but `iPlotX/iPlotY`
retain A's coordinates. B therefore receives a message carrying the hidden capital's
location.

The reveal predicate itself is correct; the defect is state leaking across iterations.

DETERMINISTIC ORDINARY REPRO
----------------------------
AdvCiv's `PlayerIter<MAJOR_CIV>` uses the `CvAgents::MAJOR_ALIVE` sequence. `CvAgents`
builds and maintains these sequences in ascending player ID order.

Use a normal game in which:

1. Player 0 is a major civilization pursuing Space Race.
2. Player 1 is another living major civilization.
3. Player 1 has never revealed Player 0's capital.
4. Player 0 completes the spaceship requirements and launches.

The current Space Race victory remains enabled in shipped
`CIV4VictoryInfo.xml` (`VICTORY_SPACE_RACE`, 10-turn base delay), with the usual
victory projects in `CIV4ProjectInfo.xml`.

During `Player 0::launch`:

* observer Player 0 is visited before Player 1;
* Player 0's own team has its own capital revealed, so `iPlotX/iPlotY` become the true
  capital coordinates;
* observer Player 1 then fails the `pCapital->isRevealed(Player1Team)` test;
* the code does NOT restore `-1,-1`;
* Player 1 receives `TXT_KEY_VICTORY_TEAM_HAS_LAUNCHED` with Player 0's true capital
  coordinates.

More generally, once any earlier observer has revealed the capital, every later
unrevealed observer inherits the location until another assignment (which is the same
location anyway).

PLAYER-FACING CONSEQUENCE
-------------------------
`CvDLLInterfaceIFaceBase::addMessage` forwards `iFlashX/iFlashY` into the EXE message
payload. Its current AdvCiv comment explicitly says the flash information supplies
"the text color and coordinates stored in the Turn Log -- not just for the (disabled)
icon."

The launch call also requests on/off-screen arrows. Thus `(x,y)` is meaningful
player-facing map/message information, not an unused local.

This is the same visibility contract used in the already-confirmed F454 family:
unrevealed message locations should be `-1,-1`, while revealed observers can receive
the actual map coordinate.

ANCESTRY
--------
Stock BtS/Civ4CE `CvPlayer::launch` declares:

    int plotX = -1;
    int plotY = -1;

INSIDE the `for (i = 0; i < MAX_PLAYERS; ++i)` observer body. Each recipient therefore
starts from hidden coordinates and receives the capital location only if that
recipient's team has revealed it.

K-Mod 1.46 retains the same per-observer initialization.

AdvCiv 1.14 changes this under `advc.106`:

    // Cut from the loop below. Use this for the replay message as well.
    int iPlotX = -1;
    int iPlotY = -1;

The variables are hoisted before `PlayerIter<MAJOR_CIV>`, but no reset is inserted at
the top of each observer iteration. The refactor therefore converts correctly
observer-local state into persistent loop state.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS contain the same hoisted implementation.

This ancestry makes intent especially strong: pre-AdvCiv code explicitly preserved
per-recipient reveal privacy; the bug appears exactly when the variables are moved for
replay-message reuse.

DUPLICATE / ALBUM CHECK
-----------------------
The reconciled album has:
* F454: AdvCiv third-party Force Civic/Religion espionage announcement attaches raw
  target-capital coordinates rather than observer-aware coordinates;
* prior Space-capital/UWAI controls concerning whether a launched Space victory should
  make the CAPITAL an AI military target.

No existing root covers `CvPlayer::launch` carrying one recipient's revealed
coordinates into a later unrevealed recipient's launch message. F464 is independent.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR
-------------------
Restore per-observer coordinates for the UI message while keeping separate coordinates
for the replay message.

For example:

    CvCity const* pCapital = getCapital();

    int iReplayX = -1;
    int iReplayY = -1;
    if (pCapital != NULL)
    {
        iReplayX = pCapital->getX();
        iReplayY = pCapital->getY();
    }

    for (PlayerIter<MAJOR_CIV> it; it.hasNext(); ++it)
    {
        CvPlayer const& kObs = *it;
        int iPlotX = -1;
        int iPlotY = -1;
        if (pCapital != NULL && pCapital->isRevealed(kObs.getTeam()))
        {
            iPlotX = pCapital->getX();
            iPlotY = pCapital->getY();
        }
        ...
        gDLL->UI().addMessage(..., iPlotX, iPlotY, true, true);
    }

    GC.getGame().addReplayMessage(..., iReplayX, iReplayY);

This restores the BtS/K-Mod recipient contract and preserves AdvCiv's intended replay
location.

A minimal regression test should launch as Player 0 while Player 1 has not revealed
Player 0's capital and verify that Player 1's launch message stores `-1,-1`; after
revealing that capital, the same observer should receive the real coordinates.

LATENT ADVC REFACTOR BUG — INDEPENDENCE MEMORY USES THE PARENT'S
`FreedomAppreciation` INSTEAD OF THE NEW COLONY'S
----------------------------------------------------------------
Current `CvPlayer::splitEmpire` grants the new colony's AI:

    GET_PLAYER(eNewPlayer).AI_changeMemoryCount(
        getID(), MEMORY_INDEPENDENCE,
        2 * GC.getInfo(getPersonalityType()).getFreedomAppreciation());

`this` is the parent. The memory count belongs to `eNewPlayer`, and the old pre-advc.130r
attitude implementation makes the intended personality subject clear:

    if (getParent() == ePlayer)
        iAttitude += GC.getInfo(getPersonalityType()).getFreedomAppreciation();

That old function executes on the CHILD AI. When advc.130r transformed the permanent
colony-attitude bonus into decaying `MEMORY_INDEPENDENCE`, using the parent's
`getPersonalityType()` therefore changed the semantic subject. The child-side value
would preserve the pre-refactor behavior.

This is a real AdvCiv abstraction/refactor error, but CURRENT SAS DATA MASKS IT:
the generated Sevopedia runtime cache contains 55 playable leader entries and every
one reports:

    getFreedomAppreciation = 10

`LEADER_DEFAULTS` likewise supplies 10; the only explicit 0 in XML is the Barbarian
leader. Therefore choosing the parent or child personality produces the same current
memory amount for every ordinary playable colony relationship, including Random
Personalities.

The AdvCiv manual also describes the converted feature as the old +10 gratitude being
represented as decaying memory, consistent with current uniform data.

Preserve this as a latent/data-dependent AdvCiv bug. Do NOT spend F465 unless shipped
leader data later differentiates `FreedomAppreciation` (or another ordinary producer
creates such differentiation).

A semantically correct cleanup would use:

    2 * GC.getInfo(GET_PLAYER(eNewPlayer).getPersonalityType()).
        getFreedomAppreciation()

if preserving the old child-personality behavior is desired.

The compiled diplomacy use inspected in this pass belongs to religion-demand

F465 / KI#788 — PERMANENT ALLIANCE TEAM-MEMBER REASSIGNMENT DOES NOT REFRESH
VASSAL-CITY MAINTENANCE, LEAVING BOTH ALLIES' REAL GOLD COSTS STALE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED. Ordinary current Permanent Alliance + Vassal States gameplay reaches the
defect. The root is inherited from stock BtS/Firaxis and remains in Civ4CE, K-Mod,
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

ROOT CONTRACT
-------------
City number-of-cities maintenance is cached in `CvCity::m_iMaintenance`; each city
refresh contributes its delta to the owner's cached `CvPlayer::m_iTotalMaintenance`.

Current `CvCity::calculateNumCitiesMaintenanceTimes100` includes a master team's
vassal-city burden and divides that burden among the CURRENT number of master-team
members:

    int iNumVassalCities = 0;
    for (PlayerIter<ALIVE,VASSAL_OF> it(kOwner.getTeam()); it.hasNext(); ++it)
        iNumVassalCities += it->getNumCities();

    iNumVassalCities /=
        std::max(1, MemberIter::count(kOwner.getTeam()));

    int iMaintenanceCities =
        kOwner.getNumCities() + iExtraCities +
        iNumVassalCities / 2;

Thus a change in the number of players on a master team changes every member's
correct number-of-cities maintenance even if:
* no city changes owner;
* the vassal relationship itself does not change;
* no city population or local maintenance modifier changes.

The maintenance is NOT dynamically recomputed when queried. `CvPlayer::doGold`
ultimately uses:

    calculatePreInflatedCosts()
        -> ... + getTotalMaintenance() + ...

and `getTotalMaintenance()` reads the stored player total. `CvCity::doTurn` does not
perform an unconditional maintenance refresh.

THE NORMAL VASSAL TRANSITION ALREADY PROVES THE INVALIDATION REQUIREMENT
------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvTeam::setVassal` explicitly refreshes every member of the MASTER team at the end of
a vassal-state change:

    for (MemberIter it(eMaster); it.hasNext(); ++it)
        it->updateMaintenance();

The stock BtS implementation has the same refresh (expressed as a player loop over the
master team). K-Mod retains it.

That is authoritative evidence that master-side cached maintenance must be rebuilt
when the set/share of vassal cities relevant to the formula changes.

PERMANENT ALLIANCE CHANGES THE SAME FORMULA INPUT WITHOUT INVALIDATING THE CACHE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A Permanent Alliance is implemented by `CvDeal` calling `CvTeam::addTeam`; the lower
team ID survives.

`CvTeam::addTeam` eventually reassigns every absorbed player:

    if (GET_PLAYER((PlayerTypes)i).getTeam() == eTeam)
        GET_PLAYER((PlayerTypes)i).setTeam(getID());

`CvPlayer::setTeam` changes:
* old/new team member counts;
* alive / ever-alive counts;
* team city/population/land totals;
* leader and attitude state.

It does NOT call `updateMaintenance`.

`CvTeam::addTeam` likewise contains no maintenance refresh after the reassignment.

The cleanest case needs no vassal migration at all:

    Team A / Player A = lower-ID surviving singleton team
    Team B / Player B = absorbed singleton team
    Team C            = already a vassal of Team A

When B joins A:
* C remains a vassal of the SAME surviving Team A;
* therefore no `setVassal` transition for C is needed to repair the cache;
* Team A's member count changes from 1 to 2 through B's `setTeam`;
* that directly changes the divisor in
  `calculateNumCitiesMaintenanceTimes100`;
* A's old city caches are not refreshed;
* B's old city caches are not refreshed.

A should now pay only its per-member share of A's vassal burden, while B should begin
paying its own share. Instead both retain their pre-alliance values.

CURRENT SHIPPED REACHABILITY
----------------------------
Both required systems are normal visible game options:

    GAMEOPTION_PERMANENT_ALLIANCES
        bVisible = 1

    GAMEOPTION_NO_VASSAL_STATES
        bDefault = 0
        bVisible = 1

Therefore a player can enable Permanent Alliances while leaving Vassal States active.

Current SAS enables Permanent Alliance trading through:

    TECH_GAME_THEORY
        bPermanentAllianceTrading = 1

`CvPlayer::canPossiblyTradeItem(TRADE_PERMANENT_ALLIANCE)` requires each alliance
partner team itself not to be a vassal and to have one member. It does NOT prohibit
either partner from being the MASTER of one or more vassal teams.

So a singleton master with vassals can normally form a Permanent Alliance with another
singleton non-vassal team.

DETERMINISTIC CURRENT-SAS NUMERIC REPRO
---------------------------------------
Use:
* Standard world;
* Noble handicap;
* eight civilization players ever alive on Standard, matching the current recommended
  player count of 8, so AdvCiv's crowdedness factor is exactly 1;
* no number-of-cities maintenance modifier;
* no WLTKD / no-maintenance suppression in the example cities;
* Team A and Team B each have five population-10 cities;
* Team C, already a vassal of Team A, has ten cities;
* Team A has the lower team ID and therefore survives the PA.

Current XML gives:

    Standard NumCitiesMaintenancePercent = 30
    Noble    NumCitiesMaintenancePercent = 75

For a population-10 city the base multiplicative factor is therefore:

    (10 + 17) / 18 * 30/100 * 75/100
        = 27/18 * 3/10 * 3/4
        = 27/80
        = 0.3375

The current AdvCiv/SAS city-count cap is far above all counts in this construction
(`MAX_CITY_COUNT_FOR_MAINTENANCE = 31` with the Standard divisor), so the cap does not
mask the difference.

BEFORE THE PA:

Team A has one member, so its ten vassal cities are:

    10 / 1 = 10 vassal cities per member

K-Mod/AdvCiv then half-counts them:

    10 / 2 = 5 effective maintenance cities

Player A's city-count input is therefore:

    own 5 + vassal share 5 = 10

Each population-10 A city has this component proportional to:

    10 * 27/80 = 3.375 gold

Player B has no vassal burden:

    own 5 + 0 = 5

so each B city has:

    5 * 27/80 = 1.6875 gold

AFTER B JOINS A:

Team A now has TWO members. The correct shared vassal input is:

    10 / 2 members = 5
    5 / 2 (reduced-vassal rule) = 2

So EACH member should use:

    own 5 + vassal share 2 = 7

and each population-10 city should have:

    7 * 27/80 = 2.3625 gold

Thus, before local rounding:
* each A city should FALL by 1.0125 gold of number-of-cities maintenance;
* across five A cities that is about 5.06 pre-inflation gold/turn;
* each B city should RISE by 0.675 gold;
* across five B cities that is about 3.38 pre-inflation gold/turn.

Current code performs neither refresh at alliance formation. A stays cached near its
old higher value; B stays cached near its old lower value.

IMMEDIATE REAL-GOLD CONSEQUENCE
-------------------------------
The error does not have to survive for many turns to matter.

A human Player A can accept/form the Permanent Alliance during its ordinary active-turn
input phase. `CvDeal::addTrades` calls `CvTeam::addTeam` immediately.

When A then ends the turn, `CvPlayer::doTurn` executes:

    AI_assignWorkingPlots();
    ...
    doGold();
    doResearch();
    ...
    for each city:
        city->doTurn();

`doGold()` therefore consumes `getTotalMaintenance()` BEFORE A's city turns. There is
no unconditional player/city maintenance rebuild between the alliance merge and this
economic charge.

So A can be charged the stale pre-PA maintenance on the very first economy processing
after the alliance. B later reaches the same problem in its own `doGold`.

The stale values can persist beyond that until a specific maintenance-invalidating
event occurs (population change, government-center/maintenance modifier transition,
corporation/religion/occupation/WLTKD-related refresh, whole-player
`updateMaintenance`, etc.). Maintenance is not refreshed merely because another turn
passes.

ANCESTRY
--------
This root is Firaxis/BtS-inherited.

Stock BtS/Civ4CE `CvCity::calculateNumCitiesMaintenanceTimes100` already:
* sums cities belonging to teams vassalized to the owner team;
* divides them by `GET_TEAM(getTeam()).getNumMembers()`.

Stock BtS also explicitly calls `updateMaintenance()` for the master team's players at
the end of `CvTeam::setVassal`.

But stock `CvTeam::addTeam` reassigns absorbed players with `CvPlayer::setTeam` and
contains no subsequent maintenance refresh, and stock `CvPlayer::setTeam` itself has
none.

K-Mod retains the same invalidation omission. Its 04/sep/10 change reduces the vassal
burden from full count to half count, but the team-member divisor and PA cache problem
already existed in BtS.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the member-count-dependent formula and the PA omission.
Current SAS retains both.

DUPLICATE / ALBUM CHECK
-----------------------
The reconciled album and current Known Issues were searched for Permanent Alliance +
maintenance, vassal maintenance + alliance, team-member maintenance and related terms.
No same-root numbered finding exists.

Nearby confirmed PA roots are independent:
* F455 / KI#778 — city military-happiness unit cache not recounted after PA team
  reassignment;
* F458 / KI#781 — player outside-unit/supply cache not recounted after PA team
  reassignment;
* earlier PA roots cover relationship history, espionage state, visibility, UWAI,
  deals and other team-keyed state.

F465 specifically concerns cached CITY MAINTENANCE / player total maintenance changing
because the vassal-city burden is divided by current master-team member count.

The existing maintenance roots are also distinct:
* F421 / KI#744 — corporation maintenance cache embeds stale inverse inflation over
  time;
* F399/F400 and other earlier roots concern maintenance UI/valuation/decomposition,
  not PA team-member invalidation.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR
-------------------
After Permanent Alliance player reassignment is complete, rebuild maintenance for the
members of the surviving merged team:

    for (MemberIter it(getID()); it.hasNext(); ++it)
        it->updateMaintenance();

Placement should be after all absorbed players have received the surviving team ID so
`MemberIter::count(getID())`, owner team, and vassal enumeration all reflect the final
merged identity.

This also naturally repairs both directions:
* original survivor members lose the excess burden caused by the old smaller
  denominator;
* absorbed members acquire the vassal burden associated with their new master team.

A regression test should:
1. create singleton master A with vassal C;
2. create singleton B with no vassals;
3. record A/B `getTotalMaintenanceTimes100`;
4. form an A+B Permanent Alliance;
5. compare cached totals immediately against a forced `updateMaintenance()` result;
6. assert that the PA path itself leaves no difference.

Keep current-data reachability, ordinary caller consequence, full cache/callee chain,
ancestry and duplicate proof mandatory before promotion.

END C031-WIP186

POST-F465 CONTROL — PERMANENT ALLIANCE TRADE-ROUTE YIELDS ARE REFRESHED THROUGH
THE `updatePlotGroups` CALLEE CHAIN
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A neighboring cache initially looked like another PA sibling.

`CvCity::totalTradeModifier` treats a route as foreign when the two cities' teams
differ and then adds:
* the city foreign-trade-route modifier;
* AdvCiv's peace-duration foreign-trade modifier.

A PA immediately changes old A<->B routes from foreign-team to same-team, while the
route cities and `m_aiTradeYield` are cached. `CvPlayer::setTeam` and `CvTeam::addTeam`
do not visibly call `updateTradeRoutes` at the reassignment site.

The full callee chain closes the candidate:

    CvTeam::addTeam
        -> GC.getGame().updatePlotGroups()
            -> each alive CvPlayer::updatePlotGroups()
                -> verifyCityProduction()
                -> updateTradeRoutes()

This runs after the absorbed players have their new team ID. Thus route selection and
trade yield are rebuilt under the merged same-team identity before the next economic
processing. No F466 from trade-route caching.

This control further isolates F465: `updatePlotGroups` does not rebuild maintenance.


F466 / KI#789 — VASSAL CITY COUNT CHANGES DO NOT INVALIDATE THE MASTER PLAYERS'
CACHED NUMBER-OF-CITIES MAINTENANCE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED. Ordinary current vassal founding, conquest and city loss can reach the
defect. This is inherited from stock BtS/Firaxis. K-Mod changes the size of the vassal
burden but retains the missing invalidation; Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS inherit
it.

ROOT CONTRACT
-------------
The same maintenance formula underlying F465 also depends on the TOTAL NUMBER OF
CITIES owned by the player's living vassals:

    int iNumVassalCities = 0;
    for (PlayerIter<ALIVE,VASSAL_OF> it(kOwner.getTeam()); it.hasNext(); ++it)
        iNumVassalCities += it->getNumCities();

    iNumVassalCities /=
        std::max(1, MemberIter::count(kOwner.getTeam()));

    int iMaintenanceCities =
        kOwner.getNumCities() + iExtraCities +
        iNumVassalCities / 2;

Current city maintenance is cached. Each `CvCity::updateMaintenance()` changes the
owner's stored `m_iTotalMaintenance`; `CvPlayer::calculatePreInflatedCosts()` later
reads `getTotalMaintenance()` rather than recomputing every city.

Therefore any vassal city-count change that changes `iNumVassalCities / members / 2`
must invalidate the MASTER players' city-maintenance caches.

NORMAL CITY CREATION / DESTRUCTION DOES NOT DO THAT
----------------------------------------------------
Current `CvCity::init` performs:

    getArea().changeCitiesPerPlayer(getOwner(), 1);
    GET_TEAM(getTeam()).changeNumCities(1);
    GC.getGame().changeNumCities(1);
    ...
    kOwner.updateMaintenance();

The whole-player refresh is only for the city OWNER.

Current `CvCity::kill` similarly performs:

    GET_TEAM(eOwner).changeNumCities(-1);
    GC.getGame().changeNumCities(-1);
    ...
    kOwner.updateMaintenance();

again refreshing only the player who lost the city.

`CvTeam::changeNumCities` itself is only:

    m_iNumCities += iChange;
    FAssert(getNumCities() >= 0);

It has no master-team maintenance invalidation.

A whole-tree inventory of `updateMaintenance()` callers finds no generic hook that
refreshes a vassal's MASTER when the vassal city count changes. `CvPlayer::acquireCity`
also supplies no extra master refresh: the old city is killed and the replacement is
initialized through the same owner-local paths.

THE EXISTING `setVassal` REFRESH CONFIRMS THE DEPENDENCY
--------------------------------------------------------
When a team first becomes or ceases to be a vassal, `CvTeam::setVassal` explicitly
refreshes the master members:

    for (MemberIter it(eMaster); it.hasNext(); ++it)
        it->updateMaintenance();

That correctly initializes/removes the vassal-city burden at the relationship
transition.

The missing sibling is what happens AFTERWARD: as the already-established vassal
founds, captures, loses or razes cities, the numerator used by the master maintenance
formula changes but the master caches are left untouched.

CURRENT SHIPPED REACHABILITY
----------------------------
Vassal States are active by default unless the visible
`GAMEOPTION_NO_VASSAL_STATES` option is selected.

No Permanent Alliance, scenario-only setup, Python mutation or debug action is needed.
Ordinary examples include:
* a voluntary or capitulated vassal founding a new city;
* a vassal conquering a city;
* a vassal losing a city to a third party;
* a vassal razing or otherwise losing a city.

Current K-Mod/AdvCiv's reduced-vassal rule half-counts the per-member vassal city
total, so not every +/-1 city changes the final integer input. Crossing the relevant
integer boundary does.

DETERMINISTIC CURRENT-SAS NUMERIC REPRO
---------------------------------------
Use:
* Standard world;
* Noble handicap;
* eight civ players ever alive on Standard so AdvCiv's crowdedness factor is exactly
  1;
* singleton master Team A / Player A;
* singleton vassal Team C / Player C;
* A owns ten population-10 cities;
* C owns nine cities and then founds or captures its tenth;
* no number-of-cities maintenance modifier and no WLTKD/no-maintenance suppression in
  A's example cities.

Current XML:

    Standard NumCitiesMaintenancePercent = 30
    Noble    NumCitiesMaintenancePercent = 75

For each population-10 A city:

    rNumCitiesFactor
        = (10 + 17) / 18 * 30/100 * 75/100
        = 27/80
        = 0.3375

The current city-count cap is not reached in this construction.

BEFORE C GAINS ITS 10TH CITY:

    vassal cities / master members = 9 / 1 = 9
    reduced-vassal contribution    = 9 / 2 = 4
    A maintenance-city input       = own 10 + 4 = 14

AFTER C GAINS ITS 10TH CITY, the CORRECT input is:

    10 / 1 = 10
    10 / 2 = 5
    own 10 + 5 = 15

So each A population-10 city should gain:

    1 * 27/80 = 0.3375 gold

of number-of-cities maintenance before inflation.

Across A's ten cities the master player's correct pre-inflation maintenance rises by
about:

    10 * 0.3375 = 3.375 gold/turn

before the engine's hundredth/whole-gold rounding.

But the new vassal city calls only C's `updateMaintenance()`. A's ten existing city
caches remain at the old 14-city input and `m_iTotalMaintenance` stays stale.

The reverse 10 -> 9 vassal-city loss produces an analogous overcharge for A.

REAL ECONOMIC CONSEQUENCE / PERSISTENCE
---------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::doTurn()` calls:

    doGold();
    doResearch();
    ...
    each owned city -> doTurn();

There is no unconditional `updateMaintenance()` at player-turn or city-turn start.

For a deterministic sequential-turn case, let lower-ID master A finish its turn and
then let later-turn vassal C found the tenth city. Nothing refreshes A's maintenance.
On A's next turn, when A eventually ends the turn, `doGold()` can consume the stale
master total before any of A's city turns.

The stale value can survive indefinitely in a sufficiently stable master empire; it
is repaired only when some unrelated maintenance invalidator happens to touch the
master's cities (population change, maintenance modifier, capital/government-center
change, religion/corporation/occupation/WLTKD state, explicit whole-player refresh,
etc.).

Thus this is not merely a display delay. It directly changes stored expenses and
gold.

ANCESTRY
--------
Stock BtS/Civ4CE already has the essential root.

Its number-of-cities formula:
* sums cities belonging to vassal teams;
* divides them by master-team member count;
* then counts the FULL resulting vassal share in number-of-cities maintenance.

Stock `CvTeam::setVassal` explicitly refreshes the master players when the
relationship changes.

But stock city creation/destruction refreshes only the city owner, stock
`CvTeam::changeNumCities` has no maintenance invalidation, and the master is not
refreshed when an established vassal's city total changes.

K-Mod 04/sep/10 reduces the vassal burden by half:

    own cities + iNumVassalCities / 2

which means a single city change matters only when it crosses the integer half-count
boundary. It does not add the missing master invalidation.

Base AdvCiv and current SAS retain the same structure.

DUPLICATE / ALBUM CHECK
-----------------------
The reconciled album and current Known Issues were searched for vassal city-count
maintenance, vassal expansion/loss maintenance, and related wording. No same-root
numbered finding exists.

F465 / KI#788 is a sibling but independent:
* F465 changes the DENOMINATOR (`master team member count`) through Permanent Alliance;
* F466 changes the NUMERATOR (`total vassal city count`) through ordinary vassal city
  lifecycle.

Fixing only PA `addTeam` does not repair normal vassal expansion/loss. Fixing only the
vassal-city lifecycle does not necessarily repair a master-team member-count change.

Existing maintenance findings such as F421 concern other cache dependencies
(corporation inverse inflation) and are not duplicates.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR
-------------------
When the number of cities on a team changes and that team is currently a vassal,
refresh the current master team's players.

A centralized direction is `CvTeam::changeNumCities`, after changing the stored count:

    if (iChange != 0 && isAVassal())
    {
        for (MemberIter it(getMasterTeam()); it.hasNext(); ++it)
            it->updateMaintenance();
    }

This naturally covers city founding, capture and loss regardless of which high-level
city lifecycle path produced the count change.

Care is still needed around initialization / bulk transitions to avoid unnecessary
work or calling into partially initialized state. A guarded helper or explicit
post-city-change hook can provide the same invariant if initialization timing makes
the centralized form undesirable.

A regression test should:
1. establish A as master of C;
2. record A's cached `getTotalMaintenanceTimes100`;
3. make C cross a half-count boundary by founding/capturing a city;
4. compare A's cached total immediately against the result after a forced
   `A.updateMaintenance()`;
5. assert there is no difference on the repaired path;
6. repeat for vassal city loss.

NUMBERING
---------

F467 / provisional KI#790 is the next unused root.

C031-WIP188 — QUEUE 004 CVPLAYER.CPP — F467 / KI#790 CONFIRMED
