POST-F471 PLAYER-DEATH / LIFECYCLE CONTROLS
-------------------------------------------
The immediate player-death seam was continued before moving back to the historical
low-coverage ranking.

1. NORMAL-PEACE SIDE EFFECTS BESIDES WAR-WEARINESS ANGER DID NOT PRODUCE A NEW
   INDEPENDENT ROOT.

`CvTeam::makePeace` performs several network/unit/trade refreshes that are not invoked
through exactly the same path when a team disappears. In the final-team-death case,
however:
* AdvCiv deliberately kills the defeated player's units before clearing team war state
  so active blockades/plunder are lifted while the former at-war relation still exists;
* final-city conquest / city cleanup supplies the relevant ownership/plot updates;
* the dead team has no continuing city/trade network that makes a missing post-peace
  route/plot refresh independently consequential.

War-weariness anger remains distinctive because it is cached state owned by a LIVING
former enemy and AdvCiv's own `advc.001` comment explicitly identifies the missing
`makePeace` side effect. No F472 from the other peace siblings.

2. DEATH-SIDE GLOBAL ATTITUDE UPDATE ASYMMETRY CLOSES UNDER THE GAME UPDATE CADENCE.

`setAlive(true)` explicitly calls global `CvPlayerAI::AI_updateAttitudes()` because
rank-difference attitude between players other than the revived player can change.
`setAlive(false)` has no matching direct call.

Player elimination nevertheless ends with `CvGame::setScoreDirty(true)`.
`CvGame::update()` calls `updateScore()` on normal update slices; when score is dirty,
`updateScore()` rebuilds player ranks/scores and then calls the global
`CvPlayerAI::AI_updateAttitudes()`.

Thus survivor-vs-survivor rank-attitude caches are rebuilt through the existing score
update after elimination. No durable independent F472 was established.

3. `CvTeam::updateLeaderID()` DOES NOT CONSUME THE TEMPORARILY STALE ALIVE-MEMBER
   AGENTITERATOR CACHE.

`CvPlayer::setAlive(false)` changes `m_bAlive`, then calls
`GET_TEAM(getTeam()).updateLeaderID()` before `CvAgents::playerDefeated()` removes the
player from `MEMBER_ALIVE`. This ordering initially looked vulnerable.

`CvTeam::updateLeaderID()` performs a raw `MAX_PLAYERS` scan, filters each player by
the current team, and explicitly weights only `kPlayer.isAlive()`. It therefore sees
the just-updated false alive flag directly and does not rely on the stale
AgentIterator membership vector. Close.

4. FINAL-TEAM VASSAL CLEANUP DOES USE THE PRE-`playerDefeated()` MEMBER CACHE, BUT NO
   BAD INDEPENDENT CONSEQUENCE WAS ESTABLISHED.

`CvTeam::changeAliveCount` can free the dead team's vassals before
`CvAgents::playerDefeated()` removes the just-dead player from alive-member caches.
`CvTeam::setVassal` consequently still sees that member in its MemberIter operations.

That ordering is at least partly useful: relationship sight/unit/city cleanup can still
touch the dying participant before later `killCities` / `killAllDeals` cleanup. No
separate authoritative corruption was proven from this temporary window.


DUPLICATE CONTROL — GOLDEN-AGE READINESS UNITCLASS VS CONSUMPTION UNITTYPE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
The K-Mod mismatch was reconciled against the earlier album before re-investigation.

`unitsGoldenAgeReady()` intentionally counts distinct `UnitClassTypes`, while
`killGoldenAgeUnits()` marks already-consumed kinds by `UnitTypes`.

This is already preserved in WIP158/WIP174/WIP179 as a latent data-extension defect.
Current SAS has exactly one Golden-Age-capable unit type for each relevant Great Person
class and no civilization mapping that creates two Golden-Age-capable UnitTypes in the
same UnitClass. Current shipped state therefore cannot make readiness and consumption
disagree.

Do not duplicate this as F472.


F472 / KI#795 — ADVANCED START ROUTE PURCHASE IGNORES ROUTE BONUS/RESOURCE
PREREQUISITES, ALLOWING RAILROAD WITHOUT COAL OR OIL
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED. Ordinary current shipped Advanced Start gameplay reaches the defect.

The root is inherited from stock BtS/Firaxis through K-Mod and Base AdvCiv. AdvCiv
changed Advanced Start pricing and fixed a separate route-counting issue but retained
the route legality omission. Current AdvCiv-SAS retains it.

CURRENT NORMAL ROUTE LEGALITY
-----------------------------
Current `CvPlayer::canBuild` delegates to `CvPlot::canBuild` for plot/build legality.

For a route Build, `CvPlot::canBuild` validates both mandatory and OR bonus
prerequisites when `bTestVisible == false`:

    if (GC.getInfo(eRoute).getPrereqBonus() != NO_BONUS)
    {
        if (!isAdjacentPlotGroupConnectedBonus(ePlayer,
            GC.getInfo(eRoute).getPrereqBonus()))
        {
            return false;
        }
    }

    bool bFoundValid = true;
    for (int i = 0; i < GC.getInfo(eRoute).getNumPrereqOrBonuses(); i++)
    {
        bFoundValid = false;
        if (isAdjacentPlotGroupConnectedBonus(ePlayer,
            GC.getInfo(eRoute).getPrereqOrBonus(i)))
        {
            bFoundValid = true;
            break;
        }
    }
    if (!bFoundValid)
        return false;

Current `ROUTE_RAILROAD` has:

    iAdvancedStartCost = 18

    PrereqOrBonuses:
        BONUS_COAL
        BONUS_OIL

and current `BUILD_RAILROAD` requires:

    TECH_STEAM_POWER

Therefore an ordinary Worker may build Railroad only when:
* the player has Steam Power; AND
* the plot's adjacent plot-group/network can provide Coal OR Oil.

This is a real strategic-resource prerequisite, not merely help/UI metadata.

ADVANCED START VALIDATOR CHECKS ONLY THE BUILD TECHNOLOGY
---------------------------------------------------------
Current `CvPlayer::getAdvancedStartRouteCost` performs plot ownership/basic-terrain
checks and then:

    FOR_EACH_ENUM(Build)
    {
        if (GC.getInfo(eLoopBuild).getRoute() == eRoute)
        {
            if (!GET_TEAM(getTeam()).isHasTech(
                GC.getInfo(eLoopBuild).getTechPrereq()))
            {
                return -1;
            }
        }
    }

It never checks:
* `CvRouteInfo::getPrereqBonus()`;
* `CvRouteInfo::getPrereqOrBonus(...)`;
* `CvPlot::isAdjacentPlotGroupConnectedBonus(...)`;
* or `CvPlot::canBuild` through the matching route Build.

Thus Steam Power alone makes Railroad return a nonnegative Advanced Start price even
when the player has neither Coal nor Oil available to the plot/network.

EXECUTION DOES NOT REVALIDATE
-----------------------------
`CvPlayer::doAdvancedStartAction` handles a route purchase as:

    int iCost = getAdvancedStartRouteCost(eRoute, bAdd, pPlot);
    if (bAdd && iCost < 0)
        return;

    if (bAdd)
    {
        if (getAdvancedStartPoints() >= iCost)
        {
            pPlot->setRouteType(eRoute);
            changeAdvancedStartPoints(-iCost);
        }
    }

There is no subsequent `canBuild` or route-resource check.

Once the incomplete cost helper approves the purchase, `setRouteType` installs the
Railroad directly.

CURRENT SHIPPED REACHABILITY
----------------------------
Advanced Start is a normal visible option:

    GAMEOPTION_ADVANCED_START
        bDefault = 0
        bVisible = 1

Current start-era data supplies ordinary points, including:

    ERA_MODERN
        iAdvancedStartPoints = 7500

The normal game-setup tech initialization grants every technology from an era EARLIER
than the selected start era.

Current Steam Power is:

    TECH_STEAM_POWER
        Era = ERA_INDUSTRIAL
        iAdvancedStartCost = 100

Therefore a Modern-era Advanced Start begins with Steam Power already known.

Current AdvCiv's worker-build price modifier is:

    ADVANCED_START_WORKER_BUILD_MODIFIER = 67

and Normal-speed BuildPercent is 100. Railroad's base Advanced Start price 18 is
therefore cheap and normally purchasable once a city/owned plot exists.

DETERMINISTIC CURRENT-SAS REPRO
-------------------------------
1. Start a normal Custom Game with:
       GAMEOPTION_ADVANCED_START enabled
       Start Era = Modern
       a normal land map.
2. The player receives 7500 Advanced Start points and automatically knows Industrial-
   era Steam Power.
3. Establish the required first city / owned plot through the ordinary Advanced Start
   interface.
4. Use a position whose player/network has NO connected Coal and NO connected Oil.
5. On that owned non-city land plot compare:
       normal BUILD_RAILROAD legality
   against:
       getAdvancedStartRouteCost(ROUTE_RAILROAD, true, pPlot).

Normal Worker construction:
* fails `CvPlot::canBuild`, because neither Railroad OR-bonus prerequisite is connected.

Advanced Start:
* sees Steam Power;
* returns a nonnegative Railroad price;
* the UI/action accepts the purchase;
* `doAdvancedStartAction` directly executes
      pPlot->setRouteType(ROUTE_RAILROAD).

The player therefore owns a functional Railroad on a plot where its normal workers are
not legally allowed to build Railroad at all.

The same reproduction can be done in an earlier Advanced Start by purchasing Steam
Power first if sufficient points/prerequisites are available; Modern start simply
removes that extra setup variable.

PLAYER-FACING CONSEQUENCE
-------------------------
This bypasses a normal strategic-resource gate during game setup.

A player without Coal or Oil can spend Advanced Start points to construct Railroad
segments anyway, receiving the route's current movement/network behavior despite
failing the ordinary route requirement.

Because the action directly writes the route type, the illegally purchased Railroad
does not disappear when Advanced Start ends. It becomes normal map state for the game.

The AI Advanced Start code also calls the same route-cost helper and dispatches the
same `ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_ROUTE`, so the legality omission is not limited to direct
human Python/UI invocation. A human reproduction is sufficient for reachability.

ANCESTRY
--------
This is inherited from stock BtS.

Stock BtS/Civ4CE:
* `ROUTE_RAILROAD` already has Coal/Oil `PrereqOrBonuses`;
* normal `CvPlot::canBuild` checks route bonus prerequisites;
* `CvPlayer::getAdvancedStartRouteCost` checks the matching Build tech but does not
  check route bonus prerequisites;
* `doAdvancedStartAction` directly installs the route after the cost helper succeeds.

K-Mod 1.46 retains the same Advanced Start route validator/execution structure.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the missing resource validation. Its changes include:
* Advanced Start route/improvement price tuning under `advc.250c`;
* the `advc.001` fix so `AdvancedStartCostIncrease` counts only the current player's
  routes instead of every route on the map.

Neither change adds the missing route bonus legality test.

Current SAS inherits the same omission while moving Railroad's Build prerequisite to
Steam Power; current Railroad still requires Coal OR Oil in `CIV4RouteInfos.xml`.

Thus F472 is best classified as a Firaxis/BtS Advanced Start legality bug inherited
through the lineage.

DUPLICATE / ALBUM CHECK
-----------------------
The reconciled C031 album and current Known Issues were searched for:
* Advanced Start Railroad;
* Advanced Start route bonus/resource;
* `getAdvancedStartRouteCost`;
* Railroad + Coal/Oil Advanced Start.

No existing numbered root owns this legality bypass.

The earlier Queue-004 `getBestRoute(NULL)` control is distinct:
* that helper deliberately supplies technologically unlocked automatic CITY routes and
  its resource omission was classified as inherited/intended city-route semantics;
* F472 is an explicit player purchase of a route on a normal plot through Advanced
  Start, where a normal Worker's route legality rejects the exact same state.

AdvCiv manual/history also records a different Advanced Start route bug:
`AdvancedStartCostIncrease` had counted routes/improvements owned by other players.
That was fixed by AdvCiv's owner filter and is not F472.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR
-------------------
For an ADD operation on a concrete plot, validate through the matching route Build
rather than separately reproducing only part of normal Build legality.

Conceptually:

    bool bFoundBuild = false;
    FOR_EACH_ENUM(Build)
    {
        CvBuildInfo const& kBuild = GC.getInfo(eLoopBuild);
        if (kBuild.getRoute() != eRoute)
            continue;

        if (GET_TEAM(getTeam()).isHasTech(kBuild.getTechPrereq()) &&
            (pPlot == NULL || canBuild(*pPlot, eLoopBuild, false, false, true)))
        {
            bFoundBuild = true;
            break;
        }
    }
    if (!bFoundBuild)
        return -1;

Exact flags should preserve Advanced Start's intended visibility/setup semantics, but
the route's bonus prerequisites must be applied.

If multiple BuildInfos can produce one Route, the correct contract is that at least
one currently legal matching Build suffices. Do not reject a route merely because a
different alternate Build for the same route lacks its tech.

Removal/refund does not need to retroactively demand the resource; removing an already
present route should remain possible.

REGRESSION TEST
---------------
1. Modern Advanced Start, Steam Power known.
2. Own a city and adjacent owned land plot.
3. No connected Coal and no connected Oil.
4. Assert:
       normal canBuild(BUILD_RAILROAD) == false
       getAdvancedStartRouteCost(ROUTE_RAILROAD, true, plot) < 0.
5. Connect Coal or Oil to the appropriate plot group/network.
6. Assert:
       normal canBuild(BUILD_RAILROAD) == true
       Advanced Start Railroad cost is now nonnegative.
7. Purchase Railroad; verify points are charged and route is placed.
8. Test route removal/refund independently.
9. If alternate BuildInfos for one route are ever added, verify any one legal Build is
   sufficient.

POST-WIP193 ADVANCED START SIBLING RECONCILIATION
--------------------------------------------------
1. Technology removal/refund remains the previously REJECTED F088 / KI#410 backend
   caveat, not F473.

The Advanced Start backend can compute technology-removal prices, and removing an
enabling technology after buying dependent state is therefore an API-level concern.
The shipped Tech Chooser path, however, only submits technology additions; the AI also
does not perform Advanced Start technology refunds. No ordinary current repository
producer exposes the removal action. Preserve the older F088 rejection.

2. Improvement, unit and building purchases remain materially better validated than
   F472's route purchase.

* Improvement purchase resolves a matching Build and enters normal `canBuild` legality.
* Unit purchase enters `canTrain` plus plot/unit placement legality.
* Building purchase enters `canConstruct`.

No independent current-data sibling bypass comparable to Railroad's missing route
bonus prerequisite was established.

3. `getAdvancedStartCityCost` and `getAdvancedStartCultureCost` were re-read as large,
   lightly covered helpers.

City placement goes through `canFound`; no current supported city-placement legality
bypass was established. The culture-level `+1` indexing shape is a generic upper-bound
robustness concern if an external caller attempts to purchase culture beyond the final
level, but current Advanced Start points/culture pricing do not provide an ordinary
route to buying a city beyond Legendary. Keep this below the numbered threshold.

HISTORICAL-FIX x LOW-COVERAGE PASS
----------------------------------
4. `CvPlayer::validateDiplomacy` is already semantically owned by an earlier album
   control and remains closed.

The initially suspicious Defensive Pact stale-offer check examines the first trade
item, but the actual AI Defensive Pact contact producer constructs a one-item DP offer
on each side. There is no supported producer where a later-list DP silently bypasses
that validation. Do not duplicate the earlier control merely because the function has
few literal mentions.

5. `DIPLOEVENT_JOIN_WAR` `GET_TEAM(ePlayer)` is a FALSE POSITIVE under the active SAS
   helper overloads.

At first comparison, K-Mod/Civ4CE spell the declaration target as:

    GET_TEAM(GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).getTeam()).declareWar(...)

whereas AdvCiv/current SAS use:

    GET_TEAM(ePlayer).declareWar(...)

Because `ePlayer` is `PlayerTypes`, this looked especially dangerous after a Permanent
Alliance, where a player's current team can differ from its original player index.

Full helper-layer reconciliation closes it. In the active non-AI gameplay layer:

    #define GET_TEAM(x) CvGamePlay::getTeam(x)

and `CvGamePlay` provides a `getTeam(PlayerTypes)` overload that resolves through:

    CvTeam::getTeam(TEAMID(ePlayer))

Therefore the short AdvCiv spelling maps the player to its CURRENT team, including
after Permanent Alliance reassignment. It is semantically equivalent to K-Mod's more
explicit spelling.

This is the same enum-overload trap already documented elsewhere in the album for
`CvPlayer::canContact` and related false positives. Do not revive a raw
PlayerTypes->TeamTypes bug from `GET_TEAM(ePlayer)` syntax without checking the active
overload context.

6. `CvPlayer::isValidTriggerCorporation` retains K-Mod's explicit corporation-count
   bugfix and closes normally.

For non-city trigger evaluation, current code requires:

    getHasCorporationCount(eCorporation) > 0

before applying optional headquarters ownership checks. The old inverted/early-return
shape remains commented out next to K-Mod's repair. No missing religion/corporation
sibling was found here.

7. `CvPlayer::removeBuildingClass` remains consistent with its normal production
   caller and the Unofficial Patch intent.

The helper removes exactly one real instance of the civilization's mapped building
class. Its normal DLL caller is the ORDER_CONSTRUCT completion path when the class has
become maxed while an already-started order is finishing. The 2010 Unofficial Patch
changed the old behavior from zeroing the building count to subtracting one instance,
which avoids deleting multiple real copies in data sets that permit them.

Current Palace data (`MaxPlayerInstances=1`, `ExtraPlayerInstances=1`, `bNoLimit=1`)
uses this mechanism to move the capital cleanly: the extra slot permits starting the
replacement, and completion removes one old Palace before installing the new one. No
independent wrong-building or count-underflow producer was established.

8. `CvPlayer::setCommercePercent` closes under its two-pass balancing contract.

The first pass redistributes against other flexible commerce types; if forced changes
cannot balance under those restrictions, the second pass broadens the eligible types.
The apparently odd negative `iAdjustment` when total commerce falls below 100 is
intentional: subtracting a negative adjustment raises another eligible percentage.
The final assertion requires the total to return to 100, and the function refreshes
commerce, human commerce weights, assignment dirtiness and relevant UI state after an
actual change. No stale authoritative percentage/cache root was established.

9. `CvPlayer::initFreeUnits` remains setup-heavy rather than exposing a new runtime
   invariant in this pass.

The main historical seams checked were Advanced Start points/visibility, starting-site
Goody removal, AI handicap start-unit multipliers and `addFreeUnitAI` legality. The
normal non-Advanced-Start path selects starting defenders/workers/explorers through
`canTrain`; actual placement funnels through `addFreeUnit`, which rejects missing
starting plots and performs the existing explorer-placement checks. No current normal
setup failure cleared the F473 threshold.

10. `CvPlayer::disbandUnit` remains primarily policy/valuation.

The routine excludes cargo, Golden Age and non-production-cost units, protects the only
military-happiness unit on a plot, then chooses among remaining units by cost,
experience, level, defensive placement and UnitAI weighting. The previously tempting
questions in this area concern tuning choices rather than copied state or a violated
current invariant. No F473.

CONTROL — `getKnownPlayerColor` IS AN ACTIVE-OBSERVER UI CONCEALMENT HELPER
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::getKnownPlayerColor(TeamTypes eObserver)` initially deserved a privacy
check because it substitutes the Barbarian player color for an unknown civilization.
The current compiled callers resolve the intended observer contract:

* `CvPlot::plotMinimapColor`;
* `CvPlayer::getResourceLayerColors`;
* `CvPlayer::getCultureLayerColors`;
* the external player-color/UI accessor.

These are active-observer presentation paths rather than authoritative diplomatic or
gameplay knowledge stores. The default-observer handling through the active team is
consistent with those callers. No independent information leak or stale-state root was
established.

CONTROL — `getNumGovernmentCenters` IS DYNAMIC / UI-FACING, NOT A STALE CACHE
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
`getNumGovernmentCenters()` walks the player's current cities and counts
`isGovernmentCenter()` dynamically. Its DLL use is essentially UI/Python-facing; core
maintenance logic consumes city-level government-center state rather than a copied
player count. No invalidation family exists here.

CONTROL — `keepCity` CREATIVE CULTURE HAS THE MATCHING OCCUPATION-END HOOK
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::keepCity` deliberately calls `CvCity::initTraitCulture()` only when the
acquired city is not in occupation. That initially looked like a possible permanently
missed trait effect for conquered cities.

The lifecycle closes cleanly: `CvCity::setOccupationTimer` detects the transition from
occupied to non-occupied and calls `initTraitCulture()` before refreshing culture
level. This is exactly the historical advc.908b intent (Creative/free trait culture
starts after occupation ends), not a missing delayed application.

CONTROL — `getSplitEmpireLeaders` PRESERVES THE RANDOM-PERSONALITIES LIBERATION FIX
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The historical practical-2423 repair deliberately changed liberation/colony leader
selection from hidden personality identity to the displayed leader identity, leaving
personality randomization to `CvGame::addPlayer` afterward.

Current `getSplitEmpireLeaders` still excludes civilizations/leaders used by
`EVER_ALIVE` players through `getLeaderType()`, not `getPersonalityType()`. The intended
Random Personalities separation therefore survives. Malformed recycled-player colony
state remains independently owned by F447 / KI#770; no new colony root here.

CONTROL — PLAYER HISTORY OOB REPAIR SURVIVES CURRENT SAS LOGGING / PLAYER SWITCHING
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The old AdvCiv PlayerHistory out-of-bounds family was rechecked because current SAS
adds substantial game-record logging and active-player/lifecycle instrumentation.
The present contracts remain coherent:

* `initContainers` grows every PlayerHistory through the current game turn for late-
  start / scenario players;
* `PlayerHistory::grow(iSize)` guarantees storage through index `iSize`;
* normal per-turn history updates cover the seven current history enum values;
* active-player switching fills the departing living player's current entry before
  the switch, preventing the historical player-switch gap;
* SASGameRecord reads through the safe history accessor rather than indexing an
  assumed-current vector directly.

The current history enum is still exactly the set handled by the rewritten switch.
No current logging-induced reopening of practical-2635 was found.

CONTROL — `setFoundedFirstCity` PARENT GUARD IS THE INTENDED COLONIAL-CTD FIX
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
The UWAI update suppression in `setFoundedFirstCity` for players with a non-NO parent
can look like a missing cache update in isolation. Historical practical-1522 resolves
it: this guard was added specifically to avoid the colonial-vassal creation crash.
The colony initialization pipeline later establishes the new player's broader state.
No independent stale-cache consequence was established.

CONTROL — `initPlotGroup` IS ONLY THE ALLOCATION PRIMITIVE; CURRENT CALLER OWNS THE
REAL NETWORK INVARIANT
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::initPlotGroup` itself merely allocates/initializes a plot group. Its live
caller is `CvPlot::updatePlotGroup`, which performs trade-network eligibility,
adjacent-group joining/recalculation, and creates a new group only after those checks.
The historical bug in which group creation sat inside the wrong branch is no longer
present. No second plot-group initialization defect survived.

ROBUSTNESS NOTE — IMPROVEMENT-UPGRADE RATE CAN GENERICALLY REACH ZERO, BUT CURRENT
SAS DATA DOES NOT PRODUCE THE UNSAFE RATE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
AdvCiv's improvement-upgrade rewrite expresses the authoritative player upgrade rate
in percent and clamps it to nonnegative. Some downstream upgrade-time arithmetic no
longer carries the old explicit zero-rate guard. A future producer of a total
ImprovementUpgradeRateModifier <= -100 could therefore make that path unsafe.

Current SAS XML masks the structural concern: the only shipped nonzero civic producer
is positive (+100), and no ordinary current transition drives the rate to zero. Keep
as configuration/robustness debt rather than F473.

CONTROL — `killGoldenAgeUnits` DELAYED DEATH DOES NOT USE A DETACHED / DELETED UNIT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The ordering initially looks dangerous:

    pBestUnit->kill(true);
    if (pBestUnit->getPlot().isActiveVisible(false))
        pBestUnit->getGroup()->pushMission(MISSION_GOLDEN_AGE, 0);

Full `CvUnit::kill(true)` tracing closes the lifetime concern. The delayed path calls
`startDelayedDeath()` and returns before `setXY`, `joinGroup(NULL)`, or object deletion.
The unit therefore still owns its plot/group when the animation mission is queued.
The nearby comment saying kill removes the unit from groups is misleading for this
delayed path, but no UAF/null-group root exists.

The separate readiness-UnitClass vs consumption-UnitType distinction is also NOT new:
the album already preserves it as current-data-masked. Current SAS has one Golden-Age
unit type per relevant UnitClass, so the distinction cannot alter shipped behavior.

CONTROL — `getWorkRate(BuildTypes)` DOUBLE BASE-100 IS REAL SOURCE DEBT BUT ALREADY
PARKED AND NOT AUTHORITATIVE AI WORK PROGRESS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The player-level predictor contains the conspicuous inherited expression:

    iRate *= max(0, 100 + AIWorkRateModifier + 100);

where actual `CvUnit::workRate` uses the ordinary single-base form. With current SAS
handicap data (`AIWorkRateModifier == 0`) the AI branch of this PLAYER predictor would
indeed estimate twice the ordinary base work rate.

This is an exact existing album control, not F473. Caller tracing reconfirms why:

* live human build-turn help/warning paths use the active human player, so the bad AI
  branch is not taken;
* AI worker planning uses overloads fed by actual `CvUnit::workRate` or iterates
  actual workers rather than this player-only predictor;
* SASGameRecord likewise uses actual-unit work-rate/build-turn data.

AI Auto Play can expose an inaccurate UI-style estimate, but authoritative worker
progress is not doubled. Preserve the already-parked source defect; do not duplicate.

CONTROL — SPY DESTROY/BRIBE TARGET-OWNER VALIDATION IS THE EARLIER DORMANT FINDING
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A fresh low-coverage pass over `canSpyDestroyUnit` / `canSpyBribeUnit` noticed the
same structural ownership weakness preserved in WIP172/WIP179: the helper does not
itself prove that `kUnit.getOwner()` is `eTarget`, while the generic espionage costing
fallback can iterate third-party units on the plot.

Current shipped SAS still has all `iDestroyUnitCostFactor` and `iBuyUnitCostFactor`
values at zero. The affected mission families therefore have no current gameplay data
producer. This remains dormant robustness debt, not F473.

closely related changes:

* `setAlive(false)` clears the capital before killing components;
* bonus import/export updates skip `AI_updateBonusValue` while the player is dying;
* deal destruction is deferred until `m_bAlive` is false because that cleanup depends
  on death state.

Current source retains those guards/orderings. The currently known elimination-order
war-weariness failure is independently F471; this historical sibling pass did not
expose another death-time dereference/cache update that survives current ordering.

CONTROL — `changeHurryCount` RAW `iChange` ALGEBRA REMAINS SAFE UNDER SHIPPED
PRODUCERS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
The function stores per-Hurry source counts and maintains derived pop-rush / gold-rush
availability counters. On a 0 <-> positive boundary it adds raw `iChange` to the
derived counter. Generic API calls of magnitude >1 would make that algebra wrong.

Current compiled producer is civic processing. Hurry availability is a boolean XML
source and `processCivics` calls `changeHurryCount` with exactly +1 or -1 when that
civic is installed/removed. Current XML has one population-hurry civic and one gold-
hurry civic. Therefore every real boundary transition changes the derived counter by
exactly one. This matches the earlier album control; no F473.

  AI; corporation availability is dynamically filtered through `isActiveCorporation`;

* building-only-healthy and specialist-valid transitions dirty assignment logic;

  mutate -> new-contribution where required.

No independent current zero-boundary/cache sibling was established.

POST-WIP195 CONTROL — TEAM-EVENT PROPAGATION CONDITION IS INVERTED, BUT CURRENT SAS
HAS NO TEAM EVENTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::setEventOccured(..., bOthers=true)` contains a real inherited AdvCiv
iterator-refactor regression in the team-event propagation branch:

    else if (GC.getInfo(eEvent).isTeam())
    {
        for (MemberIter itOtherMember(getTeam()); itOtherMember.hasNext();
             ++itOtherMember)
        {
            if (itOtherMember->getID() != getID())
                continue;
            itOtherMember->setEventOccured(eEvent, kEventTriggered, false);
        }
    }

The condition retains only `this` player instead of the OTHER teammates. K-Mod and
Civ4CE/BtS use the opposite semantic condition and propagate the occurrence to the
other team members.

This is nevertheless NOT F473. Current SAS EventInfos contain no `bTeam=1` event, so
there is no shipped gameplay producer for the broken branch. The giant album had also
already preserved this exact source defect as dormant/data-masked robustness debt.


POST-WIP195 CONTROL — TEAM RESEARCH OVERFLOW USES CALLER MODIFIER, BUT CURRENT
PLAYER-SPECIFIC RESEARCH MODIFIERS ARE DISABLED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::getResearchTurnsLeftTimes100` correctly asks every teammate for that
teammate's ordinary research rate, but scales each teammate's stored overflow through
`this->calculateResearchModifier(eTech)` rather than
`kMember.calculateResearchModifier(eTech)`.

That is generically fragile for team games. Current SAS, however, has both human and AI
Groundbreaking penalty toggles disabled; that penalty is the only player-specific
component presently capable of making the relevant research modifier differ between
teammates. Current data therefore keep the modifiers symmetric. This exact generic
weakness was already preserved earlier in the album. No F473.


POST-WIP195 CONTROL — EVENT CLEAR LIST MULTIPLICITY REMAINS CURRENT-DATA MASKED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The event-clear code has ordering semantics that become awkward if one event can clear
multiple prior events with independently meaningful percentages. Current SAS XML does
not exercise that shape: every event with a positive ClearEvents entry has only one
positive clear target in shipped data. Preserve the generic configuration concern;
no current root.


POST-WIP195 DUPLICATE CONTROL — AREA-LOCAL MISSIONARY TRAINING OMISSION IS F451
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::countReligionSpreadUnits(pArea, ..., bIncludeTraining=true)` filters
existing missionary units by area but counts missionaries being trained in every city
without applying the same area test. Its corporation sibling filters both the unit and
production sides.

The current AI caller genuinely uses the religion helper for an area-local missionary
coverage estimate, so this looked strong on a fresh low-literal-coverage pass. Semantic
album reconciliation shows that it is exactly F451 / KI#774, already confirmed with
its ordinary `AI_missionaryValue` consequence. Do not duplicate it as F473.


F473 / KI#796 — BBAI `initInGame` TREATS DEAD ASSIGNED TEAMMATES AS AN EXISTING TEAM,
SO A RECYCLED COLONY CAN REVIVE A FULLY DEFEATED MULTI-MEMBER TEAM'S STALE TECHNOLOGY
STATE AND MISS PLAYER-LEVEL TECH EFFECTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED. This is a Better BTS AI / K-Mod lifecycle regression inherited by Base
AdvCiv and current AdvCiv-SAS. It is distinct from F447's recycled-player / LIVE-team
mismatch: here the selected player's old team is fully DEAD, so `CvGame::addPlayer`
does run, but `CvPlayer::initInGame` fails to reset the dead multi-member team because
another dead player is still assigned to it.


ROOT — `initInGame` TESTS ASSIGNED MEMBERSHIP, NOT LIVE TEAM EXISTENCE
---------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvGame::addPlayer` recycles a slot by changing its leader/civilization/status/color
and then calling:

    GET_PLAYER(eNewPlayer).initInGame(eNewPlayer);

`CvPlayer::initInGame` first resets the PLAYER:

    reset(eID);

`CvPlayer::reset` clears the player's serialized gameplay state, including:

    m_iExtraHealth = 0;
    ...
    m_bAlive = false;
    m_bEverAlive = false;

but it then restores `m_eTeamType` from `CvInitCore` through `updateTeamType()`. It does
not move the recycled slot to a new team and does not reset the old `CvTeam` object.

The BBAI team-reset logic then counts every other PLAYER ASSIGNED to that team,
regardless of whether the player is alive:

    int iOtherTeamMembers = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < MAX_CIV_PLAYERS; i++)
    {
        if (i != getID() && TEAMID((PlayerTypes)i) == getTeam())
            iOtherTeamMembers++;
    }

and resets the team only when there are no other assigned members, or when the team's
stored total member count is zero:

    if (iOtherTeamMembers == 0 || GET_TEAM(getTeam()).getNumMembers() == 0)
    {
        bTeamInit = true;
        GET_TEAM(getTeam()).init(getTeam());
        ...
    }

This is not equivalent to asking whether the team still has a live identity.

Player death calls `CvTeam::changeAliveCount(-1)`. It does NOT decrement
`m_iNumMembers`. Current source has only player initialization and `CvPlayer::setTeam`
as producers of `changeNumMembers`; ordinary elimination leaves defeated players
assigned to their old team.

Therefore, for an old two-player Team T whose members X and Y are both dead:

    T.getAliveCount()  == 0
    T.isAlive()        == false
    T.getNumMembers()  == 2

If X is recycled, `initInGame` sees Y through `CvInitCore` and computes:

    iOtherTeamMembers == 1
    T.getNumMembers() == 2

Both reset conditions are false. `CvTeam::init(T)` is skipped even though Team T has
no living members.

`initOtherData()` then calls `setAlive(true)`, reviving X and thereby reviving Team T
without ever clearing the old defeated team's serialized team state.


WHY DEAD TEAM STATE SURVIVES
----------------------------
`CvTeam::changeAliveCount` performs elimination teardown when AliveCount reaches zero:
it releases vassals, exposes the dead team's identity, clears wars and war plans, and
updates related lifecycle state. It does NOT call `CvTeam::reset` and does not clear
technology ownership, research progress, project counts or the other serialized team
arrays.

By contrast, `CvTeam::reset` / `CvTeam::init` explicitly clears, among many fields:

    m_iNumMembers
    m_iAliveCount
    m_iTechCount
    m_aiProjectCount
    m_aiResearchProgress
    m_abHasTech

The skipped team initialization is therefore gameplay-significant, not merely stale
metadata.


DETERMINISTIC CURRENT-SAS CONSEQUENCE — BIOENGINEERING IS KNOWN BUT ITS +3 HEALTH IS
MISSING FROM THE NEW COLONY PLAYER
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS `TECH_BIOENGINEERING` is a Future Era technology with:

    <iHealth>3</iHealth>

When a technology is newly processed, `CvTeam::processTech` applies persistent
player-level effects to team members, including:

    kMember.changeFeatureProductionModifier(...);
    kMember.changeWorkerSpeedModifier(...);
    kMember.changeTradeRoutes(...);
    kMember.changeExtraHealth(kTech.getHealth() * iChange);
    kMember.changeExtraHappiness(...);
    kMember.changeAssets(...);
    kMember.changePower(...);
    kMember.changeTechScore(...);
    ...

Use this supported state:

1. Human player P has an eligible colony area.
2. No never-alive player slot remains, so `getSplitEmpirePlayer` must use AdvCiv's
   human-only defeated-player recycling fallback. The same supported scenario
   reachability already established for F447 applies: all 48 player slots can have
   been ever alive while scenario/custom setup repeats civilizations and leaves at
   least one valid unused civilization/leader combination for colony creation.
3. X is the first recyclable dead player.
4. X and another dead player Y are both still assigned to old Team T. T is fully
   defeated: `T.isAlive()==false`, but `T.getNumMembers()==2`.
5. Before defeat, Team T acquired Bioengineering, so its surviving team state still
   has `m_abHasTech[BIOENGINEERING] == true`.
6. Parent P also knows Bioengineering.
7. P creates the colony.

`CvPlayer::splitEmpire` correctly sees that T is dead:

    bool bPlayerExists = GET_TEAM(eNewPlayer).isAlive();

so this time, unlike F447, `bPlayerExists == false` and `CvGame::addPlayer` DOES run.

`initInGame` resets X's player state, clearing the previous Bioengineering-derived
player health, but skips `CvTeam::init` for T because dead teammate Y remains assigned.
Thus Team T still says Bioengineering is known.

The colony-inheritance loop later executes:

    if (GET_TEAM(getTeam()).isHasTech(eLoopTech))
        kNewTeam.setHasTech(eLoopTech, true, eNewPlayer, ...);

For Bioengineering, `CvTeam::setHasTech` immediately returns at:

    if (isHasTech(eTech) == bNewValue)
        return;

because stale Team T already has the tech. `processTech` is never replayed for the
newly reset X.

The result is internally inconsistent:

* Team T / colony X owns Bioengineering;
* X's reset player state lacks Bioengineering's +3 `m_iExtraHealth` contribution;
* colony cities use `GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).getExtraHealth()` directly in their health
  calculation, so the missing effect is immediately gameplay-visible.

The same mechanism can skip other player-level effects for any old team technology
that the parent also owns. Conversely, old Team T can also retain technologies that
P does NOT know because the colony inheritance loop only adds parent technologies; it
does not remove old-team technologies.

The Bioengineering +3-health case is enough to prove a concrete current-data failure
without relying on the broader stale-state surface.


THE MISMATCH SURVIVES SAVE/LOAD
-------------------------------
The incorrect state is serialized on both sides:

* `CvTeam::write/read` stores `m_abHasTech` directly;
* `CvPlayer::write/read` stores `m_iExtraHealth` directly.

Loading does not replay every already-known team technology through `processTech`.
Therefore a save made after the malformed colony is created preserves both “team knows
Bioengineering” and “player is missing its +3 health contribution”; save/load does not
self-heal the mismatch.


ANCESTRY — STOCK BTS RESETS THE TEAM; BBAI INTRODUCED THE CONDITIONAL RESET
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The root is not stock BtS colony behavior.

Civ4CE's reconstructed BtS `CvGame::addPlayer` obtains the selected player's old team
and unconditionally does:

    GET_TEAM(eTeam).init(eTeam);
    GET_PLAYER(eNewPlayer).init(eNewPlayer);

Thus a fully dead recycled team is cleared before the replacement player is
initialized.

Better BTS AI changed `CvGame::addPlayer` on 2008-12-30. K-Mod retains the patch and
its comments:

    // Team init now handled when appropriate in player initInGame
    // Standard player init is written for beginning of game ...
    GET_PLAYER(eNewPlayer).initInGame(eNewPlayer);

K-Mod's `initInGame` contains the same `iOtherTeamMembers` / `getNumMembers()`
conditional team-reset logic shown above. Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains it, and current SAS
retains it.

So F473 is an inherited BBAI/K-Mod lifecycle regression caused by replacing BtS's
unconditional recycled-team reset with a conditional test that treats dead assigned
teammates as evidence that the old team should be preserved.


DUPLICATE / ALBUM RECONCILIATION
--------------------------------
F473 is independent of the surrounding confirmed lifecycle roots.

F447 / KI#770:
* selected player X is dead;
* X's OLD TEAM IS STILL ALIVE because another teammate survives;
* `splitEmpire` therefore sets `bPlayerExists=true` and SKIPS `addPlayer/initInGame`
  entirely;
* city transfer later revives the old player identity through `verifyAlive`.

F473 / KI#796:
* selected player X is dead;
* X's OLD TEAM IS FULLY DEAD because every teammate is dead;
* `splitEmpire` therefore sets `bPlayerExists=false` and DOES call
  `addPlayer/initInGame`;
* the PLAYER is reset/rebranded, but `initInGame` skips resetting the dead TEAM because
  another dead assigned member still counts toward `iOtherTeamMembers` / NumMembers;
* stale team technology state then conflicts with the new player's reset persistent
  tech-derived state.

F094 / KI#416 is also different. F094 was AdvCiv practical-1837's alive-only
technology-processing regression: a dead member of a STILL-LIVING team could miss
tech effects acquired while dead. Current SAS has repaired that by processing
EVER_ALIVE assigned members. F473 happens later when the recycled player's own state
is explicitly RESET while its fully dead team's already-known technologies survive;
the inheritance call then no-ops because those technologies are already marked known.

F470 / KI#793 concerns missing `CvAgents` cache rebuilding after HUMAN-involved
Permanent Alliances and subsequent iterator consumers. F473 does not depend on stale
agent iterators or Permanent Alliances.

The earlier album control about `initInGame` comparing a team-loop integer with
`getID()` concerned minor-team declaration logic and did not audit this conditional
team-reset invariant.

No prior album root owns the fully-dead-multi-member-team / recycled-player reset
split above.


CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Do not fix this merely by changing the existing condition to “no other ALIVE member”
and then blindly resetting a multi-member team. If dead Y remains assigned to T while
`CvTeam::reset` changes `m_iNumMembers` back to zero/one, team membership bookkeeping
can become inconsistent and a later revival of Y creates another lifecycle problem.

For colony recycling, the safest narrow policy is to refuse a defeated player slot
whose old team has any other assigned member. Conceptually:

    recyclable dead player must belong to an old singleton team

This single restriction also complements F447's live-team case: a defeated member of
any multi-member old team is not a safe identity to repurpose as a fresh colonial
civilization without explicit team detachment/reassignment.

If full multi-member-slot recycling is desired instead, move the replacement player
onto a genuinely clean team (or explicitly detach/reconcile all old team membership)
before `addPlayer/initInGame`, then initialize that team and rebuild all dependent
team/member caches. Merely forcing `CvTeam::init` on T while leaving other dead players
assigned to T is incomplete.

Regression coverage should include:

* no never-alive slots remaining;
* recyclable X and dead teammate Y assigned to the same fully defeated team;
* old team and parent both owning a technology with a player-level persistent effect,
  e.g. current SAS Bioengineering +3 health;
* colony creation must either reject the unsafe recycled slot or produce a clean
  colony whose team technologies and player-level effects agree.


SECONDARY ROBUSTNESS NOTE — `initInGame` MINOR-TEAM SELF SKIP COMPARES TEAM LOOP ID
WITH PLAYER ID
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The later initialization loop iterates TeamTypes but skips:

    if (i == getID() || !kTarget.isAlive())
        continue;

rather than comparing `i` with `getTeam()`.

For normal one-player/one-corresponding-team colony creation, PlayerTypes and TeamTypes
coincide and this is masked. Current WorldBuilder/scenario data can assign players to
arbitrary team IDs, so a recycled/custom slot where player ID and team ID differ can
make the loop skip an unrelated same-numbered team instead of the new player's team.
In combination with a live minor team this can omit the setup declaration of permanent
war that the loop is meant to establish.

This is real generic/scenario robustness debt but is not needed for F473 and remains
below the numbered threshold here. The stronger fully-dead-team reset defect above has
a concrete persistent current-data consequence.

---------
F473 is CONFIRMED and consumes KI#796.
F474 / provisional KI#797 is the next unused root slot.

POST-F473 SIBLING CONTROL — TEAM MEMBERSHIP / UWAI ORDERING
-----------------------------------------------------------

back out of colony lifecycle code.

The team membership counter does not independently repair F473. `initInGame` decides
whether to reset/increment the selected team from its preexisting assigned-member state;
that is part of F473's stale fully-dead multi-member team root rather than a second
counter defect.

The apparent UWAI ordering seam also closes. `initInGame` calls:

    getUWAI().initNewPlayerInGame(getID());

before `splitEmpire` later installs the colony parent and vassal state, but that helper
only initializes the new player/team UWAI objects and clears the WarEvaluator cache.
The substantive:

    getUWAI().processNewPlayerInGame(eNewPlayer);

call occurs near the END of `splitEmpire`, after parent assignment, inherited techs,
`assignVassal`, city transfer, plot-group rebuilding and free-defender creation. That
later update is the point that populates the new player's UWAI cache and runs team
`turnPre`. No independent parent/vassal-dependent stale UWAI state was established.

The minor-team `initInGame` self-skip (`i == getID()` in a TeamTypes loop) remains the
scenario/robustness note preserved in WIP196; no ordinary colony producer was found
that promotes it.


F474 / KI#797 — RECYCLING ANY DEFEATED COLONY SLOT DUPLICATES ADVC'S
`CIV_EVER_ALIVE` AGENT CACHES; THE COLONY CAN LOSE FIRST-DISCOVERY REWARDS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED. This is an AdvCiv `advc.agent` integration defect reached by the same
supported human colony-slot recycling fallback that underlies the broader recycled
player family, but it does NOT require F473's stale multi-member-team condition.
A defeated singleton-team slot is enough.

ROOT
----
`CvAgents::playerDefeated` deliberately removes a defeated player/team only from the
ALIVE caches. It correctly leaves the historical EVER_ALIVE sequences intact:

    eraseFromSeqCache(playerSeqCache(CIV_ALIVE), eDeadPlayer);
    ...
    if (!GET_TEAM(eTeam).isAlive())
        eraseFromSeqCache(teamSeqCache(CIV_ALIVE), eTeam);

There is no removal from:

    playerSeqCache(CIV_EVER_ALIVE)
    teamSeqCache(CIV_EVER_ALIVE)

because the player/team really has been alive historically.

When a new colony uses a never-used slot, `CvPlayer::initInGame` eventually calls:

    GC.getAgents().colonyCreated(getID());

and `CvAgents::colonyCreated` does:

    playerSetAliveInGame(eNewPlayer, false);

`playerSetAliveInGame(..., false)` unconditionally performs:

    insertIntoVector(teamSeqCache(CIV_EVER_ALIVE), pTeam, false);
    ...
    insertIntoVector(playerSeqCache(CIV_EVER_ALIVE), pPlayer, false);

The final `false` merely suppresses the duplicate assertion. It does NOT request
unique insertion. `insertIntoVector` always inserts the pointer after walking to its
sorted position:

    FAssert(!bAssertSuccess || iPosID != iAgentID);
    ...
    v.insert(pos, pAgent);

So for a truly never-alive player/team this is correct, but for a RECYCLED defeated
slot both pointers are ALREADY present in their EVER_ALIVE vectors and are inserted a
second time.

The comment above `colonyCreated` explicitly says:

    // Normally, players shouldn't be reused; if reuse does occur, call should still succeed.

but the suppressed assertion makes reuse silently duplicate the historical sequences
instead of making it safe.

WHY THIS DOES NOT REQUIRE F473
-------------------------------
Use a defeated player X whose OLD TEAM WAS A SINGLETON.

On recycling:
* `splitEmpire` sees X's old team dead, so `CvGame::addPlayer` DOES run;
* `initInGame` sees no other assigned teammate, so it correctly resets that team;
* player and team state are therefore clean — F473 is absent;
* nevertheless `playerDefeated` never removed X/T from the `CIV_EVER_ALIVE` caches;
* `colonyCreated(..., false)` inserts X and T into those same caches again.

Thus F474 survives even when the F473 team-reset invariant is completely satisfied.

The ALIVE sequences are different: defeat DID remove X/T from those caches, so their
new insertion is expected. The defect is specifically the duplicate historical
EVER_ALIVE entries.

DETERMINISTIC CURRENT-SAS CONSEQUENCE — TRUE FIRST DISCOVERY IS COUNTED AS TWO TEAMS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvGame::countKnownTechNumTeams` was converted by AdvCiv from the stock/K-Mod raw
MAX_TEAMS scan to:

    int iCount = 0;
    for (TeamIter<EVER_ALIVE> itTeam; itTeam.hasNext(); ++itTeam)
    {
        if (itTeam->isHasTech(eTech))
            iCount++;
    }

After recycled singleton Team T is duplicated in `CIV_EVER_ALIVE`, any technology T
owns is counted TWICE by this routine.

That directly feeds `CvTeam::setHasTech`'s first-discovery contract. After setting the
technology true, current code calculates:

    bool const bFirstToDiscover =
        (kGame.countKnownTechNumTeams(eTech) == 1);

and all first-discovery rewards are gated by that boolean.

Current SAS provides a particularly clean late-game reproducer:

    TECH_ROMANTICISM
        Era = ERA_INDUSTRIAL
        FirstFreeUnitClass = UNITCLASS_GREAT_ARTIST

Ordinary reproduction shape:

1. Exhaust all never-alive player slots while preserving at least one valid unused
   colony civilization/leader combination, as already source-proven possible for the
   supported human recycling path in F447/F473.
2. Let singleton Player X / Team T be eliminated.
3. A human later creates a colony; `getSplitEmpirePlayer` selects X as the recyclable
   dead slot.
4. Because T is fully dead, `addPlayer/initInGame` executes normally. Because T was a
   singleton, its team is also reset normally — no F473 dependency.
5. `CvAgents::colonyCreated(X)` duplicates X and T in `CIV_EVER_ALIVE`.
6. Leave `TECH_ROMANTICISM` unknown to every team until after the colony exists.
7. Let the colony become the TRUE FIRST team in the world to research Romanticism.
8. `setHasTech` marks T as owning Romanticism, then calls
   `countKnownTechNumTeams(TECH_ROMANTICISM)`.
9. The EVER_ALIVE iterator encounters the same Team T pointer twice and returns 2.
10. `bFirstToDiscover` is therefore false even though no other team owns the tech.
11. `CvPlayer::getTechFreeUnit` would map Romanticism's
    `UNITCLASS_GREAT_ARTIST` to the colony civilization's Great Artist, but the entire
    first-discovery block is skipped.
12. The colony permanently loses the shipped free Great Artist reward.

Current SAS also has many other Industrial/Modern/Future technologies with non-NONE
`FirstFreeUnitClass` (and Theory of Evolution with a first-free-tech reward), so the
issue is not tied to an obsolete Ancient-only race that a late colony could never win.
Romanticism is simply the smallest current-data example.

PERSISTENCE / SAVE-LOAD
-----------------------
`CvAgents::gameStart(true)` calls `updateAllCachedSequences()`, which reconstructs the
vectors from current player/team state and therefore removes the duplicate pointers.
So saving and loading immediately after colony creation can MASK F474.

But if the colony completes Romanticism before that rebuild, the first-discovery
reward has already been skipped. Loading does not replay `setHasTech`'s first-discovery
reward block for technologies already known. The missed Great Artist therefore does
not self-heal.

This gives a clean diagnostic:
* recycle colony -> save/load -> discover first-perk tech: iterator cache repaired;
* recycle colony -> discover first-perk tech -> save/load: missed reward persists.

ANCESTRY / COMPARISON
---------------------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same `CvAgents::playerDefeated`,
`playerSetAliveInGame`, `colonyCreated` and `insertIntoVector` behavior. Current SAS
retains it.

K-Mod 1.46 and stock BtS/Civ4CE do NOT have the `advc.agent` cached sequence layer.
Their `CvGame::countKnownTechNumTeams` scans each TeamTypes slot exactly once:

    for (int iI = 0; iI < MAX_TEAMS; iI++)
        if (GET_TEAM((TeamTypes)iI).isEverAlive() &&
            GET_TEAM((TeamTypes)iI).isHasTech(eTech))
            iCount++;

So recycling a player cannot duplicate the same team in that calculation upstream.
F474 is specifically an AgentIterator cache-integration regression introduced after
K-Mod's direct index scans.

DUPLICATE / ALBUM RECONCILIATION
--------------------------------
F470 / KI#793 is a different `CvAgents` root. F470 leaves MEMBER and ALIVE-team caches
stale after HUMAN-involved Permanent Alliances because the generic transaction omits
`allianceFormed()` / `updateAllCachedSequences()`.

F474 does not involve Permanent Alliances or team reassignment. It creates literal
DUPLICATE pointer entries in otherwise correctly selected EVER_ALIVE vectors when an
existing historical identity is recycled as a colony.

F473 / KI#796 is also independent:
* F473 = dead multi-member old team is not reset, preserving stale authoritative team
  state while the player is reset;
* F474 = historical AgentIterator entries are inserted twice; singleton-team recycling
  with a clean team reset is sufficient.

F447 / KI#770 skips `addPlayer/initInGame` entirely when the recycled dead player's old
team is still alive, so `colonyCreated` is not reached on that malformed branch. F474
therefore belongs specifically to the fully-dead-team recycling branch where
`addPlayer/initInGame` DOES run.

No previous album root covers duplicate `CIV_EVER_ALIVE` entries from recycled colony
creation or the resulting first-discovery miscount.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
The EVER_ALIVE insertions must be uniqueness-preserving.

A narrow repair is for `playerSetAliveInGame(..., bRevive=false)` to insert the player
and team into `CIV_EVER_ALIVE` only when the corresponding pointer is not already
present. This preserves the intended fresh never-alive colony behavior while making
recycled identities idempotent.

Equivalent safe options include:
* a dedicated unique-insert helper;
* erase-then-insert for the two EVER_ALIVE sequences;
* rebuilding all AgentIterator sequences when a recycled slot is detected.

Do not simply change the `false` argument to `true`: that would only turn the existing
silent duplication into a debug assertion while release behavior would still insert.
The operation itself must avoid the duplicate.

Because F473/F447 show that recycling multi-member old-team identities has deeper
problems, the broader conservative colony policy can still reject such slots entirely.
F474 nevertheless needs its own invariant if singleton defeated slots remain recyclable.

REGRESSION TEST
---------------
1. Start with a defeated singleton Player X / Team T already represented once in
   `CIV_EVER_ALIVE` player/team caches.
2. Recycle X through human colony creation.
3. Assert immediately that X and T each occur exactly once in the corresponding
   EVER_ALIVE sequence and exactly once in their expected ALIVE sequence.
4. Ensure no team knows `TECH_ROMANTICISM`.
5. Let recycled Team T research Romanticism first.
6. Assert `countKnownTechNumTeams(TECH_ROMANTICISM) == 1` at first acquisition and
   that X receives the free Great Artist.
7. Repeat with save/load before discovery and after discovery.
8. Also test a genuinely never-alive colony slot to ensure normal insertion still
   occurs exactly once.

===============================================================================
C031-WIP198 — QUEUE 004 CVPLAYER.CPP — F475 / KI#798 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

POST-WIP197 COLONY / UWAI ORDERING CLOSURE
------------------------------------------
The immediate F474 aftermath first produced a plausible UWAI ordering concern:
`CvPlayer::initInGame` calls:

    getUWAI().initNewPlayerInGame(getID());

before `splitEmpire` assigns the new player's parent, makes the new team a vassal,
inherits the parent's technologies or transfers colony cities.

The full call chain closes that concern. `initNewPlayerInGame` only clears a shared war
evaluation cache and initializes the new team/player UWAI objects. The substantive new
player reconciliation occurs much later in `splitEmpire` through:

    getUWAI().processNewPlayerInGame(eNewPlayer);

By then parent assignment, inherited techs, vassalization, city transfer, plot-group
updates and free defenders have all happened. `processNewPlayerInGame` performs the
forced new-player cache update and team `turnPre` pass. No independent F475 arises
from the apparent early UWAI initialization.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F475 / KI#798 — MIDGAME PLAYER INITIALIZATION FORGETS OLD GLOBAL NON-RECURRING
TRIGGERS ONCE THEIR SHORT-LIVED EVENT RECORDS EXPIRE, ALLOWING GLOBAL EVENTS TO
BECOME ELIGIBLE A SECOND TIME
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED. This is an inherited BtS/BBAI/K-Mod midgame-player random-event state
initialization defect. It does NOT require recycled player slots: an ordinary colony
created in a genuinely NEVER-ALIVE slot is sufficient.

ROOT
----
Global trigger state has two very different lifetimes in `CvPlayer`:

1. the durable trigger-fired identity in `m_triggersFired`;
2. the particular EventInfo occurrence record in `m_mapEventsOccured`.

For a non-recurring trigger, authoritative future eligibility uses the FIRST state:

    if (!kTrigger.isRecurring())
    {
        if (isTriggerFired(eTrigger))
            return 0;
    }

When a trigger actually fires, `CvPlayer::applyEvent` calls:

    setTriggerFired(*pTriggeredData, true);

before applying the chosen EventInfo. For a GLOBAL trigger,
`CvPlayer::setTriggerFired(..., bOthers=true)` propagates that fired bit to EVERY
player slot:

    if (kTrigger.isGlobal())
    {
        for (int i = 0; i < MAX_CIV_PLAYERS; i++)
        {
            if (i != getID())
                GET_PLAYER((PlayerTypes)i).setTriggerFired(
                        kTriggeredData, false, false);
        }
    }

That loop does not require the destination player to be alive or ever alive. Thus a
never-used future colony slot correctly receives the durable global fired flag at the
time of the original event.

The associated EventInfo occurrence has deliberately SHORT lifetime. In
`CvPlayer::checkExpireEvent`:

    if (!kEvent.isQuest())
        return (GC.getGame().getGameTurn() - kTriggeredData.m_iTurn > 2);

and `CvPlayer::doEvents` then calls `expireEvent` and erases the occurrence from
`m_mapEventsOccured`. This does NOT clear `m_triggersFired`; existing players continue
to remember the non-recurring trigger permanently, as intended.

The defect appears when a new player is initialized in the middle of the game.
`CvPlayer::initInGame` first calls `reset(eID)`, whose reset path clears:

    m_mapEventsOccured.clear();
    ...
    m_triggersFired.clear();

It then explicitly attempts to rebuild already-fired global/team trigger state:

    // Reset all triggers at first, set those whose events have fired in next block
    FOR_EACH_ENUM(EventTrigger)
        resetTriggerFired(eLoopEventTrigger);

    FOR_EACH_ENUM(Event)
    {
        EventTriggeredData const* pEvent = NULL; // Has global trigger fired already?
        for (int i = 0; i < MAX_CIV_PLAYERS; i++)
        {
            if (i == getID())
                continue;

            pEvent = GET_PLAYER((PlayerTypes)i).getEventOccured(eLoopEvent);
            if (pEvent == NULL)
                continue;

            CvEventTriggerInfo& kTrigger = GC.getInfo(pEvent->m_eTrigger);
            if (kTrigger.isGlobal())
            {
                setTriggerFired(*pEvent, false, false);
                break;
            }
            else if (kTrigger.isTeam() && TEAMID((PlayerTypes)i) == getTeam())
            {
                setTriggerFired(*pEvent, false, false);
                break;
            }
        }
        resetEventOccured(eLoopEvent, false);
    }

The comment states the intended contract correctly — preserve global triggers that
have fired already — but the reconstruction source is wrong. It searches the
EPHEMERAL `m_mapEventsOccured` records instead of the DURABLE trigger-fired state.

Therefore:
* during the first two turns after a non-quest event, another player's occurrence
  record can allow `initInGame` to reconstruct the global fired flag;
* once `checkExpireEvent` has expired that record, the same already-fired global
  trigger becomes invisible to `initInGame` even though all existing players still
  have it in `m_triggersFired`;
* the newly initialized player's cleared fired flag remains absent.

This is a direct lifetime mismatch between the state being reconstructed and the state
used as its reconstruction source.

ORDINARY NEVER-ALIVE COLONY REACHABILITY
----------------------------------------
No F447/F473/F474 recycling setup is necessary.

`CvPlayer::getSplitEmpirePlayer` explicitly prefers a slot that has never been alive:

    for (PlayerIter<> itPlayer; itPlayer.hasNext(); ++itPlayer)
    {
        if (!itPlayer->isEverAlive())
        {
            eNewPlayer = itPlayer->getID();
            break;
        }
    }

`splitEmpire` then calls:

    kGame.addPlayer(eNewPlayer, eBestLeader, eBestCiv);

and current `CvGame::addPlayer` deliberately uses the BBAI middle-of-game initializer:

    /* Team init now handled when appropriate in player initInGame.
       Standard player init is written for beginning of game,
       it resets global random events for this player only among other flaws. */
    GET_PLAYER(eNewPlayer).initInGame(eNewPlayer);

So the very routine designed to avoid losing global event state during ordinary colony
creation still loses it whenever the EventInfo occurrence has aged out.

CURRENT-SAS DATA — MANY LIVE GLOBAL NON-RECURRING TRIGGERS
----------------------------------------------------------
This is not a dormant API branch.

A mechanical parse of current SAS `CIV4EventTriggerInfos.xml` finds 116 trigger
entries satisfying all of:

    bGlobal = 1
    bRecurring = 0
    iPercentGamesActive > 0
    iWeight != 0

Many are ordinary positive-weight random events.

For example current SAS `EVENTTRIGGER_FEDERAL_RESERVE` has:

    iPercentGamesActive = 90
    iWeight = 200
    Civic = CIVIC_FREE_MARKET
    iMinTreasury = 1000
    OrPreReq = TECH_CORPORATION
    bRecurring = 0
    bGlobal = 1

and no PythonCanDo gate.

Its two EventInfos are explicitly NON-QUEST:

    EVENT_FEDERAL_RESERVE_1: bQuest = 0, iInflationMod = -10
    EVENT_FEDERAL_RESERVE_2: bQuest = 0, iGold = -200,
                            iInflationMod = -25

So its EventInfo occurrence is guaranteed to become eligible for the ordinary
`> 2 turns` expiration rule while the global non-recurring trigger-fired bit is meant
to persist indefinitely.

Current XML also gives a dramatic 100%-active example:

    EVENTTRIGGER_MARATHON
        iPercentGamesActive = 100
        iWeight = 800
        bRecurring = 0
        bGlobal = 1

whose non-quest `EVENT_MARATHON_1` grants a Golden Age. Its Python trigger conditions
are narrower (first turn of a war with an enemy unit inside the player's territory),
so Federal Reserve is the cleaner arithmetic reproducer; Marathon demonstrates that
the affected live data is not limited to 90%-active entries or small rewards.

DETERMINISTIC CURRENT-SAS CONSEQUENCE — FEDERAL RESERVE WEIGHT BECOMES 200 INSTEAD
OF 0
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Use a game in the normal 90% set where `EVENTTRIGGER_FEDERAL_RESERVE` is active.

1. Player A satisfies Federal Reserve and the trigger fires normally.
2. Because the trigger is global, `setTriggerFired(..., true)` marks it fired on every
   PlayerTypes slot, including slots that have never yet been alive.
3. A chooses either Federal Reserve event. The chosen EventInfo is non-quest.
4. Let more than two turns pass. `doEvents/checkExpireEvent` erases A's
   `m_mapEventsOccured` record. A and all other existing slots still retain the durable
   `EVENTTRIGGER_FEDERAL_RESERVE` entry in `m_triggersFired`.
5. Later an ordinary player releases a valid overseas colony while a never-alive slot
   X remains available. `getSplitEmpirePlayer` deliberately chooses X.
6. `addPlayer -> X.initInGame(X) -> reset(X)` clears X's already-propagated durable
   Federal Reserve fired bit.
7. The `initInGame` reconstruction scan searches other players' EventInfo occurrence
   records. The Federal Reserve occurrence expired in step 4, so X does NOT regain the
   fired bit.
8. The parent can pass `TECH_CORPORATION` to the colony through normal colony tech
   inheritance. Later let X adopt Free Market and accumulate at least 1000 gold.
9. Call the authoritative trigger eligibility weight calculation.

Correct global non-recurring state requires:

    getEventTriggerWeight(EVENTTRIGGER_FEDERAL_RESERVE) == 0

because this trigger already fired once for the game.

Current state instead reaches the XML base weight and returns:

    200

provided its ordinary current conditions are met, because X's
`isTriggerFired(EVENTTRIGGER_FEDERAL_RESERVE)` is false.

That weight mismatch is deterministic. The subsequent random-event selection is of
course stochastic, but the supposedly globally exhausted trigger has been returned to
the live candidate pool.

If selected again, X can obtain a SECOND occurrence of the globally non-recurring
Federal Reserve event and permanently change its inflation modifier by -10, or pay 200
gold for -25. `applyEvent` changes the stored player inflation modifier directly, so
this is gameplay state, not merely an announcement or UI discrepancy.

SAVE/LOAD DOES NOT REPAIR THE NEW PLAYER
-----------------------------------------
`m_triggersFired` itself is serialized explicitly:

    uint iSize = m_triggersFired.size();
    pStream->Write(iSize);
    ...

and read back directly into the vector.

Therefore, once `initInGame` has omitted the old global trigger from colony X, saving
and loading simply serializes/restores that MISSING entry. Loading does not rerun the
midgame global-trigger reconstruction from other players.

This differs usefully from F474, whose malformed AgentIterator cache can be rebuilt by
save/load before the damaging tech discovery. F475's lost per-player fired state is
normal serialized state and survives a reload.

ANCESTRY / INTENT
-----------------
K-Mod 1.46 contains the same middle-of-game trigger reconstruction block: reset every
trigger, iterate EventInfos, query other players' `getEventOccured`, and call
`setTriggerFired` only when an extant occurrence belongs to a global or same-team
trigger. Current AdvCiv/SAS retains that BBAI lineage.

The current `CvGame::addPlayer` comment states why BBAI introduced this special path:
standard beginning-of-game player initialization was unsuitable in midgame because,
among other flaws, it "resets global random events for this player only."

Stock BtS/Civ4CE still follows the older pattern:

    GET_TEAM(eTeam).init(eTeam);
    GET_PLAYER(eNewPlayer).init(eNewPlayer);

so the broader late-player/global-trigger problem originates upstream. BBAI/K-Mod
attempted to repair it with `initInGame`, but reconstructed durable trigger identity
from short-lived occurrence records and therefore only repaired the first two turns
after ordinary non-quest events.

F475 is best classified as an inherited midgame-player event-state defect with an
incomplete BBAI repair, retained by K-Mod -> AdvCiv -> SAS.

DUPLICATE / ALBUM RECONCILIATION
--------------------------------
The album already contains a different event-expiration robustness note: for copied
QUEST records, `checkExpireEvent`'s obsolete-tech branch can inspect the holder's team
rather than the event originator's team. Current XML masks that path because no
EventInfo is both Quest and Global. F475 uses ordinary NON-QUEST events and does not
rely on that asymmetry.

The album also preserves the data-dormant `setEventOccured` team-propagation iterator
inversion. F475 is GLOBAL-trigger state, is live under current XML, and occurs even
when EventInfo records are intentionally local.

F457 / KI#780 is the World News identity leak in global PickPlayer trigger
announcements. It concerns observer visibility of an event that legitimately fires.
F475 instead loses the durable global one-shot gate for a newly initialized player and
can make the trigger eligible to fire again.

F447/F473/F474 concern recycled colonial identities. F475 deliberately reproduces
with a NEVER-ALIVE player slot, so none of those roots is required.

No previous album root covers `initInGame` reconstructing persistent global trigger
state from EventInfo records that normally expire after two turns.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Do not reconstruct durable trigger-fired identity from `m_mapEventsOccured`.

For each EventTriggerType during `initInGame`, derive inheritance from the durable
`isTriggerFired(eTrigger)` state of other players:

* if the trigger is global, preserve it for the new player when any authoritative
  existing player/slot records it as fired;
* if the trigger is team-scoped, preserve it when an appropriate teammate records it
  as fired;
* local trigger-fired history from a recycled old identity must NOT be inherited just
  because that slot once fired it.

A small dedicated helper that records the trigger type without replaying announcements
or Python after-event callbacks would be cleaner than fabricating an old
`EventTriggeredData` merely to call `setTriggerFired`.

An even stronger architecture would keep game-global and team-global one-shot trigger
state at game/team scope instead of duplicating it into each player's vector, but a
narrow `initInGame` repair is sufficient for this root.

REGRESSION TEST
---------------
1. Enable events and choose a setup where `EVENTTRIGGER_FEDERAL_RESERVE` is active.
2. Fire Federal Reserve for Player A and assert every relevant player slot reports
   `isTriggerFired(EVENTTRIGGER_FEDERAL_RESERVE)` true.
3. Advance at least three turns until A no longer has either Federal Reserve EventInfo
   in `m_mapEventsOccured`.
4. Create an ordinary colony in a never-alive Player X slot.
5. Immediately assert X still reports the global Federal Reserve trigger as fired.
6. Give/retain Corporation, adopt Free Market and set X gold >= 1000.
7. Assert `getEventTriggerWeight(EVENTTRIGGER_FEDERAL_RESERVE) == 0`.
8. Save/load after colony creation and repeat the assertion.
9. As a positive control, ensure genuinely local non-recurring triggers from an old
   recycled identity are not inherited into a fresh colony merely because that old
   identity once fired them.
10. Repeat with a current bGlobal=1 / bRecurring=0 100%-active trigger such as Marathon
    to ensure the fix is generic rather than Federal-Reserve-specific.

C031-WIP199 — QUEUE 004 CVPLAYER DEEP RE-AUDIT: POST-F475 EVENT CLOSURE + F476 / KI#799 STATE-RELIGION BUILDING-COMMERCE CACHE INVALIDATION
