POST-F475 IMMEDIATE EVENT-INHERITANCE SIBLING CLOSURE
-----------------------------------------------------
Before leaving the `initInGame` random-event family, the immediate F475 siblings were
reconciled against current SAS data rather than multiplied into artificial roots.

* Current SAS has ZERO `bTeam=1` EventTriggerInfos and ZERO `bTeam=1` EventInfos.
  The analogous team-state reconstruction branch therefore remains dormant under
  shipped data.
* Current SAS EventTriggerInfo XML has ZERO nonempty trigger-level PythonCallback
  entries. Reconstructing a fired trigger through `setTriggerFired` therefore cannot
  currently replay a second trigger callback as a separate live consequence.
* Event countdowns / AdditionalEvents are player-local follow-up state belonging to
  the player that actually received the event. They are not a second game-global
  one-shot identity that a later colony should inherit.

So F475 remains the live durable trigger-state root from this family. F476 was kept
unused while the audit returned to low-semantic-coverage authoritative player state.

F476 / KI#799 — STATE-RELIGION BUILDING-COMMERCE CACHE IS NOT INVALIDATED WHEN THE PLAYER'S STATE RELIGION OR EMPIRE-WIDE BONUS CHANGES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT / CACHED FORMULA
---------------------
`CvCity::getBuildingCommerceByBuilding` includes an empire/player dependency inside the
city's cached building-commerce total:

    if (kBuilding.getReligionType() != NO_RELIGION &&
        kBuilding.getReligionType() == GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).getStateReligion())
    {
        iCommerceRate += GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).
                getStateReligionBuildingCommerce(eCommerce) *
                getNumActiveBuilding(eBuilding);
    }

The result is accumulated by `CvCity::updateBuildingCommerce(eCommerce)` into:

    m_aiBuildingCommerce[eCommerce]

and the ordinary commerce-rate path subsequently reads that cached value through
`getBuildingCommerce(eCommerce)`.

Two different player-level inputs can therefore change the correct cached value in
EVERY city without changing the city's own buildings:

1. `CvPlayer::getStateReligion()` — which religion's buildings qualify;
2. `CvPlayer::getStateReligionBuildingCommerce(eCommerce)` — how much qualifying
   commerce each active state-religion building receives.

Current code fails to invalidate/recompute `m_aiBuildingCommerce` for BOTH transitions.

MISSING INVALIDATION 1 — STATE RELIGION CHANGES
-----------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::setLastStateReligion` changes the effective player religion and refreshes:

    updateMaintenance();
    updateReligionHappiness();
    updateReligionCommerce();

but does NOT call `updateBuildingCommerce()`.

`updateReligionCommerce()` is a different cache. Its city implementation recomputes
`m_aiReligionCommerce` from ReligionInfo state/holy-city commerce and then calls
`updateCommerce`; it never recomputes `m_aiBuildingCommerce`.

Therefore a temple/monastery/etc. of the OLD state religion can continue contributing
an empire-wide state-religion-building bonus from the stale building cache, while a
religious building of the NEW state religion can remain missing that bonus.

MISSING INVALIDATION 1B — CIVICS CHANGE THE EFFECTIVE STATE RELIGION WITHOUT CHANGING `m_eLastStateReligion`
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`getStateReligion()` is defined as:

    return (isStateReligion() ? getLastStateReligion() : NO_RELIGION);

so the same cached building formula also changes when a civic transition toggles
whether the player is allowed to have a state religion.

`CvPlayer::setCivics` even snapshots the old effective religion before changing the
civic and logs the old/new effective state religion afterward. Its `processCivics`
path calls:

    changeStateReligionCount(civic.isStateReligion() ? iChange : 0);

`changeStateReligionCount` refreshes maintenance, religion happiness and religion
commerce, but — like `setLastStateReligion` — never calls `updateBuildingCommerce`.

Current SAS Religion civics make this live: Prehistoric Religion, Organized Religion,
Pacifism and Theocracy have `bStateReligion=1`, while Free Religion has
`bStateReligion=0`. A zero-anarchy switch into or out of Free Religion therefore changes
`getStateReligion()` immediately while leaving the religious-building commerce cache on
the old effective state.

This is the same F476 cache invariant, not a separate F477: the external input to
`getBuildingCommerceByBuilding` is the player's EFFECTIVE state religion, and both
`setLastStateReligion` and `changeStateReligionCount` are producers of that input.

MISSING INVALIDATION 2 — EMPIRE-WIDE BONUS AMOUNT CHANGES
---------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::processBuilding` changes the player-wide source through:

    changeStateReligionBuildingCommerce(c,
        kBuilding.getStateReligionCommerce(c) * iChange);

but the mutator only does:

    m_aiStateReligionBuildingCommerce.add(eCommerce, iChange);
    updateCommerce(eCommerce);

`CvPlayer::updateCommerce(eCommerce)` merely calls `CvCity::updateCommerce` for every
city. That recomputes the final rate from the city's EXISTING cached
`m_aiBuildingCommerce`; it does not call `CvCity::updateBuildingCommerce`.

When a city itself gains/loses a building, `CvCity::processBuilding` eventually calls:

    updateBuildingCommerce();

at the end of that ONE city's processing. This repairs the producing/acquired city,
but not the owner's other cities whose religious buildings are affected by the new
player-wide bonus.

The team and game `processBuilding` hooks do not repair this: they only process their
own vote/team-wide building effects and do not perform an empire-wide building-commerce
recount.

WHY ORDINARY WONDER COMPLETION ALONE IS NOT THE BEST REPRO
----------------------------------------------------------
There is an important self-heal control that prevents overstatement.

`CvGame::setGameTurn` calls:

    updateBuildingCommerce();

which loops all alive players and all their cities. Thus a stale building-commerce
cache is globally rebuilt at each game-turn boundary.

Also, in sequential turns `CvPlayer::doTurn` books gold/research BEFORE city
`doTurn` / `doProduction`. Therefore simply completing Spiral Minaret or Sankore at
end-of-turn normally creates a transient stale state after that turn's economy has
already been booked, and the next global turn-boundary refresh can repair it before the
owner's next normal economic turn.

That closure is why F476 is NOT based merely on "build wonder in City A, City B stale."

CURRENT LIVE REPRO 1 — ZERO-ANARCHY STATE-RELIGION CONVERSION BOOKS WRONG GOLD
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The state-religion transition happens at a different and gameplay-relevant time.

Current turn handling for a normal human sequential turn is:

* player is active and may issue a religion conversion during the active turn;
* on ending the turn, `CvPlayer::setTurnActive(false, true)` calls `CvPlayer::doTurn()`;
* `CvPlayer::doTurn()` performs:

      AI_assignWorkingPlots();
      verifyGoldCommercePercent();
      doGold();
      doResearch();
      doEspionagePoints();
      FOR_EACH_CITY ... city->doTurn();

* only the later game-round transition reaches `CvGame::setGameTurn` and its global
  `updateBuildingCommerce()` self-heal.

Current SAS has straightforward zero-anarchy conversion routes:

* `TRAIT_SPIRITUAL` has `<iMaxAnarchy>0</iMaxAnarchy>`, and
  `getReligionAnarchyLength()` immediately returns 0 when `getMaxAnarchyTurns()==0`;
* independently, `getReligionAnarchyLength()` returns 0 during a Golden Age.

A compact current-SAS reproduction is therefore:

1. Own `BUILDING_SPIRAL_MINARET`.
2. Use Hinduism as the current state religion.
3. Have one active `BUILDING_HINDU_TEMPLE` in an ordinary city. Current XML gives that
   building `ReligionType=RELIGION_HINDUISM` and `ObsoleteTech=NONE`.
4. Have Judaism present somewhere so conversion to Judaism is legal, but do not need a
   Jewish temple for the repro.
5. Be Spiritual or be in a Golden Age, so the conversion creates zero anarchy.
6. During the player's active turn, convert from Hinduism to Judaism.
7. `setLastStateReligion(JUDAISM)` changes the state religion but does not rebuild city
   building commerce. The Hindu Temple's cached building-commerce contribution still
   includes Spiral Minaret's old +2 Gold bonus.
8. End the turn. Before any game-turn-boundary building-commerce rebuild,
   `CvPlayer::doTurn -> doGold -> calculateGoldRate` consumes the cached player/city
   commerce rate.

With no other Gold-rate modifiers in the test city, the player is credited 2 Gold that
should have disappeared when Hinduism stopped being the state religion. More old-state
religion buildings or city Gold modifiers can enlarge the error.

The next turn-boundary recount repairs the CACHE, but it does not subtract the Gold
already booked in step 8. The one-turn economic error is therefore a permanent gameplay
consequence, not merely a stale tooltip.

The same root can invert direction: buildings of the new state religion remain missing
the bonus until the recount. Current Sankore (+3 Research) and Natya Shastra (+2
Culture) allow analogous research/culture manifestations.

CURRENT LIVE REPRO 1B — ZERO-ANARCHY SWITCH TO FREE RELIGION LEAVES OLD STATE-RELIGION BUILDING BONUSES ACTIVE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The civic producer gives an equally direct current path without changing
`m_eLastStateReligion` at all.

1. Own Spiral Minaret and an active building of the remembered state religion.
2. Run any current `bStateReligion=1` Religion civic.
3. During a Spiritual/Golden-Age zero-anarchy window, switch the Religion civic to
   current `CIVIC_FREE_RELIGION` (`bStateReligion=0`).
4. `processCivics -> changeStateReligionCount(-1)` makes `getStateReligion()` become
   `NO_RELIGION`, but only refreshes maintenance/religion-happiness/religion-commerce.
5. The old religious building remains in `m_aiBuildingCommerce` with the Spiral bonus.
6. Ending the turn reaches `doGold()` before the next game-turn-wide recount and books
   the stale Gold exactly as in repro 1.

The reverse transition can leave the remembered religion's buildings missing the bonus
until the next recount.

CURRENT LIVE REPRO 2 — CAPTURING SPIRAL MINARET MID-TURN MISSES ITS BONUS IN OTHER CITIES
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The bonus-AMOUNT mutator itself also has an ordinary mid-turn producer.

Current `BUILDING_SPIRAL_MINARET` has:

    bNeverCapture = 0
    iConquestProb = 100
    StateReligionCommerces = [2]

and `CommerceTypes` order begins:

    COMMERCE_GOLD,
    COMMERCE_RESEARCH,
    COMMERCE_CULTURE,
    COMMERCE_ESPIONAGE

so `[2]` is +2 Gold per active building of the player's state religion.

During `CvPlayer::acquireCity`, surviving captured buildings are restored with
`CvCity::setNumRealBuildingTimed`. That immediately calls `CvCity::processBuilding`,
which reaches the new owner's `CvPlayer::processBuilding` and therefore
`changeStateReligionBuildingCommerce(+2)`.

Suppose the capturing player already has a state-religion temple in another city.
Capturing the Spiral Minaret city during the active military phase changes the correct
player-wide temple bonus immediately, but the mutator performs only `updateCommerce`.
The captured city later refreshes its OWN building-commerce cache at the end of its
building processing; the other city does not.

When the human ends the same turn, `doGold()` therefore books Gold before the next
`setGameTurn` global refresh, and the other city's temple can miss the newly acquired
+2 Gold for that turn.

Current Sankore and Natya Shastra are likewise fully capturable (`bNeverCapture=0`,
`iConquestProb=100`) and exercise the same cache dependency for Research/Culture.

CURRENT SAS DATA
----------------
Current `CIV4BuildingInfos.xml` has three live nonzero
`StateReligionCommerces` producers:

    BUILDING_SPIRAL_MINARET   [2]       -> +2 Gold
    BUILDING_SANKORE          [0,3]     -> +3 Research
    BUILDING_NATYA_SHASTRA    [0,0,2]   -> +2 Culture

All three have `ObsoleteTech=NONE` in current SAS.

Religious buildings are likewise live ordinary data. For example
`BUILDING_HINDU_TEMPLE` has:

    ReligionType   = RELIGION_HINDUISM
    PrereqReligion = RELIGION_HINDUISM
    ObsoleteTech   = NONE

so the cached formula has direct current producers/consumers without hypothetical XML.

CACHE-CONTROL COMPARISON INSIDE CURRENT CODE
--------------------------------------------
The omission is especially persuasive because neighboring dependencies of the SAME
`getBuildingCommerceByBuilding` formula already trigger the stronger refresh.

Global religion/corporation building commerce depends on world religion/corporation
counts. Current player count mutators call:

    CvGame::updateBuildingCommerce();

which deliberately recomputes every alive player's city cache.

City-specific `setBuildingCommerceChange` calls:

    updateBuildingCommerce(eCommerce);

when an active building is affected.

So the codebase already treats this formula as a derived cache requiring explicit
recomputation when its external inputs change. The state-religion identity and
StateReligionCommerce amount are the missed inputs.

SERIALIZATION / SELF-HEAL CHARACTERIZATION
-------------------------------------------
`m_aiBuildingCommerce` is serialized directly in `CvCity::read/write`; however F476
does not need save/load persistence to clear the gameplay threshold.

The global `CvGame::setGameTurn -> updateBuildingCommerce` call gives a normal eventual
self-heal. The important point is that the zero-anarchy conversion and captured-wonder
paths can occur AFTER the current game-turn refresh and BEFORE that player's
`doGold`/`doResearch` / city culture processing. The stale value can therefore be
CONSUMED and booked before the self-heal. Rebuilding the cache on the following turn
cannot refund/reverse that already-applied output.

ANCESTRY
--------
This is inherited engine behavior rather than a SAS-created regression.

Current base AdvCiv 1.14 has the same
`changeStateReligionBuildingCommerce -> updateCommerce` implementation and the same
state-religion-dependent building-commerce formula.

K-Mod 1.46 likewise changes `m_aiStateReligionBuildingCommerce` and calls only
`updateCommerce(eIndex)`, while `setLastStateReligion` refreshes maintenance, religion
happiness and religion commerce but not building commerce.

Civ4CE/stock-lineage code contains the same building-commerce dependency and the same
`changeStateReligionBuildingCommerce -> updateCommerce` pattern. Thus the missing
cache invalidation predates AdvCiv/SAS and survives through the upstream lineage.

DUPLICATE / ALBUM CHECK
-----------------------
The reconciled album contains no previous root for:

* `changeStateReligionBuildingCommerce`;
* `m_aiBuildingCommerce` invalidation from state-religion identity;
* Spiral Minaret / Sankore state-religion-building bonuses staying on the wrong
  religious buildings;
* mid-turn wonder acquisition leaving other cities' state-religion building commerce
  stale.

Earlier `setLastStateReligion` mentions concern conversion legality, diplomacy/message
coordinates and other religion-state behavior, not this city building-commerce cache.

The earlier state-religion BUILDING HAPPINESS audit is also a different derived value
and had its own refresh chain. F476 specifically concerns cached building COMMERCE.

F445 and other rank/cache findings concern different city/player caches and different
invalidators. F476 has its own current data and direct economic consumer.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Both external inputs to the cached formula need explicit building-commerce
recomputation.

1. After changing `m_eLastStateReligion` in `setLastStateReligion`, call player-wide
   `updateBuildingCommerce()` (after the new religion is stored). This makes every
   city's religious-building qualification match the new state religion immediately.

2. When `changeStateReligionCount` crosses a boundary that changes the effective
   `getStateReligion()` (most notably state-religion civic <-> Free Religion), also
   rebuild player building commerce. Calling the refresh for every raw +1/-1 during
   civic processing is safe but can be avoided by comparing old/new effective state
   religion once in `setCivics` and refreshing only if it changed.

3. In `changeStateReligionBuildingCommerce(eCommerce, iChange)`, recompute building
   commerce for every city for that commerce type rather than merely calling
   `updateCommerce(eCommerce)`. A narrow per-commerce player helper would avoid
   recomputing unrelated commerce types; the existing full `updateBuildingCommerce()`
   is the simplest conservative repair if this rare transition does not warrant a new
   overload.

Do not remove the existing turn-boundary global recount; it also services time-based
building-commerce dependencies such as delayed commerce doubling and remains a useful
safety rebuild.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Religion-switch test:

1. Own Spiral Minaret and one Hindu Temple; have Judaism available as a legal target.
2. Ensure zero religion anarchy (Spiritual or Golden Age).
3. Populate/verify the Hindu Temple's building-commerce cache while Hinduism is state
   religion.
4. Convert to Judaism during the active turn.
5. Immediately assert the city's Gold building commerce has lost the +2 Spiral bonus.
6. End turn and verify `doGold` does not credit the stale +2.
7. Add a Jewish religious building as a positive-control variant and verify the bonus
   moves to it immediately.

B. Civic effective-religion test:

1. Own Spiral Minaret and a building of the remembered state religion.
2. In a zero-anarchy window, switch from a current `bStateReligion=1` Religion civic
   to `CIVIC_FREE_RELIGION`.
3. Assert the old religious building immediately loses the state-religion building
   bonus and that end-turn Gold does not book it.
4. Switch back in another zero-anarchy window and verify the remembered religion's
   buildings immediately regain the bonus.

C. Captured-wonder test:

1. Capturer has a state religion and a matching temple in City B.
2. Enemy city contains Spiral Minaret.
3. Capture that city during the capturer's active turn; current XML guarantees the
   wonder is capturable at 100% conquest probability.
4. Immediately assert City B's building-commerce cache gains +2 Gold.
5. End turn and verify the bonus is included in that turn's booked Gold.
6. Repeat with Sankore / Research to ensure the fix is commerce-type generic.

D. Turn-boundary control:

After deliberately producing the old stale state in an unpatched build, verify that
`CvGame::setGameTurn` does repair the cache on the next turn. This preserves the
important distinction between F476's consumed one-turn error and an indefinitely stale
cache.

POST-WIP199 CURSOR RECONCILIATION
---------------------------------
The immediate continuation was the recycled-player cleanup path, specifically the
BETTER_BTS_AI_MOD `CvPlayer::resetPlotAndCityData()` routine used by
`CvGame::addPlayer -> CvPlayer::initInGame` when a mid-game colony reuses a dead
PlayerTypes slot.

The audit first rechecked the intended cleanup surface. Current SAS still carries the
12/30/08 BBAI routine with the explicit contract/comment:

    Reset all data for this player stored in plot and city objects

For every plot it clears:

    plot culture indexed by recycled player
    found value indexed by recycled player

and, for every city, it clears:

    city culture indexed by recycled player
    revolt count indexed by recycled player
    EverOwned indexed by recycled player
    TradeRoute indexed by recycled player

That is useful cleanup, but it only handles fields whose KEY is the recycled
PlayerTypes. It does not scrub persistent city/plot fields whose STORED VALUE is that
PlayerTypes identity.

This difference matters because a recycled player slot does not receive a generation
number or historical identity token. If extinct old player X and unrelated new colony
Z use the same numeric PlayerTypes slot, any untouched historical field containing X
now compares equal to Z.

F477 / KI#800 — RECYCLED DEAD PLAYER SLOTS ALIAS PERSISTENT HISTORICAL PlayerTypes
                  REFERENCES TO THE NEW COLONY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: CONFIRMED.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayer::getSplitEmpirePlayer` first tries a never-alive player slot. If none exists,
current AdvCiv-SAS deliberately allows a HUMAN splitter to reuse an `EVER_ALIVE` dead
player:

    /* <kekm.24> Reusing a defeated player might not work correctly. advc:
       Allow human players to try it, but don't let the AI wreck the game somehow. */
    ...
    if (!itPlayer->isAlive())
        eNewPlayer = itPlayer->getID();

The reuse path changes the slot's leader/civilization and calls
`CvGame::addPlayer -> CvPlayer::initInGame -> resetPlotAndCityData`.

However, map/city objects can contain bare PlayerTypes VALUES that refer to the old
historical identity. Important current examples include:

    CvCity::m_eOriginalOwner
    CvCity::m_ePreviousOwner
    CvCity::m_aeBuildingOriginalOwner[BuildingTypes]
    CvPlot::m_aiRevealedOwner[TeamTypes]

`resetPlotAndCityData()` does not search for values equal to the recycled slot and does
not clear/remap them. The old numeric identity therefore aliases the new colony.

This root is independent of the immediately preceding recycled-player findings. A dead
SINGLETON old team is sufficient here, so F447's live-team skip and F473's dead
multi-member-team reset failure need not occur. The concrete consequences below do not
need F474's AgentIterator duplicate, F475's event reconstruction error, or F476's
building-commerce invalidation problem.

PRIMARY CURRENT-SAS REPRO A — CAPTURED GREAT LIBRARY BECOMES "ORIGINAL" TO AN
UNRELATED RECYCLED COLONY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current city building commerce contains this authoritative gate:

    if (kBuilding.isCommerceChangeOriginalOwner(eCommerce) &&
        getBuildingOriginalOwner(eBuilding) != getOwner())
    {
        return 0;
    }

Building original owner is stored as a serialized PlayerTypes in
`m_aeBuildingOriginalOwner`.

`CvPlayer::acquireCity` explicitly copies each surviving building's original owner from
the old city and restores it to the new city through `setNumRealBuildingTimed`. So
capture intentionally preserves the historical builder identity.

Current SAS XML gives this path abundant live data. 51 BuildingInfos have a nonzero
`CommerceChangeOriginalOwners` entry; 50 of those are fully capturable with
`iConquestProb=100` and `bNeverCapture=0`.

A particularly simple stable example is:

    BUILDING_GREAT_LIBRARY
    CommerceChangeOriginalOwners = [0, 0, 1]
    ObsoleteSafeCommerceChanges = [0, 0, 6]
    iConquestProb = 100
    bNeverCapture = 0
    ObsoleteTech = NONE

Commerce order is Gold, Research, Culture, Espionage, so the Great Library has +6
Culture that is granted only when the city's current owner equals the building's
stored original-owner PlayerTypes.

Supported repro:

1. Old player X builds the Great Library.
2. Player Y captures that city. The building survives deterministically under current
   XML and retains `BuildingOriginalOwner = X`.
3. X is later fully eliminated while Y still owns the Great Library city.
4. Exhaust all never-alive player slots, then have a human player split a colony.
   `getSplitEmpirePlayer` may recycle dead X's PlayerTypes slot into unrelated new
   civilization Z. Use a dead singleton old team so F447/F473 are not prerequisites.
5. BBAI `resetPlotAndCityData()` clears X-indexed culture/revolt/etc., but does not
   touch Y's city's stored `BuildingOriginalOwner = X`.
6. Z later captures the Great Library city from Y. `acquireCity` again preserves the
   building original-owner value.
7. Numerically, `getBuildingOriginalOwner(GREAT_LIBRARY) == getOwner()` now succeeds,
   because both are the recycled X/Z PlayerTypes slot.
8. Z therefore receives the Great Library's +6 Culture as though Z had historically
   built it, despite being a completely different civilization created after X's
   extinction.

The bad value is serialized through `m_aeBuildingOriginalOwner.read/write`, so save/load
does not distinguish old X from new Z or self-heal the alias.

PRIMARY CURRENT-SAS REPRO B — STALE CITY ORIGINAL OWNER CAN DRIVE NEW COLONY'S
`CitiesLost` NEGATIVE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvCity::m_eOriginalOwner` is another serialized PlayerTypes value intentionally
preserved across capture. `CvPlayer::acquireCity` restores it into the replacement city
with:

    kNewCity.setOriginalOwner(eOriginalOwner);

The city-loss bookkeeping then contains:

    if (pOldCity->getOriginalOwner() == pOldCity->getOwner())
        GET_PLAYER(pOldCity->getOriginalOwner()).changeCitiesLost(1);
    else if (pOldCity->getOriginalOwner() == getID())
        GET_PLAYER(pOldCity->getOriginalOwner()).changeCitiesLost(-1);

Player reset correctly sets the new/recycled player's `m_iCitiesLost = 0`.
`changeCitiesLost` simply adds its delta; it has no generation check, clamp or
historical-owner validation.

Supported repro:

1. Old X founds City C.
2. Y captures C, preserving `OriginalOwner = X`.
3. X is fully eliminated.
4. A later human colony Z reuses X's dead PlayerTypes slot.
5. Z starts with `CitiesLost = 0`, but City C still stores original owner X.
6. Z captures C from Y.
7. The second `acquireCity` branch sees the stale numeric X value as equal to new Z's
   `getID()` and executes `changeCitiesLost(-1)`.
8. Z now has `CitiesLost = -1` despite never having lost a city.

This counter is serialized directly. It is also authoritative gameplay state when Max
City Elimination is enabled:

    getCitiesLost() >= getMaxCityElimination()

can eliminate a player. Starting Z at -1 means it can survive one additional qualifying
loss compared with the configured limit once it later founds and loses its own cities.

SAME-ROOT SUPPORTING MANIFESTATIONS
-----------------------------------
A. `CvCity::m_ePreviousOwner`

`m_ePreviousOwner` is serialized and is not scrubbed by player-slot recycling.
Current `CvCity::canCultureFlip` uses it under the visible/supported
`GAMEOPTION_NO_FLIPPING_AFTER_CONQUEST` rule:

    getPreviousOwner() == NO_PLAYER ||
    TEAMID(getPreviousOwner()) != TEAMID(eToPlayer)

A city directly captured from extinct X can therefore later treat unrelated recycled
Z as its previous owner solely because Z reused X's PlayerTypes slot. The AI city-trade
denial code also tests `kCity.getPreviousOwner() == eToPlayer`, so the alias is not
merely historical UI metadata.

B. `CvPlot::m_aiRevealedOwner[TeamTypes]`

This serialized fog-of-war memory stores a PlayerTypes VALUE. Team-side recycled-player
cleanup clears only the row for the recycled TEAM:

    kPlot.setRevealedOwner(getID(), NO_PLAYER);

It does not scan other observers' stored revealed-owner values for the extinct player.
Therefore another team O can have a fogged plot whose last-seen owner is old X. After
X's slot becomes Z, that unchanged numeric value resolves through `GET_PLAYER` to Z.

Current plot hover code does exactly that when a revealed tile is not currently
visible:

    CvPlayer const& kRevealOwner = GET_PLAYER(eRevealedOwner);
    ... kRevealOwner.getCivilizationDescription()

and minimap coloring likewise resolves the remembered owner through
`GET_PLAYER(getRevealedOwner(...)).getKnownPlayerColor()`.

Thus old fog memory can spontaneously relabel extinct X's observed territory with the
new colony Z's identity/color. Multiple AI revealed-owner consumers also receive the
same aliased identity.

These are manifestations of the same missing historical-ID sanitization, not separate
F numbers.

ANCESTRY / WHY THE ROOT EXISTS
------------------------------
Stock BtS/Civ4CE already supports recycling a dead PlayerTypes slot when no never-alive
slot remains in `getSplitEmpirePlayer`. Stock `CvGame::addPlayer` reinitializes the
selected team/player but bare historical PlayerTypes values in other cities/plots have
no generation mechanism.

The 12/30/08 BETTER_BTS_AI change introduced `resetPlotAndCityData()` as an explicit
mid-game recycled-player cleanup. K-Mod 1.46 still has the same field list and comment;
AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain it.

That cleanup repairs per-player-indexed state but never became a comprehensive scrub of
PlayerTypes-valued historical references. AdvCiv's own `<kekm.24>` comment now warns
that reusing a defeated player "might not work correctly" and restricts the fallback
to human splitters, but the supported human path remains live.

DUPLICATE / ALBUM CHECK
-----------------------
The reconciled album through WIP199 contains no prior root for:

* `CommerceChangeOriginalOwners` aliasing after PlayerTypes reuse;
* building original-owner IDs becoming a new colony;
* `m_eOriginalOwner` decrementing the recycled colony's `CitiesLost` counter;
* `m_ePreviousOwner` or other observers' `m_aiRevealedOwner` changing semantic
  identity after dead-slot reuse.

F447 is different: a dead PLAYER on a still-alive team can bypass `addPlayer` entirely.
F473 is different: a recycled player on a fully dead MULTI-MEMBER old team enters
`initInGame`, but the team reset is skipped due to dead assigned teammates.
F474 is a duplicate AgentIterator EVER_ALIVE insertion.
F475 is lost global trigger-fired inheritance.
F476 is state-religion building-commerce cache invalidation.

F477 can be reproduced with a dead singleton old team and therefore does not depend on
any of those roots.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
The safest fix is architectural rather than an ever-growing scrub list:

1. Do not recycle an `EVER_ALIVE` PlayerTypes slot for a new civilization identity.
   If no never-alive slot exists, return `NO_PLAYER` from the fallback instead of
   reusing a defeated player.

This avoids generation-alias problems in every present and future PlayerTypes-valued
historical reference, including structures outside CvPlayer's 2008 cleanup inventory.

If dead-slot reuse must remain supported, then the engine needs a comprehensive
sanitization/remapping pass BEFORE the slot is given the new identity. At minimum audit
and clear/remap every persistent external value equal to the recycled PlayerTypes,
including:

    city original owner
    city previous owner
    building original owner for every building
    every team's plot revealed-owner memory

and then audit other derived/persistent map state such as second-owner and plot-group
references. Because PlayerTypes has no generation tag, adding only the four currently
proven cases risks leaving another identity alias behind.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Great Library identity test

1. X builds Great Library; Y captures it.
2. Eliminate X.
3. Exhaust never-alive slots; human colony creation attempts to recycle X.
4. Under the preferred fix, X must not be reused at all.
5. If recycle support is retained, let new Z reuse X and later capture the Great
   Library city.
6. Assert `getBuildingOriginalOwner(GREAT_LIBRARY)` does not become semantically Z and
   that Z receives 0 original-owner-only Great Library Culture rather than +6.

B. CitiesLost test

1. X founds C; Y captures C; eliminate X.
2. Recycle X into new Z if recycle support remains.
3. Assert Z starts at `CitiesLost == 0`.
4. Z captures C from Y.
5. Assert Z remains at `CitiesLost == 0`, never -1.
6. Repeat with Max City Elimination N and verify Z gets exactly N qualifying future
   losses, not N+1.

C. PreviousOwner control

With No City Flipping after Conquest enabled, retain a city whose previous owner was old
X, recycle X into unrelated Z, and assert Z is not treated as that city's historical
previous owner for flip/trade-denial logic.

D. RevealedOwner control

Let observer O reveal an X-owned plot, lose current visibility, eliminate X, then
recycle X into Z. Assert O's old fog memory does not display/AI-resolve that plot as Z.

IMMEDIATE F477 SIBLING RECONCILIATION
-------------------------------------
The first post-WIP200 pass stayed inside the BBAI recycled-player cleanup family rather
than immediately returning to unrelated CvPlayer helpers.

`m_eSecondOwner` remains worth including in the comprehensive "do not recycle identity"
audit because `resetPlotAndCityData()` clears recycled-player plot culture with
`bUpdate=false`, but the strongest second-owner gameplay consumers are primarily tied
to AdvCiv's `OWN_EXCLUSIVE_RADIUS` system (recommended/default current value 0). No
independent F478 was spent on that field.

`m_aiPlayerCityRadiusCount` and `m_aaiCultureRangeCities` are derived player-keyed plot
counts whose ordinary city kill/acquisition/culture-level hooks explicitly decrement
and increment them. The pass did not establish an independent recycled-slot failure in
those counters.

The remaining `m_aiPlotGroup[PlayerTypes]` field did survive as a different root.

F478 / KI#801 — RECYCLED PLAYER RETAINS PER-PLOT PLOT-GROUP IDS; NEW FREE-LIST IDS
                  CAN REBIND OLD PLOTS INTO THE COLONY'S NEW TRADE NETWORK
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: CONFIRMED.

ROOT
----
Each plot stores a per-player plot-group ID:

    ArrayEnumMap<PlayerTypes,int,...> m_aiPlotGroup;

and resolves it dynamically through the CURRENT player's free-list:

    return GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).getPlotGroup(m_aiPlotGroup.get(ePlayer));

`CvPlayer::resetPlotAndCityData()` does not clear this field.

When a recycled player is reset, `CvPlayer::uninit()` destroys the player's
`m_plotGroups` free-list:

    m_plotGroups.uninit();

but no corresponding pass invalidates the IDs already stored in every `CvPlot`.
Those integers therefore survive after the old objects they named have been destroyed.

This would be less dangerous if new plot-group object IDs could never equal old ones,
but the current free-list deliberately restarts its ID sequence on a fresh init:

    m_iCurrentID = FLTA_MAX_BUCKETS;
    ...
    pData->setID(m_iCurrentID + iIndex);

K-Mod's free-list has the same reset/reuse behavior. Thus the new colony's first,
second, ... plot groups can receive exactly the same full IDs as the extinct player's
first, second, ... groups.

DEFEAT ORDER MAKES STALE MAP-SIDE IDS REACHABLE
-----------------------------------------------
Current `CvPlayer::setAlive(false)` sets:

    m_bAlive = false;

BEFORE it runs the later dead-player `killCities()` cleanup.

`killCities()` kills each city with `bUpdatePlotGroups=false` and then calls:

    GC.getGame().updatePlotGroups();

but `CvGame::updatePlotGroups()` iterates only `PlayerIter<ALIVE>`. The just-defeated
player is already absent, so this global pass does not recalculate or clear that
player's map-side plot-group mappings.

A particularly deterministic supported setup is Max City Elimination. If X reaches the
configured city-loss limit while it still owns additional cities/network plots,
`verifyAlive()` kills X immediately. The remaining cities are then removed only after X
has become non-alive, guaranteeing that the final global plot-group rebuild excludes X.
This avoids relying on a civ that naturally reached zero cities having any residual
network.

RECYCLING / ID REBINDING
------------------------
Later, with no never-alive slot available, a human splitter can recycle dead X into
colony Z through the already-supported `getSplitEmpirePlayer` fallback.

`initInGame -> reset` destroys X's `m_plotGroups` objects, but BBAI's map/city reset does
not invalidate `CvPlot::m_aiPlotGroup[X]`.

For a singleton old team, the new team reset also clears the new team's revealed map.
The initial `setAlive(true) -> updatePlotGroups()` therefore cannot normally rebuild a
real network yet. During `splitEmpire`, the parent then supplies the colony's map
knowledge and transfers cities/plots; the final:

    kGame.updatePlotGroups();

constructs the new colony's plot groups from scratch.

The first new group again receives the same first free-list ID as old X's first group.
Any old plot that still stores that numeric ID now makes:

    getPlotGroup(Z)

return Z's newly allocated group object, even though the plot was never inserted in that
object's plot list and can be geographically disconnected.

WHY THE FINAL `updatePlotGroups` DOES NOT GUARANTEE REPAIR
---------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::updatePlotGroups()` first recalculates the NEW groups' own internal plot
lists, then walks every map plot with:

    updatePlotGroup(getID(), false, false);

The second parameter is `bRecalculate=false`.

`CvPlot::updatePlotGroup` begins by resolving the map-side stored ID. If the stale ID
has now rebound to a valid new group, `pPlotGroup != NULL`; because `bRecalculate` is
false, the function SKIPS the connectivity/membership validation branch that would
remove a disconnected plot from that group. A non-network plot can even return later
without invalidating the stale ID.

So the safety rebuild can preserve the rebinding instead of repairing it.

CURRENT GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCE — FALSE TRADE NETWORK / RESOURCE TRADE
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Current `CvPlot::isConnectedTo(CvCity const&)` treats equal per-player plot-group IDs as
physical connectivity:

    isSamePlotGroup(kCity.getPlot(), getOwner()) ||
    isSamePlotGroup(kCity.getPlot(), kCity.getOwner())

and `CvPlayer::canTradeNetworkWith` uses those city connections authoritatively.
Resource trade availability then directly returns:

    case TRADE_RESOURCES: return canTradeNetworkWith(eWhoTo);

Ongoing resource deals likewise call `canTradeNetworkWith` from `CvDeal::verify`.

Deterministic supported repro construction:

1. Enable Max City Elimination = 1.
2. Old player X has more than one city and a valid first plot group G0. Arrange that
   future colony-parent P's capital is part of X's G0 trade network (e.g. normal
   revealed/peaceful connected trade network).
3. X loses one qualifying city. `CitiesLost` reaches 1, `verifyAlive()` eliminates X
   while X still has other cities/network state.
4. Because `m_bAlive` is already false when those remaining cities are killed, the
   final `CvGame::updatePlotGroups()` excludes X. P's capital retains its stored
   `m_aiPlotGroup[X] = G0`.
5. Exhaust never-alive slots. Later human P splits a geographically disconnected
   colony and `getSplitEmpirePlayer` recycles X into new player Z.
6. X's old plot-group objects are destroyed. The old map-side G0 integer on P's capital
   is not cleared.
7. Arrange map/index/trade-network layout so Z's actual colony network is the first new
   plot group created by the final rebuild. Fresh free-list initialization assigns it
   the same G0 ID.
8. When the later map walk reaches P's physically disconnected capital, its stale
   `m_aiPlotGroup[Z] = G0` now resolves to Z's real colony group. With
   `bRecalculate=false`, the false membership is not removed.
9. `Z.canTradeNetworkWith(P)` tests Z's capital against P's cities. The P capital and Z
   capital now compare equal under Z's plot-group mapping, so the function can return
   true despite there being no physical trade connection.
10. `canPossiblyTradeItem(..., TRADE_RESOURCES)` therefore permits resource trade that
    should be unavailable; `CvDeal::verify` can continue accepting the same false
    network afterward.

The geographical disconnection can be made explicit in a supported scenario (separate
route/river networks with no connecting network terrain/route and no applicable water
trade connection). P and Z are parent/vassal, so contact/relationship ambiguity is not
needed for the repro.

SERIALIZATION / STABILITY
-------------------------
`CvPlot::m_aiPlotGroup` is serialized directly in `CvPlot::read/write`.

The numbered issue does not depend on saving during the narrow reset window: once the
stale ID has rebound to a valid new Z plot-group ID, ordinary `getPlotGroup` calls
cannot distinguish it from a legitimate mapping. The standard final
`updatePlotGroups()` itself can preserve it for the reason above.

A later event that forces the specific plot through a true `bRecalculate=true`
connectivity check can repair that mapping, but there is no guarantee of such a change
before resource-trade/network consumers use the false connection.

ANCESTRY
--------
The key ingredients predate SAS:

* K-Mod's BBAI `resetPlotAndCityData()` has the same field list and does not clear
  `m_aiPlotGroup`.
* K-Mod's `FFreeListTrashArray::init` also resets `m_iCurrentID` to
  `FLTA_MAX_BUCKETS`, so dead-player object IDs are reusable after a fresh free-list.
* AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same recycled-player reset approach and its
  `CvPlayer::updatePlotGroups` map walk likewise calls
  `updatePlotGroup(getID(), false, ...)`.
* Current SAS inherits those mechanics.

The defect is therefore an inherited recycled-player cleanup/lifetime bug rather than a
SAS-specific regression.

DUPLICATE / RELATION TO F477
----------------------------
The reconciled album before this tranche has no root for recycled `m_aiPlotGroup` IDs,
free-list plot-group ID reuse, or a false trade network produced by player-slot recycle.

F477 and F478 share the dangerous feature "reuse a dead PlayerTypes slot," but the
stored aliases and direct repair requirements differ:

F477:
    external fields store the OLD PlayerTypes identity itself; after reuse they
    semantically name the new civilization.

F478:
    a field keyed by that player stores an OLD plot-group OBJECT ID; player reset
    destroys the object, then the new free-list reuses that numeric object ID and old
    map entries bind to the wrong new object.

A blanket policy of never recycling EVER_ALIVE player slots fixes both, but if recycle
support remains, F478 requires explicit plot-group-map invalidation in addition to
F477's historical-identity scrub.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Preferred architectural repair remains:

1. Do not recycle EVER_ALIVE player slots into a new civilization identity.

If recycle support is retained:

2. Explicitly invalidate every plot's raw `m_aiPlotGroup[eRecycledPlayer]` entry before
   any new plot group can be allocated for that slot.

Be careful with the existing `CvPlot::setPlotGroup(ePlayer, NULL)` API AFTER player
reset. It first resolves the old ID through the player's current free-list; when the old
object has already been destroyed, both resolved old pointer and requested new pointer
can be NULL, causing the setter to return early without overwriting the stale integer.
A dedicated raw invalidation helper (set the enum-map entry to
`FFreeList::INVALID_INDEX`) or cleanup performed BEFORE `m_plotGroups.uninit()` is safer.

3. After clearing raw IDs, perform the normal new-player plot-group rebuild and assert
   that every plot whose stored group is non-invalid is actually contained in the
   resolved group's plot list / is connected under the owning team.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Raw reset test

1. Give X at least one plot group and record a representative plot's stored group ID.
2. Eliminate X through Max City Elimination while other X cities still exist.
3. Recycle X into Z.
4. Before allocating Z groups, assert every plot's raw group ID for Z is INVALID.

B. ID-reuse test

1. Confirm old X's first group ID G0.
2. Recycle X and create Z's first group.
3. Confirm the free-list is allowed to reuse G0, but no unrelated old plot still stores
   G0 for Z.

C. False-network test

1. Old X's G0 includes parent P's capital.
2. Eliminate X as above and recycle it into physically disconnected colony Z.
3. Force Z's real first group to receive G0 before the map walk reaches P's capital.
4. Run the normal final `CvGame::updatePlotGroups()`.
5. Assert P capital's plot is NOT in / does not resolve to Z's colony group.
6. Assert `Z.canTradeNetworkWith(P) == false` and a resource trade is unavailable.

D. Rebuild invariant test

After the repair, run a full `updatePlotGroups` and for every alive player/plot with a
non-null `getPlotGroup(player)`, verify that the plot is present in that group's actual
plot list and satisfies the intended connectivity component.

-------------------------------------------------------------
The K-Mod pollution helper remains internally consistent with the health API it reads.
Building, bonus and power bad-health components are represented with the opposite sign
from population unhealth in this calculation, and the subtract/add arrangement matches
that documented convention. Current gameplay consumers are the global-warming code;
SASGameRecord also reads the same helper for diagnostics. No new arithmetic/sign root
was established.

CONTROL — DEAD PLAYER STALE `m_aVote` ID IS NOT AN INDEPENDENT F479
-------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvGame::setVoteOutcome` clears `CvPlayer::m_aVote` only for currently alive players,
while triggered-vote objects come from a recyclable free-list. Therefore a dead player
can retain an old ballot keyed by an ID after the triggered vote object is deleted.

However, ordinary vote resolution iterates living major civilizations, so the stale
ballot is inert while the player remains dead. Bringing that exact CvPlayer object back
without `reset()` requires the malformed recycled-colony revival already owned by F447
(or debug/WorldBuilder-style revival). A later reused vote ID would therefore be a
downstream consequence of F447, not an independent current root. Preserve the stale-ID
lifetime asymmetry as robustness debt; F479 remains unused.

CONTROL — `setLoyalMember` / VOTE-SOURCE BONUS TOGGLE ORDER IS CORRECT
---------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::setLoyalMember` intentionally calls `processVoteSource(..., false)` before
changing the loyalty bit and calls it again with `true` afterward. `CvCity::processVoteSource`
first checks the current `isLoyalMember` state. Consequently:

* true -> false: the pre-toggle call sees loyalty and removes the bonuses; the post-toggle
  add call is ignored;
* false -> true: the pre-toggle removal is ignored; the post-toggle call sees loyalty and
  adds the bonuses.

The ordering is therefore deliberate and symmetric, not a missed refresh.

CONTROL — SPECIALIST / IMPROVEMENT YIELD MUTATORS REFRESH THEIR LIVE CONSUMERS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`changeSpecialistExtraYield` updates the stored specialist/yield value, then runs the
empire-wide extra-specialist-yield refresh and assignment-AI dirtying.
`changeImprovementYieldChange` updates its stored value and calls `updateYield`, which
recomputes affected city/plot yield state. No copied-state sibling was established.

CONTROL — ADVANCED-START RELIGION-FOUNDING LEAD REMAINS REJECTED
----------------------------------------------------------------
The prior WIP201 candidate stays closed. Advanced Start tech purchase calls
`CvTeam::setHasTech(..., bFirst=false, ..., TECH_ACQUISITION_ADVANCED_START)`; the
religion first-discovery block requires `bFirst && bFirstToDiscover`. A legal zero-city
Advanced Start teammate therefore does not enter `foundReligion` through that producer.

F477 SCOPE REFINEMENT — `m_eParent` IS ANOTHER BARE PLAYER-ID ALIAS
-------------------------------------------------------------------
The recycled-identity root already owned by F477 also reaches a surviving colony's
serialized `CvPlayer::m_eParent`.

`setParent` deliberately treats parenthood as permanent for the life of that player;
there is no later clearing when the parent dies. Thus:

1. Old parent X creates colony C, so C stores `m_eParent = X`.
2. X later becomes extinct while C survives.
3. Human dead-slot colony fallback eventually recycles PlayerTypes X into unrelated
   civilization Z.
4. C's unchanged numeric parent value now resolves as Z.

A concrete gameplay consumer is `CvPlayer::getSplitEmpirePlayer(CvArea const&)`:

    for (PlayerIter<MAJOR_CIV> itOldDeriv; itOldDeriv.hasNext(); ++itOldDeriv)
    {
        if (itOldDeriv->getParent() != getID())
            continue;
        if (itOldDeriv->hasCapital() &&
            itOldDeriv->getCapital()->isArea(kArea))
            return NO_PLAYER;
    }

Z can therefore treat old colony C as Z's own derivative and refuse a later split on
C's capital landmass even though Z never created C. `CvCity::getLiberationPlayer`,
`CvTeam::isParent` and AI city-trade trust checks also consume the aliased relation.

This is not F479. It is another manifestation of F477's already-confirmed architectural
problem: an EVER_ALIVE PlayerTypes slot is reused as a new identity while durable bare
PlayerTypes references elsewhere have no generation/version tag.

CONTROL — `CvArea::m_aiBestFoundValue[player]` SELF-HEALS BEFORE AI USE
------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvArea::m_aiBestFoundValue` is serialized and is not explicitly scrubbed by
`CvPlayer::resetPlotAndCityData`, so it was a reasonable recycle candidate.

However, `CvPlayerAI::AI_doTurnUnitsPre()` begins with `AI_updateFoundValues()`. That
function first sets every area's `BestFoundValue(getID())` to zero and then recomputes
all current plot found values and area maxima. The new colony has no ordinary consumer
of the stale old-player area maximum between `addPlayer` and that mandatory refresh.

Therefore this is stale storage but not a demonstrated current gameplay defect.

PARKED ROBUSTNESS LEAD — `CvArea::m_aTargetCities[player]`
----------------------------------------------------------
Area target-city state is a different shape: `CvArea::m_aTargetCities[PlayerTypes]` is
serialized, player reset does not clear it, and `AI_reset` resets the city-target TIMER
but not the per-area target pointers. A surviving foreign target city can therefore
remain attached to recycled player slot X after X becomes unrelated colony Z.

Unlike best-found values, the normal target refresh is not unconditional:
`AI_doTurnUnitsPre` calls `AI_updateAreaTargets()` only when the timer is zero AND a
1-in-8 synchronous random check succeeds. Many unit-AI and some player/city-AI routines
consult `AI_getTargetCity`.

This is real stale derived state and deserves continued robustness attention. It is not
numbered here because the fresh new-team area strategy is recomputed before ordinary
turn decisions, the colony begins with a restricted unit set, and this tranche did not
establish a sufficiently direct current consequence independent of later refresh/RNG.
F479 is reserved for the stronger blockade-state failure below.

F479 / KI#802 — CONFIRMED — RECYCLED TEAM INHERITS PERMANENT STALE BLOCKADE COUNTS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvPlot::m_aiBlockadedCount[TeamTypes]` is persistent/serialized map-side state. It is
maintained by blockading units, but the BBAI mid-game team recycle cleanup does not
clear the recycled team's entries:

    CvTeam::resetPlotAndCityData()
    {
        ...
        kPlot.setRevealedOwner(getID(), NO_PLAYER);
        kPlot.setRevealedImprovementType(getID(), NO_IMPROVEMENT);
        kPlot.setRevealedRouteType(getID(), NO_ROUTE);
        kPlot.setRevealed(getID(), false, ...);
        ...
    }

There is no corresponding removal of:

    kPlot.getBlockadedCount(getID())

The old count can moreover become permanently stranded when the old team dies.

WHY ELIMINATION STRANDS THE COUNT
---------------------------------
Suppose naval unit U of Team Y is legally blockading Team X. `CvUnit::updatePlunder(+1)`
has incremented `m_aiBlockadedCount[X]` on water plots in U's blockade range.

When the last player of X dies:

1. `CvPlayer::setAlive(false)` kills X's own units before lowering X's team AliveCount.
   This is important for blockades maintained BY X, but U belongs to Y and survives.
2. `CvTeam::changeAliveCount(-1)` reaches zero and clears bilateral war state directly
   through `setAtWar(..., false)`; it does not first call U's `updatePlunder(-1)`.
3. On U's later turn, `canPlunder` is now false and `setBlockading(false)` correctly
   invokes `updatePlunder(-1)`.
4. But `updatePlunder(-1)` enumerates target teams through:

       TeamIter<ALIVE,KNOWN_POTENTIAL_ENEMY_OF>

   Dead X is already excluded. Therefore the old positive
   `m_aiBlockadedCount[X]` entries are never decremented.

`CvPlot::m_aiBlockadedCount` is serialized in `CvPlot::read/write`, so saving/loading
does not repair the orphaned count.

CURRENT SUPPORTED RECYCLE CONSEQUENCE
-------------------------------------
Use the same current human dead-slot fallback already source-proved for F477/F478.
A fully ordinary concrete setup is:

1. Team X owns a coastal city C and is at war with Teams P and Y.
2. Y has a naval unit legally blockading water tiles adjacent to C, so those tiles have
   positive `getBlockadedCount(X)`.
3. Human P captures X's final city C and eliminates X while Y's blockader survives.
4. X's war state disappears. Y's blockader later leaves blockade state, but the dead-X
   counts cannot be decremented because the removal loop sees only alive teams.
5. P keeps C/the former X area. Once no never-alive player slot remains, P uses the
   supported human colony fallback and that defeated singleton X slot/team is selected
   for the new colony Z.
6. `initInGame` reinitializes singleton Team X and calls
   `CvTeam::resetPlotAndCityData`, but that routine does not clear the old blockade
   counts. P then transfers C/the area to Z.

Z now owns a coastal city beside water plots whose `getBlockadedCount(Z.getTeam())` is
positive solely because Z reused dead Team X's numeric ID. There need be no current
blockading unit and no current enemy responsible for the value.

DIRECT GAMEPLAY EFFECT
----------------------
This is not cosmetic. `CvCity::canWork` rejects a water tile immediately when:

    kPlot.getBlockadedCount(getTeam()) > 0

and `CvCity::isBlockaded()` returns true if any adjacent plot has a positive count.
Trade-network logic also consults plot blockade counts.

Thus the recycled colony can be unable to work valid coastal tiles and can be treated
as blockaded by a blockade that ended with an unrelated extinct civilization.

INDEPENDENCE / DUPLICATE CONTROL
--------------------------------
The reconciled album through WIP202 contains substantial blockade coverage, including
F144/KI#467's group-wide cancellation problem, but no prior root for orphaned
team-indexed `m_aiBlockadedCount` surviving team death and later slot recycling.

This is also distinct from the recent recycle roots:

* F477: bare PlayerTypes historical VALUE aliases become the new civilization identity.
* F478: stale per-player plot-group object IDs are rebound to newly allocated groups.
* F479: an independently maintained TeamTypes-indexed blockade COUNTER is orphaned on
  death and omitted from the team recycle cleanup.

F479 does not require F473's dead multi-member-team reset omission. A defeated singleton
team is sufficient and follows the normal `bTeamInit` + `resetPlotAndCityData` path.

ANCESTRY / INTEGRATION CONTEXT
------------------------------
The failure lives in inherited BBAI/K-Mod mid-game player/team recycling architecture.
The 12/30/08 BBAI path explicitly introduced plot/city cleanup for recycled identities;
K-Mod's locally available `CvPlayer::resetPlotAndCityData` still has that same limited
field list and AdvCiv/SAS retain it. Current SAS also labels the matching team cleanup
as BETTER_BTS_AI_MOD code.

The exact historical first revision in which the team cleanup omitted blockade counts
was not independently reconstructed from a full local K-Mod CvTeam history in this
tranche, so do not overclaim a precise upstream commit. The present inherited omission
and current execution chain are source-complete.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
When a team slot is reinitialized for a genuinely new civilization identity, clear its
map-side blockade counts as part of `CvTeam::resetPlotAndCityData`, e.g. for every plot
remove the full current `getBlockadedCount(getID())` through the normal mutator (or an
equivalent reset that preserves working-city dirtying / trade-network invalidation).

Architecturally, F477's broader recommendation of never reusing an EVER_ALIVE player
identity would also prevent this recycle manifestation, but the blockade counter is a
separate stale-state invariant and can be repaired directly.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Orphan-on-death test

1. Let Y blockade X's coastal tile and assert `BlockadedCount[X] > 0`.
2. Eliminate X while Y's blockader survives.
3. Advance Y until the unit exits blockade state.
4. Assert the dead X entry returns to zero. Current code fails this assertion.

B. Recycle cleanup test

1. Preserve a positive dead-X count as above.
2. Recycle singleton X into a new colony.
3. Immediately after team/player initialization, before city transfer, assert every
   plot has `getBlockadedCount(Xteam) == 0`.

C. Gameplay test

1. Have parent P own former-X coastal city C after X's elimination.
2. Recycle X into colony Z and transfer C.
3. With no legal blockader in range, assert C can work otherwise valid water tiles and
   `C.isBlockaded() == false`.

CONTROL — RECYCLED STOLEN-VISIBILITY STATE IS REAL GENERIC DEBT BUT CURRENT-DATA DORMANT
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlot::m_aiStolenVisibilityCount[TeamTypes]` has a genuine death/recycle lifetime
problem in generic source. If a team that is stealing another team's visibility dies
while its stolen-visibility timer is active, then:

* dead teams no longer run `CvTeam::doTurn`, so their timer stops ticking;
* source-team visibility changes propagate stolen visibility only to alive stealing
  teams;
* later team reset raw-resets the timer but does not statefully drain old plot counts.

A recycled numeric TeamTypes slot could therefore inherit ghost visibility.

However, current SAS has no normal producer. Repository-wide shipped-data search in the
2026-09-01 light source finds zero units with `bStealPlans=1`, and the DLL's positive
producer of `changeStolenVisibilityTimer` is the legacy `CvUnit::stealPlans()` action.
Python exposes query state but not an ordinary setter. This remains robustness debt,
not F480.

This current-data fact also narrows runtime reachability of the already-fixed F099
Permanent-Alliance stolen-visibility bookkeeping root. F099 is not renumbered or
retracted here; retain this as a current-data annotation only.

CONTROL — OTHER IMMEDIATE RECYCLED TEAM PLOT STATE
---------------------------------------------------
The neighboring real visibility and invisible-detection counts are drained by ordinary
unit/city lifecycle. Recycled-team revealed-map/owner/improvement/route/city espionage
state is explicitly cleared by the team reset path. No additional live current root was
established there.

The cross-player AI reset is also comparatively thorough: surviving players' persistent
religion/favorite-civic counters, trade/grant/gold values, attitude extras, memories,
contact timers, first-contact state and related player-indexed AI state are scrubbed in
both directions when a player slot is reset. The core reset similarly clears surviving
players' GPT/demographics/espionage-weight entries involving the recycled identity.

F480 / KI#803 — CONFIRMED — TEAM FIRST-DISCOVERY CAN SELECT A CITYLESS MEMBER AND PERMANENTLY CONSUME A RELIGION SLOT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
The team first-discovery religion selector in `CvTeam::setHasTech` chooses among alive
team members but does not require the selected `eBestPlayer` to own a city:

    for (MemberIter it(getID()); it.hasNext(); ++it)
    {
        CvPlayer const& kMember = *it;
        int iValue = 10 + SyncRandNum(10);
        ...
        if (kMember.getCurrentResearch() != eTech)
            iValue *= 10;
        if (iValue < iBestValue)
            eBestPlayer = kMember.getID();
    }

Once a member is selected, the slot is reserved before actual city placement:

    kGame.setReligionSlotTaken(eLoopReligion, true);
    ...
    GET_PLAYER(eBestPlayer).foundReligion(eLoopReligion, eLoopReligion, true);

`CvPlayer::foundReligion` independently sets the slot taken again, searches only the
selected player's cities, and then simply returns if there is none:

    kGame.setReligionSlotTaken(eSlotReligion, true);
    ...
    if (pBestCity == NULL)
        return;

Thus the team-level selection contract and player-level placement contract disagree:
being an alive team member is sufficient to receive the entitlement, but having a city
is necessary to realize it.

WHY THE EARLIER ADVANCED-START LEAD WAS CORRECTLY REJECTED
-----------------------------------------------------------
C031-WIP201/202 rejected a zero-city Advanced Start teammate as the producer because
Advanced Start tech purchase calls `CvTeam::setHasTech(..., bFirst=false, ...)`, while
the religion first-discovery block requires `bFirst && bFirstToDiscover`.

That rejection remains correct. F480 uses a different ordinary producer whose call does
set `bFirst=true`: full technology completion from a tribal-village technology result.

CURRENT SAS DATA MAKES THE GOODY PRODUCER LIVE
-----------------------------------------------
Current SAS has religion prerequisites that are also GoodyTechs:

* Hinduism -> `TECH_CALENDAR` (`bGoodyTech=1`, Ancient, base cost 80)
* Daoism -> `TECH_PAPER` (`bGoodyTech=1`)
* Islam -> `TECH_NAVIGATION` (`bGoodyTech=1`)

Current `GOODY_TECH` supplies 23 base research plus two random 0..19 additions, i.e.
23..61 under the XML random convention used by the goody code. AdvC's modified goody
logic converts that progress into a full discovery when it is at least 80% of the
remaining team research.

`CvPlayer::isGoodyTech` contains an important safeguard, but only for the PLAYER
receiving the hut:

    if (!isFoundedFirstCity() && ...)
    {
        if (unfounded religion/corporation uses eTech)
            return false;
    }

Therefore the hut owner cannot personally obtain an immediately founding tech before
founding its first city, but the check says nothing about a different cityless teammate
whom `CvTeam::setHasTech` may later select as the religion founder.

DETERMINISTIC SUPPORTED REPRO
-----------------------------
Use ordinary team-game state with Pick Religion disabled; no death, recycle, debug or
malformed scenario state is required.

1. A and B are alive members of the same team.
2. A has founded at least one city. B has not yet founded a city and still has its
   settler/unit, so B is alive and remains a normal team member.
3. Hinduism is unfounded and its Calendar slot is untaken.
4. Make Calendar the only eligible GoodyTech for the hut result (or simply condition on
   Calendar being selected by the normal synchronized goody roll).
5. Leave at most 28 research points on Calendar. This guarantees even the minimum
   23-point GOODY_TECH award satisfies the 80%-of-remaining full-discovery threshold.
6. B keeps Calendar as its current research. A switches its current research to another
   technology before A receives the goody.
7. A receives GOODY_TECH. A passes `isGoodyTech` because A has founded its first city,
   and Calendar is completed through:

       setHasTech(Calendar, true, A, true, true, false, TECH_ACQUISITION_GOODY)

8. In the religion-founder member selection, B's score is 10..19. A is not currently
   researching Calendar, so A's score is multiplied by 10 and is at least 100 before
   any additional religion-count penalty. B is therefore selected deterministically.
9. The Hinduism slot is marked taken. With Pick Religion disabled,
   `B.foundReligion(Hinduism, Hinduism, true)` executes immediately.
10. B has no city, so `pBestCity == NULL` and `foundReligion` returns without calling
    `CvGame::setHolyCity`.

PERSISTENT CONSEQUENCE
----------------------
The slot reservation is persistent game state (`m_abReligionSlotTaken` is serialized),
while no Holy City and no founded-religion turn were created.

`CvGame::doHolyCity` cannot repair this later because its first gate is:

    if (isReligionSlotTaken(eReligion))
        continue;

So Hinduism's founding opportunity is permanently consumed even after B later settles a
city. Saving/loading preserves the bad state. The team has also already consumed the
first-discovery branch and will not replay it for Calendar.

This is gameplay-significant: the game can permanently lose one religion/Holy City and
its normal founding reward solely because the team selector chose an alive cityless
member.

DISTINCTNESS / DUPLICATE CONTROL
--------------------------------
The reconciled album contains F320 / KI#643, the Pick Religion pending-popup reservation
loss. F480 is independent:

* Pick Religion can be OFF.
* No popup or deferred network choice exists.
* No player elimination occurs.
* The slot is consumed synchronously because `CvTeam::setHasTech` selects a cityless
  teammate and `CvPlayer::foundReligion` cannot realize the already-reserved entitlement.

The WIP201/202 Advanced Start lead is likewise not duplicated: that producer was
correctly rejected because `bFirst=false`; the goody full-tech producer uses `bFirst=true`.

No prior album root was found for this team-member city-presence contract mismatch.

ANCESTRY / INTEGRATION CONTEXT
------------------------------
The city-agnostic team-member selection and `foundReligion` no-city early return are
inherited from Firaxis BtS/Civ4CE through K-Mod and AdvCiv. K-Mod and Civ4CE show the
same first-discovery player scoring without a `getNumCities() > 0` filter.

AdvC later added `isGoodyTech` safeguards to prevent the goody OWNER from immediately
receiving an unfounded religion/corporation tech before founding a first city, but the
safeguard is player-local and therefore does not cover a different cityless teammate.
Current SAS's religion-tech rework makes this inherited gap materially reachable because
Calendar, Paper and Navigation are both religion prerequisites and GoodyTechs.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
The narrow invariant repair belongs at the team first-discovery selection boundary:
only team members capable of realizing the founding entitlement should be candidates.
For religion/corporation founding, require `kMember.getNumCities() > 0` (or an equivalent
city-capability predicate) when choosing `eBestPlayer`.

If no team member has a city, do not reserve/consume the slot yet. Let the existing
`CvGame::doHolyCity`/doHeadquarters-style fallback claim it once a valid city owner
exists, or explicitly defer the entitlement in synchronized team/game state.

A secondary defensive guard could move slot reservation in `foundReligion` until after
`pBestCity` is known, but by itself that does not fix the earlier reservation in
`CvTeam::setHasTech`; the team-level contract is the primary repair boundary.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------

1. Team A+B; A owns a city, B owns none but is alive.
2. B's current research is the founding tech; A's is not.
3. Complete the founding tech with `bFirst=true`.
4. Assert the founder chosen has at least one city, or that the slot remains untaken if
   no valid member exists.

B. Current Calendar goody test

1. Hinduism unfounded; Calendar nearly complete and only eligible GoodyTech.
2. A owns a city; cityless teammate B selects Calendar; A selects another tech.
3. A receives GOODY_TECH and completes Calendar.
4. Assert Hinduism receives a valid Holy City and `isReligionFounded(Hinduism)` becomes
   true; current code consumes the slot without a Holy City.

C. Persistence test

1. Produce the current bad state.
2. Save/load and advance turns after B settles a city.
3. Assert an unfounded but taken religion slot cannot remain permanently orphaned.

F481 / KI#804 — CONFIRMED — A NEVER-SETTLED PLAYER CAN FULL-DISCOVER A FIRST-FREE-UNIT TECH FROM A GOODY HUT AND SILENTLY LOSE THE ONE-TIME UNIT
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvTeam::setHasTech` awards a technology's `FirstFreeUnitClass` specifically to the
`ePlayer` credited with the first acquisition, and assumes that player's capital is a
valid placement site:

    UnitTypes eFreeUnit = GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).getTechFreeUnit(eTech);
    if (eFreeUnit != NO_UNIT)
    {
        bFirstPerk = true;
        bAnnounceFirst = true;
        CvCity* pCapital = GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).getCapital();
        if (pCapital != NULL)
            pCapital->createGreatPeople(eFreeUnit, false, false);
    }

If the first discoverer is alive but has never founded a city, `getCapital()` is NULL.
The code nevertheless records the first-perk/announcement state and simply skips unit
creation. There is no deferred entitlement and no later replay of the first-discovery
block.

This is a different contract from F480. F480's organization block independently chooses
some team member as founder and can choose a cityless teammate even though the actual
tech-acquisition player has a city. F481 uses the actual `ePlayer` acquisition owner;
the defect is that a perfectly valid cityless acquisition owner can reach a reward
whose only placement path assumes a capital.

ORDINARY CITYLESS PLAYER STATE IS SUPPORTED
--------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::verifyAlive` does not eliminate a never-settled player merely for having zero
cities. With Advanced Start inactive, it kills a zero-city player only when either:

    getNumUnits() <= 0

or

    isFoundedFirstCity()

is already true.

Therefore a teammate that has never founded a city and still owns a settler/scout/other
unit can remain alive while another teammate develops the team through the technology
tree. This needs no debug/WorldBuilder revival and no recycled-player defect.

CURRENT-SAS PRODUCER: ROMANTICISM + GOODY_TECH
-----------------------------------------------
Current SAS `TECH_ROMANTICISM` has all of the properties needed for a live supported
producer:

    Era = ERA_INDUSTRIAL
    FirstFreeUnitClass = UNITCLASS_GREAT_ARTIST
    bGoodyTech = 1
    prerequisite = TECH_LIBERALISM

`CvPlayer::getTechFreeUnit(TECH_ROMANTICISM)` therefore resolves the player's Great
Artist unit normally (absent the unrelated No-Espionage special case for spy-like free
units).

Current `GOODY_TECH` grants research progress and can convert that progress into a full
technology discovery. `CvPlayer::receiveGoody` performs:

    if (iGold <= 0 || 0.8 * researchLeft <= iGold)
        kOurTeam.setHasTech(eBestTech, true, getID(), true, true, false,
                TECH_ACQUISITION_GOODY);

The important arguments are:

* `ePlayer = getID()` — the unit owner who opened the hut;
* `bFirst = true` — unlike Advanced Start, so first-discovery perks execute.

`CvPlayer::canResearch` has no personal-city requirement; prerequisites are team-wide.
So a never-settled member can research/receive Romanticism once its team has Liberalism.

`CvPlayer::isGoodyTech` also does NOT reject Romanticism for a cityless player. Its
special no-first-city guard only rejects a full goody discovery when that technology is
an unfounded religion or corporation prerequisite. Romanticism is neither, and its
explicit `bGoodyTech=1` passes the normal goody-tech gate.

Current `GOODY_TECH` starts from 23 + two SyncRandNum(20) research components and then
applies the normal goody-hut effect factor. Thus a test can simply leave Romanticism
close enough to completion that even the minimum current goody progress satisfies the
80% completion test. The exact late-game buff is not needed for the root; it only makes
completion easier.

DETERMINISTIC CURRENT-SAS REPRO SHAPE
--------------------------------------
A controlled supported team-game test can be made deterministic with respect to the
critical branch:

1. Team A+B begins normally. A founds/develops cities. B NEVER founds a city but keeps
   at least one unit alive, so `verifyAlive` leaves B alive.
2. Through A's economy, the shared team reaches Liberalism and all other prerequisites.
3. Keep an unpopped tribal village reachable by B until the Industrial era. This is rare
   on an ordinary playthrough but fully supported game state; no debug/API action is
   required.
4. Know every other currently eligible GoodyTech (or otherwise arrange Romanticism as
   the sole eligible one), leaving only `TECH_ROMANTICISM` eligible for the tech goody.
5. Put team research progress on Romanticism sufficiently close to completion that the
   minimum `GOODY_TECH` progress satisfies the 80%-of-research-left full-discovery test.
6. B opens the hut and receives `GOODY_TECH`.
7. `receiveGoody` calls `setHasTech(ROMANTICISM, true, B, true, ..., GOODY)`.
8. Assume no other team knows Romanticism, so `bFirstToDiscover` is correctly true.
9. The first-free-unit block resolves B's Great Artist and sets `bFirstPerk=true`.
10. `B.getCapital()` is NULL because B has never settled.
11. `createGreatPeople` is skipped. No Great Artist is created anywhere.
12. The technology is already team-owned and the first-discovery condition will never
    execute again, so B later founding a city does not recover the reward.

The random roll that chooses which goody outcome is received is not part of the defect;
once the supported GOODY_TECH outcome occurs, the XML/eligibility setup above makes the
technology/reward path deterministic. A regression test can invoke the same ordinary
`receiveGoody`/setHasTech path directly at that point.

PERSISTENCE / CONSEQUENCE
-------------------------
The missed Great Artist is a one-shot first-discovery reward. There is no stored
"free unit owed" state. Saving/loading cannot replay the reward because Romanticism is
already known and `countKnownTechNumTeams` will no longer represent a new first
acquisition. Settling B's first city later likewise does not call the first-discovery
block.

So this is not a temporary presentation issue: the world's true first discoverer can
permanently lose a shipped technology reward.

DISTINCTNESS / DUPLICATE CONTROL
--------------------------------
F474 / KI#797 also has a Romanticism/Great-Artist consequence, but its root is entirely
different. F474 duplicates a recycled team's pointer in the AdvCiv `CIV_EVER_ALIVE`
iterator, causing `countKnownTechNumTeams` to return 2 for the true first discoverer;
the whole first-discovery block is skipped.

F481 requires no player recycling and no AgentIterator defect. `bFirstToDiscover` is
correctly TRUE and the reward block executes; the free unit alone is dropped because
its placement code silently accepts a NULL capital.

F480 / KI#803 is also independent. F480 selects a different cityless TEAM MEMBER to
receive a religion-founding entitlement. F481 does no member selection at all: the
actual acquisition owner B legitimately obtains the tech, and the first-free-unit code
has no valid placement fallback.

No prior album root was found for a cityless acquisition owner silently losing the
first-free-unit perk.

ANCESTRY / COMPARISON
---------------------
Civ4CE/stock-style code and K-Mod contain the same inherited pattern:

    eFreeUnit = GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).getTechFreeUnit(eIndex);
    if (eFreeUnit != NO_UNIT)
    {
        bFirstBonus = true;
        pCapitalCity = GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).getCapitalCity();
        if (pCapitalCity != NULL)
            pCapitalCity->createGreatPeople(eFreeUnit, false, false);
    }

AdvCiv/SAS retain the same NULL-capital skip. SAS makes the inherited assumption
materially easy to connect to a current full-tech goody path because Romanticism is
explicitly both `bGoodyTech=1` and `FirstFreeUnitClass=UNITCLASS_GREAT_ARTIST`.

IMMEDIATE SIBLING RECONCILIATION
--------------------------------
* First-free-tech rewards do not share the capital assumption. AI players receive them
  through `AI_chooseFreeTech`; human players receive `chooseTech`. No city placement is
  required, so no F481 sibling was established there.
* Technology-triggered corporation founding is current-data unused in SAS: shipped
  corporation infos have no technology prerequisite, and AdvCiv itself labels this
  `setHasTech` corporation branch unused/not properly tested. It therefore does not
  provide another current cityless founding root.
* Religion founding is owned separately by F480 because its problem is the team member
  selection and pre-reservation contract, not `ePlayer` free-unit placement.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Do not silently consume `FirstFreeUnitClass` when the credited first discoverer has no
capital. Reasonable synchronized policies include:

1. choose another valid city owned by `ePlayer` if one exists (capital should already
   exist whenever any city exists, but this is a defensive fallback);
2. if `ePlayer` has no city, defer the free-unit entitlement until its first city is
   founded; or
3. if design policy permits team sharing of a first-discovery unit, explicitly choose a
   valid teammate city/recipient rather than silently discarding it.

The safest semantic choice should be decided deliberately; the essential invariant is
that a valid first discovery must not mark the one-shot perk consumed without either
creating the reward or persisting an owed entitlement.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Cityless first-discoverer test

1. Keep B alive with one unit and zero cities; `isFoundedFirstCity()==false`.
2. Give Team A+B Liberalism and leave Romanticism unknown globally.
3. Bring Romanticism close enough to completion for a minimum GOODY_TECH completion.
4. B receives the tech goody and becomes the true first discoverer.
5. Assert exactly one appropriate Great Artist reward is created or explicitly deferred.
   Current code creates zero.

B. Capital-present control

Repeat with B owning a capital and assert current behavior still creates exactly one

C031-WIP206 — MIXED HUMAN/AI TEAM FIRST-FREE-TECH ROUTING; F482 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

CONTINUATION ANCHOR
