F482 / KI#805 — CONFIRMED — MIXED HUMAN/AI TEAM ROUTES AN AI DISCOVERER'S FIRST-FREE-TECH REWARD INTO A HUMAN-ONLY POPUP ON THE AI PLAYER, STRANDING THE REWARD
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvTeam::setHasTech` handles `iFirstFreeTechs` according to TEAM humanity:

    if (!isHuman())
    {
        for (...)
            GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).AI_chooseFreeTech();
    }
    else
    {
        ...
        GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).chooseTech(kTech.getFirstFreeTechs(), ...);
    }

But the reward is player-specific: `ePlayer` is the player credited with the technology
acquisition. In a mixed human+AI team, `CvTeam::isHuman()` is true whenever the team has
a human leader/member, even when `ePlayer` is an AI teammate.

Current AdvC optimizes `CvTeam::isHuman()` to:

    return (getLeaderID() != NO_PLAYER && GET_PLAYER(getLeaderID()).isHuman());

and `updateLeaderID()` explicitly prefers a human member. K-Mod/Civ4CE use a full member
scan and likewise return true if ANY teammate is human. Thus this is not a questionable
SAS interpretation of mixed-team semantics; the branch really is team-human while the
reward recipient can be AI.

NORMAL RESEARCH CAN CREDIT THE AI TEAMMATE
------------------------------------------
Each player executes `CvPlayer::doResearch` independently and contributes its own research
rate to the shared team technology through:

    GET_TEAM(getTeam()).changeResearchProgress(eCurrentTech, ..., getID(),
            TECH_ACQUISITION_RESEARCH);

If AI teammate B's contribution crosses the team research cost, `setResearchProgress`
passes B straight through to:

    setHasTech(eTech, true, ePlayer, true, true, true, eCause);

So ordinary team research can make `ePlayer == B` even though human teammate H makes the
team satisfy `CvTeam::isHuman()`.

HUMAN-ONLY CHOOSETECH IS THEN CALLED ON THE AI
-----------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::chooseTech` begins with the contract:

    FAssert(isHuman());

and, for a free choice, increments that PLAYER'S local free-tech token:

    changeChoosingFreeTechCount(1);

It then queues a `BUTTONPOPUP_CHOOSETECH` popup specifically for that player ID.

Under F482, B is AI, so:

* a debug build hits the `FAssert(isHuman())` contract violation;
* release code increments B's `m_iChoosingFreeTechCount` anyway;
* the popup is queued to AI B rather than human teammate H;
* the normal AI reward path `AI_chooseFreeTech()` was skipped solely because the TEAM is
  human.

THE UI CANNOT RESCUE B'S TOKEN
------------------------------
The only current DLL decrement/consumer of `m_iChoosingFreeTechCount` is the research
widget path in `CvDLLWidgetData::doResearch`, and it always operates on:

    CvPlayer& kActivePlayer = GET_PLAYER(getActivePlayer());

For a free-tech click it checks/decrements `kActivePlayer.isChoosingFreeTech()`.

Likewise `CvDLLButtonPopup::OnFocus` for `BUTTONPOPUP_CHOOSETECH` checks the ACTIVE player's
free-tech state and cancels a free-tech popup when the active player is not choosing one.
The popup click path also uses the active player/UI research flow.

There is no AI-turn consumer of `m_iChoosingFreeTechCount` anywhere else in the current
DLL. Therefore B's token is not converted into a technology by AI logic and is not
transferable to H. It can simply remain serialized on the AI while the one-shot first-
discovery reward has already been claimed.

CURRENT-SAS PRODUCER
--------------------
Current SAS `TECH_THEORY_OF_EVOLUTION` is a normal Industrial technology with:

    iFirstFreeTechs = 1

and ordinary research prerequisites. No special goody/recycle setup is required.

Supported reproduction:

1. Create an ordinary team game with human H and AI B on the same team.
2. Leave Theory of Evolution unknown to all teams.
3. Let H and B both contribute to the shared research race normally.
4. Arrange the final required beakers so B's `doResearch()` contribution crosses the
   Theory of Evolution cost first.
5. `setHasTech(..., ePlayer=B, bFirst=true)` sees the team as human.
6. Instead of `B.AI_chooseFreeTech()`, current code calls `B.chooseTech(1, ...)`.
7. Debug: assertion because B is not human. Release: B gets a free-tech-choice counter
   and an AI-addressed popup, but no AI free tech is selected.
8. Human H does not own B's token; normal active-player popup/widget logic cannot spend it.
9. Theory of Evolution is already known, so the first-discovery block is never replayed.

The free technology is therefore stranded/lost rather than awarded.

PERSISTENCE
-----------
`m_iChoosingFreeTechCount` is serialized in `CvPlayer::read/write`. Saving/loading can
therefore preserve the malformed AI free-tech-choice state, but loading does not convert
it into `AI_chooseFreeTech()` and does not replay Theory of Evolution's first-discovery
reward. The missed reward is not self-healing.

DISTINCTNESS / DUPLICATE CONTROL
--------------------------------
F313 / KI#636 is different. F313 starts with a HUMAN player who legitimately owns a
free-tech popup; while that popup is open a teammate acquires one displayed technology,
and clicking the stale entry decrements the human token before the invalid selection is
rejected. F313 is stale popup CONTENT after valid routing.

F482 is wrong RECIPIENT/CONTROL routing before a valid popup exists. The team-level
`isHuman()` branch calls the human-only API on AI `ePlayer`, leaving the token on the AI
and bypassing `AI_chooseFreeTech()` entirely.

F481 is also independent: it concerns a cityless acquisition owner's first-free-unit
placement at a NULL capital, not free-tech UI ownership.

No prior album root was found for this mixed-team first-free-tech routing mismatch.

ANCESTRY / COMPARISON
---------------------
The same structural mismatch exists in Civ4CE/stock-style and K-Mod code: team
`isHuman()` is true if any member is human, while the first-free-tech block invokes
`GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).chooseTech(...)` on the credited acquisition player. AdvC/SAS retain
that inherited design (with a faster human-team test based on the human-preferred leader).

Current SAS supplies an explicit live first-free-tech producer through its reworked
`TECH_THEORY_OF_EVOLUTION` (`iFirstFreeTechs=1`).

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Route the reward according to the RECIPIENT player's control type, not the team:

    if (GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).isHuman())
        GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).chooseTech(...);
    else
        GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).AI_chooseFreeTech();

If team design instead intends a human teammate to control all team first-discovery free
techs, then an explicit human recipient must be selected and the free-tech token/reward
must be assigned to that human player; do not call a human-only popup method on an AI.

The narrow per-recipient branch is the least surprising match for current `ePlayer`
semantics and mirrors the ownership of `m_iChoosingFreeTechCount`.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Mixed-team AI completion

1. Human H + AI B share a team.
2. Theory of Evolution is globally unknown and one beaker short before B's research turn.
3. Let B complete it.
4. Assert B receives exactly one AI-selected free technology, no human-only assertion is
   hit, and B's `m_iChoosingFreeTechCount` remains zero.

B. Mixed-team human completion

Repeat with H supplying the final beakers. Assert H receives exactly one normal free-tech
choice popup/token.

C. Save/load malformed-state prevention

After B completes the tech, save/load. Assert no unresolved AI `ChoosingFreeTechCount`
exists and the awarded free technology remains exactly one.

could theoretically leave changed sibling percentages without `updateCommerce()`.

the problematic fallback-to-self shape is not reached in current supported state.

the same early-return hazard. No current F483.

F483 / KI#806 — CONFIRMED — A SURVIVING MASTER TEAM LOSES PART OF ITS VASSAL POPULATION/LAND SCORE WHEN ONE MASTER TEAMMATE DIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED. Ordinary current team-game + Vassal States gameplay reaches the defect.
It is inherited from the Warlords/BtS vassal-score implementation through Civ4CE,
K-Mod, Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.


ROOT CONTRACT
-------------
CvPlayer::getPopScore(true) and getLandScore(true) implement the vassal-score transfer
in two complementary halves:

1. A player whose TEAM is a vassal returns only half of its own raw population / land
   score:

       if (bIncludeVassals && isAVassal())
           return m_iPopulationScore / 2;

   (and analogously for land).

2. A master player sums half of every living vassal player's raw score, then divides
   that master-team contribution by the master's team-member count:

       iVassalScore += itVassal->getPopScore(false) / 2;
       ...
       return m_iPopulationScore +
           iVassalScore / std::max(1, GET_TEAM(getTeam()).getNumMembers());

The division is necessary in a multi-player master team: without it, every teammate
would receive the full transferred half and CvGame's team-score sum would multiply the
vassal contribution by the number of master players.

When all master teammates are alive, the implementation therefore has a clear invariant:
collectively the master TEAM receives one half of the vassal's population/land score,
independent of the number of master-team members.


BROKEN DEATH TRANSITION
-----------------------
CvTeam::getNumMembers() is persistent team membership. Player death changes
CvTeam::m_iAliveCount through changeAliveCount, but does NOT remove the dead player from
m_iNumMembers; membership changes only through player/team initialization or
CvPlayer::setTeam.

At the same time, CvPlayer::calculateScore explicitly returns zero for a dead player:

    if (!isAlive() || GET_TEAM(getTeam()).getNumMembers() <= 0)
        return 0;

CvGame::updateScore then computes each team score by summing the cached player scores of
all players assigned to that team. Thus a dead teammate contributes zero to the team
score, including zero of the vassal share that had been allocated to that teammate.

But every surviving master member still divides the vassal contribution by the old,
persistent getNumMembers() count. The dead member's fraction is therefore not reassigned
to the survivors; it simply disappears from the master team's score.


DETERMINISTIC TWO-MASTER EXAMPLE
--------------------------------
Let master Team M contain living players A and B, and let living vassal V have a raw
population-score input of 100 (the same arithmetic applies to land).

Before B dies:

* V's own getPopScore(true) contributes 50 because V is a vassal.
* Each master member computes half of V's raw score (50), then divides by
  Team M getNumMembers()==2, receiving +25.
* A+B collectively therefore receive +50, exactly the other half of V's score.

Now eliminate B while A survives:

* Team M remains alive and its vassal relationship remains; CvTeam::changeAliveCount
  only performs full-team death cleanup when the team's alive count reaches zero.
* Team M getNumMembers() remains 2.
* B's calculateScore becomes 0 because B is dead.
* A still receives only +25 because it divides by persistent NumMembers==2.

The master team therefore receives only one quarter of V's raw population contribution
instead of the intended one half. The missing +25 is not credited anywhere. The same
loss occurs independently in land score.

With N original master members but only L currently alive, the master team's collective
vassal share is effectively multiplied by L/N.


CURRENT GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCE
----------------------------
CvPlayer::setAlive marks the game score dirty. CvGame::updateScore recomputes dead B as
zero and recomputes A with the unchanged persistent member divisor, then builds
m_aiTeamScore by summing the per-player scores assigned to Team M.

Current SAS ships VICTORY_TIME with bEndScore=1. The resulting team score is therefore
not merely scoreboard presentation: an eliminated teammate can lower the surviving
master team's end-score / Time-victory ranking by deleting part of its still-valid
vassal population and land contribution. Team-score consumers in AI/ranking logic see
the same reduced m_aiTeamScore.

No debug, WorldBuilder, revival, recycled-player defect or Permanent Alliance is needed.
A normal multi-player/team setup in which one member is eliminated while another member
of the same team survives, with an existing living vassal, is sufficient.


WHY THIS IS NOT F469 OR THE EARLIER PA SCORE CONTROL
----------------------------------------------------
F469/KI#792 concerns an AdvCiv-specific cached CITY-MAINTENANCE formula whose divisor was
changed to alive-only MemberIter::count without adding death invalidation. F483 is the
opposite shape: score is dynamically recomputed correctly on death, but the live formula
itself uses the wrong persistent membership domain for distributing a team-level vassal
share among the players who actually contribute to team score.

C031-WIP179 previously checked Permanent Alliance team-size score changes and correctly
closed that transition because CvTeam::addTeam calls updateScore(true) after membership
changes. F483 is not stale score after a PA. Death dirties/recomputes score too; the
recomputed value is itself wrong because dead members remain in getNumMembers().

Semantic duplicate search found no prior album root for the eliminated-master-member
vassal-share loss.


ANCESTRY
--------
The same design is present in the local Civ4CE Warlords and BtS sources:

    vassal player -> own population/land score / 2
    master player -> (sum vassal raw / 2) / team getNumMembers()

K-Mod retains it. Base AdvCiv 1.14 converts the vassal-player loop to its iterator form
but retains getNumMembers() as the divisor. Current SAS inherits the same arithmetic.

This is therefore a stock Warlords/BtS edge-case defect, not a SAS-local regression and
not an AdvCiv AgentIterator regression.


REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Distribute the master-team vassal share across currently ALIVE master members, i.e. use
an authoritative alive-member count rather than persistent membership for the divisor:

    std::max(1, GET_TEAM(getTeam()).getAliveCount())

in both getPopScore(true) and getLandScore(true).

Using CvTeam::getAliveCount is preferable to relying on a cached member iterator for this
repair: it directly matches calculateScore's alive-player participation contract and is
not exposed to the human-PA AgentIterator invalidation family from F470.

A regression test should use a two-member master team with one vassal, record the
collective master vassal population/land contribution, eliminate one master member, and
assert that the surviving master receives the full remaining team allocation rather than
letting half of the transfer disappear.

`CvTeam::getResearchCost` deliberately scales technology cost by persistent team
membership, and AdvCiv's `CvPlayer::adjustMissionCostToTeamSize` deliberately derives
its espionage team-size adjustment from the same TECH_COST_EXTRA_TEAM_MEMBER_MODIFIER
and the same persistent member counts.

Unlike F483, there is no conservation identity here saying that only players who still
contribute a score may remain in the divisor. Making these costs shrink when a teammate
dies would itself create an abrupt mid-research / mid-game discount and would change an
established paired balance rule. No upstream contract or current caller proved that the
team-size handicap is intended to follow alive count. Keep the F483 `getAliveCount()`
repair local to the vassal-score distribution; no F484.

POST-WIP208 DUPLICATE CONTROL — PROJECTED UNIT-COST ASYMMETRY IS F446
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A fresh arithmetic pass rediscovered that `calculateUnitCost(..., iExtraUnits)` applies
its generic projected unit delta in a way that also distorts the projected military paid
count. Semantic album reconciliation shows this is exactly F446/KI#769. Do not duplicate
it as F484.

  F444/KI#767, not a new CvPlayer root.

  established in this pass.

The latest September 1 SAS Building XML was rechecked rather than relying on old

PURPOSE OF THIS CHECKPOINT
This checkpoint preserves the settled tranche after C031-WIP209. It is intentionally conservative: several plausible leads were traced through current SAS callers/data, ancestry and semantic-duplicate controls and then closed. F484 remains unused.

PRIOR ANCHOR
F483 / KI#806 remains CONFIRMED: getPopScore(true) and getLandScore(true) split the master's transferred vassal half using persistent CvTeam::getNumMembers(), while dead players contribute zero player score. If only L of N persistent master-team members remain alive, the master team's intended vassal share is effectively multiplied by L/N. Current VICTORY_TIME uses end score, so the error can affect victory ranking. This is an inherited Civ4CE/BtS -> K-Mod -> AdvCiv -> SAS edge case, distinct from F469's stale city-maintenance cache. Natural repair candidate: use alive membership for this score-allocation divisor.

POST-WIP209 TRANCHE

1. Persistent-team-size research / espionage scaling: CLOSED AS POLICY
The earlier follow-up from F483 was completed. Research and espionage team-size modifiers deliberately share the persistent team-size concept. Unlike F483's explicit conservation contract (one transferred half split among actual scorers), no source contract was found saying these balance modifiers must shrink when a teammate dies. Changing them on death would itself create a mid-tech / mid-game balance discontinuity. No F484.

2. calculateUnitCost(..., iExtraUnits) asymmetry: DUPLICATE
A fresh arithmetic pass rediscovered the civilian/military projected-unit asymmetry, but it is exactly F446 / KI#769. Excluded from new numbering.

3. TeamShare building revalidation against latest 2026-09-01 data: ROBUSTNESS DEBT, NOT CURRENT WRONG EFFECT
Current SAS now has live TeamShare buildings (Three Gorges Dam and Great Wall), so an older masked control had to be rechecked. Permanent-alliance/team replay gives the merged team the intended live boolean effect. A later removal can over-decrement an old team-keyed area count because absorbed members' pre-merge increments are not migrated; with current content this leaves only a negative dormant count after the sole source disappears/obsoletes, not a wrong live boolean effect. No F484.

4. Great Person / Great General threshold zero: CLOSED
Threshold calculation defensively clamps modifier+100 at zero. Current producer tracing shows the threshold modifiers are changed only by the normal escalating GP/GG creation path; no shipped negative producer can drive the threshold multiplier to zero. No award loop under current data.

5. Cityless Great General under Complete Kills: CLOSED
AdvCiv no longer implements ordinary post-city Complete Kills survival semantics in verifyAlive. The supported cityless-alive state is essentially pre-first-city. If combat XP crosses the GG threshold there, the XP is not consumed; it remains banked and can award after a city exists and combat XP changes again. Delayed award, not lost award. No F484.

6. Team Power / Assets alive-vs-persistent membership: CLOSED
MemberIter is PlayerIter<ALIVE, MEMBER_OF>. CvTeam::getPower() and getAssets() therefore stop summing an eliminated teammate automatically, even if some serialized player-level quantities survive teardown. This is another reason F483 is a special domain mismatch rather than a general getNumMembers/getAliveCount replacement campaign.

7. Event propagation name collision kept separated
setTriggerFired team propagation is correct. The previously identified inverted predicate is specifically setEventOccured's Team EventInfo propagation. Current SAS has zero Team EventInfos, so that source defect remains dormant. Do not repair setTriggerFired by analogy.

8. getEventTriggerWeight building probability multiplier: CURRENT-DATA CLOSED
The minimum required building count gates eligibility; BuildingsRequired defines the building classes counted by the multiplier. More decisively, current SAS ships zero triggers with bProbabilityBuildingMultiply=1. No F484.

9. isValidEventTech apparent PlayerTypes/TeamTypes mismatch: FALSE POSITIVE, IMPORTANT ADV-CIV ACCESSOR RULE
Current SAS has:
    if (eOtherPlayer != NO_PLAYER && !GET_TEAM(eOtherPlayer).isHasTech(eTech))
Literal comparison with K-Mod/Civ4CE looks suspicious because they write the explicit player->team conversion. However AdvCiv deliberately changed GET_TEAM into overloaded accessors in CvGamePlay.h:
    #define GET_TEAM(x) CvGamePlay::getTeam(x)
    #define TEAMID(x) GET_PLAYER(x).getTeam()
    getTeam(TeamTypes) -> team directly
    getTeam(PlayerTypes) -> CvTeam::getTeam(TEAMID(ePlayer))
Therefore GET_TEAM(eOtherPlayer) is type-correct and resolves the player's team. This also protects similarly written AdvCiv/SAS calls elsewhere. K-Mod/Civ4CE needed the explicit GET_PLAYER(...).getTeam() spelling because they lack this overload. Do NOT classify these lines by syntax ancestry alone.
Current XML even supplies a live tech+other-player route (Airliner Crash), so this was worth proving rather than dismissing as dormant. No F484.

10. expireEvent / checkExpireEvent / persistent OtherPlayerCityId quest references: SHIPPED QUEST GRAPH CLOSED
The earlier concern was that a persistent quest record containing another player's city ID might expire incorrectly when that city changes owner. Current shipped quest tracing narrows the important other-player-city case to Crusade. CvPlayer::acquireCity contains an explicit inherited repair for the acquirer: if an event record points to the old owner's captured city ID, m_iOtherPlayerCityId is reset to -1 so the event does not expire merely because the acquirer conquered the target. Crusade's Python expiry logic separately treats a third-party capture / wrong owner as quest failure. That matches the intended distinction. No independent F484.

11. getDiscoveryTech / popResearch: CLOSED
getDiscoveryTech keeps the inherited Great-Person discovery behavior: among currently researchable technologies, choose the highest positive flavor overlap; no source-proven current defect was established.
popResearch removes the matching queue node when present and then clears the player's researching-tech boolean. That state is a boolean set, not a decrementing counter. The live CvTeam::setHasTech acquisition caller first checks isResearchingTech(eTech) before popResearch. clearResearchQueue removes the full list and clears all corresponding booleans. No negative-count or unrelated-tech corruption route found. Research-path selection remains semantically owned by earlier F453; do not duplicate it here.

12. foundCorporation: CURRENT-DATA DORMANT
Current SAS ships seven corporations and all seven have TechPrereq=NONE. CvGame::doHeadquarters explicitly skips corporations with NO_TECH prerequisite in the tech-triggered founding path; CvTeam::setHasTech likewise can only found a corporation whose prerequisite equals the newly acquired tech. Thus CvPlayer::foundCorporation's tech-triggered path is dormant under shipped corporation data. No current F484.

13. getModifiedWarWearinessPercentAnger: SAS CHANGE IS PERFORMANCE-ONLY; NO NEW DEFECT
The current SAS body is functionally the AdvCiv body with a cached CvGame reference. The player/building/civic war-weariness modifier is applied later in city anger calculation rather than omitted here. No current independent state error established.

14. changeGoldenAgeTurns / changeGoldenAgeModifier: CLOSED
SAS differences are logging and cached color lookups, not gameplay arithmetic changes. Decrement callers are guarded by positive turns; event/GP additions use valid golden-age lengths. Current XML's live GoldenAgeModifier source is positive (e.g. Pyramids +50), with no shipped extreme negative producer that would establish a current bad rescale path. No F484.

15. changePersonalityType: CLOSED
Current SAS change is a static cache of BARBARIAN_LEADER. Random-personality selection semantics remain inherited. No gameplay regression established.

16. disbandUnit: CLOSED FOR THIS PASS
Current SAS functional differences from AdvCiv are the renamed UNITAI_GREAT_* enums plus a cached message color; selection behavior is inherited. No current independent source defect survived caller/data review. Great-person UnitAIs are deliberately protected. No F484.

17. validateDiplomacy: CLOSED FOR THIS PASS
The removal loops are structurally safe: invalid offer deletion is followed by break/restart where needed rather than iterator reuse. Stop-trading, defensive-pact-after-war, and peace/surrender validation paths were reviewed; no independent current defect was established.

18. spy helper/current espionage XML reachability: CLOSED FOR UNIT BRIBE/DESTROY PATHS
canSpyDestroyUnit and canSpyBribeUnit may look worth auditing in isolation, but current CIV4EspionageMissionInfo.xml has no mission with nonzero iDestroyUnitCostFactor or iBuyUnitCostFactor. The live destroy-building and destroy-project missions use their own checks and cost branches. No F484 from the dormant unit paths.

19. Advanced Start improvement/route build-prerequisite multiplicity: CURRENT-DATA MASKED, NO F484
getAdvancedStartImprovementCost and getAdvancedStartRouteCost iterate Builds that produce the requested improvement/route and require their prerequisite technologies. This would need careful OR semantics if multiple alternative Builds produced the same target. Current SAS BuildInfos has no improvement with more than one Build; ROUTE_ROAD has only BUILD_ROAD and ROUTE_RAILROAD only BUILD_RAILROAD. Thus no shipped current mismatch. Advanced Start tech-removal territory also has prior semantic ownership (including F088 controls), so duplicate gate remains mandatory.

20. PARKED LOW-SEVERITY UI ISSUE REMAINS AVAILABLE, STILL UNNUMBERED
postProcessMessages() subtracts one from m_iNewMessages whenever getCurrentResearch()==NO_TECH, using that as a proxy for 'a technology just completed'. After all technologies are known, NO_TECH can persist indefinitely. Therefore exactly MessageLimit+1 genuine interturn messages can be treated as only MessageLimit, preventing the Turn Log from auto-opening. Deterministic and reachable, but UI-only/low severity. Leave unnumbered while stronger gameplay/state territory remains.

================================================================================
C031-WIP211 — F484 / KI#807 CONFIRMED
================================================================================

F484 / KI#807 — AdvCiv's generic Steal Technology affordability check chooses the
candidate by FULL research cost after actual steal pricing was changed to REMAINING
research cost, so the human espionage popup can hide the entire mission even when a
specific stealable technology is currently affordable

STATUS
CONFIRMED current gameplay root.
Inherited by current AdvCiv-SAS from AdvCiv 1.14.
Not present with this contradiction in K-Mod / Civ4CE-BtS, because those ancestors
priced both generic and specific technology theft by full research cost.

ROOT
Current CvPlayer::getStealCostTech(eTargetPlayer) scans all stealable technologies and
selects the one with the smallest FULL research cost:

    int iProdCost = MAX_INT;
    FOR_EACH_ENUM(Tech)
    {
        if (canStealTech(eTargetPlayer, eLoopTech))
        {
            int iCost = GET_TEAM(getTeam()).getResearchCost(eLoopTech);
            if (iCost < iProdCost)
            {
                iProdCost = iCost;
                eR = eLoopTech;
            }
        }
    }

That helper was extracted by advc.120d from the old generic branch of
getEspionageMissionBaseCost.

But the actual Buy/Steal Tech mission-cost branch no longer prices the selected tech by
full research cost. AdvCiv's advc.120i deliberately changed it to OUR REMAINING research:

    if (eTech == NO_TECH)
        eTech = getStealCostTech(eTargetPlayer);
    int iProdCost = (eTech == NO_TECH ? -1 : GET_TEAM(getTeam()).
            getResearchLeft(eTech)); // advc.120i: Count own progress

    if (eTech != NO_TECH && canStealTech(eTargetPlayer, eTech))
    {
        iMissionCost = iBaseMissionCost +
            ((100 + kMission.getBuyTechCostFactor()) * iProdCost) / 100;
    }

Therefore the generic NO_TECH path now combines TWO DIFFERENT ordering metrics:

    candidate choice:  minimum getResearchCost(tech)
    actual price:      getResearchLeft(chosen tech)

A more expensive technology that the player has already mostly researched can have a
much LOWER actual espionage cost than the lower-full-cost technology selected by the
helper.

CURRENT HUMAN CALLER — THIS IS AN ACTION-AVAILABILITY BUG, NOT ONLY A DISPLAY BUG
CvDLLButtonPopup::launchDoEspionagePopup constructs the first espionage mission popup.
For every active mission, including two-phase missions, it first calls:

    canDoEspionageMission(eLoopMission, target, plot, -1, pUnit)

and skips the mission entirely if that returns false.

For ESPIONAGEMISSION_BUY_TECH, -1 is NO_TECH. canDoEspionageMission therefore reaches
the generic cost path above. Its default bCheckPoints is true, so after calculating the
generic mission cost it requires current espionage points to be at least that cost.

Only AFTER the player is allowed to choose the first-phase "Steal Technology" button
does CvDLLButtonPopup::launchDoEspionageTargetPopup iterate every technology and call:

    canDoEspionageMission(..., eLoopTech, pSpyUnit)

for each specific target. Those specific calls correctly price each technology using its
own getResearchLeft(eLoopTech).

Thus the first-phase generic gate can suppress access to a valid second-phase choice.

DETERMINISTIC CURRENT-DATA EXAMPLE
Current shipped XML keeps ESPIONAGEMISSION_BUY_TECH active with:

    iCost = 0
    bIsTwoPhases = 1
    bTargetsCity = 1
    TechPrereq = NONE
    iBuyTechCostFactor = 50

Current shipped technology data includes, for example:

    TECH_IRON_WORKING   iCost = 260, ERA_CLASSICAL, prereq Bronze Working
    TECH_PAPER          iCost = 425, ERA_CLASSICAL, prereqs Literature + Construction

A normal player can satisfy both prerequisite sets while knowing neither technology,
and an espionage target can know both. canStealTech merely requires the target team to
have the tech and our player still to be able to research it, so partial own research is
fully compatible with the technology remaining stealable.

Take a state where:
- both Iron Working and Paper are currently stealable from the target;
- our team has no meaningful progress on Iron Working;
- our team has partially researched Paper until Paper has only a small amount left;
- current espionage points lie between the resulting specific Paper steal cost and the
  resulting Iron Working steal cost.

Because current SAS has the relevant groundbreaking penalties disabled and both example
techs are in the same era, their normal full-cost ordering follows the XML ordering:
Iron Working is the lower-full-cost candidate. getStealCostTech therefore returns Iron
Working.

Yet the actual Buy Tech base formula is 150% of RESEARCH LEFT (base cost 0 and factor
50). If, illustratively, Paper has only 25 research points left while Iron Working still
has its much larger remainder, Paper's specific pre-location cost is tiny compared with
Iron Working's. The team-size adjustment and espionage mission modifier are the same
for both choices at the same spy/plot/target; getEspionageMissionCostModifier does not
use iExtraData. The ordering therefore survives the common modifiers.

Choose current EP in that interval:

    specific Paper cost <= EP < generic-selected Iron Working cost

Then:
1. Paper is a legal, affordable steal target.
2. The first espionage popup evaluates Buy Tech with iExtraData=-1.
3. getStealCostTech selects Iron Working from full cost.
4. Generic cost is computed from Iron Working's larger research LEFT.
5. canDoEspionageMission returns false because EP is below that representative cost.
6. launchDoEspionagePopup skips the entire Steal Technology button.
7. The second popup is never reached, so its correct specific Paper affordability check
   cannot rescue the action.

The human is therefore prevented from performing a legal, currently affordable
espionage mission solely because generic candidate selection still uses the old metric.

SECOND CURRENT CONSUMER — FOREIGN ADVISOR MISREPRESENTATION
Current CvForeignAdvisor.py also uses the same generic pair:

    getEspionageMissionCost(..., -1)
    getStealCostTech(target)

for the active mission row. It can therefore display the wrong representative technology
and a non-minimal cost under the same partial-research state. This is secondary to the
blocked gameplay action but confirms the helper is intended to represent generic steal
cost information.

AI CONTROL — DO NOT OVERSTATE THE SCOPE
Current CvUnitAI::AI_bestPlotEspionage does NOT rely on getStealCostTech for Buy Tech.
When getBuyTechCostFactor() > 0 it iterates every technology ID and prices each specific
candidate with the acting Spy. Therefore F484's direct availability failure is a human
first-popup / generic-cost contract bug, plus advisor representation; do not describe it
as the same AI target-selection defect as F349.

SIBLING CONTRACT CONTROL
Other two-phase generic target families reinforce the intended contract rather than
weakening the finding:
- switch-civic generic cost explicitly loops all forceable civics and keeps iMinCost;
- switch-religion generic cost explicitly loops all forceable religions and keeps
  iMinCost;
- destroy-project / destroy-building generic branches choose the cheapest currently
  valid target using the same production metric that their specific price formula uses.

The generic first-phase price is therefore supposed to stand in for an actually usable
cheap target. Buy Tech became inconsistent only because advc.120i changed the specific
price metric after the generic candidate-selection logic had been factored out.

ANCESTRY
Civ4CE/BtS and K-Mod keep the entire Buy Tech generic selection inside
getEspionageMissionBaseCost. In both lineages:
- the NO_TECH scan chooses the stealable technology with minimum getResearchCost;
- the chosen/specific technology is also priced with getResearchCost.

The selection metric and pricing metric therefore agree in those ancestors.

AdvCiv introduces two relevant changes retained by current SAS:
1. advc.120d extracts the old generic scan into getStealCostTech, still minimizing
   getResearchCost;
2. advc.120i changes actual mission pricing to getResearchLeft with the explicit comment
   "Count own progress".

The integration failed to update the extracted generic helper to the new metric. This is
best classified as an AdvCiv-origin regression inherited by SAS, not a vanilla/K-Mod bug
and not an SAS-local regression.

SEMANTIC DUPLICATE PROOF
The reconciled C031-WIP209 album contains no earlier finding owning getStealCostTech or
this full-cost-vs-research-left generic gate. In fact, the prior Queue-004 cursor
explicitly named getStealCostTech/getEspionageMissionBaseCost as the next unclosed path.

Keep F484 separate from:
- F315 / KI#638: selection-bound modal popups can rebind to a replacement unit/group
  after K-Mod Rapid Unit Cycling. F315 is launch-time ACTOR/TARGET identity loss. F484
  occurs with a perfectly stable Spy/selection and is a generic COST/AVAILABILITY metric
  mismatch before the first target popup is even opened.
- F348 / KI#671: AI_espionageVal's unitless current-EP gate defeats AI save-for-later
  valuation and stationary discounts. F348 is an AI valuation/context contract. F484 is
  the human first-popup generic technology-choice metric after partial research.
- F349 / KI#672: AI_doCommerce reuses one tech-theft accumulator across rival targets.
  F349 is AI strategic target-state contamination. F484 neither shares that state nor
  depends on AI_doCommerce.

REPAIR DIRECTION
The smallest coherent repair is to make getStealCostTech minimize the same quantity that
Buy Tech actually prices now:

    int iCost = GET_TEAM(getTeam()).getResearchLeft(eLoopTech);

rather than getResearchCost(eLoopTech).

That makes the helper return the cheapest current steal target under advc.120i and keeps
the Foreign Advisor's representative technology consistent with its displayed generic
cost.

A more structural alternative is for the NO_TECH Buy Tech branch to iterate all
stealable technologies and directly take the minimum base mission cost, matching the
switch-civic / switch-religion generic pattern. But because getStealCostTech is also a
current Python/UI helper, updating its metric is the simpler coherent fix unless some
caller intentionally needs "lowest full tech cost" semantics. Current callers found are
only the generic C++ mission-cost branch and the Foreign Advisor row, both of which want
cost representation rather than an abstract full-cost ranking.

NUMBERING
F484 / KI#807 CONFIRMED.
F485 / provisional KI#808 is now UNUSED.

and the other current two-phase target families compute a generic minimum using the same
metric as their specific prices. This makes the mismatch sharply localized rather than a
general "two-phase espionage uses arbitrary target" issue.

F485 / KI#808 — ADVANCED START UNIT/ROUTE REMOVAL FALLBACKS CAN DESTROY ANOTHER
PLAYER'S UNIT OR ROUTE AFTER THE INITIAL PLOT-AWARE VALIDATION HAS ALREADY FAILED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED current supported gameplay root.

The destructive fallback contract is inherited from stock BtS through K-Mod and Base
AdvCiv. AdvCiv partially hardened the unit fallback under `kekm.11` by preserving the
plot in its second cost query, but it still kills the unit after that query reports
`-1`. The route fallback remains the stock no-plot form and therefore bypasses the
ownership test completely. Current SAS retains both branches.

ROOT — THE UI EXPOSES REMOVAL ON REVEALED FOREIGN PLOTS
-------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS's repository manifest contains its tracked `Assets/Python/Screens` files but
contains no `CvWorldBuilderScreen.py`. It therefore does not override the BtS Advanced
Start screen; the supplied Civ4CE/BtS reconstruction provides the inherited screen.

`CvWorldBuilderScreen.removeObject()` first requires only that the clicked plot be
REVEALED to the active team. For the Unit tab it then sends, without an owner check:

    sendAdvancedStartAction(ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_UNIT,
        currentPlayer, plotX, plotY, selectedUnitType, false)

For the Route list it likewise sends, without an owner check:

    sendAdvancedStartAction(ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_ROUTE,
        currentPlayer, plotX, plotY, selectedRouteType, false)

This lack of Python-side ownership filtering is not itself enough to be a bug: the DLL
cost helpers deliberately own authoritative validation. In fact the same Python screen
performs explicit owner checks before removing population/buildings, and entirely
disables City and Visibility removal with comments warning about exploits. Unit and
Route therefore reach the DLL and depend on its plot-aware validators.

CURRENT SUPPORTED MULTIPLAYER/HOTSEAT PRODUCER
----------------------------------------------
The state does not require WorldBuilder or a forged network message.

Advanced Start is per-player state. `CvGame::update` automatically re-enters Advanced
Start whenever the newly active player still has nonnegative Advanced Start points:

    if (getActivePlayer() != NO_PLAYER &&
        GET_PLAYER(getActivePlayer()).getAdvancedStartPoints() >= 0 &&
        !UI.isInAdvancedStart())
    {
        UI.setInAdvancedStart(true);
        UI.setWorldBuilder(true);
    }

Thus a supported Hotseat / sequential-multiplayer sequence can have human A complete
part of its Advanced Start setup, then human B become active and perform B's own
Advanced Start while A's already-created city, units and routes remain ordinary map
state.

B can purchase Visibility outward until A's relevant plot is revealed. The inherited
`removeObject` condition is merely `isRevealed(activeTeam,false)`, so the foreign plot
then becomes a legal UI input to the Unit/Route removal messages above.

MANIFESTATION A — FOREIGN UNIT DELETION
---------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::getAdvancedStartUnitCost(eUnit,false,pPlot)` correctly enforces ownership.
With the default city-placement form it requires an own city:

    pCity = pPlot->getPlotCity();
    if (pCity == NULL || pCity->getOwner() != getID())
        return -1;

If units-outside-cities is enabled instead, it still requires:

    if (pPlot->getOwner() != getID())
        return -1;

Therefore any attempted Advanced Start removal on another player's city/plot produces
`iCost == -1`, exactly as intended.

But `doAdvancedStartAction(ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_UNIT)` treats negative cost specially
only for ADD actions:

    int iCost = getAdvancedStartUnitCost(eUnit, bAdd, pPlot);
    if (bAdd && iCost < 0)
        return;

On REMOVE, a negative initial cost skips the matching-unit loop and enters the fallback:

    CLLNode<IDInfo>* pNode = pPlot->headUnitNode();
    if (pNode != NULL)
    {
        CvUnit* pUnit = ::getUnit(pNode->m_data);
        iCost = getAdvancedStartUnitCost(pUnit->getUnitType(), false, pPlot); // kekm.11
        FAssertMsg(iCost != -1, "Trying to delete a unit which shouldn't exist");
        pUnit->kill(false);
        changeAdvancedStartPoints(iCost);
    }

On a foreign plot the second, actual-unit cost is STILL `-1`, because `kekm.11`
correctly preserved `pPlot`. The code merely asserts. In an ordinary release DLL the
assertion does not protect execution: `pUnit->kill(false)` still deletes the foreign
unit and `changeAdvancedStartPoints(-1)` merely charges the attacker one Advanced Start
point.

This is an unusually clear validation/execution contradiction: the authoritative cost
API says the unit MUST NOT be removable, the source assertion explicitly recognizes
that state as invalid, and the release branch performs the destructive action anyway.

DETERMINISTIC UNIT REPRODUCTION
-------------------------------
1. Start a supported two-human Hotseat game with Advanced Start enabled and enough
   points (a later start era makes the setup especially easy).
2. Human A founds a city, buys exactly one unit in it, finishes Advanced Start and then
   proceeds until human B becomes active.
3. B founds B's own required first city and uses Advanced Start Visibility purchases to
   reveal A's city.
4. B opens the Unit tab, selects any unit entry available in B's palette and right-clicks
   A's revealed city.
5. Stock `CvWorldBuilderScreen.removeObject` sends UNIT / bAdd=false without checking
   ownership.
6. B's initial plot-aware unit cost is `-1` because A owns the city.
7. The fallback obtains A's sole unit, recomputes its plot-aware removal cost, again gets
   `-1`, hits only the debug assertion, and calls `kill(false)` anyway.
8. A's unit is permanently removed. In release, B also loses 1 Advanced Start point.

The selected unit type need not equal A's unit type. The fallback exists specifically
for the case where the requested type was not accepted/found and deletes the first unit
on the plot.

MANIFESTATION B — FOREIGN ROUTE DELETION + BOGUS REFUND
-------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::getAdvancedStartRouteCost(eRoute,false,pPlot)` likewise correctly requires:

    if (pPlot->getRouteType() != eRoute)
        return -1;
    ...
    if (pPlot->getOwner() != getID())
        return -1;

However the Route removal fallback loses the plot entirely:

    int iCost = getAdvancedStartRouteCost(eRoute, bAdd, pPlot);
    ...
    if (pPlot->getRouteType() != eRoute)
    {
        eRoute = pPlot->getRouteType();
        iCost = getAdvancedStartRouteCost(eRoute, bAdd); // pPlot omitted
    }
    if (iCost < 0)
        return;
    pPlot->setRouteType(NO_ROUTE);
    changeAdvancedStartPoints(iCost);

When `pPlot == NULL`, the helper cannot perform the route-presence or plot-owner checks.
The fallback therefore converts an initially invalid foreign/mismatched request into a
positive generic refund and then mutates the original foreign plot.

Current SAS has exactly the convenient pair needed for a deterministic reproduction:
`ROUTE_ROAD` and `ROUTE_RAILROAD`. At Normal speed, Road's current base Advanced Start
cost 12 with `ADVANCED_START_WORKER_BUILD_MODIFIER = 67` becomes 8 points before any
zero cost-increase (12 * 67 / 100 truncates to 8; Normal BuildPercent and speed are
100%).

DETERMINISTIC ROUTE REPRODUCTION
--------------------------------
1. Use a Modern Advanced Start Hotseat game so both humans know the ordinary Road and
   Railroad enabling technologies and both route entries are straightforwardly
   available.
2. Human A founds a city and buys a Road on an owned non-city plot, then later human B
   becomes active for B's Advanced Start.
3. B founds B's city and purchases visibility until A's Road plot is revealed.
4. B selects RAILROAD in the Advanced Start Route list, then right-clicks A's ROAD.
5. Python sends `ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_ROUTE(..., ROUTE_RAILROAD, false)` with no owner
   precheck.
6. The initial plot-aware query returns `-1` because the actual route is Road rather than
   Railroad (and the plot is foreign in any case).
7. The fallback replaces `eRoute` with the actual Road but calls
   `getAdvancedStartRouteCost(ROAD,false)` WITHOUT `pPlot`.
8. The generic Road cost is positive because B knows the Road technology.
9. `setRouteType(NO_ROUTE)` deletes A's Road even though B does not own the plot.
10. B receives the positive Road refund (8 points under the Normal-speed current values
    above) despite never having purchased that route.

If B selects the same route type as the foreign plot, the initial plot-aware cost stays
negative and the later `if(iCost < 0) return` protects the route. The exploit therefore
specifically uses the stock fallback's advertised purpose: replace a mismatching
selected route type with the route actually present. Current two-route data makes that
state ordinary rather than hypothetical.

PAIRED CONTROL — IMPROVEMENT REMOVAL DOES THIS CORRECTLY
--------------------------------------------------------
The adjacent Improvement branch demonstrates the intended safe fallback contract:

    if (pPlot->getImprovementType() != eImprovement)
    {
        eImprovement = pPlot->getImprovementType();
        iCost = getAdvancedStartImprovementCost(eImprovement, bAdd, pPlot);
    }
    if (iCost < 0)
        return;
    pPlot->setImprovementType(NO_IMPROVEMENT);

It preserves `pPlot`, then ACTUALLY ABORTS on negative validation before mutation.
Foreign Improvement removal therefore remains blocked. This paired branch is strong
local evidence that Unit/Route are implementation defects rather than an intentional
policy permitting removal of arbitrary revealed foreign assets.

ANCESTRY
--------
Stock BtS/Civ4CE already contains both unsafe fallback structures.

UNIT:
- stock/K-Mod first use a plot-aware cost;
- if that fails or the selected type is absent, they pick the first unit;
- they then recompute `getAdvancedStartUnitCost(actualType,false)` WITHOUT `pPlot`;
- the generic removal query has no owner/presence context, so it can return a positive
  refund for a foreign unit;
- they assert, kill and refund.

Base AdvCiv's `kekm.11` changes that second unit query to:

    getAdvancedStartUnitCost(actualType, false, pPlot)

This is a genuine partial hardening: the foreign target now produces `-1` instead of a
positive generic refund. But the caller still treats the assertion as if it were a
runtime guard. It never checks the negative result before `kill(false)`. Current SAS
therefore inherits unauthorized foreign-unit deletion with a 1-point attacker charge
instead of stock's unauthorized deletion plus refund.

ROUTE:
The no-plot fallback is unchanged across Civ4CE/BtS, K-Mod, Base AdvCiv and current
SAS. All retain the plot-aware initial cost, then generic no-plot cost after replacing a
mismatching requested route with the actual route.

The best attribution is consequently an inherited Firaxis/BtS Advanced Start destructive
fallback bug, with AdvCiv partially but incompletely repairing the unit half.

CURRENT SAS UI / REPOSITORY PROOF
---------------------------------
The current light-source snapshot's `_SNAPSHOT_CONTEXT/repo_file_manifest.txt` lists the
tracked Python Screens and does not contain `Assets/Python/Screens/CvWorldBuilderScreen.py`.
Current SAS therefore has no mod-level replacement for this screen in the repository.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 likewise ships no `CvWorldBuilderScreen.py`, leaving the stock BtS
screen in effect through the normal asset fallback chain. The supplied Civ4CE/BtS file
is therefore the appropriate local control for the live UI producer.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
The full reconciled C031-WIP209 album was searched for the exact fallback comments,
assertion text, Advanced Start unit removal, foreign-unit removal, foreign-route removal
and route-refund wording. No existing F/KI owns this destructive removal contract.

Keep F485 distinct from:
- F440/KI#763 and F441/KI#764: Advanced Start military-cap help/generic-availability
  mismatches. Those affect ADD availability, not destructive removal or ownership.
- F472/KI#795: Advanced Start route ADD ignores Railroad's Coal/Oil prerequisite. F472
  creates a route on the acting player's plot; F485 removes another player's route
  after failed plot-aware validation.
- rejected F084/F085/F088: dormant technology-refund backend paths with no shipped
  removal UI. F485 has an explicit stock right-click UI producer for Unit and Route.
- the current post-WIP211 city/visibility refund leads: stock UI explicitly disables City
  and Visibility removal, so those remain backend-only and are not folded into F485.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR
-------------------
Preserve the UI convenience of resolving the actual asset when the selected palette type
is not what the clicked plot contains, but make the substituted target pass the SAME
plot-aware validation before destructive mutation.

Unit direction:

    CvUnit* pUnit = resolve intended matching unit / fallback first unit;
    if (pUnit == NULL)
        return;
    iCost = getAdvancedStartUnitCost(pUnit->getUnitType(), false, pPlot);
    if (iCost < 0)
        return;
    pUnit->kill(false);
    changeAdvancedStartPoints(iCost);

The runtime guard must exist even in assertion-enabled builds; `FAssertMsg` is diagnostic,
not authorization.

Route direction:

    if (pPlot->getRouteType() != eRoute)
        eRoute = pPlot->getRouteType();
    iCost = getAdvancedStartRouteCost(eRoute, false, pPlot);
    if (iCost < 0)
        return;
    pPlot->setRouteType(NO_ROUTE);
    changeAdvancedStartPoints(iCost);

Do not omit `pPlot` from the fallback recomputation.

Defense in depth could also add Python-side owner checks for Unit/Route removal, matching
Population/Building, but DLL validation should remain authoritative because network/API
callers can bypass Python.

POST-WIP212 ADVANCED START REMOVE-SIBLING CLOSURES
---------------------------------------------------
The remaining removal/refund siblings were finished before leaving Advanced Start.
They do NOT broaden F485 and do not consume F486.

1. Population add/remove cost is transactionally symmetric at the same population step.
   The add cost from population N uses the growth threshold for N and the current
   cost-increase term based on the pre-purchase population. Removal from N+1 decrements
   the test population to N before computing the refund and reaches the same terms.
   No buy-low/refund-high arithmetic mismatch was established.

2. Building removal retains an authoritative owner boundary and dependency checks.
   The concrete city must belong to the acting player; free start-era buildings are not
   refundable; dependent currently-owned buildings can block removal. The action does
   not share F485's validate-one-target / mutate-fallback-target structure.

3. Culture removal remains intentionally unavailable through the stock Advanced Start
   screen. There is no ordinary shipped UI producer to turn the backend's generic remove
   support into a current gameplay root.

4. Advanced Start initialization itself does not grant ordinary free starting units and
   then expose them to a refund. `initFreeUnits` supplies Advanced Start points and the
   setup visibility package; normal free starting-unit creation belongs to the
   non-Advanced-Start branch. No free-unit-refund sibling survives.

5. `CvPlayer::disbandUnit` was then re-read at normal-turn depth. Its destructive
   eligibility boundaries remain coherent: cargo / Golden-Age / zero-production-cost
   exclusions and the sole military-happiness protection are explicit. The remaining
   candidate-ordering questions are policy/valuation, not a violated authoritative
   state invariant. Preserve the earlier Queue-004 closure; no F486 there.


F486 / KI#809 — RANDOM-EVENT REPLY VALIDATION TREATS A VANISHED UNIT TARGET AS
LEGAL, SO A UNIT-ONLY EVENT CAN BE RECORDED / GLOBALLY CONSUMED WITHOUT APPLYING
ANY OF ITS EFFECTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED. Current shipped random-event data plus supported simultaneous multiplayer
produce the defect without malformed packets, WorldBuilder-only data or a mod-mod.

The source root is inherited unchanged from stock BtS through K-Mod, Base AdvCiv 1.14
and current AdvCiv-SAS.

ROOT — UNIT TARGET EXISTENCE IS OPTIONAL AT REPLY-TIME VALIDATION
---------------------------------------------------------------
A human random event stores its concrete target unit as the player-local ID in
`EventTriggeredData::m_iUnitId`.

`CvPlayer::canDoEvent` performs strict existence checks for concrete city effects:

    if (kEvent.isCityEffect())
    {
        CvCity* pCity = getCity(kTriggeredData.m_iCityId);
        if (pCity == NULL || !pCity->canApplyEvent(eEvent, kTriggeredData))
            return false;
    }

and likewise rejects a missing other-player city.

The concrete unit path is materially weaker:

    CvUnit* pUnit = getUnit(kTriggeredData.m_iUnitId);
    if (pUnit != NULL && !pUnit->canApplyEvent(eEvent))
        return false;

If the stored target unit no longer exists, `pUnit == NULL` simply skips the test and
`canDoEvent` continues as though the unit portion were valid.

This is not merely a loose helper contract. `applyEvent` re-runs `canDoEvent` on the
synchronized reply path and then later applies the unit-local effect only when that same
ID still resolves:

    CvUnit* pUnit = getUnit(pTriggeredData->m_iUnitId);
    if (pUnit != NULL)
    {
        FAssert(pUnit->canApplyEvent(eEvent));
        pUnit->applyEvent(eEvent);
    }

So the two layers together encode the problematic state explicitly:

    missing stored target unit
        -> canDoEvent says YES
        -> event bookkeeping / non-unit effects proceed
        -> unit-local effect is silently skipped

CURRENT CLEAN REPRODUCER — `AT THE SWORD`
-----------------------------------------
Current shipped `CIV4EventTriggerInfos.xml` gives a particularly unambiguous event:

    EVENTTRIGGER_AT_THE_SWORD
        bSinglePlayer = 0
        iPercentGamesActive = 100
        iWeight = 500
        bRecurring = 0
        bGlobal = 1
        iNumUnits = 1
        UnitsRequired = UNITCLASS_SWORDSMAN
        iUnitDamagedWeight = 1
        iUnitDistanceWeight = 0
        iUnitExperienceWeight = 0
        bShowPlot = 1

`CvUnit::getTriggerValue` makes the damaged-unit requirement authoritative:

    if (getDamage() == 0 && kTrigger.getUnitDamagedWeight() > 0)
        return MIN_INT;

and restricts the class through `UnitsRequired`. Thus the stored target is a concrete,
living, DAMAGED Swordsman when the trigger is constructed.

The sole event outcome is:

    EVENT_AT_THE_SWORD_1
        iGold = 0
        iUnitExperience = 3
        UnitName = TXT_KEY_EVENT_UNIT_AT_THE_SWORD
        bDisbandUnit = 0

There are no independent gold/city/empire/tech effects that could justify applying a
partial result after the target disappears. Its runtime substance is unit-local.

`CvUnit::applyEvent` handles `iUnitExperience` by:

    setDamage(0);
    changeExperience(kEvent.getUnitExperience());

and applies the event unit name as well. Consequently the outcome's concrete effects
are: fully heal the stored damaged Swordsman, grant +3 XP and give it the event name.
(The hidden-heal help omission is already separately owned by F414 / KI#737; do not
merge that UI root with F486.)

SUPPORTED POPUP / DISAPPEARANCE WINDOW
--------------------------------------
Current player-turn ordering gives random events a genuine delayed-decision lifetime.
`CvPlayer::doTurn` explicitly documents that it runs at the end of a human turn and
calls `doEvents()` near the end of that sequence. For a human, `trigger(kData)` queues:

    CvPopupInfo(BUTTONPOPUP_EVENT, kData.getID())

rather than applying an outcome immediately.

The earlier Queue-019 F307 archaeology already established the ordinary lifecycle:
random events are generated at the end of a human player's turn and their choice popup
can be handled later. More importantly for F486, after the popup has actually launched,
it remains an ordinary modal human choice until the player answers it.

Current `EVENTTRIGGER_AT_THE_SWORD` explicitly has `bSinglePlayer=0`, so it is enabled
in multiplayer. Under supported simultaneous turns, another human can continue issuing
synchronized game actions while the local event popup is unanswered. This is the same
class of supported modal/remote-action timing already proved independently for F315;
no fabricated UI mutation is required.

A damaged Swordsman chosen by the trigger can therefore remain in an exposed combat
position. A remote enemy can kill that exact Swordsman after the event popup is shown
but before its owner clicks the sole outcome.

DETERMINISTIC CONTROL-FLOW REPRODUCTION
---------------------------------------
Use a simultaneous-multiplayer game with random events enabled and a player owning a
currently eligible damaged Swordsman.

1. `EVENTTRIGGER_AT_THE_SWORD` fires for player A and stores Swordsman S's player-local
   unit ID in `m_iUnitId`.
2. The normal human `BUTTONPOPUP_EVENT` is launched and displays its sole At the Sword
   outcome while S is still alive.
3. Leave the modal unanswered.
4. Remote player B attacks and kills S through ordinary synchronized combat while the
   simultaneous turn remains live.
5. A now clicks the already-displayed At the Sword outcome.
6. `CvMessageControl::sendEventTriggered` reaches the synchronized event receiver and
   `CvPlayer::applyEvent` for A's original trigger ID.
7. `applyEvent` calls `canDoEvent(EVENT_AT_THE_SWORD_1, oldTriggeredData)`.
8. `getUnit(old.m_iUnitId)` returns NULL. Because the condition is only
      `pUnit != NULL && !pUnit->canApplyEvent(...)`,
   missing S does NOT invalidate the event.
9. `applyEvent` calls `setTriggerFired` and `setEventOccured`, then runs the outcome.
10. When it reaches the unit block, `getUnit(old.m_iUnitId)` is still NULL, so healing,
    +3 XP and renaming are all skipped.

The player has therefore successfully "applied" a random-event outcome whose entire
runtime effect target no longer exists.

PERSISTENT / GLOBAL CONSEQUENCE
-------------------------------
This is stronger than a one-frame no-op.

`EVENTTRIGGER_AT_THE_SWORD` is both:

    bRecurring = 0
    bGlobal = 1

`applyEvent(..., bUpdateTrigger=true)` executes `setTriggerFired(*pTriggeredData, true)`
before applying the event's payload. `CvPlayer::setTriggerFired`, when the trigger is
global, propagates the fired state to every player slot.

Therefore the stale reply can globally consume the non-recurring At the Sword trigger
even though its target died and none of the event's advertised/runtime effects occurred.
The trigger will not later fire for a valid damaged Swordsman merely because the stale
popup produced no unit effect.

A second current-data manifestation exists through other unit-local event outcomes. For
example Toxcatl's second option combines `iGold=-65` with `iUnitImmobileTurns=3`. If its
stored unit disappears after popup launch, current validation can still charge the gold
while silently omitting the immobilization. At the Sword is the preferred proof because
its sole outcome is entirely unit-local and therefore avoids any ambiguity about a
partially meaningful non-unit remainder.

WHY F307 DOES NOT OWN THIS ROOT
-------------------------------
F307 / KI#630 concerns Base AdvCiv's `launchEventPopup` "revalidation" calling
`initTriggeredData` as a side-effectful constructor:
- it allocates/leaks a second EventTriggeredData;
- consumes synchronized RNG / runs construction hooks;
- validates some freshly rerolled trigger instance instead of the original queued one.

F486 survives independently AFTER the original popup has already launched with a valid,
live target. A unit can disappear during the unanswered modal's lifetime. No launch-time
pure-validator repair can prevent that later transition.

The synchronized reply path is supposed to provide the final safety net:
`applyEvent` deliberately re-resolves the old trigger ID and re-runs `canDoEvent` before
mutation. F486 is that receiver-side validator accepting a missing concrete unit target.

Likewise this is separate from F315 / KI#638. F315 concerns selection-bound modal actions
being rebound to a DIFFERENT current selection after Rapid Unit Cycling; the popup lacks
launch-time actor identity. Random-event EventTriggeredData DOES retain stable target
identity (`m_iUnitId`). F486 is instead the validator treating failure to resolve that
stored identity as permission to continue.

ANCESTRY
--------
The exact permissive unit-existence pattern is present in all supplied lineage controls:

Civ4CE/BtS:

    CvUnit* pUnit = getUnit(kTriggeredData.m_iUnitId);
    if (NULL != pUnit)
    {
        if (!pUnit->canApplyEvent(eEvent))
            return false;
    }

K-Mod 1.46 retains the same structure.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 condenses it to the current form:

    CvUnit* pUnit = getUnit(kTriggeredData.m_iUnitId);
    if (pUnit != NULL && !pUnit->canApplyEvent(eEvent))
        return false;

Current SAS retains that Base AdvCiv form unchanged in substance.

This is therefore an inherited Firaxis/BtS event reply-validation defect, not a SAS-local
regression.

DUPLICATE / ALBUM CONTROL
-------------------------
The reconciled album was searched for:
- `m_iUnitId` in random-event validation;
- missing / vanished event units;
- At the Sword target lifetime;
- event reply `canDoEvent` target existence.

No existing root owns this missing-target acceptance.

Related roots remain distinct:
- F307/KI#630: launch-time event re-randomization/state leak.
- F315/KI#638: selection-bound popup actor identity / Rapid Unit Cycling.
- F414/KI#737: At the Sword/Friendly Locals XP help omits the runtime full heal.
- existing event AI/value/count roots concern effect valuation or help/runtime amounts,
  not concrete target lifetime at synchronized reply.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR
-------------------
Do not globally require every EventTriggeredData with an old unit ID to retain a unit:
some triggers may pick a unit only as context while a particular event outcome has no
unit-local payload.

Instead make target existence part of legality whenever the chosen EventInfo actually
requires a concrete unit effect. A helper makes that contract explicit, e.g. treat the
event as unit-targeted when any of these are active:
- `bDisbandUnit`;
- nonzero `iUnitExperience`;
- nonzero `iUnitImmobileTurns`;
- nonempty `UnitPromotion`;
- nonempty `UnitName`;
- any other field whose runtime implementation is specifically applied through
  `pUnit->applyEvent` rather than globally.

Then:

    CvUnit* pUnit = getUnit(kTriggeredData.m_iUnitId);
    if (eventRequiresConcreteUnit(eEvent))
    {
        if (pUnit == NULL || !pUnit->canApplyEvent(eEvent))
            return false;
    }
    else if (pUnit != NULL && !pUnit->canApplyEvent(eEvent))
        return false; // preserve any intentional contextual validation

The exact helper should be derived from the fields consumed by `CvUnit::applyEvent` so
future unit-local XML additions cannot silently bypass the existence requirement.

The synchronized DLL-side `canDoEvent` check is the authoritative repair boundary; UI
popup cancellation/rebuild can improve presentation but cannot substitute for receiver
validation in multiplayer.

POST-WIP213 TARGET-LIFETIME / EVENT-STATE CONTROLS
--------------------------------------------------
Before spending F487, the remaining event-lifetime siblings were challenged against
current XML and the reconciled album.

1. Missing stored OTHER-player target remains below the numbered threshold.

   Several shipped multiplayer PickPlayer triggers can retain an `m_eOtherPlayer` that
   later dies. However the enabled event choices either revalidate through concrete
   city/network/war conditions, or mutate relationship / espionage state whose ordinary
   behavioral consequence disappears with the dead target. No current effect comparable
   to F486's consumed event with a missing required payload survived. Keep this as
   target-lifetime robustness debt only.

2. `checkExpireEvent`'s ObsoleteTech receiver is generically fragile but current-data safe.

   The function resolves the original trigger owner as:

       CvPlayer& kPlayer = GET_PLAYER(kTriggeredData.m_ePlayer);

   and uses `kPlayer` for the stored religion/civic/city/unit/other-player lifetime checks,
   but the later obsolete-tech loop asks `GET_TEAM(getTeam())` on `this` rather than
   `GET_TEAM(kPlayer.getTeam())`.

   That could matter if a copied team/global QUEST occurrence were expired on a recipient
   rather than the original trigger owner. Current SAS closes the producer: every shipped
   quest EventInfo has `bGlobal=0` and `bTeam=0`. Quest occurrence state is player-local,
   so current callers run the test on the original owner and the two team expressions are
   equivalent. No F487.

3. `setEventOccured` contains a real reversed Team-event propagation loop, but current XML
   has no Team EventInfo producer.

   Current source says:

       else if (GC.getInfo(eEvent).isTeam())
       {
           for (MemberIter itOtherMember(getTeam()); itOtherMember.hasNext(); ++itOtherMember)
           {
               if (itOtherMember->getID() != getID())
                   continue;
               itOtherMember->setEventOccured(eEvent, kEventTriggered, false);
           }
       }

   This retains self and skips every other teammate — the opposite of the Global branch's
   propagation shape. It is therefore real generic/moddability source debt. A mechanical
   parse of current `CIV4EventInfos.xml`, however, finds zero `<bTeam>1</bTeam>` EventInfos;
   current EventTriggerInfos likewise have no Team-trigger producer requiring this copied
   occurrence state. Do not number under the current-data rule.

4. Delayed-event countdown use-after-erase is an exact album duplicate and remains dormant.

   The source obtains a pointer to a value inside `m_mapEventCountdown`, applies the due
   event, erases that map node through `resetEventCountdown`, then dereferences the old
   pointer for cleanup. WIP209 already preserved this exact C++ lifetime defect and its
   BtS -> K-Mod -> AdvCiv ancestry. Current SAS has empty EventTimes tables and no ordinary
   producer of countdown nodes, so it remains dormant robustness debt rather than F487.

5. Global EventInfo ClearEvents propagation closes normally.

   `applyEvent` explicitly resets a cleared Global EventInfo occurrence on every
   non-Barbarian player and a Team EventInfo occurrence on every team member. Thus the
   ordinary ClearEvents path does not leave propagated global occurrence records stale on
   observer players merely because `resetEventOccured` itself is player-local.


F487 / KI#810 — APPLYEVENT MARKS A TRIGGER FIRED BEFORE REPLY-TIME EVENT VALIDATION,
SO A STALE INVALID HUMAN EVENT CHOICE CAN PERMANENTLY CONSUME A GLOBAL NON-RECURRING
TRIGGER WITHOUT APPLYING ANY EVENT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED. Ordinary current shipped simultaneous-multiplayer random-event flow reaches
this inherited Firaxis/BtS ordering defect. Current global/non-recurring city-targeted
events provide a direct permanent gameplay consequence.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayer::applyEvent` resolves the stored EventTriggeredData and, for an ordinary chosen
triggered event (`bUpdateTrigger=true`), performs these operations in this order:

    if (bUpdateTrigger)
        setTriggerFired(*pTriggeredData, true);

    if (!canDoEvent(eEvent, *pTriggeredData))
    {
        if (bUpdateTrigger)
            deleteEventTriggered(iEventTriggeredId);
        return;
    }

    setEventOccured(eEvent, *pTriggeredData);
    ... apply event payload ...

The durable trigger identity is therefore committed BEFORE the authoritative synchronized
reply-time legality check.

For a Global trigger, `setTriggerFired(..., true)` immediately propagates the fired state
through all player slots. For a non-recurring trigger, future trigger eligibility rejects
that trigger whenever `isTriggerFired(eTrigger)` is true. There is no rollback when the
subsequent `canDoEvent` call fails.

Consequently a stale choice can take the failure path in a contradictory state:

    trigger is permanently recorded as fired
    EventInfo occurrence is NOT recorded
    EventInfo payload is NOT applied
    triggered-data record is deleted

The trigger has been consumed even though the chosen event was rejected.

INTENT CONTROL — THE POPUP LAUNCHER ALREADY SAYS INVALID EVENTS MUST NOT COUNT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This is not merely a debatable interpretation of when a trigger should count as fired.
Current AdvCiv/SAS `CvDLLButtonPopup::launchEventPopup` performs a pre-display availability
pass over the same EventInfos. If no choice is legal, it executes:

    if (!bEventAvailable)
    {   // advc.001: Don't count this as having been triggered
        kActivePlayer.deleteEventTriggered(pTriggeredData->getID());
        return false;
    }

The comment makes the intended policy explicit: if current state invalidates every event
choice, cancel the pending instance WITHOUT counting the trigger as fired.

The synchronized reply path violates that same policy only because its transaction order
commits `setTriggerFired` before re-running `canDoEvent`.

CURRENT SHIPPED REPRODUCTION — HORTICULTURE
-------------------------------------------
Current `EVENTTRIGGER_HORTICULTURE` gives a compact live state:

    bSinglePlayer = 0
    iPercentGamesActive = 80
    iWeight = 200
    bRecurring = 0
    bGlobal = 1
    bPickCity = 1
    OrPreReq = TECH_CALENDAR
    requires one owned Forest/Jungle plot

Its selectable current EventInfos include `EVENT_HORTICULTURE_1` and
`EVENT_HORTICULTURE_2`; both are concrete own-city effects (`bPickCity=1`). The first
also applies +1 commerce to the selected plot, and the second has its own current city /
follow-up payload. Either provides an ordinary legal button while its stored city exists.

Use a simultaneous-turn multiplayer game in which human A has a Horticulture instance:

1. A's ordinary random-event flow constructs EventTriggeredData with a concrete
   `m_iCityId` and queues the Event popup.
2. `launchEventPopup` resolves that original instance and runs `canDoEvent` for its choices.
   With the city still alive, at least one Horticulture button is available and the popup
   is displayed.
3. A leaves the modal unanswered. Simultaneous multiplayer allows remote human B to keep
   acting while A's local popup waits — the same supported timing class already established
   for the F315/F486 popup-lifetime reproductions.
4. B captures A's selected Horticulture city before A clicks the still-visible event
   choice.

City acquisition gives an exact identity-lifetime proof. `CvPlayer::acquireCity` saves the
old owner-local city ID, then calls:

    pOldCity->kill(false, false);
    pOldCity = NULL;

before the acquiring player initializes its replacement city. Thus A's stored old
`m_iCityId` no longer resolves through `A.getCity(oldId)` after conquest.

5. A clicks the event button that was valid when the popup was rendered. The network event
   reply reaches synchronized `CvPlayer::applyEvent(..., bUpdateTrigger=true)`.
6. `applyEvent` FIRST calls `setTriggerFired`. Because Horticulture is Global, the fired
   state is propagated to every player slot.
7. `applyEvent` THEN calls `canDoEvent` on the stale triggered data. Horticulture's city
   event validation performs:

       CvCity* pCity = getCity(kTriggeredData.m_iCityId);
       if (pCity == NULL || !pCity->canApplyEvent(...))
           return false;

   A's old city is gone, so this correctly returns false.
8. `applyEvent` deletes the triggered-data object and returns BEFORE `setEventOccured` and
   before any Horticulture payload executes.
9. Nevertheless Horticulture's durable global trigger-fired bit remains set. Because the
   trigger is non-recurring, future `getEventTriggerWeight` / event eligibility rejects it
   for the rest of the game.

The result is therefore not merely a stale popup no-op. A current global event that never
actually occurred has been permanently removed from the event pool for every player.

BROADER CURRENT SURFACE
-----------------------
Horticulture is only a deterministic current example. Current SAS contains many active,
multiplayer-enabled, Global, non-recurring triggers with stored city/player/unit context.
Any state change between popup rendering and synchronized reply that makes the chosen
EventInfo fail `canDoEvent` enters the same commit-before-validation ordering.

City capture/destruction is especially clean because `canDoEvent` already has the correct
strict missing-city rejection. F487 does not depend on F486's separate missing-unit
acceptance bug.

ANCESTRY
--------
The exact order is present in every supplied lineage control:

Civ4CE/BtS:

    if (bUpdateTrigger)
        setTriggerFired(*pTriggeredData, true);
    if (!canDoEvent(eEvent, *pTriggeredData)) ...

K-Mod 1.46 retains the same order.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same order.
Current AdvCiv-SAS retains it unchanged in substance.

This is therefore an inherited Firaxis/BtS event transaction-ordering defect, not a
SAS-local regression.

AdvCiv later added stronger popup-launch revalidation (`advc.001` / practical 4304
history, already investigated under F307), but did not change the synchronized
`applyEvent` ordering. The newer launcher comment provides especially strong evidence
that a now-invalid instance is intended to be cancelled without counting as fired.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
The reconciled album was searched for `setTriggerFired`, stale event choices, failed
`canDoEvent`, and trigger consumption. No existing root owns this commit-before-validation
ordering.

Keep related findings separate:

- F307 / KI#630: AdvCiv's popup LAUNCH revalidation incorrectly calls the state-creating /
  randomizing `initTriggeredData`, leaking a second record and touching SyncRand.
- F486 / KI#809: reply-time `canDoEvent` treats a MISSING REQUIRED UNIT as legal, so a
  unit-targeted event can be recorded/applied while its unit payload silently no-ops.
- F487 / KI#810: `canDoEvent` CAN CORRECTLY REJECT the stale instance, but the trigger was
  already durably marked fired before that rejection.
- F475 / KI#798: midgame new-player initialization reconstructs durable global trigger
  state from short-lived EventInfo occurrence records and can forget an OLD truly-fired
  trigger. F487 is the opposite transaction problem: it creates a durable fired flag for
  an event that DID NOT pass execution validation.

The roots require different repairs and produce different state shapes.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR
-------------------
Make the reply transaction validate before committing trigger-fired state:

    EventTriggeredData* pTriggeredData = getEventTriggered(iEventTriggeredId);
    if (pTriggeredData == NULL)
        return;

    if (!canDoEvent(eEvent, *pTriggeredData))
    {
        if (bUpdateTrigger)
            deleteEventTriggered(iEventTriggeredId);
        return;
    }

    if (bUpdateTrigger)
        setTriggerFired(*pTriggeredData, true);

    setEventOccured(eEvent, *pTriggeredData);
    ...

This preserves the existing semantics for valid event choices while making reply-time
stale cancellation agree with `launchEventPopup`'s explicit "Don't count this as having
been triggered" contract.

Do not try to repair F487 solely in `CvDLLButtonPopup`: event replies are synchronized
network actions and must remain safe even if a stale or custom caller reaches the DLL.
`CvPlayer::applyEvent` is the authoritative transaction boundary.

F486's missing-unit validation still requires its independent repair. Reordering F487
alone would not help F486 because its current `canDoEvent` incorrectly returns true when
the required unit is gone.

REGRESSION TEST
---------------
1. Create a valid human Global, non-recurring city event such as Horticulture.
2. Preserve its triggered-data ID and verify the chosen EventInfo is currently legal.
3. Remove/capture the stored city before executing the event reply.
4. Assert `canDoEvent(event, oldData) == false`.
5. Execute the stale reply.
6. Assert the trigger is NOT marked fired for the owner or propagated global recipients.
7. Assert no EventInfo occurrence is recorded and no payload is applied.
8. Positive control: with the city still valid, execute the same event and assert normal
   trigger-fired propagation + EventInfo occurrence + payload.
9. Repeat with F486's missing-unit At-the-Sword case after that independent validator fix,
   confirming that both stale-target families now cancel before trigger commitment.
