POST-F489 MESSAGE-LIFETIME CONTROLS
------------------------------------
The retained-message subsystem was re-extracted directly from the supplied September-1
SAS source and compared with supplied Base AdvCiv 1.14, K-Mod 1.46 and Civ4CE/BtS.

* `showMessageCopies` does not create an earlier independent use-after-free. In
  `postProcessMessages`, the major-message display and HotSeat-missed-message display are
  `if` / `else if`; a doubly-classified message is shown through only one container
  before the common cleanup.
* reset, AI-Auto-Play and turn-activation cleanup all call the same
  `clearMessageCopies()` owner cleanup. They are additional detonation sites for F490,
  not separate ownership producers.
* copied HotSeat INFO/MINOR messages are deliberately constructed with
  `MESSAGE_TYPE_MAJOR_EVENT` for retained display. No authoritative state or independent
  heap-lifetime failure was established from that type substitution.
* the earlier `postProcessMessages` `getCurrentResearch()==NO_TECH` completion-message
  proxy remains a live Turn-Log counting heuristic edge, but not an ownership defect and
  not promoted here.


F490 / KI#813 -- ADVC HOTSEAT MISSED-MESSAGE SUPPORT STORES THE SAME
`CvTalkingHeadMessage*` IN TWO OWNING VECTORS; COMMON CLEANUP DELETES IT TWICE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED. Ordinary sequential HotSeat play can produce the exact alias. Base AdvCiv
1.14 and current SAS contain the same ownership logic. Supplied K-Mod 1.46 and
Civ4CE/BtS do not contain the extra retained-message owning vectors.

OWNERSHIP ROOT
--------------
Current SAS `CvPlayer::addMessage` computes:

    bool const bMissedMsg = (kGame.isHotSeat() && isActive() &&
            (eMessage == MESSAGE_TYPE_MINOR_EVENT ||
             eMessage == MESSAGE_TYPE_MAJOR_EVENT ||
             eMessage == MESSAGE_TYPE_INFO));

    if (eMessage == MESSAGE_TYPE_MAJOR_EVENT || bMissedMsg)
    {
        CvTalkingHeadMessage* pCopy = new CvTalkingHeadMessage(...);
        if (eMessage == MESSAGE_TYPE_MAJOR_EVENT)
            m_aMajorMsgs.push_back(pCopy);
        if (bMissedMsg)
            m_aHotSeatMsgs.push_back(pCopy);
    }

For a HotSeat `MESSAGE_TYPE_MAJOR_EVENT` delivered while the recipient is still the
active UI player, both predicates are true. ONE heap allocation is inserted into both:

    m_aMajorMsgs
    m_aHotSeatMsgs

Both vectors are subsequently treated as owners.

DELETION ROOT
-------------
The default cleanup independently clears both vectors:

    clearMessageCopies(&m_aMajorMsgs);
    clearMessageCopies(&m_aHotSeatMsgs);

and each concrete clear does:

    for (...)
        SAFE_DELETE((*pContainer)[i]);
    pContainer->clear();

`SAFE_DELETE` nulls only the element in the vector currently being traversed. The other
vector contains a distinct raw-pointer slot holding the same address. The first owner
therefore deletes the allocation; the second owner later calls delete on that same
allocation again.

This is direct raw-pointer double ownership and double deletion / heap corruption.

ORDINARY HOTSEAT REACHABILITY
-----------------------------
The `isActive()` part of `bMissedMsg` is reachable in the exact local HotSeat window the
workaround is intended to cover.

Current `CvPlayer::isActive()` is simply:

    GC.getInitCore().getActivePlayer() == getID()

Current `CvPlayer::doTurn()` sets:

    if (!kGame.isNetworkMultiPlayer())
        kGame.setInBetweenTurns(true);

when the just-finished local/sequential turn enters between-turn processing.

Current `CvPlayer::setTurnActive(true)` changes `ActivePlayer` for HotSeat/PBEM only when
the NEWLY activated participant is HUMAN:

    if ((kGame.isHotSeat() || kGame.isPbem()) && isHuman() && bDoTurn)
        kGame.setActivePlayer(getID());

Thus in a normal order Human H0 -> AI A -> Human H1:

1. H0 ends its turn; local `doTurn` sets `inBetweenTurns=true`.
2. AI A becomes turn-active.
3. A is not human, so activation does NOT replace the UI ActivePlayer.
4. H0 remains `isActive()==true` while A acts.
5. A generates a global major event addressed to H0.
6. H0's `addMessage` sees HotSeat + active H0 + between-turn processing + MAJOR_EVENT.
7. The early `if (!isInBetweenTurns() && isActive()) return` does not fire.
8. The same `pCopy` enters both owning vectors.

CURRENT ORDINARY PRODUCER
-------------------------
No debug/Python malformed message is required. Current `CvGame::setHolyCity` loops all
major-civilization observers and sends:

    MESSAGE_TYPE_MAJOR_EVENT

for an ordinary announced religion founding. Corporation founding, global project
completion and multiple other current engine paths also use major-event messages.

A controlled ordinary reproduction can therefore arrange H0 -> AI A -> H1 and have A
found a religion during its intervening AI turn. H0 receives the world announcement in
the exact alias-producing HotSeat state.

DISPLAY / CLEANUP CONSEQUENCE
-----------------------------
At H0's next message processing, only one display branch runs:

* if the Turn Log auto-opens, `m_aMajorMsgs` is shown;
* else in HotSeat, `m_aHotSeatMsgs` is shown.

Then `postProcessMessages` unconditionally calls:

    clearMessageCopies();

which independently deletes both owners and double-frees the shared allocation.

The same bad ownership can also reach reset / other common cleanup calls; these are
consequences of the same root.

ANCESTRY / CONTROL
------------------
Direct supplied-source comparison:

* current SAS: contains `m_aMajorMsgs`, `m_aHotSeatMsgs`, the one-allocation/two-push
  logic and independent deleting cleanup;
* Base AdvCiv 1.14: same relevant code;
* K-Mod 1.46: `CvPlayer::addMessage` only pushes the value into the ordinary game-message
  queue; there are no retained raw-pointer vectors;
* Civ4CE/BtS: same stock-style absence of the AdvC retained-copy ownership machinery.

A prior locally traced history branch recorded the introduction as AdvC practical 4171,
commit `8bfa61dfd7fc7f43b47519a34ac893066517907d`, "Work around messages missed at the end
of Hotseat turns". The current classification does not depend on that historical
metadata: the supplied Base-vs-K-Mod/BtS source comparison independently establishes the
AdvC-specific lineage.

DUPLICATE / ALBUM CHECK
-----------------------
The full reconciled WIP209 album was searched for:

* `m_aHotSeatMsgs`;
* `m_aMajorMsgs`;
* `clearMessageCopies`;
* `double free` / retained HotSeat message ownership.

No existing numbered or latent root owns this raw-pointer alias. The nearby Turn-Log
message-count heuristic is independent and has no heap-ownership component.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Restore an unambiguous ownership invariant.

For a minimal VC2003-era patch, the most local repair is to allocate an INDEPENDENT
`CvTalkingHeadMessage` object for each owning vector when both classifications apply.
Then the existing independent cleanup remains correct.

Alternatives are one canonical owner plus explicit non-owning classification, or a
shared-ownership model compatible with the old toolchain. Do not merely deduplicate raw
addresses inside `clearMessageCopies`; that masks the ownership violation only at one
sink and leaves future show/remove/reset code with ambiguous ownership.

---------------

   current producer).
3. Assert H0 remains the active UI player while A acts.
4. Assert repaired retained-message storage never has the SAME raw address owned by both

5. Exercise both display branches: Turn Log auto-open and ordinary HotSeat missed-message
   replay.
6. Run common cleanup and assert no double delete / allocator failure / crash.
7. Verify non-HotSeat major-event retention remains unchanged.

POST-F490 RETAINED-MESSAGE / POINTER-LIFETIME SIBLING SWEEP

1. `showMessageCopies` does not independently double-consume or remove an aliased message.

`postProcessMessages` chooses the retained-message display with an `if` / `else if`:

    if (auto-open Turn Log)
        showMessageCopies(&m_aMajorMsgs);
    else if (HotSeat)

Only one retained vector is displayed in a given pass. The actual failure remains F490's

All of them eventually use the same `clearMessageCopies()` ownership model. A shared raw

3. Popup ownership remains coherent in the sampled queue paths.

`addPopup` owns the pointer while queued. `popFrontPopup` removes it from the owning queue

5. `refreshGroupCycleList`'s temporary `std::vector<CvSelectionGroup*>` is non-owning and
survives the list-node edits it was designed to decouple.

The routine removes group-cycle LIST NODES while retaining `CvSelectionGroup*` objects in
`update_list`; it does not delete the selection groups. The later `updateGroupCycle`
therefore receives live group objects under the already-audited group lifecycle invariant.
This is inherited from K-Mod/AdvCiv structure and does not reproduce F490-like lifetime
aliasing.

POST-WIP224 LIFECYCLE / CALLBACK / ONE-SHOT STATE PASS
------------------------------------------------------
The audit moved out of retained-message ownership and resumed low-coverage lifecycle
state. Several initially suspicious seams were traced to a clean closure. F491 is not
spent merely to keep numbering moving.

1. `disband(last city)` -> `setFoundedFirstCity(false)` is inherited intentional
   pre-first-city / acquisition-disband semantics, not a new historical-flag corruption.

`CvPlayer::disband(CvCity&)` contains:

    if (getNumCities() == 1)
        setFoundedFirstCity(false);
    ...
    kCity.kill(true);

and `verifyAlive` later uses:

    if (getNumCities() == 0 && getAdvancedStartPoints() < 0)
    {
        if (getNumUnits() <= 0 || isFoundedFirstCity())
            bKill = true;
    }

At first glance this looks like a reversible historical flag allowing a once-settled
civilization to become "never settled" again. The caller/lifecycle context closes the
ordinary-current concern:

* the compiled DLL caller of `disband` is the acquired-city disband task (plus the
  intentionally exposed Python API);
* `BUTTONPOPUP_DISBANDCITY` is created for a HUMAN city acquisition that is neither
  conquest nor trade -- the stock-style choice to reject/disband a just-acquired city;
* ordinary established civilizations that have already lost all prior cities do not
  remain freely alive waiting to exploit this reset: `verifyAlive` eliminates a
  zero-city player once `FoundedFirstCity` is true (AdvC has removed Complete Kills);
* the reset therefore principally preserves the longstanding ability of a still-
  unsettled player to reject its first non-founded acquisition and return to the
  pre-first-city state rather than being defeated solely because that transient city
  existed.

The exact reset is inherited through Civ4CE/BtS -> K-Mod -> Base AdvCiv -> SAS. No
independent current path was established where an ordinarily settled surviving player
uses this call to erase genuine settlement history and gain a new lifecycle exemption.
Preserve as intentional inherited semantics; no F491.

2. `AI_conquerCity(kNewCity, ...)` and auto-raze can delete the newly acquired city, but
   `CvPlayer::acquireCity` deliberately stops dereferencing that city afterward.

Current acquisition explicitly comments:

    else if (!isHuman())
    {   // May delete kNewCity!
        AI().AI_conquerCity(kNewCity, ...);
    }

The same branch can call `kNewCity.doTask(TASK_RAZE)`, which also destroys the city.
A continuation audit verified that after these potentially destructive calls the
function no longer dereferences `kNewCity`. Remaining work uses durable snapshots or
independent objects:

* old event IDs (`eOldOwner`, `iOldCityId`);
* `kCityPlot`, a map plot object independent of the killed city allocation;
* saved reveal-state bits;
* player/team identities and caches.

Thus the "May delete" comment is backed by a real lifetime boundary, and the code honors
it. No post-kill city UAF is hidden immediately below the branch.

3. `cityAcquired` Python/event reporting occurs before the later `canRaze` / AI conquest
   decision, but CURRENT shipped Python handlers do not destroy or transfer the city.

The event reporter forwards the live city to Python. Current SAS `CvEventManager`'s
`onCityAcquired` only records SAS battle-history metadata and optionally logs the city;
installed Contrib handlers are notification/logging consumers. No current shipped
handler was found that razes, gifts, transfers or otherwise destroys the city during
this callback.

A modmod/Python extension could violate that implicit callback lifetime contract, but an
API-extensibility hazard without a current producer is below the threshold for F491.
Do not manufacture a callback UAF from what current SAS does not do.

4. The nearby `cityRazed` reporter likewise does not establish a current callback-kill
   race before native `disband(kCity)`.

Current raze ordering is:

    kCity.doPartisans();
    CvEventReporter::getInstance().cityRazed(&kCity, getID());
    disband(kCity);

The shipped Python cityRazed path is notification/logging-oriented; no current handler
was found that destroys the city before native disband. The native order therefore
retains one authoritative destruction point in shipped SAS.

5. `changeHurryCount`'s transition-side aggregate update is safe under its only compiled
   producer.

The method changes `m_iPopRushHurryCount` / `m_iGoldRushHurryCount` by the full `iChange`
when an individual HurryTypes count crosses zero. This would be suspicious if callers
could jump a hurry source count by magnitude >1 in one call: a 0->2 transition should
add one enabled hurry TYPE to those aggregate counts, not two.

A whole current C++ caller search finds the only gameplay producer in `processCivics`:

    changeHurryCount(eLoopHurry,
        GC.getInfo(eCivic).isHurry(eLoopHurry) ? iChange : 0);

Civic processing applies/removes one civic source at a time with `iChange` +/-1. The
problematic magnitude >1 transition has no ordinary compiled producer. Keep as generic
API robustness only; no F491.

6. Advanced Start validate/substitute siblings remain closed apart from F485.

The re-loop compared the F485 unit/route fallback pattern with neighboring actions:

* Improvement removal substitutes the actual plot improvement when the requested type
  differs, but crucially recomputes `getAdvancedStartImprovementCost(..., pPlot)` with
  the SAME concrete plot and aborts on a negative result before mutation.
* Population / culture / building actions keep the validated concrete city object and
  abort on negative plot/city-aware cost.
* City removal obtains a nonnegative plot-aware city-removal cost before killing the
  plot city; no substitute object is introduced afterward.

So the dangerous "validate A -> substitute B -> recompute generically -> mutate B"
shape remains localized to the already-confirmed F485 route fallback (and F485's unit
release-assert path). No F491 sibling was established here.

F491 / KI#814 CANDIDATE -- HQ OWNER TRANSFER CAN CHANGE PROTECTIONISM CORPORATION
ACTIVITY WITHOUT REBUILDING THE OWNERS' OTHER CORPORATION CITIES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: STRONG CURRENT CANDIDATE; NOT YET CONFIRMED / NUMBERED.

ROOT SHAPE
----------
Current player corporation policy is dynamic:

    bool CvPlayer::isActiveCorporation(CorporationTypes eCorp) const
    {
        if (isNoCorporations())
            return false;
        if (isNoForeignCorporations() && !hasHeadquarters(eCorp))
            return false;
        return true;
    }

Current `CIVIC_PROTECTIONISM` has:

    bNoCorporations         = 0
    bNoForeignCorporations  = 1

so under Protectionism a corporation is active for a player exactly when that player owns
its HQ (subject to the city having the corporation/resource prerequisites).

Changing the civic itself is handled correctly: `changeNoForeignCorporationsCount` calls
`CvPlayer::updateCorporation()`, rebuilding every city. The candidate is a DIFFERENT input
to the same predicate: HQ OWNER IDENTITY.

`CvPlayer::hasHeadquarters` is not cached player state. It resolves the current global HQ
city and compares its CURRENT owner:

    CvCity const* pHeadquarters = GC.getGame().getHeadquarters(eCorporation);
    return (pHeadquarters != NULL && pHeadquarters->getOwner() == getID());

Thus transferring the HQ between players changes `isActiveCorporation` immediately even
if neither player's civic changes.

`CvGame::setHeadquarters`, however, only updates the OLD HQ CITY and the NEW HQ CITY:

    m_aeHeadquarters.set(...);
    if (pOldCity != NULL)
        pOldCity->updateCorporation();
    ...
    pHeadquarters->setHasCorporation(...);
    pHeadquarters->updateCorporation();

It does NOT call `oldOwner.updateCorporation()` or `newOwner.updateCorporation()` for all
of either player's other cities.

WHY OTHER CITIES MATTER
-----------------------
`CvCity::updateCorporation` rebuilds authoritative stored state:
* corporation-produced bonuses (`m_aiNumCorpProducedBonuses`);
* building commerce affected by those bonuses;
* corporation yields (`m_aiCorporationYield`), applied through base-yield changes;
* corporation commerce (`m_aiCorporationCommerce`);
* maintenance.

The per-corporation yield/commerce calculations call `isActiveCorporation`, so a changed
HQ owner is a direct input to those caches. A branch city that is not itself the old/new
HQ therefore needs a rebuild when its owner's HQ status flips under Protectionism.

ORDINARY ACQUIRECITY TRANSFER SEQUENCE -- PROVED TO THE CURRENT CHECKPOINT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::acquireCity` snapshots both corporation presence and HQ identity from the old
city:

    abHasCorporation[eCorp] = pOldCity->isHasCorporation(eCorp);
    abHeadquarters[eCorp]   = pOldCity->isHeadquarters(eCorp);

It then kills the old city. `CvCity::kill` removes the corporation and, if this is the HQ,
calls:

    GC.getGame().setHeadquarters(eCorp, NULL, false);

This clears the global HQ pointer. If old owner O is running Protectionism, O's player-
level `isActiveCorporation(eCorp)` therefore flips TRUE -> FALSE immediately. The setter
updates the dying old HQ city only; O's surviving branch cities are not globally rebuilt.

The replacement city is then created for new owner N. `acquireCity` restores:

    kNewCity.setHasCorporation(eCorp, true, false);
    kGame.setHeadquarters(eCorp, &kNewCity, false);

Before the second call, N does not yet own the HQ, so under Protectionism the restored
corporation in the new city is initially evaluated as foreign/inactive. Restoring the HQ
then makes N's player-level predicate flip FALSE -> TRUE and refreshes the NEW HQ city.
N's pre-existing branch cities are again not globally rebuilt.

Consequently the same ordinary HQ capture/trade can create BOTH directions of stale
branch state:
* OLD owner O can retain cached active corporation yields/commerce/produced bonuses /
  maintenance in surviving branches after losing the HQ;
* NEW owner N can retain cached INACTIVE/zero corporation state in pre-existing branches
  after gaining the HQ.

PLOT-GROUP REBUILD DOES NOT GENERALLY CLOSE THE ROOT
----------------------------------------------------
`acquireCity` later calls `CvGame::updatePlotGroups()` when requested. This does not imply
a full corporation rebuild. `CvPlayer::updatePlotGroups` asks each existing plot group to
`recalculatePlots`; `CvPlotGroup::recalculatePlots` returns immediately when all plots in
that group remain connected. A pre-existing branch city can be placed in an unrelated /
separate stable plot group from the captured HQ city. Its bonus counts therefore need not
change and no incidental `changeNumBonuses -> updateCorporation` is guaranteed.

Even when a plot group is rebuilt, corporation updates arise from actual bonus-count
changes, not from an explicit HQ-owner dependency invalidation. The missing old/new-owner
rebuild therefore remains a live architectural concern rather than being automatically
repaired by `updatePlotGroups`.

CURRENT DATA SUPPORT -- PARTIALLY SETTLED
-----------------------------------------
Protectionism is a current normal Economy civic (Banking prerequisite) with
`bNoForeignCorporations=1`.

Current corporations have ordinary nonzero branch outputs. For example `CORPORATION_1`
(Cereal Mills in the existing album terminology) consumes grain bonuses and has
`iYieldProduced=100`, giving a simple positive branch-yield state when prerequisites are
connected. Other current corporations produce commerce and/or corporation-created bonus
resources, so the stale-state family is not XML-dormant.

A deterministic reproduction can therefore be shaped without debug/Python state:
1. Corporation C has HQ owner O and at least one non-HQ branch city O1 with a qualifying
   resource.
2. O runs Protectionism. Because O owns the HQ, C is active and O1's corporation cache is
   positive/current.
3. Player N also runs Protectionism and has a pre-existing C branch N1. Because N does NOT
   own the HQ, its civic-change rebuild has made C inactive there (zero corporation
   output/cache).
4. N captures or otherwise acquires O's HQ city through ordinary city transfer.
5. `acquireCity` performs the HQ NULL -> new-HQ transition described above.
6. Correct post-transfer state:
      O1 should become inactive;
      N1 should become active.
7. Candidate current code leaves those remote branch caches unchanged until some unrelated
   corporation/bonus/occupation/civic/anarchy refresh happens.

F491 / KI#814 -- PROTECTIONISM HQ TRANSFER CHANGES CORPORATION ACTIVITY FOR BOTH
PLAYERS BUT REFRESHES ONLY THE HQ CITIES, LEAVING OTHER BRANCH CACHES WRONG
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS / CLASSIFICATION
-----------------------
CONFIRMED current gameplay defect.

The core bug is inherited from stock BtS/Civ4CE through K-Mod and Base AdvCiv. Current
AdvCiv-SAS keeps the same DLL contract and has a directly live current civic/data
reproduction through Protectionism and ordinary corporation branch output.

ROOT -- HQ OWNERSHIP IS A LIVE INPUT TO PLAYER CORPORATION ACTIVITY
------------------------------------------------------------------
Current `CvPlayer::isActiveCorporation` is:

    bool CvPlayer::isActiveCorporation(CorporationTypes eCorp) const
    {
        if (isNoCorporations())
            return false;
        if (isNoForeignCorporations() && !hasHeadquarters(eCorp))
            return false;
        return true;
    }

Current `CIVIC_PROTECTIONISM` has:

    TechPrereq               = TECH_BANKING
    bNoCorporations          = 0
    bNoForeignCorporations   = 1

Therefore, while a player runs Protectionism:
* a corporation whose HQ that player OWNS is active;
* the same corporation is foreign/inactive for a player who does NOT own its HQ.

`hasHeadquarters` is dynamic, not a separately maintained player flag:

    CvCity const* pHeadquarters = GC.getGame().getHeadquarters(eCorporation);
    return (pHeadquarters != NULL && pHeadquarters->getOwner() == getID());

So changing the global HQ city owner immediately changes the correct active-corporation
state for the OLD owner and NEW owner even though neither player's civic changed.

CONTRAST CONTROL -- CIVIC POLICY CHANGE DOES INVALIDATE THE WHOLE PLAYER
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
The existing civic-source transition is correctly wired:

    CvPlayer::changeNoForeignCorporationsCount
        -> updateCorporation()
        -> every owned city -> CvCity::updateCorporation()

Thus entering/leaving Protectionism rebuilds every city. This proves that corporation
activity is treated as derived city state requiring explicit invalidation.

The missed dependency is the OTHER input to the same predicate: `hasHeadquarters`.

BROKEN INVALIDATION -- `CvGame::setHeadquarters` UPDATES ONLY TWO CITIES
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Current setter:

    CvCity* pOldCity = getHeadquarters(eCorp);
    ...
    m_aeHeadquarters.set(...);
    if (pOldCity != NULL)
        pOldCity->updateCorporation();
    ...
    CvCity* pHeadquarters = getHeadquarters(eCorp);
    if (pHeadquarters == NULL)
        return;
    pHeadquarters->setHasCorporation(eCorp, true, bAnnounce);
    pHeadquarters->updateCorporation();

The OLD HQ city is rebuilt and the NEW HQ city is rebuilt. There is no:

    GET_PLAYER(eOldOwner).updateCorporation();
    GET_PLAYER(eNewOwner).updateCorporation();

and no equivalent scan over their other branch cities.

That is insufficient whenever HQ owner identity changes under a NoForeignCorporations
policy, because the correct corporation activity changes simultaneously in EVERY city of
both affected players that contains that corporation and its required resources.

WHAT `CvCity::updateCorporation` STORES
---------------------------------------
This is not merely a dynamic-query/UI mismatch. The routine reconstructs authoritative
stored state:

    updateCorporationBonus();
    updateBuildingCommerce();
    for each Yield:
        updateCorporationYield();
    for each Commerce:
        updateCorporationCommerce();
    updateMaintenance();

Those fields include:
* corporation-produced resource counts (`m_aiNumCorpProducedBonuses`);
* corporation yield (`m_aiCorporationYield`);
* corporation commerce (`m_aiCorporationCommerce`);
* dependent building commerce;
* cached city maintenance.

`updateCorporationYield` ultimately changes `m_aiBaseYieldRate` through
`changeBaseYieldRate`. Once stale, normal `getYieldRate` reads the wrong base yield until
some later corporation invalidator happens.

ORDINARY CITY ACQUISITION PROVES BOTH DIRECTIONS
------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::acquireCity` explicitly preserves headquarters identity across ownership
transfer. Before deleting the old city it snapshots:

    abHasCorporation[eCorp] = pOldCity->isHasCorporation(eCorp);
    abHeadquarters[eCorp]   = pOldCity->isHeadquarters(eCorp);

It then executes:

    pOldCity->kill(false, false);

`CvCity::kill` removes corporation presence and, for an HQ, calls:

    GC.getGame().setHeadquarters(eCorp, NULL, false);

At that moment the global HQ pointer becomes null. If old owner O runs Protectionism,
O's correct player-level corporation activity flips:

    TRUE -> FALSE

because O no longer satisfies `hasHeadquarters(eCorp)`. `setHeadquarters` refreshes the
old/dying HQ city, but does not refresh O's other surviving branch cities.

`acquireCity` then recreates the city for new owner N and restores:

    kNewCity.setHasCorporation(eCorp, true, false);
    kGame.setHeadquarters(eCorp, &kNewCity, false);

Before the second line N does not own the HQ, so under Protectionism the restored city
initially treats the corporation as foreign/inactive. After the second line N DOES own
the HQ and N's correct player-level corporation activity flips:

    FALSE -> TRUE

The new HQ city is explicitly rebuilt. N's pre-existing branch cities are not.

Thus one ordinary HQ capture/trade can create both stale directions at once:

OLD owner O, other branches:
    correct after transfer = inactive / zero corporation output
    cached current result  = still active / old positive corporation output

NEW owner N, other branches:
    correct after transfer = active / corporation output present
    cached current result  = still inactive / zero corporation output

CURRENT-SAS DETERMINISTIC NUMERIC REPRO -- CEREAL MILLS
-------------------------------------------------------
Current `CORPORATION_1` (Cereal Mills in the existing album terminology) has grain
prerequisites and:

    iYieldProduced[FOOD] = 100

Current Standard world size has:

    iCorporationMaintenancePercent = 100

Therefore a normal non-disordered Cereal Mills branch with exactly one qualifying Wheat
and no other grain contributes exactly:

    100 * 1 * 100 / 100 = 100 hundredths
    intdiv::uceil(100, 100) = +1 FOOD

Supported reproduction:

1. Player O owns the Cereal Mills HQ and a separate non-HQ branch city O1.
2. Player N owns a separate Cereal Mills branch city N1 but not the HQ.
3. Give O1 and N1 exactly one connected Wheat relevant to the corporation.
4. Place O1/N1 in stable plot groups unrelated to the HQ city's plot group.
5. Both players adopt Protectionism and finish any anarchy so all corporation caches are
   freshly rebuilt under stable pre-transfer state.
6. Pre-transfer authoritative cache state is therefore:

       O owns HQ -> O1 corporation FOOD = +1
       N no HQ   -> N1 corporation FOOD = 0

7. During N's ordinary active turn, N captures O's Cereal Mills HQ city.
8. Acquisition clears the old HQ pointer and later restores it on N's replacement city.
9. Dynamic player policy now correctly says:

       O.isActiveCorporation(Cereal Mills) = false
       N.isActiveCorporation(Cereal Mills) = true

10. But only old/new HQ city corporation caches were rebuilt, leaving:

       O1 cached corporation FOOD = +1   // should now be 0
       N1 cached corporation FOOD = 0    // should now be +1

A forced:

    O.updateCorporation();
    N.updateCorporation();

immediately produces the correct opposite values, demonstrating that the live cache and
its own current formula disagree solely because the ownership transition missed the
invalidator.

AUTHORITATIVE GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCE -- STALE FOOD IS BOOKED
----------------------------------------------------------
`CvCity::setCorporationYield` / `updateCorporationYield` apply corporation yield to the
stored base yield through `changeBaseYieldRate`.

Normal `CvCity::doTurn` does NOT call `updateCorporation`. Its ordinary sequence includes:

    doGrowth();
    doCulture();
    doProduction(...);

`doGrowth` calls:

    int iDiff = foodDifference();
    changeFood(iDiff);

and `foodDifference` reads current `getYieldRate(YIELD_FOOD)`, which includes the stored
base-yield cache.

Therefore the stale state is consumed, not merely displayed:
* N1 can miss the +1 food it should receive on the SAME turn N captured the HQ;
* O1 can keep receiving +1 food after O has lost the HQ, including on O's next turn.

Choose branch food totals exactly at consumption if a maximally visible test is desired:
correct HQ ownership then changes foodDifference by exactly one. Over enough turns the
same error can change growth/starvation timing. Current corporations with production or
commerce output provide parallel authoritative consequences.

NO UNCONDITIONAL TURN SELF-HEAL
-------------------------------
A complete current `updateCorporation` caller scan finds no unconditional city-turn or
player-turn rebuild.

Whole-player refreshes occur only on specific unrelated inputs/events, e.g.:
* entering/leaving anarchy;
* NoCorporations / NoForeignCorporations civic count changes;
* relevant technology processing.

City-local refreshes occur on specific corporation/bonus/occupation changes.

Consequently an unaffected branch can remain wrong until some unrelated invalidator
fires. Advancing the turn alone does not restore the HQ-dependent cache.

WHY `acquireCity -> updatePlotGroups` DOES NOT RESCUE THE BRANCHES
-----------------------------------------------------------------
The acquisition path can later call global `updatePlotGroups`, but this is not a full
corporation rebuild.

`CvPlayer::updatePlotGroups` asks each existing group to `recalculatePlots`.
`CvPlotGroup::recalculatePlots` explicitly returns immediately when its existing plots
remain connected:

    if (iCount == iOldCount)
        return;

So O1 and N1 can be placed in separate stable plot groups unrelated to the transferred
HQ. Their bonus counts do not need to change and no incidental
`changeNumBonuses -> updateCorporation` occurs.

Even a group recalculation updates corporation state only through actual resource-count
transitions. There is no explicit dependency from HQ owner identity to all branch caches.
The plot-group step therefore cannot serve as the required invalidation contract.

ANCESTRY
--------
This is inherited from stock BtS.

Civ4CE/BtS has the same player predicate:

    if (isNoForeignCorporations() && !hasHeadquarters(eIndex))
        return false;

and stock `CvGame::setHeadquarters` likewise updates only:
* `pOldValue->updateCorporation()`;
* `pHeadquarters->updateCorporation()`.

Stock current data already makes the dependency live through `CIVIC_MERCANTILISM`, which
has both:

    bNoCorporations        = 0
    bNoForeignCorporations = 1

K-Mod 1.46 retains the same predicate and the same old/new-HQ-only setter.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains both unchanged in substance.
Current SAS retains the DLL architecture while its current Economy civic
`CIVIC_PROTECTIONISM` carries the same NoForeignCorporations mechanism.

Thus F491 is a Firaxis/BtS corporation-cache invalidation bug inherited through the full
lineage, with current SAS exposure through Protectionism.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Whenever `CvGame::setHeadquarters` changes the HQ OWNER for a corporation, rebuild
corporation state for the affected old/new owners' other cities after the global HQ
pointer has reached the new state.

The invariant is:

    if HQ ownership changes and a player's corporation activity can depend on HQ
    ownership, every affected branch city's corporation cache must match
    CvPlayer::isActiveCorporation before normal city/economy processing resumes.

Implementation should respect the city-kill path. `setHeadquarters(eCorp, NULL)` can be
called while the old HQ city is partway through `CvCity::kill`; blindly calling a full
old-owner `updateCorporation()` that includes the dying city may introduce reentrancy
risk. Safe approaches include:

* in `setHeadquarters`, snapshot old/new PlayerTypes and refresh the affected owners'
  OTHER cities while skipping the explicitly handled old/new HQ objects; or
* defer a narrowly tracked affected-player corporation rebuild to a stable point after
  city deletion/acquisition, while also covering generic non-capture HQ changes.

Do not fix only the new owner: losing the HQ under Protectionism is equally a TRUE->FALSE
transition for the old owner's surviving branches.

A. Two-direction Cereal Mills capture test
1. Standard map; O and N both Protectionism.
2. Cereal Mills HQ belongs to O.
3. O1 and N1 are ordinary non-HQ branch cities with one qualifying Wheat each and stable

4. Force corporation caches current.
5. Assert before capture:
       O1 corporation FOOD == 1
       N1 corporation FOOD == 0
6. N captures HQ city.
7. Immediately assert dynamic policy:
       !O.isActiveCorporation(Cereal Mills)
        N.isActiveCorporation(Cereal Mills)
8. Without an explicit repair call, assert branch caches already match:
       O1 corporation FOOD == 0
       N1 corporation FOOD == 1
   Current code fails both.

B. Gameplay booking test
1. Configure O1/N1 with non-corporation food exactly equal to consumption.
2. Perform the HQ capture before N's end-of-turn city processing.
3. Repaired N1 gains exactly +1 food from Cereal Mills; current N1 gains 0.
4. On O's next city turn, repaired O1 gains 0 corporation food; current O1 still gains
   the stale +1 until an unrelated corporation refresh occurs.

C. Control without NoForeignCorporations
Repeat while both players use a civic where `isNoForeignCorporations()==false`.
HQ owner transfer should not change branch active status merely from owner identity.
This protects against gratuitous behavior changes outside the relevant dependency.

F492 / KI#815 — NO-SLAVERY SACRIFICIAL-ALTAR POP-RUSH ENTITLEMENT IS MIS-CACHED WHEN THE BUILDING IS COMPLETED DURING AI AUTO PLAY
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: CONFIRMED — inherited AdvCiv human-status/source-processing bug, live in current SAS.

ROOT
----
AdvCiv's No Slavery feature gives human players a special city-local population-rush
permission from a building with negative HurryAngerModifier. The source is processed in
`CvCity::processBuilding` only while the owner is CURRENTLY human:

    if (kGame.isOption(GAMEOPTION_NO_SLAVERY) && kOwner.isHuman() &&
        kBuilding.getHurryAngerModifier() < 0)
    {
        changePopRushCount(iChange);
    }

That is source-time cached state. `CvCity::canPopRush()` later consumes the stored count:

    return (m_iPopRushHurryCount > 0 || GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).canPopRush());

and `m_iPopRushHurryCount` is serialized in the savegame.

AI Auto Play deliberately changes the active human to `isHuman()==false` by
`CvPlayer::setHumanDisabled(true)`. If the relevant building is completed while Auto
Play controls the player, `processBuilding(...,+1)` sees a non-human owner and therefore
does NOT add the building's No-Slavery pop-rush source.

When Auto Play ends, `setHumanDisabled(false)` restores human status, updates AI-facing
state and messages, but performs no city rebuild and no `m_iPopRushHurryCount`
recalculation. The building remains present while the city-local permission remains 0.

CURRENT SAS DATA / ORDINARY REPRODUCTION
----------------------------------------
Current SAS has a direct live producer:

    GAMEOPTION_NO_SLAVERY
        visible = true

    BUILDING_AZTEC_SACRIFICIAL_ALTAR
        BuildingClass = BUILDINGCLASS_MONUMENT
        PrereqTech = TECH_MYSTICISM
        Cost = 30
        HurryAngerModifier = -50
        ObsoleteTech = TECH_LIBERALISM

The No Slavery help explicitly states that human players cannot change to Slavery and
that ONLY the Aztec Sacrificial Altar allows humans to sacrifice population.

Deterministic gameplay sequence:

1. Start a normal human Aztec game with No Slavery enabled and remain in a non-pop-rush
   Labor civic.
2. Begin constructing a Sacrificial Altar but start AI Auto Play before completion.
3. The AI completes the Altar while `isHuman()==false` and `isHumanDisabled()==true`.
4. `CvCity::processBuilding` installs every ordinary building effect but skips
   `changePopRushCount(+1)` solely because the owner is temporarily non-human.
5. End Auto Play and return control to the same player.
6. The city owns a live, non-obsolete Sacrificial Altar with negative
   HurryAngerModifier, but `m_iPopRushHurryCount` is still 0.
7. With the player's civic not otherwise granting HURRY_POPULATION,
   `CvCity::canPopRush()` is false. The returned human therefore cannot use the exact
   exception promised by the No Slavery option.

This does not require a rare API producer, WorldBuilder mutation, save editing or an AI
valuation assumption. Building completion during current SAS Auto Play is an ordinary
shipped path.

PERSISTENCE / NO SELF-HEAL
--------------------------
`setHumanDisabled(false)` does not call `processBuilding` for existing cities/buildings
or otherwise rebuild `m_iPopRushHurryCount`.

The count is not dynamically recomputed from buildings by `canPopRush`; it is read
straight from stored city state. It is also serialized. Thus an Altar completed during
Auto Play can remain present and wrong after control returns, across turns and saves,
until some later source transition happens to process that building again.

The inverse source transition is vulnerable for the same reason: if a qualifying source
that had been counted while human is removed/obsoleted while the player is human-disabled,
the `iChange < 0` call is gated out too and can leave an entitlement that should have
been removed. The completion case alone is sufficient for confirmation and is the clean
regression target.

ANCESTRY
--------
This root is inherited from AdvCiv, not stock BtS/K-Mod's base rules.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same No Slavery building hook:

    if (kGame.isOption(GAMEOPTION_NO_SLAVERY) && kOwner.isHuman() &&
        kBuilding.getHurryAngerModifier() < 0)
        changePopRushCount(iChange);

and the same `setHumanDisabled` human-status transition with no city pop-rush rebuild.
The No Slavery feature (`advc.912d`) was added by AdvCiv on top of the earlier AI Auto
Play machinery. Current SAS retains that architecture and supplies a live current
Sacrificial Altar with `iHurryAngerModifier = -50`.

DUPLICATE / RECONCILIATION CHECK
--------------------------------
The current full album was searched for No Slavery, `GAMEOPTION_NO_SLAVERY`, Slavery,
Sacrificial Altar, population rush and the human/Auto-Play combination.

The only direct No-Slavery numbered neighbor is F396 / KI#719, which is a player-context
TECH HELP contradiction: Masonry can advertise that it enables Slavery even though the
option blocks human adoption. F492 is authoritative runtime city state after an ordinary
building completion during Auto Play. It changes whether the player can actually hurry
production and persists in the savegame. It is not a help/UI duplicate.

No existing root in the reconciled album owns `m_iPopRushHurryCount` being conditioned
on transient `isHuman()` at source-processing time without a human-status invalidation.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
For the No Slavery building exception, treat the temporarily AI-controlled human as the
same policy subject as the human player. The minimal source-side repair is conceptually:

    if (kGame.isOption(GAMEOPTION_NO_SLAVERY) &&
        (kOwner.isHuman() || kOwner.isHumanDisabled()) &&
        kBuilding.getHurryAngerModifier() < 0)
    {
        changePopRushCount(iChange);
    }

This keeps add/remove/obsolescence processing symmetric throughout Auto Play and avoids
needing a whole-city rebuild when control toggles.

The pattern is supported by AdvCiv's own old `getFoodKept` No-Slavery experiment, whose
comment explicitly warned that toggling human state during AI Auto Play could make
stored city data inconsistent and therefore used `(isHuman() || isHumanDisabled())`.
That old food-retention rule is disabled today, but the lifecycle principle applies
exactly to the still-live pop-rush counter.

Do not repair only Auto Play END: that would need to reconstruct source multiplicity and
would still leave state wrong during Auto Play. Keeping source processing stable across
human-disabled status is narrower and symmetric.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Completion during Auto Play
1. Human Aztec; No Slavery enabled; Labor civic does not grant HURRY_POPULATION.
2. City has no Sacrificial Altar and `m_iPopRushHurryCount == 0`.
3. Start Auto Play.
4. Complete BUILDING_AZTEC_SACRIFICIAL_ALTAR while human-disabled.
5. Assert immediately that the city-local pop-rush source is 1 despite temporary AI
   control.
6. End Auto Play.
7. Assert `CvCity::canPopRush()` is true solely from the Altar exception.

B. Removal/obsolescence symmetry
1. Human Aztec with No Slavery and a counted Altar source.
2. Start Auto Play.
3. Trigger the ordinary building removal or obsolescence source transition.
4. Assert the city-local pop-rush count loses the source while human-disabled.
5. End Auto Play and assert no stale population-rush permission remains.

C. Control without No Slavery
Repeat the building add/remove with GAMEOPTION_NO_SLAVERY disabled. The special city
counter should remain untouched; ordinary civic-based population rushing continues to
be governed by the player's hurry counts.

F493 / provisional KI#816 is the next UNUSED root.

F493 / KI#816 — NO-SLAVERY AI AUTO PLAY CAN ADOPT SLAVERY FOR THE TEMPORARILY DISABLED HUMAN AND RETURN CONTROL WITH THE FORBIDDEN CIVIC STILL ACTIVE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — AdvCiv-introduced gameplay bug retained by AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS.
The root combines AdvCiv's human-only No-Slavery legality predicate with the inherited
AI Auto Play mechanism that temporarily makes the human slot report `isHuman()==false`.

ROOT / CONTRACT
---------------
AdvCiv's visible No Slavery option explicitly says:

    Human players cannot change their civics to Slavery.
    Only the Aztec Sacrificial Altar allows humans to sacrifice population.

The runtime legality hook in `CvPlayer::canDoCivics` is:

    if (kGame.isOption(GAMEOPTION_NO_SLAVERY) && isHuman())
    {
        FOR_EACH_ENUM(Hurry)
        {
            if (GC.getInfo(eCivic).isHurry(eLoopHurry) &&
                GC.getInfo(eLoopHurry).getProductionPerPopulation() > 0)
            {
                return false;
            }
        }
    }

For an ordinary human this correctly rejects `CIVIC_SLAVERY`, whose current XML grants
`HURRY_POPULATION` with positive production per population.

AI Auto Play deliberately changes that identity test. `CvGame::setAIAutoPlay` calls
`CvPlayer::setHumanDisabled(true)` for the active player; `setHumanDisabled` sets
`m_bDisableHuman`, calls `updateHuman`, and `updateHuman` then stores `m_bHuman=false`.
The same slot now has:

    isHuman()         == false
    isHumanDisabled() == true

Therefore the No-Slavery branch in `canDoCivics` is bypassed during Auto Play.

ORDINARY AI PRODUCER
--------------------
This is not merely an API route. `CvPlayerAI::AI_doCivics` runs for the temporarily
AI-controlled player and calls `AI_bestCivic` for each CivicOption. `AI_bestCivic`
considers every civic for which `canDoCivics` returns true, so Slavery becomes a normal
AI candidate while the human is disabled.

Current SAS data make the selection especially clean. `CIVIC_TRIBALISM` and
`CIVIC_SLAVERY` have the same Labor option, LOW upkeep, AI weight 0 and otherwise the
same gameplay fields; their only gameplay differences are:

    Tribalism: TechPrereq NONE, no Hurry source
    Slavery:   TechPrereq TECH_MASONRY, HURRY_POPULATION = true

`AI_civicValue` assigns a positive value to population rushing based on city count,
current production-per-population and growth threshold. Thus, once Masonry is known,
Slavery has a strictly higher civic value than Tribalism. In an ordinary several-city
empire the hurry term clears SAS's minimum civic-switch slack, so the disabled human's
AI can and does have a normal path to selecting Slavery. No Python, WorldBuilder or
forced `setCivics` call is needed.

HAND-BACK / PERSISTENCE PROOF
-----------------------------
The Auto Play end path does not normalize civics.

`AIAutoPlay.py::checkPlayer` calls `game.endAIAutoPlay(...)`. The DLL then executes
`CvGame::setAIAutoPlay(0, true, ...)`, which in single player calls only:

    GET_PLAYER(getActivePlayer()).setHumanDisabled(false);

`CvPlayer::setHumanDisabled(false)` restores `isHuman()==true`, updates AI-facing human
state and UI/replay bookkeeping, but it does NOT call `verifyCivics`, `setCivics`,
`processCivics` or any No-Slavery-specific validation.

The later Python fallback `if not pPlayer.isHuman(): ... setIsHuman(True)` normally does
not run for the surviving active human because the DLL has already restored human
status.

Consequently a player who adopted Slavery during Auto Play returns to human control
with:

    GAMEOPTION_NO_SLAVERY == true
    isHuman()             == true
    canDoCivics(SLAVERY)  == false
    getCivics(LABOR)      == CIVIC_SLAVERY
    HURRY_POPULATION source from Slavery still processed and active

The state is not permanent, but it is gameplay-significant. `CvPlayer::verifyCivics`
would replace the now-illegal civic, yet the normal `CvPlayer::doTurn` calls
`verifyCivics()` only AFTER gold/research processing and every city `doTurn`. More
importantly for scheduled Auto Play, the Python controller deliberately ends automation
on the preceding alive player's turn so that the disabled human is restored before its
next turn. The human therefore receives an ordinary active turn while Slavery is still
selected and can use the population-rush entitlement that the game option says humans
cannot obtain from civics. Verification happens only when that turn later completes.

COMPACT CURRENT REPRODUCTION
----------------------------
1. Start a human game with GAMEOPTION_NO_SLAVERY enabled.
2. Remain in CIVIC_TRIBALISM and acquire TECH_MASONRY. Use an ordinary developed empire
   with enough cities for Slavery's positive hurry valuation to clear the civic-switch
   slack; do not unlock a stronger competing Labor civic.
3. Start AI Auto Play for enough turns that the AI's civic timer permits a reevaluation.
4. While human-disabled, `canDoCivics(CIVIC_SLAVERY)` becomes true and AI civic choice
   can adopt Slavery through the normal `AI_doCivics -> AI_bestCivic -> revolution`
   path.
5. Let scheduled Auto Play end immediately before the human's next turn.
6. On hand-back, assert `isHuman()==true`, `canDoCivics(CIVIC_SLAVERY)==false`, but the
   selected Labor civic is still Slavery and `getHurryCount(HURRY_POPULATION)>0`.
7. Before ending that human turn, a city can population-rush through the civic source,
   contrary to the visible No-Slavery contract.
8. End the turn; the late `verifyCivics()` then selects a legal Labor civic. This late
   self-heal does not erase the already-exposed human turn or its possible whip.

ANCESTRY
--------
The underlying AI Auto Play identity mechanism predates AdvCiv and exists in K-Mod.
`GAMEOPTION_NO_SLAVERY` and the human-only `canDoCivics` restriction are AdvCiv feature
`advc.912d`; Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same `&& isHuman()` test and the same
`setHumanDisabled` hand-back without civic validation. Current SAS retains both.

Stock BtS/K-Mod do not have the No Slavery game option, so this exact root begins in
AdvCiv rather than stock BtS.

DUPLICATE / RECONCILIATION CHECK
--------------------------------
The full reconciled album was searched for No Slavery, Slavery, canDoCivics,
human-disabled, AI Auto Play civic changes and illegal/forbidden current civics.

* F396 / KI#719 is help/UI only: Masonry tech help can claim Slavery is enabled while
  the No Slavery option blocks human adoption.
* F492 / KI#815 is a distinct city-source cache bug: a Sacrificial Altar added/removed
  while human-disabled fails to update the city-local No-Slavery pop-rush counter.
* F459 / KI#782 also leaves an unavailable civic temporarily selected, but its root is
  loss of the final building-granted CivicOption source without immediate revalidation.
  F493 does not lose a civic source. Instead transient `isHuman()==false` changes the
  legality predicate itself and creates a new civic selection that should never have
  been legal for the same human policy subject. The common late `verifyCivics` cleanup
  is a shared consequence, not the root.

No prior numbered finding owns this human-status legality transition.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
The narrow source-side repair is to treat a temporarily disabled human as human for the
No-Slavery policy test, matching the lifecycle principle already used elsewhere in
AdvCiv:

    if (kGame.isOption(GAMEOPTION_NO_SLAVERY) &&
        (isHuman() || isHumanDisabled()))
    {
        ... reject population-rush civics ...
    }

This prevents the invalid civic from being selected in the first place, keeps AI Auto
Play from changing the human's policy envelope, and is consistent with the old
`getFoodKept` advc.912d comment that explicitly used `(isHuman() ||
isHumanDisabled())` to avoid Auto-Play state inconsistencies.

A hand-back-only `verifyCivics()` would reduce the exposed turn but would be broader and
would still allow Auto Play to run the human civilization under a civic that the game
option specifically forbids that human player from changing into. Source-side policy
stability is cleaner.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Auto Play legality
1. Human + No Slavery + Masonry + Tribalism.
2. Assert Slavery is illegal before Auto Play.
3. Enable Auto Play.
4. Assert Slavery remains illegal while `isHumanDisabled()==true`.
5. Let AI civic evaluation run and assert it cannot select Slavery.

B. Ordinary AI control
1. Separate genuine AI player + No Slavery + Masonry.
2. Assert Slavery remains legal for that AI, preserving the feature's documented
   human-only restriction.

C. Hand-back invariant
1. Run Auto Play across civic reevaluation.
2. End Auto Play before the human turn.
3. Assert every selected civic passes `canDoCivics` and no civic-derived
   HURRY_POPULATION entitlement exists unless supplied by an independently legal source.

F494 / KI#817 — AI AUTO PLAY CAN HAND A HUMAN A CULTURE PROCESS WITHOUT K-MOD'S BORDER-EXPANSION STOP MARKER
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — K-Mod-introduced gameplay/production-control bug inherited by Base AdvCiv
1.14 and current SAS. It requires the existing AI Auto Play human-status transition and
an ordinary Culture process selected by the temporary AI.

ROOT / K-MOD CONTRACT
---------------------
K-Mod replaced BtS's direct "stop Build Culture when borders expand" behavior with
per-order metadata. When a Culture process is pushed, `CvCity::pushOrder` snapshots the
CURRENT culture level into `OrderData::iData2` — but only if the city is human:

    if (isHuman() && GC.getInfo(eProcess).
        getProductionToCommerceModifier(COMMERCE_CULTURE) > 0)
    {
        FAssert(iData2 == -1);
        iData2 = getCultureLevel();
    }

Later in `CvCity::doProduction`, an existing Culture process is stopped after a border
expansion only when that saved marker is positive and the city has advanced beyond it:

    if (kOrder.iData2 > 0 && GC.getInfo((ProcessTypes)kOrder.iData1).
        getProductionToCommerceModifier(COMMERCE_CULTURE) > 0 &&
        getCultureLevel() > kOrder.iData2)
    {
        popOrder(0, false, ALL_CHOOSE);
    }

That human-only producer is normally coherent. AI cities do not need the snapshot
because `CvCity::doProduction` deliberately calls `AI_chooseProduction()` whenever an
AI city is running a process. `AI_chooseProduction` clears/reconsiders the current
process and can push a fresh AI order each turn.

AI Auto Play creates a third state that the pair does not cover: the SAME city can have
an order created while `isHuman()==false` and then become an ordinary non-automated
human city while that order remains at the head of its queue.

HAND-BACK TRANSITION
--------------------
During AI Auto Play the active human slot has:

    isHuman()         == false
    isHumanDisabled() == true

If its AI selects `PROCESS_CULTURE`, `pushOrder` leaves the default `iData2 == -1`.
When scheduled Auto Play ends, `CvGame::setAIAutoPlay(0,true,...)` calls
`CvPlayer::setHumanDisabled(false)`. That restores human identity but does not clear,
re-push, dirty or normalize city production orders.

The Python end path also does no city-production normalization. `AIAutoPlay.py` calls
`game.endAIAutoPlay(...)`; after the DLL has restored the surviving active player to
human status, the later Python `if not pPlayer.isHuman()` fallback normally does not run.

The remaining generic production checks do not repair the metadata:

* `CvCity::doCheckProduction()` sees the existing `ORDER_MAINTAIN` as valid and does not
  open choose-production because the city already has production.
* `checkCanContinueProduction` only asks whether the process can still be maintained.
* `m_bAutoPlayJustEnded` is used for alert/message suppression, not queue normalization.
* Once human again, `CvCity::doProduction` no longer calls `AI_chooseProduction()` for a
  normal non-automated city, so the AI's per-turn process reconsideration disappears.

The inherited process therefore crosses the human-status boundary intact with
`iData2 == -1`.

CURRENT SAS DATA / CLEAN ORDINARY REPRODUCTION
----------------------------------------------
Current SAS has a live Culture process:

    PROCESS_CULTURE
        TechPrereq = TECH_DRAMA
        ProductionToCommerceModifier(COMMERCE_CULTURE) = 50

`CvCityAI::AI_bestProcess` evaluates every maintainable process. `AI_processValue`
explicitly adds the Culture conversion value for first-ring/low-culture expansion while
`getCultureLevel() <= 1`, and ordinary `AI_chooseProduction` has both a process-by-value
choice and a final process fallback that push:

    pushOrder(ORDER_MAINTAIN, eBestProcess);

The strongest differential setup uses CULTURE LEVEL 1 rather than level 0. A human who
manually starts Culture at level 1 receives `iData2 = 1`, and K-Mod's stop condition
therefore fires when the city reaches level 2. The temporary AI instead creates the
same process with `iData2 = -1`.

Compact reproduction:

1. Human player has TECH_DRAMA and a city at culture level 1.
2. Start AI Auto Play. Let the temporary AI select PROCESS_CULTURE through its ordinary
   city-production logic while the city remains at culture level 1.
3. Arrange the scheduled hand-back while the city is still below the level-2 culture
   threshold and the Culture process remains its head order. This is an ordinary timing
   state: AI process orders are re-evaluated/re-pushed each AI production turn.
4. Auto Play ends before the human's next active turn. The city is now human-controlled,
   non-production-automated and still running PROCESS_CULTURE, but its head order has
   `iData2 == -1` rather than the human marker 1.
5. On the returned human turn, `CvCity::doTurn` performs `doCulture()` before
   `doProduction()`. The process's culture can therefore raise the city from culture
   level 1 to level 2 on that turn.
6. `setCultureTimes100 -> updateCultureLevel` updates the level immediately. When
   `doProduction` runs afterward, the correct human-created order would satisfy
   `iData2 > 0 && getCultureLevel() > iData2` and be popped.
7. The inherited AI order has `iData2 == -1`, so the stop condition fails solely because
   the human stop metadata was never installed. Build Culture continues beyond the
   border expansion until the player notices and manually changes production (or some
   unrelated queue transition replaces it).

This costs real city production/commerce allocation and defeats the explicit K-Mod
human convenience behavior. It is not merely a hidden metadata discrepancy.

WHY AI'S NORMAL REEVALUATION DOES NOT SELF-HEAL AFTER HAND-BACK
---------------------------------------------------------------
At the start of `CvCity::doProduction`:

    if (!isHuman() || isProductionAutomated())
    {
        if (!isProduction() || isProductionProcess() || isChooseProductionDirty())
            AI().AI_chooseProduction();
    }

This explains why `pushOrder` originally needed the marker only for humans: a genuine
AI running a process comes back through `AI_chooseProduction` every turn. But it also
makes the Auto Play boundary decisive. Once `setHumanDisabled(false)` changes the city
back to an ordinary human city, that reevaluation branch stops immediately while the
last AI process order remains.

ANCESTRY
--------
Stock BtS/Civ4CE does not use this per-order marker. On culture-level increase it
contains the direct logic:

    //Stop Build Culture
    if (isProductionProcess())
    {
        if (GC.getProcessInfo(getProductionProcess()).
            getProductionToCommerceModifier(COMMERCE_CULTURE) > 0)
        {
            popOrder(0, false, true);
        }
    }

K-Mod replaced that direct pop with the current `pushOrder` culture-level snapshot plus
`doProduction` comparison, explicitly commenting that the new mechanism avoids the old
overflow/OOS problems. K-Mod also contains AI Auto Play and the human-disable mechanism.
Its `pushOrder` and `doProduction` have the same human-only marker architecture as
current SAS.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains both K-Mod snippets essentially unchanged and has its evolved
`setHumanDisabled` hand-back with no city-production normalization. Current SAS retains
the same architecture. Therefore this exact root begins with the K-Mod redesign rather
than stock BtS.

DUPLICATE / RECONCILIATION CHECK
--------------------------------
The reconciled album was searched for Culture process, `ORDER_MAINTAIN`, `iData2`,
border expansion, Build Culture and AI Auto Play. Existing process/help findings concern
process valuation/help or generic order semantics; none owns a Culture process created
while human-disabled crossing back to human control without K-Mod's stop marker.

F492 and F493 are nearby only because the same Auto Play identity transition exposed
them:

* F492 / KI#815 is a persistent city pop-rush source counter skipped while human-disabled.
* F493 / KI#816 is No-Slavery civic legality bypassed while human-disabled.
* F494 / KI#817 is production-order metadata whose producer intentionally differs for
  AI vs human, followed by an unhandled AI-order -> human-order ownership transition.

The roots and affected state are distinct.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Do not automatically change the `pushOrder` test to `(isHuman() || isHumanDisabled())`
without considering AI behavior. Unlike the No-Slavery rules, K-Mod intentionally gives
genuine AI process orders different semantics because AI production is reconsidered
every turn; forcing human stop metadata onto all temporary-AI process decisions could
change Auto Play AI behavior before hand-back.

The narrow semantic repair is at the hand-back boundary: when a disabled human becomes
human again, normalize any CURRENT head Culture process that came from AI semantics.
For a non-production-automated city with a maintain order whose Culture conversion is
positive and whose marker is negative, initialize its stop baseline to the city's
current positive culture level. That preserves K-Mod's human behavior from the moment
human control resumes without changing how the AI manages processes during Auto Play.

If implementation prefers a shared helper, the invariant to establish is:

    ordinary human + active Culture process + current culture level > 0
        => head-order iData2 is a valid baseline culture level

Care is needed not to overwrite a legitimate existing human marker and not to arm the
known level-0 case, because K-Mod's current stop test itself requires `iData2 > 0`.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Differential human marker
1. Human city at culture level 1 with Drama.
2. Push PROCESS_CULTURE normally as human; assert head `iData2 == 1`.
3. Cross to level 2 through process Culture and assert the process is popped.

B. Auto Play hand-back
1. Same city/state, but let AI Auto Play queue PROCESS_CULTURE at level 1.
2. Before hand-back assert head `iData2 < 0` while human-disabled.
3. End Auto Play while Culture remains the head process.
4. Assert hand-back normalization establishes the human stop baseline at level 1.
5. On the next human turn let process Culture cross to level 2 and assert the process is
   popped exactly as for a human-created order.

C. Genuine AI control
1. Separate genuine AI city running PROCESS_CULTURE.
2. Ensure the repair does not force persistent human stop metadata onto that AI and its
   ordinary per-turn `AI_chooseProduction` behavior is unchanged.

D. Production automation control
1. Human city with production automation intentionally enabled.
2. Ensure any normalization policy does not conflict with governor/AI production
   semantics chosen for production-automated human cities.

POST-F494 HUMAN/AI IDENTITY / PROCESSBUILDING / LOW-COVERAGE COUNTER PASS
------------------------------------------------------------------------
The continuation deliberately kept F495 unused while widening from F494's AI-Auto-Play
hand-back boundary. The remaining `isHuman()` sites and lightly named persistent counters
were challenged as transition-sensitive state rather than assumed buggy from surface
asymmetry.

1. RANDOM-EVENT `OtherPlayerAI` HUMAN-IDENTITY SEAM IS CURRENT-DATA MASKED.

`CvPlayer::canTrigger(EventTriggerTypes, PlayerTypes ePlayer, ...)` contains:

    if (isHuman() && kTrigger.isOtherPlayerAI())
        return false;

Caller orientation was re-traced: when one player searches for the trigger's other-player
target, it invokes `candidateOtherPlayer.canTrigger(..., initiatingPlayer, ...)`, so the
`isHuman()` predicate classifies the candidate target, not an accidentally inverted caller.
A namespace-aware scan of current `CIV4EventTriggerInfos.xml` finds no trigger with
`bOtherPlayerAI=1`. Therefore AI Auto Play cannot currently expose a shipped trigger whose
eligibility permanently differs through this flag. Generic/modmod sensitivity remains, but
there is no current F495 producer.

2. THE REMAINING HUMAN/AI GATES ARE MOSTLY TEMPORARY CONTROL-MODE POLICY, NOT CACHED STATE.

The broad `CvPlayer.cpp` / `CvCity.cpp` identity sweep closes the obvious neighboring
families:

* AI handicap research/growth/upkeep/worker/training modifiers deliberately apply while
  the player is AI-controlled;
* religion, event, production and diplomacy decisions become AI decisions while Auto Play
  owns the turn;
* human popups/reminders are deliberately suppressed, with comments explicitly accounting
  for Auto Play in several paths;
* production decay / AI production reevaluation differences are control-mode semantics;
  F494 was special because the AI-created Culture process survives the boundary into the
  later human regime without K-Mod's required human stop metadata.

No second persistent source comparable to F492/F494 was established from these generic
policy gates.

3. `processBuilding` / `processCivics` SOURCE-COUNTER RECONCILIATION REMAINS CLEAN APART
   FROM ALREADY-OWNED ROOTS.

The current building-effect producer set was re-enumerated against the player mutators and
the earlier WIP181/WIP182/WIP184 controls. Live sources either use dynamic consumers or
perform the needed cache/assignment refresh. Obsolescence replays building effects
symmetrically through `CvTeam::changeObsoleteBuildingCount` -> city `processBuilding`.

Current notable producers checked include:

* CivicOption grants: Colossus -> Government, Mausoleum -> Economy,
  Shwedagon Paya -> Legal (the WIP226 sentence claiming none exist was already corrected
  in WIP228); their LOSS-side problem is F459/KI#782, not a new root;
* global GP/GG/anarchy/Golden-Age/war-weariness modifiers;
* Statue of Liberty / Notre Dame free-specialist effects;
* Great Lighthouse coastal trade route and sea-plot yield effects;
* global health/happiness and Three Gorges Dam area clean power;
* specialist extra commerce/yield and state-religion building commerce.

The known state-religion building-commerce invalidation is F476/KI#799. TeamShare
area-counter noncanonical signed counts remain the earlier robustness note. No independent
F495 source/cache mismatch survived.

4. LOW-COVERAGE HISTORICAL / LIVE COUNTERS RECONFIRMED THEIR CONTRACTS.

* `m_iNumUnitGoldenAges` is intentionally monotonic. `CvUnit::goldenAge` consumes the
  required distinct Great People and then increments it once; `unitsRequiredForGoldenAge`
  uses the count to raise the price of later unit-triggered Golden Ages.
* `m_iHighestUnitLevel` is likewise a historical maximum, not a live-unit count; prior
  audit already covered its prerequisite use.
* unit/building class Count/Making arrays remain paired through unit init/kill and city
  push/pop/upgrade queue transitions (reconfirmed against the WIP226 class-Making pass).
* `m_aiImprovementCount` is paired by plot owner/improvement transitions; the separate
  F181 issue is its misuse as a build-capability proxy in CitySiteEvaluator, not a stale
  count producer in CvPlayer.
* `m_aiUpkeepCount` is dead legacy state guarded by `FErrorMsg`; current civic upkeep is
  derived from active civics and has no ordinary compiled mutator consumer.
* cities-lost is already inside F477's recycled-PlayerTypes identity family; it is not a
  fresh counter-lifecycle root here.
* StrikeTurns execution was already audited earlier; the thin mutator itself adds no new
  transition defect.

5. PLAYER-SLOT / TEAM-SLOT INDEXED ARRAYS ARE ALREADY SCRUBBED ON RESET.

A reset/serialization re-loop specifically challenged indexed player/team arrays. Current
`CvPlayer::reset` clears this player's arrays and also clears other players' entries keyed
by the recycled identity where necessary:

    other.m_aiGoldPerTurnByPlayer.resetVal(getID());
    other.m_abEverSeenDemographics.resetVal(getID());
    other.m_aiEspionageSpendingWeightAgainstTeam.resetVal(getTeam());

The espionage-weight recycle concern was already recorded as a clean control in WIP219.
No new recycled-slot alias was found in these arrays.

6. CITY-TRADE ANGER-TIMER COPY DURING AUTO PLAY IS NOT PROMOTED.

`CvPlayer::acquireCity` snapshots Hurry / Conscript / Defy-Resolution anger timers but,
for `bTrade`, AdvCiv copies them into the replacement city only when:

    isHuman() && (old owner's team is human || old owner is on our team)

A temporary human-disabled player therefore follows the AI branch and can receive a traded
city without those timers. This is persistent and initially resembles F492/F494.

The semantic challenge does not establish a hand-back invariant, however. The AdvCiv
change is explicitly transactional anti-exploit policy: it preserves timers only when the
RECIPIENT is human at the moment of the trade and the counterpart relationship makes a
reset exploitable. AI recipients intentionally get the AI transfer semantics. Auto Play
also legitimately lets that AI make irreversible city/diplomacy decisions. Unlike F492
(current-human building entitlement) and F494 (a surviving process later governed by human
queue semantics), there is no later calculation whose correctness says these historical
transfer timers must be reconstructed when control changes back. Treat this as intended
control-at-action-time behavior unless a stronger explicit Auto-Play contract or ordinary
reproduction proves otherwise; no F495.

7. `m_cancelingExport` IS TRANSIENT TRADE-UI BOOKKEEPING, NOT A PERSISTENT IDENTITY ROOT.

The list remembers resource exports whose cancellation popup is expected so the renegotiate
trade table does not temporarily hide the just-canceled resource. It is rebuilt from saved
CANCEL_DEAL diplomacy popups on load and cleared at player-turn end (explicitly because the
importer may have died). It does not drive authoritative trade state; the actual deal has
already been killed. A recycled PlayerTypes alias in this transient window was therefore
not promoted without a concrete authoritative consequence.

8. CVPLAYER RESET / SERIALIZATION COVERAGE CHECK FOUND ONLY INTENTIONAL TRANSIENTS.

A mechanical comparison of CvPlayer header members against reset/read/write found no new
persistent member omitted from both initialization and serialization. Fields absent from
serialization are expected transient/derived state such as `m_bDisableHuman`,
`m_bAutoPlayJustEnded`, popup-relaunch count, start-time/UI flags, replay-save state,
scoreboard expansion, message counts and bonus-help caches. `m_bHuman` itself is derived
from InitCore slot status via `updateHuman` rather than serialized as authoritative player
state.

Post-WIP232 closures / controls:

1. Human-disabled defeat in CvPlayer::acquireCity is deliberate deferred cleanup, not an orphaned player-state bug.
   - acquireCity skips oldOwner.verifyAlive() only when the old owner isHumanDisabled(), with the local AdvCiv comment explaining that immediate Auto-Play defeat handling can crash when the Unit map layer is enabled.
   - The normal game update subsequently runs updateMoves() and then unconditional CvGame::testAlive(); testAlive calls verifyAlive() for every player.
   - CvPlayer::verifyAlive has a dedicated human-disabled Auto-Play defeat branch that transfers the disabled-human identity to another alive AI slot and kills the defeated slot before normal hand-back.
   - AIAutoPlay.py itself treats CvPlayer::verifyAlive as the normal transfer mechanism; its popup path is fallback behavior.
   - Therefore the acquireCity guard postpones elimination to the safe game-update phase rather than losing the lifecycle transition. No F495.

2. CvGame::setVoteSourceReligion has a generic cache-invalidation omission, but current ordinary SAS gameplay has no producer for the unsafe transition.
   - CvCity::processVoteSource caches vote-source free specialists and religion-building yield/commerce according to CvGame::getVoteSourceReligion().
   - setVoteSourceReligion merely replaces m_aeVoteSourceReligion and optionally announces; it does not remove old vote-source effects or add new ones. A generic API/Python change from one non-NO religion to another while a vote source is active could therefore leave old cached city effects and miss new ones.
   - Current compiled gameplay only assigns a vote-source religion when a state-religion vote-source building is first created and the stored religion is still NO_RELIGION. That assignment occurs before processBuilding/changeDiploVote activates the vote source, so the ordinary first-activation path caches the correct religion.
   - Full current source search found no shipped Python call that later changes an already-active vote source to a different religion. Existing ordinary membership/religion/diploVote transitions wrap processVoteSource correctly.
   - Preserve as API/robustness knowledge only; current shipped reachability does not justify F495.

1. TEAM EVENT OCCURRENCE PROPAGATION INVERSION IS AN EXACT EXISTING CONTROL.

`CvPlayer::setEventOccured` still contains the reversed Team-event member predicate:

    for (MemberIter itOtherMember(getTeam()); itOtherMember.hasNext(); ++itOtherMember)
    {
        if (itOtherMember->getID() != getID())
            continue;
        itOtherMember->setEventOccured(eEvent, kEventTriggered, false);
    }

This only writes the occurrence back to self instead of the other team members. The
album already preserves this source defect repeatedly, and current SAS XML still has no
Team EventInfo producer that reaches it. No F495 duplicate was created.

2. DELAYED EVENT COUNTDOWN USE-AFTER-ERASE IS ALSO AN EXACT EXISTING DORMANT CONTROL.

`CvPlayer::doEvents` retains:

    EventTriggeredData const* pTriggeredData = getEventCountdown(eLoopEvent);
    ...
    applyEvent(eLoopEvent, pTriggeredData->m_iId);
    resetEventCountdown(eLoopEvent);
    aCleanup.push_back(pTriggeredData->m_iId);

`resetEventCountdown` erases the map node whose value address is `pTriggeredData`, so
the last dereference is invalid C++. This had already been fully recorded in the album;
current SAS event data does not provide a live AdditionalEventTime producer. No F495.

3. `setLoyalMember` VOTE-SOURCE CACHE ORDER RECONFIRMED CORRECT.

Defying or endorsing an AP/UN-style resolution changes `m_abLoyalMember`, and it was
worth rechecking whether city vote-source bonuses could survive stale. The setter is
explicitly transactional:

    processVoteSource(eVoteSource, false);
    m_abLoyalMember.set(eVoteSource, bNewValue);
    processVoteSource(eVoteSource, true);

`CvCity::processVoteSource` consults the player's current loyalty. Thus true->false
removes the old effects before the flag changes and does not re-add them; false->true
does not remove anything and then correctly adds them. No stale city source was found.

4. CANCELLED TRIGGERED VOTES LEAVE OLD `m_aVote` ENTRIES, BUT NORMAL FREE-LIST ID
   GENERATIONS PREVENT THEM FROM ALIASING A LATER VOTE.

A strong-looking candidate arose in `CvGame::doVoteResults`. If a resolution becomes
invalid between launch and result processing:

    if (!canDoResolution(eVoteSource, subdata))
    {
        ... election cancelled messages ...
    }
    ...
    deleteVoteTriggered(pVoteTriggered->getID());

Unlike the normal result path, this branch does not call `setVoteOutcome`, and therefore
does not clear each living player's `CvPlayer::m_aVote` entry for the cancelled vote.
This is genuine leftover state.

However, it does NOT create the initially suspected ordinary stale-ballot alias.
`m_votesTriggered` is an `FFreeListTrashArray`. Reusing a freed physical slot does not
reuse the same public ID. `FFreeListTrashArray::add()` assigns:

    pData->setID(m_iCurrentID + iIndex);
    m_iCurrentID += FLTA_MAX_BUCKETS;

while `CvPlayer::getVote` compares the complete stored integer ID. A later triggered
vote that reuses the same array index therefore has a different generation-bearing ID,
and the old `m_aVote` pair does not match it. This is untidy/stale storage and could be
cleaned on cancellation, but no current authoritative wrong vote was established.

This also refines the earlier dead-player stale-vote control: the free-list is recyclable
at the slot level, but ordinary generation-tagged IDs prevent direct old->new aliasing.
Do not describe the normal vote ID as simply reused without this qualification.

5. VOTE/RESOLUTION PLAYER HELPERS IN THIS BLOCK ARE PRIMARILY DYNAMIC CONSUMERS.

`getVotes`, `isVotingMember`, `isFullMember`, `canDoResolution`, `canDefyResolution`,

from current player/team/city state. Apart from the separately recorded stale candidate
eligibility findings in Queue 019 and the vote-source religion API-only invalidation
note from WIP233, this re-loop did not expose a new CvPlayer-owned cached source requiring
F495.

STATUS

Queue 004 `CvGameCoreDLL/CvPlayer.cpp` remains OPEN.
