F495 / KI#818 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------
TITLE:
ADVCIV `acquireCity` INDEXES THE OLD-CITY BUILDING SNAPSHOT BY THE RECIPIENT'S
MAPPED BUILDING TYPE, SO ORDINARY CROSS-CIVILIZATION UNIQUE-BUILDING
CONVERSIONS DISAPPEAR ON CITY TRANSFER

ROOT
----
`CvPlayer::acquireCity` correctly snapshots the OLD city's concrete building types:

    FOR_EACH_ENUM2(Building, eBuilding)
    {
        aiNumRealBuilding.set(eBuilding, pOldCity->getNumRealBuilding(eBuilding));
        aeBuildingOriginalOwner.set(eBuilding,
                pOldCity->getBuildingOriginalOwner(eBuilding));
        aiBuildingOriginalTime.set(eBuilding,
                pOldCity->getBuildingOriginalTime(eBuilding));
    }

Later, while rebuilding the replacement city, it iterates each SOURCE building type
`eLoopBuilding`, derives its BuildingClass, and maps that class to the acquiring
civilization's concrete type:

    BuildingClassTypes eBuildingClass = GC.getInfo(eLoopBuilding).
            getBuildingClassType();
    BuildingTypes const eBuilding = (GC.getInfo(eLoopBuilding).isWorldWonder() ?
            eLoopBuilding : getCivilization().getBuilding(eBuildingClass));

That mapping is required: a foreign unique building must become the recipient's
civilization-equivalent building of the same class.

The AdvCiv/SAS refactor then uses the DESTINATION type `eBuilding` to read the OLD-city
snapshot:

    kNewCity.setNumRealBuildingTimed(eBuilding,
            ...
            kNewCity.getNumRealBuilding(eBuilding) +
            aiNumRealBuilding.get(eBuilding),
            false,
            aeBuildingOriginalOwner.get(eBuilding),
            aiBuildingOriginalTime.get(eBuilding));

When source and destination concrete BuildingTypes differ, the snapshot is normally
stored under `eLoopBuilding`, not `eBuilding`. The destination entry was absent from the
old city and is normally zero / unknown. `setNumRealBuildingTimed` therefore receives no
positive count; its `iChange == 0` early return performs no conversion.

The result is not merely lost provenance metadata. The building itself disappears.

DETERMINISTIC CURRENT-DATA REPRO — MAYA BALL COURT -> COLOSSEUM BY CITY TRADE
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS data has:

    CIVILIZATION_MAYA:
        BUILDINGCLASS_COLOSSEUM -> BUILDING_MAYA_BALL_COURT

while the default BuildingClass mapping is:

    BUILDINGCLASS_COLOSSEUM -> BUILDING_COLOSSEUM

Both current concrete buildings have `bNeverCapture=0` and `iConquestProb=66`.

Use an ordinary legal city gift/trade, which reaches:

    CvDeal::startTrade(TRADE_CITIES)
      -> CvCity::doTask(TASK_GIFT / TASK_CEDE)
      -> recipient CvPlayer::acquireCity(city, false, true, ...)

`bTrade=true` makes the example deterministic; no conquest-retention roll is involved.

Suppose Maya owns a non-capital city with one real Ball Court and transfers it to a
non-Maya civilization whose Colosseum-class mapping is the ordinary Colosseum.
The snapshot contains:

    aiNumRealBuilding[BUILDING_MAYA_BALL_COURT] = 1
    aiNumRealBuilding[BUILDING_COLOSSEUM] = 0

During restoration the source loop reaches `BUILDING_MAYA_BALL_COURT`, maps its class to
recipient type `BUILDING_COLOSSEUM`, and then incorrectly reads:

    aiNumRealBuilding.get(BUILDING_COLOSSEUM) == 0

instead of the source snapshot entry. The new city therefore receives zero Colosseums.
The Ball Court is gone with the killed old city, and no later acquisition pass converts
or reconstructs it.

The reverse direction fails symmetrically. If Maya receives an ordinary Colosseum city,
the source snapshot has Colosseum=1 and BallCourt=0; the mapped destination is Ball Court,
so the code reads BallCourt=0 and loses the class building rather than converting it.

CURRENT DATA BREADTH
--------------------
A full current SAS CivilizationInfo/BuildingClass scan finds 43 non-default concrete
BuildingType mappings, 36 of them on non-Barbarian civilizations. Therefore this is not
a one-off Maya-data quirk. Any transfer in which an actually present non-world building
maps to a different concrete type for the recipient exercises the same wrong snapshot
key.

Representative current major-civilization mappings include:

    Maya      Colosseum  -> Ball Court
    America   Courthouse -> Federal Courthouse
    China     Market     -> Changpingcang
    Celts     Forge      -> La Tene Smithy
    Ireland   Aqueduct   -> Muileann Uisce
    Korea     Library    -> Gyeongdang
    Rome      Market     -> Forum
    Zulu      Barracks   -> Ikhanda

The exact gameplay effect depends on whether the city transfer/conquest otherwise keeps
that building, but legal `bTrade=true` transfers provide a deterministic ordinary path.

NO NORMAL SELF-HEAL
-------------------
The old `CvCity` is killed before the replacement city is initialized. The only generic
building restoration is this `acquireCity` loop. `CvCity::setNumRealBuildingTimed`
returns immediately when the requested count equals the current count, and there is no
later BuildingClass reconstruction pass that notices the missing unique/base equivalent.
The transferred city therefore permanently loses the building until it is rebuilt by
normal gameplay.

ANCESTRY — ADVCIV REGRESSION
-----------------------------
Stock/BtS-lineage Civ4CE and K-Mod 1.46 both keep the source loop index for OLD-city data.
Their acquisition loop conceptually does:

    source = (BuildingTypes)iI;
    destination = recipient civilization building for source BuildingClass;
    ...
    iNum += paiNumRealBuilding[iI];
    setNumRealBuildingTimed(destination, ...,
            paiBuildingOriginalOwner[iI], paiBuildingOriginalTime[iI]);

They also test the source concrete building's `isNeverCapture` and
`getConquestProbability` while using the recipient building only for the destination
location/class checks.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same destination-key snapshot reads as current SAS. Thus
the confirmed count/provenance mix-up was introduced in the AdvCiv refactor lineage
between K-Mod and current base AdvCiv and then inherited by SAS; it is not stock BtS or
K-Mod behavior.

ADJACENT SOURCE/DESTINATION METADATA NOTE
-----------------------------------------
The same AdvCiv refactor also changed conquest policy lookups from the SOURCE concrete
building to the mapped DESTINATION `kBuilding`:

    kBuilding.isNeverCapture()
    kBuilding.getConquestProbability()

where K-Mod/BtS use the source type. Current major-civ UB mappings happen to match their
base buildings for these two fields, so the count-loss bug is the independently live
major-civ consequence. Current Barbarian Granary/Harbor/Lighthouse mappings do differ
(33% vs the normal 66% conquest probability), so once the count-key bug is repaired the
source/destination policy choice must also be restored or deliberately specified rather
than silently left on the recipient type. Treat this as an immediate F495 sibling, not
a separate F496 while the primary count bug masks its conversion consequence.

DUPLICATE / ALBUM CHECK
-----------------------
The reconciled album has no prior numbered root for `aiNumRealBuilding` being read under
the mapped recipient BuildingType during `acquireCity`, nor for unique/base building
conversion disappearing on ownership transfer.

One earlier Queue 003 city-bar control sentence stated that non-Wonder foreign UBs are
converted to the new owner's civilization-equivalent BuildingClass entry during
acquisition. That statement assumed the acquisition loop's intended behavior while
checking city-bar iteration; it did not inspect the source-vs-destination snapshot key.
C031-WIP235 explicitly SUPERSEDES that narrow control sentence. It is not a duplicate
finding.

Earlier acquisition findings involving state-religion building-commerce refresh,
TeamShare building effects, BuildingOriginalOwner PlayerTypes recycling and corporation
HQ transfer have different roots. F495 concerns the concrete building restoration key
itself.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Keep source and destination identities distinct throughout the loop.

Suggested shape:

    BuildingTypes const eSourceBuilding = eLoopBuilding;
    BuildingClassTypes const eBuildingClass =
            GC.getInfo(eSourceBuilding).getBuildingClassType();
    BuildingTypes const eDestBuilding =
            (GC.getInfo(eSourceBuilding).isWorldWonder() ?
            eSourceBuilding : getCivilization().getBuilding(eBuildingClass));

Then:

* read old-city count from `aiNumRealBuilding[eSourceBuilding]`;
* read original owner/time from the SOURCE entries;
* set the surviving count on `eDestBuilding`;
* use destination type for destination-validity/location and destination count;
* preserve/restore the inherited source-building conquest policy unless a deliberate
  design change is documented (`isNeverCapture`, `getConquestProbability`).

This is essentially the K-Mod/BtS source/destination separation expressed through the
AdvCiv enum-map refactor.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Deterministic Maya -> normal trade:
1. Maya city has one Ball Court and no ordinary Colosseum concrete entry.
2. Legally gift/trade the city to a civilization using ordinary Colosseum.
3. Assert the replacement city has one real Colosseum.
4. Assert original owner/time metadata came from the Ball Court source record.

B. Deterministic normal -> Maya trade:
1. Non-Maya city has one ordinary Colosseum.
2. Legally transfer it to Maya.
3. Assert the replacement city has one real Ball Court.

C. Conquest source-policy test after A/B are fixed:
Use a source/destination pair whose conquest metadata intentionally differs (current
Barbarian Granary is a direct data control) and verify the chosen retention policy uses
the documented/source semantics rather than accidentally switching with recipient civ.

C031-WIP236 — F495 EXACT REGRESSION HISTORY + F496 STARTING-PLOT CACHE CONTROL

F495 / KI#818 — EXACT REACHABLE-HISTORY REFINEMENT
--------------------------------------------------
The reachable AdvCiv history now identifies the regression much more precisely than the
broad K-Mod-vs-AdvCiv ancestry proof in WIP235.

1. Practical commit 1582, `ad0fd03d9476e947b828098800d566c605ec896b`,
   "Walls and Castles are destroyed upon reconquest", refactored the acquisition building
   loop and changed conquest-policy lookups to the mapped destination `kBuilding`.
   Crucially, however, OLD-city count and provenance were still read with the SOURCE loop
   index:

       paiNumRealBuilding[iI]
       paiBuildingOriginalOwner[iI]
       paiBuildingOriginalTime[iI]

   Thus foreign-UB conversion itself was still correct after this commit.

2. Practical commit 2416, `b9b15b001b7f47a1bef8f264332988026f87dedb`,
   "Use EnumMap in CvPlayer; and other refactoring changes.", converted those raw arrays
   to EnumMaps. The old source-indexed reads became:

       aiNumRealBuilding.get(eBuilding)
       aeBuildingOriginalOwner.get(eBuilding)
       aiBuildingOriginalTime.get(eBuilding)

   while the same loop also repurposed/mapped `eBuilding` to the RECIPIENT's concrete
   building type. This is the actual source-vs-destination snapshot-key regression behind
   F495.

3. Practical commit 2438, `8aab6ddd80272abaf81e271207f05fc1d43d3690`,
   "Fix recently introduced freeze on city conquest", introduced a separate source loop
   variable `eLoopBuilding` and correctly changed the early source-count test to:

       aiNumRealBuilding.get(eLoopBuilding)

   but left the later restoration reads indexed by mapped destination `eBuilding`.
   The freeze was fixed while the quieter UB-conversion data-loss bug survived.

This exact history also explains why the current code looks almost correct: the source
identity is already available as `eLoopBuilding`; the final restoration block simply
uses the wrong one of the two concrete BuildingTypes for OLD-city data.

IMMEDIATE F495 SIBLING CLOSURES
-------------------------------
* `CvPlot::canConstruct(eBuilding)` in this acquisition context is the destination
  building-location/geometry validity test (water/river/min-area etc.), corresponding to
  the old K-Mod city-location check; it does not add a second source-key bug.
* BuildingClass extra yield/commerce/happiness/health snapshots are keyed by
  `BuildingClassTypes`, so source/destination concrete BuildingType remapping does not
  misindex those arrays. Their missing effect when a UB disappears is an F495 symptom.
* World wonders keep source == destination and are therefore not exposed to F495.
* Free-building state is conceptually separate: the acquisition snapshot intentionally
  records real buildings, while recipient player/trait/free-building sources govern the
  replacement city.
* `isProductionMaxedBuildingClass` is class-keyed and appropriate for this conversion.
* Source/destination original-owner/time loss remains part of F495's same wrong-key root,
  presently masked whenever the wrong destination count is zero.

F496 CANDIDATE CONTROL — setStartingPlot REBUILDS THE OLD AREA TOO EARLY
------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::setStartingPlot(pNewValue, true)` has an inherited ordering oddity. When an
existing start moves, it decrements the old area's starting-plot count and immediately
calls:

    GC.getMap().updateMinOriginalStartDist(pOldStartingPlot->getArea());

BEFORE `m_pStartingPlot` is changed. `CvMap::updateMinOriginalStartDist` clears the area
cache and then scans every player's current `getStartingPlot()`. The moving player still
points to the old plot, so the old-area rebuild reintroduces distances from a start that
is about to leave. If the new start is on another area, the second rebuild touches only
the new area; clearing a start to NULL has no second rebuild at all.

This ordering is inherited unchanged in substance from BtS/Civ4CE through K-Mod and
AdvCiv.

CURRENT-CONSEQUENCE CHECK
-------------------------
The stale-cache state is real, but current AdvCiv no longer has the old C++ AI consumer
of `CvPlot::getMinOriginalStartDist()`. In current SAS source, executable consumers are
only the shipped Highlands.py, Boreal.py and Rainforest.py start-assignment routines.
Those scripts consult the value while assigning previously-unassigned players and call
`setStartingPlot(..., true)` from a NULL starting plot; the bad OLD-area branch is not
entered.

Other shipped scripts do reassign existing starts with `bUpdateStartDist=true`:
* BTG_Lagoon.py and BTG_Grid.py swap starts during team-position normalization;
* Equal_Islands_V2_beta.py relocates already-assigned starts while copying the selected
  template island/region.

However, none of those scripts subsequently reads `getMinOriginalStartDist()`. Equal
Islands performs the move in `normalizeAddExtras`, after its assignment phase; the BTG
normalization/resource code likewise has no such consumer. The now-stale cache therefore
has no demonstrated shipped gameplay consumer after those moves.

`CvPlayer::startingPlotWithinRange`, still Python-exported, is also not a hidden consumer
in current SAS: AdvCiv reduced it to a compatibility wrapper returning false.

DISPOSITION
-----------
Do NOT number this as F496. Preserve it as an inherited robustness/API/cache-ordering
control. If future map code begins consuming `MinOriginalStartDist` after a cross-area
start move, the safe ordering would be to change `m_pStartingPlot` first and then rebuild
both distinct affected areas (or otherwise exclude the departing start from the old-area
rebuild).

STATIC-LOCAL HOIST RECHECK — DUPLICATE/CLOSED
---------------------------------------------
The post-WIP236 SAS-specific scan re-enumerated local `static` uses in current
`CvPlayer.cpp`, looking specifically for a game/player-dependent expression accidentally
frozen by a performance hoist. Executable local statics are overwhelmingly immutable
GlobalDefine reads, fixed color/type IDs or translation constants. The one mutable replay
name scratch `static CvWString` is explicitly reassigned on each call.

A mechanical comparison of the GlobalDefine names read by these statics against current
runtime `setDefineINT/FLOAT/STRING/BOOL` writers found no overlap. More importantly, album
reconciliation shows this exact source class was already audited and recorded in WIP181
(`CONTROL — STATIC LOCAL GLOBALDEFINE CACHES ALREADY MECHANICALLY AUDITED`). Therefore
this is a duplicate closure, not F496. Do not repeat it unless a genuinely game-state-
dependent static expression is found later.

TRUE STARTS / processCivics CONCRETE-BUILDING CACHE CANDIDATE — CURRENT DATA CLOSES
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A narrower runtime-civilization-change concern survived WIP182's generic developed-player
`changeCiv` caveat long enough to deserve a current-data check.

`CvPlayer::processCivics` stores civic BuildingHappinessChanges / BuildingHealthChanges
against the CURRENT civilization's concrete BuildingTypes. Player initialization installs
initial civics before `CvGame::setInitialItems` reaches `TrueStarts::changeCivs()`, while
`CvPlayer::changeCiv` calls `resetCivTypeEffects(false)` and does not remove/reapply civics
for a living player. In principle, therefore, a pre-installed civic with a BuildingClass
modifier could leave its concrete-building cache keyed to the civilization that existed
before True Starts even though no city exists yet; later construction of a replacement
civilization's UB would then consult another concrete key.

The current shipped XML masks this architecture completely:
* all 38 current civilizations have the same five initial civics:
  CIVIC_DESPOTISM, CIVIC_BARBARISM, CIVIC_TRIBALISM, CIVIC_DECENTRALIZATION and
  CIVIC_PREHISTORIC_RELIGION;
* none of those five has any BuildingHappinessChanges or BuildingHealthChanges;
* the only current civic BuildingHappinessChanges are on CIVIC_FREE_SPEECH
  (University), CIVIC_NATIONHOOD (Colosseum/Courthouse/Jail), CIVIC_TRADE_BLOC
  (Custom House), and CIVIC_FREE_MARKET (Supermarket); those are not initial civics.

Therefore ordinary current True Starts cannot pre-cache one of these class-to-concrete-
building modifiers before changing civilization. The broader developed-player/debug
`changeCiv` weakness remains the WIP182 robustness caveat; no current shipped True Starts
root consumes F496.

CONTROL — COLONY CREATION WITH RANDOM PERSONALITIES PERFORMS A REDUNDANT DISCARDED
RANDOMIZATION, BUT ONLY SYNCHRONIZED RNG-STREAM CONSUMPTION SURVIVES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A historical partial-fix audit found a real AdvCiv regression in the colony/player-
initialization chain, but the surviving consequence does not meet the present threshold
for F496.

Reachable-history practical commit 2423,
`386a1a5d3a44dc71e40ef82f4922f9ed8970bd6`, "Fix potential issues with Random
Personalities and liberation", added an explicit

    GET_PLAYER(eNewPlayer).changePersonalityType();

immediately before

    GET_PLAYER(eNewPlayer).initInGame(eNewPlayer);

inside `CvGame::addPlayer`.

Later practical 2565 / original-history 2576 repaired Random-Personalities
initialization by making `CvPlayer::initOtherData` call `changePersonalityType()`.
Current colony creation therefore performs:

    CvGame::addPlayer
      -> changePersonalityType()          // first randomization
      -> CvPlayer::initInGame
           -> reset
           -> initOtherData
                -> setAlive(true)
                -> changePersonalityType() // actual surviving randomization

The first randomization is discarded by `reset`. With the current SAS leader table it
nevertheless consumes the synchronized personality-selection draws (56 candidate
leader draws for the 57 current leader entries after the Barbarian exclusion), plus
any synchronized PeaceWeight randomization performed by the selected personality.

The non-reset-side-effect challenge closes the stronger interpretations:
* `reset`/`AI_reset` clears the personality-derived AI state written by the first pass,
  including PeaceWeight, espionage weight and victory-weight caches;
* the final personality is independently and validly randomized by the second pass;
* multiplayer peers consume the same synchronized RNG draws, so this is not a desync;
* the only surviving effect established is perturbation of the later synchronized RNG
  stream.

K-Mod does not contain the extra pre-`initInGame` randomization. This is therefore a
real AdvCiv redundant-RNG regression, but presently preserve it as a low-value
historical/control observation rather than manufacturing F496 from an otherwise valid
final player state.

A conservative cleanup would remove the obsolete `CvGame::addPlayer` pre-init
`changePersonalityType()` call and leave personality initialization owned by
`initOtherData`.

CONTROL — PRACTICAL 2328 OTHER-PLAYER ANARCHY TRADE-ROUTE DEPENDENCY HAS A GLOBAL
INVALIDATION HOOK
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
AdvCiv's `CvPlayer::canHaveTradeRoutesWith` deliberately makes another player's anarchy
invalidate trade with that player (including teammate trade except self-trade). Because
city trade-route partners are cached, this initially suggested a cross-player stale-
route root when B enters/leaves anarchy.

The complete transition closes it. `CvPlayer::changeAnarchyTurns` detects the actual
anarchy-state edge and performs:

    updateCommerce();
    updateMaintenance();
    updateTradeRoutes();
    updateCorporation();
    GC.getGame().updateTradeRoutes();

The global call iterates the living players and rebuilds their trade routes, so A's
cached routes to B are invalidated when B's anarchy status changes. This is an explicit
`advc.124` dependency repair, not a missing cross-player invalidator.

The same semantic family had already been noted earlier in the album; this pass adds the
historical practical-2328 connection rather than a new finding.

POST-WIP238 CONTROL — `setCurrentEra` DOES NOT ESTABLISH A LIVE STALE-UWAI CACHE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The final current-era cache challenge was completed before widening again.

`CvPlayer::setCurrentEra` changes the authoritative era and immediately refreshes the
player's AI era factor. A few UWAI cache values are era-sensitive (for example building
production valuation and deployment-distance calculations), so the lack of a direct
full `UWAICache::update()` initially looked like a missing invalidation.

The consumer timing closes the stronger interpretation. UWAI's war/deployment cache is
rebuilt during the next team/player turn preprocessing before the corresponding war-
evaluation consumers execute. Normal research can cross into a new era later in
`CvPlayer::doTurn`, but sampled post-research city/unit/gameplay formulas read
`getCurrentEra()` dynamically rather than consuming the old cached UWAI era values. No
same-turn authoritative consumer of a stale era-sensitive UWAI field was established.

Preserve as a clean timing/invalidation control; no F496 from `setCurrentEra`.


POST-WIP238 CONTROL — HURRY-DERIVED COUNTER ARITHMETIC IS CURRENTLY UNIT-DELTA ONLY
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`changeHurryCount` is generically fragile because on a zero/nonzero edge it changes the
player's derived population/gold-rush counter by the caller's full `iChange` rather than
normalizing the edge to +/-1. A magnitude greater than one could therefore inflate the
derived count.

Current compiled gameplay has exactly one producer, `processCivics`, and it supplies
only `+1`, `-1` or `0` from a civic boolean. The reconciled album had already proved the
same source constraint. Keep this as API/configuration robustness only; no F496.


POST-WIP238 CONTROL — HIRED TRADE-EMBARGO MEMORY ATTRIBUTION IS POLICY, NOT A TYPE BUG
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The AdvCiv comment in `handleDiploEvent(DIPLOEVENT_STOP_TRADING)` wondering whether all
members of the requesting player's team should receive `MEMORY_HIRED_TRADE_EMBARGO`
looked suspicious in team games.

Reconstructing the event roles shows that `getID()` is the individual leader who made
the diplomatic request. Player-specific memory against that requesting leader is
internally coherent, and the analogous hired-war memory also attributes the request to
the requesting player rather than automatically to every teammate. Extending resentment
to the whole team would be a design-policy choice, not a correctness invariant. No F496.


F496 / KI#819 — CORPORATION-SUPPRESSION CIVIC TRANSITIONS CHANGE GLOBAL CORPORATION
LEVELS WITHOUT INVALIDATING OTHER PLAYERS' HQ BUILDING-COMMERCE CACHES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: CONFIRMED CURRENT GAMEPLAY BUG.
ANCESTRY: inherited Firaxis/BtS -> K-Mod -> Base AdvCiv -> SAS.
CURRENT SAS PRODUCERS: `CIVIC_PROTECTIONISM` and `CIVIC_STATE_PROPERTY`.

ROOT INVARIANT
--------------
Global corporation headquarters commerce is not based on raw branch presence. The
player accessor deliberately filters raw corporation counts through current corporation
activity:

    int CvPlayer::getHasCorporationCount(CorporationTypes eCorp) const
    {
        if (!isActiveCorporation(eCorp))
            return 0;
        return m_aiHasCorporationCount.get(eCorp);
    }

    bool CvPlayer::isActiveCorporation(CorporationTypes eCorp) const
    {
        if (isNoCorporations())
            return false;
        if (isNoForeignCorporations() && !hasHeadquarters(eCorp))
            return false;
        return true;
    }

`CvGame::countCorporationLevels` then sums exactly those FILTERED counts across all
living players:

    for (PlayerIter<ALIVE> itPlayer; itPlayer.hasNext(); ++itPlayer)
        iCount += itPlayer->getHasCorporationCount(eCorporation);

That world count is a direct input to corporation-HQ building commerce. For every active
building with `GlobalCorporationCommerce`:

    iCommerceRate +=
        GC.getInfo(eGlobalCommerceCorp).getHeadquarterCommerce(eCommerce) *
        GC.getGame().countCorporationLevels(eGlobalCommerceCorp) *
        getNumActiveBuilding(eBuilding);

The result is NOT recomputed on every query. `CvCity::updateBuildingCommerce` stores it
in serialized `m_aiBuildingCommerce`, and normal base-commerce calculation reads that
stored cache through `getBuildingCommerce(eCommerce)`.

MISSED INVALIDATION
-------------------
Raw religion/corporation population changes already establish the intended dependency.
`CvPlayer::changeHasReligionCount` and `changeHasCorporationCount` both call:

    GC.getGame().updateBuildingCommerce();

which rebuilds building commerce for every living player's cities because changing a
world religion/corporation level can alter somebody else's shrine/HQ income.

Changing corporation ACTIVITY through civics alters the same effective world-level
input but does not perform that global rebuild:

    void CvPlayer::changeNoCorporationsCount(int iChange)
    {
        ...
        m_iNoCorporationsCount += iChange;
        ...
        updateCorporation();
    }

    void CvPlayer::changeNoForeignCorporationsCount(int iChange)
    {
        ...
        m_iNoForeignCorporationsCount += iChange;
        ...
        updateCorporation();
    }

`CvPlayer::updateCorporation()` only loops that player's own cities. Each
`CvCity::updateCorporation()` does rebuild THAT CITY'S building-commerce cache, but it
does not call `CvGame::updateBuildingCommerce`. Therefore headquarters buildings owned
by OTHER players remain stale when this player's active branch count changes solely
because of corporation-suppression policy.

`processCivics` directly drives both mutators. `setCivics` / `revolution` contains no
later global building-commerce rebuild that closes the dependency.

CURRENT SAS DATA MAKES BOTH POLICY EDGES LIVE
---------------------------------------------
Current Economy civic XML has:

    CIVIC_PROTECTIONISM
        bNoCorporations        = 0
        bNoForeignCorporations = 1

    CIVIC_STATE_PROPERTY
        bNoCorporations        = 1
        bNoForeignCorporations = 0

Current SAS also has all seven corporation HQ buildings:

    BUILDING_CORPORATION_1 ... BUILDING_CORPORATION_7

with matching:

    GlobalCorporationCommerce = CORPORATION_1 ... CORPORATION_7
    ObsoleteTech              = NONE

and every current corporation has headquarters commerce:

    HeadquarterCommerces = [4 Gold, 0 Research, 0 Culture]

Thus every active corporation level is worth exactly +4 cached Gold in that
corporation's HQ building under current data.

DETERMINISTIC CURRENT-SAS REPRO — PROTECTIONISM, ONE FOREIGN CEREAL-MILLS BRANCH
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A minimal ordinary-game shape avoids any State-Property/HQ-owner local-refresh nuance:

1. Player A owns `CORPORATION_1` / Cereal Mills HQ.
2. Player B does NOT own that HQ and has exactly one Cereal Mills branch city.
3. B begins on a civic where foreign corporations are active.
4. All corporation and building-commerce caches are first allowed to settle.
5. B adopts `CIVIC_PROTECTIONISM` during B's active turn.

Before the switch, B contributes one level to:

    CvGame::countCorporationLevels(CORPORATION_1)

and A's HQ building therefore contains +4 Gold attributable to B's branch.

After the switch, the dynamic truth changes immediately:

    B.isNoForeignCorporations() == true
    B.hasHeadquarters(CORPORATION_1) == false
    B.isActiveCorporation(CORPORATION_1) == false
    B.getHasCorporationCount(CORPORATION_1) == 0

so the mathematically correct world corporation level falls by one and A's HQ building
should lose exactly 4 Gold.

B's `changeNoForeignCorporationsCount` calls `B.updateCorporation()`, correctly zeroing
B's own foreign-branch corporation output. A's HQ city is not part of B's city loop, so
A's `m_aiBuildingCommerce[GOLD]` remains +4 too high.

AUTHORITATIVE SAME-ROUND CONSEQUENCE
------------------------------------
This is not just stale display state.

`CvCity::getBaseCommerceRateTimes100` includes the stored:

    getBuildingCommerce(COMMERCE_GOLD)

and `CvPlayer::calculateGoldRate` consumes the player's city commerce. `CvPlayer::doGold`
then books that rate through `changeGold`.

`CvGame::setGameTurn` does perform a global `updateBuildingCommerce`, so there is an
eventual next-round self-heal. But a civic switch occurs after the current game-turn
refresh. In an ordinary sequential single-player game, use the human B as an earlier
player and the HQ owner A as a later AI player. B can adopt Protectionism before ending
its active turn; A's later `doGold()` in the same round can then book the stale extra
+4 Gold from B's now-inactive branch before the next `setGameTurn` refresh.

With N foreign B branches, the error is exactly:

    stale HQ Gold = +4 * N per affected corporation HQ

for that consumption window. Leaving Protectionism produces the reverse direction:
A's HQ can remain 4*N Gold too LOW until the next global building-commerce invalidator.

`CIVIC_STATE_PROPERTY` supplies the same root for every corporation branch of the
switching player. If an affected HQ belongs to another player, that HQ city's cache is
likewise outside the switching player's local `updateCorporation()` loop.

WHY THIS IS NOT F491 / KI#814
-----------------------------
F491 and F496 share the dynamic `isActiveCorporation` predicate but have different
missed inputs and different authoritative caches.

F491:
* producer/input change: HQ OWNER identity (`CvGame::setHeadquarters`);
* missed targets: old/new owners' OTHER branch-city corporation caches;
* stale state: corporation yield, corporation commerce, produced resources, maintenance;
* typical current exposure: HQ capture/trade while Protectionism is active.

F496:
* producer/input change: NoCorporations / NoForeignCorporations CIVIC activity state;
* missed targets: OTHER PLAYERS' HQ building-commerce caches;
* stale state: `m_aiBuildingCommerce`, specifically global corporation/HQ commerce;
* current exposure: ordinary Protectionism or State Property civic entry/exit with
  foreign branches contributing to another player's HQ.

The prior WIP179/WIP195/WIP226 closure that civic changes call `updateCorporation()`
remains correct for the switching player's OWN corporation-city output. F496 narrows the
missing second invariant: the same activity transition also changes GLOBAL corporation
levels, which require a global HQ building-commerce invalidation.

The album's F476 cache-control discussion explicitly notes that raw
religion/corporation count mutations call global `CvGame::updateBuildingCommerce()`.
F496 identifies an additional input to that same global formula that those earlier
controls did not test.

ANCESTRY
--------
This root is inherited from stock BtS.

Civ4CE/BtS has the same four required pieces:
* `getHasCorporationCount` returns zero when the corporation is inactive;
* `CvGame::countCorporationLevels` sums that filtered accessor;
* HQ building commerce multiplies `HeadquarterCommerce` by that world count;
* `changeNoCorporationsCount` and `changeNoForeignCorporationsCount` call only the
  player's `updateCorporation`, while raw `changeHasCorporationCount` explicitly calls
  global `updateBuildingCommerce`.

Stock current data already exposes it through:
* `CIVIC_MERCANTILISM` -> `bNoForeignCorporations=1`;
* `CIVIC_STATE_PROPERTY` -> `bNoCorporations=1`.

K-Mod 1.46 preserves the same architecture and live civics.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 preserves the same architecture; current SAS changes the foreign-
corporation civic from Mercantilism to Protectionism but retains the dependency.

The global next-game-turn self-heal (`CvGame::setGameTurn -> updateBuildingCommerce`)
is likewise inherited, which explains why the bug is transient but still economically
consumable within the round.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
When `changeNoCorporationsCount` or `changeNoForeignCorporationsCount` crosses a state
edge that changes corporation activity, rebuild global building commerce after the
player's corporation state has been updated, e.g. conceptually:

    updateCorporation();
    GC.getGame().updateBuildingCommerce();

The global call should occur only when the effective boolean state actually changes if
future code ever allows multiple stacked sources; current compiled producers are civic
booleans and therefore normal +/-1 edges.

Do not replace the local `updateCorporation()`: that rebuild is still needed for the
switching player's branch yields/commerce/resources/maintenance. F496 is the missing
SECOND invalidation for other players' global HQ building commerce.

F497 / provisional KI#820 - CONFIRMED CURRENT ADVCIV CACHE-INVALIDATION REGRESSION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TITLE
    Domestic/capital-network resource availability changes do not invalidate
    `CvPlayerAI`'s cached bonus values, even though AdvCiv made one bonus's value depend
    on whether OTHER substitute bonuses are currently available.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_baseBonusVal` caches one value per BonusType in `m_aiBonusValue`
(and a trade variant in `m_aiBonusValueTrade`). AdvCiv practical commit 1291,
8493e0199b0dcf756b92ac0bd17351d7e0a4e88c (`advc.036`, "Toward v0.92"), explicitly
re-enabled K-Mod's disabled cross-resource dependency inside `AI_baseBonusUnitVal`:

    iOrBonusesWeHave += (ePrereqBonus != eBonus &&
            getNumAvailableBonuses(ePrereqBonus) > 0) ? 1 : 0;

K-Mod had deliberately left this line commented out and documented the reason: using
state-dependent `NumAvailableBonuses` inside a locally callable cached valuation could
make the cache unsafe / OOS-prone. AdvCiv's same `advc.036` work changed the cache policy:
in network multiplayer `AI_updateBonusValue` eagerly recomputes synchronized values;
in single-player it invalidates and lets later authoritative calls repopulate lazily.

That makes current resource availability a semantic input to EVERY cached resource whose
unit value includes OR-resource substitutes.

INVALIDATION ASYMMETRY
----------------------
AdvCiv does explicitly invalidate all bonus values for import/export changes:

    CvPlayer::changeBonusExport -> AI().AI_updateBonusValue();
    CvPlayer::changeBonusImport -> AI().AI_updateBonusValue();

and performs full turn-pre refresh/invalidation:

    CvPlayerAI::AI_doTurnPre -> AI_updateBonusValue();

Relevant civic/tech/team/lifecycle paths also have explicit refreshes.

Ordinary DOMESTIC resource availability, however, changes through the plot-group path:

    improvement / route / plot-group topology change
      -> CvPlot::updatePlotGroupBonus
      -> CvPlotGroup::changeNumBonuses
      -> CvCity::changeNumBonuses
      -> CvCity::processBonus / production verification

The complete current `AI_updateBonusValue` caller set contains no call in this domestic
connection/disconnection path. `CvCity::processBonus`, `CvCity::verifyProduction`, and
the plot-group rebuild likewise do not repair the player AI cache.

Thus resource trades are treated as cache-invalidating availability changes, but the
same effective availability transition caused by workers, pillaging/repair, routes,
plot-group splits/merges, free bonuses or capital-network topology is not.

CURRENT SAS DATA - COPPER / IRON SUBSTITUTE PROOF
--------------------------------------------------
Current UnitInfos contain many units with exactly:

    PrereqBonuses = BONUS_COPPER OR BONUS_IRON

including ordinary Axemen, Spearmen and Macemen plus several UUs (Vulture, Gallic
Warrior, Legionary, Immortal, Quechua, Samurai, Viking, Impi, Hoplite, Zhuge Nu,
Disciplined Crossbowman, Houfnice) and Privateer.

For such a unit, while evaluating Iron in `AI_baseBonusUnitVal`:

    iOrBonuses = 2

If Copper is NOT available:

    iOrBonusesWeHave = 0
    resource-enabling component = iBaseValue * 2 / (1 + 2 + 0)
                                ~= 2/3 * iBaseValue

Once Copper IS available:

    iOrBonusesWeHave = 1
    correct component          = iBaseValue * 2 / (1 + 2 + 2)
                                = 2/5 * iBaseValue

So connecting Copper materially reduces the marginal military value of Iron. This is
precisely the cross-resource redundancy effect AdvCiv intentionally uncommented.

DETERMINISTIC NETWORK-MULTIPLAYER SAME-TURN REPRODUCTION
--------------------------------------------------------
Network multiplayer supplies a particularly clean cache-population proof because
`AI_doTurnPre -> AI_updateBonusValue()` eagerly computes and stores every bonus value.
An ordinary game can include AI players, so no debug/API producer is required.

1. AI player P has the relevant military technologies but no connected Copper. Iron's
   cached `AI_baseBonusVal` is eagerly computed at P's turn start using
   `iOrBonusesWeHave == 0` for the Copper-or-Iron units.
2. P has a Worker with an already queued legal improvement/route mission that connects
   Copper during this active turn.
3. K-Mod/AdvCiv movement ordering gives land Workers priority 9. Ordinary fighting
   groups are centered around priority 65, so the Worker completes first.
4. The Copper connection updates plot-group/city bonus counts, making
   `getNumAvailableBonuses(BONUS_COPPER) > 0`, but no `AI_updateBonusValue` call occurs.
5. `CvPlayerAI::AI_unitUpdate` continues through later groups in priority order. Reserve,
   defender and related routines can call `CvUnitAI::AI_guardBonus`.
6. `AI_guardBonus` values candidate resource plots with:

       GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).AI_bonusVal(eBonus, 0)

   so an Iron guard/ranking candidate reads the still-cached PRE-Copper Iron value.
7. Correct Iron marginal value has already fallen through the current Copper-or-Iron
   unit dependencies from roughly 2/3 to 2/5 of each relevant base component. The stale
   higher value feeds `AI_guardBonus`'s threshold/ranking/path scoring and can therefore
   alter which resource plot a later military group guards or whether the routine acts.

The next turn-pre cache refresh eventually self-heals the value. The defect is a real
same-turn AI decision window, not an indefinitely sticky cache.

SINGLE-PLAYER EXPOSURE
----------------------
Single-player `AI_doTurnPre` resets values to -1 and later calls populate them lazily.
The same defect occurs whenever the affected bonus was evaluated earlier in the active
turn before the domestic connection/disconnection, then consumed again afterward. The
network-multiplayer sequence is used as the deterministic proof because it guarantees
prepopulation of every bonus cache entry without needing to force an earlier evaluator.

ANCESTRY / REGRESSION BOUNDARY
------------------------------
Stock BtS/Civ4CE does not have this exact AdvCiv cache/dependency combination.

K-Mod 1.46 already has the bonus-value cache, but deliberately DISABLES the
`iOrBonusesWeHave` availability dependency and leaves the warning explaining why.

AdvCiv practical 1291 (`advc.036`) explicitly uncommented that state-dependent term and
changed multiplayer cache handling so cached values are eagerly recomputed at explicit
invalidation points. Current Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the re-enabled dependency and the
same missing domestic-resource invalidation. Current SAS retains it unchanged.

Classification: inherited Base-AdvCiv regression introduced when `advc.036` made the
cache depend on mutable cross-resource availability without covering the domestic
availability mutation family.

WHY THIS IS NOT AN EXISTING RESOURCE FINDING
--------------------------------------------
* F214/KI#537: UWAI `MilitaryBranch::m_eTypicalUnit` fails to clear when no current
  trainable candidate exists. Different cache and refresh contract.
* F321/KI#644 and neighboring CvPlayerAI findings: prospective trade/resource pricing
  uses the wrong pre/post-change state. F497 is stale persistent `m_aiBonusValue` after
  the authoritative availability state has already changed.
* F434/KI#757: resource-layer UI help (`m_aszBonusHelp`) is stale after resource state
  changes. F497 is authoritative AI valuation used by gameplay decisions.
* F491/F496: corporation activity/HQ cache invalidation. Different state family.

The reconciled WIP239 album contains no prior root for `m_aiBonusValue` missing domestic
capital-network availability invalidation.

SCOPE / SAME-ROOT SIBLINGS
--------------------------
Copper -> Iron is the clean shipped-data proof, but the root is not metal-specific.
Any domestic availability transition that changes `getNumAvailableBonuses(X)` can
change cached valuation of another bonus Y when a current unit treats X and Y as OR
substitutes. Plot-group splits/merges, pillage/repair, route completion/removal, free
bonus changes and similar capital-network transitions are same-root producers when they
change effective availability.

Do not split connection and disconnection directions into separate findings.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Invalidate/recompute the owning player's complete bonus-value cache whenever effective
CAPITAL-NETWORK bonus availability changes, because one changed bonus can alter the
cached value of OTHER bonuses.

Do NOT naively call the expensive full refresh inside every
`CvPlotGroup::changeNumBonuses`: K-Mod documents that plot-group rebuilding can make
those counts temporarily negative/intermediate, and network multiplayer eagerly
recomputes the whole cache. Hook the refresh at a stable post-recalculation boundary (or
track a dirty generation and rebuild before the next authoritative AI consumer) so the
cache sees the final synchronized resource state.

Preserve AdvCiv's multiplayer requirement that locally-triggerable help/UI calls cannot
install state-dependent cache values from an unsynchronized local path.

7. Pending-event city/unit ID reuse: generation-safe closure

EventTriggeredData stores integer city/unit IDs, and deleteCity/deleteUnit do not scrub
every pending event record. This superficially resembles stale-reference rebinding.

However cities and units use FFreeListTrashArray generation-bearing full IDs. Reusing
the same physical slot advances the public ID generation; getCity/getUnit -> getAt
checks the full ID. A later object in the same slot cannot satisfy the stale event ID.
This closes analogously to the earlier cancelled-vote-ID control. No F498.

8. Organized Religion / SpecialBuildingNotRequired queued-production candidate: closes

Current Organized Religion can make SPECIALBUILDING_MONASTERY not required, and
processCivics changes m_aiSpecialBuildingNotRequiredCount without immediately calling
verifyCityProduction(). A queued missionary therefore looked capable of surviving a
civic switch that removed its exemption.

Mandatory city-turn verification closes it: CvCity::doCheckProduction runs before
production, checkCanContinueProduction re-runs canTrain, and an invalid queued unit is
removed before that turn's production is applied. No F498.

9. War-weariness civic-modifier cache candidate: closes

m_iWarWearinessPercentAnger is a cached/base player value, but civic/player/city
WarWearinessModifier values are applied dynamically by CvCity::getWarWearinessPercentAnger.
Changing the civic modifier does not require rebuilding that cached base value. No F498.

10. setCurrentEra / UWAI era-cache challenge: closes for persistent state

The remaining era-sensitive UWAI values traced are refreshed before the next war/deploy
planning consumers. Ordinary post-research city/unit AI consumers sampled read current
era dynamically. No same-turn persistent old-era cache consequence was found.

CURRENT UNCONFIRMED F498 LEAD
-----------------------------

Capital identity -> stale city YIELD-RANK caches under CapitalYieldModifier

STATUS: STRONG CANDIDATE ONLY. NOT CONFIRMED. F498/KI#821 remains UNUSED.

Current CvPlayer::setCapital does:
* update capital-network plot-group bonuses when needed;
* change m_iCapitalCityID;
* update maintenance;
* update trade routes;
* call updateCommerce() and setInfoDirty(true) on old/new capitals.

It does NOT call CvPlayer::invalidateYieldRankCache().

This matters because CvCity::getBaseYieldRateModifier explicitly includes:

    if (isCapital())
        iModifier += GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).getCapitalYieldRateModifier(eYield);

and immediately documents the cache contract:

    player->invalidateYieldRankCache() must be called for anything checked here

The actual yield rate therefore changes dynamically and correctly as capital identity
moves. The potential stale state is the K-Mod/AdvCiv cached city yield ranking:
CvCity::getYieldRateRank / getBaseYieldRateRank store ranks behind
m_abYieldRankValid / m_abBaseYieldRankValid, and capital identity is one of the inputs
to the resulting getYieldRate through the modifier above.

Current SAS data makes the input LIVE:
CIVIC_BUREAUCRACY has CapitalYieldModifiers:
    YIELD_FOOD       0
    YIELD_PRODUCTION +50%
    YIELD_COMMERCE   +50%

So while Bureaucracy is active, moving the capital changes old/new capital production
and commerce-yield modifiers by 50 percentage points. setCapital explicitly refreshes
commerce accounting but currently appears not to invalidate cached YIELD RANKS.

UNFINISHED BEFORE PROMOTION
---------------------------
Need to prove before spending F498:
* ordinary shipped capital-relocation producer(s) and exact ordering;
* that at least one old/new city yield-rank cache can already be valid before the move;
* a real gameplay/AI/UI consumer can read the stale rank before some unrelated yield
  change invalidates it;
* self-heal cadence, if any;
* exact ancestry (BtS/K-Mod/Base AdvCiv/SAS) and regression/inheritance boundary;
* exhaustive semantic album duplicate search;
* whether commerce rank and yield rank interactions create same-root symptoms or are
  separately repaired by setCapital::updateCommerce().

Do NOT number this candidate merely because current Bureaucracy data makes it reachable.

WIP241 CAPITAL-YIELD-RANK CANDIDATE - CLOSED / OLD F445 RETRACTION REDISCOVERED
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The WIP241 candidate was challenged before spending F498.

The candidate had argued that changing capital identity while Bureaucracy is active can
change old/new capital production and commerce yields without an explicit
CvPlayer::invalidateYieldRankCache() call in CvPlayer::setCapital.

That argument misses a transitive invalidator already proved when old F445/KI#768 was
retracted:

    CvPlayer::setCapital
        -> old/new capital CvCity::updateCommerce()
            -> GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).invalidateYieldRankCache()

Current CvCity::updateCommerce begins by invalidating the owning player's yield-rank
cache. Therefore the first old/new-capital commerce refresh in setCapital invalidates
all city yield/base-yield ranks before a persistent stale Bureaucracy capital rank can
be consumed.

This is exactly the reason F445 was previously retracted. The WIP241 lead is therefore
not new and does not consume F498.

F498 / KI#821 - CONFIRMED
-------------------------
Title:
K-Mod's city construction-value cache is cleared before AI research valuation but can
survive later same-turn commerce/policy changes and then be reused by city production
after the newly selected tech completes

ROOT
----
K-Mod introduced a city construction/building-value cache:

    CvCityAI::AI_buildingValue(...)
        if (bUseConstructionValueCache &&
            m_aiConstructionValue[eBuildingClass] != -1)
            return m_aiConstructionValue[eBuildingClass];
        ...
        m_aiConstructionValue[eBuildingClass] = iValue;

The cache is intentionally reused by neutral building-value calls. The player-level
turn setup clears it only once, before research selection:

    CvPlayerAI::AI_doTurnPre()
        AI_updateBonusValue();
        AI_updateCommerceWeights();
        [periodic AI_updateGreatPersonWeights()]
        AI_doEnemyUnitData();
        AI_ClearConstructionValueCache();
        if (isHuman()) return;
        AI_doResearch();
        AI_doCommerce();
        AI_doMilitary();
        AI_doCivics();
        AI_doReligion();
        AI_doCheckFinancialTrouble();

Thus values installed by AI_doResearch can survive all later state changes in
AI_doTurnPre.

RESEARCH POPULATES THE CACHE FOR BUILDINGS THAT ARE NOT YET TECH-UNLOCKED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
The ordinary synchronized/randomized AI research path reaches:

    AI_bestTech
        -> AI_techValue(... bRandomize=true)
            -> AI_techBuildingValue(eTech, bAsync || !bRandomize, ...)

For the normal synchronous randomized path, bConstCache is false.
AI_techBuildingValue evaluates candidate-tech buildings while deliberately ignoring the
tech prerequisite and calls AI_buildingValue. Therefore it can install a construction
value for a building before the player actually knows the enabling tech.

MUTABLE INPUT AFTER CACHE POPULATION
------------------------------------
AI_buildingValue reads mutable empire state. A clean inherited input is the current
commerce slider. Its commerce-modifier valuation contains the live
getCommercePercent(eLoopCommerce) value.

But AI_doCommerce runs after AI_doResearch and can change those percentages, including:

    setCommercePercent(COMMERCE_RESEARCH, ...)
    changeCommercePercent(COMMERCE_GOLD, ...)

CvPlayer::setCommercePercent updates the actual commerce state, assignment/UI dirtiness
and human-side commerce-weight state, but it does not clear the AI construction cache.

A complete current-DLL search finds AI_ClearConstructionValueCache only at city
initialization/reset and the single pre-research player-turn boundary above; slider,
civic, religion and tech-acquisition transitions do not supply a second clear.

SAME-TURN CONSUMER
------------------
The stale value is not merely carried to an abstract future turn.

CvPlayer::doTurn runs AI_doTurnPre first. Later in that same turn CvPlayer::doResearch
applies current research and overflow, so the tech selected/evaluated earlier can
complete on that turn. City turns then run, and an empty/dirty production queue reaches:

    CvCity::doProduction
        -> CvCityAI::AI_chooseProduction
            -> AI_bestBuildingThreshold
                -> AI_buildingValue

A building that was tech-locked when its value was cached during AI_doResearch can now
be legally constructible. The ordinary neutral AI_buildingValue lookup can therefore
return the pre-slider/pre-policy cached value before the next turn's clear.

CLEAN INHERITED MARKET / CURRENCY REPRODUCTION
-----------------------------------------------
Market and Currency provide a stock/K-Mod-compatible example.

1. An AI begins a turn without a current research target.
2. AI_doResearch / AI_bestTech evaluates Currency and caches the Market value while
   Currency is still unknown.
3. AI_doCommerce subsequently changes the Gold/Research slider.
4. CvPlayer::doResearch later that same turn completes Currency from the current turn's
   research plus overflow.
5. A city with an empty/dirty queue reaches AI_chooseProduction.
6. Market is now constructible, but AI_buildingValue can return the value computed
   before the slider change.
7. That stale value can alter the building ranking and therefore the chosen production.

The slider contribution is numerically real. With 100 raw commerce, the K-Mod
flexibility term used by the building commerce-modifier valuation changes from roughly
4 at a floored 5% Gold share to 9 at a 10% Gold share. For a +25% Gold Market, that
piece alone changes building value by 5 points, before the larger direct base-Gold
change and other terms are included.

POLICY / RELIGION SAME-ROOT PRODUCERS
-------------------------------------
The root is broader than slider movement. AI_doCivics and AI_doReligion also run after
research-time cache population, while AI_buildingValue reads policy-sensitive state
such as health, state religion and specialist extra commerce.

Current SAS supplies additional live examples (e.g. Organized Religion extra health;
Representation specialist extra commerce). These are manifestations of the same cache
lifetime and must not be split into separate findings.

ANCESTRY
--------
Civ4CE/BtS does not contain m_aiConstructionValue / AI_ClearConstructionValueCache.
K-Mod introduces the construction cache and the relevant turn ordering. Its standard
Market/Currency data makes the slider reproduction live without SAS XML changes.
Base AdvCiv retains the K-Mod cache and ordering. Current SAS retains them and adds
further mutable valuation inputs.

F498 is therefore a K-Mod-introduced cache-lifetime defect inherited by AdvCiv and SAS.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
The reconciled album contains many building-value, civic, production-dirty and cache
findings but no prior root for m_aiConstructionValue surviving state changes after its
single pre-research clear.

F498 is separate from F497/KI#820, which concerns CvPlayerAI bonus-value cache
invalidation after domestic resource availability transitions.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Retain the existing pre-research clear because AI research valuation needs a fresh cache,
but ensure city production cannot consume values computed before later mutable player
state changes.

The simplest robust shape is a second AI_ClearConstructionValueCache() after the
commerce/civic/religion policy-changing work and before city production/other
post-policy consumers. More targeted invalidation is possible but must cover every
semantic input to AI_buildingValue and is therefore easier to make incomplete.

Do not remove the first clear merely to move it later; that would let research valuation
itself begin from previous-turn values.

UNNUMBERED CACHE-KEY ROBUSTNESS NOTE
------------------------------------
AI_buildingValue's cache key is only the building class even though the function also
has semantic flags such as bAllowRecursion, bIgnoreSpecialists and bObsolete.
AI_doHurry deliberately requests restricted variants.

A current shipped-data collision was not proved. Research-time entries are normally for
tech-locked buildings, and the current building dependency graph does not provide the
ordering/recursive chain required for a cached full-recursion child value to contaminate
a later bAllowRecursion=false recursive evaluation. Keep this as robustness debt rather
than allocating a finding.

F498 SIBLING - PERIODIC GREAT-PERSON WEIGHT REFRESH CAN READ THE SAME OLD
CONSTRUCTION CACHE BEFORE THE TURN'S CLEAR
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A second consumer strengthens F498 without creating a separate finding.

AI_doTurnPre orders the periodic Great Person calculation before the construction-cache
clear:

    AI_updateCommerceWeights();
    if ((gameTurn + strategyRand) % 3 == 0)
        AI_updateGreatPersonWeights();
    ...
    AI_ClearConstructionValueCache();

AI_updateGreatPersonWeights evaluates special Great-Person-created buildings through
AI_buildingValue. Several shipped examples are cost -1 special buildings with ordinary
tech prerequisites, including:

    Academy            -> Literature
    Jewish Shrine      -> Code of Laws
    Military Academy   -> Military Science
    Scotland Yard      -> Monarchy
    corporation HQs    -> their corporation-era techs

Because the construction cache is not cleared until after this periodic GP pass, a
neutral value installed during an earlier turn's tech/building evaluation can be read by
AI_updateGreatPersonWeights before the clear. This is another consequence of F498's
cache lifetime, not F499.

GREAT-PERSON WEIGHTS' THREE-TURN CADENCE - CONTROL / INTENTIONAL HEURISTIC LAG
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The Great Person weight map itself is cleared/recomputed only once every three turns.
That means mutable city/civic state can naturally change between refreshes.

K-Mod explicitly documents this cadence as a performance tradeoff:

    "GP weights can take a little bit of time,
     so lets only do it once every 3 turns."

Without a stronger violated correctness/invalidation contract, ordinary up-to-three-turn
heuristic lag is intentional policy, not an independent F499.

AI_buildingValue SEMANTIC-FLAG CACHE KEY - CURRENT SHIPPED COLLISION NOT PROVED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The cache lookup does not include bAllowRecursion, bIgnoreSpecialists or bObsolete.
AI_doHurry can ask for restricted values, which superficially makes the key too coarse.

The live building prerequisite/free-building graph was checked for the ordering needed
to turn this into a shipped wrong-value collision. Current data does not provide a case
where a previously cached child both precedes its prerequisite in the relevant scan and
itself has recursive downstream value so that full-recursion and no-recursion values
actually differ at the collision. Keep this as hardening/robustness debt only.

AI_updateCommerceWeights AFTER AI_doCommerce - CONTROL
------------------------------------------------------
K-Mod comments that commerce weights are updated before Great Person weights and asks
whether they perhaps should be updated again after AI_doCommerce or when sliders change.
The current implementation was traced before treating that comment as evidence of a bug.

For current AI players:
* Gold and Research AI_commerceWeight values are calculated dynamically and read the
  current slider/financial state directly rather than coming from AI_updateCommerceWeights.
* The cached per-city Culture weight no longer infers an AI cultural-victory plan from
  the live Culture slider; current SAS intentionally keeps that slider inference for
  humans only, while AI culture targeting uses victory-strategy state.
* The cached player Espionage weight is derived from espionage-point, opponent, attitude
  and strategy state rather than the Gold/Research slider changed by AI_doCommerce.

Therefore the nearby comment currently describes heuristic/timing possibilities, not a
proved stale slider cache affecting an AI consumer. No F499.

NEXT CACHE FAMILY OPENED
------------------------
The audit is widening from the explicitly periodic/heuristic caches to state with a
stronger freshness or invalidation responsibility. The next targets include the
per-turn empire average/available-income caches and other K-Mod/AdvCiv cached state,
with special attention to transitions that occur after cache refresh but before a
consumer and to cache keys that discard per-object state.

Do not allocate F499 merely because a cache is intentionally sampled once per turn or
once every three turns; require a concrete violated contract, shipped producer and
consumer, and duplicate/ancestry proof.

C031-WIP244 - F499 / KI#822 CONFIRMED
================================================================================

F499 / KI#822 - GPT CHANGES IMMEDIATELY RUN AI_doCommerce WITHOUT REFRESHING
K-MOD'S CACHED AVAILABLE INCOME, SO THE EVENT-DRIVEN COMMERCE RESPONSE CAN USE THE
PRE-DEAL FINANCIAL-TROUBLE STATE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED - K-Mod-introduced cache/event-response defect inherited by Base AdvCiv 1.14
and current AdvCiv-SAS. Civ4CE/BtS has the immediate GPT-triggered commerce response but
calculates financial trouble from live income instead of K-Mod's stored available-income
cache.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayer::changeGoldPerTurnByPlayer` mutates the authoritative recurring-gold state and
then deliberately asks an AI player to reconsider its sliders immediately:

    m_iGoldPerTurn += iChange;
    m_aiGoldPerTurnByPlayer.add(ePlayer, iChange);
    ...
    if (!isHuman() && isAlive())
        AI().AI_doCommerce();

Ordinary `CvDeal::startTrade` and `CvDeal::endTrade` use this mutator for
`TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN`, so creating or cancelling a normal GPT deal is a shipped producer.

K-Mod changed `AI_isFinancialTrouble` to use:

    int iNetCommerce = AI_getAvailableIncome();

where `AI_getAvailableIncome()` is only:

    return m_iAvailableIncome;

and `AI_updateAvailableIncome()` explicitly incorporates the live GPT balance:

    m_iAvailableIncome = ...;
    m_iAvailableIncome += std::max(0, getGoldPerTurn());
    ...

The problem is lifetime. Current source has no refresh of `m_iAvailableIncome` in
`changeGoldPerTurnByPlayer` or in `AI_doCommerce`. The ordinary updater is called from
`AI_updateCacheData`, which runs at player turn activation. Thus a GPT deal created or
cancelled after that refresh changes the state represented by the cache and then invokes
the exact consumer that assumes the old cached value.

CLEAN +GPT FINANCIAL-STATE FLIP
-------------------------------
The receiving side gives the cleanest arithmetic because a positive GPT change raises
the correct available-income numerator while leaving the expense term unchanged.

Choose a normal non-Barbarian state in which the effective financial-trouble safety
threshold is 35 percent (no focus-war / repeat-research / avoid-science adjustment, and
an era/city-count state where the base threshold remains 35), treasury is low enough not
to trigger AdvCiv's large-cash safe override, and the turn-activation cache contains:

    m_iAvailableIncome = 100
    calculateInflatedCosts() + max(0, -getGoldPerTurn()) = 66

The cached state gives:

    funded = 100 * (100 - 66) / 100 = 34 percent
    margin = 34 - 35 = -1
    AI_isFinancialTrouble() = true

Now the AI receives an ordinary +20 GPT deal. The authoritative `getGoldPerTurn()` is
updated immediately. If `AI_updateAvailableIncome()` were recomputed, all other inputs
being unchanged, its explicit `max(0, getGoldPerTurn())` term raises available income to
120 while expenses remain 66:

    funded = 100 * (120 - 66) / 120 = 45 percent
    margin = 45 - 35 = +10
    AI_isFinancialTrouble() = false

But the call to `AI_doCommerce()` made from `changeGoldPerTurnByPlayer(+20)` still reads
the cached 100 and therefore executes as financially troubled.

CONCRETE COMMERCE-DECISION CONSEQUENCE
--------------------------------------
The stale boolean is not diagnostic-only. `AI_doCommerce()` consumes it immediately.

First, `AI_goldTarget()` scales the empire-wide unit-upgrade reserve by the financial
state. In peace and outside Culture stage 4, a raw 400-gold upgrade estimate contributes:

    stale trouble:   400 / 10 = 40 gold
    correct healthy: 400 /  4 = 100 gold

All common non-upgrade components can be denoted C. A post-deal full-science forecast
between C+40 and C+99 therefore produces opposite slider behavior: the stale call sees
its smaller gold target already covered, while the correctly refreshed call still enters
the Gold-increase loop. Such a forecast interval is directly reachable because the same
GPT payment changes `calculateGoldRate()` immediately.

There is an even more direct branch consequence later in `AI_doCommerce`: active control
of the Espionage slider requires `!bFinancialTrouble`. In any ordinary state with a
positive espionage target and the other documented gates satisfied, the stale pre-deal
`true` suppresses the allocation that the correct post-deal `false` state permits.

The event-driven recalculation can therefore choose different commerce percentages
solely because the GPT-dependent cache was not refreshed before the recalculation.

SHIPPED PRODUCER / TIMING
-------------------------
No special Python or WorldBuilder path is required.

`CvDeal::startTrade` handles `TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN` with:

    kFromPlayer.changeGoldPerTurnByPlayer(eToPlayer, -trade.m_iData);
    kToPlayer.changeGoldPerTurnByPlayer(eFromPlayer, trade.m_iData);

and `CvDeal::endTrade` applies the reverse deltas. Each nonhuman living player therefore
runs `AI_doCommerce()` immediately when its annual payment changes.

The stale-cache window is ordinary:

1. player turn activation runs `AI_updateCacheData()` and stores available income;
2. later, a GPT deal starts or ends (during the AI turn or another player's diplomacy);
3. `changeGoldPerTurnByPlayer` updates the live GPT balance;
4. without refreshing available income, it calls `AI_doCommerce()`;
5. financial-trouble-sensitive slider logic reads the pre-change cached value.

If the deal is signed during another player's turn, the cache can be older still; that is
not needed for the root, because a same-turn post-activation deal already suffices.

ANCESTRY
--------
Civ4CE/BtS already contains the same immediate response in
`CvPlayer::changeGoldPerTurnByPlayer`:

    if (!isHuman())
        AI_doCommerce();

However BtS `AI_isFinancialTrouble()` derives its net commerce directly from live
`getCommerceRate(...)` and `getGoldPerTurn()` on each call. It has no
`m_iAvailableIncome` member.

K-Mod retains the BtS immediate `AI_doCommerce()` call but introduces:

* `m_iAvailableIncome`;
* `AI_updateAvailableIncome()`;
* `AI_getAvailableIncome()` in financial trouble; and
* the turn-activation `updateCacheData()` cadence.

That combination creates the stale event-response boundary. Base AdvCiv 1.14 preserves
it, adding only the alive guard around the immediate response. Current SAS retains the
same lifetime and financial-trouble dependency.

F499 is therefore K-Mod-introduced and inherited by AdvCiv/SAS, not a SAS regression.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
A full album semantic search found no prior root for GPT mutation leaving
`m_iAvailableIncome` stale during the immediate `AI_doCommerce()` response.

F499 is independent of:

* F338/KI#661 - AdvCiv's queued human-deal cancellation remains live during a later
  per-rival GPT-cap enforcement pass. That is transaction projection/order inside
  `AI_doDeals`, not the K-Mod available-income cache.
* F364/KI#687 - entering financial trouble can lose an intended production-dirty refresh
  when a shared cooldown suppresses it. F499 can make the observed trouble state itself
  wrong during GPT-triggered commerce recalculation before that edge scheduler matters.
* F365/KI#688 - unit-upgrade reserve estimation has a UnitType cache-key defect. F499
  merely uses the ordinary reserve scaling as one concrete downstream decision boundary.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
At minimum, refresh the GPT-dependent available-income cache after changing
`m_iGoldPerTurn` and before the immediate AI commerce recalculation.

A targeted repair is preferable to recomputing all `AI_updateCacheData()` state:

    change live GPT state
    -> AI_updateAvailableIncome()
    -> AI_doCommerce()

The method's visibility/API shape may need a small wrapper if the refresh remains an
AI-private helper.

A broader transaction-aware design could defer the immediate `AI_doCommerce()` until a
whole deal has been installed/removed, which would also avoid reacting to a partially
applied multi-item deal. That is a sibling hardening direction and should not be required
to fix F499's narrower stale-GPT cache root.

32/169 unique files complete.
F445 / KI#768 RETRACTED.
F446 / KI#769 through F499 / KI#822 CONFIRMED.
F500 / provisional KI#823 UNUSED.
Latest physical checkpoint: C031-WIP244.
No repository source files modified.

NEXT
----
Resume under F500 unused.

1. Define the F499 sibling boundary around deal installation/removal: test whether the

   in a way that changes a real later decision independently of stale available income.
2. Continue K-Mod per-turn empire caches, but promote only event-driven consumers whose
   code explicitly requests immediate reconsideration after a state mutation.
3. Return to the Queue-004 mutator-vs-invalidator comparison, prioritizing cross-object
   and owner/source transitions rather than intentional one-turn heuristic sampling.

C031-WIP245 ADDENDUM — Queue 004 CvPlayer.cpp / CvDeal transaction sibling
F500 / KI#823 CONFIRMED; F501 / KI#824 UNUSED

F500 / KI#823
Title:
  A GPT item can run AI_doCommerce in the middle of a multi-item deal before a
  later resource item changes happiness, leaving the AI's commerce sliders based
  on a partial transaction state.

Root:
  CvDeal applies trade bundles item-by-item. All non-vassal items in the first
  player's list are started before the second player's list. TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN
  has an unusual synchronous side effect: changeGoldPerTurnByPlayer immediately
  calls AI_doCommerce for each living AI whose GPT changes. Later
  TRADE_RESOURCES items update bonus import/export state, plot-group bonus counts,
  city bonus happiness/health and AI bonus valuation, but do not rerun
  AI_doCommerce. Thus a transaction can commit a slider decision while only the
  first half of the accepted bundle exists.

Current SAS source path:
  CvDeal::addTradeItems
      first-player list:
          startTrade(item, first, second, ...)
      then second-player list:
          startTrade(item, second, first, ...)

  CvDeal::startTrade(TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN)
      kFromPlayer.changeGoldPerTurnByPlayer(eToPlayer, -GPT)
      kToPlayer.changeGoldPerTurnByPlayer(eFromPlayer, +GPT)

  CvPlayer::changeGoldPerTurnByPlayer
      ... mutate live GPT state ...
      if (!isHuman() && isAlive())
          AI().AI_doCommerce();

  CvDeal::startTrade(TRADE_RESOURCES)
      kFromPlayer.changeBonusExport(bonus, +1)
      kToPlayer.changeBonusImport(bonus, +1)

  CvPlayer::changeBonusImport
      rebuilds plot-group bonus state
      AI().AI_updateBonusValue()
      // no AI_doCommerce

  The same first-list-then-second-list ordering exists in killSilent/endTrade, so
  teardown can expose the reverse partial-state shape as well.

Ordinary AI-AI producer:
  CvPlayerAI::AI_proposeResourceTrade can have AI A seek a resource from AI B.
  The counterproposal machinery is explicitly allowed to add compensation from A,
  including TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN. The accepted lists are then passed as:

      kGame.implementDeal(A, B, weGive, theyGive)

  Therefore an ordinary result can be:
      A / first list:  GPT payment
      B / second list: happiness resource

  No malformed save, Python-only producer or human-human-only bundle is needed.

Concrete shipped-data reproduction:
  Use an AI A that has researched Drama, is not pursuing a Culture victory stage
  that adds its own slider target, is not avoiding science, and has one city with
  average culture pressure 100.

  Current SAS data:
      COMMERCE_CULTURE iInitialHappiness = 10
      TECH_DRAMA makes COMMERCE_CULTURE flexible
      BONUS_GOLD has iHappiness = +1 and is tradable after Mining

  CvCity::getCommerceHappinessByType computes:
      getCommerceHappinessPer(CULTURE) * culturePercent / 100

  Hence 10% Culture produces +1 happiness in an ordinary city.

  Arrange A's city to have exactly one angry citizen before receiving Gold and no
  other Culture-slider target. A agrees to pay B GPT for B's Gold resource.

  1. A's first-list GPT item executes.
  2. changeGoldPerTurnByPlayer immediately calls A.AI_doCommerce().
  3. Gold has not been imported yet, so angryPopulation() is still 1.
  4. AI_doCommerce computes the happiness target as
         1 * 100 / 10 = 10%
     and sets Culture to 10% (with the normal 10-point commerce increment).
  5. The second-list Gold item then executes.
  6. changeBonusImport -> plot-group/city bonus processing grants the +1 resource
     happiness; the correct final-deal happiness target is now 0% Culture.
  7. No final AI_doCommerce call occurs, so A exits the deal transaction at 10%
     Culture despite the completed deal no longer requiring that allocation.

Real consumer before self-heal:
  AI-AI deal proposals occur in AI_doTurnPost, after doGold, doResearch and city
  turns. The wrong slider can therefore survive the turn boundary.

  A particularly clean sequence is to let A finish its final queued technology
  earlier in that same turn. CvTeam::setHasTech pops the acquired technology from
  the research queue; current SAS explicitly documents that a completed final
  queue target normally leaves currentResearch == NO_TECH until the AI chooses
  again.

  On A's next turn:
      CvPlayer::doTurn
          verifyDeals()
          AI_doTurnPre()
              AI_ClearConstructionValueCache()
              AI_doResearch()   <-- consumer
              AI_doCommerce()   <-- eventual self-heal

  Thus AI_doResearch chooses a new technology while the stale 10% Culture /
  reduced Research allocation is still authoritative. This does not depend on
  F498's stale construction cache: that cache has just been cleared.

  AI_chooseResearch -> AI_bestTech -> AI_techBuildingValue -> AI_buildingValue
  reads live commerce percentages. In the general building-value commerce-
  modifier term K-Mod explicitly uses getCommercePercent(eLoopCommerce) when
  inflating base commerce for slider flexibility. Current Universities, for
  example, have +25% Research and are unlocked by Broader Education. With a city
  producing 100 raw commerce and no complicating modifiers, 90% Research gives a
  research base of roughly 90 + 9 flexibility = 99 for this term, whereas the
  correct 100% Research state gives 100 + 0 = 100. The +25% modifier therefore
  contributes 99 versus 100 before later tech-value scaling. Across relevant
  cities, or at an otherwise close tech comparison, the wrong post-deal slider
  can change the selected research target.

  The exact University is only a compact numerical witness; AI_bestTech has many
  other slider-dependent building valuations, so the root is not specific to that
  building.

Teardown sibling:
  killSilent ends all first-list items before all second-list items. If A's GPT
  payment is first and B's happiness resource second, ending GPT can run
  AI_doCommerce while A still temporarily retains the soon-to-be-removed import.
  The resource is then removed without a final commerce pass. This is the same
  transaction-boundary root in the opposite direction, not a separate finding.

Ancestry:
  In Civ4CE/BtS:
    * CvDeal already applies the first list item-by-item before the second list;
    * TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN already calls changeGoldPerTurnByPlayer;
    * changeGoldPerTurnByPlayer already immediately invokes AI_doCommerce for AI;
    * resource start/end changes import/export state without a final commerce
      recomputation;
    * Drama makes Culture flexible and COMMERCE_CULTURE has
      iInitialHappiness = 10.

  K-Mod retains this transaction shape, Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains it, and current
  SAS retains it. SAS's current Gold bonus supplies a direct +1-happiness witness.
  The root is therefore inherited from Firaxis/BtS rather than introduced by SAS.

Dedup / sibling boundary:
  * F499 / KI#822 is stale m_iAvailableIncome during the GPT-triggered
    AI_doCommerce call. F500 survives a targeted F499 repair: even if available
    income is refreshed perfectly, AI_doCommerce is still running before the
    later resource item exists.
  * F292 / KI#615 is a transaction-precondition bug: a mixed city+resource bundle
    passes validation although the city transfer destroys the resource promise.
    F500's deal remains fully valid; the defect is a mid-transaction side effect
    whose decision is not recomputed after the remaining valid item is applied.
  * F287 and neighboring queue-042 findings concern persistent-deal teardown
    granularity / peace-item lifetime, not an AI decision committed from a partial
    transaction state.
  * No prior album root for deal-item -> AI_doCommerce -> later resource-state
    mutation was found in the semantic duplicate sweep.

Repair boundary:
  Treat AI commerce recomputation as a transaction-level consequence of a deal,
  not as a per-GPT-item side effect while the bundle is half-applied.

  Preferred direction:
    * while CvDeal is installing or removing a bundle, defer the GPT-triggered
      AI_doCommerce response for affected AI players;
    * after every item in both lists has reached its final state, refresh any
      state required by that response (including F499's available-income cache)
      and run AI_doCommerce once per affected AI.

  A simpler "run it again at the end" repair would correct the final sliders, but
  still allows the premature pass to perform other side effects (working-plot
  assignment, cache population, etc.). Deferring the response is the cleaner
  transaction boundary.

Status after this pass:
  Queue 004 / CvGameCoreDLL/CvPlayer.cpp remains OPEN.
  32 / 169 unique files complete.
  F445 / KI#768 remains retracted.
  F446 / KI#769 through F500 / KI#823 are confirmed.
  F501 / KI#824 is UNUSED.
  Latest physical checkpoint: C031-WIP245.
  No repository source modified.

NEXT:
  1. Bound F500 siblings: audit other startTrade/endTrade item side effects that
     invoke substantial AI/player recomputation before the bundle is complete;
     absorb symptoms under F500 when the same partial-transaction root owns them.
  2. In particular inspect tech/civic/religion/city/war-peace items adjacent to
     GPT/resource bundles for synchronous AI cache/production/diplomacy decisions.
  3. Then resume Queue-004 mutator/invalidation ranking under F501 unused, with
     priority on event-driven recalculations whose prerequisites can change again
     before the enclosing transaction finishes.

C031-WIP246 - POST-F500 COVERAGE SWEEP + F501 / KI#824 CONFIRMED
