-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F509 / KI#832 — CONFIRMED
ADVC PEACEFUL-ACCESS / PLOT-OWNERSHIP CHANGES DO NOT INVALIDATE CACHED
SURROUNDING HEALTH AND HAPPINESS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
AdvCiv's `advc.901` surrounding health/happiness cache deliberately makes
POSITIVE feature/improvement effects conditional on whether the city team can
access the plot peacefully:

    CvCity::updateSurroundingHealthHappiness()
      -> CvTeam::canAccessHappyHealth(kPlot, iHealthOrHappy)

and:

    bool CvTeam::canAccessHappyHealth(CvPlot const& kPlot,
                                      int iHealthOrHappy) const
    {
        return (iHealthOrHappy <= 0 || !kPlot.isOwned() ||
                canPeacefullyEnter(kPlot.getTeam()));
    }

`canPeacefullyEnter` in turn depends on mutable RELATION / IDENTITY state:

    isOpenBorders(eTerritoryOwner)
    || getID() == eTerritoryOwner
    || getTeam(eTerritoryOwner).isVassal(getID())

Thus the mathematically correct cached city value can change when:

* Open Borders with the plot owner begins or ends;
* a relevant master-vassal relationship begins or ends;
* the plot changes owner (including owned <-> unowned or between teams).

None of those transitions changes the feature or improvement itself.

STORED CITY STATE
-----------------
`CvCity::updateSurroundingHealthHappiness()` stores four derived values:

    m_iSurroundingGoodHappiness
    m_iSurroundingBadHappiness
    m_iSurroundingGoodHealth
    m_iSurroundingBadHealth

The positive values are used by the ordinary authoritative city happiness and
health calculations:

    happyLevel / angryPopulation
    goodHealth / healthRate
    foodConsumption / foodDifference

so this is gameplay state rather than tooltip-only information.

INVALIDATION ASYMMETRY
----------------------
AdvCiv explicitly event-refreshes this cache when the LOCAL SOURCE changes:

* `CvPlot::setFeatureType` iterates nearby cities and calls
  `updateSurroundingHealthHappiness()`;
* `CvPlot::setImprovementType` does the same;
* player feature-happiness changes call `CvPlayer::updateFeatureHappiness`,
  which refreshes every city through the same surrounding updater.

But the other inputs to the same calculator are not wired to it:

* `CvTeam::setOpenBorders` updates attitude, unit validity, paths and trade
  routes, but not surrounding health/happiness;
* `CvTeam::setVassal` updates sight, unit/outside-unit state, war relations,
  military happiness, culture/plot groups etc., but not surrounding
  health/happiness;
* ordinary non-city `CvPlot::setOwner` updates ownership, sight, working city,
  yields and plot groups, but not nearby surrounding health/happiness.

The complete current caller set for `updateSurroundingHealthHappiness` is only:

* city initialization;
* the late once-per-city-turn refresh;
* the player feature-happiness wrapper;
* feature changes;
* improvement changes.

There is therefore no hidden relation/ownership invalidator.

CURRENT SHIPPED NUMERIC REPRODUCTION — OPEN BORDERS / FOREST HEALTH
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS ships the standard Forest feature with:

    FEATURE_FOREST
    iHealthPercent = 50

Arrange an A-owned city whose city radius contains TWO B-owned Forest plots.
The feature itself does not change during the reproduction.

While A and B have Open Borders:

    A.canPeacefullyEnter(B) == true

so both positive Forest-health contributions are accessible and the city caches:

    50 + 50 = 100 percent -> +1 surrounding good health.

Now end Open Borders.

The live access predicate immediately becomes false for B-owned plots, so the
correct surrounding health contribution from those two Forests is now 0.
However `CvTeam::setOpenBorders` does not refresh A's city, leaving the cached
+1 health in place.

Choose the rest of the city state so this point of health is exactly the
boundary between:

    correct post-OB healthRate = -1
    stale cached healthRate    =  0

The stale city therefore has a directly different food-consumption result.

REAL NEXT-TURN CONSUMER BEFORE SELF-HEAL
----------------------------------------
The routine city refresh is too late to prevent gameplay consumption.

At the start/end-processing of A's next player turn, `CvPlayer::doTurn()` runs:

    AI_doTurnPre
    AI_assignWorkingPlots
    doGold
    doResearch
    ...
    each CvCity::doTurn

Inside `CvCity::doTurn`, the order begins:

    AI().AI_doTurn()
    doCheckProduction()
    doGrowth()
    doCulture()
    doProduction()
    ...

and only much later executes:

    updateSurroundingHealthHappiness();

Therefore the stale +1 health survives through `doGrowth()`.
`foodDifference()` consumes `foodConsumption()`, which consumes `healthRate()`;
with the boundary state above, the city books ONE EXTRA FOOD before the late
refresh finally removes the inaccessible Forest health.

This provides a deterministic authoritative gameplay consequence, not merely
an AI-value, citizen-assignment or UI mismatch.

HAPPINESS SIBLING — FOREST PRESERVE
-----------------------------------
Current SAS also ships:

    IMPROVEMENT_FOREST_PRESERVE
    iHappiness = +1

A B-owned Forest Preserve inside A's city radius therefore gives A +1 cached
surrounding happiness while A can peacefully access B's territory, and should
stop doing so when access is lost. The same missing invalidator can leave the
+1 happiness active through A's next global citizen-assignment pass and the
city's early AI/growth/production work.

The Forest-health reproduction is preferred as the primary proof because its
+1 point can be made to alter `doGrowth()` directly without relying on an AI
assignment choice.

OTHER INPUT SIBLINGS UNDER THE SAME ROOT
----------------------------------------
Plot ownership
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
`canAccessHappyHealth` treats an unowned plot as accessible and an owned plot as
accessible only according to the city team's peaceful-entry relation. Ordinary
`CvPlot::setOwner` therefore changes an input to the surrounding cache even
when the feature/improvement is unchanged, but it has no surrounding-cache
refresh for nearby cities.

Master-vassal access
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
`canPeacefullyEnter` lets a master access territory owned by its vassal.
`CvTeam::setVassal` can therefore add/remove positive surrounding effects from
master cities whose radii overlap vassal-owned plots, but it likewise has no
surrounding-cache refresh.

These are not separate findings: they mutate different inputs to the same
`canAccessHappyHealth` dependency and require the same class of missing
invalidation.

ANCESTRY / INTRODUCTION BOUNDARY
--------------------------------
This root is AdvCiv-specific rather than inherited from BtS/K-Mod.

Current K-Mod and Civ4CE/BtS do not contain `canAccessHappyHealth` or the older
`canAccessImprovement` access gate.

AdvCiv practical commit 1732 (`d595a1df9e`, title:
"Health tag for improvements; merge xml-tags-as-enums branch.") introduced the
`advc.901` combined surrounding cache and `CvTeam::canAccessImprovement`, making
positive IMPROVEMENT health/happiness conditional on `canPeacefullyEnter`.
That commit added feature/improvement source refreshes, but no Open Borders,
vassal or ownership refresh.

AdvCiv practical commit 2203 (`7d75582d60`, title:
"No Forest health from closed-borders rivals") deliberately generalized the
same rule into `canAccessHappyHealth` and applied it to positive FEATURE health
and happiness too. Again, no corresponding relation-state invalidator was
added.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains that dependency and its `setOpenBorders` lacks a
surrounding-health/happiness update. Current SAS inherits the same structure.

Thus the bug was introduced with AdvCiv's `advc.901` access-dependent
surrounding-effect design and broadened when Forest health was explicitly made
closed-border-sensitive.

----------------

The closest old material is a Queue-003 CONTROL around

Other nearby player-mutator controls established that direct
`changeFeatureHappiness` correctly calls `updateFeatureHappiness`; that is the
SOURCE-change side of the asymmetry and strengthens rather than duplicates
F509.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The cache invariant is:

    whenever ownership or diplomatic-access state changes whether a city team
    can peacefully access a plot in that city's radius, the affected city's
    cached surrounding health/happiness must be rebuilt before health/happiness
    is next consumed.

Natural repair hooks are therefore:

1. Open Borders changes:
   refresh member cities of the affected teams after the relation bit changes
   (or use a targeted nearby/dirty mechanism if performance warrants it).

2. Vassal relation changes:
   refresh the master-side cities whose access to vassal territory can change;
   a conservative affected-team refresh is simpler and safer.

3. Plot ownership changes:
   after non-city ownership has settled, call
   `updateSurroundingHealthHappiness()` for nearby cities, matching the existing
   feature/improvement hooks.

A centralized "surrounding access state changed" helper would reduce the risk
of repairing Open Borders while leaving ownership/vassal siblings behind.

Classification: AdvCiv-introduced cross-object surrounding-health/happiness
cache invalidation bug.

POST-F509 BOUNDARY CLOSURE
--------------------------
The immediate `canPeacefullyEnter` sibling sweep is clean. Its other current uses are
live movement / legality / pathfinding / diplomacy predicates rather than persistent
city aggregates. `canAccessHappyHealth` is the relevant place where peaceful-access
identity is copied into long-lived city health/happiness state, so F509 does not need
to absorb unrelated movement-state behavior.

F510 / KI#833 -- War-plan transitions do not refresh the cached player strategy hash, so a newly chosen war can enter the same unit phase with pre-war CRUSH / PRODUCTION strategy bits
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT / CONTRACT
---------------
Current AdvCiv/SAS stores the whole AI strategy set in `CvPlayerAI::m_eStrategyHash`.
K-Mod changed the old BtS lazy getter into an explicit `AI_updateStrategyHash()` refresh,
and current sequential player activation runs that refresh BEFORE the team's war-planning
turn:

    CvPlayer::setTurnActive(true)
        -> AI().AI_updateCacheData()
            -> AI_updateStrategyHash()
        -> GET_TEAM(getTeam()).doTurn()          // team leader only
            -> CvTeamAI::AI_doTurnPost()
                -> AI_doWar()
                    -> AI_setWarPlan(...)
        -> doTurnUnits()
            -> AI().AI_doTurnUnitsPre()

`CvTeamAI::AI_setWarPlan()` changes strategic state immediately. It:

    * updates cached war-plan counts;
    * stores the new plan;
    * resets the plan-state counter;
    * recalculates area strategies;
    * dirties every AI member's city production;

but it never recomputes / invalidates any member's strategy hash.

This is a real missing dependency because current `AI_updateStrategyHash()` directly reads
war-plan state for multiple strategy bits, most clearly `AI_STRATEGY_CRUSH` and
`AI_STRATEGY_PRODUCTION`.

Therefore the normal scheduler can deliberately install a new war plan and dirty production
so that the plan affects same-turn behavior, while all player strategy queries in that same
unit/player turn still see the hash computed before the plan existed.

CURRENT CRUSH THRESHOLD REPRODUCTION
------------------------------------
A compact current-data witness can be built with a one-member Bismarck team.
Current SAS XML gives Bismarck:

    FLAVOR_MILITARY = 10

so the CRUSH random term is:

    AI_getStrategyRand(13) % (4 + 10/2)
    = AI_getStrategyRand(13) % 9

Use an ordinary state where:

1. the pre-turn strategy hash already has `AI_STRATEGY_DAGGER`;
2. the team has no existing war plan;
3. there is exactly one close, non-vassal eligible target;
4. current war-success contribution is 0;
5. `AI_getStrategyRand(13) % 9 == 4`.

The random remainder is reachable by the real strategy-random generator; e.g. in the
Ancient-era shift, multiple legal stored strategy-rand values produce remainder 4.

Before the team war decision:

    iWarCount = 0

so CRUSH cannot activate regardless of the score.

During `AI_doWar()`, the existing Dagger strategy is itself one of the values read from the
already-computed hash. If total-war target selection succeeds, current code deliberately uses
Dagger to skip preparation and installs a direct total plan:

    AI_setWarPlan(eBestTarget,
        iDaggerCount > 0 ? WARPLAN_TOTAL : WARPLAN_PREPARING_TOTAL);

Re-evaluating the CRUSH formula against the now-correct post-plan state gives:

    strategy random                         +4
    current Dagger                          +3
    new WARPLAN_TOTAL (6, halved by advc)  +3
    ------------------------------------------
    iCrushValue                            10

The one close target now also gives:

    iWarCount = 1

and the current activation condition is:

    iWarCount == 1 && iCrushValue >= 10

Therefore the mathematically correct post-plan player strategy is CRUSH = true.
The stored `m_eStrategyHash`, however, remains the pre-plan value CRUSH = false.

This fixture does not need the optional +2 typical-defender advantage term. It also does not
depend on a future XML extension: Bismarck's Military flavor 10, Dagger, direct total-war
selection and the threshold are all live current code/data.

IMMEDIATE SAME-UNIT-PHASE CONSEQUENCE
-------------------------------------
The stale bit is consumed before any later turn can repair it.
Immediately after the team turn, `CvPlayer::doTurnUnits()` starts with:

    CvPlayerAI::AI_doTurnUnitsPre()

which contains:

    if (AI_isDoStrategy(AI_STRATEGY_CRUSH) && AI_isFocusWar())
        AI_convertUnitAITypesForCrush();

The two predicates now disagree about time:

    * `AI_isFocusWar()` reads the LIVE new war-plan/area state and can already return true;
    * `AI_isDoStrategy(AI_STRATEGY_CRUSH)` reads the stale pre-plan strategy hash.

Thus the newly chosen total war can correctly qualify as a focus war but still skip the
CRUSH conversion pass solely because the cached hash was not refreshed.

`AI_convertUnitAITypesForCrush()` is state-changing gameplay code, not logging or a minor
score. It scans spare attack-capable Reserve / Collateral / suitable city-defense units,
ranks them for `UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY`, and directly executes:

    AI_setUnitAIType(UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY);

for qualifying units. Missing the CRUSH bit therefore changes unit roles before any selection
group performs its ordinary movement turn.

There is also a clean later tactical threshold consequence in `CvUnitAI` city attack logic.
Current SAS has:

    BBAI_ATTACK_CITY_STACK_RATIO = 122

and the war-strategy adjustment begins at +5 but subtracts 10 when CRUSH is active.
Holding the other optional adjustments at zero gives:

    stale non-CRUSH required ratio = 122 + 5  = 127
    correct CRUSH required ratio   = 122 - 5  = 117

A stack comparison of 120 therefore refuses the attack under the stale hash but accepts it
under the correct post-plan CRUSH state. This is a secondary manifestation; the earlier
UnitAI conversion already proves a same-unit-phase behavioral divergence.

PRODUCTION-STRATEGY SIBLING
---------------------------
K-Mod added a further direct war-plan dependency in `AI_STRATEGY_PRODUCTION`.
Current AdvCiv/SAS computes:

    if (AI_isFocusWar())
    {
        iProductionValue++;
        if (WARPLAN_TOTAL or WARPLAN_PREPARING_TOTAL exists)
            iProductionValue += 3;
    }

so installing a qualifying total/preparing-total plan after the hash refresh can increase the
correct Production-strategy score by +4. `AI_setWarPlan()` simultaneously calls
`AI_makeProductionDirty()` for AI members, showing that same-turn production is specifically
intended to respond to the new war-plan state, yet `AI_STRATEGY_PRODUCTION` can remain the old
bit while those dirty cities are reconsidered.

This is the same strategy-hash invalidation root as CRUSH, not a separate finding.

BROADER SAME-ROOT TRANSITIONS
-----------------------------
The defect is not restricted to adding the first war plan.
`AI_setWarPlan()` is also used for:

    * PREPARING -> active LIMITED/TOTAL transitions;
    * plan cancellation / timeout;
    * ATTACKED / ATTACKED_RECENT changes;
    * dogpile changes;
    * declaration/post-declaration updates;
    * selected unit-AI plan changes in later tactical code.

Any such transition can change a direct war-plan input to CRUSH/PRODUCTION, and the
`AI_updateAreaStrategies()` call can additionally change area-AI inputs used by other strategy
calculations (e.g. Dagger). These are siblings of one missing strategy invalidation contract.

ANCESTRY
--------
The root begins in BtS, while K-Mod makes the stale window deterministic and adds more affected
strategy inputs.

BtS / Civ4CE
~~~~~~~~~~~~
BtS stores `m_iStrategyHash` lazily for a game turn. `AI_getStrategyHash()` returns the cached
value whenever `m_iStrategyHashCacheTurn == current game turn`; the explicit invalidator is
`AI_forceUpdateStrategies()`.

BtS `CvTeamAI::AI_setWarPlan()` changes the plan, updates area strategies and dirties member
production, but does NOT call `AI_forceUpdateStrategies()`.

Moreover, in the ordinary no-war-plan branch of BtS `AI_doWar()`, the team first queries each
member's:

    AI_STRATEGY_DAGGER
    AI_STRATEGY_GET_BETTER_UNITS
    AI_STRATEGY_FINAL_WAR

before it selects and installs a new plan. The first such query can populate the entire lazy
strategy hash from the pre-plan state. BtS CRUSH already directly scans war plans (with an even
larger +6 Preparing/early-Total contribution), so the newly installed plan can make the correct
CRUSH state differ while the same-turn lazy hash remains cached.

Thus the fundamental missing `AI_setWarPlan` -> strategy-cache invalidation is inherited from
BtS.

K-Mod
~~~~~
K-Mod removes the BtS lazy cache-turn invalidation mechanism and makes strategy hashing eager in
`AI_updateCacheData()`. It also restructures sequential turn order so the player's cache update
runs at activation and the leader team's `CvTeam::doTurn()` follows immediately afterward.
This turns the old possible lazy-staleness pattern into a straightforward structural order:

    strategy snapshot -> team war-plan mutation -> player unit phase.

K-Mod additionally adds the war-plan-sensitive Production-strategy calculation.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Both retain K-Mod's eager activation refresh and the later team war turn. AdvCiv refines the
CRUSH/PRODUCTION formulas, adds cached war-plan counts and area/focus-war helpers, but still gives
`AI_setWarPlan()` no strategy-hash invalidation. Current SAS inherits the same lifetime.

DUPLICATE LEDGER
----------------
Full-album searches for `AI_updateStrategyHash`, strategy hash/cache, `AI_STRATEGY_CRUSH`,
CRUSH conversion, war-plan strategy, `AI_setWarPlan` and stale strategy found no prior numbered
root for a WAR-PLAN TRANSITION leaving the player strategy hash stale.

Nearby findings are distinct:

* F042 / war-plan-count cache concerns vassal target counting and disagreement between
  `m_aiWarPlanCounts` / `m_bAnyWarPlan` and raw plans. F510 reproduces with one ordinary
  non-vassal target and correct war-plan counts.
* F344 concerns a local `AI_isFocusWar` multiple-pushover flag typo. F510 can use a single
  ordinary close non-pushover target and assumes `AI_isFocusWar` itself is correct.
* F456 concerns one wrong favorite-civic INPUT inside Missionary strategy calculation under
  Random Personalities. F510 concerns strategy-hash LIFETIME after a later state transition.
* Earlier Queue-001 strategy-hash controls compared current formula content / cached defines;
  they did not audit war-plan mutation after hash computation.

Therefore F510 is not an alternate symptom of an existing strategy-calculation finding.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The required invariant is:

    after a war-plan / area-strategy transition changes inputs to a player's strategy hash,
    all affected AI members must see a refreshed hash before the next strategy consumer.

Potential implementations:

1. Add a real strategy-cache dirty/invalidation mechanism and mark all AI team members dirty in
   `AI_setWarPlan()` after the plan and area-strategy state have settled. Recompute lazily on the
   next `AI_isDoStrategy` query.

2. With the current eager architecture, minimally refresh all AI member strategy hashes once
   after the team's war-planning turn and before any member unit phase. This fixes the ordinary
   sequential path but is less comprehensive for later mid-turn `AI_setWarPlan()` callers.

3. Recompute member strategy hashes directly from `AI_setWarPlan()` after
   `AI_updateAreaStrategies()`. This is simple semantically but may repeat a relatively expensive
   full strategy calculation multiple times while `AI_doWar()` changes several plans.

A dirty/lazy member-level invalidation is the broadest repair because it also covers declaration,
plan cancellation and tactical later callers without forcing repeated eager recomputation.

Do NOT merely dirty city production: current code already does that, and the demonstrated first
bad consumer is `AI_doTurnUnitsPre()` before city production.

Classification: BtS-inherited strategy-cache invalidation defect, made structurally deterministic
by K-Mod's eager activation cache and broadened by K-Mod's additional war-plan-sensitive strategy
bits.

F510 SIBLING BOUNDARY
---------------------
The first post-F510 team-turn mutation challenge separates into a distinct root rather than
another F510 symptom.

F510's producer is a WAR-PLAN mutation after the strategy hash has already been computed.
The new war plan itself changes strategy-hash inputs such as CRUSH and PRODUCTION; the bad
consumers occur after `AI_setWarPlan`.

The new root below happens earlier. TEAM DIPLOMACY COUNTERS change and the full attitude
cache is refreshed before `AI_doWar`, but the strategy hash is not. `AI_doWar` therefore
simultaneously has the correct new attitude and a Dagger strategy bit calculated from the
old attitude. Invalidating only from `AI_setWarPlan` (the natural F510 repair) does not fix
this earlier contradiction.

F511 / KI#834 -- K-Mod snapshots the player strategy hash before the team updates diplomacy counters / attitudes, so same-turn war planning can use a stale DAGGER bit and skip war preparation
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT / ORDERING CONTRACT
------------------------
Current sequential AdvCiv/SAS player activation performs these relevant steps in order:

    CvPlayer::setTurnActive(true)
        -> CvPlayerAI::AI_updateCacheData()
            -> AI_updateStrategyHash()
        -> GET_TEAM(getTeam()).doTurn()       // team leader activation
            -> CvTeamAI::AI_doTurnPre()
                -> AI_doCounter()
            -> CvTeamAI::AI_doTurnPost()
                -> every member:
                    AI_updateCloseBorderAttitude()
                    AI_updateAttitude()
                -> AI_updateAreaStrategies(false)
                -> AI_doWar()

The source comment in `AI_doCounter()` explicitly acknowledges the split:

    "Attitude isn't updated here. Should be soon enough in AI_doTurnPost."

And `AI_doTurnPost()` explicitly performs the full K-Mod attitude-cache refresh before
calling `AI_doWar()`.

That ordering is internally inconsistent with the eager strategy cache because current
`AI_updateStrategyHash()` itself reads diplomatic attitude while deciding whether a close
rival is eligible for `AI_STRATEGY_DAGGER`:

    if (kTeam.AI_getWarPlan(itRival->getTeam()) != NO_WARPLAN ||
        (AI_playerCloseness(itRival->getID()) > 0 &&
         GET_TEAM(getTeam()).AI_noWarProbAdjusted(itRival->getTeam()) < 90))
    {
        iCloseTargets++;
    }

`AI_noWarProbAdjusted()` obtains the team's current attitude, and current player attitudes
are stored in `m_aiAttitude` until `AI_updateAttitude()` refreshes them.

Thus the normal scheduler does:

    1. compute Dagger using YESTERDAY / pre-counter cached attitude;
    2. increment team diplomatic counters;
    3. recompute the member's attitude from those new counters;
    4. enter `AI_doWar()` with the NEW attitude cache;
    5. nevertheless read Dagger from the OLD strategy hash.

This is not merely a generic one-turn heuristic cadence. `AI_doWar()` is deliberately
positioned after the attitude refresh so current diplomatic relations govern the team's
war decision, yet one of its major aggression inputs still encodes the pre-refresh relation.

CURRENT GENGHIS OPEN-BORDERS THRESHOLD WITNESS
----------------------------------------------
Current SAS provides a compact shipped-data threshold crossing with Genghis Khan.
His current leader XML has:

    iMaxWarRand = 50
    FLAVOR_MILITARY = 10

and no-war probabilities:

    ATTITUDE_ANNOYED  = 10
    ATTITUDE_CAUTIOUS = 50
    ATTITUDE_PLEASED  = 90

The AdvCiv-SAS leader defaults inherited by ordinary leaders include:

    iOpenBordersAttitudeDivisor   = 25
    iOpenBordersAttitudeChangeLimit = 2

and current `RELATIONS_THRESH_PLEASED = 4`.

Use a one-member Genghis team and one close known potential rival under Open Borders.
Arrange the already-cached raw attitude toward that rival at exactly 3 (Cautious) and the
team Open Borders counter at 24 at player activation. This is ordinary long-lived
relationship state; no debug-only API is required.

At activation-time strategy computation:

    cached raw attitude = 3 -> ATTITUDE_CAUTIOUS
    Genghis no-war probability = 50
    `AI_noWarProbAdjusted` returns 50 while Open Borders is active
    Dagger close-target gate: 50 < 90 -> TRUE

During the immediately following team `AI_doCounter()`, the Open Borders counter update is
an ordinary supported `AI_randomCounterChange` (binomial 0..2) whose positive outcome can
advance 24 -> 25. At counter 25, `AI_getOpenBordersAttitude()` changes from:

    24 / 25 = 0

to:

    25 / 25 = +1

so the subsequent full `AI_updateAttitude()` changes the raw attitude from 3 to 4:

    raw 4 -> ATTITUDE_PLEASED
    Genghis no-war probability = 90
    Dagger close-target gate: 90 < 90 -> FALSE

The correct post-counter/post-refresh state therefore no longer has this rival as a Dagger
close target. The stored strategy hash still contains the result computed when the same
rival was Cautious.

This witness does not rely on assuming that the Open Borders counter always increments by
one. `AI_randomCounterChange` explicitly permits +1 (and +2); a supported ordinary random
outcome reaching the relationship threshold is sufficient to prove the lifetime defect.

DAGGER SCORE CAN FLIP ON THAT TARGET ALONE
------------------------------------------
The target-eligibility change can independently flip the actual Dagger bit rather than only
perturb a score.

For Genghis:

    12000 / max(100, 50 + MaxWarRand)
      = 12000 / 100
      = 120

Choose a legal stored strategy-random state for which:

    AI_getStrategyRand(12) % 11 == 5

The real current generator has many such reachable states (for example legal stored
`m_iStrategyRand` values 6, 28, 37, 46, 55, 64, ... in the Ancient-era shift produce
remainder 5).

The random Dagger term is then:

    120 * 5 / 10 = 60

Military flavor contributes:

    5 * min(8, 10) = 40

Subtotal:

    60 + 40 = 100

which already meets the normal Dagger threshold before any unique-unit, handicap or
area-strategy bonus is needed.

Therefore a state can be chosen where the PRE-COUNTER close-target test is the only reason
Dagger evaluation runs, and it sets Dagger=true. After the counter/attitude refresh, the
correct current state has zero close targets and should have Dagger=false.

IMMEDIATE SAME-TEAM-TURN WAR-PLANNING CONSEQUENCE
-------------------------------------------------
`CvTeamAI::AI_doWar()` runs only after the full attitude refresh, but it counts Dagger from
the stale member strategy hash:

    int iDaggerCount = 0;
    ...
    bool const bDagger =
        kMember.AI_isDoStrategy(AI_STRATEGY_DAGGER) || ...;
    if (bDagger)
    {
        iDaggerCount++;
        bAggressive = true;
    }

So the stale bit immediately alters the team's war-planning mode even though the same
function's direct attitude reads already use the updated Pleased relation.

Most strongly, when total-war target selection succeeds, current code stores:

    AI_setWarPlan(eBestTarget,
        iDaggerCount > 0 ? WARPLAN_TOTAL : WARPLAN_PREPARING_TOTAL);

A stale Dagger=true therefore installs DIRECT `WARPLAN_TOTAL`, while the correct current
Dagger=false state installs `WARPLAN_PREPARING_TOTAL`.

A clean fixture can make the newly Pleased close rival the only valid total-war target and
satisfy the ordinary power / war-random / `AI_startWarVal` checks. The bug then causes the
team to skip the intended preparation phase because of an attitude classification that the
team itself has already refreshed away earlier in the same `AI_doTurnPost()`.

This is a state transition, not merely a +/- few-point valuation difference. It changes the
stored war-plan type and immediately feeds the F510 family of focus-war/area/unit/production
behavior.

K-MOD ORIGIN / BTS NEGATIVE CONTROL
-----------------------------------
This particular cache-order root is K-Mod-introduced.

BtS/Civ4CE:
- `CvPlayerAI::AI_getAttitudeVal()` computes attitude from live diplomatic counters on every
  call; there is no K-Mod full `m_aiAttitude` cache.
- the strategy hash is lazy per game turn (`m_iStrategyHashCacheTurn`);
- `CvTeamAI::AI_doCounter()` runs before `AI_doWar()`;
- therefore the first ordinary Dagger strategy query made by the war planner after the team
  counter update reads the updated counters through live attitude calculation.

BtS does have the separate F510-class issue where a strategy hash already populated earlier
in the turn can become stale after a WAR-PLAN mutation. That does not create this specific
counter/attitude-order contradiction.

K-Mod changes both sides needed for F511:
1. it introduces the full `m_aiAttitudeCache`, and `AI_getAttitudeVal()` becomes a direct
   cache read;
2. it moves the full member attitude-cache refresh to team `AI_doTurnPost()` after
   `AI_doCounter()`;
3. independently, it makes `AI_updateStrategyHash()` eager through player `updateCacheData()`.

Current sequential activation computes that eager player strategy snapshot before the team
turn. K-Mod's own Dagger calculation already uses the cached attitude to decide whether a
close rival has enough war probability to count (`iAttitudeWarProb > 10`, equivalent to a
no-war probability below 90). AdvCiv later rewrites the close-target block but preserves the
same semantic threshold through `AI_noWarProbAdjusted(...) < 90`.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the K-Mod cache/order architecture.

SEMANTIC DEDUP
--------------
Full-album searches for Dagger, `iDaggerCount`, `AI_noWarProbAdjusted`, OpenBordersCounter,
attitude-cache timing, strategy hash and close-target logic found no same-root finding.

Nearest but distinct roots/controls:
- F035 / KI#356: `AI_doWar` used invalid set subtraction between total Dagger members and
  independent FinancialTrouble / GetBetterUnits populations. That is team-population
  arithmetic, not Dagger cache freshness.
- F049 / KI#370: Permanent Alliance reverse merge omitted outsider-side OpenBordersCounter.
  That loses relationship history at team merge; F511 uses a correctly maintained ordinary
  Open Borders counter but snapshots strategy before its same-turn increment is reflected.
- F296 / KI#619: one direction of recurring annual deal processing refreshed third-party
  attitude caches prematurely inside `CvDeal::doTurn`. That is deal-loop refresh timing and
  rival-trade resentment, not strategy/war planning.
- F456: wrong favorite-civic/personality input inside strategy calculation; content error,
  not strategy lifetime.
- F510 / KI#833: war-plan mutation after strategy computation leaves CRUSH/PRODUCTION bits
  stale. Different producer, earlier/later boundary and repair hook.

No existing numbered root was found for TEAM DIPLOMACY COUNTERS / ATTITUDE REFRESH occurring
after the eager strategy snapshot while the same `AI_doWar()` consumes stale Dagger.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The architectural invariant should be:

    before `AI_doWar()` consumes member strategies, every strategy bit that depends on
    diplomatic counters / cached attitudes must correspond to the attitude state that
    `AI_doWar()` itself will use.

Safe repair directions to evaluate:

1. Preferred normal-turn boundary:
   after `AI_doTurnPost()` refreshes every member's close-border/full attitude cache (and,
   ideally, after other pre-war team state that strategy calculation reads is settled),
   refresh/invalidate each AI member's strategy hash BEFORE `AI_doWar()`.

   This naturally repairs F511 and can also cover normal-turn portions of F510 if positioned
   after area-strategy refresh; however F510 still needs a true invalidation contract for
   war-plan mutations that occur after this point or through other callers.

2. More general dependency mechanism:
   restore a real strategy-dirty/lazy-refresh contract and dirty affected member strategies
   whenever attitude-affecting team counters / attitude cache state changes. This is broader
   and safer for nonstandard midturn callers but potentially more invasive.

Do not merely special-case the Open Borders counter. The same ordering can apply whenever
`AI_doCounter()` changes a relationship component that crosses an attitude/no-war threshold
(Defensive Pact, Share War and other counter-derived attitude inputs). Open Borders supplies
the compact numeric witness, not the full dependency boundary.

Do not fix only `iDaggerCount` inside `AI_doWar()` by recomputing one ad-hoc Dagger condition.
Dagger is a player strategy with multiple consumers, and the root is the freshness contract
between the strategy snapshot and refreshed diplomatic state.

POST-F511 CURSOR
----------------
F512 / KI#835 remains UNUSED.

First bound F511 against other strategy-hash inputs mutated by the same team turn:
- `AI_updateAreaStrategies(false)` runs after the attitude refresh and before `AI_doWar`;
  current Dagger / paranoia / Production strategy calculations read area/focus-war state.
  Decide which are F510/F511 siblings versus a distinct cache producer.
- `m_bLonely` is updated in team `AI_doTurnPost()` after the player's strategy snapshot;
  `AI_getFlavorValue()` changes several flavors when lonely, so determine whether a
  loneliness transition can change a strategy bit before same-turn `AI_doWar` / unit use.
- team worst-enemy / strength-memory changes and any victory/tech-team inputs should be
  challenged only where the strategy calculator reads them and an immediate consumer exists.

Then resume the persistent-CvPlayerAI cache dependency ranking under F512 UNUSED rather than
manufacturing a new root from intentionally sampled heuristics.

POST-F511 STRATEGY-INPUT BOUNDARY
---------------------------------
The routine `AI_updateAreaStrategies(false)` that runs before `AI_doWar()` can also change
strategy-hash inputs after the activation snapshot. That belongs to F510's already recorded
WAR-PLAN / AREA-STRATEGY freshness boundary rather than deserving a new number.

The AdvCiv loneliness state is different. It is an independently cached team field with a
separate producer/history and a separate input contract (`AI_getFlavorValue`). It can flip
after player strategy computation even without a war-plan or attitude transition, and an
F510 war-plan invalidator or F511 attitude/counter invalidator would not repair it.

F512 / KI#835 -- AdvCiv updates cached team loneliness after the player's eager strategy snapshot, so a newly non-start-era isolated AI can enter same-turn war planning with non-lonely flavor / DAGGER values
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT / CURRENT ORDERING
-----------------------
Current AdvCiv/SAS makes leader flavors depend on cached team loneliness:

    int CvPlayerAI::AI_getFlavorValue(FlavorTypes eFlavor) const
    {
        ...
        int r = GC.getInfo(getPersonalityType()).getFlavorValue(eFlavor);
        if (GET_TEAM(getTeam()).AI_isLonely())
        {
            if (eFlavor == FLAVOR_SCIENCE)
                r += 3;
            else if (r > 1)
                r /= 2;
        }
        return r;
    }

`AI_isLonely()` is just the stored team field `m_bLonely`.

But normal sequential activation computes the player's whole strategy hash BEFORE the team
recomputes that field:

    CvPlayer::setTurnActive(true)
        -> CvPlayerAI::AI_updateCacheData()
            -> AI_updateStrategyHash()
                -> AI_getFlavorValue(...)       // reads old m_bLonely
        -> GET_TEAM(getTeam()).doTurn()
            -> CvTeamAI::AI_doTurnPost()
                -> if (getCurrentEra() > game start era)
                       m_bLonely = ...           // recomputed here
                -> AI_updateAreaStrategies(false)
                -> AI_doWar()                    // consumes stale strategies

Current loneliness calculation is:

    int iHasMet = getHasMetCivCount(false);
    int iYetToMeet = GC.getGame().countCivTeamsAlive() - iHasMet;
    m_bLonely = (iYetToMeet > iHasMet + 1 && iHasMet <= 2);

The previously audited `+1` arithmetic here is intentional self-count compensation; F512 is
not an off-by-one in this predicate. The defect is the cache lifetime around an otherwise
valid predicate.

DETERMINISTIC FIRST-POST-START-ERA TRANSITION
---------------------------------------------
The cleanest producer does not require a random contact event.

`m_bLonely` resets to false. While the team remains in the game start era,
`AI_doTurnPost()` deliberately does not recompute it at all:

    if (getCurrentEra() > GC.getGame().getStartEra())
        ... update m_bLonely ...

Take a normal Ancient-start game with enough living civilizations that a team which has met
only one rival satisfies the loneliness predicate once the guard becomes active.

During player A's previous turn, `doResearch()` completes a tech that advances A/team from
Ancient into Classical. `CvPlayer::setCurrentEra()` immediately updates the player's era
factor, but the team's `m_bLonely` is still false because that turn's team update already
occurred at activation while the team was Ancient.

On A's next activation:

    1. player `AI_updateStrategyHash()` runs in Classical and still reads m_bLonely=false;
    2. the immediately following team `AI_doTurnPost()` now passes the post-start-era guard
       and recomputes m_bLonely=true;
    3. `AI_doWar()` runs after that flip while the player strategy hash remains the
       non-lonely snapshot.

Thus this is a deterministic cache transition tied to normal era progression; no save/load,
Python, autoplay identity switch or unsupported API is needed.

CURRENT GENGHIS / MONGOL DAGGER NUMERIC WITNESS
-----------------------------------------------
Current shipped SAS provides an exact threshold flip with the normal Genghis/Mongolia pair.
Relevant current data/code:

    Genghis iMaxWarRand       = 50
    Genghis FLAVOR_MILITARY  = 10
    Noble iAITrainPercent    = 100
    Mongol UU                = UNIT_MONGOL_KHISHIGTEN
    Khishigten prereq tech   = TECH_CHIVALRY (Medieval)
    Khishigten AND bonus     = Horse
    Khishigten OR bonus      = Iron

Use the first Classical activation above, a neutral capital AreaAI state, non-Aggressive-AI
game option, one ordinary close Dagger-eligible rival, no Culture2/Missionary blocker, and
no Horse or Iron. Chivalry is not yet researched.

Choose a legal stored strategy-random state with:

    AI_getStrategyRand(12) % 11 == 5

(the same real-generator reachability proved in F511; many stored values produce this).

Random Dagger term:

    12000 / max(100, 50 + 50) = 120
    120 * 5 / 10 = +60

NORMAL NON-LONELY flavor term used by the stale snapshot:

    5 * min(8, MilitaryFlavor 10) = +40

Once `m_bLonely=true`, the correct live Military flavor is halved:

    10 / 2 = 5
    5 * min(8, 5) = +25

The current Khishigten unavailable-UU block contributes exactly +10 in this fixture:

    Chivalry is Medieval and therefore within current Classical era + 1,
    but not yet known                                      +30
    generic unavailable-UU allowance                       +20
    missing required Horse                                 -20
    at least one OR bonus exists but Iron is also absent   -20
    -----------------------------------------------------------
    Khishigten contribution                                +10

Noble's handicap term is:

    range(100 - iAITrainPercent(100), 0, 15) = 0

and the neutral capital area gives no area-strategy Dagger bonus.

Therefore:

    stale pre-team non-lonely Dagger = 60 + 40 + 10 = 110  -> ACTIVE
    correct post-team lonely Dagger  = 60 + 25 + 10 = 95   -> INACTIVE

The normal threshold is 100. The same player's correct flavor state therefore flips Dagger
off before `AI_doWar()`, while the stored strategy hash still says Dagger=true.

The Classical Dagger era gate is also live: absent a custom `iAIEraFactor`, AdvCiv maps era
index to `100 * era`, so Classical has AI era factor 1 and satisfies the current early-rush
era condition.

SAME-TURN GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCE
------------------------------
Exactly as in the independent F511 producer, the immediately following team `AI_doWar()`
counts each member's stored Dagger strategy:

    if (bDagger)
    {
        iDaggerCount++;
        bAggressive = true;
    }

The stale non-lonely Dagger therefore makes a team aggressive even though the team's own
`m_bLonely` flag has already become true.

Most strongly, when a valid total-war target is selected:

    AI_setWarPlan(eBestTarget,
        iDaggerCount > 0 ? WARPLAN_TOTAL : WARPLAN_PREPARING_TOTAL);

The stale flavor snapshot can therefore cause newly Classical but still isolated Genghis to
skip the preparation phase and enter immediate `WARPLAN_TOTAL`; a strategy recomputation
using the already-current lonely flag would use `WARPLAN_PREPARING_TOTAL` in the fixture.

This is not just an exploration/tech-priority effect of loneliness. The stale cached flavor
state changes a stored war-plan transition in the very same team turn.

HISTORY / ORIGIN
----------------
The reachable AdvCiv history makes the regression boundary unusually clear.

Practical 1253 (`f6ff6a182f...`, "Initial commit (cont.)") contains the early `advc.109`
implementation as a DYNAMIC player function:

    bool CvPlayerAI::isLonely() const
    {
        if (getCurrentEra() == game start era)
            return false;
        ... compute hasMet / yetToMeet live ...
    }

and `AI_getFlavorValue()` calls that live function. Under that form, a strategy calculation
cannot read an older separately stored loneliness state.

AdvCiv practical 1386 (`dc9c167dfc...`,
"Refactoring and a couple of minor corrections in AdvCiv code") changes the contract:

    * removes the dynamic `CvPlayerAI::isLonely()` flavor query;
    * changes `AI_getFlavorValue()` to `GET_TEAM(getTeam()).AI_isLonely()`;
    * adds cached team `m_bLonely = false`;
    * recomputes `m_bLonely` in `CvTeamAI::AI_doTurnPost()`.

That refactor preserves K-Mod's eager player `AI_updateStrategyHash()` earlier in activation.
Therefore practical 1386 is the clean origin of the stale-loneliness strategy window.

K-Mod and BtS/Civ4CE do not have AdvCiv's `m_bLonely`/lonely-flavor mechanism, so they cannot
contain this root. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS retain it.

SEMANTIC DEDUP
--------------
Full-album and current Known-Issues searches for `m_bLonely`, `AI_isLonely`, lonely flavor,
strategy/loneliness and related terms found no same-root numbered issue.

Existing Album mentions are controls / other contexts:
- Permanent-Alliance/team-merge audits note that lonely state is derived/recomputed rather
  than copied. That says nothing about when the recomputation occurs relative to strategy.
- F456's deterministic Random-Personalities Missionary fixture deliberately uses a two-civ
  game where loneliness is false; it is a favorite-civic input bug, not loneliness lifetime.
- F510 is war-plan/area-strategy mutation after strategy hashing.
- F511 is diplomacy-counter / attitude refresh after strategy hashing.

F512 has a separate producer (`m_bLonely` recomputation), separate historical origin
(advc.109 practical-1386 cache migration), and is not repaired by only invalidating on war
plans or attitude-counter changes.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The invariant should be:

    any cached player value built from `AI_getFlavorValue()` must observe the current
    loneliness classification for the turn in which it is consumed.

Repair directions to evaluate:

1. Recompute team loneliness BEFORE member strategy/victory/other flavor-dependent caches
   are built at activation. Because loneliness depends only on current era and met-team
   population, this is cheap and conceptually clean.

2. Alternatively, after `m_bLonely` changes in `AI_doTurnPost()`, invalidate/recompute every
   member cache whose construction reads `AI_getFlavorValue()` before those caches are
   consumed. At minimum this includes the strategy hash; a broader audit should check any
   other persistent flavor-dependent values rather than hard-coding Dagger only.

3. Reverting loneliness to a cheap dynamic predicate, as the earlier advc.109 implementation
   did, would remove the stale field entirely but may have been refactored for team semantics /
   reuse and should be weighed against the current architecture.

Do not fix only the first Classical transition or only Dagger. Contact changes can also flip
`m_bLonely` true<->false between team recomputations, and the flavor transformation affects
Science plus every non-Science flavor above 1.

C031-WIP258 — F513 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F513 / KI#836 — AdvCiv's cached AI_neededExplorers snapshot is built before unit
exploration, so newly revealed tiles can lower the correct explorer target while later
same-turn city production still uses the old higher target

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — AdvCiv performance-cache regression introduced in v0.87 / practical 1264
(commit 0884de493c5d4034cfa833d053e3234bf647ddc6) and retained in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
current SAS. BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod calculate AI_neededExplorers dynamically and therefore
do not have this cache-lifetime root.

ROOT
----
K-Mod/BtS calculate explorer demand directly from current map revelation each time:

    AI_neededExplorers(area)
        -> area.getNumUnrevealedTiles(getTeam())
        -> current demand

AdvCiv v0.87 changed this into an activation-time performance cache. The introducing diff
explicitly says:

    "Now cached. advc.017b adds another call to AI_neededExplorers,
     and it gets called by several UnitAI members too. Probably no noticeable
     difference in performance, but who knows."

It adds:

    AI_updateCacheData()
        -> AI_updateNeededExplorers()

and replaces the former dynamic AI_neededExplorers body with a lookup in
m_neededExplorersByArea.

Current SAS retains exactly that architecture:

    CvPlayer::setTurnActive(true)
        -> AI().AI_updateCacheData()
            -> AI_updateNeededExplorers()
        -> team doTurn()
        -> doTurnUnits()

whereas the economic/city turn comes later:

    CvPlayer::doTurn()
        -> AI_doTurnPre()
        -> ...
        -> city doTurn / AI production

A complete current-source caller search finds no refresh of m_neededExplorersByArea when
plots are revealed. Outside initialization/save reconstruction, AI_updateNeededExplorers is
called only by AI_updateCacheData at activation.

MUTABLE INPUT AFTER THE SNAPSHOT
--------------------------------
The cached land demand still depends directly on live unexplored-tile count:

    iNeeded = min(
        area.getNumUnrevealedTiles(getTeam()) /
            max(150 - 20 * getCurrentEra(), 50),
        min(3, getNumCities() / 3 + 2));

Exploration units move only AFTER the cache has been populated. Normal unit sight then
reveals tiles and immediately lowers area.getNumUnrevealedTiles(getTeam()), but no cache
invalidator/recompute accompanies that revelation.

CURRENT DETERMINISTIC THRESHOLD WITNESS
---------------------------------------
Use an ordinary non-Pangaea Ancient game, one city in a large land area, exactly one
UNITAI_EXPLORE unit, no land war/danger/financial trouble, and arrange the area's revealed
frontier so that the activation snapshot contains exactly 300 unrevealed land tiles.

Ancient divisor:

    max(150 - 20 * 0, 50) = 150

One-city cap:

    min(3, 1 / 3 + 2) = 2

Therefore at activation:

    300 / 150 = 2
    cached AI_neededExplorers(area) = 2

The existing Explorer then moves during doTurnUnits and reveals at least one of those
frontier tiles. Once unrevealed tiles fall to 299 or below (while remaining at least 150),
the mathematically correct target is:

    299 / 150 = 1
    correct AI_neededExplorers(area) = 1

The cache nevertheless remains 2 for the rest of the turn.

SAME-TURN PRODUCTION CONSEQUENCE
--------------------------------
Current city production has an explicit missing-explorer branch:

    int iMissingExplorers = kPlayer.AI_neededExplorers(kArea) -
            kPlayer.AI_totalAreaUnitAIs(kArea, UNITAI_EXPLORE);
    if (iMissingExplorers > 0)
        AI_chooseUnit(UNITAI_EXPLORE, 34 * iMissingExplorers);

After the Explorer has moved/revealed tiles, the physical explorer count is still one.
Thus:

    stale cached target = 2, existing = 1 -> iMissingExplorers = 1
    correct live target = 1, existing = 1 -> iMissingExplorers = 0

The AdvCiv cache therefore turns a state that should make NO missing-explorer build attempt
into a 34% Explorer-production attempt later in the same turn.

Current SAS also has a central area-usefulness gate immediately before ordinary explorer
production:

    if (AI_neededExplorers(area) <= AI_totalAreaUnitAIs(area, UNITAI_EXPLORE))
        reject UNITAI_EXPLORE;

The same stale target changes this hard gate from:

    correct: 1 <= 1 -> reject extra Explorer

to:

    stale:   2 <= 1 -> false -> permit the extra Explorer

so the defect is not merely a soft valuation difference. The cache can admit an explorer
whose demand disappeared during the preceding unit phase.

The water-area version has the same lifetime issue at its 400-tile thresholds; the land
fixture is enough to establish the root.

PRE-CACHE SEMANTICS / ANCESTRY
------------------------------
BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod both retain a dynamic AI_neededExplorers function that reads
getNumUnrevealedTiles at each call. Consequently their city-production call after unit
exploration observes the newly revealed map state.

AdvCiv practical 1264 / commit 0884de493c (v0.87) moves the old function body into
AI_neededExplorersBulk, adds m_neededExplorersByArea, calls AI_updateNeededExplorers from
updateCacheData, and makes AI_neededExplorers return the stored map entry. The change is
explicitly tagged as caching/performance work rather than an intended one-turn gameplay
policy.

Base AdvCiv and current SAS preserve the cache and the pre-unit activation update point.
This is therefore an AdvCiv performance optimization that changes observable AI behavior
within the turn.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
Full album and current Known-Issues searches found no existing root for
m_neededExplorersByArea becoming stale after exploration/revelation.

Nearby explorer findings are distinct:

- F341 / KI#664: AI_isExcessSeaExplorers subtracts a PLAYER-GLOBAL queued explorer count
  from a WATER-AREA-LOCAL count. That is a scope mismatch between disconnected seas, not
  a cache lifetime issue.
- F342 and the later sea-explorer retirement work concern UnitAI transformation/retirement
  once a target is evaluated, not when the target itself becomes stale.
- F366 concerns Advanced Start assigning a sea explorer the wrong UNITAI_EXPLORE role.
- Current SAS naval-trade-fallback fixes concern fully explored water and physical ship
  counting in a separate fallback path; they do not refresh m_neededExplorersByArea.
- KI#192's central land-area usefulness gate actually makes F513 more observable because
  that hard gate trusts the same stale target; it does not cause the root.

The earlier Queue-001 AI_doEnemyUnitData own-unit question also remains only a control and
is unrelated to this cache.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The invariant should be:

    explorer demand used after unit exploration must reflect the map revelation state that
    exists when the demand is consumed.

Possible repairs:

1. Restore dynamic AI_neededExplorers calculation. The original AdvCiv comment itself says
   the performance gain is probably negligible, and current callers are not obviously hot
   enough to justify semantic staleness.

2. Keep the cache but invalidate/recompute the affected player's area entry when that team
   reveals tiles. This is more surgical but risks putting work into the very hot sight/
   revelation path that the cache presumably meant to avoid.

3. Keep activation-time caching for unit-AI decisions if desired, but perform one cheap
   AI_updateNeededExplorers refresh after doTurnUnits and before city/economic production.
   This preserves most of the cache benefit while restoring the pre-cache semantics for the
   important production consumers.

Do not repair only the 300->299 example. Any threshold crossing in land or water demand,
and contact/city-count/era inputs that change after the snapshot, should obey the same
freshness rule.

POST-F513 CONTROLS / CURSOR
---------------------------
The unit-class/combat-weight cache family was challenged first. Its apparent no-visible-
enemy early-return problem is mostly neutralized by an old, already-recorded quirk:
AI_doEnemyUnitData gives every visible fighting unit a baseline value of 1 and does not
exclude the player's own visible combat units, so normal own military keeps iTotal positive
and the normal 25% decay running even with no visible rival. The old own-unit question
remains unnumbered because the baseline may be intentional smoothing/prior behavior.

m_aeBestTechs was also sampled. It is rebuilt by every synchronous AI_bestTech search and
is consumed only as a soft percentile modifier in AI_techTradeVal. No sufficiently strict
event-driven freshness contract / hard same-turn contradiction has yet survived; keep it
as a control unless a stronger producer is found.

F514 / KI#837 remains UNUSED.

----
1. Continue the persistent CvPlayerAI member inventory under F514 UNUSED:
   - finish m_eVictoryStageHash lifetime vs post-snapshot team/player mutations;
   - inspect m_bWasFinancialTrouble / m_iTurnLastProductionDirty only for distinct stale
     state not already owned by F364/F499/F502;
   - inspect remaining relationship and unit-role caches with explicit mutator contracts.
2. Treat one-turn heuristic sampling as intentional unless an optimization/refactor changed
   former live semantics or a same-turn producer/consumer contract proves otherwise.
3. Resume Queue 004 CvPlayer.cpp cross-object mutator sweep once the remaining player-AI
   persistent members are exhausted.

F514 / KI#837 -- K-Mod practical 170 reversed strategy/victory cache update order, so Conquest staging uses the previous strategy hash even though current CRUSH is computed moments later
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT / CURRENT ORDER
--------------------
Current AdvCiv-SAS eagerly rebuilds both the victory-stage hash and the ordinary strategy
hash during player activation:

    CvPlayer::setTurnActive(true)
        -> CvPlayerAI::AI_updateCacheData()
            -> AI_calculateAverages()
            -> AI_updateVictoryStageHash()
            -> AI_updateStrategyHash()
            -> ...

The order matters because current Conquest staging has a live dependency on the ordinary
strategy hash:

    CvPlayerAI::AI_calculateConquestVictoryStage()
        ...
        iValue += (iDoWs > 1 || AI_isDoStrategy(AI_STRATEGY_CRUSH) ? 10 : 0);

`AI_isDoStrategy` is not lazy in current AdvCiv/SAS; it reads the stored `m_eStrategyHash`.
Consequently the Conquest calculation in `AI_updateVictoryStageHash()` reads the PREVIOUS
strategy snapshot. Only after the victory hash has been permanently stored for the new turn
does `AI_updateStrategyHash()` compute the current CRUSH state.

This is not merely the unavoidable existence of a dependency cycle. Current AdvCiv explicitly
removed the opposite Conquest3 -> CRUSH edge:

    /* Not clear that conq3 should make the AI more willing to neglect
       its defense. Also, once crush is adopted, the AI becomes more inclined
       towards conquest; should only work one way. */
    /* if (AI_atVictoryStage(AI_VICTORY_CONQUEST3))
           iCrushValue += 1; */

The remaining intended one-way edge is therefore CRUSH -> Conquest. The current update order
makes precisely that live edge one turn late.

HISTORY / EXACT REGRESSION BOUNDARY
-----------------------------------
This ordering was changed by a K-Mod cache refactor, and the reachable history lets the
regression be identified unusually precisely.

Before practical 170, after K-Mod had already replaced the old lazy getters with explicit
update functions, `CvPlayerAI::AI_doTurnPre()` ran:

    AI_calculateAverages();
    AI_updateStrategyHash();
    AI_updateVictoryStrategyHash();
    AI_updateGoldToUpgradeAllUnits();

Thus the rewritten K-Mod Conquest-stage calculation saw the strategy hash freshly computed
for that same player turn.

K-Mod practical 170 / commit `8bd260f741645fd4b5410e7470519f7a56be5ecb`, titled:

    "Cache data is now updated when player is initialized, and when turn becomes active..."

moved the cache work out of `AI_doTurnPre()` into `updateCacheData()`. In THE SAME DIFF it
removed the old:

    AI_updateStrategyHash();
    AI_updateVictoryStrategyHash();

order and introduced:

    AI_updateVictoryStrategyHash();
    if (!isHuman())
        AI_updateStrategyHash();

The refactor therefore reversed the semantic dependency order while relocating the work.
Final K-Mod 1.46 retains victory-before-strategy. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the
same order (`AI_updateVictoryStageHash()` followed by `AI_updateStrategyHash()`).

K-Mod's Conquest-victory function is itself explicitly marked "completely rewritten for
K-Mod" and contains the CRUSH +10 dependency. Civ4CE/BtS does not contain this K-Mod
victory-stage/cache architecture. Classification: K-Mod practical-170 cache-refactor
ordering regression, inherited by AdvCiv and SAS.

CURRENT NORMAL-GAME NUMERIC WITNESS
-----------------------------------
A current-data fixture can make BOTH transitions land exactly on their thresholds without
using F510's war-plan-transition invalidation root.

Use Shaka in the Classical era with:

- current XML Conquest victory weight = 60;
- current Military flavor = 10;
- UWAI enabled, so the old Dagger branch is suppressed by `bNoDagger`;
- exactly one close known potential enemy under `WARPLAN_PREPARING_TOTAL`;
- nonnegative war success (so the `min(0, warSuccess/15)` term contributes 0);
- the target still using Archer as its typical city defender;
- Shaka finishing Construction during the PREVIOUS player turn;
- a reachable stored strategy-rand value such as 578 in the Classical-era shifts.

For that legal random value, the current generator yields simultaneously:

    AI_getStrategyRand(4)  % 100 = 40    // Conquest random
    AI_getStrategyRand(13) % 9   = 5     // CRUSH random, Military flavor 10

The one Preparing Total plan contributes 6 in K-Mod's CRUSH logic, halved by AdvCiv to +3.

Before Construction was completed, both Shaka and the selected rival can use Archer as their
typical city defender. Current Archer data is strength 2, 1 first strike, 1 chance first
strike, so the CRUSH defender-advantage test:

    100 * ourTypicalDefence >= 110 * rivalTypicalDefence

is false when the two typical defenders are equal. The correct pre-Construction CRUSH score
is therefore:

    random 5 + Preparing Total 3 = 8 < 10  -> CRUSH false

Construction completes only later in that previous turn, after that turn's strategy snapshot.
Current Longbowman data is:

    strength 4
    first strikes 1
    chance first strikes 1
    prereq TECH_CONSTRUCTION
    no resource prerequisite
    UNITAI_CITY_DEFENSE enabled

so on the next activation `getTypicalUnitValue(UNITAI_CITY_DEFENSE)` can jump from Archer to
Longbowman. Because Archer and Longbow have the same first-strike profile while Longbow has
double base strength, the 110% comparison is now comfortably true and contributes +2:

    random 5 + Preparing Total 3 + defender advantage 2 = 10  -> CRUSH true

This is an ordinary between-turn tech/trainability input to the strategy calculation. It does
not depend on F510's same-turn `AI_setWarPlan` invalidation omission; the war plan can already
exist throughout both turns.

CONQUEST STAGE FLIP
-------------------
Use three alive major civ teams, all relevant rivals known, no conquered rivals, exactly one
DECLARED_WAR memory for Shaka, and ordinary strength/attitude values chosen so that:

- Shaka is top-ranked in power but not >2x average rival power;
- `bVeryStrong`, `bWarmonger`, `bHateful` and both -30 penalties are false;
- `bTopRank` is true;
- `iDoWs == 1` (enough for the level-1 readiness condition, but NOT enough for the separate
  `iDoWs > 1` +10 shortcut).

Then the Conquest-interest value is:

    personality / redistributed Conquest weight  60
    strategy random                              +40
    ------------------------------------------------
    without current CRUSH                        100
    with current CRUSH                           110

With more than two alive civ teams, the current entry gate returns stage 0 when `iValue < 110`.
At 110 it proceeds. The level-1 readiness condition succeeds because `iDoWs > 0` and
`bTopRank` is true, while the level-2 condition can remain false. Therefore:

    previous/stale CRUSH=false -> Conquest stage 0
    correct current CRUSH=true -> Conquest stage 1

Current cache order nevertheless executes:

    AI_updateVictoryStageHash()
        -> Conquest sees stale CRUSH=false
        -> stores Conquest0
    AI_updateStrategyHash()
        -> now correctly computes CRUSH=true

The player thus begins the rest of its turn in a self-inconsistent state: current strategy
says CRUSH while the stored Conquest stage was just computed as though CRUSH were false.

SAME-TURN GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCES
-------------------------------
The stale victory stage is consumed immediately before any next-turn refresh can rescue it.

1. Research valuation
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
`AI_doTurnPre()` runs `AI_doResearch()` after activation cache setup. `AI_techUnitValue()`
boosts military unit value when Conquest stage 1 (or Domination stage 2) is active:

    iMultiplier = 100;
    if (AI_atVictoryStage(AI_VICTORY_CONQUEST1 | AI_VICTORY_DOMINATION2) || ...)
        iMultiplier += 25;
    ...
    iMilitaryValue *= iMultiplier;
    iMilitaryValue /= 100;

Holding the other strategy gates neutral, the stale Conquest0 therefore values the military
portion of candidate technologies at 100% where the correct Conquest1 state values it at 125%.
This can alter the technology selected in the same `AI_doResearch()` pass.

2. City military-production spending cap
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Later same-turn city production calls `AI_maxUnitCostPerMil()`. Current code adds:

    if (AI_atVictoryStage(AI_VICTORY_CONQUEST4))
        iMaxUnitSpending += 30;
    else if (AI_atVictoryStage(AI_VICTORY_MILITARY3))
        iMaxUnitSpending += 20;
    else if (AI_atVictoryStage(AI_VICTORY_CONQUEST1))
        iMaxUnitSpending += 10;

Let all other terms produce a baseline cap M. Then:

    stale Conquest0 cap   = M
    correct Conquest1 cap = M + 10

City production contains hard gates such as:

    if (!bUnitExempt && iUnitSpending < iMaxUnitSpending + 5)
        ... choose floating defender ...

For an ordinary funding state `iUnitSpending = M + 7`, the stale stage fails this gate while
the correct Conquest1 state passes it (`M+7 < M+15`). Thus the order bug can directly suppress
a military build that the current strategy/victory state is meant to permit.

The same Conquest-stage bit has many additional AI consumers, but these two are enough to show
that the mismatch is live gameplay state rather than logging/UI drift.

---------------------------
Full album and current Known-Issues searches for victory/strategy update ordering, stale
Conquest stages, `AI_updateVictoryStageHash`, `AI_updateVictoryStrategyHash`, CRUSH->Conquest,
and K-Mod cache ordering found no existing numbered root for this reversal.

Nearby findings are distinct:

- F510 / KI#833: a WAR-PLAN MUTATION occurs AFTER an already-computed strategy hash and does
  not invalidate that strategy hash. F514 reproduces with the war plan already present and
  changes CRUSH through Construction/typical-defender trainability. Even a complete F510
  `AI_setWarPlan` invalidation repair therefore leaves F514 intact.
- F511 / KI#834: team diplomacy counters/attitude become fresh after strategy snapshot while
  stale Dagger is used by `AI_doWar`.
- F512 / KI#835: AdvCiv cached loneliness is refreshed after strategy snapshot, leaving flavor-
  dependent strategy stale.
- F373 / KI#696: SAS-local Culture competing-victory logic was evaluated before Diplomacy was
  inserted into the victory hash. Current SAS has already repaired that specific intra-victory
  ordering by calculating Diplomacy before Culture. It does not address victory-vs-strategy
  order.
- Earlier Queue-001 strategy/victory controls audited formula content, disabled defines and
  individual stage behavior; they did not identify the K-Mod170 order reversal.

REPAIR BOUNDARY / CAUTION
-------------------------
The required invariant for the live CRUSH -> Conquest dependency is:

    the Conquest victory stage stored for a player turn must be based on that turn's current
    CRUSH state, not the previous strategy snapshot.

The most historically conservative repair is to restore K-Mod's pre-practical-170 order:

    AI_updateStrategyHash();
    AI_updateVictoryStageHash();

That directly restores the semantics that existed immediately before the cache relocation and
matches AdvCiv's own comment that CRUSH should influence Conquest, not vice versa.

However, strategy calculations also read some victory-stage bits (Culture2 gates Dagger;
Conquest4/Space4 contribute to Production/Final-War logic). Therefore do NOT blindly reorder
without regression-testing those dependencies. The two hashes form a partially cyclic heuristic
system. A two-pass or explicitly staged dependency design may be preferable if current-turn
freshness is desired on both sides.

At minimum, any repair must preserve the intentional one-way `advc.018` relationship and prove
that the final stored victory hash no longer reads a previous-turn CRUSH bit.

This reinforces the caution already recorded in WIP259: victory and strategy have multiple
cross-dependencies, so a repair must make the intended dependency staging explicit rather
than treating one CRUSH symptom in isolation.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F515 / KI#838 -- CONFIRMED
INHERITED BTS CITY-SITE CACHE SURVIVES CONSUMPTION BY CITY FOUNDING
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_doTurnUnitsPre()` rebuilds the player's persistent city-site list once before
any unit moves:

    AI_updateFoundValues();

`AI_updateFoundValues()` clears/rebuilds `m_aeAICitySites` (BtS/K-Mod name:
`m_aiAICitySites`) from the currently legal/revealed found-value landscape. The list is then
read throughout the unit phase and later player/city AI.

An ordinary Settler can consume one of those cached sites during that same unit phase:

    CvUnit::found()
        -> CvPlayer::found(x, y)
        -> initCity(...)
        -> Settler kill(true)

But neither `CvUnit::found`, `CvPlayer::found`, city initialization, nor the normal plot-owner /
city-placement path calls:

    AI_invalidateCitySites(...)
    AI_updateFoundValues(...)
    AI_recalculateFoundValues(...)

for this transition. Source-wide current call-site enumeration leaves ordinary refreshes at
unit-pre (plus setup/Advanced-Start/special first-city paths); there is no post-founding
ordinary refresh.

The cached vector therefore continues to contain the just-consumed city plot. Its stored
FoundValue also remains the pre-founding value; ordinary founding contains no `setFoundValue`
or surrounding found-value recalculation hook.

This is a semantic cache-invalidation defect, not merely an old coordinate that later code
always validates dynamically. The raw vector count/value is itself consumed directly.

CLEAN CURRENT-SAS 1 -> 0 SITE WITNESS
-------------------------------------
Use an ordinary AI empire with:

- one currently legal/high-value site S in the relevant land area;
- one existing Settler able to found S during the unit phase;
- no other valid land or water city site after S is founded;
- no financial trouble / defensive emergency needed for the normal expansion branch.

At `AI_doTurnUnitsPre()`:

    m_aeAICitySites = { S }
    AI_getNumAreaCitySites(...) = 1

The Settler then founds S. Correct post-founding expansion state is:

    valid city sites = 0
    existing Settlers = 0          // founding Settler has died

but the cache remains:

    m_aeAICitySites = { S }
    cached area-site count = 1
    S FoundValue = old high value

Suppose the empire had one city before founding S. It now has two. Later same-turn
`CvCityAI::AI_chooseProduction()` computes:

    iNumAreaCitySites = 1                  // stale; correct 0
    iNumSettlers = 0
    iMaxSettlers = min((iNumCities + 1)/2,
                       iNumAreaCitySites + iNumWaterAreaCitySites)
                 = min((2 + 1)/2, 1)
                 = 1

Thus the expansion logic sees room for another Settler although the cached site's very
purpose has just been consumed and the correct maximum is zero.

CURRENT SAS'S EXTRA SETTLER SAFETY GATE DOES NOT SELF-HEAL
-----------------------------------------------------------
SAS added `SAS_getSettlerBuildSiteStatus` / `SAS_isSettlerBuildWorthwhile` as an additional
production-side safeguard. That is useful generally but cannot rescue this lifetime defect,
because it trusts the SAME persistent data:

    AI_getNumAreaCitySites(...)
    AI_getNumAdjacentAreaCitySites(...)
    AI_getCitySite(...).getFoundValue(...)

It does not re-check `canFound()` for every stored entry. Because the consumed plot S still
has its old positive FoundValue and remains in the vector, the helper can report a valid/high-
value build site even though S now contains the newly founded city and no real site remains.

The stale state therefore reaches both inherited K-Mod expansion logic and SAS's newer
anti-bad-Settler production gate.

OTHER LIVE SAME-ROOT CONSUMERS
------------------------------
The stale site is not limited to the `iMaxSettlers` calculation. Current same-turn consumers
include, among others:

- `AI_getNumCitySites()` / `AI_getNumAreaCitySites()` expansion and Settler-production gates;
- `AI_calculateSettlerPriority` inputs;
- Settler-sea transport demand / overseas-site counts;
- the early `AI_chooseProduction` rule that keeps food-production Settlers when
  `AI_getNumCitySites() > 0`;
- expansion-related building-value and chop heuristics that ask whether area/city sites
  remain;
- unit/city-site helper code that iterates the vector directly.

Settler movement itself often performs a fresh `canFound`/path/mission legality check, so this
finding does NOT claim that a later Settler must literally found on top of the new city. The
confirmed bug is that non-validating count/value consumers continue to treat the consumed
site as available and can consequently make wrong production/expansion decisions.

TURN-ORDER / REAL CONSUMER PROOF
--------------------------------
This survives the normal sequential AI turn architecture.

BtS, K-Mod, Base AdvCiv and current SAS all run unit actions while the player turn is active:

    setTurnActive(true)
        -> doTurnUnits()
            -> AI_doTurnUnitsPre()
            -> Settler can found city

The sequential player's `doTurn()` is then performed when its turn ends. That function runs
AI turn-pre and subsequently each city `doTurn`, where production can be reconsidered. Hence
the stale site vector created by unit-phase founding has a normal later same-turn consumer;
it is not necessarily overwritten first.

ANCESTRY
--------
Civ4CE/BtS already has all essential pieces:

- persistent `m_aiAICitySites`;
- `AI_doTurnUnitsPre()` calls `AI_updateFoundValues()` once before unit movement;
- `CvPlayer::found()` does not invalidate/rebuild that list;
- `CvCityAI` uses cached area-site counts in expansion/Settler logic;
- sequential turn activation runs units before the end-turn player/city processing.

K-Mod preserves that architecture and makes the raw site-count impact especially explicit via
its `iMaxSettlers = min((numCities+1)/2, numAreaSites+numWaterSites)` logic. K-Mod also changes
the site invalidation implementation, but does not add a founding hook.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same lifecycle. Current SAS retains it and adds stronger Settler
production gates that still consume the same cached vector/value.

Classification: inherited BtS city-site cache invalidation defect; K-Mod/AdvCiv/SAS retain
and expose concrete production consequences.

DUPLICATE / CONTROL CHECK
-------------------------
Full album and current Known-Issues searches for `m_aeAICitySites`, `m_aiAICitySites`,
`AI_updateFoundValues`, stale/consumed city sites, Settler-site counts and `iMaxSettlers`
found no existing numbered root for a JUST-FOUNDED own city failing to invalidate the
persistent site list.

Nearby material is distinct:

- F385 concerns duplicate guard missions to a PLANNED future city site.
- F513 concerns AdvCiv's cached *needed Explorer count* becoming stale after exploration.
- the many CitySiteEvaluator findings concern how FoundValue is CALCULATED, not failure to
  invalidate a site after it is consumed by founding.
- KI#180/KI#181/KI#185 and related SAS Settler work change selection/quality/production policy;
  they do not add a general post-founding city-site-cache refresh.
- the old `CvArea::m_aiBestFoundValue` control self-heals at the next unit-pre recomputation;
  F515 specifically proves consumers in the interval after the unit-pre rebuild and before
  that next refresh.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Required invariant:

    once a city is founded, no later consumer may continue to count the founded plot (or
    nearby now-invalidated/reranked plots) as an available cached city site.

Simply erasing S from `m_aeAICitySites` would fix the narrow 1->0 stale coordinate but is not
fully equivalent to recomputation: a new city changes `canFound` spacing, ownership/culture,
city-count-dependent found valuation and rankings of nearby sites. Clearing the whole vector
would avoid false-positive expansion but can create a false-negative until the next turn.

The robust direction is therefore an event-driven found-value/site refresh for the founding
player after the new city has been fully established (or an equivalent targeted invalidation
that also recomputes all affected candidates). `AI_updateFoundValues()` is expensive, but city
founding is rare enough that correctness may justify the event cost; the exact safe hook should
be tested because calling too early during `initCity` could observe partially initialized city /
plot state.

Regression tests should include:

1. one cached site -> found it -> zero legal sites -> no new Settler demand later that turn;
2. multiple nearby cached sites -> founding one invalidates/reranks overlapping candidates;
3. overseas/adjacent-area site counts and Settler-sea demand;
4. ordinary BtS/K-Mod-style expansion logic and current SAS minimum-found-value gate;
5. simultaneous/network-turn behavior, where event-driven invalidation is preferable to
   relying on turn-boundary refresh ordering.

----------------

   sites; absorb only transitions sharing the same `m_aeAICitySites` invalidation root.
2. Continue remaining persistent CvPlayerAI members / relationship caches after the city-site
   vector is exhausted.
3. Resume Queue 004 `CvPlayer.cpp` cross-object mutator/derived-cache sweep with the same
   source -> stored dependency -> invalidator -> consumer method.
