C031-WIP261 APPEND -- 2026-09-03 -- F515 city-removal boundary / F516 persistent-cache continuation
================================================================================

F515 SIBLING / CITY-REMOVAL BOUNDARY
------------------------------------
The first post-WIP260 boundary check broadens F515 slightly, but does NOT spend F516.

A city razed during the active AI's unit phase is another producer of the SAME persistent
`m_aeAICitySites` / FoundValue lifetime root already proved by F515.

Normal sequential ordering is:

    setTurnActive(true)
        -> doTurnUnits()
            -> AI_doTurnUnitsPre()
                -> AI_updateFoundValues()          // city-site vector rebuilt here
            -> selection groups act
                -> attacker captures city
                    -> CvUnit::setXY / conquest path
                        -> acquireCity(...)
                            -> AI_conquerCity(...)
                                -> raze/disband city
            -> later groups may still act
        ...
        -> player doTurn() / later same-turn production consumers

`AI_updateFoundValues()` has no city-raze/acquisition event hook; its ordinary runtime rebuild
is the single pre-unit call. Therefore, if an enemy city had blocked otherwise attractive
settlement locations, capturing and razing that city can make those plots newly legal after
`m_aeAICitySites` was already built. The cached vector cannot discover those newly legal sites
until the next rebuild. A later Settler group in the same unit phase, or later expansion /
production logic in the same player turn, can consequently see a false-negative "no site" or
an obsolete ranking.

This is the mirror image of F515's founding witness:

- founding can leave a consumed / newly invalid site falsely PRESENT;
- razing can leave newly legal / newly valuable sites falsely ABSENT.

Both are repaired by the same invariant: city-topology changes after the pre-unit FoundValue
snapshot must invalidate or refresh the affected player city-site state before later consumers.
Accordingly this is an F515 scope addendum, not F516.

CITY ACQUISITION WITHOUT RAZING -- CONTROL
-----------------------------------------
Keeping a captured city does not provide an equally clean city-spacing witness because the
city already existed on that plot before ownership changed. Acquisition/cession can still
change ownership, culture, FoundValue and candidate ranking nearby, so an event-driven F515
repair should treat ownership changes conservatively; however, this pass does not promote a
separate hard bug solely from kept-city reranking.

The strong same-turn proof is city REMOVAL by razing, where actual canFound legality can change
from false to true after the vector snapshot.

----------------------------------------

Initial controls from the current pass:

- `m_aiVictoryWeights` has explicit refreshes at player initialization, game finalization,
  `CvGame::setVictoryValid`, and `AI_setHuman`; no missing ordinary mutable dependency has yet
  survived.
- `m_GreatPersonWeights` is explicitly a sampled heuristic cache (updated one turn in three),
  so ordinary between-sample changes are not by themselves an invalidation defect.
- the religion / favorite-civic / bonus-trade relationship counters are persistent state, not
  derived caches. Their ordinary end-turn mutation is followed by a full own-attitude refresh
  through `AI_updateExpansionistHate() -> AI_updateAttitude()` before `AI_doDiplo()`; no new
  attitude-cache root is claimed from that path.
- `m_aiNumTrainAIUnits` / `m_aiNumAIUnits` are event-maintained counts and remain to be checked
  specifically at unit ownership / AI-role transition boundaries rather than treated as sampled
  cache data.

WIP262 CONTINUATION -- PERSISTENT PLAYER UNIT-ROLE COUNTS CONTROL
================================================================================

Status entering this tranche:
- Queue 004 CvPlayer.cpp OPEN.
- 32/169 unique files complete.
- F446-F515 confirmed.
- F516 / KI#839 UNUSED.
- No repository source modified.

m_aiNumAIUnits / m_aiNumTrainAIUnits lifetime audit -- CONTROL, no new finding:

1. Live-unit role counts are event-maintained at all normal structural transitions.
   - CvUnitAI::finalizeInit increments both the owning player's m_aiNumAIUnits role and the area's corresponding count.
   - CvUnitAI::AI_setUnitAIType decrements the old player/area role, changes m_eUnitAIType, then increments the new role.
   - CvUnit::setXY maintains area-role counts when a unit moves between areas.
   - CvUnit::kill(false) decrements the owning player's AI role before removing the unit.
   - CvPlayer::initUnit normalizes NO_UNITAI to the unit's default AI before initialization, so ordinary initialized units do not enter the count under an undefined role.

2. Upgrade looked briefly suspicious but closes as a transient internal state, not an escaped stale-count defect.
   - CvUnit::upgrade creates the replacement first through initUnit, so the replacement increments the same player/role count before CvUnit::convert calls kill(true) on the old unit.
   - kill(true) only marks delayed death and returns before the old count is decremented, therefore old+replacement are temporarily both represented.
   - Crucially, the normal AI caller CvUnitAI::AI_upgrade immediately calls doDelayedDeath() on the old unit directly after upgrade(). For a non-fighting upgrade this executes kill(false), removes the old count, and only then does AI_upgrade continue with post-upgrade grouping logic / return to CvPlayerAI::AI_doTurnUnitsPost.
   - Human COMMAND_UPGRADE / gift command handling also ends CvUnit::doCommand with getGroup()->doDelayedDeath().
   - I found no AI decision consumer in the tiny replacement-init -> old-doDelayedDeath interval. Therefore the temporary double count is an implementation detail, not F516.

3. Gift / ownership transfer follows the same create-new / delayed-remove pattern, with the new unit initialized for the recipient and the old unit later removed from the donor. The ordinary command path performs delayed-death cleanup before returning. No persistent cross-owner count drift was found.

4. Queued-training counts are similarly balanced.
   - CvCity::pushOrder(ORDER_TRAIN) increments city-area getNumTrainAIUnits and owner AI_changeNumTrainAIUnits for the order's UnitAI.
   - CvCity::popOrder decrements both before removing/completing the order.
   - queued-unit automatic upgrade adjusts the old and replacement UnitAI counters when the old role is no longer valid.
   - CvCity::kill calls clearOrderQueue(), which repeatedly popOrder()s queued orders, so conquest/raze/city transfer does not strand the former owner's queued UnitAI counts.

Conclusion:
The persistent unit-role count family is tightly event-maintained and the one apparent upgrade double-count window is synchronously closed by AI_upgrade/doDelayedDeath before a relevant consumer. Do not spend F516 here.

Next:
- relationship/value mutators whose stored counters feed cached attitude or diplomacy;
- distinguish mutators that adjust m_aiAttitude incrementally from annual counters deliberately refreshed later in AI_doTurnPost;
- then return to remaining CvPlayerAI persistent members / CvPlayer.cpp sweep.

Durable state after WIP262:

RELATIONSHIP / VALUE MUTATOR CONTROLS

- AI_setMemoryCount measures the memory-attitude delta and applies AI_changeCachedAttitude.
- same/different-religion, favorite-civic and bonus-trade annual counters are changed during
  the team counter phase and followed by the normal full attitude refresh before war/diplo.

LIVE F516 CANDIDATE -- CLOSE-BORDER SUBCACHE AFTER LATE BORDER-GEOGRAPHY CHANGE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS has a sharper cross-object lifetime mismatch:

1. At the beginning of the team's active turn, CvTeamAI::AI_doTurnPost refreshes every member's
   m_aiCloseBordersAttitude and then the full m_aiAttitude.
2. The player later reaches CvPlayer::doTurn. Each CvCity::doTurn executes doCulture() and
   doPlotCultureTimes100(...), which can change plot culture / ownership and therefore the live
   close-border geometry.
3. There is no generic city-culture / plot-ownership invalidation hook among the current
   AI_updateCloseBorderAttitude call sites. The visible refresh sites are the team-turn sweep
   plus special war-state / vassal paths.
4. CvPlayerAI::AI_doTurnPost then reaches AI_updateExpansionistHate() / AI_updateAttitude and
   AI_doDiplo(), but the full attitude rebuild does NOT recompute the close-border subcache. It
   simply reads AI_getCloseBordersAttitude(), i.e. the already-stored m_aiCloseBordersAttitude.

Therefore the apparent late full-attitude refresh is not a repair when border geography itself
changed after the team snapshot: it can rebuild m_aiAttitude from a stale subcomponent and
AI_doDiplo immediately consumes that stale result.

NORMAL NUMERIC GEOMETRY WITNESS UNDER CONSTRUCTION
---------------------------------------------------
Current Genghis has iCloseBordersAttitudeChange = -4. On a Standard map, target city count is 5.
For a small player with total land 5, the close-border land factor is clamped to 1, making the
adjacent-land weight 5.

A clean threshold is therefore adjacent foreign-team land 5 -> 6:
- at 5, the special adjacent-land contribution is absent because the code requires > 5;
- at 6, it contributes +30 percentage points;
- with Genghis's -4 close-border limit, that is enough to change the component by -1.

Thus a cached raw attitude of exactly +4 (Pleased) can correctly become +3 (Cautious) after one
ordinary culture-driven ownership/adjacency transition, while the stored subcache still says 0
and the late full-cache rebuild incorrectly preserves Pleased.

A first multi-member-team sibling also survives structurally: because the team-wide close-border
refresh runs only once, a first member's later cultural border change can leave stale member
attitudes for a later teammate's eager strategy snapshot. The later teammate's Dagger gate can
therefore use a stale team-averaged Pleased/Cautious category. This remains secondary until the
simpler single-member diplomacy consumer is fully proved.

ANCESTRY STATUS -- NOT YET CLASSIFIED
--------------------------------------
K-Mod definitely contains the lifetime mismatch: it moved close-border attitude maintenance to
an eager team-turn refresh, before subsequent player city turns, and does not generically refresh
it after culture changes.

BtS already has a lazy m_aiCloseBordersAttitudeCache and invalidates it in AI_doTurnPre before
city turns. The unresolved ancestry question is whether an ordinary/reachable pre-city consumer
repopulates that lazy cache after invalidation but before city culture changes. If so, the root is
BtS-inherited; if not, K-Mod's eager team snapshot is the regression boundary.

C031-WIP264 -- F516 CONFIRMED: LATE BORDER-GEOGRAPHY CHANGES LEAVE CLOSE-BORDER ATTITUDE STALE

F516 / KI#839 -- BtS-inherited close-border attitude cache is not invalidated/refreshed after same-turn culture / plot-ownership changes, so later diplomacy and strategy consumers can use an obsolete attitude category
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

CURRENT SAS PRODUCER / CONSUMER ORDER
-------------------------------------
Current sequential SAS has a deterministic stale window.

At activation, the team leader executes the team turn. CvTeamAI::AI_doTurnPost refreshes each
member in this order:

    AI_updateCloseBorderAttitude();
    AI_updateAttitude();
    ...
    AI_doWar();

The active player's units then act. At deactivation, CvPlayer::doTurn runs. Its relevant order is:

    AI_doTurnPre();
    ...
    for each city:
        CvCity::doTurn()
            AI_doTurn();
            doGrowth();
            doCulture();
            doPlotCultureTimes100(...);
            doProduction(...);
    ...
    AI_doTurnPost();
        for each other player:
            other.AI_updateAttitude(getID());
        AI_updateExpansionistHate();
            ...
            AI_updateAttitude();
        AI_doDiplo();

CvPlot::updateCulture can call setOwner(calculateCulturalOwner(...)). Plot-owner/culture code has
no generic close-border-attitude invalidation hook.

The current generic close-border refresh call sites are instead limited to:
- the once-per-team sweep in CvTeamAI::AI_doTurnPost;
- special war-state contested-plot maintenance in CvTeam.cpp;
- a vassal/capitulation-specific CvTeam.cpp path.

Therefore ordinary city culture can change the exact map geometry from which
m_aiCloseBordersAttitude is derived after that cache was snapshotted and before AI_doDiplo.

WHY THE LATE FULL-ATTITUDE REFRESH DOES NOT REPAIR IT
-----------------------------------------------------
Current AI_updateExpansionistHate ends by calling AI_updateAttitude(), but AI_updateAttitude does
not calculate close borders from the map. It simply adds:

    AI_getCloseBordersAttitude(ePlayer)

and current AI_getCloseBordersAttitude is a direct return of stored m_aiCloseBordersAttitude.
Thus the late full-attitude rebuild can faithfully rebuild m_aiAttitude from an already stale
subcache and preserve the wrong category immediately before diplomacy.

CURRENT NUMERIC / GEOMETRIC WITNESS
-----------------------------------
Current Genghis Khan has:

    iCloseBordersAttitudeChange = -4

Current Standard world has:

    iTargetNumCities = 5

For a Genghis player with 5 total land tiles, AdvCiv's close-border land factor is clamped to 1,
so the adjacent-land weight remains 5. The adjacent-land contribution is only applied when
AI_calculateAdjacentLandPlots(eTheirTeam) > 5.

Use an ordinary same-continent rival for which AI_hasCitiesInPrimaryArea is true and arrange the
other close-border percentage contributions below the first -1 threshold. In the cleanest map
shape, a cultural expansion claims a previously neutral frontier plot and thereby exposes one
additional rival-owned land plot to team adjacency:

    adjacent rival land: 5 -> 6

At 5 there is no adjacency contribution. At 6 the code adds:

    6 * 5 = 30 percentage points

With limit -4, +30% is enough to change the close-border component by -1. The neutral-plot
frontier shape can keep the newly exposed rival plots outside the player's city radius, so the
stolen-radius component need not change at all; more generally any preexisting subtotal below
25% gives the same threshold witness.

Current relation thresholds make raw +4 Pleased and +3 Cautious. Therefore arrange all other
attitude components so the cached pre-culture relation is exactly +4:

    team-turn snapshot: close-border component 0 -> raw +4 -> Pleased
    after culture:      correct close-border -1 -> raw +3 -> Cautious

The late AI_updateAttitude still reads stored close-border 0, so m_aiAttitude remains +4/Pleased.

DIRECT SAME-TURN GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCE
-------------------------------------
Current AI_doDiplo has a concrete state-changing Pleased/Cautious gate in its give-help branch.
For a sufficiently weaker known rival who can receive technology and is not excluded by the
victory/vassal checks, it requires:

    AI_getAttitude(ePlayer) > getNoGiveHelpAttitudeThreshold()

AdvCiv's LEADER_DEFAULTS sets NoGiveHelpAttitudeThreshold = ATTITUDE_CAUTIOUS, and ordinary
leaders such as current Genghis inherit that value when they do not override it.

Choose CONTACT_GIVE_HELP's reachable success roll, contact timer 0, and at least one tradable
technology. Then:

    stale cached Pleased  > Cautious  -> branch is allowed; AI target can receive a real tech gift
    correct live Cautious > Cautious  -> false; the gift branch is forbidden

For an AI recipient, the successful branch reaches implementDeal and actually transfers the
technology in the same player post-turn. This is an immediate state-changing consumer, not a
mere evaluation/scoring difference.

OTHER NORMAL PRODUCERS / SIBLINGS
---------------------------------
Culture is the clean automatic witness, but the dependency boundary is broader. Any event after
the team close-border snapshot that changes territory / border geometry can stale the same
subcache, including suitable city founding, acquisition, razing and plot-ownership transitions.
Those are F516 producers even when another cache family (e.g. F515 city sites) is independently
staled by the same event.

Multi-member teams also extend the window: the team-wide close-border/full-attitude sweep runs
once, then one member can change territory during its own turn before a later teammate activates.
That later teammate can build eager strategy state from the stale team/member attitudes. This is
a sibling consumer of the same close-border invalidation root, not a separate finding.

BTS / K-MOD / ADVCIV ANCESTRY
-----------------------------
This root is BtS-inherited.

BtS already stores a mutable lazy m_aiCloseBordersAttitudeCache. Its normal AI_doTurnPre does:

    AI_invalidateCloseBordersAttitudeCache();
    ...
    AI_doCommerce();
    ...

But the invalidation is before the cities act, not after them. A reachable ordinary pre-city
path repopulates the cache immediately: when espionage commerce is flexible and a met rival is
eligible for espionage weighting, AI_doCommerce calls team AI_getAttitudeVal; the team routine
calls member AI_getAttitudeVal; player attitude calculation calls AI_getCloseBordersAttitude,
which fills the lazy cache.

BtS then runs city doCulture / doPlotCulture, and its CvPlot ownership/culture paths contain no
AI_invalidateCloseBordersAttitudeCache hook. BtS AI_doTurnPost subsequently runs AI_doDiplo, whose
live AI_getAttitude calculation now incorporates the stale already-populated close-border cache.
BtS therefore already permits the same cache-lifetime contradiction.

K-Mod did not originate the dependency, but made it deterministic and longer-lived:

- K-Mod practical 793 / commit bd52939528, "Changed the close-border attitude cache system",
  disables the lazy MAX_INT invalidation scheme and changes close-border attitude into an eager
  stored cache.
- K-Mod practical 804 / commit 8efe75ac36, "Rearranged calls to CvTeam::doTurn to fix a balance
  problem", moves the close-border/full-attitude refresh into CvTeamAI::AI_doTurnPost.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain this K-Mod eager architecture, with AdvCiv adding richer
close-border inputs such as weighted adjacent land but no generic post-geography invalidation.

SEMANTIC DEDUP
--------------
Full album and Known-Issues searches for close-border cache, m_aiCloseBordersAttitude,
AI_updateCloseBorderAttitude, stolen-city-radius and adjacent-land roots found no numbered finding
with this producer/consumer lifetime.

Nearest distinct findings:
- F511 / KI#834: team diplomacy counters/full-attitude refresh occur after the eager strategy
  snapshot, so AI_doWar can consume stale Dagger. F516 instead changes a SUBCACHE INPUT -- border
  geography -- after both close-border and full-attitude caches were refreshed.
- F515 / KI#838: city founding/removal leaves m_aeAICitySites stale. The same city event can be a
  producer for both findings, but the stored object, consumer and repair contract are different.
- F296 / KI#619: annual-deal processing refreshed attitude at the wrong deal-loop boundary; it is
  not a geographic close-border invalidation problem.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The required invariant is:

    before an attitude/diplomacy/strategy consumer relies on close-border attitude, the stored
    close-border component must correspond to the current territory geometry.

A minimal current-turn repair for the direct single-member witness is to refresh the current
AI player's close-border cache after city/territory mutations and before the final full-attitude
refresh / AI_doDiplo.

However, because team territory changes can affect every member's border relation and a later
teammate can activate before the next team-turn sweep, a robust repair should not update only one
player in isolation. Practical safe directions are:

1. refresh affected team-member close-border caches (and then their full attitudes) at a
   post-territory boundary before later same-team consumers; or
2. introduce a true dirty/invalidation contract on plot/city ownership changes and lazily/eagerly
   rebuild close-border + dependent full attitude before consumption.

If strategy remains eagerly cached, any F516-driven attitude correction must also participate in
the strategy invalidation contract established by F511 rather than leaving Dagger/other
attitude-dependent strategy bits frozen.

F516 is therefore CONFIRMED as KI#839.

POST-F516 WORST-ENEMY CONTROL -- CLOSED, NO NEW FINDING
------------------------------------------------------
A first sibling challenge asked whether the full attitude cache could become stale immediately
inside the normal team refresh because AI_updateAttitude runs before AI_updateWorstEnemy, while
AdvCiv rival-pact attitude terms read the current worst enemy.

That apparent order contradiction is explicitly repaired by current CvTeamAI::AI_updateWorstEnemy.
When m_eWorstEnemy changes, the function comments that EnemyPeacetime-driven attitude updates were
still based on the old worst enemy, then reruns AI_updateAttitude(..., false) against every known
rival. Thus a changed worst enemy does not leave the just-computed member attitudes inconsistent.
This family is a useful control and does not spend F517.

LIVE F517 CANDIDATE -- ORDERING ROOT
-----------------------------------
Current sequential AdvCiv/SAS ordering exposes a sharper cache boundary:

    CvPlayer::setTurnActive(true)
        -> AI_updateCacheData()
        -> team leader: GET_TEAM(getTeam()).doTurn()
            -> CvTeamAI::AI_doTurnPre()
                -> team AI_doCounter()
            -> CvTeamAI::AI_doTurnPost()
                -> each member:
                    AI_updateCloseBorderAttitude()
                    AI_updateAttitude()
                -> ...
                -> AI_doWar()
        -> doTurnUnits()

Later, when the player's own doTurn runs, CvPlayerAI::AI_doTurnPre performs:

    AI_doCounter();

    /* K-Mod note: attitude cache is not refreshed here because there are still
       some attitude-affecting changes to come, in CvTeamAI::AI_doCounter. ... */

    AI_updateBonusValue();
    AI_updateCommerceWeights();
    ...
    AI_doResearch();
    AI_doCommerce();
    AI_doMilitary();
    AI_doCivics();
    AI_doReligion();

In the current sequential scheduler, that inherited K-Mod comment no longer describes the actual
order: the team's AI_doCounter and its full member-attitude refresh already happened earlier at
player activation. The later PLAYER AI_doCounter therefore changes attitude inputs after the full
m_aiAttitude snapshot, then immediately enters multiple AI consumers without rebuilding it.

PLAYER COUNTERS THAT MUTATE WITHOUT FULL-ATTITUDE MAINTENANCE

- m_aiBonusTradeCounter;
- m_aiPeacetimeGrantValue;
- m_aiPeacetimeTradeValue.

Their ordinary set/change helpers modify the stored counter/value only; they do not generally

Current AdvCiv later added an advc.001 player-post repair before diplomacy: other players refresh

CLEAN CURRENT-DATA THRESHOLD WITNESS UNDER CONSTRUCTION
-------------------------------------------------------
Genghis Khan is a convenient shipped personality. Current XML inherits:

    iSameReligionAttitudeChange  = +1
    iSameReligionAttitudeDivisor = 10

and Genghis sets:

    iSameReligionAttitudeChangeLimit = 3

For two known major players sharing a state religion, current CvPlayerAI::AI_doCounter calls
AI_changeSameReligionCounter with the team's AI_randomCounterChange(). The helper is explicitly a
2-trial binomial whose legal result includes +1.

Arrange a single-member Genghis team whose already-cached raw attitude toward one rival is exactly
+3 (Cautious) while SameReligionCounter == 9. A supported +1 counter result gives 9 -> 10. Provided
the ordinary ideology-prevalence adjustment leaves at least the first positive step available,
AI_getSameReligionAttitude gains +1 at divisor 10, so the correct live raw attitude becomes +4
(Pleased). The stored m_aiAttitude remains the pre-counter +3/Cautious value.

DIRECT CONSUMER LEAD -- AI_doCommerce ESPIONAGE
------------------------------------------------
The immediately following AI_doCommerce reads team attitude. On a one-member team,
CvTeamAI::AI_getAttitude/AI_getAttitudeVal is directly based on this player's stale m_aiAttitude.
Its espionage loop has a categorical branch:

    if (iTheirEspPoints > iDesiredMissionPoints &&
        kOurTeam.AI_getAttitude(eRival) <= ATTITUDE_CAUTIOUS)
    {
        ...
        iDesiredMissionPoints = max(iTheirEspPoints-adjusted, iDesiredMissionPoints);
    }

Thus the candidate can cross an exact branch boundary:

    stale cache:   raw +3 -> Cautious -> espionage catch-up branch ENTERED
    correct state: raw +4 -> Pleased  -> branch SKIPPED

With no war plan, no preexisting desired mission target, positive rival espionage points and low
own espionage points, the stale branch can create a positive aiTarget where the correct Pleased
state leaves the target at zero. AI_doCommerce then writes per-team espionage spending weights
through setEspionageSpendingWeightAgainstTeam and uses the aggregate target rate when deciding
whether to move commerce from research into espionage. This is a direct same-call AI-state / slider
consumer; exact arithmetic is still being tightened before F517 is spent.

F516, but not this full-attitude snapshot contradiction.

Current classification is therefore likely K-Mod-introduced and inherited by Base AdvCiv 1.14 /
SAS, pending final ancestry wording.

F517 / KI#840 -- K-Mod's player relationship counters advance after the team full-attitude snapshot, so same-turn commerce can act on yesterday's attitude
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT / SCHEDULER CONTRADICTION
------------------------------
F517 is confirmed. In ordinary non-simultaneous turns, current SAS performs the relevant work in
this order for an AI player:

    CvPlayer::setTurnActive(true)
        -> AI_updateCacheData()
        -> team leader: CvTeam::doTurn()
            -> CvTeamAI::AI_doTurnPre()
                -> CvTeamAI::AI_doCounter()
            -> CvTeamAI::AI_doTurnPost()
                -> each member:
                    AI_updateCloseBorderAttitude()
                    AI_updateAttitude()
                -> ...
                -> AI_doWar()
        -> doTurnUnits()

    CvPlayer::setTurnActive(false)
        -> CvPlayer::doTurn()
            -> CvPlayerAI::AI_doTurnPre()
                -> CvPlayerAI::AI_doCounter()
                -> AI_updateCommerceWeights()
                -> ...
                -> AI_doResearch()
                -> AI_doCommerce()
                -> AI_doMilitary()
                -> AI_doCivics()
                -> AI_doReligion()

The K-Mod comment immediately after PLAYER AI_doCounter says attitude is deliberately not refreshed
there because attitude-affecting changes in CvTeamAI::AI_doCounter are "still" to come. Under the
sequential scheduler, that premise is inverted: the TEAM counter pass and full member-attitude
refresh already ran earlier at activation. The PLAYER counter pass therefore mutates relationship
inputs AFTER m_aiAttitude was snapshotted.

The affected ordinary player-state inputs include SameReligionCounter, DifferentReligionCounter,
FavoriteCivicCounter, BonusTradeCounter and the peacetime trade/grant values. Their ordinary
set/change helpers mutate stored state without rebuilding full attitude. Memory changes are not a
blanket example because memory mutators have dedicated cached-attitude delta maintenance.

AdvCiv practical advc.001 later recognizes that player turns occur after the team turn and adds a
late player-post attitude repair before diplomacy. Current AI_doTurnPost refreshes other players'
attitude toward this player and AI_updateExpansionistHate refreshes this player's own full attitude
before AI_doDiplo. That prevents the stale full attitude from necessarily reaching current SAS
post-turn diplomacy, but it occurs only after the research/commerce/military/civic/religion AI
above and therefore does not repair F517's earlier consumers.

CURRENT SHIPPED-DATA +3 -> +4 RELIGION WITNESS
----------------------------------------------
Current Genghis Khan provides a compact ordinary threshold. The inherited leader defaults give:

    iSameReligionAttitudeChange  = +1
    iSameReligionAttitudeDivisor = 10

and Genghis sets:

    iSameReligionAttitudeChangeLimit = 3

Current relation thresholds classify raw +3 as Cautious and raw +4 as Pleased
(RELATIONS_THRESH_PLEASED = 4).

Use a one-member Genghis team and one known rival sharing Genghis's state religion. Arrange the
already-cached attitude subtotal at raw +3 and SameReligionCounter == 9 at activation. Current
player AI_doCounter calls:

    AI_changeSameReligionCounter(ePlayer, kOurTeam.AI_randomCounterChange());

AI_randomCounterChange is explicitly a two-trial binomial and +1 is an ordinary legal result.
Choose that supported result, so the player counter advances 9 -> 10.

The current AdvCiv ideology-prevalence adjustment cannot eliminate Genghis's FIRST positive step
in this fixture. For SAME_RELIGION the positive limit is reduced by at most:

    round(0.5 * ratio * 3)

with ratio <= 1. Even at ratio == 1 this removes at most 2 from limit 3, leaving limit >= 1.
Therefore counter 10 reaches the first divisor and AI_ideologyAttitudeChange adds +1.

The correct live attitude consequently becomes:

    before player counter: raw +3 -> Cautious
    after  player counter: raw +4 -> Pleased

but m_aiAttitude remains the team-turn +3/Cautious snapshot throughout the immediately following
AI_updateCommerceWeights / AI_doResearch / AI_doCommerce sequence.

EXACT AI_doCommerce ESPIONAGE WITNESS
-------------------------------------
AI_doCommerce supplies a direct state-changing consumer with an exact categorical boundary. On a
one-member team, CvTeamAI::AI_getAttitude and AI_getAttitudeVal ultimately read this same player's
stored full-attitude cache.

Inside the no-war-plan espionage loop, current code first obtains:

    int iAttitude = range(kOurTeam.AI_getAttitudeVal(eRival), -12, 12);

and later has:

    if (iTheirEspPoints > iDesiredMissionPoints &&
        kOurTeam.AI_getAttitude(eRival) <= ATTITUDE_CAUTIOUS)
    {
        ... catch-up target calculation ...
    }

Use an ordinary midgame setup with:

    game speed / target turns          = Normal / 4
    no war plan                        = yes
    rival current EP against us        = 360
    our current EP against rival       = 0
    rival espionage points ever        = 360
    our espionage points ever          = 0 (the code floors this total to 4)
    our UNITAI_SPY count               = 0
    rival has no cities in our primary area
    no cheap-tech-steal override       = yes
    gold commerce percent              = 0
    personality espionage weight       = 100 (current Genghis)

With the stale raw +3/Cautious cache:

1. No-war desired mission points stay 0 because the ordinary demographics branch requires
   iAttitude < 3, while stale iAttitude is exactly 3.

2. The base rate divisor is:

       4 target turns * 3 = 12

   The raw-attitude correction is integer 12 / 20 = 0; no spy adds +4; no primary-area cities
   adds +2. Therefore:

       iRateDivisor = 18

3. The Cautious catch-up gate ENTERS. Rival current points are relation-adjusted:

       360 * (34 - 3) / 36
     = 360 * 31 / 36
     = 310

4. With own total floored to 4 and rival total 360, the long-run scaling gives:

       310 * (3*4 + 360) / (2*4 + 4*360)
     = 310 * 372 / 1448
     = 79   (integer result)

5. The stale rival target is therefore:

       aiTarget = (79 - 0) / 18 = 4

   and aggregate iEspionageTargetRate becomes 4.

The rival's initial spending weight is 6, and iAttitude/3 subtracts 1, leaving 5. Because this is
the only positive target:

    aiWeight += 100 * 4 / max(4, 4)
              = 100

so current code stores:

    stale Cautious spending weight = 105

With the CORRECT post-counter raw +4/Pleased state, the catch-up gate is false. There are still no
ordinary desired mission points in this controlled setup, therefore:

    correct aiTarget              = 0
    correct iEspionageTargetRate  = 0
    correct stored spending weight = 5

The stale full-attitude cache thus changes a persistent rival espionage allocation from 5 to 105
in the same AI_doCommerce call.

DIRECT COMMERCE-SLIDER CONSEQUENCE
----------------------------------
The same fixture can make the consequence immediately player-economic rather than only a stored
weight difference. AI_doCommerce controls the espionage slider when research and espionage are
flexible and the player is not in financial trouble, not researching the first technology and not
at Culture-4. Arrange those ordinary conditions, begin with 100% research / 0% espionage, and keep
gold safely above the target check.

For stale Cautious, iEspionageTargetRate == 4 and current espionage commerce rate is 0, so the loop
executes and first performs:

    changeCommercePercent(COMMERCE_RESEARCH,  -10);
    changeCommercePercent(COMMERCE_ESPIONAGE, +10);

The subsequent science-ratio guard does not undo that first step. With 90 research / 10 espionage,
its test is 180 <= 60, false.

For correct Pleased, iEspionageTargetRate == 0, so the loop condition 0 < 0 is false and NO
research-to-espionage step occurs.

Thus the F517 cache-order defect can directly spend 10 percentage points of commerce on espionage
that the live relationship state would not request. This is a same-call state change, not merely a
one-point heuristic approximation.

SIBLING CONSUMERS / SCOPE
-------------------------
AI_updateCommerceWeights also runs immediately after player AI_doCounter and reads team attitude;
it is another same-root consumer. AI_doResearch, AI_doMilitary and other subsequent AI routines
contain additional attitude-sensitive paths. They do not warrant separate numbers: the shared
root is the missing full-attitude synchronization after PLAYER relationship-counter maintenance.

The producer family should likewise not be split by counter type. SameReligionCounter is the clean
numeric witness, while DifferentReligionCounter, FavoriteCivicCounter, BonusTradeCounter and
peacetime trade/grant-value decay are other ways to make the stored full attitude disagree with
its live inputs at the same boundary.

K-MOD ORIGIN / BTS NEGATIVE CONTROL / ADVCIV INHERITANCE
--------------------------------------------------------
This full-attitude-cache root is K-Mod-introduced.

BtS/Civ4CE has the same broad player ordering -- AI_doCounter before AI_doCommerce -- but
CvPlayerAI::AI_getAttitudeVal calculates the complete attitude dynamically from current counters
on every call. It has no K-Mod full m_aiAttitude cache. Therefore the same 9 -> 10 religion-counter
change is visible to the immediately following BtS commerce evaluation. BtS's separate lazy
close-border subcache can be stale under F516, but that does not create F517's full-attitude
snapshot contradiction.

K-Mod 1.46:
- stores full player attitude in m_aiAttitudeCache and AI_getAttitudeVal returns it directly;
- refreshes member close-border/full-attitude caches in CvTeamAI::AI_doTurnPost;
- under sequential turns, invokes CvTeam::doTurn at team-leader ACTIVATION, while player doTurn /
  AI_doTurnPre occurs later when that player is deactivated;
- retains the AI_doTurnPre comment claiming team AI_doCounter is still forthcoming after player
  AI_doCounter, even though the scheduler now does the reverse.

K-Mod's v1.32 changelog explicitly says it rewrote attitude and close-border caches to update only
at explicitly specified times, accepting that cache inaccuracies could otherwise manifest as a
delay rather than OOS; the same v1.32 turn-mechanics work rearranged team-turn timing. In the live
code, the player-counter/full-attitude ordering is therefore a systematic explicit-snapshot
freshness gap rather than BtS dynamic-attitude behavior.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same scheduler, eager full-attitude member refresh and player-pre
counter ordering. Its advc.001 late player-post refresh reduces the lifetime before diplomacy but
does not move the snapshot behind the earlier commerce/research/military consumers. Current SAS
inherits that architecture.

SEMANTIC DEDUP
--------------
Full-album and Known-Issues searches found no existing root with this producer / stored object /
consumer boundary.

Nearest distinct findings:
- F511 / KI#834: TEAM relationship counters and the full attitude cache become current AFTER the
  eager STRATEGY snapshot, so AI_doWar sees fresh attitude but stale Dagger. F517 is the opposite
  cache layer: PLAYER relationship counters change AFTER the full-attitude snapshot, so direct
  player-AI consumers see stale m_aiAttitude itself. Refreshing strategy at F511's team-war
  boundary does not repair F517.
- F516 / KI#839: territory changes stale the close-border SUBCACHE after its refresh. F517 needs no
  geographic mutation; its full-attitude inputs themselves change through the ordinary player
  counter pass.
- F296 / KI#619: annual deal processing refreshed one direction at the wrong deal-loop boundary.
  Different producer and synchronization batch.
- F362 / KI#? BonusTrade ceiling work concerns how high a relationship counter can accumulate;
  F517 remains even when every counter's numerical evolution is otherwise correct.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The required invariant is:

    after CvPlayerAI::AI_doCounter changes relationship components and before any player AI
    consumer reads attitude, m_aiAttitude must represent those new components.

The direct narrow repair is to rebuild the current AI player's full attitude immediately after
AI_doCounter (close-border need not be recomputed merely for religion/civic/trade-counter changes)
before AI_updateCommerceWeights / AI_doResearch / AI_doCommerce.

An architectural alternative is a true full-attitude dirty/lazy contract in which the affected
counter/value mutators mark the relevant relationship dirty and the next consumer rebuilds it.
That is broader but avoids future event-order assumptions.

Do not merely refresh before AI_doDiplo: current AdvCiv already effectively does that and F517's
commerce consequence occurs much earlier. Do not patch only the espionage Cautious gate either;
the stale object is general full attitude and has multiple consumers.

F517 is therefore CONFIRMED as KI#840.

POST-F517 SIBLING BOUNDARY

The immediate sibling sweep does not justify another finding number.

1. `AI_updateCommerceWeights()` is another SAME-ROOT F517 consumer. It executes directly
   after player `AI_doCounter()` and can query team/player attitude while the full attitude
   snapshot still predates the just-advanced player relationship counters. This broadens the
   repair invariant but not the root: F517 should be understood as

       player relationship counters mutate
           -> full `m_aiAttitude` snapshot is not rebuilt
           -> attitude-dependent player AI runs in the same player turn.

   The explicit espionage-spending/slider witness remains the strongest deterministic proof.

   strategy-freshness family (especially F511), not to F518. Repairing the full attitude cache

   attitude. Do not split this cache-layer interaction into another number merely because a

EXPANSIONIST-HATE CACHE -- INTENTIONAL SAMPLED CONTROL
------------------------------------------------------
A cross-player candidate involving `m_arExpansionistHate` was challenged and CLOSED.

At first glance the stored ratio looks vulnerable because it is refreshed only at selected
maintenance points, while later team attitude / war decisions can run before another refresh.
The actual semantic split is important:

- `AI_getExpansionistAttitude(ePlayer)` dynamically rescans the rival's CURRENT revealed
  cities, highest-culture team and culture percentages every time the full attitude value is
  calculated. Thus city founding/capture/culture changes are not hidden behind
  `m_arExpansionistHate`.
- The stored `m_arExpansionistHate` value is only a PERSONAL HOSTILITY MULTIPLIER derived
  primarily from peace-weight/warmonger personality and relative team power.
- Current AdvCiv explicitly documents this as intentional sampling:

      "Can't update the AI attitude cache whenever the power ratio shifts;
       that happens too frequently. Instead cache the expansionist hate ratio,
       and update the cached ratio only at certain times."

- Major city acquisition already triggers global expansionist-hate maintenance for met
  players because it is treated as a major power shift.

Therefore a rival expanding between snapshots is still seen by the next full-attitude
calculation through the live city/culture scan; only the frequently changing power multiplier
is deliberately sampled. No event-driven cache contract comparable to F516/F517 is violated.
Do not spend F518 on this family absent a different producer that contradicts the documented
sampling contract.

F513 SIBLING SCOPE -- SAME `m_neededExplorersByArea` INVALIDATION ROOT
---------------------------------------------------------------------
F513 proved the AdvCiv regression created when dynamic `AI_neededExplorers(area)` was replaced
with an activation snapshot in `m_neededExplorersByArea`, using unit exploration/revelation as
its clean producer. Re-reading `AI_neededExplorers_bulk` shows that MAP REVELATION is not its
only mutable input. The cached result also depends on:

- `getCurrentEra()` through the land divisor `max(150 - 20 * era, 50)`;
- `getNumCities()` through the land/water explorer caps;
- `countCivTeamsAlive()` and the team's current met-civilization count;
- capital existence/location and whether an unmet major rival has a capital in the same land
  area;
- Pangaea classification for the water branch (normally stable during ordinary play).

No additional `AI_updateNeededExplorers()` caller was found for ordinary changes to these
inputs; current SAS still rebuilds the map only from `AI_updateCacheData()` at activation.
Consequently ordinary same-turn changes in these inputs are additional manifestations of F513,
not new cache roots.

Two especially clean siblings are now bounded:

A. ERA CHANGE DURING RESEARCH

`CvTeam::setHasTech` synchronously raises each team member's `CurrentEra` when a newly acquired
tech has a later era. This can happen in the player's `doResearch()` after the activation-time
explorer snapshot but before city turns/production. No explorer-cache rebuild follows.

For example, with one city and exactly 260 unrevealed land tiles:

    Ancient snapshot divisor = 150 -> 260 / 150 = 1
    Classical live divisor   = 130 -> 260 / 130 = 2
    one-city cap             = 2

If the player enters Classical through that research completion, the stored target can remain
1 while the correct current target is 2. Later city production in the same player turn can
therefore suppress an Explorer that the live post-tech state calls for. This is the same
stored object, same missing invalidation contract and same city-production consumer as F513.

B. FIRST CONTACT DURING UNIT MOVEMENT

When the ordinary tile-count term is 0, the land branch can still request one Explorer if the
player has not met all major civilization teams and an unmet rival capital lies in the
player's capital area. A unit can establish first contact after the activation snapshot.
The team then immediately knows that rival, so the live unmet-capital reason can disappear,
but there is no `AI_updateNeededExplorers()` call. Later unit/city consumers can still read the
old target of 1. Again this is F513, not F518.

City-count/capital-area changes from founding/capture/raze are governed by the same principle:
when they change an input to `AI_neededExplorers_bulk` after activation, the stored area target
cannot follow until the next cache rebuild. They should be absorbed into F513 unless a future
case exposes a genuinely different cached object or repair boundary.

F518 LIVE CANDIDATE -- `AI_calculateAverages()` MOVED BEFORE UNIT-PHASE CITY ACQUISITION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The first genuinely different cache family after WIP267 is the empire-average snapshot built
by `CvPlayerAI::AI_calculateAverages()`.

Current SAS activation order is:

    CvPlayer::setTurnActive(true)
        -> AI_updateCacheData()
            -> AI_calculateAverages()
        -> team turn
        -> doTurnUnits()
            -> ordinary AI unit movement / combat / city capture / city founding
        ...
    CvPlayer::doTurn()
        -> AI_doTurnPre()
            -> AI_doResearch()
            -> AI_doCommerce()
        -> doGold()
        -> doResearch()
        -> doEspionagePoints()
        -> city turns

The current average getters are simple stored accessors. No ordinary acquisition/founding
hook calls `AI_calculateAverages()`; in the fresh source the only live ordinary call is the
activation-time call in `AI_updateCacheData()`.

The snapshot contains a WHOLE FAMILY of current-city-set aggregates:

- `m_aiAverageYieldMultiplier`;
- `m_aiAverageCommerceMultiplier`;
- `m_iAverageGreatPeopleMultiplier`;
- `m_aiAverageCommerceExchange`;
- K-Mod `m_iAverageCulturePressure`.

All are recomputed by iterating the player's current cities. A city acquired or founded after
the activation snapshot therefore changes the correct input set while every stored aggregate
continues to describe the pre-unit empire until the next activation. F518, if confirmed, should
own this whole `AI_calculateAverages` city-set lifetime root rather than numbering one finding
per average member.

HISTORY -- EXACT K-MOD RELOCATION BOUNDARY
-----------------------------------------
K-Mod practical 56 / commit `2034aebc356ff90d54dd05effd2610154d5d887c`
introduced the cached average culture-pressure member and a lazy same-game-turn getter.
The commit log explicitly says:

    Average (K-Mod) culture pressure factor is now cached (although it isn't being used yet).

Practical 57 / `cdfa07682c2a7a87a07bb384e21924345ba3f2d4` immediately began using that
average in culture valuation, and practical 103 / `5750806e12638791999cb664ed82602822e05e6b`
added the still-current culture-slider consumer:

    iIdealPercent += (AI_averageCulturePressure() - 100) / 10;
    iIdealPercent = max(iIdealPercent,
            (AI_averageCulturePressure() - 100) / 5);

Practical 165 / `f2c41e4abdd234768bd14062c99c97c7c82a15e5` disabled the lazy getter refreshes
and explicitly called `AI_calculateAverages()` from `AI_doTurnPre()`.

That ordering is significant: under the sequential K-Mod/AdvCiv scheduler,
`AI_doTurnPre()` belongs to the player's later `doTurn()`, after `doTurnUnits()`. Thus a city
captured/founded during the active unit phase was already part of the average snapshot before
later research/commerce consumers.

K-Mod practical 170 / commit `8bd260f741645fd4b5410e7470519f7a56be5ecb`, titled:

    Cache data is now updated when player is initialized, and when turn becomes active.
    (this fixes the problem of cache not being initialized on the first turn, and it also
    fixes the problem of cache data being 1 turn old.)

moved `AI_calculateAverages()` out of `AI_doTurnPre()` into activation-time `updateCacheData()`.
That fixed between-turn age but reversed the city-acquisition freshness boundary: averages now
snapshot the empire BEFORE the unit phase and are consumed AFTER it. Current K-Mod ancestry,
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain this activation-time architecture.

CULTURE-PRESSURE SLIDER WITNESS -- NUMERIC CORE NOW PROVED
----------------------------------------------------------
The strongest deterministic consumer is `AI_doCommerce()`.

Construct a normal sequential AI turn with one pre-existing city A when activation starts:

    city A culture commerce rate = R > 0
    city A `AI_culturePressureFactor()` = 100

Activation stores:

    m_iAverageCulturePressure = 100

During `doTurnUnits()`, the AI recaptures and keeps border city B. `CvPlayer::acquireCity`
preserves city culture; a recapture bypasses the normal conquest building-loss roll; and
occupation is added only when current team city culture is below the inherited
`OCCUPATION_CULTURE_PERCENT_THRESHOLD` (75). Thus a high-own-culture recapture can immediately
be non-disordered and retain ordinary nonzero culture output.

Arrange B to have the same culture commerce rate R and live culture-pressure factor 200.
Then the current correct empire average after acquisition is exactly:

    (R * 100 + R * 200) / (R + R) = 150

but the stored activation snapshot remains 100.

Pressure 200 itself is reachable with ordinary current arithmetic. On a Normal game started
from the first turn, current GameSpeed XML contains exactly 500 turns and
`getEstimateEndTurn()` is initialized to that sum. At game turn 100, one BFC plot with 15%
our culture and 85% culture from a third major rival, with both cultures in range and culture
flipping allowed, contributes:

    foreign share = floor(100 * 85 / (85 + 15)) = 85
    squared        = 7225
    late-game dull = floor(7225 * 500 / (100 + 500)) = 6020
    factor         = 100 + floor(6020 / 60) = 200

All other BFC plots can have zero foreign culture. Using a third rival for the pressure avoids
any `canCultureFlip` exclusion tied to the city's immediate previous owner.

With no angry citizens, no Culture2/3/4 victory-stage bonus and no `AI_avoidScience`, current
`AI_doCommerce()` therefore gives:

    stale pressure 100:
        ideal = max(0 + 0, 0) = 0 -> 0% culture

    correct pressure 150:
        ideal = 0 + 5
        max(5, 10) = 10
        10-point commerce increment keeps 10 -> 10% culture

So the stale activation snapshot can produce an actual 0% instead of 10% culture slider in
that same player turn. `CvPlayer::doTurn()` then immediately executes `doGold()`, `doResearch()`
and `doEspionagePoints()` with that commerce allocation, giving a direct same-turn economic
consequence rather than merely a valuation difference.

Current SAS executes, in an ordinary sequential AI turn:

    CvPlayer::setTurnActive(true)
        -> CvPlayerAI::AI_updateCacheData()
            -> AI_updateNeededExplorers()
            -> AI_calculateAverages()              // snapshots CURRENT city set here

The current getters simply return stored values; their old lazy refresh checks are commented

`AI_updateCacheData()` are player initialization and turn activation. City founding,
acquisition, keeping, razing and ordinary city initialization do not refresh these averages.

The single snapshot contains:

    m_aiAverageYieldMultiplier
    m_aiAverageCommerceMultiplier
    m_iAverageGreatPeopleMultiplier
    m_aiAverageCommerceExchange
    m_iAverageCulturePressure

Each value is derived by iterating the player's current cities (culture pressure uses the

CLEAN CURRENT-SAS NORMAL-GAME WITNESS -- CREATIVE SETTLER FOUNDING
------------------------------------------------------------------
The conquest/recapture witness from WIP268 remains valid as a secondary producer, but current
SAS provides a simpler ordinary founding witness that needs no occupation/building-survival
assumptions.

Current `TRAIT_CREATIVE` has:

    iFreeCityCulture = 10
    CommerceChanges[COMMERCE_CULTURE] = +1

`CvCity::init` calls `initTraitCulture()` for a newly founded city before updating its culture
level. On Normal speed the current Fledgling threshold is exactly 10 culture, so a Creative
new city immediately has the corresponding cultural footprint. The player's +1 free city
culture commerce is also part of the city's base commerce calculation. Ordinary city-yield
initialization updates commerce, so the new city is a real nonzero-culture-rate member before
the later `AI_doCommerce()` pass.

Use a Creative AI on current Normal speed at game turn 100, with Drama or any other current
condition making Culture commerce flexible, not pursuing a Culture2+ victory stage,
`AI_avoidScience()` false and no angry-population culture demand.

At activation it owns only city A, arranged with:

    culture commerce rate = 100 (the Creative +1 alone is sufficient)
    AI_culturePressureFactor(A) = 100

Thus activation stores:

    m_iAverageCulturePressure = 100

During `doTurnUnits()`, a normal Settler founds border city B. B likewise has culture commerce
rate 100 from Creative. Arrange one plot in B's cultural footprint at 15 own / 85 rival plot
culture, with the rival also in culture range, not a vassal, and normal city flipping allowed;
other relevant plots have no rival culture.

Current Normal GameSpeed XML has exactly 500 turns, and `CvGame::init` initializes
`getEstimateEndTurn()` to the sum of those turn increments. At game turn 100 the current
`AI_culturePressureFactor()` integer arithmetic is therefore:

    rival share = floor(100 * 85 / (85 + 15)) = 85
    range/flip divisor = 2, so 85 * 2 / 2 = 85
    squared pressure contribution = 85^2 = 7225
    late-game dulling = floor(7225 * 500 / (100 + 500)) = 6020
    city factor = 100 + floor(6020 / 60) = 200

No malformed map state is needed: the Settler can found on an own/unowned city tile while a
frontier BFC plot already carries strong culture from a neighboring rival. Creative's free
10 culture immediately establishes the new city's current range.

The correct post-founding empire average is now exactly:

    (100 culture-rate * 100 pressure +
     100 culture-rate * 200 pressure) /
    (100 + 100)
      = 150

but the stored activation snapshot remains 100.

DIRECT SAME-TURN SLIDER CONSEQUENCE
-----------------------------------
Current SAS retains K-Mod's `AI_doCommerce()` pressure terms:

    iIdealPercent += (iAverageCulturePressure - 100) / 10;
    iIdealPercent = max(iIdealPercent,
            (iAverageCulturePressure - 100) / 5);

The inherited commerce increment is 10 and current SAS contains no XML override of that BtS
default.

Under the neutral conditions above:

    stale cached pressure 100:
        ideal = 0
        rounded target = 0% Culture

    correct live pressure 150:
        +5 from /10 term
        max(5, 10 from /5 term) = 10
        10-point increment preserves 10
        ordinary cap 20 preserves 10
        target = 10% Culture

This is an actual state mutation, not just a valuation perturbation. `AI_doCommerce()` first
zeros flexible Culture/Espionage and then installs the calculated Culture target. Immediately
after `AI_doTurnPre()`, `CvPlayer::doTurn()` runs `doGold()`, `doResearch()` and
`doEspionagePoints()`, so the stale 0% rather than correct 10% culture allocation changes the
same player's current-turn economy/research allocation as well.

A kept city acquisition is a second producer of the same root and can make the other empire
averages especially different through captured buildings, population, specialists and yield /
commerce modifiers. It does not need its own finding number: all members are populated by the
same `AI_calculateAverages()` snapshot and share the same missing post-unit refresh boundary.

HISTORY / ANCESTRY
------------------
BtS/Civ4CE already contains the shared average cache for yield, commerce, Great-People and
commerce-exchange values. Its getters are lazy per-game-turn caches: when
`m_iAveragesCacheTurn` differs from the current turn, the first getter calls
`AI_calculateAverages()`.

K-Mod practical 56 / `2034aebc356ff90d54dd05effd2610154d5d887c` added
`m_iAverageCulturePressure` to that shared lazy cache. Its log says:

    Average (K-Mod) culture pressure factor is now cached (although it isn't being used yet).

Practical 57 / `cdfa07682c2a7a87a07bb384e21924345ba3f2d4` began using it in Culture
weighting. Practical 103 / `5750806e12638791999cb664ed82602822e05e6b` added the direct
culture-slider terms that current SAS still uses.

Practical 165 / `f2c41e4abdd234768bd14062c99c97c7c82a15e5` disabled the lazy getter refresh
checks and explicitly rebuilt averages in `AI_doTurnPre()`:

    AI_calculateAverages();
    AI_updateStrategyHash();
    AI_updateVictoryStrategyHash();
    AI_updateGoldToUpgradeAllUnits();

K-Mod's sequential player schedule already placed `doTurnUnits()` at activation and ordinary
`CvPlayer::doTurn()` when the player turn deactivates. The initial K-Mod history itself shows
that ordering. Therefore practical 165's explicit average refresh occurred AFTER the AI's unit
moves and same-turn city founding/capture.

Practical 170 / `8bd260f741645fd4b5410e7470519f7a56be5ecb` is titled:

    Cache data is now updated when player is initialized, and when turn becomes active.
    (this fixes the problem of cache not being initialized on the first turn, and it also
    fixes the problem of cache data being 1 turn old.)

The same diff adds `updateCacheData()` at turn activation, puts `AI_calculateAverages()` inside
it, and removes `AI_calculateAverages()` from `AI_doTurnPre()`. This correctly solves
between-turn age / first-turn initialization but creates the current post-unit mutation gap:
the averages are now guaranteed to be from before the active unit phase and are not rebuilt
before later player-AI decisions.

Final K-Mod 1.46, Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS all retain this activation-time average
refresh and the K-Mod culture-slider consumer. Classification for the deterministic current
witness: K-Mod practical-170 cache-relocation regression, inherited by AdvCiv and SAS, on top
of a BtS-origin shared average-cache family plus K-Mod's culture-pressure extension.

SEMANTIC DEDUP
--------------
Album and Known-Issues searches are clear.

- The earlier `AI_doCommerce` SAS-delta control only proved that calling the stored
  `AI_averageCulturePressure()` accessor once and reusing the local value is equivalent to
  calling that same non-refreshing accessor twice. It explicitly did not inspect the lifetime
  of `m_iAverageCulturePressure` itself.
- F499 is stale `m_iAvailableIncome` across an event-driven GPT change and immediate
  `AI_doCommerce`; different stored object, producer and repair boundary.
- F513 is the separate AdvCiv `m_neededExplorersByArea` activation snapshot.
- F514 was also exposed by practical 170 but is an internal cache dependency reversal:
  victory stage is calculated before current strategy. Fixing victory/strategy order leaves
  `AI_calculateAverages()` before units and does not repair F518.
- F515 owns `m_aeAICitySites` / FoundValue invalidation after founding/razing. The same city
  founding can be a producer for both, but the stored object and consumers are independent:
  refreshing FoundValue sites does nothing to current empire averages, and vice versa.
- The earlier UWAI city-set findings concern UWAICache asset/geometry wrappers, not
  `CvPlayerAI` economy-average state.

No existing KI owns this current `AI_calculateAverages` post-unit city-set lifetime root.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Do not merely fix the culture slider locally; that would leave the other members from
`AI_calculateAverages()` stale.

Two principled directions are:

1. keep practical 170's activation refresh for first-turn/unit-phase users, but refresh the
   average family again before the later player-AI consumers (restoring practical 165's
   post-unit freshness contract); or
2. add a dirty/invalidation contract for city-set / relevant city-average mutations and make
   the first later consumer rebuild the whole average family.

A second unconditional full `AI_calculateAverages()` at the start of `AI_doTurnPre()` is the
simplest correctness reference but may duplicate an expensive culture-pressure city/plot/player
scan every turn. A dirty flag can avoid that cost, but its invalidation scope must cover all
inputs to all five stored aggregate families, not merely city count.

Regression tests should include:

1. Creative AI has one pressure-100 city at activation, founds a pressure-200 border city,
   then reaches `AI_doCommerce()` with expected live average 150 and 10% Culture target;
2. same fixture with no city founded remains pressure 100 / 0% Culture;
3. kept conquest with materially different city yield/commerce/GP modifiers updates the other
   `AI_calculateAverages` members before later research/commerce valuation;
4. city raze/no-net-new-city paths do not spuriously retain a transient acquired city in the
   rebuilt averages;
5. first-turn initialization and any unit-phase consumers that motivated practical 170 remain
   valid after repair.

F518 SIBLING-SCOPE CLOSURE -- NON-CITY-SET MUTATIONS STAY UNDER F518
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Before spending another number, the remaining same-turn producers for the
`AI_calculateAverages()` family were challenged. City-set mutation remains the cleanest F518
witness, but it is not the only way the activation snapshot can become old.

In particular, Great-Person actions occur during `doTurnUnits()` after the activation-time
`AI_calculateAverages()` call and before the later `AI_doTurnPre()` / commerce-research
consumers. A Join changes specialist/output state; Construct can add a building with yield,
commerce or Great-People modifiers; Great Work can change culture-pressure inputs. Whenever
such an action changes an input to one of the stored empire averages, the old aggregate remains
until the next activation for exactly the same reason as the F518 founding witness.

These are additional PRODUCERS of F518, not F519 findings: the stored objects, stale lifetime,
consumer boundary and repair contract are all the same `AI_calculateAverages()` family. No
extra number is spent on them.


F519 / KI#842 -- ADVCIV PRACTICAL 2093 INITIALIZES A NEW CITY AS `CITYSAFETY_SAFE`
WITHOUT COMPUTING ITS REAL SAFETY, SO A SAME-TURN FOUNDED THREATENED CITY CAN BE TREATED AS
SAFE BY LATER UNIT AI
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED -- AdvCiv practical-2093 regression, retained by Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current
AdvCiv-SAS. BtS/Civ4CE and final K-Mod 1.46 do not contain AdvCiv's `AI_isSafe` /
`AI_updateSafety` city-safety cache, so this exact root is AdvCiv-specific.

The strongest witness is ordinary AI city founding during the land-unit pass. A freshly
created `CvCityAI` starts with the optimistic enum value `CITYSAFETY_SAFE`; neither `initCity`,
`found` nor `AI_cityCreated` computes its actual safety. A later Great-Person group in the same
land-unit pass hard-filters candidate cities through `AI_isSafe()` and can therefore Join,
Construct or Hurry in the new city even when an immediate `AI_updateSafety()` would classify
that city as threatened/evacuating and exclude it outright.

ROOT / CURRENT ORDER
--------------------
At turn activation current SAS computes the normal city-importance/safety bundle only for the
cities that already exist:

    CvPlayer::setTurnActive(true)
        -> CvPlayerAI::AI_updateCacheData()
            -> collect `AI_assetVal` for CURRENT cities
            -> AI_setCityValPercent(...)
            -> AI_updateSafety()

Later:

    CvPlayer::doTurnUnits()
        -> DOMAIN_LAND pass
            -> Settler group can found a city
                -> CvPlayer::found(...)
                    -> initCity(...)
                        -> CvCityAI constructor / init
                    -> AI_cityCreated(...)
            -> another land group can act afterward
                -> Great Person -> AI_greatPersonMove()

Current `CvCityAI` construction contains:

    m_iCityValPercent = 0;          // advc.139
    m_eSafety = CITYSAFETY_SAFE;    // advc.139

`CvCityAI::init()` then calls base city initialization, working-plot assignment, best-build
refresh and worker-count refresh. It does NOT call `AI_updateSafety()` and does not assign a
real city-value percentile.

The current `CvPlayer::found` / `CvPlayer::initCity` path likewise contains no city-safety or
city-percentile refresh. The generic AdvCiv city-created observer is only a UWAI notification:

    CvPlayerAI::AI_cityCreated(CvCity& kCity)
    {
        if (getUWAI().isEnabled() || getUWAI().isEnabled(true))
            uwai().getCache().reportCityCreated(kCity);
    }

So, unlike the cities present at activation, a city born during units enters the remainder of
that same turn with constructor defaults rather than a computed `advc.139` state.

CLEAN CURRENT-SAS NORMAL-GAME WITNESS -- ESCORTED SETTLER + GREAT PERSON
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Use an AI that already owns at least one city elsewhere. On another land area, have:

1. an escorted Settler group on a valid cached founding site;
2. a separate Great Scientist/Engineer/other ordinary Great-Person land group on the same
   tile (or otherwise zero/short path to the new city);
3. an enemy land stack on an adjacent tile, strong enough that the new city's live
   `AI_updateSafety()` comparison would fail the safe test once the city exists;
4. no enemy unit on the founding tile itself.

This is reachable under the real Settler code. `AI_found()` considers a Settler group safe when
its group can defend (or is invisible), and its enemy-unit exclusion is about the candidate
SITE itself. It does not impose a generic "no adjacent hostile unit" rule. Thus an escorted
Settler can legally found while a materially stronger hostile stack is adjacent.

When the city is created, the owner now has at least two cities, so a real
`AI_updateSafety()` would not take the one-city shortcut. It would calculate adjacent hostile
land attack strength and local defense strength. Choose ordinary strengths satisfying:

    iAttStrength * 2 >= iDefStrength

and the newly founded city is not safe (THREATENED or, under the additional evacuation
conditions, EVACUATING).

But no such update occurs. The new object simply keeps:

    m_eSafety == CITYSAFETY_SAFE

for the rest of the current unit pass unless some unrelated explicit refresh happens.

The land-pass ordering needed for the witness is ordinary and reachable: `doTurnUnits()`
iterates the player's existing selection groups for the DOMAIN_LAND pass. A Settler group can
therefore execute its Found mission before a separately existing Great-Person group later in
that same pass.

DIRECT SAME-TURN STATE-CHANGING CONSUMER -- `AI_greatPersonMove`
----------------------------------------------------------------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS `CvUnitAI::AI_greatPersonMove()` begin the city target loop with
this hard gate:

    FOR_EACH_CITYAI(pLoopCity, kOwner)
    {
        if (!pLoopCity->AI_isSafe())
            continue;
        ...
        // Join / Construct / Hurry candidates
    }

The check precedes the candidate-value calculations. It is therefore not merely a safety score
modifier: correct unsafe state removes the city from the Join/Construct/Hurry action set.

Make the just-founded city the Great Person's only land-reachable owned city (for example, the
older city is on another landmass). If the Great Person is already on the founding tile,
`generatePath` to the new city succeeds trivially. Configure an ordinary high-value slow action
such as a legal Academy/other Great-Person Construct or permanent-specialist Join so that the
slow mission wins the existing mission comparison.

With the stale constructor state:

    AI_isSafe() == true
        -> new city enters slow-action candidate loop
        -> Join/Construct/Hurry candidate can win
        -> because the GP is already at the target, the corresponding MISSION_JOIN /
           MISSION_CONSTRUCT / MISSION_HURRY is pushed immediately
        -> the Great Person can be consumed in the actually threatened city that same unit pass

With a correct post-founding safety computation:

    AI_updateSafety()
        -> CITYSAFETY_THREATENED or CITYSAFETY_EVACUATING
        -> AI_isSafe() == false
        -> city is skipped before any slow-action candidate is considered
        -> that same GP action cannot be selected there

This is an immediate state-changing gameplay consequence, not a one-turn display/cache
approximation.

A second current-SAS consequence exists in the KI#204 Great-General birth hardening:
`CvPlayer::setCombatExperience()` now prefers cached-safe cities when selecting a Great-General
birth city. A combat later in the same unit phase can therefore also see a newly founded
threatened city as safe. That consumer is SAS-specific and is only extra scope evidence; the
inherited Great-Person hard filter above is the primary proof.

WHY THE EXISTING TACTICAL REFRESH HOOKS DO NOT REPAIR IT
--------------------------------------------------------
AdvCiv has tactical city-safety refresh hooks, but none establishes a fresh city's initial
state.

`CvPlayerAI::AI_attackMadeAgainst()` is deliberately one-directional. Its own comment says an
attack made from a city is unlikely to tip the city from safe to unsafe, and it calls
`AI_updateSafety(false)` only when the cached city is already NOT safe -- i.e. primarily to
notice possible relief after an attacker is killed. A newly founded city whose constructor says
SAFE therefore fails the hook's refresh condition.

`AI_humanEnemyStackMovedInTerritory()` reacts to human enemy movement and has its own local
transition tests; it is not a generic AI-city-created initialization hook.

A whole-current-core call inventory finds no `AI_updateSafety()` invocation in `initCity`,
`found`, city acquisition initialization or `AI_cityCreated`. The ordinary comprehensive
refresh remains the activation-time `AI_updateCacheData()` pass, which is already over when the
witness city is founded.

HISTORY / ANCESTRY -- PRACTICAL 2093 IS THE REGRESSION BOUNDARY
---------------------------------------------------------------
BtS/Civ4CE and final K-Mod 1.46 have no matching AdvCiv `AI_isSafe` / `m_eSafety` city-safety
cache, so they are negative ancestry controls for this exact defect.

Earlier AdvCiv `advc.139` used separate booleans. Immediately before practical 2093, the fresh
`CvCityAI` constructor/reset initialized them conservatively:

    m_bEvacuate = m_bSafe = false; // advc.139

Therefore an unrefreshed just-created city was NOT considered safe by `AI_isSafe()` consumers.
That was imperfect as an initialization policy, but it failed conservatively in the direction
needed by Great-Person safety filters.

AdvCiv practical 2093 / commit
`e3b5a1f536bb761f065c9cffaef06faac52b7a7d` is titled:

    Replace CvCityAI::m_bSafe and m_bEvacuating with an enum

Its constructor diff is exactly:

    - m_bEvacuate = m_bSafe = false; // advc.139
    + m_eSafety = CITYSAFETY_SAFE;    // advc.139

The same change rewrites the normal recomputation routine to start from SAFE and then derive
PERFECT / THREATENED / EVACUATING as appropriate, but it does NOT add a first recomputation on
city creation. Thus a refactor intended to represent the existing safety states also silently
changed the semantics of every freshly constructed, not-yet-refreshed city from "not safe" to
"safe".

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the practical-2093 constructor state and the inherited Great-Person
`AI_isSafe()` hard gate. Current SAS retains both. Classification: AdvCiv practical-2093
initial-state regression, inherited by SAS.

--------------
Album and Known-Issues searches are clear.

- KI#172 / the existing SAS change to `AI_setCityValPercent` concerns the DIRECTION of the
  city-value percentile calculation. F519 concerns a newly created city that never receives a
  current percentile/safety calculation at all, and especially the practical-2093 optimistic
  safety default.
- KI#204 repairs CONSUMER-side Great-General issues: Great-General birth previously ignored
  safety and an inherited Great-Person/General construction test had an inverted safety

  fed an incorrect/default-safe producer state.

  Founding is a shared producer event, but neither repair updates `CvCityAI::m_eSafety` or city

No existing finding owns the root:

    city born after activation -> no initial advc.139 refresh -> constructor says SAFE ->
    later same-turn safety consumer trusts SAFE

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Do not repair only `AI_greatPersonMove()`. Many consumers intentionally rely on cached
`AI_isSafe()`, including current Great-General placement and multiple movement/evacuation paths.
The producer state must become valid.

The correctness reference is to establish the `advc.139` city-importance/safety bundle after a
city-set mutation has completed enough initialization for its real inputs to exist:

1. after founding/acquisition is fully initialized, ensure the new city receives a real
   `AI_updateSafety()` before later same-turn AI consumers;
2. because `m_iCityValPercent` is an empire percentile and city-set changes alter the rank set,
   rebuild/dirty the city-value percentiles for all owned cities as part of the same event
   boundary, then refresh safety where percentile affects evacuation classification;
3. city loss/raze should likewise dirty/rebuild surviving-city percentiles rather than leaving
   ranks from the prior city set;
4. avoid calling the full calculation too early in `initCity`, before ownership, culture,
   units and acquisition/founding effects have reached their final state;
5. as a defensive fallback, a freshly constructed city should not advertise optimistic SAFE
   to gameplay consumers before its first real computation. Restoring a conservative default
   can protect the gap, but it is not a substitute for maintaining current percentiles/safety.

A dirty/event-driven bundle is preferable if unconditional whole-empire percentile + safety
recalculation on every city mutation is considered too expensive.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
1. AI owns another city, escorted Settler founds beside a stronger hostile land stack; after
   founding, the new city's safety must equal an immediate `AI_updateSafety()` result rather
   than constructor SAFE.
2. Separate Great Person on the founding tile acts later in the same land pass; when the new
   city is threatened, the city must be excluded from Join/Construct/Hurry candidates.
3. Identical unthreatened founding should obtain SAFE/PERFECT according to the real safety
   calculation, proving the repair is not merely "always unsafe for new cities."
4. Kept conquest / transfer producing a front-line city should establish current safety before
   later same-turn consumers.
5. City gain/loss should rebuild city-value percentiles for surviving cities, preserving
   KI#172's corrected "higher = more valuable" direction.
6. Current KI#204 Great-General safe-city birth selection should receive current safety rather
   than a constructor default.
7. Save/load and OOS behavior should remain deterministic; no serialized-layout change is
   required merely to add correct refresh/invalidation.

F519 SIBLING BOUNDARY -- CITY-SET PERCENTILES STAY UNDER F519
-------------------------------------------------------------
The immediate post-F519 sibling check confirms that city-set changes also make existing
`m_iCityValPercent` ranks stale until the next full player cache update. Gaining a city adds a
rank member; losing/razing one removes a rank member; the new city's constructor percentile is
0. Because `AI_updateSafety()` uses `AI_getCityValPercent()` when deciding EVACUATING versus
THREATENED, the percentile and safety state are one event-maintained `advc.139` bundle at this
city-set boundary.

That scope is already owned by F519's repair contract. It does not consume another finding:
F519's producer is city creation / city-set mutation after the activation refresh, and the
correct repair is to dirty/rebuild percentiles and establish the new/current city safety state
once the mutation is complete.

The next issue is different: an EXISTING city's local military inputs can change during the
unit phase even when the city set is unchanged. AdvCiv added a tactical refresh hook for this,
