F520 / KI#843 -- ADVCIV `AI_attackMadeAgainst()` ONLY REFRESHES ALREADY-UNSAFE CITIES,
SO AN OWN ATTACK THAT REMOVES A DEFENDER CAN LEAVE AN EXISTING CITY STALE-SAFE FOR LATER
SAME-TURN UNIT AI
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED -- AdvCiv `advc.139` tactical city-safety invalidation defect, present in Base
AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS. BtS/Civ4CE and final K-Mod 1.46 have no matching AdvCiv
city-safety cache/hook. AdvCiv practical 1687 explicitly introduced the current
`AI_attackMadeAgainst` "possible relief" update philosophy and hard-coded the one-directional
condition "It's only going to get safer"; later AdvCiv refactors preserve that asymmetry.

This is independent of F519. F519 is a new-city INITIAL-STATE regression created by practical
2093. F520 uses a city whose activation safety state was correct, then becomes wrong because a
same-turn tactical mutation removes friendly defensive strength and the dedicated combat hook
refuses to refresh cached-SAFE cities.

CURRENT ORDER / INVALIDATION ASYMMETRY
--------------------------------------
At activation current SAS runs:

    CvPlayerAI::AI_updateCacheData()
        -> for every existing city
            -> AI_setCityValPercent(...)
            -> AI_updateSafety()

`AI_updateSafety()` bases SAFE versus unsafe in part on:

    iAttStrength = AI_localAttackStrength(city, ..., range 1, ...)
    iDefStrength = AI_localDefenceStrength(city, ownerTeam,
            DOMAIN_LAND, range 3, ..., bCheckMoves=true, ...)

and uses:

    bSafe = (iAttStrength * 2 < iDefStrength);

Friendly land units in range therefore contribute directly to cached city safety.

During the later unit phase, combat can remove one of those friendly units. AdvCiv practical
1687 added an immediate post-combat hook specifically because the cached city state may have
changed:

    GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).AI_attackMadeAgainst(*pDefender);

Current `AI_attackMadeAgainst()` scans owned cities around the attacked defender but contains:

    /* Unlikely that an attack from within the city will
       tip the scales from safe to unsafe */
    if (!kCity.AI_isSafe())
        kCity.AI_updateSafety(false);

So it deliberately repairs only cities whose OLD cache already says unsafe. That catches the
intended "possible relief" case when killing an enemy attacker makes a threatened city safer,
but it cannot detect the opposite transition even though an own attack can remove defensive
strength from the city.

CLEAN SAME-TURN NUMERIC WITNESS -- TWO DEFENDERS, ONE EQUAL ATTACKER
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Use an existing AI border city C whose activation-time safety computation sees:

- two friendly full-health land combat units A and B that have equal effective defensive
  strength S for C;
- one adjacent hostile full-health ordinary land attacker E with equal effective attack
  strength S against C;
- no other relevant nearby attackers/defenders; neutral enough promotions/terrain/defense that
  the equal-S construction holds (or any nearby integer strengths satisfying the same
  inequalities).

`AI_localDefenceStrength` applies AdvCiv's small multi-defender stack factor. With two defenders:

    iDefStrength = (2S * (75 + (2 - 1))) / 75
                 = 152S / 75
                 > 2S

while the single hostile attacker contributes:

    iAttStrength = S

Therefore activation correctly records:

    iAttStrength * 2 = 2S < 152S / 75
    -> CITYSAFETY_SAFE (or PERFECT if the optional perfect-safety condition also holds)

Now let unit A, in its own land selection group, attack adjacent E. Choose the ordinary combat
outcome in which A dies and E survives with more than half of its original effective strength.
This requires no abnormal state; it is a normal reachable combat result between comparable
units.

Inside `CvUnit::resolveCombat`, after A has become dead, AdvCiv immediately calls the attack
hook. A fresh `AI_updateSafety()` at that exact point would no longer count A because
`AI_localDefenceStrength` explicitly skips `kUnit.isDead()`. Only B remains, so approximately:

    fresh iDefStrength = S
    surviving E effective attack E' > S/2
    2E' > S
    -> city is NOT safe

The exact unit strength need not be identical after combat; any E' >= S/2 produces the same
flip. The defender E is adjacent to C, ordinary DOMAIN_LAND, able to attack, not
mostly-defensive and not standing in a city, so it passes the current
`AI_attackMadeAgainst()` eligibility checks and its scan reaches C.

But C still has its activation cache:

    kCity.AI_isSafe() == true

and therefore the hook executes NO `AI_updateSafety(false)` call. The correct SAFE ->
THREATENED/EVACUATING transition is missed immediately after the combat that caused it.

DIRECT SAME-TURN STATE-CHANGING CONSUMER
----------------------------------------
Use a separate ordinary Great-Person group that is still waiting to act in the same DOMAIN_LAND
pass and is in city C. The same inherited `AI_greatPersonMove()` hard gate used for F519 is a
particularly clean consumer:

    FOR_EACH_CITYAI(pLoopCity, kOwner)
    {
        if (!pLoopCity->AI_isSafe())
            continue;
        // consider Join / Construct / Hurry
    }

Make C the GP's only land-reachable owned city and give the GP a legal high-value slow action
(e.g. an Academy/other Construct or permanent-specialist Join) that wins its ordinary mission
comparison.

Stale path:

    activation says C SAFE
        -> A attacks and dies
        -> live state is unsafe
        -> AI_attackMadeAgainst sees cached SAFE and skips refresh
        -> later GP still sees AI_isSafe()==true
        -> C remains in Join/Construct/Hurry candidate set
        -> GP already in C can push MISSION_JOIN / MISSION_CONSTRUCT / MISSION_HURRY
           immediately and be consumed there

Correct path:

    after A dies, recompute C safety
        -> C becomes THREATENED/EVACUATING
        -> later AI_greatPersonMove hard-skips C
        -> that same GP action cannot be selected there

Thus the asymmetric tactical invalidation has an immediate same-turn gameplay effect. It is
not merely a cached diagnostic or a next-turn approximation.

WHY THE EXISTING HOOK IS NOT A DEFENSE AGAINST THE WITNESS
----------------------------------------------------------
The hook runs at the right time but checks the wrong OLD-state direction for this case.

`resolveCombat()` calls `AI_attackMadeAgainst()` after death has been established, so a fresh
local-defense calculation would already exclude the dead attacker A. The problem is not call
timing. It is the guard:

    if (!kCity.AI_isSafe())

which prevents the calculation precisely when the old cache says SAFE and a defensive
contributor has just disappeared.

The rough `bCheckMoves` implementation in `AI_localDefenceStrength` is also not an obstacle to
this witness: regardless of how current movement points are approximated, a dead unit is
explicitly skipped. The proof therefore does not depend on route/move-point edge behavior.

Other ordinary same-turn friendly-unit movements can plausibly create the same stale direction
by moving defensive strength away without combat. Those are additional manifestations of the
same local-safety invalidation family if proven; the combat-death witness alone is sufficient
because it passes through AdvCiv's dedicated refresh hook and demonstrates the asymmetry
without requiring a generic movement-callback argument.

HISTORY / ANCESTRY
------------------
BtS/Civ4CE and final K-Mod 1.46 do not contain AdvCiv's `AI_isSafe` /
`AI_updateSafety` cache, so this exact issue is AdvCiv-specific.

The AdvCiv safety cache (`advc.139`) already exists before practical 1687. Practical 1687 /
commit `ef52c71628f14cf9751a2246ef520fce41617c28`, titled:

    Improvements to AI city safety, stack strength evaluation.

strengthened the safety calculation and ADDED `CvPlayerAI::AI_attackMadeAgainst`. The
introducing diff documents its intended direction explicitly:

    /* May have to update city safety status after one of our units
       has attacked (possible relief). ... */

and then:

    if (!kCity.AI_isSafe()) // It's only going to get safer
        kCity.AI_updateSafety();

That assumption is false whenever the attacking unit itself was part of the city's defensive
strength and is removed (death is the cleanest case). Later AdvCiv changes refactor the scan
and enum representation but preserve the same one-directional guard and even the current
comment that safe -> unsafe is merely "unlikely."

Therefore the exact current defect is best classified as an AdvCiv `advc.139` invalidation
asymmetry, explicitly codified by practical 1687, inherited by Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS. This
is older and independently rooted from F519's practical-2093 constructor regression.

SEMANTIC DEDUP
--------------
Album and current Known-Issues searches are clear.

- F519 / KI#842: new city is born with optimistic `CITYSAFETY_SAFE` and receives no first
  computation. F520: an existing city's activation safety was CORRECT, then a friendly combat
  death changes its live defense and the tactical invalidator refuses SAFE -> UNSAFE refresh.
  Repairing new-city initialization alone does nothing to F520.
- KI#172: city-value percentile direction; no tactical local-defense invalidation.
- KI#204: consumer-side Great-General safety filters / inverted test; F520 proves a correct
  safety consumer can still receive stale producer state.
- F515/F518: different cached objects (`m_aeAICitySites`, empire averages) that can share a
  unit-phase event but not this local military-strength dependency.
- Earlier album safety controls discuss safety consumers and tactical approximations, but no
  numbered finding owns the practical-1687 one-way `AI_attackMadeAgainst` invalidation root.

No existing finding repairs:

    existing city correctly SAFE -> own attack removes defense -> dedicated hook sees OLD SAFE
    and skips -> later same-turn unit AI consumes stale SAFE

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The minimum correction for the proven combat path is to stop assuming the transition direction
inside `AI_attackMadeAgainst()`. For owned cities in the affected scan, recompute safety even
when the cached state is SAFE (or establish a precise condition proving that the attacking unit
could not have contributed to their local defense).

A broader robust design should treat city safety as dirty when relevant local attack/defense
inputs change during the unit phase, including friendly unit death/departure and hostile
movement/death. Then refresh before the first safety-sensitive consumer. That would avoid
trying to enumerate SAFE->UNSAFE and UNSAFE->SAFE cases separately.

If preserving the cheap tactical hook rather than a dirty system:

1. `AI_attackMadeAgainst` must cover both transition directions for nearby affected cities;
2. the scan should be based on geometry that can affect the same local-strength ranges used by
   `AI_updateSafety`;
3. ordinary non-combat defender movement should be reviewed separately, because no attack hook
   fires there;
4. do not fold F519's city-created initialization into a combat-only repair -- both producer
   boundaries need coverage.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
1. Existing city has two equal-strength friendly defenders and one equal-strength adjacent
   enemy; activation safety is SAFE through the multi-defender factor.
2. One friendly defender attacks that enemy, dies; enemy survives >50% effective strength;
   city safety must immediately become non-safe.
3. Same combat with enemy killed/relieved should still support the intended unsafe->safer
   refresh path from practical 1687.
4. Great Person in the city acts later in the same land pass; after the defender death, unsafe
   city must be excluded from Join/Construct/Hurry.
5. Current KI#204 Great-General safe-city placement should likewise see current safety after
   combat.
6. Non-combat friendly defender departure should be tested while evaluating whether the repair
   is generalized to a safety-dirty contract.
7. No synchronized-RNG/OOS behavior should depend on whether a diagnostic-only refresh occurs;
   the safety computation itself must remain deterministic.

F520 SIBLING SCOPE -- ORDINARY UNIT MOVEMENT
--------------------------------------------
The immediate local-safety sibling sweep does not spend F521.

The F520 combat-death witness is the cleanest proof because AdvCiv's dedicated
`AI_attackMadeAgainst()` callback actually runs and demonstrates its one-way old-state guard.
But the same cached-object lifetime is broader:

- a friendly defensive group can simply move away from an existing city during the land-unit
  pass, reducing the live `AI_localDefenceStrength` input after the activation safety snapshot;
  no generic friendly-movement safety callback runs, so SAFE can remain stale;
- a reinforcing friendly group can move into range, increasing live defensive strength while a
  cached THREATENED/EVACUATING city remains stale in the opposite direction;
- hostile unit movement/death can likewise change the local attack-strength side; AdvCiv has a
  narrow human-enemy movement hook and the "possible relief" combat hook, which itself shows
  that tactical freshness is intended, but these are not a complete invalidation contract.

All of those manifestations share F520's stored object (`m_eSafety`), mutable local military
inputs and robust repair direction: dirty/recompute affected city safety when local
attack/defense state changes, or before the next safety-sensitive consumer. They must not be
split into extra finding numbers merely by choosing a different unit movement that changes the
same live strength balance.

F519's `m_iCityValPercent` city-set lifetime remains separate and already scoped there. No
independent non-city-set producer changes a city's relative empire asset percentile without
also changing the city/output valuation itself in a way that warrants a distinct proven
invalidation contract in this pass.

CONTROL — `getCivicPercentAnger` TEAMMATE / UNMET-CIV FILTER IS INTENTIONAL
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
The current AdvCiv/SAS loop differs deliberately from K-Mod: it iterates alive players
known to our team, excludes only self, and therefore includes known teammates while
excluding unmet civilizations.

Reachable history makes the intent explicit. AdvCiv practical 2381,
commit 473d5c468d8e89cf217df9df8574cf276bf722f2, is titled:

    "Emancipation anger from teammates; none from unmet civs."

The patch replaces K-Mod's `kOther.getTeam() == getTeam()` exclusion with exactly the
current `PlayerIter<CIV_ALIVE,KNOWN_TO>` + self-only exclusion. The current implementation
therefore matches the authored rule rather than exposing an accidental team-role drift.
No F521.

CONTROL — POLLUTION / RESEARCH ARITHMETIC REMAINS PREVIOUSLY COVERED
---------------------------------------------------------------------
`calculatePollution` was already explicitly rechecked in WIP161 and WIP202. Its bad-health
sign convention is coherent with the city health APIs and current global-warming callers.
The only SAS-local changes in the current helper are static define caches; no arithmetic
semantic change was introduced.

`calculateResearchRate` is semantically identical to Base AdvCiv 1.14 in the current tree.
The nearby teammate-overflow receiver mismatch in `getResearchTurnsLeftTimes100` was already
preserved as a real generic/config-dependent source defect in WIP175, but current SAS masks
it because `RESEARCH_MODIFIER_EXTRA_TEAM_MEMBER=0` and both AI/human groundbreaking
penalties are disabled. The tooltip groundbreaking interaction was likewise already bounded
under current defines. No new F521 from this family.

CONTROL — PLAYER `BuildingOnlyHealthy` TOGGLE IS LIVE-READ, NOT A STALE HEALTH CACHE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::changeBuildingOnlyHealthyCount` initially looked suspicious because it changes a
player-wide health rule but only calls `AI_makeAssignWorkDirty()` rather than recomputing
all city health members.

The full callee/read chain closes the concern:

* `CvCity::isBuildingOnlyHealthy()` dynamically reads
  `GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).isBuildingOnlyHealthy()` before falling back to the city-local
  count;
* `CvCity::totalBadBuildingHealth()` dynamically returns 0 whenever that predicate is true;
* per-building bad-health access (`getBuildingBadHealth`) is dynamically masked the same way;
* health consumers therefore observe the changed player count without needing a stored
  bad-health rebuild.

The assignment dirtying is sufficient for population reassignment. This is a useful
negative cache-control and not F521.

POST-WIP273 THIN-STATE CONTROLS
--------------------------------
1. Event-persistent free promotions close under the full application path.
   `applyEvent` first grants the event promotion to every currently matching unit and then
   calls `setFreePromotion(UnitCombat/UnitClass, promotion, true)`. The setter de-duplicates
   exact pairs and preserves the grant for future units. There is no existing-unit omission
   hidden behind the thin setter.

2. `changeNoForeignTradeCount` deliberately skips the expensive global trade-route rebuild
   while the player is in anarchy. This is not a missing permanent refresh: the anarchy
   transition handler `changeAnarchyTurns` calls both player `updateTradeRoutes()` and
   `GC.getGame().updateTradeRoutes()` whenever the anarchy boolean changes. Thus trade routes
   are rebuilt when anarchy ends, matching the source comment.

3. `updateMaxAnarchyTurns` initially appeared dangerously init-only because `m_iMaxAnarchyTurns`
   is derived from traits. The lifecycle closes the concern. `CvPlayer::processTraits` calls
   `updateMaxAnarchyTurns()` after processing trait effects, and live leader replacement
   `changeLeader` invokes `processTraits(-1)`, swaps the leader, then `processTraits(1)`.
   Therefore a live trait-set change refreshes the derived maximum-anarchy cache on both sides
   of the transition. No F521.

4. `setResearchingTech` remains a thin mirror of research-queue membership rather than an
   independent authority. `pushResearch`, `popResearch` and `clearResearchQueue` update it in
   lockstep, and duplicate queue entries are prevented by the existing `isResearchingTech`
   gate. No standalone stale-state root established.

5. `hasReadyUnit` / `hasBusyUnit` / `setAutoMoves` were reopened because they have near-zero
   semantic album coverage. Their K-Mod turn-control contract remains coherent in this pass:
   automated groups are intentionally excluded from manual-ready detection; `isBusy` already
   handles empty groups; and `CvGame::updateMoves` clears AutoMoves only after all automatic
   missions/automated-unit AI are no longer busy. No premature-turn-completion witness was
   established.

TYPE-AWARE CONTROL — `GET_TEAM(PlayerTypes)` IS NOT A PLAYER/TEAM-ID BUG
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
A renewed direct-cast/accessor scan briefly made `CvPlayer::canStealTech` look severe:

    GET_TEAM(eTarget).isHasTech(eTech)

where `eTarget` is a PlayerTypes. This is the exact false positive already rejected in
WIP152. `CvPlayer.cpp` includes `CoreAI.h`, whose `GET_TEAM(x)` macro dispatches to overloaded
`CoreAI::getTeam`; the PlayerTypes overload converts through TEAMID(ePlayer). The analogous
`canSpyDestroyProject` spelling is safe for the same reason. BtS/K-Mod spell the conversion
explicitly; AdvCiv deliberately changed the source spelling during the CoreAI accessor
refactor without changing semantics.

This control is important for the remainder of Queue 004: do not diagnose a numeric player/
team-ID collision from `GET_TEAM(variable)` until the variable's static type and the active
CoreAI overload are resolved.

CURRENT DIRECT CAST / PAYLOAD SWEEP — CLEAN SO FAR
--------------------------------------------------
The explicit `(TeamTypes)iData1` / `(TeamTypes)item.m_iData` sites reviewed in the high-risk
normal-game paths are encoded TeamTypes payloads rather than disguised PlayerTypes:

* `handleDiploEvent` JOIN_WAR / STOP_TRADING / SET_WARPLAN receives a target team in iData1;
  the surrounding player/member lookups consistently compare against that target team.
* TRADE_PEACE / TRADE_WAR / TRADE_EMBARGO store a target team in TradeData.m_iData and assert
  the MAX_CIV_TEAMS bounds before conversion in structural validity checks.
* the corresponding diplomacy text rows decode the same TeamTypes payload and resolve the
  target team's live leader only for display/icon selection.

No player/team enum-domain root survives this subset.

HIGH-RISK INHERITED ZERO-MENTION ADVC DELTAS — CONTROLS
-------------------------------------------------------
The zero-mention methods that differ between K-Mod and Base AdvCiv were not dismissed merely
because current SAS matches Base. The higher-risk semantic samples close:

* `countNumCoastalCities` / `countNumCoastalCitiesByArea`: AdvCiv's parameterless
  `CvCity::isCoastal()` uses the default -1, which `CvPlot::isCoastalLand` resolves to the
  same `MIN_WATER_SIZE_FOR_OCEAN` define K-Mod passed explicitly. No water-size semantic
  regression.
* `invalidateCommerceRankCache(eCommerce)`: AdvCiv intentionally narrows invalidation to the
  commerce bucket just recomputed by `CvCity::updateCommerce(eCommerce)`. A full update loops
  every commerce type; no sibling rank remains valid across a changed value.
* `expireMessages`: the `getExpireTurn(isHuman() || isHumanDisabled())` change is explicit
  Rise & Fall / advc.700 policy so temporarily AI-controlled human players retain human-style
  message history. It is not accidental identity inversion.
* `getUnitArtInfo`: advc.001 deliberately redirects city-screen unit art to the selected
  city's owner. The later SAS change only caches the Barbarian civilization define.
* compact counter/setter changes (`setOverflowResearch`, `setConversionTimer`, free-unit and
  military-unit cost/support fields, state-religion production modifiers, score mirrors,
  upkeep legacy state) preserve inherited authoritative fields or UI dirties; their live
  gameplay consumers read those fields dynamically or are covered by the established

CONTROL — `SAS_AI_findBestFallbackUnit` SUCCESS / SIEGE-CAP CONTRACT SURVIVES FIRST DEEP PASS
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This entirely SAS-local helper had essentially no literal Album coverage and feeds both the hard
CvCity::doTurn no-production safety net and AI_chooseUnit's concrete-unit replacement path, so it
was audited first.

The helper's output contract is internally coherent in the current tree:
* outputs start at NO_UNIT / NO_UNITAI;
* every candidate must pass canTrain, be a fighting land unit, and have one of the explicitly
  accepted offensive/defensive default UnitAI roles;
* `eSkipUnit` is excluded before bucket selection;
* siege / trebuchet-like gates are applied before both normal and absolute-cheapest candidates
  are recorded, so the cheapest emergency backup does not bypass a rejected siege category;
* the XML-cost cap is intentionally only a preferred-unit cap; the absolute-cheapest above-cap
  fallback is enabled only by callers that explicitly request that final safety net;
* return true requires both a concrete UnitTypes and UnitAITypes result.

A tempting multi-city cap-overrun concern is INTENTIONAL POLICY rather than a new root.
`AI_countUnitsByCombat*` and `AI_countTrebuchetsLike` deliberately count only completed owned
units, not units currently being trained. The source comment explicitly explains that counting
'makings' can create queue cancellation/reshuffle oscillation and accepts a little cap overshoot
as the tradeoff. Therefore simultaneous cities queuing siege beyond the completed-unit threshold
does not by itself violate the authored contract. Do not promote that smoothing choice as F521.

No success-without-pick, siege-category bypass, or caller legality mismatch has been established
from this helper so far. Preserve it as a Queue-005 control unless a later caller interaction
reveals a different root.

AI_chooseUnit CONTROL — LAND-SPY WAR-PLAN / MAP GATE LOOKS REVERSED IN ISOLATION, BUT IS AUTHORED SAS POLICY
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The concrete-unit SAS gate for `UNITAI_SPY` initially looked like a strong copy/paste defect.
Current code says that land Spies are valuable "especially on land maps", permits them in calm
conditions, but when `bWarPlan = AI_isFocusWar()` is true it rejects them specifically when the
map is NOT naval-heavy. The same condition was introduced in practical 4957 for both Spy Sea and
land Spy; it is naturally intuitive for Spy Sea but looks backwards for a land unit.

The inherited higher-level production logic makes the contradiction look even stronger:
`AI_chooseProduction` deliberately gives Spy production +10 odds for
`WARPLAN_PREPARING_TOTAL` and +5 for `WARPLAN_PREPARING_LIMITED`, while those plans are chosen-war
plans and can make `AI_isFocusWar()` true before actual war. On an ordinary Pangaea map
(`bNavalHeavyMapname=false`), a calm city below its Spy need can therefore pass the inherited
war-preparation Spy roll and then have the concrete SAS gate reject the resolved `UNIT_SPY`.

However, the current authored KI#53 documentation explicitly records this exact resulting rule:

    Spies: ... Block if bAtWar || bEnemyStrong || bDanger;
    if bWarPlan && !NavalHeavy -> block
    rationale: "Don't stall land wars with spy spam"

That documentation is specific enough to establish an intentional SAS policy override rather
than an accidental Player/Team/map-orientation invariant. The nearby source comments are
internally confusing/stale (especially "useless or ineffective at land warfare" inside the land
Spy block), and the policy deliberately overrides AdvCiv's inherited preparing-war Spy boost,
but the audit must not renumber an authored tuning choice merely because the older caller points
in the opposite strategic direction. No F521 from this branch.

LIVE F521 CANDIDATE — AREA-LOCAL WORKER FLOOR CAN BE VETOED BY AREA-DEPENDENT CAP APPLIED TO AN EMPIRE-WIDE WORKER COUNT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The Worker branch exposes a materially different contract mismatch.

Current production establishes an explicit AREA-LOCAL minimum before ordinary priorities:

    iExistingWorkers = AI_totalAreaUnitAIs(kArea, UNITAI_WORKER)
    iMinimumAreaWorkers = AI_getSASMinimumAreaWorkers(kArea)
    if (!bDanger && iExistingWorkers < iMinimumAreaWorkers)
        AI_chooseUnit(UNITAI_WORKER, 100)

The shared helper is intentionally area-local. For the primary area it applies the current
tunable 200%-per-city floor with the signed reserve (-1 by default); secondary areas are bounded
by their own calculated demand and may fall to zero when truly complete.

But the later concrete `AI_chooseUnit(UnitTypes, UnitAITypes)` Worker gate uses a GLOBAL count:

    iMaxUnits = era-decayed empire cap (~2.5 * total cities, floor 60%)
    iMaxUnits = max(iMaxUnits, AI_getSASMinimumAreaWorkers(getArea()))
    iTotalUnitAIs = AI_totalUnitAIs(UNITAI_WORKER)   // empire-wide, includes training
    if (iTotalUnitAIs >= iMaxUnits)
        return false

The attempted synchronization is dimensionally inconsistent: an area-specific minimum is used to
raise a cap that is compared against the entire empire's Worker population. The effective empire
cap therefore depends on WHICH AREA'S CITY happens to call the function.

Clean current-default shape under final challenge:
* 10-city AI empire in the Future era.
* Primary land area has 9 cities; one secondary landmass has 1 city and real Worker work.
* Current primary floor = 2*9 - 1 = 17 Workers.
* Current era-decayed generic empire cap = 2.5*10*60% = 15 Workers.
* Primary-area production is allowed to rebuild up to 17 because its concrete call executes
  max(15, primaryMinimum=17).
* Put those 17 existing/queued Workers on the primary landmass and none on the secondary one.
* The secondary area's `AI_neededWorkers` is positive, so its shared minimum is 1 and the
  high-level area-floor branch deterministically asks for a Worker with iOdds=100.
* In the concrete secondary-area call, however, max(15, secondaryMinimum=1) is only 15.
  `AI_totalUnitAIs(WORKER)` is the empire-wide 17, so the request is rejected before the later
  area-usefulness gate can approve the genuine local shortage.

This is stronger than a heuristic difference: the same shared minimum that primary-area cities
were allowed to build can make a secondary area's own minimum impossible to rebuild. The final
area-usefulness Worker check does not repair it because it runs after the global-cap return; if
reached, it would correctly see `AI_neededWorkers(area) > AI_totalAreaUnitAIs(area)` and allow the
Worker.

HISTORY BOUNDARY SO FAR
-----------------------
Practical 4957 (`fe58e134631681ba9e79e481dd29a761b8820696`) introduced the generic empire-wide
Worker production cap in the large SAS AI_chooseUnit production/scrapping rewrite.

Practical 5916 (`9f18ea297837942da844afac467278d9927d1dc7`), titled "Ensure AI rebuilds a minimum
worker force...", introduced `AI_getSASMinimumAreaWorkers` and the explicit area-local production
floor, but left the concrete global Worker cap in place. This appears to be the birth of the
cross-layer contradiction.

Practical 6093 (`b3b83cf78fc58a509bc639573445452f0903e9b1`) strengthened KI#198's primary-area floor
and explicitly tried to keep the generic Worker cap from vetoing it by adding:

    iMaxUnits = max(iMaxUnits, AI_getSASMinimumAreaWorkers(getArea()))

That fixes a same-area late-era floor/cap collision only while the caller's area supplies the
largest relevant minimum. It does not reconcile an empire-wide count with multiple area-local
minimums, and in the clean 9+1-city example it creates two different effective empire caps (17
from a primary-area city, 15 from a secondary-area city).

DEDUP / CLASSIFICATION STATUS AT THIS SAFETY CHECKPOINT
-------------------------------------------------------
This does NOT currently look like existing F006 / KI#213. F006 is the legacy city-best-build vs
custom Worker-evaluator split that can make `AI_neededWorkers` falsely report no demand. The new
candidate assumes the area demand/minimum is CORRECT and demonstrates that a later independent
concrete production cap vetoes it. Repairing the demand source under KI#213 would not remove this
mismatch.

The earlier Queue-001 re-audit called the KI#192/KI#198 shared minimum coherent after checking the
helper and its production/usefulness/scrap consumers, but did not inspect this later CvCityAI
empire-wide cap interaction. No cumulative Album wording found so far owns the exact
"area-local minimum vs empire-global cap" root.

F521 remains deliberately UNUSED until the following are finished:
1. final current-data arithmetic/caller proof including the high-level iOdds=100 -> concrete call;
2. verify no Worker transport/reassignment mechanism constitutes an immediate guaranteed repair
   of the area-local production contract (it need not if no transport is available, but trace it);
3. exact semantic collision against KI#198/F006 and other Worker production findings;
4. finish ancestry around practicals 5916/6093 and check for a later authored statement that
   explicitly accepts this cross-area cap behavior;
5. establish the narrow repair invariant before promotion.

KI#198 REOPENED/BROADENED — AREA-LOCAL LAND-WORKER MINIMUM CAN BE VETOED BY THE EMPIRE-WIDE CONCRETE WORKER CAP
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED current SAS implementation gap, but classified under existing KI#198 rather than a new F521 root because it violates KI#198's own explicit cross-subsystem synchronization contract.

ROOT / CURRENT ORDER
--------------------
`AI_chooseProduction` correctly establishes an area-local standing Worker floor before ordinary priorities:

    iExistingWorkers = kPlayer.AI_totalAreaUnitAIs(kArea, UNITAI_WORKER);
    iMinimumAreaWorkers = kPlayer.AI_getSASMinimumAreaWorkers(kArea);
    if (!bDanger && iExistingWorkers < iMinimumAreaWorkers)
        AI_chooseUnit(UNITAI_WORKER, 100);

`AI_getSASMinimumAreaWorkers` is intentionally area-local. The primary area receives the XML-tuned standing force; secondary areas remain demand-driven and can legitimately return zero once complete.

The later concrete `AI_chooseUnit(UnitTypes,UnitAITypes)` Worker gate instead combines an area-local minimum with an empire-global count:

    iMaxUnits = era-decayed generic empire Worker cap;
    iMaxUnits = max(iMaxUnits, kPlayer.AI_getSASMinimumAreaWorkers(getArea()));
    iTotalUnitAIs = kPlayer.AI_totalUnitAIs(UNITAI_WORKER); // empire-wide, includes training
    if (iTotalUnitAIs >= iMaxUnits)
        return false;

That synchronization is dimensionally incomplete. The same empire has a different effective global cap depending on which land area's city is making the call.

DETERMINISTIC CURRENT-DEFAULT WITNESS
-------------------------------------
Use a Future-era AI with 10 cities:
* 9 cities on the primary land area;
* 1 city on a disconnected secondary land area with real Worker work and no Worker.

Current default arithmetic:
* generic empire Worker maximum before the area floor: 2.5 * 10 = 25;
* Future-era decay clamps at 60%, so generic cap = 15;
* primary 9-city Worker floor with current 200% and -1 reserve = 17.

A primary-area city therefore uses:

    max(globalCap 15, primaryAreaMinimum 17) = 17

and can legitimately rebuild/retain the primary standing force up to 17. Worker scrapping is also area-aware and refuses to scrap when the primary area's Worker count is at or below its local minimum.

Now consider the secondary city's genuine local shortage:
* secondary area `AI_neededWorkers` is positive;
* `AI_getSASMinimumAreaWorkers(secondary)` = 1;
* area Worker count = 0;
* `AI_chooseProduction` deterministically asks for `UNITAI_WORKER` with odds 100.

The concrete call then uses:

    max(globalCap 15, secondaryAreaMinimum 1) = 15
    empire AI_totalUnitAIs(WORKER) = 17

so `17 >= 15` rejects the Worker before the later central area-usefulness gate is reached. If that later gate were reached, it would correctly see `AI_neededWorkers(area) > AI_totalAreaUnitAIs(area,WORKER)` and approve the local shortage.

The result is therefore not merely a soft tuning disagreement: Workers that the primary-area KI#198 floor is explicitly allowed to create/protect can make a secondary area's own positive local minimum impossible to rebuild through the city production path that requested it.

NO GUARANTEED TRANSPORT SELF-HEAL
---------------------------------
Current overseas Worker transport logic is useful but contingent:
* Settler transports can carry/reload Workers when a destination area has a positive `AI_neededWorkers` deficit;
* destination-aware unload logic avoids excess cargo and can service an island when a suitable transport/mission exists;
* completed-area Worker rescue handles the opposite zero-demand case.

None of those paths guarantees an immediate Worker for a newly founded/disconnected secondary area. A supported state with no available Worker transport remains possible. The explicit city-side local production floor is therefore a real producer contract and cannot rely on a future transport being available to repair this veto.

SAME-FILE NEGATIVE CONTROL — WORKER SEA ALREADY USES THE CORRECT GLOBAL-CAP/LOCAL-DEFICIT SHAPE
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The current `UNITAI_WORKER_SEA` concrete gate has the same conceptual problem and already contains the appropriate solution pattern:

    iTotalUnitAIs = kPlayer.AI_totalUnitAIs(UNITAI_WORKER_SEA); // global
    iLocalAvailableSeaWorkers = ... current city's primary/secondary water areas ...;
    iLocalNeededSeaWorkers = AI_neededSeaWorkers();
    bLocalSeaWorkerDeficit = (iLocalNeededSeaWorkers > iLocalAvailableSeaWorkers);
    if (iTotalUnitAIs >= iMaxUnits && !bLocalSeaWorkerDeficit)
        return false;

Its source comment explicitly explains why: the empire-global Work Boat cap was reached elsewhere even though the current city's own water areas still needed a Work Boat. The cap remains for idle/excess boats, but a real local deficit bypasses it.

Land Workers need the analogous invariant. The current land branch instead performs an unconditional global-cap rejection before its area-local usefulness/demand check.

HISTORY / AUTHORED CONTRACT
---------------------------
Practical 4957 (`fe58e134631681ba9e79e481dd29a761b8820696`) introduced the broad SAS concrete-unit production caps, including the empire-wide Worker maximum.

Practical 5916 (`9f18ea297837942da844afac467278d9927d1dc7`), 2026-06-05, is titled:

    Ensure AI rebuilds a minimum worker force

Its commit text says it adds "a shared AdvCiv-SAS minimum worker floor per area" and uses it "in both city production and worker scrapping guards" so AIs reliably rebuild Workers while keeping "production and scrap thresholds synchronized."

The current KI#198 documentation later makes the synchronization contract even more explicit:

    `AI_neededWorkers`, the relevant production ceilings and Worker-scrapping safeguards all respected the same minimum so one subsystem did not immediately undo another.

Practical 6093 (`b3b83cf78fc58a509bc639573445452f0903e9b1`) strengthened KI#198 and explicitly says the same minimum is synchronized through `AI_neededWorkers`, production ceilings and scrapping. The added concrete line

    iMaxUnits = max(iMaxUnits, kPlayer.AI_getSASMinimumAreaWorkers(getArea()));

is therefore an attempted implementation of that contract. It repairs the same-area late-era collision, but not cross-area empires because the compared Worker count is empire-wide while the floor used to raise the cap belongs only to the current area.

This is SAS-local; Base AdvCiv/K-Mod do not contain this SAS floor/cap combination.

DEDUP / CLASSIFICATION
----------------------
Do NOT allocate F521.

* F006 / KI#213 is a different Worker-demand architecture root: `AI_neededWorkers` can become falsely low because the legacy city best-build cache does not see jobs handled by the custom Worker evaluator. The present witness assumes demand/minimum is correctly POSITIVE and gets vetoed afterward by an unrelated concrete global cap.
* Nevertheless, the new cross-area veto is best classified as an incomplete KI#198 repair rather than an independent KI family. KI#198 expressly owns the standing Worker minimum and the requirement that its demand, production ceilings and scrapping safeguards agree. The narrow repair completes exactly that promise.

NARROW REPAIR INVARIANT
-----------------------
Preserve the empire-wide cap for excess Workers, but do not let it veto a current-area shortage below the shared local minimum. Conceptually:

    iTotalWorkers = AI_totalUnitAIs(UNITAI_WORKER);
    iAreaWorkers = AI_totalAreaUnitAIs(getArea(), UNITAI_WORKER);
    iAreaMinimum = AI_getSASMinimumAreaWorkers(getArea());

    if (iTotalWorkers >= iGlobalMax && iAreaWorkers >= iAreaMinimum)
        return false;

The exact implementation can retain the existing era-decayed global cap and logging. The important contract is the same one already implemented by Worker Sea: global excess limits apply only once the current locality's authoritative minimum/deficit has been satisfied.

A more global alternative would raise the empire cap to the sum of all current area minima, but that changes policy more broadly and is unnecessary for the narrow defect. A local-deficit bypass is simpler and follows the existing Worker Sea precedent.

POST-WIP279 AI_chooseUnit — FINAL ROLE / SUBSTITUTION MECHANICS CONTROL
---------------------------------------------------------------------
The concrete overload stores `eChangedUnit` / `eChangedUnitAI`, performs the early strict-defender replacement/hijack, refreshes `pUnitInfo` when the concrete unit changes, and only THEN builds the naval / land-civilian UnitAI classification booleans. Therefore the earlier cautionary source comment saying those booleans are not recomputed is stale: the relevant downstream booleans are first computed from the FINAL role after replacement. Earlier siege/defender checks are consumed before replacement. The old File-005 control remains valid; no stale-final-UnitAI branch was established.

The replacement helper itself only returns a concrete trainable fighting LAND unit with an accepted offensive/defensive DEFAULT UnitAI. A replaced unit therefore cannot silently turn into a civilian/naval/air candidate and bypass those later category gates. The UnitAI-hijack fallback checks `getUnitAIType(...)` before changing the role. No illegal final role was established.

CONTROL — APPARENT WRONG NON-TREBUCHET COUNT ARGUMENT IS REDUNDANT AT THE CURRENT CALLER
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A fresh type/parameter audit noticed that the helper parameter is explicitly named and consumed as:

    iSiegesAllNonTrebuchetsLike

whereas the strict-defender replacement caller supplies:

    iSiegesAll = AI_countUnitsByCombat(UNITCOMBAT_SIEGE)

rather than the dedicated:

    AI_countUnitsByCombatNoTrebuchetsLike(...)

The sibling `CvCity::doTurn` fallback caller DOES use the dedicated non-Trebuchet count, so this initially looked like a strong wrong-aggregate bug.

At the strict-defender caller, however, the same total-siege bound is already encoded one level earlier:

    bEnoughSiegeAlready = (iSiegesAll >= iNumCities)
    bAllowSiege = (!bEnoughSiegeAlready && !bNoNewSiegeRightNow)

and the helper immediately rejects every siege candidate when `!bAllowSiege`. Therefore whenever a non-Trebuchet candidate reaches the supposedly wrong `iSiegesAll >= iNumCities` helper comparison, `bAllowSiege` has already proved the opposite (`iSiegesAll < iNumCities`). The broad count passed into that particular parameter is redundant under this caller's current gates and does not itself create a live rejection. Do not promote the misleading parameter mismatch alone.

PRACTICAL-5329 REFACTOR SEMANTIC DELTA — REAL HISTORY DRIFT, CURRENT DATA MASKS THE UNIT CHOICE
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reachable commit diff `SASBranch_5329_8fb9a5bb93.diff` provides a useful historical control. Its commit message says the new shared `SAS_AI_findBestFallbackUnit` helper consolidates the duplicated `CvCity::doTurn` and `CvCityAI::AI_chooseUnit` loops while "preserving the existing caps and siege gating."

The old strict-defender replacement loop did this for every siege candidate:

    if (bEnoughSiegeAlready || bEnoughTrebsLikeAlready || bNoNewSiegeRightNow)
        continue;

with:

    bEnoughSiegeAlready = (iSiegesAll >= iNumCities)
    bEnoughTrebsLikeAlready = (iTrebsLike >= 3)

Thus three Trebuchet-like units blocked ALL further siege fallback choices, including Catapult-like units.

Practical 5329 rewrote this as two category controls:

    bAllowSiege = !bEnoughSiegeAlready && !bNoNewSiegeRightNow
    bAllowTrebuchetsLike = !bEnoughTrebsLikeAlready && !bNoNewSiegeRightNow

and the helper only applies `bAllowTrebuchetsLike` to Trebuchet-like candidates. Therefore, for e.g. five cities / three Trebuchets / fewer than five total siege, the current helper may consider a Catapult whereas the pre-refactor loop would have rejected every siege fallback. No later helper-history diff found intentionally documenting this as a strategic change; it is a genuine failure to preserve the exact old predicate promised by the refactor commit.

However this does NOT clear the current-gameplay finding threshold. Current shipped data make Trebuchets available at `TECH_ENGINEERING`; that same ordinary state also makes stronger no-resource offensive-default alternatives available (notably Crossbowman, cost 65, default `UNITAI_COUNTER`, versus Catapult cost 50). The helper is offense-default-only here and selects the highest cost/UU-inflated score within its generous era cap. Consequently admitting the Catapult under the refactored category split does not change the selected fallback in the ordinary current data state examined. Other current no-resource offensive lines similarly prevent a clean shipped "old chooses no/other unit, new chooses Catapult" witness.

Classification: preserve as a practical-5329 refactor-semantic / future-data robustness note associated with the KI#53.3 siege-production family, not F521. A future data change that removes the stronger concurrent alternative or changes the fallback score could expose it. The narrow historical-preservation repair, if desired, is to retain an explicit "Trebuchet cap reached => no siege fallback" gate for this caller rather than relying on the helper's category-specific parameters.

POST-WIP280 AI_chooseProduction — CROSS-ROOT / DUPLICATE CONTROL
---------------------------------------------------------------
The resumed production-call audit immediately re-encountered the inherited late
`UNITAI_MISSIONARY_SEA` request under financial trouble. This is not a fresh Queue-005
root. The same ordinary `AI_chooseProduction -> AI_chooseUnit(UNITAI_MISSIONARY_SEA)`
caller is already part of F340's proof that the generic carrier UnitAI validation can
select ships whose SpecialCargo cannot carry the requested missionary. Keep the
caller under F340; do not renumber it merely because the production branch itself
looks odd in isolation.

KI#197.11 REOPENED/BROADENED — SECURED NAVAL PRODUCTION SHARE IS MEASURED PER WATER AREA AGAINST AN EMPIRE-WIDE DENOMINATOR, SO MULTIPLE DISCONNECTED SEAS CAN EACH FORCE THE FULL 'EMPIRE' NAVAL PERCENTAGE
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS / CLASSIFICATION
-----------------------
CONFIRMED implementation mismatch inside the recently introduced KI#197.11 secured-
primary-area naval-floor feature. Reopen/broaden KI#197.11 rather than consume F521:
this is the same production-share floor, same configuration contract and same narrow
repair surface.

AUTHORITATIVE DECLARED CONTRACT
-------------------------------
Practical 6389 / commit `679d3f6b96e2c7e7eae819e002aac7de7ca3cc1e`, titled for
KI#197.11, introduced the secured land/naval split. The accompanying XML does not
describe a separate quota for every ocean. It explicitly defines the secured naval
curve as a minimum share of EMPIRE production:

    "Minimum secured-profile naval production share by era."

and the secured land curve as:

    "Minimum share of empire base production ..."

The naval documentation further says that the defaults complement the secured land
values so the TOTAL Medieval+ floor remains 20 / 30 / 35 / 40 / 40 on naval-heavy
maps, merely shifting part of that existing total from land attackers into usable
naval logistics.

The KI#197.11 Known-Issues explanation uses the same semantics: after a primary
landmass becomes secure, "part of the released land share is redirected" to invasion
transports / escorts / attack ships, and the land + naval curves preserve the same
total floor. This establishes one empire-production percentage, not N independent
full percentages for N disconnected water areas.

CURRENT IMPLEMENTATION
----------------------
Practical 6389 replaced the old global land-only helper with:

    SAS_getMilitaryProductionCapacityPercent(kPlayer, pNavalWaterArea, ...)

The denominator is always every productive city in the player empire:

    FOR_EACH_CITY(...)
        iBaseProduction = getBaseYieldRate(YIELD_PRODUCTION)
        iTotalBaseProduction += iBaseProduction

For the NAVAL call, however, the numerator accepts a producing city only when:

    pLoopCity->waterArea(true) == pNavalWaterArea &&
    SAS_isNavalOffensiveProductionAI(eProductionAI)

Thus:

    navalCapacity(this sea)
        = base production currently making Assault/Escort/Attack ships on THIS SEA
          / base production of ALL productive cities in the empire

Production of the same tracked naval roles on every other disconnected sea is absent
from the numerator while remaining present in the denominator.

`AI_chooseProduction` then compares that per-sea value directly against the XML
`iNavalTargetPercent` and may force another ship whenever:

    iNavalCapacityPercent < iNavalTargetPercent

Every city therefore evaluates the full empire percentage separately for whichever
`pWaterArea` it happens to use.

CLEAN CURRENT-DEFAULT NUMERIC WITNESS
-------------------------------------
Use an ordinary naval-heavy-map AI whose secured primary land area touches two
DISCONNECTED useful water areas, East and West. This is a normal map topology: one
continuous landmass can have ports on water bodies that cannot reach each other.

Take a Modern/Future secured-profile state with the current 20% naval target and ten
productive cities, each supplying 10 base Production. Total empire base production is
therefore 100.

Have at least two port cities on East and two on West. Before the two later cities
choose production:

    E1 is producing UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA / ESCORT_SEA / ATTACK_SEA: 10 base hammers
    W1 is producing one of the same tracked naval roles:             10 base hammers

The empire is already devoting:

    (10 + 10) / 100 = 20%

to exactly the secured naval roles. Under the declared empire-share contract, the
20% naval floor is satisfied.

Now E2 reaches the KI#197.11 block. Its helper call uses East as `pWaterArea`, so W1's
perfectly valid naval production disappears from the numerator:

    East reported naval capacity = 10 / 100 = 10% < 20%

The floor is therefore eligible and can force E2 into another tracked naval unit,
raising actual empire naval commitment to 30%.

When W2 later evaluates the same turn/production state, its West-only numerator sees
W1 but not E1/E2. In the simple equal-production shape it likewise remains below the
20% target and can force another tracked naval unit. The empire can now be committing
roughly 40% of its base production to the secured naval roles even though the XML
setting and KI#197.11 rationale call for a 20% empire share.

This is not an abstract many-ocean limit. Two disconnected coastal water areas are
sufficient. More independently productive seas can compound the same dimensional
mismatch further.

WHY THE PEACEFUL STOCK GUARD DOES NOT REPAIR THE SHARE MATH
-----------------------------------------------------------
The later practical-6391 stock guard is deliberately a separate anti-accumulation
brake. It stops the EXTRA secured naval floor only after the relevant water area has
reached:

    portCitiesInThisWaterArea * 5 tracked ships   [current default]

At the low-stock production-share fixture above, each two-port sea has a stock limit
of 10 tracked ships; one/few existing or queued ships are far below that threshold.
The stock guard therefore remains open while the duplicate production-share floor is
already forcing excess current production.

During actual war/assault projection the stock guard is intentionally disabled, so it
cannot serve as a general correction for the percentage denominator either.

The guard itself being water-area-local is reasonable because actual fleet stock and
reachable ports are geographically local. That does NOT imply the configured
production PERCENTAGE is local: its explicit contract says empire base production and
total secured floor.

BIRTH / ANCESTRY
----------------
This defect is born with KI#197.11 practical 6389. Before that commit the feature had
one global land-offense capacity numerator and one global empire-production
denominator. Practical 6389 generalized the helper so naval matches are restricted by
`pLoopCity->waterArea(true) == pNavalWaterArea` but retained the original empire-wide
denominator unchanged.

The same birth commit's XML and Known-Issues rationale establish that the new naval
percentage was intended to redirect part of the existing EMPIRE production share,
which makes the numerator/denominator scope mismatch locally provable rather than a
subjective naval-tuning preference.

Practical 6391 added the per-water stock guard after an empirical excessive-fleet case
but did not change the production-capacity numerator/denominator, so the multi-water
share defect remains in the current 20:00 source snapshot.

DEDUP / ROOT BOUNDARY
---------------------
No prior album entry was found for `SAS_getMilitaryProductionCapacityPercent` or this
per-water numerator / empire denominator mismatch.

Do NOT assign F521:
- KI#197.9 / .10 created and tuned the offensive production-capacity FLOOR itself;
- KI#197.11 changes that SAME floor after the primary landmass is secured, including
  the naval redirection whose percentage is wrong here;
- the narrow repair belongs in the same helper/feature and does not require changing
  any independent game-state architecture.

This is distinct from WIP279/KI#198: WIP279 concerns an empire-wide Worker COUNT cap
undoing an explicit AREA Worker minimum. The present issue is a dimensional mismatch
inside one percentage calculation for the secured naval floor.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
If `SAS_AI_CHOOSE_PRODUCTION_SECURED_NAVAL_OFFENSE_CAPACITY_*_PERCENT` is retained as
an EMPIRE production-share target (the current documentation), count all empire
production currently committed to the tracked secured naval roles in the numerator;
do not filter that production to the caller's one `pWaterArea` when comparing with the
empire-wide denominator.

Geographic water-area information can still be used AFTER the global shortage is
established to decide WHICH sea should receive the next ship and which role is most
useful there. The existing `SAS_rankNavalProductionUnitAIs`, port/stock guard and
`AI_chooseUnit` locality can provide that second-stage allocation.

Alternatively, if the desired design is genuinely one quota per disconnected sea,
then both numerator and denominator/configuration/documentation must be made local;
e.g. compare naval production on a water area against production capacity of cities
that can actually serve that water area. The current hybrid (local numerator / global
denominator while documenting an empire percentage) should not remain.

KI#194 REOPENED/BROADENED — CENTRAL SETTLER WATER-AREA REPAIR IGNORES `secondWaterArea()`, SO A COASTAL/ISTHMUS CAPITAL CAN STILL MISS WORTHWHILE ISLANDS REACHABLE THROUGH ITS OTHER SEA
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS / CLASSIFICATION
-----------------------
CONFIRMED incompleteness in the KI#194 repair helper. Keep this under KI#194 rather
than spend F521: the same central `SAS_getSettlerWaterArea` / Settler-site gate that
was added to stop reachable overseas sites from disappearing still drops another
ordinary reachable-water topology.

CURRENT WATER-AREA CONTRACT
---------------------------
For a land city/plot, `CvPlot::waterArea(bool)` scans adjacent passable water plots and
returns only the LARGEST adjacent water `CvArea` by tile count. `CvCity::waterArea`
just forwards to that helper.

AdvCiv/BBAI separately exposes:

    CvCity::secondWaterArea()
        -> CvPlot::secondWaterArea()

which returns the largest OTHER adjacent passable water area, explicitly excluding the
primary `waterArea()` result. Thus a normal coastal/isthmus/canal-style city can border
two disconnected usable seas. The engine models both; the second one is not an
unsupported geometry.

`CvPlayerAI::AI_getNumAdjacentAreaCitySites(...)` is likewise one-water-area-specific:
it counts cached city sites whose plots are adjacent to the ONE `CvArea` passed to it.
A valid site on the second sea is not recovered when the caller passes only the first.

KI#194 REPAIR BIRTH
-------------------
Practical 6066 / commit `6210495792304d589225485f197d8d8954f5fde4`, titled
"Fix AdvCiv-SAS Settler regressions blocking worthwhile island expansion (KI#179,
KI#194)", introduced:

    SAS_getSettlerWaterArea(CvCityAI const& kCity)

because the KI#181 final concrete Settler gate could report no water sites even though
existing Settler transports made a worthwhile island reachable.

The current helper is:

    pWaterArea = kCity.waterArea(true);
    if (pWaterArea != NULL && !team.AI_isWaterAreaRelevant(*pWaterArea))
        pWaterArea = NULL;
    if (pWaterArea == NULL)
    {
        pWaterArea = map.findBiggestArea(true);
        if (pWaterArea != NULL &&
            AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs(*pWaterArea, UNITAI_SETTLER_SEA) <= 0)
            pWaterArea = NULL;
    }
    return pWaterArea;

There is no `secondWaterArea()` test.

Practical 6066 deliberately changed BOTH `SAS_getSettlerBuildSiteStatus` (the final
concrete `AI_chooseUnit(UNITAI_SETTLE)` safety gate) and the surrounding broad
`AI_chooseProduction` water-site setup to use this shared result. The omission is
therefore centralized and deterministic rather than one caller being rescued by the
other.

CLEAN CURRENT-GAME REPRODUCTION
-------------------------------
Use a capital on a narrow isthmus whose city plot touches two passable disconnected
water areas:

    East = larger adjacent sea -> `waterArea(true)`
    West = smaller adjacent sea -> `secondWaterArea()`

Let both seas be strategically relevant. East contains no qualifying adjacent cached
city site. West contains a worthwhile revealed island site whose found value is above
`SAS_getSettlerBuildMinFoundValue`, and the player already owns a usable
`UNITAI_SETTLER_SEA` transport on West. Leave the capital's own land area without a
qualifying site, so the overseas opportunity is the reason to build the Settler.

Current execution:

1. `SAS_getSettlerWaterArea(capital)` obtains East because `waterArea(true)` chooses the
   larger adjacent sea.
2. East is relevant, so the helper keeps it and never enters the biggest-water
   fallback.
3. West / `secondWaterArea()` is never queried, despite the existing Settler transport
   and qualifying island there.
4. `AI_getNumAdjacentAreaCitySites(... East ...)` returns zero useful water sites.
5. `SAS_getSettlerBuildSiteStatus` therefore has no land site and no water site and
   returns false.
6. The broad `AI_chooseProduction` Settler-site quantities are built from the same
   helper, so the ordinary expansion logic is blind to West too.
7. Even if some other production path tries a concrete `UNITAI_SETTLE`, the final
   `SAS_isSettlerBuildWorthwhile` / site-status gate repeats the same omission and can
   reject it before the push.

The existing transport network and worthwhile island can therefore remain unused for
the same fundamental reason KI#194 was intended to fix: the production gate's chosen
water-area proxy does not represent all reachable adjacent overseas opportunities.

A second variant exists when the primary adjacent sea is irrelevant: the helper jumps
to the GLOBAL largest water area, not necessarily the city's valid second adjacent
sea. If the useful second sea is not that global largest area, it can still be missed.
The primary-relevant East/West fixture above is cleaner because it requires no fallback
subtlety.

WHY THIS IS KI#194, NOT F521
----------------------------
KI#194's documented root is specifically a mismatch where the new weak-site/Settler
production gate ignores a worthwhile island that existing Settler transports can
reach. Practical 6066's stated cure is a shared water-area helper so the broad
production logic and final concrete gate see the same reachable overseas opportunity.

This finding does not introduce a new cache, lifecycle or unrelated production rule.
It shows that the shared KI#194 helper still selects only one of multiple engine-
supported adjacent seas. The narrow repair modifies the same helper/site aggregation
and necessarily repairs both affected production layers together.

No prior cumulative album entry was found for a `secondWaterArea()` Settler-site
omission or this isthmus-capital variant.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Do not force one `CvArea*` to represent a potentially multi-water Settler opportunity.
For the build-worthwhile/site-status contract, evaluate all directly adjacent usable
water areas that the city can serve (at least `waterArea(true)` and
`secondWaterArea()`), and aggregate/count the qualifying adjacent-area sites without
double-counting the same site if it touches both seas.

For an inland city, preserve KI#194's existing-transport fallback to a non-adjacent
main sea; that is a different reachability case. A clean design would therefore be:

1. direct adjacent seas first (primary + second, each relevance/transport semantics as
   intended);
2. only when no direct sea can supply the opportunity, use the KI#194 inland/global
   fallback backed by existing Settler transport capacity.

If the production code still needs one water area for choosing/producing a
`UNITAI_SETTLER_SEA`, carry the best/selected opportunity's area separately from the
boolean "does any worthwhile reachable overseas site exist?" contract rather than
collapsing site existence to one arbitrary largest adjacent sea.

KI#193.2 REOPENED/BROADENED -- DOCKED ASSAULT TRANSPORTS AT A DUAL-COAST PORT ARE
MISSED WHEN THE TARGET SEA IS THAT PORT'S `secondWaterArea()`
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED INCOMPLETE REPAIR OF EXISTING KI#193.2; do not consume F521.

ROOT / CURRENT CODE
-------------------
KI#193.2 added a narrow target-backed assault-transport production request. Once a
specific overseas city has been selected through the producing city's relevant water
area, the repair deliberately calculates how much usable assault cargo space already
exists before asking for another transport.

The current actual-unit capacity scan is:

    FOR_EACH_UNITAI(pLoopUnit, kPlayer)
    {
        if (pLoopUnit->AI_getUnitAIType() != UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA)
            continue;
        CvCity const* pPortCity = pLoopUnit->getPlot().getPlotCity();
        if (!pLoopUnit->isArea(*pWaterArea) &&
            (pPortCity == NULL || pPortCity->waterArea() != pWaterArea))
        {
            continue;
        }
        iOpportunisticExistingCapacity += pLoopUnit->cargoSpace();
        iOpportunisticExistingTransports++;
    }

This correctly repaired the ordinary docked-ship problem: a sea unit in a city sits on
the city's LAND plot, so `pLoopUnit->isArea(*pWaterArea)` alone is false. But the port
fallback recognizes only the city's PRIMARY `waterArea()`.

The engine explicitly supports a second disconnected passable sea adjacent to a city:

    CvCity::waterArea(...)       -> CvPlot::waterArea(...)
    CvCity::secondWaterArea()    -> CvPlot::secondWaterArea()

`CvPlot::waterArea()` chooses the largest adjacent water area. `secondWaterArea()`
chooses the largest OTHER adjacent passable water area. `CvCity::sharedWaterArea()`
then explicitly considers all primary/second combinations when deciding whether two
cities share a usable water area. The second sea is therefore real engine topology,
not a diagnostic fiction.

The KI#193.2 target finder likewise already accepts a foreign coastal target whose
PRIMARY OR SECOND water area equals the concrete target water area:

    if (pTargetCity->waterArea(true) != &kWaterArea &&
        pTargetCity->secondWaterArea() != &kWaterArea)
    {
        continue;
    }

Thus the feature itself understands dual-coast connectivity on the TARGET side, while
its existing-capacity repair recognizes only the primary sea on the OWN-PORT side.

SHARED HELPER DOES NOT RESCUE THE COUNT
---------------------------------------
The following queued-capacity estimate uses inherited
`CvPlayerAI::AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs`:

    int const iWaterAreaTransports =
        kPlayer.AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs(*pWaterArea, UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA);
    iOpportunisticTrainingTransports =
        max(0, iWaterAreaTransports - iOpportunisticExistingTransports);

That helper is inherited all the way from BtS/BBAI -> K-Mod -> AdvCiv. Its special
city scan exists precisely to add ships docked on land city plots and the owner's
ships currently being trained. But it too requires:

    pLoopCity->waterArea() == &kArea

and never tests `secondWaterArea()`.

Consequently the same dual-coast port is absent from BOTH the exact actual-cargo scan
and the queued-ship augmentation. The second calculation cannot accidentally self-heal
the first omission.

CLEAN CURRENT-GAME REPRODUCTION
-------------------------------
Use two owned coastal cities and one worthwhile nearby overseas target:

    P = producing city. Its primary/relevant sea is West.
    Q = an isthmus / dual-coast owned port.
        Q's larger adjacent sea is East  -> Q.waterArea() / primary.
        Q's smaller adjacent sea is West -> Q.secondWaterArea().
    T = revealed worthwhile enemy/Barbarian overseas city reachable through West.

Let the normal KI#193.2 conditions pass at P: P is safe, the land area is not
AREAAI_DEFENSIVE, the target passes long-term retention / distance / attacker-strength
checks, and P can train an assault transport.

Dock at Q one `UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA` transport whose real cargo space is already enough
for the target-backed `iOpportunisticTargetCapacity`. A sea unit on Q's city plot can
leave Q into the adjacent West sea; the engine's second-water/shared-water topology is
exactly what represents that dual-coast connection.

Current evaluation at P:

1. `pWaterArea` is West.
2. `SAS_findNearbyOverseasConquestTarget(P, West, ...)` finds T.
3. Capacity scan reaches the docked transport at Q.
4. `transport.isArea(West)` is false because Q is a LAND city plot.
5. `Q.waterArea() == West` is false because Q's larger/primary sea is East.
6. The code never tests `Q.secondWaterArea() == West`, so the real cargo capacity is
   skipped.
7. `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs(West, UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA)` also ignores Q for the same
   primary-only city test.
8. `iOpportunisticExistingCapacity` can therefore remain below the target despite the
   already-usable docked transport.
9. `bOpportunisticAssaultTransportDemand` becomes true and P can order another assault
   transport solely because Q's connected port exposes West as its secondary sea.

This is the same duplicate-transport symptom that KI#193.2's docked-capacity follow-up
was specifically written to prevent, reached through an ordinary supported map shape
rather than malformed state.

DOCUMENTED CONTRACT / CLASSIFICATION
------------------------------------
KI#193.2 explicitly promises:

    "real transports at sea or docked in a connected port count by their actual cargo
     space, and ships currently being trained count by their expected cargo space"

and:

    "once enough existing or queued capacity is found, other cities do not duplicate
     the request"

A port whose `secondWaterArea()` is the selected target sea is a connected port under
the engine's own multi-water-area city topology. Therefore this is a direct incomplete
implementation of KI#193.2's existing capacity contract.

Birth/current lineage:
- practical 6065 / commit c54b256ece7dc339eb5420ad484bf9903c6c4022 introduced
  KI#193.2 and the current docked-capacity repair shape;
- the same birth code already used target `secondWaterArea()` when validating target
  reachability, but own docked capacity used only `pPortCity->waterArea()`;
- Base AdvCiv/K-Mod/BtS already have the primary-only
  `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` city augmentation, so the inherited helper shares the
  blind spot but did not create this SAS target-backed production promise.

Keep this under KI#193.2 rather than assigning F521. The narrow KI#193.2 repair owns the
exact selected-water-area capacity calculation and necessarily fixes this duplicate
request.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
For the target-specific actual-capacity scan, a docked transport belongs to the selected
`pWaterArea` when its port has that area as EITHER primary or second:

    bool bPortServesWater =
        pPortCity != NULL &&
        (pPortCity->waterArea() == pWaterArea ||
         pPortCity->secondWaterArea() == pWaterArea);

Then count actual cargo space when `unit.isArea(targetSea) || bPortServesWater`.

Queued capacity needs the same selected-sea semantics. Do NOT blindly change the shared
`AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` helper to count every dual-coast docked/training ship in BOTH
water areas without auditing all callers: one flexible docked ship cannot satisfy two
simultaneous independent deficits at once, so unconditional double attribution can
create the opposite overcount. A safer KI#193.2-local implementation can count queued
assault transports from ports that serve the selected sea, or a future shared helper can
make its allocation semantics explicit.

SHARED-HELPER AUDIT NOTE -- NOT YET F521
----------------------------------------
`CvPlayerAI::AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` is primary-water-only in BtS, K-Mod, Base
AdvCiv and current SAS. Current SAS has multiple callers that explicitly query/sum both
primary and second water areas for local Work Boat / Spy-transport decisions, so the
second water area is behaviorally meaningful. However the correct generic attribution
of a docked or queued ship at a dual-coast port is not simply "count it in both": that
could double-credit one flexible unit against simultaneous demands.

No independent generic helper root is therefore promoted from this observation yet.
Continue caller-by-caller and require a target/locality contract whose correct ownership
of the unit is unambiguous. KI#193.2 above meets that bar because one concrete target sea
has already been selected.

KI#197.6 REOPENED/BROADENED -- CORRECTED NAVAL-TRADE `<3` SEA-UNIT CAP STILL
MISSES SHIPS DOCKED AT A PORT WHERE THE RELEVANT SEA IS `secondWaterArea()`
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED INCOMPLETE REPAIR OF EXISTING KI#197.6; do not consume F521.

ROOT / CURRENT CODE
-------------------
KI#197.6 repaired AdvCiv's special naval-trade sea-explorer fallback. The inherited
branch deliberately ignores the ordinary sea-explorer target and may request a
`UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA` with 25% probability while the relevant sea has a tiny navy. The
repair changed the old physical-water-area count into an explicit count of actual
DOMAIN_SEA ships, including docked ships and ships being trained, and added an
unrevealed-water prerequisite.

The current decision computes one concrete `pWaterArea` for the producing city and then
counts:

    FOR_EACH_UNIT(pLoopUnit, kMember)
    {
        if (pLoopUnit->getDomainType() != DOMAIN_SEA)
            continue;
        if (&pLoopUnit->getArea() == pWaterArea)
            iSeaUnitsAtSea++;
        if (pLoopUnit->getPlot().waterArea() == pWaterArea)
            iSeaUnitsIncludingDocked++;
    }

    FOR_EACH_CITY(pLoopCity, kMember)
    {
        if (pLoopCity->waterArea() != pWaterArea)
            continue;
        ... count trained sea UnitAIs ...
    }

    iWaterUnits = iSeaUnitsIncludingDocked + iSeaUnitsTraining;
    bEnoughWaterUnits = (iWaterUnits >= 3);
    bSeaExplorerEligible =
        (pWaterArea->getNumUnrevealedTiles(getTeam()) > 0 && !bEnoughWaterUnits);

Both the actual-docked and training-city tests use only PRIMARY `waterArea()`.
`secondWaterArea()` is ignored.

The outer branch also uses:

    iSeaExplorersNow =
        AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs(*pWaterArea, UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA);

and requires `iSeaExplorersNow == 0`. As recorded in WIP283, the inherited helper's
city augmentation is primary-water-only too, so it does not rescue a secondary-sea
port.

CLEAN CURRENT-GAME REPRODUCTION
-------------------------------
Use:

    P = producing coastal city; P's relevant/primary sea is West.
    Q = owned isthmus / dual-coast port.
        Q.waterArea()       = East (larger primary sea)
        Q.secondWaterArea() = West (smaller disconnected sea)

Leave at least one West tile unrevealed and satisfy the ordinary naval-trade branch
conditions: P is not in danger, its area is not defensive, naval trade is available,
and the ordinary sea-explorer count for West is zero.

Dock THREE already-built DOMAIN_SEA ships in Q. They need not be explorer-role ships;
KI#197.6 deliberately retains the inherited safety cap of three actual sea-domain ships,
not three explorers. A ship on Q's city plot can move into adjacent West through the
engine's dual-coast city topology, so these are real sea units available to the relevant
West water area.

Current evaluation at P:

1. Each docked ship is physically on Q's LAND city plot, so
   `&ship.getArea() == West` is false.
2. `ship.getPlot().waterArea()` resolves Q's larger PRIMARY East sea, so it is not West.
3. The code never tests Q's `secondWaterArea() == West`.
4. `iSeaUnitsIncludingDocked` therefore receives 0 from all three usable ships.
5. With no West training orders, `iWaterUnits` remains 0 instead of the correct >=3.
6. `bEnoughWaterUnits` is false and the branch remains eligible as long as West has one
   unrevealed tile.
7. The inherited 25% roll can therefore request another `UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA` despite the
   already-satisfied three-ship safety cap.

No queued-ship attribution ambiguity is needed for this witness. Three actual ships are
already present and all can enter the selected West sea directly from Q.

BIRTH / DOCUMENTED CONTRACT
---------------------------
Practical 6090 / commit `1a80ca7cff...` introduced KI#197.6. Its patch replaces the
old `CvArea::getNumAIUnits(..., NO_UNITAI)` cap with the current explicit loops.
The birth implementation already used:

    pLoopUnit->getPlot().waterArea() == pWaterArea
    pLoopCity->waterArea() == pWaterArea

and therefore omitted second-water ports from day one.

KI#197.6's current documentation states that the corrected branch:

    "counts actual sea-domain ships associated with the relevant water area, including
     ships docked in coastal cities and sea-domain UnitAIs already being trained there"

and that every confirming choice had fewer than three corrected sea units.

A docked ship at a dual-coast city whose secondary sea is the concrete relevant water
area is associated with that sea under Civ4's engine topology. The primary-only test is
therefore an incomplete implementation of the same corrected cap, not a new strategic
policy.

CLASSIFICATION / DEDUP
----------------------
Keep this under KI#197.6, not F521.

- KI#197.6 owns the exact naval-trade `<3` corrected sea-unit safety cap and its docked /
  queued accounting.
- WIP283's KI#193.2 broadening concerns assault TRANSPORT CARGO CAPACITY for one selected
  conquest target. The same dual-coast topology exposes both, but their consumers and
  narrow repairs are separate feature-local accounting blocks.
- The inherited `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` primary-only city scan remains a shared audit
  note rather than a generic F521 root. The KI#197.6 actual decision proves its defect
  independently without relying on that helper.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
For KI#197.6's selected `pWaterArea`, count a docked sea unit when the city plot serves
that water area as either primary OR second. Likewise, if training orders are intended
to count as available to either directly adjacent sea, include training at a city whose
`waterArea()` or `secondWaterArea()` matches. The actual-ship witness should be repaired
even if queued-ship allocation is kept more conservative.

A helper local to this one selected sea can use a predicate such as:

    city.waterArea() == pWaterArea || city.secondWaterArea() == pWaterArea

Do not globally double-count dual-coast ships in every `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` caller
without deciding simultaneous-demand allocation semantics first.

C031-WIP285 — QUEUE 005 DEEP RE-AUDIT — KI#44.5 MANDATORY-CITIZEN FALLBACK GAP

STATUS
------
