KI#44.5 REOPENED/BROADENED — THE "UNLESS ABSOLUTELY NECESSARY" CITIZEN EXCEPTION
IS NOT IMPLEMENTED, AND THE RESULT DIRECTLY EXPLAINS THE RECORDED ASSIGNMENT ASSERT CASCADE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

CURRENT ROOT
------------
`CvCityAI::AI_addBestCitizen` still uses the inherited K-Mod chooser contract:

    int iBestValue = -1;
    ...
    if (isSpecialistValid(eLoopSpecialist, 1))
    {
        int iValue = AI_specialistValue(...);
        if (iValue > iBestValue)
            eBestSpecialist = eLoopSpecialist;
    }

`AI_specialistValue(..., bRemove=false)` delegates directly to:

    AI_jobChangeValue((specialist,new), (none,old), ...)

Current SAS then intercepts the engine default specialist (Citizen) at the start of
`AI_jobChangeValue` and, for every AI player, returns:

    SAS_AI_JOB_CHANGE_VALUE_AI_JOB_FORBIDDEN = -100000

The same effective block is enabled for human governor assignment when
`SAS_CONVENIENCE_HUMAN_NO_AUTO_CITIZEN_SPECIALIST` is enabled.

Because `-100000` can never satisfy `iValue > -1`, the default Citizen is not merely
"strongly disfavored". It is impossible for `AI_addBestCitizen` to select even when it
is the ONLY remaining legal job.

ENGINE DEFAULT-SPECIALIST CONTRACT
----------------------------------
`CvCity::isSpecialistValid` explicitly makes the default specialist unlimited:

    return (assigned + extra <= maxCount ||
            player.isSpecialistValid(eSpecialist) ||
            eSpecialist == eDefaultSpecialist);

Thus the default Citizen is the engine's unconditional sink for otherwise unassigned
population. Ordinary specialist slot limits do not apply to it.

The surrounding city code also relies on this fallback contract. For example,
`CvCity::alterSpecialistCount` can directly convert a removed non-default specialist to
the default specialist, and its later fallback branches call `AI_addBestCitizen` when a
citizen needs reassignment.

DIRECT ASSERT-CASCADE CONSEQUENCE
---------------------------------
`AI_assignWorkingPlots` first calls `verifyWorkingPlots()`, then repeatedly assigns every
remaining unassigned population:

    while (extraPopulation() > 0)
    {
        if (!AI_addBestCitizen(true, true))
        {
            FErrorMsg("failed to assign extra population");
            break;
        }
    }

It then similarly attempts any `extraSpecialists()` and ultimately asserts that no extra
population remains.

If every normal plot/specialist candidate is unavailable while extra population remains,
current SAS behaves as follows:

1. The default Citizen passes `isSpecialistValid(...,1)` because it is the default.
2. `AI_specialistValue(Citizen,...)` reaches `AI_jobChangeValue`.
3. The SAS Citizen guard returns -100000.
4. `AI_addBestCitizen` began from -1, so Citizen is never selected.
5. No plot or ordinary specialist wins either.
6. `AI_addBestCitizen` returns false.
7. `AI_assignWorkingPlots` emits exactly the already-recorded
   `failed to assign extra population` failure; remaining extra specialist / final
   population assertions can then cascade.

This gives a direct source explanation for the KI#44.5 Known-Issues note that had already
recorded the three-assert cascade while saying it was unknown whether the cascade was
caused by Citizen no longer being usable as a fallback.

ORDINARY CURRENT-GAME REACHABILITY
----------------------------------
A giant city is not required.

`CvCity::canWork` rejects a BFC plot when:

    kPlot.plotCheck(PUF_canSiege, getOwner()) != NULL

and rejects water plots while blockaded. Therefore ordinary war can suddenly remove
several formerly valid citizen jobs from a moderate-population city. `verifyWorkingPlots`
then removes those assignments.

Construct an ordinary AI city where:
- population was fully assigned before the tactical change;
- ordinary specialist slots are absent or already full;
- enemy siege-capable units occupy enough remaining BFC plots and/or naval blockade makes
  the water jobs unavailable so no unworked normal plot remains;
- at least one citizen consequently remains unassigned.

The default Citizen is still valid by engine rule and is precisely the last-resort job
that can absorb that population. Current SAS rejects it below `AI_addBestCitizen`'s -1
selection floor and therefore leaves population unassigned.

The same condition can also occur naturally in very large cities after ordinary workable
plots and limited specialist slots are exhausted, but the wartime plot-loss fixture is
cleaner and needs only moderate population.

ANCESTRY — THE REGRESSION BOUNDARY IS ESPECIALLY CLEAR
------------------------------------------------------
K-Mod and Base AdvCiv 1.14 have the same `AI_addBestCitizen` `iBestValue=-1` architecture,
but they do NOT contain SAS's unconditional Citizen early-return. The default specialist
receives ordinary `AI_jobChangeValue` valuation and remains selectable.

SAS practical 4919 / commit `fcf32edcd9...` first added the anti-Citizen gate. Crucially,
its birth implementation returned `1`, and the comment explicitly documented the intended
last-resort semantics:

    "This ensures that the AI will only pick it if literally no other valid option exists"

Because 1 > -1, that implementation preserved `AI_addBestCitizen`'s emergency fallback.

SAS practical 5130 / commit `710c78523c...` reintroduced/hardened the gate after it had
been lost and changed the Citizen result to a large negative forbidden value. The new
comment says "never *hire* a citizen" and the current define is -100000. No corresponding
change was made to `AI_addBestCitizen`'s -1 acceptance threshold or to provide a separate
last-resort fallback.

Thus practical 5130 converted a strong preference into an absolute impossibility while
leaving both the engine and the Known-Issues design language expecting an exception.

DOCUMENTED INTENT / CLASSIFICATION
----------------------------------
Keep this under KI#44.5, not F521.

The issue title itself is:

    "Disallow citizen specialist as it is a really bad choice (unless absolutely necessary)"

and its recorded cascade explicitly asks whether Citizen no longer being usable as a
fallback is the cause. The present deep pass answers that question: yes, the current
`-100000` guard removes the inherited fallback that practical 4919 originally preserved.

For human automated assignment, the same mechanism is also a sibling of KI#44.6 when
`SAS_CONVENIENCE_HUMAN_NO_AUTO_CITIZEN_SPECIALIST` is enabled. Manual assignment is a
separate path and need not be weakened.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Preserve the intended anti-Citizen policy for ordinary ranking, but restore the
"absolutely necessary" fallback explicitly.

A robust shape is:
1. rank normal workable plots and non-default specialists exactly as now;
2. do NOT let Citizen compete normally;
3. if and only if no normal candidate was selected and the default specialist is valid,
   assign one default Citizen as the terminal fallback.

This is safer than simply returning `1` again from `AI_jobChangeValue`, because the
current code now has many more job-comparison/juggling callers than the original practical
4919 change; a dedicated fallback in `AI_addBestCitizen` keeps Citizen out of ordinary
swap/value competition while preserving population conservation.

For human auto-assignment with the convenience define enabled, the same terminal fallback
should apply only when leaving population unassigned would otherwise be necessary. Manual
Citizen choices remain untouched.

KI#197 REOPENED/BROADENED — POWER-PER-CITY CATCH-UP COUNTS VASSAL POWER BUT NOT VASSAL CITIES
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
The KI#197 under-strength catch-up computes the city-weighted rival average through:

    iRivalPower = kRival.getPower(true);
    iRelevantRivalPower += iRivalPower;
    iRelevantRivalCities += kRival.getNumCities();
    rivalPowerPerCity = 100 * iRelevantRivalPower / iRelevantRivalCities;

The numerator and denominator describe different populations whenever a relevant free rival has
vassals.

`CvTeam::getPower(true)` explicitly sums:
- every member of `kRival`, AND
- every living player that is a vassal of `kRival`.

`CvTeam::getNumCities()` returns that team's own `m_iNumCities`. City creation/destruction updates
`changeNumCities` on the city's owning team; it does not fold vassal cities into the master's
stored city count.

Therefore the current metric can divide master+vassal coalition power by MASTER-ONLY cities.

DOCUMENTED FEATURE CONTRACT
---------------------------
KI#197 and practical 6087 describe the new signal as:

    "power per city"
    "city-weighted average power per city of relevant rivals"

with the explicit rationale that military density, rather than raw total army size, should drive
catch-up. The implementation's mixed coalition numerator / master-only denominator violates that
unit of measure.

CLEAN CURRENT-GAME REPRODUCTION
-------------------------------
Use one relevant free rival master M with a normal living vassal V:

    M: 5 cities, 500 power
    V: 5 cities, 500 power

Let our team A have:

    A: 5 cities, 600 power

Both coherent interpretations say A is NOT under-strength per city:

1. compare free teams only:
       M own density = 500 / 5 = 100
       A density     = 600 / 5 = 120

2. compare the rival master/vassal coalition as one threat:
       M+V density = (500 + 500) / (5 + 5) = 100
       A density   = 600 / 5 = 120

Current code instead evaluates:

       rival numerator   = M.getPower(true) = 1000
       rival denominator = M.getNumCities() = 5
       reported density  = 200

and therefore invents:

       100 - (100 * 120 / 200) = 40% power-per-city deficit

for A, despite A actually having the higher military density.

With ordinary KI#197 gates satisfied (not in financial/economy suppression, not waiting for
better units, war possible, inherited high-power throttle inactive), that false deficit raises
`AI_buildUnitProb` by up to 40% multiplicatively in this fixture. KI#197.8 can then add its
separate affordable absolute response from the same false deficit, making the state-changing
production bias stronger.

REACHABILITY
------------
No malformed scenario or unusual API state is needed. Voluntary vassals and capitulated vassals
are ordinary supported game states, and the KI#197 loop intentionally iterates FREE relevant rival
teams, i.e. precisely the master team from which `getPower(true)` can pull vassal power.

ANCESTRY / CLASSIFICATION
-------------------------
The inherited K-Mod/Base-AdvCiv high-power throttle already used `kRival.getPower(true)` to value
how strong the rival threat is in TOTAL. Practical 6087 / commit `6c8d14b04e...` reused that same
value while adding the new power-PER-CITY average, then paired it with `kRival.getNumCities()`.
Thus the mismatch was born with the SAS KI#197 density feature; it is not a stock BtS/K-Mod
power-counting bug.

Keep this under KI#197, not F521. KI#197 owns the exact under-strength power-per-city metric;
KI#197.8 merely adds a second response from that metric and therefore inherits the bad input.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Make numerator and denominator describe the same population.

Two coherent designs are available:

A. FREE-TEAM DENSITY:
   - use `kRival.getPower(false)` with `kRival.getNumCities()`.
   - This compares each free rival team's own military density and leaves vassal strength to the
     inherited total-threat throttle.

B. MASTER/VASSAL-COALITION DENSITY:
   - keep `kRival.getPower(true)`;
   - add the living vassal players' city counts to the denominator as well.
   - This treats the master locus as one military coalition consistently.

Because the inherited high-power target deliberately includes vassal power, coalition density may
fit the surrounding threat model better, but the policy choice should be explicit. Do not keep the
current mixed population.

KI#53.3 BROADENING — A CONCRETE SIEGE VETO CAN SUPPRESS A LEGAL SAME-ROLE ALTERNATIVE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This pass does NOT spend F521. It identifies a same-feature weakness in the centralized
KI#53/KI#53.3 production-cap architecture.

Current role-selection path:

    AI_chooseUnit(UnitAI)
        -> AI_bestUnitAI(UnitAI)        // selects exactly one concrete UnitTypes
        -> AI_chooseUnit(UnitTypes, UnitAI)
             -> SAS concrete composition/cap checks
             -> pushOrder only if selected concrete unit survives

If the concrete unit is rejected, `AI_chooseUnit(UnitAI)` returns false immediately. It does
not retry the second-best trainable unit for the same UnitAI role.

Current shipped ATTACK_CITY control:
* `UNIT_TREBUCHET` and `UNIT_CATAPULT` are both ordinary no-resource
  `UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY` candidates.
* Trebuchet has +100% city attack and 16 bombard versus Catapult 0% city attack and
  8 bombard, so K-Mod's inherited `AI_unitValue(..., UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY, ...)` can rank
  Trebuchet first. Existing stored Trebuchet production can make that selection especially
  strong because `AI_bestUnitAI` explicitly discounts remaining production cost.
* Catapult remains a positive candidate under the inherited ATTACK_CITY valuation; the
  raw value difference does not inherently remove it from the best-unit candidate set.
* KI#53.3's later concrete gate can nevertheless reject the chosen Trebuchet through
  `TREBUCHET_SHARE_CAP` while the same Trebuchet-specific condition does not reject a
  Catapult.
* The role request then returns false instead of considering Catapult.

Live caller consequence:
The advc.300 Barbarian-city attacker branch explicitly computes a needed
`UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY` count and calls `AI_chooseUnit(UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY)` when below that
quota. A Trebuchet-first / Trebuchet-cap state can therefore make that request fail even
though a legal Catapult could satisfy the requested city-attacker role. The generic early
city-hunting ATTACK_CITY branch has the same shape.

Important negative control — not a hard KI#197.9 floor failure:
The newer offensive production-capacity floor uses `AI_chooseLeastRepresentedUnit` with
both `UNITAI_ATTACK` and `UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY`. That helper retries the next UnitAI when the
first role fails. Catapult is also a valid ATTACK candidate and its city-attack disadvantage
no longer helps Trebuchet in that role. Thus this pass does not prove that the hard empire
offensive-production floor collapses merely because ATTACK_CITY's preferred Trebuchet is
vetoed.

CLASSIFICATION / INTENT
-----------------------
Keep under KI#53.3 rather than allocate F521.

The parent KI#53 documentation explicitly says:

    "The 'best unit' picker remains the same; only the final 'should we actually queue it?'
     logic is centralized."

KI#53.3 intentionally accepts some siege underproduction as a tradeoff while suppressing
Trebuchet/siege excess. Current source also explicitly describes Catapults as a more
versatile valid alternative in some early no-resource compositions. The no-retry behavior
therefore looks like an architectural weakness of the same post-selection cap feature,
not a separate gameplay subsystem/root.

Conservative improvement:
Do not weaken the Trebuchet or all-siege caps. When the selected concrete unit is rejected
solely by a KI#53 composition/cap rule, allow the role chooser to consider the remaining
`AI_bestUnitAI` candidates for that same UnitAI, in descending value order, until one
survives or none do. Preserve random/production valuation semantics carefully; avoid a
blanket retry after unrelated failures such as role-level strategic vetoes or odds failure.

POST-WIP287 INHERITED-METHOD SATURATION CONTROLS
------------------------------------------------
1. `AI_getYieldMultipliers` is semantically identical to Base AdvCiv 1.14; current SAS only
   collapsed the function signature onto one line. Its dangerous-looking reciprocal/divisor
   chain does not produce a current zero divisor under shipped data: city yield multipliers
   remain positive under current modifiers and the player-average getters assert/rebuild
   positive values. The old ordinary `ExtraYieldThreshold` projected-yield `>`/`>=` shape
   is also data-dead in current SAS because Financial now uses only
   `ExtraYieldNaturalThreshold` and every shipped ordinary `ExtraYieldThreshold` is zero.

2. `AI_healthHappyImprovementValue` contains a real inherited AdvCiv receiver bug, but it is
   CURRENT-SAS MASKED and therefore does not spend F521. The `advc.901` loop says that other
   affected team cities matter, finds `pCity`, but then calls the helper again on `this`
   instead of on `pCity`. With its default `bIgnoreOtherCities=true`, each neighbor therefore
   contributes another copy of the evaluating city's marginal health/happiness value. The bug
   was introduced in AdvCiv practical 1732 (`d595a1df9e...`, "Health tag for improvements;
   merge xml-tags-as-enums branch."). Current Forest Preserve (+1 happiness) makes the
   arithmetic visibly wrong in Base AdvCiv: e.g. a happy-surplus city can value +1 at about
   5-6 while a neighboring city at the happiness boundary values it at about 600-800, yet
   current code duplicates the first city's value. Current SAS, however, deliberately returns
   zero from `AI_getImprovementValue` for every LAND plot and delegates authoritative land
   Worker choices to the custom `CvUnitAI::AI_bestCityBuild`; current WATER improvements have
   no happiness/health source. Thus the source defect is live in Base AdvCiv architecture but
   lacks an authoritative current-SAS gameplay producer. Preserve as a masked upstream note;
   do not report it as F521. A future repair is `pCity->AI_healthHappyImprovementValue(...)`
   with recursion suppressed.

3. `AI_emphasizeIrrigatingPlot`, `AI_buildingSeaYieldChangeWeight` and
   `AI_finalImprovementYieldDifference` were re-read as inherited low-coverage helpers. No
   independent current contract failure survived. In particular, the land-improvement path
   containing the irrigation helper is largely superseded by SAS's custom land Worker
   evaluator, while sea-yield weighting remains internally consistent with its K-Mod caller.

F521 / KI#844 — CONFIRMED
ADVC EARLY FEATURE-CLEAR TECH BONUS COMPARES PLOT `PlayerTypes` OWNER TO CITY OBJECT ID,
SO `AI_countOvergrownBonuses` ALWAYS RETURNS ZERO AND THE BLOCKED-RESOURCE TECH BONUS IS DEAD
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED current SAS gameplay/AI valuation defect.
Inherited from Base AdvCiv; not present in BtS/Civ4CE or K-Mod because the
`advc.129` blocked-resource tech-value helper is an AdvCiv addition.

ROOT
----
Current `CvCityAI::AI_countOvergrownBonuses(FeatureTypes eFeature)` scans the city radius
for an owned, unimproved feature tile containing a resource that could be improved once the
feature is removed. Its ownership gate is:

    if (p.getOwner() == getID() && p.getFeatureType() == eFeature && !p.isImproved())

The two sides are DIFFERENT ID DOMAINS:

    p.getOwner()   -> PlayerTypes
    getID()        -> CvCity object ID

The intended receiver is plainly the city's owner:

    p.getOwner() == getOwner()

This is not a numerically-accidental player/city coincidence in the current engine.
`CvPlayer::initCity` allocates cities from `FFreeListTrashArray` and passes
`pCity->getID()` into `CvCity::init`. `FFreeListTrashArray::init` starts
`m_iCurrentID = FLTA_MAX_BUCKETS`, and:

    FLTA_ID_SHIFT   = 13
    FLTA_MAX_BUCKETS = 1 << 13 = 8192

The first allocated object receives:

    m_iCurrentID + iIndex >= 8192

whereas current SAS has:

    MAX_CIV_PLAYERS = 48
    BARBARIAN_PLAYER = 48
    MAX_PLAYERS = 49

Thus an ordinary plot owner is 0..48 while every ordinary generated city ID is at least
8192. `p.getOwner() == getID()` is therefore impossible. The helper returns zero for every
ordinary city regardless of how many qualifying blocked resources actually exist.

LIVE CONSUMER / AUTHORED PURPOSE
--------------------------------
`CvPlayerAI::AI_techValue` contains the only current gameplay caller. While the player has
at most two cities, whenever the technology being evaluated removes a feature it does:

    FOR_EACH_CITYAI(c, *this)
        iBuildValue += 30 * c->AI_countOvergrownBonuses(eFeature);

The surrounding source comment states the intended rule explicitly:

    "Very early game: Is the feature blocking a resource?
     (especially Silver, which can now appear on Grassland Forest)"

So one qualifying blocked resource is deliberately worth +30 tech-value points; two are
+60, etc. The broken ownership comparison removes that entire authored term for every AI.
This feeds normal `AI_techValue` / `AI_bestTech` research ranking, so it is not diagnostic
or UI-only state.

DETERMINISTIC CURRENT-SAS DATA WITNESS — FOREST SILVER / MASONRY
----------------------------------------------------------------
The original AdvCiv comment discussed Bronze Working, but current SAS's reworked build techs
move ordinary Forest removal to Masonry. The same generic helper therefore remains fully
live with an updated current-data witness.

Current shipped facts:

    BONUS_SILVER
        TechReveal = NONE
        can occur on FEATURE_FOREST + TERRAIN_GRASS

    IMPROVEMENT_MINE
        BonusTypeStruct includes BONUS_SILVER with bBonusMakesValid=1

    BUILD_MINE
        PrereqTech = TECH_MINING
        FEATURE_FOREST removal PrereqTech = TECH_MASONRY

    TECH_MINING  era = ERA_ANCIENT
    TECH_MASONRY era = ERA_ANCIENT

Use any ordinary non-Barbarian AI with one or two cities and a Silver resource on an owned
Grassland Forest tile in a city radius, without an improvement. Let Mining already be known
and evaluate Masonry while still in the Ancient era.

During `AI_techValue(TECH_MASONRY)`:

1. The Feature loop sees that a Build removes `FEATURE_FOREST` at Masonry and enters the
   blocked-resource valuation block.
2. For that city, the Silver/Forest plot satisfies the intended semantic conditions:
   owned by this player, Forest, unimproved, visible Silver.
3. The inner Build scan can use `BUILD_MINE`: Mine makes Silver valid, and its ordinary
   prerequisite Mining is Ancient/current-era-compatible.
4. Correct `AI_countOvergrownBonuses(FEATURE_FOREST)` therefore includes this plot once.
5. Correct Masonry `iBuildValue` gains +30.
6. Current code first tests `PlayerTypes owner == city object ID >=8192`, which is false.
7. Current count is 0 and Masonry receives +0 from the entire feature.

The error therefore deterministically removes 30 valuation points per qualifying resource.
`AI_bestTech` chooses among technologies from this score, so the defect can alter early
research order precisely in the resource-blocking situation that `advc.129` introduced the
bonus to correct.

ANCESTRY
--------
BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod do not contain `AI_countOvergrownBonuses` / the corresponding
blocked-resource +30 tech-value feature.

AdvCiv practical 1389, commit:

    5c007429ae034192cad8bf8032bf499970255ff3
    "Some AI tweaks concerning ships; Japan added to EuroWorld scenario"

introduced the helper under the old name `AI_countBonusesToClear` and the +30-per-city call
in `AI_techValue`. The very first implementation already contained:

    p->getOwnerINLINE() == getID()

so the wrong receiver/domain is a birth defect in the feature, not a later SAS regression.

Practical 1910 (`32028ef437...`, "CityPlotIterator (refactor city radius loops)") renamed it
to `AI_countOvergrownBonuses` and replaced the raw plot loop with `CityPlotIter`, but
preserved the same `p.getOwner() == getID()` condition. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS
still retain it.

The reachable AdvCiv log describes the intended feature as:

    "Increased AI tech value for Bronze Working when a Forest blocks a resource near the
     capital (e.g. Silver or Pig). [advc.129]"

Current SAS's Masonry-based Forest-removal tech tree changes the concrete tech in the
witness, not the helper's generic purpose.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
Full album / Known-Issue searches for `AI_countOvergrownBonuses`, overgrown/blocked bonus,
city-ID vs plot-owner, and the nearby-resource tech bonus found no existing root for this
helper.

This is independent of:
* F165/KI#488, which concerns SAS cautious-health scoring dropping Forest/Jungle HEALTH when
  the plot contains a visible bonus;
* Worker/job-demand and KI#198/KI#213 families, which concern improving resources after a
  technology is known rather than valuing the technology that unlocks feature removal;
* the Queue-004 player-vs-team/ID-domain findings, which involve different objects and
  callers.

The narrow repair for those roots does not change this impossible CityID/PlayerID equality.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Replace the wrong ownership receiver only:

    p.getOwner() == getOwner()

Do not broaden the radius, resource eligibility, early-game `getNumCities() <= 2` gate,
+30 weight, build prerequisite approximation or feature-removal policy as part of this fix.
Those are deliberate heuristic choices and can be tuned independently.

Suggested regression check:
1. Create an AI player with <=2 cities and one owned unimproved Forest Silver in a city BFC.
2. Assert `AI_countOvergrownBonuses(FEATURE_FOREST) == 1` after the ownership fix.
3. Add/remove a second qualifying blocked resource and assert the helper follows 2/1.
4. Compare `AI_techValue` for the current Forest-removal tech and verify the resource term
   changes by exactly 30 per qualifying plot before later/randomized ranking terms.
5. Run the same fixture for a nonzero player slot to ensure no ID-domain coincidence is
   involved.

F522 / KI#845 -- ADVC PRACTICAL 1675 CHANGED HIGH-PRODUCTION EMPHASIS FROM
CLEARING OLD AI EMPHASIS TO FREEZING IT, SO STALE COMMERCE/RESEARCH EMPHASIS
CAN OVERRIDE THE SPECIAL-PRODUCTION GOVERNOR DURING WORKER/SETTLER/WONDER BUILDS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED current gameplay bug. Inherited by current SAS from Base AdvCiv.
The semantic regression was introduced by AdvCiv practical 1675,
commit `fedca1cf525955e008cfd75ce5ae3dd68de17570`, titled
`Remove pure virtual functions from CvCity`.

ROOT / PRE-REGRESSION CONTRACT
------------------------------
`CvCityAI::AI_doEmphasize` is legacy K-Mod/BBAI governor state. Its own comment says
emphasis is clumsy, has mostly been replaced by `AI_specialYieldMultiplier`, and ideally
AI cities should never need emphasis.

Immediately BEFORE practical 1675, the loop had this effective shape:

    bool bEmphasize = false;
    if (AI_specialYieldMultiplier(YIELD_PRODUCTION) < 50)
    {
        ... possibly set bEmphasize = true ...
    }
    AI_setEmphasize(eEmphasize, bEmphasize);

Therefore a special-production state of 50 or more explicitly executed
`AI_setEmphasize(..., false)` for every Emphasize type. Any old Commerce/Research/GP
emphasis was cleared before the city continued operating under the newer special-yield
system.

PRACTICAL-1675 REGRESSION
-------------------------
Practical 1675 mechanically flattened/refactored `CvCityAI` while removing pure virtual
functions. In the same hunk it changed that control flow to:

    bool bEmphasize = false;
    if (AI_specialYieldMultiplier(YIELD_PRODUCTION) >= 50)
        continue;
    ...
    AI_setEmphasize(eEmphasize, bEmphasize);

That is not equivalent. `continue` skips the setter entirely, changing:

    high special-production -> CLEAR old emphasis

to:

    high special-production -> KEEP/FREEZE whatever emphasis bit was already set.

The commit title/log is a structural refactor, not an authored AI-policy change that
explains this semantic reversal. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the post-1675
`continue` shape.

NORMAL PRODUCER / LIFETIME
--------------------------
The stale state is ordinary and is consumed before any repair:

1. While pursuing a technology for which `AI_isFirstTech` is true, `AI_doEmphasize`
   enables `EMPHASIZE_COMMERCE` (and, for a sufficiently high-ranked city, Research).
   The inherited EmphasizeInfo data gives `EMPHASIZE_COMMERCE` +1 Commerce yield
   emphasis.
2. `AI_setEmphasize(true)` persists that bit/count and immediately calls
   `AI_assignWorkingPlots`.
3. Later production can switch to a Worker, Settler or Work Boat; World Wonder/project
   production also creates the high-production mode.
4. At the next citizen-assignment pass, `AI_updateSpecialYieldMultiplier()` is called
   BEFORE citizen values are evaluated. Worker/Settler/Worker-Sea production contributes
   +50 Production and -25 Commerce before the rest of the special-yield adjustments.
5. The OLD emphasis bit is still present while this new special-production multiplier is
   consumed by `AI_yieldValue` / `AI_plotValue` / `AI_jobChangeValue`.
6. Only later, in `CvCity::doTurn -> CvCityAI::AI_doTurn -> AI_doEmphasize`, would old
   code have cleared emphasis. Current code instead `continue`s when Production special
   multiplier >=50 and preserves it again.

A current normal way to cross 50 despite advc.121 inertia is a Production-flavor leader.
Current `LEADER_FREDERICK` has `FLAVOR_PRODUCTION=10`, which contributes +25 special
Production. During Worker production the raw pre-inertia production special value is at
least 75 in an otherwise neutral setup. If the old value has converged near the
pre-Worker +25 state, successive updates are approximately:

    first Worker update:  (75 + ~24) / 2 = 49
    second Worker update: (75 + 49)  / 2 = 62

Thus a multi-turn Worker normally reaches the >=50 freeze. Keeping the first-discovery
research state through the first Worker turn preserves the emphasis until that point; if
research then completes during the later player economic phase, the subsequent city
`AI_doEmphasize` cannot clear it because the >=50 `continue` fires first.

DETERMINISTIC CURRENT-DATA CITIZEN FLIP
---------------------------------------
Use a Worker-producing AI city in the simple normalized state below:

- current Production special multiplier = 62;
- current Commerce special multiplier = -25 (the Worker contribution; avoid unrelated
  strategy shifts for the fixture);
- base and empire-average yield multipliers = 100;
- no extra production modifier;
- 100% Research slider;
- Research AI commerce weight = current XML/default 105;
- no happiness-driven hammer divisor relevant here (Worker is food-production);
- compare two ordinary current plot yields:

    A: Plains + Forest = 1 food, 2 hammers, 0 commerce
    B: Plains + Village = 1 food, 1 hammer, 3 commerce

Current XML supports exactly those components:
- Plains = 1F/1H;
- Forest = +1H;
- Village = +3 Commerce.

Because Worker production is food-production, the 1 food is also counted into production
value. With the normal base production value 8 and base commerce value 4:

NO STALE COMMERCE EMPHASIS (the pre-1675 intended high-production state)

    A raw production value = (1F + 2H) * 8 = 24
      after +62% special Production = floor(24 * 162 / 100) = 38

    B raw production value = (1F + 1H) * 8 = 16
      after +62% special Production = floor(16 * 162 / 100) = 25

    B raw weighted Research commerce:
      floor(105 * 300 * 4 / 10000) = 12
      after -25% special Commerce = floor(12 * 75 / 100) = 9

    B total = 25 + 9 = 34

Therefore the intended high-production governor prefers:

    Plains Forest 38 > Plains Village 34.

CURRENT STALE `EMPHASIZE_COMMERCE`

`AI_yieldValue` applies Commerce emphasis BEFORE the special-yield multipliers:
- Production value is reduced to 75%;
- Commerce value is raised to 140%.

    A: floor(24 * 75 / 100) = 18
       floor(18 * 162 / 100) = 29

    B production: floor(16 * 75 / 100) = 12
                  floor(12 * 162 / 100) = 19

    B commerce: floor(12 * 140 / 100) = 16
                floor(16 * 75 / 100) = 12

    B total = 19 + 12 = 31

The stale legacy emphasis therefore reverses the citizen preference:

    Plains Village 31 > Plains Forest 29.

This is not just a standalone-value illustration. `AI_juggleCitizens` fills its worked
and unworked job lists with `AI_plotValue`, sorts them by those values, and when the
candidate outranks the worked plot performs the final `AI_jobChangeValue` comparison
under the SAME emphasis/special-yield state. Both fixture plots supply equal food, so the
starvation guard does not block the swap.

GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCE
--------------------
The obsolete legacy Commerce emphasis can therefore make a city work a more commercial
plot instead of the higher-hammer plot while the newer special-yield system is explicitly
trying to emphasize Production for Worker/Settler/Wonder/project completion. The wrong
assignment can persist for the whole high-production order because every later
`AI_doEmphasize` call freezes the stale bit again rather than clearing it.

ANCESTRY
--------
- K-Mod / pre-practical-1675 AdvCiv: high special Production did not evaluate new emphasis
  but still reached `AI_setEmphasize(..., false)`, clearing old state.
- AdvCiv practical 1675 / `fedca1cf52`: broad CvCity pure-virtual/refactor commit inserts
  the `>=50 -> continue` shape, unintentionally changing the lifetime semantics.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14: retains the regression.
- Current AdvCiv-SAS 20:00 source: retains the same `continue` and the same live emphasis
  consumers, with current Worker/Settler production and Production-flavor data providing
  an ordinary producer.

DEDUP / ROOT SEPARATION
-----------------------
This is independent of:
- KI#44.5: missing terminal default-Citizen fallback / population conservation;
- KI#70: forced-specialist target sanitation;
- KI#34/KI#40/KI#320: SAS food-vs-hammer citizen valuation tuning;
- the low-impact direct-Artist-culture per-turn cache note;
- F501/KI#824: player COMMERCE SLIDER scheduling before zero-anarchy civic/religion
  changes. F522 concerns persistent CITY EMPHASIS bits inside citizen valuation.
No prior album root owns practical-1675's high-production emphasis clear->freeze
semantic regression.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Restore the old state-transition contract without reviving legacy emphasis during strong
special-production modes. For example, before skipping the detailed emphasis evaluation,
explicitly clear any active AI emphasis entries:

    if (AI_specialYieldMultiplier(YIELD_PRODUCTION) >= 50)
    {
        AI_setEmphasize(eLoopEmphasize, false);
        continue;
    }

However, note that `AI_setEmphasize` triggers `AI_assignWorkingPlots` on every actual
change. A more efficient implementation should preferably clear all relevant bits/counts
through a batched helper and perform one assignment refresh, or restructure `AI_doEmphasize`
so `bEmphasize=false` still reaches the common setter as before practical 1675.
Preserve the authored special-yield system; do not weaken the >=50 production threshold.

REGRESSION TEST
---------------
1. Give an AI city Commerce emphasis from a first-discovery research state.
2. Start a multi-turn Worker under a Production-flavor leader/state until
   `AI_specialYieldMultiplier(PRODUCTION) >= 50`.
3. End/replace the first-discovery condition while Worker production remains active.
4. Assert after `AI_doEmphasize` that stale AI Commerce/Research emphasis is false.
5. In the normalized Plains-Forest vs Plains-Village fixture above, assert that the
   Worker-production assignment favors the Forest under the special-production state.

POST-WIP289 INHERITED-HELPER CONTROLS
-------------------------------------
1. `AI_neededCultureDefenders` was challenged against the current revolt/culture-defense
   arithmetic. No independent divisor/object/sentinel mismatch survived.

2. `AI_updateRouteToCity`'s apparently inverted path condition is intentional: it seeks a
   same-area team city that is NOT already connected by the best currently available route.
   The path predicate therefore expresses the missing-route target rather than a reversed
   success test. No F523.

3. `AI_estimateReligionBuildings` remains approximate but its owner/team orientation is
   coherent with the Apostolic-Palace / religion-building valuation caller. No wrong-owner
   root survived.

4. `AI_getEmphasizeCommerceCount()` is poorly named/typed: it returns
   `(m_aiEmphasizeCommerceCount[eCommerce] > 0)` despite its `int` return type, whereas the
   Yield sibling returns the raw count. Current whole-DLL callers use it only through the
   Boolean `AI_isEmphasizeCommerce` contract (plus nonnegative assertions), and ordinary
   toggling does not expose a consumer that needs magnitude. Preserve as API/clarity debt,
   not F523.

5. `AI_growthValuePerFood` uses `std::partial_sort(..., std::less_equal<int>())` for the
   worst worked jobs. `less_equal` is not a strict weak ordering and is formally invalid for
   the standard sorting contract, especially when equal-valued jobs occur. No deterministic
   current gameplay failure was established in this pass, so preserve as C++ robustness /
   portability debt rather than a numbered root.

6. `AI_countNumImprovableBonuses` can pass `NO_TECH` from a bonus `TechCityTrade=NONE` to
   `CvTeam::isHasTech`, but the team accessor deliberately treats `NO_TECH` as true. Current
   seafood entries therefore exercise a supported sentinel contract rather than an invalid
   lookup. No F523.

7. `AI_neededAirDefenders` can distribute zero local need to every city when all floating-
   defender weights are zero even though the empire-wide desired fighter count is positive.
   This does not make existing `UNITAI_DEFENSE_AIR` units inert: `AI_defenseAirMove` still
   reaches `MISSION_AIRPATROL` whenever interception is possible. Keep as documented
   allocation approximation, not a correctness root.

8. `AI_playerCloseness` is a genuine per-turn cache whose inputs (city set, populations and
   positions) can change later in the same turn through founding/capture. Current proven
   consumers in this pass are heuristic threat/staging/assault weights rather than a hard
   legality/accounting contract, and K-Mod deliberately designed this family as a per-turn
   performance cache. Preserve as a cache-granularity audit note unless a harder consumer is
   found; do not merge it into F515/F516/F519/F520 without a distinct proven consequence.

F523 / KI#846 -- CONFIRMED
K-MOD/BBAI `AI_stealPlots` NEVER RELEASES A SHARED-PLOT WORKING-CITY OVERRIDE WHEN
THE CULTURAL-VICTORY CITY THAT STOLE IT LATER LOSES ITS SPECIAL IMPORTANCE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED current gameplay/state-lifetime defect.
Inherited from the BBAI/K-Mod city-importance/plot-stealing feature; present in K-Mod,
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS. Stock BtS/Civ4CE does not contain this
`AI_stealPlots` feature.

ROOT
----
Every AI city calls `AI_stealPlots()` during `CvCityAI::AI_doTurn`.

Current `AI_getCityImportance(true, false)` returns a positive value only when:
- the owner is currently at Culture victory stage 3; and
- this city currently ranks within the number of cities required for Cultural Victory.

Current shipped Cultural Victory requires 3 culture cities.

When importance is positive, `AI_stealPlots` may reserve a same-owner shared BFC plot for
this city:

    if (iImportance > pWorkingCity->AI_getCityImportance(true, false))
        kPlot.setWorkingCityOverride(this);

The cleanup, however, is unrelated to the priority that created the override:

    if (kPlot.getWorkingCityOverride() == this &&
        kPlot.getOwner() != getOwner())
    {
        kPlot.setWorkingCityOverride(NULL);
    }

Thus the override is cleared only when plot ownership stops matching the city owner.
If the city later loses Culture3/top-N importance while the plot remains owned, its old
priority reservation is never reconsidered.

PERSISTENT ENGINE CONSEQUENCE
-----------------------------
`CvPlot::setWorkingCityOverride(A)` is authoritative state, not a soft AI preference.
It calls `updateWorkingCity`, which selects the override before the normal/default working
city for a non-city plot:

    pBestCity = getWorkingCityOverride();
    ...
    if (pBestCity == NULL && isOwned())
        pBestCity = defaultWorkingCity();

The result is stored as the plot's actual `workingCity`.

`CvCity::canWork` then begins with:

    if (kPlot.getWorkingCity() != this)
        return false;

Therefore a stale override pointing to city A makes the plot unavailable to city B's
governor even if B would naturally own the shared plot and urgently needs it.

NORMAL CURRENT-DATA REPRODUCTION
--------------------------------
Use one AI player pursuing Culture3 with at least four cities A, B, C, D.
Current Cultural Victory requires the top 3 culture-rate cities.

1. Let A be culture-rate rank 3 and B rank 4.
2. Give A and B a shared same-owner BFC plot P whose natural `defaultWorkingCity()` is B
   (ordinary city-plot priority / founding-order rules can establish this).
3. While A is rank 3, A has positive city importance while B has zero. During `AI_stealPlots`,
   A sees B as P's current working city and calls `setWorkingCityOverride(A)`.
4. Later, keep Culture3 active but let city C's current culture rate overtake A. Rank-cache
   invalidation follows the normal commerce-update path, so A now ranks 4 and
   `AI_getCityImportance(true,false)` correctly becomes 0.
5. On every later A city turn, `iImportance == 0` skips the stealing/recomparison block.
   The only cleanup sees that P is still owned by the same player and leaves the override.
6. B is also non-important and therefore does not reclaim P through `AI_stealPlots`.
7. Arrange A to have better jobs and leave P unworked, while B needs P (e.g. P is a strong
   food tile and B is stagnant/starving). `B.canWork(P)` remains false solely because the
   stale working-city override still points at A.

The lost plot assignment can persist indefinitely. Ordinary culture-rate/rank changes do
not clear it. Current generic cleanup sites are ownership change, city death, and explicit
manual/UI override operations -- none is a normal lifecycle response to the AI importance
that originally created the reservation disappearing.

This is therefore a persistent gameplay-state error, not a one-turn heuristic lag.

ANCESTRY / INTENT
-----------------
K-Mod's initial reachable-history commit (`2414225e6415911ac28483d2bdac67b4100d36ff`,
"Initial commit. K-Mod, 27/dec/10") already contains `AI_stealPlots` with this exact
lifetime shape: set an override when our importance exceeds the current working city's,
but clear it only after ownership changes.

That initial K-Mod source carries the Better BTS AI victory-strategy code and originally
used Culture2 importance.

K-Mod commit `009357153d370c9ca0072d0eee299a36a98bfd6a` (2012-10-31,
"Made a minor tweak to AI_getCityImportance and added some comments") explicitly says
`AI_getCityImportance` is currently used by `AI_stealPlots` "in a very binary way" and
changes its culture gate from Culture2 to Culture3. It does not add any inverse/cleanup
transition when that binary state later returns to zero.

Subsequent K-Mod refactors found in reachable history preserve the same `AI_stealPlots`
state shape. Base AdvCiv and current SAS retain it substantively unchanged.

The feature's own binary-importance model makes the missing inverse transition especially
clear: the code knows when a city is no longer special, but persistent state installed on
the earlier positive transition is not removed.

DEDUP / ROOT SEPARATION
-----------------------
No prior Album entry mentions `AI_stealPlots`, `workingCityOverride`, or this stale
Culture-priority override lifetime.

This is independent of:
- F375 and Worker/shared-BFC accounting findings: those concern custom Worker job/readiness
  accounting and which plots are counted, not persistent CvPlot working-city authority;
- KI#44.5 / KI#70: citizen/specialist assignment legality inside a city;
- F522/KI#845: stale legacy emphasis bits altering job VALUE, not which city is legally
  permitted to work the plot;
- F515/F516/F519/F520: different cached city-site/attitude/safety state families.

F523's root is the missing inverse transition for persistent `CvPlot::workingCityOverride`
state created by `AI_stealPlots`.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Do not merely add more one-way stealing rules. The AI needs a symmetric lifecycle for its
shared-plot overrides.

At minimum, when a plot override points to `this`, clear it whenever this city's CURRENT
importance no longer strictly beats the competing/natural city's current importance. In
particular, `iImportance <= 0` must release an AI-created cultural-priority override while
ownership remains unchanged.

A more robust design is a player-level/shared-plot recomputation:
- determine current importance for all same-owner cities that can work the plot;
- reserve the plot only for a uniquely/higher important city;
- otherwise clear the override so `defaultWorkingCity()` regains authority.

That avoids sequential city-turn order preserving an obsolete reservation. Be careful not
to introduce blind clearing of human/manual overrides; the repair should apply to AI-owned
AI-managed cultural-priority overrides or structurally recompute AI shared-plot assignment.

REGRESSION TEST
---------------
1. AI player at Culture3 with A rank3, B rank4; A/B share P and defaultWorkingCity(P)=B.
2. Run A `AI_stealPlots`; assert `P.getWorkingCityOverride()==A` and `P.getWorkingCity()==A`.
3. Increase C's culture rate enough that A becomes rank4 while Culture3 remains active.
4. Run subsequent AI city turns.
5. Assert stale-state repair:
       A.AI_getCityImportance(true,false)==0
       P.getWorkingCityOverride()!=A
       P.getWorkingCity()==B  (assuming no other current higher-priority override)
       B.canWork(P)==true.
6. Give A a better alternative job and make B depend on P; assert P can be assigned to B
   rather than remaining unavailable/unworked.

C031-WIP291 - QUEUE 005 DEEP RE-AUDIT - F524 / KI#847 CONFIRMED

STATUS
------
Queue 005 `CvGameCoreDLL/CvCityAI.cpp` remains OPEN.
32/169 unique files complete.
F446 / KI#769 through F524 / KI#847 CONFIRMED.
F525 / provisional KI#848 UNUSED.
Current source basis: `AdvCiv-SAS_light_source_20260903T225830.zip`.
Base comparison: AdvCiv 1.14; ancestry comparison: K-Mod reachable history;

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F524 / KI#847 - CONFIRMED
AI_citizenSacrificeCost COUNTS EACH SPECIALIST TYPE'S YIELDS ONCE WHILE COUNTING
EVERY ASSIGNED SPECIALIST IN THE JOB-LOSS DENOMINATOR, SO MULTIPLE SAME-TYPE
SPECIALISTS CAN TURN A REAL POPULATION-SACRIFICE COST INTO A NEGATIVE SUBSIDY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvCityAI::AI_citizenSacrificeCost` builds two related descriptions of the city's
citizen jobs when estimating the cost of a population hurry:

1. `job_scores` plus `iTotalScore`: which citizens/jobs exist and which of them are
   expected to be lost;
2. `iYields[]`: aggregate output of those jobs, used to estimate the per-turn value
   lost while the city regrows.

Worked plots are accumulated consistently: every worked plot contributes once to
`job_scores`, once to `iTotalScore`, and once to `iYields[]`.

The specialist branch is asymmetric. For each specialist TYPE with one or more
assigned specialists, current code does essentially:

    int iSpecScore = 0;
    ...
    iYields[j] += y;
    ...
    iYields[YIELD_COMMERCE] += c;
    ...
    iTotalScore += iSpecScore * getSpecialistCount(eLoopSpecialist);
    job_scores.resize(job_scores.size() +
            getSpecialistCount(eLoopSpecialist), iSpecScore);

Thus `iTotalScore` and `job_scores` correctly represent N assigned Scientists as N
citizens, but `iYields[]` represents their output as though only ONE Scientist exists.
The mismatch occurs for every specialist type whose assigned count exceeds one.

That is not merely a rough-weight disagreement. `iYields[]` is subsequently treated as
aggregate job output:

    iBaseCostPerTurn += 4 * iYields[j] * AI_yieldMultiplier(...) *
            kOwner.AI_yieldWeight(...) / 100;

and then scaled by the lost-job score fraction:

    iCostPerTurn *= iScoreLoss;
    iCostPerTurn /= max(1, iTotalScore * 100);

So the numerator can omit most specialist output while the denominator and lost-job
fraction still count those omitted specialist citizens. The more same-type specialists
there are, the larger the downward bias in sacrifice cost.

CURRENT-SAS DATA REPRODUCTION
-----------------------------
A compact shipped-data witness exists through Korea's current Library replacement,
`BUILDING_KOREAN_GYEONGDANG`:

- available at Writing;
- +25% Research;
- 3 Scientist slots.

Current `SPECIALIST_SCIENTIST` supplies +3 Research. The sacrifice helper intentionally
uses a rough `*3/2` specialist-output estimate, so each Scientist contributes 4 rough
commerce and a job score of 16 with the helper's commerce weight 4.

Use an ordinary AI city with the following state:

- population 4;
- Slavery active (`HURRY_POPULATION` is enabled in current CIV4CivicInfos.xml);
- Gyeongdang already built;
- three assigned Scientists;
- one ordinary worked plot yielding 4 Food and no other relevant yield;
- city center supplies the inherited 2 Food minimum, so total city Food is 6;
- healthy (`healthRate()==0`);
- happiness surplus `iHappyLevel=2` and no pre-existing hurry anger;
- 100% Research;
- Normal game speed / Noble-like 100% growth factors;
- current early-game yield weights: Food 275, Commerce 100;
- Gyeongdang makes `AI_yieldMultiplier(YIELD_COMMERCE)==125` in the simple
  100%-Research case;
- current production state requires a legal 2-pop population hurry.

A size-4 city may legally sacrifice 2 population because `maxHurryPopulation()` is
population/2 (the current MAX_HURRY_POP define is effectively non-binding at 1000).
The pre-cost "whip to reduce food loss" shortcut does not consume this fixture:
foodDifference is exactly -2 and that shortcut requires `< -iHurryPopulation`, i.e.
strictly less than -2.

The helper's rough job data are:

    worked 4-Food plot score = 4 * 9 = 36
    each Scientist score     = 4 * 4 = 16
    iTotalScore              = 36 + 3*16 = 84
    job_scores               = [36,16,16,16]

For a 2-pop loss, the two lowest jobs are the Scientists. After the helper's flattening
against the average score, each lost job scores 18, so initial `iScoreLoss=36`.

BUGGY aggregate yields:

    iYields = [4 Food, 0 Production, 4 Commerce]

because all three Scientists add their count to `job_scores`/`iTotalScore`, but their
commerce enters `iYields[YIELD_COMMERCE]` only once.

Count-consistent aggregate yields would be:

    iYields = [4 Food, 0 Production, 12 Commerce]

With the current formula and the state above:

    buggy iBaseCostPerTurn     = 6400
    count-aware base cost      = 10400

First regrowth step (2 citizens missing):

    iFoodLoss = 25
    iFoodRate = 0
    buggy iCostPerTurn = -13
    corrected            = +4

Second regrowth step (1 citizen missing):

    iFoodLoss = 27
    iFoodRate = -1
    buggy iCostPerTurn = -7
    corrected            = +2

Total helper result:

    current buggy AI_citizenSacrificeCost = -514   (units of 4x commerce)
    count-aware result                    = +154

`AI_doHurry` then divides the helper result by 4 using C++ integer division:

    current buggy population cost = -128
    count-aware population cost   = +38

So this is not a small underpricing. In a fully current, legal specialist-heavy city,
the missing `* specialistCount` term can reverse the sign: sacrificing two productive
citizens is represented as a 128-commerce BENEFIT instead of a positive cost.

LIVE AI_doHurry CONSEQUENCE
---------------------------
`AI_doHurry` does not clamp a negative `iPopCost` to zero. After adding any gold-hurry
component it forms:

    iHurryCost = iPopCost + iGoldCost;

For a population-only whip in the fixture, `iGoldCost==0`, so the wrong negative value
flows directly into production decisions.

The unit branch ultimately accepts when:

    iHurryCost < iValue + iOverflow

and the building branch first tests:

    iProductionAdded + iOverflow > iHurryCost

then later:

    iValue + iOverflow > iHurryCost

A negative `iHurryCost` therefore makes these gates dramatically easier to satisfy. The
bug can cause a real AI population whip that the same decision with count-consistent
specialist output would reject. The exact choice still depends on the current unit or
building value, but the 166-point difference (-128 versus +38 after `/4`) creates a
large ordinary decision interval where the result flips.

The root is especially dangerous in specialist-heavy cities because the undercount
increases precisely when multiple citizens of one type are assigned -- i.e. when the
population being sacrificed can be economically valuable despite low worked-plot count.

ANCESTRY
--------
This is inherited K-Mod arithmetic, not a SAS regression and not a stock-BtS helper.

K-Mod practical 485 / commit
`1f464176a18621c512e7e9715bacd8b78b83266d` (2012-02-05,
"Heaps of changes to CvCityAI::AI_doHurry -- laying the foundations for the new
slave-whip / hurry method") introduced `AI_citizenLossCost` with the same specialist
asymmetry already present:

    iYields[...] += specialist output                    // once per TYPE
    iTotalScore += iSpecScore * getSpecialistCount(...) // multiplied by COUNT
    job_scores.resize(... + getSpecialistCount(...))    // multiplied by COUNT

K-Mod practical 517 / commit
`c3d1c81aec3c0e8dba0a5c0c5e52111022e453d4` (2012-02-16) renamed the helper to
`AI_citizenSacrificeCost`, added anger/recovery accounting and explicitly "fixed some
mistakes", but retained the same one-per-type `iYields` accumulation while continuing
to multiply `iTotalScore` and `job_scores` by assigned count.

The immediate practical-518 food-component repair (`7143f627e521...`) changed how
`iYields[]` feeds `iBaseCostPerTurn` and food cost; it did not repair specialist
multiplicity. Later AdvCiv iterator/refactor work likewise preserves the semantic
mismatch. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS still contain it. Civ4CE's stock BtS tree does
not contain `AI_citizenSacrificeCost` / the K-Mod helper.

DEDUP / ROOT SEPARATION
-----------------------
The reconciled album contains no prior root for `AI_citizenSacrificeCost` or this
one-per-specialist-TYPE versus per-specialist-CITIZEN aggregate-yield mismatch.

It is distinct from:

- F324 / KI#647: `AI_civicValue` reuses one finite population pool across multiple
  unlimited-specialist TYPES when valuing Caste System. F524 concerns already-assigned
  multiple citizens of ONE type inside hurry-cost arithmetic.
- F428 / KI#751: UI help for free specialists omits Great-Person points. F524 is an AI
  gameplay decision and counts assigned specialist commerce/yields incorrectly.
- F504 and other `AI_doHurry` findings: those concern stale upgrade-budget/cache inputs;
  F524 is an independent local population-value numerator/denominator contradiction.
- citizen assignment / emphasis roots such as KI#70 and F522: those decide which jobs
  are worked; F524 misprices population loss after the jobs already exist.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Make specialist output multiplicity match the multiplicity already used by
`iTotalScore` and `job_scores`:

    int const iCount = getSpecialistCount(eLoopSpecialist);
    if (iCount <= 0)
        continue;

    ...
    iYields[j] += y * iCount;
    ...
    iYields[YIELD_COMMERCE] += c * iCount;
    ...
    iTotalScore += iSpecScore * iCount;
    job_scores.resize(job_scores.size() + iCount, iSpecScore);

Do not multiply `iSpecScore` itself before inserting jobs; each job entry should remain
one specialist's score. Only the aggregate-yield accumulator is missing the count.

A small local variable also avoids repeated `getSpecialistCount` calls and makes the
contract visually obvious.

REGRESSION TEST
---------------
Use a deterministic specialist-heavy sacrifice-cost fixture, preferably the current
Korean Gyeongdang case above or an equivalent synthetic city state:

1. population 4, 3 same-type Scientists, one 4-Food worked plot;
2. 2-pop legal hurry; healthy, happiness surplus 2, no existing hurry anger;
3. 100% Research, +25% Research city modifier;
4. call `AI_citizenSacrificeCost(2, 2, HURRY_POP_ANGER, hurryAngerLength)`;

   Normal/Noble baseline);

For an integration test, put an `AI_doHurry` unit/building value between the buggy and
corrected thresholds and assert that the negative-cost version hurries while the repaired
version declines.

POST-F524 SHORTLIST CONTROLS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AI_experienceWeight - NEGATIVE-SENTINEL LEAD CLOSED
---------------------------------------------------
Current AdvCiv/SAS intentionally returns `-2` for a city with no production/domain free
experience, with the explicit advc.017 comment that cities without Barracks should be
more hesitant to train units.

A first-pass concern was that `AI_chooseUnit(UnitAI, iOdds)` treats `iOdds < 0` as an
unconditional-build sentinel. That does not form a live inversion here:

- ordinary city military probability uses `AI_buildUnitProb`, which starts from the
  leader BuildUnitProb plus the XP weight and then applies explicit caps/floors;
- when not greatly reduced it raises early military probability to
  `25 - 2*numCities`, and the final scaled probability is capped normally before
  returning an integer percent;
- current real leader XML has positive BuildUnitProb values (the 10-point
  `LEADER_DEFAULTS` template is not an ordinary selected personality; Gandhi is the
  lowest ordinary leader at 25);
- the separate governor-production caller adds `AI_experienceWeight()` to a local odds
  value and calls `SyncRandSuccess100` directly rather than passing that value through
  `AI_chooseUnit`'s negative sentinel.

Thus the `-2` remains a real hesitation as documented, not an accidental unconditional
unit request. No F525.

AI_doDraft - CONSCRIPT POPULATION FORMULA CONTROL
-------------------------------------------------
`AI_doDraft` locally recomputes:

    max(1, conscriptUnitProductionCost / CONSCRIPT_POPULATION_PER_COST)

The authoritative `CvCity::getConscriptPopulation()` uses the same integer formula after
checking for NO_UNIT / zero divisor. `AI_doDraft` has already returned unless
`canConscript()` succeeds, so those exceptional states are excluded before the local
calculation. No population-cost contract mismatch was found.

The remaining draft gates in this pass are explicit strategic policies (unit-spending,
city shrinkage, war/danger, happiness and BuildUnitProb), not hidden arithmetic/object
identity failures. No F525.

AI_citizenValue - CONTROL
-------------------------
The helper remains the small inherited AdvCiv era-scaled heuristic:

    6 + ownerCurrentEra

Its live uses treat the value as a positive weight/cost term. With current nonnegative
era indices there is no zero divisor, sentinel collision or wrong-owner receiver. No
independent root found.

================================================================================
C031-WIP292 — QUEUE 005 DEEP RE-AUDIT — KI#195 BARBARIAN WORK-BOAT COUNTING REOPENED
================================================================================

STATUS
------
Queue 005 `CvGameCoreDLL/CvCityAI.cpp` remains OPEN under deep-method re-audit.
32/169 unique files complete.
F446 / KI#769 through F524 / KI#847 remain CONFIRMED.
F525 / provisional KI#848 remains UNUSED.
No repository source files modified.

WHY THE POST-F524 LOW-COVERAGE PASS REOPENED KI#195
---------------------------------------------------
The low-covered SAS delta in `AI_barbChooseProduction` had previously been stamped as the known
KI#195 Barbarian Work-Boat accounting repair. Directly opening the helper used by that repair now
shows that the second half of KI#195 rests on an incorrect helper contract.

Current SAS says:

    int const iWaterAreaSeaWorkers = (pProductionWaterArea == NULL ? 0 :
        kPlayer.AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs(*pProductionWaterArea, UNITAI_WORKER_SEA));
    int const iExistingSeaWorkers = iWaterAreaSeaWorkers +
        kPlot.plotCount(PUF_isUnitAIType, UNITAI_WORKER_SEA, -1, getOwner()) +
        getNumTrainUnitAI(UNITAI_WORKER_SEA);

The accompanying KI#195 comment says `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` finds docked/queued ships by
iterating major-civilization cities and therefore misses the Barbarian player's own cities. It
also says the intended composition is:

- Work Boats already sailing in the relevant water area, plus
- Work Boats docked or training in THIS Barbarian city,
- while docked/training boats in unrelated Barbarian cities must not suppress this city's local
  demand.

The actual helper does something different.

ACTUAL `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` CONTRACT
-----------------------------------------
Current `CvPlayerAI::AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` first calls `AI_totalAreaUnitAIs(kArea, ...)`, then:

    for (PlayerIter<ALIVE> it; it.hasNext(); ++it)
    {
        CvPlayer const& kOwner = *it;
        ...
        FOR_EACH_CITY(pLoopCity, kOwner)
        {
            if (pLoopCity->waterArea() != &kArea)
                continue;
            iCount += pLoopCity->getPlot().plotCount(
                PUF_isUnitAIType, eUnitAI, -1, getID());
            if (kOwner.getID() == getID())
                iCount += pLoopCity->getNumTrainUnitAI(eUnitAI);
        }
    }

`PlayerIter<ALIVE>` is explicitly NOT major-only. `AgentIterator.h` uses the `CIV_ALIVE` cache for
this template specialization and `bADD_BARBARIANS` adds the Barbarian agent because `ALIVE <
CIV_ALIVE`. `ExplicitAgentIterator::passFilters` for `ALIVE` only requires `isAlive()`; it does not
exclude Barbarians. K-Mod's pre-AgentIterator version is even more explicit: it loops every
`iI < MAX_PLAYERS`, checks `GET_PLAYER(iI).isAlive()`, then iterates that player's cities.

Therefore an alive Barbarian player's own coastal cities ARE in this helper. For each own city on
the tested water area it already counts:

1. own `UNITAI_WORKER_SEA` units docked on that city plot, and
2. own `UNITAI_WORKER_SEA` training orders in that city.

So the KI#195 statement that Base AdvCiv's helper only scans major-civilization cities is false.
The helper inherited from K-Mod/AdvCiv was specifically written to scan all alive players' cities.

WHAT THE CURRENT KI#195 ADDITION ACTUALLY DOES
----------------------------------------------
In the ordinary case where `waterArea(true)` equals the city's normal `waterArea()`, the helper
already includes this city's docked and queued Work Boats. The extra:

    + kPlot.plotCount(...UNITAI_WORKER_SEA...)
    + getNumTrainUnitAI(UNITAI_WORKER_SEA)

therefore counts those current-city objects a second time.

That duplicate does not by itself change the present `iExistingSeaWorkers <= 0` Boolean test: a
positive count stays positive. It is nevertheless proof that the implemented formula does not
match its documented decomposition.

More importantly, `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` also counts docked and queued Barbarian Work Boats in
OTHER Barbarian cities whose ordinary `waterArea()` is the same `kArea`. Therefore the current
code does NOT satisfy KI#195's explicit local-independence contract. A queued/docked boat in city A
can make `iExistingSeaWorkers > 0` in city B even when B has its own positive city-local
`AI_neededSeaWorkers()` demand.

The helper's initial `AI_totalAreaUnitAIs(kArea, UNITAI_WORKER_SEA)` also counts Work Boats physically
in the water area, so a sailing Work Boat suppresses another production request as intended by the
KI#195 text. The problem is that `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` adds city-based dock/queue accounting on
top of that; it is not a "sailing boats only" primitive.

EDGE CASE THAT EXPLAINS WHY THE EXTRA LOCAL TERMS CAN SOMETIMES MATTER
---------------------------------------------------------------------
`AI_barbChooseProduction` passes `waterArea(true)` to `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs`, while that helper
matches cities using `pLoopCity->waterArea()` with the default `bNoImpassable=false`.

`CvPlot::waterArea(true)` excludes impassable adjacent water plots when choosing the largest water
area; `waterArea()` does not. If an impassable-Ice-adjacent larger sea and an accessible smaller sea
compete, a city's `waterArea(true)` and `waterArea()` can differ. In that case the helper may indeed
miss that city's docked/queued unit for the accessible production water area. Adding the current
city's plot/queue terms repairs THAT mismatch. It does not establish the broad "Barbarian cities
are absent from the helper" diagnosis recorded by KI#195.

This also connects naturally to the later KI#216 discovery about `waterArea(true)` / secondary-area
identity; water-area accessor semantics matter here and are not interchangeable.

CURRENT GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCE / CLEAN FIXTURE
--------------------------------------------
Use two alive Barbarian coastal cities A and B sharing the same ordinary accessible water area.
Give each city one owned, buildable, reachable unimproved seafood plot assigned to its own BFC, so:

    A.AI_neededSeaWorkers() == 1
    B.AI_neededSeaWorkers() == 1

Let A already have one `UNITAI_WORKER_SEA` training order and let B have no local docked or queued
boat.

When B evaluates its KI#195 production branch, `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` visits A because A is an
alive Barbarian city on the same water area and adds A's training order. Therefore B sees
`iExistingSeaWorkers > 0` and skips its local Work Boat even though B's own local demand is valid.
The same happens if A's boat is docked. Once the boat is physically at sea, the initial area count
also suppresses B until the boat is consumed or otherwise leaves the relevant UnitAI/area.

Thus the current branch can serialize local Barbarian seafood servicing across a shared sea rather
than allowing the per-city demand model promised by KI#195. With several Barbarian cities/targets
on one sea this can delay otherwise parallel improvements substantially.

ANCESTRY / SOURCE CROSS-CHECK
-----------------------------
- Current SAS and Base AdvCiv 1.14 both have the all-alive-city
  `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` helper.
- Current K-Mod has the same semantics in older explicit form: loop `iI=0..MAX_PLAYERS`, require
  `isAlive()`, count docked units in every city on the water area, and count queues in the current
  player's cities.
- KI#195 was introduced by SAS practical 6074 / commit
  `f03333ae1541517390a59da1afd60d73841f74da` (2026-07-22). Its patch adds the incorrect
  major-civilization-only comment and combines `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` with extra local
  plot/queue counts.
- The first half of KI#195 remains valid: Base AdvCiv's Barbarian `AI_neededSeaWorkers` used only
  `FOR_EACH_ADJ_PLOT`, so outer BFC seafood demand really was omitted. This reopening concerns the
  second "docked/queued boats" diagnosis/cure only.

NATURAL REPAIR DIRECTION
------------------------
If the intended KI#195 policy is exactly the one its docs state — boats physically sailing in the
relevant water area + docked/queued boats in the CURRENT Barbarian city, but not unrelated
Barbarian-city dock/queues — then `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` is the wrong primitive.

The natural existing primitive for the first component is:

    kPlayer.AI_totalAreaUnitAIs(*pProductionWaterArea, UNITAI_WORKER_SEA)

For a water area this counts sea units physically in that area (and area-attributed training, if
any), without the extra cross-city `waterArea()` scan that `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` performs.
Then add the current city's docked and queued counts explicitly, as KI#195 already does.

The exact final patch should still be validated against area-attributed training semantics and the
Ice/waterArea(true) edge before changing repository source. The important audit result is the
helper-contract mismatch, not a premature patch.

F525 arithmetic control - losing-war production odds denominator is safe
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current AI_chooseProduction contains the losing-war adjustment:

    int iOdds = iBuildUnitProb;
    if (iWarSuccessRating < -50)
        iOdds -= iWarSuccessRating / 3;

    iOdds *= (-iWarSuccessRating + 20 + iBestBuildingValue);
    iOdds /= (-iWarSuccessRating + 2 * iBestBuildingValue);

This initially deserved a divisor/sign audit. The live branch requires
`iWarSuccessRating < -10`. CvTeamAI::AI_getWarSuccessRating() clamps its result
to [-99, 99]. `iBestBuildingValue` is produced by AI_bestBuildingThreshold();
that helper rejects candidate buildings whose underlying AI_buildingValue is
<= 0 and only positively rescales accepted values. Consequently the denominator
is at least 11 in the live branch and cannot be zero or negative. The numerator
is likewise positive. No divide-by-zero, sign inversion or negative-sentinel
failure is present here.

F525 false positive killed - GET_TEAM(getOwner()) is type-safe by design
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Several inherited sites initially looked like a very strong PlayerTypes /
TeamTypes domain bug, e.g. AI_bestProject and AI_bestUnit use:

    GET_TEAM(getOwner())

`CvCity::getOwner()` returns PlayerTypes, and a superficial reading of GET_TEAM
would therefore suggest that the player slot is being mistaken for a team slot.
That reading is WRONG in current AdvCiv/SAS. CoreAI.h defines GET_TEAM(x) through
an overloaded CoreAI::getTeam, including a PlayerTypes overload which converts
through TEAMID(ePlayer):

    CoreAI::getTeam(TeamTypes)
    CoreAI::getTeam(PlayerTypes) -> CvTeamAI::AI_getTeam(TEAMID(ePlayer))

History confirms this was deliberate preservation of the old TEAMREF(ePlayer)
convenience when practical 1679 removed/refactored the old macro layer. Thus the
naval-terrain-trade, capitulation/unit, World-Wonder and project sites all resolve
the owner's actual team correctly even when player ID != team ID. Do NOT report
or rediscover these as wrong-ID bugs.

Inherited chop-value arithmetic note - advertised relative-production boost dead
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
AI_bestPlotBuild contains inherited K-Mod arithmetic:

    // Increase the value if it is large compared to city's natural production rate
    // note iValue = chop production * 10
    iValue += iValue / (getBaseYieldRate(YIELD_PRODUCTION) * 20 + iValue);

For positive chop `iValue` and positive base production, the denominator is
strictly greater than iValue, so integer division contributes exactly 0. If base
production is zero, it contributes exactly 1. Therefore the source-described
"large compared to natural production" boost is effectively dead. This is a
real upstream arithmetic defect/robustness note, but current SAS's authoritative
land Worker planning bypasses this legacy evaluator. No sufficiently independent
current gameplay consequence has yet justified F525.

KI#213 reconfirmed - Advanced Start still consumes disabled legacy land cache
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Following that legacy best-build cache into its consumers reconfirmed an existing
cross-file architecture root rather than a new finding. SAS deliberately makes
AI_getImprovementValue return 0 / NO_BUILD for every land plot so that the custom
CvUnitAI::AI_bestCityBuild system owns ordinary land Worker planning. Advanced
Start still calls AI_updateBestBuild and purchases improvements through
AI_getBestBuildValue / AI_getBestBuild. Therefore custom land improvement policy
is invisible to Advanced Start. This exact disconnect is already owned by KI#213
in the reconciled album; do not duplicate it as F525. (Advanced Start F370-F372
are separate already-confirmed action/termination bugs.)

F525 control - AI_isAirDefended ignores bCountLand deliberately
---------------------------------------------------------------
Current helper:

    bool CvCityAI::AI_isAirDefended(bool bCountLand, int iExtra) const
    {
        return (getPlot().plotCount(PUF_isAirIntercept, -1, -1, getOwner()) +
                iExtra >= AI_neededAirDefenders());
    }

The only live current caller found is CvUnitAI::AI_defenseAirMove, which invokes
`AI_isAirDefended(true, -1)` while deciding whether the current aircraft must
remain on Air Patrol under a moderate direct land threat. BBAI's disabled helper
once used bCountLand to add land-unit interception probability. K-Mod explicitly
reverted AI_isAirDefended to simple aircraft counting because its redesigned
AI_neededAirDefenders was not suitable for the BBAI probability-based version,
retained the bool parameter only to match BBAI usage, and AdvCiv documents:
"Either way, only aircraft are currently counted." This is acknowledged design /
architectural debt, not an accidental current regression.

Post-WIP293 control - AI_bestProject capitulation early return violates its
out-parameter convention but has no demonstrated gameplay consequence
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
AI_bestProject(int* piBestValue, ...) normally writes *piBestValue even when
there is no best project; its own exit comment explicitly documents that
convention. The advc.014 capitulated-vassal early return happens before the
write:

    if (GET_TEAM(getOwner()).isCapitulated())
        return NO_PROJECT;

Thus an input value such as AI_chooseProduction's -1 "not calculated" sentinel
survives the call rather than becoming the normal no-project value 0. This is a
real API-contract/performance blemish, but all current live consumers close
safely:

- callers that need a concrete project gate value use on eBestProject != NO_PROJECT;
- AI_chooseProduction's intermediate weighting uses
  max(iProjectValue, iBestBuildingValue), and iBestBuildingValue is guaranteed
  nonnegative, so max(-1, B) == max(0, B);
- the late `if (iProjectValue < 0)` path merely calls AI_bestProject again for a
  capitulated city and receives NO_PROJECT again; the subsequent project-value
  comparison remains false.

No current state-changing consequence justifies a finding. Retain as inherited
out-parameter/performance debt; F525 was not spent here.
