F525 / KI#848 - K-Mod human auto-production governor validates one XP building
but queues a different building variable
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: CONFIRMED CURRENT BUG (inherited K-Mod -> AdvCiv -> SAS)

CURRENT ROOT
------------
In CvCityAI::AI_buildGovernorChooseProduction, the military branch first picks
its desired unit and then deliberately searches for the best experience-focused
building for that exact unit:

    BuildingTypes eExperienceBuilding = AI_bestBuildingThreshold(
            BUILDINGFOCUS_EXPERIENCE);
    if (eExperienceBuilding != NO_BUILDING)
    {
        const CvBuildingInfo& kBuilding = GC.getInfo(eExperienceBuilding);
        if (kBuilding.getFreeExperience() > 0 ||
            kBuilding.getUnitCombatFreeExperience(kUnit.getUnitCombatType()) > 0 ||
            kBuilding.getDomainFreeExperience(kUnit.getDomainType()) > 0)
        {
            // This building helps the unit we want
            // ...so do the building first.
            pushOrder(ORDER_CONSTRUCT, eBestBuilding); // WRONG OBJECT
            return;
        }
    }

The object whose effects were tested is `eExperienceBuilding`; the object queued
is the earlier, unrelated general-purpose `eBestBuilding` computed at the top of
the governor. The branch therefore establishes a property about building X and
then acts on building Y.

HARD CONTRACT / INVARIANT
-------------------------
Once the branch has selected `eExperienceBuilding` and verified that this same
building grants free experience to the chosen unit's exact unit-combat or domain,
the ORDER_CONSTRUCT target must be `eExperienceBuilding`.

This is not a tuning preference. The branch comments explicitly say "This
building helps the unit we want ... so do the building first," and all three
predicates immediately above refer to the local `kBuilding` obtained from
`eExperienceBuilding`.

LIVE CURRENT CONSEQUENCE
------------------------
AI_buildGovernorChooseProduction is the production-automation governor for human
cities. CvCity::doProduction calls AI_chooseProduction for a human city when
`isProductionAutomated()` is true; AI_chooseProduction then dispatches human
cities directly to AI_buildGovernorChooseProduction.

The two building searches are intentionally different and can normally disagree:

- `eBestBuilding = AI_bestBuildingThreshold()` performs the ordinary all-role
  building evaluation;
- `eExperienceBuilding = AI_bestBuildingThreshold(BUILDINGFOCUS_EXPERIENCE)`
  uses the focus path, whose first pass specifically values XP effects and can
  reject buildings with no experience contribution before the ordinary second
  pass.

Current SAS supplies straightforward live data for the distinction. For example,
BUILDING_BARRACKS is a normal buildable 50-hammer Hunting building with +3 land
DomainFreeExperience, while ordinary economic buildings such as the 45-hammer
Granary have strong non-XP value (40% food kept) but no XP. In any ordinary
production-automated human city state where the general building scorer ranks a
non-XP building above Barracks while the focused scorer selects Barracks for the
chosen land combat unit, a successful military-governor roll reaches this block,
validates Barracks, and then queues the unrelated general building instead.

The consequence is state-changing and persistent until the next production
choice: automated production delays the military unit for the wrong building,
while the very XP building that justified the delay is not what was ordered.
This can recur every time the governor revisits the same decision state.

The defect does not require `eBestBuilding` to be invalid. The common and clean
failure is simply X != Y: an economic/general building is legal and valuable, an
XP building is also legal and specifically useful for the chosen unit, and the
branch queues the former after proving the latter.

ANCESTRY / BIRTH BOUNDARY
-------------------------
The wrong variable is born cleanly in K-Mod practical 251,
commit ce5a1952a160a27345e555e640c6c5be9d7b3bb2,
titled:

    "Many and various numerical adjustments. Changed the way the AI refuses
     peace when going for conquest - again. (the previous method also prevented
     capitualtion)"

Immediately before that commit, the governor's military branch simply did:

    if (AI_chooseBuilding(BUILDINGFOCUS_EXPERIENCE, 10))
        return;
    if (AI_chooseUnit(NO_UNITAI))
        return;

Practical 251 deliberately made this more selective: it first chose the exact
best unit, introduced the new local `eExperienceBuilding`, checked whether that
building actually grants XP applicable to that unit, and intended to build it
before the unit. But the newly introduced success block accidentally retained
`eBestBuilding` as the order target:

    + BuildingTypes eExperienceBuilding = AI_bestBuildingThreshold(...);
    + ... inspect eExperienceBuilding ...
    + pushOrder(ORDER_CONSTRUCT, eBestBuilding, ...);

That is a textbook variable-substitution typo introduced in the feature's birth,
not an inferred strategy disagreement.

K-Mod practical 365, commit 5dc0ad28676fbf3aeb3e52d551fb20a28a275dbb,
was specifically titled:

    "Fixed a rare bug which could potentially cause the auto-production governor
     to crash the game."

It added the current `kUnit.getUnitCombatType() != NO_UNITCOMBAT` guard around
this exact block, but retained the wrong `eBestBuilding` queue target. Thus the
nearby crash was repaired while this separate wrong-object bug survived.

UPSTREAM / CURRENT BOUNDARY
---------------------------
- K-Mod current source retains the wrong `eBestBuilding` target.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same wrong target.
- Current AdvCiv-SAS retains the same wrong target; SAS changes in this function
  are diagnostics/caching and do not repair the object mismatch.
- Stock BtS / current Civ4CE BtS does not contain this K-Mod targeted-unit /
  targeted-XP-building rewrite; its older governor directly calls an experience-
  focused building chooser. Therefore this exact root begins in K-Mod, not stock
  Civ4 BtS.

------------------------------------

Culture-process metadata transition) concern different state and ownership

Preserve all existing branch conditions, unit-combat guard, building predicates,
RNG timing and the subsequent unit order. No broader governor rewrite is needed
to fix this root.

F526 / KI#849 - AI_neededFloatingDefenders cache ignores bIgnoreCulture,
so AIR->LAND call order can feed culture-inclusive floating demand into the
culture-excluding AI_neededDefenders calculation
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
Current Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS expose two semantically different calculations
through the same helper:

    int AI_neededFloatingDefenders(
        bool bIgnoreEvac = false,
        bool bConstCache = false,
        bool bIgnoreCulture = false) const;

`AI_calculateNeededFloatingDefenders` first computes the ordinary floating-defender
share F. It then conditionally applies the culture-garrison floor:

    if (!bIgnoreCulture)
    {
        int iCultureDefendersNeeded =
            AI_neededCultureDefenders() - AI_minDefenders();
        iFloatingDefenders = std::max(
            iFloatingDefenders, iCultureDefendersNeeded);
    }

Thus, for the same city and game state, there are legitimately two answers:

    ignore-culture answer  = F
    include-culture answer = max(F, C - M)

where C = AI_neededCultureDefenders() and M = AI_minDefenders().

But the cache has only one value and one key component:

    m_iNeededFloatingDefenders
    m_iNeededFloatingDefendersCacheTurn

and lookup is only:

    if (m_iNeededFloatingDefendersCacheTurn != kGame.getGameTurn())
        calculate(... bIgnoreCulture ...);
    return m_iNeededFloatingDefenders;

`bIgnoreCulture` is not part of the cache identity. Therefore whichever semantic
variant first performs a non-const calculation in a turn becomes the answer for
both variants for the rest of that cache lifetime.

`bIgnoreEvac` does not create the same problem: evacuation is checked before the
cache and a non-ignored evacuating city returns 0 immediately. `bConstCache` is a
cache-write policy, not part of the mathematical value. The missing semantic key
is specifically `bIgnoreCulture`.

WHY AI_neededDefenders DELIBERATELY REQUESTS THE OTHER VALUE
------------------------------------------------------------
`AI_neededDefenders` calls:

    int iNeededFloating = AI_neededFloatingDefenders(
        bIgnoreEvac, bConstCache, true);

The comment at that call is explicit:

    // To save time (avoid calling AI_neededCultureDefenders 2x)

The function later applies the culture requirement exactly once as the final floor:

    iDefenders = std::max(iDefenders, AI_neededCultureDefenders());

So this is not an interchangeable approximation. The `true` call intentionally
means: return floating demand WITHOUT the culture component, because culture will
be applied separately at the end.

If the cache instead supplies the default include-culture answer, the culture
requirement is partly added into `iDefenders` and then applied again as a floor.
That changes the result whenever non-culture defender terms already put the city
above its minimum-defender baseline.

DETERMINISTIC NORMAL-TURN CALL ORDER
------------------------------------
The strongest reproduction does not rely on an uncertain caller ordering.

For ordinary sequential turns, `CvPlayer::setTurnActive(true, bDoTurn=true)` runs:

    doTurnUnits();

and `CvPlayer::doTurnUnits()` processes unit domains in fixed passes:

    pass 1: DOMAIN_AIR
    pass 2: DOMAIN_SEA
    pass 3: DOMAIN_LAND

A `UNITAI_DEFENSE_AIR` executes `CvUnitAI::AI_defenseAirMove`. In an ordinary
valid city it calls:

    pCity->AI_neededAirDefenders();

with default `bConstCache=false`.

`AI_neededAirDefenders` then loops over EVERY city owned by the player and calls:

    pLoopCity->AI_neededFloatingDefenders(false, bConstCache);

The third argument defaults to `bIgnoreCulture=false`. Consequently one defensive
aircraft can populate the shared floating-defender cache of every city with the
CULTURE-INCLUSIVE answer during the AIR pass.

The LAND pass follows later in the same `doTurnUnits`. A normal city-defense unit
runs `AI_cityDefenseMove()`, then `AI_guardCityMinDefender(true)`. Its city search
calls:

    pLoopCity->AI_neededDefenders(true);

`AI_neededDefenders` requests `AI_neededFloatingDefenders(..., true)` -- the
CULTURE-EXCLUDING answer -- but the game-turn cache is already valid from the air
pass. No recalculation occurs and the culture-inclusive value is returned instead.

This is therefore a normal, deterministic AIR -> LAND contamination sequence for
an AI player that owns a defensive aircraft. The aircraft does not even have to be
based in the affected culture city, because `AI_neededAirDefenders` scans all of
the player's cities and can prime all of their floating-defender caches.

CONCRETE GARRISON ARITHMETIC FLIP
---------------------------------
Use a legal culture-pressured city state with:

    ordinary floating share F                         = 0
    AI_minDefenders M                                 = 2
    AI_neededCultureDefenders C                       = 5

and ordinary non-culture city-defense conditions that make the other defender
terms total 3 by the time the final culture floor is applied. One simple shape is
an important city (capital / active World Wonder / Holy City adds one defender)
plus the ordinary flat-city defensive-war increment. The exact identities are not
important; the current formula contains several independent ways for the
non-culture baseline to exceed M.

Correct `AI_neededDefenders` path:

    ignore-culture floating = F = 0
    non-culture defender total = 3
    final culture floor = max(3, C=5)
    correct need = 5

AIR-primed contaminated path:

    cached include-culture floating
        = max(F=0, C-M = 5-2)
        = 3

    the same non-culture terms now total 6
    final culture floor = max(6, C=5)
    contaminated need = 6

So a city that should request 5 defenders can request 6 solely because an air-unit
calculation happened first. This is a hard parameter/cache-contract error, not a
strategy preference.

The general failure condition is straightforward. Let B be the non-floating,
non-culture defender contribution at the final culture-floor point. If:

    C - M > F
    and B > M

then reusing the include-culture floating value inside the ignore-culture path can
make the culture requirement additive above its intended floor.

LIVE CONSEQUENCES
-----------------
The wrong result is consumed in ordinary land-unit allocation immediately in the
same LAND pass:

- `AI_guardCityMinDefender(true)` compares current defenders with
  `AI_neededDefenders(true)` and can pull an unnecessary extra defender toward the
  contaminated city.
- `AI_guardCity(...)` also uses `AI_neededDefenders` for current-city stay/leave
  decisions and candidate-city shortfalls.
- Additional `CvUnitAI` and `CvPlayerAI` callers use the same required-defender
  count for reinforcement and city-defense allocation.

The opposite contamination direction is also possible in other call orders: if
`AI_neededDefenders` first stores the ignore-culture answer F, a later ordinary
`AI_neededFloatingDefenders(..., false)` or `AI_neededAirDefenders` call receives
F and loses the culture-pressure component. That can underweight defensive-air
allocation to culture-sensitive cities. The deterministic AIR-before-LAND witness
above is sufficient by itself; this reverse direction shows that the cache cannot
correctly represent both API modes in either order.

ANCESTRY / BIRTH
----------------
K-Mod and stock BtS/Civ4CE have only one semantic floating-defender calculation,
so their game-turn cache does not have this parameter-key problem.

Base AdvCiv practical 1902, commit:

    9460039260f5d8a152616c7396607845b9ad8868

Title:

    "Performance tweak to the AI culture garrison code"

introduced `bIgnoreCulture` specifically to avoid calling
`AI_neededCultureDefenders` twice from `AI_neededDefenders`.

The local preserved commit diff shows that practical 1902 simultaneously:

1. changed `AI_neededDefenders` from

       AI_neededFloatingDefenders(bIgnoreEvac, bConstCache)

   to

       AI_neededFloatingDefenders(bIgnoreEvac, bConstCache, true)

2. added the `bIgnoreCulture` parameter to both
   `AI_neededFloatingDefenders` and `AI_calculateNeededFloatingDefenders`, and

3. wrapped the culture contribution in:

       if (!bIgnoreCulture)

but DID NOT add that new semantic dimension to
`m_iNeededFloatingDefendersCacheTurn` or provide a second cache value.

So practical 1902 changed one cached mathematical function into two functions of
`bIgnoreCulture` while retaining the original one-dimensional game-turn cache.
The bug is born exactly in that performance tweak.

UPSTREAM / CURRENT BOUNDARY
---------------------------
- Stock BtS / current Civ4CE BtS: one floating-defender mode; no such missing
  `bIgnoreCulture` cache key.
- K-Mod current source: one floating-defender mode; no such missing semantic key.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14: bug present.
- Current AdvCiv-SAS: bug present and semantically inherited. SAS only caches the
  `CvGame` reference locally in these helpers; it does not alter the cache identity
  or repair the mode collision.

DUPLICATE / ROOT-SEPARATION CHECK
---------------------------------
The reconciled album was searched for `AI_neededFloatingDefenders`, floating
Defenders, `bIgnoreCulture`, culture-garrison cache and related cache-key language.
No prior numbered root owns this missing parameter dimension.

Nearby cache findings are distinct:

- the AI_playerCloseness same-turn cache note concerns mutable city geometry and
  currently has only softer heuristic consequences;
- F514/F515/F516/F519/F520 concern strategy/victory/team cache freshness and
  ordering, not a function parameter omitted from the cache identity;
- F523 is persistent `workingCityOverride` lifecycle state, not a cache;
- KI#213 is the intentionally empty legacy land best-build cache used by Advanced
  Start and is unrelated to defender allocation.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
The cache must distinguish the two semantic modes.

Preferred robust design: keep separate per-turn cached values (and validity turns)
for:

    include culture  (bIgnoreCulture=false)
    ignore culture   (bIgnoreCulture=true)

A smaller surgical repair can add `bIgnoreCulture` to the cache identity and
recalculate whenever the requested mode differs from the stored mode. That is
correct but can thrash if callers alternate modes; two slots preserve the original
performance intent better.

Do not simply remove the `true` argument from `AI_neededDefenders`: that would
restore the duplicate culture calculation and, more importantly, would make the
culture component partially additive before the function's explicit final culture
floor. The intended semantics of practical 1902 are sound; the cache identity is
what is incomplete.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Two-mode cache identity
1. Arrange one city with F != max(F, C-M).
2. Call `AI_neededFloatingDefenders(false, false, false)` and record include value.
3. In the same game turn call `AI_neededFloatingDefenders(false, false, true)`.
4. Assert the second result is the independently calculated ignore-culture value,
   not the first cached value.
5. Repeat in reverse order.

B. AIR -> LAND ordinary-turn reproduction
1. Sequential-turn AI player owns at least one `UNITAI_DEFENSE_AIR` and one land
   city-defense unit.
2. Give a city culture pressure with C-M > F and non-culture defender terms B>M.
3. Let AIR pass call `AI_neededAirDefenders`, thereby priming city floating caches.
4. Let LAND pass reach `AI_guardCityMinDefender(true)` / `AI_neededDefenders(true)`.
5. Assert required defenders equal the fresh ignore-culture calculation followed
   by one final culture floor; result must not depend on the earlier air call.

C. Exact arithmetic control
For F=0, M=2, C=5 and a non-culture final baseline of 3:

    correct AI_neededDefenders = 5

and assert that an earlier include-culture cache population cannot change it to 6.

D. No-culture-pressure control
If C <= M or C-M <= F, both semantic floating results are equal. Assert behavior
remains unchanged and no unnecessary recalculation changes the result.

E. Const-cache control
Calls with `bConstCache=true` must continue to avoid mutating either cache slot.

C031-WIP296 APPEND -- 2026-09-04 -- F527 / KI#850 CONFIRMED

F527 / KI#850 -- `AI_culturePressureFactor()` MULTIPLIES AN ALREADY MULTI-RIVAL
PRESSURE SUM BY `getEstimateEndTurn()` IN 32-BIT `int`, SO SUPPORTED HIGH-PRESSURE
GAMES CAN OVERFLOW AND TURN MAXIMUM CULTURE PRESSURE INTO A LARGE NEGATIVE VALUE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED -- inherited K-Mod arithmetic overflow with a direct current SAS gameplay
consumer. Current SAS's 48-player DLL and added Slow / Very Slow game speeds enlarge the
reachable state substantially, but the unsafe multiplication itself was introduced upstream.
This is independent of F518's stale average-culture-pressure snapshot: F527 corrupts the live
per-city pressure value before any caching/averaging occurs.

CURRENT CODE / ROOT
-------------------
Current `CvCityAI::AI_culturePressureFactor()` accumulates one squared pairwise culture
pressure contribution for every relevant BFC plot and every alive rival civilization:

    iAnswer += iForeignCulture * iForeignCulture;

where `iForeignCulture` is bounded to at most 100 for one rival/plot pair. Thus one pair can
add 10,000. After the nested loops, K-Mod's late-game dulling performs:

    iAnswer *= kGame.getEstimateEndTurn();
    iAnswer /= kGame.getGameTurn() + kGame.getEstimateEndTurn();

Both `iAnswer` and `getEstimateEndTurn()` are ordinary signed 32-bit `int`. The mathematically
intended result is later capped to 500, but the cap occurs only AFTER the unsafe product.
Therefore the cap cannot protect the intermediate multiplication.

CURRENT SUPPORTED BOUNDS
------------------------
Current SAS has:

    MAX_CIV_PLAYERS = 48

so one city can theoretically be evaluated against as many as 47 non-team major rivals.
`CityPlotIter(*this)` covers the ordinary 21-city-plot BFC. The accumulator itself therefore
has a current structural upper bound of roughly:

    21 plots * 47 rivals * 100^2
      = 9,870,000

which still fits in signed 32-bit integer storage.

`CvGame::setStartTurnYear` initializes `getEstimateEndTurn()` from the sum of the selected
GameSpeed XML turn increments. Current SAS totals are:

    Nitro       165
    Turbo       250
    Quick       330
    Normal      500
    Epic        750
    Marathon   1000
    Slow       1500
    Very Slow  2000

Consequently the safe pre-scale ceiling `INT_MAX / estimateEndTurn` is only about:

    Normal       4,294,967
    Epic         2,863,311
    Marathon     2,147,483
    Slow         1,431,655
    Very Slow    1,073,741

The current maximum pressure sum is therefore far above the safe product range on the longer
supported speeds.

CLEAN CURRENT VERY-SLOW DISCONTINUITY WITNESS
---------------------------------------------
Use a current 48-player-capable Very Slow game (`estimateEndTurn = 2000`) at game turn 500.
Construct a valid old, heavily contested cultural intersection around city A. On each of its
21 BFC plots, let A have plot culture 10 from its owner and let seven alive rival civilizations
each have plot culture 90. Each rival is in culture range on the relevant plots and at A's city
plot, is not a vassal of A's team, and city flipping is allowed. These are ordinary legal plot-
culture values: the helper compares each rival only against A (`90 / (90+10)`), not against
the total culture from all rivals.

For each rival/plot pair current arithmetic gives:

    foreign share = floor(100 * 90 / (90 + 10)) = 90
    range/flip divisor = 2
    adjusted share = 90
    squared contribution = 8,100

With six such rivals:

    pre-scale iAnswer = 21 * 6 * 8,100 = 1,020,600
    product           = 1,020,600 * 2,000 = 2,041,200,000

which still fits signed 32-bit. At turn 500:

    dulled = 2,041,200,000 / 2,500 = 816,480
    factor = min(500, 100 + 816,480 / 60) = 500

So the city correctly reaches the intended maximum-pressure cap.

Add only the seventh otherwise-identical rival:

    pre-scale iAnswer = 21 * 7 * 8,100 = 1,190,700
    mathematical product = 2,381,400,000

This exceeds `INT_MAX` (2,147,483,647). Signed overflow is undefined by the language; on the
actual legacy x86/MSVC arithmetic model used by Civ4 the runtime multiply wraps modulo 2^32:

    wrapped product = -1,913,567,296

Then current integer arithmetic at turn 500 gives approximately:

    -1,913,567,296 / 2,500 = -765,426
    pressure factor = min(500, 100 + (-765,426 / 60))
                    = -12,657

Thus ADDING foreign culture changes the same city discontinuously from the intended maximum
pressure factor 500 to a huge negative pressure factor. This violates the helper's monotonic
meaning and its own lower baseline of 100 in ordinary non-overflow states.

DIRECT CURRENT GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCE -- CULTURE WEIGHT BECOMES NEGATIVE
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayerAI::AI_updateCommerceWeights()` consumes the live city pressure directly:

    int iPressureFactor = pCity->AI_culturePressureFactor();
    int iPressureWeight = iWeight * (iPressureFactor - 100) / 100;
    ...
    iWeight += iPressureWeight;
    pCity->AI_setCultureWeight(iWeight);

Current COMMERCE_CULTURE XML AI weight is 30. Choose otherwise neutral conditions: no cultural
victory weighting, no war-plan scaling, and an era/state that does not enter the late no-
pressure reduction branch.

Six-rival safe state:

    pressure = 500
    pressureWeight = 30 * (500 - 100) / 100 = +120
    final culture weight = 30 + 120 = 150

Seven-rival overflowing state:

    pressure ~= -12,657
    pressureWeight = 30 * (-12,657 - 100) / 100 ~= -3,827
    final culture weight ~= -3,797

The normal per-city culture-commerce consumer contains:

    iWeight = pCity->AI_getCultureWeight();
    FAssert(iWeight >= 0);

so the overflow does not merely perturb an internal score: it can directly violate the
consumer's asserted invariant and makes Culture commerce strongly NEGATIVE in precisely the
city under the greatest foreign cultural pressure.

CURRENT SAS CULTURE-PROCESS CONSEQUENCE
---------------------------------------
Current SAS additionally uses `AI_culturePressureFactor()` in `AI_processValue` to decide
whether Culture process is justified as a local emergency. The current define is:

    SAS_AI_CULTURE_PROCESS_MIN_PRESSURE_FACTOR = 150

For a non-cultural-victory city above first-ring expansion, the correct pressure 500 preserves
the emergency Culture-process path. The overflowing -12,657 is instead `< 150`, so the same
extreme pressure can make SAS classify Culture process as non-emergency and skip it unless the
separate cultural-victory-candidate exception applies. This is the opposite of the intended
local-border-pressure policy.

`SAS_AI_directArtistCultureValuePercent()` also calls the pressure helper, but its later
full-BFC-control / culture-percent checks independently reject the extreme contested fixture;
therefore it is NOT needed as a reproduction and should not be claimed as an additional direct
consequence for this witness.

OTHER LIVE PROPAGATION
----------------------
The same corrupted pressure also feeds:

- `AI_calculateAverages()` via culture-rate-weighted `m_iAverageCulturePressure`;
- culture spreading / espionage mission valuation;
- culture victory / city culture-weight calculations.

These can amplify the error, but the direct negative city-culture-weight invariant and Culture
process inversion above are sufficient. Do not split downstream consumers into separate roots.

ANCESTRY / BIRTH
----------------
K-Mod introduced the culture-pressure feature earlier, initially dulling pressure by era. The
critical multiplication is born in K-Mod practical 730, commit:

    a38e2befe3e774ac8966f5bc72643c9167de2217

That diff changes the previous safe small-era scaling:

    iAnswer *= GC.getNumEraInfos();
    iAnswer /= GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).getCurrentEra() + GC.getNumEraInfos();

into the still-current turn-horizon formula:

    iAnswer *= GC.getGame().getEstimateEndTurn();
    iAnswer /= GC.getGame().getGameTurn() + GC.getGame().getEstimateEndTurn();

without widening the multiplication. The final K-Mod source retains the same 32-bit formula in
`CvCity::culturePressureFactor`. Base AdvCiv later moved the helper to `CvCityAI` but preserves
the arithmetic. Base AdvCiv 1.14 still has `MAX_CIV_PLAYERS = 18` and current Marathon length
1250, so sufficiently multi-rival culture intersections can already overflow upstream; SAS's
48-player DLL and 1500/2000-turn speeds make the reachable range substantially wider.

UPSTREAM / CURRENT BOUNDARY
---------------------------
- Stock BtS / Civ4CE: does not have this K-Mod culture-pressure formula.
- K-Mod: unsafe turn-horizon multiplication present.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14: unsafe multiplication present, with 18-player cap.
- Current AdvCiv-SAS: unsafe multiplication present; 48-player support and longer Slow / Very
  Slow speeds materially increase exposure. SAS only caches `CvGame` / owner locally around
  this helper and does not change the arithmetic root.

DEDUP / ROOT SEPARATION
-----------------------
Whole-album searches for `AI_culturePressureFactor`, culture pressure, integer overflow and
related terms found no prior numbered root for this live per-city arithmetic overflow.

Important nearby findings are distinct:

- F518 / KI#841: `AI_calculateAverages()` snapshots city-set averages before same-turn city
  founding/acquisition. That is a CACHE-LIFETIME / ordering root; F527 can corrupt the live
  pressure even with a perfectly fresh average.
- F526 / KI#849: `AI_neededFloatingDefenders` omits `bIgnoreCulture` from its cache identity.
  That concerns culture GARRISON demand, not this commerce-pressure arithmetic.
- the older `countTotalCulture()` range note was retained as UI/history hardening because no
  current gameplay decision was proved. F527 has direct production/commerce consumers and an
  asserted nonnegative invariant.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Widen the late-game dulling product BEFORE multiplication, e.g. with the legacy compiler's
supported `__int64`:

    __int64 iDulled = (__int64)iAnswer * kGame.getEstimateEndTurn();
    iDulled /= kGame.getGameTurn() + kGame.getEstimateEndTurn();
    iAnswer = (int)iDulled;

The mathematically intended dulled value is bounded by the pre-scale `iAnswer`, so converting
back to int after division is safe under the current accumulator bounds. Keep the existing
500 cap and formula semantics.

A secondary hardening pass could separately consider widening `100 * iForeignCulture` if plot
culture itself can grow to extreme integer values, but that is NOT required to fix or prove
F527 and should not be conflated with this confirmed root.

    min(500, 100 + 952,560 / 60) = 500

F528 / KI#851 - AI_removeWorstCitizen fallback removes a forced specialist but leaves its force target alive
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv regression; current human citizen automation consequence.

CURRENT CODE SHAPE
------------------
`CvCityAI::AI_removeWorstCitizen(SpecialistTypes eIgnoreSpecialist)` has two specialist-removal
passes.

The ordinary pass refuses to choose an ignored or fully forced specialist:

    if (eIgnoreSpecialist == eLoopSpecialist ||
        getSpecialistCount(eLoopSpecialist) <= getForceSpecialistCount(eLoopSpecialist))
    {
        continue;
    }

After that pass chooses a specialist, current Base AdvCiv/SAS performs:

    changeSpecialistCount(eWorstSpecialist, -1);
    // K-Mod. If we had to remove a forced specialist, reduce the force count to match what we did.
    if (getSpecialistCount(eWorstSpecialist) < getForceSpecialistCount(eWorstSpecialist))
        setForceSpecialistCount(eWorstSpecialist, getSpecialistCount(eWorstSpecialist));

But the condition is mathematically dead in this branch. Selection required:

    assigned > forced

and after exactly one removal that becomes:

    assigned_after >= forced

so `assigned_after < forced` cannot occur.

If no ordinary removable specialist or worked plot exists, the function deliberately retries all
assigned specialists, this time ignoring neither `eIgnoreSpecialist` nor force counts:

    if (extraFreeSpecialists() < 0)
    {
        FOR_EACH_ENUM(Specialist)
        {
            if (getSpecialistCount(eLoopSpecialist) <= 0)
                continue;
            ... choose worst specialist ...
        }
    }

    if (eWorstSpecialist != NO_SPECIALIST)
    {
        changeSpecialistCount(eWorstSpecialist, -1);
        return true;
    }

This fallback is the branch that CAN remove a fully forced specialist, but current AdvCiv/SAS no
longer lowers its force count after doing so.

ENGINE / FORCE-TARGET CONTRACT
------------------------------
`CvCity::alterSpecialistCount` is the ordinary TASK_CHANGE_SPECIALIST handler used by the city UI.
When Citizens Automated is enabled, a positive user specialist adjustment first raises that
specialist's force target, then tries to make room while explicitly telling
`AI_removeWorstCitizen` not to remove the newly requested type:

    changeForceSpecialistCount(eSpecialist, ...);
    ...
    if (extraPopulation() > 0 || AI().AI_removeWorstCitizen(eSpecialist))
    {
        if (isSpecialistValid(eSpecialist, 1))
            changeSpecialistCount(eSpecialist, 1);
    }

`extraPopulation()` is based on ACTUAL worked/assigned citizens:

    visiblePopulation() + min(0, extraFreeSpecialists())

and `extraFreeSpecialists()` is:

    totalFreeSpecialists() - getSpecialistPopulation()

Neither subtracts or otherwise accounts for unfulfilled force targets. Therefore removing an
assigned forced specialist without lowering the target leaves a persistent latent demand rather
than a self-correcting population count.

CURRENT SHIPPED REPRODUCTION - CASTE SYSTEM, POPULATION 1
---------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS Caste System (`CIVIC_CASTE_SYSTEM`) retains player-wide unlimited validity for:

- SPECIALIST_ARTIST
- SPECIALIST_SCIENTIST
- SPECIALIST_MERCHANT

so no building-dependent specialist-slot edge is needed.

Use a human population-1 city under Caste System with Citizens Automated ON, no relevant free
specialists, and no non-home worked plot because its sole population citizen is a specialist.
Start with:

    assigned Scientist = 1
    forced Scientist   = 1
    assigned Merchant  = 0
    forced Merchant    = 0

The user clicks +1 Merchant (TASK_CHANGE_SPECIALIST -> alterSpecialistCount).

1. `alterSpecialistCount(Merchant,+1)` raises `forced Merchant` to 1.
2. `extraPopulation()` is 0, so it calls `AI_removeWorstCitizen(Merchant)` to make room.
3. The ordinary specialist pass skips Scientist because `assigned Scientist <= forced Scientist`.
   Merchant is the ignored requested type. There is no non-home worked population plot to remove.
4. The fallback pass now considers ALL assigned specialists and can choose Scientist.
5. It decrements `assigned Scientist` from 1 to 0 and returns WITHOUT lowering
   `forced Scientist`, which remains 1.
6. Merchant is valid under Caste System and is added. Immediate state becomes:

       population          = 1
       assigned Scientist  = 0
       forced Scientist    = 1
       assigned Merchant   = 1
       forced Merchant     = 1

   The sum of forced targets is now 2 for a population-1 city.

NEXT ASSIGNMENT CYCLE - PERSISTENT IMPOSSIBLE TARGET
----------------------------------------------------
`AI_assignWorkingPlots()` later contains a pass whose explicit purpose is:

    // make sure at least the forced amount of specialists are assigned

For Scientist it sees `assigned 0 < forced 1`. Under Caste System the missing Scientist is fully
legal by specialist capacity, so it executes:

    setSpecialistCount(Scientist, 1);

Now the population-1 city temporarily has both Scientist=1 and Merchant=1. The newly-forced flag
causes the overpopulation trim:

    while (extraPopulation() < 0)
        AI_removeWorstCitizen();

Both specialists are exactly at their force targets and there is no removable non-home plot, so
the ordinary pass again has no candidate. The fallback removes one of the forced specialists and,
again, leaves that specialist's force target unchanged.

After the call the city can be population-consistent again (one assigned specialist), but it still
has two impossible force targets. On every later citizen reassignment, the missing target is
restored and another forced specialist is removed. The user/governor state therefore remains
permanently inconsistent instead of resolving the replacement request.

This is a persistent lifecycle defect, not merely one transient frame with assigned < forced.

K-MOD INTENT AND THE LOST SAFEGUARD
-----------------------------------
K-Mod practical 1141, commit:

    ce9fd13beda19a871da4cc9ab333b9ce0536809b

is titled exactly:

    Forced specialist count can no longer exceed total population.

That commit adds the following repair to the FINAL FALLBACK removal branch:

    changeSpecialistCount(eWorstSpecialist, -1);
    // K-Mod. If we had to remove a forced specialist, reduce the force count to match what we did.
    if (getSpecialistCount(eWorstSpecialist) < getForceSpecialistCount(eWorstSpecialist))
        setForceSpecialistCount(eWorstSpecialist, getSpecialistCount(eWorstSpecialist));

That is precisely the branch and invariant required by the current reproduction.

ADVCIV REGRESSION BOUNDARY
--------------------------
The first reachable AdvCiv continuation snapshot, practical 1253 / commit:

    f6ff6a182f...

contains an explicit code-motion diff inside `AI_removeWorstCitizen`:

1. it ADDS the K-Mod force-count repair after the EARLIER ordinary specialist removal;
2. it REMOVES the same four-line repair from the FINAL fallback removal.

The relevant diff therefore does not merely omit an upstream fix accidentally; it physically
moves the safeguard from the branch that can remove forced specialists to the branch whose
`assigned > forced` selection predicate makes `assigned_after < forced` impossible.

Later AdvCiv refactors preserve that placement. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS are substantively
identical at the two removal exits (apart from SAS cached/default-specialist spelling).

The later AdvCiv `advc.121` change (`5cac5b3ad38b64d34d6f86fdc5f21e9101231dd0`, practical 3599,
"Smarter interpretation of addtl. forced specialists") strengthens the UI-side meaning of human

Worker/improvement helpers. Revisit the unsaved SAS culture-targeting fields only if a normal
save/load or human-automation consumer can observe them before `AI_updateCommerceWeights`
refreshes them; do not promote a merely transient/cache-design smell.

================================================================================
C031-WIP298 - F529 / KI#852 CONFIRMED
CvCityAI::AI_updateSpecialYieldMultiplier - project production emphasis is unreachable
================================================================================

STATUS
------
F529 / KI#852 CONFIRMED.
F530 / provisional KI#853 is the next UNUSED root.
Queue 005 CvGameCoreDLL/CvCityAI.cpp remains OPEN.
Repository source untouched.

ROOT
----
`AI_updateSpecialYieldMultiplier()` intends to give major production work the same special-yield
push when a city is producing either a World Wonder OR a Project:

    BuildingTypes eProductionBuilding = getProductionBuilding();
    if (eProductionBuilding != NO_BUILDING)
    {
        if (GC.getInfo(eProductionBuilding).isWorldWonder() || isProductionProject())
        {
            m_aiSpecialYieldMultiplier[YIELD_PRODUCTION] += 50;
            m_aiSpecialYieldMultiplier[YIELD_COMMERCE] -= 25;
        }
        ...
    }

The `isProductionProject()` half is nested inside `eProductionBuilding != NO_BUILDING`.
A city producing a Project has no production Building, so `getProductionBuilding()` returns
NO_BUILDING and the outer block is skipped. Therefore `isProductionProject()` can never cause the
+50 Production / -25 Commerce project emphasis.

This is not a policy/tuning disagreement. It is an unreachable half of an explicit `A || B`
condition caused by putting the `B` test under a prerequisite that excludes B's state.

LIVE CALLER / STATE
-------------------
`AI_assignWorkingPlots()` calls `AI_updateSpecialYieldMultiplier()` before forced-specialist
repair, population assignment and `AI_juggleCitizens()`. `AI_yieldValue()` then consumes:

    AI_specialYieldMultiplier(YIELD_PRODUCTION)
    AI_specialYieldMultiplier(YIELD_COMMERCE)

when ranking worked/unworked plots and specialists.

Thus the missing project branch directly changes ordinary citizen allocation throughout Project
production. It is not dead UI/debug state.

CURRENT ADVCIV/SAS INERTIA DETAIL
---------------------------------
AdvCiv practical 121 added inertia only to the Production special multiplier:

    m_aiSpecialYieldMultiplier[YIELD_PRODUCTION] += iOldProductionMult;
    m_aiSpecialYieldMultiplier[YIELD_PRODUCTION] /= 2;

Therefore, from a neutral previous Production multiplier of 0, a correctly reachable project
+50 would become +25 on the first assignment refresh, then +37, +43, ... on subsequent refreshes.
The Commerce side is not averaged and would immediately receive -25.

The current bug instead contributes 0 / 0 from the Project-specific branch on every refresh.
Other strategy/flavor modifiers can coexist, but they do not restore the missing project-specific
term.

DETERMINISTIC CITIZEN-CHOICE FLIP
---------------------------------
Use a neutral controlled city where all food/growth terms are equal between two candidate jobs,
base/average modifiers are 100%, Commerce weight is 100, and no unrelated emphasis differs.
`AI_yieldValue()` uses base values:

    Production: 8 per hammer
    Commerce:   4 per commerce

Compare equal-food jobs with relevant yields:

    Job H: 2 hammers
    Job C: 1 hammer + 3 commerce

CURRENT BUGGED PROJECT STATE (no project special multiplier):

    H = 2 * 8 = 16
    C = 1 * 8 + 3 * 4 = 20

so the governor prefers C.

CORRECT FIRST PROJECT REFRESH FROM NEUTRAL PRIOR STATE:
Project +50 Production is averaged by AdvCiv inertia to +25; Commerce receives -25 immediately.

    H = 16 * 1.25 = 20
    C = (8 * 1.25) + (12 * 0.75) = 10 + 9 = 19

so the governor prefers H.

The unreachable branch therefore produces an actual assignment flip on the very first refresh;
subsequent project turns would strengthen the Production bias further as the inertial multiplier
approaches +50.

This is exactly the purpose implied by the source: major long-term production (World Wonder OR
Project) should make the city temporarily emphasize Production over Commerce. World Wonders get
that behavior; Projects do not.

ANCESTRY / BOUNDARY
-------------------
The defect predates K-Mod.

- Civ4CE BtS reconstruction: same nesting and same unreachable `|| isProductionProject()` half.
- K-Mod 1.46: same nesting; K-Mod retains the explicit World Wonder OR Project comment/behavior.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14: same nesting; later AdvCiv refactors/inertia do not repair it.
- Current AdvCiv-SAS: same semantic defect, with only surrounding refactors/custom changes.

So this is an inherited stock-BtS root that survives through K-Mod, AdvCiv and SAS.

DEDUP
-----
Whole-album literal/semantic search found no existing root for Project production being excluded
from `AI_updateSpecialYieldMultiplier` by the Building-only outer guard.

Do not merge with F522 / KI#845:
- F522 is stale Emphasize state preserved by the practical-1675 clear->continue refactor.
- F529 is the Project-specific producer term never being generated at all, even with clean emphasis
  state and a fresh multiplier calculation.

Do not merge with project/building-choice roots: this bug occurs after a Project is already in the
production queue and changes citizen yield assignment, not whether the Project gets selected.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Separate the Project test from the Building-only block, e.g. conceptually:

    BuildingTypes eProductionBuilding = getProductionBuilding();
    if ((eProductionBuilding != NO_BUILDING &&
         GC.getInfo(eProductionBuilding).isWorldWonder()) ||
        isProductionProject())
    {
        m_aiSpecialYieldMultiplier[YIELD_PRODUCTION] += 50;
        m_aiSpecialYieldMultiplier[YIELD_COMMERCE] -= 25;
    }

    if (eProductionBuilding != NO_BUILDING)
    {
        // Building-specific FoodKept adjustment only.
        ...
    }

Do not modify source during the audit.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Project multiplier generation
1. City with neutral old special multipliers begins a Project.
2. Run `AI_updateSpecialYieldMultiplier()`.
3. Assert the Project contributes the same raw +50 Production / -25 Commerce term as the existing
   World-Wonder branch (before AdvCiv Production inertia).

B. Building-only control
A normal non-Wonder building must not receive the Project/Wonder +50/-25 term.

C. World-Wonder control
World Wonder behavior must remain unchanged.

D. Citizen-choice flip

prior Production multiplier, assert the intended Project term changes the relative ranking from
C > H to H > C.

E. Inertia control

special multiplier follows existing AdvCiv inertia rather than jumping directly to +50; the repair

================================================================================
C031-WIP299 - F530 / KI#853 CONFIRMED
CvCityAI::AI_yieldValue - anger-expiry modulo maps exact full anger cycles to zero turns
================================================================================

STATUS
------
F530 / KI#853 CONFIRMED.
F531 / provisional KI#854 is the next UNUSED root.
Queue 005 CvGameCoreDLL/CvCityAI.cpp remains OPEN.
Repository source untouched.

ROOT
----
While valuing food for future growth, `AI_yieldValue()` tries to estimate whether one point of
temporary anger will disappear before the city grows. For all three stacked anger timers it uses
plain modulo:

    int iTurnsUntilAngerIsReduced = iHurryAngerTimer % flatHurryAngerLength();
    int iTurnsUntilAngerIsReduced = iConscriptAngerTimer % flatConscriptAngerLength();
    int iTurnsUntilAngerIsReduced = iDefyResolutionAngerTimer %
            flatDefyResolutionAngerLength();

and then:

    if (iTurnsUntilAngerIsReduced <= iApproxTurnsToGrow)
        iFutureHappy++;

That modulo is wrong at every exact multiple of the anger-stack length. In particular, for the
extremely ordinary state `timer == length`, it returns 0 and says the next unhappy point is
reduced immediately.

The engine's authoritative unhappy-count formula proves the opposite. `CvCity` computes Hurry,
Conscript and Defy anger stacks as:

    ((timer - 1) / length) + 1

(i.e. `ceil(timer / length)` for positive timers). Therefore when `timer == length`, the current
anger point remains for all `length` decrements; it does not disappear at turn 0.

For a positive timer, the correct number of decrements until the NEXT anger stack disappears is:

    ((timer - 1) % length) + 1

not:

    timer % length

This is an arithmetic boundary error, not an AI-policy disagreement.

NORMAL PRODUCER - FIRST WHIP / FIRST DRAFT
-----------------------------------------
This boundary is not rare or synthetic.

`CvCity::hurry()` does:

    int iHurryAngerLength = hurryAngerLength(eHurry);
    ...
    changeHurryAngerTimer(iHurryAngerLength);

So when a city had no previous whip anger, its first anger-causing whip creates exactly:

    hurryTimer == hurryAngerLength

`CvCity::conscript()` likewise does:

    int const iAngerLength = flatConscriptAngerLength();
    ...
    changeConscriptAngerTimer(iAngerLength);

so a first draft creates exactly the same `timer == length` boundary.

On stock/current Normal speed with the ordinary `HURRY_ANGER_DIVISOR = 10` and
`HurryConscriptAngerPercent = 100`, a normal zero-modifier city therefore has a 10-turn anger
length. Immediately after the first whip/draft, `AI_yieldValue` predicts 0 turns until the next
anger point disappears although `CvCity::doTurn` has to decrement the timer ten times before the
one anger stack reaches zero.

Other current game speeds simply change the cycle length; the exact-multiple error remains.
Defy-resolution anger has the same formula and can also hit exact multiples (including ordinary
full-length additions when not religion-divided), but Hurry/Draft alone are enough to prove F530.

LIVE GROWTH-VALUATION CONSEQUENCE
--------------------------------
The false zero is consumed in the normal food-growth path, not merely logged.

Use a healthy, non-disordered city with no food-production order and no food/avoid-growth emphasis.
Immediately after a first whip:

- before the whip the city had one spare happy;
- the new whip anger leaves `iHappinessLevel == 0`;
- the food bar is already above the `bBarFull` 80% threshold;
- the city can grow in fewer than the real anger-length turns;
- at least one genuinely useful future job exists;
- `iGrowthValue > 0`.

BUGGED calculation:

    timer % length == 0
    0 <= iApproxTurnsToGrow
    => iFutureHappy += 1
    => iPopToGrow = 1

CORRECT calculation:

    ((timer - 1) % length) + 1 == length
    length > iApproxTurnsToGrow
    => no future happiness yet
    => iPopToGrow = 0

Because the food bar is already >80% full, the correct `iPopToGrow == 0` state does not enter the
fallback `bFillingBar` food-growth valuation. The bugged state does enter ordinary growth
valuation. Food therefore receives a positive `iFoodGrowthValue` for growth that the city's
current happiness cap cannot actually support before the anger expires.

CONTROLLED JOB FLIP
-------------------
The effect is large enough to change citizen ranking, not just a hidden counter.

Take neutral 100% yield modifiers, no process, no Slavery contribution, no emphasis, and pass a
controlled positive `iGrowthValue = 10` to the same `AI_yieldValue` path. Current SAS uses:

    iBaseProductionValue = 8

and its ordinary non-emphasized happy/non-angry food baseline adds 3 points for one food.

Compare otherwise-neutral candidate jobs:

    Job F: +1 food
    Job H: +1 hammer

At `iAdjustedFoodPerTurn = 0`:

CORRECT full-bar / no-growth-headroom state:

    F = 3
    H = 8
    => H wins

BUGGED invented `iPopToGrow = 1` state:

    devalueRate = 18 - 1*3 = 15
    one food receives about +10 growth value at this controlled scale
    F ~= 13
    H = 8
    => F wins

The exact numeric growth score varies with ordinary city context, but the branch-level difference
is deterministic: at the exact anger-cycle boundary, the current code can activate positive growth
food value when the authoritative anger timer says no happiness will recover before growth. The
citizen governor, Worker/job comparisons and other `AI_yieldValue` consumers can observe that
misvaluation.

UPSTREAM / CURRENT BOUNDARY
---------------------------
The defect is inherited from stock BtS rather than introduced by SAS.

- Civ4CE BtS reconstruction: same `% flat...AngerLength()` formulas for Hurry, Conscript and Defy.
- K-Mod 1.46: same three formulas.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14: same three formulas.
- Current AdvCiv-SAS: same arithmetic; SAS adds surrounding food-growth tuning but does not repair
  the expiry calculation. Those SAS growth incentives can make the wrong headroom more visible,
  but they are not the root.

DEDUP / ROOT SEPARATION
-----------------------
Whole-album searches for `iTurnsUntilAngerIsReduced`, `% flatHurryAngerLength`, anger modulo and
future-happiness expiry found no prior numbered root for this arithmetic boundary.

Do not merge with Hurry-policy / sacrifice-cost findings:
- F524 / KI#847 concerns specialist-count accounting inside `AI_citizenSacrificeCost` and can make
  population sacrifice itself look like a subsidy.
- F530 begins AFTER valid anger already exists and predicts the expiry of that anger incorrectly
  while valuing future city growth.

The producer, variable, invariant and repair are independent.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
For each positive timer, replace plain modulo with the positive-cycle remainder:

    int iTurnsUntilAngerIsReduced =
            ((iHurryAngerTimer - 1) % flatHurryAngerLength()) + 1;

and analogously for Conscript and Defy anger.

The surrounding `timer > 0` guards already make `timer - 1` safe. `flat...AngerLength()` is clamped
to at least 1 by the corresponding city helpers. Do not alter growth policy, happiness weights or
anger duration itself.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. First-whip exact-cycle boundary
1. City with zero hurry anger; perform an anger-causing whip.
2. Assert `timer == flatHurryAngerLength()`.
3. Assert predicted turns until the next anger point disappears equals `length`, not 0.

B. First-draft exact-cycle boundary
Repeat A with `conscript()` and `flatConscriptAngerLength()`.

C. General cycle arithmetic
For length 10, assert:

    timer  1 -> 1 turn
    timer  9 -> 9 turns
    timer 10 -> 10 turns
    timer 11 -> 1 turn
    timer 20 -> 10 turns
    timer 21 -> 1 turn

D. Growth-headroom control
At `iHappinessLevel=0`, full food bar, growth in fewer than `length` turns and `timer==length`,
assert the anger source does NOT add `iFutureHappy`; `iPopToGrow` must not become positive solely
from that timer.

E. Citizen-value control
With the controlled +1F vs +1H fixture above, assert an exact-cycle anger timer does not activate
the premature growth-food term. Non-boundary timers must preserve their existing intended behavior.

NUMBERING / CURRENT STONE
-------------------------
F530 / KI#853 is CONFIRMED.
F531 / provisional KI#854 is the next UNUSED root.

Queue 005 `CvGameCoreDLL/CvCityAI.cpp` OPEN.
32/169 unique files complete.
Repository source untouched.
Latest physical checkpoint: C031-WIP299 (this file).

----

slavery and happiness timing) for the same exact-cycle / denominator / sign class, then resume the

the owner of consequences caused solely by SAS's deliberately disabled legacy land best-build

END C031-WIP299

================================================================================
C031-WIP300 - F531 / KI#854 CONFIRMED
CvCityAI::AI_yieldValue - anger recovery is compared to growth before the anger decrement occurs
================================================================================

STATUS
------
F531 / KI#854 CONFIRMED.
F532 / provisional KI#855 is the next UNUSED root.
Queue 005 CvGameCoreDLL/CvCityAI.cpp remains OPEN.
Repository source untouched.

ROOT
----
F530 corrected the number of anger-timer decrements required for the next unhappy point to vanish.
There is a second independent error in the immediately following comparison:

    if (iTurnsUntilAngerIsReduced <= iApproxTurnsToGrow)
        iFutureHappy++;

`iApproxTurnsToGrow` is the number of upcoming `doGrowth()` executions needed to reach the growth
threshold. In the ordinary player/city turn sequence, however, the city's anger timers are
decremented AFTER `doGrowth()`, not before it.

Therefore an anger point requiring N decrements is gone in time for growth only when growth occurs
after MORE than N upcoming growth executions:

    iTurnsUntilAngerIsReduced < iApproxTurnsToGrow

not when the two counts are equal.

NORMAL TURN ORDER PROOF
-----------------------
`CvPlayer::doTurn()` performs:

    AI().AI_doTurnPre();
    ...
    AI().AI_assignWorkingPlots();
    ...
    FOR_EACH_CITY_VAR(pLoopCity, *this)
        pLoopCity->doTurn();

Thus the ordinary citizen assignment / `AI_yieldValue` pass happens before the city's own turn.

Inside `CvCity::doTurn()` the relevant order is:

    AI().AI_doTurn();
    ...
    doGrowth();
    doCulture();
    ...
    doProduction(...);
    ...
    if (getHurryAngerTimer() > 0)
        changeHurryAngerTimer(-1);
    if (getConscriptAngerTimer() > 0)
        changeConscriptAngerTimer(-1);
    if (getDefyResolutionAngerTimer() > 0)
        changeDefyResolutionAngerTimer(-1);

So every upcoming `doGrowth()` sees the anger timer BEFORE the decrement belonging to that same
city turn.

DETERMINISTIC LAST-ANGER-TURN WITNESS
------------------------------------
Use the corrected F530 remainder calculation and an ordinary city whose current anger timer is 1.
That state occurs naturally on the final turn of any whip/draft anger stack because the timer is
decremented by one each city turn.

Suppose the current food state will grow on the upcoming `doGrowth()`:

    iTurnsUntilAngerIsReduced = 1
    iApproxTurnsToGrow = 1

CURRENT comparison:

    1 <= 1  -> true
    => iFutureHappy++

ACTUAL sequence:

    citizen valuation sees timer 1
    -> upcoming doGrowth runs while timer is still 1
    -> only afterward timer changes 1 -> 0

The extra happiness therefore is NOT available to the growth being evaluated.

The next case proves the exact strict relation rather than merely saying there is some ordering
ambiguity:

    timer-decrements-needed = 1
    iApproxTurnsToGrow = 2

Current city turn:
    first doGrowth does not yet grow
    then timer 1 -> 0

Next city turn:
    second doGrowth occurs with the anger already gone

So 1 < 2 must count the future happiness, while 1 == 1 must not.

GENERAL PHASE TABLE
-------------------
Let D be decrements needed for the next anger point to disappear and G be upcoming `doGrowth()`
executions until growth.

    D=1, G=1 -> anger still active at growth   -> false
    D=1, G=2 -> anger gone before growth       -> true
    D=2, G=2 -> anger still active at growth   -> false
    D=2, G=3 -> anger gone before growth       -> true

The correct condition for the normal assignment-before-city-turn path is therefore `D < G`.

LIVE CITIZEN-VALUATION CONSEQUENCE
----------------------------------
As with F530, the false future happiness feeds directly into `iPopToGrow` and therefore the food
growth component of `AI_yieldValue`.

A particularly clean ordinary state is:

- one anger stack remains with timer 1;
- without that stack the city would have one spare happiness, so current `iHappinessLevel == 0`;
- food is already above the 80% `bBarFull` threshold;
- the city will grow on the upcoming `doGrowth()` (`iApproxTurnsToGrow == 1`);
- no avoid-growth / food-production / severe-unhealth exception applies;
- a useful future job exists and `iGrowthValue > 0`.

BUGGED phase test:

    1 <= 1
    => iFutureHappy = 1
    => iPopToGrow = 1
    => normal positive growth-food valuation remains active

CORRECT phase test:

    1 < 1 is false
    => no recovered happiness yet
    => iPopToGrow = 0

Because the food bar is already full enough to disable the fallback `bFillingBar` path, the
correct state does not give food a growth bonus for a population increase that will occur before
anger expires. The bugged state does. The same +1F versus +1H controlled ranking used for F530 can
therefore flip here as well, but on a NON-multiple timer value; this is why F531 is not merely an
extension of F530's modulo boundary.

UPSTREAM / CURRENT BOUNDARY
---------------------------
The `<= iApproxTurnsToGrow` comparison is inherited throughout the same code lineage:

- Civ4CE BtS reconstruction: present.
- K-Mod 1.46: present.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14: present.
- Current AdvCiv-SAS: present.

SAS does not change the relevant city-turn ordering: normal player citizen assignment still occurs
before city `doGrowth`, and the three anger timers still decrement later in `CvCity::doTurn`.

DEDUP / ROOT SEPARATION
-----------------------
F531 is adjacent to but independent from F530 / KI#853.

F530:
- expression defect: `timer % length`;
- maps exact cycle multiples (e.g. timer 10 at length 10) to 0 instead of 10;
- remains wrong even if comparison uses strict `<`.

F531:
- event-phase defect: `D <= G` despite anger decrement occurring after each `doGrowth`;
- fails on ordinary non-boundary states such as timer 1 / growth 1;
- remains wrong even after replacing modulo with F530's correct positive-cycle remainder.

The two bugs require independent corrections and regression cases, so keep separate roots despite
sharing the same future-happiness block.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
After F530's corrected positive-cycle remainder is calculated, use a strict comparison for the
normal pre-city-turn valuation path:

    if (iTurnsUntilAngerIsReduced < iApproxTurnsToGrow)
        iFutureHappy++;

Because `AI_yieldValue` is callable from multiple contexts, implementation should verify that no
important caller deliberately invokes this specific future-growth estimate after the current
turn's anger decrement but before the next growth. If such a context exists, encode the event
phase explicitly rather than silently preserving the wrong normal-turn result. The confirmed root
is the ordinary `CvPlayer::doTurn -> AI_assignWorkingPlots -> CvCity::doTurn -> doGrowth -> anger
decrement` path.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Last anger turn / immediate growth
1. Set one anger source to timer 1.
2. Arrange growth on the upcoming `doGrowth` (`iApproxTurnsToGrow=1`).
3. During the normal pre-city-turn citizen assignment, assert that source does NOT add future
   happiness.

B. Last anger turn / growth one city turn later
1. Timer 1.
2. `iApproxTurnsToGrow=2`.
3. Assert the source DOES add future happiness because the timer reaches zero after the first
   non-growing `doGrowth` and before the second.

C. Two-decrement boundary
Assert D=2/G=2 is false and D=2/G=3 is true.

D. Combined F530+F531 matrix
With length 10, use F530's corrected decrement counts and then the strict phase comparison:

    timer 10, growth 10 -> false
    timer 10, growth 11 -> true
    timer  1, growth  1 -> false
    timer  1, growth  2 -> true
    timer 11, growth  1 -> false
    timer 11, growth  2 -> true

E. Citizen ranking
At current happiness balance 0 and an already-full food bar, verify that timer 1 / immediate growth
does not activate the premature growth-food value and cannot flip a neutral +1H job to +1F solely
through predicted anger recovery.

NUMBERING / CURRENT STONE
-------------------------
F531 / KI#854 is CONFIRMED.
F532 / provisional KI#855 is the next UNUSED root.

32/169 unique files complete.
Repository source untouched.
Latest physical checkpoint: C031-WIP300 (this file).

----
Continue under F532 unused. Finish adjacent `AI_yieldValue` timing arithmetic, especially anger

C031-WIP301 — POST-F531 F532 CONTROLS / SAS FILE-LOCAL HELPER COVERAGE

1. AI_yieldValue ADJACENT SLAVERY / HURRY ARITHMETIC — CLOSED
-------------------------------------------------------------
After F530/F531, the remaining obvious Slavery denominator and hurry-loop concerns were challenged
against current shipped XML.

`AI_yieldValue` can divide its population-rush value by `getHurryCostModifier(true)`. The generic
engine formula could mathematically reach zero if XML/player hurry modifiers reached -100, but
current SAS has no negative `iHurryCostModifier` / `iGlobalHurryModifier` data that supplies such a
state. Current `CIV4HurryInfo.xml` has:

- HURRY_POPULATION: 27 production per population, anger enabled;
- HURRY_GOLD: 0 production per population, 3 gold per production, no anger.

The unusual `kOwner.canHurry(eHurry) || canPopRush()` loop can therefore inspect Gold hurry while
population rushing is available, but the inaccessible Gold entry contributes zero production per
population and cannot win the maximum. No current divide-by-zero or valuation collision was proved.
Keep as robustness/style debt only.

2. AI_timeWeightedImprovementYields UPGRADE NORMALIZATION — CLOSED
-----------------------------------------------------------------
The apparent `1-exp(0)` denominator risk does not occur with current improvement data. The shipped
upgrade graph is Cottage -> Hamlet -> Village -> Town with positive upgrade times (10/20/40), while
`iTimeScale == 0` has an explicit never-upgrades path. No zero-time upgrade cycle / live zero
denominator witness exists.

3. AI_growthValuePerFood TRANSIENT SPECIALIST COUNTS — CLOSED
-------------------------------------------------------------
The inherited comment about free specialists and a possible negative
`getMaxSpecialistCount - getSpecialistCount` state was challenged. A transient negative
`iAvailable` does not append phantom jobs; the assertion path is tolerant because negative extra
specialists can satisfy `isSpecialistValid`, and only positive availability is appended to the
unworked-job list. Free specialists do not consume ordinary population jobs. No current gameplay
root was established.

The separate `std::partial_sort(..., std::less_equal<int>())` non-strict-comparator issue remains a
formal STL robustness note already recorded earlier; no deterministic current gameplay witness was
added here.

4. SAS FILE-LOCAL HELPER COVERAGE — KI#197.11 BROADENING, NOT F532
-----------------------------------------------------------------
The previously zero-literal-coverage SAS file-local helpers were audited before returning to the
large inherited bodies.

`SAS_countPortCitiesForWaterArea` counts only:

    pLoopCity->waterArea(true) == &kWaterArea

and ignores `secondWaterArea()`. In a dual-coast city whose relevant selected sea is its secondary
water area, the secured peaceful naval profile undercounts local ports. Since the stock ceiling is:

    navalPortCities * MAX_TRACKED_UNITS_PER_PORT_CITY

this can lower the peaceful stock limit and shut the forced secured-naval production floor off too
early on that sea.

`SAS_getMilitaryProductionCapacityPercent` has the same primary-water-only topology when called for
a selected naval water area: a dual-coast city producing a tracked naval role for its secondary sea
does not contribute to the selected-sea numerator.

These are real topology/accounting broadenings, but DO NOT spend F532. They belong to the existing
KI#197.11 secured-naval-production-share / selected-water-area accounting family (and overlap the
already documented second-water topology family around KI#193.2 / KI#197.6). Keep one root and
broaden its repair/test matrix.

5. AI_strictAdditionalHappy GLOBAL HAPPINESS OMISSION — CURRENTLY MASKED / CLOSED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The custom helper intentionally counts reliable local happiness channels but does not add
`CvBuildingInfo::getGlobalHappiness()`.

Current XML contains exactly two positive global-happiness buildings discovered in this pass:

- Hagia Sophia: +2 global happiness;
- Eiffel Tower: +1 global happiness.

Both are Wonders. Crucially, every live use of `AI_strictAdditionalHappy` sits inside:

    if (!bWonder && SAS_AI_BUILDING_VALUE_REGULAR_BUILDINGS_OPTIMIZE)

Therefore neither shipped global-happiness building can reach the strict regular-building
prefilter at all. The omission cannot currently misclassify a live building in this code path.
Treat as future-proofing debt only. If a future non-Wonder receives `iGlobalHappiness > 0`, extend
the helper or re-evaluate the gate.

6. PERSISTENT CvCityAI MEMBER / SAVE-LOAD INVENTORY — CLOSED
------------------------------------------------------------
Decision-bearing `CvCityAI` members were checked across constructor initialization and read/write
serialization. The new culture-victory rank and investment fields are explicitly transient and
intentionally not serialized. Normal AI turn start calls `CvPlayerAI::AI_updateCommerceWeights()`
before that AI's research/commerce/military/production work, refreshing those fields before the
normal AI decision path. Other persistent decision state has matching constructor/read/write
handling; obvious caches are intentionally serialized for deterministic mid-turn/replay behavior.
No independent save/load discontinuity was proved.

7. AI_projectValue LOW-COVERAGE LARGE BODY — CURRENT SAS DELTA CLOSED
--------------------------------------------------------------------
`AI_projectValue` had only one literal album mention despite being a large live project-production
valuation helper. A direct Base AdvCiv 1.14 vs current SAS semantic diff shows that SAS changes in
this body are reference caching only (`kGame`, `kTeam`, `kOwner`) and do not alter the project
formula. The inherited TechShare, SDI, Manhattan and Space-victory arithmetic was challenged for
obvious invalid sentinels / zero divisors / wrong receiver use; no live independent F532 candidate
survived this tranche.
