C031-WIP302 — F532 / KI#855 CONFIRMED: NATURAL-YIELD THRESHOLD OMITTED FROM
FINAL-IMPROVEMENT PROJECTION; FINANCIAL COTTAGE JOBS CAN BE RANKED BELOW WORSE JOBS
================================================================================

STATUS
------
Queue 005 `CvGameCoreDLL/CvCityAI.cpp` remains OPEN.
32/169 unique files complete.
F446-F532 confirmed.
F533 / provisional KI#856 is the next UNUSED root.
Repository source untouched.

This checkpoint first closes the temporary-citizen Worker-demand concern opened after WIP301, then
promotes a separate inherited AdvCiv/K-Mod projection defect that survives a current-SAS XML fixture
and a direct ordinary citizen-assignment flip.

1. AI_updateWorkersHaveAndNeeded TEMPORARY AI_addBestCitizen MUTATION — CLOSED
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
`AI_updateWorkersHaveAndNeeded()` temporarily models the extra citizen expected from future growth by
calling:

    CityPlotTypes eBestPlot = NO_CITYPLOT;
    SpecialistTypes eBestSpecialist = NO_SPECIALIST;
    if (angryPopulation() == 0)
        AI_addBestCitizen(true, true, &eBestPlot, &eBestSpecialist);

It later removes exactly the job returned through those out-parameters:

    if (eBestPlot != NO_CITYPLOT)
        setWorkingPlot(eBestPlot, false);
    if (eBestSpecialist != NO_SPECIALIST)
        changeSpecialistCount(eBestSpecialist, -1);

The full `AI_addBestCitizen()` body was checked rather than assuming the out-parameters were merely
advisory. Every successful mutation reports the object it actually added:

- a plot mutation sets `eBestPlot` and works that plot;
- a specialist mutation sets `eBestSpecialist` and increments that specialist;
- when no job can be added, the helper returns false without creating an unreported citizen job.

The secondary setter effects were then checked. `setWorkingPlot(true/false)` symmetrically changes
working population and plot-yield accounting; the extra `updatePlotBuilder()` call is graphical
plot-builder maintenance and does not alter authoritative AI/gameplay state. Specialist assignment
similarly updates specialist population, yields/commerce and Great-Person rate through the ordinary
specialist processing path, and the inverse `changeSpecialistCount(...,-1)` restores those values.
No gameplay-side state that survives the rollback was found.

Conclusion: this is an intentional inherited K-Mod simulation of the city's next citizen, not an
unbalanced persistent mutation. Do not spend a finding on it.

2. F532 ROOT — ADVC NATURAL-THRESHOLD MIGRATION DID NOT REACH K-MOD'S FINAL-UPGRADE
   PROJECTION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS Financial no longer uses the original ordinary extra-yield threshold. Its trait XML is:

    <ExtraYieldThresholds/>
    <ExtraYieldNaturalThresholds>
        <iExtraYieldNaturalThreshold>0</iExtraYieldNaturalThreshold>
        <iExtraYieldNaturalThreshold>0</iExtraYieldNaturalThreshold>
        <iExtraYieldNaturalThreshold>3</iExtraYieldNaturalThreshold>
    </ExtraYieldNaturalThresholds>

The source comment identifies this as `advc.908a`: the original Financial +1-commerce threshold was
replaced with a "natural" commerce threshold of 3.

The authoritative tile-yield calculation in `CvPlot::calculateYield()` knows about BOTH mechanisms.
After the ordinary `getExtraYieldThreshold` test, AdvCiv separately applies:

    int iThresh = GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).getExtraYieldNaturalThreshold(eYield);
    if (iThresh > 0)
    {
        if (iYield >= iThresh || iNatureYield + 1 >= iThresh)
            iYield += EXTRA_YIELD;
    }

Thus actual current Financial plot yields correctly receive the extra commerce whenever the AdvCiv
natural-threshold rule is met.

`CvCityAI::AI_finalImprovementYieldDifference()`, however, is still structurally the old K-Mod
projection. It calculates the raw current-improvement -> final-upgrade yield difference and then
contains only this threshold correction:

    int extraYieldThresh = kOwner.getExtraYieldThreshold(eLoopYield);
    if (extraYieldThresh > 0 &&
        kPlot.calculateNatureYield(eLoopYield, getTeam()) < extraYieldThresh)
    {
        if (kPlot.getYield(eLoopYield) > extraYieldThresh)
            iYieldDiff -= EXTRA_YIELD;
        if (kPlot.getYield(eLoopYield) + iYieldDiff > extraYieldThresh)
            iYieldDiff += EXTRA_YIELD;
    }

There is no `getExtraYieldNaturalThreshold()` branch.

With current XML, every ordinary `ExtraYieldThreshold` is zero for Financial, so this entire
correction is dead precisely where the live Financial rule is now stored. The helper therefore
projects only the raw improvement-yield delta and can omit the +1 commerce that the final upgrade
will really receive under `calculateYield()`.

3. WHY THIS IS NOT THE OLD WIP288 EXTRA-YIELD CONTROL
----------------------------------------------------
WIP288 challenged an apparent `>` / `>=` asymmetry in the older ordinary
`ExtraYieldThreshold` projection path and correctly closed that specific issue for current data:
Financial had moved to `ExtraYieldNaturalThreshold`, while shipped ordinary thresholds were zero.

That negative control was too narrow. The exact reason the ordinary-threshold comparator was
currently data-dead creates the new live defect: the replacement natural-threshold mechanism was
never added to K-Mod's projected final-improvement calculation.

Therefore WIP288's conclusion should be read narrowly as:

    ordinary ExtraYieldThreshold comparator edge -> current-data dead

NOT as:

    all current Financial projected-upgrade threshold handling -> correct.

F532 corrects that audit boundary rather than colliding with the old note.

There is also an earlier Queue-004 AdvCiv defect in `CvPlayer::updateExtraYieldThresholds`: the
natural-threshold minimum-selection condition compares against the unrelated ordinary threshold.
That source typo is currently masked because only Financial supplies one positive natural threshold.
F532 is independent: even when the player's stored natural threshold is the correct value 3,
`AI_finalImprovementYieldDifference()` never reads it at all.

4. CURRENT SAS PLAINS COTTAGE -> TOWN WITNESS
---------------------------------------------
Use a Financial AI city after Machinery but before Printing Press and Steam Power, with no river on
the candidate plots.

Current SAS XML gives:

Plains terrain:

    1 food, 1 hammer, 0 commerce

Cottage:

    +1 commerce
    upgrades through Hamlet / Village to Town

Town:

    +4 commerce

Financial natural threshold:

    +1 commerce when the AdvCiv natural-threshold rule reaches Commerce 3

Therefore a non-river Plains Cottage currently yields:

    1 food, 1 hammer, 1 commerce

It does not yet meet the Financial threshold.

Its true eventual Financial Town yield is:

    base Plains                  1F / 1H / 0C
    Town raw improvement                    +4C
    Financial natural threshold             +1C
    --------------------------------------------
    actual eventual Town         1F / 1H / 5C

But `AI_finalImprovementYieldDifference()` sees only the raw Cottage->Town improvement change:

    Town raw 4C - Cottage raw 1C = +3C

and never adds the natural-threshold crossing. Starting from the currently worked Cottage's 1C, its
projected final job is therefore only:

    BUG projection:              1F / 1H / 4C
    correct projection:          1F / 1H / 5C

The projection is one commerce low exactly because the upgrade chain crosses the current Financial
natural threshold.

5. CURRENT SAS SAME-FOOD COMPETITOR
-----------------------------------
Current SAS moved Lumbermill construction to Machinery. Before Steam Power, a non-river Plains
Forest + Lumbermill has:

    Plains             1F / 1H / 0C
    Forest                  +1H
    Lumbermill                       +1C
    ------------------------------------
    total              1F / 2H / 1C

The Lumbermill has no upgrade chain and, in a no-bonus fixture, no special-improvement value that is
needed to create the comparison. A fresh Cottage can likewise use zero upgrade-progress bonus for
the controlled comparison.

The two jobs therefore have equal food, which removes starvation/growth-food differences from the
ranking and lets the omitted future commerce determine the result directly.

6. DIRECT AI_jobChangeValue / AI_addBestCitizen RANKING FLIP
------------------------------------------------------------
Use a controlled normal production/research state:

- city is producing;
- 100% Research;
- current Research commerce AI weight 105;
- ordinary/average yield modifiers 100%;
- no extra production modifier;
- no emphasis or special-yield multiplier changing these two jobs;
- enough happiness/production to avoid unrelated low-production or excess-happiness adjustments;
- neither a specialist nor another plot outranks the two candidates.

Under this state, the non-food portion of `AI_yieldValue` is:

    1 hammer   -> 8
    1 commerce -> 4 at Research weight 105 after integer arithmetic

So:

Current Financial Plains Cottage:

    1H + 1C = 8 + 4 = 12

BUG projected final Town:

    1H + 4C = 8 + 16 = 24

CORRECT projected Financial Town:

    1H + 5C = 8 + 21 = 29

Plains Forest Lumbermill:

    2H + 1C = 16 + 4 = 20

K-Mod deliberately blends an improving plot's current and final job values. When the final value is
higher, `AI_jobChangeValue()` uses:

    (40 * current + 60 * final) / 100

Therefore:

    BUG Cottage     = floor((40*12 + 60*24) / 100) = 19
    CORRECT Cottage = floor((40*12 + 60*29) / 100) = 22
    Lumbermill      = 20

The common food contribution is identical and cancels.

Current code therefore ranks:

    Lumbermill 20 > Cottage 19

while the same city's actual Financial rule requires:

    Cottage 22 > Lumbermill 20.

This is a direct citizen-job reversal, not merely a displayed projected yield being one point low.
`AI_addBestCitizen()` normally ranks unworked plots through `AI_plotValue()` / `AI_jobChangeValue()`
during `AI_assignWorkingPlots()`, and `AI_juggleCitizens()` uses the same valuation path for swaps.
An ordinary Financial city can consequently choose the Lumbermill when the K-Mod long-term
improvement policy, evaluated with the real current trait rule, would choose the Cottage.

7. SECONDARY CURRENT POLICY WITNESS — GOOD-TILE THRESHOLD
---------------------------------------------------------
A second current path demonstrates that the missing commerce can cross a hard heuristic threshold,
although the direct Plains-Cottage assignment flip above is the stronger primary witness.

Current SAS Tundra has 1F / 0H / 1C. On a NON-river fresh-water Tundra Cottage (fresh water can make
Cottages valid), the current Financial plot has 2 commerce and the true Town reaches 6 commerce;
the stale final-improvement projection reaches only 5.

Under the healthy `AI_getPlotMagicValue` arithmetic used by `AI_countGoodTiles`, this can move the
plot approximately from:

    BUG:     95
    CORRECT: 135

across the live `AI_countGoodTiles(..., 100)` boundary used by Great-Person emphasis logic.

Do not use a riverside Tundra fixture for this witness: riverside natural commerce can make the
Financial bonus apply to the current Cottage already, changing the threshold-crossing delta.

8. ANCESTRY / ROOT BOUNDARY
---------------------------
K-Mod introduced `AI_jobChangeValue`, `AI_finalImprovementYieldDifference` and the surrounding
long-term improvement-job valuation in its 2014 lineage (commit
`313e2ae739864fd5968c5c0de3c80487cdee6f08`). At that time the ordinary
`ExtraYieldThreshold` was the Financial mechanism, so consulting that API was appropriate for
K-Mod's data model.

AdvCiv later introduced the nerfed/natural Financial rule under `advc.908a` (earlier lineage around
`a44438ed380640a052f574cd47c299e00f91020b`) and ultimately separated it into the dedicated
`ExtraYieldNaturalThreshold` XML/API while restoring the original semantics of
`ExtraYieldThreshold` (commit `d01463b2942fc623578fadd059c92b302c83d29b`).

The authoritative `CvPlot::calculateYield()` was migrated to the new natural-threshold API, but the
K-Mod projection helper in `CvCityAI` was not. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS therefore inherit
the stale projection. K-Mod itself predates the separate natural-threshold feature; Civ4CE/BtS do
not provide this AdvCiv rule in the same form.

The most useful root description is therefore an AdvCiv feature-migration omission, not "K-Mod
implemented Financial incorrectly."

9. SAME-ROOT PARALLEL PROJECTION SITES
--------------------------------------
The audit also found parallel projection code that should be repaired/tested with F532 rather than
numbered separately:

A. `CvPlot::getYieldWithBuild()`

This helper preserves `iNatureYield`, calculates projected build/improvement yields, and then has
only the old K-Mod ordinary-threshold block:

    int iThreshold = GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).getExtraYieldThreshold(eYield);
    if (iThreshold > 0 &&
        (iYieldRate > iThreshold || iNatureYield >= iThreshold))
        iYieldRate += EXTRA_YIELD;

It never queries `getExtraYieldNaturalThreshold()`. Water-side Worker/Work-Boat projections can
therefore also be one commerce low when a build crosses Financial's natural threshold. SAS's custom
land-Worker evaluator masks many land consequences of this helper, but it does not make the shared
projection rule correct.

B. `CvCityAI::AI_timeWeightedImprovementYields()`

The source contains an explicit inherited TODO:

    todo: Extra yield for finacial civs
    (see AI_finalImprovementYieldDifference for guidence.)

This routine time-weights raw improvement yield changes without applying either current Financial
threshold mechanism. Audit/fix it as the same projected-yield semantic family rather than spending
a new finding unless a genuinely separate implementation root appears.

10. REPAIR DIRECTION
--------------------
Do not merely replace `getExtraYieldThreshold()` with `getExtraYieldNaturalThreshold()`: both APIs
remain legitimate and have different semantics.

For `AI_finalImprovementYieldDifference`, determine the trait-extra contribution for the CURRENT and
FINAL projected yields under both rules, then add only the difference:

    projected threshold delta =
        final extra-yield contribution - current extra-yield contribution

For the natural rule, mirror `CvPlot::calculateYield()` exactly:

    qualifies if projected total yield >= natural threshold
              OR nature yield + 1 >= natural threshold

The nature term and feature-removal state must correspond to the projected plot state. Preserve the
ordinary `ExtraYieldThreshold` semantics independently. Avoid double-counting when a trait/config
uses both mechanisms.

Prefer a shared projected-threshold helper if practical so `calculateYield`, `getYieldWithBuild`,
`AI_finalImprovementYieldDifference` and time-weighted improvement valuation cannot drift apart
again.

C031-WIP303 APPEND — QUEUE 005 / CvCityAI.cpp
===============================================================================

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F533 / KI#856 — ADVC PRACTICAL 1808 LOOP-STYLE REFACTOR REPLACED K-MOD'S
PREREQUISITE-SHORTAGE STATE UPDATE WITH `break`, SO OUTSIDE-TARGET CULTURE
CITIES ARE TREATED AS HAVING ENOUGH TEMPLE CAPACITY FOR EXTRA CATHEDRALS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED
Primary file: `CvGameCoreDLL/CvCityAI.cpp`
Supporting files: current `CIV4BuildingInfos.xml`, `CIV4BuildingClassInfos.xml`,
`CIV4WorldInfo.xml`, `CIV4VictoryInfo.xml`, `CvPlayer.cpp`, and the retained
AdvCiv practical-1808 diff/history.
Classification: inherited AdvCiv practical-1808 mechanical refactor regression;
K-Mod source is correct; Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the regression.
Ordinary current gameplay under a Cultural-victory strategy.

ROOT
----
Inside `AI_buildingValue`, K-Mod deliberately devalues a culture-multiplier
building in a city outside the required Cultural-victory target set when the
empire does not yet have enough prerequisite buildings to support an EXTRA copy
while reserving copies for the target culture cities.

K-Mod's loop keeps the shortage state explicitly:

    bool bHaveEnough = true;
    for (...; bHaveEnough && ...; ...)
    {
        ...
        if (kOwner.getBuildingClassCount(prereqClass) < iPrereqBuildings)
            bHaveEnough = false;
    }

and immediately consumes it:

    if (bHaveEnough &&
        iCultureRank - iCulturalVictoryNumCultureCities <= 3)
    {
        iCommerceMultiplierValue /= 20;
    }
    else
        iCommerceMultiplierValue /= 50;

AdvCiv practical 1808 / commit
`9fa16c2c7f2b709d0502354b8a7ea1f6bd8827b5`, titled
"Some style changes in CvCityAI (loops)", mechanically converted the indexed
loop to `FOR_EACH_ENUM(BuildingClass)`. In the same diff it changed the decisive
line from:

    bHaveEnough = false;

to:

    break;

but did not change the consumer after the loop. Therefore a prerequisite
shortage terminates the scan while `bHaveEnough` remains `true`.

This is not an interpretation of the old code: the retained diff shows the
semantic change directly, and the commit title describes loop/style cleanup,
not a change in Cultural-victory building policy.

CURRENT SAS DATA / PREREQUISITE ARITHMETIC
------------------------------------------
Current Cultural victory requires 3 Legendary cities.

All seven current Cathedral-style buildings are live non-limited buildings
with:

    +50% culture
    raw prerequisite = 2 matching Temples
    cost = 220

On `WORLDSIZE_STANDARD`, current
`iBuildingClassPrereqModifier = 38`, and `CvPlayer::getBuildingClassPrereqBuilding`
rounds upward:

    ceil(2 * 138 / 100) = 3 Temples per Cathedral step.

For a rank-4 culture-rate city with zero Cathedrals of the class completed,
the K-Mod reserve check passes:

    iExtra = required culture cities - completed Cathedrals
           = 3 - 0
           = 3

and, because Cathedrals are not limited, `getBuildingClassPrereqBuilding`
requires prerequisite capacity for:

    completed + iExtra + the candidate
    = 0 + 3 + 1
    = 4 Cathedrals

hence:

    4 * 3 = 12 matching Temples.

With only 3 matching Temples, the first Cathedral is perfectly legal to start,
but there is plainly NOT enough prerequisite capacity to spend that copy in an
outside-target city while preserving capacity for the three intended culture
cities.

K-Mod therefore sets `bHaveEnough = false` and divides the culture-modifier
component by 50. Current AdvCiv/SAS hits `break`, leaves `bHaveEnough = true`,
and (for ranks 4 through 6) divides by only 20.

Thus that culture-multiplier component is 2.5 times the intended value:

    current / correct = (1/20) / (1/50) = 2.5.

CLEAN CURRENT TWO-CATHEDRAL CONTROL
-----------------------------------
The current XML supplies a particularly clean same-city comparison.
`BUILDING_BUDDHIST_CATHEDRAL` and `BUILDING_DAOIST_CATHEDRAL` are structurally
identical in every gameplay field apart from their religion / building-class /
matching-Temple identity (and presentation identifiers); both even use Copper
for the 25% production bonus. Each has +50% culture, +2 state-religion
happiness, +1 happiness with Incense, two Priest slots and cost 220.

Construct a rank-4 city that contains both religions and can build both:

    Buddhist Temples empire-wide = 3
    Daoist Temples empire-wide   = 12
    completed Cathedrals of each = 0

The Buddhist Cathedral is legal but scarce: correct K-Mod policy applies `/50`.
The Daoist Cathedral has enough reserved prerequisite capacity: `/20` is valid.

Current SAS applies `/20` to BOTH because the Buddhist shortage merely executes
`break`. The raw `AI_buildingValue` therefore loses the intended distinction
between two otherwise-equal candidates. Generic `AI_bestBuildingThreshold`
(and the several focus-0 `AI_chooseBuilding` production gates) consume that
value, so the scarce outside-target Cathedral can remain competitive or be
selected when K-Mod deliberately meant to suppress it.

This fixture also avoids relying on the focused Culture-only path. That path
still contains a separate, correct `bAvoid = true` prerequisite-reservation
check. F533 is specifically the broken GENERAL commerce-multiplier valuation
used by generic building selection.

PLACEMENT-GUARD CHALLENGE
-------------------------
`AI_bestBuildingThreshold` has a later K-Mod placement guard for non-limited
buildings whose quantity is constrained by prerequisite classes. That guard can
sometimes prevent a lower-value city from consuming the only currently
available Cathedral slot when another city can already construct the same
Cathedral and values it more than 25% higher.

It does NOT make F533 data-dead:

* the outside-target city can be the only current city containing the relevant
  religion, while the three eventual Cultural-victory target cities do not yet
  have that religion and therefore fail `canConstruct`;
* the three Temples making the first Cathedral legal can reside in the rank-4
  city and other non-target cities;
* the very purpose of the K-Mod prerequisite-reserve branch is to avoid
  consuming capacity before the target cities are ready, including before
  religion spread makes their Cathedral construction possible.

Thus the broken general valuation has an ordinary reachable consumer and is not
made unreachable by the later placement heuristic.

ANCESTRY
--------
Retained source comparison:

* K-Mod 1.46: correct `bHaveEnough = false` state update;
* AdvCiv practical 1808 / `9fa16c2c7f...`: the loop/style refactor changes that
  update to `break` in the exact diff;
* Base AdvCiv 1.14: still has `break` and the unchanged `if (bHaveEnough ...)`
  consumer;
* current SAS: substantively retains the same regression.

DEDUP / BOUNDARY
----------------
No existing album root was found for this `bHaveEnough` state-loss.

It is independent of:

* F442 / KI#765, which is a queued-building UI prerequisite-counting mismatch;
* F532 / KI#855, which is Financial projected-yield threshold migration;
* the correct `BUILDINGFOCUS_CULTURE` `bAvoid` check later in
  `AI_buildingValue`;
* generic building cache/invalidation findings.

Do not broaden F533 into a claim that Cathedral legality is wrong. Runtime
`canConstruct` correctly enforces the currently required Temple count. The bug
is specifically the AI's reserve-aware VALUE policy for an extra culture
multiplier outside the Cultural-victory target cities.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR
-------------------
Restore the state transition, preserving the current enum loop:

    if (kOwner.getBuildingClassCount(eLoopBuildingClass) < iPrereqBuildings)
    {
        bHaveEnough = false;
        break; // optional after setting state
    }

or make the loop condition/consumer carry an equivalent explicit shortage
boolean. Do not merely remove `break`: the scan may stop once any prerequisite
shortage is found, but that fact must survive the loop.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
1. Standard-size Cultural-victory strategy, 3 target cities, rank-4 evaluator,
   zero matching Cathedrals, exactly 3 matching Temples:
   assert `bHaveEnough == false` after the reserve check.

2. Same state with 12 matching Temples:

===============================================================================
C031-WIP304 — F534 / KI#857 CONFIRMED
CvCityAI::AI_doPanic accepts / force-hurries sea combat units for a land-only
panic deficit, then returns without selecting a land defender
===============================================================================

STATUS
------
F534 / KI#857 CONFIRMED.
F535 / provisional KI#858 is the next UNUSED root.

ROOT
----
`CvCityAI::AI_doPanic()` decides whether the city is in immediate panic from a
LAND-war / LAND-strength comparison, but its shortcut for an already-produced
combat unit tests only generic `UnitInfo::getCombat() > 0`:

    int iOurDefense = GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).AI_localDefenceStrength(
        plot(), getTeam());
    int iEnemyOffense = GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).AI_localAttackStrength(plot());
    ...
    UnitTypes eProductionUnit = getProductionUnit();
    if (eProductionUnit != NO_UNIT && getProduction() > 0 &&
        GC.getInfo(eProductionUnit).getCombat() > 0)
    {
        AI_doHurry(true);
        return;
    }

The default domain parameter of BOTH strength helpers is `DOMAIN_LAND`:

    AI_localDefenceStrength(..., DomainTypes eDomainType = DOMAIN_LAND, ...)
    AI_localAttackStrength (..., DomainTypes eDomainType = DOMAIN_LAND, ...)

and the function is entered only when `AI_isLandWar(getArea())` is true.

`getCombat() > 0`, however, is not a land-unit predicate. Current shipped sea
units including Galley, Trireme, Privateer, Frigate and Destroyer are
`DOMAIN_SEA` and have positive `iCombat` (e.g. current Frigate: DOMAIN_SEA,
iCombat=8).

Consequently a coastal city that is losing the LAND-strength comparison can
classify a ship in its queue as if it were already producing a relevant panic
defender.

CURRENT DETERMINISTIC FIXTURE
-----------------------------
Use an ordinary AI coastal city with:

* an active land war in its area;
* enemy local LAND attack strength greater than own local LAND defence strength;
* a partially built Frigate (`getProduction() > 0`);
* Slavery active and enough population for `canHurry(HURRY_POPULATION)`.

Current `UNIT_FRIGATE` is DOMAIN_SEA with positive combat, so the shortcut is
entered. `AI_doHurry(true)` loops the legal hurry types and, in force mode,
immediately executes the first legal one:

    if (bForce)
    {
        hurry(eHurry);
        break;
    }

The city therefore pays the Population-hurry cost / anger to accelerate the
Frigate and `AI_doPanic()` returns immediately.

It never reaches its actual emergency land-unit chooser:

    AI_chooseUnit(UNITAI_CITY_COUNTER)
    AI_chooseUnit(UNITAI_CITY_DEFENSE)
    AI_chooseUnit(UNITAI_ATTACK)

The rushed Frigate is outside the DOMAIN_LAND defence value whose shortage
triggered the panic and cannot defend the city against the land assault. Thus
this is not a subjective choice between two useful defenders: the shortcut's
accepted object is outside the domain of the quantity the routine is trying to
repair.

NO-HURRY CONTROL / BOUNDARY
---------------------------
If no hurry method is currently legal, `AI_doHurry(true)` simply finds no
`canHurry` entry and returns; `AI_doPanic()` nevertheless returns as well.
That can also leave the city continuing its current combat unit instead of
choosing a panic defender.

Do NOT make that failed-hurry behavior a separate finding here. K-Mod / BtS
already treat an in-progress generic combat unit as a handled panic case, and
for a LAND combat unit retaining the current build can be an arguable authored
policy. F534's hard correctness boundary is narrower: DOMAIN_SEA units pass the
same shortcut even though the panic trigger is explicitly DOMAIN_LAND.

CURRENT TURN CONSEQUENCE
------------------------
`CvCity::doTurn()` calls `AI_doTurn()` before growth and production.
`AI_doTurn()` calls `AI_doPanic()` for AI cities before the normal draft/hurry/
emphasis calls. Therefore the forced population hurry is an authoritative
same-turn state change: population / hurry anger are spent before production is
processed later in that city turn.

Later generic production logic does not undo that cost. Even if another SAS
emergency/fallback mechanism subsequently chooses a land defender, the panic
routine has already consumed scarce population / hurry capacity on a ship and
failed to use its own land-defender branch.

ANCESTRY
--------
This is inherited rather than SAS-authored:

* stock BtS source as preserved by Civ4CE contains the same
  `getCombat() > 0 -> AI_doHurry(true) -> return true` shortcut;
* K-Mod 1.46 retains the same generic-combat condition while replacing the
  local-strength implementation;
* the earliest retained K-Mod import (`KMod_3_2414225e64...`) already contains
  the same logic;
* AdvCiv practical 2179 / `3676ec243b...` refactors `AI_doPanic` from bool to
  void and flattens the body, but preserves the same generic-combat shortcut;
* Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain it.

The current SAS land-strength API makes the mismatch especially explicit
because `AI_localDefenceStrength` and `AI_localAttackStrength` both document
DOMAIN_LAND as their default domain.

DEDUP / INDEPENDENCE
--------------------
No prior album root was found for `AI_doPanic`, panic hurrying a ship, or this
land/sea domain mismatch.

This is independent of:

* KI#213 legacy land best-build / Worker-cache architecture;
* KI#193 / KI#197 dual-coast and naval-cap accounting families;
* ordinary `AI_doHurry` population-cost valuation findings (the panic call uses
  force mode and the root is the wrong unit domain selected before hurrying);
* generic naval-production tuning.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR
-------------------
Only take the "current combat unit already helps the panic" shortcut for a
LAND-domain unit that can actually contribute to the land defence problem, for
example at minimum:

    CvUnitInfo const& kUnit = GC.getInfo(eProductionUnit);
    if (eProductionUnit != NO_UNIT && getProduction() > 0 &&
        kUnit.getDomainType() == DOMAIN_LAND && kUnit.getCombat() > 0)
    {
        AI_doHurry(true);
        return;
    }

A stronger future repair could test actual defensive usefulness / UnitAI rather
than generic combat strength, but that is a policy broadening and is not needed
to fix F534. The minimal correctness repair is to exclude DOMAIN_SEA (and any
other non-land domain) from a land-panic shortcut.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
1. Coastal city, land-war deficit, partially built Frigate, legal Population
   hurry: assert `AI_doPanic` does NOT force-hurry the Frigate merely because
   `iCombat > 0`, and continues to a land-defender choice.

2. Same fixture with a partially built ordinary land combat defender: preserve
   the existing shortcut / forced-hurry behavior.

3. No legal hurry method + sea combat unit: assert the sea unit does not block
   the panic land-defender chooser.

4. Air-unit control: preserve existing behavior unless separately redesigned;
   current air units are not the F534 witness because their `iCombat` field is
   generally not the positive land/sea combat field used by this shortcut.

F535 / provisional KI#858 is the next UNUSED root.

1. AI_doPanic FAILED-HURRY BROADENING — NOT A SEPARATE ROOT

F534's hard root is the DOMAIN_SEA acceptance inside a DOMAIN_LAND panic.

When the current positive-combat unit cannot legally be hurried,

2. AI_chooseDefender — CLOSED
-----------------------------
The helper first tries one CITY_SPECIAL if none is currently stationed on the
city plot, then one CITY_COUNTER under the same condition, then falls back to
CITY_DEFENSE. Its owner/plot/UnitAI orientation is consistent with the helper's
purpose; no wrong domain / stale out-parameter / sentinel issue was found.

3. AI_updateAssignWork — CLOSED
-------------------------------
`AI_updateAssignWork()` is intentionally a small dirty-bit dispatcher:

    if (AI_isAssignWorkDirty())
        AI_assignWorkingPlots();

The authoritative plot/specialist/happiness/health setters examined in this
pass mark assignment work dirty through their existing city-state update paths.
No separate missed-reset or stale-assignment lifecycle was established here.

4. AI_citizenValue — CLOSED
---------------------------
The low-covered helper is simply:

    return 6 + GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).getCurrentEra();

Its live consumers use it as the documented approximate citizen opportunity
cost. Current era values are nonnegative and small; no sign, overflow, enum or
receiver defect exists in the helper itself.

5. AI_nukeEplosionValue — CLOSED AS ROUGH AUTHORED ESTIMATE
-----------------------------------------------------------
Despite its misspelled historical name, the helper is a bounded local estimate:

    10 + (production * 5 + commerceYield * 3) / 2

It is deliberately described by K-Mod/AdvCiv as a rough proxy used for both
nuclear defense and project valuation. The fact that a project-building city's
own output is used as a proxy for target-city nuclear damage is explicitly
acknowledged by the source comment; no accidental wrong receiver or invalid
sentinel was uncovered.

6. AI_calculateMilitaryOutput — CLOSED
--------------------------------------
The formula

    baseProduction * (100 + militaryProductionModifier
                      + 10 * productionExperience) / 100

has safe current shipped modifier / XP ranges and uses the intended city's
production state. No zero divisor, negative-domain transition, or wrong object
was found.

7. AI_highestTeamCloseness — CLOSED
-----------------------------------
The helper initializes to -1 and takes the max player-closeness among team
members. Its live team-war valuation caller supplies a valid living team; a
living team has a member, so the -1 empty-team sentinel is not a normal live
return there. Player/team orientation is correct.

8. AI_getHappyFromHurry — NO NEW MECHANICAL ROOT
------------------------------------------------
The helper's `getHurryAngerTimer() <= 1` restriction is conservative policy
about when population whipping should be credited as a happiness remedy. The
net immediate population-vs-new-anger arithmetic itself is coherent with the
engine's stacked hurry anger. Do not merge it into F530/F531 merely because it
reads the same timer: those findings are exact expiry / city-turn phase-order
errors in future-growth prediction, whereas no independent wrong phase or sign
was proved here.

9. AI_growthValuePerFood FREE-SPECIALIST WARNING — RETAINS PRIOR CONTROL STATUS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The K-Mod comment that worked-specialist accounting "could get messed up by free
specialists" remains a real modeling caveat, and current SAS has generic free
specialists (e.g. Protectionism) as well as specific free-specialist building
effects. This pass did not yet derive a deterministic current citizen/job flip
that is independent of the already-recorded growth/specialist findings.

Do not promote from the comment alone. If revisited, distinguish generic free
specialist capacity (`totalFreeSpecialists`) from explicit typed
`getFreeSpecialistCount`, because the latter is stored/processed separately and
is not the same population-accounting mechanism.

CONTINUATION FROM WIP307

This checkpoint preserves the completed assertion/refactor controls after WIP307

1. AI_bestBuildingThreshold LIMITED-PREREQ ASSERTIONS -- CLOSED CONTROL

The apparently Release-relevant assertions:

    FAssert(iPrereqEach > 0);
    ...
    FAssert(iLimit > 0);

were challenged against the actual producer/caller contract rather than assumed
safe from the assertions alone.

CvPlayer::canConstruct(eLoopBuilding, bContinue=false) already applies the same
prerequisite-building requirement, including buildings currently being made.
If a prereq-scaled building reaches the later limited-placement calculation,
available prerequisite capacity is necessarily sufficient for at least one
additional slot beyond built+making.

Thus:
- iPrereqEach is positive for the prerequisite class that caused this branch;
- iPrereqBuilt / iPrereqEach - iBuilt - iBuilding is at least 1.

No divide-by-zero / nonpositive-slot Release witness exists here.

2. AI_growthValuePerFood FREE-SPECIALIST / PARTIAL_SORT CONTROL

The K-Mod warning about free specialists was rechecked.

Free specialists are stored separately from getSpecialistCount(), so they are
correctly absent from the population-consuming worked-job list. The known
transient state in which getMaxSpecialistCount(type)-getSpecialistCount(type)
can become negative after obsolescence does not create invalid indexing or a
Release arithmetic failure in this helper.

The use of std::less_equal<int> as a partial_sort comparator remains formally
non-strict and therefore poor STL practice / robustness debt. Equal-valued jobs
are common, but no deterministic current gameplay consequence beyond unstable
selection among equivalent/worst jobs has been established. Do not promote it.

- old bWonderOk / !isLimitedWonderClass condition equals the new limited-wonder
  branch for ordinary focus flags;
- automated prereq-building rejection still occurs after canConstruct and before
  any candidate can win;
- iValue>0 nested body equals new iValue<=0 continue;
- wonder placement, rank/rand and iMaxTurns/hurry checks retain their logic.

4. K-MOD PRACTICAL 1139 / 7d9e34dc78... GROWTH/HAPPINESS REWRITE

Commit:
  7d9e34dc788433a3d9ce3795bfcfe73dcedca934
Title:
  "Tweaked the handling of happiness and growth in AI_yieldValue."

This commit is the birth of F531's < -> <= change and was audited for adjacent
siblings.

The already-owned defects remain:
- F530: exact anger-cycle modulo maps a full remaining cycle to zero.
- F531: <= compares anger expiry to a growth event that happens BEFORE that
  turn's anger decrement.

A third, independent pre-gate defect survives.

===============================================================================
F535 / KI#858 CONFIRMED
CvCityAI::AI_yieldValue -- future-happiness pre-gate says at most +2 although
three independent anger-expiry channels can each add +1
===============================================================================

CURRENT SOURCE SHAPE
--------------------

Current SAS around AI_yieldValue:

    int const kMaxHappyIncrease = 2;

    // if happy is large enough so that it will be over zero after we do the checks
    if (iHappinessLevel + kMaxHappyIncrease > 0)
    {
        ... Hurry anger expiry ...
            iFutureHappy++;

        ... Conscript anger expiry ...
            iFutureHappy++;

        ... Defy-resolution anger expiry ...
            iFutureHappy++;
    }

The pre-gate therefore claims the following block can recover at most +2, while
the block visibly contains THREE independent +1 recovery channels.

EARLIEST REACHABLE HISTORY
--------------------------

The contradiction is not a later SAS/AdvCiv edit. It is already present in the
earliest reachable K-Mod import (2414225e64...), whose source comment says:

    // currently we can at most increase happy by 2 in the following checks
    const int kMaxHappyIncrease = 2;

and then immediately checks:
1. hurry anger;
2. conscript anger;
3. defy-resolution anger;

with each successful expiry incrementing the modeled happiness by one.

K-Mod 1.46, Base AdvCiv 1.14, Civ4CE's BtS reconstruction and current SAS all
retain the same mismatch.

CURRENT-DATA REACHABILITY
-------------------------

All three anger sources can coexist in current SAS.

- CIVIC_NATIONHOOD is a LEGAL civic and has iMaxConscript=3.
- CIVIC_SLAVERY is a separate LABOR civic and enables HURRY_POPULATION.
  Nationhood and Slavery can therefore be active simultaneously.
- Defy-resolution anger is independent city state from Apostolic/UN resolution
  defiance and can coexist with both.

Thus a city can legitimately have positive Hurry, Conscript and Defy-resolution
anger timers at once.

CLEAN INDEPENDENT FIXTURE
-------------------------

Use a healthy ordinary city with:

    current iHappinessLevel = -2

and all three anger sources due to lose their next unhappy point before the
candidate growth event.

To make independence from F530/F531 explicit, use the corrected timing model:

    each timer = 1
    iApproxTurnsToGrow = 2

After the F530 positive-cycle correction:
    decrements needed for each next anger drop = 1

After the F531 phase correction:
    1 < 2
so each of the THREE recoveries is genuinely available before growth.

INTENDED result:

    iFutureHappy = +3
    -2 + 3 = +1
    => at least one population of future happiness headroom exists

CURRENT pre-gate:

    -2 + kMaxHappyIncrease(2) = 0
    0 > 0 is false
    => the code skips ALL three timer checks
    => iFutureHappy remains 0 from these sources
    => -2 stays nonpositive

So the micro-optimization suppresses a real transition from unhappy/no-growth
headroom to +1 future happiness.

LIVE AI CONSEQUENCE
-------------------

The value feeds directly into:

    iPopToGrow = max(0, iHappinessLevel + iFutureHappy)

and therefore into the ordinary food-growth branch of AI_yieldValue.

With the bug:
    iPopToGrow = 0

With all three legitimate recoveries:
    iPopToGrow = 1

Because current happiness is negative, the bFillingBar fallback also does not
rescue the bugged state (it requires iHappinessLevel >= 0). The bug can therefore
remove growth-food value entirely when the city actually has enough stacked
anger expiry to become happy by the time it grows.

As in the controlled F530/F531 +1-food vs +1-hammer fixtures, any sufficiently
positive ordinary iGrowthValue can make the correct iPopToGrow=1 state prefer a
food job while the bugged iPopToGrow=0 state prefers the hammer/non-growth job.
The important deterministic root is the branch/state difference itself; it does
not depend on a subjective strategic threshold.

DEDUP / INDEPENDENCE
--------------------

Whole-album search found no prior root for kMaxHappyIncrease / the false "+2"
upper bound.

F535 is adjacent to but independent from F530 and F531:

F530:
- wrong number of decrements at exact timer multiples;
- can be fixed while F535 remains.

F531:
- wrong growth-vs-decrement phase comparison;
- can be fixed while F535 remains.

F535:
- even with both corrected decrement counts and strict phase comparison, the
  outer pre-gate can prevent all three correct checks from running when
  iHappinessLevel == -2.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------

At minimum, make the upper bound match the following channels:

    int const kMaxHappyIncrease = 3;

A more future-proof repair is to remove this tiny optimization or derive the
upper bound from the channels being evaluated so a future fourth/removed anger
source cannot silently desynchronize it again.

REGRESSION TEST
---------------

1. Set iHappinessLevel=-2.
2. Give Hurry, Conscript and Defy timers each a next anger drop one full city
   turn before growth (e.g. corrected D=1, G=2).
3. Assert all three recovery checks are evaluated.
4. Assert modeled future happiness from these sources is +3.
5. Assert iPopToGrow becomes at least 1 rather than remaining 0.
6. Controls:
   - only two expiring sources at happiness -2 should NOT create positive
     growth headroom;
   - three sources whose next drops occur at/after growth should not count;
   - F530 exact-cycle and F531 D==G tests remain separate.

CONTINUATION FROM WIP308

The post-WIP308 cursor was K-Mod practical 199 / obsolete-building defensive
valuation. That investigation produced an independent, live obsolete-tech-value
root. F536 is confirmed below.

===============================================================================
F536 / KI#859 CONFIRMED
AI_obsoleteBuildingPenalty / AI_buildingValue bObsolete mode values building
effects that explicitly survive obsolescence as though the tech removed them
===============================================================================

ROOT CONTRACT
-------------

CvPlayerAI::AI_obsoleteBuildingPenalty states that it returns the positive value
of:

    "the buildings we will lose by researching eTech."

Current AdvCiv/SAS calls, for each currently active building obsoleted by eTech:

    pLoopCity->AI_buildingValue(
        eLoopBuilding, 0, 0, bConstCache,
        true, false, /*bObsolete=*/true);

The intended quantity is therefore the DELTA in building effects caused by
CvCity::processBuilding(..., bObsolete=true), not the value of the whole
building.

But AI_buildingValue's bObsolete parameter is used only in the defensive helper.
The rest of AI_buildingValue still values effects that the engine deliberately
retains after obsolescence.

CURRENT ENGINE SEMANTICS
------------------------

CvCity::processBuilding(BuildingTypes eBuilding, int iChange, bool bObsolete)
splits building effects into two groups.

The main block executes on an obsolescence transition and removes ordinary active
effects such as:
- happiness / health;
- trade routes;
- commerce/yield modifiers;
- specialist slots;
- air / nuke modifiers;
- many player/team effects.

But the later:

    if (!bObsolete)

block is intentionally skipped for an obsolescence transition. It retains,
among other things:
- local building defense;
- local building bombard defense;
- Great Person point generation from the building;
- building/class/wonder existence bookkeeping.

Separately, obsolete-safe commerce is explicitly independent of active-building
state. CvCity::getBuildingCommerceByBuilding starts from:

    kBuilding.getObsoleteSafeCommerceChange(eCommerce) *
        getNumBuilding(eBuilding);

and only adds normal commerce inside the getNumActiveBuilding() branch.

Thus ObsoleteSafeCommerceChange is, by definition, not lost when the building
obsoletes.

CLEAN CURRENT MONUMENT WITNESS
------------------------------

Current SAS BUILDING_MONUMENT:

    ObsoleteTech = TECH_LIBERALISM
    iCost = 30
    ObsoleteSafeCommerceChanges:
        +1 culture

It has no ordinary CommerceChanges and no other gameplay effect needed for this
witness.

Before Liberalism:
- getNumActiveBuilding(Monument) > 0, so AI_obsoleteBuildingPenalty evaluates it.

After Liberalism:
- the Monument remains physically present;
- its +1 ObsoleteSafe culture remains, because obsolete-safe commerce is based
  on getNumBuilding(), not getNumActiveBuilding();
- therefore this +1 culture suffers ZERO actual loss from Liberalism.

Current AI_buildingValue nevertheless contains, in its generic commerce
valuation:

    iTempValue = kBuilding.getCommerceChange(eLoopCommerce) * 4;
    iTempValue +=
        kBuilding.getObsoleteSafeCommerceChange(eLoopCommerce) * 4;

and equivalent focused-commerce additions.

bObsolete does not gate those terms.

Therefore every current active Monument contributes positive "lost building"
value to Liberalism even though its sole relevant +1 culture survives the tech.

This is a deterministic false obsolete-tech penalty, not a heuristic
disagreement.

CURRENT UNIQUE-BUILDING WITNESSES
---------------------------------

The same current Liberalism path is also live for Monument replacements with
+1 ObsoleteSafe culture:
- Egyptian Obelisk;
- Aztec Sacrificial Altar;
- Sumerian Ziggurat.

Some replacements have additional effects that really do obsolete, but their
ObsoleteSafe culture is still incorrectly included in the loss value.

CURRENT CASTLE / DEFENSE BROADENING
-----------------------------------

AdvCiv practical 1777 explicitly noticed one part of the root:

    "Defense abilities don't go obsolete. Looks like K-Mod had gotten that
     wrong. Tagging advc.001 (bugfix)."

It added:

    bool bRemoveDef = (bRemove && !bObsolete);

This correctly prevents the obsolete mode from entering the "remove local
defense" branch.

However, bRemoveDef=false then falls through the NORMAL ADD-BUILDING branch.
For an already-present obsolete Castle, that does not necessarily produce zero.

Current BUILDING_CASTLE:
    ObsoleteTech      = TECH_MILITARY_SCIENCE
    iRaiseDefense     = 100
    iBombardDefense   = 25
    prerequisite      = Walls

Current BUILDING_WALLS:
    iRaiseDefense     = 50
    iBombardDefense   = 50

No current SAS unit has bIgnoreBuildingDefense=1, so the local defensive
valuation is live in a normal non-isolated area.

Ordinary city with Walls + Castle:
    current city defense          = 100
    current building bombard def  = 50 + 25 = 75

For bRemove=true, bObsolete=true:
    bRemoveDef = false
    iOldDefenseModifier = 100
    iNewDefenseModifier = 100

The RaiseDefense term therefore happens to add 0 in this fixture.

But bombard valuation computes:

    iOldBombardMod = 75
    100 * min(25, 100 - 75) /
        max(80, 8 * (100 - 75))
    = 100 * 25 / 200
    = 12

Then:
    peaceful weighting -> 12 * 2 / 3 = 8
    war-plan weighting -> 12 * 3 / 3 = 12

So obsolete-mode valuation assigns +8 or +12 raw defensive value to Castle
bombard protection that CvCity::processBuilding explicitly DOES NOT REMOVE on
obsolescence.

For a science-flavor-0 leader, AI_obsoleteBuildingPenalty's normal 50% scale
turns that phantom local-defense component alone into roughly 4 or 6 tech-value
penalty per Castle, before legitimate lost Castle effects are counted.

The important root is not the exact number: retained defense should contribute
zero to the obsolete delta.

RETAINED GREAT-PERSON-POINT BROADENING
--------------------------------------

The same engine if (!bObsolete) block preserves building Great Person point
generation.

Current obsoleting Wonders such as:
- Great Lighthouse;
- Colossus;
- Great Wall

have GreatPeopleRateChange = +2 and ObsoleteSafe culture (+4 in these examples).

AI_buildingValue's generic GPP valuation and ObsoleteSafe commerce valuation do
not test bObsolete, so AI_obsoleteBuildingPenalty can count both retained
components as though the obsoleting tech destroyed them.

This is the same root, not additional finding numbers.

ANCESTRY
--------

Stock BtS / current Civ4CE does not contain AI_obsoleteBuildingPenalty.

K-Mod practical 199 / a865535e85... introduced the meaningful obsolete-building
penalty and calls the ordinary AI_buildingValue of each building that the tech
will obsolete. K-Mod therefore introduced the basic whole-building-vs-
actually-lost-effects mismatch.

K-Mod itself also treated Walls/Castles' local defense as lost.

AdvCiv practical 1777 / c0439987e0... introduced bObsolete and explicitly tried
to repair that defense mistake. It:
- passes bObsolete=true from AI_obsoleteBuildingPenalty;
- adds bObsolete to AI_defensiveBuildingValue;
- changes bRemoveDef to bRemove && !bObsolete.

But the repair is partial:
- bObsolete is not used to exclude ObsoleteSafe commerce;
- it is not used to exclude retained building GPP;
- the retained-defense path falls into add-mode and can still produce phantom
  bombard-defense value.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS inherit this partial repair.

DEDUP / ROOT SEPARATION
-----------------------

Whole-album searches for:
- AI_obsoleteBuildingPenalty;
- obsolete building defense;
- Castle obsolescence;
- bObsolete;
- ObsoleteSafe commerce

found no prior finding for valuing retained building effects as obsolete losses.

This is separate from:
- F498 construction-cache lifetime/invalidation;
- WIP242's unnumbered semantic-cache-key note (cache ignores bObsolete);
- prior CvPlayer building-obsolescence lifecycle controls, which correctly proved
  that processBuilding removes/adds the effects that are SUPPOSED to obsolete.

F536 concerns the AI valuation model of that already-correct engine transition.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------

bObsolete mode should value the actual effect delta produced by:

    processBuilding(eBuilding, -1, /*bObsolete=*/true)

rather than treating the whole building as lost.

At minimum:
1. ObsoleteSafeCommerceChange must contribute 0 to obsolete-loss valuation.
2. GreatPeopleRateChange that survives obsolescence must contribute 0.
3. Local defense / bombard defense must contribute 0 when bObsolete=true;
   do not route retained defense through the normal add-building branch.
4. Preserve ordinary bRemove / spy-removal behavior when bObsolete=false,
   because physically removing a building really does lose those retained
   effects too.

A future-proof implementation should make the bObsolete valuation mirror
CvCity::processBuilding's obsolete-vs-remove split rather than maintain an ad-hoc
list that can drift again.

----------------

4. ADJACENT AI_yieldValue RECHECK AFTER F530/F531/F535
======================================================

The three previous findings corrected:
- F530: wrong next-drop remainder at exact anger-cycle multiples;
- F531: wrong <= phase relation because growth occurs before that turn's timer
  decrement;
- F535: hard-coded kMaxHappyIncrease=2 despite three independent anger sources.

A fourth independent issue survives even if all three are repaired.

===============================================================================
F537 / KI#860 CONFIRMED
AI_yieldValue counts at most one future happiness recovery per anger SOURCE,
even when multiple stacked unhappy layers of that same source will expire
before the projected growth
===============================================================================

CURRENT SOURCE SHAPE
--------------------

For each temporary-anger timer, AI_yieldValue asks only when the NEXT anger
point is reduced and then increments future happiness once:

    if (iHurryAngerTimer > 0)
    {
        int iTurnsUntilAngerIsReduced =
            iHurryAngerTimer % flatHurryAngerLength();
        if (iTurnsUntilAngerIsReduced <= iApproxTurnsToGrow)
            iFutureHappy++;
    }

Conscript and Defy-resolution anger use the same one-increment shape.

No loop or quotient accounts for a second/third stacked unhappy point of the
same source disappearing before growth.

AUTHORITATIVE ENGINE STACK COUNT
--------------------------------

CvCity's actual hurry anger count uses:

    (((getHurryAngerTimer() - 1) / flatHurryAngerLength()) + 1)

for positive timers, i.e. ceil(timer / length).

Conscript and Defy use the same structure.

Thus timer=19 with length=10 is TWO current unhappy layers, not one.

NORMAL PRODUCER
---------------

Repeated whipping naturally creates exactly such a state.

CvCity::hurry does:

    changeHurryAngerTimer(iHurryAngerLength);

It ADDS one full length to the existing timer; it does not replace it.

Normal-speed zero-modifier example:
1. first whip -> timer 10;
2. city turn later -> timer 9;
3. second legal whip -> timer 19.

The city now has:
    ceil(19 / 10) = 2
hurry-anger layers.

Repeated drafting produces the same stacked-timer structure because conscript()
also adds flatConscriptAngerLength() to the existing timer. Defy-resolution
anger can stack analogously. Hurry alone is enough for the proof.

CLEAN INDEPENDENT FIXTURE
-------------------------

Use:
    anger length L = 10
    Hurry timer T = 19
    no Conscript/Defy anger
    current iHappinessLevel = -1
    projected next growth G = 20 doGrowth executions away

This avoids every adjacent finding:

F530:
    T=19 is NOT an exact multiple of 10.
    The next-drop remainder is genuinely 9.

F531:
    next drop at 9 and final drop at 19 are both STRICTLY before G=20.
    No equality / phase-boundary ambiguity exists.

F535:
    outer gate with the old constant already passes:
        -1 + 2 > 0
    so the missing recovery is not caused by the +2 prefilter.

ACTUAL TIMER / GROWTH ORDER
---------------------------

Citizen valuation occurs before the upcoming city doGrowth. Each city turn:
    doGrowth()
    ...
    anger timer -= 1

Starting at timer 19:
- after the 9th growth/decrement cycle, timer becomes 10 and the first unhappy
  layer has disappeared;
- after the 19th growth/decrement cycle, timer becomes 0 and the second layer
  disappears;
- the 20th projected growth therefore occurs with BOTH anger layers gone.

Actual future happiness recovered before G=20:
    +2

CURRENT MODEL
-------------

Current code computes only the next reduction:
    19 % 10 = 9
    9 <= 20
    => iFutureHappy += 1

There is no second increment for the same Hurry source.

So:

CURRENT:
    iHappinessLevel + iFutureHappy
    = -1 + 1
    = 0
    => iPopToGrow = 0

CORRECT:
    -1 + 2
    = +1
    => iPopToGrow = 1

This is a deterministic state difference in the exact quantity that the
future-happiness block is trying to estimate.

LIVE CITIZEN/JOB CONSEQUENCE
----------------------------

Because current happiness is -1, the bugged iPopToGrow=0 state cannot enter the
fallback bFillingBar path either; that path requires iHappinessLevel >= 0.

Therefore the bug can remove growth-food value entirely.

Using the same controlled scale as the F530/F531 regression tests:
    iGrowthValue = 10
    ordinary production value of +1 hammer = 8

At current happiness -1:
- bugged +1 food gets only its small current-food baseline (~1) and loses to
  +1 hammer (8);
- correct iPopToGrow=1 activates positive growth-food value, pushing the +1
  food job above the hammer job at this controlled scale.

The direct branch difference is deterministic even though exact live
iGrowthValue varies by city context.

ROOT / LINEAGE
--------------

The one-recovery-per-source logic is already present in the Civ4CE BtS
reconstruction. K-Mod, Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain it.

K-Mod later refactored the recovered happiness into iFutureHappy and changed
other timing details, but never generalized one source to multiple expiring
layers.

This is therefore an inherited BtS-era growth-forecasting defect, not a SAS
regression.

DEDUP / INDEPENDENCE
--------------------

Whole-album searches found no prior root for multiple anger layers of one source
expiring before growth.

It is independent of:
- F530 next-drop modulo;
- F531 growth/decrement event order;
- F535 outer maximum-happiness prefilter.

All three can be fixed while F537 remains:
with T=19, G=20, a correct next-drop/phase calculation still adds only +1
because the source is visited once.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------

For each anger source, compute the number of unhappy LAYERS present now and the
number still present immediately before the projected growth.

For positive timer T, length L:

    layersNow = ceil(T / L)

Given G upcoming doGrowth executions until the growth being evaluated, timers
have received only G-1 decrements BEFORE that growth:

    timerAtGrowth = max(0, T - (G - 1))
    layersAtGrowth =
        timerAtGrowth <= 0 ? 0 : ceil(timerAtGrowth / L)

Then:

    recoveredBeforeGrowth = layersNow - layersAtGrowth

and add that full count to iFutureHappy.

This formulation naturally handles:
- F530 exact-cycle boundaries;
- F531 phase ordering;
- F537 multiple layers.

The F535 outer gate should then be removed or derived from the true maximum
recoverable count rather than remain a stale constant.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------

================================================================================
C031-WIP311 - F538 / KI#861 CONFIRMED
CvCity worker-availability cache double-counts a Worker on its completion turn
================================================================================

STATUS
------
F538 / KI#861 CONFIRMED.
F539 / provisional KI#862 is the next UNUSED root.
Queue 005 CvGameCoreDLL/CvCityAI.cpp remains OPEN.
32/169 unique files complete.
Repository source untouched.

ROOT
----
`CvCityAI::AI_updateWorkersHaveAndNeeded()` deliberately includes a Worker that is
already close to completion in the city's cached available-Worker count:

    if (getProductionUnit() != NO_UNIT)
    {
        if (getProductionUnitAI() == UNITAI_WORKER)
        {
            if (getProductionTurnsLeft() <= 3)
                iWorkersHave++;
        }
    }

That refresh runs at the beginning of `CvCity::doTurn()`, through
`CvCityAI::AI_doTurn()`, before `CvCity::doProduction()`.

When the same queued Worker finishes later in that city turn, `CvCity::popOrder()`
performs another unconditional cache increment before removing the training order:

    /* advc.113b: So that the new worker can already be taken into account
       for choosing the next order */
    if (eTrainAIUnit == UNITAI_WORKER)
        AI().AI_changeWorkersHave(1);

For an ordinary Worker that was already <=3 turns from completion at the morning
refresh, these are not two different Workers. The first +1 is the near-complete
queued Worker; the second +1 is that exact Worker transitioning from queued to
completed. The cache therefore becomes one too high until the next full
`AI_updateWorkersHaveAndNeeded()` refresh.

DETERMINISTIC TURN TIMELINE
---------------------------
Let a city begin its turn with N live/assigned Workers and one UNITAI_WORKER order
that will complete this turn.

1. `CvCity::doTurn()` calls `AI().AI_doTurn()`.
2. `AI_updateWorkersHaveAndNeeded()` sees `getProductionTurnsLeft() == 1` and stores
   `m_iWorkersHave = N + 1`.
3. Later in the same `CvCity::doTurn()`, `doProduction()` completes that same Worker.
4. `popOrder()` calls `AI_changeWorkersHave(1)`, producing `m_iWorkersHave = N + 2`.
5. Only N + 1 Workers actually exist / are represented by that cache contract.
6. If the order queue is now empty, `popOrder()` subsequently invokes
   `AI_chooseProduction()` before any full Worker-cache refresh repairs the value.

Thus the overcount is directly observable by the exact next-production decision
that the completion increment was intended to inform.

LIVE PRODUCTION CONSEQUENCE
---------------------------
Normal `AI_chooseProduction()` reads the local cache in its high-priority Worker
branch:

    bValid = (3 * (AI_getWorkersHave() + 1) / 2 <
              AI_getWorkersNeeded() + 1 && ...);

A clean boundary example with local Worker need 3 is:

    correct completed-worker cache: have = 1
        3 * (1 + 1) / 2 = 3;  3 < 4 -> true

    bugged completion-turn cache: have = 2
        3 * (2 + 1) / 2 = 4;  4 < 4 -> false

So, when the area still has unmet Worker demand, the double count can demote what
would have been a deterministic local Worker-production qualification into the
fallback probabilistic path, changing the city's immediate next build choice.
Other same-turn `AI_getWorkersHave()` consumers can likewise observe the inflated
cache before the next city turn repairs it.

ANCESTRY
--------
The root is AdvCiv-specific, introduced by practical commit 1583
`715fa87579778a04e8da1adb5a6f1170f141aed5` ("Several improvements to AI worker
production and assignment"). That commit added the completion-time
`AI_changeWorkersHave(1)` hook as part of advc.113b while retaining the existing
near-complete production Worker in `AI_updateWorkersHaveAndNeeded()`.

Controls:
- Civ4CE BtS reconstruction retains the near-complete Worker count (<=2) but has no
  completion-time `AI_changeWorkersHave(1)` hook.
- K-Mod 1.46 likewise retains the near-complete count (<=2) without the AdvCiv
  completion increment.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 has both sides of the contradiction (with <=3 after advc.113),
  as does current AdvCiv-SAS.

This therefore appears to be an AdvCiv practical-1583 regression inherited by SAS,
not a BtS/K-Mod defect.

DEDUP
-----
Whole-album and current Known-Issues / archaeology searches found no existing root
for the same near-complete Worker being counted once by the morning cache refresh
and again by the completion hook.

Do not merge with KI#198 or KI#213:
- KI#198 concerns Worker demand floors / worked featureless land and the later
  area-vs-empire cap interaction.
- KI#213 concerns the split city-side vs Worker-side best-build policy hiding valid
  custom land jobs.
- F538 is a lifecycle/cache transition error even when Worker demand and best-build
  policy are both otherwise perfect.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Do not blindly remove the completion hook: a Worker can in principle complete after
an event not represented by the morning <=3 prediction (most notably same-turn
hurry/production-state changes), and advc.113b intentionally wants completion to be
visible before the next order is chosen.

The safest repair is to re-establish the authoritative Worker-availability cache
when a Worker completes before `AI_chooseProduction()` consumes it, or otherwise
track whether the current production Worker was already included in the most recent
refresh and increment only when it was not. A localized full recomputation on Worker
completion is simpler and harder to desynchronize than trying to infer the old
morning prediction from post-production state.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Ordinary one-turn completion
- City starts with N live/assigned Workers and a UNITAI_WORKER at 1 turn left.
- Morning refresh must report N+1.
- After completion and before choosing the next order, the cache must still report
  N+1, not N+2.

B. Three-turn prediction control
- A Worker at 2-3 turns left should remain represented exactly once while queued.

C. Unexpected/same-turn accelerated completion
- If a Worker was not included by the prior refresh but completes before the next
  order choice (e.g. through a valid hurry/production change), the completed Worker
  must nevertheless be counted once.

D. Production-choice boundary
- With local Worker need 3 and one newly completed Worker, verify the local
  `3 * (have + 1) / 2 < needed + 1` test receives have=1 rather than the phantom 2.

POST-F538 OPEN WORKER-ACCOUNTING LEADS
--------------------------------------
Two additional consistency leads were identified but are NOT numbered yet:

1. Old assignment vs physical-city mismatch in `AI_workerMove(bool)`:
   the full cache attributes a non-cargo Worker with a MissionAI target to the
   mission target's working city, but the wrapper snapshots `pOldCity` only through
   `AI_getCityToImprove()` (physical plot city/working city). K-Mod turn-start danger
   handling can clear the queued mission and force reassessment while retaining the
   old MissionAI target, so reassignment may decrement the wrong city / fail to
   decrement the formerly targeted city until the next full refresh.

2. Range mismatch:
   the full group refresh counts an off-city MISSIONAI_BUILD Worker only when its
   mission target is within the era-scaled `iRange = 9 * (1 + eraFactor / 2)`, while
   the incremental wrapper immediately adds the newly targeted city's cache with no
   equivalent range test. Base AdvCiv's `AI_nextCityToImprove` and current SAS can
   select same-area targets without that maximum-distance bound.

Both are plausible transient same-turn cache inconsistencies. Continue under F539
unused and promote only if an independent gameplay consequence survives the full
contract/dedup proof; otherwise retain as robustness/control notes.

C031-WIP312 - F539 / KI#862 CONFIRMED
AI_workerMove incremental Worker cache forgets the old MissionAI target city
================================================================================

STATUS
------
F539 / KI#862 CONFIRMED.
F540 / provisional KI#863 is the next UNUSED root.
Queue 005 CvGameCoreDLL/CvCityAI.cpp remains OPEN.
32/169 unique files complete.
Repository source untouched.

ROOT
----
AdvCiv 113b updates `m_iWorkersHave` incrementally around every land-Worker AI
reassessment:

    if (bUpdateWorkersHave)
    {
        CvCityAI* pOldCity = AI_getCityToImprove();
        AI_workerMove(false);
        CvCityAI* pNewCity = NULL;
        if (plot() != NULL)
        {
            CvPlot* pNewMissionPlot = AI_getGroup()->AI_getMissionAIPlot();
            if (pNewMissionPlot != NULL)
                pNewCity = pNewMissionPlot->AI_getWorkingCity();
            if (pNewCity == NULL)
                pNewCity = AI_getCityToImprove();
        }
        if (pOldCity != pNewCity)
        {
            if (pOldCity != NULL)
                pOldCity->AI_changeWorkersHave(-1);
            if (pNewCity != NULL)
                pNewCity->AI_changeWorkersHave(1);
        }
        return;
    }

The OLD side and the authoritative full refresh do not use the same ownership
contract.

`AI_getCityToImprove()` looks only at the Worker's current physical plot:

    if (getPlot().getOwner() != getOwner() || isCargo())
        return NULL;
    CvCityAI* pCity = getPlot().AI_getPlotCity();
    if (pCity == NULL)
        pCity = getPlot().AI_getWorkingCity();
    return pCity;

But `AI_updateWorkersHaveAndNeeded()` deliberately attributes a non-cargo Worker
with a build MissionAI target to the TARGET city's Worker cache. Its city-plot
predicate `PUF_isMissionPlotWorkingCity` substitutes the group's MissionAI plot for
the physical plot when one exists, and the later group scan counts an off-city
`MISSIONAI_BUILD` group for the target city when it is inside the refresh range.

Therefore an en-route Worker can be represented in city B's `m_iWorkersHave` while
`AI_workerMove(true)` records its `pOldCity` as city A or NULL. If the mission is
then cancelled/replaced during that reassessment, B is never decremented.

DETERMINISTIC INTERRUPTION PATH
-------------------------------
No hypothetical external mission mutation is needed. The normal AI group turn has
an explicit interruption path:

1. At the start of the player turn, city B's
   `AI_updateWorkersHaveAndNeeded()` sees Worker W en route to a BFC build target
   with `MISSIONAI_BUILD` and counts W for B.
2. Later, land groups receive `CvSelectionGroup::doTurn()`.
3. For an AI-controlled noncombat Worker group, danger can enter:

       setForceUpdate(true);
       clearMissionQueue();
       AI().AI_cancelGroupAttack();

4. `clearMissionQueue()` removes queued missions but does NOT call
   `AI_setMissionAI(NO_MISSIONAI, ...)`; the old B target remains stored.
5. `readyToMove()` explicitly treats `isForceUpdate()` as sufficient to re-enter
   AI evaluation, and `CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_update()` clears the force marker
   only after entering its update loop.
6. The Worker therefore reaches `AI_workerMove(true)` while its old MissionAI
   target is still B.
7. The wrapper snapshots `pOldCity` from the physical plot instead of that old B
   assignment.
8. `AI_workerMove(false)` can retreat, wait, or choose a different build target,
   replacing/clearing the old MissionAI target.
9. The wrapper adjusts the physical city (if any) and the new city, but never B.
   B retains a phantom Worker until its next full city-turn refresh.

This is especially clear for W traveling between city radii: `pOldCity == NULL`
although B's cache contains W. After the interrupted mission is replaced, there is
literally no decrement operation capable of removing W from B.

LIVE SAME-TURN CONSEQUENCE
--------------------------
The stale value is transient across turn boundaries because the next full city
refresh repairs it, but advc.113b exists specifically to make Worker availability
meaningful WITHIN the turn. Later Worker groups in the same AI unit-update pass read
`AI_getWorkersHave()` while choosing destinations and redistribution actions.

Base AdvCiv's `AI_nextCityToImprove()` gives a direct numerical witness. For a city
whose authoritative `AI_getWorkersNeeded()` is 1, the function first relaxes the
movement target to `iWorkersNeeded = 2` and scores Worker shortage roughly as:

    iValue = max(0, iWorkersNeeded - iWorkersHave) * 100;
    iValue += iWorkersNeeded * 10;
    iValue *= iWorkersNeeded + 1;
    iValue /= iWorkersHave + 1;

If interrupted W was B's only assigned Worker:

    correct after cancellation: have = 0
        (200 + 20) * 3 / 1 = 660

    stale cache: have = 1
        (100 + 20) * 3 / 2 = 180

before the common path-distance scaling. Thus a stale +1 can reduce B's Worker
redistribution score from 660 to 180 and readily flip the next Worker's target to a
competing city. Current SAS also consumes the cache in its cross-city readiness
scoring, so the root remains live after the custom Worker rewrite.

ANCESTRY
--------
The mismatch was introduced by AdvCiv practical 1583
`715fa87579778a04e8da1adb5a6f1170f141aed5` together with the advc.113b incremental
Worker-availability wrapper.

- Civ4CE BtS and K-Mod do not contain this wrapper and therefore do not contain
  this specific old-snapshot regression.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the physical `pOldCity = AI_getCityToImprove()` snapshot
  while its full refresh attributes incoming build Workers by MissionAI target.
- Current SAS retains the same old-side contract and the same full-refresh target
  attribution.

So F539 is an AdvCiv regression inherited by SAS.

DEDUP
-----
No matching root was found in the album, current Known Issues, or historical
archaeology.

Do not merge with:
- F538/KI#861: same cache family, but F538 double-counts one Worker during the
  production-order -> completed-unit transition; F539 loses the OLD target during
  an existing Worker's mission reassignment.
- KI#198: Worker-demand/floor calculation.
- KI#213: split best-build policy.
- the older ferry note around F383: cargo delivery/cache-range handling, not a land
  Worker's old target transition.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The robust repair is to centralize the definition of "which city currently counts
this Worker" and use that same helper both for full refresh and for the before/after
incremental transition.

At minimum, the OLD snapshot must inspect the pre-recursion MissionAI assignment
before falling back to the physical city; simply calling `AI_getCityToImprove()` is
not sufficient. The helper should also preserve the full-refresh cargo, mission-type
and distance rules rather than treating every MissionAI plot as equivalent (the
remaining range/new-side mismatch is still under F540 review).

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Interrupted incoming build Worker
- W is off-city, within the authoritative incoming range, and has MISSIONAI_BUILD to
  city B.
- Morning city refresh reports B WorkersHave += 1.
- Cancel/replace W's mission through the normal AI danger force-update path.
- Before any next-turn city refresh, B must lose exactly that +1.

B. Physical-city mismatch
- Place W physically in city A's BFC while its build mission targets city B.
- Full refresh must attribute W according to the same rule that the incremental OLD
  snapshot later uses; reassignment must not decrement A if A never counted W.

C. Later Worker decision
- A second Worker processed later in the same AI unit-update pass must see B's
  post-cancellation Worker count, not the stale pre-cancellation value.

D. Uninterrupted mission control
- If W remains assigned to the same B target, the before/after cache delta is zero.

POST-F539 CURSOR
----------------
The NEW side of the same wrapper still has a separate unresolved contract mismatch:
full refresh counts a remote MISSIONAI_BUILD Worker only inside an era-scaled target
range, whereas the wrapper immediately increments any target working city without
that range (and without matching all full-refresh mission-type rules). Keep that
under F540 unused until its independent consequence / intended-range semantics are
settled.
