F540 / KI#863 — CONFIRMED
`AI_countGoodTiles` treats `getCultureTurnsLeft()==-1` (NO CULTURE / NO ETA) as
"border expansion within 5 turns", which can make the human production governor
suppress Build Culture indefinitely
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED current gameplay / production-governor defect.
Inherited from Base AdvCiv; absent from K-Mod before AdvCiv's `advc.113` border-
anticipation addition.

ROOT
----
`CvCity::getCultureTurnsLeft()` has an explicit negative sentinel contract:

    int iCultureRateTimes100 = getCommerceRateTimes100(COMMERCE_CULTURE);
    if (iCultureRateTimes100 <= 0)
        return -1;
    ...
    if (iCultureLeftTimes100 <= 0)
        return -1;

So `-1` means there is no positive current ETA to the next culture threshold.

Current `CvCityAI::AI_countGoodTiles()` nevertheless tests:

    bool bValid = (kPlot.getWorkingCity() == this);
    if (!bValid && kPlot.getOwner() == NO_PLAYER &&
        getCultureLevel() == 1 && getCultureTurnsLeft() <= 5)
    {
        bValid = true;
    }

There is no `getCultureTurnsLeft() > 0` guard.

Therefore:

    culture rate = 0
    getCultureTurnsLeft() = -1
    -1 <= 5              = true

and every otherwise-good unowned city-radius plot is treated as though the border
will reach it within five turns, even though current culture output will NEVER reach
the next threshold.

This is not merely a misleading helper name. The exact positive-look-ahead branch
was added by AdvCiv to "Anticipate border expansion", and its intended finite horizon
is encoded by the literal 5. The negative no-ETA sentinel violates that contract.

CLEAN LIVE GOVERNOR CONSEQUENCE
-------------------------------
The strongest deterministic consumer is `AI_buildGovernorChooseProduction()`, used
for human cities whose production is automated.

Its border-pop block first establishes that the city still needs culture to work the
full radius:

    if (AI_needsCultureToWorkFullRadius())
    {
        ...
        if (AI_countGoodTiles(true, true, 60) == 0 &&
            AI_chooseProcess(COMMERCE_CULTURE))
        {
            return;
        }
    }

`AI_needsCultureToWorkFullRadius()` is true for a non-disordered culture-level-1 city
with zero Culture output:

    !isDisorder()
    getCommerceRate(COMMERCE_CULTURE) <= 0
    getCultureLevel() + 1 <= CITY_PLOTS_RADIUS

Construct a production-automated human city with:

- culture level = 1;
- current Culture commerce rate = 0, hence `getCultureTurnsLeft() == -1`;
- no currently workable/unworked plot above the magic-value threshold 60;
- one good UNOWNED outer-radius plot, e.g. a healthy 3-food plot (magic value about
  85), which is not currently workable;
- Culture process available;
- no qualifying best Culture building taking the earlier building branch.

Correct finite-look-ahead behavior:

    currently usable good unworked tiles = 0
    => AI_countGoodTiles(..., true, 60) == 0
    => governor chooses the Culture process
    => culture output becomes positive and the city works toward the needed border pop.

Current behavior:

    getCultureTurnsLeft() == -1
    -1 <= 5
    => the unowned 3-food plot is counted early
    => AI_countGoodTiles(..., true, 60) == 1
    => the `== 0` Culture-process gate fails
    => governor falls through to unrelated production.

Nothing about that choice changes the zero culture rate. On the next governor
production decision the same `-1 <= 5` test can repeat, so the supposedly imminent
plot can suppress the very Culture process needed to make it reachable. This is a
self-sustaining wrong-state loop, not just a small valuation bias.

The state is ordinary and reachable. A human-controlled city can be at culture level
1 while currently producing zero Culture (for example after prior/manual culture,
recapture with retained owner culture, or loss/change of the source that produced the
existing culture), and production automation then uses this governor path.

SECOND LIVE EFFECT: GROWTH / CITIZEN VALUATION
----------------------------------------------
The same helper is called from `AI_yieldValue()` with `bUnworkedOnly=true` to cap
`iPopToGrow` by the number of future useful jobs. A level-1 zero-culture city can
therefore count inaccessible outer plots as imminent jobs indefinitely.

At population >=3, with positive happiness and the food bar already above the
`bFillingBar` threshold, one phantom good tile can change:

    correct iGoodTiles = 0 -> iPopToGrow = 0 -> no growth-food branch
    bugged  iGoodTiles = 1 -> iPopToGrow = 1 -> growth-food value enabled

so the sentinel misuse can also alter citizen/job selection. The governor deadlock is
the cleaner primary witness because it directly suppresses the action that would
repair the missing culture.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod's `AI_countGoodTiles()` only accepts plots whose `getWorkingCity() == this`; it
does not contain this future-border branch.

AdvCiv practical 1568, commit
`b96f30c2d50017ebf596b496c49a6e41b1b1cf7a`
("Several AI changes concerning workers") added the `advc.113` block:

    if(!bValid && pLoopPlot->getOwner() == NO_PLAYER &&
        getCultureLevel() == 1 && getCultureTurnsLeft() <= 5)
        bValid = true;

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains it, and current SAS is semantically identical here.
Therefore F540 is an AdvCiv regression inherited by SAS.

DEDUP / RELATED SENTINEL CHECK
------------------------------
Whole-album and Known-Issues searches found no existing root for
`getCultureTurnsLeft() == -1` being interpreted as an imminent border expansion in
`AI_countGoodTiles`.

Do not merge with:
- F494/KI#817, which concerns Culture-process order metadata across AI Auto Play ->
  human hand-back;
- F342/KI#665, which concerned positive sea-resource look-ahead switching `canBuild`
  into visible/future-tech mode before an immediate Work Boat role conversion;
- the future-happiness F530/F531/F535/F537 family, which is unrelated timer arithmetic.

A cross-file sibling exists in `CvPlayerAI::AI_countUnimprovedBonuses`: its positive
`iLookAhead` branch similarly fails to reject negative `getCultureTurnsLeft()`. That
is a genuine API-contract smell, but current SAS's authoritative internal Work Boat
callers have already been repaired to pass look-ahead 0 (including the F342/KI#665
role-transition fix), so no separate current F541 is promoted from that sibling at
this checkpoint.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR
-------------------
Require a real positive finite ETA before treating an unowned plot as imminent:

    int const iCultureTurnsLeft = getCultureTurnsLeft();
    if (!bValid && kPlot.getOwner() == NO_PLAYER &&
        getCultureLevel() == 1 &&
        iCultureTurnsLeft > 0 && iCultureTurnsLeft <= 5)
    {
        bValid = true;
    }

This preserves the authored five-turn anticipation exactly while making the API's
negative "no ETA" sentinel mean what it says.

For consistency, any future positive-look-ahead use of
`CvPlayerAI::AI_countUnimprovedBonuses` should apply the same `turns > 0 && turns <=
horizon` rule rather than relying on a one-sided upper-bound comparison.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. No-culture governor fixture
- Human production-automated city, culture level 1, Culture/turn = 0.
- No currently usable good unworked plot; one unowned outer 3-food plot.
- Culture process available; no earlier qualifying Culture building.
- Assert `AI_countGoodTiles(true, true, 60)` does NOT count the outer plot and the
  governor chooses the Culture process.

B. Genuine imminent expansion
- Same geometry, but positive Culture/turn and `getCultureTurnsLeft() == 5`.
- Preserve current anticipation: the outer plot may count as good.

C. Six-turn boundary
- `getCultureTurnsLeft() == 6` must not count the unowned plot.

D. Growth valuation
- Population >=3, positive happiness, food bar >80%, no real good unworked jobs.
- With Culture/turn = 0, assert an unowned outer good tile cannot by itself raise
  `iPopToGrow` from 0 to 1.

1. `AI_defianceAngerCost` — COARSE BUT INTERNALLY INTENTIONAL
------------------------------------------------------------
The helper was reopened because it translates the global Defy Resolution anger rule
into a city-level cost and therefore looked like a plausible same-concept/different-unit
seam.

Current shape:
- a religious resolution contributes no city cost when the city lacks the resolution
  religion;
- cities that cannot become unhappy return 0;
- `iUnhappyIncr` measures the incremental angry population caused by one new defiance;
- an already-active Defy timer doubles the resulting cost.

The final `*2` does not model the exact number/timing of stacked anger layers. However,
the surrounding source explicitly uses it as extra discouragement of repeated denial;
it is not presented as an exact forward simulation like the F530/F531/F535/F537
`AI_yieldValue` block. No wrong-object, divide-by-zero or sign inversion survived.
Preserve as heuristic policy, not F541.

2. `AI_updateSpecialYieldMultiplier` INCOME ASSERTION — CLOSED

    int iRatio = (100 * iExpenses) / iIncome;

For positive city production the integer quotient is normally 0. This is a real

5. BARBARIAN WORK-BOAT COMMENT / DOUBLE COUNT — BEHAVIORALLY HARMLESS CURRENTLY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The recent `AI_barbChooseProduction()` comment says Base AdvCiv's
`AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` iterates major-civilization cities and therefore misses
Barbarian Work Boats docked or being trained. The actual iterator contract was checked.

`CvPlayerAI::AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` uses `PlayerIter<ALIVE>`. The AgentIterator
status machinery adds the Barbarian player for this status, so a Barbarian player's
own docked and queued Work Boats are already included by the inherited helper.

Current SAS then adds:
- local Barbarian Worker-Sea units on the city plot; and
- the city's Worker-Sea training count
again.

So positive existing counts can be numerically double-counted and the comment's stated
reason is inaccurate.

However the value is consumed only through:

    if (iNeededSeaWorkers > 0 && iExistingSeaWorkers <= 0)

For the current branch, double-counting a positive value stays positive and zero stays
zero. Therefore the production decision is unchanged. The discrepancy affects the
reported magnitude/comment, not current gameplay. Preserve as diagnostic/comment debt;

6. `AI_buildUnitProb` ZERO-RELEVANT-RIVAL THROTTLE — INTENTIONAL ANCESTRY
------------------------------------------------------------------------
A stronger-looking candidate arose in the inherited high-power military throttle.
The relevant-rival loop initializes:

    int iHighestRivalPow = 0;

and, if no known rival satisfies the war/relevance predicates, later computes:

    rTargetPow = (1 + rTargetAdvantage) * 0;
    rTargetPow.increaseTo(scaled::epsilon());
    rPowRatio = ourPower / epsilon;

which normally reaches the strongest `r /= 4` throttle.

At first glance this seems to contradict the nearby comment:

    "Don't throttle at all until we're clearly ahead of the best rival"

Historical reconstruction closes it as deliberate policy.

AdvCiv practical 3439 / commit
`8ac818c755148af30ba928d1d26f3140e2d3fc45`, titled:

    "AI more reluctant to throttle military production"

changed the old floor:

    int iHighestRivalPow = 1;
    rPowRatio = ourPower / iHighestRivalPow;

to:

    int iHighestRivalPow = 0;
    ...
    rTargetPow.increaseTo(scaled::epsilon());

while adding the target-advantage buffer. Thus the predecessor ALREADY treated an empty
relevant-rival set as overwhelming relative military superiority; the commit deliberately
preserved that policy while making a real rival require roughly +25% advantage before
throttling.

The semantic reading is therefore "ahead of the best RELEVANT rival"; with no relevant
military rival, the policy intentionally de-emphasizes military production. No F541.

whereas the Yield sibling returns the raw count. This is indeed a poor integer-count
contract and makes the local nonnegative assertion toothless for a negative underlying
counter.

Before treating it as new, the album was searched more deeply. WIP290 already records
this exact discrepancy and already proves that every current whole-DLL gameplay consumer
uses it only as Boolean `>0`; ordinary emphasis toggling does not need the magnitude.
It remains inherited BtS API/clarity debt, not F541.

1. PRACTICAL 4214 / d5e9dbfea7 -- CLEAN REFACTOR CONTROL

2. PRACTICAL 4013 / f366263685 -- vector<pair> -> ListEnumMap ZERO-ENTRY CONTROL
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This conversion has a REAL generic semantic distinction:
- the old vector can retain an explicit `(UnitAI, 0)` entry;
- `FOR_EACH_NON_DEFAULT_PAIR` over ListEnumMap omits an entry whose stored value is the
  map default 0.

Therefore a zero-weight role could formerly survive as a last-place candidate and then
vanish entirely after the refactor.

All converted CvCityAI producers were checked rather than assuming the distinction was
harmless:
- assault/naval/paradrop/barbarian weights have positive lower bounds in their live
  insertion states;
- the only mathematically zero-capable converted expression is the ICBM weight
  `20 * AI_nukeWeight() / 100`;
- `AI_nukeWeight()` returns zero only in conditions where the nuke role is unavailable
  or strategically inapplicable; when a meaningful nuke choice exists its calculation
  has a positive floor large enough to keep the converted integer weight positive;
- current SAS custom naval ranking inserts only weights `> 0`.

So the container-semantic difference is real API/refactor debt but there is no live
CvCityAI old-vs-new candidate loss. No finding.

4. PRACTICAL 3561 / ee7bb6c81d -- HISTORICAL CORRECTNESS REPAIR
---------------------------------------------------------------

5. PRACTICAL 2842 / 7257590b64 -- TEMPORARY FACTOR-100 REGRESSION, LATER REPAIRED

repaired; do not number the historical transient defect.

===============================================================================
F541 / KI#864 CONFIRMED
AI_neededCultureDefenders UNDERCOUNTS AFTER LOST ceil() IN PRACTICAL 2723
===============================================================================

STATUS: CONFIRMED CURRENT AdvCiv/SAS GAMEPLAY BUG
ORIGIN: Base AdvCiv practical 2723 / 97f40e51e5
TITLE: "Some minor refactoring"
SCOPE: Current Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS retain the regression.
ROOT: a deliberate upward rounding step was dropped during the double -> scaled-number
      conversion; final nearest-integer rounding is not equivalent.

A. EXACT ANCESTRY
-----------------
The culture-garrison helper was introduced with an explicit ceiling. Practical 2719
still contains:

    double const dAIEraFactor = kOwner.AI_getCurrEraFactor().getDouble();
    double r = ::ceil(targetGarrisonStr /
            std::max((dAIEraFactor + 0.5) *
            (dAIEraFactor < 3.5 ? 3 : 4), 3.0));
    ...
    return ::round(r);

The nearby practical-2719 comment explicitly says:

    Tbd.: Use scaled instead of double

Practical 2723 performs exactly that advertised conversion. It changes the intermediate
to:

    scaled r = rTargetGarrisonStr / scaled::max(3,
            (rAIEraFactor + fixp(0.5)) *
            (rAIEraFactor < fixp(3.5) ? 3 : 4));

and eventually returns:

    return r.round();

The `::ceil(...)` operation itself disappears. The commit title contains no stated AI
policy/defender rebalance; the hunk is part of a representation/refactoring conversion.
No later commit restores the ceiling. Current Base AdvCiv and SAS retain this form.

B. THIS IS NOT A SCALED-NUMBER EQUIVALENCE
-------------------------------------------
`ScaledNum` has separate, explicit `round()` and `ceil()` APIs. Its own tests assert,
for example, that `fixp(2.001).ceil() == 3`, `fixp(2.5).ceil() == 3`, etc.

Thus:
- old intermediate semantics: any positive fraction above integer N becomes N+1;
- current semantics at function return: fractions below N+0.5 become N.

The later war/occupation modifiers do not make those two operations interchangeable.
The old code intentionally established an integer minimum first, then applied those
modifiers, and finally rounded the post-modifier result.

C. CLEAN NUMERIC WITNESS
------------------------
For Ancient-era factor 0, the denominator is exactly:

    max(3, (0 + 0.5) * 3) = 3

When the city is in a will-flip state, `rTargetProb` is explicitly set to 0, so:

    rTargetGarrisonStr = iCultureStr

Take any legal culture-strength result of 4. Then before occupation/war rescaling:

    raw requirement = 4 / 3 = 1.333...

Historical intended result:

    ceil(4 / 3) = 2

Current result in the ordinary no-extra-scaling branch:

    round(4 / 3) = 1

This is not dependent on an overflow, sentinel or unsupported XML value.
`cultureStrength()` itself computes a fixed-point blend of population, era, inner-ring
culture, culture ratios, anger/grievance/religion and handicap factors and finally
returns `rStrength.round()`. There is no invariant that constrains its integer output to
multiples of 3. Therefore values in the affected residue/fraction classes are ordinary
reachable outputs, not a forbidden synthetic state.

More generally, every positive pre-modifier quotient in an interval:

    (N, N + 0.5)

is one defender lower after practical 2723 than under the original ceiling semantics.

D. LIVE CONSEQUENCES
--------------------
The value is not UI-only.

1. `AI_neededDefenders()` applies:

    iDefenders = std::max(iDefenders, AI_neededCultureDefenders());

so the lost ceiling can directly reduce the requested city garrison by one when other
floors do not already dominate.

2. `AI_calculateNeededFloatingDefenders()` applies:

    int iCultureDefendersNeeded =
            AI_neededCultureDefenders() - AI_minDefenders();
    iFloatingDefenders = std::max(iFloatingDefenders,
            iCultureDefendersNeeded);

so the same undercount can remove a culture-driven floating-defender requirement.

For a clean early-game SAS boundary, `AI_minDefenders()` starts at 1; with No Barbarians
the custom early anti-Barbarian increment is disabled, and Ancient era does not meet the
later-era defender thresholds. Thus the historical 2 versus current 1 culture floor can
remain decision-visible rather than being automatically masked.

This can change city-defense demand, unit allocation and military production/guard
behavior in culturally pressured cities.

E. DEDUP
--------
This is independent of F526.
- F526 is cache-key contamination between culture-inclusive and culture-excluding
  `AI_neededFloatingDefenders` estimates.
- F541 changes the authoritative culture-defender quantity itself before that cache is
  involved.

It is also distinct from the generic WIP290 arithmetic check of this helper, which
challenged current divisors/object/sentinel contracts but did not reconstruct the lost
historical `ceil()` operation.

F. CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
--------------------------------
Restore the old upward rounding at the same semantic stage, e.g. compute the quotient as
scaled and convert it through `ceil()` before applying the subsequent occupation / war
adjustments, preserving the historical ordering. Do NOT merely replace the final
`r.round()` with `r.ceil()`: the old implementation first ceiled the base requirement,
then applied later modifiers, then rounded the final result.

A minimal representation-preserving shape would therefore be conceptually:

    scaled r = scaled((rTargetGarrisonStr / rDenom).ceil());
    ... existing occupation/war scaling ...
    return r.round();

Exact local style/type spelling should be chosen only when implementing; audit source is
still untouched.

================================================================================
F542 / KI#865 — `m_routeToCity` IS A PREVIOUS-END-OF-TURN SNAPSHOT; ROUTE TOPOLOGY CAN CHANGE
BEFORE THE NEXT WORKER PHASE, SO `AI_routeCity()` CAN MISS OR CHASE A CONNECTION FOR A FULL
WORKER PHASE
================================================================================

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited K-Mod/BBAI city-route-target cache lifetime defect, retained by Base
AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS. Stock BtS/Civ4CE does not contain this exact
`CvCityAI::m_routeToCity` cache / `AI_routeCity` architecture.

ROOT
----
`CvCityAI::AI_updateRouteToCity()` computes one same-area TEAM city that is not connected to the
source city by the player's best currently available Route type. It stores that target in:

    IDInfo m_routeToCity;

and `CvUnitAI::AI_routeCity()` later trusts the cached result through:

    CvCityAI* pRouteToCity = kLoopCity.AI_getRouteToCity();

The cache has only two current update paths:

1. `CvCityAI::AI_doTurn()` -> `AI_updateRouteToCity()`;
2. `CvPlayerAI::AI_processNewBuild()` when a newly available Build type is processed.

There is NO update/invalidation from `CvPlot::setRouteType`, Worker build completion, pillaging,
air bombing, plot-group changes or other ordinary route-topology mutations.

The timing is the critical part. In sequential turns:

    CvPlayer::setTurnActive(true)
        -> AI_updateCacheData()
        -> ...
        -> doTurnUnits()                 // Workers consume m_routeToCity here

and only when the player's turn is deactivated does:

    CvPlayer::doTurn()
        -> ...
        -> FOR_EACH_CITY city->doTurn()
             -> CvCityAI::AI_doTurn()
                  -> AI_updateRouteToCity()

run.

Thus the Worker phase generally consumes a route-target snapshot computed at the PREVIOUS end of
that player's turn. Any relevant topology change after that snapshot can invalidate it before the
next Worker phase.

WHY THE STORED PREDICATE REALLY CHANGES WHEN A RAILROAD IS DOWNGRADED
--------------------------------------------------------------------
`AI_updateRouteToCity()` uses `GC.getRouteFinder()`. Its `routeValid` callback accepts a plot only
when:

    kNewPlot.getRouteType() == GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).getBestRoute(&kNewPlot)

for owned/team territory.

Current SAS XML gives:

    ROUTE_ROAD     iValue = 1
    ROUTE_RAILROAD iValue = 2
    Railroad RoutePillage = ROUTE_ROAD

Once Railroad is available/buildable on a plot, `CvPlayer::getBestRoute()` therefore selects
Railroad. A Road left by pillaging is still enough for ordinary trade-network connectivity, but
it is NOT valid for the best-route path used by `AI_updateRouteToCity()`.

CLEAN SINGLE-PLAYER / SINGLE-MEMBER-TEAM WITNESS — ENEMY DOWNGRADES ONE RAIL TILE
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Set up AI player A with:

* at least two own cities in the same land area;
* both cities connected to the capital and to each other through a complete Railroad path;
* Railroad still being A's best buildable route;
* one critical Railroad segment on an OWNED, NO-IMPROVEMENT, NO-BONUS tile;
* at least one ordinary Worker able to reach that segment;
* no higher-priority Worker job that would mask the route decision.

At the end of A's turn N, `AI_updateRouteToCity()` sees a complete best-route path and stores no
missing target for this pair (e.g. `m_routeToCity` is null).

Later in the sequential round, enemy B pillages the critical Railroad. Current XML downgrades it
to Road. `CvPlot::setRouteType()` repairs plot groups but does NOT call
`AI_updateRouteToCity()`.

At A's next activation / Worker phase:

1. the two cities remain ordinarily connected to the capital by ROAD, therefore
   `AI_connectCity()` has no disconnected-city job;
2. the damaged segment has no improvement, therefore the earlier
   `AI_routeTerritory(true)` pass gives it value 0 and skips it;
3. it has no bonus, so `AI_connectBonus(false)` does not select it;
4. a fresh `AI_updateRouteToCity()` WOULD now fail the best-route path across the Road segment
   and store the other city as a Railroad-connection target;
5. but no refresh has occurred, so `AI_routeCity()` reads the stale null old target and returns
   false;
6. immediately after that failed call, current `AI_workerMove()` executes:

       bCanRoute = false; // advc.opt: Don't try again

   which suppresses the later generic `AI_routeTerritory()` fallback for this Worker.

Therefore the Worker cannot select the needed Railroad repair through the city-route logic in
this Worker phase. Only at A's end-of-turn city processing does `AI_updateRouteToCity()` finally
notice the damaged best-route connection. The Worker can then react on the NEXT activation — a
full Worker phase late.

This is a decision difference, not merely a stale debug value:

    fresh cache -> AI_routeCity() pushes a MISSION_ROUTE_TO repair sequence;
    stale cache -> AI_routeCity() cannot select that repair at all this turn.

SAME-TURN REVERSE WITNESS — REDUNDANT ROUTE MISSION AFTER ANOTHER WORKER FINISHES THE PAIR
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The inverse exists within one Worker phase as additional scope evidence.

Suppose the previous snapshot correctly stores city B as city A's missing best-route target.
Worker 1 completes the final missing route segment early in the unit pass. There is no
`m_routeToCity` invalidation. Worker 2 later reaches `AI_routeCity()` after Worker 1's completed
mission no longer provides collision protection.

The stale non-null pair can still be selected. `MISSION_ROUTE_TO` does not first re-test whether
the two cities are already connected by the desired route. `groupRoadTo()` builds only when the
current tile needs a route; otherwise it calls `groupPathTo()` toward the cached endpoint. Thus a
second Worker can spend movement following an already completed connection until the stale
mission self-terminates at an endpoint.

The enemy-Railroad-downgrade witness is the primary reproduction because it requires only one
Worker and avoids dependence on same-pass Worker ordering.

WHY EXISTING REFRESHES DO NOT CLOSE THE WINDOW
----------------------------------------------
Whole-core call inventory finds only:

    CvCityAI::AI_doTurn -> AI_updateRouteToCity
    CvPlayerAI::AI_processNewBuild -> per-city AI_updateRouteToCity

`AI_processNewBuild` responds to acquiring a new Build capability, not to completing or destroying
one instance of a route. `CvPlot::setRouteType` updates plot groups and connected-resource state
but not this AI cache.

The ordinary city `AI_doTurn` refresh is deterministic self-heal, but it occurs after the current
unit phase in sequential-turn play and is therefore one phase too late for Worker decisions.

ANCESTRY
--------
Civ4CE/BtS does not contain this exact cache/helper architecture.

The K-Mod history's initial 2010 code already contains:

* `m_routeToCity`;
* `AI_updateRouteToCity()` in city AI turn processing;
* `AI_routeCity()` as a Worker consumer;
* serialization of the cached ID.

Final K-Mod 1.46 retains the architecture. Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains it, with later advc.121
refinement of the route choice and mission sequencing. Current SAS retains it.

Because the available K-Mod history begins with the large initial K-Mod snapshot, this pass does
not claim a narrower post-initial K-Mod practical regression boundary. Classification is an
inherited K-Mod/BBAI route-target cache lifetime defect.

DEDUP
-----
This root is independent of prior route findings.

* WIP290 challenged `AI_updateRouteToCity()`'s apparently inverted `!GeneratePath` condition and
  correctly closed it: the helper is SUPPOSED to store a city for which a best-route path is
  missing. F542 concerns the lifetime of that correctly computed predicate after topology changes.
* F507 / KI#830 concerns cached TRADE ROUTE partner/yield state after roads/routes change. F542
  shares the physical route-topology producer but uses a different stored object
  (`CvCityAI::m_routeToCity`), a different consumer (`CvUnitAI::AI_routeCity`) and a different
  direct consequence (Worker mission selection rather than economic booking).
* F538/F539 concern incremental Worker-count accounting, not route topology/target caching.
* The prior `AI_routeCity` WIP controls audited advc.121 midpoint/queued-mission semantics once a
  target has been chosen; they did not establish that `m_routeToCity` stays current before target
  selection.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The invariant should be:

    before Worker AI consumes m_routeToCity, the cached target must reflect CURRENT best-route
    topology for the relevant team cities.

Conservative repair options include:

1. refresh each owned city's `AI_updateRouteToCity()` at player turn activation before
   `doTurnUnits()` (batched and simple; avoids per-route-build invalidation churn);
2. dirty the route-target caches when a route topology change can affect the owner/team, then
   lazily recompute on `AI_getRouteToCity()` / before Worker use;
3. as a defensive consumer check, revalidate a non-null cached pair before pushing missions — but
   this alone does NOT fix the stale-null case after route destruction, so a dirty/pre-unit
   refresh is still needed.

Refreshing only after a Worker completes a route is insufficient because enemy pillage/air bombing
and teammate route changes can invalidate the cache between turns.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
1. Complete Railroad pair at A end-turn -> enemy pillages an unimproved/no-bonus Rail tile to Road
   -> A Worker next activation must identify/rebuild the missing Railroad connection in that SAME
   Worker phase, not one turn later.
2. Verify the cities remain road-connected to the capital so `AI_connectCity()` cannot mask the
   test.
3. Put no improvement/bonus on the damaged tile so `AI_routeTerritory(true)` and
   `AI_connectBonus(false)` cannot mask the test.
4. Two Workers: Worker 1 finishes the final missing best-route segment; Worker 2 later in the same
   pass must not receive a stale redundant city-route mission.
5. Team-member city connection: external teammate route changes should also dirty/recompute the
   relevant owner cache.
6. New route technology/build acquisition must continue to refresh correctly through
   `AI_processNewBuild`.
7. Save/load determinism should remain unchanged; no serialization layout change is required for
   a dirty/pre-unit refresh repair.

C031-WIP317 — QUEUE 005 INCREMENTAL-STATE SWEEP — STALE WORKER-DEMAND SNAPSHOT AFTER PLOT MUTATION

F543 / KI#866 — m_iWorkersNeeded CAN STAY STALE THROUGH THE NEXT UNIT PHASE AFTER WORKABLE-PLOT STATE CHANGES
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED inherited Worker-demand snapshot lifetime defect.

ROOT
----
`CvCityAI::AI_updateWorkersHaveAndNeeded()` computes and stores:

    m_iWorkersNeeded = iWorkersNeeded;
    m_iWorkersHave = iWorkersHave;

The normal refresh runs from `CvCityAI::AI_doTurn()`, which is called from `CvCity::doTurn()`.
In sequential-turn play, that city turn is the owner's END-turn processing. The owner's next
activation instead starts by calling `CvPlayer::doTurnUnits()` before any new city `AI_doTurn()`.

Therefore `m_iWorkersNeeded` is intentionally carried from the previous city turn into the next
unit phase. That is safe only if the plots/tasks on which it depends cannot change in between.
They can.

Whole-source call inventory for `AI_updateWorkersHaveAndNeeded()` finds only:

* city initialization;
* the ordinary `CvCityAI::AI_doTurn()` refresh;
* two old commented-out calls beside that refresh.

`CvPlot::setImprovementType()` updates yields, plot-group bonus state, health/happiness and UI
state, but does not dirty or refresh Worker demand. Enemy pillage, bombardment/event destruction,
feature/improvement changes and similar external plot mutations can therefore make the stored city
demand stale until the owner's NEXT end-turn city refresh.

DETERMINISTIC CURRENT-SAS WITNESS — ENEMY PILLAGES A WORKED IMPROVEMENT
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Use a civilization's SECONDARY coastal land area so the SAS primary-area standing Worker floor
does not mask zero task demand.

Initial owner end-turn state:

* coastal city C has no local Worker;
* every useful local Worker task is complete;
* no live bonus/route/future-task source keeps `AI_neededWorkers(area)` positive;
* `AI_updateWorkersHaveAndNeeded()` therefore stores `C.m_iWorkersNeeded = 0`;
* the area can legitimately report `AI_neededWorkers(area) = 0` under the current KI#192 policy.

After that city refresh, but before C's owner's next activation, an enemy pillages one IMPROVEMENT
on a currently worked, featureless, owned land tile in C's workable radius.

The current SAS city-demand code contains the explicit KI#198 worked-land fallback:

    if (!kPlot.isImproved() && kPlot.isBeingWorked())
    {
        bool const bSASWorkedLandDemand =
            (!kPlot.isWater() && !kPlot.isFeature() &&
             kPlot.getOwner() == getOwner());
        if ((AI_getBestBuild(ePlot) != NO_BUILD || bSASWorkedLandDemand) &&
            isArea(kPlot.getArea()))
        {
            iUnimprovedWorkedPlotCount++;
        }
    }

So an immediate fresh recomputation does NOT depend on the legacy best-build cache for this
fixture. It deterministically gets:

    iUnimprovedWorkedPlotCount = 1
    iWorkersNeeded += 2 * 1 = 2

The later ordinary reduction gives at least:

    (2 + 1) / 3 = 1

and the final lower bound

    max((iUnimprovedWorkedPlotCount + 1) / 2, iWorkersNeeded)

also preserves at least 1. Thus a fresh city snapshot is definitively:

    C.AI_getWorkersNeeded() >= 1

The actual snapshot remains the pre-pillage 0 throughout the next unit phase.

DIRECT CONSUMER — AI_ferryWorkers HARD-SKIPS THE CITY
-----------------------------------------------------
Now place a valid `UNITAI_SETTLER_SEA` transport carrying at least one `UNITAI_WORKER` in the
reachable water network. There is no Worker already on C's land area.

`AI_settlerSeaMove()` calls `AI_ferryWorkers()` whenever Worker cargo is present and no competing
load-settler assignment blocks it.

`AI_ferryWorkers()` loops owned coastal cities and begins each candidate with:

    int iHave = pLoopCity->AI_getWorkersHave();
    ...
    int iValue = pLoopCity->AI_getWorkersNeeded() - (2 * iHave + 1) / 3;
    if (iValue <= 0)
        continue;

With the actual stale state:

    cached needed = 0
    local have = 0
    iValue = 0 - 0 = 0
    -> city rejected before pathfinding

With the fresh post-pillage state:

    needed >= 1
    local have = 0
    iValue >= 1
    -> city passes the first gate

The area-level hard capacity gate also separates cleanly. With city demand >=1,
`CvPlayerAI::AI_neededWorkers(destinationArea)` receives `3 * AI_getWorkersNeeded()` from C and
returns a positive land-area demand; with no destination-area Worker, `iAreaHave < iAreaNeeded`.
The transport can therefore path to and select C. In the stale state it never reaches that test.

This is a real unit-mission decision difference in the immediately following activation, not a
debug-only or eventually-consistent statistic. The city self-heals only at its next END turn,
so the transport opportunity is delayed by a full unit phase.

CULTURE-EXPANSION SIBLING
-------------------------
The same lifetime window exists for natural border expansion:

    CvCity::doTurn:
        AI().AI_doTurn();   // Worker demand/best-build snapshot
        doGrowth();
        doCulture();        // can acquire new workable plots afterward

The next player activation executes `doTurnUnits()` before another city refresh. Advanced Start
contains an explicit `pCity->AI_updateBestBuild(); // to account for culture expansion`, which is
useful evidence that culture expansion can invalidate city build planning. Ordinary `doCulture`
has no corresponding Worker-demand refresh.

The pillage witness is preferred for F543 because SAS's worked-land fallback proves the fresh
Worker need without relying on an immediate best-build-cache refresh after the border change.

ANCESTRY
--------
Civ4CE/BtS does not expose this exact BBAI/K-Mod city Worker-demand cache architecture.

The earliest reachable K-Mod snapshot (practical 3 / 2414225e64...) already contains:

* `m_iWorkersNeeded` / `AI_getWorkersNeeded()`;
* `AI_updateWorkersNeededHere()` in city AI turn processing;
* the city-before-culture ordering in `CvCity::doTurn()`;
* `AI_settlerSeaFerry()` consuming `AI_getWorkersNeeded()` as a hard positive-city gate.

Final K-Mod retains the architecture. AdvCiv renames/extends it to
`AI_updateWorkersHaveAndNeeded()` and `AI_ferryWorkers()`, but still refreshes the snapshot in the
city turn and consumes it in the next unit phase. Current SAS retains that lifetime model while
making the ferry capacity checks even more explicit.

Because the available K-Mod history begins with the initial large K-Mod snapshot, this pass does
not claim a narrower post-initial practical birth. Classification: inherited BBAI/K-Mod Worker-
demand cache lifetime defect.

DEDUP
-----
F543 is independent of the existing Worker families:

* KI#213 / F006 is the SPLIT JOB-MODEL defect: the city-side demand calculation can be wrong even
  when freshly recomputed because it does not see every job handled by SAS's custom Worker
  evaluator. F543's primary witness deliberately uses `bSASWorkedLandDemand`, so a FRESH current
  SAS computation is provably correct (>=1); only its lifetime is wrong.
* KI#198 owns the standing Worker floor and cross-subsystem minimum policy. F543 uses a secondary
  area where that floor is intentionally allowed to be zero before new work appears.
* F538 is completion-turn Worker-HAVE double counting.
* F539 is stale old-city Worker-HAVE assignment after mission interruption.
* F542 is `m_routeToCity` route-topology snapshot lifetime. It establishes the same general lesson
  (end-turn city cache consumed next unit phase) but stores a different object, has different
  producers/consumers and needs a different refresh payload. F543 concerns plot-improvement/task
  demand and Worker transport/production decisions rather than city-pair route targeting.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Required invariant:

    before unit AI uses city/area Worker demand, m_iWorkersNeeded must describe current workable
    plot/task state rather than the previous end-turn snapshot.

Conservative approaches:

1. At player turn activation before `doTurnUnits()`, refresh the Worker-planning city state used by
   unit AI. Because ordinary city demand depends partly on `m_aeBestBuild`, this should normally
   refresh `AI_updateBestBuild()` before `AI_updateWorkersHaveAndNeeded()` (matching city turn
   order), rather than refreshing only the latter.
2. Introduce a dirty flag for plot/culture/task changes affecting an owned city's workable radius
   and lazily rebuild best-build + Worker-demand state before a demand consumer.
3. Event-side targeted invalidation can reduce work, but must cover enemy pillage/destruction,
   culture/working-city changes, improvement completion/removal, relevant build-tech changes and
   other task producers; a pre-unit batched refresh is simpler and harder to miss.

Refreshing only `m_iWorkersHave` does not repair this root. Likewise, patching `AI_ferryWorkers`
alone would leave the same stale demand visible to area Worker counts, production, relocation,
evacuation and other consumers.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
1. Secondary coastal city, no Worker, fully developed -> end-turn demand 0 -> enemy pillages a
   worked featureless owned improvement -> next activation Worker-carrying Settler transport must
   recognize the city/area shortage in that SAME unit phase.
2. Confirm no bonus on the pillaged plot so `AI_countUnimprovedBonuses` cannot independently mask
   stale city demand.
3. Confirm the area is secondary so the primary-area KI#198 Worker floor cannot mask the 0->1
   transition.
4. Natural border expansion after the city AI refresh should likewise expose new Worker tasks to
   the next unit phase.
5. Worker completion that removes the final task should not leave a stale positive demand that
   attracts unnecessary ferrying/retention through the next phase.
6. Save/load and human automation behavior must preserve deterministic cache contents.

POST-F543 SIBLING - STALE m_iWorkersHave AFTER WORKER DEATH/CAPTURE
-------------------------------------------------------------------
The same refresh-lifetime root proved for m_iWorkersNeeded also applies to m_iWorkersHave.

A city can finish its city turn with:

    m_iWorkersHave   = 1
    m_iWorkersNeeded = 1

because one Worker is physically/mission-assigned to it. If an enemy kills or captures that Worker
before the owner's next activation, no death/capture path performs AI_changeWorkersHave(-1).
The next unit phase can therefore still evaluate the city through AI_ferryWorkers with stale have=1.
Its replacement shortage becomes:

    needed - (2*have + 1)/3
    1      - (2*1    + 1)/3
    0

and the city is rejected. A fresh combined Worker planning refresh gives have=0, needed=1 and accepts
the shortage.

Do NOT number this separately. It has the same stale end-turn Worker-planning snapshot, the same
pre-unit-phase consumer and the same robust repair boundary as F543. F543 should therefore be read as
covering both m_iWorkersNeeded and m_iWorkersHave external-mutation staleness, while F538/F539 retain
their distinct intra-refresh/incremental accounting roots.

LOW-COVERAGE LIVE-FUNCTION INVENTORY - CONTROLS
------------------------------------------------
A function-coverage pass against the album was used to avoid repeatedly auditing already saturated
large helpers.

Several apparent zero-mention methods are dead/commented BtS/K-Mod residue in current SAS, including
AI_potentialPlot, AI_foodAvailable, AI_ignoreGrowth, AI_chooseProject and old culture helper blocks.
They do not define a current gameplay surface.

AI_countBestBuilds:
- current loop is CityPlotIter(*this, false), matching the old non-center city-radius set;
- current core C++ use is essentially the Python exposure; CvAdvisorUtils uses it for an improvement
  warning;
- no independent iterator/set defect survives.

AI_countWorkedPoorPlots:
- current semantics are inherited K-Mod semantics: a worked plot is poor when !AI_isGoodPlot;
- no separate local defect survives once the shared best-build-policy split below is recognized.

AI_emphasizeIrrigatingPlot:
- AdvCiv practical 4214 extracted the old inline K-Mod condition into the helper;
- the extraction preserves the captured plot/city conditions (later 4216 barbarian exclusions are
  intentional);
- no lost local state or changed plot identity survives.

AI_setStrongEmphasis:
- persistent-until-emphasis-change behavior is deliberate;
- it is serialized and its setter immediately reassigns plots;
- no lifecycle defect found.

BBAI SETTLER-COMPLETION TODO - CLOSED POSITIVELY
------------------------------------------------
AI_chooseProduction contains the old comment:

    // BBAI TODO: Does this work right after settler is built???

The completion ordering answers yes. CvCity::popOrder(ORDER_TRAIN) calls owner.initUnit(...) before
the empty-queue AI_chooseProduction() call. Therefore the just-completed Settler already exists when
AI_totalUnitAIs(UNITAI_SETTLE) and the city-plot Settler count are queried. No stale completion-count
bug exists there.

KI#213 ARCHITECTURAL BROADENING - DO NOT SPEND F544
---------------------------------------------------
The existing pending KI#213 split between the legacy CvCityAI best-build cache and the custom
CvUnitAI land-Worker policy affects more than AI_updateWorkersHaveAndNeeded.

AI_isGoodPlot projects a plot through m_aeBestBuild / m_aiBestBuildValue only when the legacy city
cache supplies a best build. Ordinary SAS land jobs can deliberately be absent from that cache even
when CvUnitAI::AI_bestCityBuild would choose a valid custom improvement. AI_isGoodPlot then evaluates
only current yields.

A simple family is an unimproved flat Plains plot:

    current 1 food + 1 production -> magic value 17 -> not good (land threshold >21)
    Farmed  2 food + 1 production -> magic value 27 -> good

when the current SAS Worker policy legitimately chooses the Farm under food pressure.

Consequences of the same architectural split include:
- AI_countGoodPlots -> AI_getTargetPopulation;
- target population -> food-kept building value, AI_splitEmpireValue and future Worker-demand math;
- AI_countWorkedPoorPlots -> target-population correction and draft/growth heuristics;
- CitySiteEvaluator plot-sharing protection via AI_isGoodPlot / AI_countGoodPlots;
- CvAdvisorUtils's AI_countBestBuilds-based improvement warning can likewise undercount ordinary
  custom land opportunities.

All of these belong to KI#213. The shared-policy repair already intended for KI#213 should make the
city-side projection and Worker-side choice consume one build policy. Do not allocate new finding
numbers to individual consequences.

================================================================================
F544 / KI#867 - SAS TRANSIENT CULTURE-VICTORY CITY RANK/INVESTMENT IS REFRESHED
BEFORE CITY PRODUCTION BUT CAN BECOME STALE AFTER A CULTURE BUILDING COMPLETES;
THE SAME popOrder THEN USES THE OLD ROLE TO GATE PRODUCTION AND CULTURE PROCESS
================================================================================

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED - AdvCiv-SAS-specific cache/snapshot lifetime defect introduced with the transient
culture-victory city-targeting state (practical 5982 / db0d76c10e...). Base AdvCiv/K-Mod/BtS do not
contain these two SAS fields or the SAS hard process/culture-city gates that consume them.

ROOT
----
SAS practical 5982 introduced two transient per-city fields:

    m_iCultureVictoryRank
    m_iCultureVictoryInvestmentPercent

They are recomputed empire-wide only by CvPlayerAI::AI_updateCommerceWeights(). For an AI turn,
AI_doTurnPre runs that refresh before city production.

That is correct at the refresh point, but the stored values depend on mutable city culture/culture
rate. City production can change those inputs later in the same player turn.

A completed culture building follows:

    CvCity::popOrder(ORDER_CONSTRUCT)
        -> setNumRealBuilding(...)
            -> processBuilding(...)
                -> updates the building's actual city commerce/modifier effects
        -> ...
        -> if queue empty:
             CvCityAI::AI_chooseProduction()

There is no AI_updateCommerceWeights() between setNumRealBuilding/processBuilding and this immediate
AI_chooseProduction(). A complete current call inventory finds AI_updateCommerceWeights at normal
player AI pre-turn refresh, human slider handling, and Great Work handling; ordinary AI building
completion does not refresh it.

CLEAN CURRENT-SAS HERMITAGE FIXTURE
-----------------------------------
Hermitage is a shipped current building with +50% Culture commerce modifier.

Take an AI already at Culture-2 with the standard three required Legendary cities and at least four
cities. At the pre-turn AI_updateCommerceWeights pass, suppose the four projected Legendary
countdowns are:

    city 1 = 10
    city 2 = 20
    city 3 = 30
    city 4 = 39

City 4 is stored as:

    culture-victory rank       = 4
    victory investment percent = 0

Later in that city's city turn, it completes Hermitage. In a city whose projected culture output is
substantially modifier-driven, adding +50 percentage points can reduce the projected countdown from
roughly 39 to roughly 26. The fresh empire ordering is then:

    10, 20, 26, 30

City 4 is now rank 3. As the new required bottleneck candidate, the current balancing formula gives
it a positive investment percentage (indeed 100% when its countdown is the required-city
bottleneck). There is no divisibility/ranking invariant preventing this crossing; the rank list is
explicitly sorted from mutable projected city countdowns.

IMMEDIATE HARD CONSUMERS
------------------------
The stale value is consumed in the SAME CvCity::popOrder call.

1. AI_chooseProduction culture-city role

Current SAS requires:

    AI_atVictoryStage(CULTURE2)
    stored rank > 0
    stored rank <= required culture cities
    stored investment > 0

before setting bCultureCity (subject to the separate small-empire/site exception).

Choose the fixture with enough cities / no expansion exception so that this secondary condition is
inert. Fresh post-Hermitage state sets bCultureCity=true; current stale state rank=4/investment=0
sets it false.

bCultureCity is not cosmetic. It gates or scales numerous production branches, including generic
land/naval production-capacity logic, assault/naval/air/carrier choices and invader weighting.

2. AI_processValue culture-process permission

For an AI above first-ring culture and below the configured local-pressure threshold, current SAS
hard-skips production-to-Culture conversion unless:

    Culture-2 && rank in required set && investmentPercent > 0

Fresh post-Hermitage state permits the candidate's Culture process; current stale state suppresses
its culture conversion. AI_chooseProduction calls AI_bestProcess/AI_processValue during the
immediate next-order choice, so this is a direct same-turn consumer rather than merely next-turn
heuristic lag.

ANCESTRY
--------
Practical 5982 (`db0d76c10e5e...`) introduced the transient rank/investment fields, their
AI_updateCommerceWeights producer and the required-candidate culture-process gate. Later SAS work
also consumes the fields in the bCultureCity production role.

Base AdvCiv 1.14, K-Mod 1.46 and BtS/Civ4CE do not contain this SAS transient state, so F544 is
SAS-specific.

DEDUP / ROOT SEPARATION
-----------------------
WIP301 explicitly challenged these fields for SAVE/LOAD discontinuity and correctly closed that
question: normal AI turn start recomputes them before the ordinary AI decision path.

F544 is different. The pre-turn refresh has already happened correctly; then a city mutation changes
the ranking inputs before a same-turn hard consumer. Serialization changes do not fix this.

F544 is also distinct from:
- F498, which concerns K-Mod's m_aiConstructionValue cache surviving player policy/commerce changes;
- F519/F520, stored city safety/value state;
- F542/F543, route/Worker planning snapshots;
- KI#213, split city-vs-Worker best-build policy.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Do not merely serialize the fields; that addresses the wrong lifetime.

Robust options are:
1. mark the player-wide culture-targeting snapshot dirty whenever any event materially changes a
   city's culture, culture rate, culture modifier or city set, and refresh lazily before a hard
   rank/investment consumer; or
2. at minimum, refresh AI_updateCommerceWeights after an AI completes a building that can change
   the culture-ranking inputs and before immediate AI_chooseProduction.

The first approach is safer because buildings are not the only possible post-refresh mutation source.
Any repair must avoid recursive/unbounded refresh from within AI_updateCommerceWeights itself.

        3 * GC.getGame().getCultureThreshold((CultureLevelTypes)2));

Practical 3242 / advc.192 extracted this from K-Mod's old inline first-border-pop heuristic and

the first real border-pop threshold (10 Culture on Normal), and shipped SAS keeps ConstructPercent

================================================================================
F545 / KI#868 - AI_updateSafety TRIES TO COUNT A DEFENDER FINISHING THIS TURN BUT
SKIPS THE ZERO-DEFENDER CASE; THE NEWLY COMPLETED DEFENDER CAN THEN OBEY STALE
EVACUATION STATE AND RETREAT OUT OF THE CITY IT WAS BUILT TO DEFEND
================================================================================

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED - inherited AdvCiv city-safety defect, born in practical 1687
`ef52c71628f14cf9751a2246ef520fce41617c28` ("Improvements to AI city safety, stack strength
evaluation."). Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the zero-defender exclusion. SAS's default
all-land-unit evacuation policy makes the direct unit-phase consequence especially sharp.

ROOT
----
`CvCityAI::AI_updateSafety()` explicitly tries to account for a combat unit that will finish at the
end of the current turn:

    iDefenders = getPlot().getNumDefenders(getOwner());

    // Check if we'll finish a defender at the end of our turn
    if (iDefenders > 0 && isProductionUnit() && getProductionTurnsLeft() == 1)
    {
        CvUnitInfo const& kProductionUnit = GC.getInfo(getProductionUnit());
        if (kProductionUnit.getCombat() > 0)
            iDefStrength = (iDefStrength * (iDefenders + 1)) / iDefenders;
    }

The `iDefenders > 0` guard is needed only by that averaging formula's division. Semantically it
excludes precisely the case in which the incoming defender matters most: a city with ZERO current
defenders.

In that state the completing combat unit contributes neither to `iDefStrength` nor to the
one-turn-doom classification. The subsequent evacuation test still uses the zero current-defender
snapshot:

    if (iAttackers + 1 >= iDefenders)
        bEvac = (scaled(iAttStrength, iDefStrength + 1) > rThresh);

With no current local defense, any ordinary adjacent attack force readily makes the city look doomed.

TURN ORDER MAKES THE OMITTED DEFENDER REAL BEFORE THE SAFETY STATE IS CONSUMED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This is not a forecast whose unit might fail to appear.

At player activation, before the player's normal turn work:

    CvPlayer::setTurnActive
        -> AI().AI_updateCacheData()
            -> every city AI_updateSafety()

Only afterward does the player turn run. Each city performs:

    CvCity::doTurn
        -> AI_doTurn()
        -> doGrowth()
        -> doCulture()/doPlotCultureTimes100()
        -> doProduction()

Then, after the player's city turn work, `CvPlayer::setTurnActive` calls:

    doTurnUnits()

Therefore a city whose combat unit has `getProductionTurnsLeft()==1` when safety is computed really
can complete that unit in `doProduction()` BEFORE the new unit's unit-AI phase.

CLEAN FIXTURE
-------------
Take an AI city with:

- zero current defenders;
- one visible hostile land attacker close enough to enter the city-safety attack-strength query;
- a strong ordinary combat defender (e.g. Longbow-class city defender) at exactly 1 production turn
  remaining;
- no nearby friendly defenders contributing enough defense to mask the case.

At activation-time `AI_updateSafety`:

    iDefenders = 0

The explicit finishing-defender block is skipped solely because `iDefenders > 0` is false. The city
can consequently become `CITYSAFETY_EVACUATING` from the zero-defense strength/doom calculation.

Later in the SAME player turn, `doProduction()` creates the defender. A fresh safety calculation at
this point sees the actual defender; choose the produced defender / enemy-strength fixture so that
its real local defense changes the city from Evacuating to Threatened or Safe (a strong defender
versus a weak nearby attacker makes this straightforward).

Current code performs no general post-production safety refresh, so `m_eSafety` remains the stale
pre-production EVACUATING value through the immediately following unit phase.

DIRECT CURRENT-SAS CONSEQUENCE
------------------------------
`CvUnitAI::AI_update()` checks evacuation before ordinary UnitAI movement for the principal land
combat roles, including:

    UNITAI_ATTACK
    UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY
    UNITAI_COLLATERAL
    UNITAI_PILLAGE
    UNITAI_RESERVE
    UNITAI_COUNTER
    UNITAI_CITY_DEFENSE
    UNITAI_CITY_COUNTER
    UNITAI_CITY_SPECIAL

and calls `AI_evacuateCity()` when the unit stands in its own city.

Current SAS ships:

    SAS_AI_EVACUATE_CITY_ALL_LAND_UNITS_WHEN_DOOMED_ENABLE = 1

Under that default, an eligible unit in a city still marked EVACUATING immediately attempts
`AI_retreatToCity()` rather than using Base AdvCiv's probabilistic leave/stay choice.

So the newly completed defender can be born in an allegedly doomed undefended city, enter its unit
AI later in the same activation, read the obsolete zero-defender safety classification, and attempt
to LEAVE the city it has just made defensible.

This is a direct gameplay consequence, not merely a pessimistic score. The same stale evacuation
state also rejects/redirects reinforcement, retreat, route and other city-target decisions, but the
new defender evacuating itself is sufficient as the clean witness.

ANCESTRY
--------
Practical 1687:

    ef52c71628f14cf9751a2246ef520fce41617c28
    "Improvements to AI city safety, stack strength evaluation."

introduced the prospective-production adjustment together with the exact guard:

    if (iDefenders > 0 && isProductionUnit() && getProductionTurnsLeft() == 1)

and the comment:

    // Check if we'll finish a defender at the end of our turn

Later AdvCiv refactors retain it unchanged apart from accessor/type/style updates. Base AdvCiv 1.14
and current SAS still contain the same zero-defender exclusion.

The defect is therefore not a later SAS customization, although SAS's enabled all-land-unit
forced-evacuation policy amplifies its current consequence.

DEDUP / ROOT SEPARATION
-----------------------
F545 is distinct from:

- F519/F520 and KI#172-related city-safety/value findings, which concern different safety/value
  inputs or percentile logic;
- F526 culture/floating-defender cache behavior;
- F538/F539/F543 Worker counting/snapshot defects;
- F544 culture-victory role snapshot;
- the already-audited `AI_updateSafety` / local-strength assertion and border-danger families.

The unique root here is the explicit prospective defender adjustment being undefined for zero
existing defenders and therefore omitted exactly at the production-to-unit-phase boundary.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Avoid inventing an approximate zero-defender average merely to bypass the divide-by-zero.

The cleanest repair is to refresh city safety after a combat defender actually completes, before
its same-turn unit AI can consume the cached state. This uses the real created unit, promotions,
city modifiers and current local-defense computation instead of trying to synthesize an average from
zero existing defenders.

For performance, the refresh can be restricted to AI cities whose previous safety is not already
safe/perfect and to completion of a land combat unit that can materially defend the city. A more
general event-dirty safety model would also work if maintained consistently.

If retaining the predictive pre-production optimization, its zero-defender branch must use a
well-defined defense estimate rather than silently pretending that the finishing unit does not
exist.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F545 / KI#868 SAME-ROOT BROADENING - PROSPECTIVE NAVAL UNIT CAN BE INVENTED AS LAND DEFENSE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

F545's prospective-production branch has a second current defect under the SAME producer and repair
boundary, so it does not receive a new F-number.

Current `AI_updateSafety` uses:

    if (iDefenders > 0 && isProductionUnit() && getProductionTurnsLeft() == 1)
    {
        CvUnitInfo const& kProductionUnit = GC.getInfo(getProductionUnit());
        if (kProductionUnit.getCombat() > 0) // Assume an average defender
            iDefStrength = (iDefStrength * (iDefenders + 1)) / iDefenders;
    }

The local defense being forecast immediately above is explicitly LAND defense:

    AI_localDefenceStrength(..., DOMAIN_LAND, ...)

but the production test asks only whether the completing unit has positive combat strength. It does
not require `DOMAIN_LAND`, city-defense applicability or even that the completed unit can defend the
city plot as a land defender.

Current shipped SAS provides ordinary witnesses such as Galley and Destroyer: they have positive
`iCombat` but `DOMAIN_SEA`. In a coastal city with at least one current land defender, finishing such
a ship therefore multiplies the LAND-defense forecast as though one additional average land defender
were about to appear.

For one current land defender of effective strength S, the branch changes the forecast from S to 2S.
Choose a nearby enemy land attack strength A such that:

    S / 2 <= A < S

Without the phantom ship:

    2A >= S       -> not Safe

With the current production predictor:

    2A < 2S       -> Safe

So the same F545 branch is bidirectionally wrong:

- with zero current defenders it omits a real completing land defender;
- with one or more current defenders it can invent a phantom land defender from a completing naval
  combat unit.

A post-production refresh using the real completed unit fixes both errors naturally. If the predictive
branch is retained, it must at minimum test that the production unit belongs to the same defensive
domain / can materially contribute to the LAND-defense quantity being forecast.

CONTROL - CURRENT DEFENDER COUNT DOES NOT COUNT ORDINARY DOCKED SHIPS
----------------------------------------------------------------------
A nearby suspicion closes cleanly and is recorded to prevent rediscovery. `iDefenders` is obtained by
`getPlot().getNumDefenders(getOwner())`, whose `PUF_canDefend` ultimately calls `CvUnit::canDefend`.
`canDefend` enforces valid domain for the plot. A normal city plot is land, so ordinary DOMAIN_SEA and
DOMAIN_AIR units do not inflate this count merely by being stationed in the city. The F545 naval bug
therefore belongs specifically to the prospective-production `getCombat() > 0` test above, not to the
current defender count.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F546 / KI#869 - THE SOLE-CITY SHORTCUT CONFLATES "DO NOT EVACUATE THE LAST CITY" WITH "CITY IS SAFE"
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED -- inherited AdvCiv `advc.139` safety-model defect, retained by Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current
AdvCiv-SAS. Distinct from F519/F520/F545 because the refresh DOES run; its producer deliberately
returns the wrong generalized state for a one-city empire.

ROOT
----
Current `CvCityAI::AI_updateSafety` begins:

    m_eSafety = CITYSAFETY_SAFE;
    CvPlayerAI const& kOwner = GET_PLAYER(getOwner());
    if (kOwner.getNumCities() <= 1)
        return;

Thus a player's sole city is unconditionally `CITYSAFETY_SAFE`. No attacker count, local attack
strength, local defense strength, wider-range attack or threatened/evacuating classification is ever
computed.

The historical origin explains how this happened.

Before `isSafe` existed, `advc.139` had an evacuation-only routine. Its early return for
`getNumCities() <= 1` was sensible: do not evacuate the empire's last city because there is no other
city to preserve instead.

Practical 1376 / `525e919195916c8e061678b29cf21817eb9f07b8` expanded that routine into the general
`updateSafety` / `isSafe` model. The same change introduced:

    bSafe = true;
    if (o.getNumCities() <= 1)
        return;

while also computing `bSafe` from hostile attack versus defense for every multi-city empire and
adding new callers that treat `isSafe` as a general tactical predicate. Later enum conversion merely
preserved the behavior as `CITYSAFETY_SAFE`; it did not create the root.

So an old rule with the meaning:

    "never set EVACUATING for the last city"

was carried into a broader state variable where it now means:

    "the last city is tactically SAFE."

Those statements are not equivalent. A last city can be THREATENED even though evacuation is not a
valid strategic response.

Practical 1687 / `ef52c71628f14cf9751a2246ef520fce41617c28` later made the consequence especially
explicit by replacing Great-Person target checks with hard `AI_isSafe()` gates and expanding other
city-safety consumers.

CLEAN CURRENT-SAS WITNESS
-------------------------
Use an AI that owns exactly one city. Put an enemy land stack adjacent to that city and make the
strengths satisfy the normal multi-city unsafe condition, e.g.:

    iAttStrength * 2 >= iDefStrength

with the attack close enough for the range-1 `AI_localAttackStrength` query.

A mechanically identical city owned by a two-city AI reaches the normal calculation and becomes
THREATENED or EVACUATING according to the later threshold logic.

The one-city AI instead returns before reading any attacker and remains:

    AI_isSafe() == true

regardless of how overwhelming the adjacent stack is.

DIRECT STATE-CHANGING CONSUMER - GREAT PERSON
---------------------------------------------
Current `CvUnitAI::AI_greatPersonMove` hard-filters every slow city action with:

    FOR_EACH_CITYAI(pLoopCity, kOwner)
    {
        if (!pLoopCity->AI_isSafe())
            continue;
        ...
        // Join / Construct / Hurry
    }

Thus a Great Person already in the besieged sole city may retain Join, Construct or Hurry as normal
candidate actions even though the exact same tactical strengths make the city ineligible as soon as
the empire owns a second city.

This is not merely a preference about whether a Great Person should physically flee. The safety
predicate was added precisely to prevent permanent slow-action investment in unsafe cities. The sole-
city shortcut bypasses that protection before the action-value comparison even begins.

Current SAS Great-General handling makes the contract even more explicit. `AI_join` rejects a city
when `!AI_isSafe()`, and SAS deliberately permits an immediate Military-Instructor join despite
radius-2 danger only when the General is already in an `AI_isSafe` city. A besieged sole capital
therefore receives the special "safe city" permission solely because the empire has no second city,
not because the threat calculation says the city is safe.

OTHER CURRENT CONSUMERS
-----------------------
The false Safe state also reaches broader tactical code. For example, non-land
`AI_isThreatenedFromLand()` returns `NO_PROBABILITY` immediately for an undamaged unit standing in an
`AI_isSafe` city. Retreat/upgrade/city valuation and other consumers likewise distinguish Safe from
Threatened independently of whether evacuation itself is permitted.

These consumers reinforce the semantic mismatch, but the permanent Great-Person action gate is
already sufficient as the concrete state-changing witness.

ANCESTRY
--------
The exact conceptual regression is visible in practical 1376:

old evacuation-only model:

    bEvacuate = false;
    if (o.getNumCities() <= 1)
        return;

new generalized safety model:

    bEvacuate = false;
    bSafe = true;
    if (o.getNumCities() <= 1)
        return;
    ...
    bSafe = (attStr * 2 < defStr);

The early return was retained while the meaning of the cached state widened from evacuation-only to
Safe/unsafe. Practical 1687 then added the direct Great-Person safety gate and other hard consumers.
Base AdvCiv and current SAS preserve the unconditional sole-city return.

DEDUP / ROOT SEPARATION
-----------------------
F546 is distinct from:

- F519: a newly founded city retains constructor-default Safe because it has not yet received its
  first safety computation;
- F520: an existing city's previously correct safety becomes stale after tactical unit-state changes
  because invalidation/refresh is incomplete;
- F545: `AI_updateSafety` does perform the strength calculation but its prospective completing-unit
  adjustment uses the wrong defender model;
- the evacuation-policy itself: F546 does NOT propose evacuating the last city.

The F546 producer is the `numCities <= 1` early return inside a real safety refresh. The repair is
therefore different from initialization, invalidation or production-completion refresh fixes.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Do not return `CITYSAFETY_SAFE` merely because the player has one city.

Instead, run the ordinary attack/defense classification and allow the sole city to become
`CITYSAFETY_THREATENED` when tactically unsafe, while separately suppressing only the
`CITYSAFETY_EVACUATING` outcome for a one-city empire.

Conceptually:

    compute Safe vs unsafe normally;
    if unsafe:
        if more than one city and evacuation threshold is met:
            EVACUATING
        else:
            THREATENED

That preserves the original strategic intent -- never abandon the last city -- without lying to all
other `AI_isSafe()` consumers about the tactical state.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTROL - `m_aiSpecialYieldMultiplier` IS REFRESHED BEFORE `AI_doEmphasize` CONSUMES IT
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The WIP320 continuation cursor challenged whether the cached special-yield multipliers could be stale
when `AI_doEmphasize()` reads them.

The normal AI turn ordering closes this concern:

    CvPlayerAI::AI_doTurnPre(...)
    ...
    CvPlayer::AI_assignWorkingPlots()
        -> each city AI_assignWorkingPlots()
            -> AI_updateSpecialYieldMultiplier()
    ...
    CvCity::doTurn()
        -> CvCityAI::AI_doTurn()
            -> AI_doEmphasize()

Thus the multipliers are refreshed before the normal city-AI emphasis consumer in each activation.
Moreover, changing an emphasis through `AI_setEmphasize()` calls `AI_assignWorkingPlots()` again, so
an emphasis-state mutation also triggers a new multiplier calculation rather than leaving the old
value in place.

No independent stale-cache F547 exists here.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F547 / KI#870 - PREREQUISITE-BUILDING VALUE CAN REWARD AN IMPOSSIBLE NATIONAL-WONDER UNLOCK
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED -- inherited K-Mod prerequisite-building valuation defect. K-Mod itself later left an
explicit source comment acknowledging the national-wonder-limit flaw, and current AdvCiv/SAS still
retain both the permissive visible-only test and shipped XML witnesses.

ROOT
----
`CvCityAI::AI_buildingValue()` adds extra value to a building when constructing it would enable a
valuable later building. Before valuing the later building, current code deliberately uses
`bTestVisible=true` because the prerequisite building itself must be ignored while asking whether the
future target could eventually appear in the production list.

Current civ-wide target-city loop:

    if (pLoopCity->getProductionBuilding() != eLoopBuilding &&
        pLoopCity->canConstruct(eLoopBuilding, false, true))
    {
        iHighestValue = std::max(
            pLoopCity->AI_buildingValue(eLoopBuilding, 0, 0,
                bConstCache, false),
            iHighestValue);
    }

The adjacent AdvCiv comment accurately states the contract:

    bVisible=true means: check only if the building appears in the production list.
    In particular, prereq buildings aren't checked, which is good. However, the
    national wonder limit also isn't checked, which is bad.

`CvCity::canConstruct()` confirms why. The per-city world/team/national-wonder-limit checks are all
inside:

    if (!bTestVisible)
    {
        ...
        if (kBuildingClass.isNationalWonder())
        {
            if (isNationalWondersMaxed())
                return false;
        }
        ...
    }

So `canConstruct(..., false, true)` can call a national wonder a valid future target even when that
city has no national-wonder slot left.

The same problem exists even more directly in the LOCAL prerequisite branch. That branch first uses
only the player-level visible construction test for the future building, and then, when the current
city lacks the required local building, directly evaluates:

    AI_buildingValue(eLoopBuilding, ..., bAllowRecursion=false)

without a normal `CvCity::canConstruct(eLoopBuilding)` check for the current city.

CLEAN CURRENT-SAS SHIPPED-DATA WITNESS - BARRACKS -> HEROIC EPIC
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS retains:

    BUILDING_HEROIC_EPIC
        class: BUILDINGCLASS_HEROIC_EPIC
        iMaxPlayerInstances = 1       // national wonder
        iMilitaryProductionModifier = 50
        BuildingClassNeeded in city:
            BUILDINGCLASS_BARRACKS

SAS does not override the stock BtS `MAX_NATIONAL_WONDERS_PER_CITY`; Civ4CE's authoritative BtS XML
has that value as 2 (OCC uses 5). Current `CvCity::getNumNationalWondersLeft()` therefore enforces the
normal inherited two-slot city limit for an AI.

Construct the following ordinary state:

1. The AI otherwise satisfies the player/team requirements for Heroic Epic.
2. A city already contains two national wonders, so `isNationalWondersMaxed()` is true.
3. The city does not yet have a Barracks.
4. The city is not in the SAS danger state that would independently zero Heroic Epic's military-
   production value, and it has met another civilization so the ordinary +50% military-production
   valuation is active.

A real `canConstruct(BUILDING_HEROIC_EPIC)` call is false in that city because the national-wonder
slots are exhausted.

But while valuing Barracks, the prerequisite code sees Heroic Epic as a relevant future building,
passes the visible/player-level checks, and the local-prerequisite branch evaluates Heroic Epic
anyway. Heroic Epic has a plainly positive +50% military-production contribution in an appropriate
production city, and its military-production modifier also excludes it from the later generic
capital/low-impact national-wonder slot penalty that can zero some other national wonders at zero
slots.

The resulting positive Heroic-Epic value is scaled and ADDED to the Barracks value even though this
city can never use that Barracks to unlock Heroic Epic.

This is a deterministic score error, not merely a UI visibility discrepancy: the impossible future
building raises `AI_buildingValue(BUILDING_BARRACKS)` and can therefore change the building ranking
and production choice.

CURRENT SAS HAS ADDITIONAL SHIPPED WITNESSES
---------------------------------------------
A current XML scan shows national wonders with prerequisite-building relations still include:

- Forbidden Palace <- Courthouse (3 empire-wide; Courthouse also required locally);
- Heroic Epic <- Barracks (local);
- National Epic <- Library (local);
- Wall Street <- Bank (4 empire-wide; Bank also required locally);
- Iron Works <- Forge (3 empire-wide; Forge also required locally).

For the empire-wide cases, the later `iHighestValue` loop can likewise choose a city whose national-
wonder slots are already full as the supposedly best future location. Its impossible target value can
then inflate the prerequisite building's value empire-wide. The Heroic-Epic local fixture is cleaner
because no competing target-city selection is needed.

Oxford University is NOT used as the current SAS witness: SAS has changed Oxford from a national
wonder to a world wonder. This data cross-check avoids blindly carrying K-Mod's historical example
into the modified SAS ruleset.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod practical 549 / `4defd11f3c...` introduced the local prerequisite-building value boost,
explicitly describing examples such as a prerequisite building gaining value because it enables a
later building. The code used permissive constructibility while assessing the future target.

By practical 556 / `0a31ba2ac1...`, K-Mod added the explicit comment beside this logic:

    "the above call to canConstruct will return true even if the city already has the
     maximum number of national wonders. This is a minor flaw in the AI."

AdvCiv retained the model and later added a second explanatory comment at the target-city
`bVisible=true` call. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the behavior.

DEDUP / ROOT SEPARATION
-----------------------
F547 is distinct from:

- F498: stale construction-value CACHE reuse after mutable same-turn state changes. F547 produces the
  wrong fresh value even with every cache cleared.
- F533: a lost `bHaveEnough=false` assignment in Culture-victory prerequisite-count logic. F547 is a
  constructibility-domain omission in the general prerequisite-unlock valuation.
- ordinary national-wonder placement heuristics: F547 occurs while valuing the prerequisite building,
  before the future national wonder is actually selected for construction.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
The prerequisite-building count itself must remain ignored while evaluating a future target; simply
changing every `bTestVisible=true` call to a full `canConstruct()` would incorrectly reject exactly the
future building whose missing prerequisite is being valued.

Instead, preserve the intentional prerequisite look-ahead while separately enforcing constraints that
cannot be solved by building `eBuilding`, especially the target city's exhausted national-wonder
slots. For example, exclude a national-wonder target city when `isNationalWondersMaxed()` is true,
while still using the visible-only construction test for prerequisite-building availability.

The local prerequisite branch needs the same city-level impossible-target filter before adding its
future-building value.
