------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F548 / KI#871 - AI_countOwnedBonuses completely misses owned city-radius land resources
                 on a different CvArea from their working city
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED -- inherited K-Mod/BBAI city-radius resource-count omission retained by
Base AdvCiv and current SAS. One physical owned land resource can disappear from the
AI's literal owned-resource count solely because the resource is in a different land
CvArea while still lying inside and belonging to a city's workable radius.

ROOT
----
Current `CvPlayerAI::AI_countOwnedBonuses` divides the map into two counting paths.

First it counts owned resources OUTSIDE every city radius:

    if (kPlot.getOwner() == getID() && !kPlot.isCityRadius() &&
        kPlot.getBonusType(getTeam()) == eBonus)
    {
        iCount++;
    }

Then resources inside city radii are obtained through each city's
`AI_countNumBonuses` (plus the current SAS plot-unique neutral anticipation added for
F343/KI#666).

For an owned city-radius resource, `AI_countNumBonuses` begins with this geographic
filter:

    if (!((bLand && isArea(kPlot.getArea())) ||
        (bWater && kPlot.isWater())))
    {
        continue;
    }

The default player-level call requests both land and water, but `bLand` means
"land in THIS CITY'S CvArea", not "any land plot in this city's workable radius".
Therefore an owned land plot in a separate land area is rejected before the normal:

    kPlot.getOwner() == eOwner && kPlot.getWorkingCity() == this

owned-resource branch can count it.

The plot then cannot be recovered by the player-level whole-map pass because the plot
is still `isCityRadius() == true`.

Thus the two halves form an actual gap:

    owned + city radius + land + different CvArea
        -> skipped by outside-radius map pass
        -> skipped by city helper's same-area filter
        -> counted nowhere

CITY / PLOT CONTRACT PROOF
--------------------------
This is not an impossible map state.

`CvCity::canWork(CvPlot const&)` has no same-land-area requirement. Once the plot's
working city is this city, it checks siege, water-working/blockade rules for water,
and whether the plot has yield; it does not reject a land plot merely because
`kPlot.getArea()` differs from `getArea()`.

Likewise, `CvPlot::defaultWorkingCity()` chooses among `NearbyCityIter` cities owned by
the plot owner according to city-plot priority; it contains no same-area filter.

Finally, `CvPlot::setPlotCity()` establishes the city-radius flag by iterating every
`CityPlotIter` plot and incrementing `changeCityRadiusCount(1)`, again without any
area restriction.

So a mainland city can legitimately own and work a land resource on a nearby island
inside its BFC while that island remains a distinct land CvArea.

CLEAN CURRENT-SAS SHIPPED-DATA FIXTURE - URANIUM / FISSION
----------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS supplies a particularly clean tech-value witness:

    BONUS_URANIUM
        TechReveal    = TECH_RADIO
        TechCityTrade = TECH_FISSION
        iMinAreaSize  = 3

and current `TECH_FISSION` has `TECH_RADIO` as a prerequisite.

Construct an ordinary geometry:

1. An AI owns a mainland coastal city.
2. A separate land island of at least three tiles lies partly inside that city's
   workable radius (for example across a one-tile water gap), so it is a distinct
   land CvArea while satisfying Uranium's normal minimum-area placement rule.
3. The city's culture owns the island Uranium tile and the plot's working city is the
   mainland city.
4. This is the AI's only Uranium.
5. The AI has Radio and is evaluating Fission.

The Uranium is already revealed and physically owned.

Correct physical count:

    AI_countOwnedBonuses(BONUS_URANIUM) = 1

Current count:

    whole-map path: skipped because kPlot.isCityRadius()
    city path:      skipped because !isArea(kPlot.getArea()) and !kPlot.isWater()
    result:         0

`CvPlayerAI::AI_techValue` explicitly treats the helper as the owned physical count.
For a revealed resource whose `TechCityTrade` is the tech under evaluation it does:

    int iOwned = AI_countOwnedBonuses(eLoopBonus, 2);
    if (iOwned > 0)
    {
        int iEnableValue = 4;
        iEnableValue += AI_bonusVal(eLoopBonus, 1, true) * iCityCount;
        iEnableValue *= (iOwned > 1) ? 120 : 100;
        iEnableValue /= 100;
        iValue += iEnableValue;
    }

With the off-area city-radius Uranium, current code takes `iOwned == 0` and awards no
Uranium-enabling value to Fission. A correct count of 1 enters the branch and adds the
full one-copy enabling value.

This can therefore change research ranking; it is not merely a reporting/count API
blemish.

ADDITIONAL LIVE CONSEQUENCES
----------------------------
The same helper is used as literal resource multiplicity by global corporation value.
Current corporations consume land resources including Iron, Copper, Stone, Marble,
Aluminum, Coal and Uranium. An owned off-area city-radius copy of one of those
resources is omitted from `AI_corporationValue(..., pCity == NULL)`, changing the
estimated corporation yield/commerce and maintenance.

The Fission fixture is sufficient by itself; the corporation path just confirms that
this helper's contract truly is physical owned-resource multiplicity.

ANCESTRY
--------
Vanilla BtS, as reconstructed by current Civ4CE, does NOT have this omission in
`CvPlayer::countOwnedBonuses`: it simply scans every map plot and counts every owned
plot with the requested bonus, regardless of city radius or land area.

The earliest reachable K-Mod source already contains the changed architecture. K-Mod
practical 3 / `2414225e64...` is the initial K-Mod commit; its
`CvPlayer::countOwnedBonuses` counts owned bonuses outside city radii and delegates
inside-radius/easily-claimed bonuses to `CvCityAI::AI_countNumBonuses`.
The same initial K-Mod `AI_countNumBonuses` admits only:

    pLoopPlot->area() == area()
        OR (bWater && pLoopPlot->isWater())

so different-land-area BFC resources are already omitted there. The exact pre-K-Mod
origin may lie in the Better BTS AI baseline imported by that initial tree; the
reachable history establishes the defect from K-Mod's first commit onward.

AdvCiv practical 1618 / `0de04b1e45...` later moved `countOwnedBonuses` into
`CvPlayerAI` under `advc.042` explicitly "w/o functional changes". Base AdvCiv retains
the same city helper filter (with later `bLand` cleanup), including the source TODO:

    advc.040 (tbd.): Param for including resources in different land areas?

Current SAS retains that filter. The later F343/KI#666 repair makes neutral
city-radius anticipation plot-unique but intentionally leaves the owned geographic
filter untouched, so F548 remains present in the supplied source.

DEDUP / ROOT SEPARATION
-----------------------
F548 is distinct from F343/KI#666 even though both reach
`AI_countOwnedBonuses`:

- F343 OVERCOUNTS one UNOWNED neutral physical resource once per overlapping city
  radius. Its repair deduplicates neutral plots at player scope.
- F548 UNDERCOUNTS one already-OWNED land resource to zero when it is inside a city
  radius but belongs to a different land CvArea.

They have opposite count errors, different eligibility predicates, different fixtures,
and different minimum repairs. F343's current visited-neutral-plot set does nothing
for F548's already-owned island tile.

F548 also does not depend on Worker pathing or `AI_countNumImprovableBonuses`; the
clean Fission consequence is a player-level resource-count / tech-value error even if
no Worker ever attempts to improve the island.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Do not blindly remove the same-area restriction from `AI_countNumBonuses` globally.
Some city-local callers use the helper for Worker/production heuristics where land-area
reachability can be intentional.

For `AI_countOwnedBonuses`, owned physical resources should instead be counted at
player scope independently of the city-local Worker geography. The robust structure is:

1. Count every REVEALED owned physical bonus plot exactly once map-wide, regardless of
   city-radius or land-area membership.
2. Separately add the existing "easily claimed" neutral city-radius anticipation,
   with the F343 plot-unique guard so one neutral physical plot is added at most once.
3. Preserve the current Advanced Start special handling / early cap (`iMaxCount`) as
   appropriate.

That simultaneously matches the helper's "actual count" consumers and avoids forcing
city-local Worker heuristics to treat transport-separated island land as locally
reachable.

POST-F548 CONTROLS / CONTINUATION
---------------------------------
The neighboring `AI_countNumImprovableBonuses` same-area filter has NOT been promoted
as a second defect. Its callers are Worker-production / local-improvement heuristics,
where excluding a land resource on another CvArea can be deliberate because an
ordinary local land Worker cannot walk there. F548 relies only on the physical owned-
resource contract, where the area exclusion is demonstrably wrong.

F549 / KI#872 - SAS AI_bestUnit war-mode boolean makes the defense branch unreachable
in every ordinary real war, so even when the enemy exceeds the configured strong-power
threshold the generic unit picker takes offense mode first and can zero dedicated city
defender roles.

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED in current supplied AdvCiv-SAS source.
SAS-specific; introduced by SAS practical 4932 / `6a226d0fba...`.
Current source untouched.

ROOT
----
Current `CvCityAI::AI_bestUnit()` computes:

    bool const bAnyRealWar = (kTeam.getNumWars(false, true) > 0);
    bool const bAnyPlannedWar = kTeam.AI_isAnyChosenWar();
    int const iEnemyPowerPercent = kTeam.AI_getEnemyPowerPercent(true);

    bool const bDefenseMode = (((iEnemyPowerPercent >= iDefenseModeThreshold) ||
            bAnyPlannedWar || bAnyRealWar || bDanger || bDefense) &&
            !bPeaceAloneLikely);

    bool const bOffenseMode = (((bAnyRealWar &&
            iEnemyPowerPercent <= iOffenseModeThreshold) ||
            bWarPlan || bAnyPlannedWar || bAnyRealWar || bAssault ||
            (!bDefense && bLandWar)) && !bPeaceAloneLikely);

and then chooses the strategy with:

    if (bOffenseMode)
    {
        ...
        aiUnitAIVal[UNITAI_CITY_DEFENSE] = 0;
        aiUnitAIVal[UNITAI_CITY_SPECIAL] = 0;
    }
    else if (bDefenseMode)
    {
        ... strongly increases CITY_DEFENSE / CITY_SPECIAL / RESERVE ...
    }

The `|| bAnyRealWar` near the end of `bOffenseMode` makes the earlier

    (bAnyRealWar && iEnemyPowerPercent <= iOffenseModeThreshold)

power comparison irrelevant in every real war. The same real-war term also makes
`bDefenseMode` true, but offense is tested first, so the defense branch cannot run.

CURRENT SHIPPED-DATA FIXTURE
----------------------------
Current XML defaults are:

    SAS_ENEMY_STRONG_POWER_THRESHOLD = 120
    SAS_ENEMY_WEAK_POWER_THRESHOLD   = 80

Take an ordinary land war in a non-isolated area (`bPeaceAloneLikely == false`) with
current enemy-power percentage 150.

The intended threshold classification is unambiguous:

    150 >= 120  -> defense threshold crossed
    150 <= 80   -> false; enemy is not weak

Current booleans nevertheless become:

    bDefenseMode = true
        because 150 >= 120 (and independently because bAnyRealWar == true)

    bOffenseMode = true
        because the later unconditional `|| bAnyRealWar` is true

Control flow therefore enters offense mode and never reaches defense mode.

That is not a soft score tie. The offense block explicitly removes the two most
city-anchored defensive roles from the generic choice:

    aiUnitAIVal[UNITAI_CITY_DEFENSE] = 0;
    aiUnitAIVal[UNITAI_CITY_SPECIAL] = 0;

whereas the defense block multiplies those roles heavily (with exact factors depending
on the current map branch) and also boosts reserve defense. Thus the losing/strong-
enemy state can select the exact opposite role policy from the one the two configured
thresholds and comments describe.

The generic picker is live AI production. `AI_chooseProduction()` reaches
`AI_chooseUnit()` with the default `NO_UNITAI` in its generic military-production gate
(and again in the final-war fallback); that path calls `AI_bestUnit()` and consumes
these role weights. This is therefore not dead diagnostic code.

WHY THIS IS A BOOLEAN BUG, NOT JUST A TUNING DISAGREEMENT
---------------------------------------------------------
The source itself establishes two distinct intended modes and exposes separate strong
and weak power thresholds. The current expression contains the algebraically redundant
shape:

    (realWar && enemyWeak) || ... || realWar

so `enemyWeak` cannot influence the result whenever `realWar` is true. The birth
comments explicitly notice the `(a && b) || a` redundancy, but retain it after trying
to avoid the different mistake of testing `enemyPower <= threshold` unguarded in
peacetime, where enemy power may read as zero.

The correct way to avoid the peacetime-zero problem is to keep the real-war/planned-
war guard around the weak-power comparison, not to re-add unconditional real war as a
second OR term that erases the comparison.

The branch ordering makes the contradiction observable: both modes being true would
still be ambiguous if they only contributed independent soft bonuses, but here
`if (bOffenseMode) ... else if (bDefenseMode)` gives offense absolute precedence.

ANCESTRY
--------
SAS practical 4932 / `6a226d0fba4af5688d6c9d69a5390e132c3aef8b`, title beginning
"UNITAI AI preference changes, settler slow growth AI policy...", introduced the
custom offense/defense mode block into `AI_bestUnit()` with hard-coded thresholds 130
and 70.

Its own source comment says, in substance, that `(a & b) || a` is redundant. The
commit changed the peacetime weak-power attempt from an unguarded check to:

    (bAnyRealWar && iEnemyPowerPercent <= 70)

but left another independent `|| bAnyRealWar` later in the same OR expression. Thus
the intended guard was added while the old unconditional real-war trigger remained and
made the new threshold test ineffective.

SAS practical 5072 / `6b42984519...` later parameterized the two values into
`SAS_ENEMY_STRONG_POWER_THRESHOLD` and `SAS_ENEMY_WEAK_POWER_THRESHOLD` (current
defaults 120/80), but retained the unconditional real-war term. The current source
still has that exact structure.

The neighboring settler gate also computes these booleans, but there both defense and
offense ultimately block Settlers, so the clean F549 consequence is the later
`AI_bestUnit()` role-selection branch where the two modes deliberately have opposite
unit-role effects.

DEDUP / CONTROLS
----------------
- Not a Base AdvCiv/K-Mod inherited role-weight issue: the entire offense/defense
  threshold layer is SAS-specific.
- Not a stale enemy-power/cache root: the fixture accepts the current returned value
  (150) as correct and shows that the boolean discards its classification.
- Not a UnitAI-domain mismatch. A separate XML/domain audit found the only mixed-domain
  allowed role is `UNIT_TACTICAL_NUKE` (DOMAIN_AIR with UNITAI_ICBM), and
  `AI_bestUnit()` explicitly special-cases UNITAI_ICBM into a global count, so that
  does not cause this defect.
- Not the deliberate generic-Settler suppression: current SAS intentionally routes
  Settler decisions through explicit production logic and zeroes the generic Settler
  role.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Preserve the intended distinction explicitly rather than allowing both booleans to be
true and relying on branch order. For example, define the strategic context first and
then make weak/strong enemy power select between offense and defense only when the
power value is meaningful.

At minimum, the unconditional `|| bAnyRealWar` must not remain in `bOffenseMode` after
`(bAnyRealWar && iEnemyPowerPercent <= iOffenseModeThreshold)` if the weak threshold is
supposed to discriminate real-war offense from real-war defense.

Also review the independent `bWarPlan` / `bAnyPlannedWar` terms: `AI_isFocusWar()` can
be true for defensive-war contexts too, so a robust repair should state precedence
explicitly (e.g. strong/danger/defensive posture wins defense; weak/attack posture wins
offense) rather than merely deleting one redundant term and leaving another broad war
predicate to override the same distinction.

POST-F549 CONTROLS / CONTINUATION
---------------------------------
The first `AI_bestUnit()` contract pass also checked domain accounting. Current XML
has one legal mixed-domain UnitAI:

    UNIT_TACTICAL_NUKE: DOMAIN_AIR, UNITAI_ICBM

while `AI_unitAIDomainType(UNITAI_ICBM)` returns DOMAIN_IMMOBILE. In this particular
function that is safe because UNITAI_ICBM is explicitly grouped with DOMAIN_AIR for
existing-role subtraction and uses the global `AI_totalUnitAIs` count.

The large `AI_bestUnitAI()` SAS delta mainly disables the old `bGrowMore` food-
production veto because Settler policy was moved to parent production logic; no
separate hard contract failure has been promoted from that change in this tranche.

-------------------------------

32/169 unique files complete.

C031-WIP324 APPEND - F550 / KI#873 CONFIRMED
================================================================================

F550 / KI#873 - SAS AI_bestUnit treats a land area's local isolation as probable peace
even during a known real overseas war, disabling the entire custom offense/defense
war-mode layer on the island/naval maps whose branches explicitly try to tune naval
war production.

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED in current supplied AdvCiv-SAS source.
SAS-specific; same practical-4932 custom war-mode introduction as F549, but a separate
boolean gate with an independent repair and witness.
Current source untouched.

ROOT
----
Current `CvCityAI::AI_bestUnit()` computes:

    bool const bAreaAlone = kOwner.AI_isAreaAlone(getArea());
    int const iHasMetCount = kTeam.getHasMetCivCount(true);
    ...
    bool const bAnyRealWar = (kTeam.getNumWars(false, true) > 0);
    bool const bAnyPlannedWar = kTeam.AI_isAnyChosenWar();
    bool const bPeaceAloneLikely = (bAreaAlone || iHasMetCount <= 0);

and both strategy modes are finally gated by:

    ... && !bPeaceAloneLikely

`AI_isAreaAlone()` does NOT mean "no active enemy" or "peace likely". Outside its
Ancient/start-era visibility precaution, it returns whether the land CvArea's
non-Barbarian city count is entirely accounted for by our team:

    (kArea.getNumCities() - barbarianCitiesInArea) == ourTeamCitiesInArea

Thus an island containing only our cities is "alone" even when our team is currently
at war with a known civilization on another island.

CURRENT LIVE FIXTURE
--------------------
Use a normal post-start-era Archipelago/island state:

1. Player A owns one or more cities on island LandArea A.
2. No non-Barbarian foreign city exists on LandArea A.
3. Player B owns cities on a different land area across the sea.
4. A and B have met and are currently at real war.
5. A's city is coastal and the map is recognized by the current SAS naval-heavy map
   cache.

For A's city:

    bAreaAlone      = true
    iHasMetCount     > 0
    bAnyRealWar     = true
    bPeaceAloneLikely = true || false = true

Consequently:

    bDefenseMode = (... && !true) = false
    bOffenseMode = (... && !true) = false

The current war mode is therefore skipped entirely despite the known real war.

This is particularly contradictory to the code's own structure because immediately
inside those modes SAS has explicit `bNavalHeavyMapname` branches that adjust:

    UNITAI_ATTACK_SEA
    UNITAI_RESERVE_SEA
    UNITAI_ESCORT_SEA
    UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA
    UNITAI_SETTLER_SEA
    UNITAI_MISSIONARY_SEA
    UNITAI_SPY_SEA
    UNITAI_MISSILE_CARRIER_SEA

and related land/offense/defense roles specifically for naval-heavy wartime strategy.
On the archetypal separate-island naval war, the local-area-alone gate prevents those
branches from running at all.

LIVE CONSUMER
-------------
As established for F549, `AI_chooseProduction()` has generic military-production paths
that call `AI_chooseUnit()` with default `NO_UNITAI`; this invokes `AI_bestUnit()` and
uses these role values to select the concrete unit role. The suppressed mode therefore
changes live AI production selection rather than merely a diagnostic label.

WHY THIS IS INDEPENDENT FROM F549
---------------------------------
F549 and F550 occur in the same SAS strategy block but are logically independent:

- F549: during an ordinary non-isolated real war, `bOffenseMode` contains an
  unconditional `|| bAnyRealWar`, so offense wins over defense regardless of the weak/
  strong power thresholds.

- F550: during an overseas war where the city's LAND AREA is locally alone,
  `bPeaceAloneLikely` disables BOTH modes before their offense-vs-defense precedence is
  reached.

Fixing F549's redundant real-war OR still leaves the overseas war with both modes
false. Fixing F550's peace/isolation gate still leaves F549's losing land war choosing
offense. The fixtures and minimum repairs therefore do not collapse into one root.

ANCESTRY
--------
SAS practical 4932 / `6a226d0fba4af5688d6c9d69a5390e132c3aef8b` introduced the
custom `AI_bestUnit()` war-mode layer with:

    bPeaceAloneLikely = (bAreaAlone || iHasMetCount <= 0)

and gated both offense and defense by `!bPeaceAloneLikely` from birth.

Later threshold/map-name refactors retained that gate. Current SAS still contains the
same logic.

`AI_isAreaAlone()` itself is inherited AdvCiv/K-Mod logic and its local-land-area
contract is coherent. The bug is SAS interpreting that local geography predicate as a
peace predicate after it already has authoritative real/planned-war state in hand.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Do not change `AI_isAreaAlone()` globally; its meaning is valid for its other callers.
Fix the SAS war-mode gate instead.

At minimum, local area isolation must not suppress the strategy when a real/planned war
already establishes that peace is not merely "likely". For example, derive the peace
heuristic only outside active/selected war context:

    bPeaceAloneLikely = !bAnyRealWar && !bAnyPlannedWar &&
                        (bAreaAlone || iHasMetCount <= 0);

Then reconcile this with F549's separate offense/defense precedence so strong enemy
power / defensive posture can select defense and weak enemy power / offensive posture

F551 / KI#874 CONFIRMED
-----------------------
SAS temporary "force one Artist until BFC" logic never releases the forced Artist for
AI cities, so a temporary emergency assignment can become permanent.

CURRENT CODE / INTENT
---------------------
SAS practical 5067 / commit 8a12b125dd634ab11ab5535fccddb39c451ac9d2
introduced the feature under the explicit title:

    "Force one artist if we don't have BFC and city culture per turn is low, until we do"

Current GlobalDefines_advciv_sas.xml enables it by default:

    SAS_DO_TURN_FORCE_ARTIST_IF_NO_BFC_AND_LOW_CULTURE = 1
    SAS_DO_TURN_FORCE_ARTIST_FOR_BFC_MIN_NO_CULTURE_PER_TURN_THRESHOLD = 3
    SAS_DO_TURN_FORCE_ARTIST_MIN_NO_CULTURE_LEVEL_THRESHOLD = 2

In CvCity::doTurn(), the AI branch does roughly:

    if (cultureLevel < 2 && culturePerTurn <= 3)
    {
        if (forcedArtists < 1 && isSpecialistValid(Artist, 1))
            changeForceSpecialistCount(Artist, +1);
    }
    // else: comment says AI_jobChangeValue can handle unassignment

There is no corresponding AI-side decrement after the BFC is reached.

The whole current CvGameCoreDLL mutation inventory confirms that the only explicit
Artist-force decrement in this helper is in the HUMAN-convenience branch. Generic
setForceSpecialistCount calls can sanitize an invalid forced target or clear forced
specialists when citizen automation is manually disabled, but they do not release a
still-valid AI Artist merely because the BFC purpose has ended.

WHY AI_jobChangeValue CANNOT RELEASE IT
---------------------------------------
The source comment saying AI_jobChangeValue can handle unassignment is incorrect for a
forced specialist.

AI_assignWorkingPlots treats force counts as hard targets:

    if (getSpecialistCount(e) < getForceSpecialistCount(e))
        setSpecialistCount(e, getForceSpecialistCount(e));

AI_removeWorstCitizen normally skips a specialist when:

    getSpecialistCount(e) <= getForceSpecialistCount(e)

and AI_juggleCitizens only puts a worked specialist into the removable worked-job set
when:

    getSpecialistCount(e) > getForceSpecialistCount(e)

Thus exactly one forced Artist is deliberately protected from ordinary job-value
reassignment. AI_jobChangeValue may value another job more highly, but it does not own
or decrement m_aiForceSpecialistCount and cannot make that protected Artist removable.

CURRENT SHIPPED FIXTURE
-----------------------
Use an ordinary AI running CIVIC_CASTE_SYSTEM (TECH_CODE_OF_LAWS). Current civic XML
makes Artist, Scientist and Merchant specialists unlimited/valid under Caste System.

1. The AI founds or captures a young city with culture level below 2 and culture/turn
   <= 3.
2. Artist is legally assignable because Caste System makes SPECIALIST_ARTIST valid.
3. CvCity::doTurn raises the forced Artist target from 0 to 1.
4. AI citizen assignment subsequently ensures one Artist is actually assigned.
5. On Normal speed, CULTURELEVEL_FLEDGLING (the BFC expansion threshold) is 10 culture;
   the Artist supplies the intended fast culture and the city reaches the BFC.
6. Once culture level is >= 2, the force-creation branch simply stops executing. It
   does NOT decrement forced Artist count.
7. While Caste System remains active (or the city later has an Artist slot), Artist
   remains valid, so KI#70's invalid-target sanitizer correctly does nothing.
8. Normal AI assignment/juggling continues protecting the forced Artist indefinitely,
   even though the emergency BFC objective has already been satisfied.

The consequence is persistent citizen misallocation: one population remains locked to
Artist instead of returning to the normal plot/specialist optimizer. This can reduce
food, production or other commerce and can persist for many turns or effectively the
rest of the city's life while Artist validity remains.

ANCESTRY / POSITIVE CONTROL
---------------------------
This is SAS-specific; Base AdvCiv/K-Mod do not contain the SAS BFC-Artist helper.

The later human-convenience history is especially strong evidence that forced counts do
need explicit release. Practical 5128 / commit 9d5a1a113d22683ac03a34654a30262c6876b094
is explicitly titled:

    "auto unassign the forced artist after we have BFC for the convenience human player part of the code"

and adds changeForceSpecialistCount(Artist, -1) after the human BFC condition ends.
The AI branch is left with the comment that AI_jobChangeValue should handle its
unassignment; as proved above, forced-specialist protection prevents that.

DEDUP / ROOT BOUNDARY
---------------------
Keep F551 separate from:

- KI#70: invalid forced-specialist target/capacity sanitation. F551's Artist remains
  legally valid; the defect is failure to release a no-longer-needed valid target.
- KI#313: provenance/ownership of the HUMAN convenience helper's automatic forced
  Artist. F551 concerns AI cities, where there is no manual-human provenance conflict.
- WIP285-WIP286 citizen-juggle controls: those correctly preserve forced specialists;
  that correct behavior is what makes F551 persistent once the force target is stale.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
The AI BFC helper needs explicit ownership/lifetime handling just like the corrected
human helper, but without confusing an unrelated pre-existing force with the helper's
own increment.

Safest direction:
1. record whether the AI BFC helper itself added the +1 Artist target (provenance), or
   otherwise use a narrowly scoped AI-only state that cannot steal another system's
   forced Artist;
2. once getCultureLevel() reaches the configured BFC threshold, decrement exactly the
   helper-owned force once;
3. keep KI#70's independent invalid-target sanitizer intact;
4. mark citizen assignment dirty through the existing force-count setter so the now
   unforced Artist can be re-evaluated normally.

F552 / provisional KI#875 remains UNUSED.

F552 / KI#875 CONFIRMED
-----------------------
`AI_chooseProduction()` treats any positive-combat unit currently in production as the city's
missing defender, so an undefended coastal city can keep building a combat ship instead of
reconsidering production for a real land garrison.

ROOT
----
At the top of current `CvCityAI::AI_chooseProduction()`, when a city already has production
invested, the AI normally gets an opportunity to abandon the current order and choose something
more appropriate. One emergency retention rule says:

    // if building a combat unit, and we have no defenders, keep building it
    UnitTypes eProductionUnit = getProductionUnit();
    if (eProductionUnit != NO_UNIT)
    {
        if (getPlot().getNumDefenders(getOwner()) == 0)
        {
            if (GC.getInfo(eProductionUnit).getCombat() > 0)
                return;
        }
    }

The comment and surrounding control flow clearly mean that, with zero city defenders, a combat
unit already being produced should be preserved because it can become the urgently needed
city defender.

`CvUnitInfo::getCombat() > 0`, however, does not establish that the unit can defend a LAND city.
It is true for ordinary naval combat units as well.

CURRENT SHIPPED WITNESS
-----------------------
Current SAS `CIV4UnitInfos.xml` defines the ordinary Galley as:

    <Type>UNIT_GALLEY</Type>
    <Combat>UNITCOMBAT_NAVAL</Combat>
    <Domain>DOMAIN_SEA</Domain>
    <DefaultUnitAI>UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA</DefaultUnitAI>
    ...
    <iCombat>2</iCombat>

So a Galley satisfies the retention test despite being a sea-domain unit.

Use an ordinary coastal AI city with:

    current land/city defenders = 0
    current production          = Galley
    invested production         > 0
    production turns left       > 3

and invoke an ordinary production reconsideration (e.g. any of the supported
`setChooseProductionDirty`/AI production-refresh paths). The earlier food-production and <=3-turn
retention exits need not apply.

Current code then evaluates:

    getNumDefenders(owner) == 0     -> true
    Galley.getCombat() > 0          -> true
    return

and therefore keeps the Galley.

Completing that Galley does not create the missing land-city garrison. A coastal city can hold
sea units, but sea-domain naval combat is not a substitute for a land defender against capture.
The exact emergency fact that should make the AI reconsider production is therefore converted
into a reason to preserve an irrelevant order.

The same witness can be built with other positive-combat sea units (Frigate, Destroyer, etc.);
Galley is simply an early, unambiguous shipped example.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE
----------------
This is a hard production-control return, not a soft score. Once the condition fires,
`AI_chooseProduction()` does not clear the current queue and does not reach the normal defender /
military production logic in that reconsideration. The city can spend additional turns on a
ship while remaining without a land defender.

The defect is especially adverse in the state named by the source comment itself: an undefended
city. Danger is not required by this branch and does not repair it.

ANCESTRY
--------
This is inherited, not SAS-specific.

- Stock BtS/Civ4CE contains the same zero-defender + `getCombat() > 0` retention rule.
- The earliest reachable K-Mod snapshot (practical 3 / commit
  `2414225e6415911ac28483d2bdac67b4100d36ff`) already contains the same rule.
- K-Mod practical 489 later performs only declaration/style cleanup around it.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the condition unchanged semantically.

Thus this is a BtS-era city-production contract defect surviving through K-Mod, AdvCiv and SAS.

DEDUP / ROOT BOUNDARY
---------------------
Keep F552 separate from F545/KI#868.

F545 also found a naval-vs-land mismatch involving a unit finishing production, but that root is
inside `AI_updateSafety()` and corrupts the cached `CITYSAFETY_*` forecast. F552 requires no
safety-cache involvement at all: it is a direct early return inside production selection that
keeps an unsuitable current order.

Fixing F545's safety predictor leaves this `AI_chooseProduction()` return unchanged. Fixing this
retention test leaves F545's safety classification unchanged. They are independent producers,
consumers and repair sites.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
The retention condition should ask whether the produced unit can actually serve as the missing
city defender, rather than using generic positive combat strength.

At minimum, require a land-domain combat defender (and preserve any relevant special-unit rules),
e.g. conceptually gate the emergency retention on `DOMAIN_LAND` plus positive combat/defender
eligibility. Prefer mirroring the same defender eligibility contract that `getNumDefenders` is
intended to represent rather than inventing a second approximation.

Do not globally reject naval production in undefended cities; the bug is only that the existing
"this current unit will solve zero defenders" early return treats naval combat as proof.

POST-WIP327 CONTROL - MILITARY INSTRUCTOR / HEROIC EPIC ANTICIPATORY VALUE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
The unfinished `AI_permanentSpecialistValue()` state check closes as intentional policy,
not F553.

SAS gives a Military Instructor extra value in a top production city when the city either
already has the configured Heroic-Epic-effect building or is currently constructing it:

    bHasHeroicEffectBuilding = (getNumBuilding(eHeroicEffectBuilding) > 0)
    bBuildingHeroicEffectBuilding = (getProductionBuilding() == eHeroicEffectBuilding)

This initially looked vulnerable to a cancelled Heroic Epic leaving a Great General headed
toward a no-longer-preferred city. The live Great-General producer does not freeze that score,
however. `CvUnitAI::AI_join()` scans candidate cities and calls
`AI_permanentSpecialistValue()` again on subsequent AI turns while the unit is moving. If the
Heroic Epic is cancelled, the anticipatory extra disappears at the next evaluation and the
best join city can change; if the building completes, `getNumBuilding()` preserves the intended
bonus. No hard stale-state lifetime was established.

F553 / KI#876 - SAS city-local focus-war callers were changed from the current city's land
area to the CAPITAL'S land area by replacing `AI_isFocusWar(area())` with the no-argument
`AI_isFocusWar()` under the mistaken assumption that the latter is a broader check
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED in current supplied AdvCiv-SAS source.
SAS-specific caller-scope regression introduced in practical commit 4957 /
`fe58e134631681ba9e79e481dd29a761b8820696`.
Independent of F344/KI#667, F549/KI#872 and F550/KI#873.
Current source untouched.

ROOT / API CONTRACT
-------------------
`CvPlayerAI::AI_isFocusWar` has an optional area parameter:

    bool AI_isFocusWar(CvArea const* pArea = NULL) const;

The implementation does NOT interpret NULL as "all areas", "empire-wide", or a larger
war-focus scope. It explicitly substitutes the capital's land area:

    if (pArea == NULL)
        pArea = getCapital()->area();

The function then uses that selected area's AreaAI state. In particular, for a war that is not
one of the team's chosen wars:

    if (!kOurTeam.AI_isAnyChosenWar() &&
        pArea->getAreaAIType(getTeam()) != AREAAI_DEFENSIVE)
    {
        return false;
    }

Therefore these two calls are genuinely different for a multi-landmass empire:

    AI_isFocusWar(area())  // this city's land area
    AI_isFocusWar()        // capital's land area

The current SAS comments that motivated the change say the no-argument form is the "larger
one" and might "handle more cases". That premise is false under the actual API contract: it is
a default-to-capital-area overload, not a union/global query.

INTRODUCTION / ANCESTRY
-----------------------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 deliberately uses the current city's area in its city-local consumers,
including:

    CvCityAI::AI_bestUnit:      AI_isFocusWar(area())
    CvCityAI::AI_buildingValue: AI_isFocusWar(area())

SAS practical 4957 changed four existing city-local reads from `AI_isFocusWar(area())` to the
no-argument form, including the inherited `AI_bestUnit()` and `AI_buildingValue()` calls, and
also introduced the same no-argument interpretation in the centralized concrete
`AI_chooseUnit()` production gates.

The 4957 diff contains the mistaken rationale beside the changes:

    "sometimes AI_isFocusWar is used with, sometimes without in cvcityai.cpp,
     going for the larger one ... maybe we handle more cases this way"

Current SAS retains those calls and comments. The underlying `AI_isFocusWar` implementation
still defaults NULL to `getCapital()->area()`, just as Base AdvCiv does.

SUPPORTED LIVE DIVERGENCE
-------------------------
Use an AI with two disconnected land areas:

* LandArea A contains the capital and is not `AREAAI_DEFENSIVE`.
* LandArea B contains another AI city and is `AREAAI_DEFENSIVE`.
* The team is in a reactive/non-chosen real war (e.g. an attacked war), so
  `AI_isAnyChosenWar()` is false.
* The hostile war-plan team is not a pushover.
* The AI is not globally forced true by `AI_STRATEGY_ALERT2`.

For the city on LandArea B:

    AI_isFocusWar(area())

passes the defensive-area gate and reaches the live enemy-war-plan loop; the non-pushover
enemy makes it return true.

But current SAS calls:

    AI_isFocusWar()

which substitutes LandArea A. Since no chosen war exists and the capital area is not defensive,
the function returns false immediately before considering the enemy loop.

So the same city and same game state produce opposite focus-war classifications solely because
SAS silently changed the queried CvArea from the city to the capital.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE 1 - BUILDING VALUE
-----------------------------------
Current `AI_buildingValue()` now reads:

    bool const bWarPlan = kOwner.AI_isFocusWar();

Base AdvCiv reads the city's area. This value reaches inherited quantitative valuation. For
free-experience buildings, for example:

    int iWeight = 12;
    ...
    iWeight /= (bWarPlan || (bHighProductionCity && ... ) ? 1 : 4);

In a met-rival, non-top-production city satisfying the fixture above, the correct local focus
war keeps `iWeight` at 12, while current SAS's capital-area false result reduces it to 3. Thus a
frontline secondary-area city's free-XP building value can be quartered during exactly the
local defensive war that `AI_isFocusWar(area())` was designed to detect.

The same wrong `bWarPlan` also feeds SAS hard building pre-rules (Barracks/Stable urgency,
science/gold/culture delays, national-wonder pressure gates, etc.), so the scope change is not
merely diagnostic.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE 2 - CONCRETE SIEGE HARD REJECT
------------------------------------------------
Current centralized `AI_chooseUnit(UnitTypes, UnitAITypes)` also uses the capital-area form:

    bool const bWarPlan = kPlayer.AI_isFocusWar();

With the shipped anti-excess-siege and Trebuchet-like gates enabled, a Trebuchet-like unit starts
with a 20% share cap but is tightened to 15% when `!bWarPlan`:

    int iCapTrebs = 20;
    ...
    if (!bWarPlan)
        iCapTrebs = 15;
    ...
    if (iTrebsShareOff >= iCapTrebs + iTrebuchetsLikeMinExtraCap)
        return false;

Current shipped `SAS_AI_CHOOSE_UNIT_NO_EXCESS_SIEGES = 1`,
`SAS_NO_EXCESS_TREBUCHETS_LIKE = 1`, and
`SAS_AI_CHOOSE_UNIT_NO_EXCESS_SIEGES_TREBUCHETS_LIKE_MIN_EXTRA_CAP = 0`.

Continue the secondary defensive-area fixture with a safe local city, a non-strong enemy,
relevant strategic resources, and a Trebuchet-like share between 15% and 19%. The local
`AI_isFocusWar(area()) == true` reading would retain the 20% cap and can allow the unit; current
SAS obtains false from the peaceful capital area, reduces the cap to 15%, and hard-rejects that
concrete unit. This establishes a direct production branch difference, not only a soft score.

SCOPE / CONTROLS
----------------
Not every no-argument `AI_isFocusWar()` call is wrong. Many `CvPlayerAI` consumers deliberately
ask about the player's default/capital-area strategic focus. Existing Base AdvCiv `CvCityAI`
code also has some no-argument uses where the logic is intentionally player-global. F553 is
specifically the SAS city-local substitutions/new gates whose comments treat the no-argument
form as a broader replacement for `area()`.

One 4957 Settler block is additionally protected by broader `bAnyRealWar` /
`bAnyPlannedWar` terms, so its changed `bWarPlan` can often be redundant. F553 does not require
every edited call site to have an independent symptom; the building-value and concrete-unit
consumers above are sufficient live witnesses of the shared wrong-area root.

DEDUP / ROOT SEPARATION
-----------------------
* F344 / KI#667 fixes the INTERNAL `AI_isFocusWar` state flag for the intended
  multiple-pushover-war exception. F553 assumes the helper itself returns the correct result for
  the CvArea it is given; SAS is giving it the wrong area.
* F549 / KI#872 is the SAS `AI_bestUnit()` offense-mode Boolean where an unconditional real-war
  term defeats the enemy-power discriminator. Restoring the city-area focus-war input does not
  remove that Boolean defect.
* F550 / KI#873 is the later `bPeaceAloneLikely` gate that disables both custom war modes in an
  overseas war. F553 already changes inherited building valuation and the centralized concrete
  unit gate before/without relying on that mode layer.
* This is not an `AI_isAreaAlone` semantics issue and does not require changing
  `AI_isFocusWar` globally.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Restore the explicit current-city area for city-local strategic decisions:

    kOwner.AI_isFocusWar(area())

or equivalently pass `&getArea()` where the signature/context prefers it.

At minimum, restore the Base AdvCiv area-aware calls in `AI_bestUnit()` and
`AI_buildingValue()`, and use the current city area in the SAS concrete `AI_chooseUnit()` gates
whose thresholds are meant to describe that city's local military situation. Review the other
4957 substitutions individually; do not globally replace every no-argument caller because many
player-scope callers intentionally use the default capital-area semantics.

F554 / KI#877 - THE SAS "CITY MAINTENANCE BUILDING" PREFILTER USES THE WRONG SIGN,
SO EVERY CURRENT MAINTENANCE-REDUCING BUILDING BYPASSES THE ENTIRE AUTHORED GATE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED in current supplied AdvCiv-SAS source.
SAS-specific sign inversion introduced with the building-choice prefilter.
Current source untouched.

CURRENT SOURCE
--------------
Inside the regular-building optimization block of `CvCityAI::AI_buildingValue()` SAS says:

    // not 0 (but higher value instead) to exclude false positives like ikhanda ...
    const bool bCityMaintenanceBuilding =
        (kBuilding.getMaintenanceModifier() >= 25);

    if (bCityMaintenanceBuilding)
    {
        if (iMaintenanceTimes100 < iSAS_AI_BUILDING_VALUE_GATE_M100_REGULAR_BUILDINGS)
            return 0;
        else if (bAtWar)
        {
            if (bEnemyStrong)
                return 0;
        }
    }

The comments and downstream branches clearly intend this Boolean to recognize a meaningful
CITY-MAINTENANCE REDUCER, while excluding small incidental reducers such as the Ikhanda.

ENGINE / XML SIGN CONTRACT
--------------------------
Civ4 expresses maintenance reductions as NEGATIVE `iMaintenanceModifier` values. The inherited
K-Mod/AdvCiv valuation in this same function confirms the sign contract when it computes the new
maintenance using:

    100 + getMaintenanceModifier() + kBuilding.getMaintenanceModifier()

and rewards the resulting reduction in `iMaintenanceTimes100`.

Current supplied SAS `CIV4BuildingInfos.xml` contains exactly these nonzero building maintenance
modifiers:

    BUILDING_ZULU_IKHANDA                  -15
    BUILDING_COURTHOUSE                    -50
    BUILDING_AMERICAN_FEDERAL_COURTHOUSE   -60
    BUILDING_HOLY_ROMAN_RATHAUS            -70
    BUILDING_RUSSIAN_PRIKAZ                -50
    BUILDING_VERSAILLES                    -50

There is NO current building with a positive maintenance modifier, let alone `>= +25`.

Therefore:

    kBuilding.getMaintenanceModifier() >= 25

is false for every actual maintenance-reducing building in current SAS.

The comment about excluding Ikhanda makes the intended missing sign particularly clear: a
threshold by reduction magnitude would distinguish `-15` Ikhanda from the `-50/-60/-70`
Courthouse-class reducers, but `>= +25` distinguishes none of them because the sign is reversed.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE
----------------
The whole custom maintenance-building prefilter is dead for current maintenance reducers.
For example, a normal Courthouse has `iMaintenanceModifier = -50`, hence:

    -50 >= 25  -> false

so it never reaches either authored policy:

1. low-maintenance cities should hard-reject the Courthouse-class building until current city
   maintenance reaches `SAS_AI_BUILDING_VALUE_GATE_M100_REGULAR_BUILDINGS` (currently documented
   as the 6-gpt-style threshold); and
2. an AI already at war against a strong enemy should hard-reject that economic investment and
   preserve production for the emergency.

Instead the Courthouse falls through to inherited/general scoring as if this SAS prefilter did
not exist. The same is true for Federal Courthouse, Rathaus and Prikaz. This is not merely a
threshold-tuning disagreement: the condition's sign makes the entire intended category empty
under the shipped data.

A second downstream effect is that `bCityMaintenanceBuilding` participates in
`bPreviousBuildings`, which is intended to mark already-classified regular-building families
before later economic/culture catch-all rules. Because the Boolean is false, true maintenance
reducers also do not receive that category marker. The primary F554 root remains the wrong-sign
classification; any resulting fall-through classification is a sibling consequence.

ANCESTRY
--------
SAS practical 4950 / commit `e7181173b7498ce4f6ae09140991bdfb88c459eb`, titled
"(Seemingly enhanced) Add prefiltering building choices rules to help AI choose more reponsively
and efficiently buildings depending on war context and other...", introduced the condition from
birth as:

    const bool bCityMaintenanceBuilding =
        (kBuilding.getMaintenanceModifier() >= 25);

with the same explicit Ikhanda-exclusion comment and low-maintenance / wartime hard rejects.

Later practicals 4965, 5087, 5088 and 5148 adjusted nearby thresholds, resource checks and define
names but retained the sign. Current source still has the original `>= 25` test.

DEDUP / ROOT BOUNDARY
---------------------
- KI#306 concerns insufficient SAME-TURN INVALIDATION of a government-center/top-production
  ranking cache. F554 has no cache dependency; the relevant branch is never entered even with
  perfectly fresh maintenance state.
- F399 concerns an optional/Alt saved-maintenance hover omitting government-center effects. F554
  is AI production logic and a scalar modifier sign inversion.
- The inherited `AI_buildingValue()` maintenance arithmetic itself uses the negative modifier
  coherently. F554 is confined to SAS's prefilter classifier.
- Treat every maintenance-reducer bypass caused by this Boolean as the same F554 root rather than
  numbering Courthouse/Rathaus/Prikaz separately.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Preserve the apparent authored intent: recognize meaningful maintenance REDUCTIONS while leaving
small incidental reductions such as Ikhanda outside this hard category.

With the current sign convention, the direct repair corresponding to the existing threshold is:

    const bool bCityMaintenanceBuilding =
        (kBuilding.getMaintenanceModifier() <= -25);

A magnitude form can also be used if desired, but it should explicitly require a negative
modifier so a hypothetical future maintenance-increasing building is never classified as a
reducer. After repair, retest whether the current 25-point category threshold and the 6-gpt
maintenance gate are still the desired policy; those numerical choices are tuning, separate from
the sign bug.

F555 / KI#878 - THE FINAL "UNKNOWN / MISC BUILDING" WAR-TAIL IS ATTACHED TO
`!bCultureOnlyBuilding`, SO IT HARD-REJECTS ALMOST EVERY PREVIOUSLY CLASSIFIED
REGULAR BUILDING DURING WAR/DANGER/WAR-PLAN STATES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED in current supplied AdvCiv-SAS source.
SAS-specific control-flow attachment error introduced with the building-choice prefilter.
Current source untouched.

CURRENT SOURCE / CONTROL FLOW
-----------------------------
Near the end of the regular-building prefilter, SAS deliberately accumulates the families
already handled above:

    const bool bPreviousBuildings4 = (
        bPreviousBuildings3 ||
        bEspionageBuilding
    );

It then identifies a PURE culture building only when the building has culture and was NOT
already classified:

    const bool bCultureOnlyBuilding = (
        bCultureBuilding &&
        !bPreviousBuildings4
    );

The culture-specific block is followed by a comment that explicitly describes the next branch
as an UNKNOWN / UNCOVERED BUILDING tail and says that it "doesn't handle previously covered
buildings which should have their own war rules":

    if (bCultureOnlyBuilding)
    {
        ... culture-only policy ...
    }
    // unknown or uncovered building ...
    // this doesn't handle previously covered buildings ...
    else
    {
        if (bAtWar || bEnemyStrong || bDanger)
            return 0;
        else if (bWarPlan)
            return 0;
    }

But that `else` means exactly:

    if (!bCultureOnlyBuilding)

It does NOT mean:

    if (building was not matched by any previous family)

Therefore every regular building that was previously classified but whose own category branch
falls through without an immediate return reaches this "unknown" tail and is hard-rejected
whenever `bAtWar`, `bDanger`, `bEnemyStrong`, or `bWarPlan` is true.

The only broad class that escapes the tail by construction is a PURE culture building, because
that is the one case where `bCultureOnlyBuilding` is true. This is the inverse of the intended
category partition: the supposedly conservative fallback for unknown buildings applies to most
known buildings, while pure culture avoids the fallback entirely.

CLEAN SHIPPED GRANARY FIXTURE
-----------------------------
A normal current Granary has `iFoodKept = 40`, so:

    bFoodKeptBuilding == true

Choose an ordinary AI city where:

- the regular-building optimization define is enabled (current shipped default is 1);
- the AI is at war;
- `bEnemyStrong == false` (enemy power is below the strong threshold);
- happiness is not below the food-kept minimum, so the low-happiness reject does not fire;
- the building is otherwise constructible;
- no earlier unrelated force/reject fires.

The authored food-kept branch explicitly preserves this case:

    else if (bAtWar)
    {
        if (bEnemyStrong)
            return 0;
        // else even if enemy is weak, food kept buildings could be useful to slave or grow ...
        // ... no reason to hard reject here ...
    }

So with `bAtWar == true` and `bEnemyStrong == false`, the Granary is intentionally allowed to
fall through to ordinary valuation.

Later:

    bPreviousBuildings  == true   // because bFoodKeptBuilding
    bPreviousBuildings2 == true
    bPreviousBuildings3 == true
    bPreviousBuildings4 == true
    bCultureOnlyBuilding == false // by definition, already-classified buildings cannot be pure culture

The final bare `else` therefore executes and immediately does:

    if (bAtWar || bEnemyStrong || bDanger)
        return 0;

because `bAtWar` is true.

Thus the exact state that the food-kept branch comments say should NOT be hard-rejected is
hard-rejected a few dozen lines later by a branch documented as applying only to UNKNOWN /
UNCOVERED buildings.

OTHER DIRECT CONSEQUENCES OF THE SAME ROOT
------------------------------------------
Do not number these separately; they are consequences of the same wrong `else` attachment.
Examples include:

- Health buildings: their category rejects at war only when `bEnemyStrong`; a non-strong wartime
  case is meant to fall through, but the final tail converts it to `return 0`.
- Production buildings: after the early-growth rule, wartime rejection is likewise explicitly
  limited to strong-enemy pressure; the tail broadens it to all war states that reach it.
- Happiness buildings: same broadening from "enemy strong" to any `bAtWar` that survives the
  category's own rules.
- Land-unit / naval-unit buildings and other already-classified families can similarly inherit
  the fallback veto whenever their own branch deliberately leaves the decision to ordinary
  valuation.

Science, pure economy, pure trade and pure espionage already contain broad war/danger/war-plan
rejects of their own, so F555 does not claim an additional behavioral difference for states
those branches already return from. The bug is the control-flow overreach into previously
classified categories that deliberately chose NOT to return.

DOCUMENTATION ORACLE
--------------------
Current `README_Known_Issues.md` KI#48 documents the intended prefilter as a partition. Its table
states:

    Unknown / misc | Anything not matched above | If war/danger/enemy strong or war plan -> skip

and separately documents Food-kept, Health, Production and Happiness as rejecting at war only
under their narrower category-specific conditions (notably `enemy strong`).

That documentation exactly matches the source comments and contradicts the live bare-`else`
control flow. F555 therefore does not depend on guessing which wartime policy is preferable: the
code fails to implement the project's own recorded category contract.

SHIPPED ENABLEMENT
------------------
Current `GlobalDefines_advciv_sas.xml` has:

    SAS_AI_BUILDING_VALUE_REGULAR_BUILDINGS_OPTIMIZE = 1

so the faulty prefilter is enabled by default in the supplied tree.

ANCESTRY
--------
SAS practical 4950 / commit `e7181173b7498ce4f6ae09140991bdfb88c459eb`, titled
"(Seemingly enhanced) Add prefiltering building choices rules to help AI choose more reponsively
and efficiently buildings depending on war context and other...", introduced the full category
prefilter.

The birth diff already contains:

    bPreviousBuildings4
    bCultureOnlyBuilding = bCultureBuilding && !bPreviousBuildings4
    if (bCultureOnlyBuilding) { ... }
    // unknown or/and uncovered building ...
    // this doesn't handle previously covered buildings ...
    else { wartime/danger/war-plan return 0; }

So the mismatch existed from the feature's birth; it is not a later brace/refactor regression.
Later cleanup commits retained the same attachment. Current source still has it.

DEDUP / ROOT BOUNDARY
---------------------
- KI#48 is the authored feature family and its intended behavior documentation; it does not record
  this control-flow implementation defect. F555 is a concrete bug inside that feature.
- KI#48.2 fixes the definition of immediate happiness buildings; F555 applies after category
  classification and is independent of the happiness helper's correctness.

  arithmetic error and survives with perfectly correct category inputs.
- F554 / KI#877 is the maintenance classifier wrong-sign root. Maintenance reducers can currently
  reach later categories partly because F554 makes their marker false, but F555 is independently
  witnessed by a correctly classified Granary (`bFoodKeptBuilding == true`). Do not merge them.

  F555 survives even when `bAtWar`, `bDanger`, `bEnemyStrong` and `bWarPlan` are all perfectly
  accurate; the wrong Boolean is the category condition guarding the final tail.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Preserve every category's existing authored rules and restrict the final tail to buildings that
really were not matched above.

At this exact location, because the code is already in the `else` of `bCultureOnlyBuilding`, the
smallest structural correction is:

    else if (!bPreviousBuildings4)
    {
        if (bAtWar || bEnemyStrong || bDanger)
            return 0;
        else if (bWarPlan)
            return 0;
    }

When `bPreviousBuildings4` is false and `bCultureOnlyBuilding` is also false, the building has
neither a prior category nor culture, i.e. it is genuinely unknown/uncovered for this classifier
chain. Previously classified buildings instead fall through to the inherited/general
`AI_buildingValue()` logic exactly as their category comments intend.

An equivalent explicit `bUnknownRegularBuilding` Boolean would be even clearer if desired, but
avoid altering the individual category policy thresholds while fixing this control-flow root.

C031-WIP331 - F556 / KI#879 CONFIRMED

START STATE
-----------
Resumed from C031-WIP330 with F556 / provisional KI#879 UNUSED.

PREFILTER-SPECIFIC FOREIGN-TRADE CANDIDATE BOUNDED FIRST
-------------------------------------------------------
The SAS regular-building trade prefilter reuses inherited `bForeignTrade` as if it meant
"this city currently has a genuinely foreign trade route". Its actual definition is broader:

    if (TEAMID(pTradeCity->getOwner()) != getTeam() ||
        !sameArea(*pTradeCity))
    {
        bForeignTrade = true;
    }

so a domestic/same-team OVERSEAS route also sets it.

That is a real semantic mismatch with the comment, but the new HARD trade-only prefilter does not
currently supply the cleanest shipped consequence: both current buildings with a nonzero foreign
trade-route modifier also classify earlier as economy buildings.

- Custom House: foreign trade modifier +50, plus one Merchant slot and one free Merchant;
- Netherlands Beurs: foreign trade modifier +100, trade-route modifier +50 and +50% Gold.

Therefore `bTradeOnlyBuilding` is false for those current buildings because `bPreviousBuildings2`
already includes `bEconomyBuilding`. Do not claim a current hard-veto failure from the SAS-only
trade-only branch without future XML that makes a foreign-modifier building truly trade-only.

The inherited GENERAL building scorer, however, consumes the same broad Boolean directly and is
fully live. That is the independent F556 root below.

F556 / KI#879 - `AI_buildingValue()` CONFLATES DOMESTIC OVERSEAS TRADE WITH FOREIGN TRADE,
AWARDING `ForeignTradeRouteModifier` VALUE WHEN THE RUNTIME MODIFIER CANNOT APPLY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED in current supplied AdvCiv-SAS source.
Inherited Civ4/K-Mod-family AI valuation defect retained by Base AdvCiv and SAS.
Current source untouched.

RUNTIME CONTRACT
----------------
Actual trade-route scoring in current `CvCity::totalTradeModifier(CvCity const* pOtherCity)` keeps
OVERSEAS and FOREIGN effects distinct:

    if (!sameArea(*pOtherCity))
        iModifier += OVERSEAS_TRADE_MODIFIER;

    if (getTeam() != pOtherCity->getTeam())
    {
        iModifier += getForeignTradeRouteModifier();
        iModifier += getPeaceTradeModifier(pOtherCity->getTeam());
    }

Thus an own-city / same-team trade partner on a different land area receives the normal overseas
trade bonus but does NOT receive the city's `ForeignTradeRouteModifier`.

AI PROXY CONTRACT
-----------------
`CvCityAI::AI_buildingValue()` constructs one Boolean near the top of the function:

    bool bForeignTrade = false;
    for (each current trade route)
    {
        CvCity* pTradeCity = getTradeCity(i);
        ...
        if (TEAMID(pTradeCity->getOwner()) != getTeam() ||
            !sameArea(*pTradeCity))
        {
            bForeignTrade = true;
            break;
        }
    }

So the Boolean is actually:

    has a different-team route OR has an overseas route

not:

    has a route to a different team.

The broad proxy can make sense for some of its old uses because foreign and overseas routes can
both be more lucrative than ordinary domestic same-area routes. It is not valid as the predicate
for a FOREIGN-ONLY building modifier.

LIVE WRONG CONSUMER
-------------------
In the inherited trade-route part of current `AI_buildingValue()`:

    iTempValue += 5 * kBuilding.getTradeRouteModifier() *
        getTradeYield(YIELD_COMMERCE) / max(1, iTotalTradeModifier);

    if (bForeignTrade)
    {
        iTempValue += 3 * kBuilding.getForeignTradeRouteModifier() *
            getTradeYield(YIELD_COMMERCE) /
            max(1, iTotalTradeModifier + getForeignTradeRouteModifier());
    }

The `if (bForeignTrade)` guard therefore awards positive value for a building's
`ForeignTradeRouteModifier` whenever ANY current route is merely overseas, even if every route is
to the same owner/team and the runtime foreign modifier consequently applies to NONE of them.

A second inherited raw-yield valuation later in the same function repeats the same predicate for
`kBuilding.getForeignTradeRouteModifier()`. Treat both as consumers of one F556 proxy/root, not as
separate findings.

CLEAN SHIPPED FIXTURE
---------------------
Use a coastal AI city whose current trade-route set contains an own-city route on another land
area, but no route to any different team. This is an ordinary domestic intercontinental trade
state.

Then:

    TEAMID(pTradeCity->getOwner()) == getTeam()
    !sameArea(*pTradeCity)          == true
    bForeignTrade                  == true

At runtime for that partner:

    !sameArea(*pOtherCity)         == true  -> overseas bonus applies
    getTeam() != pOtherCity->getTeam() == false
                                      -> ForeignTradeRouteModifier does NOT apply

Current shipped XML supplies live buildings whose valuation is affected:

    BUILDING_CUSTOM_HOUSE
        iCost = 160
        iForeignTradeRouteModifier = +50

    BUILDING_NETHERLANDS_BEURS
        iCost = 200
        iTradeRouteModifier = +50
        iForeignTradeRouteModifier = +100

For either building, if the city has positive current trade commerce, the AI adds a positive
foreign-modifier component even though the same-team overseas route receives zero such modifier
when the building is actually completed. The Beurs still has a real ordinary +50% trade-route
modifier and Gold effects; F556 does not claim the entire building is worthless. It claims the
FOREIGN component is phantom in this state. The Custom House also has current SAS Merchant effects;
again, only the foreign-route component is misvalued.

This is a value-ranking defect rather than construction-legality failure, but the false component
feeds the authoritative `AI_buildingValue()` used by generic AI building selection and can alter
which constructible building wins.

ANCESTRY / CONTROL
------------------
The broad `bForeignTrade` definition is not a recent SAS invention:

- the supplied Civ4CE reference has the same `different team OR different area` proxy and uses it
  to value `getForeignTradeRouteModifier()`;
- K-Mod 1.46 retains the same proxy and the same foreign-modifier consumer;
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains both;
- current SAS retains both, with local refactoring/caching around them.

K-Mod changed the detailed trade-value arithmetic relative to the older Civ4-style code but did
not separate the two concepts. The mismatch therefore survives across the supplied ancestry
controls.

The runtime contract in current `CvCity::totalTradeModifier()` remains explicit: overseas is
keyed by area; foreign modifier is keyed by team. The AI proxy merges those two independent axes.

DEDUP / ROOT BOUNDARY
---------------------
- F554 is the SAS maintenance-classifier sign inversion; unrelated field and branch.
- F555 is the final regular-building war-tail attachment; it survives with perfectly classified
  trade state and says nothing about trade-yield arithmetic.
- Existing KI#197 domain/denominator families concern military/naval production scopes, not trade
  route foreign-vs-overseas identity.
- No prior album root was found for `bForeignTrade`, `ForeignTradeRouteModifier`, Custom House or
  the `iGlobalTradeValue` consumer.
- The SAS-only trade prefilter's reuse of `bForeignTrade` is an adjacent expression of the same
  semantic naming/proxy hazard, but current XML classification prevents it from being the clean
  hard shipped witness. Keep it under F556 rather than manufacture another root.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Do not destroy the old broader information, because some inherited uses intentionally use
"foreign OR overseas" as a rough signal for more lucrative trade.

Instead split the predicates explicitly, for example:

    bool bHasForeignTrade = false;
    bool bHasOverseasTrade = false;

and while scanning current routes set them independently:

    bHasForeignTrade |= (pTradeCity->getTeam() != getTeam());
    bHasOverseasTrade |= !sameArea(*pTradeCity);

Then:

- guard `getForeignTradeRouteModifier()` valuation and the SAS foreign-only prefilter with
  `bHasForeignTrade`;
- preserve a combined `bHasForeignTrade || bHasOverseasTrade` signal only at old consumers where
  that broader rough profitability heuristic is genuinely intended.

This is safer than simply deleting `|| !sameArea(...)` from the existing Boolean globally.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
1. Domestic overseas only:
   own-city route on another land area, no different-team route.
   - `bHasOverseasTrade == true`;
   - `bHasForeignTrade == false`;
   - foreign-modifier AI component must be zero.

2. Foreign same-area route:
   - `bHasForeignTrade == true`;
   - foreign-modifier component remains valued.

3. Foreign overseas route:
   both signals true; foreign modifier remains valued and generic overseas-profit heuristics can
   still use the broader signal where intended.

4. No trade routes:
   both false; preserve zero foreign-modifier valuation.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F557 / provisional KI#880 — AdvCiv sign regression reverses the immediate-anger
change from building happiness in `AI_buildingValue`
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
Current SAS inherits this AdvCiv expression in the happiness valuation block:

    int iBuildingActualHappiness = getAdditionalHappinessByBuilding(
            eBuilding, iGood, iBad);

    int iAngerDelta = std::max(0,
            -iHappinessLevel + iBuildingActualHappiness)
            - std::max(0, -iHappinessLevel);

    // High value for any immediate change in anger.
    iValue -= iAngerDelta * 4 * iCitizenValue;

The building effect has the wrong sign inside the projected post-building anger term.

`CvCity::getAdditionalHappinessByBuilding` explicitly documents that it returns the
"total additional happiness" from adding the building, and its return value is:

    iGood - iBad - iStarting

Thus a building that adds one net happiness supplies
`iBuildingActualHappiness == +1`.

If `iHappinessLevel` is the current happiness surplus, then current angry population
from this simplified threshold is:

    max(0, -iHappinessLevel)

and projected angry population after gaining `B` happiness must be:

    max(0, -(iHappinessLevel + B))

or equivalently:

    max(0, -iHappinessLevel - B)

Current AdvCiv/SAS instead computes:

    max(0, -iHappinessLevel + B)

which treats positive happiness as if it were additional unhappiness for this term.

MINIMAL SHIPPED FIXTURE
-----------------------
Current SAS contains ordinary constructible +1-happiness buildings, e.g.
`BUILDING_COLOSSEUM` has:

    iHappiness = 1

Take a city whose evaluated `iHappinessLevel == -1` and a building whose net projected
additional happiness is +1.

Before the building:

    angry threshold = max(0, 1) = 1

Correct post-building threshold:

    max(0, -(-1 + 1)) = 0

Correct anger delta:

    0 - 1 = -1

The current code instead calculates:

    max(0, -(-1) + 1) - 1
  = max(0, 2) - 1
  = +1

So a building that removes one angry citizen is represented by the variable named
`iAngerDelta` as ADDING one angry citizen.

The next line then compounds the inversion:

    iValue -= iAngerDelta * 4 * iCitizenValue;

Correct K-Mod arithmetic gives `iAngerDelta == -1`, producing a positive immediate
value of `+4 * iCitizenValue`.

Current AdvCiv/SAS gives `iAngerDelta == +1`, producing the opposite
`-4 * iCitizenValue` penalty.

The following "positive change bias" also keys on `iAngerDelta < 0`; current code can
therefore suppress that bonus precisely when positive building happiness actually
reduces anger.

The separate later padding term for positive happiness does not repair this root. It
is an additional heuristic term; the explicitly immediate angry-citizen term still has
its sign reversed and can materially distort total `AI_buildingValue` and therefore
building ranking/construction decisions.

ANCESTRY / INTRODUCTION
-----------------------
K-Mod has the correct expression:

    int iAngerDelta = std::max(0,
            -(iHappinessLevel + iBuildingActualHappiness))
            - std::max(0, -iHappinessLevel);

The supplied reachable AdvCiv history identifies the regression exactly.

AdvCiv practical commit 2719,
commit `529ebb7b4f59681b609c10c4d3ad31838ba62d67`, titled:

    Improve AI support for mods with custom eras

refactored this block to use the newer `iCitizenValue`. In that same hunk it changed:

    - std::max(0, -(iHappinessLevel+iBuildingActualHappiness))
    + std::max(0, -iHappinessLevel+iBuildingActualHappiness)

The era-support objective gives no semantic reason to reverse building happiness; the
sign loss occurs incidentally alongside the citizen-value refactor.

Later reachable commits (including practical 2920/2954/3392) only reformat/preserve the
already-regressed expression. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain it.

Civ4CE does not contain this K-Mod happiness-valuation block in the supplied reference;
the relevant positive control is therefore K-Mod -> AdvCiv ancestry rather than an
original-BtS/Civ4CE comparison.

DEDUP / ROOT BOUNDARY
---------------------
No existing album finding owns this immediate-building-happiness sign inversion.

It is distinct from:

* F355 — event building happiness/health multiplicity;
* F367 — cross-city mutation of `iExtraPop` in player happiness/health weighting;
* F397 — LuxuryModifier omitted by the BUG additional-building-happiness preview;
* KI#48.2 — SAS regular-building prefilter classification for immediate happiness;
* F555 — the later SAS unknown/misc building-tail control-flow overreach.

F557 occurs inside inherited `AI_buildingValue` after a building has reached the normal
happiness valuation and survives even when `getAdditionalHappinessByBuilding` returns a
perfectly correct value.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Restore the post-building anger expression to the K-Mod/sign-correct form, e.g.:

    int iAngerDelta = std::max(0,
            -iHappinessLevel - iBuildingActualHappiness)
            - std::max(0, -iHappinessLevel);

or equivalently retain the original parenthesized K-Mod form:

    int iAngerDelta = std::max(0,
            -(iHappinessLevel + iBuildingActualHappiness))
            - std::max(0, -iHappinessLevel);

Do not change the later subtraction from `iValue`; with the correct delta sign, reduced
anger is negative and therefore correctly adds value.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
1. `iHappinessLevel=-1`, building happiness `+1`:
   assert `iAngerDelta == -1`, not `+1`.
2. `iHappinessLevel=-2`, building happiness `+1`:
   assert anger changes `2 -> 1`, delta `-1`.
3. `iHappinessLevel=+1`, building happiness `+1`:
   assert both before/after anger are zero and delta remains 0.
4. If a negative net-happiness building/mod fixture is supplied by a mod, verify the
   opposite direction as well: losing happiness must increase rather than reduce anger.
5. Compare the repaired arithmetic against K-Mod for a table of `(H,B)` values spanning
   negative, zero and positive happiness surplus.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F558 / provisional KI#881 — SAS regular-building difficulty skew reads the AI
PLAYER handicap instead of the GAME handicap that actually controls AI research cost
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
SAS practical 4950 introduced two handicap references near the start of the custom
`AI_buildingValue` prefilter:

    CvHandicapInfo const& hGame = GC.getInfo(kGame.getHandicapType());
    CvHandicapInfo const& hAI   = GC.getInfo(kOwner.getHandicapType());

The regular espionage-only building branch later tries to infer the AI's actual research
cost advantage/disadvantage:

    const int iHumanResearchPercent = hGame.getResearchPercent();
    const int iAIResearchPercent    = hAI.getAIResearchPercent();
    const int iResearchPercentGap =
            iHumanResearchPercent - iAIResearchPercent;

and interprets:

    gap <= -20  => AI pays much more for research; strongly prefer EP offense;
    gap >= +30  => AI pays much less for research; strongly prefer EP defense.

`hAI` is the wrong receiver for that question.

AUTHORITATIVE RUNTIME CONTRACT
------------------------------
Current AdvCiv/SAS research cost is computed in `CvTeam::getResearchCost`.
For a nonhuman non-Barbarian team it explicitly says:

    // Important to use game handicap here (not team handicap)

and applies:

    GC.getInfo(kGame.getHandicapType()).getAIResearchPercent()
        + kGame.AIHandicapAdjustment()

The acting AI player's own handicap entry is not the source of the
`AIResearchPercent` multiplier used by actual technology cost.

That distinction is deliberate throughout AdvCiv. `CvPlayer::init` contains another
historical correction whose comment states that using `this->getHandicapType()` meant
"Noble" and therefore made an AI difficulty block do nothing; that code was repaired by
reading `kGame.getHandicapType()` instead.

WHY ORDINARY SAS GAMES ARE ESPECIALLY CLEAR
-------------------------------------------
`CvInitCore::resetPlayer` initializes player handicaps from `STANDARD_HANDICAP`.
AdvCiv's own nearby historical comment identifies the ordinary AI player value as
Noble. Outside special Rise & Fall reassignment, an ordinary AI therefore reads the
Noble `CvHandicapInfo` through `kOwner.getHandicapType()` even when the human-selected
GAME handicap is Rookie, Monarch, Immortal, Deity, etc.

Current SAS also sets `iAIHandicapIncrementTurns = 0` on every one of its 11 handicap
entries, so:

    kGame.AIHandicapAdjustment() == 0

throughout current shipped ordinary games. The actual AI-research multiplier is
therefore exactly the GAME handicap's XML `iAIResearchPercent`, while the prefilter
reads the AI player's Noble value.

CURRENT SHIPPED HANDICAP DATA
-----------------------------
Current SAS uses `iResearchPercent = 100` for the human at every handicap and:

    Rookie       AIResearchPercent = 124
    Settler      AIResearchPercent = 118
    Chieftain    AIResearchPercent = 112
    Warlord      AIResearchPercent = 106
    Noble        AIResearchPercent = 100
    Prince       AIResearchPercent =  94
    Monarch      AIResearchPercent =  88
    Emperor      AIResearchPercent =  82
    Immortal     AIResearchPercent =  76
    Deity        AIResearchPercent =  70
    Deity Plus   AIResearchPercent =  64

Thus the intended real gap spans:

    Rookie:      100 - 124 = -24
    Deity:       100 -  70 = +30
    Deity Plus:  100 -  64 = +36

but an ordinary AI's `hAI` lookup uses Noble 100 and collapses the custom prefilter gap
to:

    100 - 100 = 0

on all those ordinary difficulty settings.

The feature is therefore not merely imprecise: its two shipped threshold cases can be
silently disabled by the wrong receiver.

LIVE SHIPPED BUILDING FIXTURES
------------------------------
The regular-building prefilter is enabled by default:

    SAS_AI_BUILDING_VALUE_REGULAR_BUILDINGS_OPTIMIZE = 1

Current XML provides clean espionage-only consumers that reach the difficulty block when
not at war, not in danger and not executing a war plan.

A. `BUILDING_INTELLIGENCE_AGENCY`

    CommerceModifier(COMMERCE_ESPIONAGE) = +50
    Spy specialist slots                  = 2
    no health / happiness / maintenance / production / science / gold / trade role
      that would classify it in an earlier regular-building category

It therefore qualifies as an espionage source building.

On Rookie the actual research-cost gap is -24, satisfying the authored
`iEPOffGap = -20`. The intended branch should strongly prefer the espionage source:

    AI_BUILDING_ALWAYS_PICK_FIRST - 1000

The wrong Noble `hAI` receiver yields gap 0 instead, so that priority never fires.

B. `BUILDING_SECURITY_BUREAU`

    EspionageDefenseModifier = +50
    flat espionage           = +8
    Spy specialist slots     = 2
    no earlier regular-building category under ordinary city state

It qualifies both as an espionage source and, importantly for the high-difficulty
branch, as high-enough espionage defense.

On Deity the actual gap is exactly +30; on Deity Plus it is +36. Both satisfy the
`iEPDefGap = +30` condition and should strongly prefer the defensive building. The
wrong Noble receiver again yields gap 0 and suppresses that intended priority.

This is a direct producer/consumer failure in live AI building selection, not merely a
comment mismatch or theoretical mod configuration.

------------------------------------------------------------------
The wonder timing gate later reuses the same `hAI` object:

    int const iAIWCP = hAI.getAIWorldConstructPercent();

and compares it against an assumed human 100% world-wonder construction cost.

Actual `CvPlayer::getProductionNeeded(BuildingTypes)` again obtains the AI world-wonder

plus the game AI handicap adjustment. So the receiver is wrong there by the same

Current SAS XML, however, has `iAIWorldConstructPercent = 100` at all 11 handicap
