================================================================================
C031-WIP363 CONTINUATION - RANDOM-EVENT CITY-HISTORY / CLEAR-SCOPE CENSUS
================================================================================

Scope / provenance
------------------
Continued Queue 006 (`CvGameCoreDLL/CvCity.cpp`) from C031-WIP362 with F576 /
provisional KI#899 UNUSED. The current AdvCiv-SAS source, supplied Base AdvCiv 1.14,
K-Mod 1.46 and Civ4CE/BtS source plus current shipped EventInfo/EventTriggerInfo XML
were used locally. No repository source file was modified.

The first obligation was the unfinished `canApplyEvent` food-rounding candidate from
the WIP362 handoff; after closing that against shipped XML, the pass continued into
`CvCity::getTriggerValue`, location-sensitive prerequisite history and the player/city
ClearEvents handoff.

POST-WIP362 CONTROL - EVENT FOOD VALIDATOR/RUNTIME INTEGER ORDER IS GENERICALLY
FRAGILE BUT CURRENT SAS XML DOES NOT REACH AN ELIGIBILITY DISAGREEMENT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvCity::canApplyEvent` checks city food with:

    kEvent.getFood() +
        ((100 + kEvent.getFoodPercent()) * getFood()) / 100 >= 0

whereas `CvCity::applyEvent` mutates it as:

    changeFood(kEvent.getFood() +
        (kEvent.getFoodPercent() * getFood()) / 100);

Over real arithmetic these are equivalent; under C++ integer truncation toward zero
they can differ when the percentage is negative. A generic fixture such as current
food 1, flat food -1, percent -50 would make the validator compute -1 while runtime
would land exactly on 0.

A reliable per-EventInfo parse of CURRENT SAS XML closes the shipped route. There are
only seven food-changing EventInfos:

* EVENT_HAPPY_HUNTING_1: +8 flat, 0%
* EVENT_FAMINE_2: 0 flat, -50%
* EVENT_FAMINE_3: 0 flat, -100%
* EVENT_FARM_BANDITS_2: -5 flat, 0%
* EVENT_FARM_BANDITS_3: -5 flat, 0%
* EVENT_BABY_BOOM_1: +10 flat, 0%
* EVENT_SPOILED_GRAIN_1: 0 flat, -100%

No shipped event combines a negative flat amount with a negative percentage. For the
-50%-only case, odd food values can make the validator's intermediate result one lower
than runtime's retained food, but both remain nonnegative; -100% is exact. Therefore
the generic arithmetic mismatch cannot change current event legality and is not F576.

POST-WIP362 CONTROL - REQUIRED-BUILDING LIST WITH iNumBuildings=0 IS INTENTIONAL IN
THE TWO CURRENT FIXTURES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A field census of `CvCity::getTriggerValue` found two shipped triggers with a nonempty
BuildingsRequired list but `iNumBuildings=0`:

* EVENTTRIGGER_MASTER_BLACKSMITH_DONE lists Forge;
* EVENTTRIGGER_DEFECTING_AGENT lists Intelligence Agency.

The city scorer only enforces BuildingsRequired when `iNumBuildings > 0`, which looked
like a possible skipped city prerequisite. Current caller/data contracts close both:
Defecting Agent is not a pick-city trigger and uses its building requirement through
the player/global building-count path. Master Blacksmith Done's PythonCanDo callback
explicitly checks the player's Forge target and rewrites the completion trigger's city
ID back to the original quest city. No invalid city selection was established.

POST-WIP362 CONTROL - `bPrereqEventCity` / XML `bPrereqEventPlot` NAME MISMATCH IS
INHERITED FIRAXIS LOCATION-SENSITIVE SEMANTICS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvEventTriggerInfo::read` loads member `m_bPrereqEventCity` from XML tag
`bPrereqEventPlot`. The spelling initially looked like a parser typo. Supplied
Civ4CE/BtS, K-Mod, Base AdvC and current SAS all retain the same mapping, and consumers
use it coherently as a location-sensitive prerequisite:

* pick-city triggers require the prerequisite EventType in the city's
  `m_aEventsOccured` through `CvCity::getTriggerValue`;
* plot triggers require matching stored trigger coordinates through CvPlot logic.

The odd member/tag naming is therefore legacy contract, not independently F576.

F576 / KI#899 - CONFIRMED
-------------------------
CLEAREVENTS COLLAPSES A SPECIFIC SUCCESSFUL EVENTTYPE CLEAR INTO ONE BOOLEAN, AND
`CvCity::applyEvent(..., bClear=true)` THEN ERASES EVERY CITY-LOCAL EVENT-HISTORY FLAG;
AN UNRELATED CITY EVENT CAN SILENTLY BREAK ANOTHER SAME-CITY RECURRING EVENT CHAIN.

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED. This is an inherited Firaxis/BtS execution-scope defect retained by K-Mod,
Base AdvC 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS. Current shipped XML contains a direct ordinary
single-clear-target witness; it does NOT require the multi-ClearEvents configuration
that an earlier album control correctly classified as current-data masked.

ROOT - SPECIFIC PLAYER-SCOPE CLEAR BECOMES UNSCOPED CITY-SCOPE BOOLEAN
---------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::applyEvent` evaluates every configured ClearEvents target separately. For a
successful target `eLoopEvent`, it performs the correctly scoped player/team/global
reset:

    if (kEvent.getClearEventChance(eLoopEvent) <= 0)
        continue;

    bClear = (SyncRandNum(100) < kEvent.getClearEventChance(eLoopEvent));
    if (!bClear)
        continue;

    ...
    resetEventOccured(eLoopEvent, false);

The identity of the cleared EventType is therefore known and respected at player
scope. But the function preserves only the single Boolean `bClear` for the target
city call:

    pCity->applyEvent(eEvent, *pTriggeredData, bClear);

`CvCity::applyEvent` first records the CURRENT city event:

    setEventOccured(eEvent, true);

then applies its city effects. At the end, a true Boolean does not clear the specific
successful `eLoopEvent`. It instead does:

    if (bClear)
    {
        FOR_EACH_ENUM(Event)
            setEventOccured(eLoopEvent, false);
    }

Thus one successful ClearEvents entry means "erase every EventTypes flag from this
city," even though the XML named one particular prior EventType and the player-level
code cleared exactly that one.

CITY-LOCAL EVENT HISTORY IS REAL PERSISTENT GAME STATE
------------------------------------------------------
`m_aEventsOccured` is serialized in `CvCity::read/write`; `isEventOccured` queries it,
and `CvCity::getTriggerValue` uses it whenever a trigger has the location-sensitive
prerequisite flag:

    if (kTrigger.isPrereqEventCity() && kTrigger.getNumPrereqEvents() > 0)
    {
        ...
        if (!isEventOccured((EventTypes)kTrigger.getPrereqEvent(i)))
            return MIN_INT;
    }

This is not dead/UI-only history. It is one half of live same-city event-chain
eligibility.

CURRENT SHIPPED WITNESS - SLAVE REVOLT STATE ERASED BY UNRELATED FARM BANDITS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS ships `EVENT_SLAVE_REVOLT_3` as a city event with exactly one ClearEvents
entry:

    EVENT_SLAVE_REVOLT_3 -> clear EVENT_SLAVE_REVOLT_3 with 40% chance

When option 3 occurs and that 40% roll FAILS (60% of executions), the normal ordering
leaves both:

1. the player's `EVENT_SLAVE_REVOLT_3` occurrence record; and
2. that city's local `EVENT_SLAVE_REVOLT_3` flag.

Those two records are exactly what `EVENTTRIGGER_SLAVE_REVOLT_AGAIN` expects. Current
trigger XML gives it:

    iPercentGamesActive = 100
    iWeight = -1
    PrereqEvents = EVENT_SLAVE_REVOLT_3
    bPrereqEventPlot = 1   // loaded as the city/location prerequisite flag
    bRecurring = 1
    bPickCity = 1

`CvPlayer::doEvents` directly calls `trigger(eLoopEventTrigger)` whenever
`getEventTriggerWeight` returns -1. `getEventTriggerWeight` first requires the player's
prerequisite EventInfo occurrence, while `pickTriggerCity -> CvCity::getTriggerValue`
requires the same city's local occurrence. Both layers are intentional and live.

Now let the SAME ordinary city later qualify for `EVENTTRIGGER_FARM_BANDITS`. The two
trigger families have no mutually exclusive requirements: e.g. a population-4+
Slavery city that has retained Slave Revolt 3 can also work/contain the ordinary
Farm-Bandits farm/resource/route/unit fixture.

Every current Farm Bandits outcome has one positive ClearEvents target, and option 1
provides the simplest deterministic path:

    EVENT_FARM_BANDITS_1 -> clear EVENT_FARM_BANDITS_3 with 100% chance

The player does NOT need to have previously experienced Farm Bandits 3;
`resetEventOccured(EVENT_FARM_BANDITS_3, false)` simply becomes a target-specific no-op
if that player record is absent. The 100% roll nevertheless leaves `bClear=true`.

`CvCity::applyEvent(EVENT_FARM_BANDITS_1, ..., true)` then:

1. records FARM_BANDITS_1 locally;
2. executes the chosen event;
3. loops over EVERY EventType and removes every local city occurrence.

That erases the unrelated `EVENT_SLAVE_REVOLT_3` city flag. Crucially,
CvPlayer cleared only `EVENT_FARM_BANDITS_3`; the player's
`EVENT_SLAVE_REVOLT_3` occurrence is untouched.

On subsequent event turns, `SLAVE_REVOLT_AGAIN` therefore passes its player-level
prerequisite but the formerly affected city fails the required same-city prerequisite.
An unrelated Farm Bandits resolution has silently broken the retained Slave Revolt
continuation state.

The inverse family can be used similarly: successful Slave Revolt clearing can wipe an
unrelated retained Farm-Bandits city flag. The root is not specific to either family;
these two shipped recurring chains merely provide the clearest current consequence.

WHY THE EARLIER CLEAREVENTS CONTROL DOES NOT DEDUP THIS FINDING
--------------------------------------------------------------
WIP196 preserved a separate generic concern: if ONE EventInfo had MULTIPLE positive
ClearEvents targets, repeatedly assigning one `bClear` would make the final Boolean
represent only the last roll. That control was correctly left unnumbered because
current SAS has exactly one positive ClearEvents target per EventInfo.

F576 does not require multiple targets at all. With exactly one current target, the
Boolean accurately says that THAT target cleared at player scope; the defect is the
NEXT layer throwing away its EventTypes identity and interpreting the bool as permission
to clear ALL city-local event histories. Current one-target XML therefore exposes F576
directly rather than masking it.

ANCESTRY
--------
Supplied Civ4CE/BtS contains the same pair of operations:

* `CvPlayer::applyEvent` reduces target-specific ClearEvents processing to `bool bClear`
  and passes it to the city;
* `CvCity::applyEvent(..., bClear)` loops over every EventInfo and clears every city
  occurrence when the bool is true.

K-Mod 1.46 retains the same logic. Base AdvC 1.14 translates the loops to enum helpers
but preserves the exact semantics, and current SAS retains them. This is therefore a
base Firaxis/BtS bug inherited through all supplied descendants, not a SAS-only change.

DUPLICATE CHECK
---------------
Whole-album searches for ClearEvents, `bClear`, `m_aEventsOccured`, city-local event
history, Slave Revolt Again and Farm Bandits found no numbered root owning this
specific player-target -> all-city-history scope widening. Existing event findings own
other lifecycle/propagation defects (e.g. team EventInfo propagation, stale delayed
choices, acquisition loss of city-event effects), and WIP196's multi-target Boolean
control is explicitly distinct as described above. F576 is independent.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION - NOT IMPLEMENTED
------------------------------------------------
Do not collapse successful ClearEvents targets into a Boolean before the city-local
history update. Preserve the EventTypes identities that actually passed their rolls.
A future-proof repair should support multiple successful targets even though current
XML only uses one per EventInfo:

1. accumulate the successfully cleared EventTypes in `CvPlayer::applyEvent`;
2. apply the selected city event normally so its own local occurrence is first recorded;
3. clear from that target city ONLY the local flags whose EventTypes are in the
   successful ClearEvents set.

This ordering matters when an event explicitly clears itself: the freshly recorded
current event should be removed only if its own EventType is a successful XML clear
target. Player/team/global `resetEventOccured(eLoopEvent, ...)` logic can remain
specific as it already is.

A minimally invasive current-data patch could carry one `EventTypes` instead of a bool,
but a small vector/list is safer and preserves the XML contract if multiple targets are
added later.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Unrelated-history preservation
1. Give player A / city C retained `EVENT_SLAVE_REVOLT_3` state at BOTH player and city
   scope (equivalent to option 3 with its 40% clear roll failing).
2. Apply `EVENT_FARM_BANDITS_1` to C; its Farm-Bandits-3 clear is 100%.
3. Assert the player-level Farm-Bandits-3 record is cleared if present.
4. Assert C's unrelated `EVENT_SLAVE_REVOLT_3` flag remains set.
5. Assert `EVENTTRIGGER_SLAVE_REVOLT_AGAIN` can still select C when its other conditions
   are satisfied.

B. Intended same-event clear
1. Apply `EVENT_SLAVE_REVOLT_3` with a forced successful 40% clear result.
2. Assert both the player occurrence and C's local `EVENT_SLAVE_REVOLT_3` flag are
   cleared, preserving intended self-clear semantics.

C. Failed-clear control
Force the Slave-Revolt-3 40% clear roll to fail and assert both player and city records
remain available to `SLAVE_REVOLT_AGAIN`.

D. Multiple-target future-proofing
Construct a test EventInfo with two ClearEvents entries and independently controlled
rolls; assert city-local history clears exactly the successful EventTypes, not all
history and not merely the final roll's state.

HANDOFF / SOURCE STONE
----------------------
Queue 006 `CvGameCoreDLL/CvCity.cpp` remains OPEN under the protected deep-method re-audit.
F559 / KI#882 through F576 / KI#899 remain CONFIRMED.
F577 / provisional KI#900 is CONFIRMED below.
F578 / provisional KI#901 is UNUSED.
Authoritative current source remains the user-supplied AdvCiv-SAS light-source snapshot.
Comparison/ancestry material remains the supplied Base AdvCiv 1.14, K-Mod 1.46 and

album. No repository source files modified.

CORRECTION TO WIP101 NEGATIVE CONTROL
-------------------------------------
WIP101 said that the remaining BUG additional-commerce building projection used the city's
runtime base-commerce and total-commerce-modifier structure consistently. That statement was
too broad. It correctly checked the city-local arithmetic once the hypothetical extra base
commerce/modifier values had been assembled, but it did NOT audit player-global state that the
candidate building itself mutates through `CvPlayer::processBuilding` before runtime commerce is
recomputed.

The old control is therefore amended, not silently erased: the final arithmetic shape is sound
for the inputs it models, but the hypothetical after-building state omits two live input families
owned by the candidate building itself.

F577 / provisional KI#900 - CONFIRMED
BUG BUILDING-COMMERCE "ACTUAL EFFECTS" PROJECTION EVALUATES THE CANDIDATE AGAINST THE OLD
PLAYER-GLOBAL SPECIALIST-EXTRA / STATE-RELIGION-BUILDING COMMERCE STATE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvCity::getAdditionalCommerceTimes100ByBuilding` advertises:

    Returns the total additional commerce times 100 that
    adding one of the given buildings will provide.

It constructs a hypothetical extra base-commerce value with
`getAdditionalBaseCommerceRateByBuilding` and a hypothetical modifier with
`getAdditionalCommerceRateModifierByBuilding`, then compares that to the city's current
`getBaseCommerceRateTimes100` / total modifier.

The helper does model many city-local consequences of the candidate building:

* ordinary / obsolete-safe CommerceChanges;
* city BuildingClass commerce changes;
* the CURRENT player's state-religion-building commerce if the candidate itself is a
  religious building;
* global religion/corporation commerce on the candidate;
* candidate free specialists (through the specialist helper);
* local + global commerce-rate modifiers.

But actual building completion also calls `CvPlayer::processBuilding`, which for every commerce
type performs:

    changeSpecialistExtraCommerce(c,
        kBuilding.getSpecialistExtraCommerce(c) * iChange);
    changeStateReligionBuildingCommerce(c,
        kBuilding.getStateReligionCommerce(c) * iChange);

Those are PLAYER-GLOBAL inputs to city commerce, and the hypothetical building helper never
constructs their post-building values.

That omission has two direct effects in the construction city itself.

1. SpecialistExtraCommerce granted by the candidate

Runtime base city commerce contains:

    (getSpecialistPopulation() + getNumGreatPeople()) *
        owner.getSpecialistExtraCommerce(eCommerce)

separately from the stored specialist-info commerce.

When the candidate building raises `owner.getSpecialistExtraCommerce`, every existing
specialist / settled Great Person in the construction city immediately gains that commerce.
The helper leaves the owner value at its pre-building amount.

Its handling of FREE specialists is also evaluated against the old player state:

    getAdditionalBaseCommerceRateBySpecialistImpl(...)
      -> owner.specialistCommerce(...)

`owner.specialistCommerce` includes the player's CURRENT SpecialistExtraCommerce, not the
candidate building's soon-to-be-added amount. Thus a building that both grants a free
specialist and raises SpecialistExtraCommerce undercounts the newly added specialist too.

2. StateReligionCommerce granted by the candidate

Runtime building commerce for each active religious building includes the player's current
`getStateReligionBuildingCommerce(eCommerce)` when that building's ReligionType matches the
player's state religion.

A candidate with nonzero `StateReligionCommerces` changes that player-global amount during
`CvPlayer::processBuilding`. At the end of `CvCity::processBuilding`, the construction city calls
`updateBuildingCommerce()`, so its existing matching religious buildings are recomputed using
the NEW value immediately.

The hypothetical helper never overlays the candidate's new StateReligionCommerce onto those
already-present religious buildings. It only asks whether the candidate building ITSELF has a
ReligionType and, if so, adds the player's OLD state-religion-building bonus to that candidate.

Therefore the helper is not evaluating the documented post-building city state.

PRIMARY CURRENT-SAS REPRO A - GREAT LIBRARY FALSE-ZERO RESEARCH
---------------------------------------------------------------
Current `BUILDING_GREAT_LIBRARY` has:

    SpecialistExtraCommerces = [0, 1, 0]
    CommerceChanges          = empty
    CommerceModifiers        = empty
    FreeSpecialistCounts     = empty
    ObsoleteTech             = NONE

Commerce order is Gold / Research / Culture / Espionage, so this is +1 Research per
specialist/settled-GP for the owner.

Use an ordinary constructible Great Library city with:

    one existing specialist (or settled Great Person)
    no pre-existing player SpecialistExtraCommerce(RESEARCH)
    no unrelated Research change from the Great Library itself
    ordinary 100% Research modifier for the minimal numeric fixture

PREVIEW:
`getAdditionalBaseCommerceRateByBuildingImpl(RESEARCH, GREAT_LIBRARY)` sees no direct Research
CommerceChange, no Research modifier and no free specialist, so `iExtraRate == 0` and
`iExtraModifier == 0`. `getAdditionalCommerceTimes100ByBuilding` returns 0 immediately.

RUNTIME:
completion reaches

    changeSpecialistExtraCommerce(RESEARCH, +1)

and the city already has one specialist. `getBaseCommerceRateTimes100(RESEARCH)` therefore gains
100 hundredths, i.e. +1 Research before any greater-than-100 commerce multiplier.

Thus the player-facing building projection can say 0 additional Research while the completed
building immediately raises that city's actual Research by +1. With N existing specialists /
settled Great People, the omitted base effect is N Research before modifiers.

PRIMARY CURRENT-SAS REPRO B - SANKORE FALSE-ZERO RESEARCH
---------------------------------------------------------
Current `BUILDING_SANKORE` has:

    StateReligionCommerces = [0, 3]
    CommerceChanges        = empty
    CommerceModifiers      = empty
    ReligionType           = NONE
    ObsoleteTech           = NONE

so it grants +3 Research to every active building of the owner's state religion.

Use a city that can construct Sankore and already contains one active building whose
`ReligionType` equals the owner's state religion.

PREVIEW:
Sankore itself has ReligionType=NONE and no direct Research CommerceChange/modifier, so the
building helper has no route by which the candidate's new +3 player-global state-religion bonus
can be applied to the existing religious building. The minimal projection is 0 Research.

RUNTIME:
`CvPlayer::processBuilding(SANKORE,+1)` calls

    changeStateReligionBuildingCommerce(RESEARCH, +3)

and `CvCity::processBuilding` subsequently calls `updateBuildingCommerce()` for the construction
city. The already-present state-religion building is therefore recounted at the new amount and
city Research immediately rises by +3 before modifiers.

This reproducer is independent of F476's stale-OTHER-city cache defect: the construction city
gets its explicit end-of-`processBuilding` recount. F577 is wrong even in a build where F476 is
fully repaired.

INTERACTION / REPAIR-SHAPE CONTROL - NATYA SHASTRA
--------------------------------------------------
Current `BUILDING_NATYA_SHASTRA` simultaneously has:

    FreeSpecialistCounts:       +1 Artist
    SpecialistExtraCommerces:   [0, 0, 1]  -> +1 Culture per specialist
    StateReligionCommerces:     [0, 0, 2]  -> +2 Culture per state-religion building

Current Artist intrinsic commerce is:

    [0 Gold, 1 Research, 4 Culture]

The old helper does count the free Artist, but evaluates that Artist through the owner's
PRE-BUILD `specialistCommerce`; it therefore omits Natya's own +1 Culture from the new Artist.
It also omits +1 Culture for every specialist/settled GP already in the city and +2 Culture for
every qualifying existing state-religion building.

This means a repair must model the post-building player-global state coherently rather than bolt
on only `existingSpecialists * delta` after the old helper has already valued free specialists.

LIVE USER-FACING CALLERS
------------------------
This helper is not dead and does not require enabling an obscure debug-only path.

`CvGameTextMgr::setBuildingNetEffectsHelp` describes itself as appending the:

    actual (i.e. absolute) effects of adding eBuilding to pCity

and feeds every commerce type from `getAdditionalCommerceTimes100ByBuilding`.
`setBuildingHelpActual` exposes that "Actual Effects" block for an active-owned city while Alt
is held (or through the corresponding BUG option; debug mode can broaden visibility).

The separate `setBuildingAdditionalCommerceHelp` also iterates every currently constructible
building and uses this exact helper to populate the "Building Additional Commerce" hover.
Thus false-zero / under-valued current-city projections are ordinary player-visible output.

ANCESTRY
--------
The BUG Building Additional Commerce helper is already present in supplied K-Mod 1.46 with the
same conceptual inputs and the same omission. Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains it, with mostly enum /
cleanup refactors, and current SAS retains the same semantic contract.

This is therefore an inherited BUG/K-Mod projection defect rather than a SAS-created code
regression.

The defect is live even in the supplied upstream data: K-Mod and Base AdvCiv 1.14 both have
building-level SpecialistExtraCommerce / StateReligionCommerce producers, including Sistine
Chapel plus Spiral Minaret / Sankore. SAS adds especially clean witnesses such as Great Library
SpecialistExtraCommerce and raises Sankore to +3 Research.

DEDUP / NEIGHBOR ROOTS
----------------------
Whole-album semantic search found no numbered root owning this hypothetical post-building
player-global-commerce omission.

* F438 / KI#761 is the Finance Advisor's CURRENT specialist-Gold breakdown using base-only
  `city.getSpecialistCommerce` while runtime / its own hover include player-wide
  SpecialistExtraCommerce. F577 is a different function and phase: a HYPOTHETICAL candidate
  building itself changes SpecialistExtraCommerce, but the before/after building projection
  evaluates against the old owner state.

* F476 / KI#799 is RUNTIME cache invalidation for StateReligionBuildingCommerce/state-religion
  changes across cities. F577 survives a complete F476 repair and has a clean same-city Sankore
  witness because the construction city explicitly recounts building commerce at the end of
  `processBuilding`.

* F397-F399 and F561 own other BUG building-projection domains (happiness/health/production/
  maintenance/trade-yield arithmetic). None owns the SpecialistExtraCommerce /
  StateReligionCommerce inputs to the commerce projection.

* WIP101's earlier "additional commerce structure matches runtime" statement is explicitly
  amended above. It checked the final city-local arithmetic but missed candidate-driven
  `CvPlayer::processBuilding` state mutations. It is not treated as a prior finding or a dedup.

CLASSIFICATION
--------------
CONFIRMED inherited BUG/K-Mod player-facing hypothetical-state defect; ordinary-live in current
SAS data.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION - NOT IMPLEMENTED
------------------------------------------------
Treat the projection as a true old-city-state vs post-building-city-state comparison.
At minimum the hypothetical after-state must overlay the candidate building's:

1. `SpecialistExtraCommerce(eCommerce)` onto the owner's current value, and apply the DELTA to
   every specialist / settled Great Person that will exist after construction, including free
   specialists granted by the candidate itself;

2. `StateReligionCommerce(eCommerce)` onto the owner's current value, and apply that DELTA to
   every active building in this city whose ReligionType matches the effective state religion,
   including the candidate itself if it is such a religious building;

3. existing direct building commerce / global religion / corporation / modifier inputs already
   handled by the helper.

The safest long-term design is to share one explicit projected-base-commerce routine with runtime
input semantics instead of independently reconstructing pieces in the BUG helper. Do not mutate
real CvPlayer state merely to obtain the preview.

NO_ESPIONAGE culture/espionage remapping must remain applied after the full projected input is
assembled, just as the current helper already attempts for its narrower input set.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------

With player-wide runtime building-commerce invalidation repaired, repeat the same-city Sankore

StateReligionCommerce.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F578 / provisional KI#901 - CONFIRMED
BUG BUILDING-ADDITIONAL-YIELD PROJECTION IGNORES THE CANDIDATE BUILDING'S
PLAYER-GLOBAL `SpecialistYieldChanges`, SO A WONDER CAN PREVIEW +0 PRODUCTION
WHILE IMMEDIATELY RAISING THE CONSTRUCTION CITY'S REAL BASE PRODUCTION
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvCity::getAdditionalYieldByBuilding` claims to return the total additional yield from adding a
building. Its base-yield helper models direct building yield, worked sea/river changes, city
building-class yield, trade-route changes, vote-source religion yield and candidate free
specialists. But it never models `CvBuildingInfo::SpecialistYieldChanges` owned by the candidate.

Actual building completion does. `CvCity::processBuilding` calls `CvPlayer::processBuilding` for the
appropriate team member(s). `CvPlayer::processBuilding` iterates the candidate building's
`getSpecialistYieldChange()` map and executes:

    changeSpecialistExtraYield(eSpecialist, eYield,
        candidateSpecialistYieldChange * iChange);

`CvPlayer::changeSpecialistExtraYield` then immediately calls `updateExtraSpecialistYield()` for the
player's cities. In each city, `CvCity::updateExtraSpecialistYield` recomputes:

    (getSpecialistCount(eSpecialist) + getFreeSpecialistCount(eSpecialist)) *
        owner.getSpecialistExtraYield(eSpecialist, eYield)

and applies the resulting delta through `changeBaseYieldRate`.

Therefore the candidate can change the construction city's actual base yield through specialists
that ALREADY exist in that city, even when the candidate has no ordinary YieldChange or YieldModifier.
The BUG helper evaluates all of those specialists using the player's PRE-BUILD specialist-extra-yield
state and contains no overlay for the candidate's new global SpecialistYieldChanges.

CLEAN CURRENT-SAS FIXTURE - ANGKOR WAT
--------------------------------------
Current SAS `BUILDING_ANGKOR_WAT` has:

    SpecialistYieldChanges:
        SPECIALIST_PRIEST -> +1 Production, +1 raw Commerce

For the Production-yield projection it has no confounding direct producer:

    YieldChanges(PRODUCTION)                 = 0
    YieldModifiers(PRODUCTION)               = 0
    PowerYieldModifiers(PRODUCTION)          = 0
    Sea/River/GlobalSeaPlotYieldChanges      = 0
    Area/GlobalYieldModifiers                = 0
    TradeRouteModifier / ForeignTradeRoute   = 0
    FreeSpecialistCounts                     = none

Take an active-owned city with exactly one assigned Priest, no pre-existing Priest specialist-extra
Production, and an ordinary 100% base Production modifier. Let Angkor Wat be constructible there.

Before completion:
    Priest extra Production from Angkor Wat = 0

BUG hypothetical calculation:
    getAdditionalBaseYieldRateByBuilding(PRODUCTION, ANGKOR_WAT) = 0
    getAdditionalYieldRateModifierByBuilding(PRODUCTION, ANGKOR_WAT) = 0
    => getAdditionalYieldByBuilding(...) = 0

Actual completion:
    CvPlayer::processBuilding(ANGKOR_WAT, +1, ...)
      -> changeSpecialistExtraYield(PRIEST, PRODUCTION, +1)
      -> city updateExtraSpecialistYield(PRODUCTION)
      -> one existing Priest contributes +1 new base Production
      -> changeBaseYieldRate(PRODUCTION, +1)

So the same city immediately changes by +1 real Production while the helper can report +0.
The current SAS addition of +1 raw Commerce to the same Priests supplies a second yield-domain
manifestation of the same omitted SpecialistYieldChanges root.

CURRENT-DATA BREADTH
--------------------
Current SAS has three nonzero building SpecialistYieldChanges producers:

* `BUILDING_ANGKOR_WAT`: Priest +1 Production, +1 raw Commerce;
* `BUILDING_BROADWAY`: Artist +2 raw Commerce;
* `BUILDING_CRISTO_REDENTOR`: Priest +1 Production, +1 raw Commerce.

Cristo Redentor additionally grants one free Priest. That exposes an interaction the repair must
handle: the existing BUG helper values candidate free specialists through
`getAdditionalBaseYieldRateBySpecialist`, which uses the OLD player specialist-extra-yield state.
The newly granted free Priest should receive the candidate's own Priest yield bonus too. More
generally, if C matching specialists already exist, F matching free specialists are added by the
candidate, current extra yield is E and the candidate adds D, the omitted base-yield component is
not merely C*D; the new specialists also need D, i.e. `(C + F) * D` in addition to the helper's
already-modeled `F * (intrinsic + E)` term.

LIVE USER-FACING CALLERS
------------------------
The defect is not a dead helper.

1. Building Actual Effects:
   `CvGameTextMgr::setBuildingNetEffectsHelp` describes itself as appending the "actual (i.e.
   absolute) effects" of adding a building. It calls `getAdditionalYieldByBuilding` for every yield.
   For an active-owned city this path is available by holding Alt on the building hover (or enabling
   the corresponding BUG option).

2. Production hover:
   `CvGameTextMgr::setProductionHelp` enables `setBuildingAdditionalYieldHelp(...,
   YIELD_PRODUCTION, ...)` when Alt is held or `MiscHover__BuildingAdditionalProduction` is enabled.
   That helper enumerates currently constructible buildings and calls the same city projection.

Thus an ordinary Alt hover in the Angkor-Wat fixture can omit the +1 Production that completion will
immediately create in the city.

ANCESTRY / CLASSIFICATION
-------------------------
K-Mod 1.46 already contains the BUG Building Additional Yield helpers with the same omission: after
direct/plot/trade effects it accounts for candidate free specialists but does not overlay the
candidate's `SpecialistYieldChanges` player state.

K-Mod's shipped Angkor Wat already supplies a live positive-control producer (Priest +1 Production),
so the defect predates SAS data changes. Base AdvCiv 1.14 inherits the helper. Current SAS retains it
and broadens the visible current-data witnesses. The supplied Civ4CE/BtS core does not contain this
BUG helper layer.

Classification:
    inherited BUG/K-Mod hypothetical-building yield-projection defect retained by AdvCiv/SAS.

DEDUP / ROOT BOUNDARY
---------------------
Whole-album searches found no numbered root owning candidate `SpecialistYieldChanges` omission in
`getAdditionalYieldByBuilding`.

It is distinct from:

* F398 / KI#721 - the SAME broad yield helper wrongly treats military/domain/space ORDER-SPECIFIC
  production modifiers as generic Production yield. F578 instead omits a REAL base-yield change
  produced by candidate-driven player specialist-yield state; fixing F398 does not fix F578.
* F561 / KI#884 - arithmetic/order loss in the trade-yield branch of
  `getAdditionalBaseYieldRateByBuilding`; F578 survives with no trade routes at all.
* F577 / KI#900 - the commerce projection omits candidate-driven
  SpecialistExtraCommerce/StateReligionCommerce. F578 is a different helper and authoritative state
  (`SpecialistExtraYield`) feeding base YIELDS rather than final CommerceTypes output.
* KI#306 broadened - the AI top-production-city cache can remain stale AFTER a SpecialistYieldChanges
  building mutates city production. F578 is wrong BEFORE-BUILD hypothetical calculation; even a
  perfectly invalidated KI#306 cache leaves this projection at +0.

The early album reference to Angkor Wat/Cristo Redentor SpecialistYieldChanges belongs to the KI#306
cache proof and is therefore a useful runtime oracle, not a duplicate of F578.

REPAIR DIRECTION - NOT IMPLEMENTED
----------------------------------
Extend the hypothetical base-yield state to include the candidate's
`SpecialistYieldChanges` for the construction city.

For each `(SpecialistTypes s, YieldTypes y, delta D)` supplied by the candidate:

1. count the city's current assigned + explicitly free specialists of type s;
2. include candidate `FreeSpecialistCounts(s)` in the post-building count;
3. add the post-state delta caused by D for all those specialists;
4. ensure candidate free specialists are not valued twice - the existing free-specialist helper may
   continue to add their intrinsic/current-extra yield, while the new overlay adds only the
   candidate-driven D portion.

A robust implementation should construct one coherent hypothetical post-building specialist state
rather than bolt isolated terms together; that avoids the same interaction mistake F577 exposed in
commerce projection.

This helper's local-city contract does not require summing the candidate's SpecialistYieldChanges
across every other city in the empire. It does, however, have to include the construction city's own
immediate real yield change if it claims "total additional yield" for that city.

and the define comment itself says 0 is recommended. Therefore the cultural-owner branch is not a

NEGATIVE CONTROL - ORDINARY CULTURE PROCESS DOES NOT HAVE A LEVEL-0 STOP-MARKER HOLE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
K-Mod's human Culture-process metadata stores the current culture level in `OrderData::iData2` and
later stops the process when:

    iData2 > 0 && getCultureLevel() > iData2

At first glance, a human process started at culture level 0 would never stop at its first expansion.
Current SAS culture-level data and `calculateCultureLevel()` close that ordinary case: both
`CULTURELEVEL_NONE` and `CULTURELEVEL_POOR` have threshold 0, and the calculation scans levels in
reverse. Therefore an ordinary non-occupation city with zero culture evaluates to
`CULTURELEVEL_POOR` (1), not NONE (0), and receives a positive marker. Level NONE is primarily the
forced occupation state; occupation ending is not a clean ordinary "culture process expanded from
level 0" witness. Existing F494 remains the real unhandled Culture-process metadata transition (AI
Auto Play hand-back). No F579.

PRODUCTION LIFECYCLE CONTROL - MAKING COUNTERS / PROCESS HEAD STATE
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Rechecked `pushOrder`, `popOrder`, `startHeadOrder`, `stopHeadOrder`, and `processProcess` against the
already-audited making-count family.

* Valid ORDER_TRAIN / ORDER_CONSTRUCT / ORDER_CREATE insertion increments exactly the matching
  player/team making counter before the node is installed.
* `popOrder` decrements the counter encoded by the concrete queue node before deletion/completion;
  saved-repeat insertion gives the intentional temporary +1 then -1 net state already frozen in
  the earlier counter control.
* `startHeadOrder` / `stopHeadOrder` intentionally mutate only ORDER_MAINTAIN's
  ProductionToCommerce modifiers. Unit/building/project making state belongs to queue membership,
  not head position, so reordering the head does not require making-counter changes.
* The duplicate `cityBuildingUnit` / `cityBuildingBuilding` reporter dispatch in `pushOrder` is the
  already-frozen logging/UI-quality control; current shipped handlers do not establish a new
  authoritative queue/state mutation.

No independent F579.

ROBUSTNESS ONLY - `bPop` REMOVES OLD HEAD BEFORE NEW ORDER VALIDATION
---------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvCity::pushOrder(..., bPop=true)` performs `popOrder(0)` before validating the replacement order.
Thus a stale/malformed caller could erase the existing head and then fail `canTrain` / `canConstruct`
/ `canCreate` / `canMaintain`, leaving no replacement. The normal city UI/network path supplies
`bPop=true` for direct replacement clicks, but this tranche did not establish a deterministic
ordinary current-SAS producer in which the displayed order is legal at click time and becomes
illegal before deterministic message execution. Preserve as multiplayer/API hardening unless a
concrete current transition is proved; no F579.

not create a current zero-divisor/random-domain failure.

`isMeltdownBuildingSuperseded()` also orders same-dirtiness sources coherently: larger
NukeExplosionRand means lower one-in-N meltdown probability and therefore a safer source; clean
power supersedes dirty power. No current free/multiple-risk source combination was established that
breaks this ordering. No F579.

AREA CLEAN-POWER / YIELD-RANK INVALIDATION CONTROL
--------------------------------------------------
A promising local inconsistency closes after tracing the whole caller chain. `CvCity::changePowerCount`
explicitly invalidates the owner's yield-rank cache when local `isPower()` changes, while
`CvArea::changeCleanPowerCount()` visibly calls only team `updateCommerce()` / `updatePowerHealth()`.
This initially looked able to leave Factory-style power Production changes out of cached
`findYieldRateRank()` results after area-wide clean power (e.g. Three Gorges) toggles.

The indirect chain is sufficient, however:

    CvArea::changeCleanPowerCount
      -> CvTeam::updateCommerce
      -> each member CvPlayer::updateCommerce()
      -> each city CvCity::updateCommerce()
      -> GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).invalidateYieldRankCache()

Thus area-wide clean-power transitions do invalidate yield ranks before the cache can remain stale.
No F579.

CORPORATION HEADQUARTERS / REPLACEMENT REACHABILITY CONTROL
------------------------------------------------------------
`CvCity::setHasCorporation()` contains an inherited branch that, if a newly-added corporation
competes with a corporation headquartered in the same city, calls
`CvGame::replaceCorporation(old,new)`. The replacement function converts every old-corporation city
and kills old executives but does not visibly retarget/clear the old global headquarters pointer.
This is structurally fragile and inherited from BtS/K-Mod.

Ordinary current-SAS reachability closes the candidate: `CvUnit::canSpreadCorporation()` explicitly
rejects spreading a corporation into a city that is headquarters of a competing corporation. Normal
city acquisition restores only the corporation set the city already possessed, and normal
corporation founding does not use this replacement route. Therefore the stale-HQ-pointer shape needs
a lower-level/script/injected state rather than a demonstrated shipped executive path. Preserve as
robustness/API hardening; no F579.

HEADQUARTERS FREE-UNIT CONTROL
------------------------------
`CvCity::setHeadquarters()` grants the corporation's configured `FreeUnitClass` after calling
`CvGame::setHeadquarters()`, so repeated wrapper calls would be dangerous. Current native callers are
bounded: `CvPlayer::foundCorporation()` returns if the corporation is already founded, and building
processing invokes the wrapper only while `!isCorporationFounded`. Acquisition and Python
WorldBuilder-style headquarters manipulation use the lower-level `CvGame::setHeadquarters()` and do
not award the wrapper free unit. No ordinary repeat-award route established; no F579.

PRODUCTION AUTOMATION CLEAR-QUEUE CONTROL
------------------------------------------
`CvCity::setProductionAutomated(bNewValue,bClear)` clears the order queue only inside
`isActiveOwned() && isCitySelected()`. This would be surprising for an arbitrary programmatic
`bNewValue=true,bClear=true` call on an unselected city, but current callers do not establish such a
case: the UI task is dispatched to selected cities, Python passes `bClear=false`, and RiseFall's
`bClear=true` call disables automation (`bNewValue=false`). Current behavior is therefore caller-
contract dependent but not a demonstrated gameplay defect. No F579.

CULTURE UPDATE TIMER ASSERTION - INHERITED DEBUG CONTRACT BUG ONLY
------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvCity::setCultureUpdateTimer(int iNewValue)` contains an inherited copy/paste assertion:

    m_iCultureUpdateTimer = iNewValue;
    FAssert(getOccupationTimer() >= 0);

The assertion plainly checks the wrong timer; K-Mod/AdvC carry the same defect. Current native callers
add positive mission/event revolt turns, decrement only while `getCultureUpdateTimer() > 0`, or reset
to 0, so no shipped native path was found that relies on the missing nonnegative assertion. This is
a real debug/API robustness defect but does not meet the current-live bar for F579.

ANGER / OCCUPATION INITIAL CONTROL
----------------------------------
The basic overcrowding/hurry/conscript/defy anger formulas and occupation transition setters were
re-read while looking for signed-divisor and mutation-order mistakes. `getOvercrowdingPercentAnger`
uses identical positive population terms in numerator/denominator by design to generate the base
one-citizen overcrowding anger in permillage units. Hurry/conscript/defy timers guard zero before
using their positive flat lengths; occupation transitions perform corporation/maintenance/trade/
commerce/culture updates on the actual boolean occupation-state edge. No independent current defect
was established in this slice.

================================================================================
C031-WIP369 - QUEUE 006 CVCITY.CPP / HURRY-ANGER MODIFIER RESCALE ROUNDING, F579
================================================================================

HANDOFF / SOURCE STONE
----------------------
Resumed from C031-WIP368 with F578 / KI#901 confirmed and F579 / provisional KI#902 unused.
Queue 006 `CvGameCoreDLL/CvCity.cpp` remains OPEN. Current SAS, Base AdvCiv 1.14, K-Mod 1.46 and
Civ4CE/BtS supplied trees were checked locally. Actual AdvCiv-SAS source remains UNTOUCHED.

POST-WIP368 CONTROLS BEFORE PROMOTION
-------------------------------------
1. `CvCity::getReligionGrip()` has an apparently unguarded `GET_PLAYER(cultOwner)` after
   `calculateCulturalOwner()`. The dereference is nevertheless protected by a stronger implication:
   the enclosing branch first requires `revoltProbability(true,false,true) > 0`, and
   `revoltProbability` itself calls the same `calculateCulturalOwner()` and returns exactly 0 for
   `NO_PLAYER`, same-team cultural owners and disabled Barbarian revolt owners. There is no
   intervening mutation. Thus a positive result guarantees a valid cultural-owner PlayerTypes.
   No F579 on that sentinel path.

F579 / KI#902 - CONFIRMED
-------------------------
CHANGING A CITY'S HURRY-ANGER MODIFIER RESCALES THE STORED TIMER USING THE RAW PERCENT MODIFIER
INSTEAD OF THE ACTUAL INTEGER `flatHurryAngerLength()`. ON SHIPPED SPEEDS WHERE THE FLAT LENGTH HAS
ALREADY ROUNDED, ADDING/REMOVING THE AZTEC SACRIFICIAL ALTAR CAN CREATE OR DELETE WHOLE WHIP-ANGER
STACKS. CURRENT SAS'S STONEHENGE -> FREE MONUMENT MAPPING PROVIDES AN ORDINARY EMPIRE-WIDE PRODUCER.

ROOT
----
The authoritative number of hurry-anger layers for a positive timer is:

    ((getHurryAngerTimer() - 1) / flatHurryAngerLength()) + 1

i.e. `ceil(timer / actualFlatLength)`.

But `changeHurryAngerModifier()` does not rescale against that actual old/new flat length. It uses:

    iRatio = (100 * (m_iHurryAngerTimer - 1)) /
             max(1, 100 + oldModifier);
    m_iHurryAngerModifier += iChange;
    m_iHurryAngerTimer = (iRatio *
             max(1, 100 + newModifier)) / 100 + 1;

That is equivalent only when the speed-scaled base hurry length and the modifier produce exact
integer lengths. `flatHurryAngerLength()` performs a separate integer truncation:

    base = CvGame::getHurryAngerLength();
    length = base * max(0,100+modifier) / 100;
    return max(1,length);

so the raw modifier ratio and the actual timer cycle can diverge.

CURRENT SAS SPEED WITNESSES
---------------------------
Stock/current `HURRY_ANGER_DIVISOR` is 10. Current SAS game speeds include:

    Turbo: HurryConscriptAngerPercent = 50  -> base length 5
    Nitro: HurryConscriptAngerPercent = 33  -> base length 3
    Epic:  HurryConscriptAngerPercent = 150 -> base length 15

The current Aztec Sacrificial Altar has `iHurryAngerModifier = -50`.
Therefore the actual modified flat lengths are:

    Turbo: 5 * 50 / 100 = 2   (not 2.5)
    Nitro: 3 * 50 / 100 = 1   (not 1.5)
    Epic: 15 * 50 / 100 = 7   (not 7.5)

Normal (10 -> 5), Quick (6 -> 3), Marathon/SAS slow speeds with even base lengths are controls where
this particular -50% transition is exact and the inherited formula happens to preserve the stack
cycle.

DETERMINISTIC CURRENT-SAS TURBO FIXTURE - REMOVAL DELETES AN ANGER STACK
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS deliberately maps:

    CIVILIZATION_AZTEC
      BUILDINGCLASS_MONUMENT -> BUILDING_AZTEC_SACRIFICIAL_ALTAR

and current Stonehenge has:

    FreeBuilding = BUILDINGCLASS_MONUMENT

`CvPlayer::processBuilding(STONEHENGE,+1)` therefore gives the Aztec player a free Sacrificial
Altar in every eligible city through `changeFreeBuildingCount`; losing Stonehenge removes those
free Altars through the symmetric `-1` path.

On Turbo while the free Altar is active:

    base hurry length = 5
    modifier = -50
    actual flat hurry length = 2

Repeated human whipping naturally creates timer 3:

1. First whip after the city turn: timer 2.
2. Next city turn decrements it to 1.
3. A second legal whip after that city turn adds another 2: timer 3.

Authoritative current anger count is then:

    ((3 - 1) / 2) + 1 = 2 stacks.

Now let an enemy capture the Aztec city containing Stonehenge. City destruction/acquisition removes
Stonehenge from the old owner; player building processing immediately drops the empire-wide free
Monument source, so every remaining Aztec free Sacrificial Altar is removed. In a target city with
`timer=3`, `changeHurryAngerModifier(+50)` runs:

    old modifier = -50
    iRatio = 100 * (3 - 1) / 50 = 4
    new modifier = 0
    new timer = 4 * 100 / 100 + 1 = 5

The new actual flat hurry length is 5, hence authoritative anger becomes:

    ((5 - 1) / 5) + 1 = 1 stack.

One entire whip-anger layer has disappeared because a duration-reduction source was REMOVED.
Nothing paid off or decremented that layer; the source transition itself destroyed it.

The inverse direction is also wrong on affected speeds. Turbo timer 5 with no modifier is one
anger stack; adding -50 through the current formula gives timer 3 while actual new length is 2,
which is interpreted as two stacks until a later decrement. The removal fixture is the cleaner
persistent gameplay proof because it deletes an existing stack and does not rely on observing a
short intra-city-turn state.

WHY THE STONEHENGE LOSS PATH IS ORDINARY AND PERSISTENT
-------------------------------------------------------
`BUILDING_STONEHENGE` is a live world wonder in current SAS and grants the Monument class for free.
`CvPlayer::changeFreeBuildingCount` loops every city and calls `setNumFreeBuilding`; a 1->0 building
count transition calls the city's normal `processBuilding`, including
`changeHurryAngerModifier(+50)` for the Sacrificial Altar.

When another player captures the Stonehenge city, the old city's real buildings are removed during
its kill/acquisition lifecycle, so the old owner loses the free-building source immediately. The
remaining Aztec city's transformed timer persists as ordinary serialized city state. On its next
turn it starts from the already-wrong one-stack representation; this is not merely a tooltip or a
single-expression preview.

ANCESTRY
--------
The timer-rescale implementation is inherited unchanged through:

- supplied Civ4CE/BtS;
- K-Mod 1.46;
- Base AdvCiv 1.14;
- current AdvCiv-SAS.

Thus the arithmetic defect is inherited Firaxis behavior. Current SAS gives it an especially clean
ordinary producer because the mod maps the Aztec Sacrificial Altar to Monument while Stonehenge
still grants `BUILDINGCLASS_MONUMENT` empire-wide, and SAS additionally ships very fast speeds such
as Turbo/Nitro whose integer half-lengths expose the mismatch strongly. Epic already demonstrates
the same rounding family at 15 -> 7.

DEDUP / ROOT SEPARATION
-----------------------
Whole-album searches for `changeHurryAngerModifier`, timer rescaling, Sacrificial Altar timer
rounding and Stonehenge/Sacrificial interactions found no prior numbered owner.

Distinct from:

- F492 / KI#815: No-Slavery Sacrificial-Altar pop-rush entitlement is mis-cached when the building
  is completed while the human is disabled by AI Auto Play. F579 changes authoritative hurry-anger
  timer arithmetic regardless of No Slavery or human-disabled state.
- F530 / KI#853: `CvCityAI::AI_yieldValue` uses the wrong modulo to PREDICT the next anger-stack
  expiry. F579 mutates the authoritative `m_iHurryAngerTimer` itself during a modifier transition.
- F537 / KI#860: the same AI valuation counts at most one future recovery per anger source. Again,
  F579 is runtime city state, not AI prediction.
- F574/F575 transfer-state findings: no ownership-copy omission is required; Stonehenge capture is
  merely one normal producer of the free-building source transition.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Rescale against the actual old and new integer flat hurry lengths, not the raw percentage modifier.
Conceptually:

    oldLength = flatHurryAngerLength();
    oldTimer = m_iHurryAngerTimer;
    m_iHurryAngerModifier += iChange;
    newLength = flatHurryAngerLength();
    if (oldTimer > 0)
        m_iHurryAngerTimer = ((oldTimer - 1) * newLength) / oldLength + 1;

Using `(timer - 1)` preserves the existing cycle-phase convention; using actual lengths preserves
stack count/phase across the discrete speed rounding that the current raw-modifier formula ignores.
Use a widened intermediate if desired even though current timer magnitudes are small. Do not alter
normal decrement cadence or `getHurryPercentAnger()`.

For the Turbo removal fixture:

    old timer=3, old length=2, new length=5
    repaired timer = ((3-1)*5)/2 + 1 = 6
    repaired stacks = ceil(6/5) = 2
    next stack drop = ((6-1)%5)+1 = 1 turn

which preserves both the two-stack count and the one-turn phase to the next drop.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Turbo remove -50 source
- old length 2, timer 3, assert 2 stacks;
- remove Sacrificial-Altar source;
- assert resulting state still has 2 stacks and same relative next-drop phase.

B. Turbo add -50 source
- old length 5, timer 5, assert 1 stack;
- add source;
- assert no transient second authoritative stack is created by the conversion.

Repeat 0 <-> -50 on Normal (10 <-> 5) and Quick (6 <-> 3); repaired behavior should agree with the
current implementation where integer scaling is already exact.

- on Turbo create timer 3 in the second city through two normally spaced whips;

- assert free Altar disappears but the second city's preexisting two whip-anger layers are not
  collapsed to one by the source transition.

================================================================================
C031-WIP371 - F580 / KI#903: resource health sign-flip UI invalidation uses bad-health with wrong sign
================================================================================

STATUS
------
Queue 006 `CvGameCoreDLL/CvCity.cpp` remains OPEN.
F559/KI#882 through F580/KI#903 are CONFIRMED.
F581 / provisional KI#904 is UNUSED.
Actual AdvCiv-SAS source remains UNTOUCHED.

F580 / KI#903 - CONFIRMED CURRENT ADVC RESOURCE-STATUS INVALIDATION DEFECT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
Title:
`CvCity::processBonus()` subtracts an already-negative bad-health/bad-happiness component when
predicting whether a resource change crosses the healthy/happy boundary, so current negative
building-resource health can skip the `CityInfo_DIRTY_BIT` refresh that advc.001w was specifically
added to provide after resource trades.

ROOT
----
Current `CvCity::processBonus()` accumulates resource health in the normal signed representation:

    iGoodValue >= 0
    iBadValue  <= 0

and runtime applies those values directly:

    changeBonusGoodHealth(iGoodValue * iChange);
    changeBonusBadHealth(iBadValue * iChange);

Therefore the actual health-rate delta represented by this block is:

    (iGoodValue + iBadValue) * iChange

Before applying it, however, advc.001w predicts whether the active-owned city crosses the
healthy/unhealthy boundary with:

    iHealth + (iGoodValue - iBadValue) * iChange

Since `iBadValue` is already negative, subtracting it reverses the sign of every bad component.
A pure -2 health resource effect is therefore predicted as +2.

The happiness half contains the same arithmetic shape:

    iHappy + (iGoodValue - iBadValue) * iChange

but current SAS XML has no negative `BonusHappinessChanges`, so the health branch supplies the
current shipped-game proof; the happiness expression is the same generic/future-proofing breadth.

CURRENT SAS XML PROOF
---------------------
Current `CIV4BonusInfos.xml` gives both Coal and Oil:

    iHealth = 0
    iHappiness = 0

Current `CIV4BuildingInfos.xml` contains exactly four negative building-resource health entries:

    BUILDING_FACTORY:
        BONUS_OIL  -> -2 health
        BONUS_COAL -> -2 health

    BUILDING_INDUSTRIAL_PARK:
        BONUS_OIL  -> -1 health
        BONUS_COAL -> -1 health

Thus negative `iBadValue` is not hypothetical mod-mod data; ordinary Factory/Industrial-Park cities
produce it in current SAS.

CLEAN CURRENT RUNTIME FIXTURE - FACTORY + COAL
----------------------------------------------
Take an active-human city that:

1. has an active Factory;
2. does not yet have Coal;
3. currently has `healthRate() == +1`;
4. then receives one connected Coal through an ordinary resource trade or any ordinary plot-group
   connection change.

Immediately before `processBonus(BONUS_COAL,+1)`:

    iGoodValue = 0
    iBadValue  = -2
    iHealth    = +1

The real city-state transition is:

    +1 + (0 + -2) = -1

so the city crosses healthy -> unhealthy.

The advc.001w pre-check instead evaluates:

    +1 + (0 - -2) = +3

and concludes that the sign has not changed. It therefore skips:

    gDLL->UI().setDirty(CityInfo_DIRTY_BIT, true);

The reverse disconnection is symmetric. Starting from `healthRate() == -1` and removing Coal
(`iChange=-1`), real state becomes +1 while the predictor evaluates -3 and again misses the
unhealthy -> healthy boundary.

ORDINARY RESOURCE-TRADE PRODUCER / MASKING TRACE
------------------------------------------------
The current annual resource-deal path is direct:

    CvDeal::startTrade(TRADE_RESOURCES)
      -> CvPlayer::changeBonusImport / changeBonusExport
      -> capital plot `updatePlotGroupBonus`
      -> CvPlotGroup::changeNumBonuses
      -> CvCity::changeNumBonuses
      -> CvCity::processBonus

`CvDeal::startTrade` performs no blanket `CityInfo_DIRTY_BIT` invalidation after the resource case.
`CvPlot.cpp` and `CvPlotGroup.cpp` contain no `CityInfo_DIRTY_BIT` setter. The resource plot-group
path therefore does not supply a later independent global refresh that would make the advc.001w
pre-check irrelevant.

The `changeBonusGoodHealth` / `changeBonusBadHealth` mutators do call `setInfoDirty(true)` for the
active team, and that local city dirty state predates advc.001w. It does not invalidate this finding:
practical 1387 deliberately added the separate `CityInfo_DIRTY_BIT` sign-boundary check precisely
because the pre-existing local dirtying did not reliably refresh the healthy/happy city status after
resource trades. F580 is the arithmetic bug inside that dedicated reliability fix.

ANCESTRY / INTENT
-----------------
The signed pre-check was introduced by AdvC practical commit 1387,
`40f76ddd83320144401c2d172b8315da3f0b3ef4`, titled `Misc. tweaks and bugfixes`, under tag
`advc.001w`.

Its commit message explicitly says:

    Happy and healthy status on city billboards is (reliably) updated after the players signs a
    resource trade. [advc.001w]

Supplied K-Mod 1.46 and Civ4CE BtS have no corresponding pre-check in `processBonus`; they simply
apply the signed good and bad values. AdvC 1.14 and current SAS retain the exact
`iGoodValue - iBadValue` predictor. The defect is therefore an AdvC bug introduced inside a UI
reliability fix, not inherited Firaxis/K-Mod arithmetic.

DEDUP / ROOT SEPARATION
-----------------------
Whole-album searches for `processBonus`, `advc.001w`, `CityInfo_DIRTY_BIT`, resource-health
boundary invalidation, Factory/Coal resource-health UI and the signed expression found no prior
numbered owner.

Distinct from:

- the numerous bonus-trade AI valuation findings: those affect deal legality/value, not city status
  invalidation after a resource actually changes;
- F433/KI#756: wrong-player `setBonusHelpDirty()` after world-wonder resource-help changes; that is
  the Resource globe/help cache and a wrong receiver, while F580 is the city healthy/unhealthy
  status dirty bit and wrong signed arithmetic;
- F397 and related building-preview findings: hypothetical building health/happiness valuation, not
  authoritative resource-state mutation/UI invalidation;
- F563/F564/F566/F567 and other Queue-006 production/state roots: no production validation or city
  acquisition is involved here.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Use the same signed net delta for the pre-check that runtime is about to apply:

    if ((iHealth < 0) !=
        (iHealth + (iGoodValue + iBadValue) * iChange < 0))
    {
        gDLL->UI().setDirty(CityInfo_DIRTY_BIT, true);
    }

and analogously for happiness:

    iHappy + (iGoodValue + iBadValue) * iChange

This is the smallest behavior-preserving repair and exactly matches the signed storage convention
already consumed by `changeBonusGood*` / `changeBonusBad*`. Do not take absolute values or change
the good/bad accumulators themselves.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Factory + Coal connect
- active-human Factory city, no Coal, `healthRate()==+1`;
- connect/import Coal;
- assert final `healthRate()==-1` and `CityInfo_DIRTY_BIT` is requested.

B. Factory + Coal disconnect
- same city with Coal and `healthRate()==-1`;
- disconnect/cancel Coal;
- assert final `healthRate()==+1` and dirty bit is requested.

C. Industrial Park one-point control
- use `iBadValue=-1` and a city immediately on either side of zero;
- verify both add/remove sign crossings dirty correctly.

D. Ordinary positive health control
- resource/building combination with positive BonusHealthChange;
- fixed expression should agree with the old expression when `iBadValue==0`.

E. Mixed good + bad robustness
- synthetic or future XML with both signs for one bonus;
- assert the predictor equals the actual signed net delta rather than sum of magnitudes.

F. Happiness breadth
- synthetic negative `BonusHappinessChanges` fixture;
- assert the analogous sign crossing uses `good + bad`. Current SAS has no negative producer, so
  this is defense-in-depth rather than the current proof.

===============================================================================
C031-WIP372 - QUEUE 006 CVCITY.CPP CONTINUATION - F581 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F581 / KI#904 - PROSPECTIVE-OWNER CITY MAINTENANCE FORGETS TO COUNT THE CITY
ITSELF IN NUMBER-OF-CITIES / COLONY STATE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv prospective-maintenance / AI-valuation defect.
Current SAS data and ordinary city-trade / UWAI conquest callers are live.

ROOT
----
AdvCiv added an optional `PlayerTypes eOwner` to the member maintenance helpers and documents the
parameter in `CvCity.h` as:

    Added an optional parameter to allow the computation of
    projected maintenance for cities yet to be conquered.

The member wrappers then evaluate the foreign city under the requested prospective owner:

    int CvCity::calculateNumCitiesMaintenanceTimes100(PlayerTypes eOwner) const
    {
        return calculateNumCitiesMaintenanceTimes100(getPlot(),
                eOwner == NO_PLAYER ? getOwner() : eOwner,
                getPopulation());
    }

    int CvCity::calculateColonyMaintenanceTimes100(PlayerTypes eOwner) const
    {
        return calculateColonyMaintenanceTimes100(getPlot(),
                eOwner == NO_PLAYER ? getOwner() : eOwner,
                getPopulation());
    }

However the static helpers they delegate to explicitly have an `iExtraCities` parameter for
hypothetical additions, defaulting to 0:

    static int calculateNumCitiesMaintenanceTimes100(...,
            int iPopulation = -1, int iExtraCities = 0);
    static int calculateColonyMaintenanceTimes100(...,
            int iPopulation = -1, int iExtraCities = 0);

and use it in exactly the state that differs before vs. after ownership transfer:

    int iMaintenanceCities = kOwner.getNumCities() + iExtraCities + ...;

and:

    int iNumCities =
        (kCityArea.getCitiesPerPlayer(eOwner) - 1 + iExtraCities) *
        iNumCitiesPercent;

The member wrappers never pass `1` when `eOwner != getOwner()`. They therefore ask the prospective
owner's CURRENT city and area-city counts to stand in for the POST-ACQUISITION counts while the
foreign candidate city is not yet included in either count.

The correct ownership-state invariant is simple:

- current owner: the city is already included -> `iExtraCities = 0`;
- different prospective owner: the city is not yet included -> `iExtraCities = 1`.

NUMBER-OF-CITIES MAINTENANCE - CLEAN SAME-AREA FAILURE
------------------------------------------------------
Take an ordinary trade/acquisition of a foreign city located in the prospective recipient's capital
area. Colony maintenance is therefore 0 both before and after transfer, so no colony arithmetic can
mask the count error.

Let the prospective recipient currently own N cities.

Before transfer, the buggy prospective wrapper computes the candidate city's number-of-cities
maintenance from:

    N + 0

because `GET_PLAYER(eOwner).getNumCities()` does not include the still-foreign candidate.

Immediately after transfer, authoritative runtime maintenance on that same city computes from:

    N + 1

because the city now belongs to eOwner and is included in `getNumCities()`.

Thus the city's own post-acquisition number-of-cities maintenance is systematically understated by
one full city-count unit in the prospective evaluation whenever the cap has not saturated.

This is not supplied by the heuristic directly below the call in `AI_assetVal`:

    // Estimate incr. civic upkeep and incr. maint. in other cities
    rMaintCost += ... * getNumCities();

The comment explicitly identifies that term as the incremental cost in OTHER cities (and civic
upkeep). It scales with the recipient's existing city count; it does not make the candidate city's
own maintenance helper use the post-acquisition N+1 count.

COLONY MAINTENANCE - FIRST-OVERSEAS-CITY SIGNATURE
--------------------------------------------------
The colony formula makes the hidden state assumption even more obvious.

Suppose the prospective owner has its capital on another land area and currently has zero cities in
the candidate city's area.

Prospective wrapper before acquisition:

    kCityArea.getCitiesPerPlayer(eOwner) = 0
    iExtraCities = 0
    -> (0 - 1 + 0) * iNumCitiesPercent
    -> a negative value, then SQR(...)
    -> positive projected colony maintenance (subject to its positive cap)

Actual runtime immediately after acquiring that first city in the area:

    kCityArea.getCitiesPerPlayer(eOwner) = 1
    iExtraCities = 0
    -> (1 - 1 + 0) = 0
    -> exactly 0 colony maintenance

So the projection can invent positive colony maintenance for the recipient's FIRST city in an
overseas area, even though the post-transfer runtime formula correctly charges zero. If the
recipient already has one or more cities in that area, the same missing +1 instead evaluates one
fewer "other colony city" than the actual post-transfer state.

CURRENT ORDINARY AI CALLER - CITY TRADE
---------------------------------------
`CvPlayerAI::AI_cityTradeVal` explicitly documents its acquisition case:

    If eToPlayer is this player: How much this player values acquiring kCity
    from its current owner.

For that case, the prospective recipient evaluates the still-foreign city through:

    scaled r = AI_assetVal(kCity, false);

`AI_assetVal` determines:

    bool const bOwn = (c.getOwner() == getID());

so `bOwn` is false for the acquisition case, and later subtracts:

    scaled rMaintCost = per100(c.calculateBaseMaintenanceTimes100(getID()));

`calculateBaseMaintenanceTimes100(getID())` delegates to the three owner-parameter maintenance
members above. Distance maintenance can legitimately use the prospective owner's current
capital/government-center set. Number-of-cities and colony maintenance cannot: those two require the
candidate city to be added to the prospective owner's count state first.

The erroneous result therefore directly changes AI city-trade acquisition values and, consequently,
trade price / willingness calculations.

CURRENT ORDINARY AI CALLER - UWAI CONQUEST ASSET SCORE
-------------------------------------------------------
The same helper is not limited to peaceful city trades.

`UWAICache::rebuildCities()` constructs cache-city entries for known teams, and
`UWAICache::City` calls:

    updateAssetScore(eCacheOwner);

which stores:

    m_iAssetScore =
        (GET_PLAYER(eCacheOwner).AI_assetVal(city().AI(), true) / 2).round();

For a foreign target city, `eCacheOwner` is the prospective conqueror while the city is still owned
by its current player. The same `calculateBaseMaintenanceTimes100(getID())` call therefore uses the
missing-city count state in conquest asset valuation too. This can feed UWAI target/war valuation,
not merely diplomacy.

CURRENT DATA / NONZERO REACHABILITY
-----------------------------------
The missing number-of-cities term is live under ordinary SAS settings. For example Standard world
size currently has:

    iNumCitiesMaintenancePercent = 30

and Noble has:

    iNumCitiesMaintenancePercent = 75

with ordinary positive population, crowdedness and player modifiers. Before the maintenance cap
saturates, adding one city therefore contributes a positive amount to the candidate city's own
number-of-cities maintenance. No special XML or disabled option is needed.

Standard also has positive colony-maintenance scaling (`iColonyMaintenancePercent = 45`), and Noble
has `iColonyMaintenancePercent = 100`; a sufficiently nonzero maintenance-distance cap therefore
makes the first-overseas-city `(0-1)^2` witness positive before acquisition while authoritative
post-acquisition colony maintenance is 0.

ANCESTRY
--------
The mismatch is old AdvCiv behavior rather than SAS code.

In practical 1253 / commit:

    f6ff6a182f5187541fff6e5bbbe12f9573b3778c
    "Initial commit (cont.)"

AdvC already introduces the member `eOwner` parameters with the explicit header comment about
"projected maintenance for cities yet to be conquered." The new static number-of-cities helper
already has `extraCities`, but the member wrapper passes only owner + population, leaving the
default at 0. The colony projection in that snapshot directly uses:

    (cityArea->getCitiesPerPlayer(owner) - 1)

which has the same foreign-owner count error.

Practical 1386 / commit:

    dc9c167dfc9ea3567899c58e275a2d05484d25ab
    "Refactoring and a couple of minor corrections in AdvCiv code"

adds `iExtraCities` to the static colony helper and rewrites the formula to:

    getCitiesPerPlayer(eOwner) - 1 + iExtraCities

but the prospective-owner member wrapper still does not pass 1. The refactor therefore creates the
exact repair mechanism without connecting it to the older conquered-city API.

Practical 2053 / commit:

    fd5d755af022962c4e3e09495e052fbc80bf2457
    "AI code for city trade evaluation"

introduces the current `AI_assetVal` city-trade maintenance subtraction by explicitly summing the
three `...Times100(getID())` prospective-owner members.

Practical 2463 / commit:

    fd00cf5197afe3d1c519d62ffb288ea11955e968
    "Fix maintenance calc in raze-city AI code (AdvCiv bug)"

consolidates those calls into `calculateBaseMaintenanceTimes100(getID())` while preserving the
same prospective-owner count semantics. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the omission.

DEDUP
-----
Whole-album searches for the member/static maintenance helpers, `iExtraCities`, projected/
prospective maintenance, `AI_assetVal`, city-trade maintenance and colony maintenance found no prior
numbered root owning this foreign-owner count mismatch.

Distinct from:

- F392: Settler founding-cost hover includes normal maintenance for WLTKD cities; that preview DOES
  use the static helpers with `iExtraCities=1` for founding and fails for a different no-maintenance
  state reason.
- F328: AI civic valuation cannot invert already-saturated -100% maintenance modifiers.
- F465 and nearby Queue-004 roots: vassal/team maintenance invalidation after player/team lifecycle
  changes, not prospective city acquisition arithmetic.
- F567: runtime colony-maintenance CAP double-applies MAX_DISTANCE_CITY_MAINTENANCE.
- F329: SAS prospective-city World-Wonder activity checks the current owner's obsolescence team;
  same broad city-acquisition domain, entirely different state/input.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Normalize the requested owner once and pass an extra-city count exactly when the member is being
used for a different prospective owner:

    PlayerTypes eCalcOwner = (eOwner == NO_PLAYER ? getOwner() : eOwner);
    int iExtraCities = (eCalcOwner == getOwner() ? 0 : 1);

    return calculateNumCitiesMaintenanceTimes100(
            getPlot(), eCalcOwner, getPopulation(), iExtraCities);

and analogously:

    return calculateColonyMaintenanceTimes100(
            getPlot(), eCalcOwner, getPopulation(), iExtraCities);

Distance maintenance needs no city-count adjustment. Current-owner calls remain byte-for-byte
semantically unchanged (`iExtraCities=0`). The existing `calculateBaseMaintenanceTimes100(eOwner)`
then inherits the corrected prospective behavior automatically.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Same-area acquisition / number-of-cities
- recipient has N cities, candidate is foreign and in recipient capital area;
- compare pre-transfer `candidate.calculateNumCitiesMaintenanceTimes100(recipient)` with the same
  city's actual value immediately after transfer;
- corrected prospective result must equal post-transfer result (before unrelated state changes).

B. First overseas city / colony
- recipient capital on area A, no recipient city on candidate area B;
- before transfer prospective colony maintenance must be 0;
- after transfer actual colony maintenance must also be 0.

C. Existing overseas foothold
- recipient has M>=1 cities on candidate area B;
- corrected prospective result must use M existing OTHER cities, matching post-transfer area count
  M+1 minus the candidate itself.

D. Current-owner control
- call all three member helpers with NO_PLAYER and explicit current owner;
- results must be unchanged by the repair.

  sandboxed transfer state rather than the pre-transfer N-city state.

- build a foreign `UWAICache::City` for an observer/conqueror and verify its maintenance input uses
  the observer's N+1 / area+1 hypothetical counts.

PARAMETER-VS-CURRENT-OWNER / TEAM SIEVE
----------------------------------------
F581's prospective-owner maintenance bug justified checking every low-coverage CvCity helper
where an explicit PlayerTypes/TeamTypes parameter coexists with `getOwner()` / `getTeam()`.
The strongest-looking cases in this slice close as follows.

1. `getCultureLevel(ePlayer)` - CLOSED.
   The actual owner is used only to select the city's cached culture level. For another player,
   the function computes the level from that player's culture rather than reusing the owner cache.
   This is the intended fast-path split, not an F581-style prospective-owner leak.

2. `calculateTradeTotals(..., eWithPlayer)` - CLOSED.
   `eWithPlayer` is a route-partner filter. Whether a route is domestic or foreign is correctly
   classified relative to this city's actual owner. The two concepts are intentionally different.

3. `canCultureFlip(eToPlayer, ...)` and `isMartialLaw(eRevoltPlayer)` - CLOSED.
   The explicit player parameter identifies the cultural/revolt side while defending ownership,
   war and garrison state must remain relative to the city's actual current owner/team. No hidden
   prospective transfer is implied by these APIs.

4. `doPlotCultureTimes100(..., ePlayer, ...)` - CLOSED against advc.025 semantics.
   Its capitulated-vassal reduction deliberately compares the CITY OWNER with the tile owner;
   `ePlayer` can be a different culture recipient/source in trade-culture paths. The AdvC rule is
   explicitly about culture spread BY a city owned by a capitulated vassal onto its master's tile.
   Current SAS changes the percentage but not that ownership contract.

WORLD-WONDER OBSERVER `GET_TEAM(kObs.getID())` - EXACT FALSE-POSITIVE RE-HIT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
`setNumRealBuildingTimed()` contains the superficially alarming sequence:

    CvPlayer& kObs = *it;
    ...
    GET_TEAM(kObs.getID()).isHasMet(getTeam())

This is NOT a player-ID-as-team-ID defect. It is the exact WIP340 control: because `kObs.getID()`
has type `PlayerTypes` and `CoreAI.h` supplies the overloaded `getTeam(PlayerTypes)`, overload
resolution converts through `TEAMID(ePlayer)`. Preserve as a useful type-system positive control;
do not assign F582.

`defensiveGarrison()` ENUM-AS-BOOL - LATENT RE-HIT ONLY
-------------------------------------------------------
The capital fallback still passes `pCapital->allUpgradesAvailable(...)` directly as a boolean,
where the local-city branch correctly compares the returned UnitTypes against `NO_UNIT`. Since
`NO_UNIT == -1`, that generic expression is semantically unsafe and unit type ID 0 is false.
However this is already preserved in WIP347/WIP360, and current SAS ships the associated
`DEMAND_BETTER_PROTECTION` feature disabled with its obsolete multiplier neutral. No current-live
F582 manifestation is available under shipped configuration.

`setCultureUpdateTimer()` WRONG ASSERTION - INHERITED DEBUG-CONTRACT RE-HIT
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

`failProduction()` MULTI-INSTANCE WORLD-WONDER GENERALIZATION - LATENT ONLY
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
The advc.123f failure path contains a genuine generalized-loop inconsistency. Its comment says that
if a mod-mod permits (for example) two global instances of a world wonder and two competing
instances are being built in parallel, completing one rival instance should abort only ONE of the
competing instances (the lower-investment one). But `pMinProductionCity` is declared/reset inside
the per-city loop, so the implementation would select and fail one matching order in EACH city.

That is real generic/mod-mod robustness debt. It does not qualify as current SAS F582 because the
current `CIV4BuildingClassInfos.xml` world-wonder classes all use `iMaxGlobalInstances = 1`.
At the only shipped global limit, once a rival wonder is maxed every competing instance really does
need cancellation, so the broader loop defect has no current-data witness.

CORPORATION-HQ ADDITIONAL-COMMERCE PREVIEW - WRONG HYPOTHETICAL RESULT, UNREACHABLE HERE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
All seven current corporation headquarters buildings simultaneously set `FoundsCorporation` and
`GlobalCorporationCommerce`. `getAdditionalBaseCommerceRateByBuildingImpl()` values the prospective
HQ global commerce using `countCorporationLevels(eCorp)` BEFORE construction. Before founding that
count is zero, while `processBuilding()` -> `setHeadquarters()` -> `CvGame::setHeadquarters()`
immediately calls `setHasCorporation(eCorp, true, ...)` on the founding city; the real post-build
HQ therefore has at least one corporation level. In isolation, the helper underestimates the
founding building's resulting headquarters commerce by one city's HQ-commerce contribution.

The reachability census prevents promotion: the additional-commerce-by-building helpers have no
current C++ gameplay/AI caller outside their own wrapper chain and are not exposed through CyCity /
Python in this source tree. Therefore this is an unused preview-helper correctness/API seam, not an
ordinary shipped gameplay F582.
