===============================================================================
C031-WIP375 - F582 / KI#905: PEACEFUL GOVERNMENT-CENTER TRANSFER IS OMITTED
FROM PROSPECTIVE DISTANCE MAINTENANCE / AI CITY-TRADE ACQUISITION VALUE
===============================================================================

CONTINUATION ANCHOR
-------------------
Continued from the exact C031-WIP374 stone with F582 / provisional KI#905 UNUSED and
Queue 006 `CvGameCoreDLL/CvCity.cpp` OPEN. This slice first used Civ4CE as a historical
bugfix oracle, then returned to F581's prospective-owner maintenance family only when a
mechanically distinct distance-maintenance state omission surfaced. Actual AdvCiv-SAS
repository source remains untouched.

CIV4CE EVENT-SETTER ORACLE CONTROL - DO NOT BLINDLY ASSUME CE IS THE FIXED SIDE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Civ4CE's BtS changelog contains a line saying that city Healthy/Unhealthy bonus display from
EVENTS was fixed. Its actual BtS `CvCity::setBuildingHappyChange` / `setBuildingHealthChange`
bodies, however, still contain the old BtS sign/receiver mistakes that K-Mod explicitly replaces.
Examples in the supplied CE source include removing an already-negative bad-happiness value by
passing that negative value straight back into `changeBuildingBadHappiness`, and the first-insert
health branch calling happiness mutators at all. K-Mod labels the corresponding block as original
BtS code and replaces it with the Unofficial Patch sign-correct version.

Current AdvCiv 1.14 / SAS does NOT retain those CE setter mistakes. Its live event-building family
issue is the already-owned F566/KI#889 `NO_BUILDING` class-mapping guard mismatch. Therefore this
comparison is preserved as an oracle-quality control only: Civ4CE remains useful for historical
cross-checking, but a CE changelog claim cannot be treated as proof that every corresponding CE
body is the repaired implementation.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F582 / KI#905 - CONFIRMED CURRENT ADVC CITY-TRADE VALUATION DEFECT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

TITLE
-----
`calculateDistanceMaintenanceTimes100(eOwner)` searches only the prospective owner's already-owned
cities for government centers, so AI valuation of a peaceful foreign-city acquisition cannot see a
government-center building that will survive the transfer. Current SAS's Forbidden Palace gives a
clean live case: pre-transfer AI valuation charges positive distance maintenance to the candidate,
while immediately after transfer the retained Forbidden Palace makes that city's distance
maintenance exactly zero.

ROOT
----
AdvC exposes prospective-owner maintenance through:

    int CvCity::calculateDistanceMaintenanceTimes100(PlayerTypes eOwner) const
    {
        return CvCity::calculateDistanceMaintenanceTimes100(getPlot(),
                eOwner == NO_PLAYER ? getOwner() : eOwner, getPopulation());
    }

The static helper ultimately calls:

    calculateMaintenanceDistance(&kCityPlot, eOwner)

which does:

    FOR_EACH_CITY(pLoopCity, GET_PLAYER(eOwner))
    {
        int iDist = plotDistance(pCityPlot, pLoopCity->plot());
        iLongestDist = std::max(iLongestDist, iDist);
        if (pLoopCity->isGovernmentCenter())
            iShortestGovernment = std::min(iShortestGovernment, iDist);
    }
    return min(min(iLongestDist, iShortestGovernment), cap);

For a foreign candidate city, `GET_PLAYER(eOwner)` necessarily excludes the candidate itself.
That is normally fine if the candidate will remain an ordinary city. It is not fine when peaceful
transfer preserves a building that makes the candidate a government center for eOwner.

The current city-trade acquisition path uses exactly this hypothetical state. In
`CvPlayerAI::AI_cityTradeVal`, case 1 is documented as:

    How much this player values acquiring kCity from its current owner.

and calls:

    scaled r = AI_assetVal(kCity, false);

For a foreign candidate, `AI_assetVal` later subtracts:

    scaled rMaintCost = per100(c.calculateBaseMaintenanceTimes100(getID()));

`calculateBaseMaintenanceTimes100` includes the prospective distance-maintenance wrapper above.
No parameter tells that wrapper that the foreign candidate itself may become a government center
as part of the same peaceful transfer.

CURRENT SAS DATA - FORBIDDEN PALACE IS A LIVE TRANSFERABLE GOVERNMENT CENTER
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current `CIV4BuildingInfos.xml` has only three `bGovernmentCenter=1` buildings:

    BUILDING_PALACE
        bCapital       = 1
        iConquestProb  = 0

    BUILDING_BARBARIAN_PALACE
        bCapital       = 0
        bNeverCapture  = 1
        iConquestProb  = 0

    BUILDING_FORBIDDEN_PALACE
        bCapital       = 0
        bGovernmentCenter = 1
        bNeverCapture  = 0
        iConquestProb  = 0
        PrereqTech     = TECH_CONSTITUTION
        iCitiesPrereq  = 6

`BUILDINGCLASS_FORBIDDEN_PALACE` has `iMaxPlayerInstances=1`.

The Palace cannot supply the peaceful-city-trade witness because `canTradeCityTo` explicitly
rejects capitals. The Barbarian Palace is special barbarian data. The Forbidden Palace is therefore
the clean ordinary current-SAS witness.

`canTradeCityTo` does not reject a city merely for containing a national wonder. Once the normal
city-trade conditions are met (recipient reveal, >= CITY_TRADE_CULTURE_THRESH culture, etc.), a
Forbidden-Palace city can be traded.

PEACEFUL ACQUISITION PRESERVES THE FORBIDDEN PALACE UNDER ORDINARY CONDITIONS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::acquireCity` snapshots every real building, kills/recreates the city for the new owner,
and restores each building that the recipient can legally possess/construct. The destruction block
contains:

    if (isProductionMaxedBuildingClass(eBuildingClass, true) ||
        !kCityPlot.canConstruct(eBuilding))
    {
        continue;
    }

    int iOdds = kBuilding.getConquestProbability();
    if (!bConquest || bRecapture || SyncRandSuccess100(iOdds))
        kNewCity.setNumRealBuildingTimed(...);

For a peaceful city trade, `bConquest == false`, so the conquest-probability roll is bypassed.
Therefore choose an entirely ordinary recipient that:

1. knows Constitution;
2. already has at least 6 cities;
3. does not already own its one allowed Forbidden Palace;
4. can legally receive the candidate city under the normal city-trade culture/reveal rules.

The transferred Forbidden Palace passes the recipient-side building checks and is restored in the
new city despite `iConquestProb=0` (that zero matters to conquest, not peaceful trade).

Restoring it runs normal building processing. `CvCity::processBuilding` calls:

    changeGovernmentCenterCount(kBuilding.isGovernmentCenter() ? iChange : 0);

and `changeGovernmentCenterCount` immediately calls:

    GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).updateMaintenance();

so the retained Forbidden Palace is authoritative runtime government-center state for the new
owner immediately after transfer.

CLEAN CURRENT RUNTIME FIXTURE - POSITIVE PREVIEW DISTANCE -> ZERO ACTUAL DISTANCE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Take a tradable foreign city C that contains the Forbidden Palace. Let prospective recipient R meet
the four conditions above and have no other government center except an ordinary capital. Put C at
positive plot distance D from that capital (and, more generally, at positive distance from every
currently owned government center of R).

BEFORE transfer, while C is still foreign:

    C.calculateDistanceMaintenanceTimes100(R)
      -> calculateMaintenanceDistance(C.plot, R)
      -> iterates only R's currently owned cities
      -> C is absent
      -> nearest government center is at positive distance
      -> projected distance-maintenance component is positive
         under ordinary positive distance/world/handicap modifiers.

AFTER peaceful transfer and Forbidden-Palace restoration:

    C belongs to R
    C.isGovernmentCenter() == true

The normal maintenance search now iterates C itself. For that loop entry:

    plotDistance(C.plot, C.plot) = 0
    C.isGovernmentCenter()       = true
    iShortestGovernment          = 0

Therefore:

    calculateMaintenanceDistance(C.plot, R) = 0
    calculateDistanceMaintenanceTimes100(R) = 0

for C's distance component.

So the prospective acquisition calculation charges maintenance that the transferred city will not
actually pay. The result is deterministic once the ordinary transfer/building-retention conditions
above hold.

AI EFFECT
---------
`AI_assetVal(c, false)` is the peaceful-transfer branch. The same function explicitly treats
buildings as surviving when `!bConquest`:

    if (!bConquest || bOwn) // Most mundane buildings don't survive conquest
        ... value buildings ...

Thus the valuation already distinguishes peaceful transfer from conquest for building survival,
but its maintenance component does not carry the surviving government's-center effect into the
prospective owner state.

The false positive maintenance is subtracted from the foreign city's asset value and then feeds
`AI_cityTradeVal` acquisition pricing/willingness. The AI therefore undervalues acquisition of a
tradable Forbidden-Palace city relative to the post-transfer maintenance state.

There is additional same-root breadth: a newly acquired Forbidden Palace can also lower distance
maintenance in OTHER recipient cities by becoming their nearer government center. `AI_assetVal`'s
separate heuristic immediately below the candidate-city maintenance call is explicitly an estimate
of extra civic upkeep / extra number-of-cities maintenance in other cities; it does not simulate
owner-wide distance-maintenance SAVINGS from a newly retained government center. The candidate
city's own positive->zero mismatch is sufficient for confirmation without relying on this broader
effect.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE SAME ROOT AS F581
-------------------------------------
F581/KI#904 is a count-state bug in the prospective number-of-cities and colony helpers:

- the requested owner's `getNumCities()` / `getCitiesPerPlayer()` does not yet include the foreign
  candidate;
- the static helpers already expose `iExtraCities` but the member wrappers fail to pass +1.

That error applies generally to foreign candidate cities and has a mechanical +1 repair.

F582 is a different state dimension and implementation mechanism:

- `calculateMaintenanceDistance` searches a concrete LIST of the prospective owner's existing
  cities for government centers;
- the missing hypothetical state is not merely one city count but a BUILDING EFFECT on the
  candidate that can survive peaceful transfer;
- the repair therefore requires projecting retained government-center state, not passing
  `iExtraCities=1`.

The two findings share the broad prospective-owner-maintenance domain but have separate causes,
fixtures, and repairs.

CORRECTION / NARROWING TO THE F581 WRITEUP
------------------------------------------
WIP372's F581 caller section said:

    Distance maintenance can legitimately use the prospective owner's current
    capital/government-center set.

That sentence is too broad. It is correct for ordinary candidate cities whose transfer will not
add a government center, and it is normally appropriate for the original conquest-oriented use
when the relevant government-center building does not survive conquest. F582 establishes the
peaceful-transfer exception: a retained Forbidden Palace changes the prospective government-center
set as part of the acquisition itself.

Treat this WIP375 note as the authoritative narrowing of that F581 control sentence; F581's
number-of-cities/colony proof and repair remain unchanged.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod's normal runtime distance-maintenance code is current-owner-only. Its
`calculateMaintenanceDistance()` walks the current owner's city list; when the current city itself
is a government center, that is correct because the city is already in the list and contributes
zero distance.

AdvC practical 1253 / initial-import commit
`f6ff6a182f5187541fff6e5bbbe12f9573b3778c` adds the optional owner parameter with the explicit
header contract:

    projected maintenance for cities yet to be conquered

and moves K-Mod's search into a static helper parameterized by owner. The helper loops only
`GET_PLAYER(owner)` cities. For the original conquest-oriented purpose, current SAS's ordinary
Palace/Forbidden-Palace government-center buildings have `iConquestProb=0`, so ignoring their
post-capture government-center role is not itself a current contradiction: they do not survive an
ordinary conquest transfer.

AdvC practical 2053 / commit
`fd5d755af022962c4e3e09495e052fbc80bf2457`, "AI code for city trade evaluation", introduces the
current `AI_assetVal` city-trade path. The diff adds:

    scaled r = AI_assetVal(kCity, false);

for acquisition valuation and, inside `AI_assetVal`, subtracts the sum of:

    c.calculateColonyMaintenanceTimes100(getID())
    c.calculateDistanceMaintenanceTimes100(getID())
    c.calculateNumCitiesMaintenanceTimes100(getID())

while the same function's `!bConquest` building branch assumes peaceful-transfer buildings survive.
That reuse extends the conquest-oriented prospective helper to a transfer mode where the candidate
can retain a government-center building, activating F582.

Practical 2463 / commit `fd00cf5197afe3d1c519d62ffb288ea11955e968` later consolidates the three
calls into `calculateBaseMaintenanceTimes100(getID())` but leaves the same distance-maintenance
prospective-state omission intact. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain it.

DEDUP
-----
Whole-album semantic searches for prospective/foreign distance maintenance, government centers,
Forbidden Palace, AI_assetVal and city-trade maintenance found no prior numbered root owning this
specific transfer-state omission.

Distinct from:

- F399/KI#722: the optional BUG saved-maintenance BUILDING HOVER ignores government-center savings
  when hypothetically constructing Forbidden Palace. F582 is AI city-acquisition valuation across
  ownership transfer, not UI help, and arises through the prospective-owner city list.
- F581/KI#904: prospective num-cities/colony count omission; different state and repair as above.
- KI#306 / associated cache findings: within-turn invalidation of government-center/top-production
  ranking state, not hypothetical transfer arithmetic.
- F567: runtime colony-maintenance cap arithmetic, unrelated to government-center projection.
- F329: prospective active-world-wonder owner/team obsolescence, same broad transfer domain but a
  different API and state dimension.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION
-----------------------------
Do not blindly make every foreign candidate a government center. The prospective state depends on
transfer mode and on whether a government-center building would survive / be legal for the
recipient.

A robust repair should make peaceful `AI_assetVal` project the building-retention state used by
`acquireCity` closely enough to determine whether the candidate will be a government center for the
recipient. If yes, its own prospective distance-maintenance component is exactly zero; ideally the
projection should also account for owner-wide distance-maintenance savings in other recipient
cities.

Possible implementation shapes include:

1. a transfer-aware maintenance projection helper that can treat the candidate plot as an added
   government center when acquisition rules say a relevant building survives; or
2. a narrower `AI_assetVal` adjustment for foreign peaceful acquisitions, sharing a helper with
   acquisition/building-retention legality rather than duplicating those rules.

Avoid using only `c.isGovernmentCenter()` without a recipient-side survival check: current state can
contain a government-center building that the new owner would fail to retain because of class
limits/prerequisites. The current Forbidden-Palace fixture deliberately chooses a recipient for
whom retention is legal.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. Clean peaceful Forbidden-Palace transfer
- recipient has Constitution, >=6 cities, no Forbidden Palace;
- candidate is non-capital, tradable, contains Forbidden Palace, and is at positive distance from
  every recipient government center;
- pre-transfer projected distance component for recipient should be 0 after the repair;
- immediately post-transfer runtime distance component should also be 0.

B. Recipient already has Forbidden Palace
- candidate's old Forbidden Palace cannot become a second retained national wonder;
- projection must NOT assume a new zero-distance government center merely from the candidate's
  current `isGovernmentCenter()` state.

C. Recipient fails a building prerequisite
- e.g. insufficient city count / tech in a controlled fixture;
- projection must match acquisition's failure to retain the government-center building.

D. Ordinary foreign city without government-center building
- prospective distance maintenance must remain the normal distance to recipient's existing
  government-center set.

E. Conquest control
- current Forbidden Palace has `iConquestProb=0`;
- a conquest projection must not assume that it survives and becomes a government center.

F. Other-city savings breadth
- recipient has another city whose nearest government center becomes the transferred Forbidden
  Palace;
- if repair claims full post-acquisition maintenance projection, verify that city's reduced distance
  maintenance is also represented; otherwise document candidate-city-only scope explicitly.

sibling pass. It then promoted one independent inherited gameplay-state root as F583/KI#906.

POST-WIP375 CONTROLS BEFORE F583
--------------------------------

1. Production storage / rank helpers

The remaining low-mention production-storage helpers do not expose a new lifecycle defect. Project
production intentionally has no decay timer. Unit/building production storage and timers retain the
expected completion/cancellation lifecycle. The rank-building functions themselves are coherent;
the interesting failure mode is producer-side invalidation, already covered heavily in the earlier
WIP365/WIP366 rank/cache pass.

2. Practical 3666 — food already beyond growth threshold after random event

AdvC practical 3666 repairs `getFoodTurnsLeft()` for the transient state where a random event can
leave stored food above `growthThreshold()` until the next city turn. The repair returns one turn
instead of sending a negative numerator into unsigned-ceiling division. Current `doGrowth()` then
consumes that state normally. No independent sibling event/growth invariant break was proved.

3. Practical 4331 — `GPProjection()` negative-turn-looking arithmetic

`GPProjection()` clamps its aggregate projected contribution with `std::max(0, iTurnsLeft)` while a
per-unit numerator still multiplies by raw `iTurnsLeft`. This superficially looks wrong when
`GPTurnsLeft()==-1`.

Under current shipped SAS data, however, the negative-turn case is masked by the GP-rate invariant:
outside disorder there are no negative Great-People-rate modifiers capable of reducing a positive
base GP rate to zero. Therefore `GPTurnsLeft()==-1` implies the current base GP rate is zero, and all
per-unit current GP-rate buckets multiplied by -1 are likewise zero. Preserve as defensive/API
robustness breadth, not a current-live numbered root.


F583 / KI#906 — SETTLER/WORKER FOOD-DIFFERENCE STILL CHARGES ANGRY CITIZENS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED CURRENT SAS GAMEPLAY ROOT; INHERITED FROM BTS / PRESENT IN K-MOD AND BASE ADVC.

ROOT
----
Current `CvCity` uses two different food-consumption contracts for the SAME Settler/Worker city
turn.

The production path correctly honors the special BtS rule restored by AdvC practical 2125:

    int iFoodProduction = (bFoodProduction ?
            std::max(0, getYieldRate(YIELD_FOOD) - foodConsumption(
            /* advc.001 (K-Mod bug): */ true)) : 0);

`foodConsumption(true)` excludes angry citizens from the population count used for this special
food-to-production calculation.

But `foodDifference()` still uses ordinary `foodConsumption()` when a food-production order is
active:

    if (!bIgnoreProduction && isFoodProduction())
        iDifference = std::min(0,
                getYieldRate(YIELD_FOOD) - foodConsumption());

The no-argument call is equivalent to `foodConsumption(false, 0)`, so angry citizens are charged
there.

`doGrowth()` consumes this mismatched result authoritatively every city turn:

    int iDiff = foodDifference();
    changeFood(iDiff);
    ...
    else if (getFood() < 0)
    {
        changeFood(-getFood());
        if (getPopulation() > 1)
            changePopulation(-1);
    }

Thus the special food-production order can simultaneously:

- treat an angry citizen as NOT consuming food when converting food into Settler/Worker
  production; and
- treat that same angry citizen as consuming food when subtracting from the city's stored-food
  bar.

This is not just a preview mismatch. `doGrowth()` mutates authoritative stored food and can
ultimately reduce population through starvation.

ORDINARY CURRENT-SAS TURN FLOW
------------------------------
Current `CvCity::doTurn()` orders the relevant operations as:

    doCheckProduction();
    doGrowth();
    doCulture();
    doPlotCultureTimes100(...);
    doProduction(...);

The ordering does not mask the bug. Both `doGrowth()` and `doProduction()` inspect the same active
Settler/Worker order and current food yield. In a non-starving one-turn witness, `doGrowth()` first
subtracts the false stored-food deficit; population and worked yields remain unchanged; later
`doProduction()` grants the special food-production surplus using `foodConsumption(true)`.

CURRENT SHIPPED REACHABILITY
----------------------------
Current SAS XML ships ordinary food-production units:

- `UNIT_SETTLER` has `<bFood>1</bFood>`;
- `UNIT_WORKER` has `<bFood>1</bFood>`;
- the Indian Fast Worker, Netherlands Swift Worker, Maya Quick Worker and Barbarian Worker also
  have `<bFood>1</bFood>`.

`CvCity::isFoodProduction(UnitTypes)` maps this unit flag to the special production path. No
optional mod-mod data or disabled define is required.

CLEAN NUMERIC REPRODUCTION
--------------------------
Use an ordinary healthy, non-disordered size-4 city with:

- exactly 1 angry citizen;
- no net unhealthiness or other food-consumption modifier;
- total food yield = 7;
- stored food safely above zero, e.g. 10;
- an active Settler or Worker order.

With the normal 2 food per citizen:

    ordinary foodConsumption(false) = 4 * 2 = 8
    special  foodConsumption(true)  = (4 - 1 angry) * 2 = 6

PRODUCTION ACCOUNTING:

    getYieldRate(FOOD) - foodConsumption(true)
    = 7 - 6
    = +1

So `getProductionDifference()` correctly converts +1 food into Settler/Worker production.

STORED-FOOD ACCOUNTING IN THE SAME TURN:

    foodDifference()
    = min(0, 7 - foodConsumption(false))
    = min(0, 7 - 8)
    = -1

Then `doGrowth()` applies:

    stored food: 10 -> 9

before `doProduction()` later awards the +1 special food-production contribution.

The same 7 food has therefore been classified as both:

    +1 surplus for Settler/Worker production

and

    -1 deficit for authoritative stored food

solely because one branch ignores the angry citizen while the other counts it.

A sufficiently low stored-food state broadens the same root into population loss: repeated false
negative `foodDifference()` can exhaust the bar, after which `doGrowth()` executes its normal
starvation path even though the special Settler/Worker accounting says the angry citizen is not
consuming food.

DOCUMENTED / HISTORICAL CONTRACT
--------------------------------
This behavior conflicts directly with the rule AdvC itself says practical 2125 is restoring.

AdvC practical 2125 / commit `968880bb420387f4d1022cb9296c8ada3dbfd8f9`, titled
"Fix K-Mod bug: food consumption by angry citizens", changes only the production calculation from:

    foodConsumption()

to:

    foodConsumption(true)

and the commit message states that angry citizens "indeed aren't supposed to consume food when
producing a Settler or Worker."

The AdvC manual repeats the same rule and records practical 2125 as repairing a K-Mod 1.45
regression. Current SAS also ships loading hint `TXT_KEY_ADVC_HINT_47`:

    Consider producing settlers and workers in cities with angry or unhealthy citizens.
    So long as food gets converted into production, angry citizens don't consume food, ...

The witness above is deliberately in the exact "food gets converted into production" state:
`foodConsumption(true)` produces a +1 convertible surplus. Yet `foodDifference()` still charges
that angry citizen against the stored-food bar.

The historical CivFanatics discussion linked by the AdvC commit also records Firaxis developer
alexman confirming that the angry-citizen exception was by design, with the stated purpose of
avoiding a production penalty / extra happiness-health micromanagement when using Settlers and
Workers. The local AdvC manual already records that source and rationale, so the finding does not
depend on an external page remaining available.

ANCESTRY
--------
The mismatch predates AdvC.

Civ4CE's reconstructed BtS `CvCity.cpp` has:

    getProductionDifference(...):
        ... getYieldRate(YIELD_FOOD) - foodConsumption(true) ...

while its BtS `foodDifference()` still uses:

    ... getYieldRate(YIELD_FOOD) - foodConsumption() ...

So the split accounting is present in the BtS lineage itself.

K-Mod inherits the same `foodDifference()` basis. K-Mod 1.45 later regressed the production side by
changing its production calculation to ordinary `foodConsumption()` too, making the two wrong-but-
consistent in the opposite direction. AdvC practical 2125 correctly restores the special
production-side `foodConsumption(true)`, but it leaves the inherited stored-food branch untouched,
revealing the original BtS split again.

K-Mod practical/history commit 957 (`430199d82a53d9701e0d9695dbcff4bf58e44bfb`) later adds
`bIgnoreProduction` to `foodDifference()` for AI callers that need the ordinary growth signal. It
does not alter the active-food-production branch's use of `foodConsumption()`.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS therefore retain the same split.

DEDUP
-----
Whole-album searches for `foodDifference`, `foodConsumption(true)`, angry citizens,
Settler/Worker starvation and practical 2125 found no numbered root owning this mismatch.

The only direct practical-2125 album note was WIP375's historical-repair control saying that the
food-PRODUCTION calculation correctly uses `foodConsumption(true)`. F583 is the newly proved
sibling in the authoritative stored-food calculation.

Distinct from:

- KI#48.3 / F007: `AI_buildingValue` double-subtracts unhealthiness after receiving a
  health-adjusted `foodDifference(false, true)`; AI valuation only, different arithmetic and call
  mode.
- the earlier disorder/food-display findings around `foodDifference()`: UI/display contracts, not
  angry-citizen consumption during food-production orders.
- citizen/plot-value Worker-production findings: AI assignment/value logic rather than the
  authoritative city food bar.
- practical 2125 itself: that repairs a K-Mod regression in `getProductionDifference`; F583 is the
  still-unrepaired sibling in `foodDifference` inherited from BtS.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR
-------------------
Make the active food-production branch use the same special consumption contract as production:

CURRENT:

    if (!bIgnoreProduction && isFoodProduction())
        iDifference = std::min(0,
                getYieldRate(YIELD_FOOD) - foodConsumption());

REPAIR:

    if (!bIgnoreProduction && isFoodProduction())
        iDifference = std::min(0,
                getYieldRate(YIELD_FOOD) - foodConsumption(true));

This is deliberately narrow.

- It changes only the branch where `foodDifference()` is honoring the active special
  food-production order.
- Calls with `bIgnoreProduction=true` continue to use normal `foodConsumption()` and therefore keep
  their intended ordinary growth/food signal.
- Non-food-production orders are unchanged.
- It aligns the authoritative stored-food accounting with the already-repaired
  `getProductionDifference()` contract rather than inventing a third rule.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
A. One angry citizen, positive special surplus
- size 4, 1 angry, healthy, food yield 7, stored food 10, Settler active;
- special food production must be +1;
- `foodDifference()` must be 0 after repair, not -1;
- stored food must remain 10 after `doGrowth()`.

B. Genuine deficit even after excluding the angry citizen
- same city, food yield 5;
- special consumption = 6;
- food-production contribution = 0;
- `foodDifference()` must be -1;
- true starvation remains possible. The repair must not make Settler/Worker production an
  unconditional starvation immunity.

C. No angry citizens
- food-production branch should match existing behavior; `foodConsumption(true)` equals the normal
  population-consumption basis apart from the already-intended associated health handling.

D. Non-food-production order
- switch to a building or ordinary unit;
- angry citizen must again count in normal food consumption / starvation.

E. Explicit ignore-production AI call
- `foodDifference(..., true)` must continue to use ordinary food consumption and expose the normal
  growth signal expected by K-Mod/AdvC AI callers.

F. Worker variants
- repeat A for ordinary Worker and at least one current food-production Worker UU; same contract.

G. Starvation boundary
- begin with 0 stored food, population >1, one angry citizen, and a yield that is nonnegative only
  under `foodConsumption(true)`;
- repaired food-production branch must not decrement population merely because the excluded angry
  citizen was charged by the old `foodDifference()` basis.

CLASSIFICATION
--------------
F583 / KI#906 is a current-live gameplay-state defect with base BtS ancestry. It is unusually clean
because the same city turn contains two authoritative calculations that are intended to implement
the same special Settler/Worker angry-citizen rule but use different values of the existing
`bNoAngry` parameter.

The actual AdvCiv-SAS source remains UNTOUCHED; this album only records the proof and repair/test
boundary.

1. CIV4CE "DISAPPEARING CITIZENS" CHANGELOG ITEM - NO DISTINCT CURRENT CVCITY ROOT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Civ4CE's BtS changelog contains:

    Fixed disappearing citizens when you remove one in a large city

The obvious CvCity-side candidates were compared directly across the supplied
Civ4CE BtS source, K-Mod 1.46, Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS:

    CvCity::alterSpecialistCount
    CvCity::alterWorkingPlot

Civ4CE retains essentially the same BtS lineage for these routines; there is no
Civ4CE-vs-current-SAS body difference that identifies the changelog item as a
surviving CvCity state defect. Current specialist-removal / force-target logic is

CvCity root solely from the historical changelog wording.

2. CIV4CE THREE GORGES / POWER-UNHEALTHINESS FIXES - CURRENT LINEAGE ALREADY COHERENT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Civ4CE names three old city bugs:

* Three Gorges Dam giving power unhealthiness to all cities;
* new cities failing to receive the proper Three Gorges power-health state;
* cities with only hydro/nuclear power failing to receive the intended power-health
  handling.

Current AdvC/SAS no longer has the broken state model implicated by those old bugs.
The relevant current chain remains:

    processBuilding / processBonus
      -> changePowerCount(local count, dirty classification)
      -> isPower / isDirtyPower
      -> updatePowerHealth

and area clean power propagates through the area/team/player update chain already
traced in WIP368. Current `isDirtyPower()` correctly excludes area-clean-powered
cities, while clean local Hydro/Nuclear and resource-gated dirty Coal power are
counted separately. WIP370-era health-state controls likewise already verified
`updatePowerHealth()` assignment invalidation. No F584 sibling survived.

`getBonusPower()` was rechecked as part of this pass. It counts only active
civilization buildings whose `PowerBonus` matches the changing bonus and whose
`isDirtyPower()` matches the requested bucket. `processBonus()` applies the dirty
and clean buckets independently through `changePowerCount`; the final state is
coherent even if a hypothetical bonus powered both kinds. Current SAS has ordinary
resource-gated power through Coal Plant (dirty Coal) and Nuclear Plant (clean
Uranium), and the helper matches those XML contracts.

3. CIV4CE HANGING GARDENS / GLOBAL POPULATION ITEM - CURRENT SAS DATA MASKS THE GENERIC PATH
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The generic `setNumRealBuildingTimed()` world-wonder completion path still handles
`GlobalPopulationChange` by visiting the correct owner/team-share cities, changing
population and immediately reassigning work. The Civ4CE changelog's old Hanging
Gardens failure is useful ancestry evidence that this path was historically fragile.

However, current SAS `CIV4BuildingInfos.xml` has no nonzero
`iGlobalPopulationChange` building at all. Thus the generic code cannot supply a
current shipped F584 witness even if some older BTS-era implementation had a bug.
Preserve only as historical/mod-mod robustness context.

4. `doPartisans()` - HISTORICAL CAPTURE BUGS ALREADY REPAIRED / SEMANTICALLY COVERED
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Civ4CE also says it fixed "several city capturing bugs relating to partisans."
Current SAS `CvCity::doPartisans()` was rechecked against Base AdvCiv 1.14 and the
current event XML:

* events-off and low-population/barbarian guards are explicit;
* partisan ownership is based on plot highest culture, not the captured city's
  current owner culture;
* dead/cityless cultural players and non-war states are rejected;
* `getNumPartisanUnits()` uses the documented `max(0, cultureLevel - 1)` rule;
* the manual trigger is required to be the negative-weight `EVENTTRIGGER_PARTISANS`.

The album had already frozen the culture-level/count conversion as coherent and
had separately audited the raze ordering around `kCity.doPartisans()` before native
disband. The later Python Partisans invalid-conscript problem is already KI#524.2-
KI#524.6 and is not a new CvCity root. No F584.

5. CORRECTIVE-COMMIT / FUNCTION-NAME COVERAGE CAVEAT
-----------------------------------------------------
A mechanical pass mapped historical AdvC commits with bug/fix/correct/repair-like
titles to CvCity hunk function names, then compared those names against album
mentions. This exposed an important methodology caveat: a function name having zero
album mentions does NOT imply that a bugfix in the same broad commit concerned that
function.

For example practical 1499 (`3e233e6794`, "Last batch of style changes; some
bugfixes and UI tweaks") touches many CvCity helpers with zero/one literal album
mentions, but the commit message identifies its substantive bugfixes primarily in
AI code; most CvCity hunks are style/refactoring. Likewise practical 1381's CvCity
changes support an AI strategic-resource fix by adding an assumed bonus to
`allUpgradesAvailable` / `canTrain`, rather than repairing `isBuildingsMaxed` merely
because that function appears in an adjacent hunk.

Future historical-oracle passes should therefore use function-body/commit-message
proof, not practical-number or hunk co-occurrence alone.

6. `findHighestCulture()` - POSTHUMOUS OWNER IS AUTHORED POLICY; TIE SPECULATION BELOW BAR
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current AdvC/SAS intentionally changed K-Mod's ALIVE loop to:

    for (PlayerIter<EVER_ALIVE> it; it.hasNext(); ++it) // advc.099: was ALIVE

This is consistent with the already-frozen advc.099 policy allowing posthumous city
culture. Current callers also account for liveness when a live actor is required;
for example raze memory explicitly checks `kHighestCulturePlayer.isAlive()`.

The strict `>` comparison means exact culture ties are resolved by iteration/player
ID order. Such tie handling could in principle influence `acquireCity()`'s
`bRecapture` classification, but no documented contrary contract or ordinary wrong
state was established in this tranche. Do not promote tie-order speculation as F584.

7. LOW-COVERAGE AUTOMATION / HURRY / CONSCRIPTION HELPERS - NO NEW LIVE CONTRADICTION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`setProductionAutomated` remains the already-frozen WIP368-ish control: `bClear`
clears the queue only for the active selected city, but the shipped task/UI caller
supplies that state; the non-UI RiseFall caller turns automation OFF, where clear is
irrelevant. No current hidden programmatic clear request was found.

The hurry/conscript arithmetic was challenged at its main bounded points:

* `getHurryGold` returns zero for a non-gold hurry and otherwise nonnegative cost;
  `canHurry` rejects a gold hurry with zero/insufficient gold cost under the current
  order contract.
* `getHurryPopulation` has a minimum cost of one citizen for a population hurry;
  ordinary `canHurry` first rejects an order that current/overflow/feature/minimum
  production will already complete, preventing a zero-needed-production pop-rush
  witness through that path.
* `getHurryCostModifier` can mathematically reach zero under sufficiently negative
  XML modifiers, but the album already proved current SAS ships no negative hurry
  modifier data capable of reaching that state.
* `getConscriptUnit` chooses the highest positive conscription-value trainable unit.
  Its Python override is a generic modding hook, but no current callback supplies an
  illegal replacement; current gameplay therefore stays on the validated native
  selection.
* `conscriptMinCityPopulation` simply adds the configured minimum to the current
  conscript population cost; no independent rounding/sentinel mismatch established.

Known hurry/overflow/Slavery findings and controls remain the relevant owners; this
pass does not reopen them.

-----------------------------------------------------------

  ImprovementFreeSpecialist valuation path, but current SAS has no building with a
  nonempty `ImprovementFreeSpecialists` table (WIP373 control), so no shipped F584
  witness.
* BUG building/specialist additional GP/commerce helpers with low album counts are
  preview/help-side and have no authoritative AI/gameplay caller in the current DLL
  where checked. Do not spend a gameplay root number on unreachable preview arithmetic.
* production-time setters / `isAnyProductionProgress` / rank builders remain the

* `changeNoUnhappinessCount` correctly dirties citizen assignment. The deliberately

ADV C 1.14 -> CURRENT SAS SEMANTIC BODY SIEVE
---------------------------------------------
A normalized function-body comparison was used to separate real `CvCity.cpp`
semantic divergence from comments/formatting. Only a small finite group of
current SAS bodies differs materially from Base AdvCiv 1.14; most differences
checked here are SAS logging, static-local caching, serialization of an already-
owned SAS state member, or already-owned fixes/controls.

Low-coverage changed bodies checked in this tranche include:
- `getProductionBarPercentages`: current typed-order / NO_PLAYER hardening is the

BUILDING HEALTH/HAPPINESS -> CITY BILLBOARD GLOBAL DIRTY CONTROL
----------------------------------------------------------------
A seemingly strong sibling of F580 was checked and CLOSED under current-live
reachability.

`CvCity::processBuilding()` can alter direct building health/happiness and the
bonus/extra variants without itself setting global `CityInfo_DIRTY_BIT`. Local
mutators use assignment dirty and in several cases `setInfoDirty(true)`. Because
practical 1387 explicitly added `CityInfo_DIRTY_BIT` for resource-driven sign
crossings, this generic asymmetry was worth tracing rather than assuming local
city dirty is equivalent.

Current ordinary masking/reachability:
- normal production completion, city events and meltdown happen inside a player
  turn whose normal tail sets `CityInfo_DIRTY_BIT` globally;
- a successful espionage mission explicitly dirties `CityInfo_DIRTY_BIT` in the
  normal unit espionage path, while AI espionage also runs inside the AI player
  turn with the blanket tail refresh;
- current Great-Person `construct` buildings were enumerated from shipped XML;
  the constructible shrines, corporation HQs, Academy, Military Academy and
  Scotland Yard all have zero direct `iHappiness` and zero direct `iHealth`, so
  that mid-turn construct route gives no current health/happy boundary witness;
- Advanced Start is pregame; acquisition/other turn-boundary paths have their own
  broad refresh/lifecycle coverage.

Conclusion: generic robustness/UI-invalidating asymmetry, but no ordinary shipped
path was proved that leaves the active player's healthy/unhappy billboard stale.
Do NOT promote as F584 without a current-supported unmasked producer.

LOW-COVERAGE STORED-STATE HELPERS - CLOSED
------------------------------------------
The following compact authoritative helpers were traced through their meaningful
callers/state consequences and did not yield a new root:
- `setCitizensAutomated`: enabling immediately calls `AI_assignWorkingPlots`;
  disabling clears forced-specialist counts. Selection-button dirtying is present.
- `changeSpecialistCommerce`: mutates the specialist commerce cache and immediately
  calls `updateCommerce(eCommerce)`.
- project production storage: no project decay timer exists by design; project
  production setter/UI invalidation is paired with its lifecycle.
- `changeFreeSpecialist` and `changeMaxSpecialistCount`: both assignment-dirty the
  city; type-specific free-specialist changes directly process the specialist.
- `countUniqueBonuses`: its only important C++ consumer here is AdvC bonus-trade
  attitude normalization, where a distinct-resource count is the intended signal;
  it is not attempting to value resource quantities.
- `getBuildingHappiness`: current AI plot-build happiness adjustment that once used
  this helper is commented out; remaining direct surface is mainly Python/help.
  Its state-religion, player-extra, commerce-slider and event-class components
  match the runtime ingredients inspected here.

F583 BREADTH - FOOD BAR USES THE SAME FOOD-PRODUCTION MISMATCH
--------------------------------------------------------------
`CvCity::getFoodBarPercentages()` calls `foodDifference()` directly when building
its stored/rate food bars. Therefore, while a Settler/Worker food-production
order is active, the same F583 mismatch can be visible in the food bar: angry
citizens that runtime production correctly excludes via `foodConsumption(true)`
are still counted by the current `foodDifference()` path.

This is breadth/UI manifestation of F583 / KI#906, not a new root. The repair to
the active-food-production branch of `foodDifference()` fixes both authoritative
stored-food evolution and this food-bar projection together.

NO-ESPIONAGE / GREAT-SPY GPP DESYNCHRONIZATION - REAL BUT CURRENTLY UNSUPPORTED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A stronger inherited contract mismatch was proved but deliberately does NOT
consume F584 under the album's current-supported-game threshold.

`CvCity::setGreatPeopleUnitRate(eUnit, iNewValue)` contains a stock/K-Mod guard:

    if (GAMEOPTION_NO_ESPIONAGE && GC.getInfo(eUnit).getEspionagePoints() > 0)
        return;

Current `UNIT_GREAT_SPY` has 3000 espionage points, so under No Espionage all
Great-Spy per-unit GPP rate changes are suppressed.

However both `processSpecialist()` and `processBuilding()` still add the same
source's GPP to `m_iBaseGreatPeopleRate` after calling the suppressed per-unit
setter. Thus the invariant explicitly asserted by `doGreatPeople()`:

    sum(getGreatPeopleUnitRate(...)) == getBaseGreatPeopleRate()

can be broken by ordinary content under that option. This is not merely a Spy-
specialist edge case. Current SAS XML contains shipped buildings with
`GreatPeopleUnitClass = UNITCLASS_GREAT_SPY` and positive GPP, including:
- Forbidden Palace (+1)
- Parthenon (+2)
- Versailles (+3)
- Mt. Rushmore (+3)
- Kremlin (+3)
- Military Academy (+1)
- one corporation headquarters (+1)

Consequences in a release DLL are stronger than the debug assertion: total city
GPP can advance toward the threshold while the corresponding Great-Spy unit bank
does not advance. With only suppressed sources, the threshold can be reached with
zero total per-unit selection weight; with mixed sources, threshold timing and GP
selection weights no longer describe the same contributions.

Ancestry comparison: Base AdvCiv 1.14, K-Mod and Civ4CE/BtS retain the same core
split (setter suppresses espionage-point GP units, while base GPP continues to be
updated). AdvC's advc.051 relocation narrows base-rate additions to valid mapped
GP units but does not reconnect the No-Espionage suppression result.

PROMOTION BOUNDARY:
The album has already established for F575 and related controls that current SAS
hides `GAMEOPTION_NO_ESPIONAGE`, defaults it off and ships no ordinary scenario/
map enabling it. Therefore this remains inherited optional/future-proofing debt,
not F584. If SAS restores supported No-Espionage play, this branch should be
promoted/repaired before release.

A robust repair should keep base and per-unit GPP changes atomic: when the mapped
GP unit is suppressed under No Espionage, do not add that source to base GPP
(or deliberately remap it to a supported GP type, if that is the desired policy).
Regression tests should cover a Great-Spy-point building alone and mixed with an
ordinary GP source, checking both total GPP and summed per-unit rates/progress.

C031-WIP379 - POST-WIP378 XML-BACKED IMPROVEMENT-SPECIALIST / PROCESSBUILDING CONTROLS

DURABLE STATE

PURPOSE
-------
Continue from WIP378's current-SAS-data producer/consumer sieve. Recheck old
"current-data masked" conclusions against the actual September 5 light-source XML
rather than relying on prior prose, and promote only a current-supported hard

CORRECTION - CURRENT SAS DOES SHIP IMPROVEMENTFREESPECIALISTS
--------------------------------------------------------------
WIP377 said current SAS had no building with a nonempty
`ImprovementFreeSpecialists` table. That statement is FALSE in the current snapshot.
A namespace-aware parse of shipped `CIV4BuildingInfos.xml` finds exactly two live
entries:

    BUILDING_GLOBE_THEATRE
      PrereqTech = TECH_AESTHETICS
      bNoUnhappiness = 1
      IMPROVEMENT_FOREST_PRESERVE -> +1 free specialist

    BUILDING_NATIONAL_PARK
      PrereqTech = TECH_BIOLOGY
      iUnhealthyPopulationModifier = -100
      IMPROVEMENT_FOREST_PRESERVE -> +1 free specialist

The Globe effect is a SAS addition; National Park is the inherited canonical user.
Do not reuse the old "no shipped producer" argument.

`changeImprovementFreeSpecialists` itself remains a thin mutator:

    m_aiImprovementFreeSpecialists.add(eImprov, iChange);

with no `AI_setAssignWorkDirty(true)` in that function.

CURRENT RUNTIME DIRTYING - NO F584
----------------------------------
The missing setter-local assignment dirty does not currently establish a persistent
normal-play stale citizen state.

1. Globe Theatre building completion/removal is independently masked.
   `processBuilding` applies `changeNoUnhappinessCount` before the
   ImprovementFreeSpecialists table. `changeNoUnhappinessCount` dirties citizen
   assignment. Therefore Globe's normal building-state transition already requests
   reassignment.

2. National Park does not have Globe's NoUnhappiness mask, and
   `changeUnhealthyPopulationModifier(-100)` is itself a thin setter. However the
   normal `CvCity::doTurn` path performs unconditional `AI_assignWorkingPlots()` later
   in the same city turn. A National Park completed during `doProduction()` therefore
   cannot carry stale improvement-free-specialist assignment into the next ordinary
   turn.

3. Improvement transitions are explicitly handled on the plot side. Current
   `CvPlot::setImprovementType` tests the working city's
   `getImprovementFreeSpecialists` for relevant old/new improvements and dirties
   assignment when an improvement-free-specialist effect can change.

4. `changeImprovementFreeSpecialists` is exposed through CyCity/Python, so the setter
   is not a perfect self-contained API. No current SAS Python caller was found that
   mutates this table dynamically. Preserve generic API/future-mod robustness debt,
   not a shipped F584.

SAME-TURN GP NUANCE - NOT CAUSED BY THE MISSING DIRTY FLAG
----------------------------------------------------------
When a building completes during `doProduction`, `doGreatPeople` occurs before the
later unconditional working-plot/specialist reassignment in the city turn. Thus a
newly available improvement-free specialist need not contribute a GP tick on the
completion turn.

Merely adding `AI_setAssignWorkDirty(true)` inside
`changeImprovementFreeSpecialists` would not move assignment before `doGreatPeople`;
it only marks work dirty. Therefore this timing nuance is not evidence that the thin
setter itself is the root. Do not number it without a separate intended-turn-order
contract.

GLOBE THEATRE AI VALUATION - REAL EARLY FUTURE VALUE, BUT POLICY/HEURISTIC
------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvCityAI::AI_buildingValue` values each ImprovementFreeSpecialists entry as:

    countNumImprovedPlots(eImprovement, true) * 50 * iFreeSpecialists

`CvCity::countNumImprovedPlots(..., bPotential=true)` counts either an existing target
improvement OR a workable plot for which:

    kPlot.canHaveImprovement(eImprovement, getTeam())

The latter is plot-validity, not current worker-build availability. It does not require
that the owner currently knows the BuildInfo's prerequisite tech.

Current SAS creates a large timing gap:

    Globe Theatre             -> TECH_AESTHETICS
    BUILD_FOREST_PRESERVE     -> TECH_BIOLOGY

So at Aesthetics, before a player can order a Forest Preserve, each current city plot
that is physically capable of becoming a Forest Preserve can already contribute +50
to Globe Theatre's AI building value. With e.g. 8 such forests that term is +400.

This is a REAL SAS-specific heuristic interaction, but it is not promoted as F584.
Reasons:

* `bPotential=true` is deliberate K-Mod behavior, not an accidental SAS argument;
* the Globe effect itself was deliberately added by SAS as a gradual/permanent
  forest-linked national-wonder effect;
* selecting a forest-rich city for an irrevocable national wonder in anticipation of
  a later improvement can be a defensible long-term policy;
* no hard caller contract says AI_buildingValue must count only immediately realized
  effects, and AI building valuation elsewhere intentionally contains forward-looking
  terms.

Preserve as a balance/heuristic tuning candidate. If desired, a future tuning change
could discount potential-but-not-currently-buildable improvements by tech distance or
count only existing target improvements until the relevant BuildInfo becomes available.
That would be a design choice, not a correctness repair established here.

PROCESSBUILDING SHRINE KEY - EXACT OLD CONTROL RE-HIT
-----------------------------------------------------
While inspecting XML-backed processBuilding state, this suspicious pair resurfaced:

    if (kBuilding.getHolyCity() != NO_RELIGION)
        m_aiShrine.add(kBuilding.getReligionType(), iChange);

It tests `HolyCity` but indexes the cache by `ReligionType`. This is an exact prior
album control, not F584. All seven current shrine buildings set HolyCity and
ReligionType to the same religion, and `hasShrine` reads the same religion-keyed cache.
Generic XML robustness only.

CURRENT-XML DIFFERENCE SIEVE
----------------------------
A structured SAS-vs-Base-AdvC-1.14 building XML comparison was added to the search
method. Rather than treating all inherited building fields equally, the next pass is
prioritizing fields SAS changed from zero/default/empty into active values and tracing
them into authoritative city/player/team consumers. This already caught the stale
ImprovementFreeSpecialists control and is a better current-mod oracle than literal
function-name rarity alone.

TEAMSHARE XML CORRECTION / PERMANENT-ALLIANCE CONTROL
-----------------------------------------------------
The structured current-XML pass also corrected an over-broad shorthand used while
reopening the old TeamShare/Permanent-Alliance area-counter control.

Current globally-limited BuildingInfo entries are NOT literally all TeamShare. A direct
BuildingClass + BuildingInfo parse gives 53 globally-limited entries, of which 33 have
`bTeamShare=1` and 20 have `bTeamShare=0`. Thus "most current world-wonder entries are
TeamShare" is accurate; "all" is not. Mt. Rushmore itself is globally unique but has
`bTeamShare=0`.

This correction does not promote the old PA accounting wrinkle. Ordinary player-scoped
TeamShare effects are replayed once per member by `CvCity::processBuilding` ->
`CvPlayer::processBuilding` and later removed once per member, so their counts remain
balanced. The noncanonical post-merge aggregation remains specific to the team-keyed
`CvArea` effects:

    kArea.changeCleanPowerCount(getTeam(), ...);
    kArea.changeBorderObstacleCount(getTeam(), ...);

Current live producers remain Three Gorges Dam (AreaCleanPower) and Great Wall
(BorderObstacle). The previously established behavioral masking therefore survives; only
the old wording required correction. Preserve robustness/accounting debt, not F584.

F584 / KI#907 - CONFIRMED
AI_BUILDINGVALUE DOES NOT VALUE BUILDING GREAT-GENERAL-RATE MODIFIERS, NOW A LARGE
CURRENT SAS EFFECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
Building `iGreatGeneralRateModifier` is an authoritative PLAYER-GLOBAL effect.
`CvCity::processBuilding` forwards active building state to `CvPlayer::processBuilding`,
which performs:

    changeGreatGeneralRateModifier(
        kBuilding.getGreatGeneralRateModifier() * iChange);

The stored player modifier is then consumed directly when combat experience creates
Great-General progress. Current `CvUnit::changeExperience` computes:

    int iCombatExperienceMod = 100 + kPlayer.getGreatGeneralRateModifier();
    ...
    kPlayer.changeCombatExperience(
        (iChange * iCombatExperienceMod * iGlobalPercent) / SQR(100));

So a +200 building modifier really triples the normal Great-General progress generated
by qualifying combat while active; repeated +15 sources add cumulatively to the same
empire-wide player value.

`CvCityAI::AI_buildingValue`, however, never adds value for
`kBuilding.getGreatGeneralRateModifier()`.

A whole current C++ search finds that getter in `CvCityAI.cpp` only here:

    kBuilding.getGreatGeneralRateModifier() < 40

inside AdvC's national-wonder-slot placement heuristic. That comparison can exempt a
military national wonder from a capital-slot devaluation, but it does NOT price the
Great-General-rate effect into the candidate's construction value.

This is especially diagnostic because `CvPlayerAI::AI_civicValue` DOES explicitly value
the equivalent civic field during a war plan:

    iValue += (kCivic.getGreatGeneralRateModifier() *
        getNumMilitaryUnits()) / 50;

The AI therefore understands the strategic value of this exact player mechanic in the
civic domain while omitting it in the building domain.

CURRENT SAS ACTIVATION
----------------------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and supplied K-Mod 1.46 BuildingInfos contain NO building with a nonzero
`iGreatGeneralRateModifier`. The inherited building-AI omission was consequently dormant
for their shipped data.

Current SAS deliberately activates the field on three buildings:

    BUILDING_JAPAN_DOUJOU       +15
    BUILDING_MT_RUSHMORE       +200
    BUILDING_MILITARY_ACADEMY   +50

The first two make the ordinary AI-construction consequence unambiguous.

A. JAPANESE DOUJOU

The Doujou is the Japanese Barracks replacement, cost 50. Its current XML comment
explicitly states that every early Doujou adds cumulatively to the empire-wide modifier.
Thus e.g. four active Doujous give Japan +60 Great-General rate.

The Doujou also has a fixed `iAIWeight=70`, so Japan is not necessarily prevented from
building it. But that fixed weight is not a semantic valuation of the +15 effect: it does
not scale with city count, accumulated Doujous, military size, war state, or the marginal
Great-General rate that the candidate actually adds. More importantly, the second witness
has no such fixed compensation.

B. MT. RUSHMORE - CLEANEST WITNESS

Current SAS reworked Mt. Rushmore into a globally unique military world wonder and gives
it, among other effects:

    iGreatGeneralRateModifier       = +200
    iGlobalWarWearinessModifier     = +50   (bad for the owner)
    iMilitaryProductionModifier     = +15
    iAIWeight                       = 0

The XML history/comment explicitly describes the new positive military effects as a
tradeoff/compensation for making its global war-weariness modifier positive (harmful).
Runtime implements all of those effects.

`AI_buildingValue` also explicitly prices the WAR-WEARINESS side with the correct sign:

    iValue += ... * -iGlobalWarWearinessModifier * ...;

so Mt. Rushmore's +50 global war weariness reduces its AI value. The building AI also
prices its +15 local military-production effect in the ordinary production block.

But it never reads the +200 Great-General-rate benefit at all. Hence the AI evaluates an
asymmetric subset of the intended tradeoff: it sees a designed drawback and a smaller
production upside while silently dropping the very large empire-wide Great-General-rate
upside.

This can materially lower Mt. Rushmore's rank against other build choices and can make
its intended military tradeoff appear substantially worse to AI than it really is.

The Great-General field is player-visible too: `CvGameTextMgr` emits
`TXT_KEY_BUILDING_GENERAL_RATE_MOD` whenever it is nonzero. This is not a hidden metadata
hint; it is a real advertised gameplay effect.

MILITARY ACADEMY BREADTH
------------------------
Current Military Academy also has +50 Great-General rate, but `iCost=-1` and its creation
path is Great-Person-driven rather than ordinary hammer construction. Preserve it as data
breadth of the same missing building-domain valuation, not as the primary
`AI_buildingValue` reproducer.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod's building AI has no valuation for this field and K-Mod ships no building producer.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 likewise ships no nonzero building producer. AdvC practical 1290 added the
`getGreatGeneralRateModifier() < 40` national-wonder slot-classification check, showing
that the field was acknowledged for placement characteristics, but did not add positive
building value for it.

SAS later activated the dormant field in gameplay data. Commit-diff material records
Mt. Rushmore changing from 0 to +200 (`SASBranch_4855_a9d6994c3a`) and the Japanese
Doujou receiving the deliberately cumulative +15 effect (`SASBranch_6079_921cbbd9c7`,
later wording refined). No corresponding `AI_buildingValue` valuation was added.

Classification:
    inherited K-Mod/AdvC building-AI omission made current-live and strategically large
    by SAS building data.

DEDUP / ROOT BOUNDARY
---------------------
Whole-album searches for `GreatGeneralRateModifier`, `getGreatGeneralRateModifier`, and
building/Great-General valuation found no numbered root owning this omission.

It is distinct from:

* F554 / KI#877 - SAS's regular-building maintenance classifier uses the wrong sign;
  F584 is an entirely omitted positive gameplay field after normal candidate reachability.
* F557 / KI#880 and neighboring `AI_buildingValue` arithmetic findings - those misvalue
  already-considered happiness/other terms; F584 has no Great-General-rate value term at all.
* F577/F578 - hypothetical player-facing building commerce/yield projection helpers omit
  candidate-created global state; F584 is authoritative AI construction ranking in
  `CvCityAI::AI_buildingValue`, not the BUG "actual effects" preview layer.
* Great-General unit-action findings elsewhere in the album - those concern UI/unit-ID
  targeting and do not affect building construction valuation.

REPAIR DIRECTION - NOT IMPLEMENTED
----------------------------------
Add an explicit building-domain value for `kBuilding.getGreatGeneralRateModifier()`.
Do not simply hide it inside a fixed XML `iAIWeight`: the effect is empire-wide and its
marginal strategic value naturally depends on military size / likelihood of combat and,
ideally, current Great-General progress/rate context.

The existing civic valuation supplies a conservative design oracle:

    if (bWarPlan)
        value += modifier * militaryUnits / 50;

A building formula need not copy that coefficient literally, but should preserve the same
sign and scale positively with a positive modifier. Off-war value can be discounted rather
than forced to zero because permanent buildings/wonders outlive current war plans.

For TeamShare buildings in future data, evaluate recipient-team breadth consistently with
how `CvPlayer::processBuilding` actually distributes the player-global effect.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
1. Field isolation:
   Create two otherwise-identical candidate BuildingInfos differing only by
   `iGreatGeneralRateModifier=0` vs +100; in a militarily relevant city/player state,
   assert the +100 candidate receives strictly greater `AI_buildingValue`.

2. Mt. Rushmore current fixture:
   Compare current Mt. Rushmore against a temporary clone with its GG modifier zeroed;
   assert the live +200 version gains an explicit positive AI term while its +50 global
   war-weariness drawback remains negative.

3. Doujou scaling:
   For Japan, verify the marginal +15 effect remains positively valued and that any chosen
   formula responds sensibly to military size/war state rather than relying on `iAIWeight`.

4. Runtime oracle:
   With a +200 source active, confirm qualifying combat XP adds Great-General combat
   experience at 3x the zero-source rate before other domestic/global percentages.

5. Zero control:
   Buildings with `iGreatGeneralRateModifier=0` must retain their existing AI value exactly.

POST-WIP380 STRUCTURED BUILDING-EFFECT SIEVE
--------------------------------------------
After F584's fully omitted building Great-General-rate field, the current-SAS-vs-AdvC
non-default building-effect sieve continued through effects that `AI_buildingValue` DOES
recognize but may still evaluate under assumptions inherited from BtS/K-Mod data.

The next strong seam is `StateReligionCommerces`. Unlike F584, this field has had a
building-AI term since K-Mod. The defect is that the replacement formula treats the XML
amount only as a Boolean gate and then discards its magnitude.

F585 / KI#908 - CONFIRMED
K-MOD'S "MORE ACCURATE" STATE-RELIGION-COMMERCE BUILDING VALUE DROPS THE XML COMMERCE
MAGNITUDE, SO +1 / +2 / +3 EFFECTS RECEIVE THE SAME BASE TERM
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
Current SAS `CvCityAI::AI_buildingValue` loops through commerce types and contains:

    if (eStateReligion != NO_RELIGION &&
        kBuilding.getStateReligionCommerce(eLoopCommerce) != 0)
    {
        int iCount = 0;
        ... count active / making buildings of the state religion ...
        iCount = std::max(iCount, kOwner.getHasReligionCount(eStateReligion));
        iTempValue += iCount * 35 *
            kOwner.AI_averageCommerceMultiplier(eLoopCommerce) / 1000;
    }

`kBuilding.getStateReligionCommerce(eLoopCommerce)` is consulted only in the `!= 0`
condition. Its actual integer value never enters the arithmetic.

Consequently, holding commerce type, empire state, counted qualifying buildings and
commerce multiplier constant, candidate values of:

    +1 StateReligionCommerce
    +2 StateReligionCommerce
    +3 StateReligionCommerce
    +100 StateReligionCommerce

all receive exactly the same StateReligionCommerce contribution to `AI_buildingValue`.

This is not merely a debatable heuristic coefficient. The magnitude was present in the
formula that K-Mod replaced.

K-MOD REGRESSION ANCESTRY - PRACTICAL 962
-----------------------------------------
The supplied reachable-history diff
`KMod_962_d72a951d43.diff` is titled:

    Improved the stateReligionCommerce part in CvCityAI::AI_buildingValue.

It shows the original BtS code being commented out:

    if (eStateReligion != NO_RELIGION)
    {
        iTempValue += (kBuilding.getStateReligionCommerce(iI) *
            kOwner.getHasReligionCount(eStateReligion) * 3);
    }

and replaced by K-Mod's comment:

    A more accurate calculation of the value from increasing commerce on all
    state religion buildings. (eg. Sankore)

The replacement improves the *scope/count* model by counting actual state-religion
buildings / buildings in production and falling back to religion presence, but its final
term is only:

    iCount * 35 * AI_averageCommerceMultiplier(...) / 1000

The old `getStateReligionCommerce(iI)` multiplier was not carried into the replacement.

Later K-Mod practical 1030 reformatted / moved this block but retained the same missing
magnitude. Supplied K-Mod 1.46, Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS all still contain the same
semantic formula.

That history is unusually strong evidence that this is an accidental regression inside
a replacement intended to make the calculation *more* accurate, not an intentional
policy that all nonzero XML amounts should be equivalent.

AUTHORITATIVE RUNTIME IS MAGNITUDE-LINEAR
-----------------------------------------
The gameplay effect does preserve the full XML integer.

`CvPlayer::processBuilding` performs for every commerce type:

    changeStateReligionBuildingCommerce(
        c, kBuilding.getStateReligionCommerce(c) * iChange);

`changeStateReligionBuildingCommerce` stores the full signed change in the player's
`m_aiStateReligionBuildingCommerce` and calls `updateCommerce`.

For each active building whose `ReligionType` matches the owner's current state religion,
`CvCity::getBuildingCommerceByBuilding` then adds:

    kOwner.getStateReligionBuildingCommerce(eCommerce) *
        getNumActiveBuilding(eBuilding)

Thus +3 Research is genuinely 50% more base Research per qualifying state-religion
building than +2 Research. Runtime is linear in the XML amount; the AI candidate value is
not.

CURRENT SHIPPED DATA
--------------------
Current SAS has three nonzero building producers:

    BUILDING_NATYA_SHASTRA      [0, 0, 2] -> +2 Culture
    BUILDING_SPIRAL_MINARET     [2]       -> +2 Gold
    BUILDING_SANKORE            [0, 3]    -> +3 Research

Supplied Base AdvCiv 1.14 has:

    BUILDING_SISTINE_CHAPEL     [0, 0, 3] -> +3 Culture
    BUILDING_SPIRAL_MINARET     [2]       -> +2 Gold
    BUILDING_SANKORE            [0, 2]    -> +2 Research

Supplied K-Mod 1.46 has the same +3 Sistine / +2 Minaret / +2 Sankore pattern.

Therefore the magnitude loss was already live in inherited K-Mod/AdvC data: e.g. a +3
Sistine-style effect is not 50% larger than a +2 effect in this part of building value.
Commerce-type weighting can of course make Gold/Research/Culture terms differ, but the
candidate XML magnitude itself has no influence once it is nonzero.

CURRENT SAS AMPLIFICATION - SANKORE +2 -> +3
---------------------------------------------
SAS history gives a particularly clean same-building regression fixture.

`SASBranch_4855_a9d6994c3a.diff` changes Sankore's inherited state-religion Research
bonus from +2 to +3:

    <!-- custom: was 0 / 2 -->
    <StateReligionCommerces>
        <iCommerce>0</iCommerce>
        <iCommerce>3</iCommerce>
    </StateReligionCommerces>

Runtime therefore makes the state-religion-building Research effect 50% stronger than the
inherited +2 version.

But the K-Mod AI formula only tests Research != 0. For the exact same player/city state,
changing Sankore temporarily between +2 and +3 leaves this entire StateReligionCommerce
AI term bit-for-bit identical.

So the deliberate SAS +2 -> +3 data buff has ZERO effect on this portion of AI construction
valuation.

CONCRETE VALUE WITNESS
----------------------
Take one city evaluating Sankore with a state religion, a fixed `iCount` of qualifying
state-religion buildings, and fixed average Research multiplier M.

Current +3 Sankore receives:

    iCount * 35 * M / 1000

A temporary otherwise-identical +2 Sankore receives:

    iCount * 35 * M / 1000

A +1 clone receives the same term again.

At runtime, however, each qualifying religious building gains respectively +3, +2, or +1
base Research. No other state difference is needed to expose the mismatch.

DEDUP / ROOT BOUNDARY
---------------------
Whole-album semantic search found no numbered root owning the loss of
`StateReligionCommerce` MAGNITUDE inside `CvCityAI::AI_buildingValue` or K-Mod practical
962.

It is independent from:

* F476 / KI#799 - runtime cross-city cache invalidation when player-global
  StateReligionBuildingCommerce / state religion changes. F585 exists even if every city
  cache is perfectly updated; it misranks the candidate before construction.

* F577 / KI#900 - BUG/player-facing hypothetical "Actual Effects" building-commerce
  projection evaluates the candidate against old player-global StateReligionCommerce.
  F585 is authoritative AI construction ranking in `CvCityAI::AI_buildingValue`, not the
  preview helper, and survives a complete F577 repair.

* F584 / KI#907 - building `iGreatGeneralRateModifier` has NO positive AI value term at
  all. F585 concerns an existing StateReligionCommerce term whose count logic runs but
  accidentally collapses all nonzero magnitudes to the same value.

* F557 and neighboring `AI_buildingValue` arithmetic findings concern other fields / signs
  and do not own this K-Mod practical-962 magnitude regression.

CLASSIFICATION
--------------
CONFIRMED inherited K-Mod building-AI valuation regression; current-live in K-Mod/AdvC
and amplified by SAS's deliberate Sankore +2 -> +3 data change.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR DIRECTION - NOT IMPLEMENTED
------------------------------------------------
Preserve K-Mod's improved count of actual / making state-religion buildings, but restore
an explicit dependence on:

    kBuilding.getStateReligionCommerce(eLoopCommerce)

in the final value term.

The exact coefficient is AI tuning rather than a correctness invariant. Blindly
multiplying the existing `35` by the XML amount may over-scale a coefficient that K-Mod
implicitly calibrated around the common +2 effect. A conservative compatibility shape is
to make magnitude linear while re-normalizing the coefficient so the inherited +2 case
stays near its old value, e.g. conceptually:

    legacyTerm * amount / 2

with integer ordering/rounding chosen deliberately. That would make +1 half the inherited
+2 baseline and +3 1.5x it while retaining K-Mod's improved `iCount` semantics.

Alternatively re-tune the coefficient from empirical AI tests, but keep these hard
properties:

1. zero amount -> zero term;
2. positive larger amount -> strictly larger positive term in the same state;
3. if negative StateReligionCommerce is ever supported by data, sign handling must not
   accidentally turn it into a positive benefit merely because the old condition was
   `!= 0`.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
1. Magnitude isolation:
   Evaluate otherwise-identical candidate buildings with +1 / +2 / +3 Research
   StateReligionCommerce in the same city/player state. Assert the respective field term is
   monotonic and proportional according to the chosen normalization rather than identical.

2. Current Sankore fixture:
   Compare current +3 Sankore with a temporary +2 clone. Assert the +3 version receives a
   larger AI value from this mechanic while all unrelated terms remain equal.

3. Runtime oracle:
   With N active state-religion buildings, confirm +3 produces exactly 3N additional base
   Research and +2 produces 2N before city commerce modifiers.

4. Zero control:
   A candidate with 0 StateReligionCommerce must receive no term.

5. Existing count semantics:
   Preserve K-Mod's improved counting of active/making state-religion buildings and its
   religion-presence fallback; the fix should restore magnitude, not regress to the coarse
   BtS count model.

NUMBERING / DURABLE STATE
-------------------------

F586 / provisional KI#909 is UNUSED.

48-CIV / LARGER-DATA REOPENING — RANDOM-RANGE GP RECOVERY STILL OLD-SAVE-ONLY

Current `CvCity::doGreatPeople()` still contains the AdvC recovery branch:

        (iTotalGreatPeopleUnitProgress > CvRandom::getRange());

When true, both the total and each per-unit progress bucket are independently divided by
100 with ceiling before the random choice.

The earlier album control remains correct:

* separate ceiling of the buckets can make their scaled sum slightly exceed the separately
  ceiled total, so the recovery distribution is not mathematically exact;
* however the source explicitly identifies this path as recovery for malformed old AdvC
  0.97 saves;
* ordinary current-SAS GP thresholds / progress do not approach CvRandom's range merely
  because the game supports 48 civilizations or larger maps.

No current-live F586 is established by the expanded player cardinality.

PARTHENON GLOBAL-GP MODIFIER — DYNAMIC OUTPUT IS CORRECT; REASSIGNMENT GRANULARITY ONLY
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS Parthenon has:

    iGlobalGreatPeopleRateModifier = +50

`CvPlayer::processBuilding` applies that modifier through
`changeGreatPeopleRateModifier`. The player mutator itself is intentionally thin and does
not call `AI_makeAssignWorkDirty`.

This initially looked suspicious because `CvCityAI::AI_jobChangeValue` /
`AI_specialistValue` values specialist Great-Person points using the city's current
`getTotalGreatPeopleRateModifier()`.

The runtime/output part is nevertheless coherent:

* `CvCity::getGreatPeopleRate()` reads the total modifier dynamically;
* `CvCity::doGreatPeople()` also reads `getTotalGreatPeopleRateModifier()` dynamically and
  applies it to both total and per-unit progress;
* there is no stale cached GP rate that remains numerically wrong after Parthenon changes
  the player modifier.

What can lag is only citizen *re-optimization* for cities whose assignment was chosen
before the modifier changed during the same player's city-turn sequence. But this is the
same turn-order granularity used for other legitimate empire-wide specialist effects:
individual city turns end with an unconditional `AI_assignWorkingPlots()`, and the next
normal player turn performs the full assignment pass again.

Adding a dirty flag to the player modifier would not by itself cause cities later in the
same city-turn sequence to reassess before their own production / GP tick. Therefore this
is not an isolated broken setter contract and is not promoted as F586.

SHRINE CACHE INDEX ASYMMETRY — REAL API MISMATCH, CURRENT-DATA MASKED
--------------------------------------------------------------------
The structured `processBuilding()` pass preserves one suspicious copy/paste shape:

    if (kBuilding.getHolyCity() != NO_RELIGION)
        m_aiShrine.add(kBuilding.getReligionType(), iChange);

The gate uses `HolyCity`, while the index uses `ReligionType`.

A complete current-building XML check finds seven shipped shrine-like buildings with
`HolyCity != NONE`, and for all seven:

    HolyCity == ReligionType

So the mismatched getter is behaviorally masked by current data. A mod-mod building with a
HolyCity prerequisite different from its ReligionType could corrupt the shrine cache, but
that is not a current SAS F586.
