================================================================================
C031-WIP383 — F586 / KI#909 CONFIRMED; TEAMSHARE BUILDING-AI SCOPE MISMATCH
================================================================================

CONTINUATION BASIS
------------------
Continued from C031-WIP382 with F586 / provisional KI#909 unused and Queue 006
`CvGameCoreDLL/CvCity.cpp` open. The immediate lens was the mechanical census of current
non-default BuildingInfo effects that authoritative runtime code applies versus the scope
and magnitude actually represented by `CvCityAI::AI_buildingValue()`.

The audit repository/gameplay source remains completely untouched. This checkpoint changes
only the audit album.

F586 / KI#909 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------
`CvCityAI::AI_buildingValue()` does not account for `bTeamShare` when valuing building
effects that runtime distributes to every member of the builder's team. As a result,
TeamShare world wonders are systematically valued as though their player-global,
area-global and some one-shot global effects benefit only the constructing player.

This is a scope/cardinality mismatch between authoritative runtime application and AI
construction valuation. It is inherited from BtS through K-Mod and Base AdvCiv and is
current-live in SAS data.

AUTHORITATIVE RUNTIME CONTRACT
------------------------------
Current `CvCity::processBuilding()` applies ordinary player-level building effects as:

    for (MemberIter it(getTeam()); it.hasNext(); ++it)
    {
        if (kBuilding.isTeamShare() || it->getID() == getOwner())
            it->processBuilding(eBuilding, iChange, getArea());
    }

Therefore, for a TeamShare building, each current member of the builder's team receives
`CvPlayer::processBuilding(eBuilding, ...)`.

That player function applies, among other fields:

    GlobalGreatPeopleRateModifier
    GreatGeneralRateModifier
    DomesticGreatGeneralRateModifier
    AnarchyModifier
    GoldenAgeModifier
    GlobalHurryModifier
    GlobalFreeExperience
    GlobalWarWearinessModifier
    AreaFreeSpecialist
    GlobalFreeSpecialist
    CoastalTradeRoutes
    AreaTradeRoutes
    AreaHealth / GlobalHealth
    AreaHappiness / GlobalHappiness
    WorkerSpeedModifier
    GlobalSpaceProductionModifier
    AllCityDefenseModifier
    AreaCleanPower / AreaBorderObstacle
    AreaYieldModifier / GlobalYieldModifier
    GlobalCommerceModifier
    SpecialistExtraCommerce
    StateReligionCommerce
    CommerceFlexible
    BuildingHappinessChanges
    SpecialistYieldChange

The exact semantics differ by field, but the important invariant is straightforward:
for `bTeamShare=1`, these effects are not restricted to the constructing player.

The one-shot global-population path independently confirms the same contract. In
`CvCity::setNumRealBuildingTimed(..., bFirst=true)`, a nonzero
`GlobalPopulationChange` loops all team members and skips another member only when the
building is NOT TeamShare:

    for (MemberAIIter it(getTeam()); it.hasNext(); ++it)
    {
        CvPlayerAI const& kMember = *it;
        if (kMember.getID() != getOwner() && !kBuilding.isTeamShare())
            continue;
        FOR_EACH_CITYAI_VAR(pLoopCity, kMember)
            pLoopCity->setPopulation(... + kBuilding.getGlobalPopulationChange());
    }

Thus a TeamShare Hanging Gardens genuinely changes teammate cities as part of the
building's authoritative completion effect.

AI VALUATION CONTRACT VIOLATION
-------------------------------
At the top of current `AI_buildingValue()`:

    int const iNumCities = kOwner.getNumCities();

This is explicitly the constructing player's city count. The function contains no
`kBuilding.isTeamShare()` / `isTeamShare()` handling at all.

Yet several team-distributed effects are valued directly from that owner-only count. For
example:

    iValue += (kBuilding.getGlobalGreatPeopleRateModifier() * iNumCities) / 8;

    iValue += kBuilding.getGlobalHealth() * iNumCities * 4;

    int iFreeSpecialists = kBuilding.getFreeSpecialist() +
            kBuilding.getAreaFreeSpecialist() * iNumCitiesInArea +
            kBuilding.getGlobalFreeSpecialist() * iNumCities;

    iValue += kBuilding.getGlobalPopulationChange() * iNumCities * 4;

Global happiness, global commerce/yield modifiers, global free experience and multiple
other terms likewise scale from the builder's own cities/context. TeamShare breadth is
never added.

This is not merely a disagreement about heuristic coefficients. The formula's population /
city breadth is smaller than the actual set of cities and players that receive the
candidate building's effect.

CLEAN CURRENT SAS REPRODUCER — HANGING GARDENS
----------------------------------------------
Current SAS `BUILDING_HANGING_GARDEN` has:

    bTeamShare              = 1
    iGlobalHealth           = 1
    iGlobalPopulationChange = 1

Consider an ordinary fixed two-player team before construction:

    Player A (builder): 5 cities
    Player B (teammate): 5 cities

Runtime on completion:

* `GlobalPopulationChange=+1` visits both team members through the explicit TeamShare
  completion loop -> +1 population in all 10 cities;
* `GlobalHealth=+1` reaches `CvPlayer::processBuilding()` for both A and B -> +1 global
  building health to both players, hence across the same 10-city team breadth.

But `AI_buildingValue()` sets:

    iNumCities = Player A.getNumCities() = 5

and values the corresponding cardinality-dependent terms as if only those 5 cities receive
the effects.

Using the function's own existing coefficients, the global-health term is based on 5
cities rather than 10, and the global-population term is likewise based on 5 rather than
10. No later TeamShare adjustment restores Player B's benefit.

This creates a direct current-live under-valuation of Hanging Gardens in AI team games.

CURRENT SAS BREADTH
-------------------
A namespace-aware direct parse of the supplied current
`Assets/XML/Buildings/CIV4BuildingInfos.xml` finds 33 globally-limited entries with
`bTeamShare=1`. The current TeamShare buildings with especially clear nonlocal effects
include:

    Pyramids          iGoldenAgeModifier                +50
    Hanging Gardens   iGlobalPopulationChange            +1
                      iGlobalHealth                      +1
    Parthenon         iGlobalGreatPeopleRateModifier    +50
    Hagia Sophia      iGlobalHappiness                    +2
    Notre Dame        iGlobalFreeSpecialist               +1
    Taj Mahal         iGlobalWarWearinessModifier        -25
    Eiffel Tower      iGlobalHappiness                    +1
    Statue of Liberty iAreaFreeSpecialist                 +1

For the ongoing player/area effects, current `CvCity::processBuilding()` distributes the
source through each team member's `CvPlayer::processBuilding()`, but the corresponding AI
terms are evaluated from the builder's own player/area state only.

Some effects need more than a simple team city-count correction. For example, Pyramids'
CivicOption/GoldenAge-related value can depend on each teammate's civic and Golden Age
context. The finding is therefore broader than one missing multiplication: the valuation
layer lacks the TeamShare scope dimension entirely.

ANCESTRY — BASE BTS -> K-MOD -> ADVC -> SAS
-------------------------------------------
The supplied Civ4CE BtS source is a useful original-lineage oracle here. Its
`CvCity::processBuilding()` already distributes TeamShare buildings across team members,
while BtS `CvCityAI::AI_buildingValue()` contains the same owner-only formulas, including:

    GlobalGreatPeopleRateModifier * iNumCities
    GlobalPopulationChange * iNumCities

and no building TeamShare valuation branch.

Supplied K-Mod 1.46 preserves the same pattern. Supplied Base AdvCiv 1.14 likewise has:

    iValue += (kBuilding.getGlobalGreatPeopleRateModifier() * iNumCities) / 8;
    ...
    iValue += kBuilding.getGlobalPopulationChange() * iNumCities * 4;

with no `isTeamShare()` use in `CvCityAI.cpp` building valuation.

Hanging Gardens is TeamShare with +1 GlobalPopulationChange and +1 GlobalHealth in the
supplied K-Mod, Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS XML, so this is not a SAS-created data
combination. Classification:

    inherited BtS/K-Mod/AdvC AI-building scope omission, current-live in ordinary team play.

DEDUP / ROOT BOUNDARY
---------------------
Whole-album semantic searches for TeamShare + AI/building/value/team-member breadth found
no numbered finding owning this issue.

It is distinct from:

* the WIP181/WIP209/WIP380 TeamShare Permanent-Alliance area-counter controls, which concern
  replay/removal of authoritative stored counters after team reassignment; F586 concerns
  construction AI valuing a correctly-applied live TeamShare effect with owner-only scope;
* F584 / KI#907, where `GreatGeneralRateModifier` had no positive building valuation at all;
  F586 applies to fields that DO have AI value terms, but those terms use the wrong
  recipient breadth when the building is TeamShare;
* F585 / KI#908, where StateReligionCommerce loses its XML magnitude inside K-Mod's
  replacement formula; F586 preserves magnitude but omits teammate recipients;
* acquisition/prospective-owner findings F581/F582, which concern hypothetical ownership
  of one foreign city rather than team distribution of a constructed wonder.

CORRECTION TO WIP377 CONTROL
----------------------------
WIP377 contained the statement that current SAS had no building with nonzero
`iGlobalPopulationChange`, and therefore treated the Civ4CE Hanging Gardens historical
item as current-data masked.

That statement is factually wrong for the supplied current snapshot. A direct
namespace-aware parse and literal XML inspection both show:

    BUILDING_HANGING_GARDEN
    iGlobalPopulationChange = 1

The generic path is current-live, and it becomes the clean primary F586 fixture. Preserve
WIP377 as historical audit context, but this WIP supersedes that specific XML conclusion.

REPAIR DIRECTION — NOT IMPLEMENTED
----------------------------------
Do not simply multiply every building value by team size. Local city effects remain local,
and several TeamShare player effects are contextual per recipient.

A conservative repair should introduce TeamShare-aware recipient state only for effects
that runtime actually distributes through `CvPlayer::processBuilding()` or the explicit
TeamShare one-shot block. At minimum:

1. derive an effect-recipient city count:

       own cities
       + teammate cities when kBuilding.isTeamShare()

   and a matching same-area recipient count for area effects;

2. use those counts in cardinality-based global/area terms such as GlobalPopulationChange,
   GlobalHealth/Happiness, GlobalFreeSpecialist, GlobalGreatPeopleRateModifier, etc.;

3. for recipient-context-sensitive effects (CivicOption, GoldenAgeModifier,
   StateReligionCommerce, specialist modifiers, perhaps war-weariness), ideally evaluate
   the teammate's own relevant state rather than approximating everything from the builder;

4. keep one-player teams bit-for-bit unchanged.

The narrowest safe first patch could correct only the simple count-linear fields while
leaving more contextual TeamShare valuation as documented follow-up, but the root should
remain described as missing recipient-team scope rather than separate bugs per field.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
1. Hanging Gardens fixed-team cardinality:
   Two same-team players with 5 cities each. Compare current Hanging Gardens to an
   otherwise-identical non-TeamShare clone. Assert the TeamShare version receives extra AI
   value representing Player B's five GlobalPopulationChange and GlobalHealth recipients.

2. One-player-team neutrality:
   With no teammate, patched value must match the pre-fix owner-only calculation.

3. Parthenon global modifier breadth:
   Same-team players with different city counts; +50 GlobalGreatPeopleRateModifier should
   gain value as teammate recipient cities are added.

4. Area scope:
   Statue of Liberty's AreaFreeSpecialist should include teammate cities in the wonder's

   than change runtime behavior.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
POST-WIP383 CONTROL — FREE-TECH BUILDING VALUE DROPS THE XML COUNT, BUT CURRENT
SAS ONLY SHIPS A ONE-FREE-TECH PRODUCER
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The inherited free-tech valuation checks:

    if (kBuilding.getFreeTechs() > 0)
    {
        ... estimate an available technology value ...
        iValue += iTechValue * 8 / researchPercent;
    }

The replacement term does not multiply by `kBuilding.getFreeTechs()`. The old
BtS-style code did contain an explicit count multiplier (e.g.
`getFreeTechs() * 80`). Thus a hypothetical two- or three-free-tech building
would receive essentially the same free-tech term as a one-tech building,
apart from whatever state changed between evaluations.

Current SAS does not expose that generalized defect in ordinary data: Oracle is
the only current building with nonzero `iFreeTechs`, and its value is exactly 1.
Keep this as a future/mod-mod magnitude control rather than F587.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
POST-WIP383 CONTROL / CORRECTION — NEGATIVE MILITARY-PRODUCTION VALUATION IS
NOT GENERICALLY MASKED; BARBARIAN PALACE MAKES IT CURRENT-LIVE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

An initial pass almost closed the signed-domain omission because the Barbarian
civilization receives BUILDINGCLASS_PALACE as a free building class and the
first city therefore starts with `BUILDING_BARBARIAN_PALACE` for free.
That closure was too broad and is superseded by F587 below.

The important lifecycle distinction is:

* `BUILDING_BARBARIAN_PALACE` has `bCapital=0`; it is a government center, not
  the ordinary capital marker.
* `CvCity::init` grants civilization `FreeBuildingClasses` only when the player
  has exactly one city at initialization.
* `BUILDING_BARBARIAN_PALACE` has `bNeverCapture=1`, so ordinary conquest does
  not restore it to the conquering civ in `CvPlayer::acquireCity`.
* If Barbarians still own another city after the original Palace city is
  captured, no normal `findNewCapital()` relocation recreates this non-capital
  building there.
* Once the Palace-class count is back to zero, an ordinary remaining barbarian
  city that is not already a government center can legally construct the
  mapped Barbarian Palace: it has cost 5 and no technology prerequisite.
* `CvCityAI::AI_barbChooseProduction()` explicitly calls `AI_chooseBuilding()`;
  therefore `AI_bestBuildingThreshold` / `AI_buildingValue` is a live caller
  for the reconstructed building.

So the signed-domain omission below is not merely dormant XML robustness.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F587 / KI#910 — AI_buildingValue ignores negative building military-production
modifiers; current Barbarian Palace can be rebuilt after conquest and its -25%
military-production drawback receives zero construction-value penalty
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvCity::processBuilding()` applies a building's military-production modifier
with its full signed XML value:

    changeMilitaryProductionModifier(
        kBuilding.getMilitaryProductionModifier() * iChange);

`CvCity::getProductionModifier(UnitTypes)` then applies that authoritative city
state to every military-production unit:

    if (GC.getInfo(eUnit).isMilitaryProduction())
        iMultiplier += getMilitaryProductionModifier();

and clamps only the final total at -50. Thus a negative building value is a
real production penalty, not metadata.

`CvCityAI::AI_buildingValue()`, however, gates the entire building-side
military-production valuation on positivity:

    const int iMilitaryProductionModifier =
        kBuilding.getMilitaryProductionModifier();

    if (iHasMetCount > 0 && iMilitaryProductionModifier > 0)
    {
        ... add positive military-production value ...
    }

There is no corresponding `< 0` branch or later signed correction. A negative
modifier therefore contributes exactly zero through this mechanic even though
runtime immediately slows military-unit production.

CURRENT SAS ACTIVATION
----------------------
A namespace-aware/current-XML census gives these nonzero building values:

    BUILDING_BARBARIAN_PALACE   -25
    BUILDING_MONGOL_GER          +15
    BUILDING_HEROIC_EPIC         +50
    BUILDING_MT_RUSHMORE         +15
    BUILDING_PENTAGON            +15

Supplied AdvC 1.14 and K-Mod 1.46 do not ship any negative building value in
this field; their active producers are positive (Heroic Epic and Military
Academy). The inherited K-Mod/AdvC positive-only branch was therefore dormant
for negative building data until SAS activated the signed domain.

CLEAN CURRENT-LIVE BARBARIAN RECONSTRUCTION WITNESS
---------------------------------------------------
Construct the following normal gameplay state:

1. Barbarians own at least two cities, A and B.
2. A was their first city and received the civilization's free Palace class,
   mapped to `BUILDING_BARBARIAN_PALACE`.
3. A is conquered by a normal civilization while B survives.
4. Because Barbarian Palace has `bNeverCapture=1`, the conquest reconstruction
   skips it; the Barbarian Palace-class count becomes zero.
5. B is not already a government center. Barbarian Palace has no tech
   prerequisite, only 5 hammer cost, and is the Barbarian civilization's legal
   Palace-class building, so B can construct it once the class is absent.
6. `AI_barbChooseProduction()` reaches its ordinary `AI_chooseBuilding()` calls,
   which evaluate available buildings through `AI_buildingValue()`.

At that point the candidate Palace's `-25` military-production effect is a real
marginal drawback. If B constructs it, every military-production unit gets 25
percentage points less production modifier through
`CvCity::getProductionModifier(UnitTypes)`.

But the building AI's positive-only gate contributes no negative value at all.
The Palace is ranked from its other effects/cost while the military-production
penalty is silently omitted. That can raise it above competing infrastructure
or units relative to its actual post-construction value.

This is particularly relevant to Barbarian behavior because
`AI_barbChooseProduction()` deliberately alternates building choices with a
strong military-unit-production policy. A building that makes those subsequent
military units slower is exactly the kind of effect the construction ranking
needs to price.

ANCESTRY / CLASSIFICATION
-------------------------
The positive-only check is inherited through K-Mod and AdvC. Their supplied
building XML does not use a negative `iMilitaryProductionModifier`, so the
problem is best classified as an inherited signed-domain assumption activated
by current SAS data.

It is not a general claim that K-Mod's positive valuation formula can simply be
run unchanged with a negative number: parts of that formula select preferred
high-production wonder cities and reward synergy with existing free XP. The
hard correctness point is narrower: the current function reads the field,
accepts it as signed runtime data, and then drops the entire negative domain.
A repair should add a deliberate penalty model for `< 0` rather than blindly
remove the positivity gate.

DEDUP
-----
Whole-album semantic search found no existing root for a negative
`iMilitaryProductionModifier` being ignored by AI construction value.

Distinct nearby families include:

* F398 — BUG/player-facing additional-production hover incorrectly treats
  conditional military/domain/space modifiers as generic hammer yield;
* F584 — building AI entirely omits `iGreatGeneralRateModifier`;
* F585 — StateReligionCommerce AI term retains nonzero/type context but drops
  the XML amount;
* F586 — TeamShare recipient breadth is omitted from building valuation.

F587 is a separate signed-domain construction-ranking error with its own
current producer and ordinary barbarian caller.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Preserve the current positive-value logic. Add an explicit negative-modifier
valuation path that penalizes a candidate according to expected military-unit
production lost in this city. Keep the sign handling separate from the
positive limited-wonder placement bonuses unless a broader formula is proved
safe for both domains.

At minimum, regression tests should establish:

1. positive Heroic-Epic/Ger/Pentagon-style values retain current behavior;
2. a constructible building with `iMilitaryProductionModifier=-25` receives a
   lower value than the otherwise-identical zero-modifier building;
3. Barbarian Palace is tested in the post-conquest reconstruction state above,
   not only in the first-city-free state;
4. runtime unit-production math remains unchanged; this is an AI valuation
   repair only;
5. `iHasMetCount==0` does not accidentally erase a real negative production
   penalty merely because the old positive-benefit heuristic waited until the
   AI had met another civilization.

F587 PRECISION CORRECTION — CURRENT UNPATCHED ACQUISITION DESTROYS THE BARBARIAN
PALACE THROUGH THE ALREADY-OWNED F495 SOURCE/DESTINATION BUG, NOT DIRECTLY FROM
THE SOURCE BUILDING'S bNeverCapture CHECK
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

WIP384 correctly established the important gameplay outcome needed by F587:
a Barbarian Palace can disappear when its city is conquered while another
Barbarian city survives, leaving the surviving city able to evaluate/rebuild
the Palace through `AI_barbChooseProduction` -> `AI_chooseBuilding`.

One sentence in WIP384 described today's exact conquest mechanism too simply.
Current AdvC/SAS `acquireCity()` first remaps a non-world source building class
to the RECIPIENT civilization's concrete building type:

    BuildingTypes const eBuilding =
        (GC.getInfo(eLoopBuilding).isWorldWonder() ?
         eLoopBuilding : getCivilization().getBuilding(eBuildingClass));

For an ordinary major civilization capturing a Barbarian Palace:

    source      = BUILDING_BARBARIAN_PALACE
    class       = BUILDINGCLASS_PALACE
    destination = BUILDING_PALACE

The subsequent current-code `kBuilding.isNeverCapture()` check therefore reads
the mapped normal Palace, not the source Barbarian Palace. Likewise the current
conquest-probability lookup reads the destination Palace.

More importantly, the restoration count is the already-confirmed F495 bug:

    aiNumRealBuilding.get(eBuilding)

instead of the source snapshot:

    aiNumRealBuilding.get(eLoopBuilding)

The old barbarian city has a Barbarian-Palace count, not a normal-Palace count,
so the destination-key read is zero and no Palace is reconstructed in the
captured replacement city.

Thus the present shipped path still removes the Barbarian Palace exactly as
F587 needs; the immediate current mechanism is F495's wrong source/destination
snapshot key rather than a direct source `bNeverCapture` skip.

F587 ALSO SURVIVES THE PLANNED F495 REPAIR
------------------------------------------
This precision correction does not make F587 depend on leaving F495 unfixed.
F495's recorded repair direction restores explicit source/destination identity
and also calls out that K-Mod/BtS use SOURCE-building conquest policy.

Under that intended repair:

    source BUILDING_BARBARIAN_PALACE has bNeverCapture = 1

so ordinary conquest still removes the source building. Therefore a state with
another surviving Barbarian city still reaches the post-loss reconstruction
choice and still exercises F587's ignored `-25` military-production drawback.

Keep F587 / KI#910 CONFIRMED. Supersede only WIP384's simplified statement of
the exact current acquisition branch.

BASE-YIELD / WLTKD / VASSAL CONTROLS
------------------------------------
`CvCity::calculateBaseYieldRate()` is a direct invariant recomputation of the already-applied plot,
specialist/free-specialist, active-building, trade and corporation yield sources. No producer was

calls `updateMaintenance`; `isNoMaintenance()` reads WLTKD dynamically. No stale secondary cache or

RELIGION / CORPORATION TRANSITION CONTROLS
------------------------------------------

current-data-masked corporation control; no current SAS produced corporation bonus is consumed by
another producing corporation.

HEADQUARTERS ONE-SHOT FREE-UNIT CONTROL
---------------------------------------
`CvCity::setHeadquarters()` is the founding wrapper: it calls `CvGame::setHeadquarters` and then
creates the corporation's configured free unit. That initially looked dangerous for HQ relocation.
The ownership/reconstruction path does not call this wrapper, however. `acquireCity()` restores an
HQ through `CvGame::setHeadquarters` directly. The game-level setter updates old/new HQ corporation
state but does not mint the founding free unit. Therefore capture, peaceful transfer, or ordinary HQ
restoration does not grant a second founder/executive. No F588.

PROSPECTIVE CORPORATION-MAINTENANCE BOUNDARY
--------------------------------------------
F581/F582 make prospective maintenance a high-value audit seam, but corporation maintenance inside
`calculateBaseMaintenanceTimes100(eOwner)` is intentionally excluded for a foreign prospective
owner. The source states explicitly:

    // advc.ctr: Anticipating corporation maintenance gets too complicated
    if (eOwner == getOwner())
        iR += calculateCorporationMaintenanceTimes100();

Therefore this is an acknowledged approximation, unlike F581's missing hypothetical city/area +1
or F582's retained-government-center omission. Do not relabel it as a broken eOwner contract.

EXACT RE-HIT - CULTURE PROCESS `iData2 > 0` IS WIP367'S CLOSED LEVEL-0 CASE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
The process-order lifecycle again surfaced the apparently suspicious K-Mod pair:

    // pushOrder, human Culture process
    iData2 = getCultureLevel();

and later:

    if (kOrder.iData2 > 0 && ... &&
        getCultureLevel() > kOrder.iData2)
    {
        popOrder(0, false, ALL_CHOOSE);
    }

At first glance `-1` is the unset sentinel while culture level 0 is a valid enum, suggesting a
classic sentinel-vs-zero bug. Whole-album dedup finds this exact candidate already closed in
C031-WIP367. Current `calculateCultureLevel()` scans levels in reverse and both NONE and POOR have a
0 threshold; an ordinary non-occupation city with 0 culture therefore resolves to POOR (1), so the
human process stores a positive marker. NONE (0) is primarily forced occupation state and does not
provide a clean ordinary first-border-expansion witness. F494 remains the real live Culture-process
metadata defect (AI Auto Play hand-back), not this level-0 branch.

C031-WIP387 - F588 / KI#911 CONFIRMED - TEAMSHARE GOLDEN AGE IS OWNER-ONLY

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F588 / KI#911 - TEAMSHARE TAJ MAHAL / VERSAILLES GOLDEN AGE IS GRANTED ONLY TO
THE CONSTRUCTING PLAYER
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvCity::setNumRealBuildingTimed()` handles one-shot building rewards after a
new real building is added with `bFirst=true`.

For a Golden-Age building, current AdvC/SAS mutates only the city owner:

    if (kBuilding.isGoldenAge())
    {
        if (bEndOfTurn)
        {
            for (int i = 0; i < iChange; i++)
                kOwner.startGoldenAgeDelayed();
        }
        else kOwner.changeGoldenAgeTurns(iChange * kOwner.getGoldenAgeLength());
    }

There is no `kBuilding.isTeamShare()` check and no team-member loop.
`startGoldenAgeDelayed()` and `changeGoldenAgeTurns()` are both player-local;
no later team-level mechanism propagates either state to teammates.

The immediately adjacent one-shot global-population effect has the missing
scope logic explicitly:

    if (kBuilding.getGlobalPopulationChange() != 0)
    {
        for (MemberAIIter it(getTeam()); it.hasNext(); ++it)
        {
            CvPlayerAI const& kMember = *it;
            if (kMember.getID() != getOwner() && !kBuilding.isTeamShare())
                continue;
            ... change every qualifying member city population ...
        }
    }

That contrast makes this a runtime TeamShare scope omission, not merely an AI
valuation preference.

CURRENT LIVE DATA
-----------------
Current SAS ships two buildings with BOTH:

    bTeamShare = 1
    bGoldenAge = 1

namely:

    BUILDING_TAJ_MAHAL
    BUILDING_VERSAILLES

Taj Mahal already has this combination in the supplied AdvC / BtS lineage.
SAS additionally changed Versailles from `bGoldenAge=0` to `bGoldenAge=1`, so
it supplies a second current witness.

The other TeamShare one-shot combinations support the same scope contract:

* Hanging Gardens: `iGlobalPopulationChange=+1`; the code explicitly loops all
  team members when `bTeamShare=1`.
* Oracle: `iFreeTechs=1`; the free technology is selected by one player but
  technology ownership is team-level, so the reward is intrinsically shared.

Golden Age state is different: it is stored on `CvPlayer`, not `CvTeam`, and
therefore requires explicit teammate application when a TeamShare building is
supposed to grant the reward team-wide. Current code supplies none.

CLEAN CURRENT-LIVE REPRODUCER
-----------------------------
Use a normal fixed team with two alive players A and B.

1. A and B are on the same team before the wonder is completed.
2. A completes Taj Mahal normally at end of turn.
3. `setNumRealBuildingTimed(..., bFirst=true, bEndOfTurn=true)` reaches the
   Golden-Age one-shot block.
4. Only A executes `startGoldenAgeDelayed()`; A's
   `m_iScheduledGoldenAges` increases.
5. B receives no scheduled Golden Age and no immediate Golden Age turns.
6. On player activation, A converts its scheduled Golden Age to turns; B has
   no corresponding state to convert.

The same owner-only result occurs through the immediate/non-end-turn path,
which calls only A's `changeGoldenAgeTurns()`.

Current SAS Versailles reproduces the same root because it is also TeamShare
and now has `bGoldenAge=1`.

ANCESTRY
--------
The supplied Civ4CE BtS body already has the mismatch:

* Golden-Age one-shot -> `GET_PLAYER(getOwnerINLINE()).changeGoldenAgeTurns(...)`
  only;
* adjacent global-population one-shot -> loops same-team players and checks
  `isTeamShare()`.

K-Mod preserves that structure. AdvC preserves it as well. Practical 2208
(advc.001x, "Fix issues with Taj Mahal Golden Age length") changes WHEN the
builder's wonder Golden Age begins by introducing delayed scheduling at normal
end-of-turn completion, but it does not change WHO receives the TeamShare
reward. Therefore F588 is inherited from BtS rather than introduced by
practical 2208.

SAS activates additional breadth by making Versailles a Golden-Age wonder.

TEAMSHARE CONTRACT BOUNDARY
---------------------------
This finding does NOT claim that every field in a TeamShare BuildingInfo is
blindly copied to every teammate. City-local effects such as the building
city's Great-Person points remain local by design.

The narrower contract is player/global reward scope:

* persistent player-level building effects are explicitly replayed to every
  team member by `CvCity::processBuilding()` when `bTeamShare=1`;
* the adjacent one-shot global-population reward explicitly applies to every
  team member when `bTeamShare=1`;
* a free technology is team-owned by the game's technology model;
* the one-shot Golden Age is likewise a player-global reward, but is the sole
  current TeamShare one-shot in this block that remains owner-only because its
  state lives on `CvPlayer` and the code omits the teammate loop.

That is sufficient to classify the owner-only Golden Age as a separate runtime
scope contradiction.

DEDUP
-----
Whole-album semantic searches for TeamShare + Golden Age / Taj / Versailles /
scheduled Golden Ages / teammates found no existing runtime root.

Distinct nearby families:

* F586 / KI#909: `AI_buildingValue()` values correctly-applied TeamShare
  effects using only the builder's own city/player scope. That is an AI score
  omission. F588 is the authoritative runtime reward itself being owner-only.
* WIP181/WIP209/WIP380: Permanent-Alliance TeamShare replay / area-counter

FIXED TRADE-ROUTE CAPACITY - CLEAN
----------------------------------
`CvCity` allocates its trade-city cache to `MAX_TRADE_ROUTES`, but the legal city route count is
also explicitly clamped before consumers use it:

    return std::min(iTradeRoutes, GC.getDefineINT(CvGlobals::MAX_TRADE_ROUTES));

and `updateTradeRoutes()` asserts the resulting count does not exceed the cache size.

Current SAS route-count data does not bypass that boundary. Relevant direct building changes are
small (+1 on Castle / Barbarian Castle / Airport / Spanish Lonja), while current civic changes
include Protectionism -1 and Trade Bloc +1. Protectionism's negative route count is the exact old
WIP229 control: it offsets inherited `INITIAL_TRADE_ROUTES = 1`, so current play does not enter an
unsupported negative city-route domain.

No fixed-array overflow / negative-loop F589 was established.

POWERBONUS RESOURCE-vs-BUILDING ORDER - POSITIVE CONTROL
---------------------------------------------------------
The apparent producer-order asymmetry at the prior cutoff is fully closed by the later per-resource
part of `CvCity::processBuilding`.

When the resource already exists and the conditional-power building is added, the building path
executes:

    if (kBuilding.getPowerBonus() == eLoopBonus)
        changePowerCount(iChange, kBuilding.isDirtyPower());

When the building already exists and the resource appears, `processBonus()` computes the same
active conditional-power source through `getBonusPower(...)` and changes power there.

Thus current Coal Plant / Coal and Nuclear Plant / Uranium converge to the same city power state in
both producer orders. This is a useful positive invariant, not F589.

GENERIC SELF-PRODUCED / SELF-SUPPRESSED BONUS ORDER HAZARD - CURRENT-DATA MASKED
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The same mechanical producer-order pass exposes a real generic fragility in `processBuilding` if a
single building were configured BOTH to create/suppress a resource (`FreeBonus` / `NoBonus`) and to
condition its own health, happiness, power or yield effect on that same resource.

`setNumRealBuildingTimed` changes the building count before `processBuilding` runs. Therefore:

* a hypothetical self-`FreeBonus` building can make `changeFreeBonus -> processBonus(+1)` see the
  newly active building and apply its conditional effect, after which the later per-bonus loop can
  apply the same candidate effect again;
* a hypothetical self-`NoBonus` building can make `changeNoBonusCount -> processBonus(-1)` see the
  newly active building and remove an effect that had never existed before construction.

Current shipped SAS XML masks both shapes completely. It contains no building with a non-NONE
`FreeBonus`. The only current `NoBonus` producer is `BUILDING_NATIONAL_PARK -> BONUS_COAL`, and it
has no Coal-keyed BonusHealthChanges / BonusHappinessChanges / BonusYieldModifiers / PowerBonus of
its own. The already-confirmed F563 remains the separate current NoBonus-before-verification bug.

Keep this as generic XML/mod-mod robustness debt; do not spend F589 on it.

SAS EXPANDED WORLD-SIZE / DISTANCE ARITHMETIC - NO NEW ROOT
------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS extends the world-size table through SAS24/SAS32/SAS40/SAS48. The native city
maintenance distance path was rechecked against those larger maps rather than assuming BtS-sized
geometry.

`calculateMaintenanceDistance` caps the selected distance with
`GC.getMap().maxMaintenanceDistance()`, and `calculateDistanceMaintenanceTimes100` normalizes by
`maxTypicalDistance()`. With the current SAS world dimensions and maintenance percentages, the
intermediate products remain comfortably inside signed 32-bit `int`; no zero denominator or map-
size-driven overflow was established.

The two actual nearby distance-domain defects remain the already-owned roots:

* F567: colony-maintenance cap multiplies the max-distance factor twice;
* F568: `maxTypicalDistance` is used as a hard religion-distance bound.

Do not duplicate either under the expanded-world-size lens.

CURRENT `FreeBuilding` CHAINS - THRESHOLD COUNTER IS REVERSIBLE
---------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS has several unusual but live free-building chains, especially the Barbarian building
set (e.g. Walls/Castle/Lighthouse -> Palace, Palace -> Granary, Granary -> Barracks) plus
Stonehenge -> Monument.

`CvPlayer::changeFreeBuildingCount` stores source multiplicity but installs/removes the city free
building only on the 0 -> positive and positive -> 0 boundaries. Nested free-building effects can
therefore increment the downstream source count multiple times without installing duplicate city
copies; removal unwinds the same nested source counts and removes the downstream free building only
when the last source disappears.

The current Barbarian civilization mappings resolve Palace/Granary/Barracks to the intended
Barbarian concrete types, while unsupported classes such as Monument map to NONE; the existing
`CvPlayer::processBuilding` NO_BUILDING guard handles that mapping. No recursive duplicate-copy,
negative-count or missing-mapping F589 was established here.

not as evidence by name count. Several superficially thin setters immediately collapse into prior

* sea/river plot yield setters -> `updateYield` and prior player-wide rank/cache reconciliation;

* improvement free specialists -> WIP379 current Globe/National Park control;

  in WIP365.

proxy for semantic audit coverage.

  Relational team/master-vassal eligibility is the F455/KI#778 family. The current full recount

  Ordinary population, government-center, city maintenance-modifier, WLTKD, occupation,

  other players' HQ world-level commerce), with HQ-owner activity effects in the F491 family.

  The exceptional persisted passive-visibility entitlement and directional EP/cost transitions

* surrounding health/happiness caches
  Access-dependent relation/ownership invalidation is already F509/KI#832. Local feature and
  improvement source changes still call the combined updater.

This map is important late-audit evidence: the strongest stored-state failure modes are not
unexplored; they are exactly where the earlier album findings cluster.

POWER HEALTH / POWERED-COMMERCE STATE - CLEAN CURRENT CONTROL
--------------------------------------------------------------
`m_iPowerGoodHealth` / `m_iPowerBadHealth` are rebuilt whenever local power/dirty-power truth
changes through `changePowerCount`.

The nonlocal clean-power input is also wired correctly. `CvArea::changeCleanPowerCount` compares
old/new area clean-power truth and on an edge calls both:

    GET_TEAM(eIndex).updateCommerce();
    GET_TEAM(eIndex).updatePowerHealth();

Thus Three Gorges / area-clean-power transitions refresh both powered yield/commerce consequences
and stored power health for the affected team. This remains the older positive control rather
than F589.

FRESH-WATER HEALTH - CURRENT RUNTIME RIVER-EDGE REPAIR CLOSES THE LIVE MUTATOR
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`m_iFreshWaterGoodHealth` / `m_iFreshWaterBadHealth` are stored rather than queried dynamically.
Historically that makes river-edge mutation a natural invalidation hazard.

The current SAS source now explicitly repairs this in the finalized-game river setters: both
`CvPlot::setNOfRiver` and `setWOfRiver` call the shared `updateRiverDerivedState` helper after a
real edge change. That helper updates irrigation around the edge, calls `updateFreshWaterHealth`
for nearby cities, and rebuilds plot groups. The source comments tie this to the already-repaired
KI#351 family.

Map-generation initialization still occurs before final initialization and city initialization
itself calls `updateFreshWaterHealth`, so no current ordinary runtime freshwater-cache F589 remains.

EXTRA BUILDING HAPPINESS / HEALTH - INPUTS ARE PAIRED WITH REBUILDS
-------------------------------------------------------------------
`updateExtraBuildingHappiness` and `updateExtraBuildingHealth` store owner-specific building
bonuses in four city counters. Their live mutable inputs are:

    active civilization-mapped building presence
    + player's per-BuildingType extra happiness/health maps.

Both sides are explicitly paired:

* `processBuilding` calls both city rebuilds after building state changes;
* `CvPlayer::changeExtraBuildingHappiness` mutates the player map and immediately calls the
  player-wide happiness rebuild;
* `CvPlayer::changeExtraBuildingHealth` does the analogous health rebuild.

Obsolescence/acquisition and civilization-mapping edge cases were already covered in the earlier
Queue-006 building-state work (including F566 for the separate event missing-mapping setter).
No new stored-cache root survives here.

RELIGION HAPPINESS / RELIGION COMMERCE - CLEAN DEPENDENCY PAIRING
-----------------------------------------------------------------
`m_iReligionGoodHappiness` / `m_iReligionBadHappiness` depend on city religion presence, effective
state religion, and the player's state/non-state religion happiness values.

Current transitions refresh those inputs:

* `setHasReligion` calls `updateReligionHappiness`;
* changing state/non-state religion happiness calls the player-wide updater;
* `setLastStateReligion` and state-religion-count transitions call the player-wide updater.

Religion commerce is a separate stored map. Under current `advc.172`, ordinary religion commerce
is no longer selected by state-religion identity; it depends on city religion presence and holy-
city state. `setHasReligion` rebuilds it, and `CvGame::setHolyCity` explicitly rebuilds both the old
and new holy cities. The state-religion building-commerce defect therefore remains F476's distinct
`m_aiBuildingCommerce` root, not a hidden `m_aiReligionCommerce` sibling.

SPECIALIST-DERIVED YIELD / COMMERCE - IMMEDIATE MUTATION CHAIN
--------------------------------------------------------------
Changing assigned or free specialist counts enters `processSpecialist`, which immediately:

* changes the specialist's base yields;
* changes specialist commerce and rebuilds the relevant commerce cache;
* calls `updateExtraSpecialistYield()` for the owner's player-wide specialist-extra-yield layer;
* updates GP rate / specialist free experience as applicable.

Player-side specialist-extra-yield mutation likewise calls the city updater. The thin
`changeImprovementFreeSpecialists` setter remains the WIP379 current-control/API-robustness case;
normal Globe/National-Park and improvement transitions do not establish a new persistent cache
root.

CORPORATION YIELD / COMMERCE / MAINTENANCE - EXISTING ROOTS + CURRENT LOCAL PAIRING
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`updateCorporation` remains the central local rebuild: produced bonuses, building commerce,
corporation yield, corporation commerce and maintenance are recalculated together.

`changeNumBonuses` calls it whenever the changed bonus is a prerequisite of an active corporation
present in the city; `changeNoBonusCount` calls it after resource suppression changes; occupation
and player anarchy edge changes also call corporation rebuilds. The major nonlocal/activity holes
are already represented by F491/F496 and the older corporation-maintenance cache root F421.
No separate current local resource -> corporation-cache omission was established.

CULTURE LEVEL / RANK CACHES - DIRECT INVALIDATION CONTROL
----------------------------------------------------------
`setCultureTimes100` immediately calls `updateCultureLevel`; population/base-yield/yield/commerce
rank caches continue to route through their owner-wide invalidators, including
`setBaseYieldRate -> updateCommerce -> invalidateYieldRankCache`. These remain the WIP365/WIP366
rank controls rather than F589.

CLASSIFICATION
--------------
No independent current-live F589 root survived the stored-derived-state census.

The useful result is a dependency closure: nearly every high-risk stored CvCity aggregate either
has a current explicit producer->rebuild chain or maps to a previously numbered invalidation root.
That means another pass over generic `update*`/`change*` naming would now have very low expected
value and a high duplicate rate.

C031-WIP392 - DESTRUCTIVE / REPLACEMENT TRANSITION CENSUS - F589 CONFIRMED

PURPOSE
-------

question is whether legal current city destruction, acquisition, recreation and hard-count

This tranche first closes several attractive but already-owned or current-data-masked acquisition

`CvCity::init` / `CvCity::kill` area-count lifecycle.

`GET_TEAM(eOwner)` IN `CvCity::kill` - TYPE-OVERLOAD FALSE ALARM / WIP362 RE-HIT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvCity::init` increments:

    GET_TEAM(getTeam()).changeNumCities(1);

while `CvCity::kill` decrements:

    PlayerTypes const eOwner = getOwner();
    ...
    GET_TEAM(eOwner).changeNumCities(-1);

In isolation this looks like a PlayerTypes value being used as a TeamTypes index. It is not.
AdvC deliberately overloads `GET_TEAM` by static enum type: `GET_TEAM(TeamTypes)` addresses that
team directly, while `GET_TEAM(PlayerTypes)` resolves `GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).getTeam()` first.
Therefore `GET_TEAM(eOwner)` is the old owner's actual current team, including pre-teaming /
Permanent-Alliance cases.

The album had already preserved this exact typed-overload trap in WIP362. Do not promote it.

`acquireCity()` PERSISTENT-STATE PRESERVATION CENSUS - SATURATED BY EXISTING ROOTS
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A member-by-member pass over serialized/current city state against `CvPlayer::acquireCity()` found
no independent F589 in the already-dense transfer family:

* F574 owns active espionage extra-health / extra-happiness duration state lost across the
  kill -> recreate transfer.
* F575 owns event-created persistent city-local scalar state that is not preserved; WIP360 already
  broadened that family to the relevant adjacent serialized/event state.
* WIP357 records the inherited per-owner reset semantics of revolt-history counters.
* religion influence is reconstructed from surviving religion/building/holy-city state rather than
  raw-copied.
* food, production and build-queue state follow the inherited new-owner-starts-fresh-production
  transfer policy.
* source/destination unique-building conversion, provenance and conquest-policy indexing are the
  already-confirmed F495/KI#818 family.
* current SAS BFC-artist acquisition provenance remains the WIP358 positive control.

CITY `m_szScriptData` - GENERIC TRANSFER ROBUSTNESS ONLY UNDER CURRENT SAS DATA
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
City script data are serialized and explicitly exposed to Python:

    CvCity::getScriptData()
    CvCity::setScriptData(...)
    pStream->ReadString(m_szScriptData)
    pStream->WriteString(m_szScriptData)

but `CvPlayer::acquireCity()` does not snapshot or restore `m_szScriptData`; a city with custom
script data therefore loses it when ownership is implemented as kill -> recreate.

This is a real generic scenario/API preservation seam, but current SAS searches found no shipped
map, scenario or gameplay script that assigns city ScriptData. Under the album's current-live
threshold it remains robustness debt rather than F589.

REAL/FREE BUILDING OVERLAP ON ACQUISITION - CURRENT CONTROL
------------------------------------------------------------
Acquisition restores persistent real buildings with `bFirst=false`, so their ordinary persistent
effects return without replaying creation-only one-shot rewards. If the recipient already has the
same class/type effectively present through a free-building source, the effective building-count
delta can correctly remain zero while the real copy itself is retained; removing the free source
later then exposes the already-owned real copy. No duplicate persistent processing or lost real copy
was established from this overlap.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F589 / KI#912 - `CvArea::changeCitiesPerPlayer` REPORTS EVERY POSITIVE CITY ADDITION
AS A BARBARIAN CITY CREATION, SO ORDINARY CIV CITIES AND OWNERSHIP TRANSFERS
FALSELY SUPPRESS FUTURE BARBARIAN CITY SPAWNING
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED. The defect is reached by ordinary current-SAS city founding and city ownership
reconstruction. It is inherited from AdvC's `advc.300` Barbarian-city-density feature; K-Mod and
the supplied Civ4CE/BtS body do not contain this counter.

ROOT CONTRACT
-------------
AdvC adds a per-area persistent counter whose names and only gameplay consumer establish a narrow,
unambiguous meaning:

    int CvArea::getBarbarianCitiesEverCreated() const
    void CvArea::reportBarbarianCityCreated()
    int m_iBarbarianCitiesEver;

The consumer in `CvGame::createBarbarianCity` computes:

    int iDestroyedCities = a.getBarbarianCitiesEverCreated() -
            a.getCitiesPerPlayer(BARBARIAN_PLAYER);
    FAssert(iDestroyedCities >= 0);
    iDestroyedCities = std::max(0, iDestroyedCities);
    iUnownedTilesThreshold += iDestroyedCities * 3;

Thus the intended invariant is:

    Barbarian cities ever created in this land area
      - Barbarian cities currently alive in this area
      = Barbarian cities destroyed / removed from this area.

That destroyed-city count deliberately raises the unowned-tiles denominator, making replacement
Barbarian cities progressively harder to spawn.

THE PRODUCER IGNORES WHICH PLAYER'S CITY CHANGED
-------------------------------------------------
Current SAS `CvArea::changeCitiesPerPlayer` is:

    void CvArea::changeCitiesPerPlayer(PlayerTypes eIndex, int iChange)
    {
        m_aiCitiesPerPlayer.add(eIndex, iChange);
        FAssert(getCitiesPerPlayer(eIndex, true) >= 0 || gDLL->GetWorldBuilderMode());
        m_iNumCities += iChange;
        FAssert(getNumCities() >= 0);
        // <advc.300>
        for (int i = 0; i < iChange; i++)
            reportBarbarianCityCreated();
        // </advc.300>
    }

There is no:

    eIndex == BARBARIAN_PLAYER

condition.

Therefore EVERY positive city-count change reports a Barbarian city creation, regardless of
whether the added city belongs to Rome, India, a minor civilization or the actual Barbarian player.
The positive loop prevents removals from incrementing the counter, but it does not repair the
player-domain mismatch.

NORMAL CURRENT `CvCity` LIFECYCLE REACHABILITY
-----------------------------------------------
Every ordinary city initialization performs:

    getArea().changeCitiesPerPlayer(getOwner(), 1);

and every city kill performs the inverse `-1` call.

Consequently:

1. A major civilization founds a normal city in land area A.
2. `CvCity::init` calls `A.changeCitiesPerPlayer(majorPlayer, +1)`.
3. The generic area mutator calls `reportBarbarianCityCreated()` once.
4. No Barbarian city has been created, but `m_iBarbarianCitiesEver` permanently increases by 1.
5. Later `createBarbarianCity` subtracts only CURRENT Barbarian cities, so the false major-civ
   addition survives as an extra `iDestroyedCities` penalty.

This needs no rare event, malformed save, WorldBuilder edit or unusual option. Normal expansion is
enough.

CITY TRANSFERS ADD ANOTHER FALSE CREATION
-----------------------------------------
`CvPlayer::acquireCity()` implements transfer by snapshotting the old city, calling:

    pOldCity->kill(...)

and then constructing the replacement with:

    initCity(...)

The kill's `-1` does not increment `m_iBarbarianCitiesEver`; the replacement `+1` does.
Therefore every conquest, peaceful city trade/liberation or other ownership reconstruction can add
another false "Barbarian city ever created" to the land area even though no new Barbarian city
exists.

A captured Barbarian city makes the arithmetic especially concrete:

* genuine Barbarian founding: ever += 1, currentBarb += 1;
* capture kills the Barbarian city: currentBarb -= 1, ever unchanged;
* recipient's major-civ replacement city initializes: currentBarb unchanged, EVER += 1 again.

After one genuinely destroyed Barbarian city, the current code can therefore produce:

    ever = 2
    currentBarb = 0
    iDestroyedCities = 2

instead of the intended value 1.

A major-civ-to-major-civ transfer is even more purely false: the replacement adds +1 to `ever`
without any Barbarian city having existed at all.

CURRENT GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCE
----------------------------
The false count feeds an authoritative Barbarian-city spawn-density gate, not merely logging or UI.
For each candidate land area, current code starts from the handicap's
`iUnownedTilesPerBarbarianCity` and does:

    iUnownedTilesThreshold += iDestroyedCities * 3;
    iTargetCities /= std::max(1, iUnownedTilesThreshold);

Current SAS Monarch uses an unowned-tile threshold of 105. Ten false positive city additions in one
land area therefore make the denominator 135 before any genuinely destroyed Barbarian cities are
counted:

    intended: 105
    current:  105 + 10 * 3 = 135

For the same unowned-tile numerator, the continuous target ratio becomes 105 / 135 ~= 0.778 of the
intended value (about 22% lower), before integer truncation; floor boundaries can make the concrete
eligible-city-count effect larger and discontinuous.

Current SAS's handicap thresholds make the root live throughout normal difficulty play where
Barbarian city creation is enabled (e.g. 110 Prince, 105 Monarch, 100 Emperor, 95 Immortal,
90 Deity, 85 Deity+). The exact magnitude varies with area settlement/transfer history.

The top-level `createBarbarianCities()` path is likewise live: after its normal global city-count /
elapsed-turn gates it calls `createBarbarianCity(false)`, which DOES evaluate civ-settled areas.
Thus ordinary major-civ founding in an area can suppress later Barbarian settlement in that same
area through this false destroyed-city history.

COASTAL WATER-AREA BREADTH
--------------------------
`CvCity::init` also increments an adjacent water area's city-per-player bookkeeping for coastal
cities under `advc.030b`, so the same generic producer increments that water area's
`m_iBarbarianCitiesEver` too. `createBarbarianCity` evaluates non-water candidate plots and consumes
the candidate plot's land area, so this water-side contamination is not needed for F589's current
spawn consequence. It is additional evidence that the producer is attached at too generic a layer.

ANCESTRY / INTRODUCTION
-----------------------
The supplied K-Mod 1.46 and Civ4CE/BtS bodies have the ordinary
`CvArea::changeCitiesPerPlayer` bookkeeping but no `m_iBarbarianCitiesEver` /
`reportBarbarianCityCreated` feature.

The preserved AdvC history already introduces the mismatch in practical 1253
`f6ff6a182f...` (`Initial commit (cont.)`). In that imported `advc.300` code:

    int CvArea::numBarbCitiesEver() const { return nBarbCitiesEver; }
    void CvArea::barbCityCreated() { nBarbCitiesEver++; }

and the generic player-indexed mutator receives unconditionally:

    barbCityCreated(); // advc.300

while the same history adds the consumer:

    nDestroyedCities = a.numBarbCitiesEver() -
            a.getCitiesPerPlayer(BARBARIAN_PLAYER);

So the player-domain contradiction is present from the earliest preserved implementation of this
feature in the supplied reachable history.

Practical 1740 `ea0557d9c5...` (`EnumMap adapted to BtS`) later changes the unconditional single
call into:

    for (int i = 0; i < iChange; i++)
        reportBarbarianCityCreated();

This is a partial repair in one dimension: negative city-count changes no longer increase the
"ever" counter. It still does not test `eIndex`, so every positive non-Barbarian addition remains
misclassified.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains that exact positive-loop/no-player-guard form, and current SAS inherits it.

DEDUP
-----
Whole-album searches for `BarbarianCitiesEver`, `reportBarbarianCityCreated`,
`barbCityCreated`, the destroyed-Barbarian-city subtraction, `iUnownedTilesThreshold` and the
specific `advc.300` producer/consumer relation found no existing numbered runtime root.

The album does contain many other Barbarian-city findings, but they concern site valuation,
production, capture/reconstruction, research, naval demand or AI targeting rather than this
per-area historical spawn-density counter.

The generic `changeCitiesPerPlayer` mention in the InvasionGraph family is likewise unrelated: it
establishes that the real `CvArea` city count is not graph-simulated. F589 concerns an extra
side effect incorrectly attached to that real lifecycle mutator.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The narrow repair is to report a Barbarian creation only when the player whose area city count is
being increased is actually the Barbarian player, while retaining the current positive-count
multiplicity:

    if (eIndex == BARBARIAN_PLAYER)
    {
        for (int i = 0; i < iChange; i++)
            reportBarbarianCityCreated();
    }

This preserves practical 1740's protection against decrements and makes ordinary major/minor-civ
founding or ownership reconstruction neutral to the Barbarian-history counter.

No source patch is made in this audit stone.

REGRESSION TESTS
----------------
1. Fresh land area, no Barbarians: found several normal major-civ cities. Assert
   `getBarbarianCitiesEverCreated() == 0`.
2. Found one actual Barbarian city: assert `ever == 1`, `currentBarb == 1`, destroyed == 0.
3. Destroy that Barbarian city without replacement by Barbarians: assert `ever == 1`,
   `currentBarb == 0`, destroyed == 1.
4. Capture that Barbarian city into a major civilization: the recipient's replacement-city init
   must NOT raise `ever`; destroyed remains exactly 1.
5. Transfer a major-civ city to another major civilization in the same area: `ever` must remain
   unchanged.
6. With a deterministic area/unowned-tile fixture, compare the spawn target before/after founding
   ordinary civ cities. The destroyed-city term and denominator must be unchanged unless actual
   Barbarian cities were destroyed.
7. Found a coastal major-civ city: its adjacent-water bookkeeping must not affect the LAND area's
   Barbarian-history count; if the narrow player guard is used, any remaining water-area Barbarian
   bookkeeping is behaviorally irrelevant to current city spawning.
8. Save/load after genuine Barbarian founding/destruction: the serialized ever-created count and
   corrected destroyed-city arithmetic must remain stable.

CLASSIFICATION
--------------
F589 / KI#912 CONFIRMED.

This is an inherited AdvC authoritative gameplay bug: a generic player-indexed area-city mutator
updates a Barbarian-only historical counter without checking the player index. Normal civ expansion
and ownership reconstruction therefore masquerade as destroyed Barbarian-city history and suppress
future Barbarian city spawning.

POST-`deleteCity` CAPITAL-LOSS CANDIDATE - EXACT F572/F573 RE-HIT
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Re-entering `CvCity::kill()` after the F589 area-count work immediately exposes a visually severe
sequence: the city is deleted from the owner's FreeList and later code in the same function still

Current source reaches:

    kOwner.deleteCity(getID());

and the capital-loss announcement block later contains `getID()` / `getTeam()` reads; the function

PLAIN INIT/KILL EXTERNAL COUNTS - CLEAN AFTER F589
--------------------------------------------------
After excluding F589's special-purpose side effect inside the otherwise generic
`CvArea::changeCitiesPerPlayer`, the ordinary city/team/game count pairs are simple balanced
arithmetic:

* city init increments the owning team/game city totals;
* city kill decrements the corresponding totals;
* the typed `GET_TEAM(PlayerTypes)` overload resolves a player's actual team and is already a
  WIP362 false-positive control;
* the remaining direct team/global count mutators do not attach another hidden subtype-specific

AdvC-only Barbarian-history side effect being grafted onto a broad player-indexed area mutator

GLOBAL-WARMING ICE MELT -> LAKE/FRESH-WATER HEALTH CANDIDATE - CLOSED
---------------------------------------------------------------------
The current KI#346 repair makes a runtime Ice passability change rebuild water areas:

    GC.getMap().resetPathDistance();
    if (GC.getDefineBOOL(CvGlobals::PASSABLE_AREAS))
        GC.getMap().recalculateWaterAreas();
    updatePlotGroups();

`CvCity` fresh-water health is stored (`m_iFreshWaterGoodHealth` /
`m_iFreshWaterBadHealth`) rather than queried dynamically, while `CvPlot::isFreshWater()` can read
adjacent `CvPlot::isLake()`. At first glance this suggests a new stale-cache root: melting Ice can
merge passability-split water `CvArea`s, `calculateReprAreas()` calls `updateLakes()`, and the
water-area rebuild does not explicitly call `CvCity::updateFreshWaterHealth()`.

The candidate closes under AdvC's REPRESENTATIVE-AREA contract.

`CvMap::calculateReprAreas()` deliberately groups water `CvArea`s that belong to the same BtS-style
water body even when passability rules split them into separate movement areas. For water it uses
orthogonal same-water adjacency to converge their representative IDs. `CvArea::updateLake(true)`
then classifies lake status from the SUM of the tile counts of every water area sharing that
representative ID:

    int iTotalTiles = getNumTiles();
    ...
    if (pOther->m_iRepresentativeArea == m_iRepresentativeArea &&
        pOther->getID() != getID())
    {
        iTotalTiles += pOther->getNumTiles();
        ...
    }

Therefore Ice can split or merge the PASSABLE `CvArea` representation without changing the total
BtS-style representative water body used for `isLake()`. The KI#346 melt trigger does not change
water-vs-land topology; it changes passability. The summed representative-area tile count is
unchanged, so adjacent `isLake()` does not flip merely because the Ice barrier melts.

No current lake->ocean or ocean->lake transition is produced by this trigger, and therefore no
fresh-water health input changes that would require an additional city-cache refresh. F590 is not
consumed here.

`recalculateWaterAreas()` RESTORATION CONTROL
---------------------------------------------
The current water-only rebuild first detaches/deletes water areas, rebuilds them, recalculates
representative areas/lakes, and only after every water plot has its new area restores coastal-city
counts:

    for (...) {
        if (!kPlot.isCity())
            continue;
        CvArea* pWaterArea = kPlot.waterArea(true);
        if (pWaterArea != NULL)
            pWaterArea->changeCitiesPerPlayer(kPlot.getPlotCity()->getOwner(), 1);
    }

Water-plot area statistics and unit bookkeeping are rebuilt through plot-area processing as water
plots receive their new areas. Building/area effects tied to a city's ordinary area remain land-area
state; the special coastal-water city count is the city-side water-area state that needs explicit
restoration here. No second current-live missing restoration was established.

The malformed/dormant negative-side `CvPlot::processArea` shapes encountered nearby are already
preserved in earlier audit controls and remain outside the current-live threshold; they are not a
new F590.

PROJECT `CreatedCount` NAMING CANDIDATE - CURRENT-COUNT SEMANTICS, NOT A BUG
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvTeam::changeProjectCount` always calls:

    GC.getGame().incrementProjectCreatedCount(eProject, iChange);

including negative `iChange`, despite the game member's historical `CreatedCount` name. That can
look suspicious if the member is interpreted as a monotonic 'ever created' statistic.

Its authoritative consumer shows otherwise. `CvGame::isProjectMaxedOut` compares
`getProjectCreatedCount(eProject)` against a world project's CURRENT allowed global instance count,
and project transfer/reset paths deliberately compensate the game count when moving/removing team
projects. The game member is therefore functioning as the current global project-instance total for
legality, despite its name. Negative changes are required for those transitions.

This is not an F590 root.

  change;
* water-area rebuild -> current coastal city-count restoration accounted for;
* production/order interruption -> prior WIP367/WIP386/WIP374 and related controls;
* project `CreatedCount` -> current-instance semantics, not monotonic history.

POST-WIP393 GENERIC-MUTATOR / SETTER CONTROLS
----------------------------------------------

1. CvGame::changeNoNukesCount -- ordinary vote path CLOSED

The authoritative global no-nukes counter is a thin mutator and does not itself
walk every city queue. That initially looked capable of allowing a queued nuclear
unit to finish after a successful No Nukes resolution.

The normal current vote-resolution timing closes the shipped path. Vote state is
resolved before player city production, and each city reaches `doCheckProduction`
before completing its current production. Continuing `ORDER_TRAIN` legality is
rechecked through `canTrain(..., true)`, which consumes the current global No Nukes
state. A nuke that has become illegal therefore cannot simply finish from the stale
queue after a normally resolved ban.

A hypothetical external API that mutates the counter in an arbitrary mid-city-turn
window is a broader robustness contract, not a demonstrated current F590 trigger.


2. SAS Water Wheel bIrrigation + bIgnoreIrrigation ordering -- CLOSED

Current SAS Water Wheel activates both technology flags in the same technology.
`CvTeam::processTech` applies the Irrigation count first; that transition rebuilds
map irrigation. It then applies IgnoreIrrigation without a second irrigation
rebuild.

The apparent order/cache contradiction is false after tracing the consumers:

* `bIrrigation` controls the stored irrigation-spreading network through
  `isPotentialIrrigation` / `m_bIrrigated` and therefore requires the rebuild;
* `bIgnoreIrrigation` is queried dynamically by improvement-placement legality
  when deciding whether a normally irrigation-requiring improvement may be built;
* `updateIrrigated` does not cache the IgnoreIrrigation rule.

Thus Water Wheel's current dual-flag configuration does not leave stored irrigation
state stale.


3. Construction BridgeBuilding / Engineering RouteChange pathfinder candidate --
   existing C027 control, NOT F590

Changing bridge ability or route movement can change path costs without an explicit
blanket invalidation of AdvCiv's reusable GroupPathFinder search tree. The cache's
reuse identity cannot generically encode every global movement-rule transition.

This exact Engineering-style concern was already challenged in the earlier C027
GroupPathFinder audit. The normal triggers established there did not preserve the
same group/start/moves search identity needed for harmful reuse, while final human
movement uses the cleared/final finder. No stronger ordinary current reuse sequence
was established here, so the abstract cache hole is retained as that existing
control rather than renumbered.


4. CvTeam::setForceRevealedBonus -- positive remove/flip/re-add control

The live random-event path can force-reveal a resource such as Oil before its normal
technology reveal. The setter correctly reconciles authoritative plot-group bonus
state rather than merely changing observer UI:

    for owned matching-bonus plots:
        updatePlotGroupBonus(false, false)
    change forced-reveal state
    for owned matching-bonus plots:
        updatePlotGroupBonus(true)
    update matching plot yields/layout

Therefore a newly forced-revealed connected resource is removed under the old
visibility contract and re-added under the new one, allowing resource counts and
city effects to converge immediately. Permanent-Alliance item sharing also copies
forced-reveal state. No F590.


5. Counterespionage / Disengage / StolenVisibility setter thinness -- semantic
   dedup controls

The counterespionage setters store the directional timer/modifier and dirty the
Espionage advisor, but the important passive-demographics invalidation failure is
already owned by F461. The stored passive city-visibility lifetime family is owned by
F508 and related prior work.

Disengage and stolen-visibility state likewise already have extensive Permanent-
Alliance / deal / team-lifecycle coverage. Thin local setter bodies are not evidence
of a new independent root.


6. CvArea PlayerTypes/TeamTypes mutator gate census -- F589 remains unusual

The post-F589 mechanical pass checked the other broad indexed area mutators:

* units/cities/population per player;
* building good health, bad health and happiness;
* area trade routes and free specialists;
* area power and best-found value;
* revealed tiles, clean power and border obstacles by team;
* area AI type;
* area yield modifiers and UnitAI counts.

Apart from F589's `changeCitiesPerPlayer`, the secondary effects are either pure
indexed accounting or explicitly update/dirty the same supplied player/team. No
second mutator attaches a semantically narrower Barbarian-/special-subtype effect
without first identifying that subtype.

F589 is therefore not evidence for a broad family of missing PlayerTypes/TeamTypes
gates inside CvArea.


7. Low-coverage authoritative CvPlot setter tranche -- no independent F590

`CvPlot::setBonusType` is producer-order symmetric for live resource state: old
area/map counts are removed, old plot-group bonus contribution is removed, the bonus
identity changes, the new contribution is added, new area/map counts are installed,
and yield/layout state is refreshed.

`setRevealedOwner`, `setRevealedImprovementType` and `setRevealedRouteType` maintain
team-relative fog-memory/intelligence state. Their apparently lightweight bodies do
not own the hidden authoritative economy for a plot.

`setTerrainType` updates impassability, yield and plot-group state and hands land /
water mismatches through `setPlotType`. Current terrain XML does not activate a new
post-start terrain-impassability domain requiring a separate F590 here.

`setFeatureType` remains bounded by the already-owned feature-passability/fresh-water
families; current SAS additionally contains the explicit post-finding repairs around
live Ice/global-warming and river-derived-state transitions. Do not duplicate them.

`CvPlot::changeBlockadedCount` changes the authoritative team-relative blockade state
and dirties the affected working city's assignment. Its caller `CvUnit::updatePlunder`
checks whether trade-network status changed and rebuilds affected players' plot groups.
That can still leave the city's cached trade-route selection/yield until the normal
late route refresh, but that is precisely F507's existing root: authoritative
player-specific trade-network topology changes without rebuilding cached trade routes
before economy. Record blockade as F507 breadth, not F590.

The remaining ownership-duration/city-radius/plot-group/recycled-slot state maps to
older ownership-score, hidden-city-radius and F477/F478 lifecycle work rather than a
fresh root in this tranche.


RESULT OF WIP394
----------------
No independent current-live contradiction survived as F590.

The useful result is a narrower search space:

* F589's subtype-gate mistake appears isolated among CvArea's indexed mutators;
* low-coverage literal setter counts are again a poor predictor of semantic coverage;
* several thin setters delegate the authoritative reconciliation to their callers or
  to explicit remove/mutate/re-add transitions;
* blockade supplies useful F507 breadth but not a distinct root.

F590 / provisional KI#913 therefore remains intentionally UNUSED.

Use a different mechanical lens: threshold/cross-zero transitions and paired stored
state whose behavior changes specifically at 0<->positive, NONE<->concrete or
inactive<->active boundaries. Prioritize current SAS XML/data combinations that can

5. promote F590 / KI#913 only for an independent current-live root.

Physically freeze C031-WIP395 at the next settled tranche whether F590 is confirmed
or remains unused.

POST-WIP394 THRESHOLD / LIFECYCLE CONTROLS BEFORE F590
-------------------------------------------------------
1. Live global-warming Ice melt / water-area recreation does not establish a new stale fresh-water
   health root. AdvC's water `CvArea::updateLake` classification uses the representative BtS-style

2. Water-area object recreation under the recent KI#346 repair also does not leave an ordinary-live

   the affected team's units act. The remaining non-plot-derived water-area fields are either

   loss.

3. `CvPlayerAI::m_neededExplorersByArea` is keyed by area ID and is therefore abstractly invalidated
   by water-area reconstruction. The normal turn lifecycle closes the shipped window: player AI
   cache update clears/rebuilds that map at player activation before the later team/unit/city
   consumers use it. Preserve this as a positive cache-generation control, not F590.

4. The SAS-vs-Base-AdvC XML activation sieve is more productive than continuing generic cross-zero
   setters. It exposes inherited projection helpers that were written for a narrower live XML
