C031-WIP408 — QUEUE 007 CvUnit.cpp — GIFT / PER-TURN ATTACK COUNT
===============================================================================

STATUS
------
Queue 007 `CvGameCoreDLL/CvUnit.cpp` remains OPEN.
F593 / KI#916 through F596 / KI#919 are CONFIRMED.
F597 / provisional KI#920 is UNUSED.
No repository/gameplay source files modified.

F596 / KI#919 — GIFT CONVERSION CLEARS THE UNIT'S PER-TURN ATTACK COUNT
----------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvUnit::convert()` does not preserve current AdvC/SAS `m_iMadeAttacks` from the source
unit. A fresh replacement unit starts with:

    m_iMadeAttacks = 0;

and `gift()` reconstructs the logical unit through `recipient.initUnit(...) + convert(this)`
without finishing its remaining movement afterward. `convert()` copies `m_iMoves` but not
the already-spent attack count.

Therefore a unit that has already attacked/bombarded this turn can retain its unused
movement while ownership transfer silently restores its attack allowance.

CURRENT RUNTIME CONTRACT
------------------------
AdvC practical advc.164 generalized BtS's old boolean `m_bMadeAttack` into an integer count:

    void CvUnit::setMadeAttack(bool bNewValue)
    {
        if (bNewValue)
            m_iMadeAttacks++;
        else m_iMadeAttacks = 0;
    }

    bool CvUnit::isMadeAllAttacks() const
    {
        return (getBlitzCount() >= 0 && m_iMadeAttacks > getBlitzCount());
    }

The count is authoritative per-turn state: it is serialized, reset only in normal unit
`doTurn`, and gates attacks/range strikes/bombardment through `isMadeAllAttacks()`.

`convert()` preserving only movement points is insufficient. Movement expenditure and attack
allowance are separate state machines: a multi-move non-Blitz unit can have movement left
while `m_iMadeAttacks` correctly prevents another attack.

CLEAN CURRENT SAS REPRODUCTION — FRIGATE BOMBARD/GIFT
-----------------------------------------------------
Current SAS `UNIT_FRIGATE` is an especially simple fixture:

    Domain = DOMAIN_SEA
    iMoves = 5
    iBombardRate = 12
    no Blitz

BtS/K-Mod already ship the same qualitative fixture with 4 moves and Bombard 8.

Use a simultaneous-turn multiplayer game with human A and B, both at war with C and able to
peacefully share B's territory:

1. Put A's Frigate F on a B-owned water plot adjacent to a bombardable C city.
2. F bombards the C city.
3. `CvUnit::bombard()` executes:

       setMadeAttack(true);
       changeMoves(GC.getMOVE_DENOMINATOR());

   so F has one attack recorded but still has 4 of its 5 movement points available.
4. Because the Frigate is still on a B-owned valid sea plot, `canGift()` accepts gifting F
   to B; it does not reject an already-attacked unit.
5. `gift()` creates B's replacement F2 and calls `F2.convert(F)`.
6. `convert()` copies F's used-move state, so F2 still has only 4/5 movement remaining, but
   initialization left `m_iMadeAttacks=0` and conversion never restores the source count.
7. B is also at war with C. `canBombard()` now sees `isMadeAllAttacks()==false` and F2 still
   has movement, so B can bombard the same (or another eligible) city again in the same
   simultaneous turn.

Without the gift, the same non-Blitz Frigate's `m_iMadeAttacks=1` makes
`isMadeAllAttacks()` true and blocks that second bombard.

The same root can affect ordinary attacks for multi-move units whenever a legal same-turn
gift position is reached, but bombard is the clean fixture because it spends one move and
leaves the unit on the recipient-owned plot.

TURN-BOUNDARY SCOPE
-------------------
This is specifically a same-active-turn ownership-transfer defect. Normal `CvUnit::doTurn`
resets both attack count and movement for a new owner turn:

    setMadeAttack(false);
    ...
    setMoves(0);

so a sequential game where the recipient only acts after its normal next-turn refresh does
not demonstrate the stale-transfer difference. Simultaneous multiplayer provides the direct
supported path: both players' unit-turn state has already been initialized, then gift occurs
inside that shared action window and the recipient can immediately command the replacement.

ANCESTRY
--------
The root is inherited from Firaxis/BtS rather than introduced by SAS.

Civ4CE/BtS:
* initializes `m_bMadeAttack=false`;
* `bombard()` sets it true and spends one move;
* Frigate has 4 moves and Bombard 8;
* `gift()` reconstructs the unit through `initUnit + convert`;
* `convert()` omits `m_bMadeAttack` while copying movement.

K-Mod retains the same behavior. AdvC practical advc.164 replaces the boolean with
`m_iMadeAttacks` to support multiple Blitz attacks, but `convert()` still omits the state.
Base AdvC 1.14 and current SAS therefore preserve the inherited transfer hole, with SAS's
5-move Frigate making the remaining-movement fixture even wider.

WHOLE-ALBUM DEDUP / ROOT BOUNDARY
---------------------------------
Whole-album searches for `m_iMadeAttacks`, `isMadeAllAttacks`, gift+bombard and
made-attack conversion find only unrelated SelectionGroup Blitz-policy controls. No existing
root owns loss of per-unit attack exhaustion across ownership replacement.

F596 is distinct from the preceding conversion findings:
* F593 preserves a random-event movement prohibition (`m_iImmobileTimer`);
* F594 preserves the simultaneous-turn real-time movement timestamp (`m_iLastMoveTurn`);
* F596 preserves the exact per-turn count of already-consumed attacks (`m_iMadeAttacks`).

Fixing any one of those fields leaves the other two defects unchanged. F596 also cannot be
reduced to F594: a unit can have a perfectly recent last-move timestamp yet still regain an
extra bombard solely because its attack count reset.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR
-------------------
Preserve the exact attack count during `CvUnit::convert`. In current AdvC/SAS a direct
same-class assignment is semantically appropriate, e.g.:

    m_iMadeAttacks = pUnit->m_iMadeAttacks;

or introduce an explicit exact-count setter and use that.

Do NOT restore only `isMadeAttack()` through `setMadeAttack(true)`: current advc.164 allows
more than one attack through Blitz-count effects, so a source unit may legitimately have
`m_iMadeAttacks > 1`. The transfer must preserve the integer count, not collapse it to a
boolean.

Upgrade remains safe with this repair: `upgrade()` calls `convert()` and then
`pUpgradeUnit->finishMoves()`, so preserving the count cannot grant extra same-turn movement
or attacks. Normal next-turn `doTurn` continues to reset the count as before.

REGRESSION TEST
---------------
1. Simultaneous MP: human A/B both at war with C; A Frigate on B-owned water adjacent to C
   city.
2. Bombard once. Assert source `m_iMadeAttacks == 1` / `isMadeAllAttacks()==true` and that
   movement remains.
3. Gift to B in the same active turn.
4. Assert replacement has exactly the source attack count and used-move count.
5. Assert second bombard/attack remains unavailable solely because the attack allowance was
   already consumed.
6. Positive control: gift a unit that has not attacked; its count remains 0.
7. Blitz control: after N attacks, gift a unit with positive Blitz count and assert the exact
   N is retained rather than being collapsed to 1.
8. Turn-boundary control: normal `doTurn` still resets the transferred count for a new turn.

CURRENT STONE AFTER C031-WIP408
-------------------------------

F597 / provisional KI#920 UNUSED.

----

additional current producer survives. Continue damage/death/capture and promotion/experience
invariants afterward. Whole-album semantic dedup before F597.

C031-WIP409 — QUEUE 007 CvUnit.cpp — GIFT / PER-TURN INTERCEPTION FLAG
===============================================================================

STATUS
------
Queue 007 `CvGameCoreDLL/CvUnit.cpp` remains OPEN.

F598 / provisional KI#921 is UNUSED.

F597 / KI#920 — GIFT CONVERSION CLEARS A NON-AIR UNIT'S USED-INTERCEPTION FLAG
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvUnit::convert()` does not preserve serialized `m_bMadeInterception` from the source unit.
A fresh replacement unit begins with:

    m_bMadeInterception = false;

and ownership transfer through `gift()` therefore makes a non-air interceptor that has
already intercepted this turn appear available to intercept again.

This is a real authoritative per-turn flag, not animation state. `bestInterceptor()` rejects:

    pLoopUnit->isMadeInterception()

for every candidate. After a resolved interception, current `updateAirCombat()` marks the
interceptor used when it is not itself an air-domain unit:

    if (pInterceptor->getDomainType() != DOMAIN_AIR)
        pInterceptor->setMadeInterception(true);

Normal `CvUnit::doTurn()` resets the flag for a new turn. Save/load serializes it so saving
mid-turn does not grant a second interception. Gift/conversion is the unsupported reset.

CURRENT SAS LIVE FIXTURE
------------------------
`UNIT_MOBILE_SAM` is a clean current non-air interceptor:

    Domain = DOMAIN_LAND
    iInterceptionProbability = 60
    iAirRange = 1
    iMoves = 2

`UNIT_SAM_INFANTRY` is another shipped fixture (15%, range 1). The basic
`PROMOTION_AIR_INTERCEPTION1` is available to `UNITCOMBAT_GUN` and adds +5 interception,
so ordinary promotion state can raise these values further. A deterministic code-level test
can call/force a successful interception; an ordinary game repro can simply use repeated air
missions until the first interception occurs.

SUPPORTED SAME-TURN REPRODUCTION
--------------------------------
Use simultaneous multiplayer with human A and B peacefully sharing territory and both at war
with C:

1. Station A's Mobile SAM S on a B-owned land tile. This is a valid non-cargo location and
   gift target under Open Borders.
2. C launches an air mission whose target lies within S's interception range.
3. Let S successfully intercept and survive.
4. `updateAirCombat()` sets `S.m_bMadeInterception=true`; a subsequent C air mission in the
   same state would skip S in `bestInterceptor()`.
5. A gifts S to B before the common simultaneous action window ends.
6. `gift()` reconstructs B's S2 through `initUnit + convert`. `convert()` omits
   `m_bMadeInterception`, so S2 has the default false flag.
7. C launches another eligible air mission in the same turn. B is also C's enemy, S2 can air
   defend from the same plot, and `bestInterceptor()` is now allowed to select S2 again.

Without the ownership conversion, S remains excluded after its first interception until
normal next-turn `doTurn()` clears the flag.

WHY AIR-DOMAIN INTERCEPTORS ARE NOT THE REQUIRED FIXTURE
--------------------------------------------------------
The current combat path sets `m_bMadeInterception` only for non-air interceptors. Air-domain
interceptors are constrained through their separate moved/activity rules in
`bestInterceptor()`. F597 therefore concerns precisely the land/sea interceptor state for
which this boolean is the one-interception-per-turn gate; Mobile SAM provides the strongest
current example.

ANCESTRY
--------
The omission is inherited from Firaxis/BtS:
* BtS initializes and serializes `m_bMadeInterception`;
* its interceptor-selection path consumes the flag and successful non-air interception sets
  it;
* normal unit turn resets it;
* `CvUnit::convert()` omits it;
* `gift()` uses init + convert without an interception-state repair.

K-Mod retains the same state machine and omission. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain it
as well. Unlike F596's advc.164 boolean-to-count refinement, this field remains a boolean in
current code, but the transfer hole is the same inherited lifetime mismatch.

WHOLE-ALBUM DEDUP / ROOT BOUNDARY
---------------------------------
Whole-album search found no existing `m_bMadeInterception` / gift-interception root.

F597 remains independent from the neighboring conversion findings:
* F593: temporary movement prohibition (`m_iImmobileTimer`);
* F594: simultaneous-turn physical-move timestamp (`m_iLastMoveTurn`);
* F596: active attack/bombard count (`m_iMadeAttacks`);
* F597: passive non-air interception availability (`m_bMadeInterception`).

Each has a different producer and runtime consumer. Copying the attack count does not make a
used SAM unavailable to `bestInterceptor`, and copying the interception flag does not restore
attack exhaustion.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR
-------------------
Preserve the flag in `CvUnit::convert`, e.g.:

    setMadeInterception(pUnit->isMadeInterception());

or direct boolean assignment. Normal turn reset remains unchanged. Upgrade is not harmed by
preserving the current-turn state; if an upgrade replaces a unit mid-turn, silently restoring
a consumed passive interception would be no more justified than doing so on gift.

REGRESSION TEST
---------------
1. Make a non-air interceptor successfully intercept once and survive; assert
   `isMadeInterception()==true`.
2. Confirm the same unit is excluded from a second immediate `bestInterceptor()` selection.
3. Gift it during the same simultaneous turn to a legal recipient on whose owned plot it
   stands.
4. Assert the replacement still has `isMadeInterception()==true`.
5. Confirm it remains excluded from another interception until normal `doTurn()`.
6. Next-turn control: `doTurn()` clears the flag exactly once as before.
7. Fresh-unit control: gifting a unit that has not intercepted transfers false.

-------------------------------

F593 / KI#916 through F597 / KI#920 CONFIRMED.
F598 / provisional KI#921 UNUSED.
Latest physical checkpoint: C031-WIP409.

C031-WIP410 — QUEUE 007 CvUnit.cpp — CONVERT / REPLACEMENT-STATE CLOSURE

STATUS

Queue 007 `CvGameCoreDLL/CvUnit.cpp` remains OPEN.

CONVERT-STATE CLOSURE AFTER F593-F597
-------------------------------------
A final serialized/authoritative-state pass over `CvUnit::convert()` did not justify a fifth
conversion finding. The four promoted omissions have current producers, clear same-turn
consumers and ownership-replacement semantics that require preservation:

* F593 `m_iImmobileTimer`;
* F594 `m_iLastMoveTurn`;
* F596 `m_iMadeAttacks`;
* F597 `m_bMadeInterception`.

The remaining omitted state falls into different semantic classes and should not be copied
blindly.

RECON STATE — TEAM-SCOPED EFFECT, NOT SIMPLE IDENTITY
-----------------------------------------------------
`setReconPlot()` mutates actual team sight around the recon target:

    oldPlot.changeAdjacentSight(getTeam(), ..., false, this, true);
    ...
    newPlot.changeAdjacentSight(getTeam(), ..., true, this, true);

and tracks `m_iLastReconTurn` so normal turn-end cleanup knows when to clear it.

On gift across teams, simply copying the recon coordinates into the replacement would
transfer the donor team's completed intelligence mission to the recipient. Conversely, the
source unit's normal kill path calls `setReconPlot(NULL)` and removes the donor team's sight.
That is a coherent ownership-transition policy. Preserving recon would require an explicit
game-rule decision and remove/re-add semantics under the new team, not the scalar-copy repair
used for F593-F597. No current contract establishes that such transfer is intended.

BLOCKADE — STRATEGIC TEAM/OWNER ACTION SHOULD RESET
---------------------------------------------------
`m_bBlockading` is not passive identity. `setBlockading()` immediately calls `updatePlunder`
and changes strategic blockade state for affected teams/cities. Source-unit death explicitly
clears it. Auto-copying a donor's blockade into a newly owned unit would silently start the
recipient blockading without that owner issuing the action and could change which teams are
legally affected. Reset-on-replacement is therefore the safe/current semantic control.

FORTIFICATION / COMBAT-ACTION / UI-RUNTIME STATE
------------------------------------------------
The neighboring omissions such as fortify turns, facing/action/combat-focus/runtime combat
pointers, hotkey/selection state and transient attack-plot/combat timers do not have the same
identity-preservation contract as damage, XP, promotions, name or the four promoted
same-turn legality fields. Replacement/upgrade has historically reset positional control
state, and several values are coupled to EXE animation/group lifecycle. No independent
current-live contradiction was established.

UNIT SCRIPTDATA
---------------
Unit ScriptData is serialized and exposed to Python/WorldBuilder, but current SAS source
search finds no ordinary gameplay producer/consumer beyond WorldBuilder scenario import/
export and the CyUnit API itself. Loss across gift/upgrade remains generic scenario/mod-API
robustness debt, not a current shipped F598 under this audit's current-live threshold.

CARGO / TRANSPORT FOLLOW-UP CONTROLS
------------------------------------
After excluding F595's direct cross-team cargo gift:
* normal transport movement recursively moves every linked cargo unit and preserves its
  valid transport pointer;
* `jumpToNearestValidPlot` ultimately uses `move`/`setXY`, so cargo follows transport moves
  through the same path;
* transport upgrade uses exact current cargo counts and reattaches compatible cargo one by
  one; cargo that no longer fits is detached before `jumpToNearestValidPlot`;
* unload decrements transport cargo count through `setTransportUnit(NULL)` and leaves normal
  group/activity cleanup;
* transport death intentionally kills linked cargo regardless of owner (same-team
  multi-player cargo is legal), while F595 is what could create the unsupported foreign-team
  ownership case.

No additional current-live cargo count/link asymmetry survived once F595 is treated as owned.

C031-WIP411 -- QUEUE 007: CvUnit.cpp DEATH / CAPTURE RECONSTRUCTION CONTROL
Continuation after C031-WIP410
===============================================================================

F598 / provisional KI#921 -- UNUSED
------------------------------------
No independent current-live death/capture root was promoted in this tranche.

CAPTURE-CLASS CIVILIZATION-MAPPING CANDIDATE -- CURRENT-DATA CLOSED
------------------------------------------------------------------
A mechanically sharp-looking producer/consumer mismatch exists in inherited AdvCiv
capture logic:

- CvUnit::getCaptureOdds(kDefender) rejects capture when
  kDefender.getCaptureUnitType(DEFENDER civilization) == NO_UNIT;
- final CvUnit::kill capture reconstruction instead computes
  getCaptureUnitType(CAPTURING PLAYER civilization).

Those are not generically equivalent when a UnitClass can map to NONE for one
civilization and a concrete UnitType for another. If current data activated such a
capture class, the odds precheck and executor could disagree about whether capture is
representable.

Current SAS does NOT activate that mismatch:

- the only shipped UnitInfos with a non-NONE <Capture> class are UNIT_SETTLER,
  UNIT_WORKER, UNIT_INDIAN_FAST_WORKER, UNIT_NETHERLANDS_SWIFT_WORKER and
  UNIT_MAYA_QUICK_WORKER;
- every one maps on capture to UNITCLASS_WORKER;
- CvXMLLoadUtility::InitUnitDefaults initializes every civilization's omitted UnitClass
  mapping to the UnitClass default before civilization-specific XML overrides are read;
- ordinary civilizations therefore resolve UNITCLASS_WORKER to UNIT_WORKER;
- India, Maya and Netherlands resolve it to their concrete worker UUs;
- CIVILIZATION_BARBARIAN explicitly resolves it to UNIT_BARBARIAN_WORKER;
- no current civilization maps UNITCLASS_WORKER to NONE.

Therefore the only predicate getCaptureOdds uses from the defender-side mapping
("is this NO_UNIT?") has the same answer as the captor-side executor for every current
capturable unit/civilization combination. Different concrete worker types are intended:
a captured Worker is reconstructed as the capturing civilization's Worker/UU.

This remains a useful generic robustness contract: should a future capturable UnitClass
be disabled for some civilization, getCaptureOdds should test the prospective capturing
civilization rather than the defender civilization. It does not meet this album's
current-live threshold today.

DEATH / DELAYED-DEATH / CAPTURE LIFECYCLE CONTROL
--------------------------------------------------
- setDamage reaching max HP enters kill(true, ePlayer); delayed death retains the unit
  object until doDelayedDeath can safely complete kill(false), rather than deleting an
  object still involved in combat animation/state.
- final kill snapshots owner, unit type, capturing player and captor-specific capture
  UnitType before setXY(INVALID), unitLost and deleteUnit; reconstruction therefore does
  not dereference the deleted unit for those values.
- the plot is a persistent map object; the CvPlot reference captured at kill entry
  remains valid after the unit is removed and supplies the capture coordinates.
- capture reconstruction guards NO_PLAYER / NO_UNIT and deliberately excludes the
  Barbarian player, matching the BtS/K-Mod lineage policy that Barbarians do not retain
  captured units.
- AI capture refusal is intentionally handled before initUnit; no half-created captured
  unit or leaked unit-class count was established.

BARBARIAN RANDOM-CAPTURE MESSAGE QUIRK -- NOT PROMOTED
------------------------------------------------------
AdvCiv's advc.010 randomized capture layer can set bCapture after a successful capture
roll by a Barbarian attacker, while final kill still follows the inherited BtS/K-Mod
policy of not creating captured units for BARBARIAN_PLAYER. Because bCapture suppresses
the ordinary attack-success "destroyed" message in the advc.010 combat branch, a
successful Barbarian roll can therefore produce a message-level inconsistency even
though the target ultimately disappears. This is not an authoritative capture/accounting
failure and was not assigned F598 in this gameplay-focused pass.

ANCESTRY / DEDUP
----------------
- getCaptureOdds is inherited unchanged from Base AdvCiv in current SAS (advc.010).
- BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod predate getCaptureOdds and use deterministic capture eligibility,
  while their final kill path already excludes Barbarian captors.
- whole-album semantic search found no prior independent root matching the prospective
  captor-vs-defender civilization mapping seam; the current XML proof above is why it
  remains a control rather than a new number.

DURABLE STATE
-------------

F593/KI#916 through F597/KI#920 remain confirmed.
F598 / provisional KI#921 remains UNUSED.
Actual repository/gameplay source remains untouched.

C031-WIP412 -- QUEUE 007: CvUnit.cpp PROMOTION / XP / EVENT-GRANT CONTROLS
Continuation after C031-WIP411
===============================================================================

F598 / provisional KI#921 -- UNUSED
------------------------------------
No independent current-live promotion/XP root was promoted in this tranche.

GREAT-GENERAL XP-ONLY BRANCH -- CURRENT DATA MASKED
----------------------------------------------------
CvUnit::canPromote has a special early-true branch for a Warlord unit with positive
LeaderExperience but NO LeaderPromotion. That branch can therefore admit an
`ePromotion == NO_PROMOTION` command before the normal NO_PROMOTION rejection.
CvUnit::promote would be unsafe/semantically unclear for such a mod-mod unit because
later code expects a concrete promotion.

Current SAS does not ship that configuration. The only leader unit is
UNIT_GREAT_GENERAL, with iLeaderExperience=20 and concrete PROMOTION_LEADER. Normal
CvUnit::lead therefore supplies a real promotion id. Keep the XP-only branch as generic
mod-mod robustness only; it is not F598 in current SAS.

LEVEL / EXPERIENCE OWNER-MODIFIER CONTROL
-----------------------------------------
CvUnit::convert copies the old level and rescales stored XP by the old/new owners'
LevelExperienceModifier. CvUnit::experienceNeeded applies the receiving owner's same
modifier to the level threshold. This is the inherited K-Mod contract rather than an
unpaired unit-state transform.

Current SAS TraitInfos additionally have no nonzero iLevelExperienceModifier values, so
ordinary current gift/upgrade conversion does not even activate cross-owner XP scaling.
No current F598 here.

EVENT XP -> PROMOTION-READY TIMING -- CLOSED
--------------------------------------------
CvUnit::applyEvent can add direct unit XP (current fixtures include At the Sword +3 XP
and Friendly Locals +1 XP) without calling testPromotionReady immediately. In isolation
that looked unlike CvCity::addProductionExperience and Great-General XP distribution,
which explicitly refresh promotion readiness.

The full turn contract closes it:
* ordinary combat XP uses the same changeExperience helper and likewise does not refresh
  m_bPromotionReady at the XP write itself;
* CvUnit::doTurn begins by calling testPromotionReady for every surviving unit;
* random events are resolved at the player turn boundary, so the unit's next ordinary
  turn refresh establishes the correct promotion-ready state before normal action;
* Great-General/city-production callers need the explicit refresh because those grants
  can occur outside that ordinary unit-turn boundary.

This is inherited timing policy, not an event XP omission.

EVENT-WIDE FREE PROMOTIONS / PATH-STATE CONTROL
-----------------------------------------------
CvPlayer::applyEvent grants UnitCombatPromotions and UnitClassPromotions directly with
CvUnit::setHasPromotion, then persists the exact pair through CvPlayer::setFreePromotion
for future units. This bypasses CvUnit::promote's explicit CvSelectionGroup::resetPath,
so the current event promotion set was checked mechanically against path/visibility/range
side effects rather than assuming the bypass safe.

Current live movement-sensitive fixtures:
* Horse Whispering completion grants PROMOTION_SENTRY (+1 visibility) to current and
  future mounted-melee / mounted-ranged units;
* Harbormaster completion grants PROMOTION_NAVIGATOR (+1 move) to naval units;
* Long Range Fighters grants PROMOTION_AIR_RANGE1 (+1 air range) to Fighter-class units.

The concrete state transitions close:
* changeExtraVisibilityRange removes old adjacent sight, changes the range and reapplies
  sight immediately, so Sentry does not leave stale fog/visibility state;
* extra air range is consumed dynamically by air-mission legality/range checks and has no
  reusable GroupPathFinder cost state;
* Navigator changes maxMoves/movesLeft. GroupStepMetric::canReuseInitialPathData compares
  the live group's initial moves against the cached start-node moves and resets nodes when
  they differ, so the +move event cannot silently reuse old movement-point path data;
* current event-wide grants do not include move-discount, terrain/feature double-move,
  EnemyRoute, River or other path-cost-rule promotions that could change path cost while
  leaving initial moves equal.

A machine cross-check of all 37 current UnitCombat/UnitClass event promotion grants also
found no grant that violates the normal numeric withdrawal/interception/evasion maxima or
puts Blitz onto a <=1-move non-paradrop unit. Several events intentionally grant promotions
outside ordinary UnitCombat acquisition masks; that is established event design, not a
numeric-state contradiction.

PROMOTION APPLY / REMOVE SYMMETRY
---------------------------------
setHasPromotion updates the stored promotion bit and every inspected derived counter in
matched +/- form: Blitz, Amphibious/River/EnemyRoute/AlwaysHeal, double-move counts,
visibility, moves, movement discount, air range, interception/evasion, first strikes,
withdrawal, collateral/bombard/heal modifiers, combat/city/hills modifiers, revolt/collateral
protection, pillage/upgrade/XP modifiers, Kamikaze, Cargo, terrain/feature modifiers,
UnitCombat modifiers and Domain modifiers.

For ordinary learned/Great-General promotions, CvUnit::promote performs the additional
reusable group-path reset after setHasPromotion. Trait, UnitInfo, city and persistent-player
free promotions are applied while a new unit is being initialized or through already-audited
current-event paths above. No independent stale derived promotion state survived.

C031-WIP413 -- QUEUE 007: CvUnit.cpp MOVEMENT / ACTION-COUNT AUDIT

F598 / KI#921 -- SEA-PILLAGE INTERCEPTION CAN ERASE SPENT BLITZ ATTACKS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONFIRMED -- inherited Base AdvCiv regression introduced by the advc.164
boolean-to-count Blitz redesign; current SAS remains live.

ROOT
----
CvUnit::pillage() still contains the K-Mod/BtS sea-patrol interception staging:

    if (pInterceptor != NULL)
    {
        setMadeAttack(false);
        int iWithdrawal = withdrawalProbability();
        changeExtraWithdrawal(-iWithdrawal);
        attack(pInterceptor->plot(), false, NULL, true);
        changeExtraWithdrawal(iWithdrawal);
        return false;
    }

That reset was harmless with the old Boolean made-attack state: clearing m_bMadeAttack
before the forced combat and setting it again when combat begins could only leave the
same one-bit state ("has attacked") that already existed.

AdvC practical advc.164 changed the authoritative state to an integer count:

    void CvUnit::setMadeAttack(bool bNewValue)
    {
        if (bNewValue)
            m_iMadeAttacks++;
        else m_iMadeAttacks = 0;
    }

and exhaustion is now:

    return (getBlitzCount() >= 0 && m_iMadeAttacks > getBlitzCount());

PROMOTION_BLITZ / current SAS PROMOTION_BLITZKRIEG uses iBlitz=1, i.e. one extra
attack and therefore two attacks total. The old `setMadeAttack(false)` now destroys
all prior attack-count history rather than temporarily clearing one Boolean.

CURRENT-LIVE SAS FIXTURE
------------------------
Current SAS explicitly keeps Blitzkrieg live for UNITCOMBAT_NAVAL:

- PROMOTION_BLITZKRIEG has <iBlitz>1</iBlitz>;
- its UnitCombats include UNITCOMBAT_NAVAL;
- current Frigate is UNITCOMBAT_NAVAL, has bPillage=1, 5 moves and BombardRate=12;
- Destroyer/Battleship and other current naval combat units likewise have enough
  movement/pillage capability for the same interaction;
- the inherited AdvC hint explicitly tells players that ships can reach Blitz and that
  it gives them one extra attack per turn.

MISSION_PILLAGE does not reject a unit merely because isMadeAllAttacks() is true; the
mission requires canPillage() plus remaining movement. Therefore a Blitz ship can
legally have exhausted both attacks and still attempt a sea pillage when it has moves
left.

CONCRETE STATE TRANSITION / REPRO
---------------------------------
A clean source-level fixture is a Blitz Frigate on a pillageable enemy water tile next
to a bombardable enemy city, with an enemy Sea Patrol unit in interception range:

1. Give/promote the Frigate with current PROMOTION_BLITZKRIEG.
2. Bombard twice while enough city defense remains.
   Each bombard calls setMadeAttack(true), so m_iMadeAttacks == 2.
   With iBlitz=1, isMadeAllAttacks() is true because 2 > 1.
3. The Frigate still has movement (5 base moves; the two bombardments cost one move
   each), and MISSION_PILLAGE remains legal on its current improved water tile.
4. Let bestSeaPillageInterceptor select an enemy Sea Patrol unit.
5. CvUnit::pillage calls setMadeAttack(false): 2 -> 0.
6. The forced `attack(..., bSeaPatrol=true)` begins combat and updateCombat calls
   setMadeAttack(true): 0 -> 1.
7. If the pillager survives, its previous two-spent-attack history has collapsed to one.
   `isMadeAllAttacks()` is now false because 1 > 1 is false, so the same physical ship
   is eligible for another normal attack/bombard despite already having exhausted its
   two-attack Blitz allowance before the interception.

The Sea Patrol combat may legitimately decide whether it should consume an additional
attack allowance; that design question does not affect the bug. Whatever the intended
answer, an interception cannot validly REDUCE the number of attacks already spent.

WHY THIS IS AN advc.164 MIGRATION REGRESSION
--------------------------------------------
BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod use the original Boolean made-attack contract. K-Mod already has
this same sea-pillage staging and calls setMadeAttack(false) before the forced patrol
combat. In that representation the operation cannot turn "two attacks already spent"
into "one" because no such count exists.

The preserved AdvC practical diff shows advc.164 replacing m_bMadeAttack with
m_iMadeAttacks, making `setMadeAttack(false)` reset the full counter and changing Blitz
from an unlimited Boolean property into an integer number of extra attacks. The
pillage-interceptor block was carried through with its old `setMadeAttack(false)` call
unchanged. Base AdvC 1.14 therefore already contains the mismatch, and current SAS
inherits it.

Base AdvC also explicitly enables PROMOTION_BLITZ for UNITCOMBAT_NAVAL and ships an
advc.164 hint saying ships can reach Blitz, so the regression is live in Base AdvC
itself rather than requiring SAS's renamed/rebalanced promotion.

ROOT BOUNDARY / DEDUP
---------------------
Whole-album semantic search finds no prior sea-pillage-interception / Blitz-counter
root. F596/KI#919 is related only in the data member involved: F596 loses
m_iMadeAttacks when gift/convert reconstructs ownership. F598 instead corrupts the
same authoritative count inside an ordinary same-owner sea-pillage action because an
old Boolean-clearing idiom survived the advc.164 integer migration. Fixing either path
leaves the other defect unchanged.

F143/KI#466 and the neighboring Sea Patrol work concern mixed-group patrol admission /
persistence. They do not address the pillager's attack-count mutation during an actual
interception.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR BOUNDARY
----------------------------
Preserve the attack count that existed before the temporary sea-patrol staging. A
minimal repair can snapshot m_iMadeAttacks before the legacy clear and, after starting
the patrol combat, ensure the resulting count is at least the snapshot, e.g. conceptually:

    int const iMadeAttacksBefore = m_iMadeAttacks;
    setMadeAttack(false);
    ...
    attack(..., true);
    m_iMadeAttacks = std::max(m_iMadeAttacks, iMadeAttacksBefore);

This preserves the old Boolean contract generalized to a count: a patrol interception
may establish that at least one attack has occurred, but it cannot erase already-spent
attacks. The exact implementation should keep the existing temporary-withdrawal logic
and sea-patrol combat staging intact.

REGRESSION TEST
---------------
1. Create a current naval Blitz unit with enough moves (Frigate is sufficient), on an
   improved enemy water plot next to a city with enough defense for two bombardments.
2. Put an enemy eligible Sea Patrol unit within patrol range.
3. Bombard twice; assert m_iMadeAttacks == 2 and isMadeAllAttacks() == true.
4. Trigger MISSION_PILLAGE and an interception; arrange/seed the combat so the pillager
   survives.
5. After combat, assert m_iMadeAttacks has NOT fallen below 2 and the ship cannot gain
   an extra offensive attack merely because the pillage was intercepted.
6. Also test 0- and 1-spent-attack cases so the repair does not break ordinary patrol
   interception behavior.

MOVEMENT / ACTION CONTROLS CLOSED IN THIS TRANCHE
--------------------------------------------------
- airlift and recon finish movement explicitly;
- air strike, air bomb, bombard and ordinary range strike pair their move expenditure
  with their made-attack state under current configuration;
- paradrop deliberately requires an unmoved unit, spends half a move and consumes an
  attack; the promotion-validity code explicitly contains a paradrop/Blitz exception,
  so this is inherited intended action economy rather than F598;
- current SAS movement/action bodies that differ from Base AdvC in this region are
  overwhelmingly GameRecord instrumentation, constant hoists, signature formatting or
  already-owned KI#466/KI#467 group-state repairs; no separate SAS regression survived.

FEATURE TURN-DAMAGE -> DELAYED-DEATH -> HEAL ORDERING
-----------------------------------------------------
`CvUnit::doTurn()` applies feature turn damage before its ordinary healing branch. Since
lethal `changeDamage` schedules `kill(true)` rather than immediately deleting the unit,
that source shape can generically leave a delayed-death unit executing later `doTurn`
logic; transport cargo is especially sensitive because delayed `kill` already performs
some destruction-side consequences before the unit object disappears.

Current SAS does not activate this path: every shipped `CIV4FeatureInfos.xml` entry has
`iTurnDamage = 0`. Therefore the ordering remains a real mod-mod robustness hazard but not
a current-live F599 under this audit's threshold. Preserve as a control rather than
numbering a data-masked defect.

SETXY REMOVE -> MOVE -> ADD PAIRING
-----------------------------------
The authoritative `CvUnit::setXY` transition was paired mechanically across the old and
new plots. After excluding already-owned roots, the remaining core state is balanced:

* old/new plot membership is removed then added;
* adjacent sight is removed under the old coordinates and re-added under the new ones;
* `CvArea` unit count, unit power and UnitAI count are paired -1/+1;
* outside-unit support count is paired against the same owner/team/vassal predicate;
* city military-happiness presence is paired (neighboring stale-city behavior belongs to
  F455 rather than a new movement root);
* working-plot siege dirtiness is refreshed on departure/arrival where the mechanics use it;
* the unit's cached plot/area pointers are rebuilt immediately by `updatePlot` / `updateArea`;
* blockade teardown on departure belongs to the already-audited blockade family
  (F479/F507 and KI#467 controls), not a new setXY imbalance.

Current SAS's own body differences from Base AdvC in this function are almost entirely
constant-hoist/performance changes around war-weariness/capture values; the underlying
movement lifecycle is inherited.

`unitSetXY` DESTRUCTION / NULL-PLOT CALLBACK CONTROL
----------------------------------------------------
`setXY(INVALID_PLOT_COORD, INVALID_PLOT_COORD, ...)` reports `unitSetXY(NULL, this)` near
the end of the transition, which initially looks like a possible Python null-plot hazard.
The shipped callback contract closes it:

* practical advc.003y guards this native event behind `ON_UNIT_SET_XY`;
* current SAS keeps the corresponding USE callback define disabled (`0`);
* the only shipped Python `onUnitSetXY` handler is the stock movement-log stub and has no
  gameplay listener layered on top of it;
* the broader callback-guard family was already audited in the album and remains a clean
  disabled-event control.

No current-live null-plot consumer exists, so no F599.

GOODY-BEFORE-COORDINATE-ASSIGNMENT CONTROL
-------------------------------------------
`setXY` resolves a goody hut on `pNewPlot` before removing the unit from its old plot and
before assigning the new coordinates. The full current `CvPlayer::doGoody/receiveGoody`
path was checked for a destructive/reentrant unit transition. Shipped outcomes can grant
XP/healing, map/tech/gold, spawn units and spawn hostile Barbarians, but the hut-location
operations receive `pPlot` explicitly and do not require the explorer's coordinates to
have already changed. No current outcome deletes/replaces the moving unit in-place before
`setXY` resumes. This inherited ordering therefore stays a control.

FORCED RELOCATION / jumpToNearestValidPlot CONTROL
--------------------------------------------------
`jumpToNearestValidPlot` clears the bumped group's mission/automation state, then either
uses normal `move` or the explicit advc.163 `bFreeMove` path (`setXY`). The current caller
census closes the apparent free-move / anti-double-move timestamp concern:

* the only native caller passing `bFreeMove=true` is `CvPlot::verifyUnitValidPlot`;
* that caller passes it only for `!kUnit.isHuman()` to prevent humans from trolling AI
  stacks by forcing a paid bump;
* `setXY` does record `m_iLastMoveTurn`, but the simultaneous-turn anti-double-move
  consumer is specifically a human-group throttle. Thus the free AI bump does not create
  a human F594-style timestamp exploit;
* ordinary human bumps go through `move` and spend movement as intended;
* `bForceMove` correctly excludes the current plot while retaining the same legality
  checks used by the normal relocation search;
* no-current-destination falls through to `kill(false)` and the inspected callers either
  use the returned Boolean or do not dereference the killed unit afterward.

K-MOD AIR-UPGRADE / FULL-CAPACITY ORACLE CONTROL
------------------------------------------------
a K-Mod changelog fix for air units upgrading in a city at full air capacity was used as
an ancestry oracle. Current AdvC/SAS retains the safety property: a freshly initialized
air upgrade may auto-load during placement, but `convert()` subsequently applies the old
unit's transport state; when the old air unit was not cargo, `setTransportUnit(NULL)`
removes that accidental fresh-unit auto-load. The old K-Mod bug is therefore not live in
current SAS.

K-MOD BUGFIX ORACLE: CURRENT CONTROLS
-------------------------------------
The K-Mod changelog/source was used only as an ancestry oracle: historical fixes were
re-proved against current AdvC-SAS rather than assumed to remain correct.

* Simultaneous-turn air interception retains K-Mod's availability guard: an interceptor
  that is itself fighting, or whose interception plot is already fighting, is not started
  into a conflicting air combat. This closes the old simultaneous-combat collision bug.
* The simultaneous attacker/defender cleanup safeguards around combat and unit death are
  still present; the previously-audited post-delete/unit-lifecycle roots remain the proper
  owners for the dangerous cases rather than a new F599.
* K-Mod's original BtS air-upgrade/full-city-capacity repair was already closed in WIP414:
  `convert` restores the old transport state after fresh-unit placement, undoing an
  accidental carrier auto-load when the old air unit was not cargo.
* The Mongoose/K-Mod transport/load safety patches remain present in current source:
  self-loading cargo is rejected, all-terrain land units are not auto-loaded merely for
  entering water, cargo cannot pillage, and cargo land interceptors are rejected.

  longer implicitly starts the next queued mission inside `deleteMissionQueueNode`; callers

  preserves the safety property behind K-Mod's historical single-nuke/multiple-target queue
  fix instead of blindly starting a queued action during destructive/suicide mission
  teardown.
* `jumpToNearestValidPlot` still clears the bumped group's mission queue (WIP414 control),
  preserving K-Mod's historical worker-bump repair.

These controls make the old changelog increasingly low-yield as a fresh-finding source;

C031-WIP416 -- QUEUE 007: ALL-TERRAIN AI AREA PREFILTER -- F599 CONFIRMED
Continuation after C031-WIP415
===============================================================================

STATUS
------
Queue 007 `CvGameCoreDLL/CvUnit.cpp` remains OPEN.
F593/KI#916 through F598/KI#921 remain CONFIRMED.
F599 / provisional KI#922 is CONFIRMED.
F600 / provisional KI#923 is UNUSED.
Actual repository/gameplay source remains untouched.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F599 / provisional KI#922 -- AdvC `AI_canEnterByLand` intentionally omitted
`canMoveAllTerrain`; SAS later activates that ability on real land-domain AI
units, so many AI target/reinforcement prefilters reject legal cross-water
routes before the pathfinder can test them
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
Current AdvC/SAS defines the cheap land-area prefilter as:

    // advc.030:
    // Not checked (to save time): unused canMoveAllTerrain
    bool AI_canEnterByLand(CvArea const& kArea) const
    {
        return (isArea(kArea) ||
            (canMoveImpassable() && canEnterArea(kArea)));
    }

`CvUnit::canEnterArea` is only:

    return kArea.canBeEntered(getArea(), this);

and `CvArea::canBeEntered` explicitly documents that it does NOT support
`canMoveAllTerrain`:

    /* If I wanted to support canMoveAllTerrain here, then I couldn't do
       anything more when u==NULL. So that's not supported. */

For two different land areas / representative landmasses it therefore returns
false before the unit's all-terrain ability is considered.

The nearby authoritative `AI_plotValid` comment states the optimization's
original assumption directly:

    For land units not in cargo, a faster inline check can accomplish almost
    the same thing - except for the unused NoRevealMap and MoveAllTerrain tags.
    So I've replaced some AI_plotValid calls with same-area or
    AI_canEnterByLand checks.

And `AI_plotValid` itself preserves the missing ability correctly:

    case DOMAIN_LAND:
        return (pPlot->getArea().canBeEntered(getArea(), this) ||
                canMoveAllTerrain());

So the fast replacement is knowingly narrower than the function it replaced.
That was harmless only while `MoveAllTerrain` remained unused.

CURRENT SAS ACTIVATES THE OMITTED DOMAIN
----------------------------------------
Current `CIV4UnitInfos.xml` contains three real DOMAIN_LAND all-terrain units:

* `UNIT_AIRSHIP`
  - `DefaultUnitAI = UNITAI_EXPLORE`
  - `bCanMoveImpassable = 1`
  - `bCanMoveAllTerrain = 1`
* `UNIT_ROBOTIC_RECON_DRONE`
  - `DefaultUnitAI = UNITAI_EXPLORE`
  - `bCanMoveImpassable = 1`
  - `bCanMoveAllTerrain = 1`
* `UNIT_GUNSHIP`
  - `DefaultUnitAI = UNITAI_ATTACK`
  - `bCanMoveImpassable = 1`
  - `bCanMoveAllTerrain = 1`
  - 4 moves in current SAS

The Gunship is the cleanest combat/reinforcement fixture because its normal AI
role directly calls several helpers containing `AI_canEnterByLand` prefilters.

This ability is intentional current gameplay, not an accidental XML residue.
The Main Changes Guide says Airship and Gunship can move through all terrains,
including water tiles, using `bCanMoveImpassable` + `bCanMoveAllTerrain`.

REAL MOVEMENT / PATHFINDING ACCEPTS THE SAME ROUTE
--------------------------------------------------
The false negative belongs to the coarse AI prefilter, not to movement legality.

`CvUnit::canMoveInto` for `DOMAIN_LAND` uses:

    if (!isValidDomain(kPlot.isWater()))
        ...

and `CvUnit::isValidDomain` says:

    case DOMAIN_LAND:
        return (!bWater || canMoveAllTerrain());

The group pathfinder likewise preserves the ability. Its AI destination-area
fast rejection is guarded by:

    if (!kPlot.isArea(kGroupArea) &&
        !kGroup.canMoveAllTerrain() &&
        !kPlot.isAdjacentToArea(kGroupArea))
    {
        return false;
    }

Thus an all-terrain Gunship group can legally path from landmass A, across water,
to landmass B. The pathfinder is capable of proving the route -- but many AI
callers never invoke it because `AI_canEnterByLand(B)` has already returned
false.

DETERMINISTIC CURRENT-LIVE CONSEQUENCE: AI_guardCity
----------------------------------------------------
`UNIT_GUNSHIP`'s default role is `UNITAI_ATTACK`, and normal `AI_attackMove`
repeatedly calls `AI_guardCity(..., bSearch=true, ...)`, including the one-turn
and three-turn reinforcement searches.

`AI_guardCity` scans the owner's cities in this order:

    FOR_EACH_CITYAI(pLoopCity, GET_PLAYER(getOwner()))
    {
        if (!AI_canEnterByLand(pLoopCity->getArea()))
            continue;
        ...
        if (generatePath(pLoopCity->getPlot(), ..., &iPathTurns, 10))
            ...
    }

Reproduction geometry:

1. AI player owns city A on landmass A and under-defended/endangered city B on
   distinct landmass B.
2. A current SAS Gunship is on A and is available for the normal UNITAI_ATTACK
   movement logic.
3. Water separates A and B, but an all-terrain Gunship has a legal raw path
   across those water tiles.
4. `AI_guardCity` evaluates B.
5. `AI_canEnterByLand(B.area)`:
   - B is not in the Gunship's current area;
   - `canMoveImpassable` is true, so it calls `canEnterArea`;
   - both source and target are land areas with different representative areas;
   - `CvArea::canBeEntered` returns false without supporting MoveAllTerrain.
6. `AI_guardCity` executes `continue` and NEVER calls `generatePath` for B.
7. B therefore cannot be selected by this reinforcement routine even though the
   movement engine can route the Gunship there.

This is a hard reachability contradiction, not merely a different heuristic
score: the legal destination is removed before path cost or city need is ever
considered.

BREADTH
-------
The helper is used widely. Current `CvUnitAI.cpp` contains more than twenty
`AI_canEnterByLand` call sites. Only a small minority explicitly add their own
`|| canMoveAllTerrain()` escape (notably Settler/founding code). Many others do
not, including city guarding, healing/city selection, pillaging, city attacks,
goody targeting and several Great-Person/spy/upgrade-related destination scans.
Those callers can inherit the same all-terrain false-negative when their own
semantics otherwise permit a cross-area destination.

There is also broader same-landmass AI code outside this helper. In particular,
`AI_pickTargetCity` rejects cities outside `getArea()` and `AI_goToTargetCity`
asserts that its target is in the current area. Those restrictions can further
limit cross-water use of a SAS all-terrain UNITAI_ATTACK Gunship. They are useful
breadth / follow-up territory, but they are NOT required to prove F599 and are
not folded into the helper repair without a separate call-contract audit.

ANCESTRY / ACTIVATION
---------------------
The narrow helper is inherited from pre-SAS AdvC optimization work.

Reachable AdvC history:

    practical 1925
    e4ff624d23ec90298119911fa182fa0e4c870d5a
    "Remove or replace unnecessary AI_plotValid calls"

introduced the replacement pattern and documented that MoveAllTerrain was an
unused exception. Practical 1926 then moved the helper out of the header while
retaining:

    // Not checked (to save time): unused canMoveAllTerrain

Base AdvC 1.14 data kept that assumption dormant:

* `UNIT_GUNSHIP`: DOMAIN_LAND, MoveImpassable=0, MoveAllTerrain=0.
* `UNIT_AIRSHIP`: DOMAIN_AIR, MoveAllTerrain=0.
* Robotic Recon Drone did not exist.

SAS later intentionally activates the dormant domain. The clearest Gunship
activation is:

    practical 4985
    b9e253a3ce3f13933babe7714a22ddadd31789a4

whose title includes making Gunship move impassable and whose XML diff changes:

    bCanMoveImpassable: 0 -> 1
    bCanMoveAllTerrain: 0 -> 1

Later SAS unit reworks retain those flags and add/retain the all-terrain Airship
and Robotic Recon Drone.

Classification: SAS-activated inherited AdvC optimization assumption.

DEDUP BOUNDARY
--------------
Whole-album semantic search found no existing root for all-terrain AI units
being rejected by `AI_canEnterByLand` / area prefilters.

Nearby controls are distinct:

* F376/KI#699 is the malformed `AI_connectBonus` replacement
  `kPlot.isArea(kPlot.getArea())`, a boolean tautology that makes the entire
  helper return false. Its repair note merely observed that restoring
  `AI_plotValid` would preserve unusual all-terrain semantics; it does not own
  the broad `AI_canEnterByLand` helper omission.
* F152 concerns GroupPathFinder cache membership / movement-rule invalidation,
  not target elimination before pathfinding.
* earlier Gunship/no-city-capture work concerns combat/capture valuation once a
  city is already in the relevant area, not cross-landmass reachability.
* historical archaeology C139/C140 verified that the XML/Sevopedia/engine
  movement capability itself is intentional and legal; it did not establish
  that every AI fast prefilter honors that newly activated capability.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The smallest root-level repair is to make the helper preserve the same explicit
MoveAllTerrain escape as `AI_plotValid`:

    bool AI_canEnterByLand(CvArea const& kArea) const
    {
        return (isArea(kArea) || canMoveAllTerrain() ||
            (canMoveImpassable() && canEnterArea(kArea)));
    }

This remains only a cheap coarse reachability gate. Individual terrain/feature,
ownership, war, danger and path-cost legality are still decided by the real
plot/path checks afterward. Therefore an all-terrain unit being allowed past
this prefilter does not imply that every destination becomes legal.

Regression controls should include:

1. current SAS Gunship on landmass A + own endangered city B on landmass B:
   helper must not reject B before `generatePath`;
2. raw GroupPathFinder succeeds across a legal water corridor for the same
   all-terrain Gunship;
3. ordinary Infantry on A remains rejected for B by the coarse land-area gate;
4. current Settler behavior remains unchanged (its existing explicit
   MoveAllTerrain escape becomes redundant but equivalent);
5. review the separate direct `isArea(getArea())` attack-city target filters as
   follow-up breadth rather than assuming the helper fix automatically covers
   them.

POST-F599 DIRECT SAME-AREA TARGET-SELECTOR REVIEW
-------------------------------------------------
The adjacent `AI_pickTargetCity` / `AI_goToTargetCity` same-area restrictions
were reopened because current SAS makes Gunship a real DOMAIN_LAND
`canMoveAllTerrain` UNITAI_ATTACK unit.

Current `AI_pickTargetCity` still rejects every enemy city outside the unit's
current `CvArea` before path generation:

    if (!pLoopCity->isArea(getArea()))
        continue;

and `AI_goToTargetCity` asserts that its city target belongs to the current
area and filters adjacent attack plots by the same area.

These restrictions can limit how fully the AI exploits an all-terrain Gunship,
but the evidence is not clean enough for an independent F600:

* `AI_pickTargetCity` / `AI_goToTargetCity` is explicitly the ordinary
  land-assault-city target routine rather than a generic all-terrain
  reachability helper;
* current Gunship has `bNoCapture=1`;
* normal UNITAI_ATTACK entry reaches the target-city branch only under
  `bLandWar` / group conditions, and cross-water enemy-city strategy also
  depends on area-level war architecture beyond this one filter;
* therefore restoring `canMoveAllTerrain()` only at this one city filter would
  not by itself establish a complete or clearly intended overseas attack-city
  state machine.

This is useful F599 breadth / all-terrain-AI architectural follow-up, not a
second numbered root. F599 itself remains independently proven through generic
`AI_canEnterByLand()` callers such as own-city reinforcement where the legal
cross-water destination is unambiguously within the caller's contract.

TERRITORY / DOMAIN LEGALITY PAIR
--------------------------------
The authoritative `CvUnit` territory family was traced together:

* `canEnterTerritory`
* `getDeclareWarMove`
* `canMoveInto`
* `canEnterArea`
* `isValidDomain`
* `canCargoEnterTerritory`
* `isIntruding`
* `canAdvance`

The core current rules remain coherent:

* friendly / unowned / enemy territory, RivalTerritory, always-invisible,
  hidden-nationality, Open Borders and AdvC disengagement access are handled by
  `canEnterTerritory`;
* the AdvC barbarian border-obstacle check is deliberately applied before the
  broad RivalTerritory/hidden exceptions and remains inherited from Base 1.14;
* `canMoveInto` adds plot-specific terrain/feature/domain/loading/combat rules

* cargo territory checks enumerate the actual cargo and require each passenger

No current-live owner/team/direction contradiction comparable to F595 or F599
was established in these functions.

GENERIC SPY-CARGO ROBUSTNESS CONTROL -- CURRENTLY MASKED
-------------------------------------------------------
One genuine generic mismatch was found but does not meet the current-live
threshold under shipped SAS settings.

`CvUnit::canMoveInto` contains a special Spy restriction:

    if (isSpy() && GC.getDefineBOOL(CvGlobals::USE_SPIES_NO_ENTER_BORDERS))
    {
        if (kPlot.getOwner() != NO_PLAYER &&
            !GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).canSpiesEnterBorders(kPlot.getOwner()))
        {
            return false;
        }
    }

But `canCargoEnterTerritory` asks each loaded unit only for
`canEnterTerritory(...)`. A Spy has RivalTerritory access, so with
`USE_SPIES_NO_ENTER_BORDERS=1` a transport could generically carry a Spy into
territory that the Spy could not enter under its own `canMoveInto` rule.

The inherited BtS default is:

    USE_SPIES_NO_ENTER_BORDERS = 0

and current SAS does not override that define in its shipped XML. Therefore the
extra Spy-border rule is disabled in current recommended play and the cargo
mismatch is dormant. Preserve as mod-mod / define-activation robustness debt;
do not assign F600.

ISINTRUDING CONTROL
-------------------
`isIntruding()` intentionally does not mean "unit lacks legal movement access."
Its live callers are Spy interception / Spy-AI timing. Open Borders therefore
still counts as foreign intrusion but receives the reduced
`ESPIONAGE_SPY_NO_INTRUDE_INTERCEPT_MOD`; vassal/master relationships and AdvC
Disengagement suppress intrusion explicitly. This is an intentional espionage
semantic distinction, not a mismatch with `canEnterTerritory`.

C031-WIP418 -- QUEUE 007: F600 CONFIRMED -- AIR-COMBAT DAMAGE USES ATTACKER PLOT
===============================================================================

STATUS

Queue 007 `CvGameCoreDLL/CvUnit.cpp` remains OPEN.

F600 / KI#923 -- ADVC PRACTICAL-1925 PLOT-CLEANUP REGRESSION MAKES AIR-STRIKE
DAMAGE USE THE ATTACKER'S PLOT/CITY INSTEAD OF THE DEFENDER'S TARGET PLOT/CITY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED CURRENT-LIVE BASE-ADVC REGRESSION inherited by SAS.

Current SAS and Base AdvCiv 1.14 contain:

    int CvUnit::airCombatDamage(const CvUnit* pDefender) const
    {
        int iOurStrength = airCurrCombatStr(pDefender);
        FAssertMsg(iOurStrength > 0,
            "Air combat strength is expected to be greater than zero");
        int iTheirStrength = pDefender->maxCombatStr(plot(), this);

        int iStrengthFactor = (iOurStrength + iTheirStrength + 1) / 2;

        int iDamage = std::max(1,
            ((GC.getDefineINT(CvGlobals::AIR_COMBAT_DAMAGE) *
            (iOurStrength + iStrengthFactor)) /
            (iTheirStrength + iStrengthFactor)));

        CvCity const* pCity = getPlot().getPlotCity();
        if (pCity != NULL)
        {
            iDamage *= std::max(0, (pCity->getAirModifier() + 100));
            iDamage /= 100;
        }
        return iDamage;
    }

Both `plot()` / `getPlot()` calls above refer to the attacking aircraft's own
current base plot. `pDefender` can be many tiles away on the actual air-strike
target plot.

BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod instead preserve the original target-plot contract:

    pPlot = pDefender->plot();
    ...
    iTheirStrength = pDefender->maxCombatStr(pPlot, this);
    ...
    pCity = pPlot->getPlotCity();

That distinction is authoritative gameplay state, not UI valuation.
`CvUnit::airStrike` chooses the real target defender and then directly applies:

    int iDamage = airCombatDamage(pDefender);
    ...
    pDefender->setDamage(iUnitDamage, getOwner());

CURRENT-LIVE CONSEQUENCE 1 -- TARGET BUNKER IS READ FROM THE WRONG CITY
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS ships exactly one nonzero building `iAirModifier` source:

    BUILDING_BUNKER
    iAirModifier = -50

The stock/K-Mod target-plot logic therefore halves ordinary air-strike damage
against a defender in a Bunker city:

    targetCity.getAirModifier() + 100 = 50

Current AdvC/SAS instead asks `getPlot().getPlotCity()` on the aircraft itself.
Thus, for an aircraft based in an ordinary city with no Bunker and striking an
enemy Bunker city, the target's -50% air-defense modifier is not read at all;
the multiplier is taken from the attacker's base city instead. Conversely, if
the attacking aircraft is based in a Bunker city and attacks a remote city
without one, current code can wrongly halve the outgoing strike damage.

A deterministic two-city regression fixture is therefore enough:

1. Player A owns an air-strike-capable Fighter/Bomber in city A with no Bunker.
2. Player B owns a valid defender in city B and builds a Bunker there.
3. A air-strikes B.
4. Correct BtS/K-Mod logic applies B's -50 AirModifier.
5. Current AdvC/SAS reads A's city instead and therefore ignores B's Bunker.

Terrain/defender modifiers can be chosen neutral in the fixture so that the
Bunker term alone exposes the wrong city; the source contradiction does not
depend on any particular combat-roll outcome because `airCombatDamage` is
deterministic after the defender is selected.

CURRENT-LIVE CONSEQUENCE 2 -- DEFENDER STRENGTH USES THE WRONG PLOT
--------------------------------------------------------------------
The same wrong-plot replacement feeds:

    pDefender->maxCombatStr(plot(), this)

`maxCombatStr` uses its supplied `pPlot` for authoritative defensive context,
including plot defense, city-defense status, hills defense, feature defense and
terrain defense. Passing the aircraft's base plot therefore evaluates the
defender as though it were standing on the attacker's plot for those terms,
while the defender is actually standing on the remote target plot.

This can independently overstate or understate air-strike damage whenever the
attacker's base terrain/city context differs from the target defender's real
terrain/city context. The later attacker-modifier portion of `maxCombatStr`
recovers the defender's actual `plot()` internally for `pAttackedPlot`, but the
defender-side plot modifiers above still use the caller-supplied wrong plot.

ANCESTRY / INTRODUCTION IS EXACT
--------------------------------
The regression was introduced by Base AdvC practical commit 1925:

    e4ff624d23ec90298119911fa182fa0e4c870d5a
    2020-01-13
    "Remove or replace unnecessary AI_plotValid calls"

The commit broadly optimized plot-access / legality code, cached current plots,
and replaced many `plot()->` uses with `getPlot().`. In the exact CvUnit hunk it
removed the local variable whose semantic identity was the DEFENDER plot:

    - CvPlot* pPlot = pDefender->plot();

and mechanically changed:

    - pDefender->maxCombatStr(pPlot, this);
    + pDefender->maxCombatStr(plot(), this);

    - CvCity* pCity = pPlot->getPlotCity();
    + CvCity const* pCity = getPlot().getPlotCity();

The practical's documented purpose concerns AI_plotValid and plot-access
optimization; it gives no gameplay rationale for changing the target of air
combat from defender plot to attacker plot. K-Mod and Civ4CE retain the old
correct defender-plot code. Base AdvC 1.14 and current SAS retain the practical-
1925 regression unchanged.

SAME-ROOT DORMANT BREADTH -- rangeCombatDamage
----------------------------------------------
The very next hunk in practical 1925 performs the same substitution inside
`rangeCombatDamage`:

    - CvPlot* pPlot = pDefender->plot();
    - pDefender->maxCombatStr(pPlot, this);
    + pDefender->maxCombatStr(plot(), this);

This is the same mechanical root and should be repaired at the same time by
using the defender's plot. Current SAS, however, does not provide a clean
current-live range-strike fixture through this helper: the non-air units with
positive `iAirRange` (SAM Infantry / Mobile SAM) have `iAirCombat=0`, while
`canRangeStrike()` requires `airBaseCombatStr() > 0`. Preserve this as same-root
robustness breadth rather than consuming a second finding number.

WHOLE-ALBUM DEDUP
-----------------
Broad WIP417 searches for `airCombatDamage`, `AirModifier`, `iAirModifier`,
`Bunker`, air-strike damage, target-city air defense, and defender-plot air
combat found no existing finding root.

Earlier air-strike entries concern AI assertions/selection, interception,
logging, help, or generic action-state accounting. None owns the authoritative
executor using the attacking aircraft's plot in place of the defender's target
plot when computing strike damage.

F600 is therefore independent of:

* F598's naval Blitz / sea-pillage made-attacks counter regression;
* F599's all-terrain AI reachability prefilter;
* prior air-strike AI valuation/assertion/help findings, which do not repair
  `CvUnit::airCombatDamage`'s target-plot identity.

NARROW REPAIR BOUNDARY
----------------------
Restore one explicit defender-plot identity and use it consistently:

    CvPlot const* pPlot = pDefender->plot();
    int iTheirStrength = pDefender->maxCombatStr(pPlot, this);
    ...
    CvCity const* pCity = pPlot->getPlotCity();

or the equivalent direct reference-based form.

Apply the same target-plot repair to `rangeCombatDamage` because practical 1925
introduced the identical substitution there, even though current shipped SAS
does not presently activate that sibling helper with nonzero ranged air-combat
strength.

Regression controls:

1. Air-strike a defender in a Bunker city from a non-Bunker base: target -50%
   AirModifier must apply.
2. Reverse Bunker placement (attacker base has Bunker, target does not): the
   attacker's Bunker must not reduce outgoing damage.
3. Use target vs base plots with deliberately different defensive terrain/city
   modifiers and verify defender strength follows the target plot.
4. Ordinary identical-terrain/no-Bunker strike remains unchanged.
5. If non-air range-strike content is later activated, verify its defender
   strength also uses `pDefender->plot()`.

F601 / provisional KI#924 -- SAS deliberately gives Privateer two DOMAIN_LAND
cargo slots, but the inherited hidden-nationality loading rule rejects every
current land unit; the advertised capacity is unusable and downstream code can
mistake the Privateer for a real land transport
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
Current SAS `UNIT_PRIVATEER` declares:

    <Domain>DOMAIN_SEA</Domain>
    ...
    <SpecialCargo>NONE</SpecialCargo>
    <DomainCargo>DOMAIN_LAND</DomainCargo>
    <iCargo>2</iCargo>
    ...
    <bHiddenNationality>1</bHiddenNationality>
    <bAlwaysHostile>1</bAlwaysHostile>

The two slots are not inherited stale data. SAS practical 4676 / commit
`bf2f1f436787c7e34669e156d443297974c23250` (2025-04-12), whose full message
explicitly lists "rework slightly the privateer", changes this exact field:

    <DomainCargo>DOMAIN_LAND</DomainCargo>
  - <iCargo>0</iCargo>
  + <iCargo>2</iCargo>

Thus SAS intentionally activated cargo capacity on the Privateer.

The authoritative loader, however, retains the BtS/K-Mod/Base-AdvC hidden-
nationality restriction. `this` is the proposed cargo and `kUnit` the proposed
transport:

    if (!m_pUnitInfo->isHiddenNationality() &&
        kUnit.getUnitInfo().isHiddenNationality())
    {
        return false;
    }

An ordinary land unit therefore cannot load onto a hidden-nationality
Privateer even when domain, team, plot and free cargo-space tests all succeed.

CURRENT XML EXHAUSTION -- ZERO LEGAL LAND CARGO TYPES
------------------------------------------------------
A namespace-aware census of the supplied current `CIV4UnitInfos.xml` finds:

    hidden-nationality unit types: 1
        UNIT_PRIVATEER -- DOMAIN_SEA

    hidden-nationality DOMAIN_LAND unit types: 0

    total current DOMAIN_LAND unit types: 109

Privateer itself requires DOMAIN_LAND cargo. Because every current land unit is
non-hidden-nationality, every one reaches the restriction above and is rejected.
The only hidden-nationality unit is the sea-domain Privateer itself and therefore
does not satisfy the transport's `DomainCargo=DOMAIN_LAND` contract.

There is no promotion/state escape hatch here: the loading test queries the
unit's `CvUnitInfo::isHiddenNationality()` flag directly. Current promotions do
not turn an ordinary land unit into a hidden-nationality cargo type for this
check.

Hence the currently shipped Privateer has two nominal land-cargo slots but
**zero legal current cargo unit types**.

PLAYER-FACING CONTRACT IS ALSO WRONG
------------------------------------
This is not merely an unused internal XML number. Current `CvGameTextMgr`
advertises every positive `getCargoSpace()` in unit help / Sevopedia:

    if (u.getCargoSpace() > 0)
    {
        ...
        TXT_KEY_UNIT_CARGO_SPACE, u.getCargoSpace()
    }

and live-unit help similarly displays `cargoSpace()`.

The Privateer therefore presents itself as having cargo capacity 2 while the
actual load command rejects every current unit compatible with its declared
cargo domain.

ANCESTRY / ACTIVATION BOUNDARY
------------------------------
The hidden-nationality loading rule is old and deliberate-looking rather than a
SAS invention. Civ4CE/BtS and K-Mod contain the same logic:

    if (!cargo.isHiddenNationality() && transport.isHiddenNationality())
        return false;

Base AdvC 1.14 retains it in `CvUnit::canLoadOnto` after the API refactor.

The privateer's positive cargo capacity is the new activation. Practical 4676
changes 0 to 2 while retaining `DomainCargo=DOMAIN_LAND` and the Privateer's
hidden-nationality identity. Therefore this is a SAS XML <-> inherited-C++
contract regression, not a newly introduced loader bug.

DOWNSTREAM GAMEPLAY / AI BREADTH
--------------------------------
The dead capacity can affect more than the load button because several generic
systems trust `cargoSpace()` as evidence that a hull is a usable transport.

A concrete already-audited example is `PUF_isEnemyCityAttacker`:

    if (u.getCargoSpace() <= 0 || u.getSpecialCargo() != NO_SPECIALUNIT)
    {
        if (u.getDomainType() != DOMAIN_LAND)
            return false;
        ...
    }
    return PUF_isEnemy(...);

A sea unit with positive generic cargo space bypasses the non-land rejection.
Privateer therefore qualifies for the helper's conservative "land invasion
transport" proxy solely because `iCargo=2`, even though no current land attacker
can actually load onto it.

This corrects an older album CONTROL in the `PUF_isEnemyCityAttacker` audit that
listed:

    Galley, Galleon, Transport, Privateer

as generic positive-capacity DOMAIN_LAND transports and concluded that the
cargo XML supported the helper's intended proxy. That statement was structurally
true only at the UnitInfo field level. The deeper `canLoadOnto` audit proves that
Privateer's advertised capacity is not *usable* capacity. Preserve the older
control for Galley/Galleon/Transport, but exclude Privateer from the positive
"can actually carry land attackers" premise.

ROOT BOUNDARY / DEDUP
---------------------
Whole-album searches for Privateer + cargo/load/transport, hidden-nationality
cargo/loading, and `canLoadOnto` found no prior finding that owns this content
contract.

This is independent of:

* F595/KI#918, where directly gifting already-loaded cargo can preserve an
  invalid cross-team transport pointer. F601 occurs before loading and makes
  Privateer's declared current cargo capacity unusable at all.
* F599/KI#922, which concerns all-terrain AI area prefilters.
* earlier Privateer blockade/heal/visibility findings, which do not involve
  cargo eligibility.

The older PUF transport passage is a positive-control correction/breadth witness,
not an existing root that repairs or subsumes F601.

REPAIR / DESIGN BOUNDARY
------------------------
Do not blindly delete the inherited hidden-nationality restriction. It has a
plausible gameplay purpose: nationally identifiable troops should not
necessarily be allowed to hide aboard an anonymous Privateer without diplomatic
consequences.

The current contradiction should instead be resolved deliberately in one of two
ways:

1. If Privateer was not meant to transport land units, restore `iCargo=0`
   (and keep `DomainCargo` irrelevant as before). This removes the misleading
   help/AI transport signal.
2. If the two cargo slots are intended gameplay, define which cargo can legally
   use them and modify the nationality/cargo design coherently -- e.g. a
   purpose-specific allowed class/state rather than globally allowing all
   ordinary troops aboard hidden-nationality ships without considering identity
   and diplomacy.

Regression controls for either choice:

* Sevopedia/live help must match usable cargo behavior.
* A normal current land unit should either be deliberately loadable or the
  Privateer should no longer advertise generic capacity.
* Generic threat/transport helpers must not count dead capacity as land-invasion
  capacity.
* Galley/Galleon/Transport ordinary cargo behavior remains unchanged.

DORMANT ADJACENT CONTROL -- `bGarrisonStrength`
-----------------------------------------------
The post-WIP418 semantic-operand pass also found a real arithmetic defect in the
special `maxCombatStr(..., bGarrisonStrength=true)` path: `AI_plotDefense` is
stored in `iExtraModifier` and added, the garrison branch then skips replacing it
with `fortifyModifier()`, but the common tail adds `iExtraModifier` again. Plot
strength can therefore be counted twice (or a stale preceding modifier can be
re-added).

Current SAS ships `DEMAND_BETTER_PROTECTION=0`, and this is the gameplay family
that uses that special garrison-strength mode. Preserve it as dormant
AdvC/mod-mod correctness debt, not F602.
