C031-WIP420 -- QUEUE 007 CvUnit.cpp -- F602 COMBAT-LIMIT DOMAIN ACTIVATION
===============================================================================

F602 / KI#925 -- SAS Janissary `iCombatLimit=110` exceeds max hit points;
actual combat treats it as fully lethal while combat-odds code requires 110 damage
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: CONFIRMED CURRENT-LIVE SAS CONTENT <-> COMBAT-ODDS CONTRACT BUG
SEVERITY / CONSEQUENCE: player-visible displayed combat odds and AI combat valuation
can materially underestimate Janissary attacks. The actual combat resolver kills at
normal 100 damage, while the odds model requires damage up to the raw 110 combat
limit. The same raw-limit mistake also survives in the legacy/manual AI odds fallback.

ROOT
----
Current SAS deliberately ships one ordinary combat unit whose XML combat limit is
above the engine's normal full-health range:

    UNIT_OTTOMAN_JANISSARY
        iCombat      = 12
        iCombatLimit = 110

A current UnitInfo census finds no other shipped `iCombatLimit > 100` unit. Base
AdvCiv 1.14's Janissary instead has:

        iCombat      = 9
        iCombatLimit = 100

The core combat resolver does NOT give a 110 limit any meaning beyond ordinary lethal
combat. `CvUnit::resolveCombat` checks the special non-lethal combat-limit stop with:

    bool const bLimitReached =
        (std::min(GC.getMAX_HIT_POINTS() - 1,
            pDefender->getDamage() + iDamage) >= combatLimit());

For a limit of 110 and the normal 100-hit-point unit range, the left side is capped at
99 and can never reach 110. The combat-limit withdrawal/stop branch therefore never
fires. Damage continues normally until `pDefender->isDead()` at full lethal damage.
The combat simulator uses the same `min(MAX_HIT_POINTS - 1, ...) >= combatLimit()`
contract, so it likewise treats 110 as ordinary lethal combat.

`CombatOdds::setupCombatantsImpl`, however, uses the raw combat limit as a damage
requirement:

    int iDefHitLimit =
        kDefender.maxHitPoints() - kAttacker.combatLimit();

    att.setHitsToWin(intdiv::uceil(std::max(0,
        kDefender.currHitPoints() - iDefHitLimit),
        att.damagePerRound()));

At full health with `combatLimit() == 110`, `iDefHitLimit` becomes -10. The attacker
is therefore modeled as needing:

    100 - (-10) = 110 damage

rather than the 100 damage that actually kills the defender.

This is a hard executor-vs-predictor disagreement. Values at or above full hit points
are treated as fully lethal by the real combat lifecycle and by surrounding
`combatLimit() >= MAX_HIT_POINTS` policy checks, but CombatOdds extrapolates the raw
XML number beyond the target's actual health range.

CURRENT-LIVE PLAYER / AI CONSUMERS
----------------------------------
This is not dead diagnostic arithmetic.

`CvGameTextMgr` obtains normal land-combat odds through:

    int const iCombatOdds =
        calculateCombatOdds(*pAttacker, *pDefender);

and specifically treats attackers with
`combatLimit() >= GC.getMAX_HIT_POINTS()` as normal lethal attackers when deciding
whether to show victory odds. The Janissary therefore enters the normal displayed
victory-odds path, but that displayed value is calculated with the impossible 110-
damage requirement above.

The normal LFB-enabled AI path also calls `calculateCombatOdds`, and current SAS ships
`LFB_USECOMBATODDS=1`. Thus AI attack valuation can inherit the same underestimated
Janissary odds.

Even the old/manual `CvUnitAI::AI_attackOdds` fallback has the same raw-domain
assumption:

    int iHitLimitThem =
        pDefender->maxHitPoints() - combatLimit();

followed by a rounds-needed calculation. Disabling LFB therefore does not make the
above-100 data safe by itself.

CLEAN CURRENT FIXTURE
---------------------
A neutral, full-health Janissary versus a normal full-health Musketman is enough to
expose the round-count mismatch without terrain/city complications.

Current generic Musketman:

    iCombat = 12
    no XML free promotion

Current Janissary:

    iCombat = 12
    free PROMOTION_COMBAT3 (+10% combat)
    iCombatLimit = 110

On a neutral plot, the exact damage-per-round value depends on the normal integer
strength/firepower formula, but the invariant does not: actual combat needs only
enough successful hits to accumulate 100 damage; CombatOdds asks the same attacker to
accumulate 110. Whenever one extra hit is needed to bridge 100 -> 110 -- which occurs
for the ordinary roughly-20-damage rounds in this matchup -- the displayed/AI model
requires one more winning combat round than the executor.

For intuition only (not required for the proof), roughly 20 damage per Janissary hit
means:

    actual resolver: 5 successful hits can kill at 100
    CombatOdds:       6 successful hits are requested for 110

That is large enough to move the modeled victory probability materially, not merely a
one-permille presentation rounding difference.

SAS INTRODUCTION / PERSISTENCE
------------------------------
The >100 domain is SAS-authored and deliberate-looking rather than accidental XML
parser garbage.

Practical 4957 / commit
`fe58e134631681ba9e79e481dd29a761b8820696` (2025-08-24) changes the relevant
musket-era unique-unit block from:

    iCombat      12 -> 14
    iCombatLimit 100 -> 110

alongside broader military-balance changes.

Practical 5025 / commit `8138f8af...` later reorganizes the Musketman/unique-unit
blocks and explicitly carries the 110 limit with the Janissary identity while the
generic Musketman side is restored to 100. This is useful provenance: the unusual
value does not merely remain attached to an arbitrary XML position during a reorder.

Practical 5924 later nerfs current Janissary combat strength from 14 -> 12 while
leaving:

    iCombatLimit = 110

unchanged. The >100 value therefore survives multiple later balance passes and is
current data.

ANCESTRY / ACTIVATION BOUNDARY
------------------------------
Base AdvCiv 1.14's Janissary uses `iCombatLimit=100`, and normal BtS/K-Mod unit-data
conventions keep lethal units at the full-hit-point limit rather than above it. The
combat and odds code was consequently written around the conventional domain:

    partial/non-lethal: combatLimit < MAX_HIT_POINTS
    fully lethal:       combatLimit >= MAX_HIT_POINTS

The real combat resolver is robust enough that values above the maximum simply behave
like fully lethal combat. `CombatOdds`, however, assumes the raw value itself is a
reachable damage threshold. SAS newly activates the unsupported distinction between
`== MAX_HIT_POINTS` and `> MAX_HIT_POINTS`.

ROOT BOUNDARY / WHOLE-ALBUM DEDUP
---------------------------------
Whole-album searches for `combatLimit`, `hitsToWin`, `iDefHitLimit`, Janissary and
`calculateCombatOdds` found no existing finding owning an above-max-hit-point combat
limit.

The closest earlier work is independent:

* F200/KI#523: loss of raw ordinary odds through personality adjustment + 1..99 clamp
  before nonlinear AI weighting.
* F210/KI#533 and the later current-file air controls: DOMAIN_AIR is fed into ordinary
  combat-strength/odds machinery.
* prior siege/combat-limit investigations explicitly test the normal
  `0 < iCombatLimit < 100` partial-lethal domain.
* an old Battle-History control noted that ordinary lethal fighting units used 100 and
  therefore did not exercise a partial-limit classification branch. It did not cover
  or repair a `>100` predictor/executor mismatch.

F602 is therefore an independent current-live root: SAS expands the XML domain beyond
full hit points, and the combat-odds predictor fails to clamp that value to what the
actual combat state can represent.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
For current SAS content, the smallest and clearest repair is probably data-level:

    UNIT_OTTOMAN_JANISSARY iCombatLimit: 110 -> 100

A value of 110 supplies no extra lethal capability in the actual resolver; the unit
already kills normally at 100. Unless the 110 number was intended to encode some new
mechanic that the engine currently does not implement, restoring 100 removes only the
predictor inconsistency, not a real combat advantage.

For engine robustness, odds code should also normalize any combat limit against the
defender's representable hit-point range, e.g. conceptually:

    effectiveLimit = min(attacker.combatLimit(), defender.maxHitPoints())

before deriving `iDefHitLimit` / hits-to-win. The legacy AI fallback should use the
same normalized semantics. That would make future/mod-mod values above max HP behave
in the predictor exactly as they already behave in actual combat.

Do not clamp partial siege limits upward; values below max HP are real supported
non-lethal combat and must remain unchanged.

REGRESSION CONTROLS
-------------------
- Janissary versus a full-health ordinary defender: displayed/AI hits-to-win must
  match the real resolver's lethal 100-damage threshold.
- Any `combatLimit >= defender.maxHitPoints()` must produce the same combat odds as a
  limit exactly equal to defender.maxHitPoints().
- Current Catapult/Trebuchet/Cannon/etc. sub-100 non-lethal limits must retain their
  existing partial-damage semantics and odds.
- The normal combat executor itself should remain unchanged unless the mod explicitly
  decides to invent a semantic meaning for >100 combat limits.

DURABLE STATE
-------------

F593/KI#916 through F602/KI#925 are CONFIRMED.
F603 / provisional KI#926 is UNUSED.
Actual repository/gameplay source remains untouched.

- exclude F602's above-max-hit-point Janissary CombatOdds root;
- continue the rare SAS UnitInfo-domain activation sieve from F603 unused;
- next high-value changed domains include Explorer `bNoCapture`, Scout
  `bIgnoreTerrainCost`, and the SAS Airship's AIR -> LAND capability redesign, with

- require an authoritative current producer/consumer contradiction, not merely a
  surprising balance choice;
- whole-album semantic dedup before numbering;
- physically freeze the next WIP regardless.

C031-WIP421 -- QUEUE 007 CvUnit.cpp -- F603 GUNSHIP WATER-WITHDRAWAL ACTIVATION
===============================================================================

F603 / KI#926 -- SAS SELF-PROPELLED ALL-TERRAIN LAND UNIT LOSES WITHDRAWAL ON WATER
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status:
- CONFIRMED current-live SAS activation bug in inherited CvUnit combat semantics.
- Current fixture: UNIT_GUNSHIP.
- Root is independent of F599/KI#922: movement/pathfinding is legal here; the stale
  assumption is in the combat withdrawal consumer.

INHERITED RULE / ORIGINAL DOMAIN ASSUMPTION
-------------------------------------------
Current SAS `CvUnit::withdrawalProbability()` is unchanged in meaning from Base AdvC,
K-Mod and BtS/Civ4CE:

    int CvUnit::withdrawalProbability() const
    {
        if (getDomainType() == DOMAIN_LAND && getPlot().isWater())
            return 0;
        return std::max(0,
            m_pUnitInfo->getWithdrawalProbability() + getExtraWithdrawal());
    }

Civ4CE's BtS source and K-Mod use the same DOMAIN_LAND + water hard zero. AdvC
practical 1925 only replaced `plot()->isWater()` with the equivalent
`getPlot().isWater()` during its broad plot-access cleanup; it did not change the
semantic rule.

Under ordinary BtS/K-Mod data this is a useful amphibious rule: a LAND unit whose
combat origin is water is normally cargo attacking from a sea transport, and such an
attacker must not retreat back into the sea.

SAS ACTIVATES A NEW LEGAL STATE
-------------------------------
Current SAS deliberately makes Gunship a self-propelled all-terrain LAND unit:

    Type                 UNIT_GUNSHIP
    Domain               DOMAIN_LAND
    DefaultUnitAI        UNITAI_ATTACK
    bOnlyDefensive       0
    bNoCapture           1
    bCanMoveImpassable   1
    bCanMoveAllTerrain   1
    iMoves               4
    iCombat              26
    iCombatLimit         100
    iWithdrawalProb      25

Base AdvCiv 1.14 already gives Gunship 25% withdrawal, but both movement flags are 0.
SAS practical 4985 / commit `b9e253a3ce3f13933babe7714a22ddadd31789a4`
(2025-09-04) deliberately changes both flags to 1. Current Main Changes documentation
also states that Airship and Gunship can move through all terrains, including water,
through `bCanMoveImpassable` + `bCanMoveAllTerrain`.

The authoritative movement helper honors that domain expansion:

    case DOMAIN_LAND:
    case DOMAIN_IMMOBILE:
        return (!bWater || canMoveAllTerrain());

and `canMoveInto()` uses that result. A current Gunship can therefore move onto water
under its own power; it is not merely occupying the transport's water plot as cargo.

COMBAT PATH IS ALSO LEGAL
-------------------------
Gunship is a normal attacker (`bOnlyDefensive=0`, combat limit 100). `canAttack()`
permits it, and `canAttack(const CvUnit&)` has no general LAND-vs-SEA prohibition.
The special cross-domain amphibious prohibition there only rejects LAND attackers
whose `combatLimit() < 100`; Gunship is 100.

Therefore a supported current state is:

    self-propelled Gunship moves onto water
        -> attacks an adjacent enemy naval defender on water
        -> normal CvUnit::updateCombat / resolveCombat
        -> otherwise-lethal attacker round
        -> withdrawalProbability()
        -> DOMAIN_LAND && origin water
        -> returns 0

The Gunship's XML 25% withdrawal is thus suppressed solely because the legal combat
origin happens to be water.

LIVE EXECUTOR / UI EFFECT
-------------------------
This is not presentation-only. `resolveCombat()` directly rolls
`withdrawalProbability()` when attacker damage would become lethal. The same value is
also folded into combat-message odds and other AI/odds consumers.

Live-unit help calls `pUnit->withdrawalProbability()` and therefore removes the
withdrawal line while a Gunship is on water. By contrast, UnitInfo/Sevopedia help uses
`u.getWithdrawalProbability()` and continues to advertise the Gunship's base 25%.
The UI disagreement is useful corroboration; the actual combat roll is the primary
bug.

WHY `isCargo()` IS THE PRECISE REPAIR DISCRIMINATOR
---------------------------------------------------
The inherited rule was trying to distinguish an amphibious cargo attacker, not water
as an inherently withdrawal-forbidden combat environment.

The current amphibious execution path proves that transport state survives until the
withdrawal roll:

1. `CvSelectionGroup::groupAmphibMove` gathers LAND cargo groups and pushes their
   MOVE_TO / attack mission. It does not unload them first.
2. `CvSelectionGroup::groupAttack` chooses the cargo attacker and directly calls
   `CvUnit::attack()`.
3. `CvUnit::updateCombat()` enters `resolveCombat()` before any winning advance.
4. Only after combat can `groupMove()` call `CvUnit::move()`/`setXY()` to advance the
   attacker onto the destination. `setXY()` clears its transport link when the new
   plot no longer matches its transport.

So an ordinary amphibious LAND attacker is still `isCargo()==true` when
`withdrawalProbability()` is consulted.

A semantically narrow repair is therefore conceptually:

    if (getDomainType() == DOMAIN_LAND &&
        getPlot().isWater() &&
        isCargo())
    {
        return 0;
    }

This preserves the inherited no-retreat rule for actual transported amphibious
attackers, including a Gunship that is genuinely loaded aboard a transport, while a
self-propelled Gunship on water keeps its ordinary 25% withdrawal.

Using `!canMoveAllTerrain()` as the exception would repair the current fixture, but it
is less exact: capability is not the real reason withdrawal should be blocked; actual
cargo/amphibious state is.

CURRENT-DATA PARTITION
----------------------
Current SAS has three DOMAIN_LAND units with `bCanMoveAllTerrain=1`:

    UNIT_AIRSHIP              bOnlyDefensive=1  withdrawal 20
    UNIT_ROBOTIC_RECON_DRONE  bOnlyDefensive=1  withdrawal 50
    UNIT_GUNSHIP              bOnlyDefensive=0  withdrawal 25

Airship and Robotic Recon Drone reinforce the expanded domain but cannot reproduce the
normal attack-side withdrawal loss because they are defensive-only. Gunship is the
clean current-live witness.

WHOLE-ALBUM DEDUP / ROOT BOUNDARY
---------------------------------
Whole-album searches for withdrawal, retreat, amphibious, Gunship, isCargo and
canMoveAllTerrain found no prior root owning this combat-state contradiction.

Closest earlier work is independent:

- F149/KI#472: false-success accounting in `groupAmphibMove` can consume a deferred
  landing when no cargo actually lands. That is mission/execution success state; it
  does not alter combat withdrawal semantics.
- F599/KI#922: `AI_canEnterByLand`/same-area prefilters can reject destinations that
  a MoveAllTerrain unit can physically reach. F603 begins only after legal movement
  has succeeded and the real combat resolver is running.
- Prior withdrawal references concern ordinary odds/value weighting or Battle History
  outcome classification, not suppression of a supported self-propelled water
  attacker's retreat chance.

Fixing any of those roots leaves F603 unchanged, and fixing F603 does not repair them.

DELIBERATE CONTROL: COLLATERAL LIMIT 200
----------------------------------------
The adjacent rare-domain pass also rechecked SAS's widespread
`iCollateralDamageLimit=200`. The executor can allow collateral damage to reach the
ordinary 100-HP death boundary even though the XML limit exceeds 100. However SAS
practical 4676 explicitly says to increase collateral damage limit to 200 for all
units as part of the collateral-system rework. Without contradictory design evidence,
that remains intentional SAS gameplay rather than F603.

REGRESSION CONTROLS
-------------------
- Self-propelled current Gunship on water: live-unit help and actual lethal-round
  withdrawal roll should retain its normal 25% (plus valid promotion modifiers).
- The same Gunship while genuinely loaded as LAND cargo and amphibiously attacking
  from a transport must retain the inherited 0% withdrawal behavior.
- Ordinary transported LAND attackers without MoveAllTerrain must remain at 0% when
  attacking from water.
- Land combat from land and naval combat from water must remain unchanged.
- Airship/Robotic Recon Drone remain defensive-only; no new attack permission should
  be introduced by the repair.

DURABLE STATE
-------------
Queue 007 `CvGameCoreDLL/CvUnit.cpp` remains OPEN.
F593/KI#916 through F603/KI#926 are CONFIRMED.
F604 / provisional KI#927 is UNUSED.
Actual repository/gameplay source remains untouched.

Exact continuation cursor:
- exclude F603's inherited water-withdrawal / SAS MoveAllTerrain activation root;
- continue the rare SAS UnitInfo-domain/action activation sieve under F604 unused;
- Explorer `bNoCapture`, Scout/recon `bIgnoreTerrainCost`, Airship AIR->LAND redesign
  and other unusual current UnitInfo domains remain candidate controls/frontiers;
- continue preferring producer/consumer semantic contradictions over balance opinions;
- whole-album semantic dedup before numbering;
- physically freeze the next WIP regardless.

F604 / provisional KI#927
-------------------------
TITLE
    SAS Airship and Robotic Recon Drone advertise positive withdrawal chances that can
    never execute because both units are OnlyDefensive; upgraded recon units can carry
    still more unusable Retreat withdrawal into the same impossible attacker state.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED current-live SAS content <-> inherited combat-semantics contradiction.
    This is not a balance disagreement about whether the recon units ought to attack.
    The current XML simultaneously declares them strictly defensive and deliberately
    assigns attacker-only withdrawal capability, and current help exposes both claims.

CURRENT DATA / UNIQUE ACTIVATION
    Current SAS has exactly two UnitInfo entries with both:

        bOnlyDefensive = 1
        iWithdrawalProb > 0

    They are:

        UNIT_AIRSHIP
            Domain              = DOMAIN_LAND
            DefaultUnitAI       = UNITAI_EXPLORE
            Combat              = UNITCOMBAT_RECON
            bOnlyDefensive      = 1
            iCombat             = 6
            iWithdrawalProb     = 20

        UNIT_ROBOTIC_RECON_DRONE
            Domain              = DOMAIN_LAND
            DefaultUnitAI       = UNITAI_EXPLORE
            Combat              = UNITCOMBAT_RECON
            bOnlyDefensive      = 1
            iCombat             = 10
            iWithdrawalProb     = 50

    The same census over Base AdvCiv 1.14 and Civ4CE/BtS finds zero units combining
    OnlyDefensive with positive base withdrawal. The unsupported combination is
    therefore a SAS activation rather than normal inherited stock data.

ATTACK LEGALITY MAKES THE WITHDRAWAL UNREACHABLE
    CvUnit::canAttack() is explicit:

        if (!canFight())
            return false;
        if (isOnlyDefensive())
            return false;

    The defender-specific overload is equally explicit:

        if (!canCombat() || isOnlyDefensive())
            return false;

    Thus neither recon unit can legally become the attacker in ordinary unit combat.

    CvUnit::resolveCombat, however, rolls withdrawal only for `this`, the attacking
    unit, when that attacker would otherwise receive lethal damage:

        if (getDamage() + iAttackerDamage >= maxHitPoints() &&
            SyncRandSuccess100(withdrawalProbability()))
        {
            ...
            break;
        }

    There is no corresponding defender-withdrawal roll. The sea-pillage code even
    reinforces this contract by temporarily removing the pillager's withdrawal when
    the pillager is represented as the combat attacker but is conceptually the
    defender:

        int iWithdrawal = withdrawalProbability();
        changeExtraWithdrawal(-iWithdrawal); // no withdrawal since we are really the defender
        attack(...);
        changeExtraWithdrawal(iWithdrawal);

    Therefore positive withdrawal on an OnlyDefensive unit has no execution path.

CURRENT UI CONTRADICTION
    Actual-unit help reports OnlyDefensive explicitly:

        if (pUnit->isOnlyDefensive())
            ... TXT_KEY_UNIT_ONLY_DEFENSIVE

    but later, independently, reports any positive effective withdrawal:

        if (pUnit->withdrawalProbability() > 0)
            ... TXT_KEY_UNIT_WITHDRAWL_PROBABILITY

    UnitInfo / Sevopedia help does the same pair independently:

        if (u.isOnlyDefensive())
            ... TXT_KEY_UNIT_ONLY_DEFENSIVE

        if (u.getWithdrawalProbability() > 0)
            ... TXT_KEY_UNIT_WITHDRAWL_PROBABILITY

    A current newly built Airship can therefore be described as both "Can only
    defend" and "20% withdrawal", while the Robotic Recon Drone can show the same
    contradiction at 50%. The first statement makes the second capability impossible.

UPGRADE BREADTH -- THE FALSE EFFECTIVE VALUE CAN BECOME EVEN LARGER
    Current recon upgrade chain is:

        Scout -> Explorer -> Airship -> Robotic Recon Drone

    Current Explorer has free:

        PROMOTION_RETREAT1  (+10 withdrawal)
        PROMOTION_RETREAT2  (+20 withdrawal)

    CvUnit::convert does not discard the old unit's promotions while upgrading:

        setHasPromotion(eLoopPromotion,
            pUnit->isHasPromotion(eLoopPromotion) ||
            m_pUnitInfo->getFreePromotions(eLoopPromotion));

    setHasPromotion then applies the promotion's withdrawal change through:

        changeExtraWithdrawal(GC.getInfo(ePromotion).getWithdrawalChange() * iChange);

    Consequently an Explorer upgraded into Airship can retain +30 extra withdrawal.
    Its effective live-unit value can therefore become 20 + 30 = 50 despite remaining
    unable to attack. If that line upgrades again, Robotic Recon Drone can retain the
    same +30 on top of its own 50 base value, i.e. an effective 80, still with no legal
    attacker path. This is same-root consequence breadth, not a separate promotion bug.

DESIGN / HISTORY PROOF
    SAS practical 4911:

        92fc29e26e9bfe40311c02af385f58383e09c157
        2025-07-27
        "rework the airship now a recon unit ..."

    performs the Airship AIR -> LAND/recon redesign and deliberately sets:

        bOnlyDefensive: 0 -> 1
        iWithdrawalProb: 0 -> 20

    The same UnitInfo says the unit is to be "strictly observer/explorer/recon based"
    while the withdrawal value is explicitly added.

    SAS practical 4912:

        9ac030d829b21dd2e0bbb128bb4ebf8bb6c4a144
        2025-07-27
        "add the robotic_recon_drone ..."

    introduces the Drone with the explicit comment:

        "defensive unit, not an attack drone"

    and simultaneously gives it positive withdrawal (40 at introduction).

    SAS practical 4949:

        0910e8acee9589366d50e12ff5a860bdd8aa8a8e

    later changes Drone withdrawal 40 -> 50 and, for BOTH Airship and Drone, makes the
    design intent even more explicit by documenting the base withdrawal as a way for a
    newly produced unit to have "quite good" withdrawal while an upgraded Explorer
    would have still more. That same practical removes Retreat1/2 as direct free
    promotions from Airship/Drone but intentionally relies on the base withdrawal and
    the upgrade path. Their OnlyDefensive state remains unchanged.

    The contradiction is therefore not a stale field accidentally inherited from the
    old DOMAIN_AIR Airship: SAS deliberately authored both sides and later revisited the
    withdrawal values while keeping the units strictly defensive.

ANCESTRY / ENGINE CONTRACT
    The attacker-only nature of withdrawal and OnlyDefensive attack prohibition are
    inherited Civ4/K-Mod/AdvC semantics. Base AdvC's Airship is DOMAIN_AIR and has no
    positive withdrawal / OnlyDefensive combination, and Robotic Recon Drone does not
    exist there. Current SAS activates a data combination the inherited rules make
    meaningless.

DETERMINISTIC CONSEQUENCE
    1. Build either current recon unit.
    2. UnitInfo/Sevopedia exposes its positive withdrawal percentage and OnlyDefensive
       status together.
    3. Put the unit adjacent to any legal enemy combat unit.
    4. Attack initiation fails because isOnlyDefensive() is true.
    5. Since resolveCombat is never entered with the recon unit as attacker, its 20/50
       withdrawal can never be rolled.

    For an Explorer-upgraded Airship/Drone, the live-unit helper can advertise still
    higher effective withdrawal because the inherited Retreat promotions are retained,
    but the attack prohibition remains absolute.

DEDUP BOUNDARY
    Whole-album semantic search found no existing root for positive withdrawal on a
    unit that cannot legally attack.

    Nearby findings are independent:

    * F603/KI#926 concerns a real attacking Gunship whose legal 25% withdrawal is
      wrongly suppressed only when self-propelled on water. F604 is the opposite
      boundary: Airship/Drone cannot attack anywhere, so their positive withdrawal is
      unreachable on every plot.
    * F599/KI#922 concerns all-terrain AI reachability prefilters, not combat retreat.
    * earlier promotion-validity findings concern whether effects can be acquired;
      here the effective withdrawal number is genuinely present on the unit, but the
      only combat role that could consume it is prohibited.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    The repeated "strictly observer/explorer/recon" / "defensive unit, not an attack
    drone" comments make preserving OnlyDefensive the least disruptive current-design
    interpretation.

    Under that interpretation:

    1. set Airship and Robotic Recon Drone base iWithdrawalProb to 0 so UnitInfo help no
       longer advertises an impossible intrinsic capability;
    2. harden CvUnit::withdrawalProbability() for effective/live-unit state:

           if (isOnlyDefensive())
               return 0;

       before applying base + extra withdrawal. This also prevents retained Explorer
       Retreat promotions from creating a false effective percentage after upgrade;
    3. optional UI robustness: UnitInfo help can additionally avoid displaying
       withdrawal for isOnlyDefensive() types, protecting mod-mod XML even if such a
       combination is authored again.

    The alternative repair -- clearing bOnlyDefensive so withdrawal can execute -- is
    mechanically possible, but it contradicts the repeated current design comments and
    would turn both recon units into human-usable attackers. That is a gameplay redesign,
    not the conservative audit repair.

POSITIVE CONTROLS CLOSED IN THE SAME RARE-FIELD SIEVE
    * Explorer bNoCapture 1 -> 0 is intentional, not a bug. Practical 4377 is explicitly
      titled "reworked explorer units" and its inline XML comments say the Explorer can
      conquer cities, including opportunistic very weak / Barbarian cities. The same
      rework intentionally clears OnlyAttackBarbarians and blocks offensive AI roles
      through NotUnitAIs.
    * Airship becoming DOMAIN_LAND makes generic land-only actions such as airlift
      structurally available. That is an odd consequence worth remembering, but no
      current source/design invariant has yet shown it to be erroneous. Do not promote
      "Airship can airlift" merely because the old DOMAIN_AIR version could not.
    * iCollateralDamageLimit=200 remains deliberate SAS practical-4676 design; no
      contradictory evidence was found in this pass.

NEXT CURSOR
    WIP422 physical -> F604/KI#927 confirmed -> F605/KI#928 UNUSED -> continue the rare
    SAS UnitInfo/domain/action activation sieve outside F599/F601/F602/F603/F604,
    especially remaining bIgnoreTerrainCost / unusual land-domain action consumers;
    then rebuild the next under-covered authoritative CvUnit producer/consumer frontier
    if the rare-field sieve closes. Physically freeze WIP423 regardless before changing
    file/lens.

No gameplay/source files were modified by ChatGPT-5.6-Sol during this audit.

F605 / provisional KI#928
-------------------------
TITLE
    SAS Airship and Robotic Recon Drone are given Mobility Cost as a free promotion,
    but their explicit FlatMovementCost makes the promotion's sole movement-discount
    effect unreachable; live help can advertise both effects even though the flat-cost
    executor returns before the discount is ever consumed.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED current-live SAS content <-> inherited movement-semantics contradiction.
    This is not a tuning judgment about whether the units should be fast. The current
    XML deliberately installs an iMoveDiscountChange promotion on the only two current
    explicit flat-moving units, while the movement executor structurally bypasses that
    field for every flat-movement step.

CURRENT DATA / EXHAUSTIVE ACTIVATION
    Current SAS has exactly two UnitInfo entries with explicit:

        bFlatMovementCost = 1

    They are:

        UNIT_AIRSHIP
            Domain              = DOMAIN_LAND
            Combat              = UNITCOMBAT_RECON
            iMoves              = 2
            bFlatMovementCost   = 1
            bIgnoreTerrainCost  = 0
            free PROMOTION_MOBILITY_COST

        UNIT_ROBOTIC_RECON_DRONE
            Domain              = DOMAIN_LAND
            Combat              = UNITCOMBAT_RECON
            iMoves              = 2
            bFlatMovementCost   = 1
            bIgnoreTerrainCost  = 0
            free PROMOTION_MOBILITY_COST

    Current promotion data has exactly one positive raw move-discount promotion:

        PROMOTION_MOBILITY_COST
            iMoveDiscountChange = 1

    Thus the two explicit flat-moving types are also exactly the two SAS UnitInfo types
    that deliberately receive this otherwise meaningful move-discount effect for free.

EXECUTOR -- FLAT MOVEMENT RETURNS BEFORE MOVE DISCOUNT
    CvPlot::movementCost begins with the flat-movement special case:

        if (kUnit.flatMovementCost())
        {
            return GC.getMOVE_DENOMINATOR();
        }

    Only later, inside ordinary terrain-cost calculation, can ExtraMoveDiscount matter:

        if (iRegularCost > 0)
            iRegularCost = std::max(1,
                    iRegularCost - kUnit.getExtraMoveDiscount());

    Therefore a flat-moving unit always pays exactly one MOVE_DENOMINATOR for the step
    and exits before `getExtraMoveDiscount()` is read. Whether that unit has 0, +1, or
    any larger move discount cannot change its per-tile movement cost while flat
    movement remains active.

    This is stronger than ordinary redundancy on cheap terrain: the promotion has zero
    movement-cost execution states on these UnitInfo types under their defining flat
    movement rule.

PROMOTION STATE REALLY IS INSTALLED
    CvUnitInfo::isPromotionValid normally contains a related semantic guard:

        if (isIgnoreTerrainCost() &&
            kPromotion.getMoveDiscountChange() != 0)
        {
            return false;
        }

    i.e. the inherited validator already understands that a movement-cost discount is
    meaningless when another unit rule bypasses ordinary terrain cost.

    There is no equivalent FlatMovementCost check. More importantly for the two current
    units, free promotions bypass normal validation immediately:

        if (getFreePromotions(ePromotion))
            return true;

    Mobility Cost is normally restricted by UnitCombat eligibility to mounted/armor
    families, while Airship and Drone are UNITCOMBAT_RECON. SAS therefore deliberately
    injects the promotion through the free-promotion path; this is not a promotion the
    recon units naturally selected despite failing an eligibility check.

CURRENT UI CONTRADICTION
    Actual-unit help independently reports explicit FlatMovementCost:

        if (pUnit->getUnitInfo().isFlatMovementCost())
            ... TXT_KEY_UNIT_FLAT_MOVEMENT

    and then reports any nonzero effective move discount:

        if (pUnit->getExtraMoveDiscount() != 0)
            ... TXT_KEY_PROMOTION_MOVE_DISCOUNT_TEXT

    Promotion help likewise describes Mobility Cost's iMoveDiscountChange normally.
    A current Airship/Drone can therefore advertise both flat movement and a movement
    discount even though the executor never combines them: flat movement exits first.

DESIGN / HISTORY PROOF
    The chronology resolves the remaining intent question cleanly.

    SAS practical 4676:

        bf2f1f436787c7e34669e156d443297974c23250
        2025-04-12
        broad XML/unit/collateral rework

    is where Airship was deliberately converted from its inherited air-domain model to
    a self-propelled DOMAIN_LAND unit. In the same Airship hunk:

        Domain:              DOMAIN_AIR -> DOMAIN_LAND
        bCanMoveImpassable:  0 -> 1
        bCanMoveAllTerrain:  0 -> 1
        bFlatMovementCost:   0 -> 1
        iMoves:              1 -> 2

    with the explicit comment that the change should make the Airship "walk" on all
    terrains. At this point the Airship had no free Mobility Cost promotion. So flat
    movement was already an established, intentional movement mechanic months before
    the dead promotion was added.

    SAS practical 4911:

        92fc29e26e9bfe40311c02af385f58383e09c157
        2025-07-27
        "rework the airship now a recon unit ..."

    preserves `bFlatMovementCost=1` and newly gives Airship free:

        PROMOTION_SENTRY
        PROMOTION_MOBILITY_COST
        PROMOTION_RETREAT1
        PROMOTION_RETREAT2

    The contemporaneous comment explains Mobility Cost as simulating the levitating
    Airship being able to travel day and night "freely regardless of terrain" at low
    energy cost. That is precisely the mechanical effect already enforced by flat
    movement, and the executor makes the newly added discount unable to change it.

    SAS practical 4912:

        9ac030d829b21dd2e0bbb128bb4ebf8bb6c4a144
        2025-07-27
        "add the robotic_recon_drone ..."

    introduces Robotic Recon Drone with the same deliberate pair:

        bFlatMovementCost = 1
        free PROMOTION_MOBILITY_COST

    Later documentation cleanup continues to describe Mobility Cost as a low-energy /
    continuous-movement property; no later mechanical consumer was added that gives the
    promotion an independent effect on flat-moving units.

    The history therefore distinguishes this from harmless stale XML. Flat movement
    came first as the real movement rule; Mobility Cost was later authored to reinforce
    an effect the engine had already made complete, but cannot stack with it.

ANCESTRY / ACTIVATION BOUNDARY
    BtS/Civ4CE, K-Mod and Base AdvC retain the same movement ordering: flat movement
    returns a fixed denominator before terrain movement discounts are evaluated.

    Their ordinary data does not place the SAS pair onto these current LAND recon
    units. Base AdvC's Airship remains an air-domain unit and Robotic Recon Drone does
    not exist. The unsupported/redundant combination is therefore activated by SAS
    content, not by a new current executor regression.

DETERMINISTIC CONSEQUENCE
    For either current Airship or Drone:

        flatMovementCost() == true
            -> movementCost() returns MOVE_DENOMINATOR
            -> getExtraMoveDiscount() is never queried
            -> Mobility Cost cannot reduce the step

    Removing only PROMOTION_MOBILITY_COST from the unit leaves every movementCost()
    result unchanged while the current flat-movement rule remains enabled.

    This is mechanically testable on flatland, hills, forests/jungle and any other
    traversable terrain: the unit pays the same one-denominator flat step before and
    after the promotion because all those states exit at the same first branch.

DEDUP BOUNDARY
    Whole-album semantic search found existing Mobility Cost material only in contexts
    where the promotion really works -- notably mounted/Hussar path-cost findings and
    current movement-heuristic controls. Those roots depend on ordinary terrain-cost
    execution reaching `getExtraMoveDiscount()`.

    F605 is the inverse state: explicit flat movement prevents that consumer from being
    reached at all. No previous finding owns this flat-movement / move-discount
    contradiction.

    Nearby roots remain independent:

    * F599 concerns MoveAllTerrain omitted from coarse AI reachability prefilters.
    * F603 concerns Gunship withdrawal on legal self-propelled water combat.
    * F604 concerns impossible withdrawal on OnlyDefensive Airship/Drone.
    * F605 concerns only the movement-cost effect of Mobility Cost after the same recon
      redesign; fixing any of the above does not make this discount execute.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    The conservative content repair is to remove free PROMOTION_MOBILITY_COST from
    Airship and Robotic Recon Drone while keeping their explicit FlatMovementCost.
    That preserves every current movementCost result and removes a mechanically dead /
    misleading promotion from the units and help text.

    Engine robustness can additionally make the semantic contract explicit in
    CvUnitInfo::isPromotionValid:

        if ((isIgnoreTerrainCost() || isFlatMovementCost()) &&
            kPromotion.getMoveDiscountChange() != 0)
        {
            return false;
        }

    This would protect ordinary/non-free promotion acquisition in future mod content,
    parallel to the existing IgnoreTerrainCost guard. It would not by itself reject an
    explicitly configured free promotion because free promotions intentionally return
    true before the normal validation checks; XML cleanup remains necessary for current
    Airship/Drone.

    The alternative -- removing FlatMovementCost so Mobility Cost becomes meaningful --
    would materially redesign their movement and contradict the older, explicit all-
    terrain flat-travel design. It is not the conservative audit fix.

REGRESSION CONTROLS
    * Airship and Drone must retain exactly their current per-step flat movement cost on
      all legal terrains after removing the dead promotion.
    * Ordinary mounted/armor users of PROMOTION_MOBILITY_COST must continue to receive
      their current terrain-cost reduction.
    * IgnoreTerrainCost promotion filtering must remain unchanged.
    * Free-promotion semantics generally must remain unchanged; do not move or remove the
      global free-promotion early return merely to repair these two XML entries.
    * F599/F603/F604 behavior is independent and must not be altered by this repair.

F606 / provisional KI#929
-------------------------
TITLE
    AdvC air-bomb city-defense damage still unconditionally applies the
    IgnoreBuildingDefense compensation ratio even though SAS deliberately removed
    IgnoreBuildingDefense from every current unit; ordinary Fighter/Bomber city
    bombardment is therefore amplified by defensive buildings that SAS now intends to
    affect those aircraft, and a building-only-defense city also exposes the stale
    ratio's zero-denominator boundary.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED current-live SAS content <-> inherited AdvC bombard-semantics
    contradiction. This is not a balance opinion about aircraft bomb rates. The
    calculation documents exactly why its building/culture ratio exists, and the SAS
    content deliberately invalidates that prerequisite for all current air bombers.

AUTHORITATIVE EXECUTOR CONTRACT
    Current CvUnit::airBombDefenseDamage says:

        /* <advc.004c> Same as in damageToBombardTarget except that
           IgnoreBuildingDefense doesn't have to be checked here b/c all air units
           have that */
        int iDefWithBuildings = kCity.getDefenseModifier(false);
        int iDefSansBuildings = kCity.getDefenseModifier(true);
        FAssertMsg(iDefSansBuildings > 0 || isHuman(), ...);
        return (airBombCurrRate() *
                scaled(iDefWithBuildings, iDefSansBuildings)).round();

    `airBomb()` applies that result directly:

        pCity->changeDefenseModifier(
                -std::max(0, airBombDefenseDamage(*pCity)));

    The ratio is therefore gameplay execution, not only an estimate or UI value.

    The sibling ordinary Bombard helper makes the missing semantic gate explicit:

        bool const bIgnore = ignoreBuildingDefense();
        ...
        if (!bIgnore)
            iBombardModifier -= pBombardCity->getBuildingBombardDefense();
        ...
        if (bIgnore && iDefSansBuildings > 0)
            rDamage *= scaled(iDefWithBuildings, iDefSansBuildings);

    Its comment explains that the ratio is needed so a unit which ignores defensive
    buildings reduces the visible total defense by enough to produce the intended
    reduction in the non-building defense it actually fights through.

CURRENT SAS DATA -- THE ASSUMPTION IS NOW FALSE FOR EVERY AIR BOMB
    Namespace-aware exhaustive census of current CIV4UnitInfos.xml:

        total UnitInfo entries                  = 131
        bIgnoreBuildingDefense = 1 entries      = 0

    Every current unit with positive iBombRate is an air-domain unit and has the flag
    disabled:

        UNIT_FIGHTER          iBombRate  8   bIgnoreBuildingDefense 0
        UNIT_JET_FIGHTER      iBombRate 12   bIgnoreBuildingDefense 0
        UNIT_BOMBER           iBombRate 16   bIgnoreBuildingDefense 0
        UNIT_STEALTH_BOMBER   iBombRate 20   bIgnoreBuildingDefense 0
        UNIT_GUIDED_MISSILE   iBombRate 16   bIgnoreBuildingDefense 0

    Base AdvC 1.14 and the local BtS/Civ4CE source have the same five positive-rate
    air-bomb types with bIgnoreBuildingDefense=1. Their data therefore satisfies the
    assumption written into AdvC's helper; current SAS data does not.

CURRENT SAS DESIGN INTENT IS EXPLICIT
    The current Main Changes Guide states under Military - Common:

        City defenses affect all units, including gunpowder and later.
        See bIgnoreBuildingDefense in CIV4UnitInfos.xml.

    This agrees with the exhaustive current XML state and with combat execution:
    maxCombatStr uses the attacker's `ignoreBuildingDefense()` when asking the target
    plot for its defensive modifier. SAS's 0 values therefore have a real intended
    combat meaning; they are not unused documentation flags.

DETERMINISTIC LIVE CONSEQUENCE
    The stale ratio grows whenever building defense raises the city's displayed
    defense above its non-building/cultural defense.

    Simple current fixture using Walls:

        building / raised defense = 50
        cultural defense          = 20
        Bomber iBombRate          = 16
        Bomber IgnoreBuildingDefense = false

    Current air-bomb helper nevertheless calculates:

        16 * 50 / 20 = 40

    and reduces total city defense by 40 instead of the nominal 16 before clamping at
    the city's remaining defense. The extra 24 points arise solely from the
    compensation mechanism for ignoring a building effect that this SAS Bomber no
    longer ignores.

    Castle-style fixture:

        displayed defense with building = 100
        non-building defense             = 60
        Bomber iBombRate                 = 16

    gives approximately:

        16 * 100 / 60 = 26.67 -> 27

    rather than the unscaled 16 baseline.

    The important defect is the conditionality, not either chosen example: as the
    building/non-building defense ratio increases, current SAS air-bomb damage is
    increased because of a property every current air bomber explicitly lacks.

ZERO-NONBUILDING-DEFENSE BOUNDARY -- SAME ROOT
    Current CvCity::isBombardable can legally expose a human Air Bomb mission when a
    city has positive building defense but zero non-building defense. For example,
    raised defense from Walls can make `getDefenseModifier(false) > 0` while
    `getDefenseModifier(true) == 0`.

    `airBombDefenseDamage` then constructs `scaled(iDefWithBuildings, 0)`. The ordinary
    `damageToBombardTarget` sibling explicitly protects this ratio with
    `iDefSansBuildings > 0`; the air helper omitted that guard only under its historical
    "all air units ignore buildings" assumption. Do not promote this as another
    finding: it is an edge consequence of the same stale unconditional ratio.

HISTORY / INTRODUCTION BOUNDARY
    AdvC practical 1262:

        c01c07e94be3b86fa524a1cb14cff918d0996ae3

    replaced BtS's direct:

        changeDefenseModifier(-airBombCurrRate())

    with the building/non-building ratio. The introducing source comment already says
    that IgnoreBuildingDefense need not be checked because all air units have it.

    In the same practical, ordinary siege Bombard was changed to apply the ratio only
    when `bIgnore` is true. Thus the asymmetry was deliberate and data-dependent, not a
    generic rule that every air mission should scale by defensive buildings.

    Base AdvC still satisfies that data prerequisite. SAS practical 4676
    (bf2f1f436787c7e34669e156d443297974c23250, 2025-04-12) broadly changed inherited
    bIgnoreBuildingDefense=1 military entries to 0 as part of its unit/XML rework;
    later SAS edits completed/retained the all-zero current state. The current guide
    subsequently documents that city defenses affect all units.

    SAS therefore changed the producer/configuration contract while inheriting the
    old AdvC consumer unchanged.

UI / OBSERVABILITY BREADTH
    `CvGameTextMgr::getAirBombPlotHelp` calls each eligible selected aircraft's same
    `airBombDefenseDamage()` helper when forecasting city-defense reduction. Thus the
    UI and execution agree with each other numerically, but both agree on the stale
    over-scaled result. The earlier action-help reconciliation control does not make
    the calculation semantically correct; it only established executor/help symmetry.

    This remains independent of F071/KI#393, which fixed which selected aircraft are
    included in a multi-unit Air Bomb preview. F071 can choose the correct eligible
    set while every included unit still contributes the wrong F606 damage amount.

SASGAMERECORD BREADTH -- SAME STALE ASSUMPTION REPEATED
    The current AIR city-bombard logging call is:

        logSASGameRecordCityBombard(this, pCity, "AIR",
                airBombCurrRate(), true, ...);

    The `true` increments `iIgnoreBuildingDefenseActions` in the GameRecord sequence.
    It was added in practical 6092 and retains the historical AdvC assumption even
    though every current SAS air bomber has `ignoreBuildingDefense()==false`.

    This is logging consequence breadth of the same semantic contract, not a separate
    root. A repair to air-bomb gameplay should also stop hardcoding this metadata and
    record the acting unit's actual flag (or whatever deliberately chosen post-fix Air
    Bomb semantic is intended).

DEDUP BOUNDARY
    Whole-album semantic search found several Air Bomb roots/controls, but none owns
    this calculation contract:

    * F071/KI#393: multi-unit Bombard/Air Bomb preview counted target-ineligible units.
    * F072/KI#394: Air Bomb best-unit selection could choose a target-ineligible
      aircraft and abort a valid group mission.
    * later action-help controls established that the chosen helper and executor use
      the same `airBombDefenseDamage` calculation.
    * an earlier AI_getBombardTurns control discussed synthetic global air support and
      IgnoreBuildingDefense as an approximation, not actual Air Bomb city damage.
    * F536/KI#859 independently observed that current SAS has no IgnoreBuildingDefense
      units while auditing obsolete-building valuation.

    None of those findings tests whether AdvC's unconditional air-bomb ratio is still
    legal after SAS removes the flag from the actual bomber. Fixing any of them leaves
    F606 unchanged, and fixing F606 does not repair their mission-selection roots.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR BOUNDARY
    The minimum semantics-preserving repair is to stop applying AdvC's compensation
    ratio unless the acting unit really ignores building defense, and to retain the
    same positive-denominator guard already used by `damageToBombardTarget`, e.g. in
    conceptual form:

        scaled rDamage = airBombCurrRate();
        if (ignoreBuildingDefense() && iDefSansBuildings > 0)
            rDamage *= scaled(iDefWithBuildings, iDefSansBuildings);
        return rDamage.round();

    Under current SAS XML (`ignoreBuildingDefense()==false` for all units), this makes
    normal Air Bomb city-defense damage use its configured bomb rate rather than an
    immunity-compensation multiplier.

    There is a separate design choice about BuildingBombardDefense. Ordinary
    `damageToBombardTarget` also applies a city's BombardDefense when the attacker does
    not ignore buildings. Stock/AdvC air bombers never exercised that branch because
    they all ignored buildings. If SAS intends the newly non-ignoring aircraft to obey
    Walls/Castle BombardDefense as well, `airBombDefenseDamage` can be generalized to
    mirror the full sibling formula. That would be a deliberate additional gameplay
    rule, not something this audit should silently bundle into the minimal F606 fix.

    GameRecord should likewise pass the real semantic value rather than literal
    `true` once the desired Air Bomb rule is settled.

REGRESSION CONTROLS
    * On a city with no building contribution (`defWithBuildings ==
      defSansBuildings`), current positive-rate aircraft must keep the same configured
      Air Bomb reduction after the fix.
    * Current SAS non-ignoring aircraft must no longer gain extra bombard damage merely
      because Walls/Castle raise `defWithBuildings / defSansBuildings`.
    * If a future/modded air bomber has IgnoreBuildingDefense=true, the historical AdvC
      compensation ratio should remain available with the denominator guard.
    * Human Air Bomb against positive building defense / zero non-building defense must
      not feed a zero denominator into the ratio.
    * F071 target-eligibility filtering and F072 mission selection must remain intact.
    * GameRecord AIR rows must not claim building-defense immunity inconsistent with
      the chosen gameplay semantics.

CONTROLS CLOSED IN THIS TRANCHE
    * Reused cargo-vector suspicion in `isBetterDefenderThan` is false: `getCargoUnits`
      begins by clearing the supplied vector, so the second defender's cargo valuation
      is not contaminated by the first defender's cargo.
    * Explorer city capture is deliberate SAS design: practical 4377's recon rework
      explicitly comments that Explorer can conquer opportunistic weak/barbarian
      cities; its bNoCapture relaxation is not an audit root.
    * Scout IgnoreTerrainCost remains an explicit recon redesign capability with no
      contradictory executor found in this activation sieve.
    * `iCollateralDamageLimit=200` remains explicit practical-4676 collateral design;
      its above-100 value was not promoted merely for differing from inherited BtS
      ranges.

F607 / provisional KI#930
-------------------------
TITLE
    Interceptors receive no combat experience at all for intercepting a normal
    Paratrooper: resolveAirCombat gates both interceptor-XP paths on the paradropper's
    own interception-derived retaliation damage, which is zero for the shipped
    Paratrooper even when the interceptor damages or kills it.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED current-live inherited BtS/K-Mod/Base-AdvC combat-state bug. The
    paradrop interception path is shipped and reachable in current SAS, and the XP
    suppression follows deterministically from current unit data. This is not a
    tuning disagreement about how much XP interception should grant; the existing
    function already awards ordinary interception XP, but an unrelated damage-capacity
    variable suppresses it only for the non-AIR attacker reuse.

CURRENT PARATROOPER FIXTURE
    Current SAS CIV4UnitInfos.xml:

        UNIT_PARATROOPER
        Domain                    DOMAIN_LAND
        UnitCombat                UNITCOMBAT_GUN
        iDropRange                5
        iCombat                   22
        iInterceptionProbability  0
        iEvasionProbability       25
        iXPValueAttack            4
        iXPValueDefense           2
        FreePromotions            none

    Current positive-interception defenders include Machine Gun, Mechanized Infantry,
    SAM Infantry, Mobile SAM, Destroyer, Fighter and Jet Fighter. Thus ordinary
    Paratrooper interception is not a theoretical unsupported state.

AUTHORITATIVE EXECUTION CHAIN
    CvUnit::paradrop moves the unit to the target, then calls:

        if (interceptTest(kPlot, ...))
            return true;

    interceptTest selects bestInterceptor and, on a successful interception roll,
    calls:

        fightInterceptor(kPlot, false);

    fightInterceptor routes the combat through updateAirCombat. That function is
    explicitly shared between normal air missions and paradrops:

        FAssert(getDomainType() == DOMAIN_AIR || getDropRange() > 0);
        ...
        if (DOMAIN_AIR != getDomainType())
            kAirMission.setMissionType(MISSION_PARADROP);
        ...
        resolveAirCombat(pInterceptor, pPlot, kAirMission);

    The resulting XP behavior therefore belongs to real Paradrop execution, not a
    display-only or dead helper.

WRONG STATE VARIABLE IN resolveAirCombat
    In the non-air-v-air branch, current code computes:

        iOurRoundDamage =
            pInterceptor->currInterceptionProbability() * MAX_INTERCEPTION_DAMAGE / 100;

        iTheirRoundDamage =
            currInterceptionProbability() * MAX_INTERCEPTION_DAMAGE / 100;

        if (getDomainType() == DOMAIN_AIR)
            iTheirRoundDamage = max(MIN_INTERCEPTION_DAMAGE, iTheirRoundDamage);

    `iOurRoundDamage` is damage the interceptor can inflict on the mission unit.
    `iTheirRoundDamage` is the mission unit's potential retaliation damage.

    For the current Paratrooper:

        getDomainType()                  = DOMAIN_LAND
        currInterceptionProbability()    = 0
        therefore iTheirRoundDamage      = 0

    while a real interceptor generally has iOurRoundDamage > 0 and can damage or kill
    the Paratrooper.

    Yet both interceptor-XP branches are conditioned on the *Paratrooper's*
    retaliation variable:

        if (isDead())
        {
            if (iTheirRoundDamage > 0)
                pInterceptor->changeExperience(...);
        }
        ...
        else if (iOurDamage > 0)
        {
            if (iTheirRoundDamage > 0)
                pInterceptor->changeExperience(EXPERIENCE_FROM_WITHDRAWL, ...);
        }

    Therefore an unpromoted current Paratrooper makes both guards false.

DETERMINISTIC CONSEQUENCES
    Successful interception where the Paratrooper survives:

        interceptor inflicts iOurDamage > 0
        Paratrooper iTheirRoundDamage == 0
        -> surviving-interception XP branch reached
        -> inner guard false
        -> interceptor gains 0 XP

    Successful interception where the interceptor kills the Paratrooper:

        isDead() == true for Paratrooper
        Paratrooper iTheirRoundDamage == 0
        -> kill-XP branch reached
        -> inner guard false
        -> interceptor gains 0 XP

    Thus even a Mobile SAM or Fighter that outright destroys the paradropping unit is
    denied the experience that the existing interception-combat code is otherwise
    structured to award.

WHY THIS IS NOT A GENERIC "NO RETALIATION, NO XP" RULE
    The same function already disproves that interpretation for ordinary aircraft.
    When the mission unit is DOMAIN_AIR, iTheirRoundDamage is forced to at least
    MIN_INTERCEPTION_DAMAGE even when its own interception probability is 0.

    Moreover, land/sea interceptors cannot actually be damaged in the attacker's
    successful-round branch because defender damage is applied only when:

        DOMAIN_AIR == pInterceptor->getDomainType()

    Nevertheless such ground/naval interceptors still pass the XP guard against an
    ordinary AIR attacker because iTheirRoundDamage was forced positive. The guard
    therefore does not reliably encode "interceptor was at risk" or "both sides could
    deal damage". It is an AIR-attacker-era proxy that breaks for the explicitly
    supported non-AIR Paradrop path.

PROMOTION BOUNDARY
    PROMOTION_AIR_INTERCEPTION1 is currently legal for UNITCOMBAT_GUN and can add a
    small positive interception value to a promoted Paratrooper. Such a specially
    promoted unit can make iTheirRoundDamage positive and thereby restore interceptor
    XP accidentally.

    That does not close the finding; it sharpens it. Whether the interceptor gets XP
    for damaging/killing the same paradropping unit can depend on the *target's own air
    interception promotion*, even though that value is unrelated to whether the
    interceptor successfully dealt damage. The ordinary shipped Paratrooper has no
    such free promotion and reproduces the zero-XP state directly.

ANCESTRY / ACTIVATION BOUNDARY
    The same core structure exists in local BtS/Civ4CE, K-Mod 1.46 and Base AdvC
    1.14. BtS already routes paradrop interception through updateAirCombat and already
    permits that function for `DOMAIN_AIR || getDropRange() > 0`; this is therefore
    an inherited Civ4/BtS-era bug rather than a SAS-authored regression.

    AdvC practical 2784 / commit

        160fa499a896cf595f74bcbde68b7ce41bedc466

    substantially improved Paradrop/Air mission interception UI and group execution,
    but did not change this resolveAirCombat XP contract. Base AdvC and current SAS
    therefore retain the old mismatch.

    Current SAS keeps an ordinary active Paratrooper with DropRange 5 and positive
    evasion, so the inherited defect remains live.

DEDUP BOUNDARY
    Whole-album semantic search found prior Paradrop interception-help and mission-
    eligibility findings, plus generic interception/air-defense analysis. None owns
    combat experience inside resolveAirCombat, nor the use of iTheirRoundDamage as an
    interceptor-XP gate.

    Fixing the earlier Paradrop hover/selection roots does not change XP after a real
    interception. Fixing F607 does not change which interceptor is shown/selected or
    whether the mission is legal.

CONSERVATIVE REPAIR BOUNDARY
    The safe semantic objective is narrow: when an interceptor actually damages or
    kills a paradropping unit, do not condition the interceptor's already-existing XP
    award on the paradropper having positive interception-derived retaliation damage.

    For current ordinary AIR attackers the existing `iTheirRoundDamage > 0` condition
    is effectively always true because of MIN_INTERCEPTION_DAMAGE, so removing or
    replacing that stale proxy for the interceptor-XP branches can be made behavior-
    neutral for normal air interception while fixing Paradrop.

    The exact patch should be chosen against the desired XP rule rather than blindly
    swapping variables. Strong controls are:

    * killed mission unit: interceptor receives the existing kill XP calculation when
      it was the combatant that killed the unit;
    * surviving mission unit with iOurDamage > 0: interceptor receives the existing
      EXPERIENCE_FROM_WITHDRAWL-style award;
    * ordinary AIR-vs-AIR and AIR-vs-ground interception XP remains unchanged;
    * a non-intercepted Paradrop still gains no combat XP;
    * do not alter interception odds, damage, evasion or MadeInterception state.

CONTROLS CLOSED IN THIS TRANCHE
    * `flankingStrikeCombat` recomputes iFlankedDefenderOdds but uses the main
      defender's iDefenderOdds for the flanking-success roll in BtS, K-Mod, Base AdvC
      and SAS. The unused per-target odds value is suspicious-looking but inherited
      design, not enough by itself for a new root.
    * `rangeStrike` remains unavailable to current SAS non-air units with the required
      air-combat/range combination; F600 already records its wrong-plot sibling as
      dormant robustness breadth.
    * `attackForDamage` has no current gameplay caller outside its Python exposure in
      this source snapshot; no current-live defect was promoted from it.

PURPOSE OF THIS TRANCHE
-----------------------
Continue from WIP425 without forcing a finding. The pass first completed the rare
SAS UnitInfo activation sieve, then rebuilt low-album-coverage CvUnit.cpp bodies and
checked several source-level asymmetries that looked stronger than their eventual
runtime effect.

CONTROL 1 — EXPLORER IgnoreTerrainCost × free Woodsman II: PARTIALLY REDUNDANT,
NOT F608
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS Explorer has `bIgnoreTerrainCost=1` and free Woodsman I + Woodsman II.
`CvPlot::movementCost()` establishes the interaction mechanically:

    if (kUnit.flatMovementCost())
        return GC.getMOVE_DENOMINATOR();

    ...

    if (kUnit.ignoreTerrainCost())
        iRegularCost = 1;

    bool const bHasTerrainCost = (iRegularCost > 1);
    if (bHasTerrainCost && (... terrain/feature double-move ...))
        iRegularCost /= 2;

Thus Woodsman II's Forest/Jungle double-move component cannot further reduce an
Explorer's already-one-denominator terrain movement. The promotion is not wholly
dead, however: its Forest/Jungle attack/defense modifiers remain live.

History also argues against calling the overlap a bug. SAS practical 4374 added
Woodsman I as an Explorer identity/navigation bonus; practical 4377's broader
Explorer rework deliberately added Woodsman II because the Explorer should be more
in control of forest/jungle environments and because those combat bonuses do not
make city capture too strong. Later SAS recon documentation independently gives
ground exploration units IgnoreTerrainCost.

Classification: intentional overlapping mechanics with one redundant sub-effect,
not a hard content↔executor contradiction.

CONTROL 2 — flankingStrikeCombat dead per-target values: INHERITED DESIGN / DEAD
COMPUTATION, NOT F608
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`flankingStrikeCombat()` calls `getDefenderCombatValues(*pLoopUnit, ...)` for each
potential flanked unit and computes per-target strength/odds/damage values, but the
actual flanking hit roll and damage use the primary battle's caller-supplied
`iDefenderOdds`/`iDefenderDamage` instead.

The same behavior exists through BtS/Civ4CE -> K-Mod -> Base AdvC -> SAS. The
per-target locals are stale/unnecessary computation, but the primary-battle escape
odds and primary defender round damage are the historical flanking formula. No SAS
activation changes that contract. This is therefore code-cleanup debt, not F608.

CONTROL 3 — planBattle computeWaveSize attacker fallback typo: ALGEBRAICALLY DEAD,
NOT F608
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current inherited helper contains:

    aiDesiredSize[BATTLE_UNIT_DEFENDER] =
        aiDesiredSize[BATTLE_UNIT_DEFENDER] <= 0 ? iDefenderMax : ...;
    aiDesiredSize[BATTLE_UNIT_ATTACKER] =
        aiDesiredSize[BATTLE_UNIT_ATTACKER] <= 0 ? iDefenderMax : ...;

The attacker branch superficially appears to want `iAttackerMax`. However the
returned value is:

    min(min(attackerDesired, iAttackerMax),
        min(defenderDesired, iDefenderMax))

When attackerDesired uses the wrong `iDefenderMax`, the final expression is still
capped by both `iAttackerMax` and `iDefenderMax`; replacing that intermediate value
with `iAttackerMax` cannot change the result. This is a typo-looking but
behavior-neutral line.

CONTROL 4 — planBattle BATTLE_TIME_RANGED wrong-side accumulation: REAL BOOKKEEPING
ASYMMETRY, BUT NO PROVEN LIVE CONSEQUENCE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
K-Mod's planBattle rewrite records positive combat-log damage during a ranged phase
into the defender's `BATTLE_TIME_RANGED` slot. In the symmetric branch where the
defender damages the attacker it correctly increments `iAttackerDamage`, but then
again executes:

    kBattle.addDamage(BATTLE_UNIT_DEFENDER,
            BATTLE_TIME_RANGED, combat_log[i]);

rather than updating the attacker slot with the corresponding positive damage.
`CvBattleDefinition::addDamage()` is a plain signed integer addition, so this is a
real wrong-side bookkeeping asymmetry inherited by Base AdvC and SAS.

However, the same K-Mod code explicitly comments that this ranged-time damage is
probably not used, and current `resolveCombat()` repeats that `BATTLE_TIME_RANGED`
damage is set inside planBattle "not that it actually does anything". The actual
battle-round choreography is driven by the separately built `CvBattleRound` list,
and final gameplay damage was already resolved before animation planning.

Without a demonstrated EXE/animation consumer that makes the wrong slot observable,
this remains dormant animation-metadata debt rather than a current-live F608.

CONTROL 5 — sea-pillage withdrawal suppression lifetime: SAFE / SYNCHRONOUS OUTCOME,
NOT F608
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
When a sea pillager is intercepted, `pillage()` says the pillager is "really the
defender" and temporarily removes all withdrawal:

    int iWithdrawal = withdrawalProbability();
    changeExtraWithdrawal(-iWithdrawal);
    attack(pInterceptor->plot(), false, NULL, true);
    changeExtraWithdrawal(iWithdrawal);

This initially looked unsafe because visible combat animation is asynchronous.
Tracing the lifecycle closes it: `attack()` immediately calls `updateCombat()`, and
for the real defender `updateCombat()` immediately enters `resolveCombat()` on the
initial call. All combat RNG, damage, death and withdrawal decisions are therefore
resolved before `attack()` returns. What remains deferred is the animation timer and
cleanup, not the withdrawal outcome.

The modifier restoration is therefore safe for its intended purpose.

RARE SAS UNITINFO RANGE/COMBINATION SIEVE — CURRENT CLOSED SET
--------------------------------------------------------------
A namespace-correct current UnitInfo census was compared against Base AdvC scalar
ranges and rare boolean combinations. Previously-owned activations remained the
meaningful outliers:

* `bCanMoveAllTerrain=1` -> Airship, Robotic Recon Drone, Gunship (F599/F603 family);
* `bFlatMovementCost=1` -> Airship, Robotic Recon Drone (F605);
* `iCombatLimit=110` -> Ottoman Janissary (F602);
* `iCollateralDamageLimit=200` -> deliberate SAS collateral redesign; iterator/death
  mutation control already closed;
* negative Warrior city modifiers -> current signed combat consumers examined so far
  handle them;
* new animal/hill combat values and high late-game combat/power values are ordinary
  signed/scalar balance data in their inspected consumers.

No new hard executor-domain violation was promoted from the remaining range census.

SAVE-LOAD OPTION REMAP CONTROL
------------------------------
Current `CvGame::read` deliberately removed Base AdvC's historical `uiFlag` compatibility
branches and keeps only the current-layout option remap. Its raw indices initially looked
alarming, especially because an inline comment says `or 19 - you'd need to check which is
correct`, so they were verified mechanically rather than trusted.

For the current GameOption enum/XML order they are exact:

* 17 = `GAMEOPTION_NEW_RANDOM_SEED`
* 18 = `GAMEOPTION_LOCK_MODS`
* 19 = `GAMEOPTION_RISE_FALL`
* 20 = `GAMEOPTION_TRUE_STARTS`
* 23 = `GAMEOPTION_NO_VASSAL_STATES`
* 27 = `GAMEOPTION_NO_ESPIONAGE`

Current `CvGame::write` writes `uiFlag = 27`, matching Base AdvC's latest layout marker.
Thus the hard-coded current-version mapping does not itself corrupt current-format saves.
Removal of older-layout compatibility remains an explicit SAS compatibility policy and is
not promoted as a current-live F608.

`onAllGameDataRead` was also compared to Base AdvC. The removed save-flag-dependent work is
legacy migration work for earlier layouts/rules (old handicap storage, pre-river-rule plot
groups, legacy organization seats, pre-maintenance/attitude versions). The current-layout
AI-autoplay reset remains preserved independently. No same-version missing-finalization root
has yet been established.

F608 / KI#931 — ADV CIV-SAS VICTORY FAST SAVE SERIALIZES PRE-END GAMESTATE_ON
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Classification: current-live AdvCiv-SAS lifecycle/save-state defect introduced by the optional
Fast Save feature (practical 6374 / `3d67a8f613...`), enabled by default in current SAS.

Current `CvGame::setWinner` first assigns:

    m_eWinner = eNewWinner;
    m_eVictory = eNewVictory;

For ordinary games it then fires `CvEventReporter::victory`. BUG registers
`SASFastSave.saveGameEnd` as the first victory handler specifically so the victory save occurs
before AI Auto Play's victory handler. Rise & Fall suppresses the normal victory event, so SAS
calls the same helper directly at the equivalent point in `setWinner`.

Both routes therefore execute the Fast Save BEFORE the later block that transitions the game to
`GAMESTATE_OVER` or `GAMESTATE_EXTENDED`.

This timing is explicit in current source/docs, not inferred:

* `BugEventManager.py` says the save runs after winner/victory assignment but before the later
  OVER/EXTENDED transition;
* `SASFastSave.py` repeats the same contract;
* `README_Main_Changes_Guide.md` documents that Victory Fast Saves use that pre-transition event;
* the practical-6374 commit message says victories are saved before autoplay shutdown.

`SAS_FAST_SAVE_GAME_END_ENABLE` is 1 by default, so ordinary current single-player victories can
exercise this path without special unsupported settings.

The serialization contract makes the resulting snapshot internally inconsistent as an end save.
`CyGame::saveGame` directly invokes:

    gDLL->getEngineIFace()->SaveGame(szTmp, SAVEGAME_NORMAL);

from the victory callback. `CvGame::write` serializes, in order:

    m_eWinner
    m_eVictory
    m_eGameState

At this point winner/victory are already final but `m_eGameState` is still `GAMESTATE_ON`.
`CvGame::read` restores those same three members directly, and `onAllGameDataRead` contains no
winner/victory/game-state reconciliation.

The normal victory machine also cannot complete the missing transition after that save is loaded.
`CvGame::testVictory()` begins with:

    if (getVictory() != NO_VICTORY)
        return;

So a loaded Victory Fast Save has the persistent combination:

    winner    != NO_TEAM
    victory   != NO_VICTORY
    gameState == GAMESTATE_ON

and future victory tests return before `setWinner` can ever run again. Consequently the later
`setGameState` transition that was absent from the snapshot is not reconstructed by ordinary game
progression.

That matters because `setGameState(GAMESTATE_OVER)` is itself the producer for end-of-game side
effects: `gameEnd` reporting, BUG's ordinary end save, Rise & Fall end preparation,
`showEndGameSequence`, and extended-game popup setup. A snapshot taken before that transition is
therefore not semantically equivalent to the final victory state it is named/documented to save.

AUTOPLAY / RISE-FALL BOUNDARY
-----------------------------
The exact final state must not be guessed as always `GAMESTATE_OVER`.

For ordinary AI Auto Play, the Fast Save handler is deliberately registered before
`AIAutoPlay.onVictory`; that later handler calls `endAIAutoPlay`, changing autoplay state before
`CvGame::setWinner` resumes and chooses the final game state. Engine autorun can independently
lead to the `GAMESTATE_EXTENDED` branch. Rise & Fall uses its own direct pre-transition save and
has separate end-state preparation.

Thus a narrow repair should make the permanent victory Fast Save capture the ACTUAL post-victory
state/lifecycle, rather than simply mutating the pre-event snapshot to `GAMESTATE_OVER`.
The practical repair placement may require preserving the runtime-tested reason the previous late
hooks failed to create files, but the serialized state itself needs to reflect the completed
winner/victory transition.

The older BUG AutoSave end callback is a useful positive control: `setGameState` first assigns
`m_eGameState = GAMESTATE_OVER`, then emits `gameEnd` / `gameEndSave`; a save taken there naturally
contains the completed state. SAS moved victory saving earlier for runtime reliability, but that
also moved it across this state boundary.

HISTORY / DEDUP
---------------
Practical 6374 (`3d67a8f613...`, 2026-09-01) introduced SASFastSave, the early victory event
registration, and the Rise & Fall direct call. Its runtime validation established that turn-0 and
terminal victory files were physically created, but the supplied history does not show a load-and-
resume validation of the terminal Fast Save.

No later supplied commit through the current light-source snapshot changes this victory Fast Save
placement. Whole-album search finds no earlier root owning a pre-end `GAMESTATE_ON` victory save or
winner/victory/game-state serialization mismatch. The older Queue-008 KI#336-KI#345 set is
independent.

F608 is therefore one distinct root. The ordinary-game and Rise & Fall hooks, pre-autoplay ordering,
and skipped end side effects are consequence/activation breadth of the same lifecycle snapshot
error, not separate findings.

POSITIVE / NEGATIVE CONTROLS FROM THIS TRANCHE
----------------------------------------------
* The scary-looking current-version raw GameOption remap in `CvGame::read` remains a positive
  control: indices 17/18/19/20/23/27 exactly match current enum/XML ordering.
* Newly persisted map-heaviness flags, replay-audience masks and SAS source/version history retain
  matched current read/write order in the inspected stream.
* `onAllGameDataRead` does not contain a hidden reconciliation that would rescue F608.

CONTROL A — SAVES CREATED DURING AI AUTOPLAY RESTORE HUMAN STATUS COHERENTLY
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
`CvGame::read` reads `m_iAIAutoPlay` and, when the stored value is nonzero, temporarily changes it
to -1 until all game data has been loaded. `CvGame::onAllGameDataRead` later changes that sentinel
to 0 and refreshes AI attitudes.

A possible cross-object concern was that the active civilization might remain permanently marked
as AI-controlled because normal autoplay uses `CvPlayer::setHumanDisabled(true)`. The player
serialization/lifecycle disproves that concern:

* `CvPlayer::read` begins with `reset()`;
* `CvPlayer::reset` explicitly sets `m_bDisableHuman = false`;
* it then runs `updateHuman()`, which derives the human slot from `CvInitCore` when human-disable is
  false;
* `m_bDisableHuman` itself is transient and is not restored from the save stream.

Thus the game-level -1 sentinel survives only long enough for AdvC's load-finalization logic; it
does not leave the player's human-disable bit persisted across the load. This inherited advc.127
mechanism is internally coherent under current SAS.

CONTROL B — PRACTICAL 6358 SOURCE-HISTORY SAVE-LAYOUT CHANGE IS INTENTIONALLY INCOMPATIBLE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Practical 6358 appends a variable-length `m_aSASVersionHistory` block to the end of the current
`CvGame` serialized payload. `CvGame::read` unconditionally reads that block, while the numeric
`uiFlag` remains 27. Superficially this means a pre-6358 save with the same flag cannot be parsed by
the new layout.

That is real format incompatibility, but it is explicitly documented policy rather than a current
bug. The same practical's root README states:

    As with other AdvCiv-SAS save-layout changes, older save formats are intentionally
    unsupported rather than migrated.

The Main Changes Guide repeats that older save layouts are intentionally unsupported. Therefore
F609 must not be spent on the missing version gate: current same-version streams remain paired, and
backward migration is outside the mod's declared contract.

CONTROL C — START FAST SAVE DOES NOT PRECEDE SOURCE-HISTORY CREATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A second possible interaction between practical 6358 and practical 6374 also closes cleanly.
`CvEventReporter::gameStart()` performs:

    initializeSASVersionHistoryForNewGame();
    ...
    m_kPythonEventMgr.reportGameStart();

BUG registers `SASFastSave.saveGameStart` on that later `GameStart` event. The START Fast Save is
therefore taken only after the creation-source entry exists. This is unlike F608's victory save,
where the callback is intentionally before the later game-state transition.

CONTROL D — AUTOPLAY STOP SAVE OCCURS AFTER NORMAL HUMAN RE-ENABLE
------------------------------------------------------------------
`AIAutoPlay.checkPlayer` first calls `game.endAIAutoPlay(iEndCause)` and only then invokes
`SASFastSave.saveAutoPlayStop()` for scheduled/user-interrupted completion. In single player,
`CvGame::setAIAutoPlay(0, true, ...)` re-enables the current active player through
`setHumanDisabled(false)` before returning. The ordinary STOP snapshot therefore does not share
F608's pre-transition defect.

--------------------------------------

LATE-TAIL CONTROLS
------------------
1. `CvGame` save/load during AI Auto Play is coherent across `CvPlayer`: player read begins with
   `reset()`, which clears transient `m_bDisableHuman` and reconstructs human status from

   Its README and Main Changes Guide explicitly state that older AdvCiv-SAS save schemas are

   accidental current compatibility promise. Current same-version read/write order is symmetric.
