   `initializeSASVersionHistoryForNewGame`, so they contain the creation provenance entry.

4. Scheduled/user-interrupted STOP Fast Saves occur after `endAIAutoPlay` re-enables normal human
   control, so they do not share F608's pre-transition victory snapshot defect.

   Those functions do not consume RNG. The logger writes files and recorder-owned globals only;
   it does not mutate vote outcomes or game state.

6. Practical 6250 session finalization flushes recorder-owned pending observations before reset.
   Its inspected call chain reads the old game/map state but does not mutate authoritative gameplay
   state.

7. Current 48-civilization-sensitive masks in `CvGame.cpp` use `qword`; valid Player IDs including
   Barbarians fit within bits 0..48. The relevant start/shuffle arrays use the corresponding
   `MAX_CIV_PLAYERS`, `MAX_PLAYERS`, `MAX_CIV_TEAMS` and `MAX_TEAMS` domains consistently.

8. A post-original-review XML history sweep found no new unit/building/victory/world/cardinality
   content that activates a fresh inherited `CvGame` assumption. The late GlobalDefines are
   primarily logging/AI knobs; the one directly relevant new game-global feature is Fast Save,
   already owned by F608.

F609 / KI#932 — AdvC terrain-only revelation skips its requested plot-group refresh
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CLASSIFICATION: inherited AdvC regression, current-live through shipped Advanced Start.

ROOT
----
BtS/K-Mod `CvPlot::setRevealed` updates every alive member player's plot group immediately when the
plot's revealed bit changes and `bUpdatePlotGroup` is requested. Only after that does it branch on
`bTerrainOnly`.

AdvC practical 1253 / commit `f6ff6a182f5187541fff6e5bbbe12f9573b3778c` reworked revealed
trade-network information (advc.124). To ensure owner/improvement/route/city revealed state was
settled before recomputing connectivity, it moved the plot-group update to the bottom of
`CvPlot::setRevealed`, with the explicit comment:

    all revealed status changes need to be applied first

But the inherited early exit remained above the relocated refresh:

    if (bTerrainOnly)
        return;

Consequently `setRevealed(..., bTerrainOnly=true, ..., bUpdatePlotGroup=true)` can change the
permanent revealed bit and then return without performing the plot-group refresh that the caller
explicitly requested.

CURRENT-LIVE ACTIVATION
-----------------------
Current `CvPlayer::doAdvancedStartAction(ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_VISIBILITY, ...)` uses exactly:

    pPlot->setRevealed(getTeam(), true, true, NO_TEAM, true);

for purchased visibility (and the symmetric false call for the internal removal path).

This is not an unavailable configuration:

* current `ADVANCED_START_VISIBILITY_COST = 1`, so visibility purchasing is enabled;
* `CvGameTextMgr::getVisibilityDataForAS` exposes the visibility item in the player-facing Advanced
  Start palette whenever the positive cost is available;
* `CvPlayerAI::AI_advancedStartRevealRadius` and the broader Advanced Start AI also purchase
  `ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_VISIBILITY` directly.

WHY REVELATION CAN CHANGE REAL CONNECTIVITY
-------------------------------------------
AdvC trade-network construction intentionally uses team revelation as topology state:

* `CvPlot::isTradeNetwork` returns false for an unrevealed plot;
* `CvPlot::isTradeNetworkConnected` returns false when either endpoint is unrevealed;
* `CvPlot::updatePlotGroup` consumes those predicates to attach/combine player plot groups.

Current SAS makes this especially easy to reproduce without any hidden route or improvement:
`TECH_SEAFARING` gives `TERRAIN_COAST` terrain trade. A revealed Coast plot can therefore be network
terrain purely through its terrain and the team's technology. Revealing the last fogged Coast tile
in a chain after Seafaring can change the correct network connectivity immediately.

Because terrain-only revelation intentionally does not reveal owner/improvement/route/city state,
there are no later revealed-status mutations that need to precede a refresh in this branch. The
only relevant state change is the revealed bit itself — precisely the state BtS/K-Mod refreshed
before entering the terrain-only branch.

PERSISTENCE / CONSUMER PROOF
----------------------------
`ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_EXIT` refunds leftover points, leaves Advanced Start mode and performs the
normal production/tech/civic prompts; it does not rebuild plot groups globally. There is no general
per-turn wholesale plot-group rebuild that guarantees repair immediately after Advanced Start.
Thus a purchased visibility tile can leave the player's cached plot groups reflecting the
pre-reveal topology even though `isRevealed` and the direct trade-network predicates now say the
connection is legal.

Subsequent unrelated topology/technology/city updates may eventually rebuild or locally touch the
network, but that does not make the state correct at the mutation boundary. The defect is the
omitted requested refresh and can affect connected-resource/trade-network consumers until such an
unrelated update occurs.

HISTORY / ACTIVATION BOUNDARY
-----------------------------
BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod perform the plot-group update before the terrain-only gate. AdvC's advc.124
refactor deliberately moved it later for the full-revelation case, thereby creating the early-
return hole. Current SAS inherits that ordering unchanged while keeping Advanced Start visibility
live and adding an early Coast-trade technology (`TECH_SEAFARING`) that provides a very simple
current fixture.

WHOLE-ALBUM DEDUP
-----------------
The album contains extensive Advanced Start findings (technology refund/irreversible-state,
purchase-result control flow, role assignment, city-created callbacks, etc.) and several plot-group
roots (route topology, city caches, Ice passability), but none owns `CvPlot::setRevealed`'s
`bTerrainOnly` early return skipping the explicitly requested plot-group refresh. This is a distinct
mutation/invalidation root.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Do not simply move the full bottom refresh back above all revealed owner/improvement/route handling;
that would undo advc.124's valid reason for delaying full-revelation recomputation.

A narrow repair is to preserve the delayed bottom refresh for `bTerrainOnly == false`, but before
returning from the terrain-only branch, update team members' plot groups when:

* the caller requested `bUpdatePlotGroup`, and
* the revealed bit actually changed (`bOldValue != bNewValue`).

Using the revealed-bit change specifically is preferable in the terrain-only branch: owner,
improvement, route and city revelation are intentionally not modified there, so mismatches between
those stored values and current actual values must not masquerade as terrain-only revelation
changes.

POST-WIP432 INHERITED-BODY CONTROLS
-----------------------------------
1. `CvPlot::countFriendlyCulture` / war-weariness third-party culture
   This looked surprising because the helper includes culture belonging to every living team that
   the queried team can peacefully enter. A combatant can therefore count culture belonging to a
   vassal/Open-Borders third party as "friendly" in `CvTeam::changeWarWeariness`.

   This is inherited intended semantics rather than a fresh Queue-009 defect. BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod
   already implement the same set directly as own-team OR vassal OR Open Borders culture. AdvC's
   `canPeacefullyEnter` formulation is the optimized equivalent. AdvC's advc.099 addition only
   preserves defeated culture from players that belonged to the queried team itself. Do not spend
   F610 on this inherited policy.

2. KI#346 Ice-melt -> lake/fresh-water second-order hypothesis
   `recalculateWaterAreas()` calls `calculateAreas_dfs()` and `calculateReprAreas()`, and the latter
   ends in `updateLakes()`. More importantly, `CvArea::updateLake(true)` classifies a water area by
   summing every passability-split area sharing its representative BtS-style water body. Melting
   Ice changes passable-area divisions but does not change water-vs-land topology or the summed
   representative water-body size. Therefore the KI#346 Ice repair does not by itself flip lake
   status and does not create a new city-fresh-water invalidation root. This corroborates the prior
   CvCity deep-loop control.

3. `isConnectSea`
   The helper's circular scan does not explicitly compare the last valid neighbor with the first,
   but its threshold is `iChanges > 2`; one connected sea arc cannot exceed two transitions, while
   two separated arcs necessarily create enough transitions in the linearized scan. More
   importantly, all current C++ callers are commented out. Keep as dormant helper/design code, not
   F610.

F610 / KI#933 — Global Warming can remove Oasis fresh water without refreshing derived state
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CLASSIFICATION: current-live inherited BtS mutation/invalidation defect.

ROOT
----
`CvPlot::isFreshWater()` explicitly depends on adjacent features whose XML has
`bAddsFreshWater=1`. The source immediately above it even carries the inherited warning:

    if this changes need to call updateIrrigated and CvCity::updateFreshWaterHealth

But `CvPlot::setFeatureType()` changes the feature and refreshes sight, direct plot yield,
graphics and nearby feature/improvement health/happiness only. It does NOT call either
`updateIrrigated()` or `CvCity::updateFreshWaterHealth()` when the old/new feature changes the
AddsFreshWater predicate.

CURRENT-LIVE SAS ACTIVATION
---------------------------
Current shipped `CIV4FeatureInfos.xml` has exactly the relevant ordinary feature fixture:

    FEATURE_OASIS
    iAppearance       = 500
    bAddsFreshWater   = 1
    bNoImprovement    = 1
    terrain           = TERRAIN_DESERT

Current Global Warming remains enabled (`GLOBAL_WARMING_PROB = 20`, out of 1000) and its target
selector can choose any ordinary non-city land plot, including a Desert/Oasis plot. Desert gets a
low target score, but remains eligible and can be returned when the sampled pool contains no
higher-scoring candidate.

The current player-facing Global Warming concept text independently makes the intended live path
explicit: if the selected plot has a feature including "Forest, Jungle, Floodplain, Oasis", that
feature is removed.

`CvGame::doGlobalWarming()` implements exactly that. For an Oasis, the "remove other features"
branch calls:

    pPlot->setFeatureType(NO_FEATURE);

There is no later global fresh-water-health or irrigation rebuild in `doGlobalWarming()`.

AUTHORITATIVE CITY-HEALTH CONSEQUENCE
-------------------------------------
A city adjacent to the Oasis satisfies `getPlot().isFreshWater()` because the adjacent feature
adds fresh water. `CvCity::updateFreshWaterHealth()` stores that result in:

    m_iFreshWaterGoodHealth / m_iFreshWaterBadHealth

rather than querying `isFreshWater()` dynamically whenever city health is consumed. Under the
normal inherited BtS define, fresh water contributes +2 health.

The complete current caller set for `updateFreshWaterHealth()` is essentially city initialization
plus the explicit KI#351 runtime-river repair helper. It is not a per-turn recomputation. Thus when
Global Warming removes the only adjacent Oasis, `isFreshWater()` immediately becomes false while
the city's stored fresh-water health can remain at +2 indefinitely until some unrelated operation
happens to refresh it.

IRRIGATION / YIELD CONSEQUENCE
------------------------------
The same Oasis can be the fresh-water source for adjacent Farm irrigation. `isIrrigationAvailable`
checks `isFreshWater()` and the stored irrigation network; improvement yield then grants the
Farm's `IrrigatedYieldChange` when irrigation is available.

`setFeatureType()` does not touch that irrigation network or neighboring Farm yields. Therefore
removing the Oasis can leave adjacent Farm plots and downstream irrigation chains carrying the
pre-removal `m_bIrrigated` state and cached irrigated yield after their actual fresh-water source
has disappeared.

A repair must be more careful than merely calling the current incremental `updateIrrigated()` on
an already-irrigated Farm: that routine's teardown path is entered when an irrigated plot ceases to
be *potential irrigation*, whereas loss of an external fresh-water source can leave every Farm in
the component still potential. A source-loss-aware component invalidation/rebuild (or equivalent
fresh-water-derived-state helper) is needed.

ANCESTRY
--------
This root predates SAS and AdvC:

* BtS/Civ4CE `CvPlot::setFeatureType` refreshes feature health/happiness but not fresh-water health
  or irrigation;
* BtS Global Warming can remove any non-Fallout feature on a selected land plot, including Oasis;
* K-Mod's Global Warming rewrite retains an explicit "remove other features" branch and still does
  not add the missing fresh-water-derived updates;
* Base AdvC inherits both the feature mutation omission and the K-Mod/AdvC warming path;
* current SAS keeps the same executor contract and explicitly documents Oasis removal.

WHOLE-ALBUM DEDUP / CORRECTION
------------------------------
This is distinct from:

* KI#346/F025 — impassable-feature changes leaving PASSABLE_AREAS/path/plot-group topology stale;
* KI#351/F030 — runtime N/W river-edge mutation missing fresh-water/irrigation/plot-group refreshes.

Fixing either existing root does not repair `setFeatureType(NO_FEATURE)` when an AddsFreshWater
feature disappears.

The original Queue-009 closure contained a negative control saying that `setFeatureType`'s
fresh-water facet was incomplete only in general because current data had no supported post-start
AddsFreshWater creation/removal path. That control is now CORRECTED: current Global Warming is
exactly such a shipped path, and current documentation explicitly names Oasis as removable.

The later generic statement that `setFeatureType` was "bounded by already-owned
feature-passability/fresh-water families" must likewise be read with this correction: feature
passability remains owned by KI#346, but AddsFreshWater feature removal is the distinct F610 root.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
When `setFeatureType` changes whether the plot's feature adds fresh water after final
initialization:

1. refresh `updateFreshWaterHealth()` for cities whose city plot can gain/lose fresh water from
   this feature (adjacent city plots are the direct authoritative set);
2. invalidate/rebuild irrigation connectivity for the local potential-irrigation component in a
   way that handles source loss, then refresh affected yields/layout;
3. keep this separate from KI#346 passability topology and from the ordinary
   `updateSurroundingHealthHappiness()` feature-health/happiness calculation.

Map-generation mutations should avoid unnecessary repeated live-game rebuild cost; the existing
`isFinalInitialized()` boundary used by irrigation handling is an appropriate lifecycle guard to
respect.

F611 / KI#351 REOPENED — current river repair adds irrigation but cannot remove it when fresh water disappears
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CLASSIFICATION: current supported-API AdvCiv-SAS follow-up defect in the KI#351 repair, on top of
an inherited BtS irrigation-updater limitation. This is deliberately linked to/reopens KI#351
rather than consuming provisional KI#934 because the user-visible root is the same runtime river-
edge derived-state contract.

WHY THE CURRENT KI#351 REPAIR IS ONLY HALF-CORRECT
--------------------------------------------------
Practical 6234 / commit `d29d65355088fba9563f2a0b68ebe2cd145a75ec` added the shared
`updateRiverDerivedState` helper. After a finalized-game N/W river-edge presence change, it calls:

    kPlot.updateIrrigated();
    every adjacent plot -> updateIrrigated();
    nearby cities -> updateFreshWaterHealth();
    GC.getGame().updatePlotGroups();

The corresponding KI#351 documentation says this local irrigation refresh lets the inherited
pathfinder propagate both additions and removals. The addition half is correct; the removal half
is not.

`CvMap::updateIrrigated(CvPlot& kPlot)` has only two state-changing branches:

1. ADDITION

       !kPlot.isIrrigated()
       && kPlot.isPotentialIrrigation()
       && kPlot.isIrrigationAvailable(true)

   -> flood the connected potential-irrigation component with `setIrrigated(true)`.

2. REMOVAL

       kPlot.isIrrigated()
       && !kPlot.isPotentialIrrigation()

   -> clear the triggering plot, inspect adjacent potential-irrigation components for any remaining
      fresh-water source, and clear a source-less component with `setIrrigated(false)`.

Losing a river fresh-water source does NOT make an existing Farm cease to be potential irrigation.
Once the team has the irrigation-spreading technology, an owned improved Farm carrying irrigation
remains `isPotentialIrrigation()==true` whether or not it is still beside a river. A city plot has
the same structural property while owned/flat.

Therefore an already-irrigated Farm affected by river REMOVAL enters neither state-changing branch:

    isIrrigated()            == true
    isPotentialIrrigation()  == true

The local calls added by KI#351 return without searching for a surviving fresh-water source and
without clearing `m_bIrrigated`.

ASYMMETRIC SOURCE-LEVEL REPRODUCTION
------------------------------------
The asymmetry makes the proof especially clean.

RIVER ADDITION:
* Start with a non-irrigated potential Farm/component.
* Add the river edge.
* The affected Farm now has fresh water, so `isIrrigationAvailable(true)` is true.
* KI#351 calls `updateIrrigated()`; its addition branch floods the connected component true.
* The repair works.

RIVER REMOVAL:
* Start after irrigation propagation has been enabled and a river-fed Farm/component is already
  `m_bIrrigated=true`.
* Remove its last fresh-water river source through the supported runtime river-edge setter.
* The Farm remains a valid irrigation carrier (`isPotentialIrrigation()==true`).
* KI#351 calls `updateIrrigated()` on the changed plot and every adjacent plot, but every already-
  irrigated potential Farm takes no teardown branch.
* `m_bIrrigated` remains true even though the component has no fresh-water source.

CURRENT SAS GAMEPLAY DATA MAKES THE STALE BIT MATTER
----------------------------------------------------
Current `IMPROVEMENT_FARM` has:

    IrrigatedYieldChange = +1 food
    bCarriesIrrigation   = 1

Current `TECH_WATER_WHEEL` grants both `bIrrigation=1` and `bIgnoreIrrigation=1`.
`bIgnoreIrrigation` only permits irrigation-requiring improvements to be built without an available
irrigation source; it does NOT grant the irrigated yield. `calculateImprovementYieldChange` still
uses `isIrrigationAvailable()` for the +1 food.

That makes the stale state authoritative. `isIrrigationAvailable()` first returns true when the
plot's stored `isIrrigated()` flag is true. Therefore after the last river source is removed, the
stale self flag can preserve the Farm's +1 irrigated food and can keep downstream irrigation chains
alive indefinitely.

The tech-acquisition path also removes any uncertainty about whether a river-fed Farm ever gets the
stored flag: `CvTeam::changeIrrigationCount` calls the map-wide irrigation updater, and a fresh-water
Farm that is potential irrigation enters the addition branch and propagates `m_bIrrigated=true`.

ANCESTRY / WHY THIS WAS EASY TO MISS
------------------------------------
The narrow per-plot updater is inherited in behavior from BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod. BtS/K-Mod keep the
same teardown condition: an irrigated plot must cease to be potential irrigation before the source-
search/removal path runs. Base AdvC moved the pathfinding implementation into `CvMap` but retained
the same semantics.

That inherited algorithm is well suited to its historical common trigger — removing/changing an
irrigation-carrying improvement or otherwise making a carrier cease to be potential irrigation.
It is not a general "fresh-water source changed" recomputation API.

Original BtS river setters did not call it at all. SAS practical 6234 correctly identified runtime
river edits as a missing invalidation source, but reused this narrower updater under the assumption
that it could also propagate source removal.

WHOLE-ALBUM DEDUP / RELATION TO F610
------------------------------------
Do not assign provisional KI#934 to this.

* KI#351/F030 already owns the runtime river-edge derived-state contract. Its city fresh-water-
  health and plot-group repair portions remain valid; only irrigation teardown is incomplete.
  Reopen/broaden KI#351 for the removal half rather than pretending the original root is fully fixed.
* F610/KI#933 is still independently valid: `setFeatureType(NO_FEATURE)` for an Oasis calls no
  fresh-water-health or irrigation invalidation at all. The city-health omission alone is a hard
  F610 consequence.
* F610's irrigation consequence exposes the same deeper source-loss limitation: merely wiring the
  existing per-plot `updateIrrigated()` into `setFeatureType` would not clear an already-irrigated
  source-less Farm component. A correct source-loss helper can therefore be shared by the KI#351
  reopen and F610 without merging their distinct mutator roots.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Preserve the existing efficient incremental updater for ordinary carrier additions/removals, but add
an explicit fresh-water-source-change operation. For the locally affected potential-irrigation
component(s), it must be able to:

1. traverse the component after the source mutation;
2. test whether any current member still satisfies `isFreshWater()`;
3. if no source remains, clear `m_bIrrigated` across the component through `setIrrigated(false)` so
   adjacent yields/layout are refreshed;
4. if a new source appeared, retain/reuse the existing addition flood.

The source-change operation can be called from the finalized-game river setters and from the F610
AddsFreshWater feature-change repair. It should not force a full-map reset for ordinary map
construction; the rare runtime-mutation lifecycle guard used by KI#351 is appropriate.

DOCUMENTATION CORRECTION
------------------------
Current KI#351 documentation says the local calls allow the inherited pathfinder to propagate
"additions or removals." Correct that statement when fixing this follow-up: additions work; source
removals require the new source-aware component validation described above.

FINAL SIGNED-DEFENSE ACTIVATION CONTROL — SAS JUNGLE -25 IS SUPPORTED
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS practical 5242 deliberately changes `FEATURE_JUNGLE` defense from 0 to -25, with an
inline design rationale that Jungle should be less defensible/open to attack. This is therefore an
intentional signed-domain activation, not accidental XML drift.

The remaining executor audit did not find an inherited nonnegative-only contract:

* `CvPlot::defenseModifier` adds terrain/feature/improvement/city values as signed integers.
* `CvTeamAI::AI_plotDefense` forwards that signed value unchanged.
* pathfinding treats a negative destination defense as worse defensive terrain rather than wrapping
  or reversing the preference;
* attack opportunism becomes more eager against a defender on negative-defense terrain, which is
  consistent with the feature's stated design;
* guard/healing/airbase and plot-defender heuristics value such terrain less;
* the core combat-strength modifier machinery already accepts signed combat modifiers;
* current shipped terrain/improvement data do not stack an additional negative plot-defense value
  on top of Jungle, so the current minimum native plot contribution remains modest (-25).

One UI line-budget precheck reserves a help line only for `defenseModifier(...) > 0` although the
later help body prints any nonzero defense value. Negative Jungle defense can therefore make that
heuristic under-reserve one line, but this is a tooltip/layout-budget imperfection rather than a
hard gameplay-state contradiction and does not consume F612.

FRESH-WATER DEPENDENCY FAMILY — EXHAUSTED AFTER F610 / F611
------------------------------------------------------------
`CvPlot::isFreshWater()` depends on four relevant state classes:

1. whether the plot is water/impassable;
2. direct river presence;
3. adjacent water-body lake status;
4. adjacent feature `bAddsFreshWater`.

For current shipped runtime mutations:

* river-edge changes are the KI#351/F611 family;
* `FEATURE_OASIS` is the sole current AddsFreshWater feature and Global Warming removal is F610;
* current Global-Warming terrain substitutions remain ordinary passable land and do not create a
  new water/impassability fresh-water transition;
* the KI#346 Ice-area rebuild does not change representative water-body tile count and therefore
  does not turn a lake into sea merely by opening an Ice-blocked passability channel.

No separate fresh-water invalidation root remains outside F610 and the KI#351 reopen.

UNIT-VALIDITY / SAS ALL-TERRAIN MUTATION CONTROL — CLEAN
---------------------------------------------------------
A final plot-mutation check tested whether SAS's all-terrain LAND units could be incorrectly bumped

    kUnit.isValidDomain(*this)

and `CvUnit::isValidDomain(bool bWater)` explicitly returns valid for LAND on water when

CURRENT-FORMAT CvPlot SAVE/LOAD SYMMETRY — CLEAN
-------------------------------------------------
A mechanical same-version stream comparison was performed rather than relying on visual inspection.
Current `CvPlot::read` and `CvPlot::write` each contain 61 corresponding serialization operations,
in the same semantic order.

The only syntactic representation differences are expected:

* write `areaID()` -> read temporary union member `m_iArea`, later resolved to `m_pArea`;
* write `(int)m_iRiverID` -> read int with explicit short-range validation before assigning the
  compact `short` member;
* boolean members are read through the shared temporary `bVal` and assigned in the same order.

Persisted enum maps, culture/found values, plot-group IDs, visibility/stolen visibility/blockade
counts, revealed owner/improvement/route state, build progress, culture-range counts, invisible-
visibility counts, script data, ruins name and the unit ID list are paired.

Header members absent from the stream are runtime/derived/graphical caches or pointers: border-
danger/safe-range caches, adjacency pointer/count construction state, graphical symbols/entities,
center unit/plot builder, layout-dirty/display flags and static fog/visibility caches. No omitted
current authoritative gameplay state or stream-order mismatch was established.

CURRENT-vs-BASE SEMANTIC SURFACE — SMALL AND ACCOUNTED FOR
-----------------------------------------------------------
A direct current-SAS vs Base AdvC 1.14 comparison shows that the executable semantic delta in this
2,599-line file is unusually small:

1. SAS adds `CvUnitInfo::m_eObsoleteTech`, initializes it to `NO_TECH`, loads the XML
   `<ObsoleteTech>` tag, exposes `getObsoleteTech()`, and includes it in the optional binary XML-info
   cache read/write code.
2. The four UnitInfo terrain/feature attack/defense modifier getters gain SAS define gates that
   return 0 when the corresponding optional mechanic is disabled.
3. `CvUnitInfo::isPromotionValid()` contains the already-fixed KI#324.2 integration repair: the
   inherited `getCollateralDamage()==0` veto was removed while the zero limit/max safety gates were
   retained, allowing SAS's deliberately broadened collateral promotions to work on units whose
   base collateral strength is zero.
4. The remaining Info subclasses in this file are executable-semantically inherited from Base AdvC.

BINARY XML-INFO CACHE CONTROL — DORMANT
----------------------------------------
The new ObsoleteTech member was inserted into `CvUnitInfo::read/write` without bumping that optional
cache format's local `uiFlag`. That initially looks like a cache compatibility hazard, but current
SAS ships:

    #define ENABLE_XML_FILE_CACHE 0

in `CvInfo_Base.h`. These binary Info-cache methods are compiled out. Current UnitInfos are parsed
from XML, so this does not provide a current-live F612.

OBSOLETE-TECH CROSS-FIELD AUDIT — INTENTIONAL HARD TECH CUTOFF
---------------------------------------------------------------
Current UnitInfos contain 82 non-NONE ObsoleteTech assignments. A tech-graph audit found 18 units
whose ObsoleteTech does not descend from every one of that unit's own prerequisite techs (e.g.
Bronze/Iron-Working unit branches cut off at Civil Service/Feudalism/Firearms).

That is not a contradiction with the documented feature. KI#93/Main Changes documentation defines
ObsoleteTech as a hard production cutoff once the listed technology has been discovered, intended
to remove strategically obsolete unit clutter; it is not defined as "replacement is currently
trainable." Additional controls are clean:

* no current unit has ObsoleteTech equal to its own required tech;
* no current ObsoleteTech is in an earlier/equal current tech-era/cost position than the unit's own
  required-tech set in the tested ordering;
* gameplay/AI/help consumers use `getObsoleteTech()` rather than bypassing the optional mechanic by
  reading the raw member;
* therefore the global SAS toggle coherently returns `NO_TECH` to those consumers when disabled.

The non-ancestral cases are intentional skipped-branch behavior, not F612.

FREE-PROMOTION BYPASS — DEDUP / POSITIVE CONTROL
-------------------------------------------------
`CvUnitInfo::isPromotionValid()` deliberately returns true immediately for a unit's XML free
promotion. A current-data census found 13 free UnitInfo/promotion pairs that would fail normal
player-selectable promotion eligibility (UnitCombat/effect restrictions). Most are deliberate
special-unit or UU injections whose effects remain executable.

The only mechanically inert pair family uncovered by this bypass is Airship/Robotic Recon Drone +
`PROMOTION_MOBILITY_COST`; that is already the exact root of F605/KI#928 (flat movement returns
before move-discount consumption). Do not duplicate it as F612.

PROMOTION DEPENDENCY GRAPH — CLEAN
----------------------------------
Current `CIV4PromotionInfos.xml` contains 57 promotions and 66 prerequisite edges across mandatory
and OR prerequisite fields. Mechanical graph validation found:

* zero prerequisite cycles;
* zero dangling prerequisite IDs.

Thus the recursive prerequisite calls in `CvUnitInfo::isPromotionValid()` cannot enter a current
XML recursion cycle.

UNIT MESH / BATTLE-ART CARDINALITY — CLEAN
------------------------------------------
All 131 current UnitInfos have nonempty UnitMeshGroups with positive required counts. A few values
look suspicious in isolation (`iRequired` greater than `iGroupSize`, or melee/ranged wave size

Only one shared unit's mesh tuple differs at all between Base and SAS: the Celtic Gallic Warrior's
art-definition tag name. Counts are unchanged.

  missing current Unit Art definitions.

F612 / KI#934 — CITY BOMBARD DAMAGE IS WIRED TO THE WRONG BOMBARD MECHANIC FOR AIR BOMBERS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS deliberately makes `PROMOTION_CITY_BOMBARD_DAMAGE` selectable by both
`UNITCOMBAT_SIEGE` and `UNITCOMBAT_AIR_BOMBER` and gives it:

    iBombardRateChange = 10

This field has one runtime storage path on a promoted unit:

    CvUnit::setHasPromotion(...)
        -> changeExtraBombardRate(kPromo.getBombardRateChange() * iChange)

and `CvUnit::bombardRate()` consumes it only for the ordinary adjacent Civ4 BOMBARD mechanic:

    return m_pUnitInfo->getBombardRate() + getExtraBombardRate();

Aircraft city bombing is a distinct executor. `CvUnit::airBombBaseRate()` returns only the UnitInfo
`iBombRate`, and `airBombCurrRate()` merely scales that base by current hit points. Neither function
reads `getExtraBombardRate()` or the promotion's `iBombardRateChange`.

Current shipped fixtures make the mismatch direct:

    Bomber:         DOMAIN_AIR, UNITCOMBAT_AIR_BOMBER, iBombRate=16, iBombardRate=0
    Stealth Bomber: DOMAIN_AIR, UNITCOMBAT_AIR_BOMBER, iBombRate=20, iBombardRate=0

Therefore City Bombard Damage leaves their normal AIRBOMB city-defense damage at 16/20 (before the
separate health/defense scaling already audited under F606). The +10 promotion does not increase the
mission that its SAS name and eligibility say it should improve.

WRONG-MISSION ACTIVATION — NOT MERELY AN INERT BONUS
------------------------------------------------------
The same mismatch also activates the opposite mechanic. `CvUnit::canBombard(CvPlot const&)` has no
AIR-domain exclusion; it requires positive `bombardRate()`, attack availability, non-cargo status
and an adjacent bombardable city. `CvSelectionGroup::canDoMission(MISSION_BOMBARD)` delegates to
that method and likewise has no AIR-domain exclusion.

An unpromoted current Bomber has ordinary `bombardRate()==0` and cannot use adjacent BOMBARD. Once
City Bombard Damage is acquired:

    base iBombardRate = 0
    promotion change  = +10
    bombardRate()     = 10

so a DOMAIN_AIR Bomber can become eligible for the ordinary adjacent siege/naval city-bombard
mission while its normal ranged AIRBOMB damage remains unchanged.

HISTORY / INTENT — SAS DOMAIN EXPANSION WITHOUT EXECUTOR ADAPTATION
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Base AdvC's upstream Accuracy promotion used `iBombardRateChange` for Siege, where that field is the
correct ordinary-BOMBARD executor contract.

SAS practical 4569 (`f774063b13ef8b6addc8d7f195b08643d7c646d2`) deliberately:

* renamed Accuracy to "City Bombard Damage";
* raised/kept the promotion as a city-bombard effect;
* added an XML comment `give city bombard damage to more unit types`;
* added the then-generic air combat class while explicitly noting the intent to later distinguish
  bombers from fighters.

SAS practical 4616 (`9b2a569e43...`) then introduced `UNITCOMBAT_AIR_BOMBER` and moved this
promotion's air eligibility specifically onto that new bomber class. The content intent is therefore
not inferred from a stray XML value: SAS deliberately extended an ordinary BombardRate promotion to
a unit domain whose city-bombing executor uses the separate BombRate field.

LIVE ACQUISITION / UI / AI PROOF
--------------------------------
The promotion has no tech prerequisite and no promotion prerequisite. A sufficiently experienced
current AIR_BOMBER can therefore select it normally.

`CvGameTextMgr` displays nonzero `getBombardRateChange()` through the ordinary bombard promotion
help text, so the player is shown the +10 bombard benefit.

`CvUnitAI::AI_promotionValue` also assigns positive value to `getBombardRateChange()` (especially for
`UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY`) without checking that AIR_BOMBER's actual AIRBOMB executor ignores the field.
Thus eligibility, UI and AI valuation all expose the stale field-domain contract.

DEDUP BOUNDARY
--------------
This is independent of the prior aircraft roots:

* F606/KI#929: stale IgnoreBuildingDefense compensation inside `airBombDefenseDamage()` after SAS
  removed that aircraft immunity;
* F612/KI#934: City Bombard Damage modifies ordinary BombardRate while current aircraft city bombing
  consumes BombRate.

Fixing F606 does not make the promotion improve AIRBOMB. Fixing F612 does not remove F606's defense
scaling error. The album contained no earlier `PROMOTION_CITY_BOMBARD_DAMAGE` / BombardRate-vs-
BombRate root.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Do not blindly add `getExtraBombardRate()` to `airBombCurrRate()`: that accessor also participates in
non-city aircraft bombing, so doing so could broaden the explicitly city-focused promotion into an
improvement/route-bombing bonus.

A conservative repair should instead preserve the ordinary BombardRate effect for Siege while:

1. deliberately applying the City Bombard Damage promotion to AIR-unit *city-defense* AIRBOMB
   damage (or introducing a dedicated air-city-bombard modifier); and
2. preventing DOMAIN_AIR units from acquiring the ordinary adjacent `MISSION_BOMBARD` merely
   because promotion-derived `bombardRate()` becomes positive.

paths. Interception acquisition obeys the current 100% cap; collateral protection is bounded at

F613 / KI#935 — TRUE STARTS USES CIV/LEADER-PAIR COUNT TWICE, SO 35-48 RANDOM PLAYERS CAN EXHAUST DISTINCT CIVS WHILE UNIQUENESS STAYS FORCED
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`TrueStarts::changeCivs()` correctly builds two different AI candidate cardinalities:

    aeValidAICivs   = distinct valid True-Starts civilization IDs
    m_validAICivs   = valid (civilization, leader) pairs

The pair list is the correct object for the first hard guard: there must be enough actual selectable
civ/leader combinations to assign every True-Starts player. Immediately afterward, however, the
code decides whether duplicate civilizations must be permitted:

    if (m_validAICivs.size() < m_truPlayers.size() ||
        aeValidHumanCivs.size() < m_truHumans.size())
    {
        bUniqueCivs = false;
    }

The AI term repeats the **pair-list** test from the hard guard instead of testing the already-built
`aeValidAICivs` distinct-civilization list. Because the previous hard guard has already returned if
`m_validAICivs.size() < m_truPlayers.size()`, that first term is unreachable as true here. AI-player
shortage can therefore never disable `bUniqueCivs`.

CURRENT SAS CARDINALITIES MAKE THE DEFECT LIVE
-----------------------------------------------
Current data was mechanically enumerated:

    valid AI-playable True-Starts civilizations: 34
    valid True-Starts AI civilization/leader pairs: 52
    current playable/AI-playable major civilizations: 36
    MAX_CIV_PLAYERS: 48
    WORLDSIZE_SAS40 default players: 40
    WORLDSIZE_SAS48 default players: 48

Thus a 48-random-player True Starts game passes the hard leader-pair guard because 52 >= 48. The
broken uniqueness check then also sees 52 >= 48 and keeps `bUniqueCivs=true`, despite having only 34
distinct candidate civilizations.

The assignment loop explicitly skips a candidate when:

    bUniqueCivs && m_civTaken.get(candidateCiv)

After 34 successful assignments every distinct True-Starts civilization is taken. Players 35-48
can still have many unused leaders, but every pair belongs to an already-taken civ; no candidate can
become `eeBestFit`. The later finalization consequently reaches the existing `No civ found for
player` error path for those unassigned True-Starts players instead of the intended duplicate-civ
fallback.

This is not merely a theoretical 48-slot compile configuration. SAS ships its explicit 40- and
48-player world sizes and a 48-major-player DLL, so the supported normal setup can exceed the
34-distinct-civ boundary directly.

BASE ADVC ACTIVATION BOUNDARY / HISTORY
---------------------------------------
The duplicated test is inherited unchanged from AdvC's original True Starts merge, practical 3579
(`4977b513daa6bc436f6d0ea9e8ee011b131b8d36`). The same hunk introduced both candidate vectors and
the two checks.

Base AdvC 1.14 has:

    MAX_CIV_PLAYERS = 18

while its True Starts data already provides 34 distinct major civilizations. The typo was therefore
normally dormant upstream: an ordinary Base AdvC game cannot have enough major players to exhaust
the distinct True-Starts civ pool.

SAS raises `MAX_CIV_PLAYERS` to 48 and adds 24/32/40/48-player scales while retaining the inherited
check. F613 is therefore best classified as an inherited AdvC cardinality defect activated by SAS's
expanded supported player domain.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The local variable/data model already expresses the intended distinction. The conservative repair is:

    if (aeValidAICivs.size() < m_truPlayers.size() ||
        aeValidHumanCivs.size() < m_truHumans.size())
    {
        bUniqueCivs = false;
    }

That changes only the duplicate-civilization policy when there are fewer distinct valid civs than
players, while preserving the earlier hard guard that requires enough civ/leader combinations.

DEDUP
-----
Whole-album/Known-Issues searches found no prior root owning this `bUniqueCivs` / distinct-civ-vs-
leader-pair cardinality defect. Prior True Starts findings concern tech-removal caches, latitude
contracts, changeLeader/UWAI cache invalidation, start normalization and other lifecycle/state
interactions; none repairs this assignment-pool exhaustion.

SECOND CURRENT DATA LEAD — NOT YET F614
---------------------------------------
The same current-data census found a separate SAS integration gap:

    current major playable civs = 36
    current TruCiv records       = 34

The missing major civilizations are exactly:

    CIVILIZATION_IRELAND
    CIVILIZATION_KINGDOM_OF_BENIN

Both are `bPlayable=1` and `bAIPlayable=1`. Their current leaders (Grace O'Malley, Michael Collins,
Ewuare) likewise have no TruLeader records.

This matters more than missing geographic flavor: `changeCivs()` builds the random True-Starts civ
pool solely by iterating `TruCiv`, so Ireland and Benin can never be selected for a player whose civ
is Random under True Starts. The option help states that players set to a Random civilization
receive a civilization matching their starting location; it does not state that mod-added playable
civilizations are excluded.

This is a strong possible F614 / KI#936 SAS content-integration root, but it is deliberately not
promoted in this checkpoint. Finish the civ-introduction / True-Starts-data history and determine
whether the omission was an explicit unsupported-content choice or simply missed integration.

F614 / KI#936 — SAS'S IRELAND AND KINGDOM OF BENIN ARE ABSENT FROM TRUE-STARTS CIV DATA, SO RANDOM + TRUE STARTS CAN NEVER SELECT THEM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS contains 36 major civilizations that are both playable and AI-playable, but
`Assets/XML/TrueStarts/CIV4TruCivInfos.xml` still contains only 34 major-civilization records.
The exhaustive set difference is exactly:

    CIVILIZATION_IRELAND
    CIVILIZATION_KINGDOM_OF_BENIN

Both are ordinary current playable/AI-playable civilizations. Their current leaders are likewise
absent from `CIV4TruLeaderInfos.xml`:

    LEADER_GRACE_OMALLEY
    LEADER_MICHAEL_COLLINS
    LEADER_EWUARE

The missing TruLeader records are useful breadth, but the missing TruCiv records are the decisive
selection defect.

CURRENT-LIVE RANDOM + TRUE STARTS EXECUTOR
------------------------------------------
The `TrueStarts` constructor records a normal player in `m_truPlayers` when
`CvInitCore::wasCivRandomlyChosen(player)` is true (plus the separate documented network/scenario
cases). A manually selected civilization in an ordinary single-player game is therefore left alone;
this root is specifically about players whose civilization is Random while True Starts is active.

`TrueStarts::changeCivs()` does not construct its candidate civilization pool from
`CIV4CivilizationInfos.xml`. It constructs it exclusively by iterating the TruCiv info class:

    FOR_EACH_ENUM_RAND(TruCiv, mapRand())
    {
        CvTruCivInfo const& kTruCiv = GC.getInfo(eLoopTruCiv);
        CivilizationTypes const eCiv = kTruCiv.getCiv();
        ...
        if (kLoopCiv.isPlayable())
            aeValidHumanCivs.push_back(eCiv);
        if (kLoopCiv.isAIPlayable())
            aeValidAICivs.push_back(eCiv);
    }

The later leader-pair lists are then built only by pairing LeaderHead entries with those already
accepted civilization IDs. A playable civilization with no `CvTruCivInfo` therefore has no route
into `m_validHumanCivs` or `m_validAICivs` at all.

Consequently, although ordinary Random civilization selection can use Ireland and Kingdom of Benin,
a Random player processed by True Starts can never finish as either civilization. The option help
states that players set to a Random civilization receive a civilization matching their starting
location; it does not document a smaller 34-civ subset or exclusion of SAS-added major civs.

CUSTOM-CIV INTEGRATION IS AN EXPLICIT TRUE-STARTS DATA CONTRACT
---------------------------------------------------------------
The original AdvC True Starts schema comments deliberately make mod integration lightweight. For a
new civilization, latitude and longitude are mandatory; the remaining TruCiv preference fields are
optional. The original schema explains why:

    All other elements are optional (minOccurs 0). So that mods with
    additional civs need to define only the geo coordinates,
    which are easy to look up ...

That establishes that missing custom civilizations are not an inherent limitation of the True
Starts implementation. The data format was explicitly designed so mods adding civilizations could
supply only a minimal TruCiv entry rather than reproduce all of AdvC's climate/geography research.

SAS HISTORY / OMISSION BOUNDARY
-------------------------------
Kingdom of Benin was introduced in SAS practical 4448
(`d2eae21e1ef676a01c36e1f79817e0b38b5362b3`, 2025-04-01). That large civilization/leader/content
commit does not touch any TrueStarts XML file. Later Benin work replaces/refines its leader and
continues to treat the civilization as ordinary playable content, but no later SAS commit adds a
TruCiv record.

Ireland was introduced in practical 5462
(`d191fe898b3ac9b2dd8830ff55a029294b404f3b`, 2026-02-16) with Grace O'Malley and Michael Collins.
That commit likewise does not touch the TrueStarts XML files.

A history-wide scan of SAS TrueStarts-data changes found only maintenance of already-existing
upstream records in the relevant period:

* practical 4743 — Montezuma -> Moctezuma TruLeader rename;
* practical 4749 — CHINESE_LEADER -> MAO_ZEDONG TruLeader rename;
* practical 4878 — Viking -> Scandinavia TruCiv/TruBonus references.

No SAS commit adds Ireland or Kingdom of Benin to `CIV4TruCivInfos.xml`. No current documentation or
commit message located by the audit declares either playable civilization intentionally unsupported
by True Starts.

TRULEADER BREADTH
-----------------
The three SAS leaders also lack TruLeader records. This is not what excludes their civilizations:
`changeCivs()` iterates ordinary LeaderHeadInfos once a civilization is present in the TruCiv pool.
Missing TruLeader data is handled by the contemporaries/leader-scoring code as absent optional
historical information. It does, however, mean that after adding the missing TruCiv records the new
leaders would lack the historical-reign contribution used for contemporaneity/leader fitness.
Adding Ewuare, Grace O'Malley and Michael Collins TruLeader records is therefore the natural complete
content integration, while only the two TruCiv records are required to repair the hard exclusion.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The conservative content repair is to add at least one `TruCivInfo` for each missing major civ:

    CIVILIZATION_KINGDOM_OF_BENIN
    CIVILIZATION_IRELAND

with valid geographic target coordinates. The schema intentionally permits all other TruCiv fields
to be omitted. For full-quality True Starts scoring, also add TruLeader records for Ewuare, Grace
O'Malley and Michael Collins and, where historically justified, bonus encouragement/discouragement
entries. No C++ change is required for the core F614 selection repair.

DEDUP
-----
Whole-album/Known-Issues searches found no existing root owning missing SAS civilization records in
True Starts. F613 is independent: F613 repairs distinct-civilization cardinality when many random
players need assignments; even with that typo fixed, Ireland and Benin remain absent from the
candidate pool. Adding Ireland/Benin does not repair F613's 35-48-player uniqueness bug.

F614 BREADTH UPDATE — A FIXED IRELAND/BENIN CAN ALSO NULL-DEREFERENCE TRUE-STARTS FITNESS
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The post-WIP440 geo-distance audit found a stronger consequence of F614's missing TruCiv records.
In an ordinary single-player True Starts game, a manually selected civilization is not placed in
`m_truPlayers`; `changeCivs()` records it as a fixed assignment in `m_civs` instead. If another
player is Random, True Starts evaluates candidates for that player through `calcFitness()`.

The geographic-distance portion deliberately includes already-fixed civilizations:

    FOR_EACH_NON_DEFAULT_PAIR(m_civs, Player, CivilizationTypes)
    {
        ...
        CvTruCivInfo const& kLoopTruCiv =
                *m_truCivs.get(perPlayerVal.second);
        ...
    }

There is no NULL test. Thus a normal mixed setup such as:

    human = manually selected CIVILIZATION_IRELAND
    AI    = Random
    True Starts = enabled

puts Ireland into `m_civs`; evaluating any random candidate then dereferences the missing Ireland
TruCiv pointer. Kingdom of Benin has the same defect. This is same-root severity breadth of F614,
not a new finding: adding the missing TruCiv records repairs both Random-pool exclusion and this
fixed-civ dereference.

F615 / KI#937 — EMPTY-NEW-WORLD TRUE STARTS USES +30 DEGREES INSTEAD OF -30 DEGREES AS THE AMERICAS LONGITUDE CUTOFF
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
For map scripts whose setup deliberately leaves the New World empty (`Terra`, `Earth2`, and several
supported custom-option combinations), `TrueStarts::changeCivs()` uses a first pass intended to
exclude civilizations from the Americas so that Old-World starting slots are filled by Old-World
civilizations when enough are available.

The inherited condition is:

    int iLongitudeTimes10 = kTruCiv.get(CvTruCivInfo::LongitudeTimes10);
    int iLatitudeTimes10 = kTruCiv.get(CvTruCivInfo::LatitudeTimes10);
    if (iLongitudeTimes10 < 300 || // Americas
        // Future-proof for Australia
        (iLongitudeTimes10 > 1100 && iLatitudeTimes10 < -100))
    {
        continue;
    }

The XML/schema uses ordinary signed geographic longitude in tenths of degrees and explicitly states
that a negative sign means the western hemisphere. Current examples include:

    America      -770   (-77.0 degrees)
    Aztec        -991   (-99.1 degrees)
    Native Am.   -900   (-90.0 degrees)
    England         1   (+0.1 degrees)
    France         24   (+2.4 degrees)
    Germany       130   (+13.0 degrees)
    Rome          125   (+12.5 degrees)
    Spain         -40   (-4.0 degrees)
    Portugal      -92   (-9.2 degrees)

Therefore `< 300` means **west of +30 degrees east**, not “Americas.” It excludes most of Europe and
western Africa along with the Americas. The source comment and data convention make the likely typo
particularly clear: the intended Americas cutoff is west of roughly 30 degrees west, i.e. `< -300`.

CURRENT DATA / ORDINARY GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCE
--------------------------------------------
An exhaustive current TruCiv census gives:

    total current TruCiv records: 34
    surviving first-pass records with the shipped `< 300` test: 14
    excluded records: 20

The 14 surviving civilizations are Arabia, Babylon, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Japan, Khmer,
Korea, Mongol, Persia, Russia, Sumeria and Zulu. The excluded set contains all American civs as
intended, but also Byzantium, Carthage, Celt, England, France, Germany, Greece, Holy Rome, Mali,
Netherlands, Ottoman, Portugal, Rome, Spain and Scandinavia.

For an Empty-New-World map with at most 14 True-Starts players, those 14 surviving entries satisfy
the required candidate count, so `changeCivs()` breaks after pass 0. The wrongly excluded European
and western-African civilizations never reach the valid-civ pool at all. This affects ordinary
supported Terra/True-Starts games, not malformed XML or an exotic external API state.

Even when there are more than 14 players and the fallback second pass runs, the bad boundary still
changes the intended first-pass population and composes with a separate pass-accumulation issue
currently being audited under F616.

HISTORY / ACTIVATION BOUNDARY
-----------------------------
The condition was introduced unchanged in AdvC's original True Starts merge, practical 3579
(`4977b513daa6bc436f6d0ea9e8ee011b131b8d36`, 2022-01-30), alongside the signed-longitude schema and
comments. It remains identical in Base AdvC 1.14 and current SAS.

This is therefore an inherited AdvC True Starts bug, already live upstream on Empty-New-World games,
not a SAS-authored C++ regression. SAS retains and prominently supports the relevant map scripts and
True Starts option, so it remains current-live in AdvC-SAS.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The narrow semantic repair is to correct the Americas cutoff to the signed-western value intended by
the comment/data convention, most plausibly:

    if (iLongitudeTimes10 < -300 ||
        (iLongitudeTimes10 > 1100 && iLatitudeTimes10 < -100))

The exact historical cutoff could be retuned if desired, but it must not classify London, Paris,
Rome, Madrid and the rest of western Europe as American merely because their longitudes are below
+30 degrees east.

DEDUP
-----
Whole-album/Known-Issues search found no prior root for the Empty-New-World longitude sign/cutoff.
It is independent of F613 (large-player distinct-civ cardinality) and F614 (missing SAS TruCiv
records). Adding Ireland/Benin does not repair the bad longitude comparison; correcting the
comparison does not add the missing civ data or repair F613.

F616 / KI#938 — EMPTY-NEW-WORLD FALLBACK PASS APPENDS TO FIRST-PASS CIV VECTORS, SO THE SUPPOSED DISTINCT-CIV POOL CONTAINS DUPLICATES
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`TrueStarts::changeCivs()` performs up to two passes when `m_bEmptyNewWorld` is true. Pass 0 tries to
restrict the candidate pool geographically. If those candidates are insufficient, pass 1 is intended
to broaden the pool to all available True-Starts civilizations:

    std::vector<CivilizationTypes> aeValidHumanCivs;
    std::vector<CivilizationTypes> aeValidAICivs;
    ...
    for (int iPass = 0; iPass < 2; iPass++)
    {
        FOR_EACH_ENUM_RAND(TruCiv, mapRand())
        {
            ...
            if (m_bEmptyNewWorld && iPass == 0)
            {
                ... geographical exclusion ...
            }
            if (kLoopCiv.isPlayable())
                aeValidHumanCivs.push_back(eCiv);
            if (kLoopCiv.isAIPlayable())
                aeValidAICivs.push_back(eCiv);
        }
        if (aeValidHumanCivs.size() >= m_truHumans.size() &&
            aeValidAICivs.size() >= m_truPlayers.size())
        {
            break;
        }
    }

Neither vector is cleared before pass 1, and there is no `already present` test. Every civilization
accepted in pass 0 is therefore appended a second time when pass 1 broadens to all civs.

CURRENT RAW CARDINALITIES
-------------------------
With the current shipped F615 `< +300` cutoff:

    pass-0 distinct TruCivs: 14
    full TruCiv pool:        34
    pass-1 accumulated entries: 14 + 34 = 48

Those civ entries later expand into civ/leader pairs. Current leader associations give:

    correct full-pool civ/leader pairs: 52
    pairs belonging to the 14 pass-0 civs: 21
    pass-1 m_validAICivs entries after duplication: 52 + 21 = 73

This is not merely wasted iteration. Multiple downstream consumers assume that these candidate
vectors represent the candidate population rather than a first-pass sample plus the same sample
again.

CURRENT-LIVE FITNESS DISTORTION BELOW F613'S PLAYER THRESHOLD
-------------------------------------------------------------
`changeCivs()` computes the median target oceanity by iterating every entry in `m_validAICivs`:

    for (size_t i = 0; i < m_validAICivs.size(); i++)
    {
        CvTruCivInfo const& kTruCiv = *m_truCivs.get(m_validAICivs[i].first);
        scaled rSample = per100(kTruCiv.get(CvTruCivInfo::Oceanity));
        if (rSample >= 0)
            arOceanityTargets.push_back(rSample);
    }
    m_rMedianOceanityTarget = stats::median(arOceanityTargets);

That median is then used to normalize the oceanity weight in every candidate's `calcFitness()`.
Mechanical current-data evaluation gives:

    correct 52-pair median oceanity: 30%
    duplicated 73-entry pass-2 median: 25%

Thus the duplicate accumulation changes actual civ fitness values. This does not depend on F613's
35+-distinct-civ exhaustion. Current SAS `WORLDSIZE_HUGE` itself defaults to 16 players; on Terra +
True Starts the current F615 cutoff leaves only 14 pass-0 candidates, so an ordinary 16-random-player
setup reaches pass 1 and receives this duplicate-weighted 25% baseline.

OTHER LIVE BREADTH
------------------
When Unrestricted Leaders is enabled, True Starts chooses a random available leader after selecting
the best-fit civilization by iterating `validCivs` and pushing every not-yet-taken leader. Duplicate
civ/leader entries therefore give leaders attached to first-pass civilizations extra copies in the
random draw, biasing what is intended to be the unrestricted random leader choice.

The duplicate vectors also undermine the cardinality contract behind F613. Suppose F615's longitude
cutoff is repaired first. Current data then leaves about 29 of the existing 34 TruCivs in the
Old-World first pass (the five American civs are excluded). SAS32/SAS40/SAS48 can still require the
fallback pass. Pass 1 would append those 29 again, so `aeValidAICivs.size()` would exceed the number
of **distinct** civilizations even after F613's one-line repair. A corrected F613 check could then
again keep `bUniqueCivs=true` for 40/48 players despite having only 34 distinct candidate civs.

This makes F616 independent at the repair level as well as current-live below F613's failure
threshold.

CURRENT SAS DEFINE DOES NOT ERASE THE ROOT
------------------------------------------
The duplicate civ/leader list also feeds `m_biasFromLeaderCount`. Current SAS deliberately sets
`PER_EXTRA_LEADER_CIV_SELECTION_WEIGHT=0`, which makes that one bias contribution zero. This is a
useful control, not a fix: the median-oceanity and Unrestricted-Leaders consumers above do not depend
on that define, and the distinct-civ cardinality corruption remains.

HISTORY / BASE BOUNDARY
-----------------------
The accumulating two-pass loop was introduced together with the rest of True Starts in AdvC
practical 3579 (`4977b513daa6bc436f6d0ea9e8ee011b131b8d36`) and remains unchanged in Base AdvC 1.14
and current SAS.

Base AdvC's lower supported player ceiling made the high-cardinality consequences less prominent,
although with the inherited F615 cutoff a manually configured 15-18-player Empty-New-World game can
already enter the fallback. SAS makes the path ordinary through its expanded world sizes: Huge now
defaults to 16 players, and SAS24/SAS32/SAS40/SAS48 default to 24/32/40/48 respectively.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Pass 1 is a fallback to the full candidate set, not a weighted union with pass 0. The conservative
repair is therefore to ensure that pass-0 entries are not retained as duplicates when pass 1 begins,
e.g. clear/rebuild `aeValidHumanCivs` and `aeValidAICivs` before the broad pass, or append only civs
not already present. Clearing before pass 1 most directly expresses the existing comment and avoids
letting pass-0 order/weight leak into the fallback population.

F613's distinct-civ check should still be repaired independently; F616 ensures that the vector it
uses is genuinely distinct.

DEDUP
-----
Whole-album/Known-Issues searches found no prior True Starts root owning this two-pass accumulation.
F615 fixes which civs belong to pass 0 but does not clear them before pass 1. F613 fixes the wrong
AI cardinality variable but cannot make a duplicated `aeValidAICivs` vector distinct. F614 supplies
missing SAS civ records but does not change pass accumulation.

F617 / KI#939 — POLAR PRECIPITATION TEST TREATS THE FEATURE ENUM AS A BOOLEAN, SO EVERY SNOW PLOT IS CLASSIFIED AS NORTHERNMOST TAIGA
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`TrueStarts::precipitation()` separates warm forest, temperate woodland, tundra/steppe, and finally
polar-desert precipitation. Immediately before the polar-desert fallback it contains:

    // I interpret this as the northernmost taiga
    if (eTerrain == m_ePolarDesert && m_eCoolForest)
        return 250;

`m_eCoolForest` is a `FeatureTypes` enum loaded from `TEMPERATE_FEATURE`; it is not a predicate about
`kPlot`. The function had already cached the actual feature in `eFeature`, and the neighboring
branches correctly use comparisons such as:

    if (eFeature == m_eCoolForest)

Current SAS defines are:

    FROZEN_TERRAIN    = TERRAIN_SNOW
    TEMPERATE_FEATURE = FEATURE_FOREST

and current Feature XML order makes:

    FEATURE_FOREST = 4

so `m_eCoolForest` converts to true in the `&&` expression. The malformed condition is therefore
semantically:

    if (eTerrain == TERRAIN_SNOW && true)
        return 250;

Every flat/hill Snow plot reaches the hard-coded 250 mm return, regardless of whether it has a
forest, another feature, or no feature at all.

CURRENT DATA MAKES THE INTENDED FEATURE TEST EVEN CLEARER
---------------------------------------------------------
Current `FEATURE_FOREST` is valid only on Grass, Plains and Tundra; it is not valid on Snow. Thus
under shipped SAS data a literal "Snow + Forest" northernmost-taiga fixture cannot naturally occur.
The malformed branch nevertheless captures all Snow and prevents the following polar-desert code
from ever evaluating any of it.

The intended polar-desert fallback is:

    int iExtra = 0;
    FOR_EACH_ADJ_PLOT(kPlot)
    {
        if (pAdj->getTerrainType() == kPlot.getTerrainType() &&
            pAdj->getFeatureType() == kPlot.getFeatureType())
        {
            iExtra -= 30;
        }
    }
    return std::max(1, 200 + iExtra);

For a bare Snow plot, that means the intended precipitation depends on how much same-terrain,
same-feature polar desert surrounds it:

    0 matching adjacent Snow plots -> 200 mm
    1                            -> 170 mm
    2                            -> 140 mm
    4                            ->  80 mm
    6                            ->  20 mm
    7 or 8                       ->   1 mm (clamped)

Current code returns 250 mm in every one of those states. The error is therefore at least +50 mm and
can reach +249 mm for an interior polar-desert Snow tile.

CURRENT-LIVE ACTIVATION
-----------------------
This is not a theoretical terrain state. Current map-generation code in the shared map generator
and many shipped scripts explicitly creates `TERRAIN_SNOW` (including Boreal, Highlands, Earth2,
Tectonics, PerfectMongoose, RandomScriptMap and others). True Starts climate scoring is used during
normal civilization/start matching whenever the True Starts option is enabled.

`calcClimateFitness()` calls `precipitation()` across weighted city-radius subregions, computes
regional and overall precipitation, exaggerates unusually dry/wet values, and then subtracts fitness
according to mismatch with each civilization's XML `iPrecipitation` target. The current TruCiv data
contains targets spanning extremely dry values (including 1, 106, 111, 156, 183, 208, 306 mm) through
very wet values. Replacing genuinely polar-desert values such as 1-200 with a hard 250 therefore
changes both regional precipitation and civilization fitness; it is not presentation-only data.

The same values also feed climate-variation scoring, so flattening all Snow plots to exactly 250 mm
can alter both the mean/dryness fit and the variation fit of polar starting surroundings.

HISTORY / ROOT CAUSE
--------------------
The exact malformed condition was introduced with the original AdvC True Starts merge, practical
3579 (`4977b513daa6bc436f6d0ea9e8ee011b131b8d36`), alongside the comment:

    // I interpret this as the northernmost taiga

The same newly-added function contains the correct form `eFeature == m_eCoolForest` in two nearby
branches. No later semantic True Starts change repaired or justified the polar expression; the only
later source-history hit on `TrueStarts::precipitation()` is formatting-only.

This is therefore an inherited AdvC source typo, not a SAS-authored regression. It remains live in
current SAS because Snow terrain and True Starts climate fitness are both shipped/current features.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The syntactically/directly intended repair is:

    if (eTerrain == m_ePolarDesert && eFeature == m_eCoolForest)
        return 250;

Under current SAS Feature XML that special branch will normally be unreachable because Forest is not
valid on Snow; bare Snow will then correctly reach the polar-desert fallback. If the design instead
intends a special northern-taiga feature/terrain combination that can actually occur, that content
policy can be reconsidered separately. The executor bug is the missing comparison against the plot's
actual feature.

DEDUP / CONTROLS
----------------
Whole-album/Known-Issues search found no prior root for `TrueStarts::precipitation`, polar desert,
taiga, or the `m_eCoolForest` boolean misuse. It is independent of F613-F616, which all concern
candidate civilization construction/cardinality/data integration. Correcting those candidate pools
does not change climate scoring, and correcting precipitation does not repair their assignment
errors.

During the same tranche two attractive but separate concerns were rejected or kept dormant:

* The first all-Random contemporaries normalization can form a fixed-point 0/0, but Win32 `MulDiv`
  produces an error sentinel whose final fixed-point `round()` collapses to the intended 0 contribution;
  no current fitness difference was demonstrated.
* `changeVegetation()` contains a real winner-update typo (`iScore = iBestScore` instead of
  `iBestScore = iScore`) that discards its documented best-adjacent-plot score. SAS ships both True
  Starts sanitation toggles disabled, and this function is only reached through that sanitization
  path, so it is retained as dormant Base-AdvC source debt rather than F617.

F618 / KI#940 — TRUE STARTS KEEPS CIV/LEADER AVAILABILITY COUPLED UNDER UNRESTRICTED LEADERS, SO FIXED LEADERS ERASE VALID CIVS AND FIXED CIVS ERASE VALID LEADERS
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`TrueStarts::TrueStarts()` explicitly disables leader-specific True Starts data when Unrestricted
Leaders is enabled:

    // Ignore the truLeader info when leaders are unrestricted
    if (!GC.getGame().isOption(GAMEOPTION_LEAD_ANY_CIV))
    {
        FOR_EACH_ENUM(TruLeader)
        {
            m_truLeaders.set(...);
        }
    }

and `changeCivs()` later states the intended contract equally clearly:

    /*  When leaders are unrestricted, then the best-fit has been
        selected only based on a civ. Stick to that civ, and
        combine it with a random leader. */

The candidate construction, however, still represents every candidate as a **native
(civilization, leader) pair** before that late decoupling step.

For AI candidates it builds:

    FOR_EACH_ENUM_RAND(LeaderHead, mapRand())
    {
        for (size_t i = 0; i < aeValidAICivs.size(); i++)
        {
            if (GC.getInfo(aeValidAICivs[i]).isLeaders(eLoopLeaderHead) &&
                !m_leaderTaken.get(eLoopLeaderHead))
            {
                m_validAICivs.push_back(std::make_pair(
                        aeValidAICivs[i], eLoopLeaderHead));
            }
        }
    }

and for human candidates it stores the same native pairs, merely deferring the taken-leader test
until assignment:

    if (m_leaderTaken.get(validCivs[j].second) ||
        (bUniqueCivs && m_civTaken.get(validCivs[j].first)))
    {
        continue;
    }

Only **after** choosing `eeBestFit` from those native pairs does the Unrestricted Leaders branch
replace the leader with a random available leader.

CURRENT-LIVE CIV EXCLUSION
--------------------------
This makes a taken native leader erase its native civilization even though the game option says that
civilization may use any other leader.

Concrete current setup:

    GAMEOPTION_TRUE_STARTS = on
    GAMEOPTION_LEAD_ANY_CIV = on

    fixed player:
        civilization = CIVILIZATION_JAPAN
        leader       = LEADER_SALADIN

    another player:
        civilization = Random

The fixed player is not in `m_truPlayers`, so `changeCivs()` records:

    m_civTaken[JAPAN]    = true
    m_leaderTaken[SALADIN] = true

Arabia itself is **not** taken. Under Unrestricted Leaders it should therefore remain a valid
civilization for the Random player and could simply receive any free leader.

But current Arabia has one native leader:

    CIVILIZATION_ARABIA -> LEADER_SALADIN

When `m_validAICivs` is built, the only Arabia pair fails `!m_leaderTaken[SALADIN]`; no Arabia entry
is created at all. For a Random human, the Arabia/Saladin pair exists initially but the later
`m_leaderTaken` test skips it. Either way, Arabia disappears from civilization fitness/selection
solely because its native leader was used elsewhere.

Current shipped data makes this broad rather than exotic. Among the 34 civilizations currently
represented by `CvTruCivInfo`, **20 have exactly one native leader**. Any one of those civs can be
removed from an otherwise valid Random True-Starts pool by fixing its native leader to some other
civilization under Unrestricted Leaders.

INVERSE ERROR — FIXED CIVILIZATIONS ERASE FREE LEADERS
------------------------------------------------------
The coupling also runs in the other direction. Candidate civilizations are filtered first by:

    if (m_civTaken.get(eCiv))
        continue;

so no native `(civ, leader)` pairs are created for a fixed civilization. Later, the supposedly
unrestricted random-leader draw is built only from the leaders present in `validCivs`:

    std::vector<LeaderHeadTypes> aeAvailableLeaders;
    for (size_t j = 0; j < validCivs.size(); j++)
    {
        if (!m_leaderTaken.get(validCivs[j].second))
            aeAvailableLeaders.push_back(validCivs[j].second);
    }

Thus, in the example above, fixing Japan removes its native leader Tokugawa from the Random player's
leader draw even though Tokugawa is not taken and Unrestricted Leaders should permit him to lead any
other civilization.

This is independent of the fixed leader chosen for Japan: merely taking a civilization can suppress
all of that civilization's otherwise-free native leaders from later unrestricted assignment.

F614 SAME-ROOT DATA BREADTH
---------------------------
F614's missing `TruCiv` records for Ireland and Kingdom of Benin add another manifestation: because
no candidate pairs are ever created for those civs, their native leaders Ewuare, Grace O'Malley and
Michael Collins also never enter this `validCivs`-derived unrestricted leader pool. That breadth is
still caused by F614's missing data. F618 remains independently reproducible with any of the 34
properly integrated Base-AdvC civs, e.g. Arabia/Japan above.

WHY FITNESS REALLY IS SUPPOSED TO BE CIV-ONLY HERE
--------------------------------------------------
The late comment is not merely aspirational. At construction time True Starts deliberately leaves
`m_truLeaders` empty under `GAMEOPTION_LEAD_ANY_CIV`; therefore leader historical bias and
contemporaneity data are disabled. `calcFitness()` consequently has no leader-specific True Starts
signal in this mode. The chosen native leader is effectively just a temporary key used to carry a
civilization through data structures until the final random-leader replacement.

That makes filtering a civilization according to that temporary native leader's availability a
structural contradiction: the leader is explicitly not part of the intended fitness identity under
this option.

HISTORY / BASE BOUNDARY
-----------------------
The coupling was introduced with AdvC's original True Starts implementation, practical 3579
(`4977b513daa6bc436f6d0ea9e8ee011b131b8d36`). The original commit already contains both:

    // Ignore the truLeader info when leaders are unrestricted

and the later:

    // ... best-fit has been selected only based on a civ ...

while constructing `m_validHumanCivs` / `m_validAICivs` from native civ/leader pairs exactly as
current SAS does.

Base AdvC 1.14 retains the same logic. This is therefore an inherited AdvC True-Starts /
Unrestricted-Leaders integration defect, not a SAS-authored regression. SAS current data and game
options reproduce it directly.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
When `GAMEOPTION_LEAD_ANY_CIV` is enabled, civilization availability and leader availability need to
be built independently:

* civilization fitness candidates should be the untaken playable/AI-playable `TruCiv` civilizations,
  without requiring any of their native leaders to be free;
* the final unrestricted leader draw should come from globally valid untaken playable leaders,
  without requiring their native civilization to remain available;
* leader-specific True Starts fitness should remain disabled as current code already intends.

The current pair structure could still be retained internally with a harmless representative leader
for indexing if desired, but that representative must not gate civilization eligibility, and the
final leader pool must not be reconstructed from civ-native candidate pairs.

DEDUP
-----
Whole-album/Known-Issues searches found no prior root for this True Starts / Unrestricted Leaders
availability coupling.

It is independent of the adjacent Queue-022 findings:

* F613 fixes the wrong pair-vs-distinct-civ cardinality check; it does not decouple civ and leader
  eligibility.
* F614 adds missing Ireland/Benin True-Starts records; F618 reproduces using fully integrated Arabia
  and Japan.
* F615 fixes Empty-New-World longitude filtering.
* F616 removes fallback-pass duplicates; a perfectly deduplicated pair list still filters Arabia
  because Saladin is taken and still removes Tokugawa because Japan is taken.
* F617 fixes polar precipitation scoring and does not affect candidate identity.
