F619 / KI#941 — TRUE STARTS READS AN UNINITIALIZED GLOBAL-MAX-ELEVATION MEMBER, SO ELEVATION FITNESS CAN DEPEND ON STALE STACK DATA
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`TrueStarts` contains the plain integral member:

    int m_iMaxMaxElevationTarget; // global max

There is no in-class initializer (the project is C++03-era code), no constructor initializer list,
and no assignment to this member in `TrueStarts::TrueStarts()`.

`CvGame` constructs True Starts as an ordinary automatic local object:

    TrueStarts ts;
    ts.changeCivs();

so the member has an indeterminate value when `changeCivs()` first reads it.

The first and only initialization-like operation is actually a read-modify-write:

    for (size_t i = 0; i < m_validAICivs.size(); i++)
    {
        CvTruCivInfo const& kTruCiv = *m_truCivs.get(m_validAICivs[i].first);
        ...
        m_iMaxMaxElevationTarget = std::max(m_iMaxMaxElevationTarget,
                kTruCiv.get(CvTruCivInfo::MaxElevation));
    }

Reading the indeterminate `int` is undefined behavior. If its stale stack value happens to be below
one of the real positive targets, later iterations can accidentally repair it. If it is a positive
value above the largest candidate target, that garbage value survives every `std::max` and becomes
the session's supposed historical maximum elevation.

CURRENT DATA / INTENDED VALUE
-----------------------------
All 34 current `CvTruCivInfo` records provide positive `MaxElevation` data. Across the full current
pool the range is:

    Netherlands:  322 m
    ...
    Inca:        6893 m
    India:       8586 m   <- current global maximum

Thus, when India is among the valid candidate civilizations, the intended value is 8586. If some
high-elevation civs are already fixed/taken, the intended maximum can be lower; either way it should
be derived solely from the actual candidate data, never from previous stack contents.

LIVE CONSUMER
-------------
`calcFitness()` uses this member in the MaxElevation component:

    scaled rMaxElev = (rAreaPeakScore.getPercent() + 8) * 200;
    // Scenarios may have enormous clumps of peaks
    rMaxElev.decreaseTo(m_iMaxMaxElevationTarget);

    scaled rFromMaxElev =
        (rMaxElev.sqrt() - scaled(iTargetMaxElev).sqrt()).abs() * -fixp(2.4);
    iFitness += rFromMaxElev.round();

The comment explains the purpose of the global maximum: cap the map-derived elevation estimate so
peak-heavy maps/scenarios do not produce values beyond the historical target domain.

A stale positive `m_iMaxMaxElevationTarget` above the true maximum weakens or removes that cap. This
changes `rMaxElev` and therefore civilization fitness on sufficiently peak-heavy starts. A stale
negative value can create still stranger behavior at the clamp, although common debug stack-fill
patterns being negative may also cause the later positive `std::max` iterations to mask the defect.
Release builds have no such correctness guarantee.

This is therefore not merely an analyzer warning about an unused or presentation-only field: the
indeterminate value feeds a normal True Starts civ-fitness term.

HISTORY / BASE BOUNDARY
-----------------------
The defect was introduced with AdvC's original True Starts implementation, practical 3579
(`4977b513daa6bc436f6d0ea9e8ee011b131b8d36`). That single merge added all three relevant pieces:

    int m_iMaxMaxElevationTarget;

    m_iMaxMaxElevationTarget = std::max(m_iMaxMaxElevationTarget, ...);

    rMaxElev.decreaseTo(m_iMaxMaxElevationTarget);

No constructor initialization was supplied then or in later Base AdvC changes. Base AdvC 1.14 and
current SAS retain the same member and use. The bug is therefore inherited AdvC source debt and is
live whenever True Starts evaluates MaxElevation fitness.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Initialize the member to a value below every valid target before the accumulation, preferably in the
constructor initializer list/body or immediately before the candidate loop, e.g.:

    m_iMaxMaxElevationTarget = MIN_INT;

or, because current MaxElevation values are nonnegative:

    m_iMaxMaxElevationTarget = 0;

Then the existing `std::max` accumulation deterministically derives the maximum from the candidate
set. Initializing immediately before the loop additionally makes repeated `changeCivs()` calls on a
single object safe if that were ever introduced later.

A separate optional robustness choice is to avoid applying the clamp when no valid MaxElevation
sample exists, but current shipped TruCiv data always supplies those values; that is not needed to
repair F619.

DEDUP / CONTROLS
----------------
Whole-album/Known-Issues searches found no prior root for `m_iMaxMaxElevationTarget`, uninitialized
True Starts elevation state, or this MaxElevation clamp.

It is independent of F613-F618: those alter candidate cardinality/data/fitness inputs, but even a
perfect candidate list still seeds the elevation maximum from an indeterminate integer. Conversely,
initializing this member does not repair any candidate construction, longitude, precipitation or
Unrestricted-Leaders defect.

F620 / KI#942 — TRUE STARTS OVERWRITES A MANUALLY CHOSEN LEADER WHEN ONLY THE CIVILIZATION WAS RANDOM UNDER UNRESTRICTED LEADERS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
AdvC deliberately tracks civilization-randomness and leader-randomness separately. Current
`CvInitCore` exposes both flags:

    bool CvInitCore::wasCivRandomlyChosen(PlayerTypes eID) const
    {
        return m_abCivChosenRandomly.get(eID);
    }

    bool CvInitCore::wasLeaderRandomlyChosen(PlayerTypes eID) const
    {
        if (wasCivRandomlyChosen(eID) && !getOption(GAMEOPTION_LEAD_ANY_CIV))
            return true;
        return m_abLeaderChosenRandomly.get(eID);
    }

The special case is important: when Unrestricted Leaders (`GAMEOPTION_LEAD_ANY_CIV`) is enabled,
`wasCivRandomlyChosen()` being true does **not** imply that the leader was random. The two setup
choices are intentionally independent.

`TrueStarts::TrueStarts()`, however, decides which normal single-player slots it owns solely from the
civilization flag:

    if (GC.getInitCore().wasCivRandomlyChosen(itPlayer->getID()) ||
        GC.getGame().isNetworkMultiPlayer() ||
        (GC.getGame().isScenario() && !GC.getInitCore().getWBMapNoPlayers()))
    {
        m_truPlayers.push_back(&*itPlayer);
        ...
    }

It never asks `wasLeaderRandomlyChosen()`.

Therefore the fully supported setup state:

    GAMEOPTION_LEAD_ANY_CIV = true
    civilization = Random
    leader       = manually chosen / fixed

places that player in `m_truPlayers` even though only the civilization is supposed to be rerolled.

LIVE ASSIGNMENT EXECUTOR
------------------------
`changeCivs()` excludes `m_truPlayers` from the fixed-player bookkeeping, evaluates a replacement
civilization for each True-Starts player, and then has this Unrestricted-Leaders block:

    if (GC.getGame().isOption(GAMEOPTION_LEAD_ANY_CIV))
    {
        /*  When leaders are unrestricted, then the best-fit has been
            selected only based on a civ. Stick to that civ, and
            combine it with a random leader. */
        std::vector<LeaderHeadTypes> aeAvailableLeaders;
        ...
        eeBestFit.second = aeAvailableLeaders[MapRandNum(...)];
    }

At finalization it unconditionally applies both selected identities:

    itPlayer->changeCiv(eCiv, ...);
    itPlayer->changeLeader(eLeader, ...);

Consequently, a player who asked for **Random civilization + a specific leader** under Unrestricted
Leaders does not merely receive a geographically fitted civilization. True Starts silently discards
the fixed leader and assigns another leader randomly.

This is a direct setup-contract violation, not a heuristic disagreement: current `CvInitCore` has an
explicit, separately persisted answer to whether the leader was randomly chosen, and True Starts
never consults it before replacing the leader.

CONCRETE REPRODUCER
-------------------
For example:

    True Starts:          enabled
    Unrestricted Leaders: enabled
    civilization:         Random
    leader:               Saladin (manually selected)

The setup provenance is:

    wasCivRandomlyChosen(player)    == true
    wasLeaderRandomlyChosen(player) == false

True Starts nevertheless includes that player in `m_truPlayers`; after choosing a fitted civilization,
it enters the Unrestricted-Leaders branch and randomly chooses an available leader. The later
`changeLeader()` therefore need not preserve Saladin.

KI#209 POSITIVE CONTROL / DEDUP
-------------------------------
This root is especially well bounded by current KI#209.

KI#209 fixed an inherited Base AdvC copy/paste bug in `CvInitCore::reassignPlayer` that saved
`bRandomLeader` from the civilization-randomness map. Its documentation explicitly uses the same
supported setup states as examples:

    manually chosen civ + random leader
    random civ + manually chosen leader

and states that the distinction matters notably under `GAMEOPTION_LEAD_ANY_CIV`.

The current KI#209 repair correctly preserves those two provenance flags independently. F620 begins
**after that repair has succeeded**: the flags are correct, but True Starts reads only the civ flag and
then overwrites the fixed leader itself. Thus this is not a recurrence or breadth of KI#209; fixing
KI#209 is what makes the remaining True Starts contract violation especially explicit.

Whole-album searches found no prior root for True Starts ignoring `wasLeaderRandomlyChosen()` or
replacing a manually selected leader solely because the civilization was random. F618 is also
independent: F618 concerns candidate-pool civ/leader coupling under Unrestricted Leaders; F620
concerns whether an individual player's leader should be reassigned at all.

HISTORY / BASE BOUNDARY
-----------------------
The behavior is inherited from AdvC's original True Starts merge, practical 3579
(`4977b513daa6bc436f6d0ea9e8ee011b131b8d36`). That commit introduced both:

    if (wasCivRandomlyChosen(...))
        m_truPlayers.push_back(...);

and the later Unrestricted-Leaders rule that combines the fitted civ with a random leader.

Base AdvC 1.14 retains the same structure. Current SAS retains it too. The separate
`wasLeaderRandomlyChosen()` contract also exists in Base AdvC and explicitly treats Unrestricted
Leaders as the mode where random-civ and random-leader provenance can differ.

F620 is therefore inherited AdvC True Starts source debt, current-live under the supported
Unrestricted-Leaders setup domain.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The repair should preserve True Starts' right to replace a random civilization without granting it
permission to replace a fixed leader.

A conservative design is to retain each True-Starts player's original leader whenever:

    GAMEOPTION_LEAD_ANY_CIV &&
    !GC.getInitCore().wasLeaderRandomlyChosen(ePlayer)

and only draw from the unrestricted available-leader pool when the leader was actually random.

The fixed leader also needs to participate in `m_leaderTaken` / availability bookkeeping so another
True-Starts player cannot be assigned the same leader unless the normal game rules explicitly allow
leader duplication. This should be integrated with the broader F618 decoupling repair rather than
adding another native-pair dependency.

Do not solve F620 by excluding every random-civ/fixed-leader player from `m_truPlayers`: that would
preserve the leader but also prevent True Starts from geographically reassigning the civilization,
which was the part the player did ask to randomize.

F621 / KI#943 — TRUE STARTS' OCEANITY BASELINE COUNTS CIVS ONCE PER NATIVE LEADER, SO SAS'S ZERO LEADER-COUNT-BIAS SETTING STILL CHANGES FITNESS BY LEADER COUNT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`TrueStarts::changeCivs()` stores valid AI choices as native `(civilization, leader)` pairs in
`m_validAICivs`. That representation is appropriate where leader-specific fitness or availability is
needed, but the civ-only Oceanity normalization later loops the pair list directly:

    std::vector<scaled> arOceanityTargets;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < m_validAICivs.size(); i++)
    {
        CvTruCivInfo const& kTruCiv = *m_truCivs.get(m_validAICivs[i].first);
        scaled rSample = per100(kTruCiv.get(CvTruCivInfo::Oceanity));
        if (rSample >= 0)
            arOceanityTargets.push_back(rSample);
    }
    m_rMedianOceanityTarget = stats::median(arOceanityTargets);

Oceanity belongs only to `CvTruCivInfo`; the leader component is irrelevant. Consequently a civ with
three native leaders contributes its identical Oceanity target three times, a two-leader civ twice,
and a one-leader civ once.

CURRENT SAS DATA MAKES THE DIFFERENCE MEASURABLE
------------------------------------------------
For an ordinary all-Random current True Starts setup before any fixed-civ filtering:

    distinct current TruCivs:            34
    native valid civ/leader pairs:       52

The current Oceanity targets give:

    median over 34 distinct civs:        27.5%
    median over 52 native pairs:         30.0%

Fourteen of the 34 current True-Starts civilizations have more than one native leader; America,
England, France and Russia have three in the current data, while ten others have two. The difference
therefore comes from real shipped leader cardinalities, not malformed XML.

`calcFitness()` uses the pair-weighted median to normalize every candidate's Oceanity sensitivity:

    scaled rOceanityWeight = rTargetOceanity - m_rMedianOceanityTarget;
    if (rOceanityWeight > 0 && m_rMedianOceanityTarget < 1)
        rOceanityWeight /= 1 - m_rMedianOceanityTarget;
    else if (m_rMedianOceanityTarget > 0)
        rOceanityWeight /= m_rMedianOceanityTarget;
    rOceanityWeight = rOceanityWeight.abs();
    rOceanityWeight += fixp(0.5);
    ...
    rFromOceanity = ... * -175 * rOceanityWeight;

Across current Oceanity targets, using 30% instead of the distinct-civ 27.5% baseline changes this
weight by up to roughly 7.6 percentage points (around the current 25% target). It therefore changes
actual True-Starts civilization fitness and can change which civilization wins an assignment.

DIRECT CONFIG CONTRACT
----------------------
This is especially concrete in current SAS because leader-count bias is explicitly configurable and
SAS deliberately disables it:

    PER_EXTRA_LEADER_CIV_SELECTION_WEIGHT = 0

The current SAS XML comment explains the design intent: each civilization should have an equal
leader-count chance rather than France/Rome-style multi-leader civs appearing more often than
one-leader civs such as Kingdom of Benin.

The True Starts implementation itself states the same zero-setting contract immediately before its
explicit leader-count bias term:

    /*  A weight of 0 is supposed to result in no bias from the leader count.
        We can easily do that. */

At 0, `m_biasFromLeaderCount` correctly becomes zero. The Oceanity median, however, still depends on
the number of native leaders because it is built from `m_validAICivs`. Thus the file does **not** in
fact remove all leader-count influence when the configured weight is zero.

HISTORY / INTRODUCTION BOUNDARY
-------------------------------
AdvC's original True Starts merge, practical 3579 (`4977b513da...`), introduced the pair-weighted
Oceanity median together with the rest of the fitness model.

AdvC practical 3591 (`52444489ce...`, "True Starts bias for civs w/ multiple leaders based on XML")
then connected `PER_EXTRA_LEADER_CIV_SELECTION_WEIGHT` to True Starts and added the explicit promise
that 0 should mean no leader-count bias. That commit changed `m_biasFromLeaderCount` but left the
Oceanity-median loop over `m_validAICivs` untouched. Base AdvC's recommended value is 20; current SAS
sets the define to 0 deliberately, making the stale pair weighting a particularly clear current
contract contradiction.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Compute the civ-only Oceanity median from **distinct valid civilization IDs**, not native
civilization/leader pairs. The candidate-construction block already has the conceptual object needed
(`aeValidAICivs`); the implementation can either preserve a deduplicated civ vector for this later
step or use a local seen-civ map while building `arOceanityTargets`.

The same distinct-civ principle is appropriate for any other civ-only aggregate introduced later.
Do not remove the pair representation itself: leader-specific fitness/availability still needs it
when leaders are restricted.

DEDUP / F616 ALBUM CORRECTION
-----------------------------
F621 is independent of F616.

F616 concerns **second-pass duplicate accumulation** on Empty-New-World maps. It showed that the
current pass-2 duplication changes the Oceanity median from 30% to 25%. That remains valid evidence
that F616 affects gameplay, but WIP442 called 30% the "correct 52-pair median." This wording is now
refined:

    30% = unduplicated native-pair baseline used by current code
    27.5% = semantically distinct-civ baseline when leader-count bias is disabled
    25% = additionally duplicated Empty-New-World pass-2 value under F616's current reproduction

Fixing F616 removes accidental duplicate *passes* but still leaves each civ represented once per
native leader, so F621 survives. Fixing F621 by deduplicating civ-only targets does not repair F616's
other effects (candidate cardinality, unrestricted-leader draw duplication, uniqueness counts).

F618 and F620 are also separate Unrestricted-Leaders roots. F621 reproduces with ordinary restricted
leaders and an all-Random roster; it needs neither of those option-specific states.

F622 / KI#944 — TRUE STARTS' CLIMATE-REGION DIRECTION FILTER USES RAW COORDINATE DELTAS, SO WRAPPED-SEAM STARTS SILENTLY LOSE DIAGONAL REGIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`TrueStarts::calcClimateFitness()` deliberately samples the region around the start plus eight
orthogonal/diagonal region centers on a circle around it. The outer center loop first uses the
iterator's wrap-aware plot distance:

    int const iDistBetweenRegions = (GC.getMap().getWorldSize() < 2 ? 3 : 4);
    for (PlotCircleIter itCenter(kStart, iDistBetweenRegions);
        itCenter.hasNext(); ++itCenter)
    {
        bool const bStart = (&*itCenter == &kStart);
        if (itCenter.currPlotDist() != iDistBetweenRegions && !bStart)
            continue;

It then tries to retain only the eight intended directions, but switches coordinate systems:

        /*  Only consider the 8 plots on a straight orthogonal or
            diagonal line from kStart */
        int iDX = abs(itCenter->getX() - kStart.getX());
        int iDY = abs(itCenter->getY() - kStart.getY());
        if (iDX != 0 && iDY != 0 && iDX != iDY)
            continue;

`itCenter->getX()` / `getY()` are the wrapped, on-map coordinates of the returned `CvPlot`. Raw
subtraction of those coordinates does not represent local displacement when the iterator crossed a
wrapped map seam.

ITERATOR CONTRACT MAKES THE MISMATCH EXPLICIT
---------------------------------------------
`PlotCircleIter` derives from `SpiralPlotIterator<true>`. The iterator intentionally keeps its own
unwrapped traversal coordinates even when they temporarily lie outside the map, then resolves the
actual plot through `plotValidXY`:

    m_iCurrX += ...;
    m_iCurrY += ...;
    m_pNext = GC.getMap().plotValidXY(m_iCurrX, m_iCurrY);

The iterator comments explicitly document this distinction and provide the exact helpers needed by
this directional test:

    /* World-wrap isn't applied to m_iCurrX (i.e. it can be off the map),
       hence no need to check world wrap (CvMap::xDistance) here. */
    int currXDist() const { return abs(m_pCenter->getX() - m_iCurrX); }
    int currYDist() const { return abs(m_pCenter->getY() - m_iCurrY); }

At the same time, `currPlotDist()` calls the global plot-distance helper on the resolved plots.
Current `CvMap::plotDistance` derives its components through `xDistance` / `yDistance`, whose
`coordDistance` explicitly reduces wrapped deltas to the shorter distance across the seam.

Thus the same `itCenter` can correctly pass the rim test as a nearby wrapped plot and then fail the
very next straight-line test because that second test reinterprets its wrapped storage coordinate as
an unwrapped displacement.

CONCRETE X-WRAP REPRODUCER
--------------------------
For ordinary world sizes, `iDistBetweenRegions` is 4. With the current Civ4 plot-distance metric,
the eight intended outer directions are:

    (-4, 0), (+4, 0), (0, -4), (0, +4),
    (-3,-3), (-3,+3), (+3,-3), (+3,+3)

because `plotDistance(3,3) == 4`.

Take any sufficiently large X-wrapping map of width `W`, put the starting plot at X=1, and consider
the intended northwest center at unwrapped displacement (-3,+3). The spiral iterator visits
unwrapped X=-2 and resolves that through `plotValidXY` to stored map X=`W-2`.

The wrap-aware rim test sees the intended local distances 3 and 3 and therefore keeps the point on
the radius-4 circle. The raw directional test instead computes:

    iDX = abs((W - 2) - 1) = W - 3
    iDY = 3

For every normal map width, both are nonzero and unequal, so that diagonal center is rejected. The
southwest center is rejected the same way. The west cardinal center still survives only because
`iDY == 0` bypasses the equality requirement.

Therefore an X-wrapping radius-4 start in either of the first three or last three map columns can
lose two of its eight intended outer climate-region centers solely because of where the arbitrary
coordinate seam lies. On the radius-3 path used by the two smallest world sizes, the analogous
intended diagonal displacement is (2,2), so the first/last two columns are affected. Y-wrap has the
same defect in the other axis; toroidal maps can combine both effects.

This is not merely a cosmetic region list difference. The omitted regions feed all of the following
live climate calculations:

* the weighted median precipitation of the outer regions;
* the search for a region whose precipitation reinforces the start region;
* the resulting overall precipitation target mismatch;
* the count of close precipitation matches;
* the climate-variation sample/error calculation.

A sufficiently distinct climate region on the omitted side can therefore change the civilization's
True Starts fitness. Translating the same topological terrain across the artificial map seam can
change the score even though a wrapping map has no gameplay boundary there.

CURRENT-LIVE ACTIVATION
-----------------------
Wrapping is a supported and common current map topology. `CvMap` initializes wrapping to:

    m_bWrapX = true;
    m_bWrapY = false;

before allowing map-script/init data to override it. Multiple shipped SAS scripts explicitly enable
X-wrap; for example Tectonics returns true except for its nonwrapping option, while
`SAS_Spiky_Avenues.py` and `Water.py` return true unconditionally. The ordinary Fractal,
Continents, Pangaea and Terra scripts also expose cylindrical/toroidal wrap options.

A focused pass through current `StartingPositionIteration.cpp` found no seam exclusion that prevents
valid starting plots from occupying those X columns. Such an exclusion would in any case be
geometrically unnatural on a wrapping map, where X=0 is adjacent to X=width-1.

The defect is therefore current-live whenever True Starts evaluates a sufficiently seam-adjacent
start on a wrapping map; whether a particular omitted region has enough valid land to affect the
score depends on the generated terrain, but the region-selection asymmetry itself is deterministic.

HISTORY / BASE BOUNDARY
-----------------------
AdvC practical 3579 (`4977b513daa6bc436f6d0ea9e8ee011b131b8d36`), the original True Starts merge,
introduced the exact two-stage filter already in this form: wrap-aware `currPlotDist()` followed by
raw `getX()` / `getY()` subtraction for the eight-direction test.

Across the 6,403 locally mirrored commit diffs, only one later SAS diff also mentions
`calcClimateFitness`: SASBranch practical 5961, which merely reformats the function declaration onto
one line and does not touch this region filter. Base AdvC 1.14 still contains the same body verbatim.
K-Mod 1.46 and Civ4CE do not contain AdvC's `TrueStarts` implementation. F622 is therefore inherited
AdvC True Starts source debt, not a SAS regression or a K-Mod/Firaxis carryover.

DEDUP / CONTROLS
----------------
Focused whole-album and Known-Issues searches found no prior root for `calcClimateFitness` selecting
its region centers with raw wrapped coordinates, `currXDist` / `currYDist`, or wrapped-seam climate
region loss.

KI#257 is a useful thematic control, not a duplicate: it fixed raw seam deltas in the independently
inherited Planet/C2C Python feature-spread code. F622 is a separate C++ True Starts root in a
different algorithm and was introduced independently by AdvC practical 3579.

KI#259 is also separate: that issue concerned Planet climate callbacks returning inverted latitude
bounds and thereby disabling latitude-sensitive True Starts support. F617 concerns precipitation
classification after a climate region has already been selected. Neither owns the region-center
selection asymmetry here.

The earlier climate arithmetic controls remain closed: the apparently malformed Temperate-relative
latitude scaling is numerically harmless under current XML because the relevant Temperate changes
are zero, and the singleton-region variation path has not demonstrated a current gameplay mismatch.
Those should not be folded into F622.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The narrow repair is to keep the directional filter in the iterator's unwrapped local coordinate
system:

    int iDX = itCenter.currXDist();
    int iDY = itCenter.currYDist();

and retain the existing orthogonal/diagonal predicate. These helpers were designed precisely to
measure iterator displacement before world-wrap converts the position back into an on-map plot.

Using `GC.getMap().xDistance(...)` / `yDistance(...)` would also repair ordinary wrapped distances,
but `currXDist()` / `currYDist()` more directly expresses the intended "which spoke of this spiral
are we on?" question and matches the iterator's own documented contract.

A focused regression test should place an otherwise-valid True Starts start within three columns of
an X seam on a normal world size and verify that the start plus all eight intended region directions
remain eligible. Translating equivalent terrain across the seam should no longer change the region
set or climate fitness merely because stored X coordinates wrap.

F623 / KI#945 — TRUE STARTS' EMPTY-NEW-WORLD DETECTION COMPARES LOCALIZED MAP-OPTION DISPLAY TEXT TO ENGLISH LITERALS, SO SUPPORTED NON-ENGLISH GAMES CAN LOSE THE OLD-WORLD CIV FILTER
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`TrueStarts::changeCivs()` decides whether the generated map intentionally leaves a New World empty
before it builds the candidate civilization pool. For several scripts it does so by asking
`CvMap::isCustomMapOption` to search the *display description* returned by the map script:

    m_bEmptyNewWorld =
    (
            szMapName == CvWString("Terra") ||
            szMapName == CvWString("Earth2") ||
            ((szMapName == CvWString("PerfectMongoose") ||
            szMapName == CvWString("Tectonics") ||
            szMapName == CvWString("RandomScriptMap")) &&
            // This will only work when playing in English
            GC.getMap().isCustomMapOption("Old World", true)) ||
            ...
    );

The comment is literally correct: this branch does not inspect an option ID/value or an invariant
script token. It searches a user-visible string after the Python map script has localized it.

`CvMap::isCustomMapOption` documents the contract explicitly:

    /*  ...
        Translations will have to be handled by the caller (by generating szOptionsValue
        through gDLL->getText). */

and then obtains each current option description by calling the Python map script's
`customMapOptionDescription`. Therefore the description being compared is in the active UI
language whenever the script returns a translated key.

CLEAN CURRENT REPRODUCER: TECTONICS
-----------------------------------
Current shipped `PrivateMaps/Tectonics.py` defines landmass option 0 with nine values. Selection 8
is the dedicated Terra mode whose starting positions are forced onto the best/Old-World landmass:

    selection_names = [
        ...,
        "TXT_KEY_MAP_SCRIPT_TERRA",
        "TXT_KEY_MAP_SCRIPT_TERRA_OLD_WORLD_START"]

    if (iOption == 0):
        return unicode(CyTranslator().getText(selection_names[iSelection], ()))

and later:

    userInputLandmass = CyMap().getCustomMapOption(0)
    ...
    if (userInputLandmass == 8):     # "Terra"
        allOnBest = true

The local AdvC 1.14 text data supplied with the audit gives the relevant translation key as:

    <Tag>TXT_KEY_MAP_SCRIPT_TERRA_OLD_WORLD_START</Tag>
    <English>Randomized Earth (Old World Start)</English>
    <French>Randomisation de la Terre (départ : Antiquité)</French>
    <German>Zufällige Erde (Start Alte Welt)</German>
    <Italian>Terra casuale (partenza Vecchio Mondo)</Italian>
    <Spanish>Tierra al azar (inicio en Viejo Mundo)</Spanish>

In English, the selection-8 description contains `"Old World"`, so the True Starts test succeeds.
In French it contains neither `"Old"` nor `"World"`; the same selected map option therefore fails
the English substring search and leaves `m_bEmptyNewWorld` false. German, Italian and Spanish also
do not contain the English substring.

There is no later Tectonics-specific OR term that repairs the result. Thus the same Tectonics map
configuration is classified as an empty-New-World game in English and as an ordinary unrestricted
world in another fully supported Civ4 language.

SECOND INDEPENDENT CURRENT REPRODUCER: RANDOMSCRIPTMAP
-----------------------------------------------------
This is not peculiar to one AdvC-added Tectonics label. Current `PrivateMaps/RandomScriptMap.py`
uses the standard translated key for its AI-start option 2:

    startAi_names = [
        "TXT_KEY_MAP_SCRIPT_NO_CONDITIONS",
        "TXT_KEY_MAP_SCRIPT_DEFAULT",
        "TXT_KEY_MAP_SCRIPT_ALL_IN_OLD_WORLD"]
    ...
    return unicode(CyTranslator().getText(szName, ()))

and its actual setup logic makes selection 2 unconditionally force the Old-World start rule:

    elif (aiStartMethod == 2):
        gl_aiStartType = STA_OLDWORLD

The Civ4/BtS text data supplied through the local Civ4CE reference archive defines that key as:

    <English>All In Old World</English>
    <French>Tous dans l'Antiquité</French>
    <German>Alle in Alter Welt</German>
    <Italian>Tutto nel Vecchio Mondo</Italian>
    <Spanish>Todos en el Viejo Mundo</Spanish>

Again, the English `"Old World"` substring exists only in English. A RandomScriptMap setup using a
non-Terra generation method plus `All In Old World` is therefore detected by True Starts in English
but missed in the other supported languages. (The separate `isCustomMapOption("Terra")` OR only
helps when the chosen generation method itself is Terra; it does not repair the general forced
Old-World-start option.)

WHY THIS CHANGES LIVE TRUE-STARTS BEHAVIOR
------------------------------------------
`m_bEmptyNewWorld` directly controls the first candidate-building pass. When true, True Starts
rejects civilizations whose historical coordinates lie in the New World before performing its
fallback pass:

    if (m_bEmptyNewWorld && iPass == 0)
    {
        int iLongitudeTimes10 = kTruCiv.get(...LongitudeTimes10);
        int iLatitudeTimes10 = kTruCiv.get(...LatitudeTimes10);
        if (iLongitudeTimes10 < 300 ||
            (iLongitudeTimes10 > 1100 && iLatitudeTimes10 < -100))
        {
            continue;
        }
    }

So the localization failure is not a menu-label cosmetic issue. It changes which civilizations are
eligible in the preferred True Starts pool on exactly the map modes designed to reserve an empty New
World. In a non-English game, New-World civilizations can enter the normal first-pass candidate
pool even though the map script is simultaneously forcing starting plots into its Old World.

That can alter civilization assignment for random players and defeats the intended True Starts
coordination with the map script. F615 and F616 concern what happens *after* an empty-New-World map
has been recognized; F623 prevents that state from being recognized in the first place.

CURRENT-LIVE / LANGUAGE SUPPORT BOUNDARY
----------------------------------------
French, German, Italian and Spanish are not hypothetical third-party localizations here: both the
AdvC Tectonics key and the standard BtS RandomScriptMap key contain explicit translations for those
languages in the locally supplied game/reference data. Tectonics and RandomScriptMap are shipped
current SAS map scripts, and their current option-description functions actively call
`CyTranslator().getText` for the affected selections.

By contrast, some other branches in the same True Starts expression happen to use scripts whose
current option text is literal English. For example, current PerfectMongoose selection 1 is the
literal string `"Old World (unless Pangaea); -30% players recommended"`, and current Totestra's
relevant description is literal `"Keep New World empty"`; those particular calls are not rescued by
good design, they merely remain language-invariant because those scripts themselves do not localize
that display text. The finding does not require every branch to fail: Tectonics and RandomScriptMap
already provide supported, current-live reproductions.

A useful local contrast exists in the same `TrueStarts.cpp`: the balanced-resource check correctly
passes translated text into this helper:

    m_bBalancedResources =
            kMap.isCustomMapOption(gDLL->getText("TXT_KEY_MAP_BALANCED"));

That demonstrates both the intended API contract and that True Starts already knows how to avoid
English-only comparison where a stable translated key exists.

HISTORY / BASE BOUNDARY
-----------------------
AdvC practical 3579 (`4977b513daa6bc436f6d0ea9e8ee011b131b8d36`), the original True Starts merge,
introduced the `m_bEmptyNewWorld` map-option detection with the same literal
`isCustomMapOption("Old World", true)` test. The original practical already therefore carried the
locale-dependent root.

Current Base AdvC 1.14 still has the same test and now contains the candid source comment:

    // This will only work when playing in English

No locally mirrored later commit changes the exact `Old World` call; the 6,403-diff corpus points
back to the original practical for this root. Current SAS retains the Base AdvC 1.14 behavior
unchanged. This is therefore inherited AdvC True Starts source debt, not a SAS regression and not a
K-Mod/Civ4CE True Starts carryover (those references do not contain this AdvC implementation).

The fact that the source comments on the limitation does not make the gameplay behavior correct; it
is useful provenance showing that the locale dependency was known in code but never made robust.
The current Known-Issues document and audit album do not otherwise own it.

DEDUP / CONTROLS
----------------
Focused whole-album and Known-Issues searches found no existing True Starts finding for localized
map-option descriptions, the literal `"Old World"` test, or non-English empty-New-World detection.

F615 / KI#937 is separate: once `m_bEmptyNewWorld` is true, its Americas longitude cutoff has the
wrong sign/threshold behavior. F616 / KI#938 is separate: the fallback candidate pass appends to the
first-pass vectors without clearing them. F623 occurs earlier and can leave `m_bEmptyNewWorld`
false altogether.

The source's own English-only comment is also not a duplicate issue owner; it is an acknowledgment
inside the affected code, with no implemented correction or player-facing KI entry found locally.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The robust repair should stop inferring semantic map-option state from localized display text where
True Starts already knows the map script. Script-specific numeric option IDs/selection values are
language-independent and directly encode the same conditions used by the scripts themselves.

For the clean Tectonics reproducer, the invariant test is simply its landmass option 0 being
selection 8. For RandomScriptMap, AI-start option 1 selection 2 directly means forced Old-World
starts; generation-method option 0 selection 2 is its Terra mode. PerfectMongoose likewise already
stores Old-World starts as option 1 selection 1. Using those invariant values avoids both translation
and wording drift.

A translation-based repair is possible for individual standard-key choices, but it is less general:
the scripts use different labels/keys, and literal-English scripts coexist with translated ones.
Moreover `CvMap` itself documents that display-string matching requires the caller to manage
translations. The clean architectural boundary is therefore to query known semantic option values
for these known scripts rather than parse what the UI happens to display.

Regression coverage should run at least Tectonics option 0=8 and RandomScriptMap AI-start option
1=2 under English and French and assert that `m_bEmptyNewWorld` is identical. True Starts' preferred
candidate pool should not depend on UI language.

F624 CANDIDATE CLOSED — m_rMedianSpace CANNOT BE ZERO ON THE LIVE PATH
---------------------------------------------------------------------
The first continuation cursor from WIP449 was this division in `calcFitness()`:

    scaled rSpace = kStats.areaSpaceWeights() / m_rMedianSpace;

The denominator is built in the constructor as the median of every True-Starts player's
`SurroundingsStats::areaSpaceWeights()`.

A direct iterator/weight proof shows that each individual sample is at least 1:

1. `getSurroundings()` creates a `PlotCircleIter` with the default `bIncludeCenter=true`.
2. `SpiralPlotIterator::init` therefore exposes the player's own starting plot as the first element.
3. At that center, `distWeight(kStart, kStart, radius)` is exactly 1 because plot distance is 0.
4. The rival-overlap reduction in `calculatePlotWeights()` cannot reduce the center below 1:
   `rOtherDistWeight <= 1`, while `rDistWeight == 1`, so
   `max(0, rOtherDistWeight - rDistWeight) == 0` for every rival.
5. The start necessarily belongs to its own area and is not a lake starting tile, so the
   `SurroundingsStats` same-area branch executes and adds `sqrt(1) == 1` to
   `m_rAreaSpaceWeights`.

Thus every `areaSpaceWeights()` sample is >=1, and every nonempty median is >=1. The constructor only
leaves `m_rMedianSpace` at its default when there are no True-Starts players, in which case
`calcFitness()` is never invoked for a True-Starts player. The denominator is therefore safe on the
current live path. No F624.

F624 CANDIDATE DEDUP — DISTINCT-CIV SHORTAGE IS ALREADY F613 / KI#935
---------------------------------------------------------------------
A fresh mechanical pass over `changeCivs()` independently rediscovered this suspicious test:

    if (m_validAICivs.size() < m_truPlayers.size() ||
        aeValidHumanCivs.size() < m_truHumans.size())
    {
        bUniqueCivs = false;
    }

Current shipped True-Starts data has 34 distinct supported civilizations but 52 native
civ/leader pairs (20 one-leader civs, 10 two-leader civs, 4 three-leader civs). With 35-48 all-random
players, the 52 pair count can satisfy the first comparison although 34 distinct civilizations
cannot satisfy uniqueness. The later assignment filter can then exhaust all distinct civs and leave
late players unassigned.

This is a genuine live defect, but the reconciled album confirms that this exact root and current
34-vs-52 reproducer are already F613 / KI#935, the first finding of Queue 022. It is therefore an
important dedup positive control, not F624.

ADJACENT FUTURE ROOT — PLOTRADIUSITERATOR WRAP DUPLICATION
----------------------------------------------------------
The closure pass exposed one useful cross-file observation that should be carried to the pending
`PlotRadiusIterator` audit rather than misassigned to TrueStarts.

`SpiralPlotIterator` keeps unwrapped iterator coordinates but resolves each coordinate through
`CvMap::plotValidXY`. It has no visited-plot suppression. On a wrapped dimension, once its radius
reaches at least half that dimension, opposite unwrapped coordinates can therefore resolve to the
same physical `CvPlot` and be yielded more than once.

A current shipped reproducer exists without exotic mod data:

- `WORLDSIZE_ARENA` grid width is 14;
- `TrueStarts::calculateRadius()` gives a base surroundings radius of 7 at ordinary 2/2 crowdedness;
- current `PrivateMaps/Fractal.py` defaults its world-wrap option to cylindrical (`getWrapX()==true`).

At X offsets -7 and +7 from the same Arena start, the two unwrapped coordinates identify the same
wrapped map column. `PlotCircleIter` can therefore revisit the same physical opposite-seam plots.
TrueStarts' broad `SurroundingsStats` and bonus loops can then count those physical plots more than
once.

This looks worth a dedicated root audit because the iterator is general and its own queue is still
PENDING (Queue 167 in the current album). Do not spend F624 on it here without first determining the
intended general iterator contract, breadth across callers, and prior dedup when that root file is
audited. F622 is separate: it is a TrueStarts-specific misuse of raw resolved coordinates even at
small climate-region radius and does not require duplicate iterator output.

`isCustomMapOption` drops its own `bCheckContains` / `bIgnoreCase` parameters when forwarding. It is

F624 / PROVISIONAL KI#946 — CONFIRMED INHERITED ADVC NORMALIZATION-LEVEL FALLTHROUGH
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SEVERITY / CLASS: current-live gameplay normalization defect; inherited AdvC control-flow bug.
ROOT FILE: `CvGameCoreDLL/StartingPositionIteration.cpp`,
`NormalizationTarget::isReached(..., bNearlyReached=true, ...)`.

CURRENT CODE
------------
The current function starts with a base tolerance of 2.5%, then tries to vary the extra tolerance
by the game's configured starting-plot normalization level:

    scaled rTolerance = fixp(2.5);
    if (bNearlyReached)
    {
        switch(GC.getGame().getStartingPlotNormalizationLevel())
        {
        case CvGame::NORMALIZE_HIGH: rTolerance += 2;
        case CvGame::NORMALIZE_MEDIUM: rTolerance += 4;
        default: rTolerance += 6;
        }
    }
    rTolerance /= 100;
    ...
    return (rIncreaseNeeded <= rTolerance * iCurrFoundVal);

There are no `break` statements and no intentional-fallthrough annotation.

The actual tolerances before the later handicap adjustment are therefore:

- LOW: 2.5 + 6 = 8.5%
- MEDIUM: 2.5 + 4 + 6 = 12.5%
- HIGH: 2.5 + 2 + 4 + 6 = 14.5%

This reverses the semantic direction of the normalization levels. The stronger the requested
normalization, the more tolerant the target becomes and the earlier it can report that a weak start
is already "nearly reached."

CONTRACT / LIVE CALLER PROOF
----------------------------
`CvGame.h` explicitly documents the three levels as:

    1: low    (weak starting plots on average, high variance); for single-player
    2: medium (strong starting plots, low variance); for multi-player
    3: high   (very strong starting plots, low variance); BtS/K-Mod behavior

`NormalizationTarget::isNearlyReached` simply forwards to `isReached(..., true)`. The live caller in
`CvGame::normalizeAddExtras` tests it while traversing candidate resource plots:

    if (pTarget != NULL ? pTarget->isNearlyReached(*pStartingPlot) :
        citySiteEval.evaluate(*pStartingPlot) >= rTargetValue)
    {
        ...
        goto done_placing_resources;
    }

So a *larger* tolerance means "nearly reached" succeeds sooner and resource normalization stops
sooner. HIGH and MEDIUM should not be more permissive than LOW here; that directly contradicts the
level contract.

A simple boundary illustrates the live effect. Suppose a site's computed `rIncreaseNeeded` is 10%
of its current found value before the common handicap adjustment:

- the structurally intended HIGH tolerance (4.5%; see history below) would return false and continue
  trying to normalize the site;
- current HIGH fallthrough gives 14.5%, returns true, and stops adding normalization bonuses;
- current MEDIUM likewise stops at 12.5%;
- LOW at 8.5% would continue.

The result can therefore be the opposite of the configured normalization strength.

CURRENT-LIVE ACTIVATION
-----------------------
Current SAS has:

    ENABLE_STARTING_POSITION_ITERATION = 1
    NORMALIZE_STARTPLOTS_AGGRESSIVELY = 0

So SPI and its `NormalizationTarget` are live on supported map scripts that do not override the
relevant starting-position path. With the default normalization define, ordinary single-player is
normally LOW and therefore hits only the `default` arm; that common case masks the bug. The other
supported current paths do not:

- `CvGame::setStartingPlotNormalizationLevel` promotes multiplayer games with more than one human
  from LOW to MEDIUM;
- the "Balanced" map option explicitly sets normalization to HIGH;
- HIGH is also the documented aggressive/BtS/K-Mod level and can be selected through the existing
  normalization setting path.

Thus this is not an unreachable configuration or mod-data hypothetical. MEDIUM multiplayer and HIGH
Balanced/aggressive normalization are current supported paths, and the only `isNearlyReached`
caller is specifically part of start normalization.

HISTORY — MISSING BREAKS ARE PROVABLE, NOT A STYLE GUESS
---------------------------------------------------------
The local reachable-history mirror gives unusually strong intent evidence.

AdvC practical 2302 (`d6ea7fc8701bfe2d4353437da01e5d5b392d8b7e`, title
"Starting positions (cont.), normalization.") introduced this code as:

    scaled rTolerance = 2;
    if (bNearlyReached)
    {
        switch(GC.getGame().getStartingPlotNormalizationLevel())
        {
        case CvGame::NORMALIZE_HIGH: rTolerance = 4;
        case CvGame::NORMALIZE_MEDIUM: rTolerance = 6;
        default: rTolerance = 8;
        }
    }

Without breaks, HIGH sets 4, then 6, then 8; MEDIUM sets 6, then 8. All three levels therefore
collapse to 8%. That already defeats the purpose of switching on the normalization level.

Just three practical commits later, AdvC practical 2305
(`82c08218c66b1a01049f4bf81647a77ab3949573`, title
"More tweaks, fixed miscalculations for starting positions") changed the base from 2 to 2.5 and
changed those assignments to additions:

    HIGH:   rTolerance += 2;
    MEDIUM: rTolerance += 4;
    default:rTolerance += 6;

but retained the missing breaks. With normal non-fallthrough switch semantics, this is an extremely
coherent adjustment of the earlier intended 4/6/8 values to 4.5/6.5/8.5 — each target rises by
exactly 0.5 while preserving HIGH < MEDIUM < LOW. With the inherited fallthrough, the same tweak
instead produces 14.5/12.5/8.5 and reverses that ordering.

That two-commit evolution makes the omitted breaks a concrete control-flow error rather than an
argument about preferred tuning. Current Base AdvC 1.14 retains the same fallthrough unchanged.
K-Mod and Civ4CE do not contain this AdvC-created SPI implementation, so the root is inherited AdvC,
not BtS/K-Mod/Civ4CE and not introduced by SAS.

DEDUP
-----
Focused searches of the reconciled audit album and Known Issues found no existing owner for the
`NormalizationTarget` normalization-level tolerance fallthrough or the HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW reversal.

The only prior StartingPositionIteration-specific KI found in the current Known-Issues corpus is
KI#492 / album F169, which is a separate performance defect: workable-plot precomputation performs
and discards full city-site evaluations. It does not overlap this normalization stop condition.

The repository Known-Issues file currently carries KI#946 only as the WIP449 reservation saying
F624 remained unassigned while Queue 022 was open. WIP450 subsequently closed Queue 022 without
using it. F624 is now legitimately consumed here by the first independent Queue-025 root.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The narrow semantic repair is to terminate each explicit case, preserving the apparent intended
values from practical 2305:

    case CvGame::NORMALIZE_HIGH:
        rTolerance += 2;
        break;
    case CvGame::NORMALIZE_MEDIUM:
        rTolerance += 4;
        break;
    default:
        rTolerance += 6;
        break;

That yields 4.5% HIGH, 6.5% MEDIUM and 8.5% LOW before the existing common handicap adjustment. It
restores the documented direction: stronger normalization requires a site to get closer to target
before `isNearlyReached` stops resource placement.

Regression coverage should evaluate the same SPI-produced `NormalizationTarget` / start state at
LOW, MEDIUM and HIGH and assert monotonicity:

    HIGH tolerance < MEDIUM tolerance < LOW tolerance

and, for a boundary state such as a required increase around 10%, verify that LOW may call the site
nearly reached while MEDIUM/HIGH continue normalization — never the reverse solely because the
normalization level is stronger.

   geometry is far below that threshold, and no shipped reproducer has been established yet. Keep
   this as robustness debt/candidate only; do not spend F625 without a supported current path.

2. The cross-file `PlotCircleIter` wrap-duplication observation carried from WIP450 is directly
   relevant here: `PotentialSites::recordSite` uses `PlotCircleIter(kPlot, 8, false)`, enough to
   exceed half-width on 14-wide wrapped Arena maps. This reinforces Queue 167
   `PlotRadiusIterator.cpp` as the likely root owner. Do not duplicate it into Queue 025 before the
   iterator contract/root is audited.

C031-WIP452 — QUEUE 025 DISTANCETABLE WATER-FALLBACK DISTANCE UNIT MISMATCH
===============================================================================

PHYSICAL CONTINUATION
---------------------
This checkpoint continues directly from C031-WIP451 / Queue 025
`CvGameCoreDLL/StartingPositionIteration.cpp`. F624 / provisional KI#946 remains the confirmed
normalization-level fallthrough from WIP451. F625 / provisional KI#947 was unused at that stone.

F625 / PROVISIONAL KI#947 — CONFIRMED INHERITED ADVC DISTANCETABLE UNIT MISMATCH
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SEVERITY / CLASS: current-live starting-position space-evaluation defect; inherited AdvC arithmetic /
metric mismatch.
ROOT FILE: `CvGameCoreDLL/StartingPositionIteration.cpp`,
`StartingPositionIteration::DistanceTable::DistanceTable` water-destination fallback.

CURRENT CODE / CONTRACT
-----------------------
`DistanceTable` is explicitly a weighted path-distance system. `computeDistances` runs Dijkstra and
`stepDist` assigns ordinary land movement costs of 9 for cardinal steps and 12 for diagonal steps:

    if (!kTo.isWater())
        return (bDiagonal ? 12 : 9);

The header documents the same scale through:

    /* Typical distance according to DistanceTable::stepDist
       between two friendly adjacent cities. */
    short getAvgCityDist() const { return 40; }

and the source immediately above `stepDist` warns:

    /* If the scale of the distances is changed, the value returned by
       getAvgCityDist needs to be adjusted. */

Water work tiles need special handling because a city can work them without a settler/ship path to
the water tile. The constructor therefore replaces a water destination's ordinary Dijkstra value
with the distance to a nearby legal land city site, plus working/improvement adjustments.

For land sites that are themselves destinations this is scale-consistent:

    short iDist = d(kSource, *it);
    ...
    iShortestDist = iDist;

But the explicitly documented fallback for a legal low-value city site that was omitted from the
DestinationTable does this instead:

    else if (!bDest && it->sameArea(kSource))
    {
        short iDist = static_cast<short>(kMap.plotDistance(&kSource, &*it));
        ...
        iShortestDist = iDist;
    }

It then immediately adds values expressed in the weighted DistanceTable scale:

    iShortestDist += getAvgCityDist() / 5;          // +8
    if (!bInnerRing)
        iShortestDist += getAvgCityDist() / 4;      // +10
    if (kWaterDest.getBonusType(NO_TEAM) != NO_BONUS)
        iShortestDist += (5 * getAvgCityDist()) / 8;// +25

`CvMap::plotDistance`, however, is the normal octile geometric metric in tile-distance units. A
10-tile cardinal separation returns 10, while `DistanceTable::stepDist` assigns 90 to the same ten
ordinary cardinal land steps. The fallback therefore mixes two incompatible units in one stored
`DistanceTable` value.

CONCRETE CURRENT-LIVE OCEAN-FISH / SNOW PATH
---------------------------------------------
The source itself names the intended fallback case:

    "Bad land tiles aren't stored in the DistanceTable, so this will fail for e.g.
     an Ocean Fish workable only from a Snow tile. Fall back on CvMap::plotDist ..."

Current SAS XML makes this a concrete supported map state rather than a historical comment:

- `TERRAIN_SNOW` has no base yields (`<Yields/>`), is land (`bWater=0`), passable
  (`bImpassable=0`) and city-foundable (`bFound=1`).
- `BONUS_FISH` has no reveal-tech gate, adds +1 food, and is allowed on both Coast and Ocean.

The SPI precompute stores a plot in `relevantPlots` only when its SPI workable-plot value is positive
or it is already a candidate/current city site:

    if (yieldValues.get(eLoopPlotNum) > 0 ||
        sitePlotNums.count(eLoopPlotNum) > 0)
        relevantPlots.push_back(...);

For an ordinary featureless/resource-less Snow tile, `CitySiteEvaluator::evaluateWorkablePlot`
starts from zero natural yields. The future-improvement multiplier cannot make zero positive; the
population-sustenance subtraction leaves no positive yield contribution, and the later marginal
space term also adds nothing because its `iVal` is zero. The function returns `max(r, 0)`, so such a
Snow tile can legitimately have value 0 and be omitted from `relevantPlots` despite being a legal
city site.

An Ocean Fish, by contrast, has positive food/resource value and can be retained as a water
destination. If its only legal working city site is one of those omitted Snow tiles, `bDest` remains
false and the raw-`plotDistance` fallback is taken exactly as the source comment anticipates.

NUMERIC COUNTEREXAMPLE
----------------------
Use an ordinary passable same-landmass source S and a legal zero-value Snow city site L ten cardinal
land steps away. Let an inner-ring Ocean Fish W be workable from L and from no retained land
destination.

The weighted land-path part of the intended `DistanceTable` metric is:

    10 cardinal land steps * 9 = 90

The current fallback instead stores:

    plotDistance(S,L) = 10

For an inner-ring Fish, both branches then add the same water-working/resource adjustments:

    + getAvgCityDist()/5       = +8
    + 5*getAvgCityDist()/8     = +25

So current fallback result is:

    10 + 8 + 25 = 43

where the same geometry expressed in the surrounding `DistanceTable` scale is approximately:

    90 + 8 + 25 = 123

For an outer-ring working site both receive the same additional +10, giving 53 versus roughly 133.
The error grows with land separation because every additional ordinary cardinal land tile adds only
1 in the fallback instead of 9 in the path metric.

This is not merely a display value. `SpaceEvaluator` consumes the stored distance directly:

    short iDist = kDists.d(kStartPlot, kLoopPlot) - iDistSubtr;
    ...
    rSum += claim_t(1, max(1, iDist));

and later uses the same distance for claim competition and cached access/delay factors before:

    rSpaceVal += rYieldVal * rAccessFactor;

The under-scaled fallback therefore makes affected remote water yields/resources look much closer
and more readily claimable than equivalent land/path geometry warrants, feeding the actual SPI
start-space score and consequently start-position iteration decisions.

The geometric fallback also does not preserve the obstacle/path semantics of Dijkstra's `stepDist`;
`sameArea` is only a coarse landmass check. The unit mismatch alone is sufficient to establish the
current defect, so no stronger path-topology assumption is needed for F625.

HISTORY / INHERITANCE
---------------------
AdvC practical 2302 (`d6ea7fc8701bfe2d4353437da01e5d5b392d8b7e`, "Starting positions (cont.),
normalization.") introduced the water-destination fallback and the current weighted-distance scale
in the same change.

That introduction already contains, together:

- the raw `kMap.plotDistance(&kSource, &*it)` fallback;
- ordinary land `stepDist` costs of 9/12;
- `getAvgCityDist() == 40` with the comment that it is the typical `stepDist` distance between
  adjacent cities; and
- the warning that changing the distance scale requires changing `getAvgCityDist`.

So the mismatch did not arise because a later commit rescaled `DistanceTable` while forgetting an
old fallback. It entered in practical 2302 already mixing raw tile distance with the new weighted
path metric. Focused local-history search finds the exact Ocean-Fish comment and raw fallback only in
that introduction; no later corrective change is present in the reachable mirror.

Current Base AdvC 1.14 retains the same raw fallback and the same 9/12 path costs unchanged. K-Mod
and Civ4CE do not contain this AdvC-created SPI subsystem. Classification is therefore inherited
AdvC, not SAS/BtS/K-Mod/Civ4CE.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The semantic requirement is narrow: any fallback value written into `DistanceTable` must use the
same weighted path-distance units and reachability semantics as `d()` / `computeDistances` before
the existing +8/+10/+25 water-work adjustments are applied.

A robust repair should therefore obtain the Dijkstra/`stepDist` distance to the otherwise-omitted
legal land city site (for example by retaining/querying full per-source Dijkstra distances for this
fallback, or by explicitly making the necessary fallback land sites distance destinations). Merely
copying raw `CvMap::plotDistance` into the table is not scale-compatible. Multiplying geometric
distance by an arbitrary constant would improve units but would still lose `stepDist`'s diagonal,
impassability/isthmus and frontier/path semantics, so it is a weaker approximation rather than the
clean contract repair.

Regression coverage should construct a positive water destination whose only legal working city
site is a zero-valued omitted land tile and assert that:

1. increasing ordinary cardinal source-to-city-site separation by one tile changes the fallback by
   the ordinary land `stepDist` scale (9), not by raw geometric 1;
2. the fallback is comparable to a retained-land-destination case with identical geometry; and
3. unreachable/blocked path geometry is not converted into a deceptively tiny finite access value
   merely because the plots share a `CvArea`.

OTHER QUEUE-025 CONTROL — REMOTE DOUBLE-MOVE SEARCH PRUNING
-----------------------------------------------------------
A separate code-shape candidate remains below promotion threshold for now. In `currAltSites`, remote
alternatives are iterated as:

    eRemoteSite = m_pPotentialSites->getRemoteSite(i);
    if (eRemoteSite == NO_PLOT_NUM || eRemoteSite == eTakenSite)
        break;

For the second half of a double move, `eTakenSite` is the first player's chosen site. If that site is
remote candidate 0 (or 1), `break` discards all later remote candidates even though only the taken
site is forbidden; `continue` would match the local comment "Don't move the second player to the
same site as the first." This can prune valid heuristic alternatives, but it is still being held as
a lower-severity search-quality candidate rather than consumed as F626 without a stronger outcome
proof.

F626 / PROVISIONAL KI#948 — CONFIRMED INHERITED ADVC SPI UNEQUAL-TEAM ROUND-ROBIN OVERFILLS COMPLETED TEAMS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT FILES:
- `CvGameCoreDLL/StartingPositionIteration.cpp`,
  `StartingPositionIteration::assignSitesToTeams` / `getTeamSite`;
- downstream contract in `CvGameCoreDLL/CvGame.cpp`, `CvGame::assignStartingPlots`;
- `CvGameCoreDLL/CvPlayer.cpp`, `CvPlayer::setStartingPlot`, for duplicate-start persistence.

ROOT DEFECT
-----------
`assignSitesToTeams()` distributes the already-generated SPI sites among teams by rotating through
all alive teams, normally placing two sites for one team before advancing:

    m_sitesPerTeam[eCurrTeam].push_back(*itCurrSite);
    aeAvailableSites.erase(itCurrSite);
    int const iLoopTeamSites = m_sitesPerTeam[eCurrTeam].size();
    if (GET_TEAM(eCurrTeam).getNumMembers() <= iLoopTeamSites ||
        iLoopTeamSites % 2 == 0)
    {
        iLoopTeamIndex++;
        iLoopTeamIndex %= aieTeamsBySize.size();
    }

The first condition advances away from a team once it has received all of its members' sites, but
the completed team remains in `aieTeamsBySize`. Nothing skips it when the round-robin later wraps
back around. If unassigned sites still remain, the completed team receives another site before the
same condition advances away again.

The assignment-count error depends only on team sizes, not on `teamValue` or map geometry.

MINIMAL CURRENT SUPPORTED COUNTEREXAMPLE
----------------------------------------
Two alive teams of sizes 5 and 1 (six civilization players total) are sufficient.

The current rotation is:

    Team 5: +2  -> 2/5
    Team 1: +1  -> 1/1 complete
    Team 5: +2  -> 4/5
    Team 1: +1  -> 2/1 overfilled; no sites remain

Final `m_sitesPerTeam` cardinalities are therefore 4 and 2 rather than the required 5 and 1.

This setup is not excluded by SPI's large-team safety gate. For six players and two alive teams:

    players^2 = 36
    36 * aliveTeams = 72

and the constructor bails only when `players^2 > 36 * aliveTeams`. Thus 5+1 is on the ordinary
supported SPI team-game path. Many other supported unequal arrangements fail similarly (for
example 5+2, 5+1+1, 5+2+1); this is not a single exotic partition.

CALLER CONTRACT / DEBUG FAILURE
-------------------------------
`CvGame::assignStartingPlots()` consumes the SPI result by asking for exactly one stored site for
each actual member of each team:

    apStartsPerPlayer[itMember->getID()] = spi.getTeamSite(
            itTeam->getID(), itMember.nextIndex() - 1);

`getTeamSite()` returns NULL when the requested member index is outside that team's stored vector.
For the 5+1 example, the fifth member of the size-5 team therefore receives NULL.

The caller explicitly states the intended invariant:

    // SPI should do all the work or none
    FAssert(itPlayer.nextIndex() == 1 && pNormalizationTarget == NULL);

But a completed SPI run has already executed `doIterations()`, which sets
`m_bNormalizationTargetReady = true`; `createNormalizationTarget()` therefore returns a non-NULL
target. The missing fifth site consequently violates this assertion in an FAssert-enabled build.
This is not merely a preference disagreement inside the greedy scorer; the producer returns a
shape the consumer explicitly declares invalid.

RELEASE-PATH PARTIAL-APPLICATION / DUPLICATE-START HAZARD
----------------------------------------------------------
The Release path is also behaviorally unsafe. The caller applies the SPI site permutation in alive
player order and breaks at the first NULL:

    if (apStartsPerPlayer[itPlayer->getID()] != NULL)
        itPlayer->setStartingPlot(apStartsPerPlayer[itPlayer->getID()]);
    else
    {
        bTeamAssignmentDone = false;
        ...
        break;
    }

The values stored in `m_sitesPerTeam` are player IDs only as *placeholders for their current start
sites*; `teamValue()` is free to assign any available placeholder site to any team. Consequently an
earlier player can be reassigned to the original start of a later player. If the underfilled team's
NULL member is then encountered before that later player is processed, the loop breaks and the
later player keeps the same original start.

A concrete legal placeholder shape for 5+1 illustrates the leak:

    large-team stored placeholders: [5, 0, 1, 2]   (only four entries)
    small-team stored placeholders: [3, 4]          (two entries)

If players 0..4 are the large team and player 5 is the solo team, the caller can perform:

    player 0 -> original site of player 5
    player 1 -> original site of player 0
    player 2 -> original site of player 1
    player 3 -> original site of player 2
    player 4 -> NULL => break

Player 5 is never reached and still points at its original site. Players 0 and 5 now both point at
that same plot.

`CvPlayer::setStartingPlot()` only decrements/increments area starting-plot counters and assigns the
player's `m_pStartingPlot`; it does not evict or rewrite another player whose starting-plot pointer
already names `pNewValue`. Duplicate starts are therefore allowed to persist through this partial
application.

The subsequent old BtS fallback does not restore the omitted unique-site permutation:

- its preliminary loop only calls `findStartingPlot()` for players whose start pointer is NULL;
  the partially applied players all still have non-NULL pointers;
- `rearrangeTeamStarts(false, 0)` only swaps the existing player->start assignments, so it preserves
  the multiset of currently referenced plots and cannot recreate a unique start that was lost when
  the partial permutation broke;
- its distance precomputation / team-closeness logic assumes ordinary distinct starts and can itself
  encounter zero distances if duplicate starts survived;
- `applyStartingLocHandicaps()` explicitly returns early for unequal team sizes, so that later phase
  does not rebuild the assignment either.

Thus the defect ranges from a guaranteed Debug assertion / loss of the SPI team solution to a
Release-path duplicate-start state for reachable site-placeholder permutations. The duplicate
manifestation does not require any illegal team configuration or water start; only ordinary unequal
team sizes plus a site ordering that assigns a later player's placeholder to an earlier player.

HISTORY / INHERITANCE
---------------------
AdvC practical 2708 (`9a623ad895c73c2ce0fe4d5f5cf668ab04848307`, 2020-12-12), titled
"Let SPI handle team games, plus other changes to starting sites", introduced together:

- `m_sitesPerTeam`;
- `assignSitesToTeams()` with the current round-robin;
- `getTeamSite()`;
- the `CvGame::assignStartingPlots()` consumer and its explicit
  "SPI should do all the work or none" assertion.

The full commit message describes the new code as a greedy algorithm for assigning starting sites in
team games and says SPI is deliberately skipped only for team games with sufficiently high player
count / average team size because the greedy algorithm handles those poorly. The 5+1 counterexample
passes that very gate, so it is within the feature's intended active domain rather than a bypassed
large-team case.

Focused reachable-history search finds `assignSitesToTeams` only in the original team-support work,
a later merge carrying the same implementation, a broad refactor/header touch and SAS formatting

Current Base AdvC 1.14 retains the same rotation and the same `CvGame` all-or-none consumer
unchanged. K-Mod and Civ4CE do not contain this AdvC-created SPI team assignment subsystem.
Classification: inherited AdvC defect, not a SAS regression.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Preserve the intended "two members at a time" greedy rotation, but never select a team that has
already received `getNumMembers()` sites.

A narrow repair can advance past completed teams before assigning the next site (or remove completed
teams from the active rotation). Because the total number of available placeholder sites equals the
total number of alive civilization players/team members, successful completion should establish:

    m_sitesPerTeam[eTeam].size() == GET_TEAM(eTeam).getNumMembers()

for every alive civilization team.

Add a post-assignment assertion for that exact invariant before exposing `m_sitesPerTeam` to
`CvGame`. The consumer's existing all-or-none assertion is too late because it detects the mismatch
only while already applying the permutation.

Regression coverage should include at least:

1. 5+1 teams: expected stored counts 5+1, never 4+2;
2. 5+2 teams: expected 5+2, never 4+3;
3. 5+1+1 and 5+2+1 mixed teams;
4. a placeholder ordering where the large team selects the original site of a later player, proving
   that the fixed producer lets the caller apply a complete permutation with no duplicate starts;
5. existing equal-size 2+2 / 3+3 cases to ensure the two-at-a-time clustering behavior is retained;
6. the existing large-team SPI bail condition, which should remain unchanged unless deliberately
   redesigned separately.

F627 / PROVISIONAL KI#949 — CONFIRMED INHERITED ADVC STALE DIJKSTRA QUEUE ENTRIES OVERWRITE SETTLED SHORTEST DISTANCES
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SEVERITY / CLASS: current-live central starting-position metric defect; inherited AdvC shortest-path
bookkeeping/order bug.
ROOT FILE: `CvGameCoreDLL/StartingPositionIteration.cpp`,
`StartingPositionIteration::DistanceTable::computeDistances`.

CURRENT CODE / ALGORITHM CONTRACT
---------------------------------
`DistanceTable::computeDistances` explicitly describes itself as:

    // Plain old Dijkstra's algorithm

It uses an inverse-ordered `std::priority_queue<Node>` so that the smallest queued distance is popped
first:

    bool operator<(Node const& kOther) const
    {
        return m_iDistance > kOther.m_iDistance;
    }

and keeps a reached/settled map because the same physical plot can occur in the queue more than once.
The source comment says this directly:

    /* Note: even if not yet reached, it may already be in q;
       that's what the abReached[...] check above is for. */

The current loop, however, writes the popped distance into the public `DistanceTable` BEFORE testing
whether that queue entry is stale:

    Node v = q.top();
    q.pop();
    CvPlot const& kAt = v.get();
    setDistance(kSource, kAt, v.getDistance());
    {
        PlotNumTypes eAt = kAt.plotNum();
        if (abReached.get(eAt))
            continue;
        abReached.set(eAt, true);
    }

The first pop of a reachable plot is the shortest path under Dijkstra's positive edge weights and is
correctly marked reached. But any longer copy that had already been queued later reaches the top,
executes `setDistance` FIRST, overwrites the correct settled value, and only then notices
`abReached[eAt]` and discards itself.

`setDistance` is a plain assignment for destinations:

    m_distances[eSource][eDestination] = iDistance;

There is no minimum check that could preserve the earlier shortest value.

MINIMAL CURRENT-LIVE GRID COUNTEREXAMPLE
----------------------------------------
Take a normal passable land corner/patch with source S, two cardinal neighbors A and B, and diagonal
destination D:

    B -- D
    |  / |
    S -- A

For ordinary land, `stepDist` is 9 cardinal and 12 diagonal:

    if (!kTo.isWater())
        return (bDiagonal ? 12 : 9);

Queue evolution is therefore:

1. Start with `S(0)`.
2. Pop S. Queue direct `A(9)`, `B(9)` and diagonal `D(12)`.
3. Pop A(9) before D(12). Because D is not reached yet, A queues an alternate `D(18)`.
4. Pop B(9) before D(12). B can likewise queue another `D(18)`.
5. Pop the direct D(12). Current code stores 12 and marks D reached. This is the correct shortest
   path.
6. Later pop stale D(18). Current code stores 18 first, THEN sees that D is reached and continues.

The final table therefore contains 18, not 12. This does not require a rare obstacle, water frontier,
wrapping map or special game option. It arises from an ordinary diagonal destination with a second
cardinal route. Larger open neighborhoods can have additional stale alternatives; the exact final
overwrite can depend on which longer copies had entered the queue, but it cannot be assumed to remain
the first settled shortest value.

The reproducer is current-live in SPI. During construction, all candidate/current starting sites are
explicitly forced into `relevantPlots` via `sitePlotNums`, and any other workable plot with positive
SPI yield value is also a destination:

    if (yieldValues.get(eLoopPlotNum) > 0 ||
        sitePlotNums.count(eLoopPlotNum) > 0)
    {
        relevantPlots.push_back(...);
    }

So D can simply be another starting/candidate site; no yield/XML edge case is needed.

DOWNSTREAM GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCE
-------------------------------
The corrupted table is a central SPI input rather than temporary debug state.

`SpaceEvaluator` reads `DistanceTable::d` for every retained yield destination when building claim
competition:

    short iDist = kDists.d(kStartPlot, kLoopPlot) - iDistSubtr;
    ...
    rSum += claim_t(1, std::max<short>(1, iDist));

and later directly reads the stored source/destination entry again to derive each player's claim and
access/delay factor before adding yield to expansion-space value.

More importantly, original/current starting sites are destinations too, and
`computeRivalDistFactors` uses these same corrupted values as the path distances between starting
sites:

    aiRivalDists.push_back(m_pPathDists->d(
        kStartPlot, *itRival->getStartingPlot()));

Those factors feed ordinary per-player start-value scoring. Consequently F627 can alter both
expansion-space ownership/access estimates and the rival-spacing component used to decide which
starting-position solution SPI prefers.

The bug generally biases a destination toward whichever stale longer queue copy is written last,
not toward its shortest path. It is therefore not a simple uniform rescale that would cancel in
relative comparisons.

HISTORY / INHERITANCE
---------------------
AdvC practical 2280 (`a70e4ce3a1db01c51da7fa370a706d8784191b38`,
"Algorithm for fairer starting positions (wip)", 2020-05-28) CREATED
`StartingPositionIteration.cpp` and introduced `DistanceTable::computeDistances` with this exact
ordering:

    setDistance(kSource, kAt, v.getDistance());
    if (abReached[iAt])
        continue;
    abReached[iAt] = true;

The introduction already contained the explicit duplicate-queue comment, so duplicate entries were
part of the intended algorithm from the start; only the placement of the table write is wrong.

AdvC practical 2302 changed distance/frontier semantics but retained the ordering. Practical 3134
refactored the reached state to `EnumMap`, again preserving `setDistance` before the guard. The later
3392 merge likewise preserves it. SAS practical 5961 is signature/formatting cleanup only and does
not semantically touch this loop.

Current Base AdvC 1.14 still has the same `setDistance`-before-`abReached` sequence. K-Mod and Civ4CE
do not contain the AdvC-created StartingPositionIteration subsystem. Classification is therefore an
inherited AdvC defect, not a SAS/BtS/K-Mod/Civ4CE regression.

DEDUP
-----
Focused whole-album and current `README_Known_Issues.md` searches for `computeDistances`, Dijkstra,
priority-queue, reached/settled and stale-distance wording found no prior owner for this SPI shortest-
path overwrite.

The nearby Queue-025 findings are independent:

- F624 / KI#946: `NormalizationTarget::isReached` switch fallthrough changes normalization-level
  tolerance ordering.
- F625 / KI#947: the special low-value-land water fallback writes raw `CvMap::plotDistance` units
  into the weighted `DistanceTable` metric. F625 remains real after F627 is repaired because its
  fallback explicitly replaces the ordinary Dijkstra result with a separate raw geometric value.
- F626 / KI#948: unequal-team round-robin overfills completed teams and can cause partial starting-
  plot permutation/duplicate starts.
- F169 / KI#492: discarded full city-site evaluations are a performance issue, not path correctness.

No semantic duplicate was found.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The narrow semantic repair is to discard already-settled queue entries BEFORE publishing their
queue distance:

    CvPlot const& kAt = v.get();
    PlotNumTypes eAt = kAt.plotNum();
    if (abReached.get(eAt))
        continue;
    abReached.set(eAt, true);
    setDistance(kSource, kAt, v.getDistance());

With the current nonnegative/positive `stepDist` costs, the first popped entry for a plot is the
Dijkstra shortest path. Writing only that settled entry restores the intended contract without
changing path weights, frontier heuristics, destination selection or `SpaceEvaluator` formulas.

An alternative defensive `min(old,new)` write could mask the symptom for destinations, but moving
the write behind the reached guard is the clearer algorithmic fix and avoids unnecessary stale
writes entirely.

Regression coverage should include at least:

1. ordinary land S -> diagonal D returns 12 even after cardinal alternate D(18) entries are queued;
2. several small obstacle/open-grid cases compared against a reference shortest-path calculation;
3. inter-start distances used by `computeRivalDistFactors`, not just yield destinations;
4. water/frontier routes to ensure only stale-entry publication changes, not the intended 4/5/9/12
   and frontier edge costs; and
5. F625's Ocean-Fish/omitted-land fallback separately, because fixing F627 must not be mistaken for
   fixing that independent metric mismatch.

POST-F627 CONTROLS / CONTINUATION
--------------------------------
The following candidates remain intentionally unpromoted:

- `DistanceTable` signed-short overflow on pathological long/thin custom maps remains generic
  mod-data robustness until a supported shipped-map path is established.
- `currAltSites` uses `break` when a remote alternative equals the first move's taken site; this can
  prune later remote alternatives but remains a lower-severity search-completeness concern pending a
  stronger outcome proof.
- `SpaceEvaluator`'s static delay-factor cache is safe under the current contract because
  `DistanceTable::getLongDist()` is constant (`8 * 40`), making the cache threshold invariant.
- `startingPositionValue`'s end-of-iterator `nextIndex()` divisor is safe because `AgentIterator`
  defines end `nextIndex()` as the filtered iteration count, not the absolute player ID.
- General wrapped-map `PlotRadiusIterator` duplicate visits remain reserved for Queue 167 rather than
  being consumed as a Queue-025 root.
