-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F636 / provisional KI#958 -- city-bearing WorldBuilder scenarios retain the
pre-feature water-area partition, so stock Earth1000AD ignores Ice barriers in
PASSABLE_AREAS topology for gameplay
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

STATUS
------
NEW CURRENT DEFECT ROOT, inherited AdvC scenario/PASSABLE_AREAS initialization
interaction; stock BtS Earth1000AD reproducer.

ROOT / LOAD ORDER
-----------------
Current WorldBuilder map application deliberately performs area calculation before
features are applied:

    CvWBDesc.applyMap():
      ... rebuild map ...
      pDesc.preApply() for every plot    // plot type + terrain
      CyMap().recalculateAreas()
      pDesc.apply() for every plot       // rivers/start/bonus/improvement/FEATURE/route

`CvPlotDesc.preApply()` sets PlotType/TerrainType only. `CvPlotDesc.apply()` later
calls `plot.setFeatureType(...)`, so `FEATURE_ICE` is absent when that preliminary
area partition is built.

That ordering matters because current/default `PASSABLE_AREAS=1` deliberately makes
Ice part of water-area topology. `CvMap::calculateAreas_dfs()` skips impassable roots
on its first pass and does not traverse from an impassable plot back into passable
water, allowing Ice packs to separate passable seas.

Ordinary newly generated games repair the preliminary partition after Ice/normalization
through `CvGame::setInitialItems()` -> `GC.getMap().recalculateAreas()`.
Scenarios do not call `setInitialItems`; they enter `CvGame::initScenario()` instead.
Current `initScenario()` explicitly refuses the post-feature rebuild whenever any major
player already has a city:

    if (GC.getDefineBOOL(CvGlobals::PASSABLE_AREAS))
    {
        bool bRecalc = true;
        for (...)
        {
            if (GET_PLAYER(...).getNumCities() > 0)
                bRecalc = false;
        }
        if (bRecalc)
            GC.getMap().recalculateAreas();
    }

The source comment explains the safety concern: wholesale `recalculateAreas()` was not
trusted around preplaced scenario cities/free units. The consequence is nevertheless
that city-bearing scenarios keep the earlier pre-Ice area identities for gameplay.

STOCK CURRENT-LIVE REPRODUCER
-----------------------------
The supplied Civ4CE BtS archive contains the stock public scenario
`BtS/PublicMaps/Earth1000AD.CivBeyondSwordWBSave`, a scenario usable by BtS mods.
Its map data provides a concrete supported fixture:

- grid: 124 x 68, wrap X = 1, wrap Y = 0;
- 69 preplaced cities;
- 537 `FEATURE_ICE` plot entries.

The 69 cities deterministically disable `initScenario()`'s post-feature
`recalculateAreas()` branch.

Reconstructing Earth1000AD's water graph from the WB plot data with current
`CvMap::isSeparatedByIsthmus` semantics shows that Ice is not topologically inert.
Without Ice, several high-Arctic non-Ice waters belong to the giant ocean component.
When Ice is treated as impassable, that same old giant component is split; concrete
passable pockets split out include:

- 16 tiles around `(12,64)` ... `(21,62)`;
- 9 tiles around `(95,65)` ... `(101,66)`;
- 5 tiles around `(5,66)` ... `(8,66)`;
- further 2-tile pockets in the same old ocean component.

For reference, the largest non-Ice water connectivity component is 5262 tiles when
features are ignored and 4775 passable tiles when Ice barriers are honored. The exact
CvArea tile totals also include the barrier Ice assigned to one side, but the decisive
fact is the changed connectivity of ordinary non-Ice water plots: plots in the pockets
and plots in the main sea are in one preliminary area and in different correct
PASSABLE_AREAS after features.

HARD NATIVE CONTRACT / CONSEQUENCE
----------------------------------
This is not merely stale diagnostic metadata. `CvArea::canBeEntered` uses area identity
as its strongest reachability shortcut:

    if (getID() == kFrom.getID())
        return true;

For two distinct water areas separated only by Ice, the correct post-Ice topology has
different area IDs but the same representative BtS water body. The subsequent test then
returns false for an ordinary sea unit that cannot move through impassable tiles:

    if (isWater() == kFrom.isWater() &&
        (m_iRepresentativeArea != kFrom.m_iRepresentativeArea ||
         (u != NULL && !u->canMoveImpassable())))
        return false;

Thus Earth1000AD's stale pre-feature partition changes this coarse naval reachability
answer from the intended FALSE to TRUE for ordinary ships across those Ice barriers.
Current AI/unit code deliberately consumes `CvArea::canBeEntered` and water-area identity
as coarse reachability/accounting filters before or alongside pathfinding. The scenario
therefore starts with a topology contract that contradicts the actual feature-level
passability until some later unrelated full area rebuild happens (if one ever does).

LINEAGE
-------
AdvC practical 1274 / commit `b50e4a9a5a...` introduced Ice-sensitive PASSABLE_AREAS
and explicitly noted that at least the Earth_IceAge scenario places Ice after the first
`CvMap::calculateAreas` call. It initially attempted a scenario recalculation from
`setInitialItems`.

Practical 1275 / `71fa4eef1a...` moved the ordinary post-Ice recalculation to after
starting-position normalization and documented that some scenarios do not call
`setInitialItems`.

Practical 1347 / `1cfdc903de...` then added the current preplaced-city bailout in
`initScenario`, explicitly because full `recalculateAreas()` was considered unsafe with
preplaced cities/other scenario state. Later refactors preserve this behavior. Supplied
Base AdvC 1.14 retains the same logic; current SAS inherits it.

So this is a deliberate safety workaround with an unintended correctness cost, not a
SAS formatting regression. The stock Earth1000AD data proves the excluded domain is real.

DEDUP
-----
This is independent of the earlier area/Ice findings:

- F025 / KI#346: topology becomes stale when Ice passability changes *during gameplay*
  (notably global-warming melt) after areas were initially correct. Current SAS repairs
  that mutation path with deferred `resetPathDistance`, `recalculateWaterAreas`, and
  plot-group refresh.
- F249 / KI#572: batched map generation can leave stale area pointers while map plots are
  being constructed; different lifecycle/root.
- F634 / KI#956: newly added normalization lakes temporarily retain stale cached `m_bLake`;
  lake classification/value cache, not scenario Ice-area partition.

No reconciled album/Known-Issues owner was found for the load-time city-bearing scenario
case proved here. F636 therefore owns only the missing safe post-feature water-area rebuild
for scenarios that contain cities.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Do not simply remove the historical city guard and call wholesale `recalculateAreas()`;
the source explicitly records why that was avoided.

Current SAS now has a much narrower helper introduced for KI#346:
`CvMap::recalculateWaterAreas()`. It:

1. detaches/deletes only water CvAreas;
2. leaves land/city area state intact;
3. rebuilds water areas through `calculateAreas_dfs()`;
4. runs `calculateReprAreas()` -> `updateLakes()` -> `computeShelves()`;
5. restores coastal-city counts on the newly built primary water areas.

That helper is therefore the natural repair candidate for the city-bearing scenario branch
after WB features have been applied. A scenario-start repair should also review whether any
path-distance / plot-group cache can already exist at that exact initialization point; if so,
mirror KI#346's invalidation as needed rather than broadening the rebuild indiscriminately.

Regression coverage:
1. load stock Earth1000AD with `PASSABLE_AREAS=1`;
2. preserve every preplaced city/unit and its land-area bookkeeping;
3. after scenario initialization, non-Ice Arctic pocket `(12,64)` and the main ocean should
   have different water-area IDs where Ice blocks passage;
4. their representative water-area IDs should still match as the same BtS ocean body;
5. `CvArea::canBeEntered` for an ordinary non-Ice-capable ship across those areas should be
   false, while an Ice-capable/submarine-style permitted unit retains the intended exception;
6. stock Earth_IceAge (no preplaced cities) should remain correct through its existing full
   scenario recalculation path;
7. scenarios without Ice should remain behaviorally unchanged.

Six independent current defect roots survive the full current-body, companion-header,

   detection is a shipped live reproducer.

   recomputation deletes old shelves but `uninit()`/destruction does not delete the final cache.

   making ordinary naval `canUpgrade` disagree with exhaustive upgrade-city search on dual coasts.

   area rebuild, so later normalization misses lake food/fresh-water value and can over-normalize.

   intended partially-ready groups because `readyToSelect()` polarity is inverted in ranking.
6. F636 / KI#958 -- city-bearing WorldBuilder scenarios skip the post-feature Ice-aware water-area
   rebuild; stock Earth1000AD starts gameplay with pre-Ice PASSABLE_AREAS topology.
